items.abstract: Abstract The dynamic choreography of biomolecular interactions underpins the processes of life, but its direct observation remains challenging. Here we introduce continuous mass photometry, enabling hour-long, mass-resolved observation of individual biomolecules tethered to supported lipid bilayers, their complexes and interactions, with up to sub-kilodalton mass precision and millisecond temporal resolution. Our approach represents a quantitative time-resolved single-molecule measurement modality for studying complex biomolecular mechanisms in action.

items.abstract: Abstract Deep visual proteomics (DVP) is an emerging approach for cell-type-specific and spatially resolved proteomics. However, its broad adoption has been constrained by the lack of an open-source end-to-end workflow within a community-driven ecosystem. Here we introduce openDVP, an experimental and computational framework for accessible and scalable DVP. OpenDVP combines open-source image analysis tools (MCMICRO, QuPath and napari) with scverse formats (AnnData and SpatialData) for multiomics integration. It provides two workflows: a fast-track pipeline requiring no image analysis expertise, and an artificial intelligence-powered pipeline incorporating state-of-the-art methods for image preprocessing, segmentation and spatial analysis. We apply openDVP across three archival tissue studies (human placenta, early stage lung cancer and locally relapsed breast cancer), integrating spatial single-cell phenotypes with exploratory proteomic measurements. Finally, we introduce deep proteomic profiling of cellular neighborhoods as a scalable approach for spatial discovery proteomics.

items.abstract: Abstract Adeno-associated virus (AAV) vectors have been applied for precise genome engineering in human T cells but poor tropism restricts their efficiency and translational potential. Here, through directed evolution of the AAV6 capsid in primary human T cells, we identified a family of variants containing an APR motif at residues 455–457. The lead candidate, AAV.APR31, enabled robust transduction of primary T and NK cells at nearly 100–1,000-fold lower doses than AAV6 and outperformed the human T cell-tropic capsid AAV-hT7. CRISPR screening identified CD7 as a lineage-specific entry enhancer alongside the canonical AAVR pathway and structural analysis suggested that the APR motif facilitates CD7 engagement. Unlike existing delivery systems confined to one engineering mode, AAV.APR31 enabled transient transgene delivery, site-specific knock-in and transposon integration in human T and NK cells, generating CAR-T cells functionally equivalent to lentiviral vector-manufactured products. Systemic administration of AAV.APR31-generated CAR-T cells in vivo resulted in potent tumor control in hematologic and solid tumor mouse models.

items.abstract: Abstract Here we present DynaVelo, a generative neural ordinary differential equation model that learns the joint dynamics of gene expression and transcription factor (TF) motif activity from single-cell multiome data. DynaVelo learns a functional form of the vector field, such that the model can be perturbed in silico and not only used to draw trajectories. We show that DynaVelo recovers the bifurcating in vivo dynamics of wild-type murine germinal center (GC) B cells and reveals how these dynamics change under heterozygous loss of epigenetic regulators Arid1a and Ctcf . In silico perturbation yields dynamic and cell-state-specific gene regulatory networks (GRNs) that recover known TF-to-gene edges in the wild-type GC GRN and predicts those that are disrupted in mutants. Perturbing Arid1aHet GCs in silico identified Ctcf , Stat3 and Bcl6 as rescue targets for Arid1a loss. In vivo experiments in double-heterozygous mice confirmed rescue of the Arid1aHet dark-zone phenotype in all three cases, and multiome profiling of Arid1aHet ; CtcfHet GCs validated the predicted shift toward wild-type dynamics.

items.title: Recordanelles for transcriptome-wide single-cell RNA recording in human cells
items.abstract: Abstract Transcriptomic measurement technologies provide powerful approaches to understand biology but are limited to providing either a high-resolution snapshot at a moment in time or a low-resolution history of transcription constrained to a few genes over a narrow time range. Here, we introduce the ‘recordanelle’, a single-component synthetic organelle capable of recording the transcriptome in human cells. Recordanelles are composed of a mitochondrial membrane anchor, a condensate assembler and a poly(A)-binding protein. We demonstrate that the recordanelle can be engineered to recruit engineered RNAs or a sampling of up to 90% of all endogenous mRNAs and protect them over several days. We further show that transient and dynamic transcriptional responses resulting from inducible promoters or interferon signaling are preserved throughout time within the recordanelle at the single-cell level. This work provides a nondisruptive and unbiased transcriptome-wide single-cell RNA recording technology to enable a deeper understanding of biology.

Constructing radiative dipolar excitons via frontier-state hybridization in 2D perovskites
items.abstract: Abstract Realizing dipolar excitons that simultaneously exhibit strong optical activity and long-range repulsive interactions remains a central challenge in exciton-based nonlinear optics. This challenge stems from the intrinsic trade-off between achieving spatial charge separation, which is necessary for dipole formation, and maintaining sufficient wavefunction overlap to ensure efficient radiative recombination. Here, we overcome this trade-off in the two-dimensional perovskite (AE3T)PbI 4 by leveraging organic-inorganic band-edge engineering to induce frontier-state hybridization, thereby forming bright hybridized dipolar excitons with spatially indirect character and appreciable optical transition strength. These excitons combine an out-of-plane permanent electric-dipole component, room-temperature nonlinear transport consistent with long-range dipole–dipole repulsion, and finite optical transition dipole moments. Beyond addressing a key constraint in dipolar-exciton design, this work establishes frontier-state hybridization as a molecular design principle for constructing optically active, electrically polarized excitons in low-dimensional quantum materials.

items.title: EpiPack: A computational framework for reference mapping and out-of-reference detection for single-cell ATAC-seq data with heterogeneous peak features
In-situ fabrication of ultra-conformal nanomesh epidermal sensors on arbitrary skin surface
Leveraging sequence purification for accurate prediction of multiple conformational states with AlphaFold2
items.abstract: Abstract AlphaFold2 (AF2) has transformed protein structure prediction by harnessing co-evolutionary constraints embedded in multiple sequence alignments (MSAs). MSAs not only encode static structural information, but also contain evolutionary signatures linked to protein dynamics and conformational heterogeneity, which are central to biological function. However, the subtle co-evolutionary signals that bias proteins toward distinct conformational states are often obscured by noise within MSA data and remain challenging to decipher. Here, we introduce AF-ClaSeq, a systematic framework that enriches and purifies state-specific evolutionary signals through iterative sequence classification and selection. By identifying sequence subsets that preferentially encode distinct conformational states, AF-ClaSeq enables robust predictions of alternative conformations across diverse protein systems. Our findings indicate that the accuracy of alternative-state prediction depends more on the purity of the evolutionary signal within an MSA than on sequence depth. Notably, purified sequences encoding specific structural states are distributed across phylogenetic clades and superfamilies, rather than being confined to individual lineages. By extending AF2 beyond single-state structure prediction, AF-ClaSeq provides a promising approach for exploring protein structural plasticity, establishing a foundation for future studies of the sequence determinants underlying conformational switching and allosteric regulation.

items.title: Highly conductive halide Na-ion conductor enabled by cost-effective aliovalent carbonate polyanion substitution for all-solid-state sodium batteries
4D mitochondrial network assumes distinct and predictive phenotypes through human lung and intestinal epithelial development
items.abstract: Abstract Mitochondria form dynamic three-dimensional networks that exhibit a wide range of morphology and motility depending on cell state, cell type, and cell fate. Isolated phenotypes have been described for individual cell states, but how mitochondrial morphology and motility change across the full course of human tissue development has so far been unclear. Human stem cell-derived branching lung and intestinal organoids mimic developing human organs and make these systems accessible. Here we show, by imaging at key developmental time points from human stem cell through mature organoid tissue with lattice light-sheet microscopy, that mitochondrial networks adopt morphology and motility signatures that vary with developmental stage, that mitochondrial and cellular features can be used to predict developmental stage, and that two-dimensional measurements obscure features resolved only in three dimensions over time, yielding an integrated map of mitochondrial phenotypes across human tissue development.

Improving molecular property prediction with score-based diffusion models
items.abstract: Abstract We explore diffusion-based training as a flexible approach to molecular property prediction in settings shaped by chemical, biophysical, and latent heterogeneity. To address this, we build on score-based generative diffusion models and introduce a conditional diffusion module for predictive tasks, equipped with a joint training and sampling guidance scheme and an optional gated residual mechanism that regulates feature- vs target-driven information flow across noise levels. The module acts as a plug-in learning block for existing molecular encoders, making it complementary to advances in representation learning. Across diverse feature extractors and graph neural networks, diffusion-based training improves over conventional maximum-likelihood objectives on small-molecule regression benchmarks and matches or exceeds strong baselines on multitask regression and classification datasets. It also produces well-calibrated predictive uncertainty as measured by prediction interval coverage, enables confidence-guided ranking, and performs well in challenging settings including activity cliffs and class-imbalanced multitask prediction. Overall, these results position diffusion as a promising representation-agnostic approach for effective molecular property prediction.

items.title: MyoGen: unified biophysical modeling of human neuromotor activity and resulting signals
items.abstract: Abstract Understanding human motor control requires integrating cortical and spinal activity, muscle mechanics, and electrophysiology, which are typically studied in isolation. We present MyoGen, an open-source framework that unifies spinal circuitry, proprioceptive feedback, musculotendon dynamics, and multimodal electromyography generation. Using data-driven optimization benchmarked against human motor unit recordings, MyoGen produces motor unit population activity matching experimental discharge-rate distributions and variability across muscles. The framework generates decomposable surface and intramuscular electromyography, reproduces beta-band modulation of descending drive and its transformation into force, and implements key sensorimotor loop components. Dimensionality reduction of simulated agonist-antagonist electromyography reveals low-dimensional control manifolds consistent with recordings from able-bodied individuals and those with spinal cord injury. Here, we show that MyoGen provides a physiologically grounded simulation substrate, enabling systematic investigation of motor control principles, benchmarking of signal-processing algorithms, and exploration of experimentally inaccessible sensorimotor interactions.

items.title: A near-quantum-limited diamond maser amplifier operating at millikelvin temperatures
items.abstract: Abstract Current microwave quantum technologies require the amplification of weak signals with minimal added noise at millikelvin temperatures. To date, this stringent requirement has been met exclusively by superconducting technologies, such as Josephson or kinetic-inductance parametric amplifiers. A fundamentally distinct alternative approach could be offered by masers, the microwave counterpart of lasers, which were predicted as early as the 1950s to achieve quantum-limited noise performance under ideal conditions. However, their dependence on cryogenic operation historically limited further advancement. Here we demonstrate the first-ever non-superconducting, near-quantum-limited maser amplifier operating at millikelvin temperatures utilising nitrogen impurity spins (P1 centres) in diamond. Population inversion is achieved via microwave pumping, exploiting a four-spin cross-relaxation mechanism. We realise a maximum power gain exceeding 30 dB, an added noise of approximately 2.55 quanta above the standard quantum limit, and a maximum 1 dB output compression point of −63 dBm at 6.595 GHz. The ability to operate in strong static magnetic fields of arbitrary orientation may offer a complementary, non-superconducting route for applications such as semiconducting spin-qubit readout, magnetic-resonance spectroscopy, and dark-matter axion searches.

items.title: Burst-like intracellular antibody infusion via membrane-permeabilizing peptide microcondensates
A precommissural nucleus-cingulate circuit coordinates a stress-induced agitation-like state
Structurally guided wavefront neural encoder for broad-range generalizable 3D holography
items.abstract: Abstract Deep learning has advanced computer-generated holography, but learned models remain coupled to fixed wavelengths and distances, limiting generalization. Here we present the structurally guided wavefront neural encoder (SGWN-Encoder), which integrates diffraction physics with neural networks and employs a structural propagation strategy that analytically strips the parameter-sensitive global phase. This reveals a scale-normalized description of diffraction, letting the network learn transferable light-field evolution rules and generalize across propagation distances and visible wavelengths by direct inference. A dataset-free paradigm built on statistically diverse random fields teaches the model the structural mapping from complex amplitude to phase-only holograms instead of external image distributions. Without fine-tuning, a single SGWN-Encoder maintains a distance-averaged RGB PSNR of 31.9 dB and SSIM of 0.91 over the primary 2–200 mm range, retaining reconstruction up to 500 mm. Numerical and optical experiments on full-color 3D scenes establish a physically grounded route toward adaptive holographic displays.

items.title: Co-deficiency of RECQL1 and BLM causes replication stress associated with DNA damage and cohesion loss
items.abstract: Abstract The mechanistic basis for chromosomal instability characteristic of RECQ helicase disorders remains poorly understood due to their molecular-genetic complexity. To characterize the genetic interactions of RECQL1 ( also referred to as RECQL or RECQ1) , implicated in RECON syndrome, we performed an RNA interference screen and discovered a functional relationship with BLM , a gene that is mutated in Bloom syndrome. RECQL1/BLM co-deficient cells display pronounced replication stress, DNA damage accumulation, and chromosomal instability. Strikingly, RECQL1/BLM co-deficiency induces sister chromatid separation during metaphase suppressible by depletion of the cohesin unloader WAPL, suggesting that a threshold of replication stress in the genetically co-deficient cells disrupts cohesion. Primary embryonic fibroblasts from transgenic Blm -/- ;Recql -/- mice recapitulate the sister chromatid separation phenotype and heightened replication stress observed for human cells. Our findings highlight the joint roles of RECQL1 and BLM in the replication stress response and their concurrent importance for maintenance of chromosomal stability even in the absence of exogenously induced DNA damage. Furthermore, we elucidated a genetic interaction in which sister chromatid cohesion is synergistically elevated by the loss of two conserved RECQ helicases encoded by genes in which mutations are linked to hereditary diseases that are not associated with sister chromatid cohesion defects. The findings presented provide insights into the genetic crosstalk of two prominent RECQ helicases with established importance in clinical diseases of genomic instability.

items.title: Phenotypic discovery of GABAA receptor-mediated general anesthetics with analgesic activity
items.abstract: Abstract General anesthetics are essential for invasive medical procedures; however, there remains a need for safer agents. Using a bespoke 96-well-plate format platform enabling high-throughput imaging of larval zebrafish behavior, we screen 12,000 compounds and identify an isoxazole chemotype that phenocopies the intravenous anesthetics etomidate and propofol. Its optimization via medicinal chemistry yields an anesthetic that we call nidradine. This anesthetic is efficacious in both zebrafish and mice and lacks the problematic adrenal suppression characteristic of etomidate. Mechanistic studies using electrophysiology and structural biology reveal that nidradine, like etomidate and propofol, is a positive allosteric modulator of the GABA A receptor. Remarkably, behavioral assays in mice demonstrate that nidradine differs from most general anesthetics in that it also produces analgesia at subsedative doses.

items.title: Encapsulating an iron complex within a heme and anthraquinone codecorated capsule for multiphoton C(sp3)−H bond oxygenation
Mapping dynamics of subcellular RNA and protein localization and organization using optimal transport
Facet-dependent anion adsorption for electrolyte-Cu interfacial stability in initially anode-free Li-metal batteries
Site-specific N-glycoproteomic analysis of extracellular vesicles from seminal plasma reveals the molecular typing of azoospermia
Directly visualizing the energy level structure of quantum dot molecules
items.abstract: Abstract The orbital, spin and valley degrees of freedom in silicon quantum dots (QDs) support many modes of spin qubit operation. However, it is generally challenging to probe the energy level spectrum over a large parameter space. We demonstrate a spectroscopic technique capable of mapping the energy level structure of a double quantum dot as a function of level detuning, interdot tunnel coupling, and magnetic field. In the one-electron regime, we directly observe the transition from the atom-like energy levels of isolated QDs to molecular-like bonding and anti-bonding states with increasing interdot tunnel coupling. We also resolve the Zeeman splitting of ground and excited valley states in a magnetic field. In the two-electron regime, we gain access to the detuning dependent singlet-triplet splitting. Our work may be extended to a broader class of systems, such as strong spin-orbit materials or proximitized QDs, allowing the direct extraction of various energy gaps.

items.title: An optimized PanFlu-IOA-based mRNA vaccine targeting hemagglutinin confers broad-spectrum protection against heterosubtypic influenza viruses in mice
Cytotoxic drugs and bispecific T cell engagers synergize to rewire host immunity and elicit polyclonal antitumor T cell responses
Phosphorus-mediated reverse hydrogen spillover enables rate-matched nitrate-sulfate paired electrolysis for ammonium persulfate synthesis
Chromatin priming of skeletal stem and progenitor cells governs cell fate during bone repair
Rhizospheric pH mediated thermo-signalling coordinates root growth under heat stress
items.abstract: Abstract Heat stress events pose a major threat to global agriculture due to elevated air and soil temperatures. While plant roots regulate their growth in response to elevated soil temperatures, they appear to rely on thermosensory mechanisms distinct from those used by shoots. Here, we report pH as a key component of a thermo-signaling mechanism that regulates temperature-dependent root responses via ROS-mediated control of cell cycle dynamics in Arabidopsis thaliana . At moderately high temperatures, alkalization of meristematic and transition zones increases superoxide (O₂⁻) levels, promoting cell division and root growth. Conversely, higher temperatures inhibit growth by increasing acidification and hydrogen peroxide (H₂O₂) accumulation in these zones. Elevating external pH buffers this acidification, reduces H₂O₂ levels, and confers heat resistance. Our data support that this pH-mediated heat resistance is also effective under soil conditions. The heat-induced pH shifts are controlled by plasma membrane H⁺-ATPases (PM-H⁺-ATPases), which are under the control of the kinases TOT3 and TOI5. Our findings reveal an interesting pathway for plant adaptation to heat stress, linking pH, ROS and root thermomorphogenesis, with major implications for improving plant resilience in warming climates.

items.title: Assembly of a renal countercurrent system in a beetle
items.abstract: Abstract Countercurrent exchange describes the crossover of some property between two bodies flowing in opposite direction. Countercurrent circuits, which work more efficiently than concurrent circuits, are common in nature and mimicked in human engineering. An example is the beetle cryptonephridial complex (CNC)—a multi-organ water conservation system which makes key contributions to the water budget in a vast number of species. It is even used by some to harvest water from the atmosphere. The system evolved by a radical reorganisation of insect internal anatomy bringing the renal/Malpighian tubules and rectum into countercurrent configuration, and their isolation in a chamber by an unusual tissue of unknown origin—the perinephric membrane. The CNC is richly supplied with tracheae to meet the high metabolic demands of the system. How the CNC is assembled during development is unknown. Here we characterise CNC development in the model beetle Tribolium castaneum and discover the molecular signals orchestrating its assembly. We find that dynamic crosstalk between the developing precursor cells of the rectum, Malpighian tubules, perinephric membrane, and trachea rely on a single, differentially spliced fibroblast growth factor (FGF) receptor and two FGF pathway ligands. We also map the origin of the perinephric membrane to a previously uncharacterised population of mesodermal cells, providing clues to its evolutionary origin. This work illuminates the developmental processes underpinning the reorganisation of the insect internal body plan to assemble a natural countercurrent system, one which is fundamental to beetle physiology, ecology and evolutionary success.

Functional diversity of GPCR–Gustducin complexes controls signaling output and suppresses alternative pathways
items.abstract: Abstract Gustducin (G gust ), the G protein mediating taste receptor signaling, is expressed not only in sensory taste cells but throughout the human body alongside numerous non-taste G protein-coupled receptors (GPCRs). Whether and how these receptors engage G gust , and the functional consequences of such interactions, remain poorly understood. Here, we develop two complementary biosensors that enable direct monitoring of GPCR–G gust interaction and downstream signaling in living cells, allowing pharmacological characterization of G gust activity induced by non-taste GPCRs. We find that several non-taste GPCRs do not activate G gust but instead stabilize the G protein heterotrimer and suppress basal signaling by forming unproductive GPCR–G protein complexes, whereas others induce conventional G gust activation and signal transduction. We further show that these unproductive GPCR–G gust complexes suppress the activation of alternative signaling pathways by sequestering receptors from other G proteins. This mode of interaction functionally partitions GPCRs into activators and inactivators of G gust and represents a mechanism for balancing concurrent signaling pathways within a cell.

Multi-ancestry genetic analysis reveals 29 novel rheumatoid arthritis loci, effector genes and drug repurposing opportunities
items.abstract: Abstract Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) is a complex autoimmune disease with a substantial heritable component. We perform multi-ancestry genome-wide association meta-analyses of 351,498 individuals (comprising 39,600 RA cases and 311,898 controls) by integrating published and new datasets. This analysis identifies 29 novel RA susceptibility loci and systematically classifies association signals as population-specific, population-dominant, or population-shared between East Asian and European populations. Bayesian fine-mapping and functional annotation prioritize putative causal variants, highlighting 67 variants with posterior inclusion probability>0.1 in novel loci, including an SLC27A6 missense variant (rs137898880) and a STIM1 3′ UTR variant (rs3750996). Our gene-prioritization framework combining genetic and biological evidence identifies 203 high-confidence effector genes, 16 of which reside in novel loci (e.g., IFI16 , AIM2 , RGS1 , ITPKB , CD80 , RHOH , NFKB1 , SIK3 , and CCND2 ). Colocalization analysis leveraging tissue-specific eQTL datasets provides mechanistic insights by implicating shared causal variants underlying RA association signals. Notably, the transcription factor gene RUNX3 at a novel locus shows evidence of cis -regulation in immune cells, and RUNX3-binding sites are enriched for variants explaining excess RA heritability, suggesting a potential role for RUNX3 as a trans -regulatory mediator of RA risk at distal RA loci. Finally, exploratory gene-drug interaction networks weighted by RA association strength highlight population-informed therapeutic opportunities and drug-repurposing targets driven largely by novel loci.

items.title: Field-angle-resolved heat transport in UTe2: determination of nodal positions in the superconducting order parameter
items.abstract: Abstract One of the recurring hurdles in studying unconventional superconductivity is the challenge of efficiently and conclusively identifying the symmetry of the superconducting order parameter in a new material. Uranium ditelluride (UTe 2 ) exhibits an unprecedented number of superconducting phases, and none of them has had its symmetry conclusively identified so far. Here we report results of an extensive study of the thermal conductivity of UTe 2 in the superconducting state as a function of the angle of an applied magnetic field rotated in the b-c plane. We observe substantial oscillations in the thermal conductivity as a function of field angle, and, utilizing the experimentally determined Fermi surface, we model this phenomenon for all potential gap structures in UTe 2 . This allows us to identify point nodes near the b-axis, implying that the superconducting order parameter most likely belongs to the B 2 u irreducible representation of the crystal point group.

items.title: Phenotypic variation in Drosophila complex traits is influenced more by genotype and environmental interactions than by mitonuclear coevolutionary history
A Miniaturized Electrostatic Field Sensor Based on MOS Depletion-Layer Capacitance Modulation
Theoretical frameworks for credit assignment via behavioral timescale synaptic plasticity
items.abstract: Abstract Behavioral Timescale Synaptic Plasticity (BTSP) is a form of plasticity which drives place field formation in hippocampal pyramidal neurons. Unlike traditional learning rules, BTSP learns pre-post correlations on timescales of seconds and rapidly changes single-unit activity in only a few trials. To study how BTSP-like learning can be integrated into network models, we propose a generalized theoretical framework, gBTSP, which we apply to unsupervised and supervised tasks in feedforward and recurrent networks. We show that unsupervised gBTSP learns place field maps in the feedforward case and attractor memories in the recurrent case. For supervised learning, we derive how plateau events can reduce task error, enabling gBTSP to solve trajectory matching and delayed non-match-to-sample tasks. Finally, we find that the speed of credit assignment via gBTSP is limited by network depth or CA3-like recurrence, suggesting that additional mechanisms are necessary to account for BTSP-driven few-shot learning in naturalistic settings.
