Toward personalized deep brain stimulation via white matter stimulation and microstructure in depression
A lactate-fatty acid loop drives prostate cancer bone colonization by mediating metabolic interplay between tumor cells and osteoblasts
items.abstract: Abstract Bone metastasis is the major cause of morbidity and mortality in advanced prostate cancer, yet current therapies provide only limited clinical benefit. Here, we show that prostate cancer cells metabolically adapt to the bone microenvironment by utilizing bone-cell-derived lactate as an alternative nutrient source. Beyond fueling oxidative phosphorylation, lactate serves as carbon source for fatty acid synthesis. Among the resulting lipid products, oleic acid is secreted to reward osteoblast, establishing a reciprocal metabolic interplay that supports both tumor progression and pathological bone formation. Mechanistically, we identify MCT1 as the essential transporter mediating lactate uptake in bone-colonizing tumor cells. MCT1 expression is coordinately regulated by NFAT signaling and extracellular glucose availability at both transcriptional and post-translational levels. Genetic deletion and pharmacological inhibition of MCT1 markedly suppresses prostate tumor growth in bone. Together, these findings uncover a lactate-driven metabolic crosstalk, identifying MCT1 as a promising therapeutic target for prostate cancer bone metastasis.

items.title: Temporal dynamics of premenstrual dysphoric disorder revealed through predictive symptom networks
items.abstract: Abstract Temporal dynamics of psychiatric symptoms challenge researchers and clinicians due to their inherent unpredictability. The cyclical on–off nature of symptoms linked to physiological rhythms, such as the menstrual cycle, provides a unique window to apply temporal and dynamic modeling of psychiatric symptoms. This can be studied in premenstrual dysphoric disorder, a female hormone-triggered condition characterized by cyclical symptoms. Yet intra-individual temporal patterns and dynamics of these symptoms remain unknown. Here we show that individuals with premenstrual dysphoric disorder differ widely in symptom timing, severity, and persistence, clustering into distinct temporal symptom profiles. Dynamic modelling uncovers temporal order among core psychiatric symptoms, with anxiety emerging as a central symptom in the unfolding of affective dysregulation. Depression shows the strongest predictive associations with subsequent severity of the other core symptoms, while irritability predicts the severity of depression at the longest time-interval. These temporal symptom dynamics reveal mechanistic psychoneuroendocrine pathways and inform precision, time-sensitive interventions for the mental health of individuals with premenstrual dysphoric disorder.

items.title: Prospective and genetic analyses implicate lower immunosurveillance in the aetiology of prostate cancer
items.abstract: Abstract Tumour-promoting inflammation and immune evasion are key features of cancer, but prospective evidence linking specific immune pathways to prostate cancer risk remains limited. Here we show that circulating proteins involved in immune regulation may influence prostate cancer development. We analyse 368 immune- and inflammation-related proteins measured in blood samples from men in the European Prospective Investigation into Cancer and Nutrition (EPIC), including 1434 cases and matched controls, and combine these results with data from UK Biobank. While no proteins are associated with risk in EPIC alone after multiple testing correction, meta-analysis identifies several proteins linked to prostate cancer risk, including IL15 and FLT3LG, in particular, in blood taken long before diagnosis. Higher levels of immune surveillance-related proteins, particularly those involved in natural killer and T cell activity, are associated with lower prostate cancer risk, whereas genetic evidence implicates PARP1, SPINT2 and NME3 in increased risk. These findings suggest that immune pathways play a role in prostate cancer development and highlight potential targets for prevention.

items.title: Conserved molecular properties of dissolved organic matter during Weddell Sea Deep Water formation
items.abstract: Abstract Antarctic Bottom Water (AABW) is decreasing in volume due to climate change with potential consequences for abyssal carbon storage, where carbon is locked away from the atmosphere for centuries. Understanding the formation and export of dissolved organic matter (DOM) on the Antarctic shelf is therefore essential to determine how organic carbon enters this deep-sea reservoir. Here, we investigate solid-phase extractable DOM (SPE-DOM) transformations in the Weddell Sea, where half of AABW forms. Molecular and structural properties of SPE-DOM remain unchanged during dense-water formation. Shelf processes minimally affect exported organics into the deep-sea, likely due to remineralization to inorganic carbon enhanced by long residence times on the shelf. Consequently, the dominant SPE-DOM signature in Weddell Sea Deep Water (WSDW) is established before dense shelf waters mix with warmer off-shelf waters. We estimate that 0.155 ± 0.03 PgC are transferred annually from the Weddell Sea to AABW, and that its molecular composition is expected to remain conserved despite ongoing climate-driven weakening of AABW.

items.title: The representational geometry of cognitive maps under cognitive control
items.abstract: Abstract Recent work has shown that the brain abstracts non-spatial relationships between entities or task states into representations called cognitive maps. Here, we investigate how cognitive control enables flexible top-down selection of goal-relevant information from multidimensional cognitive maps retrieved from memory. We examine the relationship between cognitive control and representational geometry by conducting parallel analyses of functional magnetic resonance imaging data and recurrent neural network models trained to perform the same task. We find both stable map-like representations in a medial temporal lobe and orbitofrontal cortical network that reflect both task-relevant and irrelevant dimensions and context-dependent, orthogonal representations of only task-relevant dimensions in a frontoparietal network. These representational motifs also emerge with distinct temporal profiles over the course of training in the recurrent neural network, with map-like representations appearing first. We further show that increasing control demands due to incongruence (conflicting responses) between current task-relevant and irrelevant dimensions impact the geometry of subjective representations, and the degree of this effect further accounts for individual differences in cognitive control. Taken together, our findings show how complementary representational geometries balance stability and behavioral flexibility, and reveal an intricate relationship between cognitive control and cognitive map geometry.

items.title: Global environmental genomics reveals vast uncultivated protist diversity and taxonomic blind spots
A national baseline for methane sink habitats and methanotroph diversity
Retraction Note: Senescent immune cells accumulation promotes brown adipose tissue dysfunction during aging
Absolute quantification and profiling of cellular tRNAs by nanopore sequencing and a deep learning classifier
Electrode-associated growth reveals structure of OmcZ-type cytochrome nanowires in anaerobic methanotrophic archaea
items.abstract: Abstract Anaerobic methanotrophic (ANME) archaea are key regulators of methane emissions in anoxic environments, yet their physiology remains poorly understood due to the lack of axenic cultures. Here, we show that cultivation on poised electrodes yields near-axenic cultures (95.8% relative abundance) of a freshwater ANME, for which we propose the name ‘ Candidatus Methanoperedens vercellensis’. We identified key physiological properties of ‘ Ca . M. vercellensis’: doubling times of 4.6 days at 30 °C, menaquinone as respiratory electron carrier, the inability to oxidize ethane, and preferential reduction of iron oxides over nitrate after cultivation on electrodes. A 3.3 Å cryo-electron microscopy structure of filaments displayed on the archaeal surface revealed polymerized OmcZ-type cytochrome nanowires, which are homologous to OmcZ nanowires essential for long-range (>10 μm) extracellular electron transfer (EET) in Geobacter sulfurreducens . The archaeal OmcZ-type nanowires include dense, collinear stacking of protected hemesakin to bacterial OmcZ nanowires, but with post-translational modification, thus yielding morphology distinct from bacterial OmcZ nanowires. Notably, in contrast to bacterial OmcZ, archaeal OmcZ-type nanowires do not form interconnected networks, and hemes are less solvent-exposed, which can protect them from the environment. Surprisingly, these archaea assemble OmcZ into nanowires even in the apparent absence of prolyl isomerase involved in folding bacterial OmcZ. This work establishes a model system for molecular understanding of nanowire-mediated EET in archaea.

items.title: Comment on “Self-organizing neuromorphic nanowire networks as stochastic dynamical systems"
Nanometer-resolution imaging of living bacteria across species and cellular orientations
items.abstract: Abstract The bacterial cell envelope is a complex superstructure that is an important target and a major barrier for antibiotics. To date, highest-resolution images of native cell envelopes have been obtained by atomic force microscopy (AFM), but its use is limited by challenges in bacterial immobilization. We establish glutaraldehyde-functionalized glass surfaces for reversible covalent attachment, enabling robust adhesion across species and cellular orientations while preserving cell viability and growth. This approach allowed imaging of Escherichia coli both expressing O-antigen and fully lacking lipopolysaccharide (LPS) oligosaccharides, revealing that AFM contrast depends on LPS complexity and confirming previously observed outer membrane domains as LPS-enriched islands. It also enabled imaging of Pseudomonas aeruginosa and Acinetobacter baumannii outer membranes, which lack the characteristic protein trimers observed in model E. coli . Finally, we discovered growth-phase dependent alterations in E. coli pole morphology, where trimer networks typical of exponential-phase cells were unresolved and morphological defects appeared.

items.title: Crystal records of erupted vs. trapped magma in volcanic arcs
items.abstract: Abstract Arc andesites are hybrids generated by mixing of mafic and silicic magmas. The silicic endmember can contribute to crustal growth or trigger explosive eruptions, yet remains difficult to constrain due to limited representation in the erupted record. Here, we show that textural, elemental and isotopic records preserved in plagioclase can distinguish between trapped and erupted crystal mush, thus constraining conditions of magma storage vs. eruption in arc systems. We define the plagioclase eruptibility field, a narrow and recurrent anorthite range (An~61) that represents erupted melt across Central Andes volcanoes upon mafic recharge. The recycled plagioclase cargo is dominantly An~43, recording prolonged crystallisation and assimilation within silicic mushes. This pattern repeats in continental and composite arcs globally, indicating strong eruptive filtering of arc magmas and widespread occurrence of dormant felsic and mafic mushes that, in most cases, contribute to crustal growth; yet exceptionally, felsic mushes can rapidly remobilise to generate super-eruptions.

items.title: LLM ensemble PREVIA predicts future PTSD risk from emergency department trauma narratives with expert-level accuracy
Correlative nanoscale chemical imaging reveals delocalized Faradaic processes at isolated MXene flakes
items.abstract: Abstract Two-dimensional transition metal carbides and nitrides (MXenes) combine an electrochemically active surface with high conductivity and hydrophilicity, which makes them a unique class of materials for electrochemical applications. While the pseudocapacitive behaviour of MXenes in acidic environments is relatively well understood on macroscale electrodes, intrinsic electrochemical phenomena occurring on single MXene flakes remain unclear. Here, we use scanning X-ray microscopy (SXM) to correlate the electronic structure of Ti 3 C 2 T x MXene flakes at the nanoscale with local electrochemical reactions triggered at the sub-flake level by scanning electrochemical cell microscopy (SECCM). For several proton-coupled electron transfer reactions, including electrochemical oxidation and the hydrogen evolution reaction, we demonstrate a delocalization of the reactions well beyond the MXene flake area in contact with the droplet cell. Furthermore, we show evidence of hydrogen storage on monolayer MXene flakes. This work highlights fundamental insights into the role of interfacial water on surface redox reactions.

items.title: Single-cell machine learning uncovers genetically anchored, cell-type specific programs of Alzheimer’s disease
items.abstract: Abstract Univariate differential expression analysis dominates single-cell transcriptomic studies of Alzheimer’s disease, yet marginal testing alone cannot resolve multivariate disease-associated structure or distinguish clinical from neuropathological signatures. Here we introduce TriSCOPE, a framework integrating multivariate predictive modeling, donor-aware differential expression, and pseudotime inference, applied to six Alzheimer’s disease snRNA-seq datasets comprising ~4.2 million nuclei from 627 donors. Across six major brain cell types and 41 subclusters, we identify cell-type-specific predictively expressed genes that are largely non-overlapping with differentially expressed genes, revealing disease-relevant signals invisible to univariate approaches. Conditional GWAS–eQTL colocalization anchors a subset of these predictively expressed genes to inherited Alzheimer’s disease risk loci, including 27 genetically supported gene–cell type pairs (among them ARL17B , JAZF1 ) with no significant differential expression. Integration across all three analytical branches nominates high-confidence convergent programs including astrocytic stress markers (such as GFAP , MT2A ), neuronal signaling genes (like RASGEF1B , LINGO1 , NRG1 ), and microglial and oligodendrocyte regulators (including SYTL3 , SPP1 , APOD ). Comparison of clinical and neuropathological models reveals cell-type-specific divergence between cognitive and pathological Alzheimer’s disease signatures. Key predictively expressed genes including ARL17B , LINGO1 , and APOE replicate across independent cohorts, with cross-cohort generalizability confirmed across all three analytical branches of TriSCOPE.

items.title: Repeated loss of the West Antarctic Ice Sheet’s Amundsen Sea sector during late Pleistocene interglacials
items.abstract: Abstract Sea-level reconstructions and numerical models suggest that the vulnerable West Antarctic Ice Sheet underwent major mass losses during the late Pleistocene, raising global sea level by several metres. However, direct evidence from ice-sheet proximal records for such retreat has remained inconclusive. Here we investigate variations in clay mineral assemblages and past ocean temperatures archived in West Antarctic continental margin sediments during the last 800,000 years. Our results demonstrate that the supply of glacigenic detritus sourced from the main outlet glaciers in the Amundsen Sea sector of the West Antarctic Ice Sheet ceased almost entirely during all previous warm periods, documenting the loss of their drainage basins. Concomitant seawater warming, revealed by a microfossil proxy, is attributed to intensified deep-water advection towards Antarctica’s Pacific margin, which is corroborated by the clay mineralogical evidence. Our findings show that ocean forcing can drive major deglaciation of West Antarctica and related global sea-level rise.

items.title: Reply to: Comment on “Self-organizing neuromorphic nanowire networks as stochastic dynamical systems”
Archival and palaeoenvironmental documentation of extreme climate events reveals generational amnesia in collective memory
items.abstract: Abstract Collective memory shapes how societies respond to extreme climate events, yet long-term evidence on how the collective memory of such events becomes perceptually biased over time is lacking. Here, we utilise four centuries (1470–1900) of climatic archives from northern China, along with tree–ring–based hydroclimate reconstructions, which are validated against instrumental observations of Wet/Dry Index (1901–2000) to fill the gap. We find that historical records reveal systematic, non-random mismatches, where severity assessments are often biased toward recent experience rather than absolute climatic anomalies. Correlations between historical and natural records increase when the natural series is re-standardised using 20–40-year sliding windows, reflecting a generational offset. A heuristic agent-based model reproduces this pattern, suggesting that generational amnesia is sufficient to explain the offsets in perception of environmental change. We argue that historical archives carry a generational imprint of perceptual bias, in which the severity of climate extremes is judged against recent lived experience rather than long-term climate variability. This has implications for bias-aware corrections for risk assessment, adaptation, and paleoclimate reconstruction.

items.title: Two functionally distinct amyloid-β intermediates link aggregation pathways to pathology in Alzheimer’s disease
items.abstract: Abstract Neurotoxic intermediates formed during amyloid-β (Aβ) aggregation are thought to drive Alzheimer’s disease, yet their rarity and transient nature have obscured their identity and formation pathways in the human brain. Here, we combine super-resolution microscopy and single-molecule functional imaging with kinetic modelling to classify Aβ intermediates according to their membrane-disrupting activity and connect their damaging effects to the aggregation pathways that generate them. Applying this framework to recombinant Aβ42, an Alzheimer’s knock-in mouse model and human Alzheimer’s brain tissue, we find two functionally distinct intermediate populations present across all systems. They form through separate aggregation routes and differ in their neurotoxicity, abundance and susceptibility to inhibition. Both damage neurons and glia, but only one converts into plaques. Suppressing these intermediates pharmacologically in mice reduces plaque burden, attenuates astrogliosis and improves cognition. Our findings connect model systems with human pathology and identify intermediate formation pathways as actionable therapeutic targets across protein-misfolding disorders.

items.title: Hydration water drives elastin’s entropic elasticity
Calpain-mediated TBP cleavage disturbs neuronal AMOT-YAP1 signalling
items.abstract: Abstract The transcription factor TATA-box-binding protein (TBP) plays a crucial role in neurons, as highlighted by its involvement in spinocerebellar ataxia type 17 (SCA17), where pathological polyglutamine expansions disrupt its function. While the molecular pathomechanisms remain unclear, our previous study showed that calcium-activated calpains cleave TBP in SCA17 cell and animal models. Here, we pinpoint a major calpain cleavage site after residue T106, C-terminal to TBP’s polyglutamine tract. The resulting polyglutamine-containing N-terminal fragments mislocalise to the cytoplasm and exhibit increased aggregation. Both the N-terminal and the nuclear-localised C-terminal fragments contribute to calpain overactivation. SCA17 cell line-based multi-omics analyses revealed that TBP fragments alter pathways linked to neuronal function and neurodegeneration, identifying AMOT as a key player. Further analyses in SCA17 cell lines, patient-derived fibroblasts and induced neurons as well as in rat and zebrafish models confirmed AMOT’s pivotal role in neurons, regulated by TBP and mediated via YAP1-dependent signalling. These findings offer further insights into TBP’s neuronal function and suggest broader implications of AMOT for neurodegenerative and neurodevelopmental disorders.

items.title: SimPoly: Simulation of polymers with machine learning force fields derived from first principles
Cancer-associated fibroblasts as architects of tumor immune geography and lymphoid organization
Evidence and measures of the digital usage divide from 40 million Windows devices
items.abstract: Abstract Digital infrastructure is crucial for economic opportunities, social inclusion, and civic participation, but benefits remain unevenly distributed. Existing measures, such as computer ownership and broadband adoption, do not capture the depth and variety of digital use. We develop measures using Microsoft telemetry collected during operating system updates from 40 million Windows devices in U.S. households. These measures provide greater coverage and granularity than existing commercial or government surveys. Device representations at the ZIP-code level reveal substantial variation in usage, including an urban-rural divide and disparities within narrowly defined Metropolitan Statistical Areas. Income and education correlate with these differences. These effects are large and suggest that digital usage gaps extend beyond the local availability of essential IT infrastructure. The findings call for interventions that complement infrastructure access with support for technology use and skills development. The resulting indices are publicly available to support future research on digital inequality.

items.title: The transcriptional regulator IκBζ is essential for ILC2 effector functions
items.abstract: Abstract Group 2 innate lymphoid cells (ILC2) are the sentinels that ensure tissue homeostasis and engage in the immune response to helminths by secreting type 2 cytokines. Here we show that IκBζ, an atypical member of the IκB family, controls basal IL-5 production by ILC2s and governs their effector program during helminth infection and asthma. Peripheral ILC2s express IκBζ at steady state, and its expression is further induced upon stimulation with IL-33 or IL-25 in an NF-κB- and STAT3/5-dependent manner. Upon activation, IκBζ refines chromatin accessibility at regulatory elements of effector cytokine loci, thereby licensing transcription. Due to reduced type 2 cytokine secretion and impaired proliferative capacity of ILC2s, mice with IκBζ-deficient ILC2s show delayed clearance of the hookworm Nippostrongylus brasiliensis and reduced papain-induced airway inflammation. Taken together, our study highlights the central role of IκBζ in orchestrating the ILC2 effector program in different tissues in health and disease.

items.title: Nanofluid wetting of Cu enables thin lithium negative electrodes for high-energy and long-cycling lithium metal batteries
items.abstract: Abstract Exploiting thin Li foils ≤ 20 μm is required for high-energy-density and long-cycling-lifespan battery, but is severely hindered by the poor processability of Li, as well as its inhomogeneous plating behaviors and resulting low Coulombic efficiency. Herein, an approach balancing Li supply and consumption is fulfilled by designing thin molten-salt-derived, nanocomposite Li@LiX metal negative electrodes. Benefitting from the formation of nanofluid due to the spontaneous reaction of inorganic nanoparticles in molten Li, the bonding states at both Li surface and Li|Cu interface are effectively regulated, displaying an enhanced wetting behaviour of Li on Cu. This approach enables the fabrication of an 800-nm-thick Li-based negative electrode foil as well as the formation of an inorganic-rich interphase upon cycling, which suppresses Li consumption by reducing corrosion susceptibility. As a result, practical pouch cells composed of 10-μm-thick Li@lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide (LiFSI) and LiFePO 4 offer stable cycling over 250 cycles, while those composed of 20-μm-thick Li@LiFSI and LiNi 0.92 Co 0.03 Mn 0.05 O 2 with an areal capacity of 4.6 mAh cm −2 achieve 100 cycles, yielding specific energy of 498 Wh kg −1 and energy density of 1,142 Wh L −1 , indicating that this design strategy is applicable to lithium metal batteries.

items.title: Fractional quantum Hall states and oscillatory Landau charge squeezing in Bernal tetralayer graphene
Ultra-high precision speckle spectrometer enabling radio-frequency scale resolution of atomic spectra
items.abstract: Abstract Laser speckle, the granular intensity pattern arising from random optical interference, provides a high-dimensional encoding of spectral information that can be exploited for precision metrology. Speckle-based spectrometers have advanced rapidly owing to their compact footprint, mechanical robustness and alignment agnostic nature, yet their spectral resolution has remained limited to the picometre scale. In this work, we break this limit by employing an integrating sphere as a multiply scattering cavity with access to a high range of path lengths to enhance spectral sensitivity. At 780 nm, the resulting device achieves a resolution of 6 fm, corresponding to a resolving power of 1.3 × 10 8 , representing an approximately 80-fold improvement over previous implementations. This ultra-high resolution enables clear discrimination of laser sidebands generated by an electro-optical modulator, with extracted sideband powers agreeing with expected values to within 1%. It further permits a direct speckle-based measurement of the hyperfine structure of the D 2 transition in 85 Rb, with transmission spectra differing by no more than 3.7% from independent wavemeter-referenced measurements. These results establish speckle as a platform for ultra-high precision spectroscopy, radio-frequency spectrometry, and microwave photonics.

items.title: Fully Integrated Deep-Ocean Flexible Temperature–Depth Sensor with Neural Network Compensation
Selective depolymerization of poly(ethylene terephthalate) for economical closed-loop recycling of mixed textiles
Coupling electrolyte mechanical reinforcement and interfacial stress relaxation for near-ambient sulfide all-solid-state lithium metal batteries
Transposable element polymorphisms underlie epigenetic variation and phenotypic diversification during foxtail millet domestication
Phosphorylation-driven targeted protein degradation of oncogenic β-catenin

Insular motor and error encoding supports self-correcting intracranial brain-computer interface
items.abstract: Abstract Error recognition is fundamental to adaptive behavior, enabling rapid compensatory action when outcomes deviate from expectations. Central to this function are neural circuits for performance monitoring, encoding cognitive signals that could support more reliable neural interfaces. Here, we recorded intracranial electroencephalography (iEEG) in epilepsy patients to enable a motor brain-computer interface (BCI) while sampling error-related activity across a distributed network. Our work reveals high-frequency population dynamics emerging in the anterior insula and propagating to the prefrontal cortex as the interface fails to follow the user’s intention. We identify spatially organized insular responses to error processing and movement feedback, highlighting it as a heterogeneous hub linking action and outcome. Frontoinsular recording sites were found to preferentially encode error-related activity, while centroparietal responses were intermixed with compensatory motor signals, making the former a compelling target for real-time error correction. Together, our findings demonstrate a human intracranial BCI harnessing insular brain activity, integrating cognitive processes directly into device control.

items.title: Topological Josephson trijunctions as a Majorana source and path
items.abstract: Abstract Majorana bound states (MBSs) are zero-energy localized states in topological superconductors, obeying non-Abelian braiding statistics. Manipulation of mobile MBSs, encompassing their on-demand generation, propagation, and fusion, is essential for braiding MBSs and operating topological qubits. We show that the manipulation is enabled by a trijunction formed on a topological insulator in a perpendicular magnetic field, where three Josephson junctions meet. While the superconducting phases at the trijunction center evolve to cross a boundary between topological and non-topological phase domains, the trijunction offers two distinct dynamics, source/sink and path, depending on the phase boundaries. At a source/sink boundary, two MBSs are pairwise generated at the center, and one of them is ejected to a Josephson junction. The reverse, pair annihilation by collision of two MBSs, can also happen. At a path boundary, an MBS moves from a Josephson junction to the trijunction center or vice versa, without involving other MBSs. Exploiting the two dynamics, fusion and braiding of MBSs can be operated in a trijunction network. We illustrate this with a double trijunction setup, where non-Abelian state evolutions associated with MBSs can be manipulated without dynamical control of the setup and detected by Josephson emission spectroscopy.

items.title: WASH orchestrates phagosomal maturation and bacterial killing in neutrophils through syntaxin 19-mediated lysosomal fusion
Genome-wide CRISPR screening in Spodoptera frugiperda reveals the determinants of insecticide activation and sensitivity
Soft robotic and computational models of left atrial hemodynamics in sinus rhythm and atrial fibrillation
Antagonistic second-messenger signalling coordinates Pseudomonas aeruginosa surface colonization and virulence
items.abstract: Abstract Efficient colonisation of host tissue surfaces is a prerequisite for bacterial infection. In the human pathogen Pseudomonas aeruginosa , the second messengers cAMP and c-di-GMP regulate surface behaviours and virulence, but how these pathways are coordinated during tissue infection has remained unclear. Here we demonstrate that cAMP and c-di-GMP establish mutually exclusive signalling states at the single-cell level, generating distinct subpopulations of motile and surface-attached cells through pathway-specific control of type IV pili (T4P). Initial surface contact triggers an increase in c-di-GMP, activating FimW and driving stable attachment via bipolar T4P formation. This state is progressively replaced by cAMP, which inactivates FimW-dependent attachment and induces FimX-mediated T4P polarisation, surface motility and virulence activation. The resulting signalling transition enforces coexisting subpopulations, with attached cells gradually displaced by spreading cells. Using a human airway tissue model, we show that both T4P-mediated adhesion and twitching motility are required for invasion and tissue damage. Based on this, we propose that reciprocal cAMP–c-di-GMP signalling coordinates complementary T4P functions to optimise P. aeruginosa surface colonisation and infection.

items.title: Propofol induces sustained suppression of alcohol drinking via habenular activation in mice
CO2 responsive nanoscopic and macroscopic materials directed by peptides
Mapping Future Energy Journeys Through Modeling the Global Transport of Synthetic Energy Carriers
items.abstract: Abstract Synthetic energy carriers can connect renewable-energy-rich potential production regions with distant demand centers, but the emergence of trade depends on total supply costs. Here, we develop a spatially resolved heuristic combining hydrogen production costs with ports, pipelines, and shipping routes, as well as syntheses, cracking, and reformation processes, to identify key import corridors. Across 10,883 production locations and seven different scenarios, we find that export regions connected to the importer through retrofit-ready pipelines remain competitive despite only moderate renewable potentials. Meanwhile, for remote exporters competitiveness depends on port availability and coastal access through pipeline networks. Gaseous hydrogen dominates short pipeline routes, and ammonia is preferred for maritime trade, whereas methanol and methane emerge in long multimodal chains. Additional results show that low-cost heat availability is required for the competitiveness of liquid organic hydrogen carriers, while accounting for market values of conventional counterparts boosts ammonia and methanol trade.

items.title: Pre-bilaterian roots of the chordate body plan
CH2Cl2 emissions from China inferred from atmospheric observations
Bistable origami robot for adaptive multimodal motion actuated by nonuniform magnetic fields
items.abstract: Abstract Conventional magnetically controlled mini-robots require operation within highly uniform and high-precision magnetic fields, which are impractical for large space applications. In this work, the bistable origami robot offloads these requirements onto the pre-programmed geometry of its mechanical architecture. These structures exhibit distinct deformation modes at each stable state when subjected to small-amplitude magnetic perturbations. Moreover, transitions between stable states—triggered by large-amplitude impulsive magnetic inputs—enable impulsive motions such as grasping. Correspondingly, a large-workspace magnetic actuation system is developed to generate low-uniform magnetic fields, and it is capable of controlling the bistable origami structure for desired multimodal locomotion and manipulation. We demonstrate capabilities including self-grasping, object capture, and adaptive locomotion modes such as crawling, turning, tumbling, scampering, jumping, and rolling at two different stable configurations. Our findings offer an approach for designing multi-functional and wireless mini/microrobots in large spaces, which is validated through analytical modeling, numerical simulation, and experimental testing.

items.title: Hippocampal transformations occur along dimensions of memory interference
items.abstract: Abstract The role of the hippocampus in resolving memory interference has been greatly elucidated by considering the relationship between the similarity of visual stimuli (input) and corresponding similarity of hippocampal activity patterns (output). However, these input-output functions can take surprisingly different forms. Here, we reconcile seemingly conflicting findings by considering the possibility that the hippocampus prioritizes different dimensions of visual similarity across different stages of learning. First, we generated a set of natural scene images from two visual categories and rigorously characterized visual similarity using a wide array of methods: neural networks, artificial intelligence models, and human perceptual and memory decisions. We then identified two orthogonal dimensions of visual similarity that each predicted memory interference, but that did so at distinct stages of learning. Using high-resolution fMRI, we then tested for dimension-specific input-output functions within the hippocampus. Within CA3 and dentate gyrus (CA3/DG), we show that dimensions of visual similarity were inverted (repulsion) at stages of learning when they contributed to memory interference. In contrast, CA3/DG preserved similarity when dimensions did not contribute to interference. These findings reveal that hippocampal representations of visually-similar stimuli are highly dynamic and critically depend on the dimensions of similarity that currently contribute to memory interference.

items.title: Redundancy maximization as a principle of associative memory learning in Hopfield networks
items.abstract: Abstract Associative memory, traditionally modeled by Hopfield networks, enables the retrieval of previously stored patterns from partial or noisy cues. Yet, the local computational principles which are required to enable this function remain incompletely understood. To formally characterize the local information processing in such systems, we employ a recent extension of information theory—Partial Information Decomposition. It decomposes the contribution of different inputs to an output into unique information from each input, redundant information across inputs, and synergistic information that emerges from combining different inputs. Applying this framework to individual neurons in classical Hopfield networks we find that below the memory capacity, the information in a neuron’s activity is characterized by high redundancy between the external pattern input and the internal recurrent input, while synergy and unique information are close to zero until the memory capacity is surpassed and performance drops steeply. Inspired by this observation, we use redundancy maximization at each neuron as an information-theoretic learning goal. This increases the network’s memory capacity to 1.59, a more than tenfold improvement over the 0.14 capacity of classical Hopfield networks, and also outperforming recent state-of-the-art implementations of Hopfield networks. Overall, this work establishes redundancy maximization as a design principle for associative memories and opens pathways for new associative memory models based on information-theoretic goals.

items.title: Pathway selection by a pendant amine proton shuttle enables stereoselective hydroarylation of internal alkynes
A 17.2T MRI atlas and multiparametric exploration of the mouse hypothalamus reveal sexual dimorphism and lateralization
[18F]FET PET enables histopathology-validated detection of non-contrast-enhancing glioblastoma
items.abstract: Abstract Accurate visualization of glioblastoma is essential for guiding biopsy, resection and radiotherapy. Contrast-enhanced MRI is routine in clinical practice, yet it can miss metabolically active tumor outside areas of blood-brain barrier disruption. In a histopathology-validated cohort with 472 tissue samples of 61 patients with IDH-wildtype glioblastoma, we show that O-(2-[¹⁸F]fluoroethyl)-L-tyrosine PET ([ 18 F]FET PET) depicts tumor tissue significantly better than contrast-enhanced MRI (CE-MRI), especially in regions that show no enhancement on MRI. [ 18 F]FET PET achieves substantially higher sensitivity for tumor detection (91.2% vs 52.6%) and maintains high reliability in non-enhancing tissue (positive predictive value 98.3%), findings that are consistent across newly diagnosed and recurrent disease and in both cohorts undergoing either resection or biopsy. These results indicate that [ 18 F]FET PET complements MRI by revealing MRI-occult tumor burden. Incorporating amino acid PET into routine planning may therefore improve the accuracy of tumor visualization and, ultimately, patient management.

items.title: Phospholipase D1 activates NAD kinase fuelling neutrophil extracellular trap formation
items.abstract: Abstract Neutrophil extracellular trap formation is a central innate immune defence mechanism that depends on NADPH oxidase–driven reactive oxygen species production. How NADP⁺ availability is regulated during neutrophil activation remains unclear. Using integrated lipidomic, biochemical and functional analyses in human neutrophils, we identify NAD kinase, the sole enzyme responsible for NADP⁺ synthesis, as a direct lipid-regulated effector downstream of phospholipase D1. Neutrophil activation induces rapid, phospholipase D1-dependent production of phosphatidic acid and phosphatidylinositol 4,5-bisphosphate, which bind and activate NAD kinase. The resulting cytosolic NADP⁺ is reduced to NADPH by the oxidative pentose phosphate pathway and consumed by NADPH oxidase during neutrophil extracellular trap formation. Pharmacological or genetic disruption of phospholipase D1 suppresses NAD kinase activity, depletes NADP⁺ and impairs neutrophil extracellular trap formation independently of direct NADPH oxidase inhibition. These findings define a lipid–metabolic axis coupling phospholipase D1-driven membrane remodelling to NADP⁺ availability and innate immune function.

items.title: Non-canonical FOXO1 signaling governs epithelial barrier integrity through spatial regulation of the E-cadherin–β-catenin complex
Photoredox cobalt-catalyzed late-stage N-methyl-selective C–H vinylation of unactivated trialkylamines with alkynes
items.abstract: Abstract Late-stage functionalization of trialkylamine-containing drugs provides a direct way to access new chemical space, but selective modification of unactivated trialkylamines remains challenging because they contain multiple competing α-amino C–H bonds. Here we show a photoredox/cobalt dual-catalytic strategy for N-methyl-selective α-C–H vinylation of unactivated tertiary alkylamines with internal alkynes. This redox-neutral method provides trisubstituted allylic amines without directing groups or external oxidants, with broad substrate scope and high regioselectivity, stereoselectivity and site-selectivity under mild conditions. The reaction accommodates diverse amines and alkynes, including electronically unbiased dialkyl alkynes, and enables gram-scale synthesis, preparation of the fungicide fenpropidin and late-stage functionalization of structurally complex pharmaceuticals. Some drug analogues show enhanced apparent human histamine H1 receptor binding affinity. Mechanistic experiments and computational studies support a reasonable reaction pathway involving α-amino carbon radical generation via photoredox catalysis, followed by aminomethyl-cobalt I -mediated alkyne migratory insertion and protonolysis. This work provides a practical strategy for selective trialkylamines editing and late-stage diversification.

items.title: Microbiome-derived proline dipeptides underpin improved nitrogen utilization efficiency in dairy cattle
A topographic video model predicts the spatio-functional organization of the human visual system
items.abstract: Abstract The human brain organizes visual processing into spatially structured functional clusters. Recent topographic neural networks model category-selective clusters but are limited to static images and ventral cortex. In this work, we model the topographic organization of dynamic visual representations across high-level visual cortex. We introduce a general method that spatially arranges and transforms units from a neural network onto a simulated cortical sheet. Applied to a pretrained video foundation model, the method produces spatially structured response correlations while preserving task performance and brain alignment. It captures ventral and dorsal clusters, including face-, body-, and motion-selective patches, and reflects system-level selectivity distributions for animacy, object size, and static versus dynamic content. Functional selectivity varies smoothly across both model and human tissue, suggesting predominantly general-purpose cortical processing with continuous transitions into local functional clusters. Taken together, we provide a computational framework for understanding the spatial and functional organization of high-level visual cortex.

Addressing the 1000-h/1000-nit stability challenge in perovskite LEDs
items.abstract: Abstract Perovskite light-emitting diodes (PeLEDs) offer exceptional colour purity and efficiency for next-generation display applications. Despite the recent advances in device stability, achieving long-term stable PeLEDs under display-relevant conditions remains a critical challenge. The actual device half-life (T 50 ) experimentally measured for visible PeLEDs were in most cases limited to below 1000 h for any given brightness, in contrast to the much longer extrapolated lifetimes reported. Here, we demonstrate stable green PeLEDs with a T 50 lifetime of 1350 h at an initial luminance of 1000 cd m −2 (nits), a maximum energy-conversion efficiency of 28.0%, and a peak external quantum efficiency of 24.5%. The exceptional performance is enabled by the insertion of a fluorinated self-assembled monolayer between the metal oxide and polymeric hole-transport layers. This molecular interlayer leads to Ohmic-like characteristics for charge injection, lowering the operating voltage at ~1000 nits to sub-bandgap levels (~2.1 V) where ion migration is suppressed. The accumulated photon output of our PeLEDs over the course of their T 50 lifespan is found to sharply increase as the driving voltage drops to sub-bandgap values, highlighting the critical role of employing low-voltage device architectures in reaching the 1350-h/1000-nit stability milestone. Finally, a flexible active-matrix PeLED display prototype is developed, showing the potential of the devices for wearable optoelectronics.

items.title: Fe(III) hydrolysis-driven Fe(III)/Fe(IV) redox couple for iron sludge-free Fenton-like oxidation
Continuous directed evolution using engineered human B cell lines
items.abstract: Abstract The B cells of the human immune system have evolved somatic hypermutation (SHM) mechanisms that introduce mutations at the immunoglobulin genomic loci at a significantly higher frequency than the rest of the genome thereby allowing them to evolve antibody sequences without compromising fitness due to genome-wide mutations. Inspired by these observations, here we develop a continuous directed evolution platform in human B cell lines (CODE-HB) that repurposes the SHM mechanisms to a stable, non-immunoglobulin genomic locus of the human B cell lines to continuously evolve cytosolic and surface displayed proteins with a broad mutational spectrum comprising of substitutions, deletions and insertions. Using our human B cell surface display platform and CODE-HB, we evolve neutralizing antibodies targeting avian influenza and escape variants of influenza. Given the modularity and simplicity of CODE-HB, we anticipate that this platform can be used for rapidly evolving biotechnologically relevant biomolecules directly in human cells.

items.title: Intra-arterial tenecteplase during thrombectomy for acute ischemic stroke: the BRETIS-TNK2 trial
Intra-arterial tenecteplase for acute basilar artery occlusion with sufficient recanalization after thrombectomy: the INSIST-IT randomized clinical trial
Estimating the resilience of non-stationary systems
items.abstract: Abstract A wide body of work has applied the concept of critical slowing down to estimate the stability of different Earth system components. Most of them – such as global vegetation – are inherently non-stationary, for example due to strong seasonal forcing that complicates the estimation of their resilience to external perturbations. Here, we introduce a method to account for non-stationarity in estimating the resilience of diverse synthetic and real-world systems via a regression-based formulation of the Langevin equation. Our method does not require extensive data pre-processing, is robust to gaps in the data record, and does not require regular time sampling. We further show that our method can incorporate time-varying data uncertainties, derive uncertainty bounds for stability estimates, and can be natively extended to examine spatial systems. Our method is a drop-in replacement for widely-used autocorrelation-based resilience estimates, and can be applied across diverse Earth system components.

Agentic AI needs a science of interaction
Resolving phonons in superconductor Bi2Sr2CaCu2O8+δ at sub-unit-cell resolution
items.abstract: Abstract The role of phonons in cuprates remains controversial, with their complex lattice structure complicating the investigation. Here, we identify phonon modes originating from charge reservoir and superconducting layers of Bi 2 Sr 2 CaCu 2 O 8+δ using sub-unit-cell resolved electron energy loss spectroscopy in a scanning transmission electron microscope. We reveal several phonon modes exhibiting layer-specific localization: ~78 meV in-plane modes localized in the CuO 2 planes, ~42 meV hybrid (in-plane and out-of-plane) modes in the CuO 2 planes, and ~38 meV hybrid modes in the BiO layers. We also observe a periodic modulation of phonon frequencies induced by the superstructure, spatially correlating with the superconducting gap variation. Our findings offer new insights into the lattice dynamics in cuprates, fostering deeper exploration of the microscopic linkage between structural modulation, electronic inhomogeneity, and electron-phonon coupling.

Personalized adjunctive phage therapy for difficult-to-treat musculoskeletal infections
The modular evolution of chitinases is governed by coevolution of auxiliary and catalytic domains
items.abstract: Abstract The modular architecture of multi-domain enzymes is a key source of functional diversity. GH18 chitinases exemplify this, possessing a variety of auxiliary domains that have been postulated to underpin their role as essential global nutrient cyclers. However, there is no evolutionary framework that accounts for the vast assortment of domain compositions observed across the protein family. Here, we map the sequence space of prokaryotic chitinases, integrating phylogenetics with a quantitative analysis of domain promiscuity to decode their evolutionary history. We reveal that diversification follows distinct trajectories: enzymes necessary for environmental chitin scavenging evolve via high modular plasticity and structural elaboration of the catalytic core, whereas sequences required for specialized, essential developmental roles fix their domain architecture to fulfil lineage-specific physiological roles. By resolving how domain accretion co-evolves with catalytic scaffolds, this work provides a framework for understanding how multi-domain enzymes adapt to complex environments.

items.title: A language model-informed minimalistic design of functional coacervate vesicles
Strong hydrogels through precisely oriented crystallization regulation
items.abstract: Abstract Achieving high mechanical strength and environmental stability is critical for hydrogels in demanding engineering scenarios. Crystalline hydrogels hold promise because their crystallites act as physical crosslinks and energy dissipators; however, precise control over crystalline architecture remains underexplored. Inspired by industrial thermoplastic processing, we report an ASGS strategy for crystalline hydrogels that integrates alkali-induced chain activation (A), ultra-stretching-driven orientation (S), and glycerol-seawater-mediated densification (GS). Alkali treatment yields moderate initial crystallinity with refined nascent crystallites. Ultra-stretching establishes a highly oriented chain network, and subsequent densification achieves maximum crystallinity and highly oriented crystallites. The resultant hydrogels, in the fully hydrated state, combine a tensile strength of 160.0 MPa, a modulus of 746.0 MPa, and a fracture energy of 26.4 kJ·m⁻². The corresponding plastic reaches 414.2 MPa tensile strength while retaining flexibility. This thermoplastic-inspired crystallization engineering provides a scalable paradigm for fabricating strong and stable crystalline hydrogels, promising for load-bearing and harsh underwater engineering applications.

items.title: Engineering filamentous myosins for optical control of contractility
Pathology-adapted peptide–oligonucleotide nanohybrid mitigates glucocorticoid-induced bone loss
Author Correction: Hippocampal-prefrontal orchestration supports higher-order learning for creative ideation
Electrolyte-dependent physico-chemical interfacial kinetics shape degradation pathways and lifetime in lithium-ion batteries
items.abstract: Abstract Electrolyte-dependent lifetime variability remains a major obstacle to sustainable deployment of lithium-ion batteries, contributing to premature retirement, increased material demand and uncertainty in lifecycle assessment. However, most continuum degradation models represent the electrolyte through bulk transport, without capturing its role in interfacial degradation. Here, we use customised multi-layer pouch cells with varied ethylene carbonate:dimethyl carbonate ratio, lithium hexafluorophosphate concentration and electrolyte amount to examine how electrolyte conditions shape degradation trajectories under accelerated degradation. Within this formulation framework, changing the solvent ratio leads to distinct lifetime trajectories across otherwise comparable cells. Electrochemical diagnostics, gas analysis and post-mortem interfacial characterisation show that this divergence is associated with electrolyte-sensitive interphase growth, parasitic reactions and spatially heterogeneous surface degradation. We incorporate electrolyte-dependent transport and thermodynamic properties into a physics-based degradation model. A transport-only implementation does not reproduce the observed separation in capacity-retention trajectories. Introducing a minimal electrolyte-sensitive refinement through an effective interphase transport parameter improves agreement in the ethylene-carbonate-rich case. These results identify electrolyte-sensitive interfacial degradation as a necessary modelling dimension for reliable lifetime prediction.

items.title: Strong-gain water-window X-ray laser driven by plasma photocathode wakefield acceleration
items.abstract: Abstract X-ray free-electron lasers are large and complex machines, limited by electron beam brightness. Here we show through start-to-end simulations how to realise compact, robust and tunable X-ray lasers in the water window, based on ultra-bright electron beams from plasma wakefield accelerators. First, an ultra-low-emittance electron beam is released by a plasma photocathode in a metre-scale plasma wakefield accelerator. By tuning the beam charge, space-charge forces create a balance between beam fields and wakefields that reduces beam energy spread and improves energy stability – both critical for beam extraction, transport, and focusing into a metre-scale undulator. Here, the resulting ultra-bright beams produce wavelength-tunable, coherent, femtosecond-scale photon pulses at strong gain. This regime enables reliable generation of multi-gigawatt-class X-ray laser pulses across the water window, offering tunability via the witness beam charge and robustness against variations in plasma wakefield strength and plasma photocathode laser jitter. Our findings help democratise access to coherent, high-power, soft X-ray radiation.

items.title: Pulsed photoelectrocatalysis enables efficient urea synthesis over Cu(salen)-COF
items.abstract: Abstract Electrocatalytic urea synthesis from carbon dioxide and nitrate under ambient conditions offers a sustainable alternative to the energy-intensive Bosch-Meiser process. However, its efficiency is constrained by the spatiotemporal mismatch of key carbon and nitrogen intermediates at the catalyst-electrolyte interface. Herein, we address this limitation through interfacial microenvironment optimization combining ionic liquid modification of copper-salen covalent organic framework, pulsed electrolysis, and photoelectrocatalytic coupling. The ionic liquid modification enriches carbon dioxide and facilitates interfacial charge transfer, pulsed electrolysis promotes the dynamic matching of carbon and nitrogen intermediates, and photoelectrocatalytic coupling boosts interfacial electron accumulation. The integrated system achieves a urea yield rate of 69.2 mmol g cat −1 h −1 with a Faradaic efficiency of 56.7% in an H-type cell and 82.5% in a flow cell. In this work, we establish a generalizable strategy for efficient urea electrosynthesis via hierarchical interfacial control and highlight the potential of pulsed photoelectrocatalysis.

items.title: Resident cardiac macrophage-like cells induced by an ILC2 cytokine cocktail confer cardioprotection through enhanced efferocytosis in a mouse model of myocardial infarction
Entangled-to-packed crossover in nonlinear extensional rheology of entangled polymers
Multiscale neural dynamics reveal how striatal subregions shape stress vulnerability and resilience
items.abstract: Abstract Effective stress coping relies on neural and endocrine coordination, with the mesostriatal system serving as a central substrate. However, how striatal subregions contribute to stress vulnerability versus resilience remains unclear. Here, we show dissociable roles of the nucleus accumbens (NAC) and dorsal caudate (dCA) and their associated brain networks in shaping stress responses. We identify neural stability (NS)—capturing stress-induced changes in state-switching frequency over the course of stress responses—as a marker: task-state NS correlates positively with stress-related NAC activity, whereas resting-state NS correlates inversely with stress-related dCA activity. NAC-mediated networks and associated NS further predict faster cortisol recovery. Intriguingly, NAC-related functional connectivity patterns spatially covary with dopamine D 2 receptor distributions and gene expression in inhibitory neurons and glia, whereas dCA-related patterns covary with μ-opioid receptor distributions. Together, these findings reveal striatal subregional heterogeneity in stress coping and characterize resilience as a multisystem homeostatic process integrating neural, endocrine, and molecular layers.

items.title: Effective enzyme engineering through modeling kinetic parameter changes upon mutations with geometric deep learning
Two distinct α2β1 integrin glycan interactions mediate cell entry of a picornavirus
items.abstract: Abstract Equine rhinitis A virus (ERAV), a picornavirus closely related to foot-and-mouth disease virus, causes respiratory infections in horses. We performed a HEK293T CRISPRi screen and identified integrin α2β1 as a protein receptor for ERAV. Using knock-out cells and pretreating cells with an antibody or soluble receptor, we confirmed the importance of this integrin for infection of multiple cell types, including equine fibroblasts. Cryo-EM and glycoproteomics analyses revealed that ERAV binds integrin α2β1 in its closed conformation by attaching to the β-propeller of the α2 chain, independent of divalent cations, as well as to a high-mannose glycan on α2 N112 and a sialylated glycan on β1 N269. Using glycan knockout and knock-in cells and by reconstituting integrin α2β1-depleted cells with mutant receptors, we demonstrated the importance of these glycans for virus entry. Our results identify a hitherto unseen combination of protein and glycan interactions between a virus and its receptor.

items.title: Chemokine and opioid peptide scavenging through constitutive and ligand-induced release of ACKR3-bearing extracellular vesicles
items.abstract: Abstract Atypical chemokine receptors (ACKRs) are non-signaling GPCRs that regulate ligand availability, with ACKR3 functioning as a dual scavenger of chemokines and opioid peptides. Here, we demonstrate that following ligand stimulation, besides the canonical internalization, ACKR3 is released on extracellular vesicles (EVs). ACKR3 was also found on EVs released under basal conditions, although to a lesser extent. These observations were confirmed across multiple cellular contexts, including endogenous systems. Mechanistically, basal and ligand-induced EV release are independent of GRKs and β-arrestin but each relies on different trafficking routes and C-terminal determinants. Ligand-induced EV release is associated with plasma membrane localization and receptor recycling pathways. In contrast, basal EV release is governed by intracellular sorting processes and influenced by receptor ubiquitination and RAMP3. Functionally, EV-associated ACKR3 retains high-affinity ligand binding, enabling sequestration of CXCL12 and opioid peptides and thereby attenuating their signaling through CXCR4 and MOR. We also show that the release on EVs, in particular under basal conditions, is observed for other receptors such as KOR, CXCR4 and several ACKRs. Collectively, these findings establish EVs as regulators in chemokine and opioid systems and as a distinct dimension of ACKR3 and more broadly GPCR biology.

items.title: Coordination-directed synthesis of two-dimensional metal-organic covalent organic frameworks

Non-van der Waals superlattices reconcile the strength and conductivity of MXene films
Mannitol-stimulated Copeptin for diagnosing Arginine Vasopressin Deficiency: a randomized controlled proof of concept and a single-arm pilot study
items.abstract: Abstract Differentiating arginine vasopressin (AVP) deficiency from primary polydipsia is challenging. The most accurate test, hypertonic saline–stimulated copeptin, requires intensive monitoring. Intravenous mannitol stimulates AVP release and may provide a simpler alternative. In a randomized double-blind crossover trial, 22 healthy adults received mannitol and placebo in random order, of whom 21 were included in the primary analysis. In a pilot study, 10 patients with AVP deficiency and 10 with primary polydipsia received mannitol. The primary outcome was copeptin after mannitol infusion. Mannitol resulted in a 2.29-fold higher copeptin at 90 minutes (+6.4 pmol/L (95% CI: +5.2, +7.7; p <0.001)) than after placebo at mean baseline copeptin levels in healthy adults. In patients, copeptin after 30 minutes was 11.7 pmol/L (95% CI: 6.5, 17.0) higher in primary polydipsia than in AVP deficiency. Mannitol infusion shows promise as a new diagnostic approach. Larger confirmatory studies are required to validate both the optimal diagnostic cut-off and patient safety. Trial Registration number: NCT06542198 .

items.title: Energy-guided combinatorial co-optimization of antibody affinity and stability
Conveyor-mode electron shuttling through a T-junction in Si/SiGe
items.abstract: Abstract Conveyor-mode shuttling in gated Si/SiGe devices enables adiabatic transfer of single electrons, electron patterns and spin qubits confined in quantum dots across several microns with a scalable number of signal lines. To realize their full potential, linear shuttle lanes must connect into a two-dimensional grid with controllable routing. We introduce a T-junction device linking two independently driven shuttle lanes. Electron routing across the junction requires no extra control lines beyond the four channels per conveyor belt. We measure an inter-lane charge transfer fidelity of $$F={100.0000000}_{-9\times 1{0}^{-7}}^{+0}\,\%$$ F = 100.0000000 − 9 × 1 0 − 7 + 0 % at an instantaneous electron velocity of 270 mm s −1 . The filling of 54 quantum dots is controlled by simple atomic pulses, allowing us to swap electron patterns, laying the groundwork for a native spin-qubit SWAP gate. This T-junction establishes a path towards scalable, two-dimensional quantum computing architectures with flexible spin qubit routing for quantum error correction.

items.title: Disrupting the semantic network shifts activity to domain-general brain regions
items.abstract: Abstract Semantic processing relies on flexible interactions between specialized lexico-semantic regions and domain-general control networks, particularly under challenging conditions. Using transcranial magnetic stimulation interleaved with functional magnetic resonance imaging, we investigated acute network adaptation when the left posterior middle temporal gyrus—a core lexico-semantic region—was perturbed during lexico-semantic decisions in 25 healthy participants. High-intensity transcranial magnetic stimulation over the posterior middle temporal gyrus induced task-specific activity increases across semantic control and lexical retrieval areas, as well as remote domain-general regions. Critically, increased local activity at the stimulation site correlated with slower reaction times, whereas greater upregulation in domain-general frontal regions was associated with less disrupted semantic performance. These findings indicate that acute semantic disruption triggers immediate, flexible recruitment of domain-general control areas consistent with the maintenance of task performance, highlighting the brain’s capacity to dynamically adapt to interference. Our findings contribute to the current understanding of putative compensatory network-level mechanisms supporting lexico-semantic cognition.

items.title: Distributed range adaptation in human parietal encoding of numbers
items.abstract: Abstract The brain’s representations are encoded in the collective activity of neural populations whose non-monotonic tuning properties define the population code. Adaptive behavior calls for flexible retuning of this code as stimulus statistics change across contexts. Yet how such adaptation occurs is unknown. Using fMRI during a numerosity-estimation task with variable number ranges, we show that number representations in human parietal cortex dynamically recalibrate to context, enabling context-sensitive behavioral accuracy. The tuning properties of neural populations collectively shift and rescale with the range. This distributed range adaptation achieves efficient coding in real time: neural precision scales with the range and predicts corresponding changes in behavioral precision. Individuals with stronger neural adaptation show larger behavioral adjustments. These findings extend static sensory efficient coding to adaptive representations of abstract magnitudes. Such flexible population tuning may constitute a canonical mechanism of encoding networks that enables the brain to sustain precise, adaptive behavior.

items.title: Engineering phosphorescence and pH-responsive fluorescence of molecular luminophores and elastomers
Single-cell atlas uncovers layer 4 heterogeneity and functional gradients in rhesus macaque visual cortex
Diacylglycerol Metabolism Drives Host–pathogen Responses During Enteric Infection in Drosophila
items.abstract: Abstract Lipid metabolism is fundamental to cellular homeostasis, supporting energy storage, membrane architecture, and cellular signaling. Beyond these canonical roles, lipids have emerged as critical regulators of host immunity. Here, we define a lipid-driven mechanism that governs host–pathogen interactions by impacting pathogen clearance and thus infection outcomes. Exploiting Drosophila , we show that enteric infection triggers robust accumulation of neutral lipids, and specifically 1,2-diacylglycerols (DAGs), in the midgut. Disruption of DAG biosynthesis or lipid transport in midgut enterocytes (ECs) impairs lipid accumulation and reduces host survival. Conversely, dietary lipid supplementation enhances lipid storage and improves survival. Mechanistically, these lipid-dependent responses regulate defecation, thereby controlling bacterial clearance from the midgut. DAGs can act as signaling lipids that activate protein kinase C (PKC), and DAG accumulation in ECs correlates with elevated PKC activity and calcium signaling in midgut visceral muscle (VM), promoting VM contraction, midgut motility, and expulsion of pathogens via defecation. Together, our findings reveal a previously unrecognized role for DAG metabolism in shaping host defenses.

items.title: Recent extreme heatwaves are no match for future events
items.abstract: Abstract In recent years, record-breaking heatwaves have occurred over many regions of the Earth causing serious impacts to human and natural systems. Here we show that recently observed exceptional heatwaves are no match to potential future 21 st century events based on multiple metrics. For several observed heatwaves, this holds even under low- and medium-emissions scenarios. In a high- to very high-emissions future, many regions are projected to experience heatwaves that generate several times more cumulative heat and are many times longer (up to several months) than the observed heatwaves. Should the Nationally Determined Contributions under the Paris Agreement not be implemented, in most regions a concerningly large proportion of projected heatwaves exceeds all analyzed heatwave characteristics at once. Our results underscore the crucial need for substantial emissions reduction and have important implications for adaptation measures, as a substantial proportion of projected heatwaves is well outside the recent lived experience.

items.title: Molecular-level control of nitrogen sites enables CO2 electro-reduction under industrially relevant conditions
items.abstract: Abstract Industrial flue gases typically contain only 3–15% CO 2 , and direct electrochemical reduction on such dilute feeds would eliminate costly upstream purification. However, mass transport limitations and competing hydrogen evolution severely restrict activity under these CO 2 -starved conditions, and the governing molecular factors remain poorly understood. Here, we demonstrate that pyridinic-nitrogen enrichment in Ni–N–C single-atom catalysts enables efficient CO 2 reduction under dilute CO 2 . By tuning the pyridinic-N to pyrrolic-N ratio in well-defined Ni–N x sites, we probe the role of local nitrogen environments in CO 2 reduction rather than the metal center alone. Electronic-state analysis and density functional theory reveal that pyridinic-N forms a reversible CO 2 adduct that enhances local CO 2 accessibility near the active Ni center through a desorption–re-adsorption relay. These findings provide molecular-level insight by identifying a neighboring motif that regulates local CO 2 availability without perturbing the intrinsic Ni–N reaction pathway, and by establishing a transferable design principle for CO 2 reduction catalysts under CO 2 -limited conditions.

items.title: Toward Ternary Computing Enabled by Origami-Inspired Modular Architectures
items.abstract: Abstract Modern mechanical computing, being envisioned as a pathway toward structure- and material-level processing, holds potential for intelligent metamaterials and robotics in extreme environments. However, current computing architectures remain constrained by binary paradigms. Here, we introduce an origami-inspired modular architecture that encodes logical mappings into its inherent kinematic responses under an input-output decoupled paradigm, enabling both binary and ternary mechanical computing. Within this emerging paradigm, the multi-stable states of two Kresling origami configurations serve as physical carriers for generating discrete signals, while torsional transitions among these states ensure signal switching, supporting operations from logic gates to advanced arithmetic. Based on this mechanical architecture, we systematically demonstrate seven common logic gates and modular arithmetic half- and full-adders in both binary and ternary systems, revealing challenges and opportunities in advancing multi-valued logic through comparative analysis. The physical platform, along with its accompanying response-programming strategy, represents a simplified and generalized paradigm that supports migration to higher-level mechanical computing mechanisms.

Wt1 splice isoforms bias lineage programmes during formative pluripotency
items.abstract: Abstract How transcriptional asymmetry arises in the epiblast before gastrulation remains a central question in mammalian development. Using a targeted CRISPRa screen, we identify Wt1 as a regulator of lineage-associated transcriptional programmes during formative pluripotency. Wt1 is transiently induced during formative pluripotency in vitro and in vivo, coincident with emerging lineage biases. Precocious Wt1 induction advances cells toward post-implantation identity, whereas Wt1 -deficient cells execute naïve exit but show impaired acquisition of formative and lineage-associated programmes. WT1 binds active regulatory elements together with OTX2, OCT4 and FOXO1. Comparison of Wt1 splice isoforms identifies KTS splice status as the major determinant of divergent anterior/neuroectodermal and posterior/mesodermal transcriptional programmes in vitro. In the E5.5 epiblast, Wt1 expression and splice composition align with lineage-biased states, linking isoform usage to anterior bias in vivo. Isoform-dependent programmes are conserved in human pluripotent cells. These findings identify alternative splicing as a mechanism tuning lineage-associated transcriptional bias before gastrulation.

items.title: Nitrene-triggered carbocationic rearrangement of tetrasubstituted alkenes enables divergent access to fused δ-lactams
items.abstract: Abstract Transition-metal-catalyzed nitrene transfer has emerged as a powerful strategy for alkene functionalization, yet its application to sterically congested tetrasubstituted alkenes remains severely underdeveloped. Here, we report an Ir(III)-catalyzed nitrene-triggered aziridination–rearrangement cascade that enables the efficient conversion of cyclic-substituted tetrasubstituted alkenes into cycloalkane-fused δ-lactams. The transformation proceeds under mild conditions with excellent yields and uniformly high diastereoselectivities and exhibits broad compatibility with carbon-, oxygen-, and nitrogen-based nucleophiles, including structurally complex and biologically relevant substrates. Combined experimental and computational studies support a concerted aziridination by an Ir–nitrenoid to generate a strained tricyclic intermediate, which undergoes a strain-release-driven aza-semipinacol rearrangement to furnish a bicyclic azacarbocation. Divergent nucleophilic interception or elimination of this intermediate provides rapid access to structurally diverse fused δ-lactam architectures. These findings establish a nitrene-triggered carbocationic rearrangement manifold for the functionalization of tetrasubstituted alkenes and expand the synthetic potential of transition-metal-catalyzed nitrene transfer.

items.title: Agentic intelligent data engine for scientific large language models
A sublattice polarimeter to probe the quantum geometry of synthetic photonic lattices
Alpha-aminoadipate in the saccharopine pathway promotes cancer metastasis through sumoylation of transcription machinery
items.abstract: Abstract Despite studies linking metabolism and cancer, our understanding of the metabolite network that drives metastasis remains incomplete. Through a metabolic RNAi-based screen for cell invasion, we identify alpha-aminoadipate (2-AAA), the intermediate metabolite of aminoadipic semialdehyde synthase (AASS) in the saccharopine pathway, as a common pivotal factor in metastasis of human cancers. Metabolite-protein connectivity mapping reveals that 2-AAA binds to SAE1, a crucial component of the SUMO-activating enzyme E1, and enhances SAE1 recruitment to UBA2, facilitating sumoylation. 2-AAA-mediated sumoylation of the RNA polymerase subunit POLR2A then partially promotes cancer cell invasion by inducing the expression of metastasis-promoting genes, including SPG11 and KCTD7 . Targeting AASS with cetalkonium chloride, a newly identified small molecule inhibitor against AASS, attenuates cancer cell invasion and tumor metastasis. Our study highlights the mechanism by which metastasis is mediated by metabolite-driven sumoylation and indicates AASS as an effective therapeutic target for mitigating metastatic cancer progression.

Seagrass sediment organic carbon burial rates are globally significant
items.abstract: Abstract Crucial for coastal carbon sequestration, global seagrass organic carbon (OC) burial rates remain uncertain as early estimates were derived from mixed methodologies across geographically and taxonomically biased datasets. Here, we present a data-driven reassessment from a synthesis of 332 sediment cores spanning the last century. Results show that seagrasses bury OC at 25 ± 3 g OC m −2 yr −1 (geometric mean), with an area-weighted global average of 33 ± 9 g OC m −2 yr −1 . Rates reflect a balance between sediment OC content and sediment accumulation, which share a negative exponential relationship driven by mineral dilution. Based on a revised mapped seagrass extent (247,700–366,400 km 2 ), global burial scales to 6–15 Tg C yr −1 . Although one-fourth of earlier benchmarks, seagrasses account for 3–4% to 3–6% of total oceanic OC burial despite covering <0.1% of the seafloor. Combined with mangroves and tidal marshes, vegetated coastal ecosystems contribute 8–13% of oceanic OC burial.

Systematic screen of RNA binding proteins that enhance circular RNA translation
Author Correction: Non-parasite genome encoded virus-like RNAs reprogram the pathogenicity of human blood flukes
Podocyte-derived palmitic acid drives p53 S-palmitoylation and CD103+ CD4+ T cell differentiation in humanized mouse model of systemic lupus erythematosus
MMC-seq enables efficient long-read eccDNA profiling from low-input samples
Precision probabilistic mapping reveals personalized functional topography in the early postnatal human brain
Author Correction: Renal resistive index-guided mean arterial pressure titration in sepsis: a prospective single-center, single-blind, parallel-group randomized controlled trial
In vitro–reconstituted Drosophila Arc capsids deliver gene editors to dystrophic muscle
items.abstract: Abstract The intracellular delivery of therapeutic macromolecules remains a major challenge in biomedicine. Capsid-forming proteins are one promising vehicle, but to date, these have required cellular assembly or rely on fusogens for cell entry, limiting their scalability and utility. Here we reconstitute the Drosophila melanogaster Arc1 (dArc1) retroelement-derived capsid entirely from purified recombinant protein components and in vitro transcribed RNA, creating a fully defined, cell-free assembled protein nanoparticle system. We engineered the dArc1 RNA-binding domain to efficiently encapsulate both mRNA payloads and Cas9 ribonucleoproteins. We show that dArc1 capsids bind mammalian cells through a direct interaction with the surface receptor SORCS2. Leveraging this interaction, we demonstrate that intramuscular injection of dArc1 capsids carrying Cas9 gene editors achieves up to 18% exon skipping and restores dystrophin expression in muscle fibers of mdx mice, a model of Duchenne muscular dystrophy. This work demonstrates the potential of in vitro-assembled protein nanoparticles for delivery of molecular cargoes.

items.title: Endocannabinoid-mediated rescue of somatosensory cortex activity, plasticity and related behaviors following an early-life concussion in male mice
items.abstract: Abstract Due to the assumed plasticity of the immature brain, early-life brain alterations are thought to lead to better recoveries in comparison to the mature brain. Despite clinical needs, how neuronal networks and associated behaviors are affected by early-life brain stresses, such as pediatric concussions, have been overlooked. Here we provide first evidence in male mice that a single early-life concussion durably increases neuronal activity in the somatosensory cortex into adulthood, disrupting neuronal integration while the animal is performing sensory-related tasks. This represents a clinically relevant mechanism that was previously unappreciated for understanding impairment of sensory-related behavior performance. We also demonstrate that pharmacological modulation of the endocannabinoid system a year post-concussion is well-suited to rescue neuronal activity and plasticity, and normalizes sensory-related behavioral performance. These findings identify persistent alterations in cortical sensory processing following early-life concussion and demonstrate that neuronal and behavioral deficits remain amenable to pharmacological intervention long after injury.

items.title: Spatial protein interactomics in solid primary human tissue
Biphasic enzymatic reaction in coacervate-containing droplets
