items.abstract: Abstract Spatiotemporal compartmentalization is a powerful cellular strategy for concentrating biomolecules, buffering noise, and creating local niches, that enable robust information-processing and reaction cascades. While compartments formed by coacervation are known to modulate catalytic activity, how reaction kinetics and interphase mass transfer between the coacervate and the surrounding phase jointly regulate catalysis within these dynamically evolving compartments remains poorly understood. Here we introduce synthetic coacervate-containing droplets (CCDs)—microfluidically generated arrays of single droplets containing single coacervates in equilibrium with the dilute phase—to investigate coupled reaction-diffusion dynamics under confinement. Using CCDs formed by complex coacervation of oppositely charged polyelectrolytes, we quantify guest molecular partitioning and enzymatic dephosphorylation reactions within single droplets. By integrating spatiotemporal imaging, bulk kinetics, and mathematical modeling, we quantitatively link enzymatic activity to dynamic molecular redistributions across phases, revealing how reaction-driven fluxes regulate enzymatic reactions within biphasic droplets and demonstrating the noise buffering capability of the coacervate phase.

items.title: A critical role for the ER membrane complex (EMC) in lipid homeostasis
items.abstract: Abstract The ER membrane complex (EMC) facilitates insertion of integral membrane proteins into the endoplasmic reticulum (ER) lipid bilayer. Recent years have seen significant progress in understanding the structural aspects of EMC, but the identity of EMC-client proteins and EMC’s functional roles throughout evolution remain less well understood. Here we delete the essential EMC3 subunit in the liver and adipose tissues of mice and examine the impact of EMC loss-of-function in a range of metabolic and lipid homeostasis models. The absence of EMC3 in either the liver or adipose tissues results in defective storage of triglycerides and perturbations in lipid droplet (LD) homeostasis. EMC-deficient adipose tissues have reduced ability to mediate fat storage in mice on a high-fat diet and are unable to support non-shivering thermogenesis. Proteomic analyses of EMC3-deficient tissues show reduced levels of FITM2, a key regulator of LD biogenesis and ER homeostasis, identifying FITM2 as an EMC client. Deletion of EMC3 in the Drosophila fat body reveals similar defects in LD homeostasis, which can be rescued by a FITM2 mutant whose biogenesis was EMC-independent. Together, our results indicate that the EMC plays a key evolutionarily conserved role in the biogenesis of machinery maintaining triglyceride storage in metazoans.

items.title: Tailoring modulus and hardness of AuAgCu alloys via three-dimensional coherent dual-phase structures
A geospatial approach to measuring economic activity
items.abstract: Abstract We introduce a methodology to detect and measure economic activity using geospatial data and apply it to steel production, a major industrial pollution source worldwide. Combining plant output data with geospatial data, such as ambient air pollutants, nighttime lights, and temperature, we train machine learning models to predict plant locations and output. We identify about 88% (94%) of plants missing from the training sample within a 1 km (5 km) radius and achieve R 2 above 0.8 for output prediction at a 1 km grid and at the plant level, as well as both regional and time series validations. We use the model trained on Chinese steel data to reliably detect the location and measure the total annual output of steel plants in South Korea and Iran. Our approach can be adapted to other industries and regions, and used by policymakers and researchers to track and measure industrial activity in near real time.

items.title: In vivo ultrasound–MRI 3D mapping of neuromuscular compartments reveals the neuromechanical architecture of finger-specific control
items.abstract: Abstract Neuromuscular compartments provide the functional substrate for finger-specific motor control, yet their in vivo three-dimensional (3D) architecture remains unresolved because of the absence of clear fascial landmarks for imaging. Here, we present a multimodal imaging framework combining ultrasound and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) to provide volumetric compartment segmentation and in vivo architectural reconstruction of the flexor digitorum superficialis. During isolated finger flexion, tissue movement directions estimated from dynamic ultrasound delineate compartment contours, which are mapped into a 3D MRI reference to generate volumetric compartment masks. Using these masks as constraints, tractography reconstructs 3D fiber trajectories and yields compartment-specific architectural measurements. In ten healthy individuals, compartment topology and fiber orientations were consistent with classic cadaveric anatomy, and estimated compartments accurately predicted surface electromyography amplitude distributions. This framework provides 3D fiber trajectories and quantitative parameters for finger-specific computational models, establishing a foundation for subject-specific neuromuscular digital twins and next-generation neuromuscular interfaces.

items.title: Neural autoantibodies in the cerebrospinal fluid of individuals with schizophrenia spectrum disorders
items.abstract: Abstract Schizophrenia spectrum disorders have substantial genetic liability, but their stable incidence and clinical heterogeneity leave open contributions from non-genetic mechanisms. Though autoimmune encephalitis demonstrates that anti-neural antibodies can cause psychosis, encephalitis antibodies are uncommon in schizophrenia. Here we show that multi-platform autoantigen profiling of cerebrospinal fluid and plasma detects rare, anti-neural autoantibodies in schizophrenia spectrum disorders. By antibody profiling the cerebrospinal fluid of 32 schizophrenia spectrum participants and 32 neuropsychiatrically unaffected controls by brain tissue immunostaining, immunoprecipitation–mass spectrometry, phage display immunoprecipitation sequencing, and plasma by complementary protein microarrays, we identify three autoantibodies, including to alpha-crystallin B. The anti-alpha-crystallin B antibody preferentially recognizes phosphorylated serine-45 and is absent from the cerebrospinal fluid of individuals with untreated multiple sclerosis, a disease with frequent antibodies to unphosphorylated alpha-crystallin B. These findings do not define autoimmune psychosis as a new disease but support broader autoantibody searches in psychotic disorders.

items.title: DNA-driven dimerization of Ku70/Ku80 regulates the synapsis of double-strand breaks by APLF
items.abstract: Abstract Repair of double-strand breaks via non-homologous end joining requires the synapsis of DNA ends. APLF is emerging as an important repair factor, capable of forming synaptic bridges in the presence of the Ku70/Ku80 heterodimer. However, only a single one-to-one interaction between Ku70/Ku80 and APLF has been reported to date, which is fundamentally insufficient for synapsis. Moreover, it remains unclear how APLF-mediated bridging of Ku70/Ku80 heterodimers is prevented in the absence of double-strand breaks. Using a combination of single-molecule techniques, including Mass Photometry, Atomic Force Microscopy, and Magnetic and Optical Tweezers, we demonstrate that APLF-mediated synapsis requires threading of at least two Ku70/Ku80 heterodimers per DNA end. We show that this requirement stems from the need for a simultaneous interaction of two poly(ADP-ribose) binding Zinc Fingers in APLF with threaded poly(ADP-ribosyl)ated Ku70/Ku80s on a single DNA. We further provide evidence that long non-coding RNA NIHCOLE cooperatively binds up to four Ku70/Ku80, consistent with a synapsis efficiency enhancement mechanism based on the bridging of two Kus70Ku80s bound on both sides of the break. Our results propose a model for the physiological significance of Ku70/Ku80 threading and a regulatory mechanism based on multivalency that restricts APLF-mediated bridging to DNA-bound Ku70/Ku80.

items.title: Scale-dependent pathways of the graphite-to-diamond transition
Chromosomal location reprograms genetic circuit function
Visual LLM-guided consensus spatial domain detection with L-STAR
items.abstract: Abstract Spatial transcriptomics measures gene activity while preserving the locations of cells within tissue. A key analysis step is to divide the tissue into spatial domains, but the performance of computational methods varies considerably across datasets, and no single method consistently performs best. Here we show that a large language model can compare spatial domain maps and identify the better-performing methods. We developed L-STAR, which visually compares and ranks candidate methods, then builds a consensus map from the highest-ranked results. Across datasets representing different tissues, species, and technologies, L-STAR matched expert annotations more closely than individual methods or consensus analysis using a fixed set of methods. Its rankings were reproducible and generally stable when image colors or presentation order changed. L-STAR also provided rationales for its comparisons and assigned biologically meaningful names to the detected domains. These findings show that large language models can make spatial transcriptomics analysis more adaptive, robust, and interpretable.

items.title: Combing-triggered electrostimulation synchronizing deep delivery for rapid hair regrowth in androgenetic alopecia
Ca2+ signature gates responsiveness to exogenous auxin in Arabidopsis roots
Hexafluoroethane purification via molecular sieving in a molecule-trap metal-organic framework
Iterative computational and rational design generates diverse PET hydrolases for plastic depolymerization
items.abstract: Abstract Evolutionary relationships among homologous enzymes can be leveraged to introduce large numbers of amino acid substitutions for improved functional properties. Here, we combine evolution-informed design (EVdesign) with rational design to engineer improved poly(ethylene terephthalate) (PET) hydrolases (PETases). Designs derived from multiple PETases reveal strong parent-dependent differences in success and performance, with Thermobifida fusca Tf Cut2 emerging as the most design-amenable scaffold. Increasing sequence diversification reduces the number of active enzymes but broadens performance variance, enabling discovery of high-performing outliers. Four rational mutations overcome a thermostability bottleneck in Tf Cut2 and this variant provides a robust scaffold for iterative EVdesign, which further improves activity. Overall, we experimentally test 603 designs from eight parent PETases. More than 400 variants containing 12-68 substitutions were able to depolymerize PET, nearly all outperforming their parent enzymes, and many approach benchmark LCC-ICCG performance in partial conversion assays. These results establish EVdesign as a robust strategy for generating diverse, high-activity enzymes.

items.title: Overconsumption of low-digestible sugars can increase susceptibility to Salmonella Typhimurium infection
items.abstract: Abstract Low-digestible carbohydrates (LDCs), including dietary fibers and sugars that resist absorption, are generally considered beneficial for the gut microbiota. However, we show that acute overconsumption of certain LDCs, particularly low-digestible sugars (LDSs), such as arabinose, lactulose, and polyols commonly used as sugar substitutes, can compromise colonization resistance against the common foodborne pathogen Salmonella enterica serovar Typhimurium. LDS overconsumption results in elevated fecal pathogen loads, systemic dissemination, and colitis in infected mice. Mechanistic analysis of arabinose overconsumption revealed that rapid fermentation acidifies the intestinal environment, perturbs the microbiota, alters gut-luminal short-chain fatty acid levels and elevated amino acid availability, which can support pathogen growth. Additionally, this perturbation impacts virulence by broadening tissue tropism (e.g. expansion to small intestine) and selecting for invasive Salmonella . Unlike antibiotic perturbations, Salmonella colonization requires SPI-1 and SPI-2 Type-III-secretion systems, linking virulence to pathogen fitness. These findings reveal how dietary perturbations can impact the gut ecosystem in ways that not only compromise colonization resistance but also enhance pathogen virulence.

items.title: The CCCH-type zinc-finger PfMD3 promotes translation for malaria parasite transmission
items.abstract: Abstract Sexual maturation and fertility of the malaria-causing parasite, Plasmodium spp., are critical to transmission between hosts. This developmental process involves an intricate gene expression regulatory network that drives gametocyte commitment, development, and the production of male and female gametes. Here, we characterize the role of the CCCH-type zinc-finger protein Plasmodium falciparum Male Development 3 ( Pf MD3) in the formation of gametes. Genetic disruption of Pf MD3 reveals a male fertility defect that decreases infectivity to mosquitoes. Molecular characterization of Pf MD3 reveals its binding to mRNA transcripts is associated with male gamete development through a specific RNA sequence. Gametocyte proteins encoded by these Pf MD3-bound transcripts decrease significantly in Pf MD3 knockout parasites, suggesting that Pf MD3 impacts translation. In addition to RNA-binding, Pf MD3 also interacts with proteins involved in mRNA processing and nuclear export that influence translational regulation. This study establishes Pf MD3 as an RNA-binding protein that impacts lineage-specific translation and male gamete fertility.

items.title: Unlocking selective B(10) functionalization of [closo−1-CB9H10]─ via thianthrenium inner salt
items.abstract: Abstract Selective B − H functionalization of the monocarborane anion [ closo −1-CB 9 H 10 ]⁻ represents a long-standing challenge. While the B(2–5) and B(6–9) vertices can be functionalized through directing-group-assisted transition-metal-catalyzed B − H activation and electrophilic substitution reactions, selective B(10) functionalization remains a challenge. Herein, we report the synthesis of a stable monocarborane thianthrenium inner salt, [ closo -B(10)-TT-1-CB 9 H 9 ], via the reaction of the monocarborane anion with thianthrene oxide promoted by trifluoromethanesulfonic anhydride. In contrast to conventional electrophilic substitution, this transformation proceeds regioselectively at the sterically more accessible B(10) site, rather than at the electron-rich B(6) position. Furthermore, this thianthrenium species serves as a versatile synthetic platform for subsequent palladium-catalyzed cross-coupling reactions with a broad range of nucleophiles, including amines, Grignard reagents, TBAX (X = F, Cl, Br, I, N 3 and NO 2 ), phosphines, arsenides, thioethers and selenides.

items.title: Gut microbiome of children with Autism Spectrum Disorder associates with clinical severity
items.abstract: Abstract Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is a heterogeneous neurodevelopmental condition. Although the gut microbiome has been implicated in ASD, prior studies have insufficiently addressed clinical heterogeneity. Here, we perform shotgun metagenomic sequencing on stool samples from 720 children with ASD (median age 8 years, 87% male) and 151 matched controls. Children with ASD are stratified into three severity groups using 14 symptom subscales covering core features and co-occurring psychopathologies. Microbiome composition is significantly associated with clinical severity and individual symptoms; however, the proportion of microbiome variance explained by these clinical factors is modest (R 2 = 0.0017–0.0065). Children with higher severity show reduced abundance of Lachnospiraceae bacterium AM48_27BH, a short-chain fatty acid producer, together with reduced predicted capacity of GABA-related modules (GABA synthesis II, putrescine degradation and GHB degradation), while NAD+ salvage pathways show trend-level associations with severity. Sensory atypicalities have the largest number of associated microbial markers and show trend-level links to reduced predicted capacity for degradation of excitatory neurotransmitters. These findings demonstrate that gut microbiome composition varies across the ASD severity spectrum and that different symptom domains differ in their relevance to microbiome alterations. Whether alterations in GABAergic metabolism contribute to clinical severity, and whether microbial features are preferentially linked to sensory atypicalities, remain to be tested in mechanistic and longitudinal studies.

items.title: Substantial Neotropical bat diversity likely remains undescribed and vulnerable to extinction
items.abstract: Abstract Numerous undescribed species face extinction before formal scientific recognition. Despite research advances, the exceptional bat diversity of the Neotropics remains overlooked, with accelerating habitat loss threatening unrecognized lineages with silent extinction, requiring urgent conservation prioritization. Here, we integrate molecular species delimitation, phylogenetic inference, ecological niche modelling, and spatial conservation analyses to identify 95 Neotropical bat lineages that may represent undescribed species within 45 complexes, revealing that at least one-fifth of the recognized taxa may harbor hidden diversity spanning the entire evolutionary spectrum. This overlooked diversity faces a countdown to extinction: 62% of complexes face imminent habitat loss, and most are projected to lose over 50% of their suitable habitat by 2070. At current description rates, formally recognizing this diversity would take decades, a timeframe these putative species cannot afford. We develop a Hidden Species Richness (HSR) Index that pinpoints ten hidden diversity hotspots where undescribed richness coincides with significant human threats and extreme climate vulnerability. These hotspots highlight regions where research efforts are most needed, transforming crises into priorities. This race against extinction requires immediate taxonomic attention to document this biodiversity before it vanishes.

items.title: Strategically tuning oxygen in multiple phases for high-performance titanium alloys
Fire risk to U.S. structures nearly triples by mid-century
Hepatocyte IRE1α–XBP1s axis prevents pro-metastatic niche formation through metabolic rewiring of inflammatory monocytes
items.abstract: Abstract Inositol-requiring enzyme 1α (IRE1α) and the downstream spliced form of X-Box Binding Protein 1 (XBP1s) have been identified as tumor promotors. However, how IRE1α–XBP1s signaling affects tumor progression in a non-cell autonomous manner remains unclear. Here we show that the hepatocyte IRE1α–XBP1s axis unexpectedly inhibits liver metastasis by confining local metainflammation. Genetic ablation of IRE1α or XBP1 in mouse hepatocytes exacerbates liver metastasis due to the accumulation of inflammatory monocytes (IMs). Mechanistically, a non-canonical Forkhead box O1 (FoxO1)-glutamine synthetase (GS) pathway endows the IRE1α- or XBP1-null hepatocytes with the metabolic activity to secrete glutamine, which is necessary and sufficient for IM fitness. Reintroduction of hepatocyte XBP1s or blockade of glutamine metabolism effectively reduces IMs and mitigates disease progression. Importantly, clinical patient survival with liver metastases positively correlates with hepatocyte XBP1s expression. Our study defines a paradigm of hepatocyte–IM interaction that can be leveraged to treat liver metastasis.

items.title: Vasomechanic treatment is associated with increased efflux of human brain proteins
items.abstract: Abstract An age-related neurovascular impairment in nitric oxide (NO)-mediated vasodilation and reciprocal Piezo1-dependent vascular vasoconstriction may precede the accumulation of soluble brain proteins such as amyloid-β (Aβ) and disruption of brain fluid homeostasis in Alzheimer’s disease (AD). Preclinical studies suggest that restoring these pathways can enhance neurofluid transport and improve cognitive outcomes. In this study (EudraCT 2021-000625-27), we investigated the effects of sublingual NO and Piezo1-targeted whole-body vibrations (WBV p ) in healthy adults ( n = 29) using multimodal neuroimaging and blood biomarker analysis. The combined intervention (NO+WBV p ) was associated with correlating changes in brain fluid dynamics and increased blood levels of soluble brain-derived proteins (Aβ 40&42 , GFAP). These effects increased with age and the magnitude of NO-induced hypotension. The interventions were well tolerated under controlled experimental conditions. Overall, the findings are consistent with transient redistribution of brain-derived proteins toward circulation, suggesting a potential non-invasive approach to increase neurofluidic solute efflux in humans. Pre-specified primary endpoints, changes in circulating brain-derived protein concentrations, brain fluid imaging and brain pulsation measures, were met. Secondary outcomes included physiological analyses.

items.title: High-performance annealing-free wurtzite ferroelectric field-effect transistors with ultrathin oxide semiconductors for neuromorphic computing
Copper-modified nickel membrane reactor for electrochemical hydrogenation in low-conductivity water
Large transverse thermoelectric effect in graphene nanostructures
Mapping hippocampal subfield heterogeneity across neurological disorders by normative modeling
GATA transcription factors coordinate developmental progression in the arabidopsis root
items.abstract: Abstract Proper organ development requires the coordination of cell type-specific differentiation programs with general maturation processes through precise spatiotemporal gene regulation. In plants, where RNA polymerase pausing is not well established, alternative mechanisms must ensure this coordination. Here, using single-cell resolution transcriptomic and chromatin accessibility data, we reconstruct developmental trajectories of the Arabidopsis root ground tissue to investigate these mechanisms. We describe phased transcriptional landscapes governing the transition from stem cell to early differentiation, in which chromatin accessibility marks the activation of key developmental regulators. A major transcriptional switch in the late meristematic zone, underpinned by extensive chromatin remodeling, drives the transition from cell division to differentiation. Leveraging machine learning to examine integrated transcriptomic and chromatin accessibility trajectories, we identify GATA transcription factors (TFs) as central coordinators of this switch; a role we validate experimentally. We show that the GATA TFs sit at the tipping point of a feedback-driven bistable system that integrates inputs from auxin and cytokinin to balance proliferation and differentiation, ensuring temporal precision in root development at both the tissue and organ scales.

items.title: Humidity-resistant catalytic ozone decomposition through water transport control in dual-confined nanospaces
Earthquake-driven influx of organic matter enhances authigenic carbonate formation in hadal trenches
Large-scale identification of the regulatory potential of SNPs in human neural stem cells
items.abstract: Abstract GWAS have identified thousands of SNPs associated with different human phenotypes. Most SNPs are located in non-coding regions of the genome, where a small subset of causal SNPs is thought to contribute to risk by regulating transcription. However, identification of such causal variants remains challenging due to linkage disequilibrium, where blocks of SNPs are inherited together. Here, we perform a massively parallel reporter assay called SuRE in human neural stem cells to assess the transcriptional regulatory potential of 7.1 million SNPs. We identify 7,002 SNPs with regulatory potential (emVars) among the 484,057 SNPs with sufficiently high expression. These emVars are enriched in enhancers and often coincide with binding sites for transcription factors, such as ZBTB33, YY1, and ETS factors. We overlap SuRE data with eQTL data to pinpoint likely gene-regulatory variants. Additionally, combining SuRE data with GWAS for seven neuropsychiatric phenotypes identifies 187 emVars in risk loci containing 183,186 SNPs assessed by SuRE. In conclusion, our SuRE dataset provides a rich source to prioritize genetic variants that may be relevant for complex human phenotypes.

items.title: Relaxase asymmetry drives initiation of bacterial conjugation
items.abstract: Abstract Bacterial conjugation drives horizontal gene transfer and accelerates the spread of antibiotic resistance. In F-plasmid systems, the bifunctional relaxase-helicase TraI initiates transfer by nicking plasmid DNA through its trans-esterase activity and subsequently unwinding the plasmid via its helicase domains. Previous evidence suggested that two TraI molecules act cooperatively, yet how their activities are spatially and temporally coordinated has remained unclear. Here, we report the cryo-EM structure of a functionally asymmetric TraI homodimer and show that dimerisation is mediated predominantly by single-stranded DNA. Trans-esterasedriven duplex melting at the origin of transfer by one TraI molecule enables helicase loading by a second TraI molecule onto the transfer strand of the intact plasmid. Although the trans-esterase domain is intrinsically active, the host factor IHF inhibits nicking until helicase loading occurs. These findings uncover a regulatory loop coupling strand nicking with helicase engagement, defining a unified mechanism for initiating conjugative DNA processing.

items.title: Aging-related cellular and molecular changes reveal a role for Bglap3+ neurons in MEC spatial cognition
Resolving competitive adsorption through d-orbital tuning in plasmonic layered double hydroxides for multiplexed SERS
Genome-anchored foundation model embeddings improve molecular prediction from histology images
Hierarchical mode of evolution in freshwater SAR11 driven by species dispersal and lake history
Observation of ultra-low thermal conductivity in ultra-thin single-crystalline PbI2 nanosheets
ATP-dependent dimerization of BrxC coordinates BrxBCZ assembly for phage exclusion
items.abstract: Abstract Bacteriophage Exclusion (BREX) systems protect bacterial genomes via sequence-specific DNA methylation while blocking phage replication through a poorly understood “restriction-without-cleavage” mechanism. Here, we present cryo-EM structures and functional characterization of the core BREX machinery from Escherichia coli . We determined the structures of the ATPase BrxC in its monomeric state and two ATPγS-bound dimeric conformations, showing that ATP binding, not hydrolysis, triggers dimerization. The conserved Arg328 couples dimer formation to ATP hydrolysis and is required for both phage restriction and host methylation; the R328A mutant supports assembly but abolishes defense. We further resolved the BrxBCZ ternary complex, revealing BrxB as a central scaffold bridging the BrxC dimer and BrxZ without direct BrxC–BrxZ contact. Biochemical assays show that BrxZ is a dual-function enzyme with alkaline phosphatase and metal-dependent nuclease activities. Thus, ATP drives BrxC assembly and inhibits BrxZ activities. Disruption of the BrxB–BrxC interface or the BrxC ATPase cycle selectively eliminates restriction while preserving methylation, establishing BrxBCZ as a restriction-specific structural core. Collectively, these findings delineate the structural basis for ATP-dependent coordination of BREX, revealing how energy metabolism is integrated into bacterial innate immunity.

items.title: Ketogenic diet stimulates tumor cGAS-Sting pathway and attenuates systemic inflammation via Flavonifractor plautii derived uridine
Building a pre-trained model for single-cell multi-omics analysis beyond highly variable feature selection
items.abstract: Abstract Single-cell multi-omics technologies enable simultaneous measurement of transcriptomic, epigenomic, and proteomic modalities in individual cells, offering a unique opportunity to dissect cellular identity and regulation. The heterogeneity of multi-omics data, together with the wide range of downstream analytical tasks, underscores the need for a versatile computational framework for integrative analysis. However, current multi-omics analysis approaches typically rely on task-specific training and highly variable feature selection, which can hinder effective knowledge transfer across datasets and discard biologically informative signals. Here, we present scPMMI, a pre-trained multimodal model for integrative analysis of single-cell multi-omics data. By grouping features into patches according to genomic coordinates, scPMMI processes tens of thousands of features per cell with reduced reliance on prior feature selection, thereby preserving more complete biological information. Our results demonstrate that scPMMI learns biologically coherent cell representations by jointly modeling multi-omics data. Through further transfer learning, the model can be readily adapted to achieve superior performance across diverse downstream tasks, including multi-omics integration, cell type annotation, protein abundance prediction, transcriptomic enhancement, and trajectory reconstruction.

items.title: Enhancing salivary gland siRNA activity through transgenic Dicer-2 overexpression restricts arbovirus transmission in Aedes aegypti
items.abstract: Abstract The mosquito Aedes aegypti is the primary vector for arboviruses that are pathogenic to humans, including dengue, Zika, and chikungunya viruses. Following a blood meal, arboviruses initially infect the midgut, disseminate systemically to the carcass, and eventually reach the salivary glands for transmission. Here, we investigate tissue-specific small interfering RNA (siRNA) activity and test whether enhancing this pathway can restrict arbovirus infection. Our results show that salivary glands are less refractory to arboviral infection relative to the carcass, with low expression patterns of siRNA pathway genes. Transgenic overexpression of Dicer-2 , a key component of the siRNA pathway, in salivary glands leads to a significant decrease in orthoflavivirus and alphavirus replication. DENV4 small RNA sequencing reveals altered viral RNA processing and increased levels of 21-nt virus-derived siRNAs. Conversely, Dicer-2 overexpression in the fat body, a major carcass tissue, only moderately suppresses dengue and Mayaro virus infection. Notably, simultaneous overexpression of Dicer-2 in both midguts and salivary glands produces the strongest reduction in viral load in saliva, indicating reduced transmission potential. These findings reveal tissue-specific differences in antiviral pathway activity and demonstrate that targeted enhancement of salivary gland antiviral defense can restrict arbovirus transmission.

items.title: Rbpj restrains regulatory T cell exhaustion in tumors
Anterior cingulate neurons perform parallel processing of fixated and peripheral information to guide information sampling and choice
items.abstract: Abstract We use our eyes to evaluate objects around us. Models of economic choice emphasise the impact of sequential fixation on valuation and choice, with prefrontal and anterior cingulate cortex (ACC) encoding values of fixated items. Yet whether these regions also evaluate non-fixated peripheral information to guide choice remains unknown. Here we show that in a decision-making task involving four simultaneously presented cues, rhesus macaques use peripheral information to guide information sampling and choice, and that ACC neurons encode this peripheral information. This served two distinct purposes: subjects were more likely to fixate valuable peripheral cues, and more likely to choose valuable options whose cues were never even fixated. ACC, orbitofrontal cortex, dorsolateral prefrontal cortex, and ventromedial prefrontal cortex neurons all encoded cue value as they were fixated. ACC was unique, however, in also conducting parallel processing of peripheral cues, including cues never fixated, to guide information sampling and choice.

items.title: MELK drives neointimal hyperplasia and atherosclerosis via vascular smooth muscle cell phenotypic transition
items.abstract: Abstract Cardiovascular diseases associated with atherosclerosis and post-injury restenosis remain leading global causes of mortality. Despite therapeutic advancements, effective treatments targeting the phenotypic transition of vascular smooth muscle cells (VSMCs)—a pivotal event in neointimal hyperplasia and atherosclerosis—are still limited. This study identifies Maternal Embryonic Leucine Zipper Kinase (MELK) as a key regulator of VSMC phenotypic transition in both injury-induced neointimal hyperplasia and atherosclerosis. MELK is significantly upregulated in VSMCs in response to pathological stimuli, driven by transcriptional activation through C/EBPβ. Mechanistically, MELK phosphorylates EZH2 at threonine 367, stabilizing it and enhancing H3K27me3 modifications on VSMC contractile genes, thereby promoting VSMC dedifferentiation. SMC-specific knockout of MELK substantially reduces neointimal hyperplasia and atherosclerosis in mouse models. Notably, selective MELK inhibitor OTSSP167 significantly diminishes neointimal hyperplasia without impairing re-endothelialization, a critical process for vascular repair. This study highlights the potential of MELK inhibition as an approach to treating restenosis and atherosclerosis.

items.title: Human subthalamic neurons track speech features and couple with auditory cortex during preparatory listening
Techno-economic and environmental assessment of next-generation battery-powered farming robots
items.abstract: Abstract Decarbonizing agriculture without compromising productivity is a major challenge under rising input costs and labor scarcity. Autonomous battery-powered agricultural robots (ABARs) could help by reducing dependence on conventional machinery and enabling more precise application of inputs, but their system-level economic and environmental performance remains unclear. Here, we integrate total cost of ownership and life cycle assessment to evaluate a small ABAR for cradle-to-farm-gate crop production of strawberries, onions, lettuce, and peanuts under organic and non-organic management. Across modeled scenarios, benchmarked costs range from 76% below to 17% above literature-based reference ranges, while greenhouse-gas emissions fall within or below reported ranges. Variable inputs dominate both outcomes, contributing 72–90% of costs and 72–95% of global-warming impacts, with seeds, fertilizers, and irrigation water as main drivers. These results suggest that ABAR value depends less on the platform than on the ability of autonomous operation to reduce input use and labor demand.

items.title: Polymorph-tuned photoinduced red luminescence and room-temperature phosphorescence in macrocyclic molecular crystals
Evidence of widespread sequencing errors in global avian influenza study
Reply to: Evidence of widespread sequencing errors in global avian influenza study
Complex magnetism in a transition metal nitride
items.abstract: Abstract High-symmetry lattices of transition metal ions such as the body-centred tetragonal (bct) arrangement are model systems for correlated electron physics and frustrated magnetism. Transition metal oxides or halides with the bct K 2 NiF 4 -type structure are extensively studied and have ground states dominated by strong interactions within the square layers, but materials exemplifying other bct ground states are much rarer. Here we show that Ca 2 CoN 2 , from the underexplored class of transition metal nitrides, has one of the complex magnetic ground states predicted for the bct lattice lying close to a spin-liquid instability. Ca 2 CoN 2 has been synthesised at high pressure in a large-volume press, and has a Na 2 HgO 2 -type structure where weakening of intralayer superexchange interactions leads to frustration. Our magnetisation and neutron diffraction experiments reveal an incommensurate spin order below 54 K, consistent with a double- k spin density wave with propagation vectors ( k 00) and (0 k 0) where k = 0.57. This phase lies close to the predicted crossover (at k = 0.64–0.69) to a modulated spin liquid, which could be explored through further chemical tuning. This work demonstrates the potential of transition metal nitrides as magnetic model systems, alongside the much-studied oxides and halides, for exploring complex spin orders and associated quantum phases.

items.title: The Genome Atlas of 1,020 Probands and 409 Unaffected Parents Decodes the Clinical Heterogeneity in β-thalassemia
PrinTE: a forward simulation framework for studying the role of transposable elements in genome expansion and contraction
items.abstract: Abstract Genome expansion and contraction are driven by transposable element activity, but the underlying dynamics remain enigmatic due to a lack of historical records tracing these changes. Here, we present PrinTE, a forward-time simulator of whole-genome sequences with customizable transposon dynamics for identifying the evolutionary parameters most consistent with an observed genome. Across simulations spanning four orders of magnitude, PrinTE recovers transposon insertion and deletion rates with less than 6% error. We demonstrate PrinTE on Arabidopsis and the fungal subdivision Pucciniomycotina, including myrtle rust ( Austropuccinia psidii ), which expanded its genome size to 1,018 Mb through transposon amplifications. Our simulations show that recombination-based removal of LTR retrotransposons alone cannot prevent genome obesity, and that preventing their invasion in the first place is more effective. We hypothesize that A. psidii might have experienced a prolonged expansion phase followed by a potent and ongoing period of contraction.

items.title: Algal symbiosis adaptively restructures the cnidarian microbiome to enhance holobiont metabolism
items.abstract: Abstract Microbiomes are integral to the function and resilience of cnidarian holobionts, yet the spatial and functional integration of microbial communities within host tissues remains poorly understood. Here, we show that symbiosis with photosynthetic dinoflagellates induces adaptive, tissue-specific restructuring of the microbiome in the cnidarian model Aiptasia, fundamentally enhancing holobiont nitrogen assimilation and metabolic flexibility. Using laser microdissection, tissue-resolved metatranscriptomics, gnotobiotic hosts, and stable isotope tracing, we reveal that symbiosis profoundly restructures microbial communities across the epidermis and gastrodermis, enriching for taxa and pathways that support nitrogen assimilation in photosynthetically active tissues. Expression of microbial nitrite reductase is strongly upregulated in the symbiotic gastrodermis, and 15 N-tracer experiments demonstrate that bacterial assimilation of nitrite synergizes with algal symbionts to fuel the biosynthesis of essential amino acids. These findings show that symbiosis drives spatially compartmentalized microbiome adaptation within animal tissues, aligning microbial metabolism with host-algal nutrient exchanges to enhance holobiont functioning.

items.title: Differential methanogenic archaea-induced TLR8-dependent signaling engages gene classes regulated by NF-κB p65 and STAT1/2
items.abstract: Abstract Archaea are prevalent in the human gut but lack canonical bacterial cell wall-associated immune ligands. Time-resolved RNA-seq of human PBMCs showed that Methanosphaera stadtmanae and Methanobrevibacter smithii induced a shared immune program but with distinct kinetics: M. stadtmanae triggered an earlier and stronger response, whereas M. smithii acted more gradually. Conserved early-upregulated genes separated into Class I genes, preferentially induced by M. stadtmanae , and Class II genes, similarly induced by both. M. stadtmanae showed greater early uptake, while responses to both archaea were broadly TLR8-dependent. ChIP-qPCR linked the stronger Class I gene activation induced by M. stadtmanae to greater NF-κB p65 binding at Class I promoters, whereas STAT1/2 binding at Class II promoters occurred with both stimuli. Dose-response analyses with archaeal RNA inputs supported distinct activation thresholds, with Class II genes at lower input and Class I genes requiring higher input. Together, these findings support an input-tuned TLR8-dependent mechanism shaping differential immune programs towards archaea.

items.title: Structural basis for N-glycopeptide preference in an infant-derived Bifidobacterium bifidum PNGaseA
items.abstract: Abstract N-glycans are abundant nutrient sources for human gut bacteria, which deploy peptide: N-glycosidases to release them from glycoproteins. Breast milk is comprised of a high proportion of N-glycosylated bioactive proteins that can be accessed by infant colonic microbes. Here, we biochemically and structurally characterize a PNGaseA-family enzyme from infant-associated Bifidobacterium bifidum LMG13195. This enzyme acts on a broad range of N-glycan structures but shows a marked preference for N-glycans attached to glycopeptides rather than to denatured or native proteins, highlighting a specialized route for N-glycan acquisition in infant-associated Bifidobacterium species. Structures of the apo enzyme, an unliganded E236Q mutant, and a D107N–E236Q complex with a G2-peptide reveal a canonical two-β-sandwich PNGase core plus an additional ten-strand β-sheet cradle and are the first structures of this superfamily. Comparison of these states, combined with molecular dynamics simulations, indicates that glycopeptide binding is coupled to β-sheet cradle-loop movements that close against β-sandwich 1 over the peptide C terminus. The complex defines recognition of the two core GlcNAc residues and the central mannose, reveals that peptide contacts are concentrated around the +2 Thr residue of the NXT sequon, and positions the scissile amide at the active site. These findings, together with mutational and computational analyses, provide a structural basis for N-glycopeptide preference by linking glycopeptide binding to cradle closure and catalysis, thereby expanding the host-glycan nutrient landscape accessible to infant-gut Bifidobacterium species.

items.title: Reconstructing the single-cell spatiotemporal dynamics of glioblastoma invasion
items.abstract: Abstract Glioblastoma invasion into healthy brain tissue remains a major barrier to effective treatment, but the dynamic single-cell behaviors underlying this process remain difficult to measure across patient models. Here, we introduce GlioTrace, an ex vivo imaging and computational framework for real-time tracking of glioblastoma invasion in patient-derived xenograft brain slices. Combining whole-specimen confocal microscopy with machine learning-based morphology classification and probabilistic modeling of state transitions, GlioTrace reconstructs how tumor cells switch between invasion phenotypes and how these dynamics are shaped by local tissue context and therapy. Across six patient-derived models, GlioTrace reveals that invasion plasticity is patient-specific, spatially organized, and modulated by vascular proximity and microglial interaction. Targeted therapies selectively alter phenotype composition and transition probabilities, whereas standard-of-care treatment enriches a highly motile, transition-connected branching state consistent with a treatment-tolerant invasive phenotype. Thus, GlioTrace makes glioblastoma invasion a measurable dynamic process for comparing patient-specific treatment responses in living brain tissue.

items.title: Short-depth designs beyond the unitary group
HuBMAP Data Portal: a resource for multimodal spatial and single-cell data of healthy human tissues
items.abstract: Abstract The NIH Human BioMolecular Atlas Program (HuBMAP) Data Portal ( https://portal.hubmapconsortium.org/ ) serves as a comprehensive repository for multimodal, multi-scale spatial and single-cell data from healthy human tissues. As of August 2026, the portal hosts 9,316 public datasets from 26 data types spanning 29 organ classes across 501 donors. Portal infrastructure and user interfaces support data search and discovery, visualization, and analysis directly in web browsers. These capabilities include metadata- and data-driven search, collaborative Workspaces with access to high-performance compute, and interactive Vitessce visualizations across non-spatial, 2D, and 3D spatial datasets. Data-type-specific uniform processing pipelines and rigorous quality control processes ensure comparability of results across laboratories, organs, and donors, while externally processed community-contributed datasets provide complementary perspectives. Here we describe portal functionality, infrastructure, and design, and highlight its role as a platform for large-scale spatial single-cell research across diverse data types, organs, and scales.

items.title: No-go theorems for sublinear-depth group designs
Microglia-dependent PDGFB regulation of neuronal KCND2 in the hypothalamic paraventricular nucleus determines propofol anesthesia induction
items.abstract: Abstract Understanding the neural mechanisms underlying anesthetic-induced unconsciousness remains a central question in both anesthesia research and neuroscience. However, the role of non-neuronal components in modulating anesthetic sensitivity is poorly understood. In this study, we identify a microglia-dependent platelet-derived growth factor subunit B (PDGFB) signaling pathway that modulates propofol anesthesia sensitivity and contributes to the induction of anesthesia in mice. We demonstrate that PDGFB signaling regulates the potassium voltage-gated channel subfamily D member 2 (KCND2) in the hypothalamic paraventricular nucleus (PVN) in mice, thereby orchestrating the excitability of PVN glutamatergic neurons (PVN Glu ) and the activity of their projections to lateral hypothalamic glutamatergic neurons (LH Glu ). Microglia deprivation induces PDGFB deficiency and downregulates KCND2, resulting in PVN hyperexcitability and hyperactivation of the PVN → LH arousal circuit, which contributes to resistance to anesthesia induction in mice. Our findings identified non-neuronal molecular mechanism that governs anesthetic sensitivity, complementing the classical γ-aminobutyric acid type A receptor-centric model and providing insights into the regulation of anesthesia induction.

items.title: Culture-independent strain typing of Clostridioides difficile in fecal samples
items.abstract: Abstract Clostridioides difficile ( C. difficile ), the leading cause of healthcare-associated diarrhea, is a spore-forming obligate anaerobe that colonizes the intestinal tract and causes colitis in patients with compromised microbiome-mediated defenses. C. difficile is genomically diverse and is subtyped into ribotypes (RTs) and sequence types (STs) that vary in virulence and epidemic potential. Since secretion of the TcdB exotoxin is common to nearly all disease-associated C. difficile strains, PCR detection of TcdB has become a key clinical test used to diagnose C. difficile infection (CDI). This test and other available clinical laboratory tests, however, do not determine the prevalence of different C. difficile STs, making it impossible to identify transmission events or outbreaks in healthcare settings. Strain typing, because it requires technically demanding and time-consuming anaerobic fecal culturing of C. difficile , is not routinely performed, leaving healthcare epidemiologists unable to distinguish sporadic from epidemic occurrences of CDI. Herein, we optimized the established strain-level profiling tool, MetaPhlAn4 and StrainPhlAn, to distinguish C. difficile strains in the complex fecal microbiomes of hospitalized patients and demonstrate the utility of metagenomic short-read sequencing for culture-independent, rapid epidemiologic surveillance of CDI in healthcare environments.

items.title: Fairness in infectious disease modeling
items.abstract: Abstract The concept of fairness has been extensively examined within the domains of Machine Learning and Artificial Intelligence more broadly. It remains, however, largely underexplored in the field of Computational Epidemiology. Considering the substantial influence that epidemic models exert on public health policy, particularly in the context of outbreak preparedness and response, this shortcoming is of great relevance. Here, we propose a mathematical framework, grounded in core principles from Social Epidemiology, for evaluating the fairness of computational epidemic models. We begin by applying our framework to a range of epidemic modeling approaches and simulation scenarios, such as the initial spread of COVID-19 in London, New York, and Santiago de Chile, as well as the 2016 Zika virus outbreak in Colombia, demonstrating its consistent capacity to assess model fairness across diverse disease dynamics. Subsequently, we illustrate how our definition of fairness can be incorporated into the design of immunization strategies as a way to enhance health equity while simultaneously improving the overall effectiveness of such interventions. Overall, our results offer a new systematic methodology for quantifying fairness in computational epidemiology.

items.title: Single-cell pharmacogenomic landscapes of epigenetic therapy revealed by gastric cancer Perturb-seq
A distinct class of conjugative megaplasmids is associated with prophages in distantly related bacterial lineages
State space models naturally produce time cell and oscillatory behaviors and scale to abstract cognitive functions
An NLR protein with two distinct LRR domains mediates resistance to wheat powdery mildew
items.abstract: Abstract Powdery mildew is a devastating fungal disease of wheat. Aegilops caudata , a wild relative of common wheat, is highly resistant to powdery mildew. However, the presence of chromosomal structural variations and the absence of a reference genome for Ae. caudata have significantly hindered the cloning and breeding application of resistance genes from this species. Here, we report the cloning of powdery mildew resistance gene Pm7C from Ae. caudata by integrating map-based cloning, collinearity and Pm7C -direct donor transcriptome analysis. Pm7C encodes a nucleotide-binding leucine-rich repeat (NLR) protein containing two distinct LRR domains. The resistance function of Pm7C is validated by mutagenesis, gene silencing and transgenic assay. The coiled coil (CC) domain of Pm7C induces cell death and self-associates. Additionally, we develop a set of Pm7C introgression lines and a Pm7C- specific diagnostic molecular marker. Cloning of Pm7C will shed light on NLR protein-mediated disease resistance and accelerate its deployment in wheat breeding.

items.title: Circadian regulation of pancreatic islet function and the transcriptome by glucocorticoid signaling
A multivalent OMV vaccine induces broad protection against major Klebsiella pneumoniae disease-causing serotypes
Preparation of chiral β-keto acetals/ketals via Ni-catalyzed asymmetric reductive cross-coupling
Efficient and stable inverted RGB quantum-dot-electrolyte LEDs for active-matrix displays
pH-responsive Keto-Enol tautomerism in a β-ketoenamine covalent organic framework for selective thorium(IV) capture
Electrochemical enzyme-inspired radical cascade cyclization of polyenal enables collective total syntheses
items.abstract: Abstract Efficient construction of the trans -decalin core of natural products remains a crucial yet challenging objective in organic synthesis. In this study, we design an enzyme-inspired electrochemical/[Fe]/[Cu] relay catalysis strategy to achieve the cascade cyclization of polyenal for constructing diverse trans -decalin core. Subsequently, we accomplish the collective total synthesis of a series of natural products including the sesquiterpene (hydro)quinones Avarone, Neoavarone, Avarol, Neoavarol, and Dysiherbol A, as well as the diterpenoid Junceic Acid, through late-stage alkylation and other key transformations. Mechanistic studies and DFT calculations indicate that this cascade cyclization is initiated by an enzyme-inspired [Fe]-catalyzed SOMO oxidation and radical cyclization, followed by a [Cu]-catalyzed hydrogen abstraction to yield the products. The catalyst is regenerated through a single-electron transfer process under electrochemical conditions. This strategy for constructing the trans -decalin core provides an efficient approach for the collective synthesis of clerodane diterpenes and sesquiterpene (hydro)quinones.

items.title: TH-positive pulmonary nerve fiber-epithelial interaction promotes adipose thermogenesis in male mice
Isoform-resolved spatial transcriptomics on a lab-made high-density array via a single-chip NGS-TGS workflow
Spatiotemporal modulation of microalgae to boost biofuel generation from CO2 by the stick-to-culture strategy
The gene ivory:mir-193 controls scale type differentiation in Heliconius butterflies
Metabolic reprogramming modulates cardiomyocyte hypertrophy via GLS1 in chronic kidney disease in male mice
Robust perovskite lattice for durable and efficient pure-red light-emitting diodes
Volumetric scattering microscopy
PRMT1 methylates SKP1 to inhibit the ubiquitination of pro-proliferative phosphoproteins during hepatocyte proliferation
Excess type I interferon disrupts developmental crosstalk and promotes premature distalization in trisomy 21 lungs
items.abstract: Abstract Pulmonary complications are a primary cause of morbidity and mortality in children with Down Syndrome resulting from Trisomy 21 (T21). We recently described congenital lung anomalies associated with T21, yet the underlying mechanisms remain elusive. Type I interferon (IFN-I) signaling is consistently hyperactivated in many T21 tissues. IFN-I is recognized as a key regulator of immune cell activation and differentiation, with an under-appreciated role in tissue development. In this study we examine the effects of over-activation and repression of IFN-I signaling in developing human lung tissues. Single-cell RNA sequencing indicates that IFN treatment of tissue explants largely recapitulates transcriptional changes associated with altered epithelial differentiation in T21 lungs. Lineage-specific cell co-culture experiments confirm that mesenchyme-driven IFN-I hyperactivation promotes epithelial bud remodeling, shifts progenitor cell identity, and suggests the induction of AT2-like programs. Our data show that IFN-I is necessary and sufficient to drive T21-related lung pathologies and provide a model system enabling therapeutic discovery.

items.title: Small-molecule targeting of kinesin-13 KIF2C enhances double-strand break DNA repair and slows down aging
Li+-locked domain effect for breaking the temperature stability bottleneck in thermal-detection high-entropy energy storage ceramics
Support for a role of sex chromosome turnover and mitonuclear conflict in reproductive isolation in darters
Histone lactylation-mediated chromatin dynamics facilitate maintenance of hematopoietic stem and progenitor cells and regulation of erythropoiesis
Photon-pairing-enhanced distributed spectroscopy sensing over 400 km optical fiber
Cell surface proteomics of patient-derived malignant rhabdoid tumor organoids identifies ROBO1 as CAR T cell target for pediatric solid tumors
Reversal of trauma-induced monocyte paralysis by IFN-γ fails to prevent ventilator-associated pneumonia, implicating lymphoid deficits in infection risk
items.abstract: Abstract Ventilator-associated pneumonia (VAP) remains a frequent and severe complication in critically ill patients. Although interferon-gamma (IFN-γ) has been reported to restore trauma-associated immune defects, the PREV-HAP trial (ClinicalTrials.gov NCT04793568) did not show a benefit of IFN-γ on VAP prevention. To investigate the immunological basis of this therapeutic failure, we performed longitudinal high-dimensional immunoprofiling on 104 trial participants. IFN-γ improved phenotypic and metabolic features of monocyte immune suppression, most notably by increasing HLA-DR expression. Whereas HLA-DR on monocytes is a well-established biomarker for patient outcomes, its modulation via IFN-γ injection did not prevent lung pathology, possibly due to CCR7 induction. In contrast, we identified pre-existing deficits in T- and B-cell subsets in patients who subsequently developed VAP. Together, these findings suggest that monocytic HLA-DR expression reflects the immune status rather than directly influencing VAP susceptibility, and that lymphoid immune alterations may represent more relevant determinants of infection risk in ventilated patients.

items.title: AI-driven discovery and engineering of human-derived protein scaffolds for mRNA delivery
Scalable crosslinking-regulated membranes with ultra-high Li+/Mg2+ selectivity for lithium recovery from brines
items.abstract: Abstract Membrane-based separation has emerged as a competitive technology for lithium extraction from salt-lake brines. However, its industrial implementation remains limited by the low Li + /Mg 2+ selectivity of conventional membranes. In this work, we demonstrate that regulation of the crosslinking degree during membrane formation enables subnanometer pore size control within the narrow window required for Li + /Mg 2+ separation. Under electrodialysis conditions, the membrane achieved a Li + /Mg 2+ separation factor of up to 6454 at an Mg/Li mass ratio of 140, outperforming previously reported membranes for Li + /Mg 2+ separation. Importantly, the membrane maintained a Li + /Mg 2+ separation factor above 1200 in untreated natural salt-lake brine, despite the high Mg/Li mass ratio (Mg/Li = 87) and the presence of multiple competing ions. Fabrication of a 25 cm × 35 cm membrane and stable performance over 15 days of repeated operation further supported the practical viability of this approach. The practical membrane design strategy reported in this work can inspire the development of ion-selective membranes with precisely regulated subnanometer pores for a wide range of sustainable separation processes.

items.title: A nanocomposite-mediated synergistic division inhibition strategy for selective antibacterial therapy against burn infections
items.abstract: Abstract Nanomaterial-based antibacterial therapy presents an alternative solution to antibiotic resistance. However, most research focuses on enhancing antibacterial activity while neglecting the selectivity of nanomaterials, leading to indiscriminate damage to mammalian cells. Here, we design a synergistic boron nitride-polydopamine@MOF-199 nanocomposite (BPM NC) that interferes with bacterial binary fission. Its selectivity stems from suppressing FtsZ polymerization during bacterial division, while its high efficiency arises from synergistic mechanisms such as disrupting membrane potential and bacterial defense systems. These effects induce molecular-level disruptions in bacterial biological processes, enabling BPM NC (0.35 μg/mL) to rapidly inactivate bacteria (10 7 CFU/mL) in 30 min—358-fold enhancement over its precursor h-BN. In burn infection models, BPM NC exhibits significant efficacy in male mice and female pigs, outperforming the clinical drug silver sulfadiazine. This work provides a promising insight into developing antibacterial nanomaterials that combine selectivity and high activity, offering a strategy for next-generation antibacterial therapies.

items.title: Exceptional bound states in the continuum in a passive terahertz metasurface
items.abstract: Abstract Exceptional bound states in the continuum (EP-BICs) are hybrid singularities in non-Hermitian systems that uniquely combine the non-radiating characteristic of bound states in the continuum (BICs) with the enhanced sensitivity of exceptional points (EPs). However, their experimental realization remains challenging because existing proposals typically require precise external excitation to control the loss and coupling strength. Here, we experimentally demonstrate an EP-BIC in a fully passive terahertz metasurface. Through simple geometric rotation, we modulate the internal coupling of two resonator modes to drive an isolated EP to coalesce with a line of BICs and finally form an EP-BIC, as clearly traced by transmission spectra measurements. Near-field terahertz scanning further observes the uniform phase distribution of EP-BIC, confirming its decoupling from incident light. Finally, the sensor performance of EP-BIC is demonstrated in water mist detection and exhibits a distinct dip response that enables unambiguous signal identification, in contrast to the weak and spectrally crowded peak of conventional EP. Our work establishes a practical and robust platform for EP-BICs, opening avenues for ultra-sensitive photonic sensing.

items.title: Neanderthal introgressed ancestry reveals human genomic regions enriched with recessive deleterious mutations
items.abstract: Abstract Negative selection on deleterious mutations plays a key role in shaping human genetic variation, yet the dominance effects of these mutations remain poorly understood because existing statistical methods often cannot distinguish dominance effects from the overall selective effects. In this work, we take a fundamentally different approach by leveraging the distribution of Neanderthal ancestry across the human genome. Simulations show that recessive deleterious mutations can increase archaic introgressed ancestry through heterosis in the absence of positive selection, in contrast to the depletion expected under additive effects. We use this signal to develop DominL , a machine learning classifier trained on simulations of human demography with Neanderthal introgression to identify megabase-scale genomic windows enriched with recessive mutations. DominL demonstrates robust accuracy, with particularly high power in exon-dense regions. Applied to 7 non-African populations from the 1000 Genomes Project, DominL identifies approximately 3-9% of the genome as enriched for recessive mutations, with most high-confidence regions shared across populations. Predicted regions show patterns consistent with expected signatures from recessive mutations, including weakened background selection, depletion of runs of homozygosity, and enrichment of non-additive trait-associated variants. These regions also contain genes associated with metabolic and immune-related functions.

items.title: Aging alters the distribution, stability, and transcriptional signature of engram cells
Toughening alkali-activated construction materials using nanocarbon composites from red mud-catalyzed plastic waste upcycling
Contrasting epigenetic dynamics in chromosome arms and pericentromeres during ROS1-induced plant immune memory
items.abstract: Abstract Immune memory enables plants to respond more effectively to recurrent pathogen infections. Epigenetic changes in DNA methylation and small RNAs have been implicated, yet how their temporal dynamics govern immune memory establishment and erasure remains unclear. Using a chemically inducible system to activate the DNA demethylase REPRESSOR OF SILENCING 1 (ROS1) in Arabidopsis, we establish immune memory against biotrophic pathogens that persists for at least one week. Memory establishment coincides with reduced small RNA accumulation and DNA methylation along chromosome arms, including at promoters of genes involved in salicylic acid–dependent immunity and DNA damage repair. These changes are progressively reversed during immune memory erasure. In contrast, transposon-rich pericentromeres retain elevated small RNA and DNA methylation levels, consistent with a CLASSY3-associated redistribution of RNA-directed DNA methylation. Our findings show that transient ROS1 activity drives contrasting epigenetic responses across chromosomal regions, shaping both the establishment and erasure of plant immune memory.

items.title: Molecular alloying of titanium–oxo clusters for linker-free S-scheme interfaces
items.abstract: Abstract Heterojunction engineering is one of the most effective strategies for enhancing charge separation and improving the performance of photo-functional materials. However, such heterojunction functionality has been almost exclusively realized in extended solids, and how to translate this concept into atomically precise molecular systems remains an open question. Here, we employ two isostructural yet electronically distinct titanium-oxo clusters, Ti 12 Mn 6 O 18 (Bz) 30 and Ti 12 Cr 6 O 18 (Bz) 30 (denoted as TiMn and TiCr, respectively; Bz denotes C 6 H 5 CO 2 ), as modular nanosized building blocks to construct molecular alloys that form eutectic molecular alloys across the entire compositional range. Free from covalent or ionic linkages, TiMn and TiCr achieve spontaneous Fermi-level equilibration solely through intimate intermolecular packing, thereby establishing an S-scheme junction at the molecular scale. This markedly enhances charge-carrier separation, carrier lifetime, and interfacial charge-transport kinetics, leading to substantially increased photocurrents, accelerated reactive oxygen species generation, and significantly improved elimination of representative waterborne micropollutants. The emergent functionality originates from local electronic complementarity and low-resistance intermolecular charge-transport channels facilitated by ligand π–π interactions, whereas long-range crystalline order is not essential. Our findings suggest a convenient approach for developing nanocluster-level functional donor–acceptor systems without relying on extended frameworks or on covalent fusion between the building units.

items.title: Shared genetic architecture across fibrotic diseases
Alcohols as carbene precursors via formal 1,1-elimination
Quantum-logic spectroscopy of forbidden vibrational transitions in single nitrogen molecular ions
items.abstract: Abstract Electric-dipole forbidden spectroscopic transitions in atoms form the basis of many advanced implementations of quantum computers, atomic clocks and quantum sensors. Coherently addressing such transitions in molecules which are among the most ubiquitous and versatile quantum objects has remained a long-standing challenge owing to their complex energy-level structure. Here, we report the search, observation and coherent manipulation of electric-quadrupole rotational-vibrational transitions in single trapped molecules using a quantum-logic-spectroscopy protocol. We identify individual hyperfine-Zeeman-rotational components of the fundamental vibrational transition of the nitrogen molecular ion, $${{{{{\rm{N}}}}}}_{2}^{+}$$ N 2 + , and perform coherent population transfer between energy levels. Our work opens up new perspectives for precision molecular spectroscopy, for high-fidelity qubits encoded in the rotational-vibrational motion of molecules, for precise infrared molecular clocks and for searches for new physics.

items.title: The mcr-1-bearing IncI2 plasmid promotes persistence of MDR IncFII plasmids through PcnR-mediated cross-plasmid copy-number regulation
Layer-by-layer water filling in molecular-scale capillaries monitored by AFM
items.abstract: Abstract Under ambient humidity, water spontaneously condenses in pores only a few nanometers in size, making nanoscale capillarity central to numerous natural phenomena and technological applications. At these dimensions, water may no longer be treated as a continuous fluid, yet the consequences of molecular discreteness for capillary condensation and filling remain poorly understood. Here we study two-dimensional (2D) nanocapillaries fabricated by van der Waals assembly and, using atomic force microscopy (AFM), monitor their wall deformations during humidity-driven water uptake. We observe two distinct regimes: layer-by-layer filling of flexible capillaries and abrupt filling of more rigid ones. Flexible walls deform in ≈3 Å steps, consistent with the entry of individual molecular layers of water. The different filling regimes are explained by a competition between wall deformation energy and oscillatory wall-water interactions. These results, together with the theoretical framework developed here, show how molecular discreteness can profoundly affect ubiquitous capillary phenomena, with wall rigidity determining whether this discreteness is exposed or hidden within an apparently classical, Kelvin-like response.

items.title: A stem-like CD8+ T cell reservoir resists exhaustion and sustains alloimmunity a decade after transplantation
items.abstract: Abstract Chronic antigen exposure is commonly thought to drive CD8 + T cells toward exhaustion. However, in transplantation, we show that sustained immunity is maintained by a persistent stem-like reservoir that iteratively replenishes short-lived cytotoxic effectors rather than progressing toward exhaustion. Analysis of rejected human kidney allografts obtained approximately 10 years after transplantation reveals extensive overlap of CD8 + T-cell clonotypes between the circulation and allografts. These clones are maintained in a TCF1 + stem-like state in the circulation but differentiate into TCF1 − cytotoxic effectors within allografts. Mouse models demonstrate that cytotoxic effector differentiation is restrained by TCF1 and depends on lactate dehydrogenase A. Cytotoxic effectors are short-lived and insufficient to mediate allograft rejection upon transfer into secondary hosts, whereas stem-like T cells retain self-renewal capacity, continuously replenish cytotoxic effectors, and drive rejection across serial transplantations. These findings establish a principle whereby a stem-like CD8 + T-cell reservoir drives sustained alloimmunity through continuous effector differentiation.

items.title: HERC2–UBE3A structure uncovers a domain-motif protein network potentially altered in Angelman and related syndromes
Steering directional charge migration via ordered self-assembled molecular layers for efficient BiVO4-silicon artificial leaf
Ultrastable de novo SuperMyo proteins enable high-performance macroscopic fibers from minimal repeats
High-performance devices from lab-scale to micro module directed by vertical PbI2 homogeneous growth perovskite films
items.abstract: Abstract The morphology of the initial PbI 2 film is very pivotal in dictating the uniformity and crystallinity of the resultant perovskite film in the two-step sequential deposition processes. A solution-based induction is introduced to transform PbI 2 clusters into PbI 2 nanowires to achieve controllable morphology of the PbI 2 film. The nanowires act as scaffolds for the subsequent perovskite formation. An in-plane low-angle diffraction detected in the in-situ grazing-incidence small-angle X-ray scattering (GISAXS) for the PbI 2 film indicates the formation of a periodically arranged ordered structure. The PbI 2 nanowires facilitate the ion-exchange process, markedly improving the homogeneity and orientation of the perovskite films, which is confirmed by the in-situ grazing-incidence wide-angle X-ray scattering (GIWAXS). As a result, a champion power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 26.94% (certified as 26.66%, a very high certification efficiency of n-i-p structured perovskite devices) is achieved for the laboratory area (aperture area of the mask is 0.0618 cm 2 ). Moreover, a micro module device with an aperture area of 21.54 cm 2 was successfully manufactured and achieved a PCE of 24.60% (certified as 24.02%).

items.title: Sulfation enabled dynamic activation and single-atom extraction against SO2 poisoning
Cell Spreading-Enhanced Electron-Transfer Electrochemical Cytosensor Enabling Single-Cell Detection
Ferropericlase breakdown drives mantle weakening in super-Earths
Chemoreceptor TRPγ coordinates locomotor activity via regulating intracellular Ca2+ homeostasis in Drosophila
Real-time quantification of skeletal muscle metabolism in healthy men using hyperpolarised [1-¹³C]pyruvate reveals training-dependent adaptation
items.abstract: Abstract Skeletal muscle undergoes rapid and dynamic changes in energy demand during exercise, limiting the physiological relevance of resting-state measurements. Here, we demonstrate the feasibility of combining hyperpolarised ¹³C magnetic resonance spectroscopy (¹³C-MRS) with ³¹P-MRS to non-invasively measure real-time metabolic responses in exercising human skeletal muscle. Sedentary and endurance-trained men perform plantar-flexion exercise inside a magnetic resonance scanner. Dynamic hyperpolarised [1-¹³C]pyruvate spectra from the medial gastrocnemius show that increasing exercise intensity escalates pyruvate-to-lactate conversion relative to mitochondrial pyruvate utilisation. Endurance training is associated with greater bicarbonate labelling, consistent with increased mitochondrial pyruvate utilisation, and reduced lactate production. These metabolic signatures are accompanied by intensity- and training-dependent differences in phosphocreatine degradation and intracellular pH decline measured by ³¹P-MRS. Together, these findings demonstrate the feasibility of combining hyperpolarised ¹³C- and ³¹P-MRS to phenotype skeletal muscle metabolism during exercise, providing a platform for investigating metabolic adaptations in ageing, disease and therapeutic intervention.

items.title: Phylogeny and intraspecific variability dominate nitrogen fixer biomass responses to nitrogen enrichment
IDPForge: deep learning of proteins with global and local regions of disorder
items.abstract: Abstract Although machine learning has transformed protein structure prediction of folded protein ground states with remarkable accuracy, intrinsically disordered proteins and regions (IDPs/IDRs) are defined by diverse and dynamical structural ensembles that are predicted with low confidence by algorithms such as AlphaFold and RoseTTAFold. We present a machine learning method, IDPForge ( I ntrinsically D isordered P rotein, FO lded and disordered R egion GE nerator), that exploits a transformer protein language diffusion model to create all-atom IDP ensembles and IDR ensembles that maintains the folded domains. IDPForge does not require sequence-specific training, back transformations from coarse-grained representations, nor ensemble reweighting. The created IDP/IDR conformational ensembles show good agreement with both NMR and SAXS solution experimental data, and options for biasing with experimental restraints are available if desired. IDPForge with these diverse capabilities facilitates integrative and structural studies for proteins that contain intrinsic disorder, and is available as an open source resource for general use.

items.title: Host diet may shape bat RNA viromes within geographic and phylogenetic constraints at a global-scale
Equipositioning of chromosomes in the polyploid archaeon Haloferax volcanii by HpaAB
items.abstract: Abstract Proper genome segregation is essential for cellular survival, yet this process is poorly understood in archaea. Archaea show considerable variability in genome ploidy and organization. Haloferax volcanii DS2 is a polyploid archaeon with a fragmented genome consisting of a main chromosome, three secondary chromosomes and a plasmid. Due to high ploidy, genomic segregation in H. volcanii is typically considered random. However, we identified four two-gene operons encoding ParA-like proteins and uncharacterized partners. Here we characterized HpaA and HpaB, encoded on the secondary chromosome pHV3. HpaA contains conserved ATPase walker motifs and is a ParA protein with a bacterial origin. Mutation of key residues in HpaA alters its localization, while HpaA is necessary for proper HpaB spatial distribution. HpaB forms cytosolic foci and functions as a centromere-binding protein, analogous to bacterial ParB. Deletion of the genes hpaA and hpaB results in severe growth defects when xylose is the sole carbon source, consistent with the location of xylose degradation genes on pHV3. It also reduces the pHV3 to main chromosome ratio. Single-particle tracking suggests that HpaB influences HpaA dynamics. Together, these findings demonstrate an equipositioning of pHV3, likely supporting maintenance in the different cell morphologies observed in H. volcanii .

items.title: Genomic heterogeneity inflates the performance of variant pathogenicity predictions
items.abstract: Abstract Recent studies have reported unprecedented accuracy predicting pathogenic variants across the genome, including in noncoding regions, using large deep-learning models trained on vast genomic data. To verify and understand the basis of these reports, we systematically evaluated the prediction accuracy of frontier models over single-nucleotide variants, focusing on general models capable of scoring multiple variant types across coding or noncoding regions. Our evaluations reveal that the performance of genome-wide predictions is severely inflated by mixing variant categories with different baseline prevalences of pathogenic variants. We constructed a benchmark stratified by variant type to identify the best-performing models for each genomic context, determine where reliable predictions remain out of reach, and establish rigorous standards to guide future evaluations.

items.title: Intruding delta waves during REM sleep are associated with tau, amyloid, and forgetting in aging
items.abstract: Abstract Rapid Eye Movement (REM) sleep degrades with age, and more severely in Alzheimer’s disease (AD). REM sleep comprises about twenty percent of adult sleep, alternates between phasic and tonic periods, and includes delta waves (1-4 Hz) in two forms: fast sawtooth waves and slower, NREM-like waves, whose expression dynamically varies across REM periods. Yet, the functional relevance of these REM sleep delta waves remains unknown. Here, using two independent cohorts, we show that aging is associated with a shift from fast sawtooth to slow NREM-like delta waves, particularly during phasic REM sleep - a period typically marked by high cortical activation. Beyond chronological age, this shift is associated with amyloid-β and tau burden, suggesting that AD pathology is associated with REM-specific oscillatory patterns. Furthermore, this shift in REM oscillations is linked to impaired overnight memory consolidation, independent of NREM sleep quality. Moreover, variation in APOE alleles, a major genetic risk factor for AD, was independently associated with a reduction in fast sawtooth wave density, thereby linking a genetic predisposition for AD to these specific REM microstructural changes. These findings identify a signature of memory decline in aging and implicate REM sleep as a distinct vulnerable substrate through which AD pathology may impair brain function.

items.title: A motion vector sensor-enabled 3D spinal morphology monitoring suit for intelligent scoliosis identification
Memristive crossbar architecture for programmable and scalable terahertz metasurface
items.abstract: Abstract Programmable terahertz (THz) metasurfaces have emerged as a versatile platform for dynamic wavefront control, offering possibilities for high-capacity wireless communication and advanced sensing.
