Realizing full wavefront control requires scaling to large-format arrays with pixel-level reconfigurability, but this is fundamentally limited by inter-pixel crosstalk and the increasing complexity of electrical interconnections. Here, we present a scalable, pixel-level programmable metasurface addressing architecture inspired by the crossbar architecture of memristor arrays, and implement it in the THz regime. By integrating VO 2 -based snapback selectors, this design effectively suppresses sneak path currents, allowing low-crosstalk addressing of each pixel. A modular row-column tiling scheme facilitates scaling to large arrays while preserving per-pixel programmability. We further demonstrate independent two-dimensional phase modulation and non-volatile THz beam steering. This work provides a theoretical framework and design paradigm for a versatile and scalable photonic platform spanning the THz to optical regimes.

items.title: Sequence Display generates large-scale sequence–activity datasets for reprogramming SlugCas9 toward difficult-to-access PAMs
Ancestry-specific and multi-ancestry genome-wide association studies of restless legs syndrome
items.abstract: Abstract Restless legs syndrome is a neurological disorder that disrupts sleep and quality of life, but its genetics have mostly been studied in individuals of European ancestry. Here, we perform GWAS of restless legs syndrome using data from individuals of African, Latin American, and European ancestry, followed by a multi-ancestry meta-analysis. We leverage biobank-based cohorts that established RLS diagnosis using validated clinical criteria, allowing for precise phenotypic characterization. We perform ancestry-specific association studies and post-GWAS analyses to prioritize candidate genes. Our analyses reveal ancestry differences in the genetics of restless legs syndrome. At the MEIS1 and BTBD9 loci, lead variants showed lower allele frequencies and did not reach genome-wide significance in African ancestry. We identify ancestry-specific and shared risk loci, including novel associations near GYPC/TEX51 and PRIMA1 in African ancestry and ISX in Latin American ancestry. The European meta-analysis identifies 11 additional loci and replicates 50 previously reported associations. The combined multi-ancestry analysis finds ten new loci. This multi-ancestry study broadens the genetic understanding of restless legs syndrome, and the absence or reduced frequency of key European restless legs syndrome alleles in individuals of African ancestry provides insights into known epidemiological differences.

items.title: Performance of artificial intelligence-assisted cytology and high-risk human papillomavirus testing for cervical cancer screening
Interfacial reinforcement relieves mechanical mismatch for stable perovskite photovoltaics
Ligand hardness as a key feature differentiating base- versus noble-metal mechanisms of nickel-catalyzed Suzuki-Miyaura cross-couplings
items.abstract: Abstract Nickel-catalyzed cross-coupling reactions that engage alkyl electrophiles provide potential routes for synthesis of molecules with high F sp3 . However, development of these reactions remains a challenge since the impact of ligand identity on competing mechanistic pathways is not yet well understood. To address this knowledge gap, we establish structure-reactivity trends across >550 Suzuki-Miyaura cross-coupling reactions with known mechanistic pathways. We evaluate reaction outcome by ligand features including heteroatom identity, hybridization, bite angle, geometry, and buried volume. The most important determinant of reactivity is heteroatom identity: nitrogen-based ligands support open-shell reactions while phosphorus-based ligands support closed-shell reactions. Here we report that experimental and calculated reduction potentials and charge density analysis correlate with catalytic activity and propose a rationale for these observations based on hard-soft acid-base theory.

items.title: Genomic surveillance meets clinical practice: rule-based individualized treatment prediction for gonorrhoea using SensiTyper
items.abstract: Abstract Extensively drug-resistant (XDR) Neisseria gonorrhoeae strains threaten the current empirical gonorrhoea treatment. We designed and analytically validated SensiTyper, a rule-based framework that predicts antimicrobial susceptibility from whole-genome sequencing data and generates susceptibility-guided individualized treatment recommendations. SensiTyper was applied to 13,701 gonococcal genomes from 68 countries in 1928-2024, including cultured isolates and clinical molecular samples, and benchmarked predictions against previous genomic and phenotypic data. Susceptibility predictions for ceftriaxone, ciprofloxacin, spectinomycin, and zoliflodacin had 98.9-100% sensitivity and specificity. Azithromycin susceptibility predictions had 92.5% sensitivity and 97.1% specificity, and gepotidacin susceptibility prediction 100% sensitivity, but 0% specificity, illustrating that low-level phenotypic gepotidacin resistance is not caused by the only known resistance determinants (GyrA A92T plus ParC D86N). The SensiTreat module integrates antimicrobial susceptibility profiles into sequential treatment logic, providing susceptibility-guided individualized treatment recommendations while also enabling alternative stewardship strategies prioritizing, e.g., ciprofloxacin. SensiTyper flags XDR isolates for expert follow-up, test-of-cure and comprehensive contact tracing. In conclusion, SensiTyper is a robust and adaptable approach for gonococcal antimicrobial susceptibility prediction, individualized gonorrhoea treatment and antimicrobial stewardship.

items.title: Process-dependent shifts in conspecific negative density dependence during boreal forest succession
items.abstract: Abstract Conspecific negative density dependence (CNDD)—the stronger negative effects of conspecific than heterospecific neighbours on plant demographic performance—is a key process proposed to stabilize forest diversity, yet how it changes during succession remains poorly understood. Using a 25-year spatially explicit dataset from 148 post-fire plots in boreal forests, we show that species richness increases with stand age and that CNDD varies in process- and abundance-dependent ways across recruitment, survival, and growth. Plot-level CNDD shows no significant change with stand age in recruitment or survival, but mean relative effects are generally stronger for recruitment, and CNDD shifts from destabilizing to stabilizing for growth as stands mature. Species-level CNDD is strongly associated with species abundance, with rare species consistently experiencing stronger CNDD in recruitment and growth, whereas common species tend toward neutral or destabilizing effects. For survival, by contrast, CNDD is stronger in common than in rare species. These abundance-related differences remain broadly consistent across stand development, except in recruitment, where CNDD intensifies in rare species but remains consistently weak or near-neutral in common species. This shifting balance of density-dependent pressures highlights succession-driven trade-offs as central to species coexistence and increases in diversity in disturbance-driven forests.

items.title: Npl4 decodes polyubiquitin length and undergoes D1-gated exchange on p97/VCP
Synthetic tools to redirect the ubiquitin E3 ligase activity of a plant-specific N-recognin
items.abstract: Abstract The Arg/N-degron pathway regulates important agronomic traits. In plants, the PROTEOLYSIS 1 (PRT1) protein binds to aromatic amino-terminal residues and recruits ubiquitin (Ub) conjugating enzymes to ubiquitinate substrate proteins. Here, we demonstrate that PRT1 recruits the UBC35-UEV1A complex via RING1 of PRT1. This stimulates UBC35 to produce K63-linked Ub chains. To afford chemical control over Ub signalling, we construct a synthetic substrate of PRT1 with an N-terminal calmodulin-binding peptide (CBP). The addition of the CBP sequence to the substrate creates an off switch for PRT1-dependent ubiquitination that is regulated by calcium and calmodulin. Finally, we produce a set of nanobodies that are recognised by PRT1 and induce the ubiquitination of a reporter protein. Altogether, we introduce and biochemically validate several tools to both redirect and chemically control the Arg/N-degron pathway.

items.title: Lamprey and hagfish VLRB signalling complex VLRB-GPIbβ-GPIX originates from lymphocyte-specific duplication of a platelet adhesion module
Minimally invasive topological light manipulation with lensless fiber endomicroscope
Structural basis for curvature generation and functional specialization in spirochete flagella
items.abstract: Abstract Spirochetes are spiral-shaped bacteria whose curved periplasmic flagella drive corkscrew-like motility through viscous environments. Despite their clinical importance, molecular mechanisms underlying flagellar assembly remain poorly understood. Here, we combine cryo–EM of flagellar filaments natively isolated from oral pathogen Treponema denticola , with proteomics and comparative genomics to characterise the molecular organisation. We resolve two filament types to sub-3 Å resolution: thin FlaB3-only cores, and thick filaments with a FlaB1/2 core asymmetrically decorated by a sheath comprising FlaA1/2/3 and lattice proteins FlaL1/2. We show sheath asymmetry imposes differential axial compaction on the FlaB1/2 core, generating convex and concave filament faces and establishing curvature. FlaB sequence and glycosylation differences at sheath–core interfaces correlate with selective incorporation into distinct filament types, supporting a mechanism for regulated filament architecture. Phylogenetic analysis reveals FlaL conservation across spirochete lineages, suggesting modular sheath lattices provide an adaptable mechanism for tuning flagellar mechanics across diverse pathogenic lifestyles.

items.title: Recruitment of TEX15 by HUSH2 drives repression of multicopy gene families in fertility regulation
A multimeric pore complex in the poxvirus core revealed by integrative structural analysis
items.abstract: Abstract It has long been known that poxviruses transcribe more than a hundred early mRNAs within their viral core, yet how these transcripts exit the core remains unknown. Here, we combine cryo-electron tomography with deep-learning-based particle picking, subtomogram averaging, cross-linking mass spectrometry, and AlphaFold3 modeling to resolve the molecular architecture of a long-sought pore within the poxvirus core. The pore is formed by a heteromeric assembly of the viral proteins E8, E6, and L3, which together create a hollow hexameric tube spanning both the core wall and the surface-exposed palisade layer. Within the pore channel, we observe a rod-like density consistent with the viral RNA helicase I8, which may contribute to the release of the newly synthesized viral mRNAs from the core. We further observe a state of the pore lacking the outer and basal rings under transcription conditions. Together, our findings identify the structure and dynamics of a candidate mRNA-release pore within the surface layer of a double-stranded DNA virus and suggest that it may form part of the poxvirus transcription machinery.

items.title: CO2 hydrogenation across the pressure gap over Ag/ZnO:Al2O3 catalysts
items.abstract: Abstract The hydrogenation of carbon dioxide to value-added chemicals is a major challenge. Metal-oxide interfaces and surface structures play fundamental roles and govern the selectivity of this reaction; thus, catalysts must be investigated under relevant reaction conditions to identify structure-activity relationships and engineer more efficient materials. This work aims to elucidate mechanisms of carbon dioxide hydrogenation to methanol and side products by using operando characterization techniques within a pressure range of 1 mbar up to 15 bar. Bifunctional Ag/ZnO and Ag/ZnO:Al 2 O 3 catalysts are studied using multiple spectroscopic techniques combined with online product analysis. During catalyst activation in hydrogen, several restructuring processes of the catalyst occur at different pressures. Under carbon dioxide hydrogenation reaction conditions carbonate, formate and CH x surface intermediates show strong pressure-dependent abundances. Combining thermodynamics with in situ and operando investigations of pressure-dependent structures and intermediates allows assessing carbon dioxide hydrogenation through the pressure gap.

Publisher Correction: Regional heterogeneity in phenotypic and genetic associations between bone and brain in humans
Precise modular engineering of neutral organometallic rectangles from binuclear palladacycles via hierarchical assembly strategy
items.abstract: Abstract Metallosupramolecular assembly provides a powerful strategy for the precise construction of well-defined architectures with diverse topologies and functionalities. However, the construction of neutral organometallic architectures supported by robust metal-carbon bonds remains underdeveloped, largely because kinetic persistence limits the reversible structural correction required for conventional self-assembly. Herein, we employ binuclear palladacycles as intrinsically neutral and geometrically preorganized building blocks and develop a hierarchical assembly strategy that temporally separates geometric programming, scaffold editing, and topology locking. Through a polymerization-cleavage-assembly process, cyclopalladated polymers are converted into discrete binuclear precursors while retaining their programmed geometrical information. Subsequent trans-effect-directed N -heterocyclic carbene ligation affords a series of size-tunable, kinetically robust, and neutral organometallic rectangles. The resulting architectures are fully characterized by spectroscopic methods and single crystal X-ray diffraction analyses. Moreover, single crystal X-ray diffraction identifies guest-mediated breathing-like geometric deformations in the solid state, driven by exo-wall π-π stacking and charge-transfer interactions with both electron-rich and electron-deficient planar guests. This work establishes a hierarchical construction principle for accessing discrete neutral organometallic architectures by separating geometric programming from the final locking of the topology through strong bond formation, while demonstrating that local geometric adaptation can occur without disrupting the framework connectivity established by Pd-C bonds.

Video-rate volumetric chemical imaging via mid-infrared photothermal optical diffraction tomography
items.abstract: Abstract Label-free vibrational microscopy provides chemically specific access to cellular structures, yet quantitative volumetric imaging of intracellular dynamics remains challenging on subsecond timescales. Here, we demonstrate video-rate mid-infrared photothermal optical diffraction tomography (MIP-ODT) by combining high photothermal sensitivity with rapid angular scanning. The system achieves 19.2 volumes per second, nearly 400 times faster than previous MIP tomography implementations, with a signal-to-noise ratio exceeding 70 and no temporal averaging. We track lipid droplets in living cells and quantify anomalous diffusion from three-dimensional trajectories, revealing heterogeneous intracellular transport behaviors obscured in two-dimensional measurements. Rapid mid-infrared wavenumber sweeping further enables broadband multi-wavenumber volumetric chemical imaging across a 300 cm⁻¹ spectral window within 1 s. These results establish MIP-ODT as a platform for high-speed, label-free volumetric chemical imaging of single cells and quantitative investigation of dynamic intracellular organization.

items.title: Canopy nutrient balance predicts autumn senescence across U.S. forests
Enzymes can activate and mobilize dense biomolecular condensates across scales
Sequential protonation and deprotonation reactions govern alternating access in a Major Facilitator Superfamily proton/multidrug antiporter
items.abstract: Abstract Drug/proton antiporters of the Major Facilitator Superfamily are key drivers of antimicrobial resistance. However, the molecular mechanisms underlying proton-coupled drug efflux are inherently complex and remain unresolved. Here, we dissect the timing and mechanism of proton coupling in the multidrug transporter LmrP, a prototypical exporter of clinically relevant antibiotics and toxins. By directly tracking chamber opening in the native plasma membrane, we capture functionally relevant conformational transitions within a lipid environment and map them onto the catalytic carboxylates that govern transport. Our results suggest that earlier DEER distance measurements in detergent solution captured a restricted subset of conformational states, which our pH 8.0 data extend and place into a broader framework. Complementary pH 5.0 measurements reveal additional mechanistic features and, together, these datasets define the transport cycle in a membrane-embedded context. Supported by molecular dynamics simulations, the results reveal a coordinated, transport cycle-dependent mechanism in which paired catalytic carboxylates act sequentially in substrate binding, proton relay, gate control, and transporter resetting.

items.title: Spatial patterning of hierarchical lamellar-cellular structured hydrogels for programmable deformation-coupled information encryption
Genome-scale eCLIP mapping of SARS-CoV-2 RNA interactions with NSP8, NSP12, and N reveals regulatory sites
items.abstract: Abstract The global impact of the COVID-19 pandemic highlights the need for a deeper understanding of SARS-CoV-2 replication. Although the essential roles of the RNA-dependent RNA polymerase (NSP12), primase (NSP8), and nucleocapsid (N) proteins are established, their contact points with the full-length viral RNA genome during active infection require further characterization. Here, we used enhanced crosslinking and immunoprecipitation (eCLIP) to map direct interactions of NSP8, NSP12, and N across the SARS-CoV-2 genome during live virus infection at early and late stages of replication. We mapped NSP8 and NSP12 binding to the 5′ and 3′ ends of positive- and negative-sense RNA, consistent with their roles in viral replication, transcription, and translation. We also observed an NSP12 binding site within the conserved Y1 domain of NSP3 that modulates RNA and protein abundance. In addition, N binds the 5′ untranslated region (UTR), supporting a role in translational regulation early in infection, and associates with the frameshift element, where it modulates ribosomal frameshifting. Together, these findings map SARS-CoV-2 RNA–protein interactions across the viral genome and delineate specific regulatory regions for potential antiviral intervention.

Hydrogen-bond-mediated quasi-two-dimensional covalent organic frameworks for ultrahigh gold extraction
A combinatorial genetics approach reveals limits to redundancy within Plasmodium falciparum invasion ligand families
items.abstract: Abstract To maintain infection in the human bloodstream, Plasmodium falciparum parasites undergo repeated cycles of invasion of and multiplication inside red blood cells (RBCs). Two protein families, the Erythrocyte binding-like (EBA) and Reticulocyte binding-like (Rh) proteins, are known to play a key role in invasion, mediating early stages of attachment of the P. falciparum merozoite to the host RBC. There is a degree of redundancy within these families, such that disrupting the function of individual EBA/Rh proteins in vitro is not sufficient to prevent invasion. By employing a novel approach to disrupt multiple EBA and Rh genes in combination, we systematically assess functional interdependency across these families for the first time. This analysis, and further characterisation of mutant parasites, reveals that disruption of some pairs of EBA/Rh ligands significantly impacts P. falciparum invasion, whereas others do not. Disruption of PfEBA175 in combination with either PfRh2b or PfRh4 significantly reduces parasite multiplication in vitro, indicating that the remaining EBA/Rh proteins cannot fully compensate for the absence of these three key invasion ligands. PfEBA175, PfRh2b and PfRh4 may therefore represent a critical nexus of the parasite invasion machinery, and combinatorial approaches that target these specific ligands could be a beneficial therapeutic approach.

items.title: Retarding efficiency loss upon scaling in perovskite photovoltaics as fill factor becomes the bottleneck
items.abstract: Abstract Perovskite solar cells approach crystalline-silicon efficiencies at small areas, yet substantial performance losses during scale-up hinder their translation into practical modules. Here we quantify the contributions of device-performance parameters to efficiency loss during scale-up across diverse perovskite technologies, identifying fill factor ( $${FF}$$ F F ) as a major contributor and target for mitigating this loss. Further analysis resolves the FF deficit into voltage-, diode-non-ideality- and transport-associated contributions. Cryo-controlled processing provides an experimental route to preserve $${FF}$$ F F by regulating intermediate-phase evolution during crystallization. The resulting $${FF}$$ F F -preservation advantage arises predominantly from reduced diode non-ideality, with the other contributions being smaller. This advantage increases across device scales. A mini-module (19.48 cm 2 aperture) achieves a record certified steady-state efficiency of 23.9% with an $${FF}$$ F F of 83.3%, the highest reported for perovskite modules. The same $${FF}$$ F F limitation governs operational performance decay, linking efficiency retention during scale-up with long-term stability. Together, these results establish $${FF}$$ F F preservation and the factors governing it as central to mitigating performance loss during scale-up and operation.

items.title: LytU is a bridge-link isopeptidase that contributes to vancomycin resistance in Staphylococcus aureus
items.abstract: Abstract Emergence of antimicrobial resistance is a pressing global issue. Although myriads of mechanisms for survival against antimicrobial pressure have surfaced, one key strategy is the structural modification of peptidoglycan, the main defense line in Gram-positive bacteria e.g., notorious pathogen Staphylococcus aureus . Here we show that the recently identified peptidoglycan hydrolase (PGH) LytU is an unusual catalyst in the lysostaphin (M23B) family of zinc-endopeptidases that hydrolyze the glycyl-glycine peptide bond in S. aureus . Unlike any other PGH recognized thus far, LytU hydrolyzes the isopeptide bond between the lysine ε amino group and pentaglycine, thus functioning as a bridge-link hydrolase. We discovered that LytM and LytU are functionally non-redundant, and they contribute to the cell wall remodeling at different stages of PG maturation. Additionally, we demonstrate that LytU particularly targets the PG precursor, pGly-Lipid II, and its overexpression leads to growth inhibition and a less densely cross-linked cell wall, which increases susceptibility to lysostaphin. Interestingly, LytU expression enhances resistance to the glycopeptide vancomycin, the drug of last resort against S. aureus .

items.title: Exaiptasia diaphana core microbiome members are lost under climate change conditions despite host thermal tolerance
items.abstract: Abstract Acute and chronic exposure to elevated temperatures associated with Global Climate Change (GCC) threatens the structure and function of host-associated microbiomes, yet predicting microbial responses to heat stress remains challenging. We exposed two lines of the sea anemone, Exaiptasia diaphana , to acute and chronic thermal stress to quantify the impacts on cnidarian physiology and microbiome composition. Acute exposure caused rapid algal bleaching that was paired with pronounced shifts in bacteriome structure in both lines within 14 days of thermal exposure. Chronic exposure significantly affected the population structure, photo-physiology and bacteriome composition in only one host line, suggesting acclimation capacity depends on host-algal genetic backgrounds. Using 16S rRNA amplicon sequencing of 493 individuals sampled across 180 days, we found that sampling date explained nine-fold more variation in the microbiome composition than temperature exposure. Despite this temporal variation, we identified 16 indicator taxa that consistently changed in relative abundance under thermal stress. These taxa became central hubs in microbial association networks with increasing levels of thermal stress, suggesting they played key roles in bacteriome reorganization. As many of these taxa were present in other cnidarians, including reef-building corals, they may represent targets for conservation strategies that aim to enhance resilience on reefs.

items.title: Secondary organic aerosol formation from sequential oxidation of toluene and cresols
Increasing prevalence and expanding diversity of tet(X4)-carrying Salmonella in China
Resolving the Kay–Dunn limit and the speed–endurance dilemma in ferroelectric Hf0.5Zr0.5O2 for DRAM-class sub-volt capacitors
items.abstract: Abstract Ferroelectric hafnium zirconium oxide can increase charge density in scaled capacitors, but its high coercive field limits the low-voltage, high endurance switching required for dynamic random-access memory and embedded ferroelectric memories. Here we show that plasma-engineered (111)-textured TiN electrodes with N-rich, oxidation-resistant surfaces suppress interfacial oxidation and enable robust switching in 5 nm Hf 0.5 Zr 0.5 O 2 capacitors. The devices exhibit saturated hysteresis at 0.6 V, with 2 P r = 31.5 μC cm −2 and E c = 0.62 MV cm −1 , and no hard electrical breakdown through 10 12 bipolar cycles. Their nucleation-limited switching kinetics extrapolate to sub-nanosecond polarisation reversal at DRAM-relevant capacitor areas. At 1.1 V, circuit simulations of a common plate 1T–1 C cell yield short- and long-term stand-by sensing margins of 482 and 201 mV under a 20 fF bit line load. Electrode texture and interface engineering therefore enable low-voltage, high speed switching without compromising endurance, mitigating the practical Kay–Dunn scaling penalty and the speed–endurance dilemma.

Ketene as a gas phase intermediate in acetic acid ketonization on TiO2
items.abstract: Abstract Reactive gas-phase intermediates are often underappreciated in heterogeneous catalysis, despite their potential to control key catalytic steps. Here, we provide direct experimental evidence that ketene can act as an intermediate in acetic acid ketonization, a mechanism that has long been debated. Using faceted TiO 2 (101) nanoparticles assembled into layers of controlled thickness, we show that ketene, formed from surface acetate, migrates through interparticle voids via desorption-readsorption events before reacting with surface acetate to yield acetone. Surface science and reactor studies reveal a direct correlation between ketene and acetone production and the depth to which the particle layers are saturated. Ab initio calculations support ketene’s reactivity via low-barrier coupling pathways that converge on a common β-ketoacid intermediate. Here, we show that ketene can act as a mobile gas-phase intermediate and underscore the broader importance of spatially decoupled elementary steps in determining reactivity and selectivity in catalytic systems.

items.title: Author Correction: Transcription regulation of African swine fever virus: dual role of M1249L
Author Correction: Applying Artificial Intelligence and machine learning in precision nutrition
Author Correction: Paired NLRs originated from Triticum dicoccoides coordinately confer resistance to powdery mildew in wheat
Widespread selection of antibiotic resistance within hospital sewers
items.abstract: Abstract Environmental microbiomes are sources of diverse antibiotic resistance determinants that can be mobilized and transferred to human pathogens under a selection pressure from antibiotics. Hospital sewers contain more antibiotics than most environments and are thus increasingly recognised as potential arenas for resistance evolution. However, it is unknown if resistance selection occurs there and what the drivers are. Here we show selection of antibiotic-resistant bacteria within Swedish hospital sewers. Evidence include; consistent selection of multiple resistances in Escherichia coli exposed to filtered wastewater from ten hospitals, but not to corresponding municipal wastewaters; in-situ enrichment of resistant over sensitive E. coli from wastewater to sewer biofilms at hospitals, but not at municipal sites; and higher resistance in bacteria collected from hospital sewers than from municipal sites as assessed by culturing and metagenomics. Evidence for drivers includes complete rescue of sensitive E. coli by addition of resistance genes to fluoroquinolones and β-lactams, and cellular effects typical for β-lactams. Measured concentrations by liquid-chromatography-tandem-mass-spectrometry compared to selective thresholds identify ciprofloxacin and cefotaxime as principal selective agents. Antibiotic concentrations and use data allow extrapolation of risks beyond Sweden. Given the absence of detectable selection at municipal sites, mitigations of risks in hospital sewers should be prioritized.

items.title: Antimicrobial peptides derived from Nemuri induce ribosomal condensation to inhibit translation
items.abstract: Abstract Antibiotic resistance is a global health threat requiring antimicrobials with alternative modes of action. Growing evidence indicates that bacteria organize key intracellular processes through biomolecular condensates and other forms of spatial organization, yet whether such spatial organization can be exploited as an antimicrobial target remains unclear. Here, we identify intrinsically disordered antimicrobial peptides, generated from the Drosophila sleep-inducing protein Nemuri, that inhibit bacterial growth by targeting ribosomal organization. Mechanistically, these peptides enter bacterial cells without overt membrane disruption and accumulate in ribosome-rich regions, where they bind broadly to RNA and ribosomal surfaces through multivalent interactions. This engagement remodels ribosome-rich regions into condensates with reduced ribosomal mobility, thereby suppressing global protein synthesis and distinguishing these peptides from canonical site-specific ribosome-targeting antibiotics. Furthermore, Nemuri-derived peptides exhibit broad-spectrum antimicrobial activity, including activity against drug-resistant pathogens, with low cytotoxicity toward Drosophila and mammalian cells. Together, our findings identify the organization and material dynamics of bacterial ribosomes as a biophysical vulnerability that can be exploited by antimicrobial peptides, revealing how a naturally evolved metazoan host-defense system turns intracellular organization itself into an antibacterial target.

items.title: Deuteration of arenes in D2O exclusively driven by single-atom Pt sites under visible light
Aberrant thymic architecture and enhanced interferon signaling in Down syndrome
Framework desymmetrization enables partial pore space partition in metal-organic frameworks
items.abstract: Abstract The pore-space-partition (PSP) has been recognized as a powerful strategy for boosting the uptake capacity of small gas molecules and has seen wide application in reticular chemistry. However, the most successful PSP platform—the partitioned- acs (pacs) net—has followed only one pattern since its inception over a decade ago: one partition agent per partition site, with a general formula of [M 3 O( L1 ) 3 ]( L2 ). This fully partitioned architecture occupies all metal sites, eliminating open metal sites (OMSs) and compromising selectivity. Herein, we introduce a partial PSP concept accessed through a framework desymmetrization strategy. By replacing traditional high-symmetry D 2h ligands with lower-symmetry C 2h ligands (e.g., fumaric acid), we introduce structural distortions into the acs network, breaking the uniformity of partition sites and allowing partition agents to occupy only a fraction of available positions. This provides access to a PSP mechanism, namely part-pacs (partially partitioned- acs ), with a general formula of [M 3 O( L1 ) 3 ]( L2 ) 1/3 . The part-pacs structures retain high acetylene capacity while exhibiting significantly enhanced selectivity compared to their fully partitioned analogues. Specifically, part-pacs-fum-tpa achieves C 2 H 2 /CO 2 separation productivity nearly twice that of its full-pacs counterpart (1.92 mol kg −1 vs 0.98 mol kg −1 ).

Cryo-EM reveals major proteolysis independent substrate rearrangements in a complement C5 convertase surrogate complex(es)
The accuracy-safety trade-off of large reasoning models in clinical diagnostics
Probing spin order via magnon transmission across quantum Hall ferromagnet heterojunctions
CryoET imaging reveals that mitotic spindles are locally organized by microtubule density and Eg5 activity
items.abstract: Abstract When eukaryotic cells divide, a mitotic spindle, composed of microtubule filaments interacting with molecular motors, self-assembles and is responsible for aligning and segregating chromosomes to the opposite daughter cells. Recent structural studies revealed that spindles are composed of short microtubules that do not span the full pole-to-chromosome distance. It remains unclear how these short, disconnected microtubules collectively assemble a bipolar spindle. Using cryo-electron tomography to map microtubule polarity in human spindles, we find that microtubules organize with consistent 8 nm wall-to-wall spacing. Spacing scales inversely with local microtubule density, consistent with organization by density-driven steric interactions, analogous to liquid crystal ordering. We find that the Eg5 motor establishes local antiparallel overlap independently of spindle bipolarity, while a balance of Eg5 and dynein regulates microtubule density to maintain spindle architecture. Together, these findings reveal the mesoscale principles by which cells build complex, self-healing cellular architectures from nanoscale building blocks.

items.title: Viral tRNA-like structure hijacks host ribosomes for poly(A)-independent translation
A training-free, domain-extensible LLM-based approach for automated extraction of standardized preparation procedures
Proximity labeling of the Listeria monocytogenes surface reveals pathogen control of a host deubiquitinase
Stabilization of insulin receptor mRNA by Star-PAP in metabolic homeostasis
Glacial CO2 drawdown by plankton metabolic balance
Impression-R1 for radiological impression generation with multicenter benchmarking and prospective evaluations
Serine supplementation reinvigorates anti-tumor immunity by counteracting tumor cell SLC1A4-induced T cell starvation
CADS: a comprehensive anatomical dataset and segmentation for whole-body anatomy in computed tomography
items.abstract: Abstract Volumetric computed tomography (CT) segmentation supports quantitative image analysis, but most AI-based methods remain organ-specific, with fragmented models, inconsistent label definitions, and heterogeneous training and evaluation protocols. Here we present CADS, a unified data–model framework for scalable and generalizable whole-body CT segmentation. We construct a SNOMED-CT-referenced anatomical label space harmonizing heterogeneous cohorts from over 100 imaging centers, yielding complete annotations of 167 structures across 22,022 CT volumes and markedly expanding anatomical coverage and scale beyond existing resources. To complete labels on sparsely annotated CTs, we combine self-training with shape-informed quality control based on neural implicit functions, curating high-quality pseudo-labels. Trained on this resource, CADS shows robust whole-body segmentation across distribution shifts and improved performance relative to state-of-the-art approaches across 18 public datasets. We further validate it in an independent, expert-reviewed real-world oncology cohort of 2864 CTs. The curated dataset, pretrained models, and user-friendly software together provide an accessible, reproducible foundation for large-scale anatomical segmentation and computational anatomy research.

items.title: Lipidated macrocyclic peptide S-880008 inhibits SARS-CoV-2 fusion by suppressing protomer dissociation at conserved spike sites
Long-read sequencing reveals telomere inheritance patterns from human trios
Health risks of hot and cold temperatures in people with pre-existing conditions and social disadvantage
items.abstract: Abstract Evidence on the health impacts of ambient temperature relies largely on population-level analyses, providing limited insight into risks among clinically and socially vulnerable individuals, including those with pre-existing disease or socioeconomic disadvantage. Here we show, in 275,763 Finnish adults and an independent UK cohort of 9,681 adults, that health risks during extreme temperatures differed substantially across vulnerability groups. We compared mortality and emergency hospital visits during the hottest and coldest 2.5% of seven-day periods with those during non-extreme temperature periods. Excess heat- and cold-related mortality was more than tenfold higher among individuals with both clinical and social vulnerability than among those with neither or only one vulnerability in both the Finnish and UK cohorts ( P = 0.03 and P = 0.003, respectively). By contrast, excess temperature-related mortality differed little between individuals with neither vulnerability and those with only one vulnerability. Our modelling suggests that future warming could increase temperature-attributable mortality across the population, particularly among individuals with both clinical and social vulnerability. These findings identify individuals with both clinical and social vulnerability as a priority group for climate adaptation strategies.

items.title: Bright and pure single-photon source in silicon by nanoscale positioning of a color center in a microcavity
items.abstract: Abstract Silicon is a leading material platform for photonic quantum technologies. However, a key challenge remains the efficient integration of high-performance single-photon sources in the near infrared. Here we present an all-silicon single-photon source at 1217 nm wavelength, fabricated by nanoscale positioning of a single W center in a circular Bragg grating cavity. The operation wavelength corresponds to the W center’s zero-phonon line that is enhanced by the cavity. Under above-gap continuous-wave excitation, we obtain a saturated photon count rate of 1.29 × 10 6 counts/s with pronounced photon antibunching ( g (2) (0) = 0.06 ± 0.02). Triggered operation under weak pulsed excitation produces single photons with 93 ± 2% purity. At saturation, we reveal purity degradation due to repumping processes, that could be mitigated using selective excitation schemes in the future. These results represent a major step towards on-demand sources of indistinguishable single photons in silicon photonics.

items.title: Genetic integration reveals causal effects of chromatin accessibility on nucleosome positioning across diverse muscle cells
CPRISP: an interpretable deep learning framework predicting circRNA-RBP interactions and guiding therapeutic discovery in neurodegeneration
items.abstract: Abstract Circular RNAs regulate gene expression through interactions with ribonucleic acid binding proteins, but their binding sites remain difficult to predict across proteins and cellular contexts. Existing methods often focus on transcript features while making limited use of protein-specific information and structural context. Here, we show that an integrated deep learning framework combining circular transcript sequence composition, physicochemical properties, secondary structure, pretrained representations and protein features improves interaction-site prediction across 37 benchmark datasets and generalizes across cell lines; model interpretation recovers conserved single-stranded sequence patterns, while analyses of proteins linked to Alzheimer disease, Parkinson disease and amyotrophic lateral sclerosis identify recurrent pathways involving nucleocytoplasmic transport, lysosomal signaling and guanosine triphosphatase activity and prioritize compounds for experimental follow-up, supporting accurate and interpretable mapping of circular ribonucleic acid protein interactions without implying therapeutic efficacy.

items.title: Evolutionary oxidation of proteins in Earth’s history
items.abstract: Abstract Evidence for Earth’s oxygenation during the Great Oxidation Event (GOE) and Neoproterozoic Oxidation Event (NOE) comes primarily from the geological record. We report rising oxidation state of carbon (Zc) in proteins over billion-year timescales, a consistent trend recovered from diverse genomic datasets. Combining statistical and thermodynamic modeling, we link this trend to environmental drivers including Earth’s progressive oxygenation and secular cooling. The oxidation trend appears in the amino acid composition of modern genomes from methanogens and sulfur-cycling organisms, phylostratigraphic gene age groups in eukaryotes, and reconstructed ancestral sequences for Rubisco, nitrogenase, thioredoxin, and 3-isopropylmalate dehydrogenase (IPMDH). Major Zc steps broadly overlap the GOE but do not exactly coincide with it; uncertainties in phylogenetic age and limited spatial associations complicate direct comparison with geochemical proxies. Gene age groups in unicellular, but not multicellular, eukaryotes show a second rise of protein Zc around the NOE. These widespread genomic signatures of protein oxidation are consistent with a thermodynamic hypothesis in which energy minimization directs protein sequence evolution across metabolic functions.

items.title: Updated global estimates of carbon burial in seagrass sediments
Coevolutionary constraints of Zika virus nonstructural protein 5 replication and interferon antagonism activities
items.abstract: Abstract The flavivirus nonstructural protein 5 performs multiple functions during infection, including RNA replication and type I interferon signaling antagonism. Although flavivirus NS5 proteins inhibit IFN signaling through distinct mechanisms, which suggests evolutionary flexibility, the evolutionary constraints for these activities to coexist within a single protein remain to be determined. Here, we map the Zika virus NS5 STAT2 antagonism determinants and compare them with replication constraints defined by deep mutational scanning. Antagonism and replication determinants extensively overlap, and no single amino acid substitution eliminates antagonism without impairing replication. Resolving these fitness landscapes in parallel identifies specific combinations of partially functional substitutions that retain replication capacity while markedly reducing antagonism. These viruses are profoundly attenuated in human STAT2 knock-in mice. Our results uncover a fundamental evolutionary constraint linking replication and immune evasion activities in NS5, highlight that STAT2 antagonism is essential for ZIKV pathogenesis and provide new avenues for attenuated ZIKV vaccines.

items.title: The integrated environmental zoning-based regulation further enhances sustainable development in China
Nonlinear responses induced by inhomogeneous edge states in a centrosymmetric topological insulator
Detector-mediated cross-spectral prediction with a gate-tunable van der Waals tunneling photodetector
items.abstract: Abstract Cross-spectral prediction infers information in one spectral band from observations acquired in another. This task is ill-posed because multiple target-band signals can be compatible with a single source observation. Image-space supervision alone does not test consistency with a measured detector response. Here, we incorporate the calibrated response manifold of a gate-tunable PdSe 2 /h-BN/WSe 2 photodetector as a differentiable detector-response layer. Parameterized by wavelength, optical power, source-drain bias and gate voltage, this layer constrains the magnitude and polarity of the predicted detector response while preserving image fidelity. In visible-to-infrared cross-spectral prediction, the framework achieves a peak signal-to-noise ratio of 26.58 dB and a structural similarity index of 0.89. It also reduces detector-space error relative to architecture-only and response-corrupted controls. Post-inference measurements further evaluate 64-mask response consistency after 1310 nm optical re-encoding. These results establish detector-mediated cross-spectral prediction as a framework that combines image reconstruction with measured response-space consistency under the tested conditions.

items.title: Lipid stoichiometry and biomarkers reflect microbial acclimation and nutrient stress across the Atlantic Ocean
Thrombin reshapes α-synuclein biochemical properties by N-terminal truncation
items.abstract: Abstract Proteolytic processing of α-Synuclein (Syn) contributes to the molecular diversity and toxicity of its aggregates in Parkinson’s disease, yet the proteases responsible for disease-relevant truncations remain incompletely defined. Here, we show that thrombin, a serine protease associated with inflammatory conditions, selectively cleaves Syn at Lys6–Gly7, generating a 7–140 fragment despite the presence of multiple potential cleavage sites. Cleavage is modulated by ionic strength and the conformational ensemble of Syn, with more extended states being preferentially cleaved. The resulting 7–140 fragment adopts a more compact conformational ensemble, delays the formation of aggregation-prone species, produces fibrils with altered morphology and shows reduced membrane-induced α-helix formation. Although 7–140 aggregates are modestly less toxic, the truncation also impairs physiological functions of the protein. These findings describe a mechanism by which an inflammation-associated protease, thrombin, may contribute to Parkinson’s disease by selectively modifying Syn structure, aggregation and function.

items.title: Integrated on-chip quantum light sources on a van der Waals platform
Biomimetic hydrophobic gating in MXene polypyrrole–based artificial Ion channels for efficient perchlorate sensing
items.abstract: Abstract Ion selective electrodes represent a promising approach for ion detection based on potentiometric sensing principle. However, their practical application is often hampered by insufficient selectivity, primarily caused by interference from structurally similar ions. Herein, inspired by biological potassium ion channels, we demonstrate an efficient perchlorate ion selective electrode via the self–assembly of pyrrole–functionalized MXene nanosheets and methylated quaternary ammonium compounds. The resulting composite sensor significantly outperforms commercial ion selective electrodes with a > 10 4 –fold lower detection limit (10 –9.7 M), 18–fold higher selectivity ( K ij of 130.4), and a maximum sensitivity up to 59.6 mV/dec for perchlorate. Synchrotron X–ray scattering and mechanistic studies attribute this superior performance to a hydrophobic gating mechanism arising from dehydration effects and transport resistance within confined channels, which effectively lowers the energy barrier for perchlorate transport by 12.13 kcal/mol compared to that of sulfate. Furthermore, the sensor was optimized via substituent engineering for broad-spectrum anion detection and integrated into a portable platform for continuous on–site monitoring, achieving accuracy comparable to ion chromatography in real–world scenarios.

items.title: Concentration quenching resistant violet-blue TADF OLEDs via indirect conformal distributions tuning in solid-state
items.abstract: Abstract Controlling conformation distributions is the key to manipulate material properties of multi-conformal molecules. Distinct from previous strategy with direct change or impact on the flexible groups, we tune the conformation distribution through changing peripheral groups to influence their intermolecular interactions. Two blue violet TADF emitters, namely tert -butyl substituted 5-(2,12-di-tert-butyl-5,9-dioxa-13b-boranaphtho[3,2,1-de]anthracen-7-yl)−10,10-diphenyl-5,10-dihydrodibenzo[b,e][1,4]azagermine (TDBA-PAG) and cumenyl substituted 5-(2,12-bis(2-phenylpropan-2-yl)−5,9-dioxa-13b-boranaphtho[3,2,1-de]anthracen-7-yl)−10,10-diphenyl-5,10-dihydrodibenzo[b,e][1,4]azagermine (TPDBA-PAG) were designed and synthesized. With the same germanium-integrated donor, the two compounds show similar emission properties in solution with calculated conformation dominantly of their quasi-axial (QA) forms (> 97%). However, TPDBA-PAG presents a lower QA ratio compared with TDBA-PAG, which endows the former with more pronounced TADF emission, higher emission efficiency and reduced concentration quenching phenomena in solid state. As a result, TPDBA-PAG performed as one of the best non-doped and doped violet-blue emitters and successfully sensitized MesB-DIDOBNA-N to achieve record high EQE max of 24.7% at 406 nm, making significant progress in NUV OLEDs.

items.title: Computational modeling and preclinical evaluation support targeting somatic instability for Huntington’s disease treatment
A human erythropoietin-albumin fusion protein tailored for enhanced plasma half-life and delivery across mucosal surfaces
items.abstract: Abstract Erythropoietin (EPO) products stimulate production of erythrocytes in patients with anemia. The drugs are delivered intravenously or subcutaneously up to several times per week due to short plasma half-life. Improving the pharmacokinetic properties of EPO will allow less frequent administration, and thus impact therapeutic utility and patient compliance. In this study, we took advantage of an albumin variant (QMP) engineered for improved engagement of FcRn, a key regulator of the plasma half-life of albumin. After genetic coupling of EPO to QMP, the fusion protein shows favorable neonatal Fc receptor (FcRn) binding, and 5.2-fold prolonged plasma half-life in human FcRn expressing mice upon intravenous administration, when comparing with EPO fused to WT albumin, with a similar half-life obtained following subcutaneous administration. Importantly, both fusions bind the EPO receptor with binding kinetics equal to that of the product darbepoetin alfa. After intravenous administration, mice receiving darbepoetin alfa experiences a faster drop in EPO levels compared to those given EPO-QMP, and moreover, we measure a prolonged increase in erythrocytes with EPO-QMP. Furthermore, intranasal administration results in 5-fold higher circulating amounts of EPO-QMP and a prolonged increase in erythrocytes compared to darbepoetin alfa. Thus, long-acting EPO-QMP could be an attractive design to explore for both invasive and non-invasive delivery to patients with anemia.

items.title: Statistical inference of keystone taxa reshaping the assembly rules of forest root microbiomes
items.abstract: Abstract Root-associated fungi and bacteria play pivotal roles in terrestrial ecosystem processes. However, identifying keystone taxa driving below-ground microbial assembly remains a major challenge. Here, we present a statistical framework for identifying microbes that reorganize microbiome assembly. Using 1,270 root samples collected from a cool-temperate forest in Japan, we reconstruct assembly landscapes describing the probabilistic structure of community states. We then find that several endophytic fungi (e.g., Phialocephala and Oidiodendron ) are strongly associated with the reorganization of assembly landscape topography along abundance gradients, coinciding with shifts in mycorrhizal symbiosis. Independent datasets from Europe confirm that the highlighted genera are significantly associated with changes in mycorrhizal colonization patterns. Prokaryotic communities exhibit transitions among states characterized by core taxa, Pseudomonadota, or Actinomycetota, strongly associated with abundance gradients of Candidatus Udaeobacter and several endophytic fungi. These findings provide a scalable framework for prioritizing candidate keystone taxa and linking microbiome assembly to ecosystem-scale processes.

items.title: Strand- and replication timing-dependent functions of DNA polymerase η in human DNA replication
Construction of planar-chiral macrocyclic phenanthridinones and their analogues through palladium/norbornene catalysis
Orbital engineering of asymmetric Cu sites in MOFs for fenton reaction towards atomic surface manufacturing
Oncogenic modulation of MAPK signaling in leukemia via SPNS2-driven sphingolipid metabolism and membrane nanodomains remodeling
items.abstract: Abstract Lipid metabolism rewiring is an essential determinant of cancer progression, yet the key metabolic checkpoints which govern this process remain poorly defined. Using functional genomics in a mouse model of acute myeloid leukemia (AML), we identify the sphingosine-1-phosphate transporter SPNS2 as a critical sphingolipid checkpoint protein which modulates leukemia progression. SPNS2 expression is regulated by MYC and progressively declines during AML differentiation, highlighting its tumor-suppressive role in a subset of Core Binding Factor AMLs. By integrating steady-state and serine isotope-tracing lipidomics, RNA sequencing, flow cytometry, and high-resolution microscopy, with gain- and loss-of-function approaches, we show that SPNS2 modulation rewires sphingolipid metabolism by modifying sphingomyelin abundance. This remodeling alters membrane nanodomain organization, active RAS localization, and MAPK signaling. Exogenous reintroduction of SPNS2 decreases sphingomyelin levels, disrupts nanodomain organization, and limits leukemic progression in various AML mouse models. We further reveal in a cohort of patients with AML that low SPNS2 expression is associated with increased sensitivity to MAPK pathway inhibition, and demonstrate functionally in vivo that SPNS2 silencing sensitizes AML cells to MEK1/2 inhibition. Collectively, our data reveal a mechanism by which sphingolipid transport dynamics intersect with oncogenic signaling to control cancer progression.

items.title: Genetic mechanisms underlying the associations between brain structure and mental health
Supervising the search process produces reliable and generalizable information-seeking agents
items.abstract: Abstract Large language models (LLMs) are transforming web search by shifting from document ranking to synthesizing answers, and are increasingly deployed as autonomous agentic search systems that iteratively interact with external knowledge sources. Despite this progress, building effective search agents remains challenging because high-quality intermediate search steps are difficult to generate. Previous approaches have primarily relied on outcome supervision, rewarding agents only for producing correct final answers. This often leads to reward hacking and excessive dependence on parametric memory, limiting generalization to out-of-domain tasks. To address these limitations, we introduce RAG-Gym, a framework that shifts supervision from final answers to the search process itself. With RAG-Gym, we systematically investigate architecture design, parameter optimization, and action evaluation, identifying reasoning reflection as a critical capability for search agents. Building on this insight, we propose Re 2 Search++, a process-supervised agent that achieves substantial improvements on multi-hop information-seeking benchmarks, especially in out-of-domain settings. Performance gains are driven primarily by higher-quality search queries rather than answer optimization alone, and the learned search critics transfer across models, including proprietary LLMs. These findings show that supervising the search process produces more reliable and generalizable information-seeking agents.

items.title: Early-life bovine respiratory virome analysis reveals phage-driven adaptation and cross-host evolutionary signatures
items.abstract: Abstract Past outbreaks of zoonotic viral infections highlight the importance of understanding respiratory virome ecology. As major food-producing animals with frequent human contact, cattle represent a critical host at the human-animal interface; however, the early-life establishment of their respiratory virome and its evolutionary connections to viruses from other hosts remain underexplored. Here, we longitudinally profile the upper respiratory tract (URT) virome of beef calves from birth to weaning using an optimized viral enrichment procedure and metagenomic workflow. Viral communities exhibited increased richness and turnover, reflecting ecological structuring during early life. Temperate phages dominate the URT phage community and share virulence- and mobility-associated genes with bacterial hosts, likely contributing to host adaptation and colonization persistence. Vertebrate-associated viruses emerge after the first week of life. Targeted reassembly from bovine URT viromes recovers near-complete betacoronavirus-like (CoV-D180) and adenovirus-like (AdV-D56) genomes positioned phylogenetically between bovine and human viral lineages. Competitive mapping of bovine-derived CoV-D180 and AdV-D56 to human respiratory metatranscriptomic datasets reveals genome-specific, regionally structured coverage patterns distinct from reference viruses, supporting shared sequence features in conserved genomic regions across host-associated viral lineages. Collectively, these findings reveal early-life assembly dynamics of the bovine respiratory virome and highlight cross-host signatures in a One Health framework.

items.title: Author Correction: Generation and characterization of neutralizing antibodies against M1R and B6R proteins of monkeypox virus
Facet engineering enables efficient H2O2 piezo-synthesis and self-activation for decentralized water purification
Sex-based differences in clinical outcomes of enfortumab vedotin and NECTIN-4 expression in urothelial cancer
items.abstract: Abstract Sex-based differences in outcomes are well documented across tumor types and treatment modalities; however, it remains unclear whether these disparities extend to antibody-drug conjugates (ADCs). We report a retrospective, international real-world analysis of metastatic urothelial carcinoma (mUC) patients treated with Enfortumab Vedotin (EV), a NECTIN-4 ADC. Male patients demonstrate significantly longer median overall survival and time on treatment compared to female patients. Analysis of NECTIN-4 expression in urothelial cancer samples from the TCGA database reveals significantly higher expression in male patients’ tumors. This difference remains significant after adjusting for molecular subtype and is further modulated by smoking status and associates with estrogen pathway activity. These findings suggest that sex-related differences in target expression and hormonal signaling correlate with clinical outcomes of EV in mUC. Prospective studies should incorporate sex as a biological variable in ADC research to optimize treatment strategies for both male and female patients.

items.title: Antibiotic contamination stimulates microbial methylmercury synthesis in rice paddies
items.abstract: Abstract Antibiotic residues are now widespread in agricultural soils, yet their influence on microbe-mediated mercury (Hg) transformations and associated risks is poorly understood. Here, we demonstrate that fluoroquinolone (FQ) antibiotics enhance the production of neurotoxic methylmercury (MeHg) in paddy soils by selectively altering microbial metabolic activity. In 40 paddy soils from China’s major rice-growing regions, FQ addition at 10 mg kg −1 increased MeHg content by 2.9%–19.7% after 21 days of incubation. Metabolic inhibition and microcosm experiments revealed that this increase stemmed primarily from stimulated microbial Hg methylation, rather than inhibited MeHg demethylation. Sulfate-reducing bacteria (SRB) dominated this process since inhibiting sulfate reduction decreased FQ-induced Hg methylation by 31%–75%. Integrated microbiome and functional prediction based on soil microbial communities and metagenomic analyses of enriched SRB consortia further identified hgcA -carrying SRB as the key methylators. FQ exposure selectively suppressed competing microbial groups while promoting metabolically active, antibiotic-tolerant SRB, particularly those using the reductive acetyl-CoA pathway, thereby elevating Hg methylation activity without significantly changing methylator abundance or community structure. Together, these findings reveal that widespread antibiotic contamination amplifies Hg risks in soils via tolerant microbial communities, potentially representing a hidden yet critical link between emerging contaminants, heavy metals, and food safety.

items.title: Enantioselective cobalt-catalyzed intermolecular [3+2] cycloaddition of cyclopropenes with terminal alkynes to access chiral cyclopentadienes
Thin-film lithium tantalate for ultraviolet integrated electro-optic modulator
items.abstract: Abstract The realization of integrated, high-speed ultraviolet modulation is pivotal for the advancement of quantum information processing, portable atomic clocks, and secure solar-blind communications. While mature photonic platforms have enabled sophisticated system-level integration across the visible and infrared spectral ranges, high-speed active modulation in the ultraviolet remains largely dependent on conventional bulk-crystal technologies. Consequently, a scalable integrated solution that simultaneously combines low insertion loss and extreme compactness with high modulation efficiency has remained challenging. Here, we report an integrated UV electro-optic modulator on a thin-film lithium tantalate platform. The device has a compact lumped-electrode of 200 μ m, exhibiting a measured 3 dB electrical-to-optical-to-electrical bandwidth above 40 GHz, a high modulation efficiency V π L of 85 mV ⋅ cm, and a measured electrical-to-electrical bandwidth beyond 67 GHz. This work establishes thin-film lithium tantalate as a disruptive platform for wafer-scale compatible active UV photonics, enabling the next generation of scalable quantum and communication systems.

items.title: Convergence in the size and frequency of macroevolutionary peak-shifts on the adaptive landscape in vertebrates
items.abstract: Abstract Empirical and theoretical support is emerging for a view of macroevolution characterised by species’ phenotypes tracking continually-moving adaptive peaks, interspersed with rare large shifts in the position of those peaks, likely corresponding to changes in species’ adaptive zones. But we lack understanding of the factors that control these movements. We show in a sample of over 21,000 species from the five Vertebrate Classes ( Mammals, Birds, Reptiles, Fish and Amphibians ) repeated convergence in the magnitude and frequencies of rare shifts in body-size peaks among species inhabiting the same dominant ecology. Peak-shifts (towards becoming larger or smaller) have been largest and most frequent among aquatic species, followed by terrestrial and then smallest and least frequent among volant species, independently of phylogenetic history. All peak-shifts are small in macroevolutionary time indicating that species in the terrestrial and aerial environments could have changed more had their environments favoured it. Within-population trait-variances from independent sources are largest in aquatic, followed by terrestrial then aerial species, consistent with evolution responding to differing macroevolutionary landscapes. Our results illustrate how ecologically varying adaptive landscapes have produced convergent outcomes of vertebrate macroevolution, giving rise to predictable evolutionary patterns even among species differing in fundamental aspects of development and thermoregulation.

items.title: Magnetic excitons in a suspended 2D antiferromagnetic membrane
items.abstract: Abstract Layered magnetic and strongly correlated materials, such as NiPS 3 , present a rich platform for condensed matter physics with intrinsic properties intertwined by magnetism and low-dimensionality. A suspended light-emitting 2D antiferromagnetic membrane forms a highly controllable hybrid system in which the interplay between spin ordering, optical and mechanical degrees of freedom can be uniquely explored. NiPS 3 hosts excitons responsible for a puzzling luminescence down to a few atomic layers, linked to its zigzag antiferromagnetic order. The exact nature of these excitons remains unclear. Here we report on the magnetic excitons of a suspended few-layer NiPS 3 membrane. We reveal nematic zigzag states and study the optical transitions induced by the magnon-mediated motion of the excitation in the magnetic lattice, resulting in magnon-dressed excitons. We observe a strain tuning of these emission lines, dependent on their microscopic origin, with rates that indicate a strong localization of the magnetic excitons, fading with the number of magnon-mediated hops.

items.title: Nanocast sodium metasurfaces for enhanced light-matter coupling
items.abstract: Abstract Sodium has been proven to be a plasmonic material superior to noble metals. However, its high chemical reactivity poses a major obstacle to direct nanopatterning via conventional techniques, hindering the pursuit of sodium metasurfaces that simultaneously deliver high coupling efficiency and high quality factor. In this work, we developed a nanocast sodium-argon metasurface by rapidly cooling liquid sodium on a polymethyl methacrylate nanomold. This metasurface supports high-Q plasmonic resonances with record-high performance, surpassing previously reported alkali metal plasmonic systems. The liquid sodium consistently maintains an ultra-low filling depth regardless of the mold depth, which not only creates a nonlocal photonic configuration but also affords precise control over the radiative-to-dissipative loss ratio. Such casting behavior enables the metasurface to transition from under-coupling to critical-coupling regimes, thereby achieving high-efficiency, tunable second harmonic generation. We further provide direct experimental evidence that sodium outperforms silver in nonlinear optical performance. By leveraging the robustness inherent to the nonlocal nanocasting technique for sodium-argon metasurfaces, we demonstrate a large-area second harmonic generation metasurface with polarization-switchable imaging. The proposed sodium nanocasting technique opens an alternative avenue for sustainable high-performance plasmonics.

items.title: Ventral CA1 perineuronal nets modulate morphine-associated contextual memory via vCA1–NAcC synaptic remodeling in male mice
Dynorphin counteracts excitatory co-transmission in a lateral hypothalamus–locus coeruleus circuit underlying stress-induced anxiety
Melanosome evolution shaped sensory biology and terrestrial adaptations in early aquatic vertebrates
items.abstract: Abstract The photic environment is a key driver of fish ecology that shapes adaptations to aquatic habitats. The evolutionary history of these adaptations, however, is difficult to trace. Melanosomes, melanin-rich organelles, offer unique insights into physiology and ecology and often fossilise. Here, we present a comparative analysis of melanosomes from extant and fossil fishes to trace the evolution of ecological and physiological adaptations through deep time. Melanosomes from internal tissues of extant fishes exhibit highly conserved geometries in all major taxonomic groups examined, indicating persistent functional constraints during evolution. Larger, more abundant melanosomes in lungfish likely reflect adaptations that underpin the vertebrate water-to-land transition. In contrast, eye melanosomes exhibit lineage-specific patterns. Bony fishes possess cylindrical eye melanosomes associated with retinomotor movements, photoreceptor protection, and improved visual acuity, whereas jawless and cartilaginous fishes possess only spheroidal melanosomes, consistent with visual sensitivity and alternative light-regulation strategies including pupillary modulation. These taxonomic differences are preserved in fossils from the late Carboniferous Mazon Creek biota, indicating that links between melanosome morphology and function were established during the early evolutionary history of these lineages in the Ordovician, approximately 445 million years ago. Early innovations in melanin biology uniquely facilitated vertebrate sensory evolution and ecological diversification.

items.title: Inflammatory memory primes the intestine for enhanced regenerative potential
Marine heat waves in vulnerable coral reef regions are skillfully predictable on multi-year timescales
Distinct conformational states of HSV-2 gH/gL captured by cryoEM reveal structural principles governing fusion activation
items.abstract: Abstract Orthoherpesviridae infect most humans for life and cause myriad diseases. These viruses distribute cell-entry functions among receptor-binding proteins such as gD, the conserved membrane fusogen gB, and the gH/gL heterodimer, which couples receptor engagement to gB activation. Here, we report cryoEM structures of HSV-2 gH/gL, including complexes with four antibody fragments, in distinct conformational states. Structural analysis suggests that these structures represent pre-activation and intermediate states rather than a post-activation state. Antibody binding appears to shift the gH/gL conformational equilibrium of gH/gL, either stabilizing the pre-activation state or promoting refolding into intermediate or post-activation-like states. Two regions – the N terminus and a domain H2 switch – adopt distinct conformations and may transmit the activating signal from gD to gB. We propose that receptor-bound gD displaces the gH N terminus, initiating allosteric rearrangements that culminate in switch refolding and may help release prefusion gB from an autoinhibited gH/gL-gB complex. Switch conservation suggests that this activation mechanism may be shared across Orthoherpesviridae . These findings uncover structural principles governing gH/gL-mediated activation of membrane fusion.

items.title: Omnidirectional photonic chiral flatband in nonlocal membrane metasurfaces
scBOA: Bayesian optimization of single-cell analysis pipelines for robust annotation and discovery
NK cells engineered with a chimeric antigen receptor delay HIV rebound and reshape HIV reservoir composition
items.abstract: Abstract Durable HIV remission requires strategies that eliminate or permanently silence the latent reservoir that persists despite antiretroviral therapy (ART). We engineer allogeneic human primary natural killer (NK) cells expressing a truncated CD4-based chimeric antigen receptor (D1D2 CAR) targeting the conserved CD4 binding site on HIV Env. D1D2 CAR NK cells selectively kill HIV-infected primary CD4 T cells in vitro and significantly delay viral rebound following ART interruption in humanized mice infected with barcoded CCR5-tropic HIV. Barcoded HIV tracking shows reductions in the number and diversity of rebounding viral RNA lineages, together with decreased inter-organ sharing of rebound-associated proviral barcodes and integration sites. Integration site and chromatin analyses suggest that rebound-associated proviruses remaining after D1D2 CAR-NK treatment are less frequently located in genic and transcriptionally active chromatin contexts. Thus, CAR-NK cells may target reactivating HIV-infected cells during early ART interruption and shape the composition of the reservoir contributing to rebound.

items.title: Nascent RNA-mediated recruitment and R-loop suppression underlie FUS-driven enhancement of transcription
Evaluation of vaccine-induced anti-lipopolysaccharide antibodies against clinically relevant Klebsiella pneumoniae strains to inform vaccine design
items.abstract: Abstract Klebsiella pneumoniae is a leading cause of neonatal sepsis in low- and middle-income countries and is increasingly multi-drug resistant, highlighting the need for vaccines. Putative vaccine targets include the lipopolysaccharide (O antigen) and capsular polysaccharide (K antigen), but capsule may mask O antigen and limit antibody-mediated opsonophagocytosis. We evaluated the activity of O antigen-specific antibodies induced by a tetravalent bioconjugate vaccine against 146 clinical isolates representing 17 prevalent capsule types associated with neonatal sepsis. Susceptibility to antibody-mediated killing varied by capsule type: four were consistently susceptible, six showed heterogeneous responses, and seven were resistant despite remaining susceptible to K antigen-specific antibodies. Killing of susceptible strains was predominantly mediated by anti-O1 antibodies, as demonstrated by competitive inhibition with purified polysaccharides. Collectively, these findings support an antigen-sparing vaccine design strategy, in which susceptible capsule types may be replaced by a single O type, reducing vaccine complexity while maintaining broad functional coverage.

items.title: A SARS-CoV-2 entry inhibitor trimerizes to lock the spike protein in a closed conformation
items.abstract: Abstract The SARS-CoV-2 spike protein binds its receptor ACE2 to initiate target-cell infection. To engage ACE2, at least one of the three receptor-binding domains (RBDs) of the spike must adopt the up orientation. Here, we describe S22, a potent, bioavailable, and non-toxic inhibitor of BA.2 and all subsequent Omicron variants. Cryo-EM analyses showed that S22 assembled as a trimer in the central cavity of the spike apex, stabilizing all three RBDs in the down orientation, thereby preventing ACE2 association. Binding studies, especially those using mixed S22-sensitive and -resistant spikes, imply a cooperative assembly of three S22 molecules with three RBDs, resulting in an unusually slow S22 off-rate. Consistent with its slow dissociation and favorable pharmacokinetics, S22 suppressed viral replication and inflammation in the lungs of XBB.1.5-infected female mice. Thus, S22 potently inhibits Omicron entry through a distinct mechanism whereby a small compound assembles cooperatively as a trimer to stabilize spike in an inactive conformation.

items.title: DEGS1-mTORC1-driven lipid metabolic reprogramming fuels rhabdomyosarcoma progression and unveils a therapeutic vulnerability
Ultra-low loss piezo-optomechanical low-confinement silicon nitride platform for visible wavelength quantum photonic circuits
items.abstract: Abstract Realizing photonic quantum computing at scale requires integrated circuits that combine ultra-low loss with fast, low-power, low-hysteresis, and low-crosstalk reconfiguration. These requirements are particularly challenging at visible wavelengths, where many quantum resource-state generators, including single-photon sources and quantum memories, naturally operate. Low-confinement silicon nitride waveguides offer the requisite loss performance, but conventional thermo-optic modulators dissipate significant static power, driving thermal crosstalk and precluding cryogenic operation. Visible-wavelength piezo-optomechanical circuits avoid these drawbacks, but existing demonstrations rely either on high-confinement waveguides with propagation losses of 35-100 dB/m, or on low-confinement platforms using foundry-incompatible lead zirconate titanate (PZT). Here we combine piezo-optomechanical actuation with a CMOS-foundry-fabricated, low-confinement silicon nitride platform, achieving 2.6 dB/m propagation loss at 780 nm, megahertz-scale modulation bandwidth, a half-wave voltage-length product of 2.8 V ⋅ m, and negligible hysteresis. We demonstrate reconfigurable Mach-Zehnder interferometers with 0.63 dB loss per spiral phase shifter, enabling deep, actively reconfigurable visible-wavelength quantum photonic circuits.

items.title: Increasing dengue outbreaks in temperate Brazil are associated with Aedes aegypti invasion and infestation levels
items.abstract: Abstract Dengue fever, caused by dengue virus (DENV), is one of the most significant mosquito-borne diseases globally, with increasing risk due to the expansion of Aedes vectors into subtropical and temperate zones. Brazil accounted for 70% of dengue cases reported worldwide in 2024, and the virus has recently become endemic in the southernmost state of Rio Grande do Sul. Here, we integrate entomological, epidemiological and environmental data and generate complementary genomic data to investigate DENV dynamics in Southern Brazil from 2015 to 2023. During this period, Aedes aegypti expanded across state municipalities, with a marked increase in dengue cases from 2020 onward. Nearly half of the municipalities surpassed the incidence threshold of ≥20 cases per 100,000 residents per year by 2023, indicating endemic transmission. Genomic analysis of 665 new DENV genomes is consistent with the local persistence of viral lineages across years, driving seasonal outbreaks. Moreover, Northwest and Metropolitan regions are identified as key hubs for viral spread within the Rio Grande do Sul state. These findings highlight the north-to-south expansion of dengue into temperate regions, emphasizing the urgent need for intensification of vector control and surveillance in newly endemic areas to mitigate dengue burden in a mostly naive human population.

items.title: Tuning ferroptosis-like, cancer-selective cell death with charge-imbalanced nanoparticles
items.abstract: Abstract It is known that nanoparticles functionalized with mixed charge monolayers – that is, monolayers composed of both positively [+] and negatively [-] charged ligands – can induce selective death of cancer cells. Remarkably, however, when the ligand polarities and proportions are kept constant, but the chemical nature of the “minority” [-] component is altered, the nanoparticles exhibit distinct intracellular localization patterns and induce different forms of iron-dependent lipid-peroxidation-driven cell death, which we term “ferroptosis-like” due to concurrent activation of caspases. In particular, changing the end groups on the [-] ligands from carboxylic to sulfonic to phosphonic acid shifts nanoparticle accumulation from lysosomes to autophagic compartments to late endosomes, respectively. These distinct cellular outcomes are accompanied by marked differences in the composition of serum protein coronas adsorbed onto the mixed-charge nanoparticles. Proteomic analysis revealed exceedingly complex corona proteomes, comprising more than 800 different proteins, many enriched hundreds- to thousands-fold compared to blood serum, with numerous proteins selectively enriched on specific nanoparticle types. Together, these findings identify charge-imbalanced constructs as potential modulators of subcellular organelle targeting and ferroptosis-like cell death.

items.title: Synthesis-by-design of ferroelectric Dion–Jacobson two-dimensional hybrid organic–inorganic perovskites
items.abstract: Abstract Dion–Jacobson two-dimensional hybrid organic–inorganic perovskites are promising ferroelectric materials, combining chemically tunable polarity enabled by their organic spacers with enhanced environmental stability.
