We show that three-dimensional mechanical loading, but not fatty acid–based metabolic maturation media, is essential for expressing Desmin, whose aggregation defines DRM. Using microengineered heart tissues, we found that contractile deficits are associated with impaired calcium handling, pointing to electromechanical uncoupling in DRM. Treatment with the Janus kinase 1 inhibitor itacitinib partially rescued contractility, providing a functional validation of this emerging therapeutic strategy.

items.title: Dual-action small-molecule VSP-51-2 ameliorates polycystic ovary syndrome via PPARγ modulation and AKR1C3 inhibition
items.abstract: Polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS), a prevalent multifactorial endocrine disorder, is inadequately managed by current therapies that fail to concurrently target its core metabolic (insulin resistance) and reproductive (hyperandrogenism) pathologies. We report VSP-51-2, a dual-target lead compound initially engineered as a selective PPARγ modulator that unexpectedly exerts potent uncompetitive inhibition of the androgen-synthesizing enzyme AKR1C3 through a putative allosteric mechanism. In preclinical PCOS models, VSP-51-2 restored regular estrous cyclicity, improved ovarian follicular morphology, enhanced systemic insulin sensitivity, suppressed hyperandrogenism, and did not significantly perturb measured hypothalamic-pituitary-ovarian (HPO) axis hormonal parameters. Mechanistically, it blocks PPARγ phosphorylation at Ser 273 , thereby enhancing adiponectin secretion and GLUT4-mediated glucose uptake, and is predicted to bind a putative allosteric pocket of AKR1C3 to constrain androgen biosynthesis. These findings support VSP-51-2 as a preclinical proof-of-concept compound for a dual-target strategy that addresses metabolic dysfunction and androgen excess through a unified molecular scaffold.

items.title: Reprogramming electron transfer at single-atom Pt sites to break the interference barrier in uric acid detection
items.abstract: Uric acid (UA) serves as a key biomarker for gout, cardiovascular disease, and kidney dysfunction, yet conventional detection methods relying on H 2 O 2 generation suffer from signal instability and interference from reductive species. Here, we report a uricase-like platinum-nitrogen-carbon nanozyme (Pt-N-C-NH 3 ) that redirects UA oxidation from a two-electron pathway toward a four-electron pathway. By decreasing graphitic nitrogen content, the local electronic microenvironment of platinum sites is modulated, which is associated with a lower calculated free-energy change for the rate-determining absorbed oxygen to absorbed hydroxyl transformation from 1.25 to 0.62 electron volts and thereby promoting oxygen reduction to water. Integrated into a microneedle sensing platform, UA is converted to allantoin for chemiluminescent readout. The sensor exhibits a wide linear range of 50.00 to 1000.00 μM and a detection limit of 15.86 μM, while maintaining 97.57% signal stability against reductive interferents. This work demonstrates that atomic-level coordination engineering enables programmable control over reaction pathways in artificial enzyme systems, thereby facilitating robust biosensing in complex biological environments.

items.title: Asymmetric cell division is predictive of human T cell vaccine responses
items.abstract: Vaccine-induced protection relies on the generation and maintenance of stem-like memory B and T cells, a process sustained by two conserved mechanisms: asymmetric cell division (ACD) and autophagy. In T cells, ACD enables them to produce progeny with the same T cell receptor but with divergent metabolic and functional fates upon antigen encounter through the unequal inheritance of cellular cargoes. Autophagy recycles cellular components, provides metabolic substrates essential for sustaining energy demands, and is relevant for the maintenance of T cell memory. Direct evidence of how these processes synergize and affect human immunity is still lacking. Here, we show that mitotic human CD8 + T cells asymmetrically segregate autophagy-related organelles, including autophagosomes and lysosomes. Furthermore, we show that ACD drives divergent transcriptional and functional fates in daughter cells. Extending these findings to an influenza vaccine trial, we demonstrate that autophagic flux follows the dynamics of clonal expansion and contraction of antigen-specific T cells. Notably, individuals with enhanced ACD capacity, especially with increased LC3B asymmetry, exhibit better vaccine responses, linking early cellular segregation events to long-term immune fitness. Last, transient use of the mechanistic target of rapamycin complex 1 inhibitor rapamycin improved memory survival, which was associated with improved ACD, measured by the asymmetric inheritance of both CD8 and LC3B. Together, these findings highlight that the asymmetric inheritance of the autophagy machinery represents another layer of human adaptive immunity and offers a potential therapeutic target to enhance vaccine outcomes.

items.title: A fully hydrogel implantable patch for in situ ultrasonic monitoring of gastric leakage
items.abstract: Gastric leakage is a common and life-threatening postoperative complication, while delayed detection often leads to severe abdominal organ damage. Current radiological imaging modalities are limited in their ability to provide timely detection of gastric leakage, while the mechanical mismatch and long-term persistence of conventional electronic sensors limit their implantable applications. In this work, we developed a fully hydrogel-based ultrasonic metagel patch (USMP) for direct, real-time monitoring of gastric leakage via ultrasound imaging. The USMP incorporates a tree-ring air cell array, in which densely distributed air cells arranged in concentric rings create a strong back-scattering effect, thereby producing distinctive and stable ultrasound imaging signatures for rapid and sensitive detection. The air cells are encapsulated within biocompatible, hydrolytically degradable pH-responsive hydrogels, forming a fully hydrogel sensing architecture. The potential of the USMP for gastric leakage monitoring up to 7 days postimplantation is validated in the live rabbit model.

items.title: Does government-assisted relocation help households
items.abstract: Climate change is intensifying floods and storms, leading governments to consider relocating households away from high-risk areas. Yet, there is little evidence on whether such programs reduce risk or improve household well-being. I evaluate the US Federal Emergency Management Agency’s property acquisition (“buyout”) program using nationwide longitudinal records that track households before and after approval. By comparing households facing similar mapped flood risks, I estimate the program’s effects on relocation, residence in high-risk flood areas, and financial outcomes. Households that participate are more likely to relocate outside Federal Emergency Management Agency–designated flood hazard areas and experience short-term reductions in debt and improvements in neighborhood socioeconomic conditions. However, these benefits are concentrated among participants from wealthier and predominantly white neighborhoods, who relocate more quickly and achieve larger reductions in risk. A benefit-cost analysis shows that the program value depends on implementation costs and realized reductions in flood-risk exposure, with benefit-cost ratios ranging from 0.84 to 1.28 across three scenarios. These results show that government-assisted relocation can be an effective adaptation tool, but its social and economic benefits remain unevenly distributed.

items.title: Segmented projection image translation for large-area, high-resolution vat photopolymerization
items.abstract: High-resolution projection-based vat photopolymerization (VP) 3D printing enables rapid fabrication of highly detailed polymeric structures. However, expanding the build area traditionally compromises resolution, creating a fundamental trade-off between projected pixel size and printable area due to fixed digital micromirror device (DMD) pixel counts. Herein, we introduce segmented projection image translation (SPIN), a simple implementation strategy that expands the effective projection area by applying controlled orbital translation to an off-axis objective lens within the optical infinity space. In this work, we demonstrate a projection-based VP printer implemented with SPIN that expands the effective build area by 4.8-fold, from a native field of 60.4 square millimeters to an expanded domain of 290.5 square millimeters. The SPIN-enabled printer produces isolated line features as thin as 9.8 ± 2.2 micrometers and fabricates intricate three-dimensional truss structures with features as small as 30 micrometers. These results validate a practical route for extending microscale projection-based VP printing to larger build areas while preserving feature fidelity across stitched exposure fields.

items.title: Real-time complex-valued RF blind source separation via in-physics computing
items.abstract: The rise of edge-centric 6G networks demands real-time intelligent processing of heterogeneous radio-frequency (RF) signals. Complex-valued blind source separation (CV-BSS) provides a physical-layer capability, enabling the blind extraction of source components from overlapping RF signals. Here, we demonstrate an integrated photonic vector processor (IPVP) that implements real-time CV-BSS via in-physics computation directly on raw RF signals. The IPVP operates across multiple RF bands up to 24 GHz and achieves blind, in-hardware adaptation to unknown sources and channels via in situ learning. Experiments demonstrate the efficacy of IPVP in multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) communications and multi-band radar interference suppression. The IPVP reduces the EVMs of the two recovered signals from over 50% to 6.18% and 5.3%, respectively, while enhancing the SIR by up to 26 dB. This work demonstrates, to our knowledge, the first photonic processor capable of real-time CV-BSS at RF, highlighting the potential of integrated photonic hardware for ultralow-latency, edge-intelligent signal processing.

items.title: A primordial heavy water reservoir in the outer solar system
items.abstract: The oxygen (O) isotopic composition of outer solar system ices is believed to be enriched in heavy O isotopes owing to photochemical processes, but evidence for this O reservoir is exceedingly rare in meteorites. Hydrated interplanetary dust particles (IDPs) collected in Earth’s stratosphere that display high densities of solar energetic particle tracks originate from Edgeworth-Kuiper belt objects. Their mineralogy is dominated by hydrated minerals that formed by alteration of anhydrous precursor minerals at low temperatures through reactions with water (H 2 O)–carbon dioxide fluids. The O isotopic compositions of track-rich hydrated IDPs implicate 17,18 O-rich ices as the source of H 2 O involved in their alteration, providing compelling evidence for the presence of a major heavy water reservoir beyond the orbits of the gas giant planets that was largely isolated from inner solar system materials.

items.title: Discovery of a likely supermassive neutron star in a remarkably wide binary
items.abstract: Supermassive neutron stars ( M ≳ 2 M ⊙ ) provide stringent constraints on the equation of state of dense matter. We report the discovery of a wide binary system composed of a red giant star and an invisible companion with an orbital period P ≈ 1218 ± 3 days and a comparatively low eccentricity e ≈ 0.09 ± 0.01 (with 1σ uncertainty). By combining radial velocity measurements from the Large Sky Area Multi-Object Fiber Spectroscopic Telescope and the Apache Point Observatory Galactic Evolution Experiment (APOGEE) with astrometric data from Gaia DR2 and DR3 catalogs, we derive a Keplerian orbit with an inclination angle i ≈ 73 ∘ ± 11 ∘ . The unseen companion has a mass in the range of 1.8 to 2.8 M ⊙ (spanning the full spread of all estimates), with a best-fit value of 2.20 − 0.13 + 0.14 M ⊙ . This potentially places the unseen companion within the mass gap between neutron stars and black holes. Spectral disentangling using high-resolution near-infrared APOGEE spectra shows no absorption features from an additional component, suggesting the presence of a compact object: either a supermassive neutron star or a low-mass black hole. The wide, low-eccentricity orbit is difficult to explain through standard binary evolution channels, pointing to the need for improved theoretical models to account for such systems.

items.title: The role of network connectivity and transcriptomic vulnerability in shaping gray matter atrophy in multiple sclerosis
items.abstract: Clinical progression is strongly linked to gray matter atrophy in multiple sclerosis (MS), detectable early on MRI and progressing nonrandomly across the brain. However, the mechanisms driving its spatiotemporal progression and individual variability remain unclear. Using MRIs from 2187 participants, alongside normative data, we systematically investigated network-based mechanisms underlying MS-related atrophy. Regional atrophy was associated with functional cortical hubness, supporting the nodal stress hypothesis, and was constrained by anatomical and functional connections, consistent with transneuronal degeneration. Lesional disconnection and transcriptomic vulnerability played marginal roles. Patient- and subgroup-level analyses revealed that network-based mechanisms are specifically linked to MS-related neurodegeneration and may operate differently in distinct subtypes or disease phases. Atrophy patterns were anchored to the connectivity profiles of disease epicenters involving the visual, sensorimotor, and temporal cortices, as well as the hippocampi, amygdalae, and thalami. Network-based measures enhanced the explanation of future atrophy progression in people with MS, providing a mechanistic framework to understand neurodegeneration in MS.

items.title: Tracing Neanderthal ancestry patterns through successive population expansions in Europe
items.abstract: During their expansion from Africa, modern humans interbred with Neanderthals, resulting in introgression of Neanderthal DNA into their genomes. This process contributed to a Southeast-to-Northwest gradient of Neanderthal ancestry across Europe. We investigate the population dynamics underlying the emergence and persistence of this gradient through two successive human range expansions. We developed a three-population, layered, spatially explicit simulation framework to track the spatiotemporal evolution of Neanderthal ancestry under a model of interactions among Neanderthals, pre-Neolithic hunter-gatherers, and Neolithic farmers. Our results indicate that the ancestry cline emerged from the interplay between the direction of the initial hunter-gatherer expansion, the northern limit of the Neanderthal range, and strong reproductive isolation, without requiring natural selection. The similar direction of the subsequent Neolithic expansion explains the cline’s persistence and Neanderthal ancestry differences between hunter-gatherers and farmers. These findings demonstrate how spatiotemporal patterns in ancient DNA provide insights into past population dynamics.

items.title: Inhibition of aberrant astrocyte activity restores auditory sensorimotor function in zebrafish spen mutants
items.abstract: Sensorimotor deficits can profoundly affect the life quality of patients with neurological disorders, yet our understanding of central dysfunction at the cellular or circuit level is limited. Using a forward genetic approach to generate loss of auditory function in zebrafish larvae, we identified a recessive mutation in split ends ( spen ), which encodes a transcription factor implicated in neurodevelopmental disorders in humans. We found that auditory sensorimotor deficits in spen mutants are associated with chronically elevated calcium levels in hindbrain radial astrocytes. Astrocytes have been previously implicated in the integration of neuronal inputs that alter arousal states and sensorimotor behavior. Inhibition of noradrenergic receptors, which are expressed in astrocytes, lowered calcium levels in mutant radial astrocytes and, notably, restored behavioral responses to sound in spen mutants. Our study highlights a role for noradrenergic signaling in spen -related disease and points to potential therapeutic approaches for pediatric patients.

items.title: Brown carbon in biomass burning aerosol enhances HONO production
items.abstract: Nitrous acid (HONO) is an important source of hydroxyl radicals (•OH). •OH drives ozone and aerosol formation, affecting air quality, health, and climate. Elevated HONO concentrations have been observed in biomass burning (BB) plumes. However, the mechanism remains unclear, hindering parameterization and quantification of the impacts. Here, we conducted flow tube experiments with BB aerosol samples and proxies to investigate renoxification, a process that converts nitrate into HONO and NO x (NO and NO 2 ). Our results reveal that renoxification in BB aerosol is enhanced by brown carbon (BrC) through electron transfer to nitrate as an alternative to surface-enhanced nitrate photolysis. We develop parameterization to assess the potential global impacts of BrC-enhanced renoxification, which suggests that BrC enhances surface-level HONO production by up to one order of magnitude in BB-affected regions, with surface HONO production exceeding 1 part per trillion per hour in regions with high aerosol nitrate. These impacts are expected to worsen as BB intensifies in a warming climate.

items.title: Input-specific deployment of the active zone scaffold RIM tunes synaptic release probability and plasticity
items.abstract: The multidomain scaffold RIM (Rab3-interacting molecule) is widely viewed as a broadly required organizer of the presynaptic active zone, clustering voltage-gated Ca 2+ (Ca v 2) channels, priming synaptic vesicles, and supporting neurotransmitter release. Whether this reliance is uniform across synapses with distinct release probabilities, however, has been difficult to resolve at convergent inputs. Here, using neurotoxin-based silencing to isolate transmission at the Drosophila neuromuscular junction, we show that the requirement for RIM is highly input-specific: RIM is essential to empower transmission at a high–release probability phasic synapse, yet is largely dispensable at a neighboring low–release probability tonic synapse. This specificity extends to plasticity: RIM is required for acute homeostatic potentiation at the phasic input, but not for chronic potentiation at the tonic input. Super-resolution imaging reveals that RIM is positioned closer to Ca v 2 channels at phasic synapses and, during acute plasticity, coordinates their nanoscale reorganization to drive the rapid expansion of the readily releasable pool.

items.title: The transcription factors OsIDD and OsSHR jointly regulate ground tissue patterning and differentiation in rice roots
items.abstract: Rice roots have a distinctive ground tissue architecture with multiple cortical layers and a single endodermal layer concentrically surrounding the stele. This architecture promotes aerenchyma formation and adaptability to waterlogged environments, but the underlying molecular mechanisms remain largely unexplored. Here, we identified the INDETERMINATE DOMAIN (IDD) and SHORTROOT (SHR) families as key regulators of ground tissue development in rice. OsIDD2/3/6/8 govern cortical radial symmetry by coordinating cortical organization and auxin distribution independently of OsSHR1/2/3/4/5. Quadruple knockout of OsIDD2/3/6/8 caused cortical asymmetry without affecting apoplastic barrier integrity or mineral uptake but reduced shoot-directed ion transport. OsIDD8 also controls the number of cortical cell layers and endodermal cells, whereas OsSHR1/2/3/4/5 redundantly promote periclinal divisions of the cortical cells, which require OsIDD8 activity. Moreover, OsIDD and OsSHR members coordinate endodermal differentiation by regulating localization of Casparian strip membrane domain protein OsCASP1 and lignin/suberin deposition. These findings establish a genetic framework underlying the spatial organization and functional differentiation of ground tissue in rice roots.

items.title: The ZmJAZ14–ZmMYC2 module regulates anthesis–silking synchrony in maize
items.abstract: The evolution of traits can increase yield potential but may create physiological constraints. Jasmonic acid (JA) signaling regulates sex determination in male (tassel) and female (ear) inflorescences in maize. Although the formation of ears laid the foundation for high yields, the asynchronous development of the tassel and the ear prolongs the anthesis-silking interval (ASI), threatening reproductive success and reducing yield. Whether JA signaling coordinates ear and tassel development remains unclear. Here, we show that the core JA signaling module, ZmJAZ14-ZmMYC2a/b, orchestrates the expression of SPL29 for reproductive transition, BA1 for female inflorescence initiation, and EXPA5 for silk elongation. Coordination of these physiological processes underpins synchronous growth of the tassel and ears, whereas disruption of ZmMYC2a/b or accumulation of the repressor ZmJAZ14 prolongs ASI. Our work suggests that the repurposing of JA signaling to coordinate ear and tassel development may represent a lineage-specific evolutionary burden in maize. Deciphering the link between gains and unforeseen costs of evolution could further improve yields.

items.title: Passive imaging with quantum advantage
items.abstract: Far-field optical imaging inevitably involves low-pass spatial filtering, limiting the resolution. Moreover, conventional imaging suppresses high spatial frequency components close to the cutoff, making them invisible under noise—particularly the shot noise arising from discrete and random nature of quantum light. Here, we propose and implement a method for reducing the effect of this noise by optically preprocessing the incoming light before detection, thereby optimizing the quantum measurement performed on it. Our scheme, termed Fourier domain division (FDD), partitions the Fourier plane into multiple regions for independent detection and subsequent post-processing for image reconstruction. By analyzing the quantum and classical Fisher information, we show that our method is advantageous with respect to direct imaging for high spatial-frequency components. As a result, the number of photons required to achieve a certain signal-to-noise ratio in the Fourier domain is reduced, thus enhancing the overall resolution in the photon-starved regime. We demonstrate our method in microscopy, achieving fivefold improvement of Fisher information on high spatial frequency components. Unlike active super-resolution methods, FDD is passive, making it broadly applicable in microscopy and other imaging scenarios, where active illumination is impractical, including astronomy and remote sensing, in the photon-starved regime. Our work establishes a general strategy for designing quantum optimized superresolution imaging systems, bridging fundamental quantum limits, practical image analysis, and computer vision applications.

items.title: Phototropin-mediated blue light signaling orients the asymmetry of Marchantia polymorpha spores
items.abstract: Multicellular organisms produced by sexual reproduction develop from single cells, and the asymmetry of these cells can define the orientation of the earliest developmental axes. The haploid multicellular stage of the plant, Marchantia polymorpha, develops from a single cell—the spore—that divides asymmetrically, producing an apical germ cell that generates the plant body and a smaller basal cell that differentiates as an anchoring germ rhizoid cell. We show that the orientation of this asymmetric cell division is controlled by an external environmental cue—blue light—that is perceived by the photoreceptor phototropin. This process requires the NCH1 (NRL PROTEIN FOR CHLOROPLAST MOVEMENT 1) protein for downstream signaling. Together, these findings define core elements of the mechanism by which a directional environmental signal orients cell division, which, in turn, orients the first axis of symmetry.

items.title: Electronic hair: Transforming hair into a scalable bioelectronic interface
items.abstract: In electroencephalography, hair remains a major barrier to electrode-skin contact, limiting signal quality. Here, we introduce electronic hair (eHAIR), a strategy that converts hair into a bioelectronic interface using mixed ionic-electronic conductive polymer dyes. Hair, a keratinized filament anchored within the skin, provides a stable and naturally distributed platform for interfacing. Two complementary approaches based on polythiophene derivatives enable rapid, washable functionalization of hair bundles or semipermanent coating of individual strands. The resulting eHAIR forms conformal, low-impedance interfaces that support electrophysiological recordings with increased signal amplitude and spectral power while preserving the underlying neural dynamics without gels or rigid hardware. Beyond passive sensing, eHAIR-based organic electrochemical transistors enable local signal amplification, with gain defined by hair geometry. By repurposing hair as an active bioelectronic interface, eHAIR establishes a wearable and biointegrated platform that can be implemented from individual hairs to larger hair-covered regions.

items.title: Cell adhesion molecule–related proteins signal to promote cytoneme elongation from Sonic Hedgehog–producing cells
items.abstract: Tissue morphogenesis and postdevelopmental homeostasis rely on efficient information exchange between communicating cells. Cytonemes are actin-based protrusions that contribute to precise information flow by facilitating contact-mediated directional transport of diverse signaling cargoes. How pathway-specific cytonemes are formed is poorly understood, as are the molecular mechanisms promoting actin organization for elongation and stability of the dynamic cellular extensions. We investigated biogenesis of Sonic Hedgehog (SHH) cytonemes, revealing functional repurposing of cell adhesion molecule-related proteins Brother of CDON (BOC) and Cell adhesion molecule-related, Down-regulated by Oncogenes (CDON) into recruiters of actin regulators FARP1 and Cdc42 for cytoneme elongation. Loss of BOC and CDON function blunts protrusion-localized Cdc42 activity, reducing cytoneme lengths and occurrence in SHH-expressing cells. Live imaging of developing murine spinal cords reveals that CDON loss in SHH-expressing cells reduces the frequency of neuroepithelial cytonemes and alters neuronal cell fate specification. These results inform a model whereby SHH-binding proteins promote ligand transport through stimulating formation of long cytonemes.

items.title: Multimodal switches exploiting electromechanical snap-through for versatile robotic information processing
items.abstract: It is highly desirable to design and engineer lightweight, low-power-consumption, and rapid physical intelligence (PI) structures that couple with multiple robotic functions. Here, we present a multimodal electromechanical switch (mEMS), consisting of a stretchable droplet-amplified electrostatic zipping structure, a convex bump, and a pair of electrical contacts, that can be used to achieve the widely used mechanical momentary, mechanical latching, and electrically actuated switching modes by simply tuning the applied voltage and using the same structure. We theoretically investigate the snap-through behavior of the elastic zipping membrane, which can be used to endow the mEMS with voltage-dependent memory, and the theoretical considerations are experimentally validated. As a result, we can apply the mEMS array for robotic memory, such as information writing and erasing; robotic communication by reprogrammable information encrypting, decrypting, and display; robotic computation by electrically reprogrammable logic gates; and reprogrammable binary information transferring. The mEMS represents a comprehensive PI structure for next-generation autonomous machines that can better adapt in unstructured and complex real-world environments.

items.title: Cocrystals for sequestering and separating large PAHs
items.abstract: Highly adaptive boroxine organic assemblies (BOAs) derived from a boronic acid and a linear alkene function as a first-generation constitutional dynamic library (CDL) to sequester and separate large polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs) in form of cocrystals. Configurational and conformational isomerism of the organoboroxines in host-guest assemblies is induced by electronic properties, shape and size of the PAHs through a “shrink-wrap” process/mechanism, which reveals a templating role of the PAH during the CDL assembly. The CDL was applied to separate up to three different PAHs. The cocrystals exhibit tunable electronic properties. The CDL afforded a cocrystal wherein alkenes of two different BOAs undergo [2 + 2] photocycloaddition in the same solid.

items.title: Dynamic plasmonic imaging of electromechanically driven nano-oscillators for charge-resolved multiplex biosensing
items.abstract: Multiplexed profiling of diverse biomarkers is essential for precision diagnostics, but remains challenging for label-free sensors because signals typically scale with analyte mass. Here, we present a dynamic plasmonic imaging platform based on electromechanically driven nano-oscillators for multiplexed, label-free quantification of nucleic acids, proteins, and small molecules within a unified sensing architecture. Size-encoded nanoparticles tethered to a plasmonic surface are electrically actuated to oscillate vertically within the evanescent field and tracked by distance-resolved surface plasmon resonance imaging. Molecular binding alters the effective surface charge of each nano-oscillator, modulating the electrostatic-driven forces and changing oscillation amplitude. This charge-to-motion transduction mechanism reduces dependence on molecular mass and enhances sensitivity for low–molecular weight analytes. This platform simultaneously detects microRNAs, proteins, and small molecules spanning a ∼300-fold molecular weight range within a single field of view. We further demonstrate multiplexed profiling of tumor-associated microRNAs in pretreated supernatants from patient-derived breast cancer cells across 24 clinical samples. Dynamic plasmonic nano-oscillators provide a scalable architecture for multiplex molecular diagnostics.

items.title: Neuromelanin-inspired metal-selenomelanin nanonetworks restore neuronal excitability in radiation-induced brain injury
items.abstract: Radiation-induced brain injury (RIBI) affects up to 30% of patients receiving cranial radiotherapy, representing an irreversible complication lacking effective therapies. Research advances are limited by poor blood-brain barrier drug penetration and overreliance on ex vivo pathology, which cannot resolve dynamic neuronal dysfunction. Inspired by neuromelanin, we fabricated metal-selenomelanin nanonetworks (MSMNs), combined with in vivo electrophysiology to investigate and mitigate radiation-triggered neural dysfunction. In 6-gray whole body–irradiated mice, MSMN normalized neuronal excitability and restored medium spiny neuron firing and striatal circuit activity, improving locomotor and anxiety-related behaviors. Besides central functional recovery, MSMN provides systemic radioprotection, ensuring full 30-day survival, protecting radiosensitive organs and facilitating hematopoietic recovery. This work identifies neuronal excitability as an underexplored therapeutic target for RIBI, establishing neuromelanin-mimetic selenomelanin nanonetworks as a bioinspired platform linking molecular radioprotection to circuit-level restoration for radiation-induced neurological injury.

items.title: Controllable fabrication of visible-spectrum 3D photonic crystals
items.abstract: The fabrication of visible-spectrum three-dimensional (3D) photonic crystals (PhCs) remains highly challenging, because existing manufacturing techniques cannot simultaneously achieve high processing precision and sufficient geometric freedom. Here, we propose a suspended pyrolysis-assisted two-photon polymerization (SP-TPP) printing strategy, achieving the controllable fabrication of visible-spectrum 3D PhCs. The resulting 3D diamond PhCs exhibit a remarkable lattice-period standard deviation of only 5.75 nm, approximately 1/45 of that achieved without suspended pyrolysis. Microscopic reflection spectra confirm these PhCs possess uniform optical responses across all spatial positions. By tuning the lattice period and structural duty cycle, the PhCs operating at diverse wavelengths are systematically realized. Moreover, through the demonstration of PhC prototype structures and in situ arrayed fabrication, the SP-TPP printing strategy paves the way for applications in photonic microcavities, 3D optical waveguides, optical splitters, and integrated micro-optical systems.

items.title: Boosting stability and charge transfer of conducting polymer poly(benzodifurandione) (PBFDO) through complementary topology
items.abstract: Poly(benzodifurandione) (PBFDO) is a benchmark n-type conjugated polymer known for its record-high electrical conductivity. Nevertheless, its thermal robustness and charge/ion transport characteristics remain insufficient. To address this issue, we report a hierarchical complementary topology strategy via doping PBFDO with choline chloride (ChCl). At the molecular scale, the cations Ch + selectively intercalate along the out-of-plane direction while simultaneously densifying the in-plane π-π stacking, accompanied by partial removal of H + . At the submicrometer scale, this induces distinct phase separation into high- and low-density stacking domains. As a result, the product PBFDO-ChCl exhibited a synergistic performance boost, with a 2.8-fold enhancement in high-temperature resilience, a 1.6-fold increase in sheet conductance, and a 15.9-fold reduction in ion diffusion resistance. Then, organic electrochemical transistors (OECTs) using PBFDO-ChCl as channel material further confirm these performance enhancements. As a whole, this work closes the performance gap between n-type PBFDO and state-of-the-art p-type conjugated polymers, potentially advancing its applications from energy storage to bioelectronics and neuromorphic computing.

items.title: Weak adsorption, strong consequences: How trace gases control ice growth and quasi-liquid-layer structure
items.abstract: Gases in the atmosphere are often treated as passive background species in cold environments, yet their molecular roles at icy interfaces remain poorly understood. Here, we show how hydrophobic and hydrophilic trace gases can actively reorganize the ice interface and regulate freezing through interfacial stabilization. We find these gases can actively modulate both the kinetics and thermodynamics of the water-ice interface. Using molecular simulations, we find that all gases examined retard ice-front propagation relative to pure water to different extents. This slowing arises from weak but preferential adsorption at the water-ice interface, where gases occupy water-dense interfacial layers and locally suppress ice-like ordering. After freezing is complete, gases do not distribute uniformly across the frozen surface, but partition selectively among multiple adsorption regions across the ice–quasi-liquid-layer (QLL)–air interfacial landscape. Relatively hydrophobic gases exhibit a three-region adsorption pattern, whereas relatively hydrophilic gases occupy only two dominant adsorption regions. Despite these differences, both classes preferentially accumulate near the QLL-air boundary and its immediate outer region rather than the ice-QLL interface. There, gases pair with and compensate for dangling surface bonds (through a surface-passivating effect reminiscent of ligand stabilization), reducing the thermodynamic driving force for premelting and thereby thinning the QLL. These results establish a unified molecular picture in which atmospheric gases are active interfacial modulators of both ice growth and ice structure, with implications for freezing, ice-cloud microphysics, and heterogeneous atmospheric chemistry.

items.title: Arbitrarily cuttable and ultrathin MXene structural colors for customizable and wearable multispectral information management
items.abstract: Structural colors based on natural and artificial microstructures show promising light manipulation. As atomically thick building blocks, Ti 3 C 2 T x sheets have been successfully assembled into the ultrathin, flexible, arbitrarily cuttable, large-size structural colors by the simple and low-cost spray methods based on the lossy thin-film interference. By ordered stacking atomically thick Ti 3 C 2 T x layer by layer at well-organized low–surface tension semidry assemble state, rich colors from yellow to gray with the thickness from ∼22 to ∼154 nanometers of uniform Ti 3 C 2 T x colors are obtained, having the thinnest framework among solution-processed flexible structural colors with similar optical performance. Low-infrared emissivity from room to 300°C temperature and region-selective patterns make highly information-fused and complex visible-infrared (VIS-IR) Ti 3 C 2 T x colors camouflage. Without conventional dielectric layer between Ti 3 C 2 T x and substrate, automated spraying system can produce meter-scale films that can be cut and sewn into VIS-IR concealment “camouflage cloaks” easily, promising ultrathin multifunctional information systems and beyond.

items.title: Single-cell profiling of the duodenum during chronic human norovirus infection
items.abstract: Human noroviruses are a major cause of diarrheal disease, yet their pathogenesis remains poorly defined. We performed single-cell RNA sequencing of duodenal biopsies and matched stem cell–derived enteroids from immunodeficient individuals with chronic norovirus infection. Norovirus RNA was detected primarily in enterocytes, enteroendocrine cells, and macrophages, with the highest proportion of viral RNA-positive cells observed among M2 macrophages, followed by late enterocytes. Despite this distribution, late enterocytes produced higher viral yields than differentiated M2 macrophages in vitro. Norovirus infection was associated with the up-regulation of MHC class I-related genes and IL15 in duodenal macrophages and late enterocytes, together with increased IFNG expression by CD8 T cells. Macrophages and late enterocytes up-regulated CXCL9 and CXCL10/11 , respectively, consistent with CD8 and CD4 T cell recruitment to the duodenum. These findings show that noroviruses infect and persist across multiple permissive cell types during chronic infection, resulting in marked dysregulation of innate and adaptive immune responses that may drive pathogenesis.

items.title: Incomplete synaptic vesicle priming functionally disconnects CA1 pyramidal cells
items.abstract: The hippocampal CA1 area is perceived as a nonrecurrent neuronal network, i.e., CA1 pyramidal cells (CA1PCs) within the CA1 area innervate mainly γ-aminobutyric acid–releasing interneurons but not each other. Here, we performed an unbiased examination of the functional properties of local CA1PC output synapses using in vitro two-photon glutamate imaging. Fluorescent transients measured with iGluSnFR3 in individual boutons displayed extraordinary heterogeneity in their amplitudes and short-term plasticity patterns upon a complex train of presynaptic action potential firing. Post hoc electron microscopy of the imaged boutons demonstrated that distinct postsynaptic structure-innervating boutons display different functional properties. Approximately 25% of the boutons innervate CA1PC spines, which either release glutamate with very low release probability or completely fail to release. Phorbol 12,13-dibutyrate and elevated calcium (2+) concentration, manipulations that enhance synaptic vesicle priming and fusion, convert these silent into properly functioning synapses. Our results provide evidence that CA1PCs are interconnected with structurally and molecularly intact glutamatergic synapses, but incomplete synaptic vesicle (SV) priming precludes SV release.

items.title: A LiDAR-based reconstruction reveals increasing Arctic phytoplankton production during low-light winter-shoulder period
items.abstract: Arctic marine productivity is traditionally considered concentrated in the sunlit season, yet low-light winter-shoulder periods remain poorly constrained because passive ocean color observations require sufficient solar illumination. Here, we use 2.39 million spaceborne LiDAR profiles from CALIOP (2006–2023) to reconstruct Arctic net primary production (NPP) and evaluate how active-sensor observations reduce this seasonal blind spot. The bio-optical retrieval model was trained using MODIS-constrained observations under illuminated conditions; accordingly, low-light estimates represent physically constrained extrapolations beyond the primary MODIS-observable training domain rather than direct NPP measurements. Within this framework, LiDAR increases winter half-year observational coverage from ∼20 to 30% to ∼70 to 75% and reveals widespread low-light winter-shoulder production across marginal seas and seasonal ice-edge regions. Pan-Arctic NPP integrated over this period increased at an estimated rate of 0.75 Tg C year −1 during 2007–2023, whereas the corresponding passive-sensor signal was negligible. Accounting for this component raises annual Arctic NPP estimates by ∼13.3% indicating that passive sensor-based assessments may underrepresent the magnitude and seasonal structure of Arctic productivity. Associations with declining sea ice and surface warming suggest this underrepresented production is consistent with ongoing seasonal reorganization of Arctic carbon fixation. Uncertainties from model parameterization, low-light extrapolation, and limited in situ validation are largest in the lowest-light and highest-latitude regimes. These findings do not imply photosynthesis during absolute polar night, but show that active LiDAR observations with explicit light constraints and transparent extrapolation limits can test how unresolved low-light winter-shoulder production may alter Arctic NPP seasonality under continuing sea-ice loss.

items.title: Structural insights into light harvesting and photosystem II evolution in the basal streptophyte Mesostigma viride
items.abstract: The basal streptophyte Mesostigma viride represents a critical evolutionary transition toward land plants, yet the molecular basis of its ancestral light-harvesting strategy remains elusive. Here, we present a 2.25-angstrom resolution cryo-EM structure of the M. viride PSII-LHCII-LHCP supercomplex, revealing a unique C 2 S 2 M p2 L p2 -type architecture. Our structure reveals a nearly complete set of conserved PSII core subunits, indicating that much of the PSII structural framework found in terrestrial plants was established early in the streptophyte lineage. At the periphery, the complex features a specialized antenna module in which two ancestral LHCP monomers flank CP29. These ancestral antenna proteins bind an unusually high number of carotenoids, with seven carotenoids per subunit, and extensively incorporate marine-type keto carotenoids, siphonaxanthin, and siphonein, throughout the complex, thereby broadening absorption in the blue-green region. The canonical LHCII trimer exhibits a distinctive chlorophyll b macrocluster and a 96-femtosecond ultrafast energy transfer component. Together, these findings provide a high-resolution molecular framework for an evolutionary intermediate that combines high-capacity aquatic light harvesting with structural features potentially relevant to photoprotection during the transition toward terrestrial life.

items.title: Piezoelectrically actuated magnetic dipole twisting resonators enable miniaturized low-frequency antennas
items.abstract: Miniaturized low-frequency antennas are essential for underwater, underground, and biomedical communications, yet their performance is constrained by the fundamental size-efficiency trade-off, a long-standing physical bottleneck. Here, we introduce a radiation mechanism that circumvents this constraint by replacing the time-varying currents in conventional antennas with the mechanical twisting oscillation of a magnetic dipole. Using piezoelectrically actuated, biomimetic twisting resonators with ultrahigh mechanical quality factors, we demonstrate that low-frequency antennas operating at 15.4 and 668 hertz can be miniaturized to centimeter- and millimeter-scale, respectively, with radiation efficiencies exceeding those of size-matched loop antennas by factors of 49,000 and 5000, respectively. This electromechanical-magnetic transduction enables underwater cross-medium communication over 115 meters with only milliwatt-level power consumption, using 99.9% less power than loop antennas. It also supports implantable wireless devices that achieve a fourfold increase in communication range at identical power consumption, opening a route to long-range, low-power wireless systems capable of operating in some of the most demanding environments.

items.title: Evolutionarily reinforced GC-rich motif enables non-AUG translation in mammals under eIF1/5MP-mediated fidelity control
items.abstract: Non-AUG translation contributes to proteome diversity, but its regulatory principles remain unclear. Here, we show that a GCC-rich upstream extension, termed the NAT1 motif, acts as a potent enhancer of near-cognate initiation in mammals. Cell-free and reporter assays revealed that eIF1 and 5MP act as conserved inhibitors of non-AUG initiation across mammals and plants, while the NAT1 motif enables enhanced initiation within this fidelity framework. Mutational analysis identified −6 and −7 positions within the GCC repeat as key determinants of motif activity. Genome-wide analyses uncovered evolutionary depletion of NAT1 -type non-AUG codons in human 5′UTRs, suggesting purifying selection against excessive initiation. Nevertheless, more than a hundred retained sites are associated with genes involved in cell proliferation and migration, suggesting that regulated non-AUG initiation may contribute to disease-relevant translational programs. The motif’s enrichment within GCC repeats further suggests a mechanistic link to repeat-associated non-AUG translation.

items.title: STAT3 controls IL-6–induced epigenomic remodeling and restrains a latent STAT1-associated interferon program in human macrophages
items.abstract: Interleukin-6 (IL-6) is a pleiotropic cytokine that drives macrophage functions ranging from tissue homeostasis to inflammation, yet how STAT3 specifies these divergent outcomes remains unclear. By integrating transcriptomic and epigenomic profiling with selective STAT3 degradation, we show that STAT3 controls IL-6–induced epigenomic remodeling and restrains a latent STAT1-associated interferon program in human macrophages. Graded STAT3 chromatin recruitment scales with locus-specific H3K27ac deposition and transcriptional output across homeostatic and inflammatory programs. STAT3 degradation permits STAT1 recruitment at a subset of regulatory regions and engages a delayed amplification loop that is partially dependent on STING and type I IFN signaling. In severe COVID-19, monocytes exhibit exaggerated STAT3-associated inflammatory signatures together with attenuated STAT1-associated interferon responses, consistent with a skewed STAT3-STAT1 balance. These findings define a framework in which STAT3 calibrates IL-6–induced chromatin output while maintaining pathway fidelity by limiting STAT1 cross-talk.

items.title: Integrating biomass production platform and identification approach for stereochemical assignment of super-carbon-chain compounds
items.abstract: Super-carbon-chain compounds (SCCCs), marine long-carbon-chain polyketides featuring numerous carbon stereocenters, fall into untapped chemical space in between drug-like small molecules and biopolymers. Due to mass-material unavailability and flexible-structure complexity, the reliable stereochemical assignment of SCCCs has long remained stagnant. In this work, a modern microalgal biomass production-platform is created for pilot-scale cultivation of marine dinoflagellates to produce over 100 milligrams of minor SCCCs. The modular fragment-based identification (MFBI) approach is successfully employed to establish the relative and absolute configurations of SCCCs. As an example, 157.7 mg of a minor SCCC, named amphidiketol A, featuring a highly-flexible C 76 -linear carbon backbone and thirty-three carbon stereocenters, is obtained from Amphidinium sp. in our platform. Its hybrid architecture contains eleven‌ distinct modular fragments. Its relative and absolute configurations are successfully established by the MFBI approach. Collectively, an undescribed paradigm for stereochemical assignment of SCCCs is presented. Nine senescence-associated protein targets of amphidiketol A in lung cancer A549 cells are identified.

items.title: Identification of a specialized lipid barrier for Drosophila metamorphosis
items.abstract: Many terrestrial insects transition from humid to dry environments at metamorphosis, yet how they avoid dehydration is unclear. In Drosophila melanogaster , we identify a lipid barrier to water loss in the pupa that is anatomically distinct from that of the adult. It comprises unisex hydrocarbons that are longer and less volatile than their sex-specific adult counterparts. These hyperlong hydrocarbons are produced by larval oenocytes and stored in the fat body for subsequent transport to the cuticle at pupariation. A fatty acid elongase, EloHL, is required for hyperlong hydrocarbon biosynthesis and for a functional barrier to dehydration during early metamorphosis. Hyperlong barrier hydrocarbons are widespread across the Drosophila genus and typically transition to shorter sex-specific versions during adult maturation. In the desert species D. mojavensis , however, adults retain hyperlong hydrocarbons. This study reveals how insect lipid barriers are tuned to environmental variations in aridity and temperature during development and evolution.

items.title: Brainstem enkephalinergic neural circuit underlying cold-induced pain relief in mice
items.abstract: Application of cold or cold-mimicking chemicals to injury has long been recognized as an effective means of pain relief. However, underlying neural mechanisms remain elusive. Here, we identified a cold-responsive neuronal subset within the lateral parabrachial nucleus (lPBN), the thermosensory relay region in the hindbrain, that mediates cold-induced analgesia in mice. Activation of these neurons and their projection to ventrolateral periaqueductal gray (vlPAG) increased the nociceptive threshold, while ablation of these neurons attenuated analgesia induced by cold-mimicking chemicals. We further identified that these neurons express precursor gene of enkephalin ( Penk ), which is necessary for TRPM8 (transient receptor potential melastatin 8)–mediated pain relief. Mechanistically, cold-responsive lPBN neurons frequency-dependently released enkephalin peptide into vlPAG to activate the descending pain modulation circuitry via disinhibition. Activation of cold-responsive neurons reduced spinal cord responses to noxious stimuli, suggesting the involvement of a top-down pain modulation pathway. These findings propose a central mechanism underlying cold-induced pain relief, which could be a novel therapeutic target.

items.title: Pink noise in dyads’ semantic similarity trajectories predicts conversation enjoyment
items.abstract: Conversation is a core component of human social life. Many influential theories treat conversation as a linear system, i.e., the sum of its parts. However, linear accounts of semantic entrainment lose explanatory power at their upper limits: Discussing perfectly aligned opinions becomes boring. We propose an alternate account that considers the multiscale organization of semantic similarity over the course of a conversation, as indexed by pink noise. Here, we test whether pink noise can be found in interlocutors’ conavigated trajectories through semantic space. Not only is pink noise present, but its strength predicts positive conversation outcomes like enjoyment and connection, increases with practice, and is reflected in a large language model’s representation of conversation quality. These results demonstrate an important role for scale-free dynamics in characterizing successful conversation.

items.title: Mevalonate pathway regulates double-negative regulatory T cell stability in metabolic dysfunction–associated steatotic liver disease
items.abstract: Lipid metabolism dysfunction and immune imbalance are critical pathogenic drivers of metabolic dysfunction–associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD). Double-negative regulatory T cells (DNTreg) are important immune regulatory cells that maintain liver immune homeostasis. However, their survival and function are compromised in MASLD. Herein, we found that mevalonate pathway and its rate-limiting enzyme HMG-CoA reductase (HMGCR) were significantly down-regulated in DNTreg from both mice and patients with MASLD, correlating with impaired DNTreg viability and immunosuppressive function. Arachidonic acid is enriched in MASLD liver and inhibits DNTreg HMGCR expression. Geranylgeranyl pyrophosphate (GGPP), a downstream product of HMGCR, mediates RAC1 geranylgeranylation, which facilitates its interaction with mitochondrial CLPX protease, thereby enhancing mitochondrial function and immunoregulatory activity of DNTreg. Adoptive transfer of Pggt1b +/− DNTreg into MASLD mice demonstrated significantly diminished therapeutic efficacy compared with wild-type DNTreg. In conclusion, mevalonate metabolism–mediated geranylgeranylation is essential for the suppressive activity and immune homeostasis of DNTreg in MASLD.

items.title: Temporal dynamics of antigen-specific T cell expansion in primary SARS-CoV-2 infection
items.abstract: Quantifying T cell response during primary infection in humans is crucial for understanding adaptive immunity. Leveraging a controlled human challenge to severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2, we characterized antigen-specific T cell responses within and across individuals. Notably, individual clones reached similar maximum frequencies despite differences in the timing of their peak expansion. Mathematical modeling within a coarse-grained framework suggested that variability in precursor frequency between different T cell clones could be one mechanism to explain this relationship. Single-cell profiling revealed distinct temporal programs for CD4 + and CD8 + T cells, with CD4 + cells expanding earlier but contracting to a lower frequency. Clones with similar receptors, likely recognizing the same antigen, expanded at similar times. Together, these findings highlight how clone-intrinsic properties such as precursor frequency and CD4/CD8 subset status shape T cell clonal kinetics. These insights provide a quantitative framework for understanding T cell response in humans, with implications for vaccine design.

items.title: Humid periods over western Sahara during the Middle Miocene Climate Transition and their implications on the carbon cycle
items.abstract: The Middle Miocene expansion of the Antarctic Ice Sheet coincides with major sedimentological changes in Malta. This interval also saw reorganisations in ocean circulation linked to closure of the Mesopotamian Seaway (MSR-events) and perturbations in the carbon cycle (CM events). The final CM event (CM-6), slightly lags the main glacial phase and remains difficult to interpret due to competing mechanisms and conflicting p CO 2 reconstructions. To explore links between cryosphere, circulation, hydroclimate, and the carbon cycle, we present new geochemical records from Malta. Our records show that cryospheric expansion was followed by large, precessionally paced variations in sea-surface salinity and a marked regional increase in biological productivity. The results indicate a shift toward stronger monsoonal influence, delivering enhanced freshwater and nutrient fluxes to the region. This enhanced local biological carbon pump may have acted as a positive feedback to a global CO 2 drawdown. However, any contribution to global CO 2 drawdown remains tentative and cannot be confirmed without contemporaneous high-resolution open-ocean records.

items.title: Revisiting the additionality and durability of carbon uptake in large-scale ocean iron fertilization
items.abstract: Climate stabilization pathways limiting global warming to 1.5° to 2°C require rapid emission reductions alongside additional carbon dioxide removal (CDR) of ∼2 to 3 PgC year −1 . Our simulations show that sustained century-scale ocean iron fertilization (OIF) in the southern sector of the Southern Ocean (SSO) provides a contribution of ∼30 PgC, equivalent to ∼0.3 PgC year −1 . This uptake nearly matches the additional carbon uptake from global fertilization. In other iron-limited regions, fertilization-induced uptake is largely offset (70 to 100%) by anomalous outgassing in nonfertilized regions. After terminating OIF following 30 years of fertilization, the ocean retains ∼50% of the additional carbon in the SSO, whereas retention is negligible elsewhere. These results identify the SSO as the most favorable region for durable carbon removal through large-scale OIF, particularly in terms of additionality and durability, although its carbon uptake is smaller than earlier estimates. OIF-induced CDR is constrained by local and remote nutrient depletion, carbon reentrainment, incomplete macronutrient drawdown, and reduced phytoplankton carbon-to-phosphorus ratios. Incomplete macronutrient drawdown reflects the uptake controls by light, top-down controls, and rates of macronutrient resupply. Further insight into OIF potential will be enabled by standardized multimodel comparisons and targeted analysis of nutrient drawdown controls.

items.title: A transcriptional and cellular exploration of obesity and type II diabetes in human adipose tissues
items.abstract: Obesity is tightly linked to metabolic disorders such as type II diabetes mellitus (T2D), although a subpopulation of individuals with obesity do not present with these morbidities. The biological factors conferring T2D vulnerability remain incompletely understood. We recruited 58 individuals with obesity with or without a clinical diagnosis of T2D (Ob + T2D and Ob). We profiled paired samples of omental and subcutaneous adipose by single-cell RNA sequencing ( n = 10), flow cytometry under basal and stimulated conditions ( n = 42), and histology ( n = 17). Flow cytometry and chemokine quantification were also performed in paired whole blood. We identified reprogramming of the omental stromal compartment, centered on mesothelial and endothelial cells, alongside contrasting innate T cell and macrophage phenotypes across depots. Mesothelial and IGFBP2 + cells exhibited a fibrotic, epithelial-mesenchymal transition–like phenotype, while omental endothelial cells exhibited a lipid-overload, inflammatory, antigen presentation profile in T2D. Omental and subcutaneous adipose innate T cells exhibited divergent inflammatory profiles between tissues. These findings reveal previously unidentified insights into the pathophysiology of T2D in adipose tissue and identify compensatory networks within the tissues that could be exploited by targeted therapeutics.

items.title: Comprehensive degron mapping in human transcription factors
items.abstract: Gene expression is regulated by the targeted degradation of transcription factors through the ubiquitin-proteasome system. Transcription factors destined for degradation are recognized by E3 ubiquitin-protein ligases through motifs termed degrons, embedded within the sequence. In this study, we systematically map degrons in all 1626 human transcription factors. We find thousands of both known and previously unidentified degrons and characterize their sequence properties. Active degrons placed within exposed and intrinsically disordered regions contribute to modulating the abundance of the transcription factors, while the most common somatic mutations that are linked to skin cutaneous melanoma lead to unfolding and exposure of a latent degron buried in the zinc finger structure. We present examples of compartment-specific degrons and demonstrate that variant effects in transcription factors correlate with degron potency. Last, we show that while >60% of all predicted transcriptional activation domains overlap with strong degrons, acidic residues within the remaining transactivating regions counter the degron potency, showing how degrons can shape the transcription factor sequence landscape.

items.title: Shape-memory scaffold targets inflammation and fibrosis to restore endometrium and fertility in intrauterine adhesions
items.abstract: Intrauterine adhesion (IUA) is a major cause of infertility, yet current treatments remain limited in preventing fibrosis and restoring functional endometrium. We report a bi-drug, bifunctional, biodegradable shape-memory regenerative (BiSMR) scaffold enabling minimally invasive implantation, sequential drug release, and barrier protection. Proteomic profiling of chemical, mechanical, and combined injury models revealed inflammatory activation, extracellular matrix remodeling, and impaired regenerative programs, providing a molecular rationale for combining epigallocatechin gallate (EGCG) with 17β-estradiol (E 2 ). BiSMR couples an E 2 -loaded PLTG [poly( l -lactide)- co -trimethylene carbonate- co -glycolic acid] backbone with a PDA-EGCG@HAMA coating, enabling rapid EGCG release followed by sustained E 2 delivery. In vitro, BiSMR promoted cell proliferation, migration, angiogenesis, and M2 polarization while suppressing myofibroblast transition. In rat IUA models, BiSMR restored endometrial structure and vascularization, reduced fibrosis, and improved implantation and live birth rates. Proteomics revealed down-regulation of fibrosis- and inflammation-related effectors and restoration of protein biosynthesis and regenerative pathways. BiSMR offers a promising strategy for IUA therapy and fertility restoration.

items.title: Ultrafast Meissner-levitated microrotor
items.abstract: Levitated mechanical systems offer a powerful and flexible platform for the realization of ultralow-noise sensors and tests of fundamental physics. Here, we report the demonstration of a levitated microrotor, consisting of a magnetic microsphere levitated by the Meissner effect at 4.2 kelvin. The rotor reaches rotation frequencies above 2.3 megahertz (138 million revolutions per minute) while exhibiting an exceptionally low damping rate of 4.75 × 10 −7 hertz. Exploiting the linear dependence of friction on the gas density, we demonstrate high-accuracy absolute pressure sensing over a wide range at cryogenic temperature. Last, we detect the thermal torque noise at intermediate pressure by operating the rotor in synchronized mode, resulting in a first preliminary narrowband search for axion-like dark matter. More broadly, the combination of high rotational speed, low temperature, and low thermal torque noise establishes a previously unidentified regime for precision measurements, with direct implications for the detection of extremely weak forces and fields.

items.title: Electron competition in azobenzene programs infection-adaptive antibacterial therapy
items.abstract: Conventional stimulus-responsive antibacterial systems generally operate through binary trigger–activation mechanisms, making them poorly suited to evolving infection microenvironments and thereby contributing to persistent infection and resistance development. Here, we establish an azobenzene-based kinetic regulatory system in which oxygen gradients commonly present in infected tissues continuously program reaction kinetics through electron competition. Oxygen acts as a competing electron acceptor within the reductive reaction network, partitioning electron transfer between azo reduction and oxygen consumption. Substituent electronic structures further reshape reduction propensity, encoding distinct kinetic behaviors. These electronically programmed kinetics translated into adaptive nanoscale dissociation and drug-release profiles: Electron-rich azobenzenes rapidly disassembled under severe hypoxia, whereas electron-withdrawing structures sustained release under mild hypoxia, generating infection state–adaptive antibacterial outputs. Moreover, the same electronic features governing reduction kinetics also reduced the reactivity and toxicity of reductive metabolites. This work establishes electron competition as a strategy for converting environmental gradients into continuous kinetic outputs for adaptive antibacterial therapy.

items.title: Explainable AI identifies recombination and chromatin environment as key predictors of subgenome evolution in maize and Brassica
items.abstract: Polyploidy, or whole genome duplication, reshapes genomes through biased gene loss and regulatory rewiring, yet the drivers of biased fractionation among subgenomes remain unclear. Using maize and Brassica rapa as model allopolyploids, we compiled 60 genomic and epigenomic features in maize and 45 in B. rapa and constructed supervised machine learning models to classify genes by subgenome identity. In both species, eXplainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI) approaches identified recombination rate as the most influential and highly interconnected feature despite nonsignificant mean differences between subgenome groups. Chromosome location, transposon density, and chromatin-associated features, including the proximity of accessible chromatin regions to genes and active histone marks such as H3K9ac and H3K27ac, consistently ranked among the top contributors to subgenome classification. XAI-derived covariation and interaction networks further revealed recombination rate as the central node connecting significant features. Together, these results highlight recombination and chromatin environment as major predictors of subgenome divergence in polyploid genomes.

items.title:
The (amide-)N-methylnicotinamide is a microbe-derived NAD
                    <sup>+</sup>
                    precursor that drives gut stem cell renewal
items.abstract: Nicotinamide Adenine Dinucleotide (NAD) is a critical cellular coenzyme whose decline associates with various chronic and inflammatory diseases. Improved NAD restoration may reduce disease risks and extend healthy lifespan. We report here that certain commensal bacteria including specific probiotic species produce (amide-)N-methylnicotinamide (N-MNA), which is a structural isomer of methylnicotinamide, a nicotinamide degradative metabolite. Patients with gut dysbiosis and inflammation show reduced stool N-MNA. Stable isotope tracing revealed that N-MNA can be rapidly taken up and incorporated into NAD redox reactions by intestinal epithelial cells (IECs) and non-IECs of fruit fly, mouse, and human. Genetic and pharmacological analyses suggest that N-MNA is converted to NAD + via the Preiss-Handler pathway, independent of the salvage pathway. Cell-type-specific ablation or overexpression of SIRT1, an NAD-consuming enzyme, in Drosophila , along with intestinal stem cell (ISC) lineage tracing in mice revealed that systemic N-MNA supplementation promotes ISC regeneration and gut epithelial repair. Compared to known NAD precursors, N-MNA brings a methyl group into host cells, representing a class of microbe-derived NAD precursor that stimulates the tissue regenerative power.

items.title: Combating drug-resistant Aeromonas veronii : Multiomics revealed the antibacterial mechanism of resveratrol
items.abstract: Aeromonas , widely distributed in aquatic ecosystems, is a prevalent fish pathogen and can cause human infections via contaminated aquatic products, polluted water contact, or tainted food consumption. Escalating antibiotic resistance in Aeromonas strains highlights an urgent need for alternative natural antimicrobial agents. This study investigated resveratrol’s antibacterial mechanisms against Aeromonas veronii and evaluated its protective efficacy in hybrid sturgeon. Resveratrol exhibited strong activity [minimum inhibitory concentration: 128 microgram per milliliter (μg/ml), minimum bactericidal concentration: 256 μg/ml], disrupting cell wall/membrane integrity, inducing reactive oxygen species accumulation, inhibiting adenosine 5′-triphosphate synthesis, and down-regulating key metabolic pathways via transcriptomic and metabolomic analyses. In the sturgeon infection model, resveratrol-nanoemulsion notably improved survival, reduced tissue bacterial loads, mitigated oxidative stress and inflammation, and restored intestinal barrier function. These findings confirm resveratrol as a promising antibiotic alternative against A. veronii , with nanoemulsion formulation enhancing its therapeutic efficacy.

items.title: A robust spin-coupled tetraradical via nonalternant design
items.abstract: Polyradicals in open-shell polycyclic hydrocarbons (PHs) offer access to multiple spin states and hold great promise for spintronics and quantum technologies. Here we report a nonalternant, air-stable tetraradical featuring two fused 7-5-7 rings and a strongly correlated singlet ground state. This molecule displays an exceptional tetraradical character ( y 0 = 1.00, y 1 = 0.89) and exhibits long ambient stability ( t 1/2 = 33 days). Comprehensive electronic structure and magnetic response analyses reveal that the spin topology is governed by both ferromagnetic and antiferromagnetic interactions, with robust electron correlation ( J 1 = +321 K, J 2 = −44 K, and J 3 = −29 K). The unique nonalternant design suppresses hyperfine and vibrational decoherence, giving rise to long spin relaxation and coherence time. These findings demonstrate that embedding nonalternant motifs into PH polyradicals provides a powerful strategy to simultaneously promote molecular stability, spin-exchange coupling, and spin robustness—key features for materials in the rising field of quantum information science.

items.title: Prebiotic magnetite enables chirality-magnetic surface feedback
items.abstract: The emergence of biomolecular homochirality requires both an initial symmetry-breaking event and a mechanism to amplify and preserve a chiral imbalance. Magnetic minerals have been shown to function as chiral agents through the chiral-induced spin selectivity (CISS) effect and may have enabled homochirality on early Earth, yet the magnetic properties of magnetite formed under realistic prebiotic conditions remain unexplored. Here, we show that magnetite synthesized through two geochemically plausible pathways—UV-driven photo-oxidation and nitrite-mediated oxidation of Fe(II)—produces particles dominated by single-vortex and multivortex magnetic domain states. Magnetic measurements and electron microscopy confirm that these populations differ markedly from the nano-fabricated thin-film substrates conventionally used in previous CISS experiments. Using three-dimensional micromagnetic simulations, we demonstrate that single-domain and vortex-state grains undergo irreversible, exchange-driven remagnetization when interacting with spin-polarized homochiral compounds. This magnetic irreversibility provides a robust mechanism for storing and reinforcing weak chiral bias, suggesting that prebiotic magnetite could have contributed to the emergence and stabilization of persistent chiral bias on early Earth.

items.title: Spatial proteomics reveals lipid droplet reorganization in symbiotic Paramecium bursaria cells
items.abstract: Endosymbiosis is an important adaptive mechanism allowing organisms to exploit previously inaccessible niches. The flexible relationship between the ciliate Paramecium bursaria and green algae represents a model system for studying early endosymbiosis evolution. However, the mechanisms underlying how P. bursaria cells maintain this endosymbiotic relationship remain unclear. Here, we use mass spectrometry–based proteomics to generate a spatial proteomic atlas of the host P. bursaria cells with and without endosymbionts. This atlas defines the protein composition of the endosymbiont-containing compartment (perialgal vacuole) and reveals pronounced remodeling of host lipid droplets upon symbiosis. Imaging analyses confirm that lipid droplets change in size, morphology, and positioning, accumulating near intracellular algae. Perturbing symbiotic cells with chemical inhibitors of lipid metabolism reduces endosymbiotic algal numbers, revealing a role for lipid droplets in the host-endosymbiont interaction. Our data provide a comprehensive resource for protein localization in P. bursaria cells and elucidate how those cells remodel an existing cellular compartment to maintain endosymbiosis.

items.title: Spatial control of enzyme orientation at the lipid droplet interface enables regio- and chemoselective metabolic flux
items.abstract: Precise spatial control over multienzyme cascade reactions is increasingly recognized as a design lever in synthetic biology for enhancing catalytic performance and directing metabolic flux. By emulating principles of cellular compartmentalization, synthetic scaffolds and engineered interfaces have emerged as powerful platforms to modulate intermediate channeling and reaction efficiency in complex biocatalytic systems. However, robust and spatially defined immobilization of multienzyme assemblies within physicochemically optimal compartments remains challenging because of the dynamic intracellular environment. Here, we reprogram the amphiphilic interface of yeast lipid droplets (LDs) as a programmable scaffold system to support regio- and chemoselective localization of enzymes. Guided by molecular dynamics simulations, we designed LD-anchoring motifs to direct the enzyme orientation at the LD monolayer interface, yielding cytosol-facing or LD inner-facing configurations. Using this designed LD-anchoring motif, we spatially reorganize a trienzyme cascade for prodeoxyviolacein (PDV) biosynthesis across the cytosol-LD interface, facilitating directional conversion of hydrophilic substrates into hydrophobic products. This spatial reorganization substantially improved PDV production by 1300%, achieving 46.25 milligrams per liter. Our approach offers a modular and tunable platform for engineering spatially organized and readily deployable enzyme cascades, opening avenues for biosynthetic catalysis at organellar interfaces.

items.title: Visualizing nanoscopic acoustic mode competition in a van der Waals ferroelectric
items.abstract: Understanding how low-dimensional ferroelectrics respond to ultrafast excitation at nanoscales is essential for controlling energy flow and mechanical functionality in next-generation polar devices, yet the nanoscopic structural response to ultrafast depolarization remains unresolved, obscuring the microscopic pathways of acoustic decoherence and energy dissipation. Here, we spatiotemporally resolve lattice motion in the van der Waals ferroelectric NbOI 2 using combined ultrafast electron microscopy and diffraction, revealing three acoustic phonons: two transverse shear modes and one longitudinal breathing mode. The transverse mode that shears the layers perpendicular to the in-plane polar axis dominates over that along the polar axis, reflecting anisotropic polarization-strain coupling. Real-space mapping uncovers spatially correlated heterogeneity in mode amplitudes and lifetimes. Regions dominated by a single shear mode exhibit significantly longer acoustic lifetimes than multimode regions, suggesting acoustic phonon–phonon scattering as a major source of decoherence. Our results provide a microscopic understanding of ultrafast depolarization-driven acoustic dynamics and spatially heterogeneous energy dissipation in van der Waals ferroelectrics.

items.title: Scaling up chemical recycling: High-yield polyolefin pyrolysis to liquid hydrocarbons using iron single atom catalysts
items.abstract: The chemical recycling of polyolefins (PO) via pyrolysis offers a circular pathway for plastic waste management, yet industrial implementation remains hindered by high energy demands and poor product selectivity. Here, we report an Fe-catalyzed pyrolysis process that achieves 97% PO conversion and a 94% yield of C6 to C35 liquid hydrocarbons. By using a zeolitic imidazolate framework (ZIF)–derived, N-doped porous carbon-supported iron single-atom catalyst (Fe 1 @NC) in combination with a strategic temperature gradient control, we overcome traditional thermolysis limitations. The process was further demonstrated on a kilogram scale, supporting the practical scalability of this catalytic system. Mechanistic investigations reveal that the rate-determining step is an acid base–promoted dehydrogenation of the polymer backbone. Specifically, electronic synergy between the single iron centers and the carbon support stabilizes reactive carbocation intermediates, facilitating their rapid decomposition into high-value olefins and alkanes. These findings provide a scalable and highly efficient catalytic framework for the upcycling of plastic waste into liquid hydrocarbon fractions and chemical feedstocks.

items.title: Adaptive dual-programming magnetic soft robot with lifelike behavior
items.abstract: Magnetic soft robots with embodied intelligence of multimodal motions, environmental perception, and functional decoupling depend on ingenious material arrangement and programmable morphing information introduction. While some efforts have been made, achieving lifelike behaviors for soft robots in system-level strategy remains a notable challenge. Here, we present dual-programming hydrogel-based soft robots (DHSRs) that couple magnetic and anisotropic programming through the spatial arrangement of patterned magnetic skeletons into responsive and structural hydrogel bodies. These DHSRs exhibit programmable exquisite and multicurved structures in three-dimensional (3D) space, environment-adaptive deformation behaviors proved by switching from random jumping on land to regular swimming in water of a fish-like soft robot, and further locomotion-function decoupling capabilities of region-selective cargo delivery in an integrated “locomotion-perception-action” workflow. Our strategy in biomedical potential is exemplified by a ring-like pH-responsive DHSR for gastric ulcer therapy, which integrates multimodal locomotion (rolling, tumbling, and rotating), adaptive matching, and microneedle-mediated penetration. By collaborating with a capsule endoscopy system, we explore the possibility of a wireless and painless diagnostic-therapeutic platform in a pig model. This strategy endows the robot with perception and multitask execution capabilities, highlighting a promising route for the intelligent evolution of soft robots across diverse application domains.

items.title: Age reshapes selection on melanoma driver mutations
items.abstract: Aging is a major risk factor for melanoma.
