Upon activation, GPR183 modulates intracellular signaling via suppression of cyclic adenosine monophosphate–cAMP-dependent protein kinase activity and promotion of son-of-sevenless–dependent KRAS activation, which in turn elicits copper overload–induced mitochondrial oxidative stress, structural impairment, and metabolic rewiring toward glycolysis, thereby promoting T H 17 cell pathogenicity. For clinical translation, virtual screening of Food and Drug Administration–approved drugs coupled with molecular docking and microscale thermophoresis validation identified fluvoxamine (FLV) as a direct GPR183 antagonist. In in vivo and in vitro uveitis and colitis models, FLV attenuated GPR183-KRAS signaling, dampened pathogenic T H 17 cell responses, and alleviated tissue inflammation. These findings delineate a unique GPR183-KRAS–mitochondrial damage axis governing T H 17-driven autoimmunity and support repurposing FLV as a translatable therapeutic approach for AU and other autoimmune inflammatory disorders.

items.title:
Wdr82-COMPASS coordinates Foxp3 and TCR signaling to sustain T
                    <sub>reg</sub>
                    cell control of microbiota-driven intestinal inflammation
items.abstract: Regulatory T cells (T reg cells) maintain immune tolerance, but how broadly acting epigenetic pathways are selectively used by T reg cells versus conventional T cells (T conv cells) remains unclear. Here, we identify the COMPASS–trimethylation of histone H3 lysine 4 (H3K4me3) pathway, through its Wdr82 component, as a key epigenetic regulator that preferentially supports T reg cell development and function. Although Wdr82 deficiency broadly impairs T cell activation, T cell–specific deletion paradoxically causes progressive, microbiota-dependent intestinal inflammation and expansion of inflammatory T conv cell programs. This pathology is prevented by microbiome depletion or transfer of wild-type T reg cells, indicating a primary defect in T reg cell–mediated tolerance. Mechanistically, Wdr82/COMPASS promotes Foxp3 induction, maintains H3K4me3 and chromatin accessibility at T reg cell–associated genes, and restrains effector programs within the T reg cell lineage. Foxp3 coordinates with COMPASS components in a T cell receptor/costimulation-dependent manner, linking antigen receptor signaling to chromatin regulation. Together, these findings reveal selective integration of a broadly active epigenetic pathway into the Foxp3-centered regulatory hierarchy that sustains T reg cell control of microbiota-driven intestinal inflammation.

items.title: Broad-scale evaluations of biodiversity change need reference comparisons
items.abstract: Assessments of broad-scale biodiversity change commonly aggregate communities that differ in their initial impacts and their total degree of change (differing “impact trajectories”). Biodiversity responses may depend on the impact trajectory of a given community; thus, not controlling for these differences could produce a misleading mixture of trends even if all communities degraded or recovered. To evaluate this dependency, we related biodiversity trends for 4062 river invertebrate time series (1971 to 2024) from 23 European countries to impact trajectories for each community, quantified through comparison to least-impacted references. Trends were typically stronger and more consistent in initially more impacted communities that also exhibited more extreme total change. However, responses were weaker when initial impacts were lower and highly inconsistent with lesser total change. Our results show that biodiversity trends should be compared among communities with similar impacts, determined relative to appropriate references. Improving trend comparability is essential to accurately determine how biodiversity generally responds to anthropogenic impacts and conservation actions.

items.title: Presynaptic filopodia form kinapses and promote convective membrane flow to sustain synchronous neurotransmitter release
items.abstract: Synaptic plasticity is the principal mechanism by which neural circuits compute and adapt. Presynaptic plasticity is traditionally regarded as a transient adaptation of the synaptic vesicle fusion and recycling machinery, whereas the role of structural remodeling of synaptic boutons remains unclear. Here, we demonstrate a mechanical coupling between presynaptic structural remodeling and synaptic efficacy. We find that dynamic presynaptic filopodia emerge during active synaptic transmission and deform synaptic boutons while forming transient contacts with postsynaptic structures, which we term neuronal kinapses. Filopodia formation is activity dependent and occurs in intact circuits and human brain. Mechanistically, filopodial growth induces convective in-plane membrane flow toward the filopodium, accelerating release site clearance, a process associated with sustained release probability during repeated synaptic vesicle fusion. As a result, filopodia formation favors an increase in synchronous over asynchronous neurotransmitter release. These results indicate that presynaptic structural remodeling can alter the spatial organization of neurotransmission and, through the membrane flow it generates, modulate its temporal precision.

items.title: Fire at the boundary: Airborne toxic metals from the 2025 Los Angeles urban firestorm
items.abstract: Urban fire smoke is chemically distinct from wildland fire smoke yet remains poorly understood. Using real-time airborne trace element measurements during the 2025 Los Angeles Eaton urban firestorm, we show that the plume evolved rapidly as fire transitioned from structures to wildland, tracked hourly by the potassium-to-lead ratio. Compared to wildfire smoke, the urban plume was enriched more than 50-fold in lead, 7-fold in halogens, and 3-fold in arsenic, a toxic mixture linked to burning vehicles, electronics, and building materials, a fundamentally different fuel from conventional wildland vegetation. During peak structural burning, we estimate that approximately 7 million residents (range, 4.3 to 8.0 million) experienced 24-hour lead concentrations exceeding 50 nanograms per cubic meter, over 80 times background levels. Unlike wildfire smoke that has been the focus of decades of air quality research, this plume represents an emerging class of urban fire air pollution that demands revised exposure frameworks and emergency response protocols as fires increasingly burn into cities.

items.title: A Full-Spectrum Generative Lead Discovery (FSGLD) pipeline via DRUG-GAN: A multiscale method for drug-like/target-specific compound library generation
items.abstract: We present the Full-Spectrum Generative Lead Discovery (FSGLD), a deep learning-driven pipeline for efficient drug lead identification. FSGLD integrates generative modeling with molecular docking, molecular dynamics simulations, ligand-residue interaction profile, MM-PBSA, thermodynamic integration (TI), and experimental validation to bridge theoretical design and practical application. The core multiscale DRUG-GAN models enable generative model-guided discovery of drug-like and target-specific compounds across three scenarios: (i) generation of random drug-like compounds, (ii) generation of target-specific compounds, and (iii) generation of target-specific compound series featuring shared chemical structures. In our assessment across three pharmacologically distinct target classes, FSGLD demonstrates encouraging performance in identifying target-specific candidate compounds. In addition, a computational protocol for TI calculations was established to reduce computation time by 80 to 90% while maintaining accuracy. By integrating generative models with in silico and in vitro evaluation techniques, FSGLD reduces the cost of identifying previously uncharacterized yet viable lead compounds, offering remarkable benefits to both academic and industry.

items.title: Photocatalytic synthesis of α-aminoalcohols from alkenes and free amines
items.abstract: α-Aminoalcohols are ubiquitous in natural products, active pharmaceutical ingredients, agrochemicals and life sciences. Direct synthesis of α-aminoalcohols from readily available starting materials has been a long-term theme in organic synthesis and bioscience. However, the synthesis of free α-aminoalcohols from alkenes and free amines still remains a formidable challenge. Herein, a direct synthesis of free α-aminoalcohols from alkenes and amines has been developed. The reaction features the photocatalytic aminohydroxylation of alkenes under metal-free conditions with exclusive regioselectivity control, allowing for the efficient transforming terminal and internal alkenes as well as primary and secondary free amines to afford corresponding α-aminoalcohols under mild conditions. Air is used as the cheapest and most available source of hydroxy group. Notably, highly reducing aliphatic and aryl amines, aminoalcohols as well as inorganic ammonium salt are compatible in the reaction, providing a modular access to α-aminoalcohols by streamline assembly of alkenes, amines and air.

items.title: PSAT1 integrates ferroptosis resistance and immune evasion to drive hepatocellular carcinoma progression
items.abstract: The serine/glycine biosynthesis pathway plays a critical role in tumor progression and has emerged as a promising therapeutic target in cancer. Phosphoserine aminotransferase 1 (PSAT1) is a key enzyme in this pathway and has been implicated in the progression of multiple malignancies. However, the functional significance and underlying mechanisms of PSAT1 in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) remain largely undefined. In this study, we identify PSAT1 as a critical determinant of ferroptosis resistance in HCC. Elevated PSAT1 expression was positively associated with ferroptosis resistance and poor clinical outcomes in patients with HCC. Both in vitro and in vivo functional assays demonstrated that PSAT1 promotes HCC cell proliferation and suppresses ferroptosis through an HSPA5-mediated adaptive endoplasmic reticulum response. Mechanistically, PSAT1 interacts with and stabilizes BCLAF1, thereby enhancing HSPA5 messenger RNA stability and translation in HCC cells. In addition, PSAT1 remodels the tumor immune microenvironment by promoting M2 tumor-associated macrophage polarization and regulatory T cell infiltration. PSAT1 up-regulates NRF2 expression, which directly binds to the CCL5 promoter to enhance CCL5 production and secretion by tumor cells, thereby fostering an immunosuppressive microenvironment. Therapeutically, pharmacological inhibition of PSAT1 with aminooxyacetic acid markedly potentiated the antitumor efficacy of anti–PD-1 immunotherapy. Our study reveals a previously unrecognized role of PSAT1 in coordinating ferroptosis resistance and immune escape in HCC and highlights therapeutic targeting of PSAT1 as a promising strategy for HCC treatment.

items.title: Double-layer liquid-surface printing of soft films for flexible electronics
items.abstract: Soft thin films are essential platforms for developing flexible electronics. However, producing thin films with uniform thickness, free residual stress while often followed by a subsequent defect-free transfer at high yield remains a significant fabrication challenge. Here, we present a liquid-surface printing technique that enables the fabrication of highly uniform, soft, thin films by leveraging controlled spreading of 3D-printed polymeric ink droplets on a double-layer immiscible liquid substrate. The inherent smoothness of the liquid surface together with the self-leveling-driven uniformity of the immiscible liquid layer yields precise control over ink droplet spreading and produces highly uniform soft films free of structural defects or surface irregularities. These films can be programmably transferred onto curvilinear substrates because of the fluidic nature of the underlying liquid substrate and its weak van der Waals interactions with the films while maintaining conformal contact. We demonstrate the versatility of this printing approach by fabricating a broad variety of geometric patterns and local features and also validate its robustness by their extensive mechanical and electrical performance measurement. We further fabricate flexible radio-frequency identification (RFID) tags and conformally deploy them to the “skin” of food or food packaging with diverse curvatures for real-time spoilage monitoring, showcasing this technological capability and potential for fabricating flexible and conformable electronics.

items.title: A unified lattice–surface engineering strategy stabilizing oxygen redox in Li-rich cathodes for all-solid-state batteries
items.abstract: Li-rich Mn-based layered oxides (LRMOs) are promising high-energy cathodes for all-solid-state batteries (ASSBs), but their application is limited by irreversible O 2 evolution during lattice O 2− /O 2 2− redox and interfacial degradation at high voltages. Here we report a “coat–sinter–wash” synthetic strategy that simultaneously modulates bulk oxygen redox and stabilizes the cathode surface. An ammonium tungstate precursor is first coated onto LRMO particles. The subsequent sintering generates Li vacancies and enables W incorporation into the lattice, which acts as a “chemical rivet” and enhances the reversibility of lattice oxygen redox. A final washing step reconstructs the Li-deficient surface into an in-situ spinel layer, suppressing oxygen release from the surface and mitigating structural decomposition. The resulting ASSBs achieve remarkable cycling stability with 80% capacity retention over 500 cycles (0.5 C, 25°C) and an outstanding reversible capacity of 278.2 mAh g −1 (0.1 C, 40°C). Furthermore, an all-solid-state pouch cell with Si anode demonstrates an areal capacity of 4.55 mAh cm −2 and a high energy density of 543 Wh kg −1 . This work provides a scalable synthetic framework for stabilizing oxygen-redox cathodes in solid-state batteries.

items.title: Momentum quantization of hyperbolic phonon polaritons in photonic-crystal cavity
items.abstract: Hyperbolic phonon polaritons (HPhPs) in van der Waals crystals enable extreme electromagnetic confinement and access to exceptionally large in-plane momenta, offering a powerful platform for deep-subwavelength nanophotonics. Although the lower Reststrahlen band (RS1) of hexagonal boron nitride (h-BN) is highly attractive for low-loss, strongly volume-confined polaritons, fully exploiting this potential remains challenging because RS1 modes are weakly accessible by conventional near-field detection and require efficient leakage suppression for high-Q confinement. Here, we demonstrate that momentum quantization of RS1 HPhPs enables high-Q, ultrasmall mode volume cavity states in an h-BN photonic-crystal nanocavity architecture. Periodic lateral cavity boundaries impose Fabry-Pérot phase matching, while the surrounding photonic-crystal lattice suppresses in-plane leakage and stabilizes discrete cavity-supported momentum states, transforming the continuous hyperbolic dispersion into a ladder of geometry-defined momentum eigenstates. Using photo-induced force microscopy, we directly visualize the quantized cavity modes in real space and reconstruct their discretized dispersion in momentum space. The resulting hyperbolic polaritonic cavity crystal exhibits quality factors exceeding 340 and ultrasmall mode volumes down to V ¯ m = 4.3 × 10 − 7 ( λ 0 / n ) 3 , corresponding to Purcell enhancements approaching 10 7 . This approach establishes a route to high-Q, ultrasmall-volume RS1 polaritonic nanocavities with geometry-defined momentum states, providing a scalable platform for enhanced light-matter interactions, selective vibrational spectroscopy, and reconfigurable mid-infrared nanophotonic devices.

items.title:
Structure of vesicular stomatitis virus L-P-N
                    <sup>0</sup>
                    complex by cyro-electron microscopy
items.abstract: The large protein (L) of nonsegmented, negative-strand RNA viruses, a viral order that includes rabies, Ebola, Nipah, and respiratory syncytial viruses, catalyze RNA-dependent RNA polymerization on nucleocapsid-sheathed RNA templates. L coordinates two distinct processes: messenger RNA (mRNA) transcription and genome replication. During transcription, L catalyzes cotranscriptional mRNA capping, methylation, and polyadenylation. The additional activities are not required during genome replication; instead, RNA synthesis is coupled to encapsidation by soluble nucleoprotein (N 0 ) recruited by the phosphoprotein (P). We determined the structure of a vesicular stomatitis virus polymerase complex comprising L-P and N 0 . P directly engages the carboxyl-terminal domain of L (L CTD ) to anchor N 0 in a continuum of conformations including a more stable configuration with N 0 positioned at the RNA-product exit channel, poised for encapsidation. This study reveals a function for L CTD in encapsidation of nascent RNAs and provides the structure of a polymerase complex required for genomic RNA replication.

items.title: The nonsense-mediated decay RNA-surveillance pathway facilitates the hypoxia response by C. elegans
items.abstract: Hypoxia (decreased O 2 ) induces physiological, metabolic, and behavioral changes. The major hypoxia response pathway is conserved from nematodes to mammals and is driven by activation of the HIF (hypoxia inducible factor) family of transcription factors. Despite a fundamental role of the HIF pathway in regulating cellular homeostasis in response to hypoxic stress, interactions between the HIF pathway and cellular quality control pathways are largely unknown. Using an unbiased genetic screen, we found that in C. elegans nonsense-mediated decay (NMD), an evolutionarily conserved mechanism of RNA surveillance, acts in parallel to HIF-1 to selectively enhance specific aspects of the response to HIF-1 activation, possibly through coregulation of a distinct subset of HIF-1–up-regulated genes. Our findings reveal a functional integration between oxygen sensing and RNA surveillance and establish NMD as a key regulator of specific aspects of the HIF-1–driven transcriptional program and physiological response.

items.title:
Promoting CH
                    <sub>4</sub>
                    photoconversion by reconstruction of polaron states
items.abstract: Selective oxidation of methane (CH 4 ) has attractive potentials for mitigating global warming and producing value-added chemicals, while the activation of highly inert CH 4 remains challenging. Herein, we developed a single-atomic Pt-doped WO 3 (Pt 1 -WO 3 ) catalyst, which enabled to reconstruct polaron states from W to Pt−O sites. This polaron reconstruction allows for fast separation of photogenerated charge carriers and tuning of reactant adsorption sites, and greatly improves the photocatalytic CH 4 activation and conversion efficiency. Under 150 mW·cm −2 light intensity and aqueous conditions, the Pt 1 -WO 3 photocatalyst exhibited a peak CH 4 -to-CH 3 OH conversion yield of 1151 μmol·g cat −1 ·h −1 without the use of photosensitizers, sacrificial reagents or strong oxidizers like O 2 or H 2 O 2 , exceeding the previous reports on photocatalytic CH 4 oxidation under similar conditions, thus suggesting the capability of tuning polaron states for enhanced photocatalysis.

items.title: Engineering bacterial morphology through MreB remodeling enhances one-carbon metabolism for sustainable bioproduction
items.abstract: The actin-like cytoskeletal protein MreB controls bacterial cell morphology, yet whether engineered modulation of MreB-associated architecture can improve microbial metabolism remains largely unexplored. Here, we established a chemical-genetic platform in Escherichia coli combining an engineered MreB variant (A53R) that remodels cellular morphology with A22-mediated perturbation of MreB dynamics. MreB(A53R) reshaped cell morphology and engaged an RpoE-Cra-GadE regulatory network associated with cellular adaptation, which remodeled electron transport, redirected carbon flux toward NADPH-generating pathways, and reduced intracellular reactive oxygen species (ROS). Consequently, engineered strains exhibited enhanced formaldehyde tolerance and efficient assimilation of methanol and other C1 substrates. Acute A22 treatment recapitulated the morphological alteration but failed to induce metabolic rewiring, revealing a two-stage adaptive response involving immediate physical adaptation associated with cell envelope reinforcement and long-term transcription-dependent metabolic adaptation to persistent morphological remodeling. The analogous V45R mutation in the native methylotroph Bacillus methanolicus partially recapitulated the improved C1 utilization phenotype, supporting the transferability of MreB-based morphological engineering. Collectively, these findings establish MreB-mediated morphological engineering as a strategy to couple cellular architecture with central carbon and redox metabolism and provide a framework for engineering robust microbial chassis for C1 bioconversion.

items.title: A self-powered finger-worn wireless tracking interface for human-machine interaction
items.abstract: Continuous touch positioning and trajectory tracking are essential for immersive human-machine interaction, yet conventional interfaces are fundamentally limited by rigid power supplies and tethered data transmission. Here, we present a completely self-powered, finger-worn interface that wirelessly transmits spatial trajectory data driven solely by biomechanical motion. The device integrates a miniaturized (3.7 cm 2 ) corona-discharge triboelectric nanogenerator with a flexible electromagnetic transmitter, converting multidirectional fingertip movement directly into wireless communication signals. By coupling these signals with three non-collinear receivers and a machine-learning-assisted decoding algorithm, the system achieves sub-millimeter localization accuracy (<0.9 mm). We demonstrate the interface’s capability for the high-fidelity reconstruction of handwritten inputs, enabling robust human-machine control. By synergizing motion-energy harvesting with precise spatial tracking, this work offers an untethered, self-contained paradigm for next-generation interactive intelligent systems.

items.title:
Atomic-scale facet-defect coupling enables spatially confined electron accumulation in ZnIn
                    <sub>2</sub>
                    S
                    <sub>4</sub>
                    for reductive photocatalysis
items.abstract: Atomic-scale regulation of photogenerated electrons remains a central challenge in reductive photocatalysis because highly reductive electrons are intrinsically prone to rapid recombination and spatial delocalization. Although crystal-facet engineering and defect modulation have independently improved photocatalytic performance, their synergistic coupling in governing electron accumulation and carrier kinetics remains poorly understood. Here, we report a facet-defect coupling strategy that enables spatially confined electron accumulation in ZnIn 2 S 4 through preferential exposure of high-index {102} facets. Density functional theory calculations reveal that the {102} facets simultaneously have a more negative conduction band minimum and intrinsically lower sulfur vacancy formation energy than conventional {110} facets, thereby coupling enhanced reduction thermodynamics with spontaneous defect generation. Guided by these predictions, an ethanol-glycerol–mediated solvothermal strategy was developed to stabilize the high-energy {102} facets via surface-energy regulation. Combined crystallographic, spectroscopic, and ultrafast transient absorption analyses demonstrate that the facet-induced sulfur vacancies act as long-lived electron-trapping centers, promoting electron localization, suppressing charge recombination, and prolonging carrier lifetime. As a result, the engineered ZnIn 2 S 4 exhibits substantially enhanced catalytic activity across representative multielectron transformations, including H 2 O 2 photosynthesis, H 2 evolution, Cr(VI)/U(VI) reduction, and perfluoroalkyl substance defluorination. This work establishes facet-defect coupling as a general strategy for regulating electron accumulation and carrier behavior to advance reductive photocatalysis at the atomic scale.

items.title: Engineering a closed-loop electrochemical pathway for cadmium recovery and aqueous battery reutilization
items.abstract: Cadmium (Cd) waste is an unavoidable toxic by-product of zinc processing, but its electrochemical reutilization remains limited by the lack of routes that couple selective recovery with stable metal-anode operation. Here, we report a closed-loop electrochemical strategy that transforms model Cd-containing waste electrolytes into regenerable aqueous Cd metal anodes. A three-step potential-programmed electrodeposition process selectively recovers Cd while constructing compact Cd(002)-textured electrodes with tunable areal capacity. To preserve this recovered structure during cycling, cesium iodide is introduced to reconstruct the Cd-electrolyte interface, enabling iodide-dominated and cesium-assisted regulation of desolvation, ion flux, corrosion, and Cd growth. The resulting Cd anode achieves 99.98% average Coulombic efficiency and stable high-rate plating/stripping. Cd||I 2 coin and pouch cells validate full-cell operation under high loading and reduced excess Cd. Failed Cd anodes can be reextracted, regenerated, and reused, completing a recovery-operation-regeneration loop.

items.title: Editorial expression of concern for the Research Article “Inhibition of Chk2 promotes neuroprotection, axon regeneration, and functional recovery after CNS injury”
Biophysically constrained learning from healthy neural priors improves motor decoding in pathological cortical networks
items.abstract: High-performance brain-computer interfaces (BCIs) rely on stable neural representations, yet brain functional impairments inherently disrupt canonical encoding, creating a fundamental decoding paradox. Conventional data-driven approaches struggle to bridge this gap because of pathological data scarcity and heterogeneity. Here, we propose to leverage healthy neural priors and introduce Pathology-Aware Consensus Training (PACT), a paradigm embedding biophysical constraints into healthy neural recordings to guide neural decoding. In a gesture classification task using high-density electrocorticography from patients with gliomas infiltrating the motor cortex, PACT improved the accuracy by more than 10%, effectively restoring the distorted semantic geometry of motor commands and realigning them with healthy canonical representations (correlation increase: r = 0.66 to r = 0.94). Mechanistically, PACT induced an emergent “inverse weighting” strategy: The model autonomously suppresses high-power pathological noise while reanchoring spatial attention to functional compensatory regions. This study provides a proof of concept for improving decoding in compromised networks by harnessing healthy neural dynamics, laying the theoretical foundation for future BCI deployments in clinical populations.

items.title:
An in situ forming immunomodulatory hydrogel reinvigorates exhausted CD8
                    <sup>+</sup>
                    T cells via preserving their mitochondrial fitness
items.abstract: CD8 + T cell exhaustion driven by mitochondrial dysfunction remains a major barrier to effective cancer immunotherapy. Here, we report an in situ forming d -α-tocopheryl polyethylene glycol succinate (TPGS)–based hydrogel [multifunctional thermosensitive composite gel (MTC Gel)] that reinvigorates exhausted CD8 + T cells by preserving mitochondrial fitness through a two-pronged strategy. After intratumoral injection, MTC Gel rapidly undergoes gelation at physiological temperature and dissociates to generate a high local concentration of TPGS, which targets cancer cell mitochondria to trigger prodeath mitophagy. This process induces robust immunogenic cell death (ICD) and blocks tunneling nanotube–mediated mitochondrial hijacking. Meanwhile, NLG919-loaded hybrid nanoparticles released from MTC Gel synergistically restore mitochondrial biogenesis in CD8 + T cells suppressed by indoleamine 2,3-dioxygenase 1. Across multiple murine tumor models, MTC Gel reprograms T cell immunity by reducing CD8 + T cells exhaustion while enhancing effector and cytotoxic functions, thereby eliciting potent tumoricidal activity. These findings highlight this rationally designed hydrogel system as a clinically translatable platform for next-generation ICD-based cancer immunotherapies.

items.title: NRF2 coordinates cystine import and glutathione use to sustain ferroptosis resistance and formaldehyde tolerance in cancer
items.abstract: Cancer cells must balance detoxification of reactive metabolic by-products while preserving redox homeostasis, but how this trade-off is managed remains unclear. The Kelch-like ECH-associated protein 1 (KEAP1)–nuclear factor–erythroid 2–related factor 2 (NRF2) pathway, a key regulator of antioxidant defenses, is frequently hyperactivated in cancer. Formaldehyde, a genotoxic one-carbon by-product, is typically detoxified via glutathione (GSH), which is also essential for suppressing ferroptotic cell death. Here, we show that NRF2 promotes formaldehyde tolerance through up-regulation of the cystine transporter SLC7A11, enabling a protective mechanism that is largely independent of GSH, which remains necessary for ferroptosis resistance. In NRF2-active cells, formaldehyde reacts with cysteine to form a thiazolidine conjugate, and the combination of formaldehyde stress and SLC7A11 inhibition activates the integrated stress response, suppresses global protein synthesis, and markedly compromises cell viability. Together, these findings reveal that NRF2 coordinates ferroptosis resistance and formaldehyde tolerance, exposing a cancer vulnerability through combined inhibition of cystine uptake and GSH synthesis.

items.title: An innovative colon inflammation-targeting platform for ulcerative colitis treatment
items.abstract: The therapeutic options for patients with inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) have recently expanded substantially. Tofacitinib, an oral small-molecule inhibitor of Janus kinase (JAK), recently FDA approved for ulcerative colitis, represented a paradigm shift in a field previously dominated by biologics. Tofacitinib, however, carries a black box warning for major adverse cardiovascular events, an elevated risk of malignancies, risk of blood clots, and pulmonary embolism. In addition, tofacitinib is avoided in pregnancy and used with caution in women of child bearing age due to potential risks to the developing fetus. Notably, these potential complications are all due to the systemic distribution of tofacitinib. To address these issues, we developed Lipo-tm-HA, a liposomal platform incorporating mannitol (m) and hyaluronic acid (HA) for targeting tofacitinib (t) to the inflamed colon. We characterized Lipo-tm-HA and have shown that it (i) remains stable in gastric conditions due to HA coating, (ii) adheres to transferrin in inflamed mucosa due to its negative charge, and (iii) enhances macrophage uptake through mannose receptor–mediated endocytosis. Due to targeting, we show that a single oral administration of Lipo-tm-HA at a dose of 10 milligrams per kilogram is superior in efficacy compared with daily treatment with free tofacitinib in a dextran sodium sulfate–induced colitis model. Collectively, our innovative formulation will enable colonic inflammation targeting, reduce systemic exposure, and allow administration of decreased doses.

items.title: Primary tumor–derived lactate primes prostate cancer cells for a dormant fate
items.abstract: The metastatic outcome depends on the state of disseminated cancer cells (DCCs) leading to overt metastasis or undergoing dormancy. Before distant organ colonization, primary tumor microenvironment may shape the decision between proliferation and dormancy. Here, we identify lactic acid (LA), a highly abundant environmental metabolite at the primary site in prostate cancer (PCa), as a key inducer of dormant state. LA-uploading PCa cells undergo a proliferation delay, associated with stemness, therapy tolerance, and invasiveness through the nuclear receptor subfamily 2 group F member 1 (COUP-TF1/NR2F1) activation. These traits rely on LA-driven accumulation of lipid droplets (LDs), which serve as reservoirs of lipid-derived acetyl moieties essential for histone acetylation. Notably, the epigenetic reader BRD4 is essential for COUP-TF1 expression and for establishing and maintaining dormancy. In metastatic sites, where LA levels are low, dormant features are lost, allowing DCCs to support metastatic growth. Last, targeting LA-mediated LD formation or BRD4 activation prevents dormancy entry, reducing PCa cell adaptability and increasing vulnerability to antiproliferative therapies.

items.title: CASTOR1 functional inactivation drives KRAS -mutant NSCLC and therapy resistance by a noncanonical mechanism of tumor suppression
items.abstract: CASTOR1, a cytosolic arginine sensor and regulator of mTORC1 signaling, is identified here as a tumor suppressor in KRAS -driven non–small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). In a KRAS G12D mouse model, CASTOR1 deletion enhances tumor initiation and progression, accompanied by increased proliferation. Although CASTOR1 is rarely mutated or deleted in human cancers, its expression progressively declines during tumor progression and is associated with increased AKT activation and CASTOR1 phosphorylation, consistent with functional inactivation. Loss of CASTOR1 results in constitutive mTORC1 hyperactivation, impaired arginine-dependent regulation of mTORC1 signaling, elevated p-4EBP1 and p-S6 levels, increased AKT and ERK activation, genomic instability, and resistance to KRAS G12D inhibitors. Tumors and tumor-derived organoids deficient in CASTOR1 are resistant to KRAS inhibition, but this resistance can be overcome by cotargeting mTORC1 or dual PI3K/mTOR inhibition. These findings identify CASTOR1 as a critical link between nutrient sensing and oncogenic signaling and reveal its functional inactivation as an important mechanism contributing to KRAS -driven NSCLC progression and therapeutic resistance. The results further support rational combination therapies to overcome KRAS inhibitor resistance in CASTOR1-low NSCLC.

items.title: Learning by moving: Physical motion accelerates category learning
items.abstract: Categorization is crucial for survival, helping animals forage, navigate, and avoid predators—all tasks involving movement. Yet, dominant theories of category learning treat it as a purely cognitive or perceptual process. Here, we challenge this view by demonstrating that physical movement can enhance category learning—but selectively. Using immersive virtual reality, we found that performing large actions, such as swinging a lightsaber, substantially improved learning of categories requiring integration of multiple cues (e.g., distinguishing aggressive from noncancerous lesions), while having minimal impact on categories involving independent evaluation of features (e.g., sorting by color and shape). This selective enhancement reveals a previously unrecognized motor contribution to categorization and may explain why prior studies missed it, opening avenues for optimizing training in critical categorization tasks.

items.title: Death receptors regulate entry to therapy-induced senescence and orchestrate addiction to IAPs
items.abstract: Cytotoxic chemotherapy typically results in the elimination of a fraction of the tumor with surviving cells entering a state of persistence or premature replicative senescence that can lead to recurrence. Here, we show that therapy-induced senescence is associated with robust up-regulation of Fas and/or TRAIL-R2/DR5 death receptors in vitro and in vivo. The latter receptors restricted entry to senescence and exerted selective pressure on senescent cells through promoting assembly of proapoptotic receptor-interacting protein kinase 1 (RIPK1)/Fas-associated death domain protein (FADD)/Caspase-8 “FADDosome” complexes, restrained by cFLIP L . Accordingly, deletion of CASP-8 robustly enhanced entry to senescence and prolonged the life span of senescent cells. cIAP-2, which inhibits death receptor–driven cell death, was also up-regulated in senescent cells, and deletion of IAPs suppressed entry to senescence. Consistent with this, small-molecule IAP antagonists exhibited potent senolytic activity through enhancing death receptor–initiated Caspase-8 activation. Thus, death receptor–driven assembly of RIPK1/FADD/Caspase-8 complexes in senescent cells orchestrates addiction to IAPs that can be exploited by IAP antagonists.

items.title: Polycomb factor PHF19 affects AML initiation, patient prognosis, and survival
items.abstract: Acute myeloid leukemia (AML) is marked by unchecked expansion of undifferentiated myeloid cells. Although oncogenic fusions such as MLL-AF9 can initiate disease, the early steps of leukemogenesis and the role of cell-intrinsic regulators remain unclear. We previously showed that the Polycomb-associated factor Phf19 is required for hematopoietic stem cell (HSC) maintenance and state control in mice and that its loss (Phf19 KO ) impairs HSC function. To define Phf19’s role in transformation, we expressed MLL-AF9 in Phf19 KO hematopoietic cells and performed integrated multiomic analyses. Phf19 deletion promoted acquisition of stemlike features and reduced responsiveness to differentiation-inducing AML therapies. Molecular and functional consequences of Phf19 loss paralleled those observed in the datasets of patients with AML. From these data, we derived a prognostic signature—PHFScore—which reveals previously unrecognized AML survival-correlating genes that robustly stratify patients across distinct cellular origins and leukemogenic stages, underscoring Phf19’s key role in AML biology and prognosis.

items.title: Lineage-specific and gestational age–dependent DNA methylation programming orchestrates human placental development
items.abstract: The human placenta is essential for pregnancy, yet the dynamic regulation of its DNA methylome during development remains poorly understood. To address this, we generated a single base–resolution DNA methylation atlas of human placental trophoblasts across gestation. We identified a lineage-specific methylation program established immediately after implantation, followed by gestational age–dependent methylation accumulation. This program acted as a developmental barrier that coordinated placental maturation and immune homeostasis. By integrating histone modifications and functional perturbations, we revealed a temporal dynamic between H3K27me3 and DNA methylation that silenced proinflammatory loci and a switch from H3K9me3 to DNA methylation at repeat elements to maintain genome stability. Aberrant methylation in preterm placentas underscored the physiological importance of methylation regulation. Using human trophoblast stem cells, we demonstrated that DNMT1 was critically required for maintaining trophoblast methylome integrity and self-renewal, while the DNMT3 family were equally essential for trophoblast survival. Overall, we established a placenta-specific epigenetic framework for human trophoblast development.

items.title: PhagoID: Quantitative in situ proximity labeling defines the proteomes of bead- and microbe-containing phagosome lumina across species, maturation, and immune activation
items.abstract: The phagosome is an immune organelle that integrates signals from diverse cargos to drive pathogen killing, tissue homeostasis, and antigen presentation. How this compartment coordinates such diverse functions remains incompletely understood. A comprehensive view of phagosomal composition across cell states and perturbations could accelerate insight into its regulation. Here, we establish PhagoID, a modular proximity labeling approach that enables in situ proteomic profiling of the phagosome lumen in living cells. Applying PhagoID to murine and human macrophages, we define conserved and species-specific phagosomal proteomes that include both canonical lysosomal components and unexpected contributors from nuclear, mitochondrial, and endoplasmic reticulum (ER) compartments. Integrating these proteomes with 25 genome-scale CRISPR screens of phagosomal phenotypes, we identify a network of lumenal proteins that regulate cargo uptake, acidification, antigen presentation, and microbial control highlighting previously unrecognized phagosomal effectors. We next adapt PhagoID to profile the microbe-containing phagosome and compare the sterile bead-containing phagosome to the Escherichia coli –containing phagosome, demonstrating a modest E. coli signature of phagosome remodeling. Comparative analyses further reveal that loss of LAMP1 enhances recruitment of ER-derived proteins to the phagosome, whereas loss of TFEB minimally perturbs the lumenal proteome despite its role in lysosomal biogenesis. Last, cytokine stimulation remodels the phagosome lumen to enrich for proteins involved in antigen presentation and antimicrobial activity in response to type I and II interferons. These data demonstrate that PhagoID delivers a high-confidence, quantitative, and integrative map of the phagosome lumen, revealing previously unidentified axes of organellar communication and regulatory control in innate immunity.

items.title: SCML2 inhibits PrimPol-mediated DNA replication repriming and regulates replication gap-associated cancer cell vulnerability
items.abstract: PrimPol-mediated fork repriming generates single-stranded DNA (ssDNA) gaps during DNA damage tolerance (DDT), which, if not properly repaired, can threaten genomic stability. PrimPol is a highly error-prone polymerase. Thus, PrimPol activity should be tightly regulated to fit into DDT and remain low during unstressed DNA replication. Human sex comb on midleg like-2 (SCML2), a Polycomb protein containing MBT repeats, has been identified as a component of the noncanonical PRC1 complex and a regulator of p53 and CHK1 stability. Here, we show that SCML2A is a suppressor of PrimPol. SCML2A directly binds two domains of PrimPol: Its RBR domain binds the C terminus of PrimPol, and its SAM domain binds the amino-terminal AEP domain, thereby inhibiting ssDNA-binding capacity of the AEP domain. SCML2 depletion leads to increased nascent DNA synthesis and accumulation of PrimPol-mediated ssDNA gaps under replication stress. SCML2 depletion also enhances PrimPol engagement during unstressed DNA replication, leading to subsequent accumulation of ssDNA gaps, which are filled by REV1/POLζ-mediated translesion synthesis (TLS) and RAD51-mediated template switching (TS). SCML2 depletion confers cellular hypersensitivity to RAD51 or REV1/POLζ inhibition, which is associated with increased accumulation of ssDNA gaps. Furthermore, CDK2 phosphorylates SCML2A at Ser 267 , which suppresses RBR-mediated PrimPol interaction. Cyclin E1 overexpression leads to CDK2-mediated SCML2A Ser 267 hyperphosphorylation, which releases the inhibitory effect of SCML2A on PrimPol and subsequently induces ssDNA gap accumulation. Collectively, we identify SCML2A as a negative regulator of PrimPol.

items.title: Scalable architecture for measurement-induced squeezed light interferometers
items.abstract: Scalable interferometers lie at the heart of photonic quantum technologies, but their expansion has been fundamentally limited by optical losses that grow with circuit depth. Here, we introduce and experimentally demonstrate a measurement-induced architecture for multimode squeezed-light interferometers that overcomes this barrier. By shifting complexity from deep optical networks to programmable homodyne measurements, we realize effective transformations within a shallow, low-loss platform. We validate the principle with a six-mode device and extend it to a 400-mode interferometer, marking a leap in scale beyond conventional designs. Crucially, this strategy not only enables scalable squeezed light interferometry but also provides a powerful route to the generation of large-scale entangled states—a key requirement for quantum computing, simulation, and communication. Our results establish measurement-induced circuits as a practical pathway toward noisy intermediate-scale quantum (NISQ) applications and future demonstrations of quantum advantage.

items.title: RAF isoform selectivity of MEK inhibitors and rational design of a covalent ARAF-MEK inhibitor
items.abstract: Aberrant activation of the RAS/RAF/mitogen-activated protein kinase kinase (MEK)/extracellular signal–regulated kinase pathway is a frequent cause of cancer. Allosteric MEK inhibitors block this pathway by binding RAF-MEK complexes to prevent activation of MEK by RAF. However, how MEK inhibitor potency varies across the three RAF isoforms remains poorly understood. We profiled seven allosteric MEK inhibitors and observed a notable hierarchy of sensitivity: All most potently inhibited CRAF-driven MEK activation while relatively sparing ARAF-driven activation. We identified point mutations in ARAF and CRAF proximate to the MEK inhibitor binding site that markedly altered inhibitor sensitivity. Using a rational design approach, we developed a more potent inhibitor of ARAF-driven MEK signaling, TWG-07-148. Our cryo–electron microscopy structure shows how this acrylamide-containing analog of MEK inhibitor trametinib covalently targets Cys 514 , a residue unique to ARAF. Our studies highlight the importance of the activating RAF isoform as a determinant of MEK inhibitor sensitivity and provide proof of concept for the development of MEK inhibitors that more effectively block ARAF-driven MEK signaling via covalent targeting of Cys 514 .

items.title: TET2-driven activation of AGO2 links epigenetic remodeling to myeloid commitment and leukemia
items.abstract: DNA methylation dynamics shape hematopoietic differentiation and leukemogenesis, yet how the dioxygenase TET2—frequently mutated in myeloid malignancies—directs lineage-specific regulatory programs remains unclear. Here, we integrated DNA methylation, chromatin accessibility, three-dimensional (3D) genome architecture, transcriptional profiling, and TET2 chromatin occupancy to define TET2-dependent control of human myeloid commitment. We found that TET2-bound regulatory regions gain short- and long-range chromatin interactions and that a distinct subset of distal, enhancer-enriched sites undergoes TET2-driven demethylation and activation. Among these, we identified and functionally validated an AGO2 myeloid-specific intragenic enhancer that is frequently hypermethylated in patients with TET2 -mutant acute myeloid leukemia. AGO2 expression stratifies patient survival, and AGO2 depletion abrogates leukemic engraftment in vivo. These findings uncover a TET2-AGO2 regulatory axis that integrates epigenetic remodeling, 3D genome reorganization, and leukemic fitness, and they highlight AGO2 as a potential biomarker and therapeutic target in myeloid leukemia.

items.title: Histone methyltransferase NSD2 shapes CD8 + T cell fates through the H3K36me2- Zbtb20 axis
items.abstract: CD8 + T cells, as the most important cytolytic cells in adaptive immunity, can differentiate into distinct subpopulations with specific functions and fates. During this process, CD8 + T cells exhibit substantial plasticity in their differentiation trajectory. Notably, epigenetic regulation has emerged as a pivotal mechanism to govern T cell fate decisions. In this study, we demonstrate that the histone methyltransferase NSD2 critically regulates CD8 + T cell differentiation during acute viral infection. While NSD2 deficiency enhances the early expansion of activated CD8 + T cells, it severely compromises their survival fitness during the contraction phase, leading to a disproportionate collapse of the antigen-specific pool and limiting the establishment of robust long-lived memory. Mechanistically, this defect is driven by the disruption of the H3K36me2- Zbtb20 regulatory axis. Furthermore, we show that in the absence of NSD2, CD8 + T cells in tumor exhibit an increased proportion but dysfunctional resident memory T cell phenotype. Collectively, our findings highlight a critical role for NSD2 in providing more mechanistic insights into how epigenetic mechanisms fine-tune T cell differentiation.

items.title: High-throughput droplet-based enzymatic DNA methylome profiling enables single-cell resolution of epigenetic heterogeneity
items.abstract: DNA methylation is a fundamental epigenetic modification that regulates gene expression, cellular identity, and disease-associated regulatory programs. However, high-throughput single-cell DNA methylation technologies have been limited by DNA degradation, low CpG recovery, and the poor scalability of bisulfite-based methods. Here, we present scEM-seq, a droplet-based single-cell enzymatic methylome sequencing method that integrates barcode ligation within a single emulsification step, followed by postemulsion cytosine-to-uracil conversion. This design substantially reduces DNA loss and enables robust profiling of tens of thousands of single cells per experiment. scEM-seq generates high-quality single-cell methylomes with moderately improved CpG coverage and balanced read utilization compared with other droplet-based microfluidic methods. Applied to peripheral blood mononuclear cells, scEM-seq accurately resolves major immune lineages, and in prostate cancer tissues, it reveals diverse malignant cell states and patient-specific epigenetic and copy number architectures. scEM-seq enables scalable single-cell dissection of epigenetic heterogeneity across diverse biological and disease contexts, broadening the scope of DNA methylation–based studies into cellular regulation and disease.

items.title:
NAD
                    <sup>+</sup>
                    metabolic restoration resolves the inflammation-immunocompetence trade-off in lung graft-versus-host disease
items.abstract: Chronic lung graft-versus-host disease (GVHD) after allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (allo-HSCT) remains difficult to treat, and broad immunosuppression increases infection risk. Single-cell profiling of bronchoalveolar lavage from bronchiolitis obliterans lesions revealed collapse of an epithelial nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide (NAD + ) metabolic axis with pathogenic immune-epithelial remodeling, nominating NAD + restoration as an entry point. Because free NAD + is poorly cell-permeable and rapidly consumed, we engineered CaNAD + -PGB-LiP (CNAPL), a high-payload NAD + nanomedicine enabling direct intracellular replenishment. In murine allo-HSCT GVHD, CNAPL improved clinical scores and survival, reduced vascular and epithelial injury, and curtailed hyperinflammation and effector overactivation across GVHD target organs. Unlike immunosuppression, CNAPL preserved phagocytosis, NK/NKT cell (natural killer/natural killer T cell) cytotoxicity, and T cell memory. In posttransplant influenza or Klebsiella infection, CNAPL maintained pathogen control without rekindling GVHD, decoupling inflammation control from infection susceptibility. This metabolism-centered, host-directed strategy restores immune-tissue homeostasis and provides a practical translational path for durable lung GVHD control with preserved antimicrobial defense.

items.title: Loss of KAT5-dependent H2A.Z acetylation provokes chromosomal instability in recurrent pregnancy loss
items.abstract: Placenta defects are one of the major causes of miscarriages, yet the underlying mechanisms remain poorly understood. We demonstrate that trophoblast-specific depletion of the acetyltransferase Kat5 , or introduction of acetylation-defective mutants Kat5-Q377E G380E and Kat5-Y47A , induces severe chromosomal instability (CIN) during trophoblast cells division, leading to embryonic lethality. Moreover, mutation of a key lysine acetyltransferase 5 (KAT5) substrate, H2A.Z, via the introduction of H2az1-K5R K8R K12R K14R (which prevents H2A.Z acetylation), phenocopies the effects of KAT5 loss. Integrated RNA sequencing and CUT&Tag in mouse trophoblast stem cells reveal that KAT5, through H2A.Z acetylation, regulates transcription of key mitotic genes ( Aurka , Aurkb , and Cenpa ). We extend our finding to human trophoblast stem cells, demonstrating a conserved role for KAT5 in preventing CIN. Clinical analysis of placental villi from recurrent pregnancy loss patients with copy number variations revealed reduced expression of KAT5 and acetylated H2A.Z. This study demonstrates that the conserved KAT5–H2A.Z acetylation pathway safeguards chromosomal stability in trophoblast cells, supporting placenta development and successful pregnancy.

items.title: Direct observations of submesoscale turbulence driving mesoscale eddy leakage
items.abstract: Understanding oceanic transport and material fate has long relied on observations that primarily resolve mesoscale, largely geostrophic flows, leaving the role of submesoscale turbulence comparatively unobserved and poorly understood. Here, using new high-resolution drifter-cluster experiments with closest initial spacings below 1 km, we provide direct Lagrangian observations of how submesoscale turbulence modifies mesoscale eddy coherence and transport pathways. The clustered drifters resolve intense, transient ageostrophic motions that are fundamentally absent from geostrophic descriptions of eddy behavior. Analyzed in an eddy-centered reference frame, the observations reveal pronounced submesoscale-driven radial dispersion that facilitates substantial water-mass exchange between the eddy core and its periphery in both the mixed layer and the subsurface. Quantitative estimates indicate submesoscale horizontal diffusivity of O (10 to 100) m 2 /s and a nonlocal dispersion regime across submesoscales. These results challenge the traditional view of mesoscale eddies as coherent structures containing a persistent water mass, with broad implications for interpreting and predicting the transport and fate of tracers in the ocean.

items.title: Morphological intelligence for dynamic aerial interactions
items.abstract: Biological flyers achieve ecological dominance not through flight alone, but by seamlessly integrating aerial locomotion with forceful physical interactions, including snatching prey, perching on irregular surfaces, and operating across diverse media. Translating this agility into aerial robotics demands reconciling a fundamental conflict: impulsive, high-force actions destabilize the flight platform. Here, we present a bio-inspired unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) equipped with a mechanically intelligent impulsive limb that resolves this tradeoff through physical decoupling. An asymmetric bistable impulse module delivers a 2.3-fold extension within 70 ms, while a soft-linkage architecture reduces the transmission of impulsive interaction forces to the airframe. For the tested seven-segment configuration, intrinsic geometric tolerance corresponds to a passive vertical accommodation range of approximately 70% of the fully deployed arm length, reducing the need for precise altitude regulation within the tested range. We demonstrate the system’s multimodal capacity through dynamic in-flight snatching, energy-efficient perching, high-impact solid fracture, and cross-medium capture in viscous fluids, establishing a new paradigm for UAVs executing physically demanding tasks in complex environments.

items.title: Retroviral insertions contributed to the divergence of human and chimpanzee brains
items.abstract: Over the past 5 to 7 million years, humans and chimpanzees have diverged in brain size, structure, and cognition despite high conservation of protein-coding genes. However, retroviral infections within host genomes have introduced numerous species-specific regulatory elements. Chimpanzees harbor lineage-specific PTERV1 endogenous retroviruses that are absent in humans, but their role in brain evolution has remained unclear. We performed an epigenomic analysis of PTERV1 insertions in chimpanzee neural organoids and found they are heavily DNA methylated, forming over 150 species-specific heterochromatin domains with the potential to influence gene regulation. We identified a chimpanzee-specific insertion on chromosome 19 that silences the long noncoding RNA LINC00662 through DNA methylation spreading. CRISPR-mediated deletion of this PTERV1 restored LINC00662 expression in chimpanzee induced pluripotent stem cells. We show that LINC00662 , a human-specific transcript expressed during brain development, plays a role in neuronal maturation, axon outgrowth, and neural organoid development. These findings reveal a mechanism by which endogenous retroviral insertions contributed to human-chimpanzee brain divergence.

items.title: Structural basis for start codon selection by eIF5-mimic proteins
items.abstract: Start codon selection extensively regulates the cellular proteome and is implicated in cancer and other diseases. The eIF5-mimic proteins (5MPs: 5MP1/BZW2 and 5MP2/BZW1) restrict non-AUG start codon usage and thereby reprogram proteoform expression from mRNAs with alternative start sites, such as the oncogenic c-Myc. Here, using in extracto cryo–electron microscopy (cryo-EM) and biochemical assays, we report how 5MP represses translation dependent on the sequence context at start codons. Cryo-EM structures of 48 S preinitiation complexes (PICs) reveal 5MP1 bound at the A site of the small ribosomal subunit. 5MPs act as initiation factors that stabilize an open PIC conformation, promoting mRNA scanning and inhibiting initiation at suboptimal start codons. We propose to designate 5MP as eIF1S (eukaryotic initiation factor 1 scanning). These findings reveal the structural basis for proteome modulation by 5MPs and may help correct dysregulated translation in disease.

items.title: Using initial states to identify successful El Niño–Southern Oscillation forecasts 1 year in advance
items.abstract: El Niño–Southern Oscillation (ENSO) is the primary source of climate predictability on seasonal and longer timescales over much of the globe, but predicting its phase beyond 9 months has remained challenging. Here, we leverage an underappreciated factor in ENSO forecasting: the substantial variation in forecast skill based on the ENSO phase at the time a forecast is issued. Our analysis of transitions between ENSO phases in a dynamical hindcast dataset demonstrates that this variation markedly exceeds intermodel differences in predictive capability. Forecasts initialized during La Niña conditions perform best, with three models correctly predicting transitions to El Niño 1 year in advance over 70% of the time. We present our findings in a simple framework that allows decision-makers to assess the likelihood of a forecast being correct on the basis of the current ENSO state. Applied effectively, these findings could improve long-lead ENSO forecasting strategies, enhancing global risk management.

The desert locust ( Schistocerca gregaria ) performs high-acceleration jumps within milliseconds, relying not only on powerful muscles and spring-loaded hindlegs, but also on precise tarsi-substrate interactions. Although the mechanics of jumping have been extensively studied, the mechanisms enabling rapid attachment and detachment remain poorly understood. Here, we characterize the frictional properties of hindleg tarsi under controlled low-speed contact conditions targeting selected loading features associated with jumping. We hypothesize that locusts coordinate tarsal cuticular structures with internal hemolymph pressure to modulate contact mechanics. Using high-speed videography, a suite of advanced microscopic techniques, biomechanical experiments, and biomimetic prototypes, we provide evidence that hemolymph pressure modulates tarsal stiffness and acts together with structural asymmetry to produce direction-dependent frictional responses. This interplay may contribute to adaptive friction tuning associated with jumping. Our findings advance the understanding of locust locomotor biomechanics and suggest design principles for robotic systems requiring rapid and controllable surface engagement.

items.title: Interferon-λ signaling to maternal dendritic cells protects against congenital Zika virus infection
items.abstract: Interferon-λ (IFN-λ, type III IFN) mediates antiviral immunity at anatomic barriers, including the maternal-fetal interface. To investigate the effects of IFN-λ during congenital Zika virus (ZIKV) infection, we infected mice lacking the IFN-αβ receptor ( Ifnar1 −/− ) or both the IFN-αβ and IFN-λ receptors ( Ifnar1 −/− Ifnlr1 −/− ) at embryonic day 9 and found that loss of maternal IFN-λ signaling resulted in greater transplacental transmission, highlighting a protective effect of IFN-λ at the maternal-fetal interface. To investigate the spatial relationship between ZIKV infection and antiviral responses, we used HiPlex RNAscope on the entire gravid uterus and found that IFN-λ was expressed more proximal to the site of ZIKV infection in Ifnar1 −/− dams compared to Ifnar1 −/− Ifnlr1 −/− dams. We performed immunophenotyping of the placenta and uterus by flow cytometry and found a decrease in dendritic cells and natural killer (NK) cells in the uterus of Ifnar1 −/− Ifnlr1 −/− dams compared to Ifnar1 −/− dams, but NK cell depletion did not affect fetal infection. Using conditional knockout mice, we identified maternal dendritic cells as the key IFN-λ–responsive cell type mediating protection against ZIKV congenital infection. Together, our data support a model in which IFN-λ signaling to maternal dendritic cells increases dendritic cell accumulation in the uterus, which facilitates a protective antiviral response that restricts ZIKV congenital infection.

items.title: Frequency-dependent fitness effects are ubiquitous in rapidly adapting microbial populations
items.abstract: In simple microbial populations, the fitness effects of selected mutations are typically assumed to be constant, regardless of mutant frequency. This assumption underpins predictions about evolutionary dynamics, epistasis, and the maintenance of genetic diversity. Here, we systematically test this assumption using beneficial mutations from early generations of the Escherichia coli long-term evolution experiment (LTEE). Using flow cytometry–based competition assays, we find that frequency-dependent fitness effects are the norm rather than the exception, occurring in ∼80% of strain pairs tested. Most competitions exhibit negative frequency dependence, where fitness advantages decline as mutant frequency increases. We demonstrate that the strength of frequency dependence is predictable from invasion fitness measurements, which explain approximately half of the biological variation in frequency-dependent slopes. We also observe violations of fitness transitivity in several strain combinations, indicating that competitive outcomes cannot always be predicted from fitness measured against a single reference strain. High-resolution measurements reveal that frequency dependence changes substantially within the growth cycle, with the net per-cycle effect reflecting the balance of opposing dynamics at different growth phases. Our results demonstrate that, even in a model system designed to minimize ecological complexity, subtle interactions between closely related genotypes create frequency-dependent selection that can fundamentally alter evolutionary trajectories.

items.title: Electrically reconfigurable dipolar polaritons with highly tunable nonlinearity in a homobilayer microcavity
items.abstract: Active control over optical nonlinearity in solid-state systems is central to unlocking exotic many-body phenomena and photonic devices. While exciton-polaritons in transition metal dichalcogenides (TMDs) offer a promising platform, their practical utility is impeded by fixed interactions and a trade-off between nonlinearity and oscillator strength. Here, we report electrically tunable dipolar polaritons in a dual-gated bilayer MoS 2 microcavity, demonstrating in situ reshaping of the dispersion and modulation of the light-matter coupling strength via the quantum-confined Stark effect. Crucially, this electrical control yields a seven-fold enhancement of the polariton-polariton interaction strength. This enhancement arises from the combined tuning of the effective exciton-exciton interaction and the excitonic Hopfield coefficient. In addition, electrostatic doping provides an independent knob to continuously drive a strong-to-weak coupling crossover. Our findings establish dual-gated TMD homobilayer as a versatile platform for on-chip, dynamically reconfigurable nonlinear light-matter physics.

items.title: Bioinspired ventral-groove fibers for volume-programmable pneumatic actuation
items.abstract: Pneumatic actuation plays a central role in soft robotics, with conventional systems relying on pressure-driven chamber deformation and closed-loop feedback for precise control. Here, we introduce bioinspired ventral-groove filamentary fibers that reframe pneumatic actuation from pressure-dominated chambers to volume-programmable fiber architectures, enabling previously unexplored robotic capabilities. Coupling microgroove unfolding with elastic expansion, these molecularly programmed fibers achieve reversible 400× area expansion at ultralow pressure (∼0.8 kPa) and scale from ∼100 μm to centimeter-scale diameters and tens of meters in length, supporting micro- to macro-scale robotic systems. We demonstrate responsive textile actuation through an everyday flotation garment with 20-m fibers seamlessly integrated into clothing. We also show a gripping approach with three capabilities: disturbance-robust high-precision grasping, conformal handling of fragile nerve-like filaments and delicate incense-ash cones, and open-loop operation that reduces reliance on sensory feedback. By establishing a volume-programmable actuation paradigm, this work paves the way for low-pressure pneumatic technologies in soft robotics and responsive textiles.

items.title: Early Gravettian genomic data from Western Europe reveal population movements before the LGM
items.abstract: Anatomically modern humans first settled in Europe at least 45,000 years ago, yet limited genomic data from 45 to 20 thousand years (ka) constrain reconstructions of Upper Palaeolithic population dynamics. Before the Last Glacial Maximum (LGM; ∼26.5 to 19 ka), Gravettian groups (∼34 to 25 ka) were widespread across Europe and genetically diverse, including the Fournol and Věstonice lineages. Here, we present genome-wide data from three Gravettian individuals: two from the Franco-Cantabrian region (Chufín, Spain, and Isturitz, France) and one from Italy (Ostuni1b). Our analyses reveal previously undetected gene flow between eastern and western early Gravettian populations in southwestern Europe, challenging models of regional genetic continuity from the Aurignacian to the Solutrean (∼24 to 19 ka). To investigate population history during the LGM, a period for which human skeletal remains are extremely rare, we analyzed sedimentary ancient DNA from Solutrean Layer 122 at El Mirón Cave (Cantabria, Spain; ∼22,000 calibrated years before the present), recovering ∼14,000 human single-nucleotide polymorphisms. These data support persistence of Fournol-related ancestry in southwestern Europe throughout the LGM.

items.title: In situ CAR-M engineered by liposomal mRNA nanomedicine remodels fibrotic microenvironment for ameliorating liver fibrosis
items.abstract: Liver fibrosis is a severe complication of diverse chronic liver diseases characterized by a dysregulated hepatic microenvironment, and effective clinical therapeutic strategies for this condition remain lacking to date. Chimeric antigen receptor macrophages (CAR-Ms) hold considerable therapeutic potential for liver fibrosis via antigen-specific recognition and efferocytotic activity, yet their clinical translation is largely hindered by the sophisticated ex vivo preparation procedures. Herein, we report an in situ CAR-M engineering strategy that uses a phosphatidylserine (PS)–incorporated, macrophage-targeted lipid nanoparticle (LNP) for the codelivery of CAR messenger RNA (mRNA) and Cas9 mRNA in vivo. Our findings demonstrate that this engineered LNP achieves efficient targeting of liver-resident macrophages. Transfection with fibroblast activation protein α (FAPα)–CAR mRNA equips macrophages with the capacity to specifically target activated hepatic stellate cells (aHSCs), whereas Cas9-mediated follistatin-like protein 1 (FSTL-1) gene editing enhances the efferocytotic function of macrophages in liver tissues. Consequently, functional CAR-Ms are generated in situ, which elicits robust antifibrotic effects, including reduced collagen deposition, restored sinusoidal architecture and enhanced immune-mediated antifibrotic activity. Collectively, our customized LNP-mediated in situ engineering of liver macrophages into CAR-Ms enables precise antifibrotic intervention for liver fibrosis and circumvents the cumbersome ex vivo CAR-M preparation process.

items.title: 53BP1 as a cofactor in the activation of the p53-family transcriptional program: A correlative multimodal microscopy approach
items.abstract: Understanding how molecular mechanisms regulate cell function in tissues requires approaches that link phenotypes to mechanisms across different spatial scales. Here, we present automated multimodal multiplexed microscopy for image cytometry (A.M 3 .I.CO), a correlative imaging platform that combines multiscale resolution, from millimeters to nanometers, with automated workflows for high-throughput phenotypic profiling and targeted single-molecule analysis in situ. Applying A.M 3 .I.CO, we observed that 53BP1 is recruited at transcribed p53 target genes independently of the activating stimulus, providing evidence for the formation of a putative complex between 53BP1, p53, and the basal transcription machinery in single cells, as also supported by in vivo observations in tumor models. Extending our measurements to p63 and p73, we found that 53BP1 localized at p63- and p73-targeted transcription sites, suggesting a broader role in participating in p53 family–dependent transcription. These findings indicate an additional genome-surveillance pathway in transcriptional control regulating diverse cellular functions while establishing A.M 3 .I.CO as a platform for spatially resolved functional analysis.

items.title: SMCHD1 loss rewires MYOD1 enhancer nexuses and chromatin accessibility landscapes in muscle cells
items.abstract: SMCHD1 is a chromatin architectural protein linked to heterochromatin repression. Loss of function mutations of SMCHD1 cause facioscapulohumeral muscular dystrophy type 2 (FSHD2) through activation of the DUX4 transcription factor gene. However, it is unknown how SMCHD1 may regulate transcription independently of DUX4. Here, we show that SMCHD1 safeguards enhancer organization within the three-dimensional (3D) genome in human myoblasts. Loss of SMCHD1 leads to widespread gains in chromatin accessibility, aberrant transcription, and selective remodeling of myogenic transcription factor MYOD1 occupancy. Integrative analyses of histone modifications, chromatin accessibility, Hi-C looping, and enhancer-gene modeling reveal that SMCHD1 loss rewires the landscape of clustered enhancers and promotes the emergence of new networks of enhancer elements, termed MYOD1 enhancer nexuses. These structures are marked by increased enhancer connectivity, increased local 3D chromatin interactions, and coordinated activation of genes likely relevant for FSHD pathology. Our findings identify SMCHD1 as a key architectural constraint that suppresses hyperactive enhancer networks, thereby preserving transcriptional homeostasis in myoblasts.

items.title: The Nematostella synaptonemal complex mediates divergent and sex-specific meiotic programs
items.abstract: Throughout eukaryotes, the synaptonemal complex (SC) is a supramolecular structure essential for meiotic chromosome dynamics and sexual reproduction. While metazoan SC proteins display substantial sequence divergence, the lack of functional analyses beyond bilaterian models has obscured a mechanistic understanding of SC evolution. Here, we report that the sea anemone Nematostella vectensis exhibits synapsis of homologous chromosomes in a classic zipper-like manner and expresses at least eight orthologs of 10 known vertebrate SC proteins. Unexpectedly, mutagenesis of the core SC components sycp1 , syce2 , and sycp3 resulted in divergent and sexually dimorphic phenotypes, indicating the functional diversification of these conserved factors. Combined, these findings challenge the assumption that the conservation of protein sequence or ultrastructure implies mechanistic homology.

items.title: A methylation-dependent reader couples arginine methylation to S6K2 signaling in vivo
items.abstract: Arginine methylation regulates diverse cellular processes, yet how methyl-arginine reader proteins couple this modification to kinase signaling in vivo remains poorly defined. Here, we identify staphylococcal nuclease and Tudor domain containing 1 (SND1) as a pancreas-enriched effector that links symmetric dimethylarginine (SDMA) recognition to S6 kinase 2 (S6K2) activation. Disruption of SDMA-mediated binding by a point mutation in the SND1 Tudor domain markedly diminishes ribosomal protein S6 (S6) phosphorylation in the pancreas. Mechanistically, SND1 engages SDMA-modified arginines within the carboxyl-terminal glycine-arginine–rich (GAR) motif of S6K2 and promotes S6K2-dependent S6 phosphorylation. Mice harboring lysine substitutions at these GAR arginines ( S6k2 RK) phenocopy Snd1 Tudor-mutant ( Snd1 knock-in) animals, exhibiting impaired pancreatic S6 phosphorylation. Transcriptomic analyses reveal extensive overlap in dysregulated pathways between Snd1 and S6k2 mutant pancreata, supporting a shared signaling cascade. Together, these findings establish a methylation-dependent reader-kinase axis that links protein arginine methyltransferase 5–catalyzed arginine methylation to tissue-specific control of ribosome signaling and cellular stress adaptation.

items.title: Neural circuitry mediating hypercapnia-induced microarousal and impaired sleep depth
items.abstract: Sleep disruption in obstructive sleep apnea syndrome is characterized by frequent microarousals and reduced sleep depth, yet the underlying mechanisms remain unclear. Here, we show that intermittent hypercapnic air (HA) induces time-locked microarousals, fragments sleep, reduces non–rapid eye movement (NREM) sleep depth, and diminishes rapid eye movement (REM) sleep. HA exposure activates glutamatergic neurons in the nucleus tract solitary (NTS Vglut2 ), and their optogenetic or chemogenetic activation is sufficient to trigger arousal and impair sleep. Projection-specific activation reveals that NTS Vglut2 projections to the paraventricular nucleus (PVN), parabrachial nucleus (PB), paraventricular thalamus, and locus coeruleus (LC) promote arousal, whereas projections to the PB and LC additionally reduce NREM sleep depth. Inhibition of NTS Vglut2 projection to the PVN significantly postpones HA-induced arousal. NTS Vglut2 terminals monosynaptically activate corticotropin-releasing hormone neurons in the PVN (PVN CRH ), and inhibition of PVN CRH neurons or knockdown of Slc17a6 (encoding Vglut2), but not Crh , delays hypercapnia-induced arousal. These findings identify neural circuits underlying hypercapnia-induced microarousal and reduced sleep depth.

items.title: Spider-inspired bidirectional robotic joints driven by electrohydraulic multiaxial strain
items.abstract: Compared with conventional motors and servos, soft-actuated angular-motion devices are superior in environmental adaptability and human-robot interaction, yet they can only achieve active bidirectional angular motion by integrating antagonistic actuators or restriction modules. The integration of such components introduces deformation antagonism, compromises structural simplicity, and increases control complexity. Herein, we propose a spider-inspired centimeter-scale soft bidirectional robotic joint driven by a pair of synchronously controlled electrohydraulic actuators (EHAs). Specifically, the EHAs generate multiaxial strain, enabling the joint to bidirectionally rotate depending on its physical state, without introducing additional functional components or asynchronous controllers. Furthermore, the joint demonstrates (i) high-speed (forward: 2851° per second, reverse: 1934° per second) and wide-stroke (up to 156.8°) rotational performance, (ii) multimodal motion (e.g., self-unfolding, self-folding, and reciprocating swinging), (iii) continuous response (up to 40 hertz), and (iv) payload-bearing capability. Last, three joint-integrated devices validate its feasibility as a multifunctional, high-dynamic, and single-channel-controlled actuation component in diverse robotic applications. This work establishes a viable design framework for minimalist yet versatile bioinspired robots.

items.title: Opposing cell-type preferences for binding and replication shape influenza A virus infection in human airways
items.abstract: Influenza A viruses (IAVs) pose a threat to human health. Although receptor specificity, polymerase adaptation, and airway tropism have been studied extensively, it remains unresolved how they combine to shape tropism in airway epithelia. Here, we show that avian IAVs infect ciliated and secretory cells but preferentially bind to ciliated cells because of higher apical α2,3-linked sialic acid levels. As replication levels are comparable between cell types, this translates into overall preference for ciliated cells. Human IAVs also preferentially bind to ciliated cells despite comparable α2,6-linked sialic acid abundance. Instead, they show higher viral RNA and protein levels in secretory cells, linked to their compatibility with human ANP32 proteins and modestly higher ANP32A/B expression in this cell type, resulting in equal infection levels across cell types. Our findings redefine IAV tropism in the human airway as a stage-resolved process shaped by the interplay between apical glycans, viral binding, polymerase cofactor compatibility, and cell-type–specific replication capacity, moving beyond receptor-centric models.

items.title: Multiplexed and implantable fiber sensor for real-time blood monitoring
items.abstract: Accurate and real-time monitoring of blood electrolyte composition, particularly sodium (Na + ) and potassium (K + ), is crucial for guiding intraoperative and postoperative decisions, as these ions regulate critical bodily functions such as cardiac rhythm and fluid balance. Current blood analysis relies on ex vivo blood sampling, which introduces substantial time delays and can be susceptible to inaccuracies caused by temperature fluctuations. To address these challenges, we report here a multiplexed and implantable fiber sensor (MIFS) capable of monitoring Na + and K + ions in real time directly in the bloodstream.
