MIFS integrates three parallel liquid metal channels with a multilayer surface-electrode architecture, which synergistically enhances sensitivity, minimizes sensing drift, ensures mechanical flexibility, and offers outstanding biocompatibility for vascular implantation. In vivo testing in rabbit models and validation in human blood samples demonstrate MIFS’s superior sensing accuracy, real-time, and stable sensing in agreement with conventional ex vivo measurements. This work paves the way for real-time blood monitoring in clinical practice.

items.title: A noncanonical meiotic cohesin complex associates with specific MCM complexes to promote cohesion establishment and homolog bias
items.abstract: A meiosis-specific cohesin complex is essential for the segregation of homologous chromosomes and sister chromatids during meiosis, yet its composition and mechanism in Drosophila remain elusive. Here, we demonstrate that SOLO directly interacts with SUNN, SSEP, and SMC1 and that these interactions are conserved between Drosophila melanogaster and Zeugodacus cucurbitae , a Tephritidae species within Diptera. SOLO associates with SMC1 via specific conserved residues within its highly conserved carboxyl-terminal domain. Furthermore, SOLO directly interacts with the MCM4 and MCM6 subunits of the MCM complex and with MMS22L to establish cohesion; consequently, postreplicative expression of SOLO results in a complete function loss. SOLO also interacts with the MEI-217 and MEI-218 subunits of the meiosis-specific minichromosome maintenance complex to promote homolog bias during meiosis. We propose that in Diptera, an evolutionarily diverged meiotic cohesin complex, composed of SOLO, SUNN, SSEP, SMC1, and SMC3, interacts with various complexes to fulfill its diverse meiotic functions.

items.title: Gradient-interlayer–based flexible pressure sensors for high-performance robotic perception
items.abstract: Tactile perception systems based on flexible pressure sensors are indispensable for humanoid robots to perform dexterous manipulation, compliant interaction, and operation in visually challenging environments. Although strategies relying on surface or spatial microstructure engineering have improved sensor performance, the long-standing trade-off among sensitivity, sensing range, and linearity continues to hinder their practical deployment. Inspired by the gradient distribution of mechanoreceptors in human fingertip skin, we report a gradient-interlayer–based flexible iontronic pressure sensor (GriFIPS) in which a single direct-ink-written elastomeric mesh-like interlayer, with a centrifugal increase in aperture size, is placed between the soft electrode and an ionic hydrogel layer. Operating upstream of the functional layer, the mesh enables progressive, stage-wise contact under increasing load and decouples macroscopic contact-area evolution from the microscopic interfacial response. The sensor simultaneously achieves a sensitivity of 175.9 kPa −1 , a linear sensing range up to 360 kPa with a coefficient of determination of 0.997, a low detection limit of about 2.1 Pa, and a response time of about 25 ms, while remaining stable over 6000 loading cycles and 2000 cycles of 50% tensile strain. Building on this single-channel device, we further extend the architecture into a 3-axis gradient-interlayer–based flexible iontronic force sensor (3-axis GriFIFS) capable of resolving triaxial forces and surface textures. When integrated onto a dexterous robotic hand and combined with a temporal convolutional network, the sensors support tactile object recognition, fabric texture discrimination, human–robot interaction, and tactile-guided assembly, offering a generalizable route to tactile sensing for embodied intelligence.

items.title: Ocean carbon sequestration during glacial climates due to combined Antarctic sea ice expansion and ocean circulation change
items.abstract: Glacial-interglacial transitions punctuate Earth’s Quaternary climate, accompanied by substantial atmospheric carbon dioxide and ocean carbon storage changes. The cause of atmospheric carbon drawdown during glaciations is uncertain, involving many mechanisms whose interactions are poorly understood. Here, we show that the combined expansion of Antarctic sea ice and associated changes in the meridional overturning efficiently sequester carbon in the ocean abyss, leading to a decline in atmospheric carbon dioxide. In contrast, changes in sea ice and circulation individually result in ocean carbon dioxide outgassing. When sea ice expansion and circulation changes act together, they enhance biological carbon storage by reducing ocean-atmosphere fluxes in the Southern Ocean, without invoking external drivers of the biological pump. This reduction inhibits the outgassing of upwelled remineralized carbon and promotes its resubduction into the abyss. Together, these results reveal a reinforcing feedback linking atmospheric cooling, Antarctic sea ice expansion, and ocean circulation changes to enhanced biological carbon storage and atmospheric carbon dioxide drawdown.

items.title: Coordinated mosquito biting dynamics at the human skin interface
items.abstract: The bite of a female mosquito is the critical point of pathogen transmission, yet the fine-scale biting dynamics on human skin remain unknown. Here, we combine high-speed videography, deep-learning–based tracking, and electrophysiology to analyze biting dynamics of the malaria vector Anopheles coluzzii in real time at the human skin interface. We uncover a previously uncharacterized synchronization of mouthpart and leg movements during probing and identify five distinct below skin sub-behaviors: piercing, vessel searching, blood ingestion, retraction, and withdrawal. We show that disruption of the orco and IR76b chemosensory genes can alter some components of normal biting but these effects are subtle, suggesting possible plasticity in direct-contact chemosensation and mosquito bite execution. Comparative analyses show genus-specific biting strategies between An. coluzzii and Aedes aegypti linked to distinct ways they find blood vessels. Our findings indicate that female mosquitoes exhibit a complex synchronization of body parts at the bite site via motor and chemosensory processes.

items.title: How high-pressure ices on large ocean worlds can support habitability: The compatibility of amino acids into ice VI and VII
items.abstract: Water oceans in large icy moons and exoplanets are isolated from the rocky interior by thick layers of high-pressure ice, which hinder the direct release of nutrients and organics derived from water-rock interaction to the ocean. Possible uptake of these bio-essential compounds into high-pressure ice phases could regulate their availability in the ocean, but this process is poorly constrained. Here, we measured partition coefficients of glycine and alanine into ices VI and VII under elevated temperature-pressure conditions using a diamond-anvil cell. We observed moderate compatibility of glycine and alanine with partition coefficients: K p ,glycine = 0.14 and 0.40 in ices VI and VII, respectively; K p ,alanine = 0.21 and 0.35 in ices VI and VII, respectively. First-principles calculations suggested that amino acids could be incorporated into high-pressure ice’s lattice via cogrowth. Compatibility of amino acids into high-pressure ices would favor their transport in large extraterrestrial oceans, opening an avenue to habitability.

items.title: In situ processing of fibrous hydrogels by photochemistry for adaptive cellular microenvironments
items.abstract: Omnipresent in biology, fibrous networks like collagen possess unique properties: dynamic network via crosslinking and degradation. This intrinsic adaptivity plays a critical role in regulating cell behavior via cell-matrix interactions. Built from biological building blocks, however, these networks are challenging to manipulate or even control. Here, we introduce dynamic network regulation via photochemical control in a synthetic and fibrous highly biomimetic hydrogel. As a proof-of-concept, we demonstrate that the dynamic control over the mechanical properties of this adaptive in vitro model can be used to modulate cell spreading and mechanotransduction in three-dimensional (3D) mesenchymal stromal cell cultures. Our approach not only opens the door to on-demand mechanically adaptive gels with unprecedented control, but simultaneously offers easy processibility and cell extraction of the used synthetic gel.

items.title: Single-cell–level digital twins for preterm birth prevention strategies
items.abstract: Digital twin models can accelerate therapeutic development by enabling low-risk testing of candidate interventions. In preterm labor (PTL), a major pregnancy complication where clinical trials face ethical and financial barriers, digital twins are especially valuable for evaluating new therapies targeting immune dysfunctions driving PTL. Yet, current models lack single-cell resolution, limiting detection of cell type–specific mechanisms, off-target effects, and the design of personalized interventions. We present Simulated Immunome Modeling of Clinical Outcomes (SIMCO), a single-cell–level digital twin framework that models immunomodulatory treatment effects on the timing of labor using immunome-wide, single-cell simulations. SIMCO’s digital twins are trained and validated on a newly generated mass cytometry atlas of the pregnant immunome exposed to nine candidate drugs preselected for PTL prevention. Applying SIMCO to an independent cohort of pregnant individuals, we simulate treatment effects on gestational length, screening for candidate drugs that delay labor timing and providing system-level mechanistic insight for each drug candidate. Tetrahydrofolate and the combination of aspirin and lansoprazole emerged as top candidates for PTL prevention, delaying labor onset primarily through enhanced mTOR signaling in innate immune cells and attenuated JAK/STAT signaling in naïve CD4 + T cells.

items.title: Towards intense single-digit attosecond pulses with a 100-mJ-class mid-infrared sub-cycle laser
items.abstract: The duration of isolated attosecond pulses created via high-order harmonic generation is determined by the number of optical cycles in the driving laser. Achieving shorter attosecond soft x-ray pulses requires minimizing the number of cycles while maintaining a high pulse energy. Here, we demonstrate a carrier-envelope-phase-stable, 100-mJ-class sub-cycle mid-infrared laser that produces a supercontinuum coherent soft-x-ray with unprecedented bandwidth. The system delivers 50-mJ, 6.7-fs (0.88-cycle) pulses at a center wavelength of 2.26 μm—over two orders of magnitude more energetic than any previous sub-cycle laser. We applied the system to high-order harmonic generation and compared the results to simulations based on the three-dimensional time-dependent Schrödinger equation to identify unique features of sub-cycle lasers. This work represents a decisive step toward high-energy half-cycle lasers and high-energy single-digit attosecond soft x-ray pulses that can be used to probe matter and light-matter interactions at previously inaccessible temporal resolutions.

items.title: Predicting upcoming visual features during eye movements yields scene representations aligned with human visual cortex
items.abstract: Natural scenes are complex arrangements of objects, surfaces, and backgrounds. For the brain’s visual system to effectively operate, it needs to extract not only what objects are present but also their spatial and semantic relations. We hypothesize that such structures may be learned, in a self-supervised fashion, by exploiting temporal regularities of natural active vision: Each fixation reveals a glimpse that is related to the previous one via co-occurrence and saccade-conditioned spatial regularities. We instantiate this idea with glimpse prediction networks (GPNs), recurrent models trained to predict the embedding of the next glimpse along human-like scanpaths. GPNs are shown to successfully extract complex scene information, including object co-occurrences and spatial object arrangements, and integrate information across glimpses. GPN representations align strongly with human fMRI responses in mid- and higher-level visual cortex and match, often outperform, alternative state-of-the-art ANN models, establishing next-glimpse-prediction as a biologically plausible route toward brain-aligned scene representations.

items.title: Scentronic: An artificial intelligence–assisted olfactory interface for remote odor sharing and transmission
items.abstract: Recent years have witnessed the surge of human–machine interfaces (HMIs) for various applications. Olfaction is a fundamental chemical sense crucial to perception, memory, and emotion. Current limitations arise from the difficulty of accurately capturing, transmitting, and reproducing odor signals, and the lack of standardized, network-enabled platforms. This work presents an internet of things (IoT)–enabled olfactory interface for remote odor sensing and stimulation. The system integrates an artificial intelligence-assisted odor sensing platform with a wearable piezoelectric olfactory actuation system. We demonstrate the design, characterization, and application of this framework, which integrates devices, circuit architecture, and software algorithms. Applications in medical contexts include psychophysical testing to study olfactory pathways and evaluate sensory loss. We further showcase multisensory stimulation through integrated olfactory and gustatory interfaces for enhanced immersion. This study establishes a scalable framework for IoT-based olfactory interaction, advancing HMIs toward a future that includes the long-overlooked chemical senses.

items.title: Ultrasonic metamaterial at MHz frequencies using microstructured glass
items.abstract: Acoustic metamaterials enhance traditional material properties, providing opportunities to shape sound fields in applications ranging from biomedical imaging and clinical therapy to nondestructive testing. However, at the megahertz frequency range, only a few metamaterial architectures exist. They are often highly attenuating or difficult to manufacture and generally provide limited control. Here, we introduce a megahertz-frequency ultrasonic metamaterial based on laser-engraved glass. By structuring metavoxels with different engraving patterns, we define an anisotropic metamaterial exhibiting local variations in the sound speed of up to 20% compared to unstructured glass and losses 100× lower than in comparable three-dimensional–printed metamaterials. We use this metamaterial to define a library of standard elements that can be modularly combined to shape complex-patterned ultrasonic fields. Our experiments are supported by a theoretical model, which provides additional insights into the microstructural origin of the metamaterial behavior and opens the door to designing tailored ultrasound fields and responses.

items.title: CREBBP loss drives immune evasion by epigenetically silencing STING and MHC-I in small cell lung cancer
items.abstract: Most small cell lung cancers (SCLCs) exhibit low immunogenicity and intrinsic resistance to immunotherapy, yet the underlying mechanisms remain poorly understood. Here, we identify CREBBP loss, a frequent genetic alteration in SCLC, as a key suppressor of tumor cell-intrinsic immune responses that drives an immune-cold tumor microenvironment in Rb1/Trp53 -driven autochthonous mouse models. Consistently, Crebbp deletion promotes immune escape in syngeneic SCLC models. Mechanistically, Crebbp loss suppresses Sting and major histocompatibility complex class-I expression by reducing histone H3 acetylation. Notably, HDAC inhibition restores histone acetylation, reactivates these silenced genes, and induces tumor cell-intrinsic immune responses. Moreover, pharmacological HDAC inhibition synergizes with immune checkpoint blockade to suppress tumor growth in both Crebbp -mutant and Crebbp -wild-type SCLCs, with a more prominent effect in Crebbp -mutant tumors. Collectively, these findings establish CREBBP loss as a key mechanism of immune evasion and immunotherapy resistance in SCLC, highlighting HDAC inhibition as a promising strategy to enhance immunotherapy efficacy.

items.title: CCAN forms the spherical shell-like structure in interphase kinetochores
items.abstract: The kinetochore is an essential structure for the faithful chromosome segregation during mitosis. The 16-protein complex known as the constitutive centromere-associated network (CCAN) localizes the centromere throughout the cell cycle and forms the basis of the kinetochore. Although cryo–electron microscopy has provided a structural model of an individual CCAN unit, how multiple CCAN units are organized within cells remains unclear. Here, using in silico and in vivo analyses, we demonstrate that multiple CCAN units form a spherical shell-like structure in interphase DT40 kinetochores. CENP-T and CENP-N localize to the CCAN shell, whereas the CENP-C cupin domain clusters at the center. Molecular dynamics simulations of CCAN assembly suggest that CENP-C–DNA interactions constrain the orientation of CCAN units, supporting a spherical shell-like organization via CENP-C oligomerization. Super-resolution imaging reveals the spherical shell-like structure at DT40 kinetochores, and CENP-C knockout or expression of a CENP-C DNA binding deficient mutant abolishes the structure, consistent with the simulation-derived model. These findings provide important insights into the spatial organization of functional kinetochores within cells.

items.title: Staphylococcus aureus wall teichoic acid structure dictates virulence potential and resistance to host defenses
items.abstract: Staphylococcus aureus is a formidable pathogen and the leading cause of skin and soft tissue infections. We recently showed that the highly conserved sasF gene, encoding for an uncharacterized sortase-anchored surface protein, is up-regulated when S. aureus colonizes skin. Here, we demonstrate that SasF is an enzyme that has glycoside epimerase activity, which is required for S. aureus resistance to skin fatty acids. Mutants of sasF are highly impaired in skin colonization and acute infection models. The SasF enzyme is crucial for maintaining the structure of wall teichoic acids and proper S. aureus surface chemistry. To our knowledge, this is the first report of a bacterial surface epimerase in this pathogen, suggesting that SasF could be a therapeutic target.

items.title:
p75
                    <sup>NTR</sup>
                    orchestrates chondrogenesis and mechanoadaptation to preserve temporomandibular joint development and homeostasis
items.abstract: The temporomandibular joint (TMJ) is essential for oral functions such as chewing, speaking, and swallowing. Temporomandibular disorders that impair these functions notably reduce patients’ quality of life, and few therapeutic strategies are available to ameliorate these conditions. Here, we identify the neurotrophin receptor (p75 NTR ) as a central regulator of mandibular condylar cartilage development, mechanoadaptation, and homeostasis. p75 NTR loss causes condylar and disc hypoplasia, reduced chondrocyte number, impaired load-induced anabolism, and accelerated degeneration. Conditional deletion experiments demonstrate chondrocyte-autonomous requirements for the brain-derived neurotrophic factor (BDNF)–p75 NTR axis, which activates phosphoinositide 3-kinase AKT serine/threonine kinase and p38 mitogen-activated protein kinase signaling to promote proliferation and chondrogenic differentiation while restraining apoptosis. Degenerative human condyles exhibit reduced p75 NTR expression levels. Together, these data establish p75 NTR as a molecular hub integrating neurotrophic and mechanical cues to preserve postnatal TMJ architecture and highlight the BDNF-p75 NTR axis as a potential therapeutic target.

items.title: RanGAP1 coordinates the ER-lamina interface to drive de novo nuclear envelope reassembly in mouse embryos
items.abstract: Nuclear envelope (NE) reassembly is essential for the zygote-to-totipotency transition in mammalian embryos. Beyond its classical roles in nuclear transport and maintenance of the RanGTP gradient, the function of RanGAP1 in embryonic NE reassembly has remained elusive. Here, we show that RanGAP1 localizes to the early embryonic NE, driving reassembly via a distinct structural mechanism. Trim-Away–mediated RanGAP1 depletion causes two-cell stage arrest and severe NE defects, including nuclear pore complex (NPC) loss, failed reassembly, and aberrant “fishnet” membrane structures. Mechanistically, RanGAP1 establishes a structural paradigm for endoplasmic reticulum (ER)–lamina coupling by recruiting Lamin A/C, B1, and B2 to the ER for coassembly. The acidic domain and SUMO-1 modification at Lys 526 (K526) are essential for the NPC localization of RanGAP1. Thus, RanGAP1 orchestrates nuclear lamina (NL) assembly by targeting lamins to the ER. These findings uncover mechanisms of NE reassembly that are critical for early embryogenesis and provide insights into NE-related developmental disorders.

items.title: Stable coexistence and transport of lytic phage infections with migrating bacterial hosts
items.abstract: Bacteriophages (phages), viruses that exclusively infect bacteria, coexist with their bacterial hosts across diverse environments at densities exceeding 10 7 per milliliter in marine surface waters, 10 8 per milliliter in soils, and 10 9 per milliliter in the human gut. In contrast, phage lysis of bacterial populations within well-mixed in vitro environments select for the emergence of phage-resistant bacterial mutants, which, in turn, select for host-range expansion phage mutants and, typically, the collapse of phage populations altogether. This gap in outcome raises a question: What enables long-term phage-bacteria coexistence? Here, we show how interactions in space can facilitate stable coexistence and long-range transport of virulent phage along with migrating bacteria. Combining theory, simulation, and experiments across multiple phage-bacteria systems, we reveal a chemotaxis-driven mechanism that robustly stabilizes coexistence and dispersal of virulent phages with migrating hosts. These findings suggest the ecological relevance of spatial interaction mechanisms that reinforce stability between antagonistic partners in the absence of perpetual cycles of defense and counterdefense, which may be broadly applicable across phage-bacteria systems.

items.title: Climatic niche conservatism shapes the macroevolution, extinction, and survivorship of crocodile-line archosaurs
items.abstract: Crocodylians are iconic thermophiles. Over 250 million years, crocodile-line archosaurs endured hyperthermals, climatic and range shifts, and two mass extinctions. Whether this niche conservatism reflects a deep evolutionary constraint or recent adaptation to novel climates remains unclear. We integrate present-day occurrences with a time-scaled phylogeny of >400 fossil and extant species. Niche models calibrated on living crocodylians were projected across 245 million years and compared with paleophylogeographic reconstructions. Macroevolutionary model fitting shows that temperature and precipitation exhibit strong phylogenetic structure, best described by bounded Ornstein-Uhlenbeck dynamics, indicating long-term niche conservatism. Poleward expansions in warm intervals and contractions in cool phases reflect tracking of conserved optima rather than niche evolution. Unlike non-avian dinosaurs, low-latitude suitability persisted across all but the most extreme end-Cretaceous scenarios, with recovery expanding from tropical refugia. Thermal and precipitation regimes shifted near the Cenomanian/Turonian hyperthermal (∼93.9 Ma) and Eocene/Oligocene aridification transition (∼33.9 Ma), respectively. Climatic niche conservatism is therefore ancient in crocodile-line archosaurs, but not completely static.

items.title: High ambipolar mobility fluorinated MXene for ultrasensitive biosensing transistors
items.abstract: Transition metal carbides and nitrides (MXenes) are emerging as transformative materials for bioelectronics. However, the advancement of MXene-based field-effect transistor (FET) biosensors is hindered by the lack of high-quality aqueous-stable materials and the low signal transduction efficiency intrinsic to their metallic nature. To address these issues, we report an ultrasensitive biosensing platform enabled by an in-situ fluorination strategy of MXene. By substituting unstable oxygen-containing terminations with chemically stable fluorine terminations in a mild reaction, we synthesized high-quality fluorinated MXene with the record-breaking ambipolar field-effect mobility (μ p = 10.42 cm 2 V −1 s −1 , μ n = 30.23 cm 2 V −1 s −1 ). The highly electronegative fluorinated interface suppresses interfacial electrical double-layer capacitance, boosting signal transduction efficiency. Consequently, the platform achieves the lowest limit of detection (LOD) of 0.26 fg ml −1 for Mycobacterium tuberculosis antigen MPT64 among MXene FETs up to date, accompanied by a high current response of 35.02% at LOD. Clinical validation across 126 serum samples demonstrated a diagnostic accuracy of 97.6% with a detection time of 38 s, exhibiting the high-performance and reliable biosensing in complex physiological environments.

items.title: Furan fatty acids reprogram hepatic lipid metabolism via acyl-CoA conjugates in obesity
items.abstract: Dietary fish oil (FO) and omega-3 fatty acids are associated with cardiometabolic benefits, yet their molecular mediators remain incompletely defined. Furan fatty acids (FuFAs), a distinct lipid class enriched in FO, have emerged as potential regulators of metabolic health. Here, we identify and quantify FuFA species in prescription omega-3 formulations and natural fish oils, and synthesize structurally engineered analogs designed to isolate antioxidant activity and β-oxidation susceptibility from FuFA bioactivity. In a diet-induced obesity mouse model, both natural and synthetic FuFAs reduced fat accumulation and inflammatory markers, while 11U3-2M additionally produced significant improvement in glucose tolerance, dyslipidemia, and hepatic steatosis. The superior activity of 11U3-2M reflects the stable accumulation of its acyl-CoA conjugate that activates peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor alpha (PPARα) signaling and allosterically inhibits acetyl-CoA carboxylases (ACCs) to reprogram hepatic lipid metabolism. These findings position FuFAs as functional dietary lipids contributing to fish oil’s metabolic effects and define fatty acid structural determinants that govern hepatic metabolic activity.

items.title: Classical quantum chemical solution of the FeMo-cofactor model to chemical accuracy and its implications
items.abstract: We use classical quantum chemistry methods to estimate the ground-state energy to chemical accuracy in a model of the FeMo cofactor of nitrogenase, which is widely studied as a target of quantum computing. Our result relies on the insight that the ground-state problem can be characterized as one of ranking many competing, but largely single-configuration, states. This allows a combination of systematic high-order coupled cluster and density matrix renormalization group calculations together with an extrapolation protocol to obtain an accurate energy. Within the model, we identify several spin isomer candidates for the ground state that are degenerate to chemical accuracy. Beyond this model, we characterize the impact of additional electronic excitations and the cluster and protein geometric fluctuations on the low-lying electronic landscape. We find that many features of the landscape are retained in more detailed representations of nitrogenase, which points to the complexity of spectroscopic interpretations of the electronic structure of the FeMo cofactor.

items.title: Chemically encoded pH-tunable covalent adhesion by a bacterial thioester domain
items.abstract: Thioester domains (TEDs) represent a family of bacterial adhesin domains that mediate covalent anchoring to target ligands via an intramolecular thioester bond. Although the broad distribution of TEDs among Gram-positive bacteria suggests a critical functional role, the biological significance of this covalent mechanism remains unclear. In this study, we demonstrated that TED-mediated covalent anchoring is reversible and that its equilibrium is regulated by pH. Specifically, SfbI-TED from group A Streptococcus binds tightly to fibrinogen at physiological pH, whereas mild acidification to pH 6.0 induces rapid dissociation of the complex. Thermodynamic analyses indicated that this pH responsiveness is largely dictated by the intrinsic pH sensitivity of the thioester-mediated acyl transfer reaction conserved within TEDs, rather than by surface residues specific to individual TEDs. Similar pH-dependent behavior was observed in phylogenetically distinct TEDs, suggesting that pH-responsive adhesion is likely to be a broadly shared feature of TED-containing adhesins across Gram-positive bacteria.

items.title: Distinct chalcophile-element inheritance from subducted continental crust in metasomatized mantle
items.abstract: Subduction recycles surface materials into the mantle and shapes its chemical evolution. Whether continental subduction leaves chalcophile-element imprints in the mantle that differ from those of oceanic subduction remains poorly understood. Here, we show that primitive basaltic magmas from the North China Craton exhibit pronounced copper depletion, silver enrichment, and low copper/silver (200 to 1200), together with continental crust–like trace element patterns and radiogenic-isotope compositions. These features contrast sharply with those of the convective mantle, mid-ocean ridge basalts, and oceanic arc basalts, and reflect chemical signatures inherited from subducted continental crust and retained over geological timescales in metasomatized domains of a relatively cold lithospheric mantle. Coupled lead enrichment and unradiogenic lead-isotope signatures further identify metasomatized mantle as an important reservoir of Earth’s unradiogenic lead. Our results reveal distinct modes of chalcophile-element recycling and mantle inheritance during continental and oceanic subduction, with broad implications for mantle chemical evolution and the critical-metal fertility of continental lithosphere.

items.title:
Anomalous phonon selection rules and Raman optical activity in RuO
                    <sub>2</sub>
items.abstract: Breakdown of selection rules and emergence of optical activity in Raman spectroscopy typically signal symmetry-breaking events essential for understanding novel phases of solids. Here, we apply our recently developed rotational anisotropy Raman spectroscopy technique to single-crystal ruthenium dioxide—a compound of recent interest as a candidate workhorse material for altermagnetism yet whose magnetic ground state remains under intense debate. Our data reveal a salient breakdown of selection rules for zone-center phonons, accompanied by clear splitting in the angle-dependent polarimetry plots for the two opposite helicity-nonconserving circularly polarized scattering channels. These observations provide definitive evidence of a previously overlooked symmetry-breaking event, involving either spatial or time-reversal symmetry. In either scenario, the underlying mechanism is likely a bulk hidden order parameter, potentially involving multipole moments of Ruthenium(IV) set by the local crystal field environment. Our work demonstrates how subtle symmetry-breaking events can manifest through lattice dynamics and calls for renewed experimental and theoretical efforts to map the phase diagram of ruthenium dioxide as a system poised near quantum phase transition boundaries.

items.title: DMRT1 is required at two steps of ovarian differentiation in rabbits
items.abstract: The transcription factor Doublesex and Mab-3 Related Transcription Factor 1 (DMRT1) is essential for testis differentiation and male fertility, but less is known about its potential involvement in ovarian differentiation. In mice, Dmrt1 −/− females are fertile, although they show a reduction of Stra8 expression. Using our DMRT1 mutant rabbit model, we analyzed ovarian differentiation when DMRT1 expression is abolished. First, we observed that during early gonadal development, DMRT1 −/− gonads display a specific transcriptome different from control ovaries and control testes. Second, we assessed the infertility phenotype of mutant females. DMRT1 is highly expressed in germ cells until meiosis initiation, and its disruption leads to a down-regulation of key genes involved in the meiotic process. Chromatin immunoprecipitation sequencing data highlighted that DMRT1 can bind these genes in the rabbit ovary. Our study using the rabbit model shows that in addition to its role in testicular differentiation, DMRT1 has two important functions in ovarian differentiation: an initial involvement in the differentiation of somatic cells and a pivotal role in the differentiation of germ cells. Our data suggested that DMRT1 could be considered in human health as a gene necessary for female fertility.

items.title:
Vortex-mediated spin current injection into two-dimensional superconductor NbSe
                    <sub>2</sub>
items.abstract: Injection of pure spin current into superconductors remains a major challenge in superconducting spintronics. Previous studies have primarily focused on spin-polarized quasiparticles and spin-triplet supercurrents, while vortices—ubiquitous topological defects in type-II superconductors—have been theoretically proposed as alternative carriers of spin angular momentum, yet direct experimental evidence is still lacking. Here, we report the vortex-mediated spin current injection in NbSe 2 /LiAl 2 Fe 3 O 8 (LAFO) bilayer, an Ising superconductor/ferrimagnetic insulator heterostructure. Under an out-of-plane temperature gradient and an in-plane magnetic field, the NbSe 2 /LAFO bilayer shows a pronounced thermoelectric peak near the upper critical magnetic field, which has the opposite sign to the conventional vortex Nernst signal observed in a single-layer NbSe 2 . The sign reversal suggests that the vortex flow induced by spin current injection is opposite to the flow driven by the temperature gradient, which is consistent with theoretical mechanisms including spin-vorticity transmutation and the inverse vortex spin Hall effect. By mapping the field–temperature phase diagram, we reveal that the spin current injection occurs exclusively in the vortex liquid phase of NbSe 2 . Absence of the thermoelectric signal above the superconducting transition temperature further rules out the quasiparticle contribution. Our results establish vortices as efficient carriers of spin information in superconductors, opening a new route towards vortex-mediated superconducting spintronic devices.

items.title: Multiple allosteric sites allow for synergistic enhancement of GPCR signaling
items.abstract: Allosteric modulation of G protein–coupled receptors (GPCRs) offers promising therapeutic opportunities. Although multiple allosteric binding sites have been identified in GPCRs, whether and how these spatially distinct sites cooperate to regulate receptor activation remain poorly understood. Here, we elucidate the molecular mechanism of cooperative multisite allostery in the dopamine D1 receptor (D1R). We developed two novel D1R positive allosteric modulators (PAMs), UNC9815 and UNC10062, and used cryo–electron microscopy to structurally identify two previously uncharacterized D1R allosteric sites occupied by UNC9815/UNC10062 and another D1R PAM, BMS-A1. Both sites localize to the transmembrane helix (TM) 1 to 7 interface as vertically adjacent allosteric pockets organized in a spatially complementary manner. Our structures demonstrate the simultaneous binding of the chemically distinct PAMs (LY3154207, BMS-A1, and UNC9815/UNC10062) in three nonoverlapping pockets. Concurrent engagement of all three allosteric sites produces pronounced functional cooperativity, increasing dopamine potency by >1000-fold, thereby demonstrating that coordinated multisite modulation can achieve substantial pharmacological amplification beyond the limits imposed by single PAM administration. Molecular dynamics (MD) simulations revealed that multisite PAM engagement restricts intracellular loop 3 dynamics and stabilizes the TM7-NPxxY activation motif, effects not achieved by binding of LY3154207 alone, thereby biasing the receptor toward a more stabilized active conformation, and may also improve agonist potency by stabilizing extracellular loop 2. Together, these findings establish the structural framework for cooperative multisite allostery in a GPCR, revealing how distributed allosteric sites act in concert to amplify receptor activation and providing a conceptual foundation for developing innovative GPCR allosteric therapeutics.

items.title: Accessing invasion-competent Plasmodium vivax merozoites reveals antibody-dependent NK cell activation
items.abstract: Malaria pathogenesis and clinical symptoms arise from blood-stage replication of Plasmodium parasites, which depends on rapid invasion of red blood cells by merozoites. Despite the central importance of this stage, direct functional studies of Plasmodium vivax ( P. vivax ) merozoites remain limited by the lack of continuous in vitro culture and restricted access to viable, invasion-competent merozoites from clinical isolates. Consequently, key aspects of P. vivax merozoite biology and immune recognition remain poorly defined. Here, we establish a robust platform enabling synchronized release and high-yield isolation of invasion-competent P. vivax merozoites from ex vivo cultures. Reversible inhibition of parasite egress using the PKG inhibitor ML10 enables synchronization at the segmented schizont stage, followed by rapid mechanical release of merozoites using a liposome-based extrusion approach. This workflow yields highly pure merozoites with recovery rates exceeding 75% while preserving structural integrity and invasive capacity. Leveraging this platform, we demonstrate that antibody-opsonized P. vivax merozoites activate human natural killer cells, revealing functional antibody-dependent immune responses.

items.title: Voice patches in the marmoset auditory cortex revealed by multimodal optical imaging
items.abstract: Species-specific vocalizations (including human voices) are important for the survival and social interactions of both humans and animals. In both humans and nonhuman primates, voice/vocalization–selective regions have been identified on the lateral temporal cortex. Here, we provide evidence of localized and hierarchically organized voice patches in the auditory cortex of the common marmoset, a highly vocal New World primate, using multimodal optical imaging techniques that directly measure activity from the smooth cortical surface in a noise-controlled environment. Both intrinsic imaging and calcium imaging data revealed two discrete voice patches in a region of the auditory cortex. Our results provided precise functional localization of the two voice patches (posterior and anterior) by anchoring their positions to the tonotopic map and core/noncore areas of the auditory cortex. Both patches preferentially respond to marmoset vocalizations, exhibit quantifiable neural selectivity beyond spectral features, and encode call type and caller identity. Distinct response properties reveal functional differentiation between the posterior and anterior voice patches, with latency differences consistent with a hierarchical relationship. These findings provide new evidence for an evolutionarily conserved cortical architecture in primates that supports vocal communication via voice patches, analogous to face processing systems in human and nonhuman primate brains.

items.title:
The mRNA-based RSV vaccine mRNA-1345 induces robust and durable CD4
                    <sup>+</sup>
                    T cell responses against RSV in younger and older adults
items.abstract: Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) remains a health threat, particularly for infants, older adults, and immunocompromised individuals. Although neutralizing antibodies can help limit infection and viral replication, T cells are essential for reducing disease severity. Assessment of age-related declines in T cell function are important for vaccine evaluation. We used intracellular cytokine staining, activation-induced marker, and Meso Scale Discovery assays and single-cell multiomic profiling to evaluate RSV vaccine mRNA-1345 responses in younger and older adults. mRNA-1345 induced comparable CD4 + and CD8 + T cell responses in both cohorts, with CD4 + responses persisting for 24 months. The CD4 + response was strongly T helper 1 (T H 1)–polarized, with increased interferon-γ, interleukin-2, and tumor necrosis factor–α and minimal T H 2 cytokines. Both CD4 + and CD8 + T cells showed increased polyfunctionality that remained elevated at 2 years. Single-cell and T cell receptor repertoire analyses showed similar Pre-F–specific phenotypes, transcriptional profiles, and clonal overlap across age groups, supporting robust, durable cellular immunity after mRNA-1345 vaccination. These findings indicate shared vaccine-elicited T cell immunity in adults.

items.title: Neurophysiological dynamics related to perception, action, and language in schizophrenia
items.abstract: Schizophrenia disrupts both how people perceive the world and how they express and act on their thoughts, yet these symptoms are usually studied separately. Using magnetoencephalography during multisensory and motor tasks, we tested whether reduced event-related beta-band (15 to 30 hertz) modulation, a signal implicated in predictive control, provides a candidate neural marker across these domains. Compared to healthy individuals, patients showed diminished beta changes during sensory processing and movement completion, suggesting reduced flexibility in updating internal models. This neural pattern covaried with audiovisual simultaneity-judgment behavior, disorganized natural speech, and greater clinical severity. These findings suggest that distributed beta modulation may serve as a candidate cross-domain marker associated with perceptual, motor, and language disturbances in schizophrenia, motivating future studies that directly test predictive updating mechanisms.

items.title: Physical confinement modulates the rate-limiting transition in the release of phosphate from actin filaments
items.abstract: The nucleotide state and rates of transitions between states regulate the dynamics of ATPases. Slow inorganic phosphate (P i ) release following ATP hydrolysis is often rate limiting and associated with key conformational changes. Actin filaments offer a unique opportunity to understand the fundamentals of P i release because identical subunits at filament ends and the interior release P i at markedly different rates. The molecular origin of this difference is debated, so we used extensive all-atom molecular dynamics simulations to characterize P i release from different subunits within an actin filament. The calculated dissociation rates of P i from ADP-Mg 2+ in the active site correlate with experimentally measured P i release rates and scale inversely with the numbers of water molecules in the cavity surrounding the γ-phosphate. Simulations show that egress of P i through the protein channels, including through the N111-R177 backdoor, is not rate limiting and that subunits at the filament ends use alternative egress pathways.

items.title: Prioritizing reducing impacts on species to minimize residual reserves
items.abstract: International conservation goals have driven rapid expansion of protected areas. This growth has favored quantity over quality, and often results in residual reserves (i.e., areas where species already experience minimal anthropogenic impact). Spatial prioritization is commonly used to help design protected area networks that represent species while minimizing costs to stakeholders. This approach can result in the siting of protected areas that do not decrease impacts on species of conservation concern. Here, we show how measures of cumulative impacts on species can be used in a spatial prioritization to site protected areas to reduce impacts on species of conservation concern. We use a trait-based vulnerability framework and anthropogenic stressor maps to quantify cumulative impacts from four human activities, and incorporate those impacts into spatial prioritizations. We demonstrate that the inclusion of cumulative impacts on species in spatial prioritization can more efficiently protect biodiversity, balance socioeconomic objectives, and avoid residual reserve outcomes.

items.title: Spatial decoupling of recognition and signaling in aptamer switches via tri-strand intermolecular competition
items.abstract: Despite decades of progress in aptamer engineering, the development of a single, modular signaling architecture capable of transducing target recognition into a measurable output across structurally diverse analytes remains an unmet challenge in biosensing. We report the Competitor Bridge Aptamer (CoBrA) framework: a modular DNA tridomain architecture that functionally isolates target recognition from signal transduction. Unlike conventional sensors where signal output depends on unpredictable aptamer folding, the CoBrA system uses an aptamer switch to trigger a predictable, concerted spatial displacement between signaling end points. By leveraging computational simulations and energetic balancing, we systematically optimized the CoBrA framework to consolidate recognition, displacement, and ratiometric signaling within a single, minimal-component system. Using the dopamine and cortisol aptamers as models, we demonstrate strong thermodynamic and kinetic synchronization between the Cy3 and Cy5 channels across both targets for dopamine (Cy3: K d = 13.3 ± 3.2 μM, τ = 447 ± 31 seconds; Cy5: K d = 24.0 ± 3.3 μM, τ = 537 ± 22 seconds) and cortisol (Cy3: K d = 36.6 ± 3.9 μM, τ = 205 ± 7 seconds; Cy5: K d = 30.7 ± 5.5 μM, τ = 259 ± 4 seconds) in buffer, serum, and artificial cerebrospinal fluid. Because the signaling event is a predictable, geometry-defined change rather than a fluorescence-specific phenomenon, this architecture is in principle adaptable to surface-based transduction modalities, including electrochemical, field-effect transistor, and plasmonic readouts.

items.title: In-memory phononic learning toward cognitive mechanical intelligence
items.abstract: Mechanical intelligence seeks autonomous materials that embody memory, perception, learning, and decision-making within the mechanical domain. A fundamental challenge is to integrate memory with information processing in an efficient, scalable, and interpretable way that supports cognitive learning and decision-making. Here, we introduce in-memory phononic learning, a framework that unifies non-volatile mechanical memory with wave-based perception in a phononic metastructure. Spatial information is stored as structural states that program elastic-wave responses, allowing probing waves to act as queries that retrieve informative features through parallel, physically transparent localization modes. Learning is achieved by offline optimization of input waveforms to selectively combine these features for multitask memory-pattern recognition without hardware redesign, with decisions inferred directly from output-energy responses. We experimentally and numerically demonstrate high-accuracy classification across tasks from geometric shapes to handwritten digits. Overall, this work elevates “materials that compute” toward “cognitive matter” that can interpret, reason, and learn through wave physics, laying a foundation for scalable and robust autonomous material systems.

items.title: All-soft organic electrochemical diodes based on asymmetric active layers for signal isolation in deformable electronics
items.abstract: All-soft electronics have emerged as a promising platform for deformable and human-centric systems, yet the development of mechanically compliant diodes remains a major challenge due to limitations in material compatibility, device architecture, and stable operation under deformation. Electrochemical approaches offer a viable route to address this challenge by enabling bulk, low-voltage charge modulation in soft materials without relying on rigid junction interfaces. Here, we report, to the best of our knowledge, the first all-soft organic electrochemical diode (OECD) based on an asymmetric active-layer geometry. The device incorporates a transfer-printed ultrathin ion-gel interface that preserves conformal coverage and the active electrochemical architecture under strain. The device achieves high rectification through polarity-dependent electrochemical potential redistribution, with a rectification ratio of up to 2.23 × 10 4 at ±1 V and stable operation under tensile strains of up to 30% and repeated mechanical deformation. This ion-gel-based architecture preserves the electrochemical asymmetry required for diode operation while maintaining structural integrity under strain. Beyond the individual device, the all-soft OECD enables deformable rectifiers and logic gates and functions as a key signal-isolation element that suppresses cross-talk in a deformable pressure-sensing array. These results establish an electrochemical diode platform that combines mechanical deformability, high rectification performance, and circuit-level compatibility, providing a pathway toward fully deformable and integrated human-centric electronic systems.

items.title:
Observations show increased nitrate in coastal cloud droplet residuals from large-particle activation and N
                    <sub>2</sub>
                    O
                    <sub>5</sub>
                    hydrolysis
items.abstract: Clouds change the chemical composition of aerosols, yet observations characterizing these processes are quite limited. Ground-based in-cloud measurements in coastal Southern California show that the highest nitrate to sulfate ratio (2.5 ± 1.7) in droplet residuals is near cloud base where cloud liquid water content and droplet number concentration are below the observed 20th percentile. The number size distribution of nitrate-rich particles peaks at a larger diameter than sulfate-rich particles, supporting growth to droplets of nitrate-rich particles at lower supersaturations than for sulfate-rich particles. Nitrate mass concentrations are up to three times higher in-cloud compared to pre-cloud and correlated with statistically significant reductions in ozone concentrations, consistent with contributions from in-cloud nitrate formation by N 2 O 5 hydrolysis. This study provides quantitative relationships of cloud properties to nitrate production in droplet residuals and associated ozone reduction, illustrating the impacts of aqueous reactions in clouds.

items.title: Submesoscale feedback suppresses marine heatwaves
items.abstract: Marine heatwaves (MHWs) are devastating extreme ocean temperature events whose frequency and severity have surged under global warming, threatening marine ecosystems and fisheries. Yet, the fundamental mechanisms that control their intensity and persistence remain incompletely understood. Here, using a submesoscale-permitting global model simulation validated by long-term observational and reanalysis data, this study reveals a previously overlooked submesoscale feedback that exerts a critical control on MHW severity. It is demonstrated that the submesoscale-induced vertical heat flux suppresses the intensity and persistence of atmosphere-driven MHWs in winter via a negative feedback mechanism. Enhanced air-sea net heat flux strengthens stratification and shoals the mixed layer, weakening submesoscale vertical heat transport by 19.4%, reducing MHW intensification by 18.1%, and accelerating decay by 21.7%. This missing regulatory mechanism indicates that models ignoring the submesoscale feedback likely overestimate MHW severity, with critical implications for future climate projections.

items.title: Wave vortices around oscillating subwavelength holes: Water-wave observation
items.abstract: We consider a two-dimensional wave system containing a subwavelength hole, such as an aperture in an interface supporting surface electromagnetic or acoustic waves or an island in a fluid surface sustaining gravity-capillary waves. Recent studies have revealed the emergence of pronounced wave vortices around such structures, termed type II vortices, in contrast to conventional (type I) vortices associated with phase singularities and intensity nulls. A notable natural manifestation of type II vortices occurs in ocean tides around islands such as New Zealand, Madagascar, and Iceland, where the tidal phase increases by ±2π around the island. Although this phenomenon is usually associated with the Coriolis effect from the rotation of the Earth, here, we demonstrate the controlled generation of type II vortices using a minimal and tunable setup: a dipole-oscillating subwavelength hole and a single incident plane wave. Using laboratory gravity-capillary waves and an oscillating subwavelength “island,” we directly measure the resulting phase structure, topological charge, and wave angular momentum. We show that the emergence and handedness of the vortices can be precisely controlled via the relative phase between the dipolar source and the incident wave. Our results offer a simple and versatile mechanism for engineering subwavelength wave vortices, with potential applications in a variety of two-dimensional wave systems.

items.title: Differential sex-dependent responses of circulating steroid hormones and cortical gene expression in a traumatic brain injury model
items.abstract: Accumulating evidence supports sex differences in traumatic brain injury (TBI) outcomes. However, the underlying processes that lead to sex differences are not well understood. TBI results in the initiation of molecular and cellular responses that facilitate the progression of neurodegeneration. Little is known about how the circulating hormone profile is altered in response to TBI and whether sex differences in endocrine responses might shape secondary injury pathologies. Using intact male and female mice in a preclinical TBI model, we assessed changes in plasma hormone concentrations and cortical gene expression at 24 and 72 hours after TBI. We demonstrate that males and females exhibit sex-specific alterations in circulating levels of testosterone, androstenedione, estradiol, and dehydroepiandrosterone (DHEA) in response to TBI. We also identified sex differences in the expression of genes that are involved in immune responses and tissue remodeling after injury. Moreover, we report divergent circulating hormone and gene expression correlations between sexes.

items.title: Enterococcus faecalis biofilm rewires neutrophil metabolism to suppress antimicrobial activity
items.abstract: Enterococcus faecalis is an opportunistic pathogen that persists in biofilm-associated infections despite robust neutrophil recruitment. How E. faecalis evades neutrophils remains poorly understood. Here, we investigated how E. faecalis biofilms alter effector functions in human neutrophils and a murine wound infection model. We found that E. faecalis biofilm suppresses neutrophil extracellular trap (NET) formation, bacterial engulfment, and neutrophil-mediated control of biofilm growth. This suppression is partly driven by production of lactic acid through the lactate dehydrogenases (LDHs) of E. faecalis , which acidifies the extracellular environment, lowers neutrophil intracellular pH, and disrupts glycolysis, the tricarboxylic acid cycle, and the oxidative pentose phosphate pathway. In a murine wound infection model, loss of LDH increased neutrophil recruitment and NETosis . We also found that high bacterial density, a defining feature of biofilms, suppresses NETosis through a lactic acid–independent mechanism. Collectively, these findings identify biofilm immune evasion strategies mediated by bacterial metabolism and the high-density structural organization of biofilm-associated bacteria.

items.title: BCG vaccination mitigates tau pathology and restores cognitive function in PS19 mice
items.abstract: Retrospective studies in patients with nonmuscle invasive bladder cancer have reported a significant reduction in Alzheimer’s disease incidence (12 to 78%) among Bacille Calmette-Guérin (BCG) recipients versus controls. To investigate the underlying mechanisms, we evaluated BCG in the PS19 mouse model of tauopathy. We found that BCG administration reduced hippocampal phospho-tau and microgliosis while preserving neuronal markers. In vivo volumetric T2–magnetic resonance Imaging (MRI) demonstrated attenuation of brain atrophy accompanied by increased glutamate-weighted chemical exchange saturation transfer–MRI signals. Functionally, BCG-treated mice showed improved performance in the novel object recognition test, as well as improved body-weight maintenance and survival. Transcriptomic profiling of the hippocampus revealed near complete normalization of the PS19 disease-associated gene expression signature toward that of healthy controls. Flow cytometric profiling of brain myeloid populations demonstrated a reduction in activated resident microglia, but total microglia cells remain elevated. Moreover, an increase of trained immunity marker CD80 on the recruited peripheral myeloid cells ensues following BCG treatment. Consistent with this shift in myeloid state, primary brain myeloid cells from BCG-treated mice also exhibited enhanced phagocytosis of fluorescein isothiocyanate-labeled tau fibrils and increased lactate production. Together, these findings indicate that BCG induces systemic and central nervous system myeloid cell reprogramming that limits neuroinflammation, enhances tau clearance, and rescues cognitive and neurodegenerative phenotypes in a tauopathy model. BCG is a safe, readily available therapy that merits consideration as a preventive agent against dementia.

items.title: Interpreting the Hall effect of highly doped conducting polymers
items.abstract: Accurate determination of carrier density and mobility is fundamental to understanding the transport physics of conducting polymers and optimizing their performance. However, Hall effect measurements, widely used for determining carrier concentrations in other materials, have been of limited use for conducting polymers. Applying the conventional Hall coefficient expression ( R H = [ n H q ] − 1 ) consistently yields unphysically high carrier densities in heavily doped polymers. Here, we resolve this problem using a quasi–one-dimensional (Q1D) tight-binding model of the band structure of uniaxially aligned polymer films to analyze the p-type to n-type transition in the Hall effect observed upon increased doping. Our Q1D framework achieves excellent agreement between Hall-derived carrier densities and other independent measurements over a wide doping range. Our findings indicate that the transport physics of aligned polymers is governed by the topology of a single Q1D band within a simple band-filling framework and establish Hall measurements as a powerful tool for studying their charge transport physics.

items.title: A continuous confinement-deconfinement transition in a triangular quantum magnet
items.abstract: A continuous transition between phases hosting distinct excitations—bosonic magnons versus fermionic spinons—is a long-sought phenomenon in quantum magnetism, analogous to the confinement-deconfinement transition in quantum chromodynamics. We report evidence for such a transition in the triangular-lattice antiferromagnet thallium ytterbium disulfide. Antiferromagnetic order develops below T N ≈ 0.53 kelvin. A c -axis field suppresses this order, driving the system into a gapless quantum spin liquid with a spinon Fermi surface above μ 0 H c ≈ 3 T , evidenced by a finite residual linear term in thermal conductivity, a Pauli-like susceptibility, and a temperature-independent nuclear magnetic resonance Knight shift. Approaching H c from above, the scattering rate of itinerant excitations is strongly enhanced, while their density of states shows no critical enhancement, atypical of conventional magnetic quantum criticality. These results point to a continuous confinement-deconfinement transition governed by fractionalized excitations beyond the Ginzburg-Landau paradigm.

items.title: A phosphorylation-gated GAPDH-MAPK6-LBD1 module controls drought-responsive transcription
items.abstract: Drought adaptation requires rapid spatial reorganization of signaling proteins to reprogram stress-responsive transcription, yet how phosphorylation coordinates this process remains unclear. Here we aimed to define how phosphorylation-gated protein relocalization regulates a BpLBD1-centered drought pathway in Betula platyphylla (birch). Drought activated two kinase branches: BpAGC phosphorylated BpMAPK6 at Ser318 within a cryptic nuclear localization signal, promoting importin α recognition, whereas BpCKII phosphorylated BpGAPDH at Thr109, Thr270, Ser279 and Thr298, promoting importin β recognition. Dual phosphorylation enabled coordinated nuclear accumulation of BpMAPK6 and BpGAPDH. In the nucleus, phosphorylated BpGAPDH acted as a scaffold-like adaptor coupling BpMAPK6 to BpLBD1, enabling BpMAPK6-mediated phosphorylation of BpLBD1 at Ser29. This weakened BpLBD1 binding to the BpMYB123 promoter, reduced expression of the drought-sensitivity regulator BpMYB123 , and de-repressed drought-responsive genes such as BpRD29B . Disrupting BpGAPDH or BpLBD1 Ser29 phosphorylation compromised drought tolerance. Thus, a phospho-spatial GAPDH-MAPK6-LBD1 switch couples nuclear protein assembly to drought-responsive transcription.

items.title: Building digital pregnancies from the single cell up
items.abstract: Single-cell digital twins connect in vitro drug screening studies with clinical outcomes, providing a new framework to evaluate therapies and advance precision medicine in pregnancy.

items.title: SNAT2-mediated amino acid import maintains osmotic balance to restrain macrophage metabolic reprogramming and inflammasome activation
items.abstract: Macrophages undergo metabolic reprogramming during inflammatory responses to microbial infection, in part because of activation of the transcription factor HIF-1α (hypoxia-inducible factor 1α). Here, we identified regulators of HIF-1α–dependent gene expression during immune activation induced by lipopolysaccharide (LPS) and during the hypoxic response using genome-wide CRISPR screens in cultured mouse macrophages. The small neutral amino acid transporter SNAT2 (encoded by Slc38a2 ) was a key inhibitor of HIF-1α activation and metabolic reprogramming in cultured and bone marrow–derived mouse macrophages in response to LPS but not to hypoxia. Inflammatory stimulation increased SNAT2 protein abundance and dynamically expanded intracellular amino acid pools in a largely SNAT2-dependent manner. Consistent with the role of intracellular amino acids as osmolytes, SNAT2 deficiency resulted in osmotic imbalance and aberrant activation of NFAT5, a central transcriptional regulator of osmotic stress responses. In turn, NFAT5 promoted nitric oxide– and HIF-1α–dependent metabolic reprogramming and augmented NLRP3 inflammasome activation under hyperosmotic conditions. Supplementation with organic osmolytes mitigated both the excessive metabolic reprogramming and hyperosmotic inflammasome activation in SNAT2-deficient macrophages. Consistent with the heightened inflammatory phenotype in vitro, myeloid-specific deletion of SNAT2 reduced bacterial burden in mice infected with Listeria monocytogenes . Together, these findings identify SNAT2 as a negative feedback regulator that restrains macrophage metabolic reprogramming and inflammatory activation by maintaining amino acid availability that supports osmotic homeostasis.

items.title:
G
                    <sub>q</sub>
                    -coupled GPCRs mediate the oncogenic activity of Gα
                    <sub>q</sub>
                    -Q209L/P mutants in uveal melanoma cells
items.abstract: G protein–coupled receptors (GPCRs) stimulate heterotrimeric G proteins (Gαβγ) to facilitate downstream signaling, termination of which relies on a glutamine (Q) residue at position 209 in G protein α subunits. In uveal melanoma (UM), the most common intraocular malignancy in adults, >90% of patients harbor Q209L (QL) or Q209P (QP) mutations in Gα q and Gα 11 proteins. Although mutationally active Gα subunits are thought to signal independently of GPCRs, some constitutively active Gα subunits may retain the ability to bind to GPCRs. Here, we demonstrated that G q -coupled GPCRs, including 5-hydroxytryptamine receptor 2B (HTR2B), enhanced the oncogenic signaling of Gα q -QL. Although HTR2B antagonists alone had little to no inhibitory effects, they enhanced the sensitivity of UM cells to the Gα q -specific inhibitor YM-254890, as measured by signaling, cell viability, and proliferation assays. Last, treatment of UM cells with HTR2B antagonists and low concentrations of YM-254890 shifted endogenous Gα q -QL/QP mutants into an inactive conformation to a greater extent than did YM-254890 alone. Our study demonstrates that G q -coupled GPCRs enhance the oncogenicity of mutationally active Gα q proteins and that antagonism of HTR2B promotes an inactive state of Gα q -QL/QP that increases sensitivity to an inhibitor of Gα q .

items.title: Erratum for the Research Article “Targeting c-MYC and gain-of-function p53 through inhibition or degradation of the kinase LZK suppresses the growth of HNSCC tumors”
Diet-directed antitumor immunity
items.abstract: A low-protein diet enhances antitumor immunity through a gut bacterium.

items.title:
Gα
                    <sub>q</sub>
                    -coupled receptors activate cAMP signaling through Ca
                    <sup>2+</sup>
                    /calmodulin-stimulated adenylyl cyclases
items.abstract: Among the various G protein–mediated intracellular signaling pathways activated by G protein–coupled receptors (GPCRs), Gα s and Gα i stimulate and inhibit adenylyl cyclases (ADCYs), leading to increases and decreases in cAMP abundance, respectively. Here, we investigated the contribution of Gα q -coupled receptors (Gα q -GPCRs), which typically activate phospholipase C (PLC) and stimulate intracellular Ca 2+ generation, to the regulation of cAMP signaling. We activated the endogenous Gα q -coupled muscarinic acetylcholine receptors (Gα q -mAChRs) and the group 1 metabotropic glutamate receptors (mGluR1/5) in ex vivo hippocampal slices from mice. We also used a chemogenetics approach to activate Gα q -DREADDs (designer receptors exclusively activated by designer drugs) through hM3Dq. We found that stimulation of these Gα q -GPCRs not only increased the abundance of cAMP but also activated downstream, cAMP-mediated intracellular signaling pathways. This GPCR-dependent cAMP signaling required both Gα q activity and intracellular Ca 2+ . Additionally, hippocampal slices from mice lacking the Ca 2+ /calmodulin-stimulated ADCYs, ADCY1 and ADCY8, did not exhibit Gα q -GPCR–mediated cAMP signaling and showed impaired synaptic long-term depression (LTD) mediated by Gα q -mAChRs. Together, our findings highlight a nonconventional function of Gα q -GPCRs in regulating cAMP signaling through distinct ADCYs.

items.title: Subunit engineering enables the generation of human interleukin-39 as a proinflammatory cytokine
items.abstract: Interleukins are signaling proteins that control immune responses. Defining the range of human interleukins, their associated receptors, signaling pathways, and functions is thus indispensable for understanding and modulating protective and pathological immunity. Interleukin-39 (IL-39), a heterodimer composed of the subunits IL-23α and EBI3, has been described as a proinflammatory cytokine in mice, but its existence in the human interleukin repertoire has remained controversial. Here, we showed that IL-39 did not readily form from IL-23α and EBI3 in human cells. A combined computer modeling and experimental approach identified structural features that destabilize the human IL-23α:EBI3 heterodimer. Using these insights, we rationally engineered human IL-23α and EBI3 to form disulfide-linked heterodimers that were secreted by cells. This engineered cytokine engaged the receptor subunits IL-23R and gp130 on primary human immune cells to stimulate phosphorylation of the transcriptional regulators STAT1 and STAT3, resulting in proinflammatory cytokine secretion. Together, our findings define limitations in the biogenesis of human IL-39 and show that these can be overcome by molecular engineering. This work highlights the potential of rational cytokine engineering for generating active immune signaling proteins and lays the foundation for further defining possible roles of IL-39 in human immunity.

items.title: Erratum for the Research Article “NLRP12 interacts with NLRP3 to block the activation of the human NLRP3 inflammasome”
Neuronal tRNA modifications in Aplysia californica are repatterned during behavioral habituation
items.abstract: Transfer RNA (tRNA) modifications are increasingly implicated as posttranscriptional regulators of basic neuronal functions. Characterizing tRNA modification profiles in specific neural circuits that control well-defined behaviors is challenging because of the complexity of conventional neurobiological models. Here, we leveraged the numerically simple central nervous system (CNS) of the marine mollusk Aplysia californica to investigate tRNA modification dynamics during habituation of a defensive reflex. We identified and quantified dozens of tRNA modifications and characterized the distribution of select small RNA modifications across different neuronal and nonneuronal tissues. Upon behavioral habituation of the siphon-elicited siphon withdrawal reflex (SSWR), we found that tRNA modification profiles in the major ganglion that controls the SSWR were repatterned with predictable, learning-related changes. We found a family of anticodon loop modifications that changed with habituation learning, including N 6 -isopentenyladenosine (i 6 A), which increased in abundance, and additional modifications N 1 -methyladenosine (m 1 A) and N 7 -methylguanosine (m 7 G), which decreased. These tRNA modification dynamics occurred independently of changes in the expression of their parent tRNAs, illustrating that behavioral habituation altered the activity of tRNA-modifying enzymes. Overall, our work reveals a link between tRNA modifications and behavioral habituation and provides insights toward understanding the posttranscriptional mechanisms of learning and memory.

items.title: Disruption of the N-terminal domain in a STAT3 hyper-IgE syndrome variant causes disease by sequestering STAT3 in the cytoplasm
items.abstract: Autosomal-dominant hyper-IgE syndrome (HIES) is characterized by chronic mucocutaneous candidiasis, recurrent sinopulmonary complications, noninflammatory atopic dermatitis, high amounts of serum IgE, and nonimmunological manifestations affecting the musculoskeletal and vascular systems. Most cases are caused by heterozygous loss-of-function, dominant-negative (LOF/DN) variants that affect the DNA binding, SH2, or transactivation domains of STAT3. Here, we report a patient with a unique STAT3 allele affecting the STAT3 N-terminal domain (R31Q), who presented with disseminated invasive aspergillosis affecting the brain and lung, bronchiectasis, and high serum IgE but lacked nonimmune disease manifestations. Biochemical analyses in cell lines demonstrated that R31Q reduced the abundance and transcriptional activity of STAT3 and caused it to exhibit negative dominance on wild-type (WT) STAT3. This was due to preferential STAT3 R31Q dimerization with STAT3 WT , sequestration of STAT3 WT :STAT3 R31Q dimers in the cytosol, and a reduction in STAT3 nuclear translocation and transcriptional activity. Lymphocytes from the patient exhibited some typical defects observed in canonical STAT3 LOF/DN HIES, such as reduced memory B cells, MAIT cells, and T H 17 cytokines. However, naïve B cells from this patient had only a partial impairment in immunoglobulin secretion induced by interleukin-21 (IL-21) in vitro, and the patient had normal numbers of T H 2 cells and circulating T FH cells. Our findings reveal that the N-terminal domain regulates STAT3 dimer formation and function and provide a previously unknown biochemical mechanism of disease pathogenesis in STAT3 LOF/DN HIES.

items.abstract: A bacterial effector inhibits translation of host mRNAs by chemically modifying them.

items.title:
Improving optogenetic control over G
                    <sub>i/o</sub>
                    -coupled receptor signaling by optimized GIRK channel expression
items.abstract: Stimulation of G protein–coupled receptors (GPCRs) that couple to G i/o leads to the activation of G protein–activated inward rectifier K + (GIRK) channels and membrane hyperpolarization in excitable cells. GIRK channel availability can determine the success of optogenetic silencing strategies based on G i/o -coupled GPCRs. To selectively enhance G i/o -mediated GIRK currents, we created expression cassettes that coupled the activity of a GIRK subunit to the light-activated G i/o -coupled GPCRs Opn4L (an opsin also known as melanopsin), longwave-sensitive opsin Opn1, parapinopsin, or Opn7b. We used the GIRK1 F137S mutant because of its fast activation, generation of large currents, and formation of homomeric channels, which reduced the size of the expression cassette. We demonstrated that light-mediated activation of GIRK1 F137S through the opsins induced robust GIRK currents in HEK293 cells, cardiomyocytes, and cerebellar Purkinje neurons. Moreover, coupling GIRK1 F137S activation to the promiscuous Opn4L changed the net effect of G protein signaling from G q/11 -mediated excitation to G i/o -mediated inhibition in cerebellar Purkinje neurons and cardiomyocytes. Thus, our tools optimize the use of GIRK activity in the optogenetic control of the G i/o pathway in excitable cells.

items.title: A PRMT5-ANGPTL4 axis in brain endothelial cells regulates cerebellar inhibitory synaptogenesis and motor coordination
items.abstract: Brain vasculature is essential for central nervous system function. Here, we found a cerebrovascular signaling axis in which the arginine methyltransferase PRMT5 in endothelial cells promoted proper inhibitory synaptogenesis and motor coordination in male mice. Cerebrovascular endothelial cell–specific deletion of Prmt5 in mice led to excessive inhibitory synaptic input onto Purkinje cells and progressive motor deficits. Mechanistically, Prmt5 deficiency epigenetically increased the expression of the gene encoding the secreted angiocrine ANGPTL4 through reduced symmetric dimethylation of Arg 8 in histone H3 and Arg 3 in histone H4, which coincided with increased acetylation of Lys 9 in histone H3, at the Angptl4 promoter. Angptl4 deletion in brain endothelium normalized inhibitory synaptic input onto Purkinje cells and partially restored motor coordination in mice with a conditional Prmt5 deficiency. Together, these findings define the endothelial PRMT5-ANGPTL4 axis as a key regulator of cerebellar inhibitory circuitry and motor function, highlighting cerebrovascular mechanisms as potential therapeutic targets for motor coordination disorders.

items.title: Vascular instructions for synaptic specificity
items.abstract: Many signals contribute to the selective assembly of neural circuits alongside the developing brain vasculature. In this issue of Science Signaling , Lu et al. identify endothelial PRMT5 as an epigenetic brake that restrains Angptl4 expression to limit inhibitory synapse formation in the cerebellum, linking angiocrine signaling to synaptic specificity and circuit function.

items.title: Frequency of pharmacogenomic variation and medication exposures among participants in the All of Us Research Program
items.abstract: Pharmacogenomics promises improved outcomes through individualized prescribing. However, the lack of diversity in pharmacogenomics studies impedes clinical translation and the application of precision medicine across populations. We evaluated the frequencies of variants in 16 pharmacogenes ( ABCG2 , CACNA1S , CYP2D6 , CYP2C Cluster , CYP2C19 , CYP2C9 , CYP3A5 , CYP4F2 , DPYD , G6PD , NUDT15 , RYR1 , SLCO1B1 , TPMT , UGT1A1 , and VKORC1 ) and predicted phenotypes and medication exposures using whole-genome sequencing and electronic health record data from nearly 100,000 All of Us Research Program participants. We report that 100% of participants carried at least one pharmacogenomic variant and nearly all (99.5%) had a predicted phenotype with prescribing recommendations. Clinical impact was high with 24.4% of participants having both an actionable phenotype for these pharmacogenes and a prior exposure to an impacted medication with pharmacogenomic prescribing guidance. Importantly, we report thousands of previously unrecognized pharmacogene variants and hundreds of alleles and predicted phenotypes that deviate from known frequencies across populations or were previously unreported, especially in the Americas and African ancestry groups.

items.title: Human antibody combinations determined by epitope mapping of orthopoxvirus A33/A35 confer therapeutic protection in mice
items.abstract: Human infections with mpox virus (MPXV) since 2022 have resulted in more than 188,000 cases reported globally as of June 2026, highlighting the urgent need for effective therapeutics. Here, we recruited smallpox vaccinees and donors with incidental vaccinia virus (VACV) exposure and isolated a panel of human anti-A33/A35 monoclonal antibodies (mAbs) from the latter using recombinant MPXV A35 as a cross-reactive bait. These mAbs recognized four distinct nonoverlapping epitopes (epitopes 1 to 4) and one composite epitope (epitope 3 + 4) on MPXV A35 and exhibited cross-reactivity against multiple orthopoxviruses (OPXVs). Cryo–electron microscopy structural analysis revealed that the high-affinity epitope 3 + 4 mAb HD15 engages an epitope at the A35 dimer interface that is conserved across OPXVs. Combinations of mAbs targeting nonoverlapping epitopes mediated synergistic, Fc-dependent neutralization in vitro; conferred therapeutic protection against lethal VACV challenge; and reduced viral burden and disease severity after MPXV challenge in mice. Together, these findings establish a single-antigen, multiepitope strategy for the development of broadly protective therapeutics against OPXVs.

items.title: Sleep-like slow waves during wakefulness are associated with hallucinations and poorer cognition in Parkinson’s disease
items.abstract: Slow waves during sleep are fundamental for neural homeostasis, metabolic regulation, and waste clearance and are known to be altered in neurodegenerative diseases. Sleep-like slow waves (SLSWs) have been observed in awake, healthy individuals, where they are linked to fluctuations in vigilance and mind-wandering.
