items.title:
Highly Selective Artificial
Lithium Channels
items.abstract: Abstract Sustainable mining and recycling of lithium (Li) have the potential to offer a secure and reliable global supply of lithium to meet rapidly growing energy-storage demands. Bioinspired technologies have the potential to increase sustainability and reduce the environmental impacts of lithium purification. In this study, we report the design of a class of bioinspired supramolecular membrane channels that, to the best of our knowledge, achieve one of the highest overall Li+ selectivities reported to date for artificial transmembrane ion channels, with conservative lower-limit selectivity estimates of Li+/Na+ ≥ 94, Li+/K+ ≥ 136, Li+/Mg2+ ≥ 286, and Li+/Ca2+ ≥ 228 under electrochemically driven transport conditions, thereby establishing a new benchmark for Li+-selective membrane channels. The single-channel conductance of this channel for Li+ ions was determined to be 13.35 pS, equating to Li+ ion transport rates of approximately 1.34 × 107 ions/s per channel at −160 mV. These channels were constructed using a central-ring pillar[5]arene appended with alkyl chains ending in diphenylphosphine oxide (DPP) ligands. Molecular dynamics simulations suggest that Li+ selectivity arises from coupled hydration-shell retention, ion-ligand coordination at the DPP-functionalized entrance, and confinement effects within the LAP5n10-DPP channel. At the DPP-functionalized entrance, Li+ retains much of its compact hydration shell while engaging the phosphoryl oxygen through a favorable ligand-exchange interaction, whereas Na+ interacts with the DPP region primarily through a water-separated outer-shell geometry, and K+ interacts more strongly with the adjacent hydrophobic/phenyl-rich region. At the central constriction, all ions experience hydration-shell disruption, but divalent Ca2+ and Mg2+ face the largest dehydration penalties because pore passage would require near-complete dehydration of their strongly bound hydration shells.
items.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society

items.title:
Smallest
Endohedral Water Cage Featuring a Nonclassic
Polyhedron: Experimental Observation of (H2O)17
items.abstract: Abstract The structural transition from clustered water molecules to the hydrogen-bonding networks of bulk liquid defines one of the most fundamental problems in physical chemistry, yet the precise size at which the endohedral cages emerge remains experimentally elusive. While theory has long predicted that a fully encapsulated water molecule requires a minimum of 16–23 surrounding molecules, direct experimental identification has been hindered by the difficulty of size selection of neutral clusters. Using infrared spectroscopy coupled to vacuum-ultraviolet threshold photoionization, we provide the first experimental evidence that (H2O)17 forms the smallest water endohedral cage, achieving a decades-standing goal of establishing the molecular limit of a solvation shell. Surprisingly, the oxygen framework of this (H2O)17 cage defines an unprecedented, nonclassic polyhedron with four tetragonal, four pentagonal, and two hexagonal faces that breaks the symmetry constraints of all classical Platonic, Archimedean, and Johnson solids. This work establishes a critical structural precursor to the hydrogen-bonding network topology observed in condensed-phase water and offers new perspectives at the multidisciplinary sciences of mathematics, materials, physics, and chemistry.
items.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society

items.title:
Highly Enantioselective
Synthesis of 1,2,3-Trisubstituted
Cyclopropanes through DNA-Catalyzed Johnson–Corey–Chaykovsky
Cyclopropanation
items.abstract: Abstract Developing enzymatic strategies for diverse reaction manifolds is a major objective in modern biocatalysis. Here, we report the first biocatalytic asymmetric Johnson–Corey–Chaykovsky (JCC) cyclopropanation via DNA catalysis. Unlike conventional small-molecule catalysis, which largely favors trans-cyclopropane formation, DNA catalysis enables diastereoselective access to both cis- and trans-cyclopropanes with excellent enantiocontrol from a single catalytic system. The platform accommodates sulfur ylides as well as amide- and ester-derived sulfoxonium ylides. In particular, phenolic ester-derived sulfoxonium ylides exhibit exceptional cis-selectivity while maintaining excellent stereocontrol, overcoming a longstanding limitation of small-molecule-catalyzed asymmetric JCC reactions. Preliminary mechanistic studies are consistent with a DNA scaffold-mediated pathway that promotes cis-diastereomer formation. Together with its scalability under low catalyst loading, this work establishes a previously inaccessible biocatalytic variant of the JCC reaction and expands the scope of DNA catalysis for diastereoselective synthesis.
items.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society

items.title:
Vacancy-Induced
Ligand-Hole Character Redirects Oxygen
Redox in Li-Rich Layered Oxides
items.abstract: Abstract Li-rich layered oxides access high capacities through the combined participation of transition-metal and oxygen redox, but oxygen oxidation is often coupled with irreversible structural rearrangement and voltage decay. Here, we show that oxygen-vacancy-preconditioning modifies the local Ni–O electronic structure and promotes oxygen-derived ligand-hole character in a Li-rich layered oxide. High-temperature quasi-single-crystal (QSC) formation generates oxygen-deficient local environments while preserving the overall layered framework. Synchrotron spectroscopy combined with density functional theory (DFT) calculations reveals enhanced Ni–O hybridization and redistribution of charge compensation toward oxygen-derived states. Mapping resonant inelastic X-ray scattering further shows earlier oxygen participation during charging, followed by increased delocalization of oxygen-derived holes within hybridized transition-metal–oxygen states. This modified redox pathway suppresses Mn reduction and is coupled to a distinct structural response in which transient lattice environments formed during the initial cycle progressively relax during prolonged cycling, while the layered framework is largely retained. The resulting cathode exhibits reduced voltage hysteresis and voltage decay, together with improved electrochemical reversibility. These results establish a direct connection between vacancy-modified ligand-hole character and oxygen-redox-driven structural relaxation, demonstrating how local electronic structure governs the structural pathway of oxygen-redox-active layered oxides.
items.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society

items.title:
Understanding the Instability
Origin for Design of
Robust Pure RuO2 Anode Catalyst in PEM Water Electrolysis
items.abstract: Abstract Ruthenium dioxide (RuO2) shows great promise as an acidic oxygen evolution reaction (OER) catalyst in proton exchange membrane water electrolysis (PEMWE), yet its insufficient stability─often attributed to Ru overoxidation─actually has a hidden cause. Herein, we show that the true culprit is instead residual chloride impurities inherited from the most commonly used RuCl3 precursor. Owing to strong Ru–Cl coordination, substantial chlorine residues are trapped in the RuO2 lattice during conventional synthesis; during electrolysis, they gradually leach out, dramatically accelerating Ru dissolution and lattice oxygen loss and triggering structural collapse. Guided by this insight, we developed a small-molecule-assisted synthesis that yields Cl-free RuO2. The resulting catalyst preserves exceptional structural integrity, sustains its initial activity through 80,000 accelerated degradation cycles, and delivers stable PEMWE operation at 500 mA cm–2 for 500 h, outperforming all reported single RuO2 catalysts and rivaling even the best doped or composite Ru-based catalysts. Our findings resolve a long-standing paradox in RuO2 catalysis and establish chloride elimination as a critical design principle for durable oxide electrocatalysts.
items.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society

items.title:
Noncovalent Metal–Water
Polarization Governs
Helmholtz Capacitance
items.abstract: Abstract Electrified metal–water interfaces govern charge storage and electrochemical reactivity, yet the microscopic origin of their metal-dependent Helmholtz capacitance has remained unresolved. Here, we use extensive density functional theory-based ab initio molecular dynamics simulations to reproduce and explain the long-established experimental capacitance trend at fcc(111) metal–water interfaces. We show that this trend is governed primarily by the electrode-side electronic response of the explicit metal–water interface, which controls the effective electron spillover length and, hence, the bias capacitance. This relation remains predictive for cross-geometry Pt/Au systems. Our findings clarify the microscopic origin of metal-dependent Helmholtz capacitance and suggest a physically grounded design principle for electrode materials in sustainable-energy technologies.
items.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society

items.title:
Biphasic Polyarylisocyanide
Liquid Crystals with Enhanced
Enantiodiscrimination for Residual Chemical Shift Anisotropy Measurements
items.abstract: Abstract Anisotropic NMR spectroscopy has emerged as a powerful tool for the structural elucidation of complex small molecules. Compared with residual dipolar couplings (RDCs), however, the application of residual chemical shift anisotropies (RCSAs) has remained relatively limited, largely owing to the lack of simple and efficient methods for their acquisition. Here, we report a biphasic polyarylisocyanide lyotropic liquid-crystalline (LLC) system based on single-handed helical polyisocyanides prepared by alkyne-Pd(II)-catalyzed controlled polymerization. The biphasic nature of this medium enables straightforward extraction of ΔRCSAs from a single one-dimensional 13C NMR experiment on a single sample, without requiring specialized instrumentation, devices, or postcorrection. We demonstrate the broad applicability of this approach by measuring ΔRCSAs for eight structurally diverse natural products and organic molecules. The resulting 13C ΔRCSAs are sufficiently large to enable reliable structural verification and stereochemical elucidation. Notably, the method allowed us to unambiguously resolve previously questionable 13C NMR assignments in cryptotanshinone. In addition, the chiral LLC medium exhibits pronounced enantiodiscrimination, as demonstrated for indanol enantiomers as well as significant enantiodifferentiating capabilities for several natural alkaloids. Furthermore, 19F RCSA measurements enable direct differentiation of two enantiomers even within a racemic mixture. Together, these results establish biphasic polyarylisocyanide LLCs as a simple, robust, and broadly applicable alignment platform for ΔRCSA measurements, thereby expanding the utility of anisotropic NMR for structural elucidation and chiral molecular characterization.
items.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society

items.title:
Solid–Liquid
Transitions in 1D Metal–Organic
Chalcogenolates
items.abstract: Abstract A lack of melt processability is noted for emerging hybrid material systems like metal–organic frameworks, lead-halide perovskites, and metal–organic chalcogenolates (MOChas). Here, we report reversible solid-to-liquid phase transitions ranging from 67 to 184 °C in silver secondary-alkanethiolate 1-dimensional (1D) MOChas. These MOChas were synthesized using five different secondary alkanethiols: 2-propanethiol, 2-butanethiol, 2-pentanethiol, 3-hexanethiol, and 4-heptanethiol. Structural characterization using small-molecule serial femtosecond crystallography (smSFX) reveals a 1D wire crystal motif. These 1D wire lattices exhibit green-yellow photoluminescence that disappears upon melting. The low melting temperature is attributed to the conformational flexibility of the secondary alkanethiol ligands, providing entropic benefits for the amorphous state. Furthermore, the transition from a nonmolecular, infinite covalent (Ag-SR)∞ network in the solid state to oligomolecular species (Ag-SR)x in the molten state contributes to a higher enthalpy of fusion. Large crystallites are observed to evolve from the liquid near the phase transition temperature. Notably, unmixing of chiral domains occurs in the racemic crystals while the inorganic network remains unchanged.
items.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society

items.title:
Solid-State NMR Reveals
a Bifunctional Disordered
Linker That Couples Katanin Microtubule Anchoring to Condensate-Activated
Severing
items.abstract: Abstract Microtubule severing by katanin drives rapid cytoskeletal remodeling for cell fate decision, yet how the catalytic subunit p60 (Kp60) recognizes the microtubule lattice to achieve efficient severing remains unresolved. Here, we report that the N-terminal intrinsically disordered region (IDR) of Kp60 is an essential bifunctional module for severing activity. Using solid-state NMR (ssNMR), we identified a microtubule-binding domain (MTBD) within the IDR which directly engages the lattice to guide substrate anchoring. Surprisingly, the same IDR also enables Kp60 phase separation. Our ssNMR analyses of the condensed phase pinpointed three discrete interaction regions within the IDR which cooperatively orchestrate this multivalent assembly. Importantly, Kp60 phase separation was associated with markedly increased ATPase activity, supporting a functional link between condensation and enzymatic activation. Using function-separation-mutation analyses, our studies show both microtubule binding and condensation are essential for severing: microtubule targeting provides spatial specificity, while condensation provides the catalytic threshold through local enrichment. Thus, the Kp60 IDR constitutes a bifunctional interface that integrates substrate recognition with enzymatic robustness, thereby establishing phase separation as a fundamental and efficient regulator of microtubule dynamics and cytoskeletal remodeling.
items.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society

items.title:
C–C
Bond Formation via the Addition or Redistribution
of Hydrogen: Chemical Synthesis Beyond Premetalated Reagents or Metallic
Reductants
items.abstract: Abstract Stoichiometric organometallic reagents are used in countless C–C bond-forming processes but are often hazardous, display poor functional group compatibility, and require multistep preparation from the parent platform chemicals. Zerovalent metals are also used to mediate reductive C–C bond formation, but their use at scale poses similar safety and engineering concerns. The formation of C-nucleophiles as transient catalytic intermediates via hydrogen transfer from abundant low-molecular-weight reductants (H2, Me2CHOH, HCO2H) offers a more ideal alternative to preformed carbanions or zerovalent metals in reductive C–C bond formation. Related hydrogen autotransfer processes where reactants serve as redox pairs en route to products of C–C coupling also are desirable, as they avoid both sacrificial reductants and premetalated reagents. In this Review, hydrogen-mediated variants of classical reactions that exploit carbanions or zerovalent metals are described.
items.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society

items.title:
Breaking Symmetry Cancellation:
Heterovalent Substitution
Unlocks Ultrastrong, Phase-Matchable Nonlinearity in Deep-Ultraviolet
Tetrahedral Crystals
items.abstract: Abstract Deep-ultraviolet (deep-UV) nonlinear optical (NLO) crystals demand a challenging integration of strong second-harmonic generation (SHG), sufficient birefringence for phase matching (PM), and a wide bandgap (λ &lt; 200 nm). In tetrahedron-based materials, the hyperpolarizabilities of constituent tetrahedra usually nearly cancel due to structural symmetry, resulting in weak SHG and small birefringence─a classic example being α-SiO2. Breaking this symmetry-driven cancellation while retaining deep-UV transparency thus represents a key chemical design challenge. Here, we report a deep-UV transparent NLO crystal BeSO4 derived from α-SiO2 via stepwise heterovalent tetrahedral substitution. This crystal crystallizes in the noncentrosymmetric tetragonal space group, with alternating BeO4 and SO4 tetrahedra forming [Be3S3O18] six-membered rings. By effectively breaking the symmetry cancellation via alternating low-valence (Be2+) and high-valence (S6+) tetrahedra, BeSO4 achieves a deep-UV cutoff at 176 nm, an exceptional SHG response of 5.1 × KDP at 1064 nm─the strongest among all deep-UV sulfates and Be-containing deep-UV crystals, and a birefringence of 0.038 at 590 nm, almost seven times that of the isostructural BPO4. Unlike BPO4 and α-SiO2, BeSO4 exhibits SHG behavior consistent with phase-matchability, and under 532 nm excitation, it produces a detectable second-harmonic signal at 266 nm. First-principles calculations reveal that the enhanced performance originates from shorter S–O bonds, stronger orbital hybridization, a narrower bandgap, and highly anisotropic electron density, all stemming from the successful cancellation-breaking strategy. It should be noted that the main novelty of this work lies in single-crystal growth, linear/nonlinear optical properties, and mechanistic analysis, since the crystal structure of BeSO4 has been previously reported.
items.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society

items.title:
MetaTag: A Biochemical
Reaction-Guided Design Strategy
for New Metabolite Discovery
items.abstract: Abstract Most small-molecule features detected in untargeted metabolomics remain unannotated, representing the dark matter of the metabolome. Here, we introduce MetaTag, a biochemical-reaction-guided framework that generates high-probability novel metabolites by combining abundant endogenous metabolites with common enzymatic transformations derived from KEGG pathways. In this proof-of-concept implementation, we focused on N-acylation and N-alkylation reactions. We synthesized and characterized a physical library of 1068 compounds, creating a public MS/MS database (https://mtdb-website.vercel.app). Screening against 27 rat tissues matched 180 previously unreported metabolites with 6 at level 1 (confirmed by RT, formula, MS/MS) and 174 at level 2 (confirmed by RT, formula). These metabolites exhibited tissue-specific distributions and participated in the interorgan exchange during fasting. Functional interrogation of one such metabolite, N-propionyltaurine, demonstrated its role as a redox-sensitive regulator in brown adipocytes. This biochemistry-guided strategy provides a scalable platform for the discovery of previously uncharacterized bioactive metabolites.
items.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society

items.title:
Hybrid Solid Oxide
Cell Enables Efficient and Robust
High-Temperature CO2 Electrolysis
items.abstract: Abstract Electrocatalytic conversion of CO2 into chemicals and fuels offers a promising route toward a circular carbon economy. High-temperature CO2 electroreduction in solid oxide electrolysis cells (SOECs) delivers high selectivity and energy efficiency, but balancing mechanical robustness and electrochemical performance remains challenging. Here, we address this challenge by introducing a hybrid ionic-conductor architecture that spatially decouples electrocatalysis, ionic transport, and mechanical support into function-specific layers. The resulting cell combines high mechanical robustness (fracture load &gt; 7 N) with 1.5–3.0-fold higher CO2-to-CO activity than state-of-the-art SOECs over 600–800 °C. Stable operation is maintained for over 1000 h at 1.0 A cm–2. Furthermore, we demonstrate scalability with a single-cell area of 100 cm2, achieving total currents up to 120 A and powers up to 200 W. This work establishes an effective strategy for developing mechanically resilient, efficient, and scalable energy conversion devices.
items.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society

items.title:
Correction to “Condensates
as Conformation
Editors of Disordered Client Proteins”
items.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society

items.title:
Finding the Sweet Spot:
Isomerization Strategy Enables
Balanced Energy Dissipation of NIR-II AIEgens for “One-for-All”
Tumor Phototheranostics
items.abstract: Abstract “One-for-all” phototheranostics with the second near-infrared window (NIR-II) emission have garnered great enthusiasm for seamlessly integrating superb imaging and high-efficiency therapy into a single formula. However, it is still a nontrivial conundrum to achieve balanced excited-state energy dissipation to guarantee high NIR-II brightness, photothermal conversion, and reactive oxygen species (ROS) generation. As a powerful tool for balancing radiative and nonradiative decays, aggregation-induced emission luminogens (AIEgens) are emerging as a promising frontier in developing “one-for-all” phototheranostic agents, while their phototheranostic performance needs to be further improved. In this contribution, we designed and synthesized two positional isomers, 5BT-PBPT and 6BT-PBPT, by attaching donors at the 5- and 6-positions of the benzo[b]thiophene (BT) segment, respectively, to investigate the effect of positional isomerism on the phototheranostic performance of NIR-II AIEgens. Interestingly, both experimental and computational results demonstrate that the isomerization affords great strength in tuning energy levels, structural conformations, aggregation behaviors, and excited-state energy dissipation. Consequently, a sweet spot for fully utilizing excitation energy was achieved in 5BT-PBPT nanoparticles (NPs), which exhibited not only strong NIR absorption but also high NIR-II fluorescence brightness, strong ROS production, and excellent photothermal conversion efficiency (η). Benefiting from this, 5BT-PBPT NPs afforded superior performance in the “one-for-all” phototheranostics for orthotopic breast tumor treatment. This study fully demonstrates the effectiveness of the isomeric engineering strategy in comprehensively improving the phototheranostic capabilities of NIR-II AIEgens and thereby provides an effective approach for the construction of high-performance NIR-II “one-for-all” phototheranostic agents.
items.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society

items.title:
Low-Temperature
Aqueous Upgrading of Waste PET Plastics
into Metal–Organic Frameworks with Confined PdNi Clusters for
High-Performance Semihydrogenation of Alkynes
items.abstract: Abstract The selective semihydrogenation of alkynes to alkenes is an important industrial process for the production of bulk and fine chemicals. However, the activity and selectivity trade-off of alkyne hydrogenation has been a long-standing challenge, due to undesirable overhydrogenation or insufficient activity of the designed catalysts. Here, we report a sustainable route for high-performance alkyne hydrogenation using a metal–organic framework (MOF) confined PdNi cluster (PdcNi) catalyst, synthesized directly from waste polyethylene terephthalate (PET) plastics under low-temperature aqueous conditions. The PdcNi@UiO-66 catalyst with dispersed Pd clusters anchored on Ni clusters not only maximizes Pd utilization but also establishes a new pathway for the recycling of plastics. Importantly, when employed as a catalyst for phenylacetylene semihydrogenation, PdcNi@UiO-66 exhibited outstanding activity and selectivity, achieving a turnover frequency (TOF) of up to 67,470 h–1 at 65 °C. This performance significantly surpasses that of previously reported catalysts and is nearly 20 times higher than that of the commercial Lindlar catalyst. DFT calculations combined with experimental results reveal that the PdcNi cluster exhibits a moderate adsorption strength toward both reactants and target products, compared with its nanoparticle and single-atom counterparts. This balanced adsorption leads to a more favorable thermodynamic tendency for styrene desorption rather than overhydrogenation, ultimately contributing to the high activity and selectivity. This study demonstrates a direct route to transforming PET waste into high-performance MOF-based catalysts for selective hydrogenation, offering a cost-effective and sustainable solution for plastic recycling and the development of high-performance catalysts.
items.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society

items.title:
Mechanistic Insights
of Jahn–Teller Effect
Suppression in High-Entropy Prussian Blue Analogue Cathodes
items.abstract: Abstract The Jahn–Teller (J-T) effect, as discovered by Hermann Jahn and Edward Teller in 1937, often causes lattice distortion and structural instability in Mn-based battery materials. Recent studies suggest that high-entropy design may help suppress J-T distortion, yet the underlying mechanism remains largely elusive due to their compositional complexity and structural disorder. Herein, using a Mn-based Prussian blue analogue as a case study, we employed a machine learning interatomic potential combined with synchrotron extended X-ray absorption fine structure spectroscopy (EXAFS) to elucidate the fundamental mechanism of the J-T suppression in high-entropy materials. Unexpectedly, EXAFS spectra reveal the absence of the typical J-T Mn–N bond-length splitting in our high-entropy Prussian blue analogue sample, but instead a broader Mn–N bond-length distribution. Machine learning-assisted calculations demonstrate the [MnN6] octahedra exhibit randomly oriented distortions along x-, y-, and z-axes in high-entropy lattices, resulting in the local distortion averaging out at the macroscopic scale. Further analysis of the local Mn coordination environment reveals that the high-entropy configuration enhances d-electron delocalization and reduces the energy splitting between Mn dx2–y2 and dz2 orbitals. This allows two structurally and electronically distinct distortion modes to coexist within the lattice, which disrupts long-range cooperative J-T order. Strikingly, the ultralong cycling stability of high-entropy K0.46[Mn0.21Co0.19Ni0.21Cu0.20Zn0.19][Fe(CN)6]0.98·1.69H2O is experimentally demonstrated, achieving 91.0% capacity retention over 50,000 cycles for aqueous ammonium-ion storage, which surpasses all of the Mn-based rechargeable batteries to date. Our study uncovers the microscopic mechanism of J-T suppression in high-entropy materials and provides an effective strategy for designing durable high-entropy battery electrodes.
items.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society

items.title:
A DNA Origami Nanodevice
Programs CD20 Spatial Organization
for Selective Apoptosis of Malignant B Cells in Lymphoma Therapy
items.abstract: Abstract Triggering CD20 clustering to induce B cell apoptosis is considered a promising therapeutic strategy for dysregulated, B cell-driven diseases, yet current methods lack the spatial precision to organize CD20 into defined clusters and fail to discriminate malignant from normal B cells. Here, we describe an intelligent DNA origami nanodevice that integrates an optimized anti-CD20 antibody array with a conformational switch to selectively induce CD20 clustering and apoptosis in B-cell lymphoma. Benefiting from the nanometric precision of DNA origami, we found that arranging anti-CD20 antibodies into a pentavalent array with approximately 10 nm spacing most effectively drives CD20 clustering and downstream apoptosis. Under resting conditions, the nanodevice stays in a closed, tubular shape that conceals the antibody array inside and therefore remains harmless to normal B cells. Upon encountering c-Met expressed on lymphoma B cells, the device unrolls into a planar sheet and exposes the antibody array, triggering potent apoptotic signaling specifically in these malignant cells. In a Raji xenograft mouse model, intravenously injected nanodevices specifically unrolled at the tumor site, inhibited tumor growth by more than 70%, and produced no significant systemic toxicity. By coupling programmable ligand nanopatterning with a shape-changing switch, this DNA origami platform offers a generalizable strategy for receptor-mediated disease therapy.
items.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society

items.title:
Photoinduced Ge(II)-Catalyzed
Divergent Functionalization
of Pyridyl Halides via Electron Donor–Acceptor Complexes
items.abstract: Abstract We report a photoinduced Ge(II)-catalyzed strategy for divergent functionalization of pyridyl halides that leverages in situ electron donor–acceptor (EDA) complex formation to catalytically generate pyridyl radicals, enabling aryl, alkynyl, and alkenyl couplings under mild, protic conditions without an external photocatalyst. Notably, the protocol exhibits excellent chemoselectivity for pyridyl C–X bonds, leaving other aryl halides, including those bearing electron-withdrawing substituents, intact. The protocol further enables unique transformations, including complete C8-selective coupling with 7-aminoquinoline and the modular assembly of benzo[f]isoquinolines from alkenyl boron reagents. Mechanistic studies support an EDA-mediated radical pathway. This work provides a sustainable platform for the divergent functionalization of pyridyl halides and expands the application of main-group elements in catalytic EDA chemistry.
items.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society

items.title:
Unraveling Water Balances
behind Salt Formation in
CO2 Reduction Electrolyzers
items.abstract: Abstract Salt precipitation in CO2 electrolyzers remains a critical barrier to long-term stability, yet the underlying water-salt transport and balance are poorly understood. Here, we established a quantitative mass balance framework to account for water entering and leaving the cathode chamber from all possible sources and across different phases, thereby elucidating the origin of bicarbonate salt formation. We revealed that although the inlet CO2 stream typically flows through a water bubbler, it is often not fully saturated with water vapor and thus results in significant liquid water evaporation inside the cathode chamber. Although water crossover from the anolyte to the cathode is, in principle, sufficient to dissolve the cotransported K+ as carbonate species (or even bicarbonate in some cases), evaporation reduces the effective local liquid water-to-K+ ratio, leading to salt precipitation. Conversely, excessive humidification suppresses salt formation but induces electrode wetting and flooding, highlighting a fundamental trade-off between dehydration-induced crystallization and overhumidification-driven mass transport limitations. Together, these findings establish water management as a governing principle for stabilizing CO2 electrolyzers and provide engineering guidelines for controlling salt formation in electrochemical reactor systems.
items.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society

items.title:
Operando Time-Resolved
Spectroelectrochemical Microscopy
Reveals Distinct Electron Depletion Pathways in Electrocatalysis
items.abstract: Abstract Understanding electrocatalysis requires direct knowledge of how charge carriers are distributed and consumed at active sites under the operating conditions. However, the spatiotemporal dynamics of injected electrons in working catalysts remain largely inaccessible, hindering a mechanistic understanding of catalytic heterogeneity. Here, we develop an operando time-resolved spectroelectrochemical microscopy that enables direct and quantitative mapping of electron density with microsecond temporal resolution and micrometer spatial resolution. Using monolayer MoS2 as a model system, we directly visualize the spatial redistribution and depletion of electrochemically injected electrons during the hydrogen evolution reaction. We observe pronounced site-specific electron depletion that correlates with catalytic activity and further identify two distinct mechanisms governing charge loss: reaction-limited depletion at highly active sites, including edges and Pt-functionalized sites, and injection-limited depletion in bilayer regions. These results establish a quantitative link between local charge carrier dynamics and catalytic activity and provide a general framework for probing nanoscale carrier dynamics in electrocatalysts.
items.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society

items.title:
Uncovering Microbial
Nitrogenous Chemical Diversity
through Isotope-Guided Molecular Networking
items.abstract: Abstract Nitrogen-containing natural products are pivotal sources of bioactive molecules. However, their comprehensive investigation by metabolomics remains challenging due to background interference from primary metabolites and their high structural diversity including peptides, alkaloids, nucleosides, and others. Here, we present NitroVISION, an integrated pipeline that combines stable isotope labeling with targeted molecular networking to selectively detect nitrogen-containing metabolites from a complex mixture. Applied to five well-characterized Streptomyces strains, NitroVISION identified 42 nitrogen-containing natural products across 23 distinct compound classes, from which we characterized menaxinnamide, a new subclass of nonribosomal peptides incorporating a methylnaphthoquinone unit, and octapiperamide, a novel ribosomal peptide featuring a unique piperazine ring. Our work reveals the hidden chemical space of nitrogenous natural products and paves the way for the systematic exploration of microbial metabolic dark matter.
items.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society

items.title:
Correction
to “Universal and One-Step Modification
to Render Diverse Materials Bioactivation”
items.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society

items.title:
Radical–Electrochemical
Coupling Enables Amination
of Methane
items.abstract: Abstract The selective functionalization of methane under ambient conditions is widely regarded as a holy grail in chemistry, yet remains fundamentally limited not only by the inertness of the C–H bond but also by the transient nature of highly reactive intermediates. Short-lived species are often difficult to preserve and utilize prior to productive coupling, constraining accessible reaction pathways and product selectivity. Here, we establish a reaction framework based on in situ interfacial interception of reactive radicals, enabling the temporal coordination between radical lifetime and subsequent reaction processes. Plasma generates short-lived methyl radicals in immediate proximity to a gas–electrode interface, allowing their direct delivery and capture at the catalytic surface, while the electrochemical interface independently converts ammonia into surface-bound amino intermediates. Their coupling enables selective C–N bond formation. This spatially and temporally coordinated process allows highly reactive radical species to be synchronized with interfacial reaction steps, facilitating their productive utilization. Guided by density functional theory, we identify a nickel–cobalt layered double hydroxide catalyst that promotes interfacial coupling between *CH3 and *NH2 intermediates. The optimized system achieves a Faradaic efficiency of 54% for methylamine at 10 mA cm–2, with a productivity of 201 μmol cm–2 h–1 under ambient conditions. Beyond methane amination, this work demonstrates that coordinating the lifetime and transformation of reactive intermediates provides a generalizable strategy for catalytic control, offering new opportunities for the activation and selective transformation of inert molecules.
items.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society

items.title:
Photobiocatalytic Diastereo-
and Enantioselective
Synthesis of Noncanonical Amino Acids Bearing Challenging Stereochemical
Dyads and Triads
items.abstract: Abstract Catalyst-controlled stereodivergent synthesis of acyclic molecules bearing multiple stereogenic centers remains a longstanding challenge in asymmetric catalysis, particularly through intermolecular radical C–C coupling. Here, we report the directed evolution of pyridoxal 5′-phosphate (PLP)-dependent biocatalysts for the stereodivergent synthesis of noncanonical amino acids bearing either skipped α,γ-stereochemical dyads or contiguous α,β,γ-stereochemical triads. Starting from a thermophilic tryptophan synthase β-subunit, protein engineering generated complementary enzyme variants that selectively construct three of the four possible α,γ-stereoisomers through biocatalyst-controlled reversal of both remote γ-stereochemistry and proximal α-stereochemistry. These engineered enzymes catalyzed intermolecular radical C–C bond formation with a broad range of secondary alkyltrifluoroborates, affording α,γ-disubstituted amino acids in excellent yields and stereoselectivities. Furthermore, directed evolution enabled efficient β-dehydroxylative radical coupling of the non-native threonine-derived aminoacrylate intermediate, providing amino acids bearing contiguous α,β,γ-stereochemical triads with up to 96:4:&lt;0.1:&lt;0.1 d.r. and &gt;99:1 e.r. To further demonstrate the synthetic utility of this platform, the stereochemically enriched amino acids were transformed into valuable γ-chiral amines through engineered PLP-dependent tryptophan decarboxylases, establishing a dual PLP enzyme-based biocatalytic cascade for the enantiodivergent synthesis of privileged amine scaffolds. Molecular dynamics simulations reveal that enzyme-controlled γ-stereoselectivity originates from active-site remodeling that modulates π–π interactions and steric contacts governing the facial selectivity of the radical addition step. This work expands the synthetic capabilities of radical biocatalysis by enabling catalyst-controlled stereodivergent assembly of complex acyclic stereochemical arrays and establishes engineered PLP enzymes as versatile catalysts for the synthesis of stereochemically complex amino acids and chiral amines.
items.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society

items.title:
Dead-Potassium
Activation Reconstructing Stabilized
Interface Enables Stable Anode-Free Potassium Metal Batteries
items.abstract: Abstract Anode-free high-energy-density potassium metal batteries (AFPMBs) are critically constrained by the irreversible accumulation of dead potassium (K) and severe dendrite growth. These issues stem from sluggish interfacial kinetics and the continuous fracture of the solid electrolyte interphase (SEI). A multifunctional electrolyte engineering strategy is proposed by incorporating bismuth iodide (BiI3) into a carbonate-based system to simultaneously regulate the bulk K+ solvation sheath, reconstruct the interfacial solvation structure, and reactivate dead K. Experimental and theoretical analyses reveal that the iodide/triiodide (I–/I3–) species weaken the coordination of K+ with solvents and FSI– in the bulk electrolyte, generating a weakly coordinated solvation structure, which facilitates K+ desolvation. At the electrode interface, Bi-derived sites preferentially recruit and selectively adsorb free FSI– over carbonate solvents and promote their enrichment toward the inner Helmholtz layer, thereby reconstructing an anion-rich interfacial solvation structure that directs the formation of a robust inorganic-rich SEI. In parallel, the reversible I–/I3– redox couple can reactivate dead K. Benefiting from the synergistic suppression of dendrite growth, reduction of irreversible K loss, and enhancement of interfacial kinetics, the symmetric cells demonstrate stable cycling for over 1300 h at 0.5 mA cm–2 and 0.5 mAh cm–2. AFPMBs also demonstrate markedly improved cycling stability and capacity retention in the carbonate-based electrolyte. This work provides a foundation for designing advanced electrolyte additives to enhance electrochemical stability in AFPMBs.
items.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society

items.title:
A Molecular Switch
with Dual Responses to Electrochemical
and Mechanical Stimuli
items.abstract: Abstract Molecular switches capable of responding to two or more orthogonal stimuli are essential for advancing molecular-scale logic, sensing, and memory technologies. However, integrating distinct control mechanisms within a single-molecule architecture remains a fundamental challenge. Here, we report a single-molecule electrochemical-mechanical dual-control switch based on difluoroboron dipyrromethene (BODIPY) molecular junctions. We demonstrate that applying an electrochemical gate voltage threshold (−0.6 V) reduces the BODIPY core to a stable radical anion, effectively serving as a logic enable (EN) signal. Under this electrochemically activated regime, precision mechanical modulation (∼5.0 Å amplitude) via an STM tip cleanly dictates the molecular conformation. Compressive strain drives the formation of a highly conductive asymmetric Au–S/Au−π contact (the SET operation) with a two-order-of-magnitude conductance contrast, while tensile strain physically ruptures the Au−π interfacial coupling to recover the symmetric terminal Au–S anchoring (the RESET operation). This dual-input sliding molecular resistor operates stably at frequencies up to 200 Hz, with density functional theory calculations elucidating the underlying radical-enhanced resonant transport pathway. By seamlessly mapping these synergistic electro-mechanical inputs to digital logic, we successfully transform this molecular junction into a nonvolatile, nanoscale gated RS latch. Ultimately, our work establishes a highly robust and versatile design strategy for constructing complex, multistimuli-responsive molecular circuitry at the single-molecule limit.
items.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society

items.title:
Subcrystal-Mediated
Hetero-Crystallization Enables
Phase-Controlled Zeolite Intergrowths with Multidimensional Disorder
items.abstract: Abstract Phase-controlled synthesis and comprehensive structural understanding of intergrowth zeolites remain challenging because of kinetic competition during crystallization and oversimplified structural models. Differences in nucleation kinetics between competing frameworks and framework interconversion during crystallization can decouple the initial synthesis composition from the final phase composition, while conventional stacking models cannot fully describe their structural complexity. Here, we develop a subcrystal-mediated heterocrystallization strategy using highly active ZSM-5 (MFI) and ZSM-11 (MEL) subcrystals (&lt;10 nm) as preorganized building units. Mixing the isolated ZSM-5 and ZSM-11 subcrystals at defined ratios under mild conditions bypasses the kinetic bias associated with the faster ZSM-5 nucleation and suppresses framework interconversion, enabling ratio-directed control over MFI/MEL phase composition. Time-resolved crystallization and persistently low concentrations of soluble species support a predominantly particle-attachment-dominated nonclassical pathway rather than extensive dissolution-regrowth. Atomic-resolution imaging combined with T12-unit analysis resolves multidimensional disorder beyond conventional one-dimensional intergrowth models, revealing two-dimensional structural disorder, diverse channel architectures, corresponding connector motifs, and connected or interrupted interfaces that accommodate 90°-rotated intergrowth. Variations in phase composition are accompanied by systematic changes in pore characteristics and acidity, together with tunable molecular diffusion and catalytic behavior. This combined control of crystallization kinetics and multidimensional structural complexity provides a general platform for engineering intergrown zeolites with tailored functionalities.
items.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society

items.title:
Water–Organic
Interfaces Drive Molecular Evolution
from Squalene to Steroids
items.abstract: Abstract In living cells, the conversion of squalene to lanosterol requires two dedicated enzymes and proceeds through 2,3-oxidosqualene as an essential intermediate. We show that water microdroplets contacting immiscible organic solvents accomplish this same multistep transformation without enzymatic catalysis. We propose that the oriented electric field across the water–organic interface generates reactive oxygen species that epoxidize squalene and then initiates acid-catalyzed ring-opening of the epoxide followed by a cationic polyene cyclization cascade to yield lanosterol. H218O labeling traced oxygen from water into TEMPO-derived and peroxyacetate ions observed by real-time mass spectrometry. LC–HRMS/MS further revealed C18–C30 reaction products with spectral matches to oxygenated terpenoid and steroid-like structures. We find that ethyl acetate is the most effective organic solvent because it generates peroxyacetic acid at the interface. Simulations show that a preformed protonated 2,3-oxidosqualene model remains hydrated and oriented after placement at the ethyl acetate–water interface, and calculations on microsolvation models indicate that an interfacial water configuration preferentially stabilizes the epoxidation transition state relative to the reactant by approximately 3 kcal mol–1. These results establish a plausible, abiotic pathway for steroid emergence and diversification at water–organic interfaces.
items.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society

items.title:
Dual-Polyhedral Distortion
for Low-Cost Amorphous
Halide Electrolytes with Improved Ionic Conductivity
items.abstract: Abstract Amorphous halide solid electrolytes (AHSEs) have emerged as promising candidates for high-performance all-solid-state Na batteries (ASSNBs) owing to their balanced comprehensive performance. However, rational design principles assisting the precursor selection are still limited for developing low-cost Na-based AHSEs with improved ionic conductivity. Herein, a series of low-cost AHSEs, xNaBF4–ZrCl4 (x = 0.3, 0.5, 1, and 2), were synthesized via a one-step mechanochemical process. Competitive coordination between the Zr4+ and B3+ cations under mechanochemical activation is proposed to promote the rearrangement of F– and Cl– anions within the halide framework. The resulting dual-distorted polyhedral coordination facilitates the formation of long-range disordered structures that are highly favorable for isotropic Na+ transport, exhibiting a high Na+ ionic conductivity up to 1.01 mS cm–1 at 30 °C with excellent oxidative stability of 4.33 V vs Na+/Na. When assembled into all-solid-state cells, the 0.5NaBF4–ZrCl4 electrolyte enables stable cycling between 2.5 and 4.2 V with a capacity retention of 71.5% after 400 cycles at 0.2 C rate. This work provides a novel design paradigm for AHSEs and highlights the promising potential of high-performance ASSNBs.
items.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society

items.title:
Simultaneous Installation
of 1,6-Stereocenters by
Asymmetric Allylation of Resorcinol Boronates: Application to the
Synthesis of Merocyclophane A
items.abstract: Abstract Installing multiple noncontiguous stereocenters in a single catalytic event offers a powerful platform for constructing complex three-dimensional molecular architectures, yet asymmetric methodologies capable of selectively forging remote 1,n-stereochemical relationships remain limited. Here we disclose a strategy for the simultaneous installation of 1,6-stereocenters via para-selective activation of chiral resorcinol boronates with π-allyl iridium complexes. Upon oxidation-induced rearomatization, the resulting dearomatized intermediates furnish the allylated products in an overall transformation that exhibits excellent regio- and stereoselectivity. Crucially, independent variation of the ligand and boronic ester configuration provides predictable access to all four stereoisomers with no observable match–mismatch effects. The synthetic potential of the methodology is exemplified by a concise total synthesis of the cyanobacteria-derived [7.7]paracyclophane merocyclophane A, in which all stereocenters are installed simultaneously on the resorcinol core in a single step.
items.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society

items.title:
Möbius Aromatic
Figure-Eight Knotted Three-Dimensional
Covalent Organic Frameworks
items.abstract: Abstract Möbius aromaticity extends the concept of aromaticity into the topological dimension. However, the synthesis of well-defined molecular systems with this unique property, especially the assembly into infinite polymeric networks, remains a significant challenge due to uncontrolled ring-strain effects. Herein, we report the synthesis of a Möbius aromatic hexa[2,3-thienylene] macrocycle (HTE) with a striking figure-eight shape and the control sample of tetra[2,3-thienylene] (TTE) with an antiaromatic nature, which is further assembled into the extended 3D covalent organic frameworks (COFs) of NUST-67 and NUST-66. The Möbius aromaticity of HTE can modulate the oxidation potential, lower the p-band center of active sites, and weaken the adsorption strength of the *OOH intermediate. As a result, the obtained NUST-67, with a thermodynamically optimized reaction pathway and kinetically enhanced mass/charge transfer, exhibits much superior electrocatalytic activity and selectivity toward H2O2 reduction with industrial-grade performance than NUST-66, featuring a current density window of 100–400 mA cm–2 and an H2O2 Faradic efficiency exceeding 88%. This study discloses the first integration of a Möbius aromatic unit into a COF and elucidates the working effect of aromaticity by a targeted electrocatalytic probe, which establishes a new paradigm for designing organic electrocatalysts by aromaticity engineering.
items.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society

items.title:
Dynamic
Extraction of Internal Active Species in Liquid
Metal-Based Biphasic Catalyst
items.abstract: Abstract Catalyst development is pivotal for industrial and energy advancements, yet it is fundamentally challenged by the static nature of the conventional solid catalysts. Their active sites, locked within rigid frameworks, are neither dynamically responsive nor regenerable, leading to an irreversible consumption during reaction cycles. Herein, we report an electrocapillary-enhanced dynamic extraction process to design a liquid metal-based biphasic catalyst (LMBC), enabling precise population control and in situ regeneration of active species. We establish two key thermodynamic criteria for the dynamic extraction mechanism to guide the LMBC development: alloying energy, which governs the tendency of active elements to form solid active alloys within the liquid metal matrix (gallium, Ga), and surface energy, which drives the dynamic extraction and surface exposure of internal active alloys. Through this mechanism, the quantity of exposed active species becomes adaptively adjustable, allowing fine-tuned control over the catalytic activity. Moreover, deactivated species can be replenished in situ from the liquid metal interior. This LMBC platform demonstrates universality and scalability in the alloy composition across diverse catalysis systems. Overall, this work provides a novel strategy for designing adaptive renewable catalytic systems.
items.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society

items.title:
When
Organic Chemistry Meets Surface Science: From
Nanographene Characterization to Single-Molecule Reactions
items.abstract: Abstract The interplay between organic chemistry and surface science allows for atomically precise characterization, synthesis, and manipulation of carbon-based nanostructures. Advances in scanning probe microscopy and on-surface synthesis have unlocked new routes to obtaining fascinating nanographenes, exotic and highly reactive molecules, and controlled single-molecule reactions. Importantly, these developments open access to transformations that are inaccessible to solution-phase chemistry. Here, we illustrate the potential of this approach and outline the future opportunities and challenges.
items.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society

items.title:
Toward the Rational
Design of Tailored Ligands for
Intrinsically Disordered Proteins through NMR
items.abstract: Abstract Understanding the driving forces governing the interactions between intrinsically disordered proteins and their potential ligands represents a key step toward the rational design of drugs targeting this type of proteins. Nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy provides a unique opportunity to achieve detailed atom-resolved information toward this ambitious goal. We present here a set of differently functionalized calix[4]arene-based multivalent ligands designed to target different regions of the well-characterized intrinsically disordered protein α-synuclein. Dedicated NMR experiments extended the analysis from backbone to side-chain nuclear spins, thus enabling the atom-resolved identification of short-range contacts between the calixarene ligands and methyl or aromatic groups of the protein surface, and revealing how these interactions refine the electrostatically driven association within different lysine-rich motifs. This approach provides a comprehensive description of how the macrocycles recognize and bind the target protein, offering a basis for the rational design of ligands capable of modulating protein function.
items.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society

items.title:
One-Pot Hierarchical
Assembly of Simple Molecules
to Vinylene- and Indole-Linked Covalent Organic Frameworks
items.abstract: Abstract The development in the synthesis of covalent organic frameworks (COFs) has been oriented toward the integration of simplicity, accessibility, stability, diversity, and functionality. However, a central bottleneck remains the lack of effective strategies for assembling simple, unsymmetric, and readily available molecules into highly ordered frameworks. Here, we report a practical synthesis of robust, diversified, and functional COFs via one-pot assembly from a low-cost and simple-structured molecule, 4-methyl-3-nitrobenzonitrile (MNBN). Leveraging the versatile but orthogonal reactivities of MNBN, a three-step cascade sequence, including nitrile cyclotrimerization, Knoevenagel condensation, and reductive cyclization, achieved the symmetrization, reticulation, and functionalization in one pot, thereby enabling the hierarchical construction of two series of COFs with stable o-nitrostyrene or indole linkages. The resulting COFs displayed high crystallinity, permanent porosity, and exceptional stability; solid-state nuclear magnetic resonance (SSNMR) experiments combined with selective isotopic-labeling synthesis further confirmed the high selectivity and controllability of the hierarchical assembly. Notably, the indole-linked COFs, featuring conjugated and electron-rich frameworks, displayed emergent photoelectronic properties and served as efficient, reusable catalysts in both metal-free photocatalytic and metallaphotoredox reactions. By hierarchically exploiting the intrinsic reactivity of a simple, unsymmetric molecule, this work bridges classical organic synthesis and cross-scale covalent assembly, achieving the programmable construction of stable, diversified, and functional COFs.
items.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society

items.title:
A Dynamic Self-Reporting
Metal–Organic Framework
System for Catalysis and Real-Time Reaction Monitoring
items.abstract: Abstract Modern catalysis research has primarily focused on improving catalyst activity, selectivity, and stability through active-site engineering, microenvironment regulation, and mechanistic understanding. However, the sustainability and efficiency of catalytic processes also depend on the dynamic evolution of reaction systems, including substrate consumption, catalyst deactivation, and product accumulation. Despite their importance, these changes are typically assessed by off-line analysis rather than real-time monitoring, which hinders efficient process optimization and sustainable operation. Here, we develop a dynamic self-reporting (DSR) catalytic system based on Ag@UiO-66-(COOH)2/NDCA that simultaneously functions as a heterogeneous oxidation catalyst and an optical reporter for reaction progress. During oxidation, the emission intensity at 440 nm increases with product formation and exhibits a strong quantitative correlation with benzaldehyde yield, enabling reaction progress to be continuously tracked across a series of substituted benzyl alcohols. Mechanistic studies indicate that the luminescence response is governed by competitive absorption and substrate-dependent interactions. Density functional theory calculations further reveal that benzyl alcohol forms stronger dispersion-stabilized π···π interactions with the emissive NDCA2– linkers than benzaldehyde, resulting in more pronounced luminescence quenching. As benzyl alcohol is converted into the more weakly interacting product, this quenching is progressively relieved, producing a measurable increase in emission intensity that reports the reaction progress. This integration provides a platform for reaction monitoring, process optimization, and future automated manufacturing.
items.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society

items.title:
Luminescent Timeline
from Confined Active Radicals
Enables Infinite Cryptograph
items.abstract: Abstract The development of encryption materials is essential to meeting the increasing demand for information security. However, the present materials are susceptible to duplication due to a finite numbers of crypto states. Here, we report one chemical method to expand anticounterfeiting information from discrete, finite states to continuous, infinite states in the temporal domain by regulating the chemical reactions of luminescent radicals with the assistance of image-analysis technology. Infinite cryptographic materials were fabricated with continuous dynamic luminescence processes by integrating reversible radical reactions into confined radical luminescent systems. The inherent chemical kinetics of active radical emitters can be converted to time-dependent emission curves, serving as unclonable keys with nearly infinite crypto states in the temporal domain. Fluorescent AIE molecules were then introduced to expand the color gamut, further enriching the encoding capacity. These infinite cryptographic materials offer a robust anticounterfeiting platform, providing novel pathways for high-level information-protection applications.
items.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society

items.title:
Protecting Groups as
Catalysts: Direct Synthesis of
Primary Amines from Ammonia under Carbonyl Catalysis
items.abstract: Abstract Primary amines are indispensable building blocks in pharmaceuticals, agrochemicals, and functional materials, yet their direct, modular synthesis from ammonia remains challenging. Here we report a carbonyl catalysis strategy that enables the direct synthesis of structurally complex primary amines from ammonia by integrating the conventional multistep sequence of protection, N–H functionalization, and deprotection into a single catalytic cycle. As a proof of concept, amino-trifluoromethylation of alkenes using ammonium salts and Togni reagent afforded a wide range of β-trifluoromethylated primary amines, including derivatives of complex natural products. 1,8-Diazafluorenone was uniquely competent as a carbonyl catalyst, highlighting the critical role of catalyst design in ammonia transformation. Mechanistic studies suggest that its distinctive electronic structure facilitates the formation of the N–H ketimine intermediate, a prerequisite for catalytic turnover. These findings establish carbonyl catalysis as a platform for the direct transformation of ammonia and demonstrate how protecting groups can function as catalysts.
items.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society

items.title:
Complementary
Acetonitrile Reduction and Amine Adsorption
on Mixed Cu–Ni Oxides for Electrocatalytic N-Ethylation
items.abstract: Abstract N-ethylamines are important motifs in pharmaceuticals and fine chemicals, but their selective synthesis from nitriles requires control over both nitrile reduction and amine availability at the catalyst-electrolyte interface. Herein, we investigate mixed Cu–Ni oxides for the aqueous electrocatalytic C–N coupling of acetonitrile (MeCN) with benzylamine (BA). The optimized Cu-NiO-0.5 catalyst affords N-ethylbenzylamine (EBA) in 75% yield with 87% selectivity and a mass-normalized formation rate of 12.5 mmol h–1 gcat–1 at −0.5 VRHE. Electrochemical testing indicates that the presence of CuO can promote the MeCN electrochemical reduction, generating abundant ethylimine for subsequent coupling. Meanwhile, the incorporation of Ni significantly enhances the adsorption of BA, accelerating the C–N coupling between the ethylimine and BA. In situ experimental measurements further confirm the sequential reduction-condensation-reduction pathway. Moreover, this strategy has also been proven to enable efficient C–N coupling between MeCN and various amine derivatives, giving the corresponding N-ethylated products in 58.3–84.6% yield and greater than 74% selectivity. This work offers an environmentally friendly strategy for the electrocatalytic synthesis of N-ethylamines.
items.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society

items.title:
A Stable Phosphinidene
Radical Anion as a Multielectron
Reducing Agent
items.abstract: Abstract The diagonal relationship between carbon and phosphorus has long inspired comparisons between the chemistries of carbenes and phosphinidenes. However, while carbene chemistry has flourished over the past three decades, isolable phosphinidenes remain exceptionally rare, and their one-electron reduction products, phosphinidene radical anions, are unknown. Here, we report the synthesis and isolation of a crystalline phosphinidene radical anion through one-electron reduction of a ring-strained phosphanorcaradiene, a phosphinidene equivalent. Structural, spectroscopic, and computational studies reveal a monocoordinate phosphorus center where the unpaired electron is predominantly localized, in line with a highly reduced phosphorus center. The radical anion exhibits multielectron redox reactivity, including radical addition to an arylalkyne, sulfur atom transfer from isothiocyanate, elemental chalcogen activation, and stepwise oxidation to high-valent P(V) compounds through an overall five-electron process, integrating formal paramagnetic P(0)/P(II)/P(IV) radicals and diamagnetic P(I)/P(III)/P(V) derivatives.
items.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society

items.title:
Cooperative Enantiomorphic-Site
and Chain-End Chirality
in Isoselective β-Lactone Polymerization
items.abstract: Abstract Polymer properties are profoundly impacted by tacticity, necessitating an understanding of the origins of stereocontrol to make high-performance materials. Recently, we reported that controlled incorporation of stereoerrors into trans-poly(3-hydroxy-2-methylbutyrate) (trans-PHMB) through the isoselective polymerization of rac-trans-3,4-dimethylpropiolactone (trans-DMPL) using racemic “sandwich” (BDI)Zn alkoxide complexes (where BDI = β-diketiminate) enables tuning of mechanical properties to match those of low-density polyethylene. However, the mechanism of stereocontrol of these catalysts was not explored. Herein, we report a thorough experimental and computational investigation uncovering a distinct manifestation of cooperative enantiomorphic-site and chain-end control, which we describe as site-mediated asymmetric chain-end control, where catalyst (Δ and Λ) and chain-end chiralities (R,R or S,S) work synergistically to influence the reaction’s stereoselectivity and rate. Experimental and computational data converge remarkably well, revealing that a Δ-catalyst with an (R,R)-chain end (Δ-RR) is isoselective 90% of the time. In contrast, a Δ-catalyst with an (S,S)-chain end (Δ-SS) is unselective. Detailed Density Functional Theory (DFT) investigations suggest molecular-level rationale for this mechanism of stereocontrol, demonstrating that chain positioning, monomer distortion, and ligand interactions work in conjunction to foster isoselectivity. Finally, DFT and kinetic modeling reveal that when polymerizing rac-trans-DMPL, the populations of Δ-RR and Δ-SS are equal and the high overall isoselectivity (mm% = 71–73%; where mm% is the percent of triads with a meso configuration across both ester linkages) of the catalyst is attributed to Δ-RR being faster than Δ-SS.
items.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society

items.title:
Perfluoroalkyl Anion
Strategy to Construct Anion–π+ Type NIR-II
Phototheranostic Agents for Enhanced Tumor Immunotherapy
via Necroptosis/Ferroptosis
items.abstract: Abstract Anion-π+ photosensitizers (PSs) possess exceptional reactive oxygen species (ROS) generation and precise organelle targeting that could disrupt intracellular metabolic homeostasis and induce nonapoptotic cell death, offering unique advantages in overcoming immunosuppression. However, previous reports mainly focused on modifying the π+ core but often overlooked the crucial role of anions. Herein, we present a facile perfluoroalkyl anion strategy to modulate the fluorescence intensity and ROS generation capacity of anion-π+ PSs. Perfluorobutanesulfonate (PFB) anions with a single-sided perfluoroalkyl chain and bis(perfluorobutylsulfonyl)amide (BPFB) anions bearing double-sided perfluoroalkyl chains were employed to readily replace the hexafluoroantimonate (HFA) counterions in A/HFA and TPQ/HFA, yielding A/PFB, TPQ/PFB, A/BPFB, and TPQ/BPFB. Compared to the incorporated PFB anions, the BPFB anions more effectively restrict intramolecular motion through anion-π+ and van der Waals interactions, thereby significantly enhancing the fluorescence intensity of the phototheranostic agents─by 50.8-fold and 4.2-fold in A/BPFB nanoparticles (NPs) and TPQ/BPFB NPs compared to their HFA analogues, respectively. Concurrently, TPQ/BPFB NPs with second near-infrared emission demonstrated superior ROS generation, excellent mitochondrial targeting, and remarkable resistance to photobleaching. Strikingly, TPQ/BPFB NPs can activate both necroptosis and ferroptosis under irradiation, triggering a robust systemic immune response. Additionally, the lipophilicity granted by BPFB enables TPQ/BPFB NPs to infiltrate deeper into tumors, guaranteeing a more extensive photodynamic therapy with a 95% tumor suppression rate. Crucially, the immune memory triggered by TPQ/BPFB NPs effectively decreases the occurrence of lung metastases. Altogether, the perfluoroalkyl anion strategy proposed in this study offers new insights for developing potent anion-π+ PSs.
items.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society

items.title:
MetallopeptiGELs: Injectable
Short-Peptide Supramolecular
Hydrogels Self-Assembled by Pd Nanosheets for Bioorthogonal Therapy
items.abstract: Abstract Controlling the delivery of chemotherapy to the tumor site is a long-standing goal of the medical field, as it could not only enhance the anticancer activity of the treatment but also reduce damage to the rest of the body. The emergence of bioorthogonal catalysis as a strategy capable of mediating continuous drug production in a nonenzymatic fashion has created the opportunity to develop so-called “bioorthogonal therapies,” which aim to generate the anticancer agents inside the tumors. Herein, we describe a novel class of supramolecular materials comprising ultrathin palladium nanosheets and fluorenylmethoxycarbonyl-diphenylalanine that self-assemble in water to form injectable, self-healing, biocompatible catalytic gels that convert inactive prodyes and prodrugs into active small molecules. The relatively weak physicochemical cross-links generated by the hybrid metal-peptide fibers facilitate the flow of the gel under mild shear stress (shear-thinning), thereby enabling precise intratumoral injections in vivo and localized prodrug activation. The strategy was validated in an aggressive pancreatic cancer xenograft model in mice, setting out a new direction for the field of bioorthogonal therapies.
items.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society

items.title:
Carbon Insertion into
Electron-Deficient (Aza)indoles
via a Radical-Polar Crossover Strategy
items.abstract: Abstract Despite a surge of progress in both strategic approaches and reagent design, carbon insertion into indoles remains limited to electron-rich substrates, notwithstanding the prevalence of electron-poor (aza)indoles in medicinal chemistry. We report herein a radical-polar crossover strategy that overcomes this limitation through a photocatalytic, iodomethyl-radical-mediated cyclopropanation/autoxidation approach. The method enables access to a range of highly substituted, electron-poor quinolines, naphthyridines, and triazanaphthalenes, many of which are challenging to prepare by traditional syntheses. We demonstrate the modification of medicinally relevant (aza)indoles, and preliminary mechanistic observations support autoxidation via an anionic cyclopropane ring opening pathway.
items.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society

items.title:
Scalable
Fluorinated Copper-Based Covalent Organic
Frameworks for Coupled Ultratrace Perfluoroalkyl Substances Monitoring
and Efficient Remediation
items.abstract: Abstract Per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) are persistent water contaminants that require both effective removal and reliable monitoring. However, these functions are typically performed separately, preventing real-time evaluation of treatment performance. Here we establish a cooperative host–guest-coupling principle, in which a single host–guest binding event simultaneously drives contaminant capture and modulates the Cu-centered redox process, thereby generating concentration-dependent electrochemical signals within a porous framework. Guided by this principle, we reported a scalable fluorinated copper-based covalent organic framework (F–Cu–COF) synthesized through an open-air one-pot strategy that enables gram-scale production while retaining high crystallinity and chemical stability. Fluorinated pore domains and redox-active Cu centers create a cooperative host–guest environment that promotes PFAS binding and enrichment with electrochemical signal generation. Consequently, F–Cu–COF achieves a detection limit of 5.2 pg L–1, an uptake capacity of 3824 mg g–1, and efficient flow-through removal. This work establishes host–guest coupling as a common molecular basis for linking electrochemical signal generation with contaminant capture in scalable porous materials, providing a general design strategy for multifunctional water-treatment platforms capable of integrated treatment verification.
items.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society

items.title:
Interhalogen of Iodine
Chloride Accelerates Charge
Transfer for Efficient Li2O2 Oxidation in Lithium–Oxygen
Batteries
items.abstract: Abstract Li–O2 batteries suffer from sluggish Li2O2 oxidation kinetics at electrode/electrolyte interfaces, leading to large charge polarization and low energy efficiency. Soluble redox mediators (RMs) provide a solution-mediated pathway for Li2O2 decomposition and reduce the charge overpotential. However, the chemical oxidation of Li2O2 by oxidized RMs remains kinetically sluggish, resulting in persistent charge polarization. Herein, iodine monochloride (ICl), an interhalogen compound, is electrochemically generated in situ during the charge process to promote the oxidation of Li2O2. The large electronegativity difference between I and Cl promotes intramolecular charge transfer from I to Cl, creating an electrophilic iodine center (Iδ+) that increases the I–Cl bond polarity and strengthens the interaction with Li2O2. This lowers the decomposition barrier of Li2O2 from 2.39 to 0.77 eV, thereby facilitating its chemical oxidation. The Li–O2 battery delivers a low discharge/charge polarization of 0.52 V, effectively mitigating parasitic reactions at high voltages and enabling an extended cycling lifespan exceeding 800 h. This work provides a valuable design principle for developing redox mediators for efficient Li2O2 oxidation.
items.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society

items.title:
Support Protection
Mechanism Enables Efficient and
Stable Anion Exchange Membrane Water Electrolyzers
items.abstract: Abstract Designing oxygen evolution reaction (OER) catalysts that simultaneously achieve high activity and long-term stability remains a critical challenge for the development of alkaline anion exchange membrane water electrolyzers (AEMWEs). Here, we uncover a unique support protection mechanism in which lattice-confined ruthenium (Ru) single atoms offer robust protection for the spinel Co3O4 support, realizing outstanding stability in AEMWEs. Theoretical calculations and structural characterizations reveal that lattice confinement promotes the formation of robust Ru–O–Co bridges by simultaneously shortening the Co–O and Ru–O bond lengths, thereby suppressing Co dissolution and optimizing the electronic structure for efficient catalysis. Furthermore, in situ electrochemical analysis demonstrates that the lattice confinement of Ru atoms accelerates OER kinetics through facilitated proton-coupled electron transfer (PCET) steps and partially activated lattice oxygen. As a result, the RuLCA-Co3O4 dominated by the adsorbate evolution mechanism (AEM) exhibits a lower overpotential of 260 mV at 10 mA cm–2, which is lower than that of RuSCA-Co3O4 dominated by the lattice oxygen mechanism (LOM) pathway. Meanwhile, the lattice-confined RuLCA-Co3O4 exhibits nearly 9-fold lower Co dissolution compared to surface-coordinated RuSCA-Co3O4 after an accelerated durability test (ADT). Moreover, RuLCA-Co3O4 maintains an outstanding stability for over 1000 h in an AEMWE system with a low degradation rate of 88.1 μV h–1, outperforming RuSCA-Co3O4. This work establishes lattice confinement as an effective strategy to decouple activity-stability trade-offs in alkaline OER and provides a viable design principle for durable AEMWE anodes.
items.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society

items.title:
Decoupling Dissolution
from Water Oxidation at Single-Faceted
High-Entropy Perovskite Electrodes
items.abstract: Abstract High-entropy oxides (HEOs) are promising anode materials for the oxygen evolution reaction (OER) due to their wide compositional space and electronic flexibility. However, their electrochemical dissolution and OER remain concurrent, preventing decoupled analysis of dissolution kinetics and stability. Here, we present a combined atomic force microscopy (AFM) and scanning electrochemical cell microscopy (SECCM) strategy to decouple lattice dissolution from water oxidation under well-defined reaction conditions. Structurally analogous, atomically flat, single-faceted (001) ABO3 perovskite electrodes, La1–xSrx(Cr0.2Mn0.2Fe0.2Co0.2Ni0.2)O3 with x = 0 and 0.3, serve as model systems to probe dissolution and OER kinetics in acid. Pipet-probed localized cyclic voltammetry and chronoamperometry reveal that the measured current contains contributions from both OER and lattice dissolution, the latter producing nanoscale dissolution pits beneath the SECCM droplet. By correlating pit-growth kinetics with total OER charge as a function of pulse duration (τ), overpotential (η), and pH, we quantitatively separate dissolution from OER. The proportional scaling between dissolution charge and total charge indicates that OER and dissolution proceed within a common kinetic regime, sharing a common intermediate. A rate-law-based analysis yields the standard dissolution rate constant (kd0 cm/s), transfer coefficient (α), and proton reaction order (b) for the dissolution of the 001 facet of both HEO-P. Our results unravel how aliovalent A-site substitution (30% Sr2+) alters dissolution kinetics, charge partitioning between dissolution and OER, and thickness-dependent stability, thereby enabling quantitative disentangling of the intrinsic activity and stability of HEO electrodes.
