Downhill migration to a stronger binding site may increase local barriers for subsequent transformation or introduce site-regeneration penalties, while kinetically accessible hopping may remain irrelevant if it does not reduce the energetic span of the catalytic cycle. In addition, apparent rate enhancements assigned to site hopping can arise from other modes of intersite communication, including desorption–readsorption, subsurface or bulk diffusion, ion–electron intersite coupling, catalyst restructuring, or changes in active-site identity. This Perspective develops a thermodynamic and kinetic framework for distinguishing these processes and assessing when site hopping becomes catalytically consequential. We discuss driving forces, hopping barriers, coverage and dynamic surface effects, kinetic signatures, and diagnostic pitfalls, with the aim of clarifying when site hopping can be used as a catalyst design principle.

items.title: Diastereodivergent Synthesis of 8,12-Guaianolides Using Engineered P450 BM3
items.abstract: Abstract 8,12-Guaianolides are a class of sesquiterpene lactones that exhibit diverse biological activities, which are often strongly influenced by structural variations, including the stereochemistry of the C8 oxygen substituent. Here, we report a concise, diastereodivergent approach to both 8α,12- and 8β,12-guaianolide scaffolds from santonin-derived triene 5 by combining engineered cytochrome P450 BM3-catalyzed allylic C–H hydroxylation with a photochemical rearrangement. The P450 BM3 mutant LG-23 selectively hydroxylates the C8α position of 5, whereas a single additional mutation, L437I, inverts the facial selectivity to favor C8β hydroxylation. Structure-guided mutagenesis and docking studies suggest that the β-methyl group of Ile437 remodels the active site and enforces a flipped substrate binding mode that directs the opposite C8 C–H bond toward the heme iron. The utility of this enzymatic stereochemical switch was demonstrated by the synthesis of the 8α,12-guaianolides xerantholide (1) and mikanokryptin (2) and the 8β,12-guaianolide 11,13-dehydroachalensolide (4). This study demonstrates that a single active-site mutation in P450 BM3 can switch the facial selectivity of C–H hydroxylation at one carbon center, providing a strategy for stereodivergent enzymatic oxidation in complex-molecule synthesis.

items.title: Influence of Extraframework Metal Species on the Kinetics and Spatial Distribution of Coke during Methanol-to-Hydrocarbons Conversion over ZSM-5 Catalysts
items.abstract: Abstract The incorporation of selected extraframework cations is a common approach to tuning the performance of zeolite catalysts in industrially relevant methanol-to-hydrocarbons (MTH) conversion processes, although the mechanistic origin of their effects remains incompletely understood. In this study, we investigated the relationships between MTH and coking kinetics, the nature and distribution of coke deposits, and the positions of extraframework calcium and zinc species in the ZSM-5 catalyst, which promote alkene and aromatic formation, respectively. At comparable Brønsted acid site densities, enhanced aromatics formation over zinc-containing ZSM-5 is accompanied by a 2× higher intrinsic MTH activity and a 150× faster active site loss than over the calcium-containing catalyst. Photoelectron photoion coincidence spectroscopy shows that faster coke-forming kinetics over the zinc-containing catalyst is linked to enhanced formaldehyde formation via methanol dehydrogenation, triggering a cascade of intermediates, such as dienes and aromatics, a pathway inhibited in the calcium-containing catalyst. This also leads to a higher fraction of high-molecular-weight coke in the zinc-containing catalyst and a predominance of surface graphitic coke in the calcium-containing catalyst, as revealed by complementary thermogravimetric, microscopic, and spectroscopic analyses. Powder neutron diffraction indicates that coke preferentially occupies the channel intersections and extends along the straight channels in both catalysts. However, the average coke orientation differs as calcium-containing ZSM-5 comprises more distorted intrapore aromatic deposits, whereas zinc-containing ZSM-5 accommodates more planar aromatic coke. The confinement of coke in micropores is consistent with the preferential location of cations determined by high-resolution X-ray diffraction analysis, which shows that calcium occupies two sites in the sinusoidal channels, with one of these pointing toward the channel intersections, whereas the smaller zinc-associated density is found at sites in five- and six-membered rings between main channels, at the expense of occupancy of sinusoidal channel-based positions. Consequently, faster coke-forming kinetics linked to the dehydrogenation activity of extraframework zinc species, together with lower spatial strain at channel intersections, favor the formation of more condensed, planar-like coke in zinc-containing catalysts. Conversely, the larger size and higher channel occupancy of calcium sites destabilize aromatics and hinder coke formation in this key intersecting zone. These results show that extraframework species influence not only the reaction kinetics but also the local organization and orientation of confined coke, in part through steric constraints associated with their crystallographic location.

items.title: Rhodium-Catalyzed Asymmetric Hydroformylation of Vinyl Ethers as a Key Step in the Synthesis of Chiral Fine Chemicals
items.abstract: Abstract The rhodium-catalyzed asymmetric hydroformylation (AHF) of vinyl ethers provides a powerful synthetic step to yield chiral aldehydes as products or intermediates for industrially relevant fine chemicals. Out of the 40 chiral ligands tested, the phosphine-phosphorodiamidite (S,S,RP,S)-BettiPhos L7 and the phosphine-phosphoramidite ligand L6 performed best in this transformation, combining high activity, regio- and enantioselectivity. Branched 2-aryloxypropionaldehydes (16 examples) were obtained with b/l-ratios ranging from 3.1:1 to exclusive branched products, and with enantioselectivities between 79 and 94% ee. Interestingly, for these substrates, the selective decomposition of the linear aldehydes to the respective arenols and acrolein via β-hydride elimination was observed. Branched 2-alkyloxypropionaldehydes (3 examples) were obtained with fair b/l-ratios (1.7:1–2.6:1) and good to high enantioselectivities (85–95% ee). The utility of this transformation was demonstrated by synthesizing the commercial herbicide (R)-Mecoprop on a gram scale in 69% yield and 91% ee via hydroformylation of 4-chloro-2-methyl-1-(vinyloxy)benzene, followed by oxidation. The catalytic system could also be used under slightly modified reaction conditions for reductive asymmetric hydroformylation to produce in one-pot chiral 2-aryloxypropanols. The synthetic potential was further explored by applying the tandem asymmetric hydrohydrazonemethylation (AHHM) followed by reduction, yielding γ-chiral N′-substituted acetohydrazides as shown for 6 examples. Hydrogenolysis of the crude product mixtures results in the corresponding chiral primary amines, as demonstrated in the synthesis of 2-phenoxypropanamine from (vinyloxy)benzene with an overall yield of 74% and 94% ee on a gram scale. Moreover, another tandem reaction—specifically, the asymmetric hydrosulfiniminomethylation (AHSM)—enables access to halogen-containing chiral primary amines, as demonstrated by the synthesis of 2-(4-chlorophenoxy)propanamine in an overall yield of 53% and &gt;99% ee.

items.title: Extremely High Turnover Number and Turnover Frequency of an Iron Chlorin Complex for Photocatalytic Water Oxidation
items.abstract: Abstract Highly active water oxidation catalysts based on earth-abundant elements are strongly demanded for practical application of artificial photosynthesis. An iron complex with a chlorin ligand derived from chlorophyll-a demonstrated the highest turnover frequency (= 21.3 ± 0.3 s–1) and turnover number (= 6920 ± 110) among homogeneous catalysts reported for photocatalytic water oxidation utilizing [RuII(bpy)3]2+ (bpy: 2,2′-bipyridine) and S2O82– as a photosensitizer and a sacrificial electron acceptor, respectively. The molecular nature of the Fe chlorin complex during the photocatalytic water oxidation was confirmed by dynamic light scattering analysis and electrospray ionization time-of-flight mass spectrometry. Also, kinetic studies suggested that the rate-determining step is O–O bond formation via coupling of two high-valent iron–oxo species formed by three-electron oxidation of the mononuclear Fe chlorin unit with water. The high planarity of the chlorin ligand enables the high-valent iron–oxo species to approach another iron–oxo unit closely, thereby facilitating O–O bond formation.

items.title: Achieving Ordered-Cationic-Vacancy-Mediated Photohole Transfer Dynamics via Phase and Facet Engineering toward Highly Efficient Photoelectrochemical Water Splitting
items.abstract: Abstract Defect engineering is promising to solve the photocarrier dynamics mismatch between rapid bulk recombination and sluggish surface oxygen evolution reaction (OER) in PEC water splitting but is limited by forming random or bulk defects. Herein, we adopt a phase and facet modulation strategy to construct a 2D defective spinel β-In2S3 photoanode with highly exposed, well-ordered indium vacancies (VIn). These VIn introduce a shallow acceptor level near the valence band (VB), which induces selective photohole capture to VIn shallow traps. The efficient and fast (∼0.13 ps) photohole transfer from the VB to the VIn state and the sharply elongated lifetime for photoholes accumulated at VIn, by facilitating band-edge exciton dissociation, induce separation efficiency nearly 100% even at low bias. Meanwhile, surface VIn lowers the OER barrier by boosting the conversion of *OH to *O and promotes surface reaction kinetics, enabling the photohole transfer efficiency to reach 95%. Thus, VIn simultaneously acts as photohole-capture centers and surface-active sites to optimize photohole separation and interfacial transfer dynamics. Through introducing and exposing ordered VIn to reaction interfaces, the β-In2S3-2D photoanode achieves a record-high photocurrent density of 9.7 mA cm–2 at 1.23 VRHE and an IPCE reaching 80% without hole scavengers. Such a regulation mechanism can guide reverse design of defective semiconductor photoanodes for efficient PEC conversion.

Abstract Present herein is a gold(I)-catalyzed asymmetric cascade reaction of 1-(1-alkynyl)cyclobutyl ketones. Upon activation by a chiral phosphoric-acid-tethered gold(I) complex, they undertake intramolecular 5-endo-dig cyclization, and the resulting oxocarbenium species engage in an asymmetric 1,2-alkyl migration to generate gold-containing cyclopenta[b]furan carbocations, which can be intercepted by a broad range of nucleophiles, including indoles, pyrroles, alcohols, and amines, providing efficient access to synthetically challenging tetrahydro-4H-cyclopenta[b]furans bearing vicinal bridged quaternary stereocenters with fair to high enantioselectivity. The intermediates can also participate in (3 + 2) annulations with suitable 1,3-dipoles to afford polycyclic architectures with high molecular complexity. Mechanistic studies and density function theory calculations elucidate the key factors governing the catalytic pathways and stereochemical outcomes.

items.title: Lewis–Brønsted Dual-Acid Sites Induced H-Down Interfacial Water Configuration and Accelerated Proton Transfer toward Enhanced Acidic Oxygen Evolution
items.abstract: Abstract Efficient activation of interfacial water molecules and fast proton transfer are critical but challenging for the acidic oxygen evolution reaction (OER). Herein, a Lewis–Brønsted dual-acid catalyst design strategy is proposed to achieve accelerated acidic OER by synergistically optimizing the configuration of interfacial water molecules and proton transfer kinetics on Mn-doped IrO2. In this catalyst, the Mn dopant serves as a Lewis acid site that readily captures hydroxyl groups, which perturbs the local hydrogen-bonding network and induces interfacial water molecules to form an H-down configuration toward surface active sites, thereby promoting the enrichment and dissociation of reactive interfacial water. On this basis, the formation of the Mn–Obri–Ir local structure enhances the Brønsted acidity of the bridge oxygen (Obri) site, accelerates the deprotonation of the Obri–H bond, promotes the formation of key OER intermediates and accelerates the reaction kinetics. Mn dopant also induces electron enrichment around Ir, suppresses excessive oxidation and dissolution of Ir species, and enhances catalyst stability performance. These synergistic effects enable Mn-IrO2 to achieve a 160 mV overpotential at 10 mA cm–2 and to operate stably for 1500 h at 10 mA cm–2 and 1200 h at 1.0 A cm–2 in proton exchange membrane water electrolysis (PEMWE), demonstrating the promising potential of the Lewis–Brønsted dual-acid strategy in acidic OER catalyst design.

items.title: Direct Amidination of Alkenes Via C–H Activation of Pyridinyl Formimidamide Synthon
items.abstract: Abstract Alkenes are among the most abundant and versatile feedstocks in synthetic chemistry, yet methods for their direct and regioselective conversion into nitrogen-containing frameworks remain scarce. In particular, the direct catalytic amidination of alkenes has remained underdeveloped. Herein, we report a rhodium-catalyzed anti-Markovnikov amidination of alkenes using a stable pyridinyl formimidamide synthon. This reaction enables the direct installation of amidine moieties onto a wide range of alkenes, including styrenes, aliphatic alkenes, and challenging internal alkenes that undergo efficient chain-walking with high regioselectivity and broad functional group tolerance, accommodating unprotected amines, phenols, and halides. The resulting pyridyl amidines can be readily transformed into amides, carboxylic acids and esters, establishing a practical platform for alkene diversification. Notably, late-stage functionalization of complex bioactive molecules, including cyclosporine A, FK506, and quinine etc., provides access to previously inaccessible analogues. Mechanistic investigations, highlighted by the crystallographic capture of a key rhodium–aminopyridinyl formimidamide intermediate, provide compelling evidence for the proposed catalytic cycle. Collectively, this work not only fills a critical gap in alkene functionalization but also offers a concise and general route to high-value nitrogen-containing architectures.

items.title: A Curvature-Induced Pentagonal Oxide Motif Governs Ethylene Epoxidation Selectivity on Silver Nanoparticles
items.abstract: Abstract Silver-catalyzed ethylene epoxidation is a cornerstone of the chemical industry, yet the operando surface structure of Ag nanoparticles and the identity of selectivity-governing active sites remain elusive. Here, we integrate machine learning potentials, stochastic surface walking global optimization, molecular dynamics simulation, and statistical analysis to resolve the surface landscape of Ag nanoparticles approaching experimentally relevant sizes under reaction conditions. Oxygen-induced reconstruction transforms pristine Ag facets into a globally amorphous oxide layer composed of three types of locally ordered ring motifs interspersed with structural defects. A pentagonal motif (ring5), topologically required to accommodate nanoparticle curvature and absent in conventional slab models, dominates the surface across all investigated particle sizes. Its recessed central Ag atom acts as an electronic charge buffer that weakens the critical C–Ag bond in the oxametallacycle intermediate, conferring high intrinsic ethylene oxide selectivity. Microkinetic analyses confirm that the oxygen species of ring5 regulate ethylene oxide yield, peaking at a nanoparticle oxidation degree of O/Ag ≈ 0.3–0.4. This work establishes a statistical paradigm for decoding active phases on realistic catalyst surfaces through dynamic structural ensembles.

items.title: Plasma-Enabled Direct Methane-to-Methanol Conversion on Zeolite-Confined Copper-Oxo Clusters: Insight into Vibrational Excitation and Radical-Mediated Process
items.abstract: Abstract Selective one-step conversion of methane (CH4) to methanol (CH3OH) remains a grand challenge in catalysis, constrained by the trade-off between C─H bond activation and product overoxidation. Here, we integrate density functional theory (DFT) calculations with plasma-catalytic experiments to investigate direct CH4-to-CH3OH conversion using H2O as the sole oxidant on CuxOy clusters within MOR zeolite, compared to the CuO(111) surface. We show that C─H bond activation proceeds preferentially via homolytic H-abstraction on zeolite-confined CuxOy clusters, with Cu3O3/MOR exhibiting a low activation barrier of only 0.21 eV, more than three times lower than that on CuO(111). Vibrational mode-specificity analysis shows that the C─H stretching modes couple most effectively on higher-barrier surfaces. Importantly, we demonstrate that plasma-generated radical intermediates (CH3·, H·, OH·) reshape the reaction thermodynamics, with the Gibbs free energy shifting from endothermic (+1.13 eV) to exothermic (–3.21 eV and –8.25 eV), enabling pathways inaccessible under thermal conditions. Experimentally, Cu/MOR catalysts prepared by ion exchange, which favor well-dispersed zeolite-confined Cu-oxo sites, achieve the highest CH3OH production rate (0.26 mmol/h) at low plasma power (6.5 W), outperforming catalysts prepared by wetness impregnation. This work bridges Cu-oxo site topology, vibrational mode specificity, and radical-mediated thermodynamics, offering valuable insights for plasma-catalytic selective CH4-to-CH3OH conversion.

items.title: Multiobjective Optimization of Synthetically Accessible Homogeneous Catalysts Reveals Tradeoffs for Methane-to-Methanol Conversion
items.abstract: Abstract The selective conversion of methane to methanol remains a major challenge in catalysis, and no earth-abundant homogeneous catalyst has been demonstrated to carry out this transformation with high turnover. To explore previously synthesized complexes that might be amenable for this transformation, we start from macrocyclic ligands from experimental structures in the Cambridge Structural Database. After expanding this set of ligands with Hammett-tuning functionalization, we construct a design space of 21.9 million Mn and Fe catalysts. We employ active learning using neural network surrogate models with quantified uncertainty to efficiently identify catalysts with optimal methane-to-methanol turnover. We do this by jointly optimizing density functional theory (DFT)-computed hydrogen atom transfer (HAT) and methyl radical rebound energetics. Square planar tetraaza-based macrocycles in combination with low-spin Fe(II) or Mn(II) emerge as a privileged class of transition metal complexes within the Pareto-optimal set, with Mn(II) catalysts exhibiting balanced energetic tradeoffs of the two steps. In contrast, porphyrin catalysts exhibit favorable HAT but unfavorable rebound, and seesaw catalysts, which are not widely employed, are indeed the least favorable in our set. Full reaction coordinate analysis of representative Pareto-optimal catalysts reveals that HAT and rebound thermodynamics no longer govern turnover, which is instead determined by the stability of the metal–oxo intermediate and the rebound kinetic barrier. Nonetheless, the resulting energetic spans for these catalysts remain competitive with known earth-abundant, methane-to-methanol catalysts, underscoring the effectiveness of active learning for discovering previously unexplored, synthetically accessible catalysts and unraveling catalyst design principles for methane-to-methanol reactivity.

items.title: Nickel-Catalyzed Enantioselective Cyclizative Alkylation of 1,6-Enynes with Diazo Compounds and Alkyl Halides
items.abstract: Abstract Transition-metal-catalyzed cyclization of 1,n-enynes represents a versatile platform for the construction of structurally diverse chiral heterocycles. Despite substantial advances in this field, the enantioselective cyclizative alkylation of 1,n-enynes remains a formidable synthetic challenge, primarily due to the inherent difficulty in simultaneous control of regio-, chemo-, and stereoselectivity. Herein, we disclose a highly enantioselective cyclizative alkylation of 1,6-enynes employing two complementary alkylating reagents: diazo compounds and readily available alkyl iodides. This protocol proceeds under mild conditions and features broad substrate scope, delivering enantioenriched γ-lactams and pyrrolidine derivatives bearing quaternary stereogenic centers in good yields (up to 81%) and enantioselectivities (53 examples, up to 98% ee). Mechanistic studies corroborate that these two types of alkylating reagents follow entirely distinct catalytic pathways.

items.title: Chemoenzymatic Cascade Recycling and Upcycling of Polyurethane Elastomers
items.abstract: Abstract The complex structure of polyurethanes (PURs) presents a major barrier to their efficient recycling. Here, we report a chemoenzymatic cascade that enables the simultaneous recycling and upcycling of PUR through rapid alkaline pretreatment followed by urethanase-catalyzed depolymerization. Using in-house-synthesized model polyether- and polyester-based PUR elastomers, we establish that soft-segment chemistry dictates the composition, morphology, and accessibility of the pretreated residues, thereby governing the efficiency of the subsequent enzymatic hydrolysis. This insight enabled translation of the cascade to a commercial PUR elastomer, achieving &gt;93% chemical conversion and recovery of up to 1 mM 4,4′-methylenedianiline (MDA) (97.2% purity), corresponding to a 40-fold increase over the nonenzymatic control, together with polyols obtained in 95% isolated yield that were directly reused for PUR synthesis. Mechanistic studies further show that alkaline pretreatment enhances substrate accessibility for the enzyme, and structural analysis of urethanase SP2 reveals a carbamate-specific hydrogen-bonding interaction that promotes urethane hydrolysis while minimizing esterase activity. The cascade was additionally applied to highly crosslinked commercial PUR foams and adhesives, demonstrating its versatility toward industrially relevant waste streams. Overall, this work establishes a mechanistically informed chemoenzymatic platform for PUR depolymerization and provides a strategy for converting chemically recalcitrant PUR waste into reusable molecular building blocks.

items.title: Entropy-Enhanced Catalysis Accelerates Low-Temperature CO2 Methanation via Intermediate Delocalization at Under-Coordinated Ru2+− V O Sites
items.abstract: Abstract In heterogeneous catalysis, the electronic structures of catalysts' active sites are modified to optimize intermediate binding and bond activation for achieving high reaction activity. However, studies on regulating the atomic structures of catalytic materials to enhance the configurational diversity of adsorbed intermediates remain scarce. Herein, we demonstrate that engineering under-coordinated active site motifs enables an entropy-enhanced catalytic mechanism that harnesses the configurational freedom of surface intermediates to improve reaction rates at reduced temperatures. Using CO2 methanation as a model reaction, we identified that under-coordinated Ru2+−oxygen vacancy (Ru2+−VO) sites promote delocalized catalyst−intermediate interactions and reduce the reaction energy barrier. Stable Ru2+−VO sites were created on Au nanoparticle-grafted (RuOx)a(CeOy)b solid-solution nanorods through plasmonic effects under reducing conditions. Eyring plot analysis revealed an activation entropy gain of TΔΔS‡ ≈ 12 kJ mol−1 for CO2 methanation at 300 °C, in situ spectroscopy revealed a *HCOO-mediated pathway, and ab initio molecular dynamics simulations indicated a 0.22 eV free-energy barrier for *HCOO formation on Ru2+−VO motifs. A CH4 production rate of 550 mmol gcat−1 h−1 with &gt;98% selectivity and &gt;280 h stability at 300 °C was achieved at a high gas hourly space velocity of 40,000−100,000 mL gcat−1 h−1. The findings provide a conceptual framework beyond adsorption energy optimization in catalyst design, showing that configurational entropy is a tunable descriptor for enhancing catalytic kinetics.

items.title: Dual-Enzyme Relay Catalysis Enables Asymmetric Construction of Nonadjacent Stereocenters in Polycyclic Alcohols
items.abstract: Abstract The asymmetric construction of nonadjacent stereocenters in a single catalytic system remains a significant challenge due to the difficulty in controlling stereochemical relay between sequential transformations. Herein, we report a dual-enzyme relay catalytic system that integrates an artificial streptavidin-based copper metalloenzyme (Sav-Cu) with an engineered ketoreductase (KRED) for the one-pot synthesis of polycyclic alcohols bearing 1,3-non-adjacent stereocenters. In this relay process, the engineered SavDMase variant (S112A/K121D) catalyzes a non-natural decarboxylative Mannich reaction to establish the R-configured stereocenter in the enantioenriched ketone intermediate, which is then recognized by the engineered KREDAV mutant (S96A/Y190V) and reduced with high diastereo- and enantioselectivity to install the S-configured alcohol stereocenter, thereby furnishing the (R,S)-configured product as the dominant stereoisomer. The optimized system furnishes the products in up to 83% yield, 99% ee, and 96% de across a broad substrate scope, and is readily applicable to 2 mmol-scale synthesis. Structural analysis, docking, and molecular dynamics simulations support complementary roles of the two catalytic modules: SavDMase promotes productive organization of the Mannich step, while KREDAV stabilizes the reactive binding pose and constrains the hydride-transfer trajectory to enforce stereoselective reduction. This work demonstrates how artificial and natural enzymes can be integrated in relay catalysis to solve challenging stereochemical relay problems beyond the reach of individual biocatalysts.

items.title: Repurposing a Donor 2-OH Group for Catalyst-Controlled Stereodivergent Glycosylation
items.abstract: Abstract The free C2-OH group of glycosyl donors is generally viewed as a liability in glycosylation because it can act as a competing nucleophile and compromise stereocontrol. Here, we show that this functionality can instead be harnessed as a programmable stereochemical element in a catalyst-controlled stereodivergent glycosylation. A single β-configured 2-hydroxy glycosyl 8-alkynyl-1-naphthoate donor was found to deliver either β- or α-glycosides simply by changing the gold(I) catalyst system. Triflate-based catalysts promoted highly β-selective glycosylation, whereas bistriflimide-based conditions enabled complementary α-selective glycosylation from the same donor. The method is applicable to a range of carbohydrate and noncarbohydrate acceptors and enables the programmable assembly of glucooligosaccharides bearing β-(1→6), α-(1→6), and alternating α/β-(1→6) linkages from a common donor platform. Mechanistic studies, including intermediate characterization, variable-temperature NMR experiments, computational analysis, and control glycosylations with the corresponding 2-O-Bn donor, reveal distinct roles of the donor 2-OH group in the two stereochemical manifolds.

items.title: The Two Opposite Faces of Ceria as Redox Mediator in Methane Dry Reforming
items.abstract: Abstract We investigate the interplay between carbon accumulation and redox-driven deactivation pathways in cerium-containing nickel (NiCe) and palladium (PdCe) bimetallic precursor materials upon eventual decomposition into a Ni- or Pd-ceria interfacial system during dry reforming of methane (DRM). By probing defined intermediate states, information from surface electronic structure, morphology, and bulk structure to track structural and chemical changes across several reaction, deactivation, and CO2 titration cycles is combined to identify how carbon accumulation, oxygen transfer, and dynamic metal–ceria interfacial interactions evolve under DRM reaction conditions. Despite their similar cerium-containing precursor architecture and surface composition, the two systems allow studying two detrimental deactivation processes. Bimetallic NiCe decomposes more readily into a Ni-ceria interface, where carbon formation is progressively suppressed. Loss of activity is a result of oxidation of Ni particles mediated by enhanced oxygen transfer from ceria. In contrast, bimetallic PdCe is much more decomposition-resistant, and the localized Pd-ceria interface exhibits high activity throughout multiple DRM cycles, even in the presence of substantial carbon deposition and filamentous carbon growth. The results demonstrate an intrinsic coupling between carbon accumulation and oxygen transfer to the metallic component, with carbon acting as a competing sink for reactive oxygen species. We emphasize the significance of dynamic interfacial structures and show that ceria-mediated oxygen transfer produces contrasting, metal-dependent catalytic outcomes. Whereas in NiCe, efficient oxygen delivery suppresses carbon accumulation, but progressively oxidizes Ni and diminishes methane activation, in PdCe, carbon generation outpaces oxygen-mediated removal, yielding a carbon-rich yet catalytically persistent surface.

items.title: Solar-Driven Highly Active and Selective Conversion of Acetonitrile to Formic Acid over Oxygen Vacancy Engineered Tungsten Oxide
items.abstract: Abstract Photocatalytic activation of inert chemical bonds represents a promising route for selective conversion of organic molecules such as acetonitrile (CH3CN) into value-added products. However, as the most common reactive oxygen species, •OH radicals are nonselective and usually lead to overoxidation reactions, making it difficult to realize the target product with both high activity and selectivity in the photocatalytic system. Here, we demonstrate that, through oxygen vacancy (Vo) engineering, selective CH3CN conversion into HCOOH is enabled over a WO3 photocatalyst under mild conditions. Under simulated solar irradiation, the as-prepared Vo-rich WO3 nanosheets display notable photocatalytic CH3CN conversion performance, with a HCOOH yield rate of 8.8 mmol g–1 h–1 and a selectivity as high as 86.5%. In combination of various in situ spectroscopic techniques, it is revealed that the Vo constructs a coupling match between of •OH radicals and •CH2CN intermediates on the WO3 photocatalyst surface, which facilitates the selective conversion of CH3CN into HCOOH while preventing its overoxidation. This work extends the conversion pathway of CH3CN in a photocatalytic route and provides deeper insight into the selective conversion of inert molecules.

items.title:
Spacer Cation-Dependent
Interfacial Dynamics in 2D/3D
Perovskites under Electrochemical Bias
items.abstract: Abstract The integration of two-dimensional (2D) perovskites into three-dimensional (3D) frameworks has been established as an effective strategy to mitigate the intrinsic instability issue of conventional 3D perovskites. However, despite the wide use of spacer cations, less is known about spacer cation-dependent interfacial energetic offsets and their impact on operational stability at a given electrochemical bias. We have now probed charge carrier recombination dynamics at 2D/3D interfaces constructed with two distinct spacer-induced binding motifs: (1) Ruddlesden–Popper phase incorporating butylammonium (BA) and (2) Dion–Jacobson framework formed with 1,4-butanediammonium (BDA) cations. Ultrafast transient absorption spectra recorded under applied electrochemical potentials from −0.2 to +0.4 V versus an Ag/Ag+ reference electrode reveal a different bias-dependent modulation of bleach recovery kinetics at 2D/3D interfaces (BA vs BDA). Interfacial band alignment and potential across interfaces govern the overall charge carrier recombination dynamics. In situ spectroelectrochemical investigations presented in this study provide insight into the critical role of spacer cations in controlling interfacial properties and assist in stabilizing 2D/3D perovskite interfaces.

items.title:
Bispecific Nanobody
Broadly Neutralizes and Cross-Protects
against Three Highly Pathogenic Human Coronaviruses
items.abstract: Abstract SARS-CoV, SARS-CoV-2, and MERS-CoV continue to infect humans or pose a threat of future outbreaks, highlighting the ongoing need for effective, broad-spectrum therapeutics that target these highly pathogenic coronaviruses. As single-domain antibodies, nanobodies have a small size, high target-binding affinity, exceptional stability, low production costs, and the ability to access otherwise hidden or cryptic epitopes. Here, we identified nanobodies targeting SARS-CoV, SARS-CoV-2, and MERS-CoV receptor-binding domains (RBDs) using phage display libraries derived from immunized nanomice and generated a bispecific nanobody to evaluate its broadly neutralizing activity and cross-protective efficacy. Nanobodies 2F11 and 4D6 targeted SARS-CoV RBD, potently neutralizing the SARS-CoV original (Tor2) strain, whereas nanobody 3B11 targeted both SARS-CoV and SARS-CoV-2 RBDs, broadly neutralizing all three SARS-CoV strains (Tor2, GD03, and SZ3) and divergent SARS-CoV-2 variants. Among MERS-CoV RBD-targeting nanobodies, 1C11 demonstrated broadly neutralizing activity against multiple MERS-CoV strains, while its Fc-fused version substantially enhanced the neutralizing potency. These nanobodies exerted neutralizing effects by blocking the interaction between the RBDs and their respective receptors. Cryo-EM structures, computational modeling, and epitope-mapping analyses revealed unique epitopes of 2F11, 3B11, and 1C11 on the SARS-CoV, SARS-CoV-2, or MERS-CoV RBD, underlying their antiviral potency. Finally, a bispecific nanobody 3B11–1C11-Fc that binds to the SARS-CoV, SARS-CoV-2, and MERS-CoV RBDs exhibited high stability and robust cross-neutralizing activity against all tested SARS-CoV, SARS-CoV-2, and MERS-CoV strains, protecting mice from infection with these three coronaviruses. Overall, the identified nanobodies, particularly the bispecific nanobody, exhibit strong neutralizing potency and protective efficacy against SARS-CoV, SARS-CoV-2, and MERS-CoV, showing the potential for further therapeutic development.

items.title:
Leveraging Parameter
Coupling for Signal Enhancement
and Early Detection of Battery Thermal Runaway
items.abstract: Abstract Lithium-ion batteries are vital power sources, but the risk of thermal runaway remains a major safety concern. Existing sensor early-warning systems struggle to detect the localized and rapid evolution of internal failures, leading to inadequate time for preemptive intervention. Here, we present a thermal runaway sensor engineered with a temperature–pressure dual-signal coupling mechanism. The proposed strategy can capture the coupled temperature–pressure signals within the battery pack, thereby enabling the detection of the precursors of battery failure. The sensor can detect abnormal signals about 40 min before the thermal runaway. Translating lab research to industry, we integrated the sensor into commercial large-capacity 314 A h cells. Coupled with a custom-built data acquisition system, the system underwent rigorous validation over 12 months in an energy storage facility under actual conditions. The dual-signal sensing strategy offers an approach for early warning of battery thermal runaway in commercial energy storage systems.

items.title:
Inverted-Mode Scanning
Tunneling Microscopy for Atomically
Precise Fabrication
items.abstract: Abstract Scanning Tunneling Microscopy (STM) enables fabrication of atomically precise structures with growing technological potential. However, reproducible manipulation of covalently bonded atoms requires control over the atomic configuration of both sample and probe–a challenge in STM. Here, we introduce inverted-mode STM, an approach that enables mechanically controlled chemical reactions for atomically precise fabrication. Tailored molecules on a Si(100) surface enable imaging of extended regions of an annealed probe apex, providing direct experimental access to the probe structure relevant to fabrication. The molecules can also react with the probe, with the two sides of the tunnel junction acting as reactants positioned with subangstrom precision. This allows abstraction or donation of atoms from or to the probe. We demonstrate this by using an alkynyl-terminated molecule to reproducibly abstract hydrogen atoms from the probe at zero volts. We then show that successive reactions can replace specific hydrogen atoms with iodine, followed by removal and manipulation of iodine. The approach is expected to extend to other elements, moieties, and materials, enabling sequential, site-selective chemistry for atomically precise fabrication.

items.title:
Subcapsular Sinus
Macrophage Transcytosis Enables
Efficient Intralymphnode mRNA Delivery
items.abstract: Abstract Lymph node (LN)-targeted mRNA vaccines hold promise for cancer immunotherapy, but their efficacy is constrained by limited parenchymal delivery imposed by the lymphatic endothelial barrier of the subcapsular sinus (SCS). The SCS is populated by macrophages that efficiently capture pathogens, raising the question of whether this innate surveillance mechanism can be repurposed for vaccine transport─provided internalized nanoparticles can be rerouted from lysosomal degradation toward transcytosis. Here, we show that yeast cell wall–coated lipid nanoparticles (YCW-LNPs) reprogram SCS macrophages to mediate efficient transcytosis, enabling active delivery into the LN parenchyma and achieving approximately 21-fold higher LN accumulation than unmodified LNPs. Co-encapsulating ovalbumin (OVA) mRNA and the STING agonist MSA-2, YCW-LNPs preferentially accumulate in LNs, drive robust mRNA expression (14.5-fold and 7.4-fold higher than free mRNA and unmodified LNPs, respectively), and concurrently activate the STING pathway to amplify antigen-specific immune responses. In intradermal and lung-metastatic B16-OVA melanoma models, YCW-LNPs achieves marked tumor inhibition (up to 99.0%), prolong survival, and induce durable immune memory protecting mice against tumor rechallenge 60 days after treatment. This pathogen-inspired strategy converts SCS macrophages from degradative sinks into active transporters, offering a generalizable platform for delivering mRNA vaccines and immunomodulators to the LN parenchyma.

items.title:
Vertically Emitted
Near-Infrared Perovskite Chiral
Lasing via a Planar Bound State in the Continuum
items.abstract: Abstract Circularly polarized (CP) coherent light sources are indispensable for quantum information, optical communications, and spintronics. Metasurfaces supporting bound states in the continuum (BICs) offer a promising platform, but planar BIC designs have so far been limited to extrinsic chirality. Such chirality simultaneously produces two oblique beams with opposite helicities on either side of the surface normal, leaving vertically emitted intrinsic chiral lasing with high purity unrealized without complex out-of-plane symmetry breaking. Here, we demonstrate a single-layer planar metasurface that overcomes this barrier by simultaneously breaking in-plane C2 and mirror symmetries, precisely positioning a circularly polarized center (C point) at the Γ-point. This yields strong vertical chiral resonance with a near-unity theoretical degree of circular polarization (DCP), without any out-of-plane symmetry breaking. When integrated with achiral perovskites, our strategy enables the first near-infrared chiral lasing from perovskites and, more critically, the first vertically emitted chiral lasing from planar metasurfaces, delivering a luminescence dissymmetry factor (glum) above 1.5 with no external optical components. This resolves the longstanding trade-off between planar integration and polarization purity, providing a robust, CMOS-compatible strategy for on-chip CP light sources in advanced photonic technologies.

items.title:
Role
of Support Facets and Interparticle Contacts
in Pt Single-Atom Dynamics on Anatase TiO2 Catalysts
items.abstract: Abstract Isolated metal sites in single-atom catalysts (SACs) are dynamic under reaction conditions, yet the role of support features in their redistribution remains to be clarified. Here, using in situ CO-probe diffuse reflectance infrared Fourier transform spectroscopy (DRIFTS) and in situ electron microscopy, we reveal that Pt single atoms on anatase TiO2 surfaces redistribute in a facet- and environment-dependent manner. Increasing the H2 reduction temperature from 250 to 450 °C decreases CO-accessible Pt sites, consistent with Pt migration from TiO2(101) surfaces to TiO2(001) facets associated with interparticle TiO2–TiO2 interfaces and diffusion into subsurface regions. This loss tracks exposed TiO2(001) coverage, but in shape-controlled TiO2 particles, oriented attachment at (001) interfaces suppresses effective facet exposure and preserves Pt accessibility. CO oxidation restores accessible Pt single atoms, revealing a single-atom analogue of strong metal–support interaction. These findings identify that facet abundance and accessibility jointly control single-atom mobility, stability, and catalytic state.

items.title:
Machine
Learning-Driven Discovery of an Endoplasmic
Reticulum-Targeting Gallium(III) Complex that Triggers Immunogenic
Paraptosis in Osteosarcoma
items.abstract: Abstract Osteosarcoma is a highly aggressive bone tumor characterized by profound chemoresistance and immune evasion, resulting in poor clinical prognoses. The rational design of metallodrugs to overcome these obstacles is a formidable challenge, as traditional discovery methods are inefficient for predicting the organelle-specific targeting required for specific mechanisms of action. Here, we introduce a machine learning-driven platform to rationally design and identify endoplasmic reticulum (ER)-targeting Ga(III) complexes capable of activating nonapoptotic immunogenic cell death. This strategy identified Ga20, a complex that triggers a dual mechanism of paraptosis and immunogenic cell death (ICD), directly addressing osteosarcoma’s apoptosis resistance. Formulated as a polymeric nanoparticle (Ga NP) for targeted in vivo delivery, this nanomedicine demonstrated profound tumor growth inhibition across aggressive and clinically relevant orthotopic, metastatic, bilateral, and patient-derived xenograft models. Critically, Ga NP treatment generated a durable in situ vaccine effect, conferring long-term immune memory and preventing tumor recurrence and metastasis. This work establishes a strategy for the computational design of organelle-targeted metallodrugs and presents a powerful chemoimmunotherapy that directly addresses the core clinical challenges of osteosarcoma.

items.title: Zero-Gap to Narrow-Gap Transition in Width-Tunable One-Unit-Cell-Thick Fe 3 Se 4 Nanoribbons Grown on Structurally Anisotropic Co 3 Se 4
items.abstract: Abstract One-dimensional (1D) nanoribbons of two-dimensional layered materials have emerged as compelling platforms for exploring quantum-size-effect-induced properties, e.g., ferromagnetism in phosphorene nanoribbons and chirality-dependent magnetoconductance in graphene nanoribbons. However, the unique electronic and physical properties of 1D metallic transition metal chalcogenide (TMC) nanoribbons have rarely been pursued due to the difficulty in directly synthesizing such 1D ribbons. Herein, we develop the template-mediated synthesis of 1D one-unit-cell-thick Fe3Se4 nanoribbons by designing an anisotropic metal-self-intercalated Co3Se4 template grown on epitaxial graphene/SiC(0001) via a molecular beam epitaxy (MBE) route. We find that a narrow band gap of ∼100 meV can be induced with the nanoribbon width of ∼6.0–20.0 nm, and the gap is reduced to zero with decreasing width to ∼3.0–5.0 nm, according to scanning tunneling microscopy/spectroscopy (STM/STS) characterizations. Metallic edge states are also detected to be confined within ∼2.0 nm around the ribbon edges. Hereby, the interplay of quantum-confinement-induced band gap increase and edge-state-induced band gap renormalization is thus proposed to account for the width-dependent band gap modification. This work should offer valuable insights into the controllable synthesis and dimensionality-related electronic property modulations of 1D TMC nanoribbons, thus paving the way for their intriguing property explorations.

items.title:
Achieving Stable
Sodium Storage in Sodium Superionic
Conductor Anodes via Iron-Enabled Bulk-Interface Confinement for Aqueous
Batteries
items.abstract: Abstract Sodium titanium phosphate (NaTi2(PO4)3, NTP), a promising sodium superionic conductor (NASICON)-type anode for aqueous sodium-ion batteries, suffers from severe capacity fade in alkaline electrolytes due to dissolution of Ti via soluble titanate formation. Herein, we introduce an iron-doping-enabled dual-scale confinement strategy that delivers high capacity and exceptional stability. Iron incorporation in NTP induces a solubility limited behavior: a fraction of Fe enters the NASICON lattice, while excess Fe migrates toward the surface to form a partially amorphous Fe3O4 shell, creating cooperative bulk-shell architecture. The iron-rich outer layer, populated with redox-active Fe3+/Fe2+ couples, acts as a barrier that intercepts and consumes inward-diffusing OH– ions, while inner Fe3+/Fe2+ redox reactions competitively consume residual OH– within the lattice, thereby effectively suppressing soluble titanate formation. This study confirms a synergistic self-protecting and capacity-enhancing mechanism for NTP-based anode design. Consequently, the as-prepared anode delivers a high specific capacity of 164.9 mAh g–1 among all reported NTP anodes, while retaining 90.9% of its initial capacity after 2000 cycles, significantly outperforming previous benchmarks. Paired with a Ni–Co layered double hydroxide cathode, the full cell delivers a high energy density of 106.4 Wh kg–1. This self-organized core–shell dual-defense architecture provides a broadly applicable strategy for stabilizing electrodes in corrosive environments.

items.title:
Critical Pore Sizes
and Distinct Ionic–Metallic
Bonding during Lithium, Sodium, and Potassium Filling of Nanoporous
Carbon
items.abstract: Abstract Nanopore filling is increasingly important as a universal mechanism for Li, Na, and K storage in a range of carbon anodes, including hard carbon, yet the mechanism remains unclear. Using defined pore features in zeolite-templated carbon (ZTC) nanopores, we find that metal–pore matching, rather than pore size alone, governs low-voltage, high-capacity storage. Li exhibits a two-regime filling mechanism in which ionic-carbon wall adsorption competes with metallic clustering, whereas K shows continuous filling with energy changes resembling a solid solution profile. In comparison, Na shows both mechanisms, depending on pore size. This metal-dependent filling chemistry enables alkali compositions beyond graphite intercalation limits, with Li approaching LiC1.2 compared with LiC6 and K reaching KC5.6 compared with KC8. This higher alkali content corresponds to predicted capacities that increase with pore size and fall within reported experimental ranges (e.g., ∼1600, 700, 400 mAh g–1 for Li, Na, and K, respectively, in ∼1.5 nm pores). However, extending the pore size toward the micropore/mesopore region does not necessarily increase useful capacity; instead, it promotes metallic regions that reduce the benefit of confined storage. Selected metal-pore combinations produce ∼0.1 V storage above the metal deposition voltage, consistent with the low-voltage plateau observed in Na-filled hard carbons. These results establish metal-specific pore topology as a design variable for optimizing hard carbon anodes beyond a one-size-fits-all pore-size strategy.

items.title:
Interfacial
Electrochemical Reconstruction Enables
Direct Regeneration of Graphite Anodes
items.abstract: Abstract Graphite anodes are structurally robust and remain largely intact after battery cycling, yet their recycling remains rarely implemented in lithium-ion batteries. Their electrochemical degradation is dominated not by bulk structural collapse but by the accumulation of resistive and heterogeneous solid electrolyte interphase (SEI) layers at the electrode–electrolyte interface. Here we report an interfacial-selective recycling strategy based on electrochemical SEI decomposition (ESD) that directly targets this interface-limited degradation mechanism. By applying a controlled linear potential ramp, ESD selectively oxidizes and removes unstable organic SEI components while reconstructing a thin and uniform inorganic-rich SEI. This process restores Li+ transport pathways and effectively reduces interfacial resistance without introducing bulk defects. Importantly, because ESD directly treats the recovered electrode without material separation, the existing electrode architecture, including the active material, binder, conductive additive, and current collector, can be preserved and reused. As a result, ESD-treated graphite exhibits near-complete recovery of reversible capacity and improved cycling stability in half cells, as well as pronounced performance recovery in full cells after long-term cycling. These findings establish interfacial electrochemical reconstruction as a low-energy and sustainable pathway for graphite anode recycling and reuse.

items.title:
Spatially
Internalized InP@ZnS Quantum Dots Facilitate
Bifunctional Catalysis for High-Efficiency Photo-Driven PHB Biosynthesis
items.abstract: Abstract Semiconductor-biological hybrid systems show potential for sustainable biomanufacturing but are limited by high transmembrane resistance, rapid photogenerated carrier recombination, and a single catalytic mode. We constructed a spatially compartmentalized dual-pathway biohybrid by integrating core–shell InP@ZnS quantum dots (QDs) in vivo into Cupriavidus necator H16. Intracellular QDs directly inject photogenerated electrons via near-field coupling into redox centers, promoting NADP+ and NAD+ reduction, while extracellular QDs photocatalytically generate H2, which acts as a diffusible auxiliary electron carrier, further elevating the pools of NADPH, NADH, and ATP. Under this dual-pathway configuration, peak bulk NADPH/NADP+ and NADH/NAD+ ratios increased by 37.8% and 48.6% (single-cell increases of 26.8% and 37.8%), and total ATP rose by 50.6% during the logarithmic growth phase and by 33.9% at the single-cell level. Without external mediators and under low ambient light (4200 lx), the hybrid achieved a polyhydroxybutyrate (PHB) titer of 6.55 g L–1, which was 2.18-fold higher than that of the light control, representing the highest enhancement reported for C. necator H16-based systems. The ZnS shell suppresses carrier recombination and reduces metal ion leakage, thereby improving stability. This work demonstrates a dual-pathway electron-delivery strategy for microbial production of sustainable materials and presents a generalizable approach that integrates internalization of QDs, dual-pathway electron transfer, and passivation with the ZnS shell.

items.title:
Lithiothermic-Twinning
Built-In LiF Ionic Mediators
within Li2S@Graphene Cathodes for Anode-Less/Free Li–S
Batteries
items.abstract: Abstract Li2S is a promising cathode candidate for Li–S batteries; however, its use is hindered by sluggish redox kinetics and severe polysulfide dissolution. Herein, we propose a collaborative multifunctional regulatory strategy via in situ construction of an integrated Li2S-LiF@graphene capsule by one-step lithiothermic symbiosis (8Li + CS2 + CF4 = 2Li2S + 4LiF + 2C). In this cathode architecture, highly dispersed built-in LiF nanocrystals twinned with active Li2S nanocrystals create abundant and fast ionic-conductive interfaces to accelerate Li-ion transport; meanwhile, symbiotic few-layer graphene shells act as electron highways and physicochemical barriers to inhibit polysulfide loss, thus promoting redox kinetics and structural stability. Multiscale structural characterization combined with in situ analysis confirms enhanced structural stability and electrochemical reversibility. Benefiting from the improved electrical and kinetic properties, as well as high volumetric efficiency for accommodating sulfur species, the Li2S-LiF@graphene cathode exhibits a high areal capacity of 6.3 mAh cm–2 under a high Li2S areal loading (8.9 mg cm–2), a thin Li anode thickness (50 μm), and a lean electrolyte-to-Li2S ratio (4.9 μL mg–1). In a completely anode-free Li2S-LiF@graphene//Ni cell, it delivers 882 mAh g–1 and retains 650 mAh g–1 after 100 cycles. This lithiothermic symbiosis approach combined with multicomponent collaborative regulation offers rational Li2S-based cathode engineering for high-performance anode-less/free Li–S batteries.

items.title:
Computational Design
of a Molecular Pulley for Nanoscale
Force Transmission
items.abstract: Abstract Molecular machines are promising tools for precision nanomachining because they can deform structures at the nanoscale without chemical damage. However, a clear engineering design framework has not yet been established. Practical use requires proper material selection, confirmation of physical feasibility based on molecular interactions, and realistic design guidance. Here, we examine cyclodextrins threaded on flexible hydrogel polymers that act as both sliders and rotational joints while attaching to each other and to surfaces. Molecular dynamics simulations show that this system can operate as a molecular pulley and allow for the evaluation of different scalable geometries and their performance. We demonstrate that pulley mechanisms, such as force direction change and force amplification, can be used to control the elastic deformation of nanopatterned solids.

items.title:
Decoupling Laser
Intensity and Laser Heating Effects
in Plasmonic Photocatalysis Reveals the Temperature Rise Plays a Dominant
Yet Nonexclusive Role
items.abstract: Abstract Separating thermal and laser intensity effects in plasmonic photocatalysis has proven challenging because the two are frequently intertwined. Higher laser intensities will increase any laser-induced heating, making it difficult to isolate the influence of laser intensity and complicating efforts to disentangle thermal versus nonthermal contributions to plasmonic photocatalysis. Here, we decouple laser intensity and laser heating effects by fabricating plasmonic nanostructures with nearly identical optical properties but divergent thermal properties, allowing us to modulate and even eliminate laser heating while applying the same range of laser intensities. We simultaneously perform upconverting nanoparticle (UCNP)-based microscale thermometry and monitor the photocatalyzed dimerization of 4-nitrothiophenol (4-NTP) to 4,4′-dimercaptoazobenzene (DMAB) with Raman spectroscopy. We show that larger temperature rises enhance the reaction and, even more importantly, the temperature rise alone dictates the degree of 4-NTP to DMAB conversion, independent of the applied laser intensity. These results are consistent across two different plasmonic nanostructures. External heating combined with a threshold laser intensity can also drive the reaction, with the degree of conversion again determined solely by the temperature rise. However, despite the critical influence of the temperature rise, external heating alone fails to catalyze the reaction. Leveraging ultrahigh thermal conductivity diamond substrates, which let us increase the laser intensity without inducing heating, we further demonstrate that higher laser intensities increase the reaction rate yet have no effect on the degree of conversion. Thus, although temperature plays an outsize role, the plasmonic photocatalysis process nonetheless cannot be explained by a purely thermal mechanism.

items.title:
Wheat Spike Topology-Inspired
Dynamic “Pearl
Necklace” Nanoarchitectures for Topological Interlocking Adhesion
and Precision Agrochemical Delivery
items.abstract: Abstract Fusarium head blight (FHB) is one of the most devastating diseases of wheat, threatening global food security through yield losses and mycotoxin contamination. Although fungicides remain essential for FHB control, their field efficacy is often restricted by poor deposition and rapid removal from wheat spike surfaces. Inspired by the hierarchical topology of wheat spikes, we transform these inherent surface features into functional anchoring sites by developing a supramolecular “pearl necklace” nanoarchitecture for enhanced pesticide retention. The nanochains are constructed through cooperative electrostatic and hydrophobic interactions between poly-l-lysine (PLL) and sodium dodecyl sulfate (SDS), where SDS nanodomains are periodically organized along PLL nanowires. Isothermal titration calorimetry, molecular dynamics simulations, and physicochemical analyses reveal the noncovalent interactions governing the hierarchical assembly. After deposition onto wheat spikes, the flexible nanochains adapt to surface microstructures through topological interlocking, while PLL amino groups form hydrogen bonds with oxygen-containing groups of fatty acids and esters on the wheat spike surface, collectively enhancing adhesion and rainfall-resistant retention. Compared with commercial prochloraz suspension concentrate, the SDS-PLL-Pro system retained 162% more model-tracer after simulated rainfall. Moreover, PLL-mediated membrane disruption synergizes with prochloraz-induced metabolic inhibition, reducing the EC50 against Fusarium graminearum to 0.37-fold that of the commercial formulation. The system also exhibits favorable biosafety and wheat growth-promoting effects. This work provides a topology-guided supramolecular strategy that converts crop surface characteristics into functional advantages for advanced agrochemical delivery.

items.title:
Correlating Defects
and Surface Contaminants: Toward
Clean Graphene with Improved Mechanical Performance
items.abstract: Abstract The mechanical performance of large-area chemical vapor deposition (CVD) graphene membranes is often compromised by coexisting lattice defects and surface contamination. However, the underlying synergistic mechanisms remain elusive, particularly regarding how defects mediate contaminant nucleation and how their coupling degrades the mechanical properties of graphene. Here, combining in situ spherical aberration-corrected transmission electron microscopy with controlled contaminant removal and redeposition experiments, we provide atomic-scale experimental validation for the causal correlation between graphene point defects and amorphous carbon contamination on CVD-grown graphene. We further achieve real-time, site-resolved visualization of active carbon species migration and defect-trapping dynamics. Multiscale simulations uncover a defect-mediated kinetic-trapping mechanism: active carbon species migrate rapidly over intact graphene yet become captured and immobilized at defects, with the calculated diffusion coefficient dropping from ∼14.4 to 1.65 nm2 ns–1. Moreover, nanoindentation tests confirm that clean graphene exhibits superior mechanical properties (stiffness: ∼305 N m–1 and fracture force: ∼1900 nN) compared to the contaminated counterpart (stiffness: ∼224 N m–1 and fracture force: ∼1077 nN). Continuum finite-element analysis indicates that the reduced stiffness of unclean graphene cannot be explained by surface contamination alone, supporting the presence of defect-induced softening beneath the contamination. Atomically resolved simulations further reveal that the mechanical response is jointly governed by defect type, contamination, and interfacial bonding. In particular, chemically bonded contamination can redistribute local stress and mitigate defect-induced stress concentration, thereby altering the failure process of defective graphene. Our study identifies point defects as both contamination traps and mechanical weak links, offering a unified strategy for high-performance graphene membrane design.

items.title:
Plasmonic Hot Carrier-Driven
Chemistry Revealed by
Dual Raman Thermometry
items.abstract: Abstract Plasmonic nanoparticles (NPs) have been employed as nanocatalysts in a myriad of photochemical reactions with the underlying mechanisms divided into two categories: thermal and nonthermal pathways. Differentiating these two pathways is the key to optimizing plasmon-mediated chemistry; however, the challenge of measuring temperature down to the nanoscale hinders the advancement and causes the ongoing debate in the field. Herein, we report an in situ spectroscopic approach that leverages two Raman thermometries─the background of surface-enhanced Raman spectroscopy (plasmonic thermometry) and molecular vibrational fingerprints (molecular thermometry) are used independently to probe the local temperature of NP/molecule hybrid systems. Using gold NP/4-nitrothiophenol as a prototype system, we demonstrate the agreement between the two thermometries and prove the nonthermal pathways for the dimerization of 4-nitrothiophenol. Since the temperatures of both metal NPs and adsorbed molecules are probed simultaneously, the dual Raman thermometry enables a detailed mechanistic understanding of plasmon-mediated chemistry.

items.title:
Regime of Geometrical
Mismatch in the Phase Separation-Regulated
Endocytosis of Nanoparticles
items.abstract: Abstract The biological responses related to microdomains formed by phase separation in cell membranes bear long-standing controversies, and, in particular, how this lateral heterogeneity impacts the cellular uptake of nanoparticles remains poorly understood. By combining theoretical models, computer simulations, and experimental discussions, we report on an unconventionally constrained regime of nanoparticle endocytosis on the membrane microdomain, emerging within the intermediate scale of the domains. This regime leads to the nonmonotonic dependence of nanoparticle endocytosis on domain size, in stark contrast to its counterparts in the homogeneous membrane and endocytosis without nanoparticles. Theoretical analysis evaluates the regime boundary and reveals that the regime arises from the geometrical mismatch between nanoparticles and microdomains governed by various energetic contributions, which capture and explain some experimental observations. The findings suggest an appealing way and useful guidelines to control cellular uptake and might be of immediate interest to the desired biomedical applications.

items.title:
Ferroelectric
Neuromorphic Devices Enable Nonphotosensitive
Neurons to Achieve Event-Driven Photosensitive Artificial Neural Interfaces
items.abstract: Abstract Neuromorphic devices integrated with biological neurons hold significant potential for rehabilitation and human-machine interfaces, thereby attracting extensive research interest. However, the effort to connect them through light stimulation is still in its very initial stages. Here, ferroelectric neuromorphic devices based on α-In2Se3 and P(VDF-TrFE) are proposed to construct hybrid neural interfaces. In contrast to neuromorphic devices employing other working principles, ferroelectricity plays a crucial role in connecting biological neurons, which enables nonphotosensitive neurons to respond to light stimuli. Various optoelectronic synaptic behaviors have been achieved. Under light pulses, the ferroelectric neuromorphic device induced a significant increase of up to 200% in the calcium ion signal of artificial neural interfaces. Patch-clamp was applied for further verification, revealing the influence of different light wavelengths and pulse frequencies on neuronal excitation signals, which is analogous to the human retina. Simulations demonstrate that the ferroelectric neural interface improves dynamic gesture recognition accuracy from 51% to 99%. Our approach offers a strategy to connect neuromorphic devices with neurons through light, which may offer a platform to investigate the fundamental principles of synaptic plasticity and learning in a hybrid setting for future remote therapy and human–machine interfaces.

items.title:
Interphase-Adaptive
Chloride Solid Electrolyte Enables
High-Performance All-Solid-State Lithium Batteries
items.abstract: Abstract Halide solid electrolytes offer a compelling combination of wide electrochemical stability and high safety for all-solid-state lithium batteries (ASSLBs), yet their practical application is severely hindered by interfacial degradation, mechanical contact loss, and low active-material utilization when paired with Ni-rich layered oxide cathodes. Here we synthesize a monoclinic Li2.4Yb0.4Zr0.6Cl6 (LYZC) with a high ionic conductivity of 2.1 × 10–3 S·cm–1 at 30 °C, and then coat it with an ultrathin amorphous organic interphase (LYZC@CH) through an organic-solvent-assisted low-temperature strategy. The adaptive organic interphase transforms the intrinsically rigid chloride electrolyte into a chemo-mechanically compliant ion conductor that accommodates cathode volume variation while preserving rapid lithium–ion transport. Consequently, the engineered electrolyte stabilizes the cathode/electrolyte interface, suppresses parasitic interfacial reactions and structural degradation, and enables composite cathodes with a high active-material content of 90%. The resulting LiNi0.83Co0.12Mn0.05O2 composite cathode delivers an electrode-level energy density of 402.22 Wh kg–1 and retains nearly 100% of its capacity after 2000 cycles at 5 C in 30 MPa. This work establishes an electrolyte-centered interfacial engineering strategy for practical high-energy all-solid-state lithium batteries.

items.title:
Microalgae-Macrophage
Hybrid Exosome-like Nanovesicles
for Mitophagy Restoration and Wound Regeneration in Aging
items.abstract: Abstract The wound healing capacity in the elderly is significantly impaired, leading to increased susceptibility to inflammation and infection, and potentially contributing to reduced lifespan. In aged wounds, dysfunctional mitophagy in senescent cells (SnCs) results in the persistent release of pro-inflammatory cytokines, fostering a chronic inflammatory microenvironment that further delays tissue repair. To address this challenge, we developed a thermosensitive hydrogel loaded with hybrid exosome-like nanovesicles to enhance wound healing in aging. These hybrid nanovesicles (termed SP-M2-ENs) were generated by extrusion-mediated fusion of spirulina-derived exosome-like nanovesicles (SP-ENs) with M2 macrophage-derived exosome-like nanovesicles (M2-ENs). SP-ENs are rich in phycocyanin and exhibit strong antioxidant activity, whereas M2-ENs carry multiple anti-inflammatory cytokines and growth factors. This synergistic combination endows the hybrid system with enhanced anti-inflammatory and regenerative capabilities. To ensure sustained release and conformability to irregular wound topographies, the hybrid nanovesicles were encapsulated within a thermosensitive hydrogel (PF-127 gel), forming the final therapeutic construct, designated SP-M2-ENs@Gel. Comprehensive in vitro and in vivo studies demonstrated that SP-M2-ENs@Gel effectively scavenges reactive oxygen species (ROS), promotes tissue regeneration, stimulates angiogenesis, modulates macrophage polarization toward a reparative phenotype, and enables prolonged delivery of therapeutic agents. Specifically, SP-M2-ENs@Gel accelerates healing in aged wounds by restoring mitophagy function in senescent cells, thereby alleviating chronic inflammation. Collectively, this platform represents a promising strategy for overcoming senescence-impaired wound repair, highlighting the clinical translatability of engineered exosome-based therapies in regenerative medicine.

items.title:
Retraction of “Bottom-Up
Engineering of Peptide
Cell Translocators Based on Environmentally Modulated Quadrupole Switches”
Issue Editorial Masthead
Issue Publication Information

Electron-Modulated
Pt–Co Dual-Atom Sites with
Hydrogen Spillover for Robust Acidic Hydrogen Evolution
items.abstract: Abstract Pt single-atom catalysts (Pt-SACs) are regarded as one of the most promising electrocatalysts for hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) owing to the maximal atom utilization and distinctive coordination structure. However, their reaction kinetics and stability at large current density are severely limited by the linear scaling relations and metal sites agglomeration. Herein, we present an “electronic anchoring strategy” to construct Pt–Co dual-atom sites (PtCo-DASs) on onion-like carbon nanospheres with carbon vacancies (OLCv) (denoted PtCo-DAS@OLCv) as a structurally integrated electrode for highly efficient and stable HER. Experimental and theoretical calculations demonstrate that Pt atoms achieve electron capture through d–π orbital coupling with Co, C, and O, subsequently guarantee superior structural stability, and establish a localized electric field. The electric field is further amplified by the confinement effect from the high-curvature of nanosized OLCv, which facilitates proton enrichment, lowers the Volmer barrier, and accelerates hydrogen spillover from Pt sites to Co sites, ultimately decoupling hydrogen adsorption and desorption at the atom scale. Consequently, PtCo-DAS@OLCv with an ultralow Pt loading of 6.16 μg cm–2 exhibits a high HER activity with a low overpotential of 14.1 mV at 10 mA cm–2 and high turnover frequency of 83.2 H2 s–1 at 100 mV, which are superior to those of commercial Pt/C and the most reported Pt-based catalysts. Interestingly, a practical proton exchange membrane water electrolyzer (PEMWE) assembled by PtCo-DAS@OLCv achieves a large current density of 1000 mA cm–2 at an ultralow cell voltage of 1.78 V and operates stably for over 2300 h with negligible degradation.

items.title:
Nondestructive Piezoelectric
Nanocomposite Sonodynamic
Toothbrush for Synergistic Dental Disinfection and Whitening
items.abstract: Abstract Over 3.47 billion people worldwide suffer from dental health and aesthetic issues, however, existing commercial toothbrushes lack synergistic antibacterial and whitening functions and fail to prevent biofilm accumulation and progressive staining. Here, we develop novel sonodynamic bifunctional piezoelectric nanocomposites by integrating piezoelectric Au@BTO nanoparticles into a porous elastomer matrix, enabling synergistic disinfection and whitening in a biosafe and efficient manner during daily toothbrushing. These nanocomposites exhibit superior mechanical and piezoelectric stability under continuous ultrasound stimulation for 30,000 s, along with robust andcontrollable generation of reactive oxygen species (ROS) based on a piezocatalytic mechanism. Under physiological conditions, the piezoelectric nanocomposites demonstrate highly efficient and durable antibacterial activity against Gram-positive S. aureus and S. mutans as well as Gram-negative E. coli and P. gingivalis (&gt;99% efficacy), while preserving &gt;95% oral cell viability. When integrated into an innovative Piezo-brush, the system maintains structural integrity for ∼5 months under daily toothbrushing and achieves 96% biofilm reduction and nondestructive whitening (CIELab color difference = 70.3, 0.6% Vickers hardness reduction), significantly outperforming existing functional toothbrushes and commercial products. This work develops a piezoelectric sonodynamic toothbrush for daily dental care, offering avenues for advanced biodevices in cosmetics, wound healing, and medical implants.

items.title:
Covalent Interface-Engineered
Bone-Targeting Piezoelectric
Heterojunction Reprograms Tumor Stress Adaptation and Reverses the
Immunosuppressive Microenvironment
items.abstract: Abstract Breast cancer bone metastasis remains a major therapeutic challenge due to endoplasmic reticulum stress (ERS)-associated stress adaptation and an immunosuppressive tumor immune microenvironment (TIME). Herein, we report a zoledronic acid (ZOL)-loaded bone-targeted covalent piezoelectric heterojunction nanoplatform (Z@BT-P) for sonopiezo-dynamic therapy (SPDT) and immune remodeling. In this platform, barium titanate (BTO) was covalently integrated with a porphyrinic porous coordination network to form a stable BT-P heterointerface, while ZOL enhanced bone-metastatic lesion enrichment. Compared with physically assembled BT@P, Z@BT-P promoted interfacial charge utilization and strengthened ultrasound (US)-triggered piezoelectric catalysis. Under US irradiation, enhanced charge utilization and Piezo1-associated mechanosensitive Ca2+ signaling jointly amplified reactive oxygen species accumulation and Ca2+ dysregulation, causing dual oxidative/Ca2+ stress. This stress cascade promoted ERS associated with glucose-regulated protein 78 and C/EBP homologous protein, leading to apoptosis and immunogenic cell death. Consequent damage-associated molecular patterns release and ZOL-containing treatment enhanced dendritic cell maturation, drove M1-like macrophage remodeling, and activated antitumor immunity. In a 4T1-luc tibial bone metastasis model, Z@BT-P + US achieved 89.4% ± 4.9% tumor growth inhibition, alleviated osteolytic bone destruction, suppressed distant metastasis, and promoted immune memory. This study establishes a covalent interface-engineered piezoelectric nanoplatform for bone metastasis therapy.

items.title:
Sulfur Doping-Induced
Surface Reconstruction of High-Entropy
Composites Boosts Bifunctional Oxygen Electrocatalysis for Zinc-Air
Batteries
items.abstract: Abstract The development of high-efficiency and durable bifunctional electrocatalysts for both the oxygen evolution reaction (OER) and oxygen reduction reaction (ORR) is essential for the widespread application of rechargeable zinc-air batteries (RZABs). Rational screening of ORR/OER components and precise regulation of their electronic structures to achieve synergistic effects currently stand as an effective solution. Here, we report a composite catalyst prepared through the high-temperature decomposition of molybdenum disulfide (MoS2), synthesizing sulfur (S)-doped high-entropy alloy (HEA) nanoparticles on carbon nanotube (S-FeCoNiMnMo@CNT) with metallic single atoms. High-valent Mo can precisely modulate the local electronic domains of HEAs. S doping not only triggers surface reconstruction of HEAs during the OER to deliver outstanding OER catalytic activity but also immobilizes metal single atoms to boost ORR: an overpotential as low as 247 mV at 10 mA cm–2 and an ORR half-wave potential of 0.746 V are achieved. Density functional theory calculations reveal that the S-doping-induced surface reconstruction promotes the adsorption of *OOH intermediates and reduces the Gibbs free energy barrier during the OER process. RZAB based on S-FeCoNiMnMo@CNT exhibits a peak power density of 229.8 mW cm–2, along with a low voltage gap of 0.716 V at 10 mA cm–2 and a cycle life exceeding 800 h. Furthermore, this work extends its applications to flexible ZABs.

items.title:
Quantifying Viscoelastic
Alterations in Virus-Infected
Cells by Optical Tweezers
items.abstract: Abstract The viscoelasticity of cells is closely related to their physiological functions, influencing processes such as differentiation, proliferation, and migration. Viruses replicate by infecting host cells and can affect the cells’ viscoelastic properties. However, current research mainly focuses on changes in the overall cellular viscoelasticity, while intracellular viscoelastic properties remain difficult to measure. Optical tweezers, due to their noncontact nature, offer a promising tool for measuring intracellular viscoelasticity. In this study, the viscoelastic moduli of host cells infected with three different viruses (H9N2, PRV, and HSV) were measured using the active-passive calibration method and microrheological techniques. The changes in viscoelastic moduli across different frequency ranges were systematically analyzed. The results showed that viral infection altered the viscoelastic properties of cells, with the extent of changes varying by virus type. We conclude that viral infection leads to an increase in viscous modulus and a decrease in elastic modulus of the host cell, and this is attributed to virus-induced depolymerization of the cytoskeleton, which reduces cellular elasticity and increases viscosity. These findings provide insights into the mechanisms of virus-induced alterations in cellular viscoelasticity and offer a theoretical foundation for further studies on the cellular mechanisms of viral infections.

items.title:
Voltage-Gated
Ionic Conductivity in Ultranarrow Confinement
items.abstract: Abstract Voltage-controlled ion transport in subnanometer pores underpins the operation of emerging filtration, energy-storage, and iontronic technologies, yet its microscopic mechanisms remain poorly understood. Using classical molecular dynamics simulations, we investigate ionic transport in ultranarrow (≤1 nm) quasi-two-dimensional nanopores in MXene electrodes filled with an ionic liquid. We reveal a nonmonotonic dependence of linear-response conductivity on electrode potential, with a pronounced asymmetry between positive and negative electrode polarizations. These behaviors originate from a competition between confinement-induced ionic ordering and charging-induced ion crowding within the pore. The resulting transition from a structure-limited to an ion-crowding-limited transport regime provides a general framework for understanding voltage-gated ionic conduction under extreme confinement, which facilitates the formulation of design principles for MXene-based nanofluidic, electrochemical, and iontronic devices.

items.title:
Competing
Surface Dynamics of Copper Catalyst Particles
during Electrochemical Carbon Dioxide Reduction
items.abstract: Abstract Copper is a powerful catalyst for the electrochemical carbon dioxide reduction reaction (CO2RR), but it faces challenges with selectivity and stability dependent on its structural characteristics. We developed a platform that combines graphitized carbon nanofibers with identical-location transmission electron microscopy (IL-TEM) to study individual copper nanoparticles at the atomic scale under various reaction conditions. Notably, we observed that competing phenomena such as Ostwald ripening, coalescence, selective etching, and Coulomb-explosion-like fragmentation coexist in the same reaction area, with the latter being qualitatively consistent with a charge-driven fission pathway in larger nanoparticles (&gt;10 nm). By tracking uniquely identifiable nanoparticles both individually and in groups, our findings focus on the range of surface-confined restructuring pathways during CO2RR. This contrasts with solution-mediated phenomena, such as dissolution–precipitation, which dominate under open-circuit potential (OCP) and significantly destabilize the catalyst prior to the reaction, highlighting the importance of eliminating this effect.
