Under CO2RR conditions, Cu nanoparticles are highly sensitive to subtle variations in the support’s nanotexture, defects, and electronic structure, leading to the coexistence of counteracting mechanisms we observed. These observations provide a structural framework for understanding the dynamic behavior of copper-on-carbon catalysts under CO2RR conditions, guiding the development of strategies to improve catalyst stability and performance.

items.title:
Accelerating the
Discovery of Synthesizable 2D Hybrid
Double Perovskites through Human–LLM Collaborative Descriptor
Engineering
items.abstract: Abstract Two-dimensional hybrid perovskites offer exceptional structural diversity and multifunctional properties, yet their synthesis remains a major bottleneck due to low hit rates and strong reliance on empirical intuition. Here we introduce AL-SynAgent, a human-in-the-loop, ML-guided screening workflow that integrates literature-derived synthetic priors, expert-refined chemical descriptors, and active learning to assess the synthesis feasibility of two dimensional (2D) hybrid organic–inorganic rare-earth double perovskites (HORDPs). By converting LLM-assisted literature knowledge and expert chemical reasoning into system-specific computable descriptors, AL-SynAgent reduces dependence on large experimental data sets while retaining chemically interpretable decision rules. With experimental feedback from only 4.8% of candidate space, the model converged and achieved successful target-phase formation for 11 of the 14 candidates in the prospectively selected experimental set, corresponding to a hit rate of 78.6%. Screening of an enumerated virtual library of 280,000 candidates further prioritized 64,482 compositions with high predicted synthesis feasibility. Notably, three newly obtained compounds also exhibit both excellent ferroelectricity and photoluminescence, including (4-F-321)4RbEu(NO3)8, which displays an exceptionally high Curie temperature of 388 K and strong emission at 592 nm. This work establishes a practical, human-in-the-loop strategy for data-efficient prioritization of candidate compositions within chemically constrained 2D HORDP space under a standardized laboratory synthesis protocol.

items.title:
Engineered
Living Materials: A Therapeutic Paradigm
beyond Conventional Biomaterials
items.abstract: Abstract Development of biomaterials in the past two decades has profoundly advanced modern medicine. However, the relatively simple and insufficiently biological functions and lack of self-renewal capability limit their ability to dynamically adapt to complex physiological environments. Engineered living materials (eLMs) use living organisms as core functional units and provide a therapeutic approach for addressing these limitations. Thus, this review systematically summarizes the recent advancements in eLMs, beginning with an overview of the primary biological chassis, including bacteria, microalgae, fungi, and mammalian cells. eLMs hold the valuable capabilities of long-term self-sustainment and self-proliferation within complex biological environments, which are endowed with intelligent regulation. For instance, they can sense environmental signals and execute programmed functional outputs, including therapeutic protein secretion or targeted migration. Moreover, they achieve precise control over therapeutic actions, encompassing spatial localization at the disease site, temporal dynamics of the intervention, and quantitative regulation of outputs. Furthermore, we highlight the broad therapeutic applications of these dynamic systems in addressing complex diseases. Finally, we discuss the current translational challenges and future directions of the field, emphasizing the potential of integrating artificial intelligence with synthetic biology and nanomaterial engineering to develop next-generation programmable eLMs and expand their utility across diverse sectors.

items.title:
Micro-LED-Activated
Formaldehyde Sensing via Au Loading-Regulated
Interfacial Engineering in Anatase TiO2 Nanofibers
items.abstract: Abstract Photoactivated metal-oxide gas sensors reduce the energy demand associated with continuous heating, yet selective detection of volatile organic compounds remains constrained by weak electrical transduction and complex surface oxidation pathways. Here, Au-functionalized anatase TiO2 nanofibers (Au/aTiO2 NFs) were integrated with a 395 nm microlight-emitting diode (LED) for low-power formaldehyde (HCHO) sensing. One-pot electrospinning followed by calcination enabled systematic control of Au loading while preserving the anatase nanofiber architecture. Au loading regulated TiO2 crystallite growth, defect states, dispersion, interfacial Au chemical states, and photoexcited carrier relaxation. At 0.15 wt % Au, finely dispersed Au nanoparticles produced a distinct Au/TiO2 interfacial environment and carrier-relaxation behavior, whereas higher loadings induced nanoparticle aggregation and additional nonradiative energy-loss pathways. Under UV micro-LED illumination at 2.63 mW, the optimized sensor exhibited a response of 1093 toward 1 ppm of HCHO, an estimated detection limit of 4.9 ppb, and stable operation over 40 consecutive cycles. Density functional theory calculations further supported the loading-dependent selectivity, showing that changes in the local Au environment selectively modify HCHO adsorption and bond reconstruction. These results identify local Au-site density as a key design parameter governing interfacial reactivity and molecular selectivity in low-power photoactivated gas sensing.

items.title:
Electrically Reconfigurable
Silicon Carbide Nanophotonic
Cavities on Thin-Film Lithium Niobate
items.abstract: Abstract Interfacing integrated photonics with solid-state spin defects holds great promise for future quantum networks, but the scaling of spin-photon architectures is hindered by frequency mismatches arising from fabrication-induced variations in photonic cavity resonances and inhomogeneous optical transition frequencies of individual spins. These challenges call for a photonic platform with deterministic and wide-range tunability. Here, we demonstrate a hybrid nanophotonic platform based on direct bonding of silicon carbide photonic crystal nanocavity arrays onto a thin-film lithium niobate-on-insulator, enabling deterministic electrical tuning of multiple SiC nanocavities into mutual spectral resonance. By exploiting the strong electro-optic response of lithium niobate, we achieve continuous and wide-range cavity tuning of 380 GHz (∼1.1 nm), sufficient to compensate both cavity disorder and spin spectral inhomogeneity. The nanocavities balance strong optical confinement with electrical tunability, exhibiting a theoretical Purcell factor of approximately 400. This hybrid platform enables electrically reconfigurable spin-photon interfaces for large-scale integrated quantum photonics.

items.title:
Fluorinated Copper(I) Iodine Cluster Scintillators
Enable High-Temperature X-ray Imaging
items.abstract: Abstract The development of scintillators that maintain excellent performance under high temperatures is a critical challenge. Here, by simply replacing the triphenylphosphine ligand with its fluorinated analogue, we successfully switched the emission pathway of Cu2I2 clusters from pure phosphorescence to a hybrid phosphorescence/thermally activated delayed fluorescence (TADF) mechanism, enabling adaptive high-temperature X-ray imaging. Combined experimental and theoretical investigations reveal that the fluorination strategy reduces the singlet–triplet energy gap to an exceptionally small value of 35 meV, thereby promoting efficient reverse intersystem crossing. The TADF contribution reaches 95.7% at room temperature. This temperature-responsive characteristic endows the fluorinated cluster with adaptive X-ray imaging capability across a broad temperature window from 293 to 413 K, overcoming the thermal quenching phenomenon in traditional phosphorescence-only scintillators. This work establishes a molecular design approach for smart scintillators capable of reliable operation in demanding thermal environments.

items.title:
Frozen
2D Adatom Gas at the Surface of Gold–Copper
Alloys
items.abstract: Abstract Isolated, undercoordinated metal atoms exhibit enhanced reactivity central to catalysis, yet their stabilization on surfaces remains challenging. In heterogeneous single-atom catalysis, activity derives from interactions between individual atoms and a host matrix, but the absence of stabilizing ligands often leads to diffusion, aggregation, and sintering, obscuring structure–activity relationships. On metal surfaces, reactivity is typically limited to sparse, dynamic, undercoordinated sites lining step edges or lattice defects. Here we report a defect-engineering strategy to stabilize isolated adatoms on dilute metal alloy substrates. Scanning tunneling microscopy reveals a high density of uniformly distributed adatoms on Au–Cu(111) terraces that persist under thermal cycling. Combined experiments and modeling attribute this stability to alloy-induced subsurface dislocation networks that trap adatoms and suppress diffusion, forming a two-dimensional frozen gas. These adatoms act as a reactive reservoir, enabling on-surface coordination chemistry inaccessible on pure metals, and providing insights into atomic-scale processes on the surfaces of defect-engineered alloys with implications for heterogeneous catalysis.

items.title:
Hybridization State
Engineering of Coal Pitch-Based
Carbon Materials Enabling Ultrastable Aqueous Zinc–Iodine Batteries
with 150,000 Cycles
items.abstract: Abstract Carbon materials with superior porosity and conductivity are widely adopted in aqueous zinc–iodine batteries to host iodine, but suffer from the polyiodide shuttle and cycling stability challenges. Traditional strategies mainly focus on pore structure engineering or heteroatom doping of carbon hosts to confine iodine, but fail to address the sluggish iodine conversion kinetics. Herein, we initially reveal the significant yet overlooked role of hybridization state in reforming the carbon intrinsic activity toward high-efficiency iodine conversion chemistry. With pitch-derived porous carbon as an example, we controllably regulate the C(sp2)/C(sp3) ratio (from 1.23 to 2.21) while maintaining high surface area. These properties lower the activation energy of iodine conversion and effectively suppress the polyiodide shuttle. The zinc–iodine battery exhibits ultrahigh cycling stability after 150,000 cycles and a low self-discharging rate with only 12.5% capacity loss after 20 days. Ah-level pouch cell with 66.6 mgiodine cm–2 achieves a cumulative discharging capacity of 103.51 Ah. The hybridization engineering was successfully extended to commercial porous carbon (YP-50F), prolonging the lifespan from 7425 to 27,000 cycles. This work presents a hybridization state engineering strategy to reform the intrinsic activity of the carbon host to favor the iodine conversion chemistry and beyond.

items.title:
5DSTEM of Liquid-Phase
Nanocrystal Growth Bridges
Ensemble Kinetics and Nanoscale Dynamics
items.abstract: Abstract Resolving how ensemble growth kinetics emerge from particle- and grain-level dynamics is essential for predictive control of nanocrystal synthesis. Here, time-resolved four-dimensional scanning transmission electron microscopy (4DSTEM), extended into five dimensions (5DSTEM) through continuous acquisition, is used to simultaneously resolve morphology, crystallographic orientation, and lattice strain during Au nanocrystal growth in aqueous HAuCl4. Although ensemble growth follows surface-reaction-limited kinetics, individual nanoparticles exhibit distinct pathways, including continuous growth and discrete coalescence through oriented attachment. These pathways display characteristic orientation dynamics, with stable or gradually selected orientations during continuous growth and abrupt reconfiguration followed by alignment during coalescence. At the ensemble level, the out-of-plane orientation distribution is established early and remains stable, whereas in-plane orientations remain broadly distributed without global alignment. Tensile strain develops progressively from particle surfaces and interfaces, directly linking lattice distortion with evolving morphology and crystallographic structure. By connecting ensemble kinetics with particle- and grain-resolved structural evolution, 5DSTEM provides a general framework for uncovering heterogeneous growth mechanisms and for relating synthesis pathways to structure-dependent properties in functional nanomaterials.

items.title:
Nano-Optical Switching
of Photochromic Material through
Ultraviolet and Visible Plasmon Nanofocusing
items.abstract: Abstract Optical control of photochromic properties is essential for optoelectronic devices. The manipulation of such properties has been limited to the microscale because of the wave nature of light; however, scaling down the volume is highly demanded for the future nanosized devices. Herein, we demonstrate optical switching at the nanoscale in an organic photochromic material. Photochromic materials such as diarylethene derivatives exhibit two different states with distinct optical and electronic properties under ultraviolet (UV) and visible light irradiation. We employed plasmon nanofocusing for optical switching of photochromic materials, which allowed the creation of a nanolight source at the apex of a tapered aluminum structure over a broad frequency range. We achieved in situ wavelength control between visible and UV light at the nanoscale for photochromic reactions. Using this technique, we demonstrated nanoscale optical switching between the two states of diarylethene. The switching performance was confirmed for at least nine cycles without degradation. This demonstration would constitute a significant step toward next-generation optoelectronic devices and benefit diverse scientific fields owing to the broad wavelength tunability of plasmon nanofocusing.

items.title:
Silencing
MSR1 in Macrophages Attenuates the Cochlear
Foreign Body Response and Preserves Electrode–Neural Interface
items.abstract: Abstract Cochlear implantation (CI) provides effective auditory rehabilitation for patients with severe-to-profound sensorineural hearing loss. Implantation can nevertheless induce local foreign body response (FBR) and cochlear fibrosis, motivating strategies to reduce tissue reactions and preserve cochlear integrity. Macrophages play a key role in FBR, but their functions are multiple and stage-dependent, and indiscriminate intervention may aggravate cochlear injury. Therefore, more precise strategies are needed to modulate macrophage-mediated FBR after CI. Here, through transcriptomic profiling of cochlear tissues from rats 30 days after cochlear implantation, we identified macrophage scavenger receptor 1 (MSR1) as a prominent signature after CI. In vitro assays further verified the role of MSR1 in reshaping macrophage phenotype and inflammatory activation. To achieve targeted MSR1 regulation in the cochlea, we engineered iRGD-modified extracellular vesicles to deliver siMSR1 (iRGD-EV/siMSR1). iRGD modification enhanced macrophage uptake of EV and enabled efficient siRNA delivery. In a rat CI model, local administration of iRGD-EV/siMSR1 reduced cochlear fibrotic tissue formation and decreased fibrosis-related protein expression. Moreover, iRGD-EV/siMSR1 preserved spiral ganglion neurons and myelin structures, contributing to residual hearing protection after implantation. Early stage analysis at 7 days after implantation showed that iRGD-EV/siMSR1 suppressed macrophage inflammatory activation, reduced TGF-β1-related profibrotic signaling, regulated matrix remodeling, and limited early apoptosis. These findings identify MSR1 as a promising molecular target for cochlear implant-induced FBR and support iRGD-EV/siMSR1 as a potentially translatable strategy for attenuating cochlear fibrosis and preserving the cochlear neural interface, also highlighting the importance of considering neural health when modulating macrophage-mediated responses to cochlear implants.

items.title:
Chronic Stress-Triggerable
Nanoprodrugs Ameliorate
Metabolic Abnormalities Driven by Hypothalamic-Pituitary-Adrenal Axis
Dysregulation in Early Alzheimer’s Disease
items.abstract: Abstract Chronic stress-induced dysregulation of the hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal (HPA) axis is a crucial early risk factor that triggers brain energy metabolism disorders to accelerate the onset and progression of Alzheimer’s disease (AD). Herein, an amphiphilic precursor conjugate of ginsenoside Rc (Rc) covalently linked with a reactive oxygen species-sensitive thioketo bond is constructed to form stimuli-responsive prodrug assemblies, which are further modified with the TGN-Tet1 dual-ligand fusion peptide TPL to obtain a chronic stress-triggerable programmed nanoprodrug (TLRN). Following TPL-mediated blood-brain barrier penetration and neuronal preferential targeting, nanoprodrugs specifically disintegrate to selectively release active Rc in the chronic stress-induced excessive reactive oxygen species (ROS) microenvironment. Benefiting from the restoration of HPA axis homeostasis by normalizing glucocorticoid receptor nuclear translocation, TLRN treatment exhibits multifaceted rectification of cerebral metabolic abnormalities, including enhancing glucose uptake, promoting oxidative phosphorylation, and mitigating mitochondrial dysfunction. In young amyloid precursor protein/presenilin 1 (APP/PS1) transgenic mouse models exposed to chronic stress, this intervention can alleviate brain energy deprivation and amyloid-β (Aβ) accumulation, ultimately rescuing depressive-like behaviors and cognitive deficits, offering a promising approach for early prevention and flexible management of AD at high risk of chronic stress.

items.title:
Ultrasound-Responsive
Electroactive Polyetheretherketone
Scaffold Promotes Bioenergetic Bone Regeneration by Regulating Mitochondrial
Permeability Transition Pores
items.abstract: Abstract Mitochondrial dysfunction and energy metabolic imbalance in senescent bone marrow mesenchymal stem cells (BMSCs) are critical pathological foundations for senile bone regeneration. Existing therapeutic strategies suffer from a lack of active mitochondrial bioenergetic driving forces, failing to effectively reverse energy metabolic suppression of senescent BMSCs. Here, an ultrasound-activated electroactive scaffold was constructed by anchoring barium titanate-transition metal carbide (MXene@BaTiO3) heterojunctions on the surface of polyetheretherketone (PEEK) to reactivate mitochondrial energy metabolism and promote bone regeneration under senescence-associated bone loss conditions. These heterojunctions adhere to BMSC membranes and generate electrical stimulation upon ultrasound stimulation, which significantly inhibits abnormal opening of mitochondrial permeability transition pores (mPTP), reduces leakage of mtDNA and Cyt c, and maintains membrane potential stability. Mechanistic investigations reveal that electrical stimulation activates the PI3K/Akt/MDM2 signaling axis to promote the degradation of accumulated p53, which relieves the competitive binding of p53 to TRAP1, thereby restoring TRAP1-CypD-mediated mPTP gating and mitochondrial homeostasis. Consequently, this ultrasound-activated electroactive scaffold drives mitochondrial energy metabolism and osteogenic differentiation of senescence-like BMSCs in vitro, which is further confirmed in a rat model. These results demonstrate the potential of this electroactive scaffold as a regulator of mitochondrial energy metabolism for senescence-associated bone regeneration.

items.title:
Switching of Exciton-Polaritons
in Covalent Organic
Framework-Based Optical Resonators through Interaction with the Molecular
Environment
items.abstract: Abstract We report a demonstration of a covalent organic framework (COF) integrated into an optical cavity for the realization of exciton–polaritons and their reversible switching through changes in the surrounding molecular environment. Films of COF nanoplates were integrated into Fabry–Pérot resonators engineered to achieve spectral matching between cavity modes and COF excitonic transitions, yielding strong light–matter coupling with a Rabi splitting above 300 meV. The cavity architecture preserves accessibility of the porous framework, enabling interaction with guest molecules. The potential of this interplay is shown by exposing the resonators to water vapor, which induces both a redshift and a pronounced reduction of the COF optical absorption. The observed hypochromic effect drives a reversible shift from strong to weak coupling, effectively switching exciton–polaritons on and off, as guest molecules are desorbed from or adsorbed in the reticular material host. The process is reversible upon desorption, with preservation of structural and optical integrity. These results establish COFs as a versatile platform for chemically tunable polaritonic systems, opening avenues for responsive photonic devices, sensing, and control of light–matter interactions in nanostructured materials.

items.title:
Shield-and-Amplify
Nanoparticle Vaccines Retune Immunodominance
for Broad Protection against SARS-CoV-2
items.abstract: Abstract Antigenic variation severely constrains the durability and breadth of vaccine-induced protection against rapidly evolving viruses. Although conserved epitopes can support cross-variant immunity, antibody responses to viral glycoproteins are often biased toward exposed, mutable immunodominant epitopes, leaving conserved protective sites subdominant. We previously identified a cryptic, conserved class 5 epitope (the 6D6/7D6 epitope) on the SARS-CoV-2 receptor-binding domain (RBD) capable of eliciting broad cross-neutralization. Here, we present a modular “shield-and-amplify” nanoparticle vaccination strategy to redirect immunodominance toward this subdominant epitope. We engineered site-specific N-linked glycans─alongside the native N343 glycan to mask variable immunodominant regions while preserving accessibility to the class 5 epitope. The resulting glycan-masked RBD antigen (RGM) was displayed on p239 nanoparticles via nanobody-mediated assembly, yielding multivalent RGM@p239 immunogens. Antigenic profiling revealed that glycan shielding preserved recognition by 6D6 and 7D6 antibodies while reducing binding of representative class 1–4 antibodies by at least 80%. In immunized animals, RGM@p239 enriched 7D6-competitive serum antibodies blocking approximately 70–80% of serum binding to RGM and broadened cross-variant neutralization against 8 representative variant strains, including detectable activity against Omicron lineages. Furthermore, RGM@p239 reduced disease severity after Omicron EG.1 challenge in a hamster model. These results support a model in which glycan shielding and nanoparticle multivalency act as complementary immune-focusing modules: shielding attenuates competing responses, while multivalency amplifies responses to conserved subdominant epitopes. This study establishes a nanovaccine design strategy to address antigenic variation by focusing immunity on conserved viral vulnerabilities.

items.title:
Polarization-Controlled
Dual-Mode Switching in van
der Waals α-In2Se3 Memristors for
Multitime-Scale Reservoir Computing
items.abstract: Abstract Electrochemical-metallization (ECM) memristors can implement both nonvolatile memory switching and volatile threshold switching, making them attractive for neuromorphic and reservoir computing; however, the stochastic formation of metallic filaments causes variability in the threshold voltage and switching instability. Here, we report a van der Waals α-In2Se3-based ferroelectric-semiconductor ECM (FeS-ECM) memristor in which a bidirectionally polarized α-In2Se3 layer is inserted between the inert electrode and the switching layer. The out-of-plane ferroelectric polarization, programmed through a decoupled in-plane poling terminal, deterministically selects within the low-compliance operating regime between nonvolatile bipolar memory switching and volatile unipolar threshold switching within a single device, with a coefficient of variation in the set voltage of 4.7% and stable operation over more than 9000 cycles. Exploiting these two modes, a single α-In2Se3 platform exhibits both the volatile reservoir dynamics and the nonvolatile conductance modulation required for the readout weights of a physical reservoir-computing system, in which the pulse width electrically programs multiple relaxation time constants. This pulse-width multitime scale reconfigurability enables efficient temporal information processing, demonstrated through MNIST classification and chaotic time-series prediction.

items.title:
Direct Observation
of Chirality-Dependent Berry Curvature
Dipole via Cross-Axial Nonlinear Hall Effect in Trigonal Te
items.abstract: Abstract Quantum geometric quantities, such as Berry curvature (BC) and quantum metric, are known to govern the physical and topological properties of materials, making access to these quantities critically important for the comprehensive understanding of the materials. Chiral crystals offer a natural platform in which structural handedness can control quantum geometry and nonlinear transport, but direct experimental access to the quantum geometric quantities has remained elusive. Here, we show that trigonal tellurium (Te) hosts an enantiomer-dependent Berry curvature dipole (BCD) that can be accessed through the measurement of the cross-axial nonlinear Hall effect (NHE), unlike in previously studied in-plane configurations, where the BCD contribution vanishes. Angle-resolved measurements on left- and right-handed Te devices reveal a second-order transverse response whose sign reverses with crystal chirality. The extracted cross-axial nonlinear susceptibility, χyxz, exceeds the in-plane susceptibility, χxxx, by more than two-fold, indicating a strong BCD-driven contribution. First-principles calculations attribute this behavior to a topologically nontrivial hedgehog-like BC texture near the H points and predict a BCD that reverses sign between opposite enantiomers, consistent with experiment. These results establish cross-axial nonlinear Hall transport as a symmetry-selective probe of chirality-controlled quantum geometry in tellurium and related chiral materials.

items.title:
Janus Biofuel Cells
for Electrosynergistic Enhancement
of Microenvironment-Adaptive Cascade Catalysis in Infected Diabetic
Wound Healing
items.abstract: Abstract The treatment of infectious diabetic wound is greatly hampered by hyperglycemia, inflammation, and microcirculatory dysfunction. Bioelectric stimulation and nanozyme catalysis provide a potential strategy for chronic wound repair but suffer from limitations including external electric power, low activity, and competitive multienzyme reactions. Given this, we developed microenvironment-responsive Janus GOx-Au@PCH–Pt nanoparticles (NPs) as biofuel cells, integrating cascade enzymatic catalysis and self-powered electrical stimulation. The biofuel cell features hydroxylated polyaniline (PCH) NPs as conductive bridges, Pt nanoclusters as the cathode, and glucose oxidase (GOx)-grafted Au (GOx-Au) as the anode. Under infection (acidic pH), conductive PCH shuttles electrons to generate microcurrent that accelerates enzyme catalysis on both the Au anode (GOx) and Pt cathode (peroxidase, POD). The enhanced GOx-POD cascade strengthens ·OH generation, and the self-powered electric field enhances ·OH diffusion across phospholipid bilayers, achieving significant bacterial killing and biofilm dispersion. During tissue repair, neutral/alkaline conditions switch Pt nanozyme from POD to catalase (CAT) and transform PCH into a benzoquinone structure as the electron acceptor. Reversed electron flow boosts the GOx-CAT cascade catalysis on the electrodes, accelerating glucose consumption, suppressing advanced glycation end product formation, and alleviating oxidative stress, while electrical stimulation reduces hypoxia-inducible factor-1α expressions. This synergistic effect promotes collagen deposition and orderly arrangement and normalizes microenvironment with oxygen-generating, hypoglycemic, anti-inflammatory, and macrophage phenotype-shifted features, thereby accelerating wound healing. This designed nanoscale biofuel cells realize adaptive microcurrent modulation and spatiotemporal cascade catalysis, offering a minimally invasive paradigm for infected diabetic wound therapy.

items.title:
Nontrivial Edge
Superconductivity in Dirac Superconductor
PdTe2
items.abstract: Abstract Superconducting topological materials with coexisted superconductivities and topological boundary states are promising platforms for realizing intrinsic topological superconductivity. In this work, the superconducting type-II Dirac semimetal PdTe2 is shown to exhibit clear periodic critical current oscillations in perpendicular magnetic fields due to the fluxoid quantization, indicating the existence of edge superconductivity in PdTe2. Furthermore, a comparative study of the different superconducting properties of the bulk and edge of PdTe2 provides direct evidence for this edge superconductivity. More importantly, by a careful analysis of the flux penetration area, the nontrivial character of the edge superconductivity is revealed, i.e., the edge superconductivity appears not only at the physical boundary of the flake, but also at the interior interface between superconducting and normal regions of PdTe2. The emergence of nontrivial edge superconductivity, indicative of the putative bulk topological superconductivity, not only reveals the great potential of PdTe2 but also provides an experimental avenue for exploring intrinsic topological superconductivity by leveraging bulk-boundary correspondence.

items.title:
Receptor-Modular
Nanocaptors for Programmable Cytokine
Sequestration
items.abstract: Abstract Pathological cytokine networks underlie inflammatory injury and tumor-associated immunosuppression, yet most cytokine-targeted therapies rely on molecularly fixed, pathway-specific antagonists. We present a receptor-modular nanomaterial strategy for constructing modular cytokine nanocaptors (MCNs) whose sequestration profiles can be reconfigured by exchanging receptor modules. Cytokine receptor ectodomains are engineered as independently producible serum albumin fusion proteins and coassembled with poly(L-lactic acid) (PLLA) into compositionally defined nanoparticles. This architecture decouples cytokine-binding specificity from nanoparticle structure, enabling high-density codisplay of multiple receptor modules on single particles. Representative MCNs simultaneously sequester IL-6, TNF-α, and IFN-γ and suppress cytokine-driven inflammatory signaling more effectively than matched soluble receptor mixtures. By altering module composition while preserving the same assembly framework, MCNs can be redirected from sequestering pro-inflammatory cytokines in sepsis, acute lung injury, and fulminant hepatitis to depleting immunosuppressive mediators in tumors. These results establish receptor-modular nanocaptors as programmable materials for disease-tailored cytokine sequestration and immune-microenvironment reconfiguration.

items.title: Cucurbit[ n ]uril-Programmed Chlorogenic Acid Release for Collagen Mineralization and Pulp–Dentin Repair in Near-Pulp Bonding
items.abstract: Abstract Long-term failure of resin–dentin bonding arises from persistent hydration and enzymatic degradation of exposed collagen in the deep hybrid layer, whereas diffusion of bioactive components through dentinal tubules toward the pulp may cause pulpal irritation. An ideal pretreatment should therefore promote collagen remineralization and interfacial stabilization while reducing pulp-adjacent cellular irritation and supporting pulp–dentin repair. Herein, supramolecular complexes of chlorogenic acid (CGA) and cucurbit[n]uril (Q[n], n = 6, 7, and 8), denoted CGA@Q[n], were constructed to regulate CGA loading, release, and interfacial exposure. CGA@Q[6] showed limited loading, release, and mineralization capacity. CGA@Q[7] exhibited faster early release and achieved complete collagen mineralization within 24 h, whereas CGA@Q[8] showed the highest encapsulation efficiency, sustained CGA supply, complete mineralization at 36 h, and a continuous, dense, integrated intrafibrillar mineral phase. Molecular dynamics simulations indicated that CGA released from Q[8] reanchored to collagen and recruited Ca2+, promoting mineral formation within confined intrafibrillar spaces. These advantages extended to three-dimensional collagen networks and demineralized dentin, yielding higher HAp content, enhanced mineral–collagen integration, tubule occlusion, mechanical recovery, and MMP-9 inhibition. As a bonding pretreatment, CGA@Q[8] reduced nanoleakage, endogenous gelatinolytic activity, and aging-induced bond-strength loss. It also improved cytocompatibility relative to free CGA and promoted mineralization and odontogenic differentiation of human dental pulp stem cells (hDPSCs). In vivo, CGA@Q[8] promoted dentin remineralization, maintained near-pulp interfacial stability, alleviated pulpal irritation, and enhanced odontogenic repair. Together, these findings identify CGA@Q[8] as the most effective formulation and show that homologue selection can tune CGA exposure kinetics for coordinated dentin interface repair.

items.title:
Ferroelectric-Empowered
van der Waals Spectrometer
with Record-High Sensitivity and Ultralow Noise
items.abstract: Abstract Miniaturized spectrometers are essential for portable and consumer-oriented applications, yet their reduced physical footprint inherently limits the detector’s active area, leading to compromised sensitivity. Conventional strategies to enhance sensitivity, such as cryogenic cooling or photomultiplier tubes, are incompatible with miniaturization due to their bulk, cost, and power demands. Here, we present a miniaturized spectrometer based on a van der Waals heterojunction integrated on a ferroelectric thin film. Spectral discrimination is enabled by engineering both interlayer and intralayer photoresponses within the heterojunction, which can be dynamically tuned solely via the source-drain bias, eliminating the need for a gate electrode and enabling a two-terminal architecture. This design is inherently compatible with simple two-pad readout integrated circuits, facilitating scalable array integration for compact spectroscopic systems. Critically, the built-in electric field generated by the ferroelectric polarization promotes efficient dissociation of interlayer excitons, yielding an ultralow noise floor of below 5 × 10–16 A Hz–1/2, more than 2 orders of magnitude lower than existing miniaturized spectrometers and surpassing the performance of most benchtop instruments. This work in sensitivity without sacrificing size or complexity present a strategy for deploying high-performance spectroscopy in real-world applications.

items.title:
MXene-PS-Based Soft
Actuator with Deformation Reversal
Capability through Time-Sequence Difference of Asymmetric Water Absorption
Kinetics
items.abstract: Abstract Many soft actuators have been developed to achieve bending deformation under external stimuli through asymmetric structures or nonuniform material distributions. However, most existing actuators can only produce bending in a single direction, and developing soft actuators with deformation reversal capability remains a challenge. To address this issue, this study proposes an MXene-PS/MXene bilayer soft actuator, which is fabricated by sequential vacuum-assisted filtration, resulting in a loose MXene-PS top layer and a dense MXene bottom layer. The MXene-PS layer features a high water absorption/desorption rate but low capacity, while the MXene layer exhibits a low rate but high capacity. This complementary kinetic-capacity coupling mechanism, termed the time-sequence difference of asymmetric water absorption kinetics, enables the actuator to achieve reversible deformation reversal under NIR light and humidity stimuli. Furthermore, simply by changing the placement orientation of the actuator, two distinct self-sustained oscillation behaviors can be obtained in a humidity gradient environment, namely, periodic motion toward or away from the water surface. Leveraging this deformation reversal capability, we demonstrate two proof-of-concept applications: a biomimetic flower and a self-sustained motion sailboat. This work introduces a deformation mode and actuation principle for MXene-based soft actuators and further broadens their application prospects in biomimetic devices and soft robotics.

items.title:
Decoupling
Conductivity and Interfacial State in Pristine-Like
Carbon Nanotube Coatings Reveals Their Distinct Contributions to Neuronal
Function
items.abstract: Abstract Carbon nanotubes (CNTs) combine high electrical conductivity, mechanical robustness, and nanoscale architecture, making them promising materials for neural interfaces. However, the strong coupling between CNT morphology, electrical transport, and surface chemistry has limited identification of the material properties that directly regulate neuronal function. Here, we establish an experimental strategy to disentangle morphology-dependent network transport from interfacial wettability using pristine-like CNT coatings. Multiwalled CNTs with comparable diameters but distinct lengths were reversibly functionalized, spray-coated, and thermally defunctionalized to produce homogeneous conductive networks while recovering pristine-like electrical transport and surface chemistry. Subsequent conditioning in phosphate-buffered saline substantially reduced surface hydrophobicity without detectable alteration of the graphitic CNT framework, generating coatings with comparable interfacial wettability but distinct network morphologies. Primary spinal cord neuron-glia cultures grown on these substrates were characterized by immunocytochemistry, electrophysiology, and calcium imaging. All CNT coatings supported comparable neuroglial density and network formation, whereas PBS-conditioned coatings, characterized by a more wettable interface, consistently exhibited enhanced spontaneous bursting and calcium activity compared with their untreated coatings. Across all conditions, neuronal network activity was more consistently associated with the initial interfacial state of CNT coatings, as experimentally reflected by their wetting behavior, than with CNT length or morphology-dependent electrical transport. These findings identify the initial CNT interfacial state, with wettability serving as an experimentally accessible descriptor, as a key design parameter for CNT-based neural interfaces. Furthermore, they suggest that the initial interfacial state may influence the subsequent evolution of the biomolecular layer at the cell-facing interface, thereby contributing to the modulation of neuronal function.

items.title:
Engineered
Peptide Nanoparticle Targeting Both Bacterial
Load Reduction and Bone Repair for the Treatment of Bone Infections
items.abstract: Abstract Bone infection is a common and serious complication in orthopedic surgery. Conventional antibiotic strategies frequently induce antibiotic resistance, leading to the persistence of bone infections. In this study, an engineered peptide nanoparticle named C8-IK21 was designed based on the coiled-coil motif. Specifically, C8-IK21 effectively targeted bacterial cell membranes, further exacerbating bacterial death through lipid peroxidation. At safe doses, local administration of C8-IK21 demonstrated high efficacy in treating S. aureus-infected cortical bone defects in mice. No detectable resistance emerged under the tested experimental conditions. Additionally, C8-IK21 exhibited anti-inflammatory activity. Furthermore, C8-IK21 could enter cells by binding to ADAM9, activating the ERK signaling pathway to regulate osteoblast differentiation. Meanwhile, C8-IK21 reduced the expression of ITGB1 via ADAM9, thereby inhibiting osteoclast differentiation and function. Moreover, the pro-osteogenic effect of C8-IK21 was validated in organoids. In conclusion, C8-IK21 represents a promising therapeutic approach for the treatment of refractory bacterial infections and bone homeostasis disorders.

items.title:
ZnO–Te Anti-Ambipolar
Switch Integration with
Complementary Field-Effect Transistors Enabling a Pull-Middle Architecture
for Standard Ternary Inverters
items.abstract: Abstract We demonstrate a pull-middle architecture for standard ternary inverters (STIs) operating at 77 K, enabled by the cointegration of a ZnO–Te antiambipolar switch (AAS) and vertically stacked ZnO/Te complementary field-effect transistors (CFETs) using a BEOL-compatible low-temperature process (≤150 °C). Operation at 77 K not only isolates the intrinsic pull-middle switching mechanism by suppressing thermally activated off-currents but also establishes the architecture’s immediate viability for extreme-environment computing, such as radiation-hardened space data centers and cryogenic aerospace systems. In this architecture, the ZnO–Te AAS acts as an independent pull-middle device connected to an explicit Vdd/2 node, while the ZnO and Te FETs in the CFET serve as the pull-down and pull-up devices, respectively. Unlike conventional ternary logic schemes governed by precise pull-up/pull-down current matching, by explicitly clamping the intermediate state, this architecture structurally prevents variation-induced voltage shifts and suppresses static power dissipation. Consequently, the proposed STI exhibits a narrow middle-state voltage distribution across 25 cells and achieves an I/O swing ratio of 1, with cascaded operation without level-restoring circuitry supported by measurement-calibrated circuit simulations. Ultimately, this vertically integrated ZnO/Te STI offers a compact and variation-tolerant platform for cryogenic logic, while presenting a material-optimization pathway toward room-temperature multivalued systems.

items.title:
Defect-Tolerant
Frenkel Exciton Delocalization in
Supramolecular Nanotubes
items.abstract: Abstract Preserving exciton delocalization in the presence of structural and environmental disorder is a central challenge for nanoscale photonic and optoelectronic materials. Here we show that Frenkel excitons in two-dimensional supramolecular nanostructures retain extensive delocalization even in the presence of intentionally incorporated deep-energy traps. Fluorescent trap molecules introduced during the self-assembly of double-walled molecular nanotubes provide a controlled model system in which strong local energetic perturbations are created without significant distortion of the host structure. Increasing the trap concentration shortens the host-exciton PL lifetime from ∼190 ps to ∼15 ps, while polarization-resolved microscopy of individual nanotubes shows that the collective excitonic polarization remains essentially unchanged. Frenkel-exciton calculations based on experimentally established molecular structures reproduce this robustness and reveal that delocalization decreases only weakly because the excitonic wave functions redistribute around the trap sites while remaining extended over large molecular domains. These results demonstrate an intrinsic defect tolerance of delocalized Frenkel excitons in a two-dimensional supramolecular architecture and identify dimensionality as an important design principle for preserving collective excitonic states in structurally imperfect nanomaterials.

items.title:
Full-Length Protein
Classification through Sequence
Reading by Solid-State Subnanopores
items.abstract: Abstract Nanopore sequencing for full-length proteins is daunting due to inaccuracy of fingerprinting amino acids with ionic current and lack of theoretical models. Here, we demonstrate that nanopores drilled in 5 nm-thick membranes with constriction diameter &lt;1 nm, i.e., subnanopores, can site-specifically read the primary structure of amyloid-β (Aβ) isoforms after 50-fold coverage. Molecular dynamics simulations reveal that charged side chains near the constriction swing and modulate the volume exclusion of neighboring residues, resulting in a sequence context-dependent signal altered between translocation orientations. Orientation of individual label-free molecules is inferred by clustering, which yields high-fidelity empirical consensus that strongly correlates with computational trajectories (PCC = 0.78 ± 0.03). A homemade self-supervised learning method categorizes Aβ42 and Aβ40 at the single-molecule level (AUC = 0.88 ± 0.02) and predicts the mole fraction in agreement with actual ratios. Solid-state subnanopores offer a straightforward strategy for proteoform single-molecule classification and sequence extraction in mixtures.

items.title:
Deciphering
Charge Delocalization across Mercaptobenzonitrile
Ligand Terminals and Inner Hydrides in Atomically Precise Cu14H10 Nanoclusters for Electrocatalytic CO2 Reduction
items.abstract: Abstract Cu hydride nanoclusters with atomic precision in composition and structure offer exciting catalytic activities and opportunities for rigorous structure–function correlations. Determination of their atomic structures, especially the hydride locations, hinges on the availability of high-quality single crystals and neutron beams, while their relatively weak UV–visible absorption and electrochemical instability challenge the analysis of their electronic properties. Herein, we synthesize a Cu14H10 nanocluster coordinated by three 4-mercaptobenzonitrile (MBN) and eight triphenylphosphine ligands. Two-dimensional NMR analyses combined with single crystal X-ray diffraction reveal unequivocally the locations of the ten hydrides in four groups (stoichiometry ratio of 1:3:3:3) with drastically different environments (chemical shifts 11–3 ppm): one H at the inversion center and three triangular layers along the C3 axial bridging together the Cu core. MBN serves two additional purposes besides stabilizing ligands: its electron-withdrawing nature and a highly sensitive vibrational reporter of its local charge density. The first property gives rise to a low-lying Cu-core-to-MBN metal-to-ligand charge transfer (MLCT) excited state, and the second property enables direct spectroscopic probing of both the charge transfer nature and dynamics of the MLCT excited state through the dynamic spectral shift of the MBN CN stretching mode. Through combined transient IR absorption spectroscopy and time-dependent density functional theory (TD-DFT) calculations, we obtained the complete atomic and electronic structure, revealing core-to-ligand charge transfers in these nanoclusters. Computed under identical conditions using an iso-structure with a mildly electron-donating ligand, the Cu14H10 featuring charge delocalization toward the electron-withdrawing MBN has a smaller HOMO–LUMO gap, which is deemed favorable for electrocatalytic CO2 reduction. The preferential formation of complex multielectron-hydrogenation products (8–12 e–, C1 hydrocarbons, and C2+ products) over two-electron pathways such as CO formation or the competing hydrogen evolution reaction highlights their promise as atomically precise catalysts for deep CO2 reduction.

items.title:
Tunable Gaussian
Random Number Generator from a Nanoscopic
Domain-Wall-Based Spintronic Device
items.abstract: Abstract Existing hardware implementations of Gaussian random number generators (RNGs) rely on large arrays of binary devices, resulting in substantial hardware footprints or sampling-time overheads. Here, we present a racetrack memory-based random number generator (RTM-RNG) that directly generates analog Gaussian random number streams from a single domain-wall-based nanoscale racetrack. A geometrically engineered racetrack tip creates a localized current-density gradient, enabling field-free stochastic domain-wall nucleation driven by nanosecond current pulses. The domain-wall nucleation probability is continuously tunable via an electrically generated Oersted field or an external magnetic field, providing direct control over the mean of the output distribution. We demonstrate more than 256 distinguishable states from a single nanoscopic RTM-RNG device, thus making a Gaussian RNG with more than 8-bit resolution possible. Compared with conventional binary random bitstreams, the RTM-RNG achieves high-quality Gaussian distributions up to 83 times faster.

items.title:
Addressable Control
of Hybrid Spin Qubit in Single-Atom
Copper-Modified Fullerene
items.abstract: Abstract Developing high-dimensional solid-state quantum technologies requires overcoming the trade-off between spin dimensionality and quantum coherence. Hybrid spin architectures offer a promising solution to expand the quantum state space bottom-up by combining rapid electronic manipulation with robust nuclear phase memory. However, solid-state hybrid spin materials capable of simultaneously supporting both electron and nuclear spin manipulations remain exceedingly rare. Here, we report a Cu2+ (S = 1/2, I = 3/2) hybrid spin system dispersed in a magnetically silent C60 matrix, in which we not only demonstrate comprehensive coherent control over both electron and nuclear spin degrees of freedom but also strike a balance between spin dimensionality and coherence time. The pristine carbon environment suppresses surrounding magnetic noise, acting in tandem with dynamical decoupling to prolong the electron spin coherence time to 16.16 μs. Simultaneously, the nuclear quadrupole interaction of Cu2+ breaks the degeneracy of the nuclear spin manifold, enabling precise addressability of an eight-dimensional Hilbert space. Furthermore, strong electron–nuclear hyperfine coupling acts as a powerful lever, accelerating the nuclear spin Rabi frequency by a factor of 17. By achieving the coexistence of a large manifold of addressable levels and long-lived quantum coherence, Cu/C60 provides a high-dimensional hybrid spin node and a compelling bottom-up approach to expanding the quantum state space.

items.title:
Data-Driven
Atomic Interplay Modulation Enables Dual-Functional
High-Entropy Alloy Mediator for Li–S Batteries
items.abstract: Abstract High-entropy alloys (HEAs) have emerged as appealing candidates to achieve performance regulation in Li–S batteries. Nevertheless, the design principles and working mechanisms of HEAs for dual electrodes remain elusive because of their structural disorder and chemical complexity. Herein, we propose a data-driven maneuver to enable rapid and precise screening of a customized HEA nanocatalyst (FeCoNiCuVMn, 6E-HEAs) via a performance-oriented theoretical criterion in the realm of Li–S electrochemistry. The delicate modulation of atomic interplay in 6E-HEAs simultaneously accelerates sulfur redox kinetics and stabilizes lithium metal deposition. Consequently, Li–S batteries sustain favorable cycling performance at 1.0 C over 1000 cycles while affording a capacity decay rate of merely 0.067% per cycle. The pouch cell harvests a specific capacity of 884.8 mAh g–1 at 0.5 C with steady cyclic operation. Our study elucidates crucial roles of effective compositional gain in boosting bidirectional Li–S electrocatalysis, offering atomic-level insights into HEA design for electrocatalytic reactions.

items.title:
Biomimetic Nanozyme-Decoys
Reprogram Immune Niches
to Intercept Colitis-Carcinoma Transition
items.abstract: Abstract Colitis-associated colorectal cancer (CAC) arises from chronic inflammatory niches characterized by persistent oxidative stress and dysregulated immune cell recruitment. Current anti-inflammatory therapies provide only transient symptom relief and fail to prevent malignant progression due to their inability to simultaneously mitigate oxidative injury and immune chemotaxis. Our analysis of clinical samples revealed markedly elevated C-X-C motif chemokine ligand 2 (CXCL2) in intestinal tissues from patients with inflammatory bowel disease and CAC, implicating the CXCL2-CXCR2 (C-X-C motif chemokine receptor 2) axis in driving excessive neutrophil and macrophage infiltration and fostering tumorigenesis. Herein, we report a biomimetic nanozyme (PB@ECM) that reprograms inflammatory immune niches to intercept CAC progression. PB@ECM integrates a Prussian blue nanozyme core with genetically engineered macrophage membranes, enabling concurrent scavenging of reactive oxygen species through superoxide dismutase- and catalase-like activities and sequestration of CXCL2 via membrane-displayed CXCR2 receptors. In murine models of colitis and CAC, PB@ECM significantly alleviated intestinal inflammation, suppressed neutrophil and macrophage infiltration, and effectively inhibited colitis-carcinoma transition. Notably, treatment with PB@ECM significantly prolonged survival compared with other groups. By disrupting the pathological crosstalk between oxidative stress and immune chemotaxis, this work establishes a biomimetic nanozyme strategy for preventing inflammation-driven carcinogenesis.

items.title:
Overcoming
Oral Environmental Barriers: Nanoengineering
Strategies for Antimicrobial Peptides in Biofilm-Associated Oral Diseases
items.abstract: Abstract Biofilm-associated oral diseases impose a substantial global health burden and are closely linked to systemic inflammation. Although antimicrobial peptides (AMPs) offer a promising alternative to conventional antibiotics, their therapeutic efficacy in the oral cavity is limited by barriers in the oral environment. Free AMPs are rapidly removed by salivary flow, destabilized by local proteases, and impeded by substantial diffusion barriers within mature biofilms. Nanoengineering provides a systematic approach to address these limitations. In this review, we present a barrier-oriented framework for AMP delivery and examine how nanomaterial design addresses the specific constraints of the oral environment. Interfacial engineering prolongs local retention, spatial protection preserves AMP stability, and microenvironment-responsive systems provide on-demand activation for effective biofilm disruption. Alongside these approaches, multifunctional nanosystems combining antimicrobial, immunomodulatory, and regenerative activities are discussed. Finally, key translational challenges, including biosafety, microbiome homeostasis, manufacturing, and regulatory barriers, are critically examined. This review traces the development of AMP nanoengineering from passive delivery vehicles toward precision therapeutic platforms that respond dynamically to the oral microenvironment.

items.title:
Ultrafast High-Photogain
UV–Vis-NIR Broadband
Photodetection in Parallelly Overlapped Stacking Type-I GaSe/MoTe2 Heterostructure
items.abstract: Abstract Broadband photodetectors are important for next-generation optoelectronic applications, ranging from fundamental science, environmental monitoring, industrial detection to artificial-intelligence-enabled Internet of Things systems, where both high responsivity and fast response are critically demanded. Typically, a trade-off exists between the two in the photogating effect, making it challenging to achieve both simultaneously. This study reports a parallelly overlapped stacking GaSe/MoTe2 heterostructure with type-I band alignment (PSH-GM), which simultaneously realizes an ultrafast photoresponse of 523 ns and a high responsivity of 8.95 × 103 A·W–1, together with a noise equivalent power of ∼0.38 × 10–14 W·Hz–1/2 and a specific detectivity of 8.01 × 1011 Jones. Furthermore, PSH-GM exhibits a responsivity of up to 103 A·W–1 over a broad spectral range of 355–1100 nm, covering the ultraviolet (UV), visible (Vis), and near-infrared (NIR) regions. The underlying photodetection mechanism of the parallelly overlapped stacking type-I heterostructure is clarified using photocurrent mapping, and the origin of the dark current shift at different operation frequencies is elucidated, both of which offer insights into the design principles of two-dimensional heterostructures optimized to simultaneously achieve high responsivity and high response bandwidth. Imaging demonstrations are conducted at 355, 520, and 850 nm, and free-space optical communication is demonstrated at 115.2 kbit·s–1, which highlights the potential of PSH-GM for broadband UV–Vis–NIR photodetection, ultrafast data communication, high-speed imaging, and integration into advanced optoelectronic systems.

items.title:
Bright
Alkyl Quantum Defects Govern Early Carbon Nanotube
Pharmacokinetics in Mice
items.abstract: Abstract Fluorescent quantum defects in single-wall carbon nanotubes (SWCNTs) are a major advance in nanocarbon research, owing to their bright, single-photon emission at telecom wavelengths and versatile conjugation chemistries for biomedical sensing and disease targeting. Here, we introduce an efficient, oxygen-free sonochemical route that generates long-chain alkyl defects, simultaneously shortening nanotubes and producing a bright, homogeneously emissive (6,5) SWCNT ensemble. Among 15 screened reactants, the branched-chain NiaproofⓇ 4, which molecular dynamics simulations show packs more densely and uniformly than linear surfactants, yields a 3.4-fold brightness enhancement and a sharp emission peak near 1108 nm. Single-particle spectroscopy reveals J-aggregate emission redshifts at high defect densities, and fibrinogen titration shows defect chemistry governs protein-driven coating displacement. Using a home-built short-wave infrared imaging system (25 mW cm–2, 989 nm excitation, 1150 nm long-pass collection), we show that these sparse defects (∼9–16 μm–1) drive different pharmacokinetics between NiaproofⓇ 4– and lipid-PEG–functionalized (6,5) at early time points, converging as protein-corona formation masks the underlying chemistry. Histology localizes the nanotubes within macrophages of mononuclear phagocyte system–associated organs. Intravenous administration (∼41 μg kg–1) causes no acute toxicity and a short ∼2-day retention. The NiaproofⓇ 4 group exhibits a reduced circulating myeloid-cell fraction following corona formation, which may reflect organ recruitment and sequestration, while the accompanying increase in CD3+ T cells may partly reflect a proportional shift in leukocyte composition.

items.title: Issue Editorial Masthead
Issue Publication Information

An Optoelectronic
SnP2S6 Memristive
Neuron for Biologically Inspired Multimodal Neuromorphic Information
Processing
items.abstract: Abstract Neuromorphic systems capable of integrating multiple sensory modalities offer a promising route toward energy-efficient information processing that more closely emulates biological neural networks. Here, we demonstrate a multifunctional ITO/SnP2S6/Ti memristive neuron that combines reproducible volatile resistive switching and integrate-and-fire dynamics under electrical-pulse stimulation with wavelength-selective photoresponses and short-term optoelectronic synaptic plasticity. Leveraging these experimentally measured device characteristics, we construct a multimodal neuromorphic recognition framework that integrates volatile memristive neurons with programmable memristive synapses. Inspired by the parallel processing of visual features in the primate visual system, structural and color information are independently encoded and processed through separate electrical and optical pathways before being integrated for classification. Importantly, inference is implemented using experimentally measured neuronal firing statistics and programmed synaptic conductance states, rather than idealized device models, thereby establishing a direct link between device characteristics and system-level functionality. As a proof-of-concept, the framework is evaluated on a fruit-recognition task using a subset of the Fruits-360 image data set, achieving a classification accuracy of 94.9% through multimodal fusion and substantially outperforming recognition based on either modality alone. These results establish SnP2S6 memristive devices as a versatile platform for integrating electrical and optical neuronal functionalities and highlight their potential for hardware-realistic multimodal in-sensor neuromorphic computing.

items.title:
Breaking the Capacity–Stability
Trade-Off in
High-Voltage LiCoO2 via Opposite Co/O Redox Activity
items.abstract: Abstract LiCoO2 (LCO) suffers from daunting capacity–stability trade-off due to deeper Co oxidation and ensuing O oxidation (O2– → Co4+ electron transfer) at high-voltage (≥4.5 V). Aggressive Co4+ and O2/On– (0 &lt; n &lt; 2) species result in pronounced mechanical/chemical failure and fast capacity decay. Most of the state-of-the-art solutions partially resolve these problems yet sacrificing capacity. Herein, facilitated Co3+/4+ redox and effectively restrained O redox are simultaneously achieved by amplifying Co t2g electron density of states (DOS) near the Fermi level while reducing O 2p electron DOS. Consequently, the engineered cathode harvests a remarkable initial capacity of 212.1 mAh g–1 at 4.6 V (vs 212.9 mAh g–1 of bare LCO). Moreover, advanced multiscale X-ray/electron spectroscopy and imaging techniques reveal that mitigated O redox prevents irreversible phase transitions, lattice O loss, and undesirable surface parasitic reactions. As a result, the cathode has reinforced electrochemical (capacity retention of 88.4% within 330 cycles at 5C) and thermal stability thanks to fatigue-free (de)lithiation channels, less new-generated Co3O4 layer, and inorganic-rich cathode/electrolyte interphase (CEI) film. This work provides a valuable inspiration for the electronic structure engineer of robust LCO cathode toward high operation voltages.

items.title:
Truly Asynchronous
and One-Hot Constraint Probabilistic
Potts Computing with Floating-Body Metal–Oxide–Semiconductor
Field-Effect Transistors
items.abstract: Abstract This work presents a truly asynchronous physical Potts node (TAPPN) using floating-body metal–oxide–semiconductor field-effect transistors (FB-MOSFETs) to overcome the scalability and encoding overhead limitations of binary Ising-based probabilistic computing. The TAPPN enables native multistate representation without external random-number generators (RNGs) or complex digital arbitration by the intrinsic stochastic single-transistor latch (STL) effect and a drain-sharing configuration. The stochastic source and the one-hot constraint are realized by three transistors, and the node requires 25 transistors and 220 nW including the readout, compared with 2160 transistors and 52 μW for a self-contained digital node evaluated at the same boundary. Its truly asynchronous operation allows efficient exploration of the problem space in large-scale graph-coloring benchmarks. In simulations of the update rule, the Potts-based system achieves a higher success probability than simulated annealing (SA) and parallel tempering (PT) on graph-coloring benchmarks. For an integrated array assumed to operate at 5 MHz, the architecture is projected to reach a time-to-solution (TTS) of 3.4 μs and an energy-to-solution (ETS) of 504 nJ. This platform establishes a complementary metal–oxide–semiconductor (CMOS)-compatible pathway toward large-scale, multistate combinatorial optimization.

items.title:
Self-Assembly of
Two-Dimensional Open Structures with
Adjustable Square Voids
items.abstract: Abstract Self-assembly of anisotropic particles offers a powerful route to design materials with tailored microstructures. Here we investigate two-dimensional systems of patchy hard rectangles using Monte Carlo simulations and free volume theory, mapping their phase diagram across packing fractions and interaction strengths. Low attraction recovers excluded-volume phase behavior (isotropic–tetratic–smectic), while intermediate attraction strengths feature a broad isotropic–smectic coexistence region. For high interaction strengths our theory predicts, and simulations confirm, a highly ordered “weaver” phase characterized by a four-rectangle unit cell that forms a regular grid of square voids. Although the pure weaver phase forms only in a narrow window of packing fractions, it coexists with either the isotropic gas or smectic solid over a wide range of packing fractions. Patchy rectangles demonstrate how shape together with tunable interactions can be utilized to self-assemble porous materials with precisely adjustable void sizes and geometries and could be realized using DNA origami structures.

items.title:
Attempts
to Understand and Manipulate the Orientation
and Retention of Peptides Inside Nanopores Expand the Toolbox for
Nanopore-Based Proteomics
items.abstract: Abstract Nanopore techniques have emerged as promising tools for deciphering complex proteomics from the single-molecule level by profiling individual peptides. The entry orientation of a peptide and its subsequent retention inside the nanopore are crucial for the analytical results but remain challenging to be properly defined, which limits the sensing capability of nanopore-based proteomics technology. Here, we propose that electrically driving peptide entry into α-hemolysin nanopores against opposing electroosmotic flows is a promising platform to guide the polypeptide with a preferential orientation. α-Hemolysin mutants with opposite ion selectivity have been engineered and employed to measure peptides at pH 3.8 and at alkaline pH exceeding 10.0. The impact of peptide charge distribution on the orientation has been investigated by simulating the peptide dipole moment and electrophysiology measurements. In addition, the retention position of the peptide has been altered by introducing tryptophan residues at position 125 within the β-barrel region of α-hemolysin, which increases the sensitivity for specific peptide region and enables the detection of initially inaccessible monomethylation modifications. Thus, we present a rational framework to investigate and manipulate the orientation and dwelling position of peptides inside the α-hemolysin nanopore, which can enhance our capability to profile polypeptides by using nanopore techniques.

items.title:
Ultrafast Imaging
of Dynamic Disorder in Superionic
Chalcocite
items.abstract: Abstract The optimal functionalities of matter often appear at emergent structural orders involving entangled changes in the lattice structures and the underlying atomic degree of freedom. Here, we report laser-induced, thermally driven dynamic structural orders evolving in the low- to high-chalcocite transition of copper(I) sulfide using time-resolved electron diffractometry in ultrafast electron microscopy. We filmed the complete phase trajectory of the transient atomic motions and the hierarchical decoupling of structural orders that unfold over time. Moreover, a transient, disordered state is unveiled. The disordered state emerges during the superionic diffusion of copper ions along a few-nanometer-thick lattice channels. Temporal gating of the various combinations of structure could expand the range of accessible functional states in matter.

items.title:
Charge-Induced Formation
and Field-Driven Directional
Motion of Vacancies in a Two-Dimensional Halide
items.abstract: Abstract Controlling defect evolution in two-dimensional (2D) materials is essential for reliable nanoelectronic functionalities, yet selectively inducing defect formation and externally driven migration remains a key challenge. Here, we demonstrate two distinct mechanisms governing halogen vacancy formation and migration in a PbBr2 monolayer on highly ordered pyrolytic graphite using low-temperature scanning tunneling microscopy combined with density functional theory calculations. We show that halogen vacancies reshape the local density of states and electrostatic potential beyond the immediate defect site. Crucially, electric fields and charge injection mediate distinct atomic-scale responses: tip-induced electric fields drive directional vacancy migration and coalescence, whereas charge injection from the tunneling current induces vacancy formation, with enhanced efficiency when coupling to shallow defect states. These results demonstrate that direct electrical stimuli can drive both vacancy motion and creation in a two-dimensional, predominantly ionic material system. Our findings establish a framework linking defect-induced electronic structure, local electrostatics, and externally driven atomic rearrangement under conditions relevant to device operation.

items.title:
Machine-Learning
Dynamics of Redox-Active Materials:
Polaron Diffusion on the TiO2(110) Surface
items.abstract: Abstract In redox-active materials, atoms dynamically change their oxidation states in response to excess charge and electronic transport, with the potential for novel technologies spanning electronics, catalysis, and energy storage and conversion. Despite the remarkable progress of modern artificial intelligence methods in accelerating atomistic simulations, capturing the quantum-mechanical nature of charge transport and dynamically varying oxidation states remains a fundamental challenge, limiting scientific and technological progress. In this work, we introduce a machine-learning-based molecular dynamics framework capable of explicitly tracking the oxidation state dynamics arising from small-polaron hopping (excess charges trapped on single lattice sites that diffuse upon thermal activation). Our model uses descriptors augmented with charge localization information at each time step and is trained on density functional theory data to capture signatures of polaronic diffusion. We apply our method to the rutile TiO2(110) surface, which is a prototypical reducible oxide. Our simulations reveal that charge-carrier diffusion is highly sensitive to the local surface environment: polarons preferentially localize near oxygen vacancies, whereas their interaction with hydroxyl groups is weaker. These results provide a microscopic interpretation of experimental observations, highlight strategies to tune charge-carrier mobility through surface engineering, and demonstrate the applicability of our approach to investigating charge transport in complex materials.

items.title:
Nanoarchitecture
of Cobalt Phthalocyanine for Enhanced
Chloramphenicol Hydrodechlorination through Direct Electron-Transfer
Mechanism
items.abstract: Abstract Electrocatalytic hydrodechlorination (ECHD) provides a sustainable method for treating water polluted with chlorinated organic compounds under ambient conditions. Cobalt phthalocyanine (CoPc) represents a molecular catalyst with economic benefits and high selectivity, although its performance is limited by significant molecular stacking. To this end, we constructed ordered CoPc nanotubes (CoTs) for ECHD studies, alongside conventional CoPc single molecules and disordered aggregates as reference systems. All materials catalyzed ECHD via a direct electron transfer (DET) route on the CoPc active state under turnover conditions. The ordered CoT architecture accelerated interfacial and internal electron transfer, boosting the intrinsic activity. Degradation involves simultaneous reduction of terminal nitro and chloro groups, and the latter is suggested to follow an energetically favorable remote attack pathway. At full chloramphenicol (CAP) conversion, CoTs delivered an ECHD ratio of 83.9%, which is superior to recent benchmarks. For practical use, a flow-cell system achieved a treatment flux of 6.79 L h–1 g–1, which is 5 times that of a standard H-cell. This work underscores the pivotal role of molecular ordering in enhancing ECHD and offers design guidelines for non-noble metal heterogeneous electrocatalysts.

items.title:
A
Flexible Complementary Memristive Synapse for Convolutional
Neural Network Applications
items.abstract: Abstract The memristive artificial synapse, which typically operates on the basis of various filamentary conductance-update mechanisms, has been extensively utilized to implement hardware neural networks for brain-inspired computing. However, the stochastic conductance-switching characteristics that arise from uncontrollable filamentary evolution within the two-terminal device have long hindered hardware neural networks from achieving training and recognition performance comparable to their software neural network. Here, we propose a flexible complementary memristive synapse that achieves highly linear conductance-update behavior while preserving a large dynamic range. This synapse consists of a homogeneous bilayer of two amorphous indium–gallium-tin oxide (a-IGTO) films deposited under different oxygen partial pressures: an oxygen-deficient, VO-rich layer formed without O2 supply and an oxygen-supplied, VO-poor layer formed with O2 supply, exhibiting incremental and decremental conductance-update behaviors, respectively. The distinct oxygen-vacancy-related states and filament-evolution characteristics of the two layers suggest vacancy-mediated layer-to-layer redistribution, which can mutually compensate the nonideal conductive filament evolution of the two different layers, thereby facilitating more gradual modulation of the net conductance. The proposed flexible synapse exhibits robust mechanical stability and durability after 12,000 bending–release cycles, as confirmed by electrical characterization while maintained in the bent state at a bending radius of 2 mm. Finally, the applicability of the proposed flexible synapses to HW-NNs is evaluated through a VGG-8-based CIFAR-10 image recognition simulation using experimentally measured synaptic characteristics for weight updates in the two fully connected layers.

items.title:
Kinetic
Control of Symmetry-Broken Spin Architectures
of Azafullerene on [10]Cycloparaphenylene Templates: From Frustrated
2D Lattices to Quasi-1D Chains
items.abstract: Abstract Supramolecular host–guest complexation provides a powerful strategy for stabilizing organic radicals and organizing them into functional spin architectures. Here, we investigate the kinetic pathways for on-surface complexation of spin-1/2 azafullerene radicals (C59N•) within templated [10]cycloparaphenylene ([10]CPP) nanohoop monolayers on Au(111), revealing a strongly anisotropic energy landscape that governs radical migration and encapsulation. Migration of isolated C59N• along the [10]CPP rims proceeds via relatively low energy barriers (∼0.45 eV), leading to preferential confinement at the nanohoop periphery prior to azafullerene encapsulation. C59N• relocation to the global energy minimum at the [10]CPP center requires overcoming substantially higher barriers of at least ∼0.8 eV, with interfullerene interactions raising these barriers further. High C59N• mobility and relaxed lateral confinement at [10]CPP template edges also activate an alternative assembly pathway in which azafullerene intercalation induces in-plane exfoliation of [10]CPP lines from the 2D [10]CPP array, creating a reconstructed two-dimensional superlattice composed of alternating zigzag chains of azafullerenes and linear rows of encapsulated C59N•⊂[10]CPP complexes. This edge-driven reorganization gives rise to anisotropic lattices of encapsulated radicals with one-dimensional structural motifs. The control over the rich energy landscape of C59N•⊂[10]CPP complexation thus enables access not only to geometrically frustrated two-dimensional lattices but also to quasi-one-dimensional chain motifs of spin-1/2 carrying radicals within a single supramolecular platform.

items.title:
Modulation of MOF
Catalytic Activity to Exploit Cystine
Dependency for Immunometabolic Therapy
items.abstract: Abstract Tumor immunometabolism plays an important role in tumor progression and immune cell activity and is therefore critical to the efficacy of cancer immunotherapy. Modulation of immunometabolism to boost cancer immunotherapy is mostly based on targeting tumor cell metabolism, which often fails to address the tumor-promoting functions maintained by stromal cells. In contrast, targeting a metabolic checkpoint shared by tumor cells and cancer-associated fibroblasts (CAFs) can potentially overcome this limitation but has been relatively underexplored. Herein, a locally delivered, ultrasound activatable nanocatalytic platform is reported for immunometabolic cancer therapy. The platform is composed of sulfasalazine and a gallium-modified Fe-TCPP metal–organic framework nanozyme codelivered in an oxidized sodium alginate-based hydrogel. Ultrasound-activated gallium-modified Fe-TCPP boosts electron transfer, peroxide activation, and reactive oxygen species production while disrupting iron balance. Simultaneously, sulfasalazine inhibits SLC7A11-mediated cystine uptake in CAFs and tumor cells, reducing matrix remodeling and weakening the tumor’s antioxidant defense. This dual approach increases oxidative stress, reshapes the tumor microenvironment, induces immunogenic tumor cell death with ferroptotic traits, matures dendritic cells, and strengthens CD8+ T-cell responses. Consequently, it suppresses tumor growth in an immunocompetent osteosarcoma model and remains effective in a patient-derived OSCC xenograft model. Together, these findings demonstrate that targeting shared SLC7A11-mediated cystine dependence integrates stromal remodeling, tumor redox disruption, and antitumor immune activation.

items.title:
Stiffness
Directs Intracellular Fate and Intercellular
Transport of Nanoparticles
items.abstract: Abstract Nanoparticles have been developed as delivery vehicles to achieve uniform distribution of drugs in the tumor, but they are still not optimal for deep tumor penetration due to the hindrance by the dense extracellular matrix. Enabling active transport via tumor cells has been explored as a solution, which has been achieved by tuning the size and surface chemistry of nanoparticles. Here, we show that particle stiffness is another key determinant. Using positively charged polyglycerol nanogels with matched size, charge, and composition, we found that stiff nanogels preferentially enter cells via clathrin-mediated endocytosis (CME), undergo lysosomal processing, and are efficiently exocytosed, enabling transcellular transport. In contrast, soft nanogels are taken up mainly by macropinocytosis, accumulate in the Golgi apparatus, and exhibit prolonged intracellular retention. Finally, the efficient CME and subsequent exocytosis of stiff nanoparticles contribute to the enhanced transcytosis efficiency, allowing them to penetrate 3D tumor spheroids. This stiffness-dependent cellular itinerary operates without additional surface modifications, revealing a general design principle whereby intrinsic mechanical properties can control intracellular and intercellular transport behavior of nanoparticles.

items.title:
Bacteria-Derived
Micro/Nanoparticles for Vaccine Design
items.abstract: Abstract Vaccines have profoundly reduced the global burden of infectious diseases and are increasingly being explored for cancer immunotherapy. However, developing vaccine platforms capable of simultaneously achieving efficient antigen delivery, precise immune modulation, and durable protective immunity remains a major challenge. Bacteria-derived micro/nanoparticles (BPs) have recently emerged as promising vaccine platforms that integrate the structural advantages of nanomaterials with the intrinsic immunostimulatory properties of bacterial components.
