Ru-associated sites preferentially accommodate H* intermediates, while electronically reconstructed Pt sites optimize the H* adsorption/desorption balance under acidic conditions, giving a low H* desorption barrier of 0.22 eV. The PtNiRuFeW/CNFs requires only 45 and 90 mV to reach 100 mA cm–2 in 1.0 M KOH and 0.5 M H2SO4, respectively. Moreover, an anion-exchange-membrane water electrolyzer using PtNiRuFeW/CNFs as the cathode maintains stable operation at 500 mA cm–2 for 470 h. This work establishes site-differentiated high-entropy catalysis as a strategy for coupling acidic and alkaline HER elementary steps within one continuous alloy surface.

items.title:
Dual
DNA Nanomaterial-Regulated Homogeneous Immunoreaction-Enabled
One-Step Electrochemical Analysis of Multiple Biomarkers in Clinical
Samples
items.abstract: Abstract Homogeneous immunoassays offer a streamlined alternative to traditional heterogeneous methods by eliminating separation and washing steps. However, they are often hampered by low sensitivity, matrix interference, and limited multiplexing capability. Herein, we reported a dual DNA nanomaterial-based homogeneous electrochemical immunoassay that achieved ultrasensitive, one-step, simultaneous detection of multiple biomarkers. The system comprised a cyclic DNA nanomaterial (C-DNM) and a Y-shaped DNA nanosphere (Y-DNM) that coordinated Ag+ and Hg2+ via base mismatching, and antibodies were conjugated by the biotin–streptavidin system. Specific antigen–antibody binding could exert spatial steric hindrance on C-DNM, thereby triggering cascade metal ions release from Y-DNM and producing a second burst of signal amplification. This mechanism enabled detection limits down to the ag/mL level. Utilizing this strategy, we successfully quantified urinary ESAT-6 and LAM for tuberculosis, as well as PD-L1/MUC1-positive small extracellular vesicles (SEVs) and circulating tumor cells for lung cancer. The whole detection could be completed within 30 min. Clinical validation was taken in 60 samples, and the receiver operating curve analysis demonstrated good diagnostic accuracy, which showed strong correlation with clinical imaging findings. This dual DNA nanomaterial strategy provided a universal, rapid, and ultrasensitive tool for homogeneous immunoassay-based precision diagnostics of diseases.

items.title:
Large-Aperture Inverse-Designed
Sparse Meta-Optics
in the Mid-Wave Infrared
items.abstract: Abstract Long-range midwave infrared (MWIR) imaging demands large apertures for high angular resolution, yet scaling conventional flat optics to the centimeter scale severely throttles multiwavelength design tractability and large-scale physical realization. While flat sparse meta-optics systems have recently emerged to mitigate the footprint of monochromatic large-scale optics, their functional scaling remains fundamentally bounded by single-wavelength operational limits and staggering computational costs under full-scale global optimization. Here, we shatter these long-standing boundaries by demonstrating an inverse-designed sparse meta-optics paradigm that transcends traditional monochromatic constraints to achieve multiband and broad-spectrum MWIR imaging. By implementing a reduced-dimensional optimization framework, we compress multiwavelength phase design complexity by orders of magnitude, mapping optimal radial phase distributions directly onto a prescribed sparse-aperture geometry. The sparse-aperture configuration is selected for its straightforward layout, mechanical robustness, and inherently compact point spread function (PSF), thereby isolating the phase optimization from the macro-scale aperture geometry. The resulting algorithmic tractability, combined with maskless, large-area laser direct writing (LDW) lithography, enables the physical realization of complex wavefront control over large areas while easing the fabrication burden. Using the integrated design-to-fabrication framework, two 89 mm-diameter all-silicon sparse metalenses are fabricated and experimentally validated, demonstrating enhanced performance across multiple wavelengths, varying object distances, and diverse sensing scenarios. Combined with a complementary backend reconstruction algorithm to mitigate inherent PSF artifacts, this work establishes a comprehensive computational design and scalable laser manufacturing platform for next-generation, large-aperture sparse meta-optics in thermal imaging systems.

items.title:
Inner-Surface
Charge Mapping in Confined Systems via
Electrical Double-Layer Dynamics
items.abstract: Abstract Surface charges at solid–liquid interfaces govern diverse emerging interfacial phenomena, yet their quantification in confined geometries remains challenging. Here, we report an electrical double-layer dynamics-enabled method for inner-surface charge characterization (EISC), using water as a mobile and conformal probe. Unlike conventional techniques that require access to exposed surfaces, the EISC method converts charge transfer at water–solid interfaces into measurable, spatially resolved electrical signals, enabling reconstruction of local surface charge density along otherwise inaccessible inner surfaces. Quantitative validation using a roll-up platform, where predefined surface charges are introduced via electrowetting, shows strong agreement with electrostatic voltmeter measurements and enables quantitative reconstruction of diverse charge distributions. Leveraging this capability, we investigate water–solid contact electrification in tubular channels and reveal a velocity-dependent charge separation process at the receding contact line, with grounding effects pronounced at low velocities. Furthermore, direct mapping of charge evolution in droplet electricity generators demonstrates that device performance is governed not only by droplet-carried charges but also by interfacial charge accumulation and redistribution on the solid surface. This work establishes a versatile strategy for probing interfacial charges in confined systems and provides valuable mechanistic insights into charge transfer processes at water–solid interfaces.

items.title:
Adenovirus-Derived
Virus-Like Particles Enable Rapid
Encapsulation and Delivery of Functional Antigen Cargo
items.abstract: Abstract Adenoviral vectors have been widely validated as effective vaccine platforms for both infectious diseases and cancer due to their strong immunostimulatory properties. However, their application to personalized cancer vaccines and other time-sensitive antigens is limited by the prolonged production time required for conventional vector generation. Here, we developed an adenovirus-derived virus-like particle (Ad5VLP) platform that enables modular incorporation of antigen cargo without reconstruction of a complete antigen-encoding adenoviral genome. Ad5VLPs successfully packaged and delivered foreign mRNA, although mRNA-derived antigen expression remained insufficient to induce robust antigen-specific immunity in vivo. In contrast, direct encapsulation of protein or peptide antigens substantially improved intracellular antigen delivery and major histocompatibility complex (MHC) class I antigen presentation. Following subcutaneous prime-boost immunization in mice, antigen-loaded Ad5VLPs induced robust antigen-specific interferon-γ (IFN-γ) responses, with functional activity preferentially enriched within CD44hi CD8+ T cells and accompanied by effector-associated CD8+ T-cell differentiation. Importantly, robust cellular immune responses were also observed using an E0771 tumor neoantigen, demonstrating that the platform extends beyond the model ovalbumin (OVA) antigen. Protein-loaded Ad5VLPs also elicited antigen-specific and antivector humoral responses. Vaccination was well tolerated over the 14 day study period, with no substantial changes in body weight, clinical observations, serum markers of hepatic or renal injury and systemic inflammation, or broad splenic inflammatory transcriptional signatures. Together, these findings demonstrate that Ad5VLPs enable modular delivery of protein and peptide antigens and induce robust cellular immune responses, supporting further investigation for personalized cancer vaccination and other time-sensitive vaccine applications.

items.title:
Bound States in
the Continuum across the Electromagnetic
Spectrum toward Nanophotonic Applications
items.abstract: Abstract Radiative loss to the surrounding continuum fundamentally limits the quality factor (Q) of the resonant modes in open systems. This constrains the light–matter coupling strength, emission coherence, and efficiency of nonlinear interactions, all of which critically depend on high-Q confinement. Bound states in the continuum (BICs) offer an elegant solution to this challenge by delivering high-Q resonances and strong field localization, even when the resonant frequency lies within the radiation continuum. In this Review, we trace the physics of BICs from their formation mechanisms to platform-dependent implementations and device-level functionalities, highlighting what they enable across different frequency regimes. We identify two broad categories, symmetry-protected and accidental BICs, each realized across metasurfaces, gratings, photonic crystal slabs, integrated waveguides, and hybrid resonant structures. Platform-dependent radiation channels and coupling conditions, in turn, determine three core physical effects, which are enhanced light–matter interaction, topological field modulation, and strong wave confinement. These effects drive applications across the entire electromagnetic spectrum from ultraviolet to radio frequencies. By establishing radiation coupling suppression as a unifying paradigm, BICs have unlocked performance regimes, broad cross platform, and research directions that extend far beyond conventional resonance-engineering applications.

items.title:
A Trojan Horse Nanotrap
with a GSH-Responsive Molecular
Gate Orchestrates Ferroptosis via Coupled Iron Release and Spatial
GPX4 Inhibition
items.abstract: Abstract Disruption of the dynamic equilibrium between ferroptotic execution pathways and cellular defense mechanisms can trigger ferroptosis, providing a compelling strategy for tumor suppression and the circumvention of drug resistance. Here, we engineered a Trojan Horse-inspired nanotrap, MIPGPX4@aMOF@CM, that integrates biomimetic recognition, redox-responsive amorphous MOF (aMOF) chemistry, and molecular imprinting to disrupt metal homeostasis and disable key protective pathways, thereby triggering cascade-amplified ferroptosis. The inner core is a molecularly imprinted polymer (MIP) that selectively recognizes GPX4, while the outer shell consists of a novel iron-based aMOF acting as a redox-activated molecular gate and is further cloaked with a cancer cell membrane. This multifunctional nanoplatform enables tumor-specific iron delivery and spatially controlled GPX4 inhibition. Upon homotypic membrane-mediated tumor targeting and cellular internalization, elevated intracellular glutathione (GSH) triggers aMOF degradation, leading to GSH depletion, iron release, and on-demand exposure of the imprinted GPX4 binding sites. This gate-controlled cascade synergistically promotes Fenton chemistry and GPX4 inactivation, substantially disrupting the balance between ferroptotic execution and antioxidant defenses and enhancing tumor-selective ferroptotic responses. Collectively, this work highlights that precisely orchestrating metal homeostasis, redox regulation, and GPX4 inhibition represents a promising strategy for precision ferroptosis-based cancer therapy.

items.title:
All-Trans
Retinoic Acid-Loaded Fe–N3–Se Single-Atom
Nanozymes Enable Redox-Guided Differentiation
Therapy for Acute Myeloid Leukemia
items.abstract: Abstract Differentiation blockade is a defining hallmark of acute myeloid leukemia (AML). While all-trans retinoic acid (ATRA)-based differentiation therapy is curative in acute promyelocytic leukemia (APL), its efficacy in non-APL AML remains limited, and the determinants of differentiation responsiveness beyond APL are poorly understood. Here, we identify redox homeostasis reprogramming as a decisive and previously underappreciated regulator of differentiation therapy efficacy in AML and establish nanozyme-enabled redox modulation as a generalizable framework to restore differentiation competence. We rationally design a Fe–Se dual-atom nanozyme that reconstructs key catalytic features of natural glutathione peroxidase, enabling controlled and homeostatic regulation of intracellular oxidative stress. When combined with ATRA, this redox-guided strategy reinstates differentiation-associated transcriptional programs, suppresses leukemic stemness, and overcomes intrinsic differentiation resistance independently of APL-specific oncogenic drivers. Efficacy is demonstrated in human AML xenograft models and a hoxa9-driven differentiation-arrest zebrafish model. Collectively, this work defines redox regulation as an actionable control point for extending differentiation-based therapies beyond genetically restricted AML subtypes.

items.title:
Spatially Decoupled
Donor and Acceptor Gradient Brush
Particle Blends for Mechanically Robust, Fatigue-Resistant, and Recyclable
Elastomers
items.abstract: Abstract Combining high mechanical strength, fatigue resistance, and reprocessability in a single soft material remains a fundamental challenge. Here, we report a strategy based on spatially decoupled interparticle hydrogen bonding in architecturally controlled brush particle blends. Complementary hydrogen-bonding motifs, namely poly(acrylic acid) (PAA) as donor and poly(dimethylaminoethyl methacrylate) (PDMAEMA) as acceptor, were incorporated into poly(n-butyl acrylate) (PnBA)-based gradient brush particles via surface-initiated atom transfer radical polymerization (SI-ATRP). Upon blending, reversible interparticle hydrogen bonds were formed, functioning as dynamic physical cross-links. The resulting materials exhibited tensile strengths up to 18 MPa, Young’s modulus of 95 MPa, and fracture strains exceeding 150–200%, a combination rarely achieved in physically cross-linked polymer networks. Hierarchical viscoelastic analysis revealed that the synergy between reversible interparticle bonding and architectural heterogeneity generates broad relaxation spectra and multiscale energy dissipation pathways. These features collectively underpin outstanding fatigue resistance, crack-propagation suppression, reprocessability, and thermally assisted self-healing, with annealing at 50 °C restoring approximately 90% of the original modulus and near-complete tensile strength. This work establishes spatial decoupling of hydrogen-bond donors and acceptors as a transferable design principle for durable, recyclable structural soft materials.

items.title: Recent Advances in De Novo Synthesis of Interfacial Two-Dimensional Polymers
items.abstract: Abstract Two-dimensional polymers (2DPs) integrate the molecular programmability of synthetic polymers with the reduced dimensionality and surface accessibility of atomically thin materials. Realizing their functional potential and establishing reliable structure–property relationships, however, require precise control over lattice topology, crystallinity, orientation, thickness, and defect structure. Interfacial polymerization is particularly suited to this objective because interfaces confine network formation while regulating molecular organization, reactant transport, bond-formation kinetics, nucleation, crystal growth, and defect evolution. This Review summarizes the molecular design principles underlying interfacial 2DP synthesis and compares four major environments according to whether polymerization occurs at a liquid or solid surface: air–liquid, liquid–liquid, solid–liquid, and vapor–solid interfaces. We contrast liquid surfaces, which couple dynamic confinement with transport-regulated molecular reorganization and scalable film growth, with solid surfaces, which provide adsorption, templating, and catalytic control while enabling direct mechanistic investigation at the molecular scale. We further examine how precursor organization, mass transport, crystallization pathways, stacking, and defect evolution collectively determine the structural quality of 2DPs. Particular attention is given to mechanistic insights from advanced characterization methods that directly track nucleation and domain-growth dynamics and resolve grain-boundary and defect structures from molecular to atomic resolution. Emerging electronic and stimuli-responsive devices are discussed to illustrate how framework design, structural quality, and interfacial organization translate into functional performance. Finally, we identify opportunities to advance interfacial polymerization from empirical optimization toward predictive synthesis that bridges local atomic precision with macroscopic structural uniformity.

items.title:
Nanotechnology-Integrated
Diagnostic Platforms toward
Decentralized Infectious Disease Management
items.abstract: Abstract Nanotechnology-integrated diagnostic platforms are increasingly being developed across infectious disease management, from screening and diagnosis to potentially treatment-guiding assessment and monitoring. Yet current progress has rarely been synthesized from a clinical management perspective, making it difficult to determine which technologies are ready for decentralized use, where progress remains fragmented, and which clinical needs remain unmet. This review examines nanotechnology-enabled strategies according to how they enable the sample-to-answer workflow, rather than classifying them by material type. Major diagnostic platform architectures are then assessed in terms of practical implementation, with emphasis on platform-specific limitations and emerging solutions. Current applications are further mapped across the infectious disease management continuum to identify established capabilities, missing links, and disconnects from clinical workflows. The broader changes needed to close these gaps are also discussed. This review aims to clarify how nanotechnology-integrated diagnostic platforms can be better developed toward decentralized, reliable, and clinically actionable infectious disease management.

items.title:
Controlling
Redox Interplay in the Formation of Anisotropic
Multimetallic Nanocrystals
items.abstract: Abstract Controlling the interplay between reduction and galvanic processes is critical for tailoring the structure and composition of multimetallic nanocrystals. Here, we report a synthetic strategy to produce anisotropic Au–Pd–Pt nanocrystals with tunable morphologies and elemental distributions. Platinum deposition on single-crystal Au@Pd nanorods (NRs) was modulated by varying the concentration of ascorbic acid, enabling control over the balance between reduction and galvanic-like processes. This approach yields distinct nanostructures, including nanoframes, cloud-like morphologies, and core–shell–shell architectures. Advanced electron microscopy, including high-resolution HAADF STEM imaging, EDX elemental mapping, and electron tomography, reveals intricate elemental distributions, the formation of cavities and tunnels, the apparent preservation of single-crystal characteristics in Au@Pd NRs under the explored conditions, and gold etching induced by the platinum precursor. A preliminary evaluation of catalytic activity suggests enhanced ethanol oxidation performance for nanoframe structures. These findings establish a versatile strategy for engineering anisotropic multimetallic nanocrystals through controlled redox interplay.

items.title:
Visualizing
Kinetic Control and Thermodynamic Selection
in Nanocluster Structural Evolution
items.abstract: Abstract It is extremely challenging to clarify the precise atomic-level evolution of nanoclusters from a dynamically trapped state to a thermodynamically selected product. Various factors play distinctly different roles in the thermodynamic and kinetic control of structural transformation reactions. In this study, we used the system Ag14(SPh)12(DPPH)4 → Ag23(SPh)18(DPPH)4 as a homologous model system, and combined single-crystal structural analysis, time-resolved electrospray ionization mass spectrometry (ESI-MS), ultraviolet–visible absorption spectroscopy, and photoluminescence measurements for correlation analysis. Crystallographic studies revealed that the Ag23 framework could be geometrically decomposed into two substructures related to Ag14, both sharing the metal and thioimine groups, providing a structural basis for the bimolecular fusion hypothesis. Time-dependent spectroscopic techniques revealed the consumption process of Ag14 and the growth process of Ag23, while temperature-dependent experiments showed a kinetic window within which the conversion rate accelerated, but higher thermal input would promote breakage/decomposition and form Ag10. Due to the ability of ESI-MS to generate gas-phase fragments, ions containing Ag5- and Ag9 were regarded as candidate species detected by ESI, rather than confirmed solution intermediates. Therefore, the core breakthrough was not the isolated Ag14 or Ag23 nuclear numbers, but the mechanistic connection of the two structurally similar cluster states in a single reaction network and the identification of thermal activation as the key factor guiding the evolution of the cluster states.

items.title:
Bipolar Redox Molecule-Assembled
Freestanding Film
Cathodes for Aqueous Zinc-Ion Batteries with Excellent Thermal Adaptivity
and Ultralong Life
items.abstract: Abstract Organic molecules with high redox potentials and large theoretical capacities are promising cathode materials for aqueous zinc-ion batteries (ZIBs). However, their practical application is hindered by issues of dissolution, low electrical conductivity, and insufficient utilization of active sites. We report herein freestanding film cathodes for high-performance ZIBs with superior charge storage and heat management, wherein a meticulously designed bipolar redox molecule is assembled into a continuous three-dimensional conductive framework of MXene-bonded single-walled carbon nanotubes. The optimal cathode-based coin cells deliver the highest specific capacity of 406.6 mAh g–1 at 0.05 A g–1 and an initial capacity of 219.61 mAh g–1 at 10 A g–1 with extraordinary cycling stability over 60,000 cycles with an average capacity decay of only 2.5 × 10–4% per cycle. Further cycling test at 55 °C and 3 A g–1 reveals an initial capacity of 252.15 mAh g–1 with over 82.75% retention after 3000 cycles and ∼100% coulombic efficiency. Importantly, thermal conductivity and infrared thermal imaging were employed for clear elaboration of temperature evolution dynamics and thermal distribution under different electrode structures. Our work correlating the structure design and thermal management of electrodes provides insights for the rational design of high-performance ZIBs.

items.title:
Intracellular Polymerization-Induced
Self-Assembly
of Peptide Nanosheets for Inflammatory Breast Cancer Therapy
items.abstract: Abstract Inflammatory breast cancer (IBC) is a highly aggressive breast cancer subtype characterized by diffuse, biologically invasive growth and poorly defined tissue boundaries, resulting in a high mortality rate even after multimodal treatment. Here, we report an intracellular polymerization-induced self-assembly (PISA) strategy that constructs mechanically active peptide nanosheets. Upon 365 nm UV irradiation, the photoinitiator Irgacure 2959 (I2959) initiates intracellular PISA of HisMAm in IBC cells. The corresponding nanosheets prepared in vitro exhibit a thickness of ∼30 nm and a wet-state apparent Young’s modulus of 8.02 ± 0.43 MPa. These nanosheets act through two coordinated materials-cell interactions: (i) increasing cellular viscosity and spatially associating with the actin cytoskeleton, suppressing cell migration and invasion; and (ii) accumulating in the endoplasmic reticulum and eliciting paraptosis-like cell death. In a subcutaneous IBC xenograft model, localized fiber-assisted light activation achieves 72.2% tumor growth inhibition without overt systemic toxicity. Overall, this work establishes intracellular PISA as a spatiotemporally controlled materials strategy for localized IBC treatment.

items.title:
Turning
Insulators into Accelerators: Deciphering
the Interfacial Ionic Conductivity Boost in Composite Solid-State
Electrolytes through Machine Learning Molecular Dynamics Simulations
items.abstract: Abstract Halide solid-state electrolytes have emerged as promising candidates for all-solid-state lithium batteries due to their high oxidative stability and deformability, yet their moderate ionic conductivity remains a bottleneck. While incorporating ionically insulating ZrO2 nanoparticles has been experimentally shown to enhance the ionic conductivity of Li2ZrCl6, the atomistic origin governing this interfacial phenomenon remains unclear. Here, we bridge the spatiotemporal gap in modeling complex heterostructures by developing an accurate machine-learned force field based on the neuroevolution potential, enabling large-scale molecular dynamics simulations of ZrO2/Li2ZrCl6 heterostructures. By systematically investigating four representative low-lattice-mismatch ZrO2/Li2ZrCl6 interfaces, we identify spontaneous interfacial amorphization driven by space-charge effects upon surface cleavage, trapping Li+ and leading to under-coordinated Li+ polyhedra with pronounced geometric distortion. These distorted amorphous interfacial regions exhibit markedly enhanced Li+ hopping activity, significantly outperforming the bulk lattice, provided that the local mobile Li+ density is not depleted by surface charge redistribution. This work establishes a computational framework for training validated machine-learned force fields for interfaces and provides one plausible origin for the experimentally observed conductivity boost in the insulator-conductor composites, guiding the rational design of electrolytes toward next-generation solid-state batteries.

items.title:
Early Pathway Selection
Precedes Conformational Locking
in Protein Self-Assembly
items.abstract: Abstract When early intermediates begin to bias subsequent pathways during protein self-assembly remains difficult to resolve experimentally because early-stage processes are transient and poorly accessible. Here, using regenerated silk fibroin as a model system, we experimentally capture and analyze an early nucleation window in which assembly pathways begin to diverge before conformational locking occurs. By combining controlled electric-field perturbation with multiscale structural characterization and coarse-grained simulations, we identify reproducible nanoscale intermediates that mediate pathway selection. Within this window, electric fields bias early assembly kinetics in a nonmonotonic manner, modulating the formation, elongation, and competition of intermediates rather than directly enforcing structure or orientation. Time-resolved measurements show that subsequent growth proceeds primarily through elongation and fusion of existing intermediates, while β-sheet formation and crystallization emerge only at later stages and serve to stabilize pathways that were biased at earlier stages. Together, we locate the emergence of detectable pathway biasing within the nucleation stage and provide a framework for understanding and guiding protein self-assembly under nonequilibrium conditions.

items.title:
Cation-Intercalated
Mott Insulator α-RuCl3 Superlattice for Actively
Tuned Optoelectronics
items.abstract: Abstract Active tuning of the spectral response within sensing materials is critical for application-specific optoelectronics. However, current approaches typically suffer from limited tunability, complex architectures, or sacrificed stability. Here we report an on-chip cation intercalation strategy that transforms the Kitaev-candidate Mott insulator α-ruthenium chloride (α-RuCl3) into a tetramethylammonium (TMA+)-intercalated RuCl3 layered superlattice. The intercalation-induced reconstruction of the Mott-derived electronic states substantially narrows the optical gap from ∼1.1 eV to ∼0.6 eV, extending the spectral response into the short-wave infrared (SWIR) regime. The introduction of an in situ van der Waals tunneling barrier suppresses dark current by &gt;3 orders of magnitude and enhances specific detectivity by 4–6 orders of magnitude. By employing machine learning models, we demonstrate device-response-guided image processing for intelligent recognition under degraded environments. This work establishes a connection between correlated-electron systems and intelligent sensing, stimulating research directions at the intersection of quantum materials, optoelectronics, and intelligent sensing systems.

items.title:
Design of Water-Resistant,
Food-Grade Microneedles
for Fish Injection and Underwater Cargo Delivery
items.abstract: Abstract Aquatic foods provide around 15% of consumed animal-derived protein worldwide and aquaculture now supplies most of it. But the industry faces significant challenges in disease prevention and excessive use of antimicrobials. Vaccination, particularly for juvenile fish, can mitigate these risks, but manual and automated needle-based vaccination methods are costly, stressful, and labor-intensive. Here, a water-resistant, food-grade microneedle platform is designed to deliver cargos underwater. Silk fibroin-based microneedles are engineered to remain water resistant from minutes to hours in order to penetrate fish skin in wet conditions. To meet the requirements of different underwater applications, three microneedle morphologies─shell, solid-tip, and hollow─are developed, and their different combinations of mechanical integrity, water-resistance performance, cargo compatibility, and release kinetics are studied. The microneedles also preserve the supercoiled conformation of ⩾50% of the loaded pIHNVw-G plasmids─developed to protect fish against infectious hematopoietic necrosis virus─outside the cold chain for 4 weeks under dry conditions. In pilot animal studies, injected microneedles remain attached to zebrafish and juvenile rainbow trout while swimming. Using this food-based microneedle platform, we envision the development of tools for underwater vaccination of juvenile fish that increase aquaculture efficiencies and reduce environmental impact.

items.title:
Air-Stable Nickel
Oxide Nanosheets as a Model Platform
for Decoupling Structure–Activity Relation in Oxygen Evolving
Electrocatalysts
items.abstract: Abstract Nickel oxides are among the most active electrocatalysts for the alkaline oxygen evolution reaction (OER), a key process in green hydrogen production. However, the fundamental reaction mechanism remains unclear, limiting the rational design of electrocatalysts capable of reducing the cost of sustainable hydrogen generation. Herein, we develop an air-stable model electrocatalyst system of submonolayer nickel oxide (NiO) nanosheets with controlled coverages and morphologies on atomically flat Au(111), enabling atomic-scale investigation of structure–activity relationships under ambient conditions. Atomic force microscopy (AFM), scanning tunneling microscopy (STM) in ultrahigh vacuum (UHV), X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS), and electrochemical measurements were combined to correlate nanosheet structure and composition with electrocatalytic performance. We reveal OER activity scales with nanosheet edge density, identifying edge sites as the dominant active sites of the reaction. XPS measurements demonstrate the formation of nickel hydroxide on the nanosheet surfaces and edges following OER testing, consistent with the generation of a catalytically active nickel oxyhydroxide phase during operation. These findings provide insight into the structure–activity relationships governing NiO electrocatalysts and demonstrate a strategy for resolving atomic-scale structure–activity relationships without the need to maintain samples under UHV. We propose that future NiO-based OER electrocatalysts are designed to maximize the number density of accessible edge sites, hence maximizing the electrocatalytic activity.

items.title:
Photodoping-Driven
Lattice Expansion Enables Polarization
Enhancement in Sliding Ferroelectric MoS2
items.abstract: Abstract Light-matter interactions provide a powerful route to dynamically control ferroelectricity in low-dimensional materials, yet the microscopic mechanisms governing light-induced polarization remain elusive in sliding ferroelectrics. However, the influence of photodoped carriers on the macroscopic polarization and lattice responses remains largely unexplored. In this work, we employ first-principles calculations to demonstrate the microscopic origin of the photostrictive response in rhombohedral bilayer MoS2 under carrier photodoping. The system exhibits a characteristic lattice deformation, including in-plane expansion with the magnitude of 2% under a moderate photodoping density, collectively enhancing electronic hybridization. The coupling gives rise to a substantial interlayer contraction and an increase in out-of-plane spontaneous polarization, accompanied by a softening of the interlayer vibrational mode. These results demonstrate a microscopic, nonthermal pathway for modulating ferroelectric properties and underscore the potential of lattice-engineered polarization control in two-dimensional sliding ferroelectrics for advanced optoelectronic and information storage technologies.

items.title:
Human Urine–Derived
Induced Pluripotent Stem
Cell Membranes Enable Personalized Transdermal Nanotherapy for Melanoma
items.abstract: Abstract Melanoma treatment remains limited by drug resistance, immune-related adverse effects, and inadequate tumor-specific drug delivery. Nanoparticle (NP)-based delivery platforms have shown promise, but their clinical translation is hindered by rapid immune clearance and suboptimal biocompatibility. Current membrane-coating strategies often depend on invasive cell sources and lack patient-specific applicability. This study introduces a personalized melanoma therapy platform that integrates MnO2 NPs (MNPs) coated with urine-derived induced pluripotent stem cell (iPSC) membranes into a hydrogel-based transdermal patch. The patient-derived iPSC membrane enhances tumor targeting and immune evasion through the CXCR4/CXCL12 axis, while the MNPs facilitate pH-responsive release of cytotoxic drugs within the tumor microenvironment, maximizing therapeutic efficacy. The hydrogel transdermal patch enables direct, noninvasive delivery to skin lesions, promoting sustained drug exposure and potentially improving patient compliance. By combining autologous cell membrane coating, pH-responsive nanocarriers, and transdermal administration, this platform addresses key limitations of current melanoma therapies and supports the potential for clinical translation of personalized nanomedicine.

items.title:
Third-Eigenmode
Atomic Force Microscopy for Resolving
Solvation Structures and Structural Defects in Organic Semiconductor
Films under Ambient Conditions
items.abstract: Abstract Organic semiconductor molecules are key elements for the development of next-generation flexible and lightweight electronic devices. Their performance is largely governed by molecular arrangement within thin films, whereas environmental sensing is governed by surface functionality and mediated by the interfacial structure at the solid–gas interface. However, experimental tools capable of accessing such information with molecular-scale resolution remain scarce. Here, we employ third-eigenmode atomic force microscopy (AFM) with moderately compliant cantilevers to directly probe the interfacial solvation structure of the liquid layer formed at the interface between small-molecule organic semiconductor thin films and the ambient gas environment. This approach also enables true molecular-resolution imaging across molecular steps, providing detailed insight into interplanar molecular organization and crystal growth mechanisms. Overall, our results establish third-eigenmode AFM as a versatile methodology for high-resolution characterization of molecular packing and for elucidating the relationship between surface functionality and interfacial structure in organic semiconductor materials.

items.title:
X-ray
Crystallography of a Nanobody/JAM-1
Complex Informs Barrier Weakening and Enhanced Drug Permeability in
a Cellular Blood–Brain Barrier Model
items.abstract: Abstract For pharmacological treatments of brain disorders, the blood–brain barrier (BBB) poses a formidable obstacle, tightly restricting the cerebral uptake of therapeutic agents. Tight junction (TJ) binders, including peptides, proteins, and monoclonal antibodies, that specifically bind to the extracellular domains (ECDs) of TJ proteins are increasingly being explored as BBB-weakening agents for enhanced drug delivery to the brain. Given that nanobodies (Nbs) can access epitopes that are often inaccessible to conventional antibodies, we obtained 16 Nbs with unique CDRs via immunization of alpaca with the ECD of either human (h) or murine JAM-1 (mJAM-1), a major TJ protein. Twelve Nb candidates exhibited high-affinity binding to mJAM-1, as measured by surface plasmon resonance (SPR), and these interactions were further validated for 9 Nbs by immunostaining of JAM-1-overexpressing cells. Five Nbs were found to weaken the barrier of the eGFP-hCldn5-MDCKII cellular monolayer, as shown by reduced transendothelial electrical resistance (TEER). X-ray crystallography revealed that the lead barrier-weakening Nb, E6, binds to the membrane-proximal nondimeric D2 domain of mJAM-1. Mutating key residues at this interface eliminated the BBB-weakening effect of E6, as evidenced by unaltered sodium fluorescence (NaFI) leakage in both eGFP-hCldn5-MDCKII and mJAM1-mGL-MDCKII cellular monolayers compared with the nontreated control. Our study highlights the potential of JAM-1-targeting Nbs as BBB modulators, offering a promising approach for generating TJ binders to enhance brain drug delivery.

items.title:
One-Dimensional
Carbon Nanostructures with Periodic
Graphitic Nitrogen Substitution
items.abstract: Abstract Heteroatom substitution is a powerful route to tune the chemical and electronic properties of carbon nanomaterials. In particular, replacement of an sp2-hybridized carbon atom in the graphene lattice with a nitrogen atom (denoted as graphitic nitrogen) induces substantial changes in the electronic properties. These include changes in the band structure that can influence electronic transport and magnetism. A key requirement for applications is both the periodic and precise incorporation of the heteroatoms in extended carbon lattices. Here, we report the on-surface synthesis and characterization of two one-dimensional carbon nanostructures─a polymer and a graphene nanoribbon─consisting of periodically incorporated graphitic nitrogen atoms. The on-surface reactions toward the formation of the nanostructures were monitored by scanning tunneling microscopy. The bond-resolved chemical structures of the reaction intermediates and products were investigated by atomic force microscopy, which enabled atomic-scale visualization of the graphitic nitrogen sites. The electronic properties of the nanostructures were studied by scanning tunneling spectroscopy and density functional theory calculations. Our analyses revealed the presence of localized nitrogen-centered electronic states in the nanostructures. In the gas phase where the nanostructures are in the neutral charge state, these states undergo spin polarization leading to an open-shell ground state. Upon adsorption on Au(111), the nanostructures exhibit electron transfer to the surface, which resulted in a closed-shell ground state. Our results demonstrate a straightforward and generally applicable route to synthesize graphitic nitrogen-substituted carbon nanomaterials with potential applications in spintronics, catalysis, and energy storage.

items.title: Wafer-Scale p-type TeSeO x for Complementary Oxide Electronics
items.abstract: Abstract The absence of a scalable p-type oxide semiconductor remains a major limitation for complementary oxide electronics, in part because improving hole conduction in amorphous oxide networks often coincides with increased defect-mediated leakage. Here, we report an anneal-free, wafer-scale predominantly amorphous tellurium selenium oxide (TeSeOx) p-type oxide semiconductor that achieves a more favorable balance between leakage suppression and hole conduction. Spectroscopic analysis and first-principles calculations indicate that Se incorporation reconfigures the local coordination environment, weakens the strongly Te–Te-dominated connectivity of Te-rich networks, and retains spatially connected valence-band states consistent with the experimentally observed partial recovery of on-state conduction. Consequently, p-channel field-effect transistors fabricated across 4-in. wafers exhibit a final screened yield of 91.4%, a mean mobility of 4.52 cm2 ·V–1 ·s–1, and wafer-scale uniformity without postdeposition annealing of the TeSeOx channel. Temperature-dependent transport measurements further support leakage suppression in the engineered network, with an on/off ratio exceeding 109 at 77 K. As a device-level proof-of-concept relevant to three-dimensional integration, vertically configured TeSeOx PFETs and IGZO NFETs were assembled into complementary inverters and multi-input logic gates, demonstrating correct functionality under a low thermal budget. Collectively, these results support local coordination engineering as a viable route toward scalable amorphous p-type oxide semiconductors for thermally compatible complementary oxide electronics, with potential relevance to 3D integration.

items.title:
Sweeping
Surface Trap States under the Carpet: Cd2+ Inclusion in
InAs Quantum Dots
items.abstract: Abstract We have investigated the effect of CdCl2 as an additive in the colloidal synthesis of amino-As-based InAs quantum dots (QDs). Our results demonstrate that this metal halide promotes the incorporation of Cd into the InAs QDs, leading to the formation of In(Cd)As alloyed QDs featuring a narrower bandgap and enhanced photoluminescence (PL) compared to their undoped InAs counterparts. By varying the relative amount of CdCl2, it was possible to synthesize, in a one-pot process, QDs with PL tunable from ∼1000 to ∼1430 nm with a quantum yield as high as 17% at ∼1430 nm, without requiring any postsynthesis shell growth. These In(Cd)As QDs feature longer exciton lifetimes compared to InAs QDs, due to suppressed ultrafast nonradiative trap pathways, and a fast biexciton lifetime that follows the expected linear scaling with nanocrystal volume. Density functional theory (DFT) calculations revealed that (i) In(Cd)As alloys, which are thermodynamically unfavorable in the bulk phase, are stabilized by finite-size effects; (ii) the bandgap narrowing induced by Cd incorporation arises primarily from a pronounced upward shift of the valence band maximum (VBM); and (iii) this upward shift of the VBM also buries the surface trap states below the valence band edge, thereby accounting for the observed high PL efficiency in In(Cd)As QDs. Overall, this work provides mechanistic insights into defect passivation in InAs QDs and establishes metal-halide-mediated growth as an effective strategy for infrared emitting InAs-based QDs.

items.title:
Capturing the Hidden
Short-Range Order in Amorphous
Oxide Interfaces That Directs Quasi-Epitaxial Thin-Film Growth
items.abstract: Abstract As solid-state device architectures become increasingly complex, buried interfaces play a critical role in determining thin-film texture, morphology, and defect formation. However, resolving the structural features that control growth on nominally amorphous interlayers remains challenging because it requires three-dimensional sensitivity at high spatial resolution. Here, we combine four-dimensional scanning transmission electron microscopy, fluctuation electron microscopy, and multislice electron ptychography to investigate ruthenium (Ru) thin films grown on an underlying amorphous Ta2O5 layer, a material stack relevant for next-generation electronic and spintronic devices. Although the Ta2O5 layer appears amorphous in conventional imaging, diffraction and depth-resolved ptychographic reconstructions reveal nanoscale β-Ta2O5-like ordered motifs near the Ru/Ta2O5 interface. These locally ordered motifs, together with the interfacial morphology, guide the orientation of the Ru layer and produce a textured, quasi-epitaxial film. The curved and atomically rough interface further induces depth-dependent strain gradients and promotes planar defect formation within the Ru layer. Collectively, these results demonstrate that hidden short-range order within nominally amorphous oxides can direct the growth of metallic thin films, providing a framework for engineering buried interfaces in advanced electronic and spintronic material stacks.

items.title:
Pressure-Regulated
Confined Crystallization Drives
Self-Organization of Bioinspired Mineral Architectures
items.abstract: Abstract Nature employs amorphous precursors to construct inorganic biominerals with highly ordered patterns within spatially confined environments. However, bottom-up fabrication of bulk materials with well-organized patterns remains challenging. Here, we report a pressure-regulated strategy to fabricate inorganic monoliths featuring periodic motifs via consolidation of hydrated amorphous calcium carbonate (ACC) gels. The applied pressure governs both structural water retention and the degree of confinement, thereby tailoring crystallization kinetics. Confined crystallization induces shrinkage through coupled dehydration and phase transformation, generating contractile stresses within bulk monoliths. These stresses trigger surface buckling and drive the spontaneous formation of long-range concentric patterns. With increasing pressure, these periodic features further evolve into three-dimensional surface relief structures. Finite element analysis simulates this dynamic morphogenesis and supports a chemo-mechanical coupling mechanism. These findings provide a bottom-up route for constructing monoliths with complex morphologies and offer insights into biomineralization.

items.title:
Cooperative H2O–CO2 Regulation
Reinforces Transport and Interfacial Stability in Deep Eutectic Solvent
Electrolytes
items.abstract: Abstract Deep eutectic solvents (DESs), as representative hydrogen-bonded electrolytes, offer unique solvation environments, high CO2 affinity, and broad opportunities in sustainable fields. However, the high viscosity, sluggish diffusion, and the low-temperature solidification tendency of DESs severely impede their electrochemical performance. This work demonstrates an H2O–CO2 cooperative regulation strategy, in which water effectively lowers the viscosity and preserves fluidity of DESs even at −40 °C, while CO2 stabilizes the hydrated DES interfaces and expands the electrochemical window over a wide temperature range. Such interfaceial stabilization is achieved through a CO2-mediated interfacial molecular mechanism rather than a conventional surface passivation process. Combining electrochemical vibrational spectroscopy, atomic force microscopy, and molecular dynamics simulations, it elucidates that the CO2 lowers the population of electrochemically accessible water at the cathodic interface and reorganizes the local hydrogen-bond network in hydrated DESs, thereby suppressing the hydrogen evolution reaction while preserving the fluidity provided by hydration. This stabilized interface further benefits an increased CO2-to-CO reduction rate by approximately 1 order of magnitude. By resolving the persistent transport-stability trade-off in DES electrolytes, this H2O–CO2 cooperative regulation concept offers molecular insights into nanoscale interfacial hydrogen-bond engineering at viscous electrochemical interfaces and provides a general strategy for CO2 conversion, electrosynthesis, etc.

items.title:
Dopant-Enhanced
Polarization in ReS2 Field-Effect
Transistor
items.abstract: Abstract Optical polarization provides an additional degree of freedom for photonic communication, yet its electrical readout requires photodetectors with strong in-plane anisotropy. Here we identify Pt through first-principles screening as a candidate for enhancing the in-plane anisotropy of ReS2. Calculations for the proposed S-site substitution model predict directional orbital hybridization and anisotropic band reconstruction. ReS2 field-effect transistors with 0.93 at. % Pt exhibit polarization-dependent current anisotropic ratios up to 16, compared with 1.45 for pristine devices. Pt incorporation also reduces the contact resistance to 0.85 kΩ·μm, accompanied by lower thermionic and tunneling barriers. Device-calibrated proof-of-concept simulations demonstrate polarization-dependent image decoding, with the peak signal-to-noise ratio increasing from 12.2 to 37.3 dB as the number of states per RGB channel increases from 2 to 10. These findings provide a route toward compact and integrated polarization-sensitive optoelectronic devices.

items.title:
Sulfur-Induced Lattice
Disordering in Halide Electrolytes
Enables Superionic Sodium-Ion Conduction
items.abstract: Abstract Amorphous solid electrolytes provide a promising route to overcoming the ion-transport limitations of crystalline halide frameworks, yet achieving superionic Na+ conduction remains challenging. Herein, we report a mixed-anion amorphous Na-ion solid-state electrolyte, TaCl5-0.5Na2S (NTSC), synthesized via high-energy ball-milling, which exhibits an ultrahigh room-temperature ionic conductivity of 2.9 mS/cm and a low activation energy of 0.276 eV. Structural analyses reveal a highly disordered framework composed of Ta-centered bipolyhedra interconnected via corner-sharing sulfur atoms [Ta2Cl10S], [TaCl5S], [TaCl4S], and [TaCl4S2], evidenced by comprehensive characterizations, forming a flexible, disordered amorphous network. Ab initio molecular dynamics (AIMD) simulations identify continuous Na+-diffusion pathways with low migration barriers. Complementary topological analyses further indicate that sulfur incorporation leads to local lattice distortions, shortens Na–Na hopping distances, and enhances framework flexibility, collectively enabling fast, multidimensional Na+ transport. When applied in all-solid-state sodium-ion batteries (ASSNIBs), NTSC enables high reversible capacity (111.95 mAh/g with a Coulombic efficiency of 92.6% at 0.1 C) and excellent cycling stability (76.9% initial capacity retention after 200 cycles at 0.2 C) at room temperature. This work establishes mixed-anion amorphization as an effective design strategy for high-performance Na-ion solid electrolytes.

items.title:
Morphology-Tunable
Nanoparticles of Aspartic Acid
Paclitaxel Conjugates for Breast Cancer Treatment
items.abstract: Abstract The structural morphologies of nanomaterials serve as vital determinants in their biological interactions and efficacy in vivo. Achieving programmable control over the assembly morphology solely through molecular design remains challenging. Herein, a supramolecular strategy to control the assembly morphology of prodrugs for the orchestration of drug delivery in vivo is reported. A paclitaxel prodrug (PCA) was synthesized by conjugating aspartic acid with paclitaxel through a succinyl linker. PCA can spontaneously self-assemble into nanofibers. Incorporating the diacylphosphatidylethanolamine-PEG2k (DSPE-PEG2k) induces a morphological transition from fibers to rods and ultimately to spheres. Molecular dynamics simulations show that intermolecular hydrogen bonds fall from approximately 50 in DP1 NFs to fewer than 5 in DP3 NPs, and carboxyl-related atoms in aspartic acid account for 53.24% of the total hydrogen bonds, proving that the carboxyl-mediated hydrogen-bond network dominates anisotropic assembly. Although fibrous and spherical assemblies exhibit the fastest release rate and optimized cellular delivery of paclitaxel in vitro, respectively, the rod-shaped assemblies achieve an optimal combination of prolonged blood circulation, enhanced tumor accumulation, and facilitated cellular internalization, resulting in superior antitumor efficacy in vivo, compared to fibrous and spherical counterparts and Abraxane. This study elucidates how supramolecular interactions regulate the macroscopic morphology of prodrug assemblies at the molecular level, establishing a design paradigm for engineering anisotropic nanomedicines with tailored in vivo fate.

items.title:
Single-Atom-Mediated
Two-Dimensional Heterointerface
Stabilizing 1T-MoS2 for Durable Hydrogen Evolution
items.abstract: Abstract The metallic 1T phase of MoS2 provides basal-plane activity and high conductivity that are absent in the semiconducting 2H polymorph, making it attractive for applications in electrocatalysis and energy conversion. However, its intrinsic metastability readily drives relaxation to the 2H ground state, and previous attempts to stabilize 1T-MoS2 have yielded only transient domains or localized perturbations without durable phase retention. Here we show that confining Pt single-atoms (SAs) at the MoS2–graphene heterointerface promotes enhanced stabilization and improved retention of 1T-associated MoS2 signatures, while simultaneously stabilizing the SAs themselves. The interfacial Pt SAs act as atomic-scale anchors, simultaneously redistributing charge and reshaping local coordination to favor the metallic 1T-associated configuration of MoS2. Spectroscopic analyses confirm persistent 1T signatures, and ex situ characterization after operation verifies reliable retention of 1T-MoS2. Density functional theory calculations further corroborate these findings, demonstrating that Pt incorporation reverses the intrinsic phase preference and energetically favors the 1T configuration. Electrochemical measurements further demonstrate nearly unchanged hydrogen evolution activity after 30,000 cycles. Together, these results establish SA-mediated heterointerface engineering as a powerful route to stabilize metastable electronic phases and unlock the full potential of layered materials for energy and electronic technologies.

items.title:
Halide Exchange
Reactions in Large Halide Perovskite
Nanocrystals
items.abstract: Abstract We have studied halide exchange reactions in large colloidal nanocrystals of lead halide perovskites, with sizes (∼40–60 nm) that are intermediate between those of typical nanocrystals synthesized and studied by the community (5–10 nm) and those of microcrystals or thin films. This size regime still allows an investigation of the nanocrystals with techniques used for colloidal nanocrystals while enabling the observation of phenomena such as phase segregation, generation of planar defects, strain accumulation and relaxation, which are harder to identify in smaller nanocrystals, also given their high instability under the electron beam. We compare nanocubes with hollow nanocubes, and highlight how the presence of the hollow region can influence structural and morphological changes during the reactions. Notably, we report core–shell epitaxial CsPbI3/CsPbCl3 heterostructures by partial I– to Cl– exchange on CsPbI3 nanocrystals. Transient absorption spectroscopy provides evidence consistent with electronic coupling and exciton transfer between the Cl-rich shell and I-rich core in these heterostructures, evidenced by the accelerated bleach decay of the CsPbCl3 component and the delayed population of the CsPbI3 band edge.

items.title: Twist-Tunable Interlayer Excitons in Anisotropic ReS 2 /ReSe 2 Heterostructures
items.abstract: Abstract Interlayer excitons (IEs) in van der Waals heterostructures offer tunable excitonic states with long lifetimes and permanent dipole moments. Prior studies focused on isotropic 2H-phase transition metal dichalcogenides, where bright IE emission is confined near high-symmetry twist angles (0° and 60°), restricting tunability. Here, heterobilayers of monolayer ReS2 and ReSe2, both in the 1T′ phase, exhibit robust polarized IE emission near 1.2 eV across the full twist-angle range (1°–88°), reflecting a hybridization landscape governed by lattice anisotropy rather than valley alignment. The lowest-energy IE transition exhibits a nonmonotonic twist-angle dependence with a total modulation range of ∼60 meV, consistent with moiré-driven band renormalization and modulation of interlayer coupling revealed by first-principles calculations and low-frequency Raman spectroscopy, respectively. Overall IE energy tunability extends to ∼100 meV with multilayer ReS2 and excitation energy variation. These results establish ReS2/ReSe2 as a versatile infrared IE platform enabling polarization-resolved emitters and detectors beyond 2H-symmetry constraints.

items.title:
Structure-Affinity
Correlations and Separable Optical
Activity in Carbon Nanotube Protein Coronas
items.abstract: Abstract Biomolecular corona on nanoparticle surfaces enriches low-abundance proteins and compresses the dynamic range of the plasma proteome. Single-walled carbon nanotubes are particularly attractive because their surface chemistry is highly tunable, and their near-infrared fluorescence directly reports corona modulation. However, how surface chemistry shapes the corona and how the corona relates to the fluorescence response remain unclear. We profiled protein enrichment patterns and the resulting fluorescence in a library of 25 chemically modified carbon nanotubes by quantitative proteomics and near-infrared fluorescence spectroscopy. We found that polymer and quantum-defect chemistry orthogonally modulate corona composition, and protein flexibility and solvent exposure are the most significant factors of enrichment, consistent with dispersion-driven, contact-maximizing interactions. Proteomics and fluorescence correlation analyses indicate that enrichment and fluorescence response are partially decoupled. A subset of corona proteins stays optically silent, but where responses occur, enriched proteins respond at lower, physiologically relevant ranges than depleted ones. Our findings inform design principles for carbon nanomaterial-based sensors and biomarker discovery platforms.

items.title:
Proximity-Induced
Charge Transfer, Strain, and Possible
Magnetic Exchange in Graphene/CrSBr Heterostructure
items.abstract: Abstract Stacking van der Waals materials provides a powerful route to engineer emergent electronic and magnetic behaviors through proximity-driven interactions. The graphene/CrSBr heterostructure has emerged as a compelling platform in this frontier, exhibiting exotic macroscopic responses (including uniaxial surface-plasmon-polariton propagation and an unconventional quantum Hall effect) indicative of strong interfacial electronic and magnetic coupling. However, a microscopic electronic landscape governing these phenomena has remained elusive. Here, we provide a comprehensive spectroscopic characterization of the graphene/CrSBr interface using a combination of angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy (ARPES), low-energy electron microscopy (LEEM), and density functional theory. We resolve a massive redistribution of interfacial charge that concurrently hole-dopes graphene and populates the quasi-one-dimensional spin-polarized conduction band of CrSBr, leading to interfacial metallization. Furthermore, electronic structure of CrSBr exhibits strong momentum-dependent renormalization distinct from conventional charge doping, and theoretical modeling supported by Raman spectroscopy points to additional interfacial compressive strain. In addition, ARPES reveals a splitting-like feature in the graphene Dirac cone consistent with spin degeneracy lifting, providing possible evidence of magnetic proximity coupling. These findings provide crucial microscopic insight into the system’s optical and transport responses and establish graphene/CrSBr as a versatile platform for charge-transfer control, strain-driven band engineering, magnetic-proximity coupling, and directionally confined excitations for next-generation spintronic and nanophotonic devices.

items.title:
Colloidal Atomic
Layer Deposition on Plasmonic Metal
Oxide Nanocrystals
items.abstract: Abstract Colloidal atomic layer deposition (c-ALD) has emerged as a powerful technique for enhancing the functional properties of nanocrystals (NCs) while preserving their solution dispersibility. Previous studies have shown that the deposition of amorphous metal oxide shells via c-ALD can passivate surface states in NCs, resulting in improved stability, photoluminescence, conductivity, and energy transfer. However, its application to doped metal oxide NCs, such as tin-doped indium oxide (ITO), which exhibit surface depletion due to surface hydroxyls, remains unexplored. In this work, we implement a c-ALD strategy using ligand-modified precursors to grow amorphous Al2O3, TiO2, and Ga2O3 shells on ITO NCs. We reveal how these coatings influence the plasmonic response and mitigate surface depletion, which we ascribe to surface state passivation. Energy-dependent X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) reveals a reduction in band bending, indicating a modification of the near-surface electronic structure. Furthermore, we demonstrate that control over shell thickness enables tunability of the collective plasmonic resonances in assembled ITO NC superlattices. This work expands the scope of c-ALD and establishes a versatile approach for tailoring the optoelectronic properties of doped metal oxide NCs in solution-processable systems.

items.title:
Carrier-Induced
and Coherent-Phonon-Controlled Band
Renormalization in Quasi-One-Dimensional α-Bi4Br4
items.abstract: Abstract Directional control of band structures at ultrafast time scales is a key requirement for nanoscale optoelectronics. Here, we realize cooperative band engineering in the quasi-one-dimensional (quasi-1D) van der Waals topological insulator α-Bi4Br4 through joint carrier-phonon band renormalization. Femtosecond excitation drives quasi-1D carrier accumulation, generating a strongly nonlinear many-body band renormalization that redshifts an optical transition by up to ∼25 meV, with &gt;90% polarization anisotropy. Superimposed Ag coherent phonons further modulate the same transition by ∼1 meV on intrinsic lattice time scales. By implementing phase-controlled dual-pump excitation, we achieve deterministic and reversible positioning of the renormalized band edge with ∼100 μeV precision within a ∼1.5 meV tuning window. First-principles calculations with charge-neutral photoexcitation constraints qualitatively reproduce the carrier-induced narrowing of the relevant interband transition, while phonon-mode analysis reveals that coherent Ag phonons modulate the same transition through interchain hopping and orbital polarization. These results establish cooperative carrier-phonon band renormalization as a scalable, all-optical mechanism for ultrafast, polarization-sensitive band engineering in quasi-1D van der Waals nanomaterials, enabling dynamically reconfigurable optoelectronic functionality.

items.title:
Highly Emissive
NIR-II Unimolecular Micelles via a
Core–Cap Synthetic Strategy for Deep-Tissue Imaging and Image-Guided
Surgery
items.abstract: Abstract High-performance fluorescence imaging in the second near-infrared (NIR-II, 1000–1700 nm) window holds promise for deep-tissue optical diagnostics. However, simultaneously achieving high fluorescence quantum yields (QYs) and ultrasmall dimensions in physiological aqueous environments remains a fundamental challenge. Here, we report a de novo core–cap synthetic strategy to construct highly emissive, renal-clearable NIR-II fluorophores based on a unimolecular micelle architecture. By integrating a rigid, donor–acceptor–donor (D–A–D) hydrophobic core containing orthogonal axial and lateral steric shielding networks with a hydrophilic polyethylene glycol (PEG) outer cap, we successfully suppress water-induced nonradiative decay and intermolecular aggregation-induced quenching without compromising lateral conjugation. Molecular dynamics simulations and experimental characterizations reveal that these amphiphilic structures self-assemble into highly monodisperse unimolecular micelles featuring an ultrasmall hydrodynamic diameter of ∼5 nm. The optimized fluorophore exhibits a peak NIR-II emission centered at 1034 nm with a high aqueous QY of 4.6%. Owing to their sub-5 nm dimensions, unimolecular micelles undergo dual renal and hepatic clearance pathways, circumventing the biosafety concerns of prolonged tissue retention typical of conventional nanoparticles. Capitalizing on their high brightness, we demonstrate high-resolution, contrast-enhanced in vivo imaging of systemic and cerebral vasculatures, allowing the quantitative morphometric visualization of structural abnormalities in transgenic brain tumors. Furthermore, these fluorophores enable high-contrast, intraoperative fluorescence-guided tumor resection with clearly defined margins. This work provides a promising strategy for the rational design of bright, fast-clearing organic NIR-II probes for advanced biomedical diagnostics.

items.title:
NanoBlocks: Creating
Genetically Encoded Protein Switches
Using Competitive Binding
items.abstract: Abstract Many regulatory mechanisms function by changing a molecule’s conformation such that it is switched between active and inactive states. Engineering macromolecules such as proteins to show robust conformational changes in response to arbitrary, well-defined molecular stimuli is of great interest in fields such as synthetic biology and nanoscale engineering, because it allows the development of “smart” molecular tools. We present a strategy that can convert “simple” affinity binders such as nanobodies into protein switches that undergo clear structural rearrangements in response to their innate targets, by introducing a peptide that competes for the binding site. We demonstrate proof-of-concept implementations of this “NanoBlock” design by developing genetically encoded fluorescent biosensors based on two entirely different binder frameworks, the ALFA nanobody and the PDZ domain of Erbin. We show that our design allows the construction of well-performing protein switches that can reliably detect their targets in vitro, in mammalian cells, as part of fluorescence-activated cell sorting (FACS) experiments, and that also generalizes to the creation of stimulus-responsive enzymes via the integration of a bioluminescent readout. We furthermore develop a theoretical model that rationalizes the observations and provides insight into the underlying molecular mechanisms. Overall, our strategy expands the possibilities to create “smart” protein-based molecules and effectors.

items.title:
Manganese
Dioxide Nanozyme-Integrated Aligned Nanofibers
Promote Diabetic Wound Repair through Growth Arrest-Specific Protein
6-Mediated Fibroblast-to-Macrophage Communication
items.abstract: Abstract Chronic diabetic wounds remain difficult to treat because excessive reactive oxygen species (ROS), persistent inflammation, and impaired neovascularization collectively hinder tissue repair. Here, we present a bioinspired aligned electrospun nanofiber membrane composed of methacrylated gelatin and o-nitrobenzyl-modified gelatin and functionalized with manganese dioxide (MnO2) nanozymes to regulate the wound microenvironment. Upon hydration and brief ultraviolet irradiation, the membrane forms a conformable nanofibrous hydrogel that closely adapts to irregular wound beds. Among three MnO2 loadings, the formulation containing 180 μg/mL MnO2 was selected as the optimized formulation because it attenuated intracellular ROS while promoting fibroblast proliferation and migration and endothelial angiogenic activity. Mechanistic studies showed that the optimized hydrogel promoted fibroblast secretion of growth arrest-specific protein 6 (Gas6), which attenuated inflammatory macrophage responses and enhanced reparative macrophage responses. Gas6 knockdown weakened these effects, whereas recombinant Gas6 recapitulated them. Single-cell RNA sequencing identified treatment-associated changes in wound cell states and suggested Gas6-associated fibroblast-macrophage communication through computational ligand-receptor analysis. In streptozotocin-induced diabetic mice, the optimized hydrogel accelerated wound closure and enhanced vascularization, re-epithelialization, and collagen remodeling. These findings establish an aligned nanozyme-functionalized nanofibrous hydrogel that links redox regulation to Gas6-associated fibroblast-to-macrophage signaling for diabetic wound repair.

items.title:
Self-Healing Magnetic
Materials for Next-Generation
Soft Electronics and Robotics
items.abstract: Abstract Bioinspired magnetic soft materials and devices have been widely developed for human–machine interaction, robotic technologies, wearable electronics, and energy harvesting. However, accidental damage and environmental changes often limit their operational durability, giving rise to the need for frequent replacements. To address this issue, this Review emphasizes the importance and advantages of integrating self-healing capabilities into flexible magnetic devices. We comparatively analyze five core healing mechanisms of the existing self-healing magnetic materials. Subsequently, their design strategies and key properties are outlined according to the major polymer matrices (gels, elastomers, and other polymeric networks). We also discuss the structure–property trade-offs across particle-filled and particle-free material systems, as well as their potential applications in sensing, robotics, energy storage/conversion, and implantable biomedicine. Despite these advances, critical challenges still remain for current self-healing magnetic soft materials and devices in terms of the trade-off between magnetic performance and self-healing capability, durability under extreme environments, long-term sustainability, and commercialization applications. Finally, this Review summarizes these challenges and presents future perspectives of such materials and devices for the fields of intelligent soft electronics and robotics.

items.title:
Degraded Reversibility
in Modulated Martensite Driven
by Kinetic Arrest
items.abstract: Abstract Achieving complete reversibility in martensite–austenite phase transitions is challenging due to structural degradation during thermal cycling, yet the atomistic pathways driving this degradation remain unresolved. Using in situ atomic-resolution scanning transmission electron microscopy on a Ni2MnGa shape-memory alloy, we reveal that although structural modulation forms through phonon softening to relieve mismatch strain between martensite and austenite, it significantly compromises reversibility. While the global lattice shear in nonmodulated martensite is reversible, the localized atomic shuffles in the modulated structure do not reverse collectively. Instead, they follow locally divergent pathways that create a kinetically arrested austenite state. Upon cooling, this arrested state triggers irregular atomic shuffling and residual defects that produce thermal hysteresis and functional fatigue. Linking this degradation to the multidirectional energy landscape of atomic shuffling provides a framework for understanding kinetic trapping and reversibility in complex materials.

items.title:
Electron Microscopy
Identifies Protein Conformational
Substates in Liquid Environment
items.abstract: Abstract Protein functions are closely linked to their dynamic behaviors, particularly involving low-abundance transient states. Quantifying these interconversions remains experimentally challenging, especially for proteins containing intrinsically disordered regions (IDRs). In this study, we utilize low-dose electron microscopy using graphene liquid cells to image and quantify interconversions between protein conformational states under optimized electron beam conditions and confinement effects. Applied to four proteins in solution: CRISPR-associated protein (Cas9), DNA binding protein (GapR), restriction enzyme (EcoRI), and an RNA binding protein with IDRs (FUS), we visualized low-abundance transient structures distinct from crystalline forms and elucidated transition pathways which are validated by cryo-electron microscopy, revealing differences in their energy landscapes through single-molecule imaging. We analyzed domain-scale rearrangements at ∼1–2 nm effective conformational resolution, cross-validated against independent computational and experimental methods. Shifts in state equilibria and conformational adaptations were observed when proteins are mutated or during biomolecular interactions, such as target searching, binding, and cleavage with nucleic acids. Notably, changes in the energy landscape were observed when proteins with IDRs and RNA were within close proximity but not in apparent contact, suggesting that conformational redistribution may precede complete binding. This study shows how to characterize protein conformations and their time-dependent changes using instrumentation that is widely available at research universities but not yet used for these purposes.

items.title: Issue Editorial Masthead
Issue Publication Information

Exceptionally Matched
p-SiNW/n-IGZO Complementary
Field-Effect Transistors for Monolithic 3D Logic
items.abstract: Abstract Monolithic three-dimensional (M3D) complementary field-effect transistors (CFETs) provide a route toward a higher logic density by vertically stacking complementary devices within the same footprint. Their realization through heterogeneous integration requires p- and n-channel transistors that are both individually high-performing and electrically matched. Here, we demonstrate high-performance heterogeneous Si/oxide M3D CFETs by vertically integrating p-type silicon nanowire (p-SiNW) FETs with n-type indium gallium zinc oxide (n-IGZO) transistors. The site-controlled p-SiNWs are formed through a scalable in-plane solid–liquid–solid (IPSLS) process without postgrowth hydrogen passivation, facilitating subsequent oxide–semiconductor integration. The vertically integrated p- and n-channel devices exhibit closely matched current-driving capabilities, near-zero threshold voltages, and subthreshold swings of 120 and 133 mV dec–1, respectively. This exceptional p/n matching enables sharp and well-balanced switching, yielding a peak voltage gain of 103 V/V at VDD = 5 V, a normalized gain of 20.6 V–1, and large, nearly symmetric noise margins (NML = 0.45 VDD and NMH = 0.44 VDD). The architecture is further extended to NOR, NAND, and OR gates with experimentally verified logic operations. These results establish a high-performance heterogeneous Si/oxide integration platform for dense and robust M3D complementary logic.

items.title:
Polymer-Derived
Tantalum Carbide Ceramic Aerogel Monoliths
for Ultrahigh-Temperature Thermal Insulation up to 2000 °C
items.abstract: Abstract Ceramic aerogels are ideal thermal insulating materials in the aerospace field because of their low density and low thermal conductivity but are plagued by the limited operating temperature due to the inherently poor high-temperature resistance. In this work, the tantalum carbide (TaC) ceramic aerogel monolith with outstanding ultrahigh temperature stability was successfully prepared through the polymer precursor conversion method combined with the sol–gel technique. Benefiting from the pyrolysis process of the polymer precursor aerogel, the TaC aerogel monoliths with the pearl necklace-like structure were obtained at a low temperature of 1500 °C. The as-prepared TaC aerogels exhibit a low density (0.46–0.63 g/cm3), high Brunauer–Emmett–Teller (BET) specific surface area (95.15–148.17 m2/g), low thermal conductivity (0.046–0.058 W·m–1·K–1), and a good compressive strength (0.043–0.297 MPa). Most importantly, after heat treatment up to 2000 °C under vacuum, the pearl necklace-like structure of the TaC aerogel is well preserved, and the thermal conductivity remains at a low level of 0.059 W·m–1·K–1, indicating the excellent ultrahigh-temperature stability of TaC aerogels. The excellent thermal insulating performance and ultrahigh-temperature stability make the TaC aerogel an attractive material for thermal insulation in extreme conditions.

items.title:
Molecular Crowding
Programs Trifluoroacetate-Solvation
Nanoclusters for Stable Aqueous Zinc Metal Chemistry
items.abstract: Abstract Aqueous zinc metal batteries offer a safe and cost-effective platform for electrochemical energy storage, yet their practical operation remains limited by water-driven parasitic reactions and spatially heterogeneous Zn deposition. Here, we report a molecule-crowding strategy that programs zinc/sodium trifluoroacetate (Zn(TFA)2/NaTFA) aqueous electrolytes into an anion-rich nanoclustered solvation environment. The balanced affinity of TFA– toward Zn2+ and H2O promotes Zn2+–TFA– association and drives the evolution from water-rich local coordination toward abundant contact ion pairs, ion aggregates, and interconnected multi-ion nanoclusters. Spectroscopic characterization, X-ray scattering, and molecular dynamics simulations collectively reveal reconstructed Zn2+ coordination, extended ion-associated correlations, and reorganization of the water hydrogen-bonding environment, accompanied by reduced water activity. The nanocluster electrolyte suppresses hydrogen evolution and Zn corrosion and promotes more uniform Zn deposition. The optimized nanocluster electrolyte sustains Zn||Zn cycling for over 2100 h, enables Zn||Cu cells to operate for more than 3000 h with an average Coulombic efficiency of 99.4%, and affords Zn||Na2V6O16·3H2O full cells with 82.4% capacity retention after 30,000 cycles at 10 A g–1. These results show that balanced anion interactions and molecular crowding regulate ion association and the water hydrogen-bonding environment, contributing to improved Zn reversibility and cycling stability.

items.title:
Topology-Programmed
Peptide Architectures Orchestrate
Durable Tumor Targeting and Cascade Antitumor Immunity
items.abstract: Abstract Peptide supramolecular systems offer recognition and biocompatibility for precision theranostics, yet their in vivo performance is limited by insufficient structural stability, poor retention, and loss of accessible recognition interfaces under physiological perturbations. Herein, a topology-programmed supramolecular assembly strategy was developed to stabilize adaptive peptide architectures through confinement-guided organization. A β-sheet-based peptide EH, with PD-L1 (programmed death-ligand 1) targeting, favorable assembly behavior, and hydrophobic anchoring potential, was screened from an amphiphilic peptide library and integrated with immunoactivating SeAD quantum dots into PLGA (poly(lactic-co-glycolic acid)) microspheres featuring an interconnected hydrophobic channel network. This network guides channel-confined EH assembly through hydrophobic anchoring and β-sheet reinforcement, enabling ordered nanofiber alignment while preserving local conformational flexibility and exposed recognition motifs.
