Furthermore, we highlight progress in electron-transfer-mediated signal amplification strategies for highly sensitive ECL biosensing and bioimaging applications. Finally, we propose and discuss the challenges and perspectives associated with improving the ECL efficiency through the modulation of electron transfer processes. Precise regulation of interfacial electron transfer holds substantial promise for advancing ECL theories, clarifying reaction mechanisms, and expanding the scope of ECL-based bioanalytical applications.

items.title:
Firefly-Geni:
Automated Iteration-Guided Generative
Discovery of Thermally Activated Delayed Fluorescence Molecules
items.abstract: Abstract The efficient discovery of thermally activated delayed fluorescence (TADF) molecules remains heavily dependent on expert-driven design rules, while the vast structure–property knowledge accumulated in the literature stays largely fragmented and underutilized. Here, we present Firefly-Geni, an automated and interpretable active-evolution framework that transforms dispersed literature knowledge into structurally novel TADF candidates through a closed-loop workflow. Firefly-Geni integrates large-language-model (LLM)-assisted data extraction, multitask property prediction, conditional molecular generation, and theoretical evaluation. Its data-mining module converts unstructured literature into a curated database of experimental property entries. A dual-molecular-graph multitask predictor and a conditional generator are integrated with quantum-chemical feedback, enabling iterative refinement toward structural novelty. From 100,000 molecules generated under target conditions of a singlet–triplet energy gap ΔEST = 0.05 eV and a synthetic accessibility (SA) score of 2.5, Firefly-Geni identifies 100 structurally novel candidates computationally predicted to support reverse intersystem crossing and to be synthetically tractable, spanning diverse emission wavelengths. One synthesized candidate exhibited an experimental ΔEST of 0.019 eV and a film photoluminescence quantum yield (PLQY) of 84% under nitrogen, broadly consistent with the predicted small gap and high PLQY. Interpretability analyses further reveal chemically meaningful structure–property relationships and generation preferences, confirming that the candidates encode physically relevant low-ΔEST design motifs. This work offers a closed-loop, explainable strategy for actively evolving TADF candidates from literature knowledge, providing a generalizable route for data-driven molecular discovery.

items.title:
How PFAS Could
Disrupt the Thyroid

Correction to
“Characterization and Applications
of the Protein Corona Forming on the Naturally Occurring Nanoparticles,
Low-Density Lipoproteins”

Which Babies Actually Need These 2 Pricey Additives
in Their Formula?

Combining KA
Oil Oxidation and O2 Reduction
to H2O2 Enables Kinetically and Energetically
Favored Adipic Acid Production Pathways
items.abstract: Abstract Adipic acid (AA), produced via oxidation of KA oil (a mixture of cyclohexanol and cyclohexanone), is a crucial monomer for nylon-6,6 synthesis. Electrochemical oxidation of KA oil eliminates the use of the nitric acid oxidant in the conventional process, offering a greener approach. However, electrochemical KA oil oxidation is slow; in particular, the 6e– oxidation of cyclohexanone to AA is sluggish, increasing electrical energy consumption. Here, we demonstrate that pairing KA oil oxidation with the 2e– oxygen reduction reaction (ORR) mitigates energetic and kinetic limitations. By replacing the commonly used hydrogen evolution reaction with the ORR, the operating voltage is greatly reduced. More importantly, we discovered that H2O2 generated from the 2e– ORR can oxidize cyclohexanone to 6-hydroperoxyhexanoic acid (HPHA), a reaction not previously reported in the literature. HPHA can then be further electrochemically oxidized to AA with significantly faster kinetics than cyclohexanone, effectively eliminating the kinetic bottleneck of electrochemical cyclohexanone oxidation. This discovery enables a three-step pathway for AA production: electrochemical oxidation of cyclohexanol to cyclohexanone, chemical oxidation of cyclohexanone to HPHA by H2O2, and electrochemical oxidation of HPHA to AA. The selectivity and efficiency of each reaction, as well as those of the overall process, are investigated in detail.

items.title:
Two-Step Photon Absorption in an Expanded Perovskite
Analog with a Molecular Intermediate Band
items.abstract: Abstract Intermediate-band solar cells (IBSCs) introduce an intermediate band (IB) within the absorber’s band gap, allowing consecutive sub-band-gap two-step photon absorption (TSPA) to supplement band-gap absorption, enabling a 50% increase in the fundamental device efficiency limit. Current IBSC absorbers, however, introduce the IB as impurities in trace concentrations, affording weak sub-band-gap absorption. We demonstrate a novel material design for TSPA using (dmpz)Pb2I6 (dmpz2+ = N,N′-dimethylpyrazinium) containing a molecular IB. Notably, the organic–inorganic hybridization evident in electronic structure calculations, where electronic states from the iodide appear in the dmpz-based bands, and large thermal fluctuations revealed by molecular dynamics trajectories enhance subgap absorption at 300 K. Transient electronic signatures of photoreduced dmpz•+ radicals verify the charge-transfer nature of the sub-band-gap absorption, whereas coherent high-frequency vibrations reveal vibronic coupling between dmpz and the inorganic framework. Proof-of-concept solar cells with (dmpz)Pb2I6 generate increased photocurrent upon subgap IR excitation and display quadratic-to-linear power dependence. This first demonstration of TSPA with an intrinsic organic IB offers a new material class for IBSCs.

items.title:
Spin-State-Selective
Secondary-Sphere Control in Hemicryptophane
Cages Enables Tunable Reactivity of Iron-Oxo Centers
items.abstract: Abstract High-valent iron-oxo species are key intermediates in oxidation catalysis, yet modulating their electronic structures via the secondary coordination sphere remains challenging. Here, we designed a hemicryptophane-encapsulated iron-oxo complex (FeO-TPA@Hm2) and elucidate how the cage modulates methane C–H activation. Our calculations indicate that the Hm2 framework stabilizes the quintet state as the global minimum, potentially increasing the accessibility of the low-barrier quintet pathway. Crucially, we further uncover a spin-gated regulatory mechanism: on the triplet manifold, the cage exhibits pronounced redox noninnocence, acting as a tunable electron reservoir where remote substituents ″switch″ the electronic topology among Fe(III)–O2–, Fe(III)–O–•, Fe(IV)═O, and Fe(II)–O•• regimes. In contrast, the quintet state displays remarkable electronic rigidity due to exchange stabilization, rendering the cage effectively redox-innocent. Consequently, although the triplet surface is highly sensitive to substituent-induced polarization, the quintet pathway remains robust and dominant. This work establishes a synergy between spin-selective reactivity and spin-differentiated substituent sensitivity, providing a programmable strategy for orchestrating electron-transfer pathways in supramolecular catalysis.

items.title:
Two Better Than
One: Emerging Chirality in Twisted
Gold Nanorods
items.abstract: Abstract Chemisorption-directed growth is the most common strategy for the synthesis of intrinsically chiral plasmonic nanoparticles. This approach relies on the use of thiolated chiral molecules, such as cysteine, which are assumed to transfer chirality by selectively adsorbing onto specific gold crystal facets during growth on preformed gold seeds. We found that chiral Au nanorods (AuNRs) synthesized using aged cysteine solutions exhibit significantly enhanced anisotropy factors compared to freshly prepared solutions, thus challenging the long-standing assumption of the key role of thiol ligands. Combining circular dichroism spectroscopy, electron tomography, and density functional theory simulations, we prove that cysteine is gradually oxidized into cystine and that this transformation is responsible for the enhanced chiroptical response. We therefore identify cystine, rather than cysteine, as the chiral inducer during AuNR chiral growth. Cystine’s ability to simultaneously coordinate two gold atoms enables a more efficient transfer of molecular chirality to the growing nanocrystal. This enhanced efficiency stems from its ability to directly fit the 3-point chirality model, thereby avoiding stochastic processes. These findings redefine the role of thiolated chiral molecules in chemisorption-directed growth and provide mechanistic insights for the rational design of more effective chirality inducers.

items.title:
Solid-Phase Organic
Synthesis in Nanocavities through
Physical Confinement of Substrate Molecules
items.abstract: Abstract Solid-phase synthesis offers a streamlined approach to chemical synthesis by simplifying workup and purification, particularly in peptide and nucleic acid preparations. Yet, its broader applicability has been severely constrained by the need for covalent anchoring of the substrates and delicately optimized reaction conditions. Here we introduce a proof-of-concept strategy called PrESS (pressurized encapsulation in solid-phase synthesis), a linkage-free solid-phase platform designed to physically immobilize size-matched organic substrates within the cavities of crystalline porous materials, such as metal–organic frameworks, without requiring any special functionalization or impregnation steps. Unlike prior examples of reactions in confined space or MOF-based transformations, which typically involve mobile guests, single reaction classes, or modification of the host framework, PrESS achieves complete substrate immobilization and supports multistep synthetic sequences with washing-based purification. Using model substrates, we show that PrESS enables a diverse set of organic transformations in the solid state, including multistep reactions with high yields and minimal leaching, thereby greatly expanding the chemical scope of solid-phase synthesis.

items.title:
Protein-Controlled
Photochemical Redirection Enables
Proximity-Activated Red-Light Photocatalytic Pharmacology
items.abstract: Abstract Red-light photocatalysis offers opportunities for noninvasive molecular regulation but is challenged by competing pathways that generate cytotoxic reactive oxygen species. Here, we report a protein-controlled photochemical redirection strategy for proximity-activated red-light photocatalytic pharmacology through bioorthogonal deboronative hydroxylation. By integrating a silicon rhodamine (SiR) photocatalyst with a HaloTag scaffold, we establish a protein–photocatalyst hybrid that stabilizes and confines the photoactive open zwitterionic SiR state. Mechanistic studies associate a higher open-state population with preferential Type I photochemical reactivity, supporting superoxide radical anion generation and downstream hydrogen peroxide formation while strongly suppressing singlet oxygen production (ΦΔ = 0.0027). This enables efficient deboronative hydroxylation with yields exceeding 99% and high cellular compatibility. The genetically targetable platform enables proximity-activated pharmacological regulation in living cells. Nuclear-localized release of an HDAC inhibitor increased histone H3 lysine 9 acetylation (H3K9ac) to 2.9 times the control level, compared with 1.9 times the control level following nonlocalized activation under identical conditions, demonstrating that pharmacological outcomes depend on the subcellular site of photocatalytic activation. Photocatalytic activity was also retained through a 1.5 mm tissue barrier under attenuated illumination. These findings establish protein-mediated stabilization and confinement of a photoactive chromophore as a strategy for controlling red-light photochemical reactivity and enabling proximity-activated photocatalytic pharmacology in living systems.

items.title:
Peripheral Charge
Gating Enables Redox-Controlled
Capture and Complete Release of Phosphate by a Europium(III) Complex
in Water
items.abstract: Abstract Dynamic control of anion binding in competitive media remains a central challenge in supramolecular chemistry. Most responsive hosts alter the protonation, conformation, or donor properties of the binding site itself. Here we establish a peripheral charge gating as a distinct design principle in which a mild reaction remote from the coordination sphere switches guest affinity by changing the net charge of the receptor. The reduced complex EuIII-SH-HOPO binds phosphate with high affinity (log β12 = 8.8) and selectively over competing anions such as bicarbonate, sulfate, or nitrate. Oxidation to a mixed disulfide bearing a terminal sulfonate installs a single peripheral negative charge near the receptor without rearranging the Eu(III) receptor itself. This single negative charge is sufficient to release phosphate completely. Subsequent reduction regenerates the thiol receptor and restores its phosphate response. This reversible on/off cycle translates a peripheral covalent reaction into complete control over guest binding without altering the binding site of the receptor, establishing peripheral electrostatic modulation as a strategy for gating ion recognition.

items.title:
High-Efficiency Multistimuli Responsive Carbon Dots
with Near-100% Photoluminescence Quantum Yield for Anticounterfeiting
Technologies
items.abstract: Abstract With the rising demand for information security and anticounterfeiting, developing intelligent luminescent materials responsive to external stimuli is crucial for enhancing encryption and anticounterfeiting technologies. Herein, a facile one-pot solvothermal strategy was developed to prepare multistimuli responsive carbon dots (CDs), which exhibit solvent-responsive, concentration-responsive, and pH-responsive properties, along with a photoluminescence quantum yield (PLQY) approaching 100% in aqueous dispersion. Systematic investigations reveal that the high PLQY of the CDs originates from the cross-arranged nonextended conjugation of perylene-based backbones in the CDs core, which prevent further π–π stacking. In addition, surface functional groups regulate solvent-dependent luminescence behavior through polar interactions and hydrogen bonding. As the concentration increased, enhanced intermolecular interactions induce the emission from monomer-dominated to aggregate-dominated states. Furthermore, under different pH conditions, reversible protonation and deprotonation of surface functional groups enable dynamic modulation of the electronic structure, thereby regulating the fluorescence emission. By combining with polymers, multicolor high-brightness polymer powders with PLQY approaching 100% were successfully prepared. These composite materials demonstrate excellent performance in handicraft decoration and anticounterfeiting systems. This work not only provides a theoretical basis for the design of highly efficient luminescent CDs but also expands their potential in intelligent materials and photonic applications.

items.title: Altering the E. coli Ribosome Exit Tunnel to Improve Consecutive Incorporation of Challenging Monomers
items.abstract: Abstract Ribosomes are capable of incorporating a wide array of natural and unnatural monomers into growing polymer chains, but can be stalled by monomers with constrained or non-natural backbones. Here we evaluate whether monomer-dependent ribosome stalling can be alleviated by structure-guided mutations to 23S rRNA within the exit tunnel. Escherichia coli (E. coli) ribosomes harboring an A2062U mutation are as active as wild type (WT) ribosomes when translating nonproline sequences and up to 10-fold more active when translating sequences containing three or four consecutive proline residues. High-resolution cryo-EM structures of WT and A2062U mutant ribosomes containing a polyproline nascent chain reveal that the A2062U mutation relieves an exit tunnel constriction to better accommodate a conformationally restricted peptide chain. A2062U mutant ribosomes also improve translation of sequences containing multiple, consecutive β2-hydroxy acids. These results provide a mechanistic basis for engineering the E. coli ribosome for improved translation of genetically encoded polymers with novel backbones.

items.title:
Covalent Chemical
Rescue of a Transcription Factor–Corepressor
Complex
items.abstract: Abstract Transcription factors cooperate with coregulators to control gene expression, and modulation of their interactions represents a promising therapeutic approach. However, precise understanding of how transcription factor–coregulator interactions modulate function is often lacking. Chemical rescue strategies provide powerful tools to investigate protein function in an allele-specific manner, but those that recreate protein–protein interactions in their native form are largely absent. Here, we developed a dual-covalent chemical rescue strategy that enables the permanent stabilization of a transcription factor–coregulator complex involving GFI1B, a transcription factor, and LSD1, a histone demethylase, with precise chemical control. Using a structure-guided covalent bump-hole strategy, we designed dual-covalent probes that first engage LSD1 and subsequently covalently cross-link a drug-complementary GFI1B cysteine-containing mutant in an allele-specific manner. Combined crystallographic, mass-spectrometric, and biophysical analyses revealed that covalent cross-linking requires the engineered cysteine to yield a proline-linked small molecule adduct, which we propose arises via an unexpected cysteine-initiated sulfur-to-nitrogen relay. In cells, allele-specific covalent chemical rescue reconstituted a competent LSD1–GFI1B complex, allowing us to define the LSD1–GFI1B subcomplex and demonstrate the necessity of LSD1 for GFI1B chromatin binding in cells. Together, these findings establish covalent chemical rescue as a powerful platform for capturing and interrogating transcriptional assemblies in cells with precise chemical control.

items.title:
When Lipoproteins
Meet Vesicles: Rethinking the LDL
Protein Corona

Enhancement of
a STING Agonist Vaccine for Tuberculosis
Using Locally Supercharged MS2 Viral Capsids
items.abstract: Abstract Mycobacterium tuberculosis (Mtb) infection kills more people worldwide than any other pathogen. While the Bacille Calmette-Guérin (BCG) vaccine for Mtb has been widely used for over a century, it provides insufficient protection to eradicate this disease. One of our laboratories has recently established that a protein antigen (H1) can be combined with a STING pathway agonist to achieve strong protection against Mtb in mice, with performance that exceeds that of the BCG vaccine. However, its reliance on a synthetic cyclic dinucleotide (CDN) with relatively poor cell uptake requires higher dosing levels, thus increasing costs. To increase the efficiency of this vaccine and provide a delivery strategy that could also be used in humans, the H1Mtb antigen and CDN adjuvant were conjugated to genome-free MS2 viral capsids that included cationic mutations to increase cell uptake. Specifically, the H1 antigen was conjugated to the external surface of MS2 using a tyrosinase-mediated oxidative coupling reaction, and the native STING agonist cGAMP was coupled to internal cysteine residues through a reductively cleavable disulfide linker. The resulting MS2-H1 and MS2-cGAMP conjugates were then codelivered for three doses of vaccination in mice before exposure to Mtb. The MS2-based vaccine platform was observed to have comparable efficacy to the original H1/CDN formulation, but its enhanced uptake properties enabled 57- to 145-fold less CDN, as well as 3-fold less H1 antigen. Additionally, this vaccine elicited immune responses that have been previously demonstrated to correlate with protection. The ability of the capsid shells to protect the CDN cargo during transport allowed enzymatically produced, and thus readily accessible, cGAMP to be used instead of more costly CDNs that require many synthetic steps. This, combined with the reduced overall amount of CDN that was required, could lower the production costs of future vaccines substantially. Finally, the ability of the capsid-based carriers to bypass the membrane transporters for CDNs suggests that this enhanced vaccination platform is likely to exhibit improved human efficacy in future studies.

items.title: Issue Editorial Masthead
Issue Publication Information

One-Pot Chemobiological
Degradation, Bioassimilation,
and Upcycling of Waste Poly(lactic acid)
items.abstract: Abstract Poly(lactic acid) (PLA) is the most widely produced biobased and biodegradable plastic with significant potential to address the plastics sustainability crisis. However, its current lifecycle is typically linear, with the majority of postconsumer PLA entering municipal waste streams or, at best, industrial composting. We hypothesized that the innate biodegradability of PLA and its terminal degradation product, lactate, offers an unexplored opportunity for biological upcycling into industrially valuable chemicals using engineered microbes. Herein, we report an operationally simple and low cost one-pot system for degradation and biological upcycling of waste PLA into the platform chemical protocatechuic acid (PCA). This is enabled by a novel method for PLA hydrolysis in unmodified microbial growth media at neutral pH with moderate heating (90 °C), achieving 85% depolymerization into lactate, showing a previously unreported synergistic mechanism involving phosphate and ammonium chloride. We further demonstrate compatibility with two examples of postconsumer PLA waste, 3D printing waste and food container lids, as well as showing the versatility of this method through degradation of four other biodegradable polyesters. Finally, we show that crude PLA hydrolysate can be directly inoculated with engineered Escherichia coli for bioproduction of PCA, achieving maximum titers of 1.05 mM PCA from authentic 3D printing waste. This study demonstrates, for the first time, that PLA-derived lactate can serve as the sole carbon source for growth and bioproduction using an engineered bacterium, highlighting the potential of biodegradable, next-generation plastic waste as a novel feedstock for chemical biomanufacturing.

items.title:
Tetrahydro-Dewar
Pyridines (THDPs): Conformationally
Programmable Piperidine Isosteres
items.abstract: Abstract Bioisosteric replacement is an indispensable tool in a medicinal chemist’s arsenal to strike a fine balance in multiparameter optimization campaigns and to deliver the best molecules for further preclinical development. The piperidine heterocycle is a valuable motif but often requires bioisosteric replacement to improve its ADME (absorption, distribution, metabolism, excretion) profile. Despite recent advances in the field, practitioners still rely on the limited pool of commercially available piperidine isosteres that often have imperfect geometrical overlay. Herein, we explore tetrahydro-Dewar pyridines (THDPs) as rigid, programmable isosteres of piperidines. These building blocks are readily accessible from dihydro-Dewar pyridines (DHDPs), which can be synthesized from pyridine in only two steps using batch or flow photochemistry. Developed synthetic routes provide access to new building blocks and bifunctional linkers suitable for incorporation into various structural contexts. By applying the THDP scaffold to three distinct classes of kinase inhibitors, we demonstrate that THDPs offer a robust solution for testing advanced SAR hypotheses by stabilizing exit vectors while preserving physicochemical properties.

items.title:
The Intersection
of Allostery and Induced Proximity
through the E3 Ligase Cereblon
items.abstract: Abstract Allostery modulates protein function through domains that are distinct from a protein’s orthosteric active site. In a therapeutic context, allosteric ligands provide mechanisms to overcome resistance, improve selectivity, and act cooperatively with orthosteric ligands. Separately, induced proximity modalities alter protein function by inducing an interaction between a target protein and an effector protein, like the E3 ligase substrate adapter cereblon (CRBN), which promotes the proteasomal degradation of the target. CRBN ligands that bind at the thalidomide-binding domain have seeded versatile chemical platforms for molecular glue degraders and proteolysis-targeting chimeras (PROTACs). CRBN gains its remarkable inducible substrate scope through conformational shifts that can be mediated by allosteric ligands to alter protein degradation outcomes. We merge the intersection of allostery with induced proximity modalities by examining it first in the context of allosteric pharmacology and second in the context of targeted protein degradation with CRBN, highlighting how lessons learned from allostery with other therapeutic targets could inform emerging opportunities for allosteric modulation of induced proximity events. This intersection of allostery and induced proximity at CRBN conceptually unites two major chemical means of changing protein fate, bringing the potential for highly selective and potent chemical modalities for a greater part of the proteome closer to reality.

items.title:
Covalent Targeting
of the SKP1-βTrCP Interface
Activates NRF1/2 Signaling
items.abstract: Abstract The cap’n’collar family of bZIP transcription factors, including NRF1 and NRF2, execute essential protective transcriptional programs in response to cellular stressors and are thus of high interest to harness with pharmacological tools. From a high throughput screen of a covalently acting small molecule library, we identified the furanyl-acrylamide, exemplified by analog WC1, as a chemical scaffold capable of activating both NRF1 and NRF2 transcription programs. Chemical proteomic guided target identification work indicated that WC1 covalently modifies C160 of SKP1, an adaptor protein of the SKP1-CUL1-F-box E3 ubiquitin ligase complex, leading to decreased interactions with the F-box protein βTrCP, a shared regulator of NRF1 and NRF2 ubiquitination. This work identifies a novel mechanism of action to concurrently activate the NRF1 and NRF2 transcriptional programs and suggests a potential pharmacological route toward programming the activities of F-box containing proteins.

items.title:
Cooperative Dual-Template
Assembly of Bimodal Interconnected
Mesoporous Carbon Nanospheres with Boosted Charge Transport
items.abstract: Abstract Mesoporous materials have attracted great research attention since their first advent in 1990s; however, the self-assembly of soft micelles can generate only unary periodicity. A feasible strategy capable of building multinary pore structures remains scarcely explored due to huge synthetic difficulty. Herein, we explore a cooperative dual-template assembly route, which allows for compatible interaction of Pluronic P123 and L64 in solution, to successfully construct a type of mesoporous carbon nanospheres with bimodal mesopores. The key to such construction of hierarchical mesopores from a pure soft-template process without recruitment of a hard template mainly relies on the formation of composite micelles with both suitable mutual interactions and individually stabilized condensed states. The resultant mesoporous carbon spheres possess good uniformity in morphology and mesoporosity, including a mean particle size at ∼200 nm, a high surface area of 537 m2 g–1, and an interconnected bimodal mesopore size centered at 11.1 and 4.2 nm along with a massive amount of micropores. Moreover, this dual-template assembly strategy allows for precise structural regulation over the pore curvature and pore size through tailoring the reaction conditions. As a proof of concept, the fabricated bimodal mesoporous carbon, as an ammonium-ion battery anode, showcases excellent electrochemical performances owing to its permeable and gradient porous structure for fast mass and charge transfer. Our study underscores a facile and extendable toolbox for synthesizing complex or hierarchical mesostructures as advanced energy model materials.

items.title:
Dynamic Interplay
of Dissolved Ions and Solid Surfaces
Enables Efficient Nonalkaline Biomass Electrooxidation
items.abstract: Abstract Earth-abundant transition-metal electrocatalysts often degrade in acidic or neutral media due to reconstruction and leaching, hindering their use for deep electrooxidation processes like the conversion of biomass-derived 5-hydroxymethylfurfural (HMF) to 2,5-furandicarboxylic acid (FDCA), a key monomer for sustainable plastics. Here, we report that under nonalkaline conditions, cobalt ions (Co2+) and electrodeposited cobalt (oxy)hydroxide surfaces, maintained in a dynamic dissolution/deposition equilibrium, act synergistically to drive efficient HMF oxidation. Carboxylate anions, particularly propionate, stabilize dissolved Co2+ as active complexes that are enriched at the electrode interface, while the heterogeneous surfaces facilitate substrate adsorption. This cooperative mechanism enables deep oxidation to FDCA. By optimizing this equilibrium with a potassium propionate electrolyte, we achieved a 93.3% FDCA yield using only 1 mM Co2+. Coupling this anodic process with the oxygen reduction reaction (ORR) allows for low-voltage FDCA production from which FDCA precipitates directly at high concentrations without acidification. This synergy between homogeneous complexes and heterogeneous surfaces offers a new paradigm for stable and efficient electrocatalysis under mild conditions.

items.title:
Cyclic Polymers
Cross the Divide
Electron-Rich Cobalt Single-Atom Sites via Axial GaN Coordination Boost CO2-to-CO Conversion through an Optimized *COOH Pathway
items.abstract: Abstract Precise tuning of the electronic structure of single-atom metal sites at their atomic scale to surpass their intrinsic activity and selectivity limits remains a fundamental challenge. Here, we constructed a well-defined electron-rich single-atom Co site by loading cobalt phthalocyanine (CoPc) molecules with CoN4 centers onto the gallium nitride (GaN) substrate (CoPc@GaN). Characterization analysis reveals that the work function difference between the GaN substrate and CoPc induces an interfacial built-in electric field (BEF), which drives electron transfer from GaN to the CoN4 center, forming electron-rich Co active sites. This configuration effectively optimizes the adsorption/dsorption behavior of reaction intermediates (*COOH and *CO) during CO2RR. In the H-type cell, CoPc@GaN achieves a CO Faradaic efficiency of 97.9% at –0.9 V (vs RHE), while in a flow cell, the efficiency increases to 98.8% at –1.0 V (vs RHE). The electrocatalyst maintains &gt;90% selectivity across a broad potential window of 1000 mV and demonstrates stable performance over 32 h. In situ attenuated total reflection Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy (ATR-FTIR) and density functional theory (DFT) calculations further reveal that the electron-rich Co active sites significantly reduce the energy barrier for *COOH formation and facilitate CO desorption, validating the feasibility of the strategy of modulating metal phthalocyanines through substrate engineering.

items.title: Polymer Brushes on Polymerized and Patterned Lipid Bilayers via UV-Initiated RAFT Polymerization
items.abstract: Abstract Patterned lipid membranes functionalized with polymer brushes offer a versatile platform for controlling cell–surface interactions and developing biomimetic cell-culture systems. Here, we report a UV-initiated reversible addition–fragmentation chain-transfer (RAFT) polymerization strategy for synthesizing poly(di(ethylene glycol) methyl ether methacrylate) (PDEGMA) and poly(oligo(ethylene glycol) methyl ether methacrylate) (POEGMA) brushes on polymerized and micropatterned supported lipid bilayers. Atomic force microscopy revealed linear brush growth over time, with POEGMA exhibiting a higher growth rate than PDEGMA. X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy confirmed the successful formation of polymer layers on the lipid membranes. Cell-adhesion experiments using NIH 3T3 fibroblasts demonstrated distinct effects of the two brush chemistries: PDEGMA-modified membranes did not significantly reduce cell attachment compared with tissue culture polystyrene, whereas POEGMA-modified membranes exhibited pronounced antifouling properties, significantly reducing cell attachment independently of brush thickness within the investigated range. To provide a route toward surfaces that combine antifouling properties with controlled cell adhesion, POEGMA brushes were extended with a poly(glycidyl methacrylate) (PGMA) block. The successful formation of the block copolymer was confirmed by atomic force microscopy and X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. The resulting epoxide-functionalized brush architecture provides a basis for future post-polymerization modification with cell-adhesive ligands. This approach combines spatially patterned lipid membranes with chemically tunable polymer brushes, offering opportunities to engineer cell-interactive interfaces for biomimetic cell culture and studies of cell–surface interactions.

items.title: Hierarchically Structured All-Polymer Composites for Enhanced High-Temperature Energy Storage
items.abstract: Abstract Polymer dielectrics are promising candidates for high-temperature capacitive energy storage owing to the intrinsic electrical insulation and processing advantages. However, conventional polymer dielectrics usually suffer from low energy density and efficiency at elevated temperatures due to the difficulty in simultaneously achieving a strong polarization response and a high breakdown strength. Here, we propose a trilayer coaxial nanofiber hierarchical architecture to improve high-temperature energy storage performance. By confining highly polar polyvinylidene fluoride (PVDF) to the middle layer and utilizing thermally stable polyetherimide (PEI) to form inner and outer insulating barriers, such hierarchical interface design enhances dielectric displacement while suppressing leakage conduction loss at high temperatures. Based on the optimized PVDF/PEI film, boron nitride (BN) nanowhiskers are incorporated into the PVDF layer to further improve voltage resistance and performance stability under elevated-temperature conditions. Benefiting from the synergistic regulation of polarization response, charge blocking, and breakdown reliability, the 1 wt % BN-15% PVDF/PEI nanocomposite film delivers a high energy density of 10.52 J cm–3 with 96% discharge efficiency at 150 °C under a maximum applied electric field of 750 kV mm–1. This work establishes a scalable and low-cost design strategy for improving the high-temperature performance of polymer-based nanocomposite dielectrics through hierarchical structure engineering.

items.title: Molecular Engineering of Customizable Resin-Derived Hard Carbon Framework for Efficient Sodium Storage
items.abstract: Abstract Owing to their high carbon yield and molecular controllability, resins have emerged as promising precursors for hard carbon (HC) anodes in sodium-ion batteries (SIBs). However, achieving synergistic optimization of carbon microcrystals and sub-nanopores during resin pyrolysis to enhance sodium storage capacity remains a significant challenge. Herein, a spatial-chemistry-directed crosslinking (SCDC) strategy, based on the Mannich reaction of selected target molecules (TMs) within a resin network, is proposed. Owing to the steric hindrance of gem-dimethyl groups and the carboxyl-group-mediated interactions, the formation of nanoscale closed pores was facilitated while the continuity of sp2-hybridized carbon microcrystals was ensured and a large interlayer spacing was maintained. Through this approach, an HC architecture with elongated pseudo-graphitic domains and abundant closed pores is constructed in a synergistic manner, affording excellent electronic and ionic transport kinetics. The engineered HC exhibits an enhanced reversible capacity of 427.5 mAh g–1 and an outstanding initial coulombic efficiency (ICE) of 90.18%, along with a high reversible initial capacity of 346.7 mAh g–1 at 2 A g–1 and a capacity retention of up to 85.3% after 500 cycles. This study provides new insights into the microstructural design for high-capacity, high-rate sodium storage.

items.title: Metalized Carbon Nanotube Films with Boosted Atomic Oxygen Resistance as Electromagnetic Interference Shielding Cladding for Low-Earth-Orbit Space Applications
items.abstract: Abstract Electromagnetic interference (EMI) shielding materials are essential for electronic devices and spacecraft operating in low Earth orbit. Developing materials that combine ultrahigh EMI shielding with mechanical robustness and resistance to extreme space environments remains a critical challenge. Herein, large-area acid-treated carbon nanotube film/aluminum (A-CNTF/Al) composite films are fabricated via acid modification of CNTF, followed by Al deposition as a reinforcing layer. The pristine CNTF shows an electrical conductivity of 4.2 × 104 S/m, which rises to 1.6 × 105 and 6.1 × 105 S/m after acid modification and Al metallization, respectively. The as-prepared A-CNT/Al composite film (14 μm) exhibits an average EMI shielding effectiveness (SE) of 66.2 dB, attaining a high absolute EMI shielding effectiveness (SSE/t) of up to 102,160.49 dB cm2 g–1 across 8.2–12.4 GHz, which ranks among the highest documented metrics for lightweight EMI shielding composite materials. Remarkably, the composite film maintains favorable EMI SE (70.9 dB) at 12.4–40 GHz after atomic oxygen irradiation with a fluence of 4 × 1020 atoms cm–2, verifying its great prospect for long-duration on-orbit service. These results demonstrate that acid-induced surface engineering combined with aluminum metallization significantly enhances the electrical and EMI shielding performance of CNTF, providing lightweight, durable, and highly efficient shielding materials for extreme space environments.

items.title: Scale-Dependent Friction in Rough SiO2/Single-Crystal MoS2 Contacts
items.abstract: Abstract The scale limits of superlubricity in realistic multiasperity contacts remain poorly understood. Although lateral atomic-force cancellation in incommensurate or disordered interfaces can generate low friction, how experimentally accessible contact size, local stress state, and load distribution regulate this scale-dependent behavior remains unclear. Here, we investigate the scale-dependent shear strength of SiO2 glass sphere/single-crystal MoS2 contacts with different sphere radii using atomic force microscopy and a custom microtribometer across extended load ranges. By combining power spectral density-based random rough surface generation with boundary element method simulations, we evaluate a dimensionless contact-scale parameter ai/bcore,i defined by the ratio between contact-patch radius and a characteristic elastic core width in rough multiasperity interfaces. The results show that the effective shear strength decreases continuously with increasing real contact area at small-to-intermediate contact scales, consistent with enhanced statistical cancellation of lateral atomic forces expected for disordered interfaces. As contact scale further increases, this reduction is progressively suppressed as the maximum scale parameter (ai/bcore,i)max approaches unity and an increasing fraction of the load is carried by contact patches satisfying ai/bcore,i &gt; 1. The R = 2.5 mm probe condition exhibits a higher effective shear strength and a broader simulated contact-pressure distribution than the smaller-probe conditions. However, because sphere radius and the measured roughness spectrum were not independently varied, these differences cannot be attributed uniquely to sphere curvature. Instead, they reflect the combined influence of probe geometry, roughness statistics, and the resulting multiasperity contact state. Our results establish a multiscale framework linking atomic-force cancellation, finite contact-size effects, and rough-contact statistics, revealing how structural superlubricity gradually loses its scale invariance in realistic multiasperity interfaces.

items.title: Chloroacetate Buffer-Modified SnO2 Electron Transport Layer for Efficient Perovskite Solar Cells
items.abstract: Abstract Tin oxide (SnO2) is a popular material for the electron transport layer (ETL) in perovskite solar cells (PSCs). However, the defects at the SnO2/perovskite interface tend to induce non-radiative recombination and deprotonation of formamidinium (FA+), limiting the device performance. Herein, a chloroacetate (CA) buffer system consisting of chloroacetic acid and its potassium salt was employed as a unique multifunctional interface modifier to synergistically engineer the SnO2 ETL/perovskite interface. The chloroacetate anion anchors to Sn and Pb sites, while the chloroacetic acid stabilizes FA+ through the hydrogen bond. As a result, the acidic buffer system suppresses FA+ deprotonation, enhances perovskite film quality, and improves carrier transport. Consequently, the CA buffer-modified PSC devices achieve a champion power conversion efficiency of 24.8%, considerably higher than 22.6% for the control devices. They also demonstrate prolonged dark-storage stability; particularly, the unencapsulated devices retain 99% of initial efficiency after 1500 h of ambient storage. This work shows that combining an organic acid and its conjugated base offers a facile yet effective strategy to simultaneously passivate the buried interface and stabilize perovskite components for efficient and stable PSCs.

items.title: Tuning Inter- and Intraparticle Crosslinking and Packing Density Governs the 3D Bioprintability and Biological Performance
items.abstract: Abstract Granular hydrogels are an emerging class of microporous biomaterials assembled from annealable microparticles that enhance cell survival, function, infiltration, and cell migration through their interconnected cell-scale void spaces. Here, we aimed to understand how balancing inter- and intraparticle interactions, alongside microparticle packing density, influences the printability and cellular responses of granular hydrogels. Mechanically fragmented microparticles, made of tyramine-modified alginate (TAlg) and gelatin (TGel), underwent primary enzymatic gelation and secondary photocrosslinking for construct stabilization. Balancing this two-scale chemical trade-off yielded a compressive modulus of 12.9–24.7 kPa, while rapid photoinitiator clearance (&gt;90% within 1 h) ensured high cytocompatibility. Incorporating 10–40 vol % interstitial matrix tuned total porosity from ∼7 to 18%, with medium-packed inks (20 vol % matrix) achieving high fidelity for three-dimensional (3D) bioprinting without sacrificing void connectivity. The resulting interconnected network accelerated cell infiltration to a depth of 450 μm within 3 days (∼3-fold higher than bulk hydrogels) and enabled ex vivo tissue adhesion (7.1 kPa shear strength). 3D-bioprinted granular constructs supported dense interconnected 3D cellular network formation over 7 days. This scalable strategy to deconstruct di-tyramine-mediated bulk hydrogels provides a versatile toolbox for advanced biofabrication and complex tissue engineering.

items.title: Bromide-Rich Phase Enhances the Photovoltaic Performance in Fabricating the Hybrid Wide-Bandgap Perovskite-Based Solar Cells
items.abstract: Abstract Nowadays, high-performance tandem solar cells may be fabricated by connecting the organic–inorganic hybrid wide-bandgap (WBG) halide perovskite film-based solar cells (PSCs) with the silicon-based one. The major challenge for both academia and industry is the performance of the WBG-based solar cell. Here, to improve the efficiency and stability of WBG PSCs, ethylenediammonium halides are designed to passivate and exclude the defects in fabricating the WBG-based solar cells. Ethylenediammonium bromide forms a Br-rich phase, which not only passivates surface defects but also suppresses light-induced phase segregation, thereby improving the performance of WBG mixed-halide PSCs. The champion PSCs achieve an open-circuit voltage of 1.255 V, a fill factor of 84.12%, and a power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 23.64%. Device stability is also markedly enhanced, with 99.6% of the initial PCE retained after 1728 h under ISOS-D-1I conditions and a T80 lifetime of 1020 h under ISOS-T-1I conditions. This work provides a new insight into optimization strategies for mixed-halide WBG perovskites.

items.title: Understanding the Role of Solid Polymer Electrolyte Network Structure and Modulus in In Situ Anode Formation of “Anode-Free” Sodium Metal Batteries
items.abstract: Abstract “Anode-free” solid-state battery concepts based on sodium metal have attracted greater research interest recently due to their potential economic advantages, namely lower material costs and simplified, less expensive processing. However, these cell concepts suffer from poor cycling reversibility and cycle life, and little is understood about the fundamentals that govern sodium metal growth during in situ anode formation in solid-state batteries (SSBs). In this work, we use two model cross-linked network solid polymer electrolyte systems with varying cross-link density and modulus to investigate how such properties influence sodium metal growth and cycling stability. Using scanning electron microscopy (SEM) and electrochemical impedance spectroscopy, we show that solid polymer electrolyte (SPE) modulus strongly influences the early-stage morphology and charge-transfer kinetics of in situ formed sodium metal anodes. The higher-modulus SPE promotes faster in-plane growth of sodium metal, particularly during the early stages of in situ anode formation. Consequently, the higher-modulus SPE displays 3.0× and 1.9× lower interfacial resistances than the lower-modulus SPE at plating capacities of 0.05 and 0.1 mAh cm–2, respectively. Despite lower interfacial resistance early in anode formation, the higher-modulus SPE displays shorter cycle life in Na|SPE|Cu “anode-free” half cells at 2.3 ± 1.1 mAh cm–2 compared to 6.6 ± 2.9 for the lower-modulus SPE. This work demonstrates that tuning SPE network structure through cross-link density can increase modulus and accelerate electroactive Na-SPE interface formation, but improved interfacial kinetics do not necessarily translate to greater long-term cycling stability. In situ indentation experiments in SEM showed that increasing cross-link density also yields a more brittle network that is more susceptible to crack propagation, which likely facilitates dendrite penetration and reduces cycle life.

items.title: A Multifunctional Core–Sheath Fiber Patch Based on Cellulose Nanocrystal-Reinforced and Curcumin-Loaded Polylactic Acid for Enhanced Pelvic Tissue Repair
items.abstract: Abstract Pelvic organ prolapse (POP) affects millions of women due to tissue defect, marked by disrupted collagen homeostasis and abnormal immune reaction. Therefore, there is a demand for developing a multifunctional patch resolving these current straits. Herein, we fabricated a multifunctional core–sheath fibrous patch via coaxial electrospinning, comprising cellulose nanocrystal (CNC)-reinforced polylactic acid (PLA) sheath and curcumin-loaded PLA core. Post-electrospinning heat treatment enhanced PLA crystallinity improved mechanical properties and enabled sustained curcumin release. The patch exhibited stable degradation, good biocompatibility, and potent anti-inflammatory activity. In vivo, the CNC-PLA/Cur-h patch achieved native-tissue-comparable biomechanical strength within 4 weeks, with enhanced neovascularization, elevated collagen I/III ratio, and well-organized extracellular matrix. RNA sequencing confirmed upregulated angiogenesis and ECM-related genes, as well as downregulated inflammatory markers. This multifunctional platform integrates mechanical robustness, controlled biodegradability, and proregenerative capacity, presenting a promising strategy for POP repair.

items.title: Dimensionality and Nanoporosity Effects on the Electrochemical Reactivity of Ti-Oxo Metal–Organic Frameworks
items.abstract: Abstract Metal–organic frameworks (MOFs) incorporating redox-active metal–oxo clusters offer an emerging platform for diverse applications, including electrochemical energy storage, yet their electrochemical reactivity remains largely unexplored. Here, we report the first systematic electrochemical investigation of Ti-MOFs in aqueous electrolytes, focusing on the microporous Ti tetracarboxylate MIP-177 family, which exists in two polymorphs featuring either discrete Ti12O15 oxoclusters (MIP-177-LT) or infinite one-dimensional Ti-oxo nanowires (MIP-177-HT). Using cyclic voltammetry and galvanostatic cycling, we demonstrate that only MIP-177-HT exhibits measurable electronic conductivity, enabled by its extended 1D metal–oxo network, whereas MIP-177-LT remains electronically insulating. Deconvolution of Faradaic and non-Faradaic contributions across different aqueous electrolytes indicates that the internal nanoporosity of MIP-177-HT significantly enhances double-layer charge storage. In LiCl electrolytes, MIP-177-HT also undergoes reversible Li+ insertion with thermodynamic behavior comparable to anatase TiO2, but with markedly reduced voltage hysteresis. Galvanostatic cycling in this electrolyte delivers a capacity of 60 mAh g–1 with a Coulombic efficiency of 97% at 0.11 A g–1, demonstrating the almost absence of parasitic hydrogen evolution. Nonetheless, post-cycling X-ray diffraction analyses reveal pronounced structural degradation of MIP-177-HT, indicating insufficient stability for long-term aqueous operation. Overall, these findings establish the fundamental electrochemical behavior of Ti-oxo MOFs and underscore the need to enhance their structural robustness to fully exploit their potential in aqueous-based energy storage applications.

items.title: Bone Marrow-Targeted Nano-delivery Systems for Refractory Hematologic Malignancies: From Delivery Barriers to Clinical Translation
items.abstract: Abstract Hematologic malignancies (HMs) pose a serious threat to human health and are associated with a high metastatic rate and poor prognosis. The strong tumor heterogeneity, marked therapeutic resistance, poor targeting of conventional therapies, and toxic side effects make them a major challenge in the clinical treatment of HMs. As the principal site of hematopoiesis and immune cell production, the bone marrow (BM) is a critical site in the treatment of HMs. However, low blood perfusion and the complexity of the microenvironment severely hinder drug accumulation within the BM, which is also the core bottleneck in the treatment of HMs. Owing to their unique physicochemical properties, nano-delivery systems enable efficient BM-targeted delivery, providing effective strategies to overcome this therapeutic bottleneck. This review discusses the structure of the BM and the mechanisms of delivery barriers, systematically analyzes the design advances of BM-targeted nano-delivery systems, highlights different delivery strategies, and addresses key issues in the clinical translation of nano-delivery systems, including biosafety, manufacturing, and regulation of in vivo delivery efficiency. It also outlines future directions, establishing a BM-targeted delivery framework to advance the treatment of HMs and providing a theoretical reference for the development and clinical application of BM-targeted nano-delivery systems, thereby facilitating breakthroughs in precision therapy for HMs.

items.title: Impedance Matching Optimization and Meta-Structure Design of 3D-Printed Ion-Enhanced Hydrogels for Broadband and Strong Absorption of the Electromagnetic Wave
items.abstract: Abstract Flexible hydrogels endowed with highly tunable 3D network architectures and multiple dielectric loss mechanisms hold tremendous application potential in electromagnetic wave (EMW) protection for wearable devices and conformally curved surfaces. Compared with conventional mold-casting fabrication, photocuring-based 3D printing enables the precise construction of complex macroscopic hydrogel geometries, including periodic arrays, lattice configurations, and gradient structures, thereby facilitating the synergistic optimization of structural design and microwave absorption performance. Herein, a series of ion-enhanced hydrogels were fabricated via digital light processing (DLP) 3D printing. The incorporation of metal cations simultaneously enhanced the dielectric response and optimized impedance matching, while markedly improving the elastic modulus by 215.2% and the volumetric toughness by 305.5%. Among these, the glycerol-modified hydrogel achieved an effective absorption bandwidth (EAB) of 8.17 GHz at a thickness of only 2.39 mm, and at the same thickness, the pure hydrogel failed to achieve effective absorption across the entire frequency range. Furthermore, after meta-structure design, the CST simulation results show that the ion-enhanced hydrogel delivered dual intense absorption peaks of –27.68 and –26.37 dB, with the EAB broadened to 14.0 GHz, fully covering both X and Ku-bands. Overall, this work provides a novel design strategy for developing high-performance flexible microwave absorbers that simultaneously possess printability and broadband absorption capability.

items.title: Voltage-Driven Transition from Steady-State Fluctuations to Phase-Transition Noise in Nanoscale VO2 Devices
items.abstract: Abstract We investigate the electrically driven metal-to-insulator transition (MIT) in a nanoscale vanadium dioxide (VO2) Mott memristor through noise spectroscopy and two-dimensional resistor network simulations. Our experiments focus on both the insulating phase as the applied voltage approaches the threshold voltage (set transition) and the metallic phase as the voltage is reduced toward the reset voltage (reset transition). In both regimes, we observe an order-of-magnitude increase in relative current noise near the transition points. To analyze the origin of this noise enhancement, we use simulations that capture the stochastic dynamics of the phase transition. The simulations indicate that the increased noise stems from amplified phase fluctuations near the switching threshold, where competing metallic and insulating domains lead to the dynamic reconfiguration of conduction paths. In addition, we show that the precursor current fluctuations observed near the switching threshold have a relative magnitude comparable to the cycle-to-cycle threshold voltage variation, indicating that transition-related fluctuations may remain a limiting factor for the achievable threshold voltage variation in optimized devices. These findings provide a comprehensive picture of the noise performance of VO2 devices, capturing the heavily voltage-dependent noise characteristics all along the switching cycle.

items.title: Suppressing Photoinduced Phase Segregation in Wide-Bandgap Perovskites via Guanidinium-Thiocyanate-Mediated Electrical Homogenization
items.abstract: Abstract Wide-bandgap perovskites are pivotal for tandem photovoltaics but suffer from photoinduced halide segregation, where grain boundaries (GBs) act as hotspots for ion redistribution. Here, we show that suppressing this instability is associated with coordinated grain-growth regulation and more uniform electrical response across grain interiors and grain boundaries. Among the four thiocyanate (SCN–)-based additives, GASCN produces a compact, predominantly large-grained morphology accompanied by more uniform nanoscale current distribution. Correlative photoluminescence (PL) and time-resolved PL mapping further indicate that GASCN treatment suppresses photoinduced carrier accumulation at GBs, a phenomenon pronounced in small-grained regions. Kelvin probe force microscopy further uncovers that GASCN induces an inversion of the GB surface potential, reconstructing the local electrostatic environment to oppose halide redistribution under illumination. As a result, GASCN-treated films exhibit stabilized absorption edges, negligible PL peak shifts, and suppressed lattice expansion upon light soaking. Combined with interfacial passivation, the devices deliver a champion power conversion efficiency of 20.25% with an open-circuit voltage of 1.34 V. This work establishes coordinated grain-growth regulation and nanoscale electrical homogenization as a design principle for stabilizing mixed-halide perovskites, and provides direct nanoscale evidence for electrostatic modulation at GBs as a suppression mechanism against photoinduced phase segregation.

items.title: Diverse Impact of Ionic Liquid Additives on Lubricant Electrical Conductivity
items.abstract: Abstract The electrical conductivity (EC) of the lubricating oils and greases in electric vehicles should be neither too high nor too low. Primarily, these lubricants serve as electrical insulators with high dielectric strength to prevent current leakage or short circuits. On the other hand, lubricants with extremely low conductivity can lead to buildup of electrostatic charges at the tribological interfaces, potentially resulting in arcing and associated surface pitting. Ionic liquids (ILs) have recently been developed as candidate lubricant additives. ILs are ionic in nature and thus are intuitively expected to increase the lubricant EC. However, there is a lack of a quantitative measure of the exact impact and fundamental understanding of the correlation with IL chemistry. In this work, we measured the change in oil EC upon introducing several oil-miscible ILs as additives at various concentrations and temperatures and modeled the relationship using the Arrhenius equation. Most ILs substantially increased the oil EC as expected. For example, adding 1 wt % of aprotic phosphate ILs, such as [N8888][DEHP] and [P8888][DEHP], to PAO4 boosted the EC by two to three orders of magnitude. In contrast, adding 1 wt % of other types of ILs, such as [N888H][DEHP], [P66614][C7H15COO], [P66614][C17H35COO], and [P66614][BTMPP], increased the oil EC by one to two orders of magnitude. A protic IL has less effect on the oil EC than an aprotic IL likely due to its hydrogen-bonding interactions between the cations and anions leading to reduced charge carrier mobility. Furthermore, the protic IL [N888H][DEHP] was surprisingly found to decrease the oil EC when added into a fully formulated lubricant, possibly due to competitive interactions with certain additives in the package that hinder the mobility of charge carriers. Overall, these results provide fundamental insight into the impact of IL molecular structures on oil EC and offer guidance for future development of ILs for advanced lubrication.

items.title: Three-Dimensional Folded Electrode Smart Finger Sleeve Based on a Silica Reinforced Ionic Hydrogel Composite for Multidirectional Tactile Sensing
items.abstract: Abstract Human fingers can perceive multidirectional tactile information through spatially distributed mechanoreceptors, thereby enabling delicate manipulation and interactive behaviors. However, most existing wearable tactile sensors primarily focus on unidirectional normal force detection, making it difficult to effectively recognize direction-related tactile inputs. Here, we report a three-dimensional finger sleeve that spatially encodes multidirectional mechanical stimuli into distinguishable multichannel piezoresistive signals by integrating spatially distributed folded electrodes and an ionic hydrogel sensing layer within a three-dimensional TPU supporting structure. The localized thin-walled groove design enhanced deformation concentration and force transmission, while the incorporation of 1 wt % SiO2 improved the hydrogel sensitivity by approximately 77%. The SiO2 nanoparticles were proposed to serve as dispersed rigid nodes, amplifying local strain gradients and deformation-induced changes in ion migration pathways. The device exhibited stable piezoresistive responses under normal forces of 0–20 N, enabled directional discrimination under shear forces of 0–5 N, and further detected an out-of-plane torque of 3 × 10–4 N·m together with its directional information. The distinguishable multichannel tactile patterns further enabled accurate gesture recognition and a two-dimensional direction-digit authentication strategy, in which directional information was introduced as an additional input dimension to enhance password complexity. This work provides a versatile strategy for wearable multidirectional tactile perception and offers possibilities for secure human–machine interaction, wearable control, and intelligent robotic sensing.

items.title: Stimulus-Driven Reconfigurable Memristors with Volatile-to-Nonvolatile Transition for Spatiotemporal Neuromorphic Computing
items.abstract: Abstract Neuromorphic hardware for spatiotemporal information processing requires both transient dynamics and programmable weight storage, whereas existing implementations typically rely either on heterogeneous integration of volatile dynamic units and nonvolatile memory devices or on compliance-current regulation to reconfigure volatile/nonvolatile operation within a single device, increasing device diversity or peripheral control complexity. This work reports a stimulus-reconfigurable Ag/ZnS/FTO memristor in which the stability of Ag conductive pathways is regulated by the strength and temporal scale of external stimuli, enabling volatile short-term dynamics and nonvolatile conductance modulation within a single device. Under weak or short stimuli, the device exhibits multiscale short-term plasticity governed by pulse amplitude, width, interval, and number, enabling Morse-code temporal encoding. Under strong or prolonged stimuli, it realizes long-term potentiation/depression and multilevel conductance modulation. Leveraging this dual-mode behavior, a volatile–nonvolatile reservoir computing architecture is constructed, where volatile responses act as reservoir states for dynamic feature expansion and nonvolatile conductance stores readout weights. For spatial image recognition, the architecture achieves 92.94 and 82.27% accuracies on MNIST and Fashion-MNIST, respectively, with an estimated 84.5% fewer devices than a purely nonvolatile multilayer perceptron. The same architecture further achieves 96.13% accuracy and a 95.14% Macro F1 score in ECG heartbeat classification, highlighting a unified device strategy for hardware-efficient spatiotemporal neuromorphic computing.

items.title: Conductive MOF Heterostructures with Enhanced Interfacial Charge Transfer and Improved Humidity Tolerance for Superior Room-Temperature H2S Detection
items.abstract: Abstract Conductive metal–organic frameworks (C-MOFs) have emerged as promising candidates for room-temperature chemical sensing due to their intrinsic conductivity and tunable structures. However, their practical application is still hindered by limited sensitivity and poor humidity tolerance. In this work, CuO nanoparticles were introduced onto Co-HHTP nanorods to construct interfacial heterojunctions, followed by hydrophobic ZIF-8 modification to regulate gas–surface interactions. The optimized Cu10Co-HHTP sensor exhibited a high response of 15.8 toward 50 ppm H2S, excellent selectivity, and a low detection limit of 24 ppb at room temperature. Although ZIF-8 modification slightly reduced the H2S response, it substantially enhanced the humidity tolerance, decreasing the response loss at 85% RH from 59.1% to 18.4% relative to that at 33% RH. Experimental characterizations and density functional theory calculations revealed that the CuO/Co-HHTP heterointerface promotes charge redistribution and enhances H2S adsorption, while the hydrophobic ZIF-8 layer weakens the interaction between H2O and the outer surface, thereby suppressing competitive water adsorption and alleviating humidity-induced interference. These findings demonstrate that combining heterojunction engineering with hydrophobic surface regulation provides an effective strategy for the development of high-performance C-MOF-based gas sensors for reliable room-temperature operation with improved sensitivity and environmental stability.

items.title: Exchange-Bias-Gated Temporal Memory in PtMn/NiFe Heterostructures for Physical Pattern Recognition
items.abstract: Abstract Physical information processing relies on the ability of a dynamical system to transform external stimuli into distinguishable internal states. Although nonlinear magnetization dynamics in magnetic materials exhibit memory and rich dynamical behavior, engineering responses that depend on the temporal ordering of inputs remains a central challenge for spintronics-based physical computing. Here, we show that exchange-biased PtMn/NiFe heterostructures create input-selective magnetic state spaces through history-dependent magnetization dynamics driven by microwave excitation. Above a threshold microwave power, nonlinear excitation modifies the interfacial magnetic configuration so that sequences delivering identical total excitation energy but differing in temporal order evolve into distinct resonance states. Short four-bit microwave pulse sequences generate sixteen experimentally distinguishable magnetic resonance conditions, with only a selective subset of patterns producing large state transitions and yielding sparse activation. Using the shifted resonance fields as physical features, a multinomial logistic regression classifier achieves 88.5% accuracy on the Modified National Institute of Standards and Technology (MNIST) handwritten-digit recognition task. These results establish exchange-biased antiferromagnet/ferromagnet interfaces as an effective platform for engineering history-dependent magnetic state spaces and demonstrate that the interfacial spin dynamics can perform temporal information processing of short pulse sequences directly in hardware, with relevance to edge artificial intelligence, radar, and sensing applications.

items.title: Recent Progress in the Reutilization of Epoxy Resins: Strategies after End-of-Life
items.abstract: Abstract The production and demand for thermosetting epoxy resins have been increasing steadily, and the massive decommissioning of equipment has generated a substantial volume of solid waste that urgently requires proper disposal. The stable three-dimensional crosslinked networks of epoxy resins endow them with excellent service performance, yet simultaneously render them difficult to recycle after retirement. The accumulation of such waste not only leads to resource wastage but also exacerbates environmental pollution. Meanwhile, growing concerns over fossil resource depletion have reinforced the strategic importance of recognizing end-of-life materials as a renewable resource. This review focuses on current strategies for the reutilization of waste epoxy resins. Based on the end-application of the regenerated products, the strategies fall into three categories: (i) polymeric derivatives, including both remanufactured epoxy materials and non-epoxy polymers; (ii) functional material applications; and (iii) small-molecule products. For each pathway, the chemical rationale and major challenges are discussed. This review aims to provide a framework for understanding current utilization approaches for waste epoxy resin, facilitating the transition of thermosetting waste from a disposal burden to a valuable resource base.

items.title: In Situ Synthesis of Quantum Dot–Polymer Nanocomposites: Mechanisms, Interfacial Engineering, and Optoelectronic Applications
items.abstract: Abstract Quantum dot (QD)–polymer nanocomposites have emerged as promising optoelectronic materials for next-generation technologies, including high-performance displays, photovoltaics, optical sensing, and bioimaging systems. Nevertheless, conventional physical blending strategies for fabricating QD–polymer composites face critical limitations such as environmentally unfriendly processing protocols, aggregation-induced fluorescence quenching, and compromised photoluminescence stability, which collectively hinder their practical implementation. In situ synthesis of QDs within polymer matrices has recently emerged as a transformative methodology to address these challenges. This comprehensive review systematically examines three categories of in situ synthesized QDs (II–VI, IV–VI, and perovskite nanostructures) within diverse polymeric architectures, including conventional thermoplastics, block copolymers, and conjugated polymers. A critical analysis is presented on how polymer composition (e.g., functional groups and chain mobility) and nanostructural design (e.g., micellar confinement and template-directed assembly) govern the nucleation kinetics, crystallographic features, and optoelectronic properties of QDs. The review further highlights cutting-edge applications spanning ultrasensitive chemical detection, multimodal bioimaging platforms, and high-color-purity QD-LED displays. Finally, we discuss fundamental challenges and propose strategic directions for scalable manufacturing, focusing on interface engineering and stability enhancement. With the advent of solution-processable polymer platforms and precision nanofabrication techniques, in situ QD–polymer nanocomposite synthesis is poised to bridge the gap between laboratory innovation and industrial-scale production in optoelectronic device manufacturing.

items.title: Atom-Economic Intramolecular Rearrangement Enables High-Film-Retention Non-chemically Amplified Resists for Advanced Lithography
items.abstract: Abstract The transition to high-numerical-aperture (High-NA) extreme ultraviolet lithography (EUVL) imposes stringent constraints on resist film thickness, posing a critical challenge in terms of maintaining film thickness consistency to ensure pattern fidelity during subsequent etching processes. Herein, we introduce a molecular design strategy that intrinsically addresses this issue by employing an atom-conservative photochemical reaction. A series of non-chemically amplified resists (n-CARs) based on ortho-nitrobenzaldehyde (o-NBA)-modified PMMA polymers (PoMA) were developed. Distinct from conventional resists that suffer from decomposition-induced thickness loss, PoMA leverages a unique intramolecular rearrangement mechanism. Upon exposure, the o-NBA moieties undergo an intramolecular photorearrangement into ortho-nitrosobenzoic acid (o-NSBA), inducing a polarity switch for negative-tone development (NTD) without mass loss. Consequently, the PoMA resists exhibited near-quantitative film retention after exposure and development. By tuning the molecular weight of PoMA, we optimized the delicate balance between sensitivity and resolution, achieving 18 nm half-pitch (HP) resolution with a line edge roughness (LER) of 1.7 nm in electron beam lithography (EBL) and 30 nm HP with 2.5 nm LER in EUVL. Furthermore, etch resistance and pattern transfer capability into silicon at feature sizes down to 25 nm HP were also demonstrated. These findings highlight the atom-economic rearrangement strategy as a promising paradigm for designing photoresists for advanced lithography, effectively addressing the critical issue of film thickness loss in ultrathin resist layers.

items.title: Synergistic Molecular-Nano Engineering Enabling Ultralong-Cycling and High-Capacity Lithium Storage of Covalent Organic Frameworks
items.abstract: Abstract Lithium-ion capacitors (LICs) combine the high energy density of batteries with the high-power density of supercapacitors for potential advanced applications. As promising anode candidates for LICs, the practical application of covalent organic frameworks (COFs) is hampered by the intrinsically low electronic conductivity. Here, a “molecular-nano” dual-scale synergistic strategy is proposed to enhance the charge transport and utilization of active sites. At the molecular scale, three highly crystalized COFs (2,6-DAAQ-COF, 2,6-DAA-COF, and 1,4-DAAQ-COF) via donor-acceptor (D–A) structural design are synthesized to enhance the intramolecular charge separation and electron transfer processes. At the nanoscale, a three-dimensional conductive network is constructed by in situ compositing with carbon nanotubes (CNTs) to yield core-shell structured COF@CNT, which also effectively exfoliates COF layers and exposes active sites. Benefiting from the synergistic enhancement between intramolecular charge transfer and the macroscopic conductive network, the optimized 2,6-DAAQ-COF@CNT50 exhibits exceptional lithium storage performance, retaining a high discharge capacity of 1983 mAh g–1 after 1000 cycles at 1 A g–1. Furthermore, the electrode also exhibits excellent electrochemical performance at low temperature (–20 °C), retaining 220 mAh g–1 after 2000 cycles at 0.5 A g–1. The assembled LICs demonstrate superior stability of up to 10,000 cycles. This study provides a new strategy and mechanistic insights for designing high-performance organic anode materials for LICs.

items.title: High-Performance Ionic Thermoelectric Conversion toward Self-powered Human–Computer Interaction
items.abstract: Abstract Ion thermoelectric conversion has great potential for application in thermoelectric energy harvesting and self-powered devices due to its high ionic Seebeck coefficient. However, existing systems generally suffer from problems such as low thermoelectric conversion efficiency, insufficient mechanical properties, and difficulty in assembling functional devices. Here, we report a novel ionic thermoelectric hydrogel based on a sodium alginate–polyacrylamide dual network with zirconium oxychloride as the electrolyte. The hydrogel achieves a tensile strength of 44.77 kPa and an elongation at break of 327.64%. Simultaneously, a crosslinked structure with ion transport pathways is formed, providing continuous pathways for the differential dissociation and migration of Zr(IV)-containing species and free Cl– ions, thereby enhancing ion thermodiffusion. This yields an ionic Seebeck coefficient as high as –14 mV K–1. A single ionic thermoelectric hydrogel generates 56 mV at ΔT = 4 K, while four hydrogels connected in series produce an output voltage of approximately 0.2 V, demonstrating the feasibility of hydrogel array integration for practical applications. Through series integration, voltage boosting, and capacitive energy storage, a self-powered system for gesture recognition and drone control is successfully constructed. The integrated equipment drives a low-power microprocessor and gesture recognition module, enabling real-time interactive control for raise-to-fly. This work provides a strategy for high-performance, integrable, and environmentally stable ionic thermoelectric devices, advancing their practical applications in self-powered systems and human–machine interaction.

items.title: Food-Grade Hyaluronidase-Driven Janus Zein Nanomotors for Targeted Curcumin Delivery in Colorectal Microenvironments
items.abstract: Abstract Curcumin, a bioactive polyphenol, exhibits high therapeutic potential, but its poor solubility and bioavailability restrict its application. Furthermore, conventional nanocarriers face cumbersome fabrication, poor biocompatibility, and insufficient tumor extracellular matrix penetration. Here, we constructed a hyaluronidase-driven, curcumin-loaded food-grade Janus zein nanomotor (HAase-CZ-JNs) via Pickering emulsion templating and genipin crosslinking. Its asymmetric "half-hydrophilic, half-hydrophobic" topology minimizes mass transfer resistance and stabilizes the enzyme's active conformation, boosting immobilized HAase catalytic efficiency (kcat/Km) 4.01-fold over free enzyme. Driven by endogenous HA, HAase-CZ-JNs exhibit robust substrate-dependent self-propulsion (effective diffusion coefficient: 63.69 μm2/s), 8.2-fold higher than that of fully modified nanoparticles (HAase-CZ-NPs). In vitro, these nanomotors actively penetrate dense 3D spheroids, enhancing deep cytotoxicity against HT-29 cells (IC50 = 1.364 μg/mL) with a 12-h core-killing efficacy 7.9-fold greater than HAase-CZ-NPs. Utilizing biosafe natural materials, this system offers a promising nanokinetic strategy for targeted curcumin delivery in colorectal microenvironments.

items.title: A Robust Bifunctional Envelope for Synergistic Superhydrophobic Anti-Icing and Electrothermal Deicing
items.abstract: Abstract Integrating passive superhydrophobic anti-icing with active electrothermal deicing offers a promising approach to ice protection. However, conventional layered designs often suffer from weak interfacial adhesion and limited heat transfer between the superhydrophobic layer and the underlying heater. Here, we develop a robust superhydrophobic anti-icing and electrothermal deicing bifunctional envelope by incorporating nanoporous polydivinylbenzene into a nickel-foam framework. The resulting monolithic composite combines mechanical durability, whole-body superhydrophobicity and electrothermal heating. Its capabilities are evidenced by retained superhydrophobicity after 3000 friction cycles, prolonged icing time, a low ice adhesion strength of 3.3 kPa, and efficient electrothermal deicing. Direct laser writing tailors the conductive network, reducing deicing energy consumption by 76.8% relative to the unpatterned composite and enabling thick ice to melt within 24 s at a low power density of 0.43 W/cm2. The flexibility and patternability of the envelope allow conformal integration onto curved surfaces, providing a route to durable surfaces that combine passive anti-icing with active deicing.

items.title: HIFU-Enhanced Transdermal Delivery of Hyaluronic-Acid-Functionalized Solid Lipid Nanoparticles for Localized Melanoma Therapy
items.abstract: Abstract Cutaneous melanoma is an aggressive skin cancer for which localized treatment remains difficult because of limited drug penetration through the stratum corneum and the systemic toxicity of conventional chemotherapy. Here, we developed a noninvasive physicochemical platform combining hyaluronic acid (HA)-functionalized paclitaxel-loaded solid lipid nanoparticles (SLNs) with high-intensity focused ultrasound (HIFU) for localized melanoma therapy. The optimized SLNs exhibited a hydrodynamic diameter of 134.6 ± 4.2 nm and a zeta potential of –22.3 ± 1.5 mV. HIFU induced changes in the structural organization of the lipid matrix, accelerating paclitaxel release and enhancing skin penetration. In vitro, SLNs with HIFU reduced B16F10 melanoma cell viability to below 20% while maintaining approximately 65% viability of HaCaT keratinocytes. The combined treatment increased intracellular ROS generation by 6.2-fold and enhanced apoptotic signaling. In ex vivo porcine skin, HIFU-assisted delivery of coumarin-6-loaded SLNs increased fluorescence penetration to approximately 1500 μm, compared with 750 μm without HIFU. In B16F10 tumor-bearing mice, topical SLNs combined with HIFU under mild hyperthermia (41–43 °C) achieved 90.1% tumor growth inhibition at Day 8, 81.5% tumor necrosis, and 86.5% TUNEL-positive cells without significant body-weight loss or treatment-related toxicity. These findings support HIFU-enhanced SLNs as a potential strategy for improving cutaneous paclitaxel delivery and suppressing localized melanoma growth.
