items.title: Silk Fibroin Nanoparticles Coated with an Extracellular Vesicle–Liposome Hybrid Shell for Controlled Cargo Delivery
items.abstract: Abstract Silk fibroin nanoparticles (SFNPs) are promising nanocarriers for drug delivery owing to their biocompatibility, bioactivity, controllable biodegradability, and low toxicity. However, their translation is limited by formulation-dependent variations in morphology, colloidal stability, drug loading, and aggregation, all of which can affect release behavior and biological performance. Here, we investigated how fibroin solubilization conditions govern the self-assembly, internal structure, surface properties, and cargo delivery performance of SFNPs, using curcumin as a hydrophobic model compound. SFNPs were prepared by lithium bromide (LiBr) solubilization followed by desolvation and were characterized using complementary scattering, microscopy, and spectroscopy techniques. Fibroin solubilization temperature and curcumin loading modulated SFNP size, internal organization, and surface roughness. In particular, SFNPs formed 70–150 nm mass-fractal aggregates composed of smaller primary nanoparticles, and this morphology affected cargo loading and release by controlling accessible internal surface area and solvent contact. To further stabilize the system and engineer the external interface, SFNPs were incorporated into a liposome/extracellular vesicle (EV) hybrid shell by sonication, generating a carrier-in-carrier system containing EV-derived membrane-associated components. The hybrid lipid–EV/SFNP platform reduced aggregation in aqueous media and provided a tunable external shell for controlled release of hydrophobic cargo. Overall, this work establishes a structure-based proof of concept connecting upstream solubilization parameters to downstream nanoparticle architecture, supporting the rational design of hybrid silk-based nanocarriers for cargo delivery.

items.title: Bio-Inspired Photothermal-Responsive P(NIPAM -co- NaAMPS)@SWCNT-COOH Hydrogel with Donnan-Driven Salt Rejection for High-Rate Solar Water Purification
items.abstract: Abstract The global water shortage and pollution crisis motivates the development of high-efficiency, durable water remediation technologies. Solar-driven interfacial evaporation attracts broad interest for its high efficiency and environmental friendliness; nevertheless, vaporization-related latent-heat loss and salt accumulation severely restrict practical water-purification performance. Inspired by biological mechanisms, we report a thermoresponsive hydrogel evaporator based on poly(N-isopropylacrylamide-co-sodium 2-acrylamido-2-methyl-1-propanesulfonate) (P(NIPAM-co-NaAMPS)) composite network. Sulfonate groups (–SO3−) from NaAMPS impart high hydrophilicity to accelerate water uptake, while local Donnan equilibrium within the network suppresses salt ingress and accumulation. Under 1 sun irradiation (1 kW·m−2), PNIPAM-derived thermoresponsiveness triggers hydrophilic-to-hydrophobic chain collapse above the lower critical solution temperature (LCST). Upon photothermal contraction, the hydrogel achieves a stable-release water-purification rate of 9.87 ± 0.19 kg·m−2·h−1 (photothermal efficiency of 96.6%) during the 0.7 h plateau, alongside a cycle-averaged productivity of 0.87 ± 0.07 kg·m−2·h−1 over the full 9.0 h absorption-release cycle. Different from reported Donnan-type salt-rejection hydrogels, thermoresponsive draw agents, and polyelectrolyte evaporators, our innovation lies in coupling photothermally activated liquid-water extrusion with Donnan-mediated salt rejection, instead of simple material blending. The hydrogel maintains good stability across 30 cycles in 3.5 wt % saline water, showing promise for partial-salt-rejection pretreatment of brackish and diluted seawater. This work provides a strategy for cyclically stable solar water purification combining salt rejection and contaminant removal.

items.title: Orientation-Controlled In-Material Physical Reservoirs Based on Polymer-Wrapped Carbon Nanotube Nanofilms
items.abstract: Abstract Semiconducting polymer poly(m-phenylenevinylene-co-2,5-dioctoxy-p-phenylenevinylene) (PmPV)-wrapped single-walled carbon nanotube (SWCNT–PmPV) nanofilms were fabricated using the Langmuir–Blodgett (LB) method to investigate the effects of structural orientation on their electrical and reservoir computing properties. Polarized ultraviolet–visible absorption spectroscopy and atomic force microscopy revealed that repeated compression–expansion cycles during LB deposition produced highly oriented SWCNT nanofilms. The oriented films exhibited an anisotropic electrical response, pronounced hysteretic current–voltage characteristics, and enhanced generation of higher-order harmonics, while water adsorption further enhanced the current and nonlinear electrical response. In waveform generation tasks, the advantage of the highly oriented films was most pronounced for the sawtooth and sin(2ω) targets, which involve more complex waveform features and frequency components. Additional delayed-input reconstruction and nonlinear autoregressive moving average (NARMA) 2 tasks revealed enhanced fading memory and nonlinear temporal processing under humidified conditions, with the highly oriented film exhibiting a larger memory capacity and lower NARMA2 error than the less-oriented film. These results indicate that structural orientation, together with humidity-dependent electrical dynamics, contributes to the nonlinear and temporal information-processing capabilities of SWCNT–PmPV nanofilms. These findings provide a practical strategy for modulating in-material reservoir computing performance through structural control of anisotropic material networks.

items.title: Hydroxy-Functionalized n-Type OMIECs as Multifunctional Conductive Biointerfaces for Simplified Biosensor Fabrication
items.abstract: Abstract Organic mixed ionic-electronic conductors (OMIECs) have emerged as key materials for bioelectronics owing to their ability to couple ionic and electronic transport. However, their potential as multifunctional biointerfaces for biosensing remains largely untapped, particularly for n-type systems. Here, we report a hydroxy-functionalized n-doped poly(benzodifurandione) (PBFDO-OH) that unifies efficient electron transport and enzyme immobilization within a single material platform. By introducing terminal hydroxy groups into the polymer backbone, PBFDO-OH enables the direct immobilization of glucose dehydrogenase through a simple one-pot strategy, eliminating the gold substrates, self-assembled monolayers, and multistep surface activation protocols that underpin conventional biosensor fabrication. This streamlined approach yields robust biofunctional electrodes with enhanced electrochemical performance while preserving enzyme activity and long-term stability. Integrated with additively manufactured electrodes, the resulting glucose biosensor demonstrates a high sensitivity of 17.4 μA L mmol–1, a low detection limit of 3.42 μmol L-1, excellent reproducibility (RSD = 5.35%), reliable quantification in human serum (RSD &lt; 10%), and outstanding operational stability over three weeks (RSD &lt; 3%). Beyond glucose sensing, this work establishes a general materials design strategy in which chemical functionalization transforms n-type OMIECs into conductive biointerfaces that simultaneously simplify device fabrication and provide stable bioreceptor integration for next-generation bioelectronic technologies.

items.title: Combustion of Boron Nanoparticles Encapsulated within Perchlorate Matrices: A Mechanistic Study
items.abstract: Abstract Boron is an attractive high-energy fuel, but its practical combustion efficiency is limited by a viscous oxide layer that impedes oxygen transport and promotes agglomeration. Here, we address these limitations by assembling boron nanoparticles into spray-dried mesoparticles in which boron is encapsulated within an ammonium perchlorate (AP) matrix and a nitrocellulose binder. This architecture enhances fuel oxidizer proximity, accelerates AP decomposition onset by ∼60 °C, and enhances reaction kinetics as evidenced by a ∼50% pressurization rate and a ∼58% shorter burn time relative to the physically mixed formulation. In situ TEM, TGA/DSC, and T-jump time-of-flight mass spectrometry reveal that mesoparticles promote interfacial reactions producing both B2O3 and boron nitride (BN). BN formation is identified as a thermodynamic efficiency-loss pathway, releasing significantly less energy per mole of boron than oxidation to B2O3. Substituting AP with potassium perchlorate eliminates the nitrogen source, significantly reducing BN formation, and further improves combustion performance. These results demonstrate that mesoscale encapsulation combined with targeted oxidizer selection provides a practical strategy to enhance boron combustion efficiency.

items.title: A Metal–Organic Framework-on-Metal–Organic Framework Chemical Nose for Intelligent Identification of Depression-Related Biomarkers via Machine Learning
items.abstract: Abstract Depression is a complex mental disorder associated with dysregulation of multiple neurotransmitter-related biomarkers, including Try, 5-HT, 5-HIAA, and 5-HTP. Herein, we report a MOF-on-MOF fluorescent sensor array, RhB@ZIF-8-on-FL@UiO-67, for simultaneous discrimination and detection of these biomarkers. Spatial separation of dyes within the hierarchical architecture effectively suppresses fluorescence crosstalk and generates multiple independent luminescent channels, enhancing signal diversity and sensing performance. The resulting multidimensional fluorescence responses enable accurate identification of Try, 5-HT, 5-HIAA, 5-HTP, and their mixtures. Both LDA and HCA achieved a classification accuracy of 100% for the tested samples. Furthermore, machine learning models, including BP, RF, DT, SVM, and KNN, confirmed the robustness of the sensing platform. This work integrates MOF-on-MOF engineering with machine learning-assisted pattern recognition, offering a sensitive and reliable strategy for multiplex biomarker analysis and providing a promising approach for intelligent diagnosis of complex diseases.

items.title: Binary-Crosslinked Alginate/Zwitterionic Interpenetrating Polymer Network Coatings for Lubricious and Antifouling Urinary Catheters
items.abstract: Abstract Hydrophilic hydrogel coatings can mitigate catheter-associated infections and friction-induced mucosal trauma during urinary catheterization by providing hydration-driven lubrication and antifouling surfaces. Here, we report an alginate/sulfobetaine methacrylate-based zwitterionic interpenetrating polymer network (Alg-ZW IPN) that integrates a binary crosslinker system into the IPN architecture by pairing a short-chain crosslinker, N,N′-methylenebisacrylamide (MbAm), with a long-chain crosslinker, poly(ethylene glycol) dimethacrylate (PEGDMA). In the binary crosslinked IPN (Alg-ZW BIPN), MbAm establishes dense local junctions for structural integrity, while PEGDMA spans the interjunction domains to mechanically bridge the network, confine alginate chains, and stabilize Ca2+–alginate coordination. This architecture redistributes mechanical stress across length scales, thereby improving coating durability. The Alg-ZW BIPN coating exhibited ultralow friction, with a friction coefficient of 0.01–0.02, and maintained 49% lower friction than MbAm single crosslinker coatings. In catheter insertion tests using a standard vascular phantom, the coating reduced insertion force by up to 75% compared with uncoated catheters. The coating also inhibited Escherichia coli adhesion by 97.4% relative to uncoated substrates and showed excellent biocompatibility, with a hemolysis ratio of 0.17% and &gt;95% endothelial cell viability after 24 h. Overall, the Alg-ZW BIPN design provides a general and scalable route to mechanically robust, lubricious, and antifouling hydrogel interfaces for indwelling medical devices.

items.title: Structural Engineering of Bio-Alkaloid Ionic Liquid-Mesoporous Silica Nanohybrids for Optimized Transdermal Atopic Dermatitis Therapy
items.abstract: Abstract Mesoporous silica nanoparticles (MSNs) are highly promising drug carriers owing to their exceptionally large surface area and tailorable pore structures for high drug-loading capacity, but their transdermal delivery is severely restricted by the skin barrier. Integrating natural ionic liquids (ILs) can modulate skin permeability; however, the mechanistic impact of distinct IL molecular structures on the interfacial properties of MSN-IL nanohybrids remains poorly understood. In this study, we engineered a structure-specific transdermal delivery platform by assembling citric acid-functionalized MSNs with various natural bio-alkaloid cations (choline, L-carnitine, and matrine). Density functional theory (DFT) and macroscopic physicochemical evaluations revealed that the matrine-based system (CA-M 1:2) forms a highly stable, tight ion-pairing conformation. This specific configuration endows the formulated MSN-IL nanohybrid with a robust dynamic viscosity, providing effective steric occlusion to prevent premature drug leakage within the MSN pores. Despite this internal cohesion, in vitro assays and transmission electron microscopy confirmed that the CA-M 1:2 hybrid dynamically facilitated the highest transdermal flux, transporting intact MSNs across the skin barrier via an IL-associated enhancement of skin permeation. In the atopic dermatitis mouse model, topical treatment with the optimized DEX/MSN-IL system significantly accelerated lesion resolution, restored epidermal architecture, and suppressed inflammatory cascades by downregulating IFN-γ, TNF-α, and IgE levels. This work establishes a physical chemistry-driven molecular-to-macro framework for the rational design of structure-specific nanohybrids, advancing high-performance topical therapeutics for inflammatory skin diseases.

items.title: Supramolecular Matrine-Proanthocyanidins Nanocomplex-Integrated Carboxymethyl Chitosan Hydrogel with Phenylboronic Acid Modification for Atopic Dermatitis Therapy
items.abstract: Abstract Atopic dermatitis (AD) is a chronic inflammatory skin disease featured by immune dysregulation, oxidative stress, and an impaired epidermal barrier. Oxidative stress and inflammation establish a self-sustaining vicious cycle that accelerates the progression of atopic dermatitis. However, few naturally derived self-assembled nanohydrogels have been developed to disrupt this reciprocal loop for the treatment of cutaneous AD. In this study, matrine (MAT) and proanthocyanidins (PAC), two Chinese medicine-derived molecules with inherent antioxidant and anti-inflammatory activities, co-assembled spontaneously into nanoparticles (PM NPs) in aqueous solution. Incorporation of PM NPs into the phenylboronic acid-modified carboxymethyl chitosan (CP) crosslinked network enhanced the mechanical strength of carboxymethyl chitosan, forming a composite hydrogel (CPPM). Spectral results verified that PM NP self-assembly was mediated by hydrogen bonding and π-π stacking. CPPM efficiently scavenged reactive oxygen species (ROS), suppressed the activation of the Ox-CaMKII and NF-κB signaling pathways, and activated Nrf2 to restore epidermal redox homeostasis. CPPM exhibited favorable moisturizing capacity, appropriate rheological properties, and mild ROS-triggered release to realize local therapeutic effects. In 1-chloro-2,4-dinitrochlorobenzene (DNCB)-induced AD mice, topical CPPM application significantly alleviated epidermal hyperplasia, itching, and inflammatory cytokine expression without obvious toxicity. This self-assembled bioactive hydrogel can concurrently regulate oxidative stress and inflammatory responses, offering a promising topical therapeutic approach against AD.

items.title: Coupled Regulation of Oxygen-Vacancy-Modified Near-Surface Structure and Interfacial Stability for High-Performance Li-Rich Mn-Based Cathodes
items.abstract: Abstract Li-rich Mn-based layered oxides (LRMOs) are prospective next-generation cathodes, delivering high specific capacities via coupled cationic and anionic redox. However, sluggish reaction kinetics, irreversible oxygen loss, and progressive interfacial structural degradation limit the practical application of LRMOs. Herein, a coupled strategy for regulating the near-surface structure and interfacial stability is developed using ammonium titanyl oxalate (ATO) as a multifunctional precursor. During thermal treatment, an approximately 10 nm Li2TiO3 coating layer forms to stabilize the cathode interface. Meanwhile, reducing gases released from precursor decomposition induce oxygen vacancy formation, whereas Ti incorporation suppresses excessive transition-metal (TM) reduction in the near-surface region, thereby alleviating the associated increase in Mn3+ content and Jahn–Teller distortion. Moreover, the coupled Ti and oxygen vacancy configuration enhances anionic redox reversibility, stabilizes the near-surface oxygen framework, and lowers the Li+ migration barrier, thereby improving Li+ transport and structural stability. The optimized ATO-2% cathode achieves an average initial Coulombic efficiency (ICE) of 90.07% at 0.1 C and a capacity retention of 88.1% after 300 cycles at 1 C. This work establishes a coupled regulation strategy for the oxygen vacancy-modified near-surface structure and interfacial stability, providing a route for optimizing oxygen vacancy engineering in LRMO cathodes.

items.title: Self-Gelling Powdered Hydrogel Dressing Based on Dynamic Ion-Cross-Linked Natural Polypeptides for Shape-Adaptive Hemostasis and Accelerated Wound Healing
items.abstract: Abstract Effective hemorrhage control and wound closure are frequently compromised by the poor shape adaptability of preformed bulk hydrogel dressings, which fail to maintain intimate contact with irregular, bleeding tissue. To address this, we developed a freeze-dried polyelectrolyte complex powder (GLF-K) composed of dopamine-grafted γ-poly-l-glutamic acid, ε-poly-l-lysine, keratin, and iron ions. The network architecture relies on primary electrostatic cross-linking, synergistically reinforced by dopamine-Fe3+ coordination, which enables the GLF-K powder to rapidly rehydrate and transition into a cohesive hydrogel upon exposure to moisture. Compared to commercial chitosan hemostats, the GLF-K powder exhibited comparable or enhanced hemostatic efficacy in both in vitro and in vivo hemorrhage models, alongside excellent biocompatibility. More importantly, in a full-thickness skin defect model, GLF-K treatment accelerated the early-stage healing rate to 55.8% by day 3, significantly outperforming the control group. These findings suggest that GLF-K powder represents a promising integrated platform for managing acute hemorrhage and promoting expedited wound healing in irregular tissue defects.

items.title: Hierarchical Composite Scaffold That Synergistically Combines Orderly Active Factor Release with Scaffold Degradation for Enhanced Bone Repair
items.abstract: Abstract Effective bone regeneration requires biodegradable scaffolds to provide temporary mechanical support while progressively creating space and delivering bioactive cues in step with tissue healing. However, achieving synergy between orderly active particle release and scaffold degradation remains a major challenge. This study aimed to develop a hierarchical scaffold for sustained bioactive-ion delivery and bone-defect repair. The scaffold consisted of a 3D-printed poly(p-dioxanone) (PPDO) framework and a freeze-dried gelatin network. Magnesium oxide-coated chitosan microspheres (MgO@CS) were incorporated into gelatin to support early cell recruitment and angiogenesis, whereas citrate-functionalized amorphous calcium phosphate (Cit-ACP) was embedded in PPDO to provide sustained osteogenic stimulation. During in vitro degradation, gelatin was largely removed within 5 weeks, progressively opening space for tissue infiltration. PPDO fibers showed morphological erosion at weeks 7–8 but persisted as the principal structural framework. The scaffold continuously released Mg2+, Ca2+, and citrate during the 14-day observation period. Cell experiments demonstrated enhanced cellular recruitment, vascularization, and osteogenic differentiation. In a rat calvarial defect model, the scaffold enhanced bone formation and improved BV/TV. These results demonstrate that coupling stage-matched scaffold degradation with compartmentalized bioactive-ion delivery provides a promising strategy for coordinating vascularized bone regeneration.

items.title: Correction to "Atomic Layer Deposited Interlayers for Robust Metal–Polymer Interfaces"
Multifunctional Shape-Memory Composite Films with Coupled Morphing–Transparency–Luminescence Modulation via Interfacial Engineering and Hybrid Nanoparticle Design
items.abstract: Abstract Shape-memory polymers offer programmable deformation, yet their use in storing and regulating optically readable information remains limited. Inspired by the adaptive optical behavior of glass squid, we developed a multifunctional shape-memory composite film integrating programmable morphing, reversible transparency modulation, optical-state storage, and phosphorescent readout. The film combines refractive-index-matched phosphorescent carbon dots/silica nanoparticles (CDs/SiO2 NPs) with a poly(ethylene-co-vinyl acetate) (EVA) shape-memory matrix. Mechanical programming generates interfacial microcavities, decreasing the transmittance from 88.4 to 18.6% while fixing the programmed optical state without continuous external force. Thermal shape recovery promotes transparency restoration and reveals the concealed information. Meanwhile, the CDs/SiO2 NPs provide visible-light-excited afterglow observable for approximately 6 s for dark-state recognition. The integration of programmable morphing, transparency modulation, and phosphorescent readout enables dynamic anti-counterfeiting/encryption and adaptive visual signaling.

items.title: Oscillatory Chemical Networks in Silicon Nanofluidic Chips for Ultra-low-power Computing
items.abstract: Abstract Chemical reactions offer unique opportunities for energy-efficient and adaptive computing. We integrate fluidic networks filled with the oscillatory Belousov–Zhabotinsky (BZ) reaction in silicon microchips to investigate the potential of these networks for on-chip chemical computation. Using nanofluidic confinement and networks of thousands of microreactors (5–30 μm) connected by nanochannels, we demonstrate stable oscillations under 300 nm vertical confinement and estimate an intrinsic chemical energy expenditure of ≈17 fJ per cycle at nanoscale reaction volumes. Reaction–diffusion waves propagate signals with diffusion lengths of ≈40 μm and speeds up to 123 μm s–1, while light-sensitive modulation provides dynamic control over the reaction dynamics, offering a route toward programmable architectures. These features support large fan-out, weighted connections, and reconfigurable pathways, laying the foundation for chemical logic, neuromorphic networks, and adaptive systems. Our results position oscillatory chemistry as a promising route toward ultra-low-power computing and bio-inspired architectures.

items.title: Hydrogen-Bonded Organic Frameworks@Bacterial Cellulose Mixed-Matrix Membranes for Pollution Elimination
items.abstract: Abstract Hydrogen-bonded organic frameworks (HOFs) represent promising porous photocatalytic candidates for water remediation, yet their practical deployment is severely hindered by their powdery nature, poor machinability, and limited recyclability. Herein, we report a facile in situ growth strategy to immobilize methyl-modified (HOF-101-CH3), fluorine-modified (HOF-101-F), and pristine HOF-101 nanocrystals within the three-dimensional interconnected nanofibrous network of bacterial cellulose (BC), yielding HOFs@BC mixed-matrix membranes (MMMs). Robust interfacial hydrogen bonding and physical cross-linking are constructed between HOF crystallites and BC nanofibers, which effectively suppress HOF aggregation, improve mechanical tolerance, and grant the composite membrane favorable hydrophilicity for aqueous-phase operation. Benefiting from the electron-donating methyl substituent, HOF-101-CH3-m delivers a more negative surface zeta potential (–28.8 mV), elevated charge-carrier separation efficiency, and superior dye-selective performance. It achieved a high selectivity ratio of 49.5 (permeation flux: 174 L m–2 h–1 bar–1) toward mixed cationic methylene blue (MB) and anionic methyl orange (MO), with 99.1% MB removal and merely 2% MO adsorption. After five separation-regeneration cycles, the membrane retains a selectivity ratio above 41.5 and maintains approximately 84% of its initial selectivity performance. Under visible-light irradiation, abundant reactive oxygen species (1O2, ·OH, and H2O2) are generated by the embedded HOF-101-CH3, endowing the membrane with photocatalytic self-cleaning capability. Notably, HOF-101-CH3-m achieves complete photodegradation of bisphenol A (BPA) within 50 min and maintains 95.3% degradation efficiency over five cyclic photocatalytic runs. This work demonstrates a feasible structural-engineering route to transform intractable powdery HOFs into mechanically robust multifunctional membranes, offering insights into the future design of HOF-derived functional materials toward integrated selective dye separation and photocatalytic elimination of organic water pollutants.

items.title: A Series of TTDO-Based Energetic Cocrystals: From Supramolecular Assembly and Structural Analysis to Energetic Performance and Combustion Modulation
items.abstract: Abstract The inherent trade-off between high energy output and safety remains a critical bottleneck in the development of advanced propellants and high-energy-density materials. Here, we present a supramolecular assembly strategy using 2,4,6-triamino-1,3,5-triazine-1,3-dioxide (TTDO) as a Lewis base host to construct energetic cocrystals. Guided by COSMO screening, five nitro-containing Lewis acid energetic molecules were successfully cocrystallized with TTDO. Single-crystal X-ray diffraction reveals diverse protonation behaviors and extensive hydrogen-bonding networks, while electrostatic potential analysis shows that the positions of electrostatic potential extrema shift upon cocrystallization, correlating with significantly reduced mechanical sensitivity. Notably, TTDO-LLM-116 and TTDO-NMTT serve as multifunctional additives in ammonium perchlorate (AP)-based composite propellants. Incorporating only 10 wt % of these cocrystals merges the two-stage decomposition of AP into a single exothermic event and reduces the decomposition activation energy from 250.2 kJ·mol–1 to 107.4 kJ·mol–1 and 63.3 kJ·mol–1. Laser ignition experiments confirm enhanced combustion with a substantially shorter duration. As combustion additives, these cocrystals reduce the activation energy of AP while avoiding the energy-dilution effect commonly encountered with inert metal oxide catalysts. This work establishes TTDO-based cocrystals as a versatile platform for developing low-sensitivity, high-performance energetic materials, and advanced combustion modifiers for propellant applications.

items.title: Loading-Dependent Osteogenic Performance of Core–Shell Nanocomposite-Reinforced Poly(ε-caprolactone) Scaffolds for Bone Regeneration
items.abstract: Abstract Bone defect repair remains challenging due to the complex biological processes involving inflammation, angiogenesis, and osteogenesis. Although therapeutic ions and natural antioxidants have been individually investigated for bone regeneration, the biological performance of scaffolds incorporating multiple functional components at different loading contents remains to be fully explored. In this study, we designed a core–shell nanocomposite (GaTe-MBG@Cur-ZIF-8) consisting of Ga/Te-codoped mesoporous bioactive glass (GaTe-MBG) as the core and curcumin-loaded ZIF-8 as the shell. The nanocomposite was incorporated into poly(ε-caprolactone) (PCL) at different contents (0, 5, 10, and 15 wt %) to fabricate three-dimensional (3D)-printed composite scaffolds. The designed scaffolds were intended to provide a multifunctional platform integrating curcumin with Ga, Te, Zn, Si, and Ca ions. Among the investigated formulations, the scaffold containing 10% GaTe-MBG@Cur-ZIF-8 (by weight) exhibited the most favorable overall biological performance, including antioxidant activity, favorable inflammation-associated responses, enhanced osteogenic differentiation, and angiogenesis-related effects. In a rat cranial defect model, the 10% scaffold demonstrated improved bone regeneration compared to the other groups. RNA sequencing analysis revealed differential gene expression and enrichment of inflammation- and osteogenesis-related pathways, including IL-17, TNF, and MAPK signaling, suggesting potential associations between the scaffold-induced cellular responses and these signaling pathways. Collectively, these findings highlight the potential of the combined GaTe-MBG@Cur-ZIF-8 nanocomposite for bone tissue engineering and identify 10% as a favorable loading content within the investigated range, providing insights into the design of multifunctional composite scaffolds for bone regeneration.

items.title: Acquisition of Ultra-low Friction by a 2D Heterogeneous Interface at a High Temperature
items.abstract: Abstract Achieving robust lubrication across extreme temperature ranges remains a fundamental challenge in tribology. Here, we report a MoS2/Ti/Ag nano-doped film, fabricated via scalable magnetron sputtering, that exhibits self-adaptive ultra-low friction from ambient conditions to 450 °C. We distinguish the governing mechanisms at homogeneous (self-mated) and heterogeneous (paired with hydrogenated amorphous carbon (a-C:H)) interfaces, respectively. While room-temperature superlubricity in self-mated pairs arises from the shear-induced alignment of long-range ordered planes but degrades under thermal stress, the heterogeneous interface maintains an ultra-low friction coefficient of 0.02–0.04 throughout the entire temperature spectrum. At elevated temperatures, we reveal a possible dynamic reconstruction process: graphitization of the a-C:H transfer film driven by localized sp2-C clustering synergizes with Ag migration to restructure the contact area. This friction-activated mechanism may entrap carbon fragments and liberate MoS2, prompting its spontaneous re-alignment into an ordered, low-friction configuration. These findings uncover a thermally resilient, self-adaptive lubrication strategy with broad implications for aerospace and industrial applications.

items.title: Magnetically Reconfigurable Liquid Metal Microdroplet Networks Enable High Thermal Conductivity and Self-healing in Dynamic Polymer Composites
items.abstract: Abstract The integration of high thermal conductivity and autonomous self-healing capability in thermal interface materials remains a critical challenge for next-generation electronic devices. Herein, we design a liquid metal (LM) magnetic droplet composite: TA-coated iron particles (Fe@TA) are compounded with Ga68.5In21.5Sn10, ultrasonicated into LM magnetic droplets, and dispersed in a dynamic polymer matrix. The TA shell architecture serves a dual function: it prevents deleterious alloying between iron and gallium-based LM, while the polyphenolic moieties of TA establish coordination interactions with Fe2+/Fe3+ and Ga3+/In3+ ions, synergistically ensuring interfacial structure and the stability. Under magnetic actuation, Fe@TA enables the directional migration and controlled deformation of LM droplets within the matrix, promoting droplet–droplet contact and the formation of efficient thermal pathways. Meanwhile, the magnetic field guides the droplets toward the damaged region, inducing matrix displacement to close the fracture gap and facilitating dynamic bond reformation, which substantially enhances the self-healing capability. Remarkably, the healed LMMC70 composite exhibits a 100% enhancement in thermal conductivity compared to its pristine sample, attributable to the synergistic magneto-thermal effect that drives droplet aggregation at damage sites, reinforces interfacial thermal contacts, and restores structural continuity through effective dynamic bond reorganization. In addition, the LMMC90 composite integrates high thermal conductivity (5.6 W·m–1·K–1), ultralow contact thermal resistance (0.1 K·cm2·W–1), excellent electrical insulation (1011 Ω·m), and effective self-healing capability. This work offers a viable strategy for designing intelligent thermal interface materials with magnetic-field-assisted thermal management and autonomous damage healing, holding great promise for reliable thermal management in advanced electronics.

items.title: A Bioinspired Phytyl Tripod Anchor for Engineering Liposomal and Cellular Surfaces as a Robust Colloidal Delivery Platform
items.abstract: Abstract Inspired by the phytyl chains of chlorophylls and tocopherols, we developed a robust phytyl tripod anchor for cell surface engineering in this work. The anchor exhibited markedly stronger membrane anchoring than the widely used 1,2-distearoyl-sn-glycero-3-phosphoethanolamine (DSPE) anchor, as reflected by a lower critical micellization concentration (0.119 vs 0.189 mM) and a more negative Gibbs free energy of liposome binding (–29.85 vs –28.15 kJ/mol). Using this anchor, we established a liposome-relayed bioorthogonal manipulation platform that enables site-specific cell surface engineering in vivo. In a zebrafish inflammation model, liposomes decorated with amphiphilic hyaluronic acid (HA) first delivered the phytyl tripod anchor selectively to inflamed tissue, and subsequently injected clickable catalase and liposomal curcumin were then captured in situ via bioorthogonal click chemistry, anchoring them onto the target cell surface. This two-step strategy produced substantially enhanced therapeutic effects. We further extended the platform into a photothermal enhanced liposome delivery system. Clickable magnetic nanoparticles, synthesized via a PEGylated gallic acid approach, were bioorthogonally conjugated to cell membranes and liposomes through the phytyl tripod anchor. Curcumin was additionally derivatized with the endoplasmic reticulum (ER) targeting KKAA peptide to enable organelle-specific delivery. In an inflammation model with RAW264.7 cells, this photothermal-enhanced system significantly improved the anti-inflammatory efficacy. The developed phytyl tripod anchor and the derived bioorthogonal strategies hold great promise for precision cell surface engineering and targeted delivery of bioactives.

items.title: Nickel Nanoparticle-Modified Carbon Nanotube Films for Energy-Efficient Out-of-Oven Curing and Damage Self-Sensing of Basalt Fiber/Epoxy Composites
items.abstract: Abstract Carbon nanotube (CNT) films can serve as a Joule heating source for low-energy out-of-oven curing, but their electrothermal performance is limited by the CNT–CNT junction resistance. Metal nanoparticles can bridge adjacent CNTs and reduce the junction resistance, but at excessively high concentrations, particle agglomeration offsets this effect. In this study, a nickel (Ni) nanoparticle-modified CNT/thermoplastic polyurethane (TPU) conductive film was prepared and used for Joule heating curing and damage self-sensing of basalt fiber-reinforced epoxy composites. Within the investigated range of Ni dispersion concentrations, the conductivity of the film increases first and then decreases. To interpret this behavior, a phenomenological competition model and a Monte Carlo resistor-network model were established, attributing this nonmonotonic change to the competition between metallic bridging and agglomeration loss. Based on the modeling and experimental results, 2 mg·mL–1 was identified as the Ni concentration with the best overall performance within the investigated range. The resulting film reached 80.96 °C at 9 V and maintained uniform and stable heating during 3600 s of continuous heating and 30 heating–cooling cycles. Subsequently, basalt fiber-reinforced polymer composites (BFRPs) were prepared using the conductive film via an out-of-oven curing process. The BFRPs exhibited mechanical properties similar to those of oven-cured samples while additionally acquiring electrothermal and damage self-sensing functions. This study provides a viable design strategy for the development of basalt fiber-reinforced composites with both electrothermal and damage self-sensing capabilities.

items.title: Preadipocyte-Derived Decellularized Extracellular Matrix-Functionalized Three Dimensionally Printed Scaffolds Regulate Vascularized Adipose Tissue Regeneration via Modulation of Selected Paracrine Factors
items.abstract: Abstract The clinical efficacy of soft tissue reconstruction is severely hindered by unpredictable graft resorption and inadequate vascularization. Traditional synthetic implant scaffolds offer mechanical support, with limited bioactivity for adipose tissue regeneration. In this study, we developed a “three-in-one” bioinstructive platform (dPCL) integrating structural support, signal induction, and immunomodulation by functionalizing a 3D-printed polycaprolactone (PCL) framework with a decellularized extracellular matrix (dECM) derived from 3T3-L1 preadipocytes. The obtained dECM-functionalized scaffold provided essential biochemical cues. In vitro assays demonstrated that dPCL significantly enhanced preadipocyte adhesion and adipogenic differentiation. Besides, the dECM-functionalized scaffold was found to modulate the secretion of selected paracrine factors, markedly upregulating the secretion of adiponectin, VEGF, and IL-10, which facilitated cell differentiation and robust endothelial network formation. In vivo evaluation in a murine subcutaneous model confirmed that dPCL scaffolds effectively supported the formation of stable, well-vascularized adipose tissue. Furthermore, the dECM-functionalized scaffold enhanced the recruitment and accumulation of proregenerative M2 macrophages, maintaining an M2-dominant tissue microenvironment that facilitated graft integration. In summary, current findings demonstrate that integrating cell-specific dECM with 3D-printed scaffolds creates a multifaceted bioactive platform that overcomes the critical barriers of vascularization and metabolic integration, presenting a highly promising strategy for functional soft tissue regeneration.

items.title: Interfacial Integration of Cross-Kingdom Membranes Establishes a Rechargeable Energy Cascade
items.abstract: Abstract Engineering modular adenosine triphosphate (ATP)-mediated energy transduction pathways from the bottom up faces two key bottlenecks: first, detergent-dependent reconstitution typically impairs protein activity and energetic coupling efficiency due to disrupted native lipid environments and randomized protein orientation; second, physically separated ATP production and consumption modules suffer from severe diffusional ATP losses and inefficient intermodule cascade coupling. To address both limitations, we report a programmable, nondestructive strategy to construct a high-performance artificial organelle—the “chrometabosome”—through orthogonal peptide-driven fusion of photosynthetic chromatophores and energy-consuming erythrosomes. Bypassing detergent solubilization and reconstitution, this strategy not only preserves membrane proteins in their native lipid environment and functional state but also colocalizes ATP-producing and ATP-consuming modules within a single nanoscale compartment. This colocalization reduces the dependence of ATP utilization on intervesicle transport, producing a 3- to 4-fold kinetic enhancement at lower vesicle concentrations relative to nonintegrated controls. This light-rechargeable system offers a modular framework for versatile biohybrid energy nanosystems.

items.title: Interface Engineering of Magnetic Ni x Co3– x O4 Cathodes by Field Polarity for Li-O2 Batteries
items.abstract: Abstract Lithium-oxygen (Li-O2) batteries offer ultrahigh theoretical energy density, but sluggish cathodic oxygen reduction reaction (ORR)/oxygen evolution reaction (OER) kinetics restrict practical application. Here, magnetically tunable NixCo3–xO4 (NCOx) spinel cathode catalysts were prepared by regulating the Ni:Co ratio to clarify the relationship among catalyst magnetization, magnetic-field polarity, and Li-O2 battery performance. Increasing Ni content raises the fraction of high-spin octahedral Ni2+, enhancing saturation magnetization; NCO3 (Ni:Co = 2:1) exhibits the highest Ms (28 emu/g) and strongest response under 300 mT. Electrochemical impedance spectroscopy reveals a polarity-dependent effect: an N-pole field decreases Rct from 27.42 to 19.74 Ω, whereas an S-pole field increases Rct, likely because it aggravates the spin mismatch between catalyst electrons and triplet-state O2, thereby increasing the interfacial charge-transfer barrier. Density functional theory (DFT) descriptor calculations show that the high-spin (HS)-initialized reference configuration strengthens O2 adsorption (–2.95 eV) and exhibits more favorable calculated ORR/OER energetics than the low-spin (LS)-initialized reference configuration; these calculations do not explicitly simulate the external magnetic field. Under optimal NCO3/N-pole/300 mT conditions, the discharge voltage increases by 107 mV and cycling life exceeds 990 h at 0.2 mA cm–2. Scanning electron microscopy (SEM) observations show that the N-pole-facing magnetic-field condition changes the discharge-product morphology from irregular agglomerates to more uniformly distributed platelet-like structures. Ex situ Li 1s X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) is consistent with more extensive removal of Li2O2 containing products during recharge, although it does not by itself prove complete Li2O2 decomposition or suppression of Li2CO3 formation. This work establishes a cooperative strategy combining catalyst magnetic design and magnetic field regulation, providing insights into the rational design of magnetic field-assisted Li-O2 batteries.

items.title: Electronic Modulation Engineering of Pt-Modified TiO2 Nanotube-Confined Co Catalyst for Efficient Low-Temperature Catalytic Oxidation of CH3SH
items.abstract: Abstract Methanethiol (CH3SH) is a typical malodorous volatile organic pollutant, and its efficient low-temperature catalytic degradation remains both an urgent priority and a formidable challenge in odor abatement. Herein, we leveraged the unique curved surface architecture of titanium dioxide nanotubes ((TiO2 NTs) and developed a targeted electronic-modulation strategy in which cobalt (Co) species were confined within the nanotube channels via vacuum impregnation, followed by the photodeposition of platinum (Pt) onto the outer surface as an electron-withdrawing layer to yield a composite catalyst (Co@TiO2 NTs-Pt). Catalytic performance evaluations showed that Co@TiO2 NTs-Pt exhibits excellent low-temperature activity toward CH3SH oxidation, achieving approximately 95% conversion at room temperature and enabling complete oxidation of sulfur-containing intermediates at even lower temperatures than those required with Co@TiO2 NTs. Comprehensive characterization indicated that depositing Pt on the exterior surface enhances the electron-deficient environment within the nanotube cavity and induces surface lattice distortion, thereby raising the oxidation state of the confined Co species and increasing the concentration of oxygen vacancies. Density functional theory (DFT) calculations further confirmed that this electronic-modulation strategy significantly strengthens CH3SH chemisorption and activation on the catalyst surface. Furthermore, in situ diffuse reflectance infrared Fourier transform spectroscopy (DRIFTS) elucidated the reaction pathways governing CH3SH oxidation over the catalyst surface. Overall, this study deepens the understanding of electronic confinement effects in TiO2 NTs and provides a theoretical basis and technical guidance for designing advanced catalysts for the efficient low-temperature abatement of malodorous organic pollutants.

items.title: GSH/pH Dual-Responsive Zwitterionic mRNA Nanocomplexes for Tumor-Enriched mRNA Delivery in a B16F10 Melanoma Model
items.abstract: Abstract Messenger RNA (mRNA) therapy offers a programmable route to melanoma treatment, but its translation is limited by nuclease degradation, off-target biodistribution and endolysosomal trapping. Here we report a glutathione (GSH)/pH dual-responsive mRNA nanocomplex (mRNA-NC) fabricated by one-pot in situ polymerization of N-(3-aminopropyl)methacrylamide (APMA), 1-vinylimidazole (VI), N,N′-bis(acryloyl)cystamine (BACA), and 2-methacryloyloxyethyl phosphorylcholine (MPC) on the mRNA template. At an N/P ratio of 40, the carrier reached an encapsulation efficiency of 92.7 ± 2.1% and a loading capacity of 87.4 ± 3.2 μg mg–1, forming monodisperse particles of 126.4 ± 7.2 nm (polydispersity index, PDI, 0.14). The zwitterionic corona limited plasma protein adsorption to 12.6 ± 1.5 μg mg–1 (4.6-fold lower than jetPEI/mRNA), kept hemolysis at 0.8 ± 0.2%, and extended the serum half-life of the mRNA to ≈27.4 h, roughly 9-fold longer than naked mRNA. Release was gated by both triggers: 86.5 ± 3.7% of the cargo was released within 8 h under 10 mM GSH, whereas leakage under physiological conditions remained ≤ 12%; in a 4 h matrix, pH 5.5 plus 10 mM GSH released 85 ± 6.8% versus 12 ± 1.5% at pH 7.4 without GSH. In B16F10 cells, the nanocomplex was taken up in a dose- and energy-dependent manner, entered the lysosomal compartment, and escaped over time in a manner consistent with imidazole-mediated proton-sponge buffering (a hypothesis; intralysosomal pH was not measured directly), producing a peak firefly luciferase (FLuc) expression of 56,140 ± 3280 RLU mg–1 protein at 24 h, about 1.5-fold higher than jetPEI/mRNA, with 93.6 ± 3.9% cell viability and 6.7 ± 1.2% lactate dehydrogenase (LDH) release. In B16F10-bearing albino C57BL/6 mice, a single intravenous dose produced tumor-dominant bioluminescence (peak 5.7 × 106 photons s–1 at 6 h), a tumor enrichment index of 1.22 ± 0.18 (vs 0.31 ± 0.03 for jetPEI/mRNA) and 2.42 × 107 FLuc mRNA copies μg–1 tumor RNA at 12 h, while all 7-day safety indicators remained at phosphate-buffered saline (PBS) levels. These results demonstrate that a single zwitterionic nanocomplex can integrate stealth, dual-triggered release, and endosomal escape for safe, tumor-enriched mRNA delivery. While this study focuses on delivery performance and reporter gene expression, it lays a solid foundation for future therapeutic applications with functional mRNA.

items.title: Triarm Polycaprolactone Interface for Spatially Controlled Functionalization of Carbon Nanotube Fibers
items.abstract: Abstract Carbon nanotube fibers (CNTF) with exceptional strength, electrical, and thermal conductivities possess the potential for deployment in electrochemical and analytical applications. For such applications, CNTF are typically encapsulated using polymeric interface membranes such as polyvinyl chloride (PVC) for accommodating functional elements or recognition molecules. These membranes typically assemble stochastically on CNTF surfaces owing to the nonuniform interfacial interaction energies between the characteristic groups of the polymers and the CNTF surface. This stochastic assembly of encapsulating membranes subsequently inhibits the homogeneous distribution of recognition molecules on the CNTF surface, which influences the analytical performances. Herein, a triarm polycaprolactone (3-PCL) block copolymer is designed to homogenize the interfacial energies between the polymeric membranes and the CNTF surface. The 3-PCL interface is hypothesized to enable spatially controlled assembly of polymeric membranes on the CNTF surface and subsequently a homogeneous distribution of recognition molecules. As an illustration, the CNTF with a 3-PCL interface is demonstrated as an ion-selective microelectrode (ISE) for selective and sensitive detection of ammonium ions (NH4+) via homogeneous incorporation of a NH4+-specific ionophores within an encapsulating PVC membrane on the CNTF surface. An LOD and linear response range of 1 × 10–7 M and 1 × 10–7 to 1.0 × 10–1 M, respectively, were achieved. These values are an order higher as compared to ionophores incorporated within the PVC membrane on the CNTF surface without the 3-PCL interface. Further, a linear two-arm polymer (2-PCL) was evaluated as an interface for validation of significantly higher and stable analytical responses that could be achieved using the 3-PCL interface. Thus, the 3-PCL possesses the potential to be an ideal interface for incorporation of functional materials and recognition elements within polymeric membranes on the CNTF surface for the development of high-performance electrochemical and analytical devices.

items.title: Stable Magnesium Negative Electrodes Achieved via Dy Microalloying for Rechargeable Magnesium Batteries
items.abstract: Abstract Rechargeable magnesium batteries (RMBs) are a promising alternative technology to lithium-ion batteries owing to the abundant resources, high theoretical volumetric energy density, and relatively high safety. Nevertheless, the nonuniform deposition/dissolution behavior, interfacial passivation, and exacerbated polarization under high current densities of magnesium metal negative electrodes severely impede their practical implementation. In this study, we propose a Dy microalloying strategy to regulate the microstructure and deposition/dissolution behavior of the magnesium negative electrode. The incorporation of low-concentration Dy (0.7 wt %) induces grain refinement and crystal texture evolution and alleviates galvanic corrosion due to the similar electrode potentials of Dy and Mg. This synergistic effect enhances the electrochemical reaction kinetics, structural integrity, and interfacial stability, thereby improving the uniformity of Mg deposition/dissolution. Therefore, the Mg–0.7Dy alloy negative electrode achieves a long cycle life exceeding 2500 h in symmetric cells at 1 mA cm–2 and 1 mA h cm–2. Moreover, the Mg–0.7Dy∥Mo6S8 full cell maintains a specific capacity of 59.67 mA h g–1 after 4000 cycles at 5 C, corresponding to a high capacity retention of 93.84%. This work demonstrates the feasibility of regulating the microstructure and deposition/dissolution behavior of the magnesium negative electrode through Dy microalloying engineering, offering a feasible strategy for developing high-performance negative electrodes for RMBs.

items.title: Multidimensional Protein-Based Antimicrobial Materials: Construction, Mechanisms, and Applications
items.abstract: Abstract Bacterial contamination and associated infections remain persistent threats to global public health. Proteins, as renewable biomacromolecules with diverse functional groups, programmable hierarchical structures, and favorable biocompatibility, have emerged as versatile building blocks for antimicrobial materials. Through self-assembly, amyloid-like aggregation, interfacial engineering, and chemical or physical functionalization, proteins can be constructed into zero-dimensional (0D) micro/nanoparticles, one-dimensional (1D) fibers, two-dimensional (2D) films and coatings, and three-dimensional (3D) hydrogels, aerogels, and sponge scaffolds. Dimensional architecture extends beyond morphological classification: it governs active-site exposure, interfacial contact, mass transport, mechanical properties, and antimicrobial-agent retention and release, thereby determining bactericidal activity, resistance to bacterial adhesion, and antibiofilm performance. Nevertheless, the relationships connecting dimensional construction, interfacial structure, antimicrobial mechanism, and application-specific performance remain fragmented. This review therefore adopts dimensionality as the central framework for critically examining the structural design, assembly, and functionalization of protein-based antimicrobial materials across 0D–3D architectures. Particular emphasis is placed on how dimensional features regulate the antimicrobial mechanisms involving membrane disruption, cell-wall hydrolysis, reactive oxygen species generation, physical bacterial trapping, controlled antimicrobial release, and resistance to bacterial adhesion. Recent advances in the applications of these antimicrobial materials, categorized by their dimensional architectures, are further evaluated across biomedicine, food preservation, functional textiles, and agriculture in relation to their operating environments and functional requirements. Finally, challenges concerning mechanistic validation, long-term stability, scalable manufacturing, biological safety, and application-specific evaluation are critically discussed to identify barriers to practical implementation and future directions for technological translation. Emerging opportunities in AI-assisted protein and peptide design, precise interfacial engineering, and multifunctional integration are further highlighted to guide the rational development of next-generation protein-based antimicrobial materials.

items.title: Cellulose-Derived Water-Free, Anti-Freezing, and Self-Initiated Ionogel for Flexible Wearable Electronics
items.abstract: Abstract The growing demand for sustainable flexible electronics has positioned cellulose as a promising candidate, yet its efficient dissolution and functionalization remain challenging due to its highly crystalline structure and strong intermolecular hydrogen bonding. While a wide variety of cellulose dissolution systems have been reported in the literature, most systems still depend on toxic initiators or complex processes. Herein, we report a sunlight-driven, initiator-free green synthesis of cellulose-based ionogels that enables direct cellulose dissolution and in situ photopolymerization, which provides a facile and sustainable route to anti-freezing ionogels via the direct in situ polymerization of ionogel precursors without initiators or crosslinkers. Notably, the incorporation of cellulose, along with the intrinsic properties of the 1-butyl-3-methylimidazolium chloride ([Bmim]Cl) and ethylene glycol (EG) significantly enhanced the mechanical properties of the conductive ionogel, which exhibited outstanding mechanical performance (fracture strain of 935%, fracture stress of 166.5 kPa), robust adhesive properties (1.48 MPa), excellent conductivity (0.028 mS·cm–1) and wide work temperature range (–20∼60 °C). These properties enabled the ionogel to function not only as a wearable strain sensor for motion detection but also as a self-powered controller for operating a remote-controlled car via human-computer interaction. This work provides a versatile and sustainable strategy for fabricating high-performance cellulose ionogels, paving the high value-added way for future soft electronic systems with multifunctional integration.

items.title: Depth-Resolved Magnetic Reversal of La0.7Sr0.3Mn1– x Ru x O3-Based Synthetic Antiferromagnets
items.abstract: Abstract Synthetic antiferromagnets based on transition metal oxides provide a versatile platform for engineering magnetic functionalities beyond those of conventional metallic systems. However, the microscopic pathways by which their magnetization reverses remain difficult to determine because conventional magnetic measurements cannot resolve the layer-specific magnetic configurations that emerge during switching. Here, we combine polarized neutron reflectometry, magnetometry, magnetotransport, and an extended Stoner–Wohlfarth model to investigate the magnetization reversal mechanisms in epitaxial La0.7Sr0.3Mn1–xRuxO3/LaNiO3 multilayers. Depth-resolved polarized neutron reflectometry reveals non-collinear magnetic configurations that are hidden from macroscopic probes and identifies the competition between tilted magnetic anisotropy and comparable bilinear and biquadratic interlayer exchange interactions as the origin of the observed behavior. Depending on the magnetic-field orientation, the system undergoes either abrupt switching between magnetic fan and synthetic antiferromagnetic states or a gradual opening of the magnetic fan. Our results establish the intimate connection between magnetic anisotropy, interlayer exchange, and reversal dynamics in oxide synthetic antiferromagnets, revealing correlated oxides as a powerful platform for tuning the balance between competing interactions and engineering tailored magnetic reversal pathways and functionalities.

items.title: A Multicyclic Catalytic Network Enabling ROS Amplification, Metabolic Disruption, and Immune Modulation for Antitumor–Antibacterial Therapy
items.abstract: Abstract Intratumoral bacteria are increasingly recognized as important regulators of tumor progression, immune suppression, and metastasis, whereas current therapeutic strategies remain insufficient to address the coupled tumor–bacteria microenvironment. Here, we report a multicyclic catalytic network (VBC-Net) that integrates alkaline polyoxovanadate with a Bi2WO6–CuSx p–n heterojunction for coordinated antitumor–antibacterial immunotherapy. Unlike conventional single-mechanism nanozymes, VBC-Net establishes interconnected catalytic cycles that sustain ROS amplification, oxygen activation, and glutathione depletion, thereby converting transient catalytic activity into persistent oxidative stress. Simultaneously, the alkaline microenvironment and Bi-associated interference with respiratory-chain-related processes may contribute to metabolic perturbation, coupling oxidative stress with metabolic disruption. VBC-Net is further associated with dendritic-cell maturation, enhanced T-cell infiltration, and pro-inflammatory immune modulation, suggesting remodeling of the tumor–bacteria–immune microenvironment. In murine 4T1 tumor and MRSA-infected models, VBC-Net achieves pronounced tumor suppression, bacterial clearance, reduced metastatic progression, and accelerated wound healing with good biocompatibility. This work establishes a multicyclic catalytic strategy for targeting complex tumor-associated ecosystems and provides a promising framework for antitumor–antibacterial therapy.

items.title: Alkali-Assisted MOCVD Growth of Polycrystalline MoS2 with Micrometer-Scale Domains on Soda-Lime Glass
items.abstract: Abstract Achieving large-scale, uniform MoS2 films with reduced grain boundary density remains a central challenge for scalable device applications. Previous studies have reported that alkali-assisted growth promotes lateral domain expansion through eutectic intermediate formation. Here, metal–organic chemical vapor deposition (MOCVD) of MoS2 on commercial soda-lime glass is investigated. The intrinsic alkali content of soda-lime glass provides a uniform supply across the substrate, while partial surface softening at growth temperature facilitates the incorporation of Mo species within the near-surface region of the glass. The systematic variation of precursor flow conditions enables controlled modulation of nucleation density and domain size while suppressing graphitic carbon co-deposition arising from precursor ligand pyrolysis. High-quality polycrystalline MoS2 with lateral grain sizes ranging from ∼500 nm to 1.5 μm is achieved as uniform, coalesced centimeter-scale films, demonstrating the scalability of this method. Substrate roughness and wafer-to-wafer variability are key factors governing nucleation, highlighting opportunities for substrate optimization. To correlate the material properties with device performance, the films are wet-transferred and integrated into bottom-gated, top-contact field-effect transistors featuring either non-interdigitated or interdigitated source-drain electrodes. The devices exhibit on/off current ratios up to ∼107 and mobilities of ∼8 cm2 V–1 s–1. Overall, this work demonstrates an accessible and scalable route for the growth of electronic-grade polycrystalline MoS2 on soda-lime glass substrates.

items.title: Engineering Ambipolar Charge Transport in Stable Solution-Processed Nanofilms of Electrically Conductive Liquid-Crystalline Anthraquinones
items.abstract: Abstract The realization of ambipolar charge transport with long-term operational and environmental stability of the transport layer is a rarely addressed challenge in organic electronics, especially with respect to solution-processed devices. This study reports the molecular engineering of redox-active liquid-crystalline anthraquinones with triazole and cyanovinylene functional units to stabilize ordered columnar mesophases at room temperature. In addition to high thermal stability, solution-processed nanofilms of these discotic liquid crystals (DLCs) also demonstrate effective charge-extraction from injecting electrodes in diode devices, with their electrical conductivity values among the highest reported for DLC nanofilms (10–4 S/m). Alongside ultra-stable electrical performance over repeated electrical cycling, these devices exhibit long-term stability for up to two years without encapsulation under ambient storage conditions. Balanced ambipolarity is achieved via the fabrication of single-carrier devices where hole and electron mobilities both match at an order of 10–3 cm2/Vs. Being a pioneering report dedicated to detailed electrical conductivity studies and ambient stability of solution-processed ambipolar DLC films, the present work enriches the scope of practical DLC-based electronic devices from the fundamental viewpoint of molecular design.

items.title: Wet-Adhesive, Swelling-Resistant Hydrogels for Human-Machine Interaction and Underwater Physiological Signal Monitoring
items.abstract: Abstract With the advancement of flexible electronics, there has been a growing focus on monitoring physiological activity and health status. However, flexible electronic devices are prone to detaching under dynamic conditions or underwater environments, resulting in inaccurate and delayed signal transmission. This work employed a “one-pot method” to prepare a hydrogel (named DPE) with a three-dimensional network structure composed of [2-(methacryloyloxy)ethyl]dimethyl-(3-sulfopropyl)ammonium hydroxide (DMAPS), polyacrylic acid solution (PAA), and ethylene glycol dimethacrylate (EDMA). It demonstrates excellent wet-adhesion properties, superior swelling-resistant (swelling rate of 5.82%), water retention capacity (88.53%), self-healing properties, biocompatibility, and reliable detection of physiological signals both in air and underwater. Additionally, the hydrogel possesses a low modulus (7.62 kPa) and a good linear operating range (gauge factor = 4.41). Given these advantages, hydrogels are highly sensitive and reliable for monitoring human motion signals, transmitting Morse code, and acquiring bioelectric signals. At the same time, based on the electrical signals generated by the hydrogel bending at different angles, the hydrogel can also drive the robotic hand to perform actions. In addition, hydrogels are capable of capturing electromyographic (EMG) signals underwater and achieving 98.75% gesture recognition accuracy using deep learning algorithms. This multifunctional hydrogel opens up possibilities for the application of flexible wearable sensors in various environments and holds great potential for next-generation bioelectronic devices.

items.title: Peptide–DNA Hybrid Selection for Chemical Functionality Recognition across Diverse Material Interfaces
items.abstract: Abstract Sequence-defined affinity ligands are powerful tools for molecular recognition, yet their selection has largely focused on defined molecular targets rather than shared chemical functionalities. Extending sequence-based recognition to a chemical moiety presents a distinct challenge because the same functionality must be recognized across structurally and chemically diverse molecular and material contexts. Here, we demonstrate that in vitro selection of peptide–DNA hybrids can generate an affinity ligand that recognizes a shared chemical functionality across distinct molecular and material interfaces. Using carboxylates as a model functionality, we selected a peptide–DNA hybrid library against a carboxylated material surface and identified R8rank1, whose enhanced binding depended on the selected DNA sequence functioning within the peptide–DNA hybrid architecture. R8rank1 hybrid preferentially recognized carboxylate-containing polymers with distinct molecular backbones over polymers bearing other functionalities, including an anionic sulfonate-containing polymer, and retained its recognition behavior across chemically distinct gold and silica nanoparticle interfaces presenting surface carboxylates. Fluorescently labeled R8rank1 further distinguished carboxylated from hydroxylated silica nanoparticles with an approximately eightfold difference in fluorescence and exhibited an apparent Kd of approximately 390 nM for the carboxylated surface, whereas the two surfaces were not significantly differentiated by zeta-potential measurements. This affinity-based readout provides chemical-functionality information complementary to conventional surface charge characterization. These findings extend sequence-based affinity selection from defined molecular targets to shared chemical functionalities and establish peptide–DNA hybrids as a selectable molecular recognition platform for identifying chemical functionalities across diverse material interfaces.

items.title: Ultrasound-Responsive Iron-Barium Titanate Schottky Heterojunction-Embedded Hydrogel Accelerates Burn Wound Healing through Bidirectional Hydrogen-Piezocatalytic Redox Modulation
items.abstract: Abstract Burn wound healing is regulated by a spatiotemporal redox hierarchy, where early reactive oxygen species (ROS) overload drives inflammation, while late ROS deficiency hinders regeneration. Programming this bidirectional sequence requires time-phased, counter-directional ROS control. Herein, we report a nanocomposite hydrogel that integrates hydrogen therapy with piezocatalytic therapy, enabling on-demand redox programming across the entire healing cascade. The system constructs a metal-semiconductor Schottky heterojunction derived from the in situ reduction of Fe2+ within the mesopores of barium titanate. The mesoporous confinement and interfacial coupling program the hydrolysis of nanoscale zero-valent iron for sustained, early-stage hydrogen delivery to scavenge toxic ROS, while the established Schottky barrier efficiently suppresses charge recombination, thereby executing ultrasound-triggered piezoelectric polarization and charge separation for on-demand ROS generation in later-stage pro-regenerative signaling. Embedded within a polyacrylamide/carboxymethyl chitosan double-network hydrogel with inherent antibacterial activity, the resulting system exhibits superior antioxidant capacity and piezocatalytic responsivity, as well as promotion of fibroblast migration, angiogenesis, and M2 macrophage polarization. In a mouse burn model, this redox-programmable platform orchestrates phased healing, attenuating early inflammation, sustaining neovascularization, and suppressing late fibrosis, achieving accelerated wound closure. Collectively, this work establishes a redox programming paradigm via heterojunction catalysis, coupling spatiotemporal ROS scavenging and generation for dynamic tissue regeneration.

items.title: Microfluidic Control of Biomolecular Condensate Growth Reveals Scaling Crossover and Interfacial Regulation
items.abstract: Abstract Biomolecular condensates, formed via phase separation, play vital roles in cellular organization, yet their nucleation and growth dynamics remain poorly understood, particularly under controlled physiological conditions. Here, we employ a microfluidic platform to precisely manipulate the nucleation and growth of PGL-3 protein condensates at fluid–solid interfaces. We demonstrate that ionic strength and co-phase-separating proteins (SEPA-1) robustly tune the nucleation rate without altering the long-term growth scaling ∼tn. Single-condensate tracking further resolves a dynamic scaling crossover from rapid isolated growth with n ≃ 1/2 to diffusion-limited collective growth with n ≃ 1/3, consistent with simulations of overlapping protein-depletion fields. Furthermore, we show that this classical scaling breaks down during viscoelastic phase separation, where elastic-dominated condensates exhibit a significantly reduced exponent. Our work establishes molecular modulation and interfacial mechanics as key regulators of condensate dynamics, revealing physical principles that govern the size and material state of biological condensates.

items.title: Geometry-Driven Ultrahigh Current Density Field Emission from Vertically Oriented MXene Film Edge Emitters
items.abstract: Abstract MXenes are promising cold cathode materials owing to their high electrical conductivity, solution processability, and tunable surface terminations; however, realizing high-current-density field emission from MXene film emitters remains challenging because their planar two-dimensional geometry generally provides limited field concentration and restricts the number of field-activated emission sites. Here, we demonstrate a geometry-driven strategy to achieve high-current-density field emission from vertically oriented MXene film edge emitters. By systematically controlling the film height and inter-electrode gap, the optimized emitter achieves a current density of 5020 mA cm–2 at 1520 V, which is more than an order of magnitude higher than the values reported for previous MXene field emitters. Enhanced performance is not governed by the field enhancement factor alone. Instead, it is enabled by the balance between sufficient local field enhancement and a large effective emission area. Experimental Fowler–Nordheim analysis, emission pattern imaging, and the screening-corrected field-enhancement model indicate that excessive field concentration can promote edge-localized emission and reduce the effective emission area, whereas the optimized geometry enables distributed edge emission with improved stability. These findings establish edge-geometry engineering as a design principle for transforming two-dimensional MXene films into high-current-density cold cathodes for vacuum nanoelectronics.

items.title: Harmonized Na-Site Occupancy and Fe Local Structure in a Mixed-Phosphate Cathode for All-Climate Sodium-Ion Batteries
items.abstract: Abstract Na4Fe3(PO4)2P2O7 (NFPP) has attracted considerable attention as a low-cost, structurally stable cathode for sodium-ion batteries. However, its commercialization is severely hampered by electrochemically inert impurities from conventional synthesis and insufficient energy density. Herein, we report a heteroatom-free strategy combining precursor pathway engineering with Na-site regulation and local Fe-environment modulation to synthesize a phase-pure NFPP-type cathode using a nominal Na3.67Fe2.67(PO4)1.67(P2O7) precursor stoichiometry. The resulting N3.67F2.67PP sample exhibits distinct Na-site occupancies from conventional NFPP. Theoretical calculations and experimental characterizations demonstrate that increased occupation ratios of Na4 and Na2 sites collectively elevate the discharge voltage plateau and enhance cycling stability. Meanwhile, precise regulation of the Na/Fe/PO4/P2O7 ratio modulates the electronic structure of Fe and increases Fe–O coordination disorder, markedly boosting Na+ migration kinetics and electronic conductivity. Consequently, the optimized material delivers a high specific capacity of 110.4 mAh g–1 at 0.1 C, retains 98.6% of its capacity after 1700 cycles at 1 C, and exhibits an impressive 103.5 mAh g–1 at 10 C. It also exhibits superior performance over a wide temperature range from –40 to 60 °C. Notably, Ah-level pouch and cylindrical batteries assembled with kilogram-scale materials achieve outstanding performance, highlighting a practical route toward commercialization. This work clarifies the structure–property relationship of NFPP-based materials and provides valuable guidance for designing high-performance mixed-phosphate cathodes.

items.title: Effective Suppression of Cu+-Migration Assisted Degradation in Perovskite Solar Cells with Cu2O as the Hole Transport Layer
items.abstract: Abstract Formamidinium-based double-cation perovskite solar cells exhibit rapid performance degradation when the Cu2O hole transport layer is in direct contact with the perovskite. This degradation is attributed to Cu+ migration into the perovskite lattice, causing structural distortion and the formation of CuI and PbI2. X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy detects Cu+ ions even at the antipodal surface of the perovskite, indicating long-range diffusion of the Cu+ ions, probably through grain-boundary migration. To suppress this, a thin film of benzotriazole is introduced at the Cu2O/perovskite interface as a diffusion-blocking layer that also provides mild surface passivation. Adding poly(acrylonitrile-co-methyl acrylate) to the perovskite synthesis solution passivates the grain boundaries and further prevents the migration of Cu+ towards the perovskite. These modifications effectively curb Cu+ migration and its reaction with the perovskite. Consequently, p-i-n perovskite solar cells with the architecture ITO/Cu2O/perovskite/C60/BCP/Ag, incorporating both modifications, exhibit a significant improvement in power conversion efficiency, from ≈4.7 to 14.4%.

items.title: Molecular Anchoring and Multiscale Porosity Synergize in 3D Printed Polyimide Composites for High-Temperature Thermal Management
items.abstract: Abstract The large-scale application of energy storage systems such as lithium-ion batteries, which feature high energy density and considerable flammability risks, has created an urgent demand for thermal management materials that offer lightweight construction, high-temperature resistance, efficient insulation, and customizable shaping. Polyimide (PI) is a promising candidate; however, its additive manufacturing is constrained by the high temperatures required for thermal imidization and the severe shrinkage that accompanies this process. To overcome these limitations, herein, an interfacial chemical anchoring strategy is introduced, through which amino-functionalized hollow glass microspheres (HGMs) are covalently integrated into a soluble PI matrix. The achieved composite ink is well-suited for vapor-induced phase separation (VIPS)-assisted direct ink writing (DIW), allowing in situ porosification. The 3D printed constructs thus feature a hierarchical thermal resistance architecture, including macroscopic air gaps from printing, microporous networks derived from phase separation, and hollow HGM cavities, which synergistically suppresses solid conduction, gas convection, and thermal radiation. In addition, the covalently anchored microspheres also serve as crosslinking nodes, enhancing compressive strength. The optimized composites achieve a 35% reduction in density, shrinkage below 5%, a thermal conductivity of 0.048 W·m–1·K–1, and a nearly fourfold improvement in compressive strength. Together, these results demonstrate that the synergy between interfacial chemical anchoring and VIPS-assisted DIW provides a versatile platform for engineering lightweight, high-strength insulation components with tailored geometries for demanding high-temperature applications.

items.title: D-A-D Engineered Electrochromic Coordination Metallopolymers for Smart Windows, Energy Storage, and Wearables
items.abstract: Abstract Electrochromic coordination metallopolymers featuring multi-redox centers and structural versatility offer great potential for smart windows and glazing, yet they are hampered in practical application owing to the intrinsic trade-off between optical modulation and charge storage. Herein, we introduce a benzothiadiazole acceptor to construct a donor–acceptor–donor architecture that enhances intramolecular charge transfer and enables intervalence charge transfer, narrowing the bandgap and improving near-infrared electrochromism and capacitance. The resulting BT-CMP//V2O5 device exhibits large optical contrast (ΔT &gt; 50%), fast switching (1.7/3.8 s), and high coloration efficiency (&gt;300 cm2·C–1), enabling efficient photothermal modulation with an annual energy saving of 155.19 MJ·m–2. The D-A-D architecture facilitates rapid and complete charge separation, endowing the polymer with superior energy storage performance, including a high areal capacitance of 38.24 mF·cm–2. Furthermore, flexible prototypes exhibit EC and energy storage, maintain stable performance after 100 bending cycles. This D-A-D strategy provides a versatile platform to overcome the intrinsic trade-off of electrochromic materials, paving the way for high-performance electrochromic energy storage devices.

items.title: Multiscale Intercalation Strategies for Reconstructing Lamellar MXene Membranes
items.abstract: Abstract Lamellar MXene membranes, constructed by stacking MXene nanosheets to form two-dimensional nanochannels with ultrafast transport and sieving ability, have emerged as a promising platform for molecular and ionic separations as well as osmotic energy harvesting. However, the performance of these MXene membranes is often constrained by swelling-induced unstable nanochannels and monotonous chemistry environments within nanochannels. One of the most effective routes to these challenges lies in the incorporation of functional intercalation matters into the confined nanochannels of MXene, which not only orchestrate interlayer spacing and nanochannel chemistry but also improve stability by forming multiple interactions with neighboring nanosheets. Over the past decade, a series of multiscale intercalation matters have been designed and explored, mainly spanning from ions to small molecules, polymers, and nanomaterials. Despite significant achievements, a timely and comprehensive review that systematically elucidates how various multiscale intercalation matters reconstruct MXene membranes is missing. In this review, we discuss recent advances in intercalation strategies for lamellar MXene membranes, categorized by the chemical nature and dimensionality of the intercalating matters. We underscore their critical roles in modulating both the structural and chemical features of nanochannels, and we systematically analyze the corresponding effects on transport behavior and separation performance. Finally, some key unresolved challenges and future directions are highlighted to guide the design and synthesis of high-performance lamellar MXene membranes.

items.title: A Rutin–Glycyrrhizic Acid Self-Assembled Nanohydrogel Promotes Early Osteogenic Differentiation Potential and Antioxidant Activity via Synergistic Inhibition of the IL-1β/NF-κB Axis
items.abstract: Abstract Plant-derived natural compounds have gained increasing attention in biomaterial development due to their intrinsic bioactivity and favorable biocompatibility. The anti-inflammatory, antioxidant, and osteogenic properties of rutin and glycyrrhizic acid have rendered them increasingly attractive candidates for therapeutic biomaterial development. However, their poor bioavailability significantly restricts their broad biomedical applications.
