Inspired by a supramolecular self-assembly strategy, we successfully constructed a rutin–glycyrrhizic acid nanohydrogel (RU–GA). The microstructure and formation mechanism were investigated through experimental characterization and computational simulations. Rutin (RU) and glycyrrhizic acid (GA) self-assemble into a carrier-free hydrogel in aqueous solution via hydrogen bonding and π–π stacking interactions, exhibiting favorable injectability, shapeability, and stability. RU–GA can disperse in water and release rutin–glycyrrhizic acid nanoparticles (RG NPs) with homogeneous particle sizes, while the hydrogel material possesses degradation and sustained-release properties. The bioavailability of RU and GA is synergistically improved through size effects and continuous release. Notably, the RU–GA hydrogel significantly promotes antioxidant activity and early osteogenic differentiation potential relative to the individual monomer components. Bioinformatics analysis further suggested that these bioactivities are associated with IL1B. Il1b knockdown experiments validated that RU and GA may synergistically suppress IL-1β-mediated NF-κB activation, thereby reducing oxidative stress and enhancing early osteogenic differentiation potential. Collectively, the rutin–glycyrrhizic acid nanohydrogel (RU–GA) represents a promising functional biomaterial, providing a strategy for the broad application of natural compounds in biomedical and related fields.

items.title: Monolithic Fabrication of Flexible Optoelectronic Neuromorphic Synapses with Bandgap-Engineered Centimeter-Scale SnSe2 van der Waals Layers
items.abstract: Abstract The transition of bandgap energies in two-dimensional (2D) materials driven by their miniaturization opens up opportunities for emerging device technologies unattainable with conventional approaches. Herein, “all” 2D optoelectronic synapse devices are reported employing the transition characteristics of wafer-scale 2D tin diselenide (SnSe2) layers directly grown on polymeric substrates at a low temperature of 300 °C. Specifically, a significant thickness-dependent reduction in their band energy from 0.8 to 0.25 eV enables a “monolithic” fabrication of flexible device arrays composed of extremely thin active/passive components; i.e., n-type semiconducting 2D channels seamlessly interfaced with heavily doped metallic-like 2D electrodes. These 2D/2D interfaces exhibit reliable Ohmic transports without the need for work function engineering of contact metals as well as well-preserved mechanical deformability. A variety of optoelectronic synaptic properties are demonstrated in the all-2D devices, including deformation-invariant plasticity updates, which are implementable for high-accuracy pattern recognition of artificial neural networks (ANNs). This study suggests new methodologies for integrating the dimensionally tunable electrical properties of near atom-thickness materials into their scalable manufacturability for emergent neuromorphic applications.

items.title: Repurposing Grain Boundaries for Graphene Origami Auxetic Metamaterials with Enhanced Fatigue Resistance
items.abstract: Abstract Graphene represents the pinnacle of intrinsic material strength, yet it remains functionally limited by a lack of plasticity and severe degradation in mechanical performance associated with porosity-driven upscaling. Although graphene origami (GOri) offers a deterministic alternative to porous networks, its realization has been restricted to chemically functionalized, metastable frameworks. Here, we demonstrate a computational design strategy that repurposes grain boundaries (GBs) observed in large-scale chemical vapor deposited (CVD) graphene as topological precursors for stable GOri structures. Using molecular dynamics (MD) simulations, we show that periodic pentagon–heptagon (5–7) ring arrays within the tilted GBs can facilitate out-of-plane corrugations of the graphene domains, mimicking macroscopic folding creases without chemical modification. Our study also shows that the mechanical response of the proposed structure is highly tunable via linear grain size (µ) and dimensionless aspect ratio (α), enabling a wide range of control over tensile strength, elastic modulus, and negative Poisson’s ratio (NPR), reaching –3.77. Furthermore, the developed GB-GOri architecture achieves a 20% enhancement in fatigue strength and a fatigue life exceeding 150% of that of functionalized counterparts through pseudo-plastic deformation. Effectively, this GB-assisted defect engineering promotes stable crack growth and provides proof-of-concept for the future experimental fabrication of graphene-based auxetic metamaterials.

items.title: Potential-Dependent Hydricities and Bond Dissociation Free Energies of Metal Surface Hydrides
items.abstract: Abstract Recent experimental studies demonstrate that the thermodynamic hydricity of surface-bound intermediates is continuously tunable via electrical polarization. Canonical density functional theory relies on constant-charge models that fail to capture this potential-dependent polarization at the electrified solid-liquid interface. This work implements grand-canonical density functional theory (GC-DFT) to compute the surface hydricity, bond dissociation free energy (BDFE), and acidity of chemisorbed hydrogen across transition metal facets. Assuming an outer-sphere transfer isolates the intrinsic hydrogen-donating capacity of the active site. By explicitly controlling the system Fermi level, we demonstrate that surface hydricity exhibits a universal linear dependence on applied cathodic bias across all evaluated facets. In contrast, the potential dependence of the homolytic BDFE is strictly governed by material identity: platinum maintains a relatively static bond strength, while silver and copper exhibit potential-induced bond stabilization. The computed hydricity slopes for Pt facets quantitatively reproduce the experimentally measured polarization-dependent hydride-transfer sensitivity. Coordination geometry dictates the baseline donor capacity, with lower coordination atop sites on Ag and Cu functioning as significantly stronger hydride donors. Adlayer saturation perturbs the thermodynamic values in a metal-dependent manner, weakening hydride donation on silver but strengthening it on copper. However, at the two coverages examined, it does not substantially alter the voltage sensitivity of the thermodynamic properties. Evaluating voltage-dependent hydricity provides a thermodynamic framework for characterizing the intrinsic hydride- or hydrogen-donating ability of electrified solid-liquid interfaces.

items.title: Nanofibrous Thermo-Optical Materials for Spacecraft Passive Thermal Control
items.abstract: Abstract Passive thermal control is essential for spacecraft operating in extreme extraterrestrial environments, where minimizing solar heat absorption while maximizing thermal radiation is critical for maintaining acceptable onboard temperatures without additional energy consumption. Here, electrospun nanofibrous materials, represented by a polymeric polytetrafluoroethylene:polyethylene oxide (PTFE:PEO) composite and ceramic silica, are introduced as a new class of lightweight spacecraft thermal control materials combining ultrahigh solar reflectance (or ultralow solar absorptance), strong infrared emittance, and environmental durability. Under flight-representative conditions in NASA's deep-space thermal simulator, including the cryogenic radiative background of deep space (&lt;20 K), high vacuum (10–6 Torr), and AM0 solar irradiation (1367 W m–2), PTFE:PEO and silica nanofibers reached equilibrium temperatures of 143.2 and 137.4 K, respectively, compared with 281.4 K for aluminum foil. These values correspond to temperature reductions of 138.2 and 144 K, respectively, relative to aluminum foil. Complementary thermal modeling demonstrated that nanofibrous materials could reduce heat ingress relative to conventional multilayer insulation (MLI). Equivalent thermal performance could be achieved with substantially thinner and lighter nanofibrous insulation. Furthermore, the silica nanofibers showed about 60% greater resistance to atomic oxygen than Kapton, while thermal treatment significantly improved the atomic oxygen resistance of PTFE:PEO. These findings demonstrate the potential of electrospun nanofibrous architectures for passive thermal control of spacecraft and emerging space-based infrastructure, where favorable thermo-optical performance, environmental durability, and low mass are critical.

items.title: Electric-Field-Driven Surface Ionic Transport on Hydroxylated SiO2 Governs Transient Leakage and Hybrid Bonding Reliability
items.abstract: Abstract Cu/SiO2 hybrid bonding is critical for 3D integrated circuit packaging, where dielectric surface activation impacts bonding quality and long-term reliability. NaOH-based wet chemical activation is a promising approach for a scalable and cost-effective processing under ambient conditions. However, this route introduces residual ions at the SiO2 surface, raising concerns regarding electrical leakage and dielectric stability. In this study, electric-field-driven surface ionic transport on NaOH-activated SiO2 and its role in transient leakage and hybrid bonding reliability were investigated. Reversible and polarity-dependent transient current peaks observed in cyclic electrical measurements provide evidence for electric-field-driven migration of the mobile ionic species at the SiO2 interface. In addition, higher NaOH concentrations promoted greater residual Na+ accumulation and intensified transient leakage peaks, supporting the selection of 0.5 M NaOH as an effective activation condition. Systematic decoupling experiments demonstrate that residual mobile Na+ ions are the dominant contributors to the transient leakage current rather than fixed hydroxyl groups. Quantitative analysis reveals Na+ surface mobility of approximately 3 × 10–10 m2V–1s–1, an order-of-magnitude upper-bound estimate that is consistent between constant-bias and ramped-bias measurements and about six orders of magnitude higher than that in bulk SiO2, suggesting a surface-dominated transport. An optimized 3 min deionized water (DI) rinse reduces the mobile Na+ population below the electrical detection limit and decreases the Na 1s XPS intensity by roughly an order of magnitude, suppressing the transient leakage to near-baseline levels while maintaining hydrophilicity and achieving the SiO2–SiO2 bonding strength of 19.7 ± 1.8 MPa, comparable to Ar plasma activation. The leakage measurements were performed on Cu/SiO2 damascene comb structures, whereas the bonding validation addresses the dielectric part of the hybrid-bonding interface; Cu–Cu contact and long-term stress testing remain to be verified. This work provides a framework for understanding electric-field-driven surface ionic transport and practical guidelines for contamination control of the dielectric surface in wet-activated Cu/SiO2 hybrid bonding.

items.title: All 3D-Printed Conducting Polymer Hydrogel-Based Soft Surface Electromyography Electrode Array for Noninvasive Fatigue Assessment
items.abstract: Abstract High-density surface electromyography (sEMG) electrode arrays allow the recording of rich myoelectric signals and provide a useful approach for monitoring exercise-induced muscle fatigue. However, existing sEMG electrode arrays often suffer from mechanical mismatches between conventional rigid electrodes and soft tissues, as well as complex fabrication processes and limited programmability, which severely constrain the rational design and practical application of sEMG electrode arrays. Herein, we successfully fabricate an eight-channel PEDOT:PSS-PVA hydrogel-based soft sEMG electrode array via a multi-material 3D printing. Through systematic rheological characterization of the composite inks and rational design of a printable three-layer electrode architecture, we achieve seamless interfacial integration and integrated sequential fabrication. The as-prepared sEMG electrode array exhibits exceptional softness comparable to that of human soft tissues (Young’s modulus ∼ 10 kPa), low electrochemical impedance (∼22 Ω), and good electrochemical stability. Leveraging these advantageous properties, our sEMG electrode array enables noninvasive sEMG signal recording and monitoring of fatigue-associated sEMG changes with a high signal-to-noise ratio (SNR &gt; 20 dB) under various grip forces before and after exercise, and captures sEMG changes associated with fatigue progression during repetitive movements. These results validate the capability of our electrode array for high-quality sEMG monitoring of fatigue-associated electrophysiological features and open up promising avenues for future applications such as scientific athletic training.

items.title: Reticular Materials as Optical Sensors of Volatile Organic Compounds for Healthcare and Environmental Monitoring
items.abstract: Abstract Volatile organic compounds (VOCs) are a family of molecules that possess high vapor pressure and are regarded as air pollutants that prevail in both indoor and outdoor settings. Prolonged exposure to VOCs poses a serious risk to human health. On the other hand, VOCs emitted by humans and plants have been recognized as key biomarkers to estimate the status of health and physiology in living beings. Profiling the total content of VOCs in human and plant fluids leads to early diagnosis of diseases and timely treatment. Monitoring the presence of VOCs, either to track air pollution or to estimate the status of health, has therefore commanded increasing attention. Among the various techniques, optical sensing methods have been sought after owing to the considerations of their fast response time, versatility, miniaturization and portability, as well as the possibility of performing non-invasive detection. Advanced functional materials, such as porous reticular solids, including metal-organic frameworks (MOFs), covalent organic frameworks (COFs), and hydrogen-bonded organic frameworks (HOFs), are well suited not only as sorbents for the detection and capture of VOCs but also as suitable substrates for various approaches of optical signaling. This review, through recent case studies, presents the advances in the optical sensing of VOCs by reticular materials. In addition, a comparative analysis between various reticular material types has been provided, along with an outline of the current challenges and the opportunities that exist for future research.

items.title: Integrated 3D Porous Copper@BiSb Alloy Anodes via Pulse Electrodeposition for High-Performance Potassium-Ion Storage
items.abstract: Abstract Antimony (Sb) and bismuth (Bi) are promising alloy-type anode materials for potassium-ion batteries (PIBs), yet Sb suffers from a massive 390% volume expansion during potassiation, while Bi is limited by a relatively low specific capacity of 384 mAh·g–1. Moreover, existing synthesis methods for BiSb alloys are complex, costly, and require binders or conductive additives that impair electrochemical performance. Herein, we innovatively fabricate an integrated 3D porous copper@BiSb (3DPC@BiSb) electrode by pulse electrodepositing BiSb alloy onto a 3D porous copper (3DPC) substrate. The 3DPC scaffold provides abundant active sites, shortens ion diffusion pathways, and mitigates volume expansion, while the binder-free design eliminates interfacial issues. Electrochemical tests demonstrate that the 3DPC@BiSb electrode delivers a reversible capacity of 400.6 mAh·g–1 at 0.1 A·g–1 after 100 cycles and retains 205.0 mAh·g–1 even at 32 C, outperforming most reported alloy-type anodes for PIBs. Kinetic analysis, ex-situ X-ray diffraction, and density functional theory (DFT) calculations reveal that the superior performance originates from the synergistic effect of Sb (high capacity) and Bi (structural stability), enhanced K+ adsorption energy, and reduced diffusion barrier. This work provides a scalable strategy for fabricating integrated alloy anodes capable of large-area electrode preparation. It offers insights into the structure-performance relationship of BiSb-based materials, advancing the development of high-performance thin-film PIBs for renewable energy storage.

items.title: Room-Temperature Phosphorescent Materials Based on β-Diketone Derivatives Exhibiting Excitation- & Concentration-Dependent Characteristics
items.abstract: Abstract Room-temperature phosphorescence (RTP) materials have attracted extensive attention owing to their potential applications in chemical sensing, optoelectronic devices, bioimaging, and information encryption. However, developing RTP materials with dynamically tunable emission colors that respond to multiple external stimuli remains a significant challenge. In this work, BA@TTA composites were constructed by doping 2-thenoyltrifluoroacetone (TTA) guest molecules into a boric acid (BA) host matrix, exhibiting efficient room-temperature afterglow. Upon changing the excitation wavelength from 254 nm to 365 nm, the afterglow emission color can be tuned from blue to yellow, indicating prominent excitation-wavelength-dependent luminescence behavior. Moreover, with increasing TTA content, the yellow afterglow under 365 nm excitation is gradually enhanced, whereas the blue afterglow component under 254 nm excitation remains nearly unchanged. This excitation- & concentration-dependent color-tunable phosphorescence of BA@TTA originates from the coexistence of isolated and aggregated TTA species, in which efficient intermolecular energy transfer and aggregation-induced electronic interactions reduce the excited-state energy gap, enhance spin–orbit coupling, and accelerate intersystem crossing, thereby enabling color-tunable room-temperature phosphorescence. This universal mechanism is extended to other β-diketone derivatives for high-security multi-level information encryption.

items.title: Selenium-Integrated MoO3 Composite Cathode for Rechargeable Magnesium Batteries
items.abstract: Abstract Owing to their high volumetric capacity, potential for low-dendrite metal deposition, and abundance of natural magnesium, rechargeable magnesium batteries (RMBs) have garnered significant interest as potential substitutes for lithium-based systems. Nevertheless, sluggish Mg2+ diffusion and the polyselenide shuttle effect in selenium-based cathodes continue to restrict their practicality. In this work, a Se-MoO3 composite cathode was prepared by solvothermal synthesis of a MoSe2 precursor followed by annealing in air. Compact MoSe2 nanosheets were annealed to create an open hierarchical Se-MoO3 architecture composed of vertically oriented nanosheets associated with MoO3 nanoribbons. The Se-MoO3 cathode delivers 312 mAh g–1 at cycle 80 at 200 mA g–1. At 500 mA g–1, the capacity reaches 237 mAh g–1 at cycle 79 and decreases to 76.8 mAh g–1 at cycle 500. Ex situ measurements reveal reversible changes in the Mo and Se chemical states during cycling, supporting the participation of both components in charge storage. Although the close association between the Se-containing phase and MoO3 may influence the electrochemical response, the present data do not directly establish interface-specific polyselenide adsorption or catalytic conversion. Overall, this work emphasizes compositional and architectural modification as a viable approach for enhanced magnesium-ion storage.

items.title: In Memoriam: Professor T. Randall Lee, a Distinguished Professor and a Dedicated Mentor with an Impactful Legacy
Superhydrophobic Self-Cleaning Polyvinyl Alcohol-Based Films for Enhanced Passive Radiative Cooling and Durability
items.abstract: Abstract Developing sustainable and durable superhydrophobic passive radiative cooling materials is crucial for reducing building energy consumption in a warming world, yet conventional radiative cooling materials often rely on nonrenewable polymeric substrates and fluorosiloxane-based surface modifiers, and present materials have poor durability of superhydrophobicity under harsh conditions, limiting their environmental sustainability and long-term applicability. Herein, we develop a biomass-derived superhydrophobic radiative cooling film by integrating waste straw cellulose with starch and poly(vinyl alcohol) as a renewable film-forming matrix, TiO2 as a solar-reflection filler, and a fluorosiloxane-free surface engineering strategy. The resulting cooling film exhibits a solar reflectance of 76.06% and an infrared emissivity of 96.66% within the atmospheric window. The film achieves an average temperature reduction of 28.2 °C relative to the blank cavity during the test period. Moreover, the superhydrophobic surface imparts excellent self-cleaning capability and enables the film to withstand acid/alkali corrosion, water washing, and prolonged high-temperature treatment (&gt;100 °C for 8 h), demonstrating its robust environmental durability. Beyond passive thermal regulation, the cooling film exhibits an excellent water collection rate of 2476.2 mg cm–2 h–1. The combination of renewable agricultural waste as the structural feedstock, fluorosiloxane-free superhydrophobicity, efficient solar reflection, high infrared emission, and multifunctional environmental stability distinguishes the cooling film from conventional petroleum-based radiative cooling systems. This work provides a sustainable materials-design strategy for converting agricultural waste into multifunctional radiative cooling materials with potential applications in energy-efficient building envelopes and sustainable thermal management.

items.title: Fe-Regulated Sulfidation of Ni-MOF to Construct an Fe-Ni(OH)2/Ni3S2 Heterojunction for Efficient Hydrogen Evolution in Both Acidic and Alkaline Media
items.abstract: Abstract Developing efficient and durable non-precious electrocatalysts for the hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) in both acidic and alkaline media is a critical challenge. Herein, we report a Fe-regulated sulfidation strategy that converts a Ni-MOF precursor into a Fe-doped Ni(OH)2/Ni3S2 heterojunction catalyst. Fe acts as a kinetic phase regulator that suppresses the complete conversion of Ni(OH)2 into Ni3S2, stabilizing a mixed phase architecture with abundant heterointerfaces and enlarged electrochemically active surface area. The optimized catalyst delivers exceptional HER performance, requiring overpotentials of only 163.3 mV at –10 mA cm−2 in 1 M KOH and 214.3 mV at –100 mA cm−2 in 0.5 M H2SO4, along with outstanding durability (200 h at –500 mA cm−2 in alkaline electrolyte and 100 h at –100 mA cm−2 in acidic electrolyte). Post-stability characterizations reveal pH-dependent reconstruction: under alkaline conditions, the Ni(OH)2 phase partially dissolves while the Ni3S2 framework remains; under acidic conditions, Fe2+ oxidation to Fe3+ forms a protective M-OH-rich oxide layer on Ni3S2. Density functional theory calculations identify Ni as the primary active site, with Fe functioning as an electronic modulator that redistributes electron density toward Ni and optimizes the d-band center. In alkaline media, the cooperative charge effect and upshifted d-band center synergistically promote water dissociation, with OH* desorption identified as the rate-determining step; in acidic media, strong electrostatic attraction from the highly negatively charged Ni sites dominates H* adsorption. This work highlights the pivotal role of heterojunction engineering and phase regulation in designing durable pH-universal HER catalysts.

items.title: Quantitative Solvation Scale for Lithium Battery Electrolytes
items.abstract: Abstract Understanding electrolyte solvation is vital for developing advanced lithium batteries, as solvation structures dictate interfacial chemistry and performance. This study evaluates the reliability of conventional 1D NMR techniques (1H, 7Li, 19F, and 13C) for probing lithium solvation. We demonstrate that absolute chemical shifts often correlate poorly with solvating ability, leading to misleading interpretations—a finding cross-validated by FTIR and DOSY. We identify that the change in chemical shift (Δδ) from 13C NMR serves as a robust descriptor, provided that the probe solvent’s solvating ability matches the system. To overcome single-probe limitations, we introduce a multiprobe strategy using ethyl methyl carbonate (EMC), trifluoroethyl methyl carbonate (FEMC), and propylene carbonate (PC). This approach establishes a quantitative solvation scale across weak, intermediate, and strong solvating regimes. The resulting scale shows strong linear correlations with coordination ratios and solvating power, enabling precise linear free-energy relationships. We demonstrate the practical utility of this framework by accurately predicting lithium nitrate solubility and guiding electrolyte design. Ultimately, this work provides a reliable, broadly applicable methodology for advancing next-generation battery electrolytes. Most importantly, this work provides a lithium solvating strength series, offering a highly useful tool for researchers to compare common solvents.

items.title: A Biomimetic Cell Membrane-Coated Nanoreactor Reshapes ROS Homeostasis and Activates STING Pathway for Synergistic Chemodynamic–Immunotherapy
items.abstract: Abstract The combination of chemodynamic therapy (CDT) and immunotherapy offers a promising therapeutic paradigm for advanced cancer treatment, yet its translation is largely hindered by inadequate intratumoral reactive oxygen species (ROS) production and the lack of a robust link between ROS-induced cytotoxicity and durable immune activation. To address these challenges, we herein engineer a multifunctional biomimetic nanoplatform (ZMGM) by encapsulating Mn2+ and glucose oxidase (GOX) within zeolitic imidazolate framework-8 (ZIF-8), followed by surface functionalization with 4T1 breast cancer cell membranes. This design integrates three synergistic functions: (1) GOX depletes glucose and generates hydrogen peroxide (H2O2) within the acidic tumor microenvironment; (2) the produced H2O2 fuels the Mn2+-mediated Fenton-like reaction to amplify ROS production; and (3) Mn2+ simultaneously serves as a potent stimulator of interferon genes (STING) agonist, triggering type-I interferon responses and promoting dendritic cell maturation. Meanwhile, the homologous cancer cell membrane coating endows ZMGM with specific tumor homing and enhanced tumor localization. Both in vitro and in vivo findings demonstrate that ZMGM not only efficiently eradicates primary tumors but also induces a systemic antitumor immune response, characterized by increased CD8+ T cell infiltration, that effectively suppresses distant metastatic lesions. Notably, the synergistic CDT–STING immunotherapy achieves a primary tumor inhibition rate of 84.22% without obvious systemic toxicity. This work provides a paradigm for rationally designing a single nanoplatform that bridges ROS-mediated cell killing and innate immune activation, offering a promising avenue for combating metastatic triple-negative breast cancer.

items.title: Enzyme-Powered Nanomotor as a Mobile Immobilization Carrier for Facilitating the Enzymatic Degradation of Chitin
items.abstract: Abstract Chitin, the second most abundant biomass after cellulose on earth, can be degraded into chitin oligosaccharides (CHOS), which hold considerable commercial value. However, the sustainable bioconversion of chitin is impeded by its mass transfer limitations and poor accessibility of chitinase to the substrate. Herein, a Janus urease-powered nanomotor (JUNM) was synthesized via a facile approach and employed as an immobilization carrier for chitinase (Chi B) to improve the enzymatic production of CHOS. It was demonstrated that the structural asymmetry of JUNM enabled the asymmetric decomposition of urea, thereby achieving more efficient self-propulsion at low urea concentrations than a symmetric urease-powered nanomotor (UNM). The self-propulsive behavior of the resulting immobilized chitinase nanomotor (Chi B@JUNM) enhanced its enzymatic performance. Compared with the passive counterpart, the enhanced enzyme–substrate contact induced by the autonomous movement and by the substrate adsorption resulting from electrostatic interactions improved the substrate affinity (a 50% decrease in apparent Km) and led to a 53% increase in catalytic efficiency (apparent kcat·Km–1). Moreover, the immobilization of Chi B on JUNM exhibited typical advantages of enhanced stability and reusability. As a result, the final CHOS yield achieved by the self-propelled Chi B@JUNM (with 50 mM urea) was 1.34 and 2.15 times the yield of passive Chi B@JUNM and free Chi B, respectively. Taken together, the reported enzyme-powered nanomotor provided an efficient platform for chitin degradation and paved the way for the design of advanced immobilization carriers to facilitate enzymatic reactions.

items.title: A Repeatable Supramolecular Adhesive with Ultrastrong Underwater Adhesion, Self-Healing Ability, and Long-Term Stability
items.abstract: Abstract Repeatable adhesives attract enormous attention for their environmental friendliness and adaptability but suffer from weak adhesion when used in underwater conditions. Herein, we develop a supramolecular adhesive by incorporating quadruple hydrogen-bonded units into isocyanate-modified polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS) polymers. By synergistically utilizing interfacial covalent bonds and multiple hydrogen bonds, the supramolecular adhesive exhibits repeatable adhesion in air for at least 5 cycles and ultrastrong underwater adhesion of ∼9.37 MPa. The rapid establishment of covalent bonds on various substrate surfaces confers the adhesive with instantaneous and tough adhesion in both air and underwater environments. Reversible multiple hydrogen bonds within the adhesive polymers endow the material with self-healing performance. In addition, rheology analysis combined with mechanical tests revealed the thermal-responsive property of the adhesive. Taking advantage of the self-healing performance and thermal-responsive adhesion, the adhesive exhibits repeatable ability. This work deepens the understanding of multiple hydrogen bonds and isocyanate-modified PDMS polymers, enabling the fabrication of repeatable adhesives for industrial applications.

items.title: Template Mineralized, Decellularized Matrix-Alginate-Based Bioink Provides Structural Reinforcement in Caprine Ex Vivo Bone Defect Model
items.abstract: Abstract Clinical management of critical-sized bone defects (CSDs) remains a significant surgical problem. Current bioinks fail to support initial loading on bone tissue. In this study, goat-derived decellularized matrix (DCM) was used as a template for controlled mineralization, while alginate improved the printability and cellular viability. DCM proteins acted as a natural template for hydroxyapatite (HA) crystal nucleation and growth, mimicking bone nanocomposite chemistry while enhancing structural reinforcement. HA formation on DCM template was visualized by atomic force microscopy (AFM) analysis, characteristic phosphate (PO43–) peaks in attenuated total reflectance-Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy (ATR-FTIR), and the HA-specific (211) diffraction peak in X-ray diffraction (XRD). Mineralized DCM was blended with alginate to formulate printable bioinks. Rheological analysis showed dominant elastic behavior (G′ &gt; G″), shear-thinning flow, and rapid post-shear recovery. Mechanical testing further demonstrated enhanced compressive strength in HA-DCM-alginate constructs. Bioprinting with osteoblast cells demonstrated higher cellular viability in the mineralized ink while enhancing osteogenic differentiation, via both biochemical and biophysical signaling from the mineralized-DCM ink. In an ex vivo defect model, the HA-DCM-alginate system significantly increased the compressive properties of the defect construct, providing immediate structural reinforcement at the defect site. Overall, the current mineralized bioink can provide both mechanical support and bone regeneration and holds promising potential for surgical application.

items.title: Photoelectrochemical CO2 Reduction to CO by a Molecular Catalyst Attached to Pyrene-Terminated Silicon through Noncovalent Interactions
items.abstract: Abstract A ruthenium-based CO2 reduction catalyst immobilized on a Si photocathode through noncovalent π–π interactions is active for the photochemical conversion of CO2 to CO, with 34% ± 20% Faradaic efficiency with current densities of j = –(0.3 ± 0.1) mA cm–2 at –1.9 V vs Fc+/0 in an acetonitrile/water electrolyte solution under 1 sun illumination. Si photocathodes were functionalized with pyrene (p-Si–Py) using a Grignard methodology. A previously reported CO2 reduction catalyst, [Ru(tpy)(Mebim-py)(NCCH3)][PF6]2 (tpy = 2,2′:6′,2″-terpyridine, Mebim-py = 1-methylbenzimidazol-2-ylidene-3-(2′-pyridine)) was modified to include a pyrene moiety in the terpyridine backbone, enabling π–π stacking of the catalyst onto the Si surface to achieve a surface coverage of (1.85 ± 0.28) x 10–12 mol cm–2 (ca. 2% to 5% of a monolayer) as quantified via inductively coupled plasma mass spectroscopy (ICP-MS). A 420 mV photovoltage (Vph) was quantified for the p-Si–Py photocathode. Measurements of charge carrier recombination kinetics through time-resolved infrared spectroscopy indicate that surface attachment of pyrene moieties introduces defects at the Si interface, even without the presence of the catalyst. These defects provide competing kinetic pathways for photogenerated carriers, hypothesized to influence the selectivity of the hybrid photoelectrode, an important implication for future designs of hybrid photoelectrodes.

items.title: Strain Gradient Engineering at Material Interfaces: Flexocatalysis Beyond Centrosymmetry
items.abstract: Abstract The flexoelectric effect, an electromechanical coupling phenomenon ubiquitous in all materials (including centrosymmetric crystals) under non-uniform strain gradients, has recently given rise to the emerging field of flexocatalysis. By eliminating the need for external light or electrical biases and circumventing the symmetry constraints of piezoelectric materials, it represents a catalytic paradigm for green chemistry, with applications spanning water splitting for hydrogen production, hydrogen peroxide generation, pollutant degradation, and biomedical therapies (e.g., tumor treatment). This review systematically outlines the fundamentals of the flexoelectric effect and the strain gradient-driven charge separation mechanisms. Recent advances in representative applications across energy, environmental, and biomedical fields are comprehensively summarized. Additionally, preliminary strategies to enhance catalytic efficiency are categorized into two main approaches: (1) amplifying the flexoelectric response, primarily interface engineering, the synergistic coupling of piezoelectric and flexoelectric effects, and doping; and (2) optimizing charge separation and transfer, mainly via introduction of vacancies, photo-flexoelectric synergistic coupling, and single-atom modification. Finally, the current challenges and future opportunities of flexocatalysis are highlighted, providing a foundational roadmap that bridges solid-state physics and interfacial catalysis.

items.title: Synergistic Effect of Hybrid Polarized Spin Currents Enables Sub-Nanosecond and Energy-Efficient Field-Free Switching on a Wafer-Scale Platform
items.abstract: Abstract Spin–orbit torque magnetoresistive random access memory (SOT-MRAM) exhibits intrinsic potential for next-generation magnetic memory, whereas robust wafer-level field-free switching (FFS) of nanosized perpendicular magnetic tunnel junctions (pMTJ) remains a critical challenge for practical applications. Here, we present a robust FFS of 90 nm pMTJs on 300 mm wafers driven by the synergistic effect of y- and z-polarized spin currents generated at the antiferromagnetic (AFM)/nonmagnetic (NM) interface. Experimental results demonstrate that an appropriate combination of both y- and z-spin polarizations is able to significantly improve the FFS performance. 90 nm pMTJ arrays are fabricated on 300 mm wafers, where a mean tunnel magnetoresistance ratio (TMR) of 140%, an endurance of exceeding 1012 cycles, and a robust field-free SOT switching at sub-nanosecond (down to 0.2 ns) are simultaneously achieved. Robust FFS is observed at temperature up to 100 °C, and the switching polarity remains unchanged after 1T magnetic field disturbance. With the assistance of the voltage-controlled magnetic anisotropy (VCMA) effect, the switching current density is reduced by 20% and the switching energy can be as low as 0.35 pJ/bit. This work paves the way for SOT-MRAM toward commercialization.

items.title: A Multimetallic Single-Atom Catalyst on a Defective Graphene Support toward Methanol Oxidation and Oxygen Reduction Reactions: Density Functional Theory, Machine Learning, and Experiments
items.abstract: Abstract Multimetallic single-atom catalysts (SACs) have emerged as promising candidates for electrocatalytic reactions. However, identifying bifunctional multimetallic SACs capable of efficiently catalyzing both the oxygen reduction and methanol oxidation reactions (ORR and MOR), applicable to direct methanol fuel cells, remains challenging due to the vast compositional design space. Here, we propose a defective graphene-supported multimetallic SAC (M1M2M3M4M5-SAC) incorporating Mn, Pt, Fe, Ni, Co, and Cu for simultaneous MOR and ORR catalysis. Density functional theory (DFT) calculations along with machine learning (ML) predictions reveal that the Co active site in PtFeNiCoCu-SAC delivers the most favorable performance, exhibiting ORR and MOR overpotentials of 0.47 and 0.46 V, respectively. Guided by these insights, we synthesized PtFeNiCoCu-SAC and a nitrogen-doped sample, confirming their atomic structures using X-ray absorption spectroscopy (XAS), X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS), and scanning transmission electron microscopy (STEM). Electrochemical measurements validate the theoretical predictions: PtFeNiCoCu-SAC achieves an experimental ORR overpotential of 0.30 VRHE and a Tafel slope of 114 mV/dec at –1 mA/cm2, along with a half-wave potential of 0.86 VRHE. This catalyst also demonstrates good MOR activity, with a pronounced oxidation peak at 0.97 VRHE. Therefore, this work establishes a DFT- and ML-guided strategy for the accelerated rational design of multimetallic SACs and highlights PtFeNiCoCu-SAC as a promising bifunctional catalyst for energy-conversion applications.

items.title: Electrode-Side Catalytic Regulation Directs Electrolyte Decomposition for Stable Silicon Anodes
items.abstract: Abstract The electrochemical stability of silicon anodes is critically influenced by the initial decomposition pathways of fluorine-containing electrolyte species, which dictate the solid electrolyte interphase (SEI) composition and stability. However, existing strategies primarily rely on electrolyte fluorination or artificial interphases to indirectly regulate SEI chemistry, whereas precise electrode-side regulation of fluorine-containing electrolyte decomposition remains challenging. Herein, a binder-free Co SACs-Si-N/C electrode is developed to direct interfacial reactions through single-atom catalysis. Atomically dispersed Co-N4 sites selectively strengthen PF6– adsorption, modulate the interfacial electronic structure, and steer fluorine-containing electrolyte species toward preferential inorganic decomposition, thereby constructing a compact LiF-rich SEI that suppresses parasitic reactions and stabilizes the silicon/electrolyte interface. As a result, the Co SACs-Si-N/C electrode delivers a reversible capacity of 1128.8 mAh g–1 after 1200 cycles at 1.0 A g–1, while lithium cobalt oxide pouch cells further demonstrate their practical applicability. Machine learning established a quantitative correlation between electrochemical characterization parameters and performance evolution. This work reveals the critical role of electrode-regulated interfacial reaction pathways in governing SEI evolution and provides a catalytic strategy for developing durable silicon-based anodes.

items.title: Berberine/Verteporfin Nanomicelles Enable O2-Economized Photodynamic Immunotherapy in Esophageal Cancer Via Tumor Metabolic Remodeling
items.abstract: Abstract Photodynamic therapy (PDT) can convert oxidative damage into systemic antitumor immunity, but mitochondrial oxygen consumption, lactate accumulation, and aberrant angiogenesis create a hypoxic and immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment that limits treatment. Here, berberine (BBR) and verteporfin (VER) were co-loaded into nanomicelles (BV NMs) through sonication-assisted self-assembly of PEG-g-(PVAc-co-PVCL), creating a “microenvironment remodeling—PDT potentiation—immune activation” strategy. BV NMs had a hydrodynamic diameter of 56.15 ± 0.30 nm. Drug loading lowered the critical micelle concentration from 11.2 μg/mL (blank micelles) to an apparent 1.3 μg/mL (BV NMs), supporting dilution stability. It also enhanced aqueous dispersibility, cellular uptake, and intratumoral accumulation. Mechanistically, BBR reduced mitochondrial complex I-associated activity, intracellular adenosine triphosphate levels, and extracellular lactate accumulation, attenuated cellular hypoxia and hypoxia-inducible factor-1α responses, and increased intracellular oxygen availability. Before irradiation, VER suppressed Yes-associated protein signaling and vascular endothelial growth factor expression, providing light-independent antitumor and antiangiogenic regulation. Under 660 nm irradiation, VER induced reactive oxygen species accumulation, mitochondrial depolarization, tumor-cell death, and immunogenic cell death. In vivo, BV NMs combined with irradiation achieved an approximately 96% inhibition rate based on terminal tumor weight. Proportions of mature dendritic cells in tumor-draining lymph nodes and splenic CD8+ T cells reached 3.33 and 2.73 times the control levels, respectively, alongside expansion of memory CD8+ T-cell populations. Treatment also reduced experimental pulmonary metastatic burden, achieved 50% survival at day 60, and caused no evident short-term systemic toxicity. This platform couples metabolic and angiogenic regulation with oxygen-dependent PDT and antitumor immunity, providing a strategy against primary and metastatic tumors.

items.title: Crystallinity-Dependent Donor Activation in RF-Sputtered SnO2 Electron-Transport Layers and the Interface-Character Origin of Their Predicted Device-Level Consequences
items.abstract: Abstract SnO2 is the electron-transport layer (ETL) in record n–i–p perovskite solar cells, grown by chemical bath deposition (CBD) without high-temperature crystallization; whether its crystallinity matters remains unresolved. Here, the same RF-sputtering process on fluorine-doped tin oxide (FTO), at room temperature or 300 °C, yields a predominantly amorphous or an FTO-templated polycrystalline rutile film. The measured film and interface properties anchor a calibrated TCAD model and a thirteen-parameter Sobol global sensitivity analysis (&gt;33,000 simulations), which, unlike one-factor-at-a-time sweeps, resolves the interactions among parameters explicitly. At the film level, crystallinity governs donor activation: UPS, XPS, and STEM-EDS show that the amorphous film holds more fluorine yet has a Fermi level farther below the conduction band, so shallow donors attributed to substitutional fluorine exist in both films but are active only in the crystalline one. At the device level, however, the predicted gain arises from the crystalline film's interface rather than its doping. The Ag/SnO2 contact is rectifying on the amorphous film and ohmic on the crystalline one, through interface-state de-pinning rather than a band-offset shift. The Sobol analysis ranks the SnO2/perovskite interface trap density first (total-effect index ≈ 0.66). A degenerately doped film could screen such traps, but the amorphous film's rectification rules out that route; its deficit is interfacial. At its trap density (∼1013 cm–2), only deep acceptor-like states pin the Fermi level (acceptor-fraction index ≈ 0.83). The predicted crystallization gain is +5.6 pp (20.5 → 26.1%). FAPbI3 half-stack PL/TRPL supports this (1.35× longer lifetime on the crystalline ETL) and bounds that interface's trap density to ≲1012 cm–2. Crystalline growth is one route to the de-pinned interface that CBD ETLs reach chemically, provided that interface is preserved. The absolute efficiencies are calibrated predictions; the benefit's sign and the lever ranking are robust.

items.title: Dual Conical Fibers for Controllable Liquid Transfer
items.abstract: Abstract Solution processes, especially those using open systems, have shown advantages of mild conditions, cost-effectiveness, and broad substrate compatibility in making micro-patterned functional films of optoelectronic devices. Owing to the extreme dynamics of liquids, finely controlling liquid transfer remains largely unsolved, particularly across dimensions from μm- to cm-scale. Here, we propose a model structure of dual conical fibers (dual-CFs) that enables liquid transfer to proceed in a well-controllable manner for micro-patterning. The critical structural parameters for fully holding liquid within dual-CFs are clarified, and quantitative correlations between fiber topology and steady liquid transfer are established. The dual-parallel-fibrous structure, representing the minimum number of CFs for the structure model, helps suppress Plateau–Rayleigh instability by virtue of the confined noncircular cross-sectional liquid film; while the conical structure enables effectively holding liquid, without any leakage during the transfer process, due to the as-generated Laplace pressure difference. The dual-CFs benefit from minimizing the rupture energy of the liquid film by the minimal cross-sectional area confined at the tips, which leads to finely anchoring the three-phase contact line. As a synergistic consequence, liquid can be transferred onto substrates in a controllable manner, resulting in micro-patterns with well-defined profiles. More importantly, the model structure of dual-CFs can be programmably arranged into multi-conical fiber arrays, by which direct-writing micro-patterns from μm-scale microlines to cm-scale uniform films can be realized. The direct-writing strategy is applicable for making functional micro-patterns, offering inspiration for micro-patterning liquid materials using fibrous open systems.

items.title: Controllable Synthesis of Porous Core–Shell NiCo Bimetallic Selenides for High-Performance Supercapacitors
items.abstract: Abstract Metal–organic framework (MOF)-derived electrode materials suffer from poor conductivity and structural instability. Herein, a porous core–shell NiCo bimetallic selenide (NiCo PBA–Se) is synthesized via a multistep liquid-phase transformation followed by low-temperature selenization. A Zeolitic Imidazolate Framework-67 (ZIF-67) shell is first epitaxially grown on a Ni-MOF core to construct a core–shell MOF hybrid as the precursor for the preparation of subsequent electrode materials. Unlike conventional methods that convert only the outer MOF layer, the precisely controlled ion-exchange process converts both the inner Ni-MOF and outer ZIF-67 into a NiCo-PBA precursor while preserving the core–shell spherical morphology. Gas-phase selenization at 350 °C yields the target product, which retains a three-dimensional porous spherical architecture composed of stacked ultrathin nanosheets. Ni and Co are uniformly incorporated into the selenide lattice, forming a single-phase (Ni, Co)Se2 solid solution that shortens ion transport paths and increases active sites. Kinetic analysis reveals a synergistic combination of diffusion-controlled and capacitance-controlled charge storage, enabling rapid charge/discharge. In three-electrode tests, NiCo PBA–Se delivers a specific capacitance of 1642 F·g–1 (738.9 C·g–1) at 1 A·g–1. The assembled asymmetric supercapacitor achieves an energy density of 42.52 Wh·kg–1 at 775 W·kg–1 and powers an electronic timer for 20 min. This work demonstrates the effectiveness of the MOF-on-MOF strategy with full conversion of both core and shell and simultaneous maintenance of the core–shell structure for constructing high-performance multimetal selenides.

items.title: Structural Insights into Proton Exchange Membrane Water Electrolyzers after Long-Term Operation Using Advanced 3D Focused Ion Beam–Scanning Electron Microscopy Tomography
items.abstract: Abstract Proton exchange membrane water electrolyzers (PEMWEs) are key to sustainable hydrogen production, but their long-term performance is limited by degradation, particularly in the membrane electrode assembly (MEA), which remains a barrier to commercial viability. Moreover, the need for corrosion-resistant materials and the intricate fabrication of bipolar plates and porous transport layers (PTLs) further impede large-scale deployment and account for a major share of the stack cost. Because lifetime and replacement costs are strongly influenced by the local microstructure and contact conditions, especially at the anode/PTL interface, a multiscale characterization approach combining 3D focused ion beam–scanning electron microscopy (FIB–SEM) with time-of-flight mass spectrometry is used to investigate degradation in an MEA after several thousand hours of operation under industrially relevant conditions. The 3D reconstruction and ppm-level chemical mapping show that local contact heterogeneities at welds in an expanded-metal mesh PTL act as degradation hotspots. At these sites, intensified catalyst utilization accelerates iridium dissolution, driving iridium migration and deposition as extended filaments into the membrane. Concurrently, membrane voids are formed beneath these sites, accompanied by iron contamination detected at both contact types. In contrast, general contact regions mainly show a thin redeposition layer without voids or filaments. These findings provide a mechanistic framework that links local contact conditions and microstructural heterogeneities to coupled catalyst and membrane degradation, supporting design rules for improved PEMWE durability.

items.title: Dielectric Mie-Resonant Metasurface Integrated ATR Chip for Spectrally Tunable Surface-Enhanced Infrared Spectroscopy in Aqueous Media
items.abstract: Abstract Fourier transform infrared (FTIR) spectroscopy provides label-free molecular fingerprints but often lacks sensitivity for trace analysis in aqueous media. Surface-enhanced infrared absorption (SEIRA) spectroscopy amplifies vibrational signals near nanostructured surfaces, yet conventional SEIRA platforms typically require sample drying, preconcentration, or noble metal substrates. Here, we introduce a monolithic all-silicon chip that integrates dielectric Mie-resonant micropillar arrays onto a microattenuated total reflection (µ-ATR) element using a complementary metal–oxide–semiconductor (CMOS)-compatible fabrication process. This µ-ATR SEIRA (µ-SEIRA) chip enables SEIRA directly in bulk aqueous media without sample drying, preconcentration, or noble metals. The µ-SEIRA chip provides spectrally tunable field enhancement, achieving a limit of detection (LOD) of 0.57 mM for aqueous sodium acetate, a 3.6-fold improvement over a flat silicon reference. Resonance tuning via the micropillar array geometry enables selective enhancement of specific vibrational bands, as demonstrated by the preferential enhancement of the Amide II band (∼1550 cm–1) over the Amide I band (∼1650 cm–1) in bovine serum albumin. The µ-SEIRA chip is low-cost, scalable, and disposable, reducing cross-contamination and throughput limitations associated with reusable ATR crystals for aqueous sample measurements.

items.title: n -Value-Tuned Quasi-2D Perovskites for Wavelength-Selective Optoelectronic Synapses
items.abstract: Abstract Neuromorphic vision systems demand optoelectronic synapses that combine wavelength-selective sensing with gradual and linear synaptic weight updates. In two-dimensional (2D) halide perovskites, extending visible-light absorption can be accompanied by accelerating ion migration and premature current saturation. Here, we regulate the phase composition of quasi-two-dimensional (quasi-2D) BA2MA(n–1)PbnI(3n+1) perovskites by tuning the nominal n value. Incorporation of the n = 2 phase extends the absorption edge from 525 nm (green) to approximately 600 nm (red), enabling distinguishable responses under blue, green, and red illumination. The nominal n = 1.2 composition provides sufficient higher-n phase for red-light absorption while suppressing excessive ion migration, yielding highly linear photocurrent weight updates. Using these wavelength-, intensity-, and duration-dependent responses, we construct a light-history regression model that maps accumulated exposure to electrical blue-light-hazard warning and literature-derived phototoxicity thresholds under different color temperatures. This phase-engineering strategy provides a material-level route to integrate spectral selectivity and linear signal integration in neuromorphic vision systems.

items.title: Porous-Architectured Composite for Fully 3D-Printed Biodegradable Soft Electronics
items.abstract: Abstract Biodegradable electronics offer the promise of implantable devices that disappear after use, reducing the need for surgical removal and mitigating chronic inflammatory responses. Achieving both tissue-level mechanical softness and sufficient electrical conductivity is critical for bioelectronics. Composite materials provide a versatile platform to satisfy these electrical and mechanical requirements, while 3D printing allows precise and customizable fabrication of complex and multi-material structures. However, in fully biodegradable composites, limited material options restrict simultaneous optimization of mechanical and electrical properties. Here, we introduce engineered internal porosity into a biodegradable electronic composite to achieve softer mechanical properties while maintaining electrical performance. In metal-polymer composites, a porous matrix promotes filler aggregation, forming a percolating conductive network at a lower filler loading compared to non-porous counterparts, thereby reducing stiffness. Engineered porosity within the printed structure reduces its elastic modulus by orders of magnitude and accelerates degradation. We also demonstrate multi-material 3D printing of porosity-programmed electronic inks for printed circuit boards and sensors applications. This structural strategy can be extended to other biodegradable filler-binder systems, thereby expanding the material palette for next-generation transient electronics.

items.title: Interfacial Solvent Engineering Enables Hydrothermally Stable MXene Heterostructures for Printed Wearable Electronics
items.abstract: Abstract Water-induced degradation of MXene during hydrothermal synthesis severely limits the construction of MXene-based heterostructures for further applications. Herein, an interfacial solvent-engineering strategy was developed to stabilize MXene under harsh hydrothermal conditions. Solvents with a stronger affinity for reactive Ti sites than water can preferentially adsorb at these sites. This competitive adsorption limits direct water–Ti contact and thereby suppresses subsequent MXene oxidation. DFT calculations were used to screen candidate solvents and support the proposed competitive adsorption mechanism, while the experimental results broadly followed the predicted trend. Deoxygenation experiments further supported the dominant role of water in MXene degradation. Molecular dynamics simulations revealed that preferential interfacial enrichment of DMF persists at 453 K despite enhanced thermal motion. In a 50 vol % DMF/H2O system, the MXene framework remained well preserved even under prolonged or higher-temperature hydrothermal treatment. This regulated solvent environment enabled the in situ growth of 1T-MoS2 on the preserved MXene framework. The conductive MXene framework and abundant active sites of 1T-MoS2 led to enhanced electrochemical performance. The resulting composite was further processed into printed microsupercapacitors and pressure sensors, which were integrated into a self-powered pressure-sensing system. This work establishes interfacial solvent engineering as an effective route to hydrothermally stable MXene heterostructures for printed wearable electronics.

items.title: Phosphate-Functionalized Macroporous Cellulose Sponges for Uranium Recovery from Seawater
items.abstract: Abstract Cellulose-based adsorbents offer a sustainable platform for uranium recovery from seawater, but simple functionalization strategies that enable effective uranium capture under highly competitive marine conditions remain limited. Here, we report a post-phosphorylation strategy for introducing uranium-binding functionality into a preformed freeze-crosslinked carboxymethyl cellulose nanofiber (CMCF) sponge while retaining its interconnected macroporous architecture. Impregnation of the cellulose sponge with NH4H2PO4/urea followed by mild thermal treatment at 120 °C introduced up to 114 ± 18 mg P g–1 sponge. In seawater spiked with 10 mg L–1 U(VI), both nonphosphorylated and phosphorylated CMCF sponges showed similarly high U removal (&gt;96%), largely obscuring the effect of phosphate functionalization. In contrast, a pronounced phosphate-dependent enhancement emerged under realistic seawater conditions: the nonphosphorylated sponge showed negligible U removal from natural seawater, whereas the post-phosphorylated P1-CMCF sponge achieved approximately 99% U removal within 24 h. SEM–EDX and XPS analyses further supported uranium accumulation at phosphate-rich cellulose interfaces and the involvement of phosphate-associated oxygen donor sites in U binding. The captured uranium was nearly quantitatively recovered using 0.1 mol L–1 NaHCO3, and adsorption performance was maintained over three adsorption–desorption cycles. These results demonstrate that simple post-phosphorylation of a preformed macroporous cellulose scaffold provides accessible uranium-binding interfaces while preserving the underlying transport architecture, offering a straightforward route to efficient and regenerable uranium recovery under chemically complex seawater conditions.

items.title: Boosting Photocatalytic Performance via Electron Transfer Regulation in Biocomponent Hybrid Heterojunctions
items.abstract: Abstract Against the backdrop of global climate change and the energy crisis, developing efficient and sustainable catalytic technologies is crucial for addressing environmental and energy challenges. Compared to traditional heterojunctions, the incorporation of natural biogenic components holds great potential for overcoming bottlenecks such as complex crystal engineering, insufficient stability, and limited selectivity. This review established an electron transfer regulation framework to guide the construction of biocomponent hybrid heterojunctions for superior photocatalysis. We systematically cover various biogenic components and their derivatives, from small molecules, conjugated polymers, and supramolecular assemblies, to three-dimensional networks and crystal frameworks such as metal–organic frameworks and covalent-organic frameworks. Based on in-depth mechanistic analysis, this review demonstrates how these biogenic components modulate band engineering, charge transfer kinetics, substrate utilization, and defect passivation, which collectively achieve sequential optimization across the entire charge-carrier lifecycle—from generation and transport to surface reaction and long-term stability. Importantly, all of these directly linked to enhanced photocatalytic performance in H2 evolution, CO2 reduction, H2O2 generation, and pollutant degradation. In addition to conventional band engineering, novel mechanisms such as exciton behavior modulation and conjugated continuity regulation are discussed. This framework transforms empirical material design into predictable catalysis optimization, aiming to accelerate the development of high-performance biocomponent hybrid heterojunctions.

items.title: Ionic Liquids and Deep Eutectic Solvents as Functional Interfacial Phases in Membrane-Based Separations
items.abstract: Abstract In this Spotlight on Applications, we describe our progress in developing membrane-based separation processes in which ionic liquids (ILs) and deep eutectic solvents (DESs) act as functional interfacial phases rather than merely as alternative solvents or extractants. Starting from stability limitations identified in supported ionic liquid membranes, our work evolved toward architectures in which polymeric materials selectively contact, confine, distribute, or stabilize ionic and eutectic liquid phases. We organize these contributions according to the location and function of the active interface: external polymer–ionic liquid interfaces in dense membrane systems; localized ionic or eutectic phases confined within multilayer membrane architectures; distributed polymer–DES domains in dense hybrid membranes; membrane-stabilized contact with mobile immiscible liquid phases; and liquid–vapor–membrane interfaces in ionic-liquid-driven osmotic distillation. Each architecture builds on an established membrane-process category – perstraction, coated liquid membranes, polymer inclusion membranes, membrane contactors, and osmotic distillation – and is distinguished by the location, flow regime, and function of the ionic or eutectic phase. These configurations were applied to fermentation-product recovery, selective separation of target molecules, ethanol dehydration, food concentration, and water recovery from saline streams. Across these applications, performance emerged from the synergistic coupling of polymer sorption and diffusion, liquid-phase affinity, wetting, morphology, interfacial stability, and resistance distribution. COSMO-RS provided a complementary progression from solute–ionic-liquid screening to direct polymer screening and, subsequently, to thermodynamic interpretation of hybrid polymer–eutectic membrane environments. Collectively, these studies indicate that the polymer, ionic or eutectic phase, solute, interface, operating mode, and membrane architecture should be designed as an integrated interfacial system.

items.title: Pneumatic Rigid-Soft Coupled Finger with Self-Powered Triboelectric Tactile Sensing toward Potential Application in Lunar Exploration
items.abstract: Abstract Robotic manipulation in future lunar-surface operations and planetary sample-return missions requires end effectors capable of accommodating irregular objects while maintaining reliable tactile feedback under uncertain contact conditions. Motivated by these challenges, we present a terrestrial proof-of-concept of a pneumatic rigid–soft coupled robotic finger integrating structural regulation and self-powered triboelectric tactile sensing. The finger combines rigid skeletons, fiber-constrained pneumatic chambers, and a finger-pad sensing unit to enable compliant deformation, posture regulation, and tactile perception. A flexible single-electrode triboelectric sensor based on a PDMS-MXene composite generates electrical signals through contact electrification and electrostatic induction without external electrical excitation, while pneumatic actuation, signal acquisition, and computational processing require external power. At an input pressure of 140 kPa, the proximal interphalangeal, distal interphalangeal, and metacarpophalangeal regions achieved bending angles of approximately 84°, 76°, and 65°, respectively. The sensor exhibited stable outputs at contact frequencies of 1–10 Hz and a sensitivity of 0.11 V/kPa over 10–120 kPa. Incorporating 6 wt% MXene increased the output voltage by 50.8% compared with pure PDMS. Combined with a convolutional neural network-long short-term memory model, the system achieved classification accuracies of 97.6% for 10 representative laboratory materials and 99.5% for four surface-roughness levels under controlled terrestrial conditions. Grasping experiments further demonstrated compliant manipulation and tactile perception. These results establish the feasibility of the proposed sensing approach under laboratory conditions, while its applicability to planetary geological materials and space environments remains to be validated.

items.title: Issue Publication Information
Issue Editorial Masthead
Rational Synthesis of Sulfonic Acid-Functionalized Covalent Organic Frameworks for Selective Capture of Trace Strontium in Natural Mineral Water
items.abstract: Abstract As a typical long-lived radionuclide, strontium-90 (90Sr) possesses persistent radiological hazards and exhibits high migratory and diffusive behaviors in groundwater. However, the development of adsorbents for the efficient and highly selective capture of trace Sr(II) remains a great challenge. In this study, covalent organic frameworks (COFs, TpPa-2SO3H and TpPa-SO3H) with different numbers of sulfonic acid groups were rationally synthesized and applied for capturing Sr(II). The introduction of sulfonic acid groups onto TpPa-2SO3H and TpPa-SO3H endowed them with high adsorption capacities of 136.4 and 68.3 mg g–1 toward Sr(II), which were 12-fold and 6-fold higher than that of TpPa without sulfonic acid groups, respectively. Meanwhile, TpPa-2SO3H and TpPa-SO3H exhibited fast adsorption kinetics, capturing 99% of Sr(II) within 3 and 10 min, respectively. In addition, TpPa-2SO3H also exhibited high selectivity, excellent anti-interference performance, and regeneration ability without high calcium backgrounds. Characterizations and theoretical calculations demonstrated that sulfonic acid groups in TpPa-2SO3H promoted Sr(II) capture through strong ion-exchange interaction. TpPa-2SO3H was further applied to extract trace Sr(II) in natural Sr-containing mineral water samples. The results showed that the extraction efficiency for Sr(II) exceeded 95% within 5 min. Furthermore, the selectivity for Sr(II) was investigated by the distribution coefficients (Kd), and the Kd was 5.6 × 104 mL g–1 for TpPa-2SO3H toward Sr(II), approximately 400 times higher than those of Na(I) and K(I), respectively. This work not only developed a promising strategy to extract trace Sr(II) from real samples but also broadened the application of COFs in separation science.

items.title: Structural Dynamics of a COF-Based Soft Actuator: Molecular Motion and Macroscopic Response
items.abstract: Abstract Translating molecular-level dynamics of crystalline frameworks into macroscopic function remains a central challenge in the design of responsive materials. Here, we report that the intrinsic flexibility of COF-300 can be systematically characterized in the bulk powder and then harnessed in a processable composite film to achieve coupled optical and mechanical actuation. In powder form, COF-300 exhibits distinct responses to applied stimuli, including solvent vapors, acid-base environments, and temperature changes. Variable-temperature solid-state NMR reveals the thermally activated coalescence of the phenylene ring signals, and variable-temperature powder X-ray diffraction uncovers colossal anisotropic thermal expansion. Periodic TDA-DFT calculations trace the acid-induced chromism to both geometric distortion and protonation of framework. Embedding COF-300 into a poly(vinylidene fluoride) matrix produces a PVDF@COF film in which solvent vapors drive reversible bending–unbending motion synchronized with a visible color shift, and heating drives the same reversible motion. Exposure to HCl turns the film orange and locks both responses through imine protonation, while thermal deprotonation unlocks them, establishing a reversible chemical switch over framework dynamics. These findings show how molecular flexibility in a crystalline framework can translate into programmable macroscopic actuation, advancing the design of multifunctional solid-state actuators with integrated optical and mechanical output.

items.title: Non-local Molecular Engineering Modulates Aluminum-Induced Crystallization toward Transferable Polycrystalline Silicon
items.abstract: Abstract Low-temperature metal-induced crystallization (MIC) has emerged as a promising and cost-effective technique for fabricating polycrystalline silicon (poly-Si), which is a key material in high-performance flexible electronics. However, conventional MIC often yields structurally compromised films due to chaotic interfacial thermodynamics and incomplete layer exchange. Herein, a molecular-level engineering strategy is presented that utilizes buried self-assembled monolayers (SAMs) to remotely control the macroscopic phase transformation and crystallization kinetics during MIC with aluminum as the metal. By systematically tailoring the terminal functional groups of the SAMs at the buried interface between the Al/Si stack and substrate (glass), a distinct structure-property relationship is established: electron-withdrawing groups intrinsically stabilize the amorphous Si (a-Si) network and suppress segregation, whereas electron-donating groups facilitate silicon dissolution. Notably, the best-performing SAM with nucleophilic –NH2 terminal groups functions as a dual-role molecular template that drastically lowers the macroscopic crystallization barrier of the MIC system. By driving a highly directed and accelerated kinetic pathway, this monolayer substantially suppresses stochastic interdiffusion, yielding a highly segregated, continuous, and transfer-ready poly-Si film. Ultimately, this SAM-mediated paradigm advances the fundamental design of non-local phase transformations, establishing a scalable, material-driven pathway for next-generation flexible silicon electronics.

items.title: Copper Oxide-Loaded Graphdiyne Nanocomposites with Hyperthermia-Enhanced Nanozyme Activity for Cuproptosis-Apoptosis Anticancer Therapy
items.abstract: Abstract Cuproptosis is an emerging copper-dependent form of regulated cell death, mechanistically distinct from apoptosis, pyroptosis, and other canonical cell-death pathways, and holds considerable potential for tumor therapeutic applications. In the present study, graphdiyne (GDY) serves as an ideal substrate for the firm immobilization and homogeneous dispersion of CuO nanoparticles. Subsequent polyethylene glycol (PEG) functionalization further enhances the biocompatibility of the hybrid system, yielding CuO/GDY-PEG nanocomposites. The catalase and peroxidase-like activities of CuO nanozymes alleviate hypoxia in the tumor microenvironment (TME) and generate cytotoxic reactive oxygen species, which inducing tumor-cell apoptosis. In addition, this nanocomposite can sustainably deplete glutathione in the TME, disrupt the oxidative balance of the TME, and improve therapeutic efficiency. Photothermal therapy is introduced to facilitate hyperthermia-enhanced tumor nanocatalytic therapy synergistically. More importantly, the intracellular copper overload of tumor cells is caused by the entry of CuO/GDY-PEG nanocomposites into cells. After internalization into tumor cells, CuO/GDY-PEG nanocomposites release Cu2+, which accumulates intracellularly in a mitochondrial-respiration-dependent manner. FDX1 mediates the reduction of Cu2+ to toxic Cu+. The generated Cu+ then binds to lipoylated DLAT and triggers DLAT oligomerization. The formation of insoluble DLAT aggregates elevates cytotoxicity and ultimately drives cuproptosis-mediated cell death. This may synergize with apoptosis to fight tumors systemically.

items.title: Nanomechanics of MXene Flakes at Gold Interfaces
items.abstract: Abstract The demand for novel self-powering and sustainable electronics requires major efforts in identifying new advanced materials for nano-applications. MXenes have gathered attention due to their electronic and mechanical properties; however, their nanomechanical compliance against a metal-like interface is still not clearly identified. In this work, we employ atomic force microscopy to characterize the nanomechanical properties of a self-assembled thin flake of titanium carbide MXene (Ti3C2Tx) against a gold probe. The investigation returns an interfacial shear stress of 399 MPa and the observation of nano-wear localized in the center of the MXene flake. Nevertheless, MXene flakes retained their crystallinity in the tribofilms, as confirmed by transmission electron microscopy and electron energy loss spectroscopy. The outcomes of this work set the basis for the use of Ti3C2Tx in novel nano harvesting systems involving metal (e.g., Au) interfaces with large scope in nanoelectronics, wearable sensing, electric vehicles, and robotics.

items.title: Poly-γ-Glutamic Acid-Modified Carbon Dots as an Enhanced Immune-Activating and Antigen-Delivering Nano-adjuvant for Improved Influenza Vaccine Efficacy
items.abstract: Abstract Vaccine adjuvants are essential components that enhance immune responses to antigens with limited intrinsic immunogenicity and shape the magnitude and quality of adaptive immunity. Although conventional adjuvants effectively stimulate innate immunity, their use is often limited by safety concerns or inefficient antigen delivery. Consequently, biologically derived and biodegradable biomaterials have gained attention as potent vaccine adjuvants. Among them, poly-γ-glutamic acid (γ-PGA) is a naturally derived biopolymer with intrinsic immunostimulatory activity that activates innate immune signaling and promotes cellular immune responses. However, γ-PGA alone shows limited antigen delivery efficiency, which can restrict formulation reproducibility and immune potency. Here, we report γ-PGA-modified carbon dots (PGA-CDs) as a rationally designed nano-adjuvant integrating γ-PGA-mediated immune activation with efficient antigen delivery. Compared with γ-PGA, PGA-CDs exhibited faster and more sustained cellular association, thereby inducing stronger dendritic cell maturation and proinflammatory cytokine production. They readily formed stable nanocomplexes with protein antigens, enhancing cellular uptake and antigen cross-presentation. In vivo, PGA-CDs formulated with ovalbumin elicited strong antigen-specific humoral and cellular immune responses. When combined with hemagglutinin (HA) from pandemic influenza A/California/04/2009 (pH1N1), PGA-CDs induced HA-specific humoral responses comparable to alum, while eliciting significantly stronger antibody and T cell responses than γ-PGA alone, resulting in complete protection against lethal viral challenge. Notably, HA/PGA-CDs also elicited more robust homosubtypic cross-reactive immunity than alum against influenza A/Puerto Rico/8/1934 (H1N1), conferring complete protection. Furthermore, PGA-CDs were well tolerated in vivo, with no detectable hematological or histopathological abnormalities. Collectively, these findings establish PGA-CDs as a promising vaccine adjuvant platform that enhances antigen delivery, amplifies immune activation, and broadens protective efficacy.

items.title: A Keratin and Polyacrylamide Dual Network Hydrogel Based on Dynamic Coordination between Polydopamine and Mg2+ for Infected Wound Repair
items.abstract: Abstract Exogenous bacterial infection severely impairs skin wound repair and creates a complex therapeutic challenge that requires simultaneous infection control, oxidative stress regulation, and tissue regeneration. In this study, a PAM/HK/PDANP-Mg2+ multifunctional hydrogel (HPPM) was developed as a cascade therapeutic dressing for infected wounds. In this system, polyacrylamide (PAM) provided a flexible covalently cross-linked framework. Hydrolyzed keratin (HK) offered bioactive and cytocompatible interfaces. Polydopamine nanoparticles (PDANPs) endowed the hydrogel with adhesiveness, photothermal antibacterial activity, and radical scavenging capacity. Coordination between Mg2+ and PDA, together with intermolecular hydrogen bonding, contributed to reversible physical cross-linking within the PAM framework. The optimized HPPM (0.012) hydrogel exhibited a porous structure, high swelling ratio (∼1277%), strong adhesion properties (31.00 kPa), and large tensile elongation (∼560%). Under 808 nm near-infrared (NIR) irradiation, HPPM achieved mild photothermal heating and over 99% antibacterial efficiency against Escherichia coli (E. coli) and Staphylococcus aureus (S. aureus). It also showed favorable antioxidant activity, cytocompatibility, and pro-migratory effects. In an S. aureus-infected rat wound model, HPPM (0.012) + NIR accelerated wound closure, reduced inflammation, enhanced collagen deposition and re-epithelialization, and regulated IL-10/TNF-α expression. These results suggest that HPPM promotes infected wound healing through dynamic coordination-driven cascade remodeling of the infected wound microenvironment.

items.title: Waterborne-Polyurethane as High-Performance Binder for Cathodes of Lithium-Ion Batteries
items.abstract: Abstract In lithium-ion batteries, the electrodes are strongly influenced by the polymer binder swelling in liquid electrolytes, which governs electrode integrity, adhesion, flexibility and Li+ transport. Herein, a series of polyacrylate-terminated waterborne polyurethanes (WPUAs) are designed by systematically varying the proportions of nonionic, anionic, and zwitterionic monomers to regulate swelling behavior in liquid electrolytes. The compositional modulation influences the polymer polarity, polymer entanglement, polymer mechanical property and their swelling in electrolytes, and finally the final electrochemical performance of WPUAs. The optimized WPUA exhibits a balanced swelling ratio, strong adhesion, and significantly enhanced Li+ diffusion. Density functional theory calculation reveals that the molecular configuration is rational and conducive to the Li+ transport, which are supported by its superior Li+ conductivity and diffusion coefficient of lithium ions much higher than those of the polyvinylidene fluoride (PVDF) binder. The calculated diffusion coefficient of lithium ions in WPUA is 2.43 × 10–12 cm2 s–1, which is twice times higher than that in PVDF. Employing the synthesized WPUA binder, the assembled LiFePO4@Li half cells show improved electrochemical performance of 110.8 mAh g–1 at 3C for over 800 cycles with 80.4% capacity retention and the high-loading LiFePO4@artificial graphite full cells also show improved performance of 135.0 mAh g–1 after 340 cycles with 87.1% capacity retention, both of which exhibit better electrochemical performance than PVDF. This work highlights controlled binder swelling as a key design parameter for balancing electrolyte accessibility, Li+ transport, and electrode integrity, offering useful guidance for the development of high-performance waterborne binders for lithium-ion batteries.

items.title: In Situ Displacement Reaction Enables a Conductive Metallized Hydrogel Interface for Smart Underwater Flexible Electronics
items.abstract: Abstract Underwater wearable sensing is severely hampered by the intrinsic drawbacks of conventional materials, including water absorption, swelling, and electrical drift during long-term immersion. Here, we develop an anti-swelling hydrogel with a surface-metallized layer, which achieves strong stability of both mechanical structure and electrical conductivity during long-term underwater immersion.
