The precise regulation of hydrophilic acrylamide and hydrophobic butyl acrylate enables anti-swelling performance, while an in-situ displacement reaction conveniently and readily constructs an interfacial silver layer on the hydrogel. The hydrogel exhibits remarkable mechanical sensing performance, including high pressure sensitivity, fast response/recovery times, and a broad tensile sensing range. The sensor is integrated into an electronic skin for motion and physiological monitoring (joint bending, respiration, electromyography, and electrocardiography). With AI assistance, this electronic skin achieves 93.75% accuracy in handwriting recognition via a ProbSparse Transformer model. More importantly, a waterproof multichannel sensing system is constructed for real-time monitoring of underwater finger movements and gesture-associated resistance responses. This hydrogel sensor thus serves as a simple, robust, and amphibious platform for healthcare and human-machine interfaces in both air and water.

items.title: Hydrogen-Bond-Regulated PAN/PTFBZ Nanofibrous Composite Barriers for Flame-Resistant Thermal Runaway Protection
items.abstract: Abstract Electrospun polymer barriers are attractive for lightweight thermal protection in compact lithium–ion battery (LIB) devices, but their limited flame resistance and structural stability under thermal abuse restrict their practical use. Herein, a hydrogen-bond-regulated nanofibrous composite barrier was developed by incorporating trifluoromethyl-modified benzoxazine (TFBZ)-derived components into a polyacrylonitrile (PAN) matrix. The benzoxazine-derived phenolic hydroxyl groups could interact with the nitrile groups of PAN through O–H···N≡C hydrogen bonding, contributing to improved interfacial compatibility and fibrous-network stabilization while retaining the processability of PAN. Thermogravimetric analysis showed that PAN/PTFBZ retained 96.1% of its mass at 300 °C, compared with 75.8% for pure PAN. Cone calorimetry showed that the total heat release and total smoke production were reduced by 64.9% and 45.1%, respectively, and the limiting oxygen index (LOI) increased from 18% to 31%. In battery-level thermal abuse tests, the time to complete thermal runaway (TR) increased from 1068.7 ± 14.6 s to 1884.7 ± 44.2 s, corresponding to 76.4% delay. These results suggest that interfacial hydrogen-bonding regulation, together with the ─CF3-modified benzoxazine-derived structure and compact char formation, contributes to improved flame resistance, structural retention, and battery-level thermal-abuse protection.

items.title: Genesis of Nucleation Sites Dictates the Fate of 2D MoS2 Growth
items.abstract: Abstract Scalable synthesis of two-dimensional (2D) transition metal dichalcogenides (TMDs) with atomic precision is critical for next-generation flexible electronics. Chemical vapor deposition is a primary strategy for the growth of 2D TMD films. The process, however, is difficult to control at large scales due to the strong interplay between time-dependent concentration gradients of the precursors, setup-specific fluid dynamics, and surface energetics. Here, we present a dual-channel reactor system that allows independent dynamic control over transition metal and chalcogen precursor dosages. This enables preprogrammed delivery of precursor partial pressures, effectively decoupling the chemical potentials governing nucleation and subsequent growth phases. This was demonstrated using molybdenum disulfide (MoS2) synthesis as an archetypical model system. By combining experiments and time-dependent fluid dynamics simulations, we have revealed that the genesis of nucleation sites, the local Mo/S ratio established during the fleeting initial nucleation event, decisively dictates the ultimate growth morphology. We demonstrate that near-stoichiometric S-rich conditions during both nucleation and growth stages favor 2D lateral expansion via heterogeneous surface reactions, whereas excessively S-rich conditions promote 3D growth through homogeneous gas-phase reactions. Furthermore, we show that the spatial limitations of traditional horizontal configurations, such as inherent concentration gradients and mass transport bottlenecks, are effectively bypassed using an optimized vertical substrate orientation. By thinning the boundary layer and stabilizing the chemical potential, this configuration shifts the rate-limiting step toward surface reaction kinetics. This dual approach of temporal precursor modulation and spatial substrate optimization provides a robust protocol for the deterministic synthesis of 2D TMDs.

items.title: Electrospun Perforated Carbon Spheres with an Ultramicropore-Rich Architecture for Sodium-Ion Storage
items.abstract: Abstract Hard carbon (HC) is a promising anode material for sodium-ion batteries (SIBs) because its disordered structure and relatively large interlayer spacing facilitate reversible Na+ storage. Polyacrylonitrile (PAN) is an attractive carbon precursor with high carbon yield and in situ nitrogen doping. However, conventional PAN-derived HC often suffers from sluggish ion transport and limited reversible capacity. Herein, electrospun perforated carbon spheres (PCS) with an ultramicropore-rich architecture were fabricated via coaxial electrospinning, sacrificial templating, and high-temperature carbonization. The optimized PCS exhibits a CO2-derived apparent specific surface area of 362.5 m2 g–1 and deliver a reversible capacity of 312.9 mAh g–1 at 20 mA g–1, including a plateau capacity of 180.2 mAh g–1. It also delivers a rate capability of 145.6 mAh g–1 at 2 A g–1 and retains 88.0% of its capacity after 400 cycles at 50 mA g–1. Ex situ XRD, in situ Raman spectroscopy and electrochemical analyses are consistent with an adsorption–intercalation/pore-filling sodium-storage mechanism. A full cell paired with a Na4Fe3(PO4)2P2O7 (NFPP) cathode delivers an energy density of 209 Wh kg–1 based on the total mass of active materials. These results demonstrate that electrospun carbon spheres with tailored pore structures are promising anodes for advanced SIBs.

items.title: Reconfigurable Exchange Bias Enabled by Photoresponsive Liquid Crystal Networks in FeGa/IrMn Magnetic Heterostructures
items.abstract: Abstract Post-fabrication tunability of magnetic properties remains a key challenge for next-generation spintronic and adaptive magneto-electronic devices. Here, we report on a fully electrically contactless strategy to reversibly manipulate the magnetic response of an exchange-biased Ta/Fe80Ga20/Ir20Mn80/Ta multilayer stack through external light stimuli. A photoresponsive azobenzene-doped liquid crystal network (LCN) substrate is employed as an active support for the heterostructure capable of transferring controllable stress to the magnetostrictive FeGa layer under ultraviolet irradiation. This strain-mediated coupling induces a tunable uniaxial magnetic anisotropy in the device, enabling continuous, angular-dependent modulation of key magnetic parameters, including exchange bias and coercivity. Their variation reaches about 11% with respect to the unstressed state. Owing to the slow thermal relaxation kinetics of the LCN, the UV-induced magnetic state is retained after the illumination is switched off over timescales relevant for device operation and can be fully erased by subsequent green-light irradiation. Notably, both the magnitude and sign of the modulation are strongly angle-dependent, reflecting the interplay among stress-induced, magnetocrystalline, and interfacial (i.e., exchange coupling) anisotropies. This approach demonstrates a pathway toward reconfigurable, energy-efficient magnetic systems with remotely tunable functionality, offering significant advantages for miniaturized devices adaptable to dynamic, multi-stimuli environments.

items.title: Epoxy-Functionalized Polysilsesquioxane Coatings for Rear-Side Impact Protection of Thin Functional Ceramics
items.abstract: Abstract High-performance protective coatings capable of preventing catastrophic impact fracture of thin brittle inorganic substrates are urgently demanded for next-generation 5G/6G consumer electronics; however rational design strategies that simultaneously retain pristine surface aesthetics and achieve prominent shock resistance are still lacking. Herein, a rigid epoxy-functionalized polysilsesquioxane hybrid resin is synthesized, followed by cross-linking with various amine curing agents through a high-efficiency synchronous thermal-moisture dual-curing route. The optimized EGSI coating crosslinked by isophorone diamine (IPDA) achieves a pencil scratch hardness of 9H and a nanoindentation modulus of 2.66 GPa. Viscoelastic characterization confirms a distinctive filler-free self-reinforcement effect originating from the siloxane skeleton; the glass transition becomes indistinct, and the optimized coating preserved ∼40% of its initial glassy storage modulus, corresponding to a remarkably high rubbery plateau modulus of ∼750 MPa up to 300 °C. Ball-drop impact tests support the effectiveness of the proposed rigid backing structural constraint mechanism. When coated on the rear face of 300 μm structural ceramic sheets, the EGSI layer elevates the maximum crack-free nominal drop energy to 63.9 mJ, representing a 233% enhancement compared with bare ceramics. Different from conventional front-side energy-absorbing coatings, this noninvasive rear-side reinforcement scheme avoids damaging the decorative exterior of ceramic components and enables low-cost upgrading of ordinary sintered ceramics to high shock-resistant grade. This study establishes a design approach for the tested systems and coating configuration optimization methodology for reinforcing brittle substrates, showing great application prospects in smartphone ceramic back covers, ultrathin glass panels, and other electronic protective components.

items.title: Stimuli-Responsive Copper Modified Mesoporous Silica Nanoparticles as Smart Antimicrobial Delivery System for Antimicrobial Applications
items.abstract: Abstract The emergence of multidrug-resistant pathogens poses a significant challenge to conventional antimicrobial therapies and underscores the urgent need for innovative therapeutic strategies using highly efficacious and less toxic antimicrobial compounds, as well as more targeted antimicrobial delivery strategies to prevent uncontrolled release, which contributes to the rise of drug resistance. In this study, the design and synthesis of copper-modified mesoporous silica nanoparticles (Cu-MSNs) were described as a stimuli-responsive, smart antimicrobial delivery system incorporating carvacrol as a bioactive alternative to conventional antibiotics. The Cu-MSNs exhibit high surface area, tunable pore size, and efficient carvacrol loading. Copper ions embedded within the silica matrix provide intrinsic antimicrobial activity and may enhance the antimicrobial effect of carvacrol. Poly(2-(dimethylamino) ethyl methacrylate) (PDMAEMA) brushes were anchored on Cu-MSNs via surface-initiated atom transfer radical polymerization (SI-ATRP). The PDMAEMA brushes provided stimuli-responsive behavior, enabling pH- and temperature-dependent modulation of carvacrol release. The successful synthesis of Cu-MSN-PDMAEMA has been confirmed by Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR), thermogravimetric analysis (TGA), elemental analysis (EA), and transmission electron microscopy (TEM). Moreover, stimuli-responsive behavior was confirmed using dynamic light scattering (DLS) experiments, demonstrating the pH- and temperature-dependent response of the PDMAEMA brushes. Finally, the carvacrol release behavior was studied at different pH values by using a sensitive paper-based electrochemical sensor. The multifunctional nanoplatform exhibited antimicrobial activity against both Gram-positive and Gram-negative bacteria as well as antiviral activity against representative enveloped and non-enveloped viral models. This synergistic design combines the benefits of a natural antimicrobial agent, intrinsic metallic activity, and smart polymer regulation, offering an strategy to enhance efficacy while minimizing off-target effects. Release studies demonstrated pH-triggered carvacrol delivery, with enhanced release under acidic conditions, confirming the gating function of the PDMAEMA brushes, highlighting the potential of these particles as an antibiotic-free alternative for preventing microbial infections while mitigating the development of antimicrobial resistance (AMR).

items.title: Diffuse Fabry-Pérot Cavities from a Bifunctional Metal Mesh for Angle-Invariant Electrochromic Camouflage
items.abstract: Abstract Tungsten trioxide (WO3) is a widely studied electrochromic material, yet its monochromatic switching behavior limits its applicability in scenarios requiring dynamic color modulation. To address this limitation, integration with a Fabry-Pérot (F-P) optical cavity has emerged as an effective strategy for expanding color tunability while reducing viewing-angle dependence. In this work, a simplified F-P cavity is constructed using stainless-steel mesh (SSM) as a bifunctional reflector and electrode, with a sputtered WO3 film serving as the electrochromic spacer. This design enables continuous full-spectrum color modulation across the visible range through precise regulation of the WO3 layer thickness. Meanwhile, the microscale topological roughness of the SSM introduces diffuse light scattering, which synergistically couples with F-P interference to compensate for optical path variations at different viewing angles. As a result, angle-independent structural coloration is achieved over a broad viewing-angle range from 15 to 90°. Furthermore, benefiting from the high electrical conductivity and unique porous structure of the SSM, a 14 cm × 14 cm inverted flexible electrochromic device was successfully fabricated. The resulting device exhibits fast switching kinetics, excellent mechanical durability under repeated bending, and stable reversible multicolor performance, demonstrating a scalable and cost-effective platform for adaptive visible-light camouflage and energy-efficient reflective display applications.

items.title: Polymer–Two-Dimensional Filler Composites for Hydrogen Barrier Materials: Transport Theory, Design Strategies, and Experimental Advances
items.abstract: Abstract Hydrogen energy is widely regarded as one of the most promising pathways toward sustainable, low-carbon energy systems. However, hydrogen permeation remains a critical challenges for pipelines, storage vessels, and other hydrogen-related equipment. These issues not only reduce structural reliability but also raise significant safety concerns during long-term service. To mitigate hydrogen permeation, various hydrogen barrier materials, including metals, ceramics, and polymers, have been extensively investigated. Recently, incorporating two-dimensional (2D) materials used as fillers into polymer matrices has emerged as an effective strategy for enhancing hydrogen barrier performance by increasing diffusion tortuosity and suppressing hydrogen transport pathways. As a result, layered silicates (e.g., montmorillonite, MMT), graphene-based materials, MXenes (e.g., Ti3C2Tx), molybdenum disulfide (MoS2), hexagonal boron nitride (h-BN), and layered double hydroxides (LDHs) have attracted increasing attention for advanced hydrogen barrier applications. Despite rapid progress in polymer/2D filler composite barrier materials, which can be implemented as surface coatings, bulk liners, or free-standing films, enhancement of barrier properties through the optimization of nanosheet alignment, interfacial stability, oxidation resistance as well as scalable fabrication and long-term durability remain major challenges. Moreover, a mechanistic understanding of hydrogen transport and the structure–property relationships that determine barrier performance remains also insufficient, limiting their practical employment in hydrogen-energy systems. Therefore, this review systematically summarizes recent advances in polymer/2D filler composite hydrogen barrier materials, with a particular focus on theoretical aspects related to gas permeability in 2D nanocomposites, hydrogen transport mechanisms, structure–property relationships, fabrication strategies, durability, and engineering applications. Finally, current challenges and future perspectives for next-generation multifunctional hydrogen barrier materials are discussed, aiming to provide guidance for the rational design and industrial implementation of advanced hydrogen barrier systems.

items.title: Electrostatically Integrated Cationic Antimicrobials Modulate Hydrogel Stability, Release, and Antibacterial Activity
items.abstract: Abstract Hydrogel platforms for antimicrobial medical devices requiring sustained function must maintain bactericidal activity without compromising mechanical stability or cytocompatibility. Conventional systems often rely on passive antimicrobial loading, which can lead to burst release, rapid payload depletion, and dose-dependent toxicity. Here, we developed an ionic-covalent hydrogel platform in which cationic antimicrobial agents (CAAs) were post-loaded into a sulfonate-rich anionic network designed to provide electrostatic retention. A citrate-cross-linked chitosan–polyacrylamide network was coupled with poly(3-sulfopropyl acrylate) (polySPA) and subsequently loaded with benzalkonium chloride (BAK) or poly(hexamethylene biguanide) (PHMB). CAA loading reduced swelling and dry-mass loss while converting the anionic phase into a regulated antimicrobial reservoir. Compared with physically loaded controls, BAK- and PHMB-containing polySPA hydrogels sustained antimicrobial release over 28 days, retained direct antibacterial activity against Staphylococcus aureus and Escherichia coli after 28 days of release aging, reduced viable bacteria in established biofilms by up to 99%, and showed lower hemolysis after 2 h and higher L929 cell viability after 24 h than physically loaded controls. BAK also reinforced the hydrogel network, with CPMSB-3 reaching nearly 13 MPa dry tensile strength and retaining approximately 2.5 MPa wet tensile strength. In a catheter demonstration, the optimized BAK-containing hydrogel improved lubrication and retained antibacterial activity and restricted Proteus mirabilis catheter-surface migration. A subsequent 7-day pilot rat catheter challenge provided exploratory macroscopic observations but was not used as definitive evidence of in vivo anti-infective efficacy. These findings support electrostatic CAA integration as a structure–property–function strategy for antimicrobial hydrogel interfaces with sustained function.

items.title: Porosity Tunable Silk Fibroin Microspheres Enhance Cartilage Repair in Rabbit Model
items.abstract: Abstract Repairing articular cartilage defects is particularly challenging due to the tissue's hypovascularity and limited intrinsic healing capacity, which pose significant clinical challenges. Biomaterial-based scaffolds have shown promising outcomes in terms of repair capacity; however, finding a robust scaffold system remains challenging in cartilage tissue engineering. In this study, silk fibroin porous microspheres were fabricated using the co-axial electrospraying technique, followed by ethanol treatment to induce crosslinking and enhance microsphere stability. Interestingly, we observed that while changing the ethanol concentration from 100% to 75% to crosslink the silk microsphere resulted in the formation of tunable micropores, with pore sizes up to 87 μm in nonporous microspheres and ranging from 80–200 μm in porous microspheres. Then, we seeded human adipose-derived mesenchymal stem cells (hAdMSCs) onto microspheres to evaluate cell adhesion and proliferation over time. The microspheres exhibited enhanced cell adhesion during in vitro cytocompatibility assessments. Notably, porous microspheres displayed superior cell migration compared to nonporous microspheres, attributed to their interconnected pore architecture. Additionally, hAdMSCs-laden microspheres were further studied for their chondrogenic potential under induction conditions, demonstrating cartilage-specific marker expression. Moreover, macroscopic observations and histological staining images showed cartilage regeneration in a rabbit cartilage-defect model, in which porous microspheres outperformed nonporous counterparts due to their enhanced nutrient transfer and host-scaffold integration. Together, these results suggest that silk fibroin microspheres can mimic the extracellular matrix microenvironment, support cell growth, and promote matrix accumulation for effective cartilage repair.

items.title: Correction to “Self-Healing Hydrogel Resulting from the Noncovalent Interaction between Ropivacaine and Low-Molecular-Weight Gelator Sodium Deoxycholate Achieves Stable and Endurable Local Analgesia In Vivo”
Decoupling Metal Deposition from Contact Formation Enables Polarity Transformation in WSe2 Transistors
items.abstract: Abstract Polarity control in two-dimensional (2D) semiconductor field-effect transistors (FETs) is essential for their integration into complementary logic circuits. However, existing polarity-engineering approaches often fail to preserve high-quality contact interfaces because atomically thin 2D semiconductors are highly sensitive to fabrication processes. Here, we introduce an effective buffer-layer removal process that enables polarity transformation while preserving a high-quality contact interface. A thin semimetal layer (Bi or Sb) is deposited prior to high-work-function metal evaporation and subsequently removed by a wet chemical treatment that preserves a high-quality metal/semiconductor interface. Minimizing the contact angle of the rinsing solution suppresses wrinkle and bubble formations and reduces Fermi-level pinning. The same WSe2 transistors transform from semimetal-dominated n-type transport before treatment to high-work-function-metal-dominated p-type transport afterward. Monolayer devices exhibit a maximum two-terminal hole field-effect mobility of 313 cm2 V–1 s–1 after treatment, while also supporting a maximum electron mobility of 41 cm2 V–1 s–1 before treatment. These results demonstrate n-to-p polarity transformation in WSe2 transistors enabled by a removable semimetal layer, providing a potential doping-free route toward complementary 2D electronics.

items.title: Follicle-Targeted Deep Eutectic Solvent-Lipid Hybrid Nanocarriers for Phloretin against Androgenetic Alopecia
items.abstract: Abstract Androgenetic alopecia (AGA) represents the most prevalent form of hair loss globally. Currently, minoxidil (MNX) is the only FDA-approved topical medication for AGA, but its use is limited by suboptimal efficacy and noticeable side effects. These limitations underscore an urgent demand for safer and more effective treatment options. Phloretin (PHL), a natural flavonoid, offers anti-inflammatory and antioxidant benefits that make it a promising candidate for AGA therapy. However, its practical application is restricted by poor water solubility and low skin permeability. To overcome these challenges, this study used a betaine-mandelic acid deep eutectic solvent (BMDES) to considerably improve the solubility and skin penetration of PHL. Due to the high viscosity of pure BMDES, which can compromise patient comfort, we developed a hybrid nanoparticle system, called BMDES-Lip@PHL, by combining 50% BMDES with liposomes. This strategy effectively harnesses the high drug-loading capacity of BMDES and the follicular targeting and retention properties of liposomes, thereby overcoming the limitations associated with each individual system. In vitro experiments BMDES-Lip@PHL significantly boosted the proliferation and migration of human dermal papilla cells and reduced oxidative stress. It also encouraged follicular angiogenesis and lowered the levels of pro-inflammatory factors. In AGA models, BMDES-Lip@PHL significantly stimulated hair regrowth and prevented collagen degradation induced by oxidative stress and inflammation. Furthermore, the system efficiently eliminated reactive oxygen species, suppressed the inflammatory cytokine TNF-α, reduced lipopolysaccharide-induced nitric oxide production, down-regulated interleukin-6, and promoted angiogenesis, all contributing to a healthier follicular microenvironment. Mechanistic analysis revealed that BMDES-Lip@PHL is associated with Wnt/β-catenin and mTOR signaling, alongside marked Sox9 and phosphorylated S6 up-regulation. Overall, BMDES-Lip@PHL showed outstanding safety and successfully delivered multiple functions including solubilization, penetration enhancement, retention, and targeting, indicating its strong potential as a treatment for AGA.

items.title: Crystalline NiO:N Templating of Uniformly Anchored Self-Assembled Monolayers for Inverted Perovskite Solar Cells
items.abstract: Abstract The buried hole-selective contact in inverted perovskite solar cells (PSCs) is expected to transport holes through its bulk while also templating a defect-free self-assembled monolayer (SAM). A crystalline, vacuum-deposited nitrogen-doped NiO (NiO:N) film deterministically templates a uniformly anchored SAM, while the reactive-atmosphere N2/O2 ratio used during pulsed laser deposition (PLD) simultaneously programs bulk hole density and interfacial anchoring chemistry. Nitrogen incorporation is proposed to act as a shallow acceptor that generates Ni3+ states and raises p-type conductivity, whereas the dense, pinhole-free template enforces uniform SAM coverage, fully suppressing the underlying substrate signal and minimizing surface hydroxyl groups relative to discontinuous nanoparticle films. Consequently, NiO:N/SAM-based PSCs achieve a 6.2% relative increase in power conversion efficiency (PCE) over pristine NiO nanoparticles, reaching one of the highest reported performances for vacuum-deposited NiO-based PSCs, with improved thermal and operational stability. These results establish reactive-atmosphere NiO:N as a general, scalable platform for hole-selective contacts in inverted perovskite photovoltaics.

items.title: SERS-Active Nanocomposite Contact Lenses for Label-Free Multiplexed Biosensing of Tear Analytes
items.abstract: Abstract Continuous monitoring remains limited by the fact that most wearable biosensors are built around single-analyte recognition chemistries, even though many physiological states are defined by changes across multiple metabolites. Tear fluid is one of the most biochemically informative biofluids accessible non-invasively, but contact lens biosensors have largely relied on enzymatic or electrochemical techniques that are difficult to extend beyond one target marker at a time. Here, we report a label-free surface-enhanced Raman spectroscopy (SERS)-active contact lens in which gold nanostars are grown in situ on commercial hydrogel contact lenses. The resulting gold nanostar-loaded contact lens (AuNS-CL) introduces a plasmonic sensing layer directly onto the wearable substrate, with a substrate-averaged SERS enhancement factor of ∼105, while preserving the lens’ physiochemical properties. Quantitative biosensing was demonstrated using a digital thresholding method to account for variable hotspot distributions. Metabolites such as lactate and urea were quantified through their diagnostic bands in several solutions, including artificial tears and a mixture of tear analytes. The AuNS-CLs showed a strong linear response in the physiological range and recovery errors below 10%. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first demonstration of a wearable contact lens for label-free SERS quantification of tear metabolites.

items.title: A Dual-Mode Fluorescence-Surface-Enhanced Raman Scattering Probe Integrated with Magnetic Separation and DSN Amplification for miR-10b Detection in Cancer Serum
items.abstract: Abstract Developing highly sensitive and reliable methods for microRNA detection is crucial for early cancer diagnosis. Herein, a dual-mode fluorescence (FL) and surface-enhanced Raman scattering (SERS) probe was constructed for the ultrasensitive detection of miR-10b, integrating magnetic separation and duplex-specific nuclease (DSN)-assisted target recycling amplification. The probe consists of Fe3O4@AuNPs modified with Cy5-labeled hairpin DNA (H1). Without miR-10b, Cy5 is fluorescence resonance energy transfer (FRET)-quenched by AuNPs (low FL) but SERS-enhanced by localized surface plasmon resonance (LSPR) (strong SERS). Upon target recognition, H1 opens and forms a DNA-RNA duplex, which DSN cleaves, releasing Cy5 fragments and intact miR-10b for recycling. This disrupts FRET and LSPR, causing FL recovery and SERS decrease. Under optimized conditions, the probe exhibited excellent linear responses over a concentration range of 101 to 105 pM in both modes, with detection limits as low as 18.20 fM (FL) and 20.33 fM (SERS). The probe demonstrated outstanding selectivity, excellent reproducibility (batch-to-batch RSD &lt; 2.26%), and good stability over 28 days of storage. Furthermore, the practical applicability was validated by analyzing miR-10b in spiked human serum (recoveries: 99.50%–104.80% for FL; 101.30%–104.09% for SERS) and clinical serum samples from lung, breast, and thyroid cancer patients, where the probe successfully distinguished cancer patients from healthy controls. This dual-mode strategy provides a sensitive and reliable platform for early cancer diagnosis via mutual signal cross-validation and effective suppression of false positives.

items.title: Deep-Learning-Empowered Gold Nanoparticle Dimer-Assisted Hyperbolic Metamaterial Surface Plasmon Resonance Fiber-Optic Sensor for Ultrasensitive Mercury Ion Detection
items.abstract: Abstract Mercury ions (Hg2+) are highly toxic heavy-metal contaminants that pose serious environmental and health hazards, necessitating the development of highly sensitive and accurate detection methods. Herein, a fiber-optic surface plasmon resonance (SPR) sensor is developed for the ultrasensitive detection of Hg2+. The sensing probe is constructed on a hyperbolic metamaterial (HMM) consisting of three repeated Ag/ITO bilayers, decorated with thymine (T)-rich DNA-functionalized gold nanoparticles (AuNPs). Upon Hg2+ addition, specific T–Hg2+–T coordination captures a second population of DNA-functionalized AuNPs, forming AuNP dimers on the HMM surface. The nanometer interparticle gap of the AuNP dimer induces strong plasmonic coupling, which amplifies the local refractive index (RI) changes at the sensing interface and produces a pronounced SPR wavelength shift, enabling highly sensitive detection of Hg2+. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed sensor exhibits a peak RI sensitivity of 8600 nm/RIU and achieves a limit of detection as low as 2.63 pM for Hg2+. Moreover, a DenseNet-based deep-learning model is employed to extract subtle spectral features from SPR spectra acquired at seven Hg2+ concentration levels, enabling quantitative concentration prediction with an R2 of 0.998505. Therefore, the proposed fiber-optic SPR sensor provides a promising strategy for sensitive and accurate Hg2+ detection.

items.title: High-Performance Self-Powered Infrared Photodetector via Semiconducting Graphene Nanoribbon/Germanium Vertical Heterojunctions with Robust Thermal Stability
items.abstract: Abstract Self-powered photodetectors stand as a cornerstone for next-generation low-power electronics, with promising applications in optical communications, environmental monitoring, night vision, and beyond. However, achieving high performance in these devices, particularly under elevated temperatures, remains a persistent challenge. Herein, a short-wavelength infrared (SWIR) self-powered photodetector based on semiconducting graphene nanoribbons (GNRs)/germanium (Ge) vertical heterojunction is presented, demonstrating high-performance detection at 1550 nm. Benefiting from the combined effects of the built-in electric field and interfacial photogating, the photodetector achieves a responsivity of 10.21 A/W, a detectivity of 2.36 × 1011 Jones, and an external quantum efficiency (EQE) of 817% in self-powered mode. Under a reverse bias of –3 V, the photodetector delivers a responsivity of 167.3 A/W, a detectivity of 1.45 × 1010 Jones, and an EQE of 104%. Notably, the device retains a measurable photoresponse at temperatures up to 95 °C, with responsivities of 3 A/W at –3 V bias and 0.1 A/W at zero bias. Together with the demonstrated self-powered infrared imaging capability, our results provide a promising strategy for high-performance, thermally robust SWIR photodetection in demanding environments.

items.title: Decoupled Attraction and Repulsion for Fast, Large, and Reversible Thermal Actuation in Hydrogels
items.abstract: Abstract In thermoresponsive poly(N-isopropylacrylamide) (PNIPAAm) hydrogels, strategies that accelerate heating-induced shrinking often slow down subsequent re-swelling upon cooling, because the driving forces favorable for shrinking and those favorable for re-swelling are fundamentally opposed within a single homogeneous network. This kinetic asymmetry limits the reversibility and cyclability of thermoresponsive actuators. To resolve this trade-off, we propose decoupled attraction and repulsion for thermal actuation (DART), in which the shrinking and re-swelling driving forces are assigned to separate structural components of a hydrogel rather than sharing a single network. Water-swollen, negatively charged poly(2-acrylamido-2-methyl-1-propanesulfonic acid) (PAMPS) nanogels, produced by planetary milling of bulk PAMPS hydrogels, were dispersed throughout a phase-separated PNIPAAm matrix to construct a composite hydrogel (PSG-Pn). The porous, phase-separated matrix enables rapid heating-induced water expulsion, while thermally modulated electrostatic repulsion among the PAMPS nanogels, governed by the temperature-dependent dielectric constant and Debye screening length, drives fast re-swelling upon cooling without impeding the shrinking process. PSG-Pn exhibited shrinking and re-swelling relaxation times of 2.24 and 219 s, respectively, approximately 1250-fold and 14-fold faster than those of a conventional non-phase-separated PNIPAAm hydrogel. PSG-Pn sustained ∼90% volume recovery over 20 heating-cooling cycles in water, and it also maintained repeated shrinking and re-swelling under open-air conditions without drying or structural failure. Building on this response, a near-infrared-responsive bilayer combining PSG-Pn with graphene oxide was steered to crawl in either direction across an unpatterned flat surface simply by switching the irradiation site, without any built-in ratchet or friction asymmetry, a behavior further supported by finite-element analysis of the localized contraction-recovery cycle. Together, these results indicate that partitioning attractive and repulsive driving forces into distinct structural elements offers a broadly applicable strategy for engineering thermoresponsive soft actuators with fast, large-amplitude, and reversible motion.

items.title: Hierarchically Porous PDMS/ZIF-8@h-BN Bilayer Composite Membrane Enabling Synergistic Passive Daytime Radiative Cooling and Efficient Thermal Conduction for Electronic Thermal Management
items.abstract: Abstract The advancement of 5G and emerging 6G communications drives the integration and miniaturization of outdoor electronics, triggering an exponential surge in chip heat flux and severe challenges for low-energy passive thermal management. Passive daytime radiative cooling (PDRC) has emerged as a novel zero-energy cooling technology. Herein, a bilayer PDRC composite (B-PDRC) integrating radiative cooling and in-plane thermal conduction is designed and fabricated. The top radiative cooling layer is a hierarchically porous Polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS)/zeolitic imidazolate framework-8 (ZIF-8) foam prepared via a template-sacrificial method combined with vacuum impregnation, while the bottom thermally conductive layer is a PDMS/hexagonal boron nitride (h-BN) dense film fabricated by solution casting. The multiscale scattering induced by micron-sized pores and 600–800 nm ZIF-8 nanoparticles delivers a high solar reflectance of 94.45%, and the C–N bonds of ZIF-8 boost the average atmospheric window emissivity to 93.22%, compensating for the emissivity valley of neat PDMS. The h-BN fillers construct continuous thermal conduction paths, elevating the in-plane thermal conductivity to 0.92 W m–1 K–1 at 20 wt % of h-BN, a 179% enhancement compared to neat PDMS. Indoor tests demonstrate a maximum temperature drop of 11.9 °C for a charging smartphone covered with B-PDRC. Outdoor measurements under sunny conditions achieve a maximum subambient cooling of 8.8 °C, and a 14.8 °C temperature reduction for an operating smartphone. Furthermore, B-PDRC exhibits excellent hydrophobic self-cleaning performance (water contact angle of 135.4°), flexibility, mechanical robustness, long-term durability under UV and humid conditions, and universal adhesion to various substrates. This work provides a feasible design strategy for high-performance flexible PDRC composites for thermal management of outdoor electronic devices.

items.title: Multifunctional Cross-Linked Micelles for the Treatment of Acute Pneumonia Caused by MDR-KP with Reduced Cytokine Storms and Restored Metabolism and Immune Balance
items.abstract: Abstract Acute pneumonia caused by multidrug-resistant superbugs such as Klebsiella pneumoniae (MDR-KP) poses a severe public health threat for clinical patients with high mortality rate, where excessive cytokine storms and cellular dysfunction are the leading causes of death. More seriously, these superbugs have evolved specialized biological mechanisms that allow them to persist long-term within macrophages, rendering antibiotics and immunomodulators ineffective. Herein, a smart and multifunctional nanomicelle (NAC151-micelle), composed of colistin-NAD+-crosslinked drug and inhibitor H151, is developed for cooperatively killing of MDR-KP bacteria, alleviating hyperinflammatory cytokine storm, and improving metabolism and immune balance. NAC151-micelles optimized through in vitro bactericidal assays can smartly be responsive to the highly reduced environment within infected macrophages, allowing rapid release of active cargoes, including colistin and NAD+, thereby achieving efficient clearance of extra- and intracellular MDR-KP while improving cellular energy metabolism. Meanwhile, co-loaded H151 can cooperatively downregulate key inflammatory pathways of STING-TBK1-IRF3 and NF-κB p65 phosphorylation in macrophages with NAD+, reducing a cytokine storm. In MDR-KP-induced acute pneumonia infection, following intranasal tracheal administration, we observe a targeted accumulation in lung and significant downregulation of MDR-KP burden, together with drastically decreased cytokine storms with good safety. Furthermore, the immune balance in the lung is also greatly improved; pathological tissue injury is effectively repaired; and notably, functional macrophages are essential mediators of their therapeutic efficacy. Collectively, our study presents a safe and multifunctional therapeutic strategy (NAC151-micelles) for acute pneumonia caused by super-bacteria MDR-KP with rapid bacterial clearance, reduced cytokine storms, and improved metabolism and immune balance.

items.title: Electrode-Templated Lateral Crystallization for Advanced Oxide Electronics
items.abstract: Abstract Amorphous InGaZnO has long served as the foundational material for display backplanes. Nonetheless, the escalating demand for ultra-high resolution and reduced power consumption necessitates higher-performance oxide thin-film transistors (TFTs) capable of replacing polycrystalline silicon and enabling fully oxide-based TFT architectures. Crystallization of oxide semiconductors offers a promising route toward higher carrier mobility, yet achieving highly ordered oxide channels on amorphous substrates remains challenging. Herein, we report an electrode-induced lateral crystallization (EILC) method that exploits crystallographic coherence and lattice matching between the electrode and oxide channel to enable formation of highly oriented, large-grained InGaO at a modest temperature of 400 °C. The resultant EILC TFTs exhibit unprecedented electrical characteristics and exceptional bias-stress stability. Structural analyses indicate that crystallographic coherence between the indium tin oxide electrode and the channel, rather than interfacial redox reactions, governs this process, positioning EILC as a paradigm-shifting strategy for next-generation oxide electronics.

items.title: High-Performance MoTe2/TFLN Waveguide-Integrated Photo-field-effect Transistors
items.abstract: Abstract Thin-film lithium niobate (TFLN) is a key platform for next-generation integrated photonics, enabled by its excellent optical properties, low propagation loss, and strong optical field confinement. However, its wide bandgap and weak optical absorption severely restrict direct photodetection, necessitating heterogeneous integration with highly photosensitive materials. Here, we report a high-performance waveguide-integrated MoTe2 photo-field-effect transistor (Photo-FET) on a TFLN platform enabled by heterogeneous integration. Benefiting from gate-voltage modulation, the device exhibits excellent optoelectronic performance, achieving an ultralow dark current of ∼180 pA at a positive gate voltage and a drain–source voltage of –1 V, nearly three orders of magnitude lower than that of the ungated device. Under 1310 nm illumination, the Photo-FET demonstrates a high responsivity of 13 A/W (15.4 nW), a large on/off ratio of 4 × 104, rise and fall times of 467 and 533 μs, respectively, and a high detectivity of 1.3 × 1013 W–1. This hybrid MoTe2/TFLN Photo-FET architecture enables low-noise, high-sensitivity operation, offering a promising route toward telecommunication-band photodetection in integrated photonic systems.

items.title: Enhanced Ferroelectric Performance of P(VDF-TrFE) Composites via MAPbI3-Mediated Crystallization for Flexible Memory Applications
items.abstract: Abstract We report a material-engineering strategy in which methylammonium lead iodide (MAPbI3) perovskite is added to poly(vinylidene fluoride-trifluoroethylene) (P(VDF-TrFE)) composites to overcome intrinsic polarization and stability limitations. MAPbI3 incorporation enhances crystalline ordering and ferroelectric response in P(VDF-TrFE) composites, enhancing β-phase formation and strengthening dipole alignment through electrostatic interactions with –CF2– dipoles while simultaneously increasing dielectric permittivity and suppressing depolarization-field-driven polarization loss. With increasing MAPbI3 content, the composite films exhibit progressively improved ferroelectric performance and reach an optimum at 1.0 wt %, exhibiting a substantial increase in remanent polarization (2Pr from 13.7 to 18.4 μC/cm2), a 2.6-fold enhancement in the ferroelectric field-effect transistor (FeFET) on/off ratio, and a memory window expansion of 0.3 V. However, extremely high loadings and excessive MAPbI3 incorporation lead to aggregation and leakage-related degradation, resulting in reduced crystallinity and switching stability. Using P(VDF-TrFE) composites with optimized MAPbI3 composition, the composite FeFETs achieve extended retention up to 103 s, while the flexible ferroelectric capacitor (FeCAP) maintains stable ferroelectric switching after 10,000 mechanical bending cycles, demonstrating excellent mechanical resilience. These results demonstrate a practical material-engineering strategy for high-performance and mechanically reliable ferroelectric memory using a polymer–perovskite composite design.

items.title: Mononuclear and Dinuclear Nickel Sites on Periodic Mesoporous Silica for CO2 Cycloaddition to Epoxides
items.abstract: Abstract The development of efficient heterogeneous catalysts for converting carbon dioxide into value-added products under mild conditions remains an important challenge. Herein, we report the synthesis of mono- and dinuclear Ni-functionalized materials through stepwise grafting onto periodic mesoporous silica (SBA-15). The materials were systematically constructed via aminosilane functionalization, ligand immobilization, and subsequent coordination of Ni centers, and were comprehensively characterized by several techniques, including PXRD, SEM/TEM, EA, ICP-OES, DRIFT-IR, N2 physisorption, XPS, and solid-state MAS NMR, confirming the successful formation of well-defined surface-bound Ni species. The resulting catalysts were evaluated for the cycloaddition of CO2 to epoxides. The immobilized dinuclear nickel naphthyridine diimine material (Ni2-NDI@SBA-15250) exhibited superior catalytic performance compared with its mononuclear nickel phenanthroline-derived analogue (Ni-PhenDI@SBA-15250) and the corresponding homogeneous systems, achieving high to full conversions and &gt;99% selectivity under relatively mild conditions (80 °C, 10 bar CO2) with only 0.1 mol % Ni. The enhanced activity is consistent with cooperative interactions between adjacent Ni centers, combined with the confinement effects of the ordered mesoporous structure. Furthermore, the catalyst demonstrated good stability and recyclability, with negligible metal leaching as confirmed by hot filtration and ICP analysis. This work highlights the potential of heterogenizing multinuclear Ni complexes within mesoporous frameworks for efficient CO2 utilization and provides insight into the design of robust heterogeneous catalysts for sustainable transformations.

items.title: Suction-Cup-Inspired Fluorescence Turn-on for Integrated Capture and Synergistic Photocatalytic Inactivation of Cronobacter sakazakii
items.abstract: Abstract Cronobacter sakazakii (C. sakazakii) poses a severe threat through contaminated powdered dairy products, necessitating rapid, specific, and effective strategies for its complete management. This work presents a capture–inactivate–detect platform based on an antibody-functionalized magnetic ZIF (Ab-M@ZIF) and a polydopamine-coated AIE photosensitizer (PDA@TPE). The platform enables immunomagnetic capture and generates ROS, while releasing Co2+ ions to permeabilize membranes, weakening their barrier function. Mechanistic studies indicate that the catechol-functionalized flexible PDA shell mediates strong binding to bacterial surfaces, leading to the subsequent generation of a potent ROS storm under light irradiation. Remarkably, this synergistic action achieves a 6-log reduction in bacterial viability within 45 min under visible light. This binding-triggered AIE response enables sensitive detection of C. sakazakii with an LOD of 4.13 CFU/mL. The platform demonstrated recovery rates of 84.01–97.07% (RSD 3.42–8.71%) and complete sterilization in real milk. Biosafety assessments confirm negligible in vitro and in vivo toxicity, with cell viability over 85% at 1 mg/mL under irradiation, verifying fine biocompatibility. This study provides a novel synergistic strategy that combines precise capture, synergistic inactivation, and sensitive detection into a single system, offering a promising solution for enhancing dairy product safety.

items.title: Procaine and Doxorubicin Coloaded Microspheres for Painless and Potent Transarterial Chemoembolization
items.abstract: Abstract Transarterial chemoembolization (TACE) is the standard treatment for intermediate-stage hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). However, its clinical efficacy is severely limited by postembolization syndrome (PES) and the physical vascular barrier induced by embolization. To address these limitations, we developed multifunctional polyvinyl alcohol embolization microspheres modified with polydopamine and coloaded with procaine (PCA) and doxorubicin (DOX), termed pDA-PVA/PCA-DOX. MD/MM-PBSA simulations and physicochemical characterization confirmed that the pDA coating enabled efficient coloading of both drugs via hydrogen bonding and π–π stacking, with the particle size meeting clinical requirements for TACE. The loading capacities of PCA and DOX in this codelivery system reached 4.6 and 4.8 times those of commercial microspheres, respectively. The adsorption kinetics fitted a pseudo-second-order model, and the microspheres exhibited distinct pH-responsive release behavior. In vitro and in vivo studies demonstrated that the sustained release of PCA downregulated proinflammatory cytokines, upregulated IL-10 expression, and reduced macrophage infiltration, thereby exerting analgesic and anti-inflammatory effects. Furthermore, the codelivery of PCA and DOX exerted synergistic antitumor efficacy with a coefficient of drug interaction (CDI) of 0.62–0.63, significantly inhibiting the proliferation, migration, and invasion of HCC cells. In mouse subcutaneous xenograft and rabbit VX2 liver tumor TACE models, the pDA-PVA/PCA-DOX significantly suppressed tumor growth, downregulated angiogenesis-related markers including VEGF, EGFR, and CD31, and modulated the immune microenvironment by increasing intratumoral infiltration of CD4+ and CD8+ T cells. Additionally, the pDA-PVA/PCA-DOX exhibited favorable biocompatibility and hemocompatibility, causing no persistent hepatic or renal toxicity post-TACE. Collectively, this multifunctional coloaded microsphere system integrates efficient embolization, anti-inflammation, analgesia, synergistic chemotherapy, and microenvironment modulation, providing experimental evidence for optimizing TACE therapeutic strategies.

items.title: Thermoresponsive Adhesive Hydrogel Enabling Dynamic Adhesion Switching for Diabetic Chronic Wound Healing
items.abstract: Abstract Diabetic chronic wounds are characterized by persistent inflammation, oxidative stress, increased susceptibility to bacterial infection, and impaired tissue regeneration, which collectively hinder wound repair. Hydrogel dressings have emerged as promising candidates for chronic wound management; however, achieving stable tissue adhesion for wound protection while enabling gentle removal during dressing replacement remains challenging. Although stimuli-responsive adhesive hydrogels have been developed to achieve on-demand debonding, their reliance on external chemical triggers and limited adaptability in complex wound environments restrict their further application. Herein, we developed a thermoresponsive multifunctional hydrogel dressing (HG-CT@Al) that integrates dynamic adhesion regulation with wound microenvironment modulation through a one-pot photopolymerization strategy. The NIPAM/AAm/AA copolymer network endowed HG-CT@Al with temperature-responsive adhesion switching, while the chitosan (CS) semi-interpenetrating network and dynamic coordination interactions between tea polyphenols (TP) and Al3+ enhanced structural stability and provided antibacterial and antioxidant functions. By optimizing the network composition, HG-CT@Al maintained strong tissue adhesion at physiological temperature (35 °C, 167.22 N/m) and reduced adhesion strength after mild heating (45 °C, 97.99 N/m), enabling on-demand gentle debonding. Meanwhile, HG-CT@Al exhibited excellent antibacterial activity against E. coli and S. aureus (99.65 and 99.69%, respectively) and strong antioxidant capacity (95.61% DPPH radical-scavenging efficiency). In a full-thickness diabetic wound model, HG-CT@Al significantly accelerated wound closure and promoted re-epithelialization, collagen deposition, angiogenesis, and M2 macrophage early enrichment. This study presents a multifunctional hydrogel strategy integrating temperature-responsive dynamic adhesion regulation and wound microenvironment modulation, providing an effective approach for diabetic chronic wound management.

items.title: Decellularized Amniotic Membrane–Mesenchymal Stem Cell Composite Enhances Corneal Repair via Mitochondrial Bioenergetics Restoration
items.abstract: Abstract Corneal alkali burn causes persistent inflammation, fibrosis, neovascularization, and vision impairment. Although amniotic membrane (AM) transplantation and mesenchymal stem cell (MSC)-based therapies have shown therapeutic potential, their combined application as a tissue-engineered construct for alkali-induced corneal injury remains insufficiently explored. Here, we developed a decellularized AM-based bone marrow-derived MSC (BMSC) composite and evaluated its therapeutic effects in a mouse model of corneal alkali burn. Compared with AM transplantation or subconjunctival BMSC injection alone, the BMSC-AM composite more effectively reduced corneal opacity and neovascularization, restored epithelial integrity and stromal architecture, and suppressed inflammatory and fibrotic responses. Moreover, BMSC-AM treatment alleviated oxidative stress, as indicated by reduced reactive oxygen species and malondialdehyde accumulation and increased total antioxidant capacity. Seahorse mitochondrial stress analysis further demonstrated that the composite restored mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation, with more pronounced effects at 14 days after injury. Collectively, this study establishes a decellularized AM–BMSC composite as a biomaterial-assisted therapeutic platform for corneal alkali injury and suggests that preservation of mitochondrial bioenergetics and attenuation of oxidative stress contribute to its reparative effects.

items.title: Photoassisted Electrodeposition of Dual-Stabilized Medium-Entropy Films for Robust Water Electrolysis
items.abstract: Abstract Water electrolysis remains constrained in combining excellent catalytic activity with long-term robustness, as both are primarily hindered by insufficient intrinsic activity and the mechanical instability induced by poor catalyst adhesion. This work presents the preparation of a medium-entropy boride (Ce-MEB) film electrocatalyst by a one-step photoassisted electrodeposition strategy. This strategy ensures strong catalyst–substrate adhesion, thereby enhancing mechanical durability. Furthermore, Ce incorporation accelerates OH– adsorption kinetics and promotes in situ formation of active oxyhydroxides, contributing to enhanced electrochemical stability. Consequently, Ce-MEB offers an exceptional OER capability, only demanding an overpotential of 218 mV to afford 10 mA cm–2. This electrocatalyst also remained stable for over 550 h at 500 mA cm–2. Notably, its practical viability is evidenced by an anion exchange membrane water electrolyzer cell sustaining ampere-level current densities for over 160 h. This work introduces an efficient synthesis strategy for advanced entropy-engineered materials.

items.title: Orchestrating a Dual-Cation Kinetic Relay in α-MnO2 Cathodes via Mg–K Site Competition for High-Rate Aqueous Zinc-Ion Batteries
items.abstract: Abstract Aqueous zinc-ion batteries (AZIBs) hold great promise for grid-scale energy storage, yet their performance is limited by sluggish Zn2+ diffusion and irreversible Mn dissolution in MnO2 cathodes. Here, we report a Mg–K dual-doping strategy that establishes a site-competition mechanism in α-MnO2 nanoneedles to enable a synergistic dual-cation kinetic relay. K+ preferentially occupies the 2 × 2 tunnels, enlarging the tunnel spacing and lowering the interfacial desolvation barrier, while Mg2+ stabilizes the MnO6 framework and facilitates bulk Zn2+ migration. This cooperative behavior tunes the pseudocapacitive contribution from ∼29% to ∼70%, indicating that charge-storage kinetics are governed by cation-site occupancy rather than fixed intrinsic properties. The optimized K0.147Mn0.965Mg0.035O2 cathode delivers 322 mAh g–1 at 0.5 A g−1,retains 63.7% capacity after 500 cycles, and exhibits excellent rate recovery (195.07 → 310 mAh g–1 upon returning to 0.1 A g–1). Mechanistic studies reveal a stepwise H+/Zn2+ co-intercalation process accompanied by the formation of ZnMn2O4 and Zn4SO4(OH)6·xH2O, while a self-limiting interfacial passivation layer gradually forms during cycling, effectively suppressing parasitic side reactions and maintaining structural robustness. This work provides insight into multi-ion site competition, offering a generalizable strategy for durable, high-rate manganese-based AZIB cathodes.

items.title: Low-Crosstalk Dual-Channel Temperature–Pressure Sensor Array Based on PEDOT:PSS/MXene/Carbon Foam Composites for Multimodal Recognition
items.abstract: Abstract Reliable electronic skin requires thermal and mechanical inputs to be resolved in the same soft device, but stacked sensor architectures often add fabrication complexity and interfacial coupling. Here, we presented a low-crosstalk dual-channel temperature-pressure sensor based on PEDOT:PSS/MXene/carbonized melamine foam (PMCF) composites, in which pressure and temperature are transduced through distinct physical processes. Reversible contact reconstruction within PMCF defined a piezoresistive channel that modulated conductance under pressure, whereas the PEDOT:PSS/MXene network determined a thermoelectric channel that converted a temperature gradient into voltage. The integrated architecture enabled pressure-dominated conductance and temperature-dominated voltage readouts within the PMCF composites. The thermoelectric channel produced a linear voltage response within ΔT of 0–50 K, a Seebeck coefficient of 37.9 μV K–1, and stable output over 12,000 s of thermal cycling, whereas the piezoresistive channel presented a linear response over 1–20 kPa, with a sensitivity of 1.6409 ± 0.016 kPa–1 and stable output during load-unload cycles for 7000 s. The minimum temperature-difference resolution was 0.1 K. Temperature/pressure channels retained their dominant stimulus origins, with pressure-to-voltage and temperature-to-current crosstalk ratios below 0.40% and 0.35%, respectively. The PMCF sensor facilitated subtle contact acoustic-vibration sensing and array-level multimodal input. A CNN-BiLSTM-attention model from machine learning was employed to classify five acoustic-vibration signals with an accuracy of 97.9%. A CNN model, applied in a 3 × 3 sensor array, recognized digit position, input mode, and joint digit-mode patterns with accuracies of 97.4%, 99.1%, and 96.4%, respectively, indicating that the PMCF sensor array supported low-crosstalk multimodal sensing and array-level human–machine input under controlled conditions.

items.title: Flexible Phase Change Adhesive Allowing Tunable Melting Point for Flexible Electronics Thermal Management with Controlled Adhesion
items.abstract: Abstract Currently, flexible phase-change materials that have been widely investigated for flexible electronics typically exhibit melting points below 60 °C and lack intrinsic interfacial adhesion. These limitations render them inadequate for thermal management under bending, twisting, and other mechanical deformations encountered in flexible devices. To overcome these constraints, we developed a strategy in which novel urea-based phase-change materials (PCMs) were incorporated in situ into a polyacrylate matrix via a solvent-free UV-curing process, thereby constructing a flexible phase-change adhesive (FPCA) that combines strong interfacial adhesion with a tunable melting point covering 60–100 °C. The optimized FPCA formulation (E90A10-H6U-40 wt %) achieves an exceptional combination of properties: high flexibility (tensile strength: 0.44 MPa; elongation at break: 1227%), melt point (74.2 °C), reliable phase change enthalpy (53.4 J/g), strong adhesion (180° peel force: 5.5 N/25 mm at phase-transition temperature), folding endurance exceeding 200 000 cycles, and stable performance after accelerated aging (85 °C/85% Relative Humidity for 168 h). The FPCA series also enables controlled thermal debonding with debonding ratios exceeding 99%, supporting temporary bonding and non-destructive device recycling. This work substantially broadens the material landscape for flexible thermal management and offers a promising pathway toward next-generation, wearable-compatible electronic devices.

items.title: Pt/Ru Ratio Balances Substrate Adsorption and Active Hydrogen for Efficient Aromatic Electrocatalytic Hydrogenation
items.abstract: Abstract Electrocatalytic hydrogenation (ECH) offers a mild route for aromatic-ring reduction without pressurized H2, but is limited by insufficient substrate adsorption and activation, coupled with the competing hydrogen evolution reaction (HER). Here, composition-tunable PtRu nanoalloys are used to investigate how the Pt/Ru ratio couples the metal-H response with benzoic acid (BZA) hydrogenation. In-situ spectroscopy and electrochemical measurements reveal distinct composition-dependent responses to BZA addition. Low-Ru catalysts show a diminishing substrate-induced perturbation under stronger cathodic polarization, whereas Ru-rich catalysts exhibit a predominantly Ru–H response that is weakly perturbed by BZA. The intermediate Pt91Ru9 composition maintains a pronounced BZA-induced decrease in the relative Pt–H contribution. Adsorption-state and reaction-energy calculations support a proposed interfacial process involving H* redistribution between Ru-associated and Pt-associated sites and subsequent hydrogenation of Pt-bound BZA. Pt91Ru9 achieves approximately 82% Faradaic efficiency (FE) in an H-cell and a time-averaged FE of 70.3% during 150 h of continuous-flow operation. These results connect composition-dependent metal-H responses with aromatic hydrogenation and guide the design of cooperative bimetallic electrocatalysts.

items.title: Reactive Oxygen Species-Scavenging Nanozyme Hydrogel for Microenvironment Modulation in Diabetic Chronic Wound Healing
items.abstract: Abstract Diabetic chronic wounds are difficult to heal because persistent hyperglycemia is associated with excessive reactive oxygen species (ROS), impaired angiogenesis, and prolonged inflammation. Here, we developed an Fe3O4@PDA-containing PVA/gelatin/borate hydrogel (FP-PVG) with catalase-like activity. FP-PVG scavenged ROS and promoted H2O2-responsive oxygen generation, while the FP nanocomposite and hydrogel matrix contributed to antibacterial activity. In vitro, FP-PVG showed strong ABTS radical-scavenging activity (98.97% at 2 mg mL–1), favorable cytocompatibility, and improved cell migration under oxidative stress. It also reduced CD86 expression and increased CD163 expression in macrophages, consistent with a shift toward a reparative phenotype. In a diabetic mouse wound model, FP-PVG accelerated wound closure and was associated with reduced oxidative stress and inflammation, increased angiogenesis, and improved tissue regeneration. These findings support FP-PVG as a multifunctional hydrogel dressing for regulating the diabetic wound microenvironment.

items.title: Hydrogen-Mediated, Voltage-Tunable Modulation of the Metal–Insulator Transition in SmNiO3 at Room Temperature
items.abstract: Abstract The broad interest in proton (or hydrogen) doping of strongly correlated oxides, such as perovskite nickelates (RNiO3), stems from their extraordinary modulation of electronic properties that lead to dramatic changes in electrical resistivity. However, the mechanism by which this occurs is not well understood. In this work, in situ X-ray diffraction (XRD), neutron reflectivity (NR), and electrical measurements are utilized to probe the mechanism for a voltage-tunable metal–insulator transition in SmNiO3 (SNO) thin films and memristive devices in hydrogen-rich environments. The SNO films show an immediate expansion of the c-axis lattice parameter at room temperature upon hydrogen exposure, which saturates at a massive value of ∼8%. NR measurements confirm for the first time that this expansion arises from hydrogen incorporation at a ratio of 1:4. In situ current–voltage (IV) measurements reveal that hydrogenation induces a dramatic resistivity change of more than three orders of magnitude, and the protonated Pt/SNO device exhibits a bipolar resistive switching (RS) hysteresis. The RS effects in this system arise from an interfacial Schottky barrier height modulation where proton migration at the Pt/SNO interface and within the SNO film serves as the main driver for the analog IV hysteresis. The dynamics of hydrogen incorporation and desorption are systematically studied in the Pt/SNO device with temperature-dependent electrical characterizations and Avrami model. These results for the first time demonstrate the mechanism by which hydrogen drives electronic transitions in SmNiO3 and, mediated by voltage control, can be used to manipulate the electronic character of neuromorphic devices.

items.title: High-Performance Quasi-2D Perovskite LEDs Enabled by a Multifunctional Small Molecular Additive
items.abstract: Abstract Quasi-two-dimensional (quasi-2D) perovskites have emerged as promising emitters for high-performance light-emitting diodes owing to their superior excitonic properties and high photoluminescence quantum yields. However, inefficient energy funneling arising from the unfavorable distribution of multidimensional phases and abundant defect states remains a major obstacle to achieving highly efficient electroluminescence. Herein, 2-bromodibenzothiophene (BDBT) is introduced as a multifunctional additive to simultaneously regulate phase distribution and suppress defect-assisted non-radiative recombination in quasi-2D perovskite films. The incorporation of BDBT modulates the interaction between organic spacer cations and the perovskite framework, promoting more efficient energy transfer among different-dimensional domains. Meanwhile, the sulfur-containing Lewis base in BDBT effectively coordinates with undercoordinated Pb2+ ions, passivating trap states and reducing non-radiative losses. As a result, the optimized quasi-2D perovskite light-emitting diodes exhibit a peak external quantum efficiency of 19.2% at 515 nm and a maximum luminance exceeding 6500 cd m−2. This work provides an effective molecular engineering strategy for simultaneously optimizing energy transfer and defect passivation, offering new insights into the development of highly efficient quasi-2D perovskite light-emitting devices.

items.title: Interfacial Synergy Triggered Intrinsic Tandem Catalysis for High-Efficiency Electrochemical Nitrate Reduction to Ammonia
items.abstract: Abstract Electrochemical nitrate reduction reaction (NO3RR) has emerged as a sustainable circular-economy approach that enables simultaneous remediation of nitrate-contaminated wastewater and green ammonia synthesis. However, practical implementation of NO3RR is severely hindered by complicated multi-proton-electron transfer processes, undesirable nitrite accumulation, and competing hydrogen evolution reactions. While bimetallic heterostructured tandem catalysts hold great potential to address these issues, conventional spatially separated dual-site configurations still suffer from sluggish intermediate relay, mismatched reaction kinetics, and uncontrollable nitrite desorption. Herein, we fabricate a nanoparticle-assembled needle-like CuO/Co3O4 heterostructure and propose an interfacial synergy-triggered intrinsic tandem catalysis strategy. The optimized CuO/Co3O4 (1:1) delivers an NH3 yield of 1.06 ± 0.07 mmol h–1 mg–1 (0.53 ± 0.035 mmol h–1 cm–2) at –0.9 V vs RHE and a maximum Faradaic efficiency of 95.57 ± 1.15% at –0.8 V vs RHE, superior to monometallic counterparts and physical mixtures. Heterointerfaces modulate intermediate (*NO3, *NO2, *H) adsorption and boost in situ active-hydrogen production to match cascade reaction kinetics. Combined operando characterizations and density functional theory calculations demonstrate that the heterointerface efficiently suppresses excessive *NO2 desorption, strengthens nitrite intermediate trapping, and enriches surface-active hydrogen species, resolving the kinetic mismatch that plagues traditional dual-site catalytic systems. This work establishes an interface-dominated pathway for the design of high-efficiency intrinsic tandem catalysts, breaking through the performance bottleneck of conventional simple phase-mixing strategies.

items.title: Dielectric Elastomers with a High Dielectric Constant and Low Loss for Advanced Soft Actuators and Sensors
items.abstract: Abstract Dielectric elastomers (DEs) show great potential in flexible actuation and strain sensing, but their performance is often limited by the coupling between low dielectric constant and high Young’s modulus, resulting in high driving fields and weak sensing signals. In this work, we propose a molecular design strategy that combines polarity enhancement with crosslinked network regulation. Using urethane diacrylate (CN9021NS) as the matrix, a highly polar -CF3 containing monomer, hexafluorobutyl acrylate (HFBA), is introduced to enhance the dielectric constant. Poly(ethylene glycol) diacrylate (PEGDA) with different chain lengths serves as a small-molecule crosslinker to regulate the network structure. By varying the PEGDA chain length and content, the influence of crosslinker molecular architecture on effective network constraints and chain mobility is systematically investigated. The results show that CHBP10-3 with long-chain crosslinkers achieves a high dielectric constant (7.42@1 kHz), a low Young’s modulus (0.28 MPa), reduced mechanical loss (6.33%), and high stress retention. In electromechanical actuation, the material exhibits a large area strain of 161.73% at 40 kV mm–1. Based on these properties, the CHBP10-3 actuator enables large-angle bending, effective load driving, and serves successfully as a soft gripper. Meanwhile, the CHBP10-3-based sensor shows stable capacitive responses over a wide strain range, allowing applications in human motion monitoring and information encoding. This work offers a simple strategy for crosslinked network regulation and new insights into high-performance dielectric elastomers.

items.title: Engineering Metal-Oxygen Covalency and Sacrificial Sites via GQD-Induced Oxide Reconstruction
items.abstract: Abstract Electrochemical reconstruction behavior under oxygen evolution reaction (OER) conditions plays a pivotal role in governing electrocatalytic performance. Despite its importance, achieving precise control over electrochemical reconstruction and directing it toward desired active structures remain a great challenge. Herein, we report an effective strategy for directing the electrochemical reconstruction of nickel oxides through the incorporation of oxidizable graphene quantum dots (GQDs). During electrochemical reconstruction, Se leaching and GQD oxidative dissolution contribute to the formation of a reconstructed NiOOH framework with modified Ni–O electronic interactions and undercoordinated Ni sites. The resulting electronic and coordination reconstruction promotes lattice oxygen reactivity, while the formation of oxygen nonbonding states helps mitigate excessive lattice oxygen activation and contributes to improved catalyst durability. Remarkably, the reconstructed g-NiOOH exhibits significantly enhanced OER activity, requiring an overpotential of only 225 mV to reach 10 mA cm–2, compared with 436 mV for NiSe2-derived NiOOH. Furthermore, an anion exchange membrane water electrolyzer employing GQDs/NiSe2 as the anode catalyst delivers 6.8 A cm–2 at 2.0 V and sustains stable operation at 2 A cm–2 for over 1000 h.

items.title: Stacking-Sequence Engineering of Functional Metal Bilayers for Rapid Direct-Contact Prelithiation of SiOx Anodes
items.abstract: Abstract Silicon suboxide (SiOx) is a promising anode material for next-generation lithium-ion batteries because of its high capacity and structural stability. However, its practical application is severely limited by substantial irreversible lithium consumption during the first cycle, making effective prelithiation essential for improving the initial Coulombic efficiency (ICE). Although direct-contact prelithiation provides a simple approach for lithium compensation, controlling lithium transfer at the electrode/Li interface remains a major challenge. Herein, Ni/Ag bilayer thin films with identical nominal total metal thickness but different stacking sequences were introduced onto SiOx electrodes to regulate direct-contact prelithiation. Single-layer Ni and Ag coatings together with Ni/Ag bilayers of opposite stacking sequences were systematically investigated to examine the influence of the SiOx-facing and Li-facing metal layers. Among them, the SiOx/Ni/Ag electrode exhibited the most efficient prelithiation behavior, achieving an ICE of 96.9% after only 7 min of direct contact, whereas the SiOx/Ag/Ni electrode reached only 87.7% even after 10 min of prelithiation. Structural and depth-resolved chemical analyses revealed that the optimized stacking sequence promoted more complete conversion toward Li-rich silicate species while suppressing electrode expansion. Consequently, the SiOx/Ni/Ag electrode exhibited lower interfacial resistance and faster electrochemical stabilization while maintaining stable cycling performance. These findings demonstrate that the arrangement of functional metal layers, rather than metal composition alone, strongly influences lithium transfer during direct-contact prelithiation, establishing stacking-sequence engineering as a useful thin-film design strategy for efficient prelithiation of high-capacity Si-based anodes.

items.title: Amyloid–Chitosan Aerogels for Multi-Contaminant Water Purification under Batch and Rapid Flow-through Conditions
items.abstract: Abstract The increasing production of chemically diverse contaminants from industrial, municipal, and healthcare activities has motivated the need for developing innovative wastewater treatment strategies. For example, pharmaceuticals, including ibuprofen (IBP) and sulfamethoxazole (SMX), and toxic heavy metals, such as hexavalent chromium (Cr(VI)) and nickel (Ni(II)), have been increasingly detected in aquatic environments. Traditional water treatment strategies did not account for the removal of such contaminants in mind. Herein, we present a class of protein–polysaccharide composite aerogels constructed from bovine serum albumin (BSA) amyloid fibers and chitosan as adsorbents for the removal of these pharmaceutical and heavy metal contaminants. Amyloid fibers were prepared via acid-induced self-assembly, and chitosan was incorporated post-fibrillation in tunable ratios, followed by crosslinking and freeze-drying to yield highly porous and mechanically durable aerogel networks. Overall, the incorporation of a higher ratio of chitosan resulted in enhanced available surface area, mechanical strength, and structural stability, which collectively contributed to improved adsorption processes. Adsorption was evaluated for individual contaminants between pH 3 and 9, whereby IBP and SMX exhibited optimum removal at pH 6 (up to 92% for SMX), Cr(VI) between pH 3 and 6 (over 97%), and Ni(II) at pH 9 (78%). The aerogels also demonstrated excellent performance in binary pharmaceutical (IBP/SMX) and heavy-metal (Cr(VI)/Ni(II)) mixtures at ppb-level residual concentrations. Finally, we demonstrated the applicability of our aerogels in flow systems, achieving high Cr(VI) removal under both gravity-driven and rapid flow-through filtration, albeit with progressive breakthrough over five consecutive cycles without regeneration of the aerogel. Notably, the rapid-flow system achieved ∼96% Cr(VI) removal in the first cycle in only ∼20 s, comparable to results seen in equilibrium batch experiments. Overall, these findings establish BSA–chitosan aerogels as promising bio-based adsorbents for practical, continuous, and sustainable water purification.

items.title: N-Doped Mesoporous Carbon Film with Pinned Carbon Nanotube as Free-Standing Anode for Fast-Charging Li-Ion Batteries
items.abstract: Abstract A N-doped mesoporous carbon film with a pinned carbon nanotube was prepared by a hydrothermal soft-template self-assembly and metal-catalyzed graphitization approach, using phenolic resin/dicyandiamide as the solid carbon and nitrogen sources and F127 micelles as a mesoporous template. The thickness of the mesoporous carbon membrane was determined by the polymerization degree of phenolic resin and was adjustable by tuning the reagent concentration in the hydrothermal reaction. These NMCF-NCNT films show a high graphitization degree, large specific surface area, rich nitrogen dopant, and high mechanical strength. Importantly, the NCNT grown on the mesoporous carbon film constructs a conductive pathway between the carbon film and coin cell, and the mesopores in NMCF accelerate the electrolyte diffusion when NMCF-NCNT films are applied as free-standing anodes in LiBs. The NMCF-NCNT-1 with a thickness of 1 μm delivered the optimum electrochemical properties of 750 mAh g–1 at 0.1 A g–1, 578 mAh g–1 at 5 A g–1 after 30 cycles, and 661 mAh g–1 at 1 A g–1 after 600 cycles. Such good electrochemical performance could be attributed to the thinnest NMCF-NCNT-1 membrane granting high electrical conductivity, fast Li+ diffusion, and preeminent structural stabilization. This work aims at the preparation of a self-supporting-structured mesoporous carbon film with pinned carbon nanotube, the regulation of micro-nanostructure, and the optimization of electrochemical performance, which may gain a new insight into the design of free-standing carbon membrane electrodes for fast-charging LiBs.

items.title: Localized Trap-State Engineering of Subthreshold Swing in Amorphous In–Ga–O Thin-Film Transistors via Vertically Positioned Sn δ-Doping
items.abstract: Abstract Precise control of the subthreshold swing (SS) in pixel-driving thin-film transistors (TFTs) is critical for accurate gray-scale expression and stable analog current modulation in active-matrix displays. Here, we demonstrate deterministic SS engineering in amorphous indium–gallium oxide (a-IGO) TFTs by controlling the vertical position of a tin (Sn) δ-doped layer within the oxide channel using plasma-enhanced atomic layer deposition. Sn δ-doped layers were selectively inserted near the passivation side, at the middle of the channel, and near the gate-insulator interface, while the macroscopic structural and chemical properties of the channel films remained nearly identical. Despite this structural similarity, the electrical characteristics were systematically modulated solely by the spatial location of the Sn layer. As the Sn δ-doped layer approached the front-channel conduction path, the SS increased from 0.128 to 0.462 V/decade, accompanied by a positive threshold-voltage shift from 0.03 to 0.99 V and a decrease in field-effect mobility from 36.5 to 19.3 cm2/V·s. Energy-band analyses indicate that these position-dependent electrical variations originate from the different degrees of interaction between Sn2+-induced trap centers and the bending quasi-Fermi level during subthreshold operation. This spatial trap-interaction model was further supported by frequency-dependent capacitance–voltage measurements, which revealed more pronounced frequency dispersion and stretch-out behavior when the Sn δ-doped layer was located closer to the front channel. Importantly, the Sn δ-doped TFTs exhibited bias-stress reliability comparable to that of the pristine IGO reference, with threshold-voltage shifts no greater than 0.60 V under the tested conditions. The capture and emission kinetics of the states associated with the Sn2+-related SS modulation remain to be established.
