These results establish vertically positioned Sn δ-doping as an effective and reliable strategy for tailoring the SS of amorphous oxide TFTs, providing a useful device-design pathway for OLED pixel-driving circuits that require precise current modulation and improved low-gray-level uniformity.

items.title: Cold Atmospheric Plasma–Enabled SiO x Nanocoatings for Surface Energy Modulation and Enhanced Seed Germination
items.abstract: Abstract Modern agricultural systems demand higher and more reliable yields under increasing constraints on land, water, and fertilizer inputs. Rapid and uniform seed germination is therefore critical for improving crop establishment and overall yield performance. Although existing strategies, such as ionizing gas treatments, polymer coatings, and nanoparticle-based seed treatments, can enhance water uptake and early vigor, they often suffer from limited stability, processing complexity, or potential seed damage. Here, we introduce a dry, cold atmospheric plasma (CAP)-assisted deposition platform for the conformal SiOx nanocoating of seeds, enabling a hydrophilic, storage-stable surface modification under ambient conditions. The deposition process was systematically optimized to achieve rapid, uniform coating formation directly on the seed surface. As a model system, corn seeds (Zea mays L.) were coated with SiOx nanofilms under optimized conditions. Wettability analysis revealed a ∼4-fold reduction in the static water contact angle for SiOx-coated seeds relative to pristine controls, compared with a ∼2.9-fold reduction for plasma-treated seeds without precursor introduction. Importantly, the SiOx-induced hydrophilicity exhibited superior stability, showing less than 3° contact angle recovery after 21 days of storage, whereas plasma-treated seeds alone displayed ∼50° recovery within 120 h. This stable and enhanced surface hydrophilicity translated into accelerated germination and improved early seedling vigor, resulting in SiOx-coated seeds exhibiting improved total seedling growth immediately after treatment and maintaining an approximately 38% increase compared with pristine controls after storage, demonstrating consistent storage stability. In comparison, the early-germination and seedling-growth advantages of plasma-treated seeds diminished substantially after storage, indicating that CAP-deposited SiOx provides a more persistent and storage-stable functional modification. Collectively, these results establish CAP-deposited SiOx nanocoatings as a scalable, solvent-free nanotechnology platform for stabilizing seed hydrophilicity, accelerating germination, and promoting early seedling growth under agronomically relevant conditions.

items.title: Quantifying Anion Selectivity in SEI Formation for Ether-Based Electrolytes in Lithium Metal Batteries
items.abstract: Abstract While current electrolyte design strategies for lithium metal batteries (LMBs) emphasize the importance of an anion-dominated Li+ solvation structure to promote an inorganic-rich solid electrolyte interphase (SEI), solvation structure-SEI composition relationships remain challenging to quantify. Here, we systematically investigate a series of ether/lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl) imide (LiFSI) electrolytes and quantify the lithium fluoride formed from FSI– decomposition using nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy. We find that both an anion-dominated electrolyte solvation structure and a reductively stable solvent are necessary to achieve anion-selective SEI formation and establish a framework for anion selectivity in ether-LiFSI electrolytes, guided by density functional theory-derived solvent descriptors, which aligns with existing examples of ether-based Li metal electrolytes. Using this model, we identify an electrolyte formulation of tert-butyl methyl ether and tert-amyl methyl ether that achieves a Coulombic efficiency of 99.3%. Ultimately, this study establishes key electrolyte solvent-interphase-performance relationships to enable high-performance LMBs.

items.title: Synergetic Nano-bending, Photo-switching, and Macrocycle Shuttling Effects of Vibration-Induced Emission Lassos on Photoluminescence Properties of Hydrazone-Based [1]Rotaxanes
items.abstract: Abstract 9,14-Diphenyl-9,14-dihydrodibenzo[a,c]phenazine (DPAC) fluorophores exhibited large Stokes shifts and vibration-induced emission (VIE) with bistable cyan (at 475 nm) and orange (at 600 nm) emissions, whereas hydrazone fluorophores (cyan emission at 475 nm) underwent reversible Z/E photo-isomerization, enabling efficient photo-switching. Herein, we introduced synergetic nano-bending and photo-switchable effects on optical switchable hydrazone linkers and macrocycle shuttling effects of VIE-active DPAC stoppers in [1]rotaxanes, wherein mechanically interlocked architecture-imposed spatial constraints could modulate photoluminescence (PL) behaviors in response to multiple external stimuli. Surprisingly, the highest lifetime τavg1 = 11.8 ns (cyan emission lifetime monitored at 475 nm) was obtained in the loosened lasso owing to stronger intramolecular hydrogen bonds of hydrazone units with minor constraints of nano-bending. While macrocycle shuttling was acid/base-triggered between the loosened lasso with a near-white-light emission [CIE (0.26, 0.32)] and the tightened lasso with an orange emission [CIE (0.37, 0.36)], [1]rotaxanes could tune synergetic PL emissions by modulating bent/planar conformations of DPAC units via acid/base controls and Z/E photo-isomerization of hydrazone units upon 365/450 nm exposures in isopropanol (IPA), respectively. The non-interlocked analogue exhibited the largest lifetime decrease (Δτavg1 = –1.9 ns), whereas the loosened and tightened lassos showed smaller decreases of Δτavg1 = –1.6 and –0.6 ns, respectively, demonstrating that nano-bending constraints suppressed hydrogen-bond disruption during Z/E photo-isomerization. Furthermore, the loosened lasso exhibited temperature- and viscosity-responsive emissions due to hydrogen-bonding disruptions of hydrazone units and progressive planarization of DPAC units upon heating to induce lower viscosity. These results highlight the potential of [1]rotaxanes as stimuli-responsive luminescent molecular systems, enabling proof-of-concept demonstrations in temperature and viscosity sensing as well as optical information encoding.

items.title: Controlling Compensation Doping via Multivalent Platinum Acceptors in Tantalum Oxide Thin Films
items.abstract: Abstract Heterostructures of platinum (Pt) and tantalum oxide (Ta2O5) find widespread use in electronic and energy-conversion device applications, yet the electronic role of Pt incorporated within Ta2O5 remains poorly understood. Here, we investigate the influence of Pt incorporation on the electronic structure and properties of amorphous Ta2O5 using two precisely controlled ternary atomic layer deposition (ALD) pathways. Oxygen plasma-enhanced deposition produces host matrices with significantly lower native defect and impurity concentrations than conventional thermal water-based ALD, enabling a systematic investigation of the interplay between Pt dopants and native defects. Controlled Pt incorporation over the range of 0.9–1.9 atom % yields homogeneous, amorphous Pt-doped Ta2O5 thin films containing exclusively Pt(II) and Pt(IV) oxidation states, with no evidence of metallic Pt formation. While the optical bandgap of the Ta2O5 host matrix remains largely unchanged, Pt incorporation introduces optically active acceptor states near the valence band maximum, increases sub-bandgap absorption, and shifts the Fermi level toward the midgap. The relative Pt(II)/Pt(IV) population depends strongly on the defect landscape of the host matrix and exhibits a linear dependence on the Fermi level position, demonstrating Fermi level-controlled charge compensation between native donor defects and multivalent Pt acceptor states. Density functional theory corroborates the acceptor character of Pt and assigns the introduced states primarily to Pt 5d orbitals. Experimentally constructed band diagrams and charge transport measurements further show that Pt incorporation provides a direct means of tuning the electronic properties of Ta2O5. These results demonstrate that multivalent Pt doping serves as a controllable strategy for engineering the electronic structure and transport characteristics of functional Ta2O5 thin films, with direct relevance to memristive, dielectric, and photoelectrochemical devices.

items.title: Simultaneously Boosting Stability and High-Temperature Performance of Ni-Rich Cathode Materials by a Negative-Thermal-Expansion Fast Ion Conductor
items.abstract: Abstract Nickel-rich layered oxide cathodes have attracted extensive attention for high-energy batteries due to their high capacity, but face challenges such as structural instability, mechanical degradation, interfacial side reactions, and thermal runaway. To address these issues, a multiple-benefit strategy is proposed to modify LiNi0.92Co0.03Mn0.05O2 (NCM92) using Li1.1La0.1Zr1.9(PO4)3 (LLZP) featuring both high ionic conductivity and negative thermal expansion through a facile way. The NCM92 modified with 3 wt % LLZP (denoted as LLZP3) exhibits the best electrochemical performance. Compared to pristine NCM92, the Li+ diffusion coefficient and the discharge specific capacity at 10 C are, respectively, increased by 94.2 and 19.9%, while the capacity retention ratios are, respectively, enhanced by 26.0 and 23.4 percentage points after 200 cycles at 25 °C and 60 °C. Meanwhile, the strain after cycling at 60 °C and the released heat when first charged to 4.3 V are reduced by 55.6% and 62.4%, respectively. According to multifarious characterizations, LLZP can significantly improve the Li+ diffusion kinetics of NCM92, alleviate released heat and volume expansion, and suppress microcrack formation and side reactions during charge/discharge cycling. Noticeably, LLZP exhibits anisotropic volumetric contraction via in situ absorbing heat to enhance thermal safety and interfacial stability. It provides a universal and practical approach for developing high-performance energy materials.

items.title: Memory-Enhanced Visible-Light Photonic Synapses in Interface-Engineered ZnON/IGZO Oxide Transistors
items.abstract: Abstract Zinc oxynitride (ZnON) thin-film transistors (TFTs) are attractive visible-light photoactive devices owing to their narrow and tunable optical bandgap; however, the limited population of deep-level trap states can restrict post-illumination carrier retention, resulting in weak photonic synaptic retention. Here, memory-enhanced visible-light photonic synapses are demonstrated using interface-engineered ZnON/Indium gallium zinc oxide (IGZO) double-layer oxide TFTs. A thin IGZO capping layer is integrated onto the ZnON channel to preserve ZnON-dominated red, green, and blue (RGB) photoresponse, while modifying the interfacial electronic environment and carrier-relaxation dynamics. The ZnON/IGZO TFT exhibits RGB responsivities of 2.93, 11.0, and 17.6 A W–1 and specific detectivities of 1.10 × 1012, 3.82 × 1012, and 6.08 × 1012 Jones under red, green, and blue illumination, respectively. The device also exhibits enhanced short- and long-term synaptic retention behavior under pulsed optical stimulation, wavelength-dependent synaptic plasticity, and analogue synaptic weight modulation. Spectroscopic ellipsometry and X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy reveal that the IGZO capping layer preserves ZnON-dominated visible-light absorption, while inducing changes in oxygen-related bonding environments across the bilayer structure. Photoinduced current transient spectroscopy reveals a redistribution of electrically active trap states toward both relatively shallow- and deep-level regions after IGZO capping. The shallow-level states are correlated with enhanced photoresponse, whereas the deep-level states are consistent with delayed carrier relaxation and prolonged post-illumination retention. These results demonstrate that ZnON/IGZO bilayer engineering provides an effective strategy for coupling broadband visible-light sensitivity with tunable carrier-retention dynamics in oxide photonic synapses.

items.title: Heterophase-Engineered Cs3Cu2I5/CsCu2I3 Memristors with Two-Step Resistive Switching
items.abstract: Abstract The quest for energy-efficient memory technologies is critically hindered by the performance gap between high-performing but toxic lead-based perovskites and their environmentally benign yet less reliable lead-free counterparts. Here, we address this challenge by engineering the controlled coexistence of crystallographically 0D Cs3Cu2I5 and 1D CsCu2I3 phases using a scalable, hot-air-assisted process. The resulting heterophase architecture produces composition-dependent structural, interfacial, and chemical environments that strongly influence resistive-switching behavior. The optimized devices exhibit a high ON/OFF ratio of up to 7.4 × 108, more than three orders of magnitude higher than that of the corresponding single-phase films, together with electroforming-free operation and a reproducible two-step SET process that provides distinct resistance states for multilevel memory operation. Combined electrical, XPS, cross-sectional STEM/EDS, and post-switching ToF-SIMS analyses support a hybrid valence-change memory/electrochemical metallization (VCM-ECM) filament-evolution framework involving halide-deficient pathways, Cu–O-related oxygen-containing environments, and redistribution of Ag- and Cu-containing species. The two-step SET behavior and two threshold-like regions in the log–log I–V characteristics are consistent with multistage changes in trap occupancy and conductive-path connectivity without requiring direct assignment of the individual transitions to specific vacancy species. These results demonstrate heterophase engineering as an effective materials strategy for regulating local ionic and electronic transport in lead-free halide memristors and provide a pathway toward high-performance, multilevel nonvolatile memory and other ionically active solid-state devices.

items.title: A Sequentially Disassembling Nanocomposite Hydrogel with Lesion-Triggered Luteolin Release for Multitarget Acne Vulgaris Therapy
items.abstract: Abstract Acne vulgaris (AV) remains challenging to treat due to antibiotic resistance, side effects, and the lack of topical formulations that concomitantly eradicate Cutibacterium acnes, resolve inflammation, and restore redox homeostasis. Here, we report a sequentially pH-disassembling nanocomposite hydrogel (TCL2.16‰@PQ; PQ represents poly(vinyl alcohol)/quaternized chitosan (PVA/QCS)) for comprehensive AV management, in which tannic acid/Cu2+/luteolin metal–phenolic network nanoparticles (TCL NPs) serve as both drug reservoirs and physical crosslinking nodes within PVA/QCS (PQ) matrix. The hydrogel optimally disassembles at pH 6.5, followed by TCL NP disassembly at pH 6.0, enabling microenvironment-triggered release of luteolin preferentially at the AV lesion site (5.0–7.5, 6.35 ± 1.30; healthy individuals: 4.1–5.8). This design enhances skin permeation flux by 1.5-fold compared to TCL NPs alone. Additionally, the hydrogel's shear-thinning and thixotropic properties make it easy to spread and adhere to the skin. In vitro, the hydrogel completely eradicates Cutibacterium acnes and reduces biofilm biomass by 7.6-fold at 0.2 g/mL, polarizes macrophages to the anti-inflammatory M2 phenotype, and scavenges reactive oxygen species through direct radical scavenging and upregulation of SOD/GPx/HO-1. In a murine AV model, the hydrogel achieved complete bacterial eradication and lesion resolution within 14 days, significantly outperforming a commercial metronidazole gel by concurrently reducing inflammation and restoring redox homeostasis. This work establishes a microenvironment-responsive, multitarget nanocomposite platform addressing the core pathogenic factors of AV, presenting a promising alternative to conventional therapies.

items.title: Carboxylic Acid-Based Hole Transport Layer with Both Anchoring and Passivation in Inverted Perovskite Solar Cells
items.abstract: Abstract The hole transport layer (HTL) plays a pivotal role in the performance of inverted perovskite solar cells (PSCs), especially in carrier transport, anchoring to the substrate as a buried interface, and defect passivation. Novel HTLs that simultaneously achieve indium tin oxide (ITO) substrate anchoring, passivation of buried perovskite defects, and favorable interfacial energy alignment are seldom addressed. In this work, we designed a novel HTL (denoted as TPCOOH), which is functionalized with dicarboxylic acid groups in the central phenyl ring, which can anchor onto ITO substrates and passivate the top perovskite, as well as coupling with methylthio-substituted triphenylamine and thiophene units to generate suitable energy alignment and transfer the hole, realizing both passivation and anchoring effects. TPHex, as a control, had dihexyl substitution in the center. Inverted PSC devices based on TPCOOH and TPHex as hole transport layers (0.1 cm2) achieved power conversion efficiencies of 24.68% and 23.72%, respectively. The improved efficiency of TPCOOH-based devices is attributed to suppressed nonradiative recombination, rapid interfacial charge transfer, and minimal energy loss due to well-matched energy levels. These improvements are ascribed to the carboxyl groups in TPCOOH, which anchor to ITO, thus ensuring better film coverage and improved charge transport, while the passivation functionality simultaneously mitigates perovskite defects. Notably, the TPCOOH and TPHex devices retain 75% and 65% of their initial power conversion efficiencies (PCEs) after 1200 h of thermal aging at 65 ± 5 °C in a nitrogen atmosphere.

items.title: Quantifying Effective van der Waals Interactions Across Two-Dimensional Material Interfaces
items.abstract: Abstract Van der Waals (vdW) interactions play a central role in determining the properties and functionality of two-dimensional (2D) materials and their heterostructures. However, quantitative nanoscale characterization of these interactions remains challenging. Here, we introduce a universal multifrequency atomic force microscopy (AFM) framework for quantitative mapping of effective vdW interaction landscapes and the extraction of effective Hamaker constants with Ångström-scale vertical resolution. Using graphene, graphene oxide, hexagonal boron nitride, molybdenum disulfide, and highly oriented pyrolytic graphite as model systems, we systematically investigate the influence of layer number, substrate, defects, step edges, surface roughness, and functionalization on local vdW interactions. The measurements reveal pronounced spatial variations and nonadditive behavior, demonstrating that effective Hamaker constants can be enhanced or suppressed by nanoscale structural and interfacial features. This work provides a rapid and versatile approach for nanoscale characterization of vdW interactions and offers new opportunities for engineering interfacial forces in 2D materials and van der Waals heterostructures.

items.title: Nanozymes as Heterogeneous Catalysts: In Operando Aggregation and Altered Apparent Substrate Affinity Affect Catalytic Properties and Immunoassay Reliability
items.abstract: Abstract Nanozymes are synthetic nanoscale catalysts that are actively explored as functional replacements for natural enzymes in various applications. Often, the properties and characteristics of enzymes are directly transferred to nanozymes without considering their unique features as nanosized heterogeneous catalysts. In this article, we explore two often-neglected factors: reduced substrate binding and aggregation of peroxidase-mimicking nanozyme particles that occur in operando (i.e., during catalysis or sample incubation). A competitive Langmuir–Hinshelwood model was utilized to evaluate the impact of organic solvent on substrate binding. In operando aggregation of Au@Pt particles was confirmed by visible spectroscopy, dynamic light scattering, and ultramicroscopy. We demonstrate that both reduced substrate binding and aggregation significantly affect the kinetic parameters of nanozyme catalysis, including approximately three-fold decrease of the apparent Michaelis–Menten constant, a six-fold decrease of the maximum reaction rate, and erroneous conclusions regarding activity inhibition. The effect of aggregation was studied in microplate immunoassays and lateral flow immunoassays of Staphylococcal enterotoxin A (SEA). The results demonstrate that aggregation leads to a reduced specific signal (from immunocomplexes of SEA with Au@Pt-mAb) and an increased nonspecific signal (from aggregated Au@Pt), resulting in a lower signal-to-noise ratio. As a consequence, this leads to false-positive results in microplate immunoassays or even ruins lateral flow immunoassay performance. These results confirm that in operando colloidal stability and substrate binding are crucial factors to be considered for the accurate quantification of kinetic parameters and for various bioanalytical applications.

items.title: Probing Counterion Distribution Around Cationic Metal–Organic Cages by Fluorescence, Analytical Ultracentrifugation, and Molecular Dynamics
items.abstract: Abstract We report a convenient fluorescence-based approach to probe the counterion association around soluble, cationic metal–organic cages (MOCs) in aqueous solution. Two MOCs incorporating tetra-(4-pyridylphenyl) ethylene (TPPE), an aggregation-induced emission (AIE) chromophore, were employed to monitor the spatial distribution and binding of counter-anions across a range of ionic strengths. Alterations in the fluorescence response of the TPPE groups sensitively respond to the changes in their local environment, providing a probe of counterion location and distribution. The results suggest a stepwise counter-anion association mechanism around MOCs: first around the Pt vertices dominated by electrostatic interactions at low counterion-to-MOC ratios, then interacting with the TPPE ligands at higher ratios. Analytical ultracentrifugation (AUC) results and all-atom molecular dynamics simulations are in good agreement with this proposed two-stage association mechanism and suggest distinct spatial preferences of different anions. This combined experimental–computational strategy provides a broadly applicable method for elucidating counterion distributions and dynamics around charged nanoscale species in solution.

items.title: Drop-to-Drop Transfer of Magnetic Activity: Imparting Significant Heterogeneity and Reactivity to a Drop via Functionality Transfer from Another Drop
items.abstract: Abstract Interactions between nanoparticles (NPs) and liquid drops have been widely utilized to manipulate both drops and NPs. However, achieving their separation without altering the intrinsic state of either component has remained a significant challenge in NP-laden drop systems. In our previous work (ACS Appl. Mater. Interfaces 2024, 16, 64253–64263), we addressed this challenge by extracting magnetic nanoparticles (MNPs) from the interior of an MNP-laden drop as a compact aggregate under the influence of an external magnetic field. In the present paper, we develop a technique that enables the seamless transfer of this extracted MNP aggregate from one liquid drop (the source drop) into the interior of a second liquid drop (the receiver drop). Remarkably, the aggregate, which can be tracked throughout the transfer process, is transferred nearly in its entirety, while neither drop undergoes any permanent deformation throughout the process. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first demonstration of a seamless drop-to-drop transfer of NPs, or, more broadly, the transfer of one drop’s functionality to another (here magnetic activity) without permanently altering the morphology of either drop. Beyond facilitating the NP transfer, the process transforms the receiver drop into a heterogeneous system that exhibits a variety of intriguing phenomena. For example, the transferred NPs can self-assemble into either skyscraper-like solid structures or magnetically responsive liquid layers. The nature of these assemblies depends on whether the MNP transfer occurs once or multiple times, and these assemblies display markedly different dynamics when subjected to magnetic fields of varying orientations, as well as oscillating and rotating magnetic fields. Furthermore, the transfer process converts the receiver drop into a highly stable microreactor for chemical reactions, enabling reaction products to form and persist while remaining minimally exposed to external disturbances that could otherwise compromise their stability.

items.title: Defect Passivation via a Bifunctional Guanidinium Sulfamate Ligand for High-Efficiency Perovskite Solar Cells
items.abstract: Abstract Achieving high crystallinity and low defect density remains a critical bottleneck for maximizing the power conversion efficiency (PCE) and operational stability of perovskite solar cells (PSCs). Herein, we introduce guanidinium sulfamate (GASM) as a bifunctional ligand to modulate the defect chemistry of perovskite films. DFT calculations reveal thermodynamically favorable binding of GASM to defect sites on selected α-FAPbI3 (100) surface models. Separately, the stronger (100) diffraction response observed by XRD is consistent with improved film crystallinity, although a change in out-of-plane texture cannot be excluded. Meanwhile, theoretical and spectroscopic results suggest Pb–O coordination involving the sulfamate moiety and N–H···I hydrogen bonding involving the guanidinium moiety, consistent with the observed defect-passivation effect. The GASM-treated perovskite films show a stronger (100) diffraction response, larger grains, and a longer photoluminescence lifetime. The resulting n–i–p structured PSCs deliver a champion PCE of 24.43%, alongside environmental stability. These results highlight the potential of GASM as an additive for improving perovskite film quality and suppressing defect-assisted nonradiative recombination, contributing to enhanced photovoltaic performance.

items.title: Decoupling Electrochemical Performance from External Pressure via Mechanically Interlocked 3D Interfaces for Ultra-low-pressure Supercapacitor Pouch Cells
items.abstract: Abstract Supercapacitor pouch cells typically require substantial external stack pressure (typically &gt;2 MPa) to maintain intimate internal interface contact. However, the heavy packaging modules introduce significant inactive mass, reducing system-level energy density. Herein, we report a two-step aligned 3D imprinting strategy that fundamentally decouples electrochemical performance from external compression. By engineering a mechanically interlocked structure, the compaction force is precisely directed toward the interfaces between the active particles, as well as between the particles and the current collector. This prevents lateral slippage, achieving ultra-low internal electrode resistance and conformal interface contact. Consequently, compared with planar electrodes, imprinted electrodes exhibit a 14.3-fold lower interfacial resistance and a 2.7-fold lower equivalent series resistance even under 0.3 MPa stack pressure, delivering an unprecedented average power density of 285 kW kg–1 at 1 mg cm–2 and 28.4 kW kg–1 at 5 mg cm–2. Notably, pouch cells based on 3D-D electrodes sustain 100,000 cycles with 99% capacitance retention, benefiting from the mechanically stabilized interface and the suppressed resistance evolution. Furthermore, this paradigm is compatible with roll-to-roll manufacturing processes, providing a versatile and scalable approach for the next generation of high-power, lightweight, and ultra-low-pressure supercapacitor systems.

items.title: High-Entropy Design of Commensurate Antiferroelectric Ceramics with Superior Energy Storage Performance
items.abstract: Abstract Antiferroelectric (AFE) ceramic dielectrics are imperative for next-generation energy-storage capacitors because of near-zero remnant polarization. In this work, we construct a new high-entropy antiferroelectric ceramic to synergistically optimize dielectric energy storage by reconstructing the commensurate polarization modulation, thereby delivering an ultrahigh recoverable energy density (Wrec) of ∼14.2 J/cm3 at 71 kV/mm while maintaining a high energy efficiency (η) of ∼84%. In addition, the ceramics deliver remarkable fatigue resistance with stable performance over 105 charge–discharge cycles. This study highlights entropy engineering as a powerful framework for designing high-performance AFE energy-storage ceramics and offers insights for the future development of advanced dielectric capacitors.

items.title: Pain-Perception-Inspired Neuromorphic Sensing: Nonmonotonic Electrical Response and Spatial Visualization in a Near-Infrared-Responsive MXene Hydrogel
items.abstract: Abstract Neuromorphic sensory devices that encode environmental stimuli at the sensing interface offer a route toward more adaptive machine–environment interactions. Ionic hydrogels provide mechanically compliant, ion-conducting hydrated networks that can incorporate photothermal components. However, many near-infrared (NIR)-responsive hydrogels show conductivity changes in one direction, while terminal electrical signals provide little information about stimulus location. Achieving response-direction reversal and spatially resolved visual feedback in one soft material using a single NIR input, therefore, remains challenging. Inspired by protective inhibition and post-stimulus rebound in pain-related neural signaling, we developed an NIR neuromorphic sensory device based on a Ca–PAA–EMB@IL-MXene hydrogel. The material couples photothermal conversion by IL-MXene with temperature-dependent ion transport in a hydrated Ca2+-coordinated PAA-EMB network. Weak irradiation transiently enhances conductivity, whereas stronger or prolonged irradiation drives the conductivity through a maximum into a suppressed state, followed by rebound and recovery after stimulus removal. Thermal, electrical, optical, and water-state measurements are consistent with heat-induced water redistribution and reorganization of the hydrated network, with the characteristic transition temperatures regulated by the EMB content. Programmed NIR pulses further produce paired-pulse facilitation-like behavior, signal accumulation, and responses dependent on recent stimulation history. Localized irradiation induces reversible whitening in the exposed region, supplementing the overall electrical signal with spatial information. An impedance-acquisition and microcontroller interface converts these responses into initial, strong-stimulus warning, and recovery states. This work provides a soft-material strategy for encoding NIR stimulus intensity, duration, history, and location through coupled electrical and optical outputs, supporting NIR-responsive neuromorphic sensing and warning interfaces.

items.title: Bright-Field-Hidden Disordered Atomic Textures for Physically Unclonable Functions
items.abstract: Abstract Optical physical unclonable functions (PUFs) relying on unique microscopic randomness serve as a root of trust for advanced hardware security. However, existing optical PUFs typically rely on disordered structural features at the hundred-nanometer or micrometer scale, facing increasing threats from rapidly advancing 3D nanoprinting technologies. Here, we exploit the atomic-scale thickness irregular texture formed during the epitaxial growth of semiconductor thin films as unclonable nanofingerprints, which demand subnanometer-level precision in the vertical direction for any cloning attempt. Such atomic textures are optically stealthy under bright-field microscopy due to their extremely low thickness. To address this, metallic nanofilms are deposited on the semiconductor surface, enabling the visualization of the patterns via surface plasmonic scattering at the metal nanostep edges under dark-field optical microscopy. The proposed PUF offers advantages, including compatibility with semiconductor fabrication processes, high randomness encoding capacity, bright-field concealment, and strong resilience against physical replication. Based on this PUF, we propose a multilevel key scheme applicable to various application scenarios, demonstrating significant application potential in high-security fields, such as device anticounterfeiting, traceability, information encryption, and authentication.

items.title: Issue Editorial Masthead
Issue Publication Information
Low-Solvent Mechanochemical MOF Carrier Nanoarchitectonics for Targeted Quercetin Delivery for Dual-Mode ROS and Anti-inflammation Protection against LPS-Induced Acute Lung Injury
items.abstract: Abstract Nowadays, inhalable administration of nanomedicines is an appealing concept for acute lung injury (ALI). For ALI nanomedicine, it is appealing to achieve targeted delivery and on-demand release in the ALI microenvironment, which is acidic, rich in reactive oxygen species (ROS), and with elevated inflammatory mediator levels. Notably, customized metal–organic frameworks (MOFs) could fulfill these requirements and thus are promising nanocarriers for ALI medicine delivery, but MOFs formulated often suffer from unreacted residues with hazardous risk. Herein, we report a low-solvent mechanochemical synthesis method to formulate cerium-doped zeolitic imidazolate frameworks (Ce-ZIFs) stabilized by Pluronic F127 as drug delivery nanocarriers to load quercetin for targeted preventive ALI therapy. The nanoplatform exhibits robust structural integrity, high drug loading capacity, excellent biocompatibility, and pH-responsive release of quercetin under acidic conditions, mimicking the inflamed lung microenvironment. Importantly, the nanoplatform ameliorates pro-inflammatory mediators (TNF-α, IL-6), inhibits pulmonary edema, and attenuates alveolar injury in an LPS-induced ALI mouse model. Notably, Ce/ZIF promotes the Ce+3/Ce+4 redox process to generate catalase-like activity for catalytic reactive oxygen species (ROS) scavenging and sustainable antioxidant properties. Transcriptome sequencing and biological validation also revealed that the nanoplatform showed its remarkable ability to counteract LPS-induced oxidative damage and inflammatory responses by suppressing Th1 cell polarization. This work demonstrates a Ce/ZIF platform formulated using a scalable, low-solvent mechanochemical synthesis method, presenting a biocompatible MOF platform with significant promise for targeted pulmonary delivery with protective potential against LPS-induced acute lung injury.

items.title: Spatially Programmed Water Access Reconciles Service Stability with Triggered Post-Use Degradation in Biobased Multilayer
items.abstract: Abstract Sustainable packaging plastics often face a fundamental paradox: the material must resist moisture and remain stable during service, yet undergo controlled disassembly after disposal. Therefore, sustainable materials should not be evaluated solely based on their service performance or degradation rate, but rather on their ability to undergo effective functional transitions at critical stages throughout the lifecycle. Here, we developed a spatially programmed design strategy that addresses these conflicting requirements by regulating not only when and where water enters the material, but also how the degradation proceeds. The film consists of a hydrophilic, pectin-based inner layer, a hydrophobic polylactic acid (PLA) outer layer, and a hydrogen-bonded interface formed via hydrogen bonding. During packaging service, the PLA layer acts as a moisture-shielding skin, maintaining wet stability, barrier performance, and mechanical integrity. A key conceptual advance of this work lies in turning an inherent weakness into a lifecycle-regulating function, where water sensitivity serves as a trigger rather than a limitation. After use, assisted by mechanical damage, water activates the pectin/deep eutectic solvent (DES) phase. The acidic, water-rich microenvironment generated by the pectin/DES supports preferential cleavage near the PLA chain ends, promoting progressive molecular weight reduction while preventing premature failure that could compromise service performance. Density functional theory (DFT) calculations further establish a molecular-level structure–function relationship within the architecture. The calculated interfacial binding energies and molecular interactions elucidate the origin of structural stability during service, while comparative analysis of PLA ester bond cleavage pathways demonstrates a more favorable energetic pathway for terminal ester cleavage after activation, supporting the chain-end-preferential degradation tendency. In contrast to conventional multilayer materials that mainly improve individual properties, this work provides insights into biopolymer design, moving beyond the long-standing trade-off paradigm of stability and degradability by spatially programming these functions as complementary components within a lifecycle-balanced architecture.

items.title: Interfacial Origin of Mn Promotion in Ni/AlO x Catalysts for Methane Pyrolysis and Carbon Nanotube Growth
items.abstract: Abstract Commercial deployment of methane pyrolysis (MP) requires H2 to be produced at a high rate while the solid carbon is recovered as a marketable product such as multiwalled carbon nanotubes (MWCNTs). Various promoters have been explored for Ni-based MP catalysts, including Mn, but the origin of its effect has remained elusive. Here, Ni/AlOx catalysts containing 0 to 5 wt % Mn were used to separate the two roles that Mn plays in activity and stability. The amount of Ni exposed at an oxide boundary correlated with the apparent CH4 reaction order across the series, identifying the Ni–O–Mn perimeter as the site at which CH4 activation is promoted. The same perimeter converted weakly bound NiO into strongly interacting species that resisted encapsulation, linking the rate and the lifetime of the catalyst to a single interface. At 1 wt %, Mn the apparent activation energy fell from 93.9 to 84.2 kJ mol–1, the CH4 reaction order rose from 0.46 to 0.84, and the turnover number increased from 375 to 456 mol C mol Ni–1. At 2 wt %, MnOx began to bury the Ni surface, and above that loading it segregated into a separate phase, so the promotion was lost. Mn also improved the graphitization and conductivity of the MWCNTs formed at the start of the reaction, but this benefit faded as disordered carbon accumulated. Co-feeding H2 suppressed this accumulation and gave MWCNTs with an electrical conductivity comparable to that of commercial material. The benefit of Mn is therefore set by where it resides rather than by how much is added, and both products of MP reach useful quality only when the promoter loading and the reaction conditions are optimized together.

items.title: Engineered Dielectric Response of Liquid-Filled Interfacial Bubbles in van der Waals Heterostructures
items.abstract: Abstract Interfacial bubbles in van der Waals (vdW) heterostructures are typically regarded as unavoidable byproducts of stacking. Here, we show that they can be repurposed as engineered dielectric nanocavities by intentionally trapping selected liquids during assembly. A simple prewetting step before stamp transfer forms liquid-filled bubbles at hBN/graphite interfaces containing acetone, ethanol, H2O, and NaCl(aq), alongside untreated reference bubbles. Electrostatic force microscopy (EFM), crosstalk correction, and finite-element modeling enable quantitative extraction of the effective dielectric constant (εeff) of individual bubbles, revealing higher εeff for all liquid-filled bubbles than for untreated ones. To estimate the apparent core permittivity of the confined contents, each bubble is modeled as a liquid core enclosed by an hBN shell. Simulations of the tip–bubble–substrate geometry yield core dielectric constants (εcore) larger than εeff yet physically consistent with the trapped media. Acetone and ethanol exhibit εcore values close to their expected dielectric properties, whereas water shows a reduced εcore consistent with nanoconfined pure water. Notably, NaCl(aq) shows a larger εcore than pure water, suggesting distinct electrolyte dielectric behavior under nanoscale confinement. This work establishes vdW bubbles as versatile platforms for engineering local electrostatic functionality and probing confined-liquid dielectric physics in two-dimensional (2D) material assemblies.

items.title: Open-Air Fabricated Pseudo-Planar Heterojunction Organic Solar Cells with Improved Efficiency and Thermostability via Suppression of Interfacial Degradation
items.abstract: Abstract Boosting both photovoltaic performance and long-term stability is currently the main challenge for organic solar cells (OSCs). In this regard, adopting a pseudo-planar heterojunction (PPHJ) photoactive layer is a promising solution because of its favorable vertical phase distribution; however, it is subject to the limitation of donor/acceptor (D/A) interfacial degradation. Herein, polyvinylidene fluoride (PVDF) is introduced as a multifunctional donor additive, enabling the suppression of interface degradation in the PPHJ photoactive layer and thereby improving the efficiency and thermostability of devices. Specifically, the introduction of PVDF slightly enhances the molecular packing and dielectric property of the photoactive layer, leading to reduced exciton binding energy (Eb) and enhanced charge transport capability of the materials. These improvements stabilize the interfacial morphology and thus suppress interfacial degradation, including deposition-induced and aging-induced degradation. Moreover, PVDF’s hydrophobicity improves moisture tolerance, enabling reliable open-air fabrication of the photoactive layer under high humidity. As a result, the open-air fabricated OSCs achieve an impressive efficiency of 19.24% with enhanced storage stability and thermal stability, which is one of the highest efficiencies for open-air fabricated OSCs. This work highlights the importance of suppressing interfacial degradation in improving performance and stability of PPHJ OSCs and provides a promising strategy to address it.

items.title: Synergistic Catalysis at the Ni3Te2–Ni3C Heterointerface: Accelerating Water Dissociation for Efficient and Robust Hydrogen Evolution in Alkaline Water and Seawater
items.abstract: Abstract The alkaline hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) is kinetically limited by sluggish interfacial water dissociation and the subsequent hydrogen intermediate conversion, making the cooperative regulation of consecutive HER elementary steps crucial for achieving efficient electrocatalysis. However, most reported HER heterostructures primarily rely on global electronic structure modulation, while function-oriented interfacial regulation of distinct reaction steps remains insufficiently explored. Herein, a Ni3Te2–Ni3C heterostructure electrode was in situ fabricated on nickel foam via a one-step electrodeposition strategy and systematically evaluated for HER in both alkaline freshwater and alkaline seawater. Mechanistic investigations indicate that Ni3C promotes interfacial water activation and dissociation, whereas the Ni3Te2–Ni3C heterointerface further optimizes the kinetics of hydrogen intermediate conversion, thereby enabling the cooperative regulation of consecutive HER elementary steps. In situ Raman spectroscopy, together with density functional theory (DFT) calculations, provides supportive evidence for the facilitated water dissociation and optimized hydrogen intermediate conversion at the heterointerface. Benefiting from such functional complementarity, the optimized Ni3Te2–Ni3C/NF electrode requires overpotentials of only 26 and 32 mV to achieve 10 mA cm–2 in 1 M KOH and alkaline seawater, respectively, while maintaining good stability under the investigated operating conditions. This work establishes a structure–interface–activity relationship and provides a reaction pathway-oriented design principle for developing efficient alkaline HER electrocatalysts.

items.title: Host-Defined Trap Polarity Enables Carrier Buffering and Regulates Exciton Dynamics in Deep-Blue MR-TADF OLEDs
items.abstract: Abstract Multi-resonance thermally activated delayed fluorescence (MR-TADF) emitters such as ν-DABNA have enabled highly efficient deep-blue organic light-emitting diodes (OLEDs). However, their device performance is strongly governed by the electronic structure of the host matrix. Here, we demonstrate that ν-DABNA displays a distinct host-dependent reversal of charge-trapping polarity in three representative host matrices—mSiTrz, mCBP, and PhCzBCz in an identical device architecture. Specifically, ν-DABNA behaves as a hole trap in mSiTrz, an electron trap in PhCzBCz, and a bipolar trap in mCBP according to its energy level. The electroluminescence (EL) spectra of ν-DABNA-based devices exhibit nearly identical peak positions around 470 nm, and the mCBP-based device delivers the highest peak EQE at low current density, a relatively serious efficiency roll-off at high current density, and a long device lifetime, indicating the bipolar carrier-buffering effect of doping ν-DABNA. Transient EL measurements reveal a clear decoupling between charge formation and emissive decay processes. The rise dynamics strongly depend on host-dependent trap polarity, leading to a significant variation in turn-on time, while the decay dynamics remain invariant across all devices, confirming that delayed fluorescence is exclusively governed by intrinsic ν-DABNA reverse intersystem crossing (RISC). The temperature-dependent single-carrier current measurement and transient EL decay once again demonstrate the mechanism of carrier trapping and thermal detrapping by ν-DABNA doping in different host systems. Based on these findings, we introduce a host-defined trap-polarity function, ΦH, which quantitatively captures electron–hole transport asymmetry governed by energy-level offsets to link the charge transport and exciton dynamics in ν-DABNA-based MR-TADF OLEDs. This work establishes a universal host-level-controlled trap-assisted emission model for doped MR-TADF OLEDs.

items.title: Aniline–Peroxide-Initiated Cyclodextrin-Containing Monoliths for Scalable PFAS Removal from Water
items.abstract: Abstract Per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFASs) are a class of persistent environmental contaminants that cause negative health effects. These health concerns and impending regulations motivate demand for PFAS removal technologies. Such technologies must be capable of high-throughput, continuous-flow operation, and maintaining treatment performance at large-scales in municipal and industrial treatment systems. Many PFAS remediation technologies rely on particle-based sorbents, which are subject to mass-transfer limitations in large-scale flow-through systems that can limit PFAS removal performance. Recently, we introduced monolithic sorbents for PFAS removal based on styrene-functionalized β-cyclodextrin polymers whose porosity can reduce these mass-transfer limitations. The first monolith formulations were prepared by photoinitiating polymerization within flow-through columns, which limited the monolith’s practical scalability. Here, we address this limitation by using a redox initiation process at room temperature, which is compatible with the high internal phase emulsion and enables scalable fabrication across column dimensions. Mercury porosimetry revealed a bimodal pore size distribution and a larger characteristic maximum pore size in the redox-initiated monoliths compared to the monomodal pore size distribution observed in the photoinitiated materials. Chemical composition and batch adsorption performance remained consistent across redox-initiated monoliths scaled to 36 times the original monolith cross-sectional area. Redox-initiated monoliths outperformed photoinitiated monoliths in flow-through columns, showing later breakthrough of the short-chain PFAS, perfluorobutanoic acid. We also evaluated the PFAS removal performance of scaled redox-initiated monoliths in columns of increasing diameters (0.5, 1, and 1.5 cm). Their performance was consistent across scales, indicating that redox-initiated monoliths with larger cross-sectional areas maintain their promising sorption performance.

items.title: EGCG@ZIF-8@Polydopamine-Functionalized Janus Nanofibrous Dressing with Directional Exudate Transport and Photothermal Antibacterial Activity for Infected Wound Treatment
items.abstract: Abstract The treatment of infected skin wounds continues to face multiple challenges, including bacterial resistance, persistent inflammation, oxidative damage, and inadequate exudate management. To address these issues, a multifunctional Janus wound dressing was constructed to achieve coordinated infection control and tissue repair. Zeolitic imidazolate framework-8 (ZIF-8) was used as a nanocarrier for the natural antioxidant molecule, and polydopamine surface coating endowed the composite nanoparticles with photothermal antibacterial activity. The composite nanoparticles were subsequently incorporated into a hydrophobic polycaprolactone layer by electrospinning and combined with a hydrophilic polyacrylonitrile layer containing a pH indicator, thereby forming a bilayer structure with unidirectional liquid transport, visual monitoring, and wound protection functions. The dressing promotes the outward transfer of wound exudate and produces an observable color response to changes in environmental pH. Under near-infrared irradiation, the antibacterial rate of the dressing reached 98.89% against E. coli and 99.99% against S. aureus. The dressing also possesses excellent free-radical-scavenging capacity, indicating its potential to alleviate excessive oxidative stress in infected wounds. Animal experiments further demonstrated that the dressing reduced the local infection burden, promoted wound closure, collagen deposition, and tissue formation, and caused no obvious histopathological abnormalities in major organs. Overall, this study presents a multifunctional Janus nanofibrous dressing that integrates antibacterial activity, antioxidant function, exudate regulation, and wound-status monitoring, providing a material-design approach for the repair of infected skin wounds.

items.title: Entropy–Enthalpy Synergistic Quinary A-Site Engineering for High-Luminance and Stable Green Perovskite Light-Emitting Diodes
items.abstract: Abstract Multicomponent A-site engineering is effective in enhancing perovskite crystallization and optoelectronic performance, yet the cooperative mechanism of different cations in regulating crystallization kinetics remains unclear. Here, we propose an entropy–enthalpy synergistic quinary A-site strategy to modulate the crystallization of green 3D perovskites. By sequentially incorporating MA+, GA+, Cs+, and Rb+ into FAPbBr3, we constructed binary to quinary systems. This approach synergistically lowers the Gibbs free energy (ΔG), strengthens the thermodynamic driving force, and reduces the nucleation barrier (ΔG*), leading to dense and uniform nucleation as well as optimized crystal growth. The quinary device achieves a maximum luminance of 222,973 cd m–2 and maintains an External Quantum Efficiency (EQE) above 8% across 30,000–170,000 cd m–2. The peak luminance and maximum EQE are improved by approximately 12-fold and 20-fold, respectively, compared to the unary control. The device also exhibits an operational half-lifetime (T50) of 80 min at 13,000 cd m–2, corresponding to a projected lifetime of 1.47 × 104 h at 100 cd m–2. This work elucidates the synergistic role of multicomponent A-site cations in crystallization control and offers a promising route toward high-luminance brightness and stable 3D Perovskite Light-Emitting Diodes (PeLEDs).

items.title: Construction of Multivariate Hierarchical Metal–Organic Framework/Polymer Composites by Redox Concomitant Reconstitution Method for Photothermal Catalytic CO2 Conversion
items.abstract: Abstract The rational design of metal–organic framework/polymer (MOF/polymer) composites featuring integrated architectures and synergistic functionalities represents an effective strategy for developing advanced materials whose emergent properties outperform those of individual components. Herein, we report a Redox Concomitant Reconstitution (RCR) strategy that enables the concomitant structural reconstitution of metastable MOFs and in situ polymer functionalization, resulting in hierarchical MOF/polymer composites with structure-function synergy. Upon exposure to a mixed methanol/pyrrole vapor, the metastable CuCo-PC precursor is structurally reconstituted into hierarchical CuCo-MOF-74 enriched with Cu(0)/Cu(I)/Cu(II)/Co(II) multimetallic sites, while pyrrole is concomitantly oxidatively polymerized into a conformal polypyrrole (PPy) layer, yielding CuCo-MOF-74/PPy composites with integrated architecture and functionality. Benefiting from the synergy among the multimetallic catalytic sites, hierarchical porosity, and PPy photothermal layer, the composite achieves a 96% yield in the photothermal catalytic CO2 cycloaddition using sterically hindered long-chain epoxides and maintains robust stability over 10 consecutive cycles. This work establishes the RCR strategy as a versatile platform for constructing advanced multifunctional MOF/polymer composites with tailored architectures and synergistic functionalities, opening new opportunities for solar-driven CO2 valorization and the rational design of next-generation MOF-based hybrid materials.

items.title: A Carrier-Free, Co-assembled Nanoplatform for Synergistic Photothermal Therapy: Integrating High-Efficiency BODIPY with Heat Shock Protein Inhibitors
items.abstract: Abstract The simultaneous delivery of boron-dipyrromethene (BODIPY) photosensitizers and heat shock proteins (HSPs) inhibitors to tumor sites can enhance the therapeutic efficacy of photothermal therapy (PTT). Current strategies mainly rely on physical encapsulation into nanocarriers or chemical conjugation onto polymer backbones for the co-delivery of BODIPY and HSP inhibitors. However, these approaches are hampered by drug leakage, reproducibility, or synthetic polydispersity. Herein, we report a carrier-free, co-assembled, and self-delivery nanoplatform to overcome these limitations. An amphiphilic BODIPY derivative (BODIPY-OEG) was synthesized and co-assembled with HSP inhibitors quercetin (Q), yielding nanoparticles (B@Q) with high photothermal conversion efficiency. The resulting B@Q nanoparticles not only possessed favorable photothermal performance in vitro but also had been demonstrated to possess potent antitumor capabilities by inhibiting the expression of HSPs in tumor cells. In vivo, B@Q demonstrated potent antitumor activity by suppressing subcutaneous tumor growth and lung metastasis, while also eliciting a potent systemic immune response, demonstrating its excellent antitumor efficacy. This work proposes a simple and precise co-assembly strategy to construct carrier-free, multifunctional nanotherapeutics, which opens avenues for the concept of self-delivered synergistic PTT agents.

items.title: Composition-Dependent Dielectric Response and Broadband Electromagnetic Wave Absorption in Sulfide/rGO Composites
items.abstract: Abstract Broadband electromagnetic wave absorption depends on the frequency dependence of the composite response, not simply on the magnitude of dielectric loss. Here, CuS, CoS, and CuCo2S4 are combined with reduced graphene oxide (rGO) at a fixed sulfide-to-carbon mass ratio to examine how sulfide composition affects dielectric response and thickness-dependent absorption. Compared with CoS@rGO and CuS@rGO, CuCo2S4@rGO exhibits superior electromagnetic wave absorption, which is attributed to the synergistic effects of interfacial polarization and balanced dielectric and magnetic losses. It achieves an effective absorption bandwidth of 6.84 GHz at 2.4 mm and a minimum reflection loss of –46.7 dB at 2.9 mm. The CuCo2S4@rGO is also processed into poly(vinylidene fluoride) films. Electromagnetic measurements on stacked and pressed film specimens establish the response of the PVDF-based composite, while individual films show bendability, altered infrared thermal contrast, and self-extinguishing behavior under the tested conditions. This study relates sulfide-dependent dielectric response to broadband absorption and examines the processing of the absorber into a polymer composite.

items.title: Light-Responsive Hybrid Lipid Nanoparticles with Gold Nanorods for Light-Triggered DNA Delivery
items.abstract: Abstract Gene therapy is a cutting-edge strategy for treating, preventing, and potentially eradicating a wide range of diseases. Its success is critically dependent on the transfection efficiency of gene delivery systems. In this context, lipid nanoparticles (LNPs) are widely investigated for the delivery of plasmid DNA. However, their performance still lacks precise spatiotemporal control. To address this limitation, we present a novel plasmonic hybrid delivery system composed of gold nanorods (AuNRs) assembled on the LNP surface. This architecture integrates the efficient delivery properties of LNPs with the optical responsiveness of AuNRs, enabling the light-induced release of plasmid DNA upon near-infrared (NIR) laser irradiation. The morphology of AuNRs was specifically tailored to achieve photothermal (PT) heating under NIR laser excitation, thereby enabling PT-assisted regulation of transfection. Thermo-optical, physicochemical, and morphological analyses confirm that LNP/AuNRs display the desired features, including an absorption band centered at 860 nm, a unimodal size distribution, and a positive surface charge. Ultrastructural evaluation by transmission electron microscopy (TEM) reveals cellular internalization of LNP/AuNRs and robust plasmid DNA transfection following NIR laser irradiation. PT heating significantly enhances transfection efficiency in human embryonic kidney 293 (HEK293) cells compared to nonirradiated samples. Biomimetic assays using anionic liposomes revealed that NIR-triggered DNA release is facilitated by nanoparticle–membrane interactions, likely involving structural destabilization of the hybrid system under PT activation. Time-lapse imaging and multichannel confocal microscopy revealed that NIR-induced PT activation modulates the intracellular dynamics of LNP/AuNRs by reducing lysosomal association and promoting a more diffusive behavior, potentially contributing to enhanced cargo availability and transfection efficiency. These findings demonstrate the multifunctional properties of LNP/AuNRs as an efficient, light-responsive platform for PT-triggered plasmid DNA delivery, opening a new avenue for on-demand gene therapy.

items.title: Correction to “Heptazine vs Triazine: Phase-Dependent Activity of V-Doped C3N4 Catalysts in Electrochemical N2 Reduction”
Toward Reuseable Particle-Based Materials: Solvency-Controlled Selective Recovery of Distinct Polymer-Coated Nanoparticles from Model and Device Surfaces
items.abstract: Abstract Selective recuperation of nanoparticles from device interfaces is a necessary condition for establishing circular economy approaches for a range of devices ranging from sensing to light harvesting in photovoltaics. We present a solution-based approach, which demonstrates “orthogonal” re-dispersion of different nanoparticle types by exposure to green solvent mixtures. Our approach is centered around co-nonsolvency-induced volume-phase transitions in polymer brushes at flat and nanoparticulate surfaces, which serve to control the adhesion force between the nanoparticles and the macroscopic surface depending on the composition of the mixed solvent. By employing polymers that enter the co-nonsolvency regime at markedly different solvent compositions—here poly(N-isopropylacrylamide) and poly(2-methacryloyloxyethyl phosphorylcholine)—it becomes possible to selectively release one sort of nanoparticles, while another particle sort remains adhered. This phenomenon was demonstrated in washing tests on silicon model substrates and real device surfaces, and it was mechanistically rationalized by coarse-grained molecular dynamics simulations. Our work thereby serves as an essential step toward disassembly strategies for particle-based materials and devices that aim at re-using the nanoparticulate building blocks.

items.title: Dynamic Decoupling as a Strategy for Highly Selective H2O2 Electrosynthesis
items.abstract: Abstract Electrochemical H2O2 synthesis via the 2e– oxygen reduction reaction (ORR) is a promising sustainable alternative to conventional industrial production. Nonetheless, its practical efficiency is fundamentally capped by the inherent coupling of catalytic kinetics, interfacial electric field, and mass transport, becoming a critical bottleneck for classical static electrolysis strategies. Here, a dynamic decoupling strategy (i.e., a temporal separation of the dominant interfacial constraint rather than a physical decoupling of involved processes) is introduced and validated on a Co-ONx-C single-atom-catalyst-based cathode, employing pulsed electrolysis to modulate the coupled processes in the time domain. This dynamic approach engineers the electrocatalytic interface through three time-separated effects of unequal weight: mass-transport replenishment during the rest interval predominantly enhances H2O2 accumulation, interfacial-field modulation across the potential of zero charge governs the selectivity improvement, and support-defect modulation enables efficient Co-site utilization. As a result, this unconventional approach promotes a 2.7-fold enhancement of H2O2 concentration over the static mode, significantly suppressing the parasitic H2 evolution reaction. Validated in a photovoltaic-driven system with over 100 day stable production, this work establishes dynamic decoupling as a smart design principle for next-generation environmental electrocatalysis.

items.title: Multiscale Magnetic–Dielectric Coupling in Bidirectionally Aligned Multilayer Graphene/FeSiAl Aerogels for Broadband Electromagnetic Wave Absorption
items.abstract: Abstract Lightweight electromagnetic wave (EMW) absorbers with broad attenuation bandwidths are highly desirable for electromagnetic protection and stealth applications, yet their development is limited by the persistent trade-off between impedance matching and attenuation capability. Although aligned porous architectures have been widely explored to enhance electromagnetic dissipation, most existing strategies rely on unidirectional or single-component alignment and rarely enable the coordinated orientation of magnetic and dielectric phases together with macroscopic impedance grading. Herein, bidirectionally aligned graphene/FeSiAl/polyimide aerogels with coupled micro- and macroscale architectures are fabricated through magnetic-field-assisted directional freezing. At the microscale, a horizontal magnetic field orients ferromagnetic FeSiAl flakes, whereas a vertical temperature gradient directs the alignment of graphene/polyimide cell walls, forming an orthogonally ordered magnetic-dielectric network that promotes conductive loss, interfacial/dipolar polarization, and magnetic dissipation while regulating impedance matching. The optimized single-layer aerogel achieves a maximum effective absorption bandwidth (EAB) of 6.13 GHz at only 1.32 mm, representing a 52.49% improvement over its temperature-gradient-only counterpart, together with a minimum reflection loss (RLmin) of –57.35 dB at 1.74 mm. At the macroscale, layer-by-layer freezing constructs multilayer aerogels, enabling broadband EMW entry and progressive energy dissipation. The optimized multilayer aerogel delivers an ultrabroad EAB of 12.49 GHz and an RLmin of –54.23 dB, yielding a pronounced radar cross-section reduction of 34.08 dB under normal incidence. This multiscale coupling strategy provides an effective route toward lightweight, thin, and broadband EMW absorbers.

items.title: Interfacial Doping and Band Bending Boosting Thermoelectric Power Factor in 1T′-MoTe2/Bi2Te3 Quantum-Dot Films
items.abstract: Abstract Superlattice films are promising candidates for obtaining excellent thermoelectric performance because the hetero-interface can effectively regulate both carrier and phonon transport. However, the atomic and electronic structures at the hetero-interface remain largely unexplored, limiting the deep understanding of interfacial effects. Here, 1T′-MoTe2/Bi2Te3 quantum-dot films were fabricated for investigating the 1T′-MoTe2/Bi2Te3 hetero-interface and its effect on electrical transport. Atomic-scale characterizations indicate apparent Mo doping at the hetero-interface, while band structure calculations and transport measurements reveal that Mo doping can reconstruct the conduction band and enhance band degeneracy, leading to a large carrier effective mass of ∼1.6 m0. Meanwhile, spectroscopy measurements verify donor-like states and local band bending at the hetero-interface, which introduce modulation doping and thereby enable synergistically optimized electron density and carrier mobility. As a result, the best (1T′-MoTe2)0.8(Bi2Te3)12 film achieves a peak power factor of ∼3.74 mW m–1 K–2 at 325 K. These findings provide new insights of interfacial effects on synergistically optimizing carrier transport and electrical properties of thermoelectric superlattice or quantum-dot films.

items.title: Composition-Dependent Atomic Layer Etching of Multicomponent Oxide Semiconductors with Preserved Electrical Performance
items.abstract: Abstract Oxide semiconductors are promising channel materials for next-generation memory device scaling, owing to their low off-state current, low-temperature processability, and excellent compatibility with back-end-of-line manufacturing. Here, we report the composition-dependent atomic layer etching (ALE) behavior of the multicomponent oxide semiconductor InGaZnOx (IGZO), enabled by a hydrogen-based surface modification chemistry. The constituent cations of IGZO exhibit markedly different reactivities toward hydrogen, allowing the overall etch rate to be systematically tuned through elemental composition. Because this reaction is largely confined to the near-surface region, ALE minimizes damage to the underlying front-channel region, achieving atomic-scale material removal with minimal degradation of electrical performance, in contrast to conventional dry-etching approaches that often degrade transistor characteristics. Leveraging this low-damage, self-limiting characteristic, we further demonstrate that ALE enables post-deposition trimming of nonuniform IGZO films conformally deposited within three-dimensional trench structures, improving step coverage to nearly 100%. These results establish hydrogen-based ALE as a versatile, composition-aware process for the atomic-scale control of multicomponent oxide semiconductor channels, offering a low-damage route toward scalable three-dimensional memory device architectures.

items.title: Immunomodulatory and Antioxidant Biomimetic Hydrogel Coloaded with Glycyrrhizic Acid and Copper Gallate for Synergistic Cartilage Regeneration
items.abstract: Abstract Articular cartilage lesions are persistently restrained by three interwoven pathological drivers: chronic inflammatory response, sustained oxidative stress, and progressive extracellular matrix (ECM) catabolism. Coupled with the inherently weak self-repair capacity of hyaline cartilage, effective therapeutic interventions for such injuries remain an unmet clinical demand owing to the inherently poor self-repair capacity of hyaline cartilage, effective therapeutic interventions remain an unmet clinical demand. Herein, we engineered a biomimetic composite hydrogel designated ECM/HAMA/GA@Cu-GA, which integrates decellularized cartilage extracellular matrix, methacrylated hyaluronic acid (HAMA), glycyrrhizic acid (GA), and copper gallate (Cu-GA). This integrated hydrogel platform simultaneously endows biomimetic mechanical support, potent anti-inflammatory and antioxidative bioactivities, as well as robust chondrogenic induction capacity. In vitro cellular evaluations verified the outstanding biocompatibility of the composite hydrogel. The biomaterial efficiently polarizes macrophages toward the anti-inflammatory M2 phenotype, suppresses the secretion of pro-inflammatory mediators and matrix-degrading proteases, and facilitates the migration and chondrogenic differentiation of bone marrow mesenchymal stem cells (BMSCs). Transcriptomic profiling suggested that its underlying molecular mechanisms may involve activation of the PI3K/Akt signaling cascade and blockade of the NF-κB-mediated inflammatory pathway. In vivo assessments using rat articular cartilage defect models demonstrated that the ECM/HAMA/GA@Cu-GA hydrogel achieves satisfactory synchronous regeneration of hyaline cartilage and subchondral bone at 4 and 8 weeks post-implantation, with superior regenerative performance relative to all control groups. Collectively, this multifunctional hydrogel enables comprehensive remodeling of the pathological joint microenvironment with favorable biosafety profiles, representing a translatable candidate strategy for clinical management of cartilage degenerative disorders.

items.title: Na-Layer K+ Pillaring with CeO2 Coating Enables High-Rate and Air-Stable P2-Type NaMn-Layered Oxide Cathodes
items.abstract: Abstract P2-type NaxMnO2 cathodes offer high capacity and elemental abundance, yet their practical application is limited by the Jahn–Teller distortion of Mn3+ and irreversible phase transitions that drive structural degradation, capacity fading, and air sensitivity. Prevailing strategies rely predominantly on element substitution at transition-metal sites, whether via single or dual doping, or in combination with coating, but inevitably impose a capacity–stability trade-off rooted in the alteration of the TM–O framework. Here, we demonstrate a synergistic strategy to construct a high-rate, air-stable P2-Na0.62K0.05MnO2/CeO2 cathode, by combining K+ bulk doping at Na sites with a CeO2 surface coating. The K+ bulk doping mitigates the Jahn–Teller effect, eliminates the low-voltage P2–P′2 transition, and converts the high-voltage P2–OP4 transition into a solid-solution reaction, while the CeO2 overlayer concurrently provides resistance to ambient air. The optimized Na0.62K0.05MnO2/CeO2 cathode delivers 67.95 mAh g–1 at 10C, retains 84.00% of its capacity after 200 cycles at 1C and 71.03% after 500 cycles at 5C, and preserves structural integrity after air exposure and water immersion. This dual-modification approach establishes Na-site doping as a design principle that decouples structural stabilization from transition-metal redox activity in P2-type oxide cathodes.

items.title: Synergistic Interface Engineering of Dopamine and SDBS for Constructing High-Performance Graphene/Sponge Composites With Enhanced Stability and Sensitivity
items.abstract: Abstract Despite significant advances in sponge-based pressure sensors for wearable devices and human–machine interfaces, achieving a sponge composite that simultaneously delivers ultrahigh sensitivity, a broad detection range and long-term mechanical stability remain a critical challenge, largely owing to the weak interfacial adhesion between the conductive nanofiller and the sponge skeleton. Herein, we demonstrate a robust interface engineering strategy for a multifunctional composite essentially consisting of a polydopamine (PDA)-modified polyurethane (PU) sponge and sodium dodecyl benzenesulfonate (SDBS)-functionalized graphene. The PDA coating affords a positively charged surface rich in catechol and amino groups, whereas SDBS imparts negative charges and stable dispersibility to graphene. First-principles density functional theory (DFT) calculations reveal the interfacial interactions and electronic structure evolution between the PDA@PU sponge and Gr@SDBS nanosheets, revealing synergistic hydrogen bonding and electrostatic attraction that ensure strong adhesion and uniform graphene decoration. Such a robust interface established by multiple noncovalent interactions facilitates the conformal and uniform decoration of graphene onto the 3D PU skeleton, thereby establishing a highly stable and continuous conductive pathway. The resulting Gr@SDBS/DPA@PU sponge composite delivers an outstanding sensitivity (6.46 kPa–1), a wide detection range (up to 550 kPa), a rapid response time (31.1 ms), and exceptional cyclic stability (up to 5000 cycles). Furthermore, by integrating a miniaturized wireless Bluetooth module, the sensor enables accurate real-time monitoring of finger joint movements and wireless gesture-based remote human-machine interaction. This work provides mechanistic insights into interface engineering of graphene/sponge composites and establishes a novel paradigm for smart wearable electronics.

items.title: Dynamic GelMA/Oxidized Hyaluronic Acid Hydrogels Enable Acid-Accelerated Localized Delivery of Photothermal Melatonin-Derived Carbon Dots for Infected Bone Repair
items.abstract: Abstract Infected bone defects remain difficult to reconstruct because bacterial persistence, acidic stress, excessive reactive oxygen species (ROS), inflammatory dysregulation, and impaired osteogenesis reinforce one another. Here, sulfur-doped melatonin carbon dots (DM-CDs) were synthesized from melatonin and d-cysteine and immobilized within a gelatin methacryloyl (GelMA)/oxidized hyaluronic acid hydrogel (GH-DM) through dynamic Schiff-base interactions. Sulfur-containing surface states endowed DM-CDs with strong 808 nm absorption, an approximately 50% photothermal conversion efficiency, stable heating cycles, and NIR-amplified antibacterial activity. The melatonin-derived surface simultaneously scavenged ROS, preserved mitochondrial membrane potential, and was associated with increased Nrf2 and Sirt1 transcript levels together with recovery of CAT and SOD activities in mouse bone marrow mesenchymal stem cells (BMSCs). Under acidic conditions, dynamic imine interactions were associated with modestly accelerated DM-CD release, whereas NIR irradiation provided an external means to amplify local heating and antibacterial performance. GH-DM reduced planktonic bacterial viability and biofilm biomass, decreased cell-associated Staphylococcus aureus signals, and enhanced BMSC osteogenic differentiation, as shown by ALP activity, matrix mineralization, and increased RUNX2, ALP, COL1, and OCN expression. Mouse BMSC RNA sequencing revealed enrichment of collagen-containing extracellular-matrix programs and attenuation of NF-κB, IL-1β, IL-6, and osteoclast-differentiation-related signatures. Separate LPS-stimulated RAW264.7 experiments supported attenuation of a pro-inflammatory state and increased IL-10 expression. In infected femoral defects, GH-DM plus NIR markedly reduced bacterial burden and improved trabecular regeneration, with no detectable major-organ histopathology or abnormalities in the measured hematological, hepatic, and renal indices. These findings support a locally delivered carbon-dot hydrogel with acid-accelerated release that coordinates infection control, redox protection, inflammatory regulation, and bone regeneration.

items.title: Shape-Memory Photonic–Plasmonic Crystals for Programmable Surface-Enhanced Raman Scattering
items.abstract: Abstract Surface-enhanced Raman scattering (SERS) has emerged as a powerful analytical technique for ultrasensitive molecular detection. Integrating photonic architectures with plasmonic nanostructures provides an effective strategy to enhance SERS by exploiting slow-photon effects. However, continuously and reversibly controlling photonic enhancement remains a significant challenge. Here, we report a shape-memory photonic–plasmonic crystal (SMPPC) that enables programmable slow-photon signal enhancement through reversible structural reconstruction. By exploiting its shape-memory properties, the optical response of SMPPC can be reversibly modulated through solution evaporation or mechanical contact. Structural reconstruction dynamically modulates the spectral detuning between the excitation wavelength and the photonic stopband edge, resulting in a nonmonotonic SERS response governed by the interplay between plasmonic hotspot evolution and slow-photon effect. The fully recovered SMPPC substrate delivers an 8.1-fold enhancement in SERS intensity compared with the plasmonic copolymer SERS substrate. As a proof of concept, the SMPPC substrate enables the detection of antibiotics in municipal wastewater effluents at concentrations down to 471 ppt. This work establishes shape-memory-enabled photonic reconfiguration as a strategy for programmable manipulation of SERS, opening new opportunities for adaptive photonic–plasmonic sensing platforms.

items.title: Bioinspired Curvature-Driven Droplet Transport on Slippery Lubricant-Infused Elastomeric Surfaces for Efficient Passive Fog Collection
items.abstract: Abstract Atmospheric fog harvesting is a promising route for decentralized water production, yet its efficiency remains limited by droplet pinning and dissipative transport. Here, we address these constraints through a bioinspired strategy that integrates cactus-like conical geometries with slippery lubricant-infused elastomeric (SLIE) coatings based on PDMS–silicone oil networks to regulate droplet dynamics. The SLIE interfaces exhibit consistently low contact angle hysteresis across liquids of varying surface tensions, confirming robust omniphobicity. Unlike conventional liquid-infused surfaces, the PDMS-based slippery elastomeric interfaces eliminate observable droplet cloaking and exhibit low contact angle hysteresis, promoting sustained low-dissipation droplet transport suitable for fog harvesting. This synergy between surface chemistry and geometric asymmetry results in a significant enhancement in fog harvesting performance. SLIE-functionalized conical substrates achieve up to (∼150%) higher water collection rates compared to hydrophilic controls, driven by reduced viscoelastic resistance and accelerated droplet shedding. Furthermore, decreasing cone apex angles (5°–10°) amplifies Laplace pressure gradients, leading to earlier droplet mobilization and improved collection efficiencies relative to larger cone angle geometries (30°–45°). These findings establish a mechanistic design framework that integrates omniphobic liquid interfaces with curvature-induced transport, providing a scalable strategy for next-generation passive water harvesting systems.

items.title: Spatially Confined Protein Condensates Enable Sustainable Food Manufacturing
items.abstract: Abstract Escalating climate pressures paired with rapid global population expansion threaten long-term animal protein security. The global plant-based protein market, presently valued at US$20–22.5 billion, is forecast to expand to US$38–43 billion by the early 2030s, signaling a robust translational demand for scalable, sustainable manufacturing of alternative proteins. However, most alternative proteins are featured by intrinsic colloidal instability, limiting their deployment in tailor-made viscoelastic food materials.
