This work establishes spatially confined liquid–liquid phase separation (SCLLPS) as a versatile approach towards viscoelastic protein manufacturing. Kinetically, driven by synergistic surface patch interactions and volume exclusion effects, proteins at a high loading (15.0 wt %) undergo selective phase partitioning and become spatially entrapped within anionic domains of polysaccharide matrices. Thermodynamically, the release of cavity-wrap water and retention of bound water jointly provide the energetic driving force forming protein-enriched liquid condensates with long-term colloidal stability. Mechanically, such spatially ordered condensates afford exceptional control over bulk viscoelasticity to tailor fluid mechanics, addressing a long-standing challenge to date. The broad generality of SCLLPS is verified across diverse plant and fungal proteins coupled with distinct anionic polysaccharides, delivering a universal condensate-tuning platform for low-impact food manufacturing with drastically reduced carbon, water, and land footprints.

items.title: Bi3+/Ln3+-Codoped Boroaluminate Phosphors with Tunable Multicolor Emission for Multidimensional Luminescence Readout and UV-Shielding
items.abstract: Abstract Combining lattice regulation of crystal-field-sensitive Bi3+ emission with Bi3+ → Ln3+ sensitization provides two complementary pathways for tuning the luminescence of single-host phosphors. Herein, Bi3+-activated Sr6Lu1-yYyAl(BO3)6 solid solutions and Bi3+/Ln3+-codoped Sr6LuAl(BO3)6 (SLAB; Ln = Eu, Dy, Sm, and Tb) phosphors were synthesized by a high-temperature solid-state reaction. SLAB:Bi3+ exhibited broadband blue-violet emission centered at 419 nm under 325 nm excitation. Isovalent Y3+ substitution for Lu3+ regulated the local environment of Bi3+ and enhanced the integrated emission intensity by approximately sixfold under 365 nm excitation, with internal and external quantum efficiencies (IQE and EQE) reaching 87.2 and 31.7%, respectively. The lifetime-derived efficiency of Bi3+ → Eu3+ energy transfer reached a maximum of 85.8% and enabled continuous color tuning from blue-violet to orange-red by adjusting the Eu3+ concentration and excitation wavelength. Bi3+ → Ln3+ sensitization was further demonstrated for Dy3+, Sm3+, and Tb3+, producing purple, purplish-red, and green emissions, respectively. Taking advantage of their strong UV absorption, the phosphors were incorporated into flexible films for a proof-of-concept evaluation of UV shielding. The tunable multicolor emissions were further used to fabricate multicolor security labels and demonstrate binary optical encryption. Differential thermal quenching of Bi3+ and Sm3+ emissions enabled ratiometric thermometry over 298–573 K, with maximum absolute and relative sensitivities of 6.55 × 10–2 K–1 and 1.07% K–1, respectively. These findings demonstrate the potential of single-host boroaluminate phosphors for multidimensional luminescence readout, optical thermometry, and UV-shielding applications.

items.title: Polymer-Passivated ZnO Microcluster Arrays for High-Responsivity, Low-Voltage UV Photodetection
items.abstract: Abstract Metal-oxide UV photodetectors typically require elevated bias to achieve high sensitivity, limiting their suitability for low-power and portable applications. Here, we demonstrate poly(methyl methacrylate) (PMMA)-engineered zinc oxide (ZnO) nano-microcluster arrays (NMCAs) that deliver outstanding UV photodetection performance at a low operating voltage of 0.1 V. The optimized device exhibited a high responsivity of 376 mA W–1, representing an ∼8.5-fold enhancement over pristine NMCA-structured ZnO under identical testing conditions, while maintaining excellent cycling stability. Controlled PMMA infiltration progressively modulates surface defects and interparticle charge-transport pathways in these mechanically robust, liquid-sintered NMCAs, with the performance enhancement primarily arising from defect passivation rather than optical absorption changes. Structural and spectroscopic analyses suggest that controlled PMMA infiltration modifies the polymer–oxide interface without altering the intrinsic wurtzite ZnO crystal structure, with the enhanced response primarily attributed to PMMA-assisted defect passivation and improved carrier lifetime. A clear responsivity-speed trade-off emerges with increasing polymer loading, whereby intermediate PMMA content yields effective defect passivation and maximum responsivity, while excessive infiltration introduces transport bottlenecks. The relatively slow rise and decay times indicate that these devices are better suited to static or quasi-static UV monitoring rather than high-speed photodetection. Moreover, by enhancing UV photoresponse at a very low operating voltage of 0.1 V through rational polymer–oxide interfacial engineering, this scalable approach provides a promising strategy for battery-compatible UV monitoring and porous metal-oxide optoelectronic systems.

items.title: Dynamic Electronic Modulation of MOF-808 via Vacancy-Driven Ligand-to-Metal Charge Transfer for Self-amplifying Photocatalysis
items.abstract: Abstract The mechanistic insight into the relationship between pollutant adsorption and the corresponding photocatalytic response remains a critical yet elusive facet of heterogeneous catalysis. Here, we unravel the multiplicity of adsorption pathways governing norfloxacin (NOR) uptake on oxygen- and organic-vacancy-engineered MOF-808 (MOF-808-OVs) and demonstrate that these interfacial interactions actively reconfigure the framework’s electronic landscape through a vacancy-driven ligand-to-metal charge transfer (v-LMCT) process. While Lewis acid–base pairing and electrostatic forces at the Zr–O clusters constitute the primary binding determinants, π–π stacking and hydrophobic contacts serve as auxiliary contributions. Crucially, combined partial density of states (PDOS) analysis reveals that the resultant MOF-808–pollutant adduct enables a v-LMCT pathway, wherein electron injection from NOR into the O 2p orbitals of the Zr–O nodes not only reinforces adsorbate retention but also primes a rapid electron shuttling cascade from the inorganic clusters to dissolved O2 in aqueous media. This synergistic charge-transfer regime substantially amplifies reactive oxygen species generation, boosting •OH and 1O2 production by factors of 2.2 and 6.0, respectively, relative to pristine MOF-808 in the absence of NOR. Thus, these findings establish a mechanistic paradigm wherein adsorption serves as an electronic tuning lever, engendering a self-amplifying photocatalytic cycle. This work provides a foundational strategy for the rational design of next-generation photocatalysts predicated on adsorption-driven electronic modulation.

items.title: A Complex-Anion-Doped Ionic-Liquid Electrolyte for High-Voltage Cathodes in Lithium-Ion Batteries
items.abstract: Abstract High-voltage cathodes can increase the energy density of lithium-ion batteries, but they impose stringent requirements on electrolyte oxidation resistance and safety. Traditional carbonate-based electrolytes can undergo oxidative decomposition at high potentials, which limits their application to high-voltage cathodes. Ionic liquids (ILs) are considered to be promising candidates for the construction of high-safety and high-voltage electrolytes due to their extremely low vapor pressure, low flammability and wide electrochemical window. In this paper, a multi-anion modification strategy was introduced into the ionic liquid electrolyte to create a complex-anion-doped ionic liquid electrolyte (CAD-ILE), which modifies the local ionic environment while retaining the main spectral features of the ionic liquid. On a formulation-component basis, CAD-ILE contains 60 mol % EMIMTFSI, 37 mol % LiTFSI, and 3 mol % auxiliary salts (LiFSI, LiPF6, LiBOB, LiBF4, LiDFP, LiOTF, LiDFOB, and LiNO3; 0.375 mol % each). This formulation is associated with a thin, LiF-containing CEI on the cathode surface. The capacity retention of the CAD-ILE electrolyte is 71% after 200 cycles at 4.6 V in a LCO||Li half cell (only 32% in commercial electrolyte), and 87% after 120 cycles at 4.55 V in a LCO||graphite full cell. This work supports a simple and effective high-voltage electrolyte design strategy.

items.title: Body-Coupled Organic Electrochemical Transistors for Imperceptible Skin Bioelectronics
items.abstract: Abstract The efficient ion-to-electron transduction mechanism makes organic electrochemical transistors (OECTs) stand out for physiological sensing. Usually, OECT operations require saline solutions or hydrogels to function as the electrolytes; however, the wet electrolytes may compromise wear comfort and device stability for human-integrated applications. In this work, we propose a body-coupled OECT (b-OECT) device mechanism, where the skin and subcutaneous tissues act as natural electrolyte for the device operation. In the b-OECT, the organic semiconducting channel forms intimate and substrate-free contact with skins, enabling biofluid-derived ionic pathways to directly mediate gate–channel coupling and electrochemical modulation. The devices exhibit body-coupled transistor characteristics, skin-coupled operation, and ion-mediated neuromorphic-like conductance modulation. Without needing external supplied electrolytes, the b-OECT offers breathable and imperceptible body integration, where biological tissue directly participates in electrochemical signal transduction, opening potentials for skin-integrated bioelectronics and body-coupled neuromorphic biointerfaces.

items.title: Phase-Transition-Driven Thermomechanical Regulation of Thermal Interfaces
items.abstract: Abstract Thermal interfaces are often limited by imperfect real contact, where surface asperities and interfacial gaps can dominate the overall thermal resistance. Here, we develop a flexible phase-change composite (FPCC) that couples the solid–liquid transition of n-docosane with mechanical softening, expansion-generated normal loading, and interfacial reconfiguration to regulate thermal contact. The composite integrates n-docosane within a compliant styrene–ethylene–butylene–styrene (SEBS) matrix supported by an interconnected expanded-graphite (EG) scaffold. The optimized FPCC exhibits a thermal conductivity of 5.18 W m–1 K–1 and a latent heat of 153.5 J g–1. Across the phase transition, the tensile modulus decreases to ∼0.60 MPa, while expansion under interfacial constraint generates a normal stress exceeding 40 kPa (∼5.8 psi). An equivalent-pressure analysis based on the measured Rcontact–P relationship indicates that a pressure increment of ∼5.8 psi corresponds to an approximately 54% reduction in contact thermal resistance from the 5 psi reference condition. Frequency-domain thermoreflectance measurements further reveal an increase in effective contact conductance from 2.32 to 8.99 MW m–2 K–1 across the transition, while synchronized mechanical-thermal measurements show reproducible co-evolution of normal loading and conductance during repeated cycling. The enhanced contact state is partially retained after cooling, indicating that repeatable thermomechanical modulation operates together with partially retained interfacial reconfiguration. In LED cooling, the FPCC lowers the device temperature by up to 6.5 °C relative to a commercial thermal pad. These results establish phase-transition-driven thermomechanical regulation as a route to improving and stabilizing low-preload thermal interfaces through the coupled effects of compliance, expansion-generated loading, and interfacial reconfiguration.

items.title: MgH2 with a Pre-Synthesized Ti–Ni Composite Catalyst: Superior Sorption Kinetics and High Saturated Capacity over Physically Mixed Ni/Ti
items.abstract: Abstract Magnesium hydride (MgH2) is a promising solid-state hydrogen storage material owing to its high theoretical capacity, earth abundance, and low cost. However, its practical application is severely hindered by sluggish sorption kinetics and high thermodynamic stability. Herein, we systematically compare the catalytic effects of elemental Ni, elemental Ti, physically mixed Ni/Ti, and a pre-synthesized Ti–Ni composite catalyst on the hydrogen storage performance of MgH2, aiming to understand the advantages and disadvantages of the catalytic performance of Ni and Ti and to exert their synergistic catalytic effect. Our results suggest that Ni is associated with faster initial hydrogenation kinetics and lower onset dehydrogenation temperatures, while Ti correlates with higher equilibrium capacities and more sustained hydrogenation/dehydrogenation behavior at elevated temperatures. These distinct catalytic tendencies are inferred from systematic comparisons of sorption kinetics, phase evolution, elemental distribution, and kinetic modeling. Simple co-doping of Ni and Ti partially combines these benefits but fails to eliminate the intrinsic drawbacks of each element. It is noteworthy that the pre-synthesized Ti–Ni composite catalyst further overcomes the above-mentioned drawbacks and exhibits a more uniform distribution of elements, which further improves both the hydrogen absorption rate and the extent of the reaction in MgH2. As a result, the MgH2–5wt%pre-Ti-Ni-c-c composite absorbs 6.10 wt % H2 within 27.3 s at 275 °C and releases 5.54 wt % H2 within 548 s at 325 °C, with a markedly reduced dehydrogenation enthalpy from 93.28 to 72.25 kJ mol–1. After 10 cycles, its hydrogen absorption and desorption capacity retentions reach 96.3 and 93.5%, respectively, demonstrating improved initial cycling stability compared with BM-MgH2 (82.6%). Mechanistic studies combining phase evolution, kinetic modeling, and DFT calculations attribute the superior performance to the combined action of three components: the NiTi bimetallic phase for a collaborative catalytic effect, reversible Mg2Ni/Mg2NiHx phases that contribute to rapid initial kinetics, and TiO2 that induces stronger lattice distortion. This work demonstrates that the pre-synthesized Ti–Ni composite catalyst, with its superior dispersion, effectively overcomes the limitations of physically mixed Ni/Ti systems and achieves a better balance between rapid initial reaction rates and deeper reactions in actual test results.

items.title: Proton Irradiation Reconfigures Temperature-Dependent Emissive Heterogeneity in Wide-Bandgap All-Inorganic CsPbI2Br Perovskite Solar Cells
items.abstract: Abstract Wide-bandgap metal-halide perovskites are attractive for space power due to their high open-circuit voltages and compatibility with tandem device architectures, but their response to orbital stressors remains under-explored. Here, we show that 1.86 eV all-inorganic CsPbI2Br perovskite solar cells (PSCs) develop an emissive heterogeneity when cooled to 193 K (–80 °C), marked by the emergence of distinctly bright, blue-shifted emission centers near 1.89 eV. This low-temperature blue shift is accompanied by an increased open-circuit voltage but reduced charge extraction, as revealed by operando current–voltage measurements. As the operating temperature increases to 373 K (+100 °C), the spatial emissive contrast becomes less pronounced and emission is quenched, yielding a comparatively more spatially uniform emission landscape and improved charge extraction. Irradiation of these n-i-p PSCs with 1.0 MeV protons at a fluence of 5 × 1013 cm–2 reconfigures the emissive heterogeneity, with enhanced spatial contrast at 193 K including linewidth narrowing of certain emissive components and persistent emissive features at warmer temperatures. These results suggest that proton irradiation modifies the emissive landscape in ways not fully captured by room-temperature device metrics alone. More broadly, we demonstrate that the apparent radiation tolerance of wide-bandgap PSCs at room temperature can mask the underlying heterogeneity that becomes significantly more visible under space-relevant thermal extremes.

items.title: Vertical Graphene/Violet-Phosphorus/Graphene Photodetectors for Wavelength-Programmed Optical Signal Encoding
items.abstract: Abstract As an emerging two-dimensional van der Waals material, violet phosphorus is particularly notable for its ambient stability, moderate bandgap, and strong light absorption, making it an excellent candidate for photodetection applications. However, conventional lateral-channel devices based on violet phosphorus typically suffer from severe carrier recombination losses over extended transport distances. Here, we demonstrate a high-performance vertical-channel photodetector based on a graphene/violet phosphorus/graphene (Gr/VP/Gr) van der Waals heterostructure. By shortening the carrier transport path, the vertical architecture enables efficient carrier collection and a high photoconductive gain. Under 532 nm illumination, the device achieves a responsivity of 1.7 × 104 A/W, a specific detectivity of 2.1 × 1013 Jones, and an external quantum efficiency of approximately 3.9 × 106%; its photoresponse spans 450–1050 nm. A transport-scaling analysis comparing vertical and lateral geometries indicates that the vertical structure reduces the carrier drift transit time to the picosecond scale, providing a quantitative rationale for the large effective gain. The device also exhibits wavelength-dependent transient dynamics, with a relatively fast response at 450 nm and a persistent response at 800 nm. These distinct temporal signatures enable a proof-of-concept demonstration of wavelength-programmed optical signal encoding. The outstanding optoelectronic performance of Gr/VP/Gr vertical heterostructures establishes them as an innovative and versatile platform for next-generation broadband photodetection and secure optical data transmission systems with enhanced quantum efficiency and spectral adaptability.

items.title: Piezoelectric-Excitation-Enabled Saturated-Charge Regulation for Active Noncontact Triboelectric Sensing
items.abstract: Abstract Surface charges on triboelectric materials inherently exist in a nonsaturated, dynamically decaying state. Consequently, passive noncontact inductive sensing produces signals with pronounced amplitude fluctuations and baseline drift. To address these limitations, we introduce an active excitation strategy based on a piezoelectric layer: periodic mechanical actuation induces reversible polarization, thereby modulating the local electric field to enable real-time replenishment and spatial redistribution of surface charges on the triboelectric layer. This mechanism markedly enhances both signal amplitude and long-term stability. Furthermore, intrinsic material properties, including relative permittivity, surface resistivity, thickness, and surface charge retention capacity, introduce systematic variations in coupling capacitance, induced charge transfer pathways, and charge relaxation dynamics across different target materials in noncontact configurations. By employing frequency-swept excitation, static dielectric and charge-related differences among materials are transduced into distinctive dynamic frequency-response signatures, substantially improving multimaterial classification accuracy. Critically, this approach retains the key advantages of noncontact operation and zero mechanical wear, while effectively reducing surface contamination and introducing active signal conditioning, thereby distinguishing it from conventional contact-mode triboelectric classification and passive noncontact sensing paradigms. Finally, by fusing time-domain, frequency-domain, and time-frequency features within a decision tree-based classification framework, the system achieves &gt;95% recognition accuracy across diverse material classes, demonstrating a scalable, robust, and actively enhanced triboelectric sensing platform suitable for online material sorting, thin-film quality inspection, and robotic tactile perception.

items.title: Printed Flexible and Recyclable Heterojunction for Water Cleanup
items.abstract: Abstract To address the issues of easy agglomeration, difficult recovery, and poor engineering applicability faced by traditional powdered photocatalysts in water treatment, this study proposes a laser-induced transient thermal modulation electrohydrodynamic jet (LTMJ) printing strategy, enabling the direct immobilization of pre-synthesized g-C3N4/BiOI heterojunction particles on flexible quartz fiber cloth in a single printing step, thereby fabricating a high-performance and recyclable photocatalytic platform. By virtue of the real-time coupling between the laser field and the electrohydrodynamic jet printing process, a controllable transient non-equilibrium thermal environment is established in the flying droplet region. The explosive evaporation triggered by laser-droplet energy coupling effectively suppresses the secondary agglomeration of particles and regulates the deposition and interparticle assembly of the pre-synthesized heterojunction particles. Without damaging the crystalline phase and heterojunction structure of the materials, this method simultaneously achieves particle size refinement and enhancement of the uniformity and compactness of the deposited layer. Under visible light irradiation, this flexible platform exhibits excellent degradation activity and cyclic stability toward various organic dyes, while it is easy to recover and regenerate. This study not only provides a new method for the precise fabrication of flexible and recyclable photocatalytic devices, but also offers novel insights into the multi-physics field coupling-regulated assembly and functionalization of micro-nanostructures.

items.title: Rational Design of Plasmonic Nanoarrays for Surface-Enhanced Raman Scattering Applications
items.abstract: Abstract Plasmonic nanoarrays have emerged as attractive platforms for surface-enhanced Raman scattering (SERS), offering systematic control over geometry, optical response, and interfacial properties. This review focuses on the rational design and template-assisted fabrication of plasmonic nanoarrays for SERS. We first summarize the electromagnetic and chemical enhancement mechanisms and discuss design considerations specific to these nanoarrays, including particle geometry, substrate effects, and collective plasmonic coupling. We then review representative fabrication strategies based on nanosphere and anodic aluminum oxide templates, highlighting how template geometry and deposition conditions, material composition, and interfacial engineering enable the construction of coupled, anisotropic, multicomponent, and flexible nanoarrays. Finally, we discuss their applications in analytical SERS and mechanistic studies of interfacial processes. Particular attention is given to hotspot engineering, molecular accessibility and selectivity, and the use of structurally defined nanoarrays to probe charge transfer, hot-carrier processes, and plasmon-mediated reactions.

items.title: Overcoming B16F10 Melanoma by Local Co-Delivering Chemotherapeutics and Anti-Angiogenic Agents Using Injectable Thermoresponsive Polypeptide Hydrogels
items.abstract: Abstract The immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment, along with the vascular barrier within B16F10 melanoma, frequently compromises the therapeutic outcomes of antitumor immunotherapy. Hydrogels, possessing three-dimensional network structures, provide a platform for localized drug delivery. Herein, we reported a thermoresponsive polypeptide hydrogel co-loaded with mitoxantrone (MTX) and the angiogenesis inhibitor nintedanib (NE), combined with immune checkpoint blockade therapy, to address these challenges. Results demonstrated that the release of MTX induced immunogenic cell death of tumor cells and released tumor-associated antigens, while the release of NE inhibited angiogenesis, promoted drug permeation and immune cell infiltration, enhanced therapeutic efficacy, and suppressed tumor proliferation and metastasis. In a melanoma-bearing mouse model, the combination of intratumoral injection of MTX/NE-loaded hydrogel with intravenous injection of anti-PD-1 elicited a strong systemic anti-tumor immune response, successfully inhibiting tumor growth and metastasis, while prolonging animal survival. Overall, this study established a hydrogel drug delivery strategy to overcome B16F10 melanoma, demonstrating strong potential in clinical cancer therapy.

items.title: Comparative PECS and LPBF Processing of Bi0.5Sb1.5Te3: Microstructure, Texture, and Thermoelectric Performance
items.abstract: Abstract Laser powder bed fusion (LPBF) is emerging as a promising manufacturing route for next-generation thermoelectric generators, offering unprecedented freedom in the fabrication of complex device geometries. However, the rapid melting and solidification inherent to LPBF produce microstructures fundamentally different from those of conventional consolidation techniques, and how these processing-induced features affect thermoelectric performance remains poorly understood. In this work, LPBF-produced p-type Bi0.5Sb1.5Te3 was compared with materials fabricated by pulsed electric current sintering (PECS), which served as a reference processing route providing a higher degree of crystallographic texture. The comparison enabled identification of the microstructural characteristics governing electrical and thermal transport. In particular, the investigated materials exhibited a wide range of preferred orientation (Lotgering factor F ≈ 0.02–0.20), while maintaining comparable Seebeck coefficients (∼160–175 μV K–1). In contrast, electrical conductivity (720–2200 S cm–1 at 300 K), thermal conductivity (0.9–1.5 W m–1 K–1), and consequently the thermoelectric figure of merit varied strongly with the processing route and crystallographic orientation. PECS samples with moderate preferred orientation reached ZT ≈ 1.1, while LPBF specimens exhibited ZT ≈ 0.4–0.5. The lower LPBF performance reflects weaker texture and processing-induced defects, partly related to nonideal powder morphology and feeding conditions. Additionally, numerical modeling (FEM) was performed to evaluate energy conversion efficiency, demonstrating higher output power and overall efficiency for the PECS samples compared to the LPBF ones. The comparative analysis demonstrates that crystallographic texture and microstructural integrity are key factors affecting thermoelectric performance and identifies processing-related limitations under the LPBF conditions investigated in this study.

items.title: Enzyme−Antibiotic Liquid Crystalline Nanoparticles for Enhanced Antibiofilm Activity, Bacterial Clearance, and Accelerated Healing of Infected Wounds
items.abstract: Abstract Biofilm-associated wound infections remain difficult to treat because bacteria are protected within extracellular polymeric matrices that restrict antibiotic penetration, promote antimicrobial tolerance, and delay tissue repair. Here, we developed liquid crystalline nanoparticles (LCNPs) for topical coformulation of gentamicin (GEN) and recombinant human DNase I (rhDNase), combining aminoglycoside therapy with an eDNA-targeting enzyme. GEN + rhDNase-LCNPs were successfully formulated as nanoscale particles with low polydispersity, high encapsulation efficiency, and formulation-dependent in vitro release behavior. LCNP formulation preserved GEN antibacterial activity against planktonic Escherichia coli Xen14 and reduced the MBIC against established biofilms by approximately 4-fold. In a minimum biofilm eradication concentration (MBEC) model, GEN + rhDNase-LCNPs achieved the greatest reduction in biofilm-associated viable bacteria, producing an approximately 6-log reduction compared with untreated biofilm controls and supporting the benefit of combining antibiotic delivery with rhDNase. Notably, GEN + rhDNase-LCNPs markedly suppressed bacterial burden and reduced recoverable bacteria at day 9 to near the limit of detection in a bioluminescent E. coli Xen14 biofilm-associated excisional wound infection mouse model. This antibacterial effect translated into accelerated macroscopic wound closure and improved histological repair, including an approximately 80% reduction in wound gape compared with infected controls. Masson’s trichrome staining further confirmed enhanced tissue remodeling, with the collagen-positive wound area increasing to approximately 88% following GEN + rhDNase-LCNP treatment, compared with approximately 21% in infected controls. In conclusion, LCNP-mediated codelivery of GEN and rhDNase improved bacterial clearance, re-epithelialization, and collagen deposition, supporting this platform as a promising topical antibiofilm strategy for infected wounds.

items.title: Synergy between UiO-66-NH2 and a Hierarchical Aluminum Reservoir for Durable, Self-Replenishing Dry Lubrication
items.abstract: Abstract Friction and wear limit the reliability and energy efficiency of mechanical systems, motivating solid lubricants for conditions where liquid lubricants fail. Metal–organic frameworks (MOFs) are attractive owing to their tunable structures and ability to form protective tribofilms, but their low-yield synthesis demands strategies that maximize performance at minimal loading. Herein, we developed a synergistic dry-lubrication strategy in which a hierarchical structure (HS) acts as an integrated reservoir for UiO-66-NH2. Drop-cast MOF particles were anchored within the interconnected concavities of an etched aluminum (Al 5052) substrate bearing a micro/nano hierarchical surface. The anchored UiO-66-NH2 was continuously supplied to the contact interface as a rolling third body, infilling worn regions. Post-test SEM–EDS detected Zr across the wear track, suggesting that the MOF was compacted into a protective MOF-derived layer. The amino-functionalized UiO-66-NH2 showed slightly better wear resistance than carboxyl-functionalized UiO-66-(COOH)2, and performance was further optimized by tuning the MOF concentration (7 mg/mL) and HCl etching time (2 min). Using only 0.56 mg/cm2 of MOF, the surface reduced wear-track width and maximum wear depth by 46.6% and 62.6%, respectively, relative to bare Al sliding against a stainless-steel pin under 1 N. The friction reduction was mainly provided by the HS, whereas UiO-66-NH2 primarily suppressed wear. This durable, self-replenishing approach offers a scalable route to practical MOF-based tribological surfaces.

items.title: Development of Novel Ridge-and-Valley Form Small-Caliber Compliant Vascular Grafts Based on a Modified Near-Field Coaxial Electrospinning Technique
items.abstract: Abstract Limited attention has been paid to the macroscopic topology of small-caliber electrospinning artificial vascular grafts. Here, we fabricated an elastic vascular graft of 2 mm diameter featuring a “ridge-and-valley” macrostructure using a modified near-field coaxial electrospinning technology, which combines the near-field electrospinning direct-writing technique and coaxial electrospinning technology, employing polyurethane (PU) as the outer shell and poly(l-lactide-co-ε-caprolactone) (PLCL) as the inner core. By adjusting the PLCL/PU ratio, the viscosity of the blended solution was tuned to meet electrospinning requirements. The electrospun grafts exhibited oriented filament alignment in the ridge regions and a relatively disordered configuration in the valley regions, demonstrating significantly enhanced kinking resistance in macroscopic testing. In vitro cell experiments and in situ rat abdominal aorta transplantation models verified the graft's ability in inducing vascular smooth muscle cell (vSMC) alignment generated by oriented fiber alignment. Importantly, partial endothelial coverage and circumferentially aligned vSMC proliferation were observed. Critically, the PLCL/PU 0.5/0.5 group showed a great patency rate and a desirable functional structure at the 12-week endpoint. These findings present a novel strategy for fabricating small-caliber biocompatible vascular grafts with favorable mechanical properties via a straightforward, continuous single-step process.

items.title: Semi-Embedded Liquid Metal Nanoparticles on Co-Electrospun Nanofibers for Scalable and High-Sensitivity Flexible Surface-Enhanced Raman Scattering Platform
items.abstract: Abstract Flexible surface-enhanced Raman scattering (SERS) substrates are essential for conformal on-site molecular detection, yet typically face a trade-off between sensitivity, uniformity, and mechanical robustness. In this work, we report a high-performance flexible SERS featuring liquid metal nanoparticles spatially confined within electrospun polyimide nanofibers. Via co-electrospinning, we engineered a unique “semi-embedded” structure where liquid metal nanoparticles are partially exposed on fiber surfaces. The optimized substrate achieves an ultralow detection limit (LOD) of 10–8 M for Rhodamine 6G with outstanding signal uniformity and excellent mechanical durability (72.5% signal retention after 500 bending cycles), compared to existing flexible platforms. Furthermore, the platform enables sensitive and differentiated SERS detection of thiol-containing molecules, with preferential trace detection of 4-aminothiophenol (LOD 10–9 M). Its practical utility is further demonstrated by the simultaneous monitoring of mixed acetamiprid and thiram residues in apple juice. Finite-element simulations suggest that the superior SERS enhancement under near‑infrared excitation is largely consistent with synergistic electromagnetic coupling between the sputtered Au nanoparticles and the highly conductive liquid metal cores, with possible additional chemical enhancement from the oxide-rich surface. This study presents a cost-effective and scalable strategy for fabricating high-performance SERS substrates while offering critical insights into the synergistic coupling between liquid metals and conventional plasmonic materials.

items.title: Vanillin-Based Covalent Adaptable Networks with Ultralow Graphene Content for Enhanced Mechanical Robustness, Photothermal Self-Healing, and Corrosion Protection
items.abstract: Abstract Designing partially bio-based covalent adaptable networks that combine mechanical robustness with thermally or optically triggered healing and reprocessability remains challenging because network reinforcement typically reduces dynamic chain mobility. Herein, we report a vanillin-derived imine-based network reinforced by silane-functionalized graphene oxide nanosheets covalently grafted at an ultralow loading of 0.5 wt %. The covalent anchoring of graphene oxide at the network interface raises the apparent activation energy of stress relaxation from 45.0 to 73.7 kJ mol–1 while preserving Arrhenius-type temperature dependence, consistent with increased network constraint rather than enhanced intrinsic exchange kinetics. The composite retains 84.1% of its tensile strength after three hot-press reprocessing cycles. Under near-infrared irradiation, the grafted graphene oxide enables photothermal heating that locally compensates for the reduced intrinsic chain mobility, allowing surface scratches to heal within 5 min. As a protective coating, the composite maintains an impedance modulus above 109 Ω cm2 after 130 d of saline immersion, with the improved barrier performance attributed to combined effects of tortuous diffusion pathways and reduced network free volume. These results demonstrate that an ultralow fraction of covalently grafted nanofiller can simultaneously introduce mechanical reinforcement, photothermal responsiveness, and prolonged barrier function without eliminating the dynamic character of the network.

items.title: Composite Cathodes for Oxide-Based Solid-State Batteries: Processing, Interfacial Mechanisms, and Performance Engineering
items.abstract: Abstract Composite cathodes are a key component in oxide-based solid-state batteries (SSBs), enabling electrochemical activity through the integration of cathode active materials, solid electrolytes, and conductive additives within a single composite architecture. However, their performance is strongly influenced by complex interfacial phenomena and chemo-mechanical effects arising from heterogeneous solid−solid contacts, which often result in high interfacial resistance, limited percolation of ionic and electronic pathways, and progressive degradation during processing and cycling. This review aims to clarify how composite cathode designs govern the performance of oxide-based SSBs, focusing on the interplay between material selection, fabrication routes (wet and dry processes), interfacial structure evolution, and transport efficiency. Emphasis is placed on critical challenges such as co-sintering-induced interfacial degradation, space−charge layer formation, poor contact, and an imbalance between ionic and electronic transport, as well as on strategies developed to address these issues, including buffer layers, co-sintering additives, and microstructural engineering. Advanced characterization techniques are also discussed for probing buried interfaces and correlating structure with performance. Finally, we identify critical gaps in current understanding and outline prospective research pathways aimed at formulating robust design guidelines for oxide-based composite cathodes with enhanced mechanical integrity and electrochemical stability, ultimately advancing high-performance oxide-based SSBs.

items.title: Fabrication of MoS2 Nanopores via Dielectric Breakdown for Single-Molecule Sensing Applications
items.abstract: Abstract This study focuses on the controllable fabrication of monolayer molybdenum disulfide (MoS2) nanopores based on dielectric breakdown and their application in single-molecule sensing. To address the poor pore-size controllability and limited reproducibility commonly encountered in the fabrication of sub-5 nm transition metal dichalcogenide (TMD) nanopores, the nanopore formation processes under voltage-stepping and current-stepping modes were systematically investigated. Experimental results demonstrate that, compared with the voltage-stepping mode, the current-stepping mode exhibits a more gradual breakdown transition. Although the average breakdown times of the two modes are comparable, the nanopores fabricated by current stepping are confined to a narrower sub-5 nm range, whereas voltage stepping produces a broader distribution. Consequently, precise and controllable fabrication of sub-5 nm TMD nanopores was achieved. The fabricated MoS2 nanopore sensor was further employed for single-molecule detection of oligonucleotide (Oligo) DNA, where distinct ionic current blockade events were successfully recorded. Combined with COMSOL Multiphysics simulations, three representative translocation behaviors were identified and elucidated. This work provides systematic experimental and theoretical insights into the high-precision fabrication of TMD nanopores and their potential applications in biosensing.

items.title: Spin-Resolved Topology of Mem-Emitter Response
items.abstract: Abstract We develop a general framework for spin-resolved mem-emitters and illustrate it unequivocally using a monolayer MoSe2/clinochlore optoelectronic device. In mem-emitters, both the intensity and energy of light emission encode the history of external driving through slowly evolving internal state variables. When spin is included as an active degree of freedom, voltage-controlled memory dynamics give rise to spin-resolved hysteresis revealed through the degree of circular polarization under magnetic fields. Using polarization-resolved magneto-photoluminescence, we observe pronounced hysteresis in excitonic and trionic emission, whose loop topology depends on magnetic field and circular polarization. A minimal spin-resolved model shows that these features are generically governed by a polarity-dependent tuning of the effective Landé g-factor, with its voltage slope uniquely determining the orientation of the degree-of-circular-polarization loops. First-principles calculations suggest that interface-induced symmetry breaking provides a microscopic route to such bias-dependent spin responses, highlighting the broad relevance of spin-resolved memory effects in optoelectronic emitters.

items.title: Comprehensively Unveiling the Dual Antifungal and Antibacterial Activity of Ultra-small Pt Nanoclusters through Membrane Impairment Induced by Oxidative Stress
items.abstract: Abstract Microorganisms, including bacteria, fungi, and viruses, can invade the human body, disrupt normal physiological functions, and trigger a variety of infectious diseases, currently posing a significant global health issue. Silver (Ag), gold (Au), and titanium dioxide (TiO2) nanomaterials have already demonstrated exciting antimicrobial properties and promising therapeutic applications. However, the antibacterial performance of Pt nanomaterials, especially nanoclusters (NCs, &lt;2 nm), has rarely been investigated. In this study, Pt NCs with an ultra-small size of 1.5 ± 0.5 nm were produced by a reduction method, and their structure presents a composite of fine atomic clusters. A series of bacteriostatic experiments proved that the sterilizing rates of Gram-negative bacteria Escherichia coli (E. coli) and Gram-positive bacteria Staphylococcus aureus (S. aureus) are 98.02 and 99.99%, respectively. In addition, the minimum inhibitory concentration (MIC) and minimum bactericidal concentration (MBC) of Pt NCs against Fusarium solani (F. solani) were determined to be as low as 0.8 and 1.7 μg/mL, and these Pt NCs exhibited fungicidal activity. The antibacterial and antifungal mechanisms were elucidated, showing that the oxidative stress generated via the excessive reactive oxygen species (ROS) induced by Pt NCs triggers the chain reaction of lipid peroxidation (LPO), consequently causing the structural degradation and functional impairment of membranes, ultimately resulting in the cytoplasmic contents leaking and bacterial/fungal death. Astonishingly, the wound healing rate for methicillin-resistant S. aureus (MRSA) infections was 98.90% at 10 days post treatment by Pt NCs, indicating significantly higher efficacy than that of the conventional broad-spectrum antibacterial fluoroquinolone drug ofloxacin. Furthermore, the antimicrobial gauze fabricated using these Pt NCs exhibited at least 99.75% inhibition of both E. coli and S. aureus within 24 h, suggesting their promising application prospects as a novel and safer antibacterial and antifungal agent.

items.title: Nonlinear Curved Metasurfaces for Enhanced Thyroid Magnetic Resonance Imaging
items.abstract: Abstract Metasurfaces offer a promising approach to enhance the signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) in magnetic resonance imaging (MRI). Thyroid MRI suffers from insufficient SNR due to the anatomical irregularity of the neck and poor coil-to-tissue proximity, which fails to meet the demands of preoperative tumor diagnosis. This work introduces a nonlinear, curved metasurface tailored to address these limitations through a nonlinear mode control scheme based on up-frequency tuning. Unlike the previously reported down-frequency tuning scheme, here the metasurface's resonant frequency is selectively shifted to a frequency above the Larmor frequency during RF transmit via an integrated diode-inductor circuit, thereby minimizing B1+ perturbation and specific absorption rate increase. Concurrently, its conformal curved geometry focuses the enhanced field on the concave side, optimizing penetration for superficial targets. This adaptive mechanism minimally perturbs the transmit field while keeping the device fully active during signal reception. Experiments demonstrate that this thyroid imaging curved metasurface (TCM) provides an SNR enhancement by a factor of over six in the target thyroid region and an effective penetration depth of approximately 60 mm over the whole range of up-frequency inductances examined (27–100 nH), for which the two-fold gain is maintained to about 70 mm, validating its potential as a practical, wireless adjunct for high-quality thyroid MRI.

items.title: Flexible Artificial Neurons Based on NbO x for Robust Tactile Perception in a Wide Temperature Range
items.abstract: Abstract Neuromorphic tactile sensing that emulates biological touch enables artificial systems to work with high efficiency and low energy consumption. As tactile-sensing scenarios may involve curved surfaces and different temperatures, artificial spiking afferent neurons require both flexibility and temperature robustness at the front end of artificial systems. Here, we report flexible artificial spiking neurons based on niobium oxide (NbOx) threshold-switching (TS) memristors prepared on polyimide (PI) substrates. Temperature-dependent transport analysis indicates that their temperature robustness is associated with a bulk switching pathway in the NbOx film. By integrating an oscillation circuit, the NbOx spiking afferent neurons convert analog inputs into frequency-modulated voltage spikes and retain oscillatory capability from –80 to 80 °C at a bending radius of 5 mm. Moreover, pressure sensors are coupled with the NbOx neurons to form mechanoreceptors that encode pressure as oscillation frequency. In the numerical tactile-recognition workflow, a convolutional neural network (CNN) classifies spatial frequency maps generated from the fitted pressure-to-frequency relations, achieving accuracies of 97.5% under the baseline condition and 93.2% at 80 °C at a bending radius of 5 mm. This work demonstrates that flexible NbOx neurons can serve as compact event-driven front ends for wide-temperature robotic tactile sensing.

items.title: Co-Assembled MOF@SiO2 Nanostructures for Superhydrophobic and Electrically Insulating Radiative Cooling Coatings
items.abstract: Abstract Passive radiative cooling (PRC) technology, characterized by zero-energy cooling capability, has shown great promise for thermal management of high-voltage electrical equipment. However, such application scenarios impose stringent multifunctional requirements on PRC coatings, including superhydrophobicity to resist surface contamination, as well as high electrical insulation strength to prevent surface flashover. Here, we report a co-assembly strategy for constructing multifunctional PRC coatings through the in situ integration of a metal-organic framework (MOF) with a silica precursor. The appropriately tailored bandgap (Eg = 4.25 eV) of the MOF, slightly exceeding the upper photon-energy bound of the measured solar band (4.13 eV), enables suppressed solar absorption while affording a strong mid-infrared emissivity. Meanwhile, the high-Eg SiO2 shell effectively passivates intrinsic insulation defects and the high surface energy associated with MOFs, thereby enhancing both dielectric reliability and superhydrophobicity. Consequently, the optimized PRC coating delivered a temperature drop of 10.6 ± 0.5 °C during outdoor testing, together with robust superhydrophobicity (153.7°) and high wet flashover strength (15.6 kV/cm). This work advances PRC coatings beyond conventional thermal regulation by integrating radiative cooling, surface self-cleaning, and electrical insulation into a unified material platform, opening new opportunities for passive thermal management of high-voltage electrical equipment.

items.title: Analysis of the Coercivity Mechanism of High-Performance Nd-Fe-B Magnets Prepared by Synergistic Diffusion
items.abstract: Abstract The grain boundary diffusion process is an important approach for preparing high-performance Nd-Fe-B magnets. In this study, Nd-Fe-B diffusion magnets with both high remanence and high coercivity were prepared via a two-step synergistic diffusion process. The process combined Pr70Ga30 pre-diffusion with subsequent DyH3 diffusion. Compared with DyH3 diffusion alone, this two-step synergistic diffusion strategy increased the coercivity increment from 3.30 to 3.84 kOe while maintaining a remanence of 15.03 kG. Microstructural and elemental analyses showed that Pr70Ga30 pre-diffusion modified the grain-boundary phase and promoted Dy diffusion to greater depths. The modified grain boundaries facilitated the formation of continuous (Dy, RE)2Fe14B shells around the main-phase grains. These shells increased the local magnetocrystalline anisotropy and strengthened the grain edges against reverse-domain nucleation. Micromagnetic simulations indicated that a complete core-shell structure increased the demagnetization nucleation field at grain edges, thereby suppressing magnetic domain reversal. This study establishes a direct relationship between grain-boundary modification, shell continuity, and coercivity enhancement in Nd-Fe-B magnets.

items.title: Nature-Inspired Directional Fluid Transport Enables Silanized Topo-Vascular Cellulose Aerogel for Efficient Oil/Water Separation
items.abstract: Abstract Oil pollution from petroleum-related activities and oily industrial wastewater pose a persistent challenge to aquatic environments, motivating the development of efficient sorbent and separation materials. However, conventional aerogels usually require multistep fabrication and show limited mechanical robustness. Herein, a silanized topo-vascular cellulose aerogel (STVCA) is developed through a top-down strategy using the oriented transport architecture of Spatholobus suberectus Dunn stems as a structural template. Vapor-phase silanization tailors the cellulose interface while the processed scaffold retains key topological features of the native hierarchical vascular architecture, combining low-surface-energy chemistry with the inherited channel organization and mechanical integrity. The resulting STVCA serves as a robust, fast mass-transfer medium for oil/water separation, showing rapid oil wetting, stable hydrophobicity, and anisotropic capillary transport. Dry STVCA reaches a compressive stress of 28.41 MPa at 80% radial strain (σ80), whereas oil-loaded STVCA reaches σ80 = 27.14 MPa and retains 91% of its initial σ80 after 80 compression cycles. The cross-sectional surface and longitudinal faces have mean static water contact angles of 151.05 ± 4.01° and 143.80 ± 5.92°, while a representative internal cut-surface measurement reaches 155.7°. Owing to the preserved vascular-bundle topology, STVCA achieves anisotropic mass transfer, a chloroform uptake capacity of 11.73 ± 0.61 g·g–1, a continuous separation flux of 13126 L·m-2·h–1, and a separation efficiency of up to 99%. This biomass-derived aerogel provides a durable platform for oil-spill remediation.

items.title: In-Situ Removal of Sr Segregation via Surface Construction to Engineer Highly Active Oxygen Electrode for Low-Temperature Solid Oxide Electrochemical Cells Operating below 500 °C
items.abstract: Abstract Recent advancements in solid oxide electrochemical cells (SOCs) heavily depend on the development of active and stable oxygen electrodes that exhibit superior activity and stability for oxygen reduction and evolution reactions at low temperatures. Here, we report a new surface-constructed oxygen electrode, Sr(Mg,Ti,Fe)O3–δ coated with Co3O4 (SMTF–Co3O4), designed to operate below 500 °C for low-temperature SOCs. The electrode electrochemical performance is primarily improved by the in situ reaction of Co3O4 with surface-segregated SrO, forming SrCoO3 and Co3O4/SrCoO3/SMTF heterointerfaces, which significantly enhances the surface oxygen adsorption capacity. The SMTF–Co3O4 electrode demonstrates a remarkably low reaction activation energy of ∼0.56 eV, with electrode polarization resistance as low as 0.56 Ω cm2 at 450 °C. The full cell, incorporating a thin scandia-stabilized zirconia (ScSz) electrolyte (∼3 μm) and the SMTF–Co3O4 oxygen electrode, reaches maximum power density and electrolysis current density (at 1.3 V) of 0.6 W/cm2 and 0.44 A/cm2, respectively, at 500 °C. Especially, 5–8 times enhancement in the cell performance at 450 °C is achieved by SMTF with the surface construction compared to the pristine electrode. Furthermore, the SMTF–Co3O4 electrode maintains stable performance in both fuel cell and electrolysis modes.

items.title: Enhanced Proton Irradiation Resistance of Mo/Si EUV Multilayers with Ultrathin B4C Barriers
items.abstract: Abstract Proton-induced structural degradation seriously threatens the long-term reliability of Mo/Si multilayers for extreme ultraviolet (EUV) astronomical observations, which calls for in-depth mechanistic analysis and anti-irradiation optimization schemes. In this work, 40 keV proton irradiation with fluences up to 5 × 1016 p/cm2 was performed on Mo/Si and Mo/B4C/Si/B4C multilayers to characterize the fluence-dependent structural evolution of Mo/Si multilayers and clarify how the interlayers formed from decomposed B4C enhance proton irradiation tolerance. Based on the experimental characterizations, the Mo/Si multilayer exhibited pronounced self-limiting period compaction and asymmetric interface broadening with increasing proton fluence. In contrast, merely sub-angstrom period expansion occurred in the Mo/B4C/Si/B4C multilayer under the maximum fluence exposure. Combined experimental characterizations and Monte Carlo simulations reveal that Si-dominated atomic interdiffusion drives the formation of dense MoSi2 interlayers and subsequent period compaction. Moreover, Si atoms preferentially diffuse forward to Si-on-Mo interfaces, resulting in asymmetric interface broadening. Meanwhile, the progressively thickened MoSi2 interlayers suppress further Si migration and lead to the self-limiting degradation behavior. For the Mo/B4C/Si/B4C multilayer, the reaction between the ultrathin B4C layers and adjacent Mo and Si layers produces boride- and carbide-containing interlayers. Compared with MoSi2 interlayers, these interlayers suppress proton-induced Si diffusion by a factor of about 3.0, which arises from their higher atomic density and larger screened Coulomb scattering cross section. These findings demonstrate that B4C insertion effectively mitigates proton-induced interdiffusion and structural degradation, offering a reliable route to improve the proton irradiation resistance of Mo/Si EUV multilayer mirrors for the forthcoming Xihe-2 mission.

items.title: Structural Reconstruction of Ternary CuCo2S4 for Boosting Electrocatalytic Nitrate Reduction to Ammonia
items.abstract: Abstract Electrocatalytic nitrate reduction to ammonia (NO3RR) represents a promising strategy for sustainable ammonia synthesis while simultaneously addressing nitrate pollution in wastewater. However, the irreversible structural reconstruction commonly observed in catalysts during NO3RR obscures the true active sites and complicates mechanistic understanding. In this study, flower-like CuCo2S4 nanocrystals synthesized via a hot-injection method serve as a model ternary sulfide system to systematically probe reconstruction dynamics and identify active phases under operating conditions. Experimental characterizations reveal that CuCo2S4 gradually evolves into Cu-Co(OH)2/Co9S8 through electrochemical reconstruction. This reconstructed catalyst exhibits excellent NO3RR performance, achieving an average Faradaic efficiency of 97.3%, an ammonia production rate of 363.1 μmol h–1 mg–1, and remarkable cycling stability. In situ FTIR spectra indicate that Cu incorporation promotes the conversion of *NO2 and accelerates subsequent hydrogenation steps. Density functional theory calculations further demonstrate that Cu doping facilitates *NH3 desorption and optimizes the balance between NO3– adsorption and *NH3 release. This work systematically deciphers the reconstruction pathway of sulfide catalysts during NO3RR, offering fundamental insights into electrocatalyst reconstruction mechanisms and providing a design strategy for high-performance ammonia-production electrocatalysts.

items.title: Interface-Enhanced Raman Scattering Sensor Enabled by Hairy-Particle-Analyte Noncovalent Coupling
items.abstract: Abstract Raman enhancement in practical sensing is dominated by surface-enhanced Raman scattering (SERS), where signal amplification relies on localized plasmonic hotspots but is often limited by inefficient analyte access. Conventional SERS platforms further require multistep assembly on rigid substrates, exhibit ligand-limited stability associated with thiol-metal coordination, and rely on time-consuming off-site detection (&gt;12 h), limiting reproducibility and practical deployment. Here, we develop an interface-engineered SERS strategy, referred to as interface-enhanced Raman scattering (IERS), in which a polymer-grafted plasmonic interface regulates analyte enrichment and access to electromagnetic hotspots. Diblock copolymer-grafted gold nanoparticles form “hairy” particles, in which an N-heterocyclic carbene-functionalized block drives spontaneous interparticle hotspot formation, while a poly(acrylic acid) block promotes noncovalent analyte enrichment and nanoconfinement. This interfacial nanoconfinement suppresses fluorescence and is consistent with an additional charge-transfer contribution. As a result, IERS enables rapid fabrication via simple mixing of “hairy” particles in soft hydrogels, robust stability through multidentate NHC coordination, and fast on-site detection (&lt;15 min). The sensor achieves broadband trace detection, strong tolerance to fluorescent interference, and excellent batch-to-batch reproducibility. The conformal sensing capability was further demonstrated by proof-of-concept detection of prothioconazole on a pesticide-spiked curved apple surface.

items.title: A Dual-Function Electrolyte Additive Suppresses Mn Crosstalk for Durable High-Temperature Graphite/LiMn2O4 Batteries
items.abstract: Abstract Mn crosstalk accelerates the degradation of graphite/LiMn2O4 (LMO) batteries, particularly at elevated temperatures, through the migration and deposition of dissolved Mn species on the graphite anode, which destabilizes the anode interphase. Here, tris(trimethylsilyl) phosphate (TMSP) suppresses this cross-electrode degradation pathway by regulating both the bulk electrolyte chemistry and the LMO/electrolyte interface. In the bulk electrolyte, the Si–O groups of TMSP consume HF and suppress continued HF generation through LiPF6 hydrolysis, thereby weakening acid-induced LMO corrosion. At the cathode interface, preferential adsorption and oxidation of TMSP promote the formation of a thin (∼3 nm) Li3PO4-rich cathode–electrolyte interphase (CEI), which limits electrolyte decomposition and Mn dissolution. These complementary effects reduce Mn dissolution and deposition on the graphite anode, thereby limiting Mn-associated SEI growth and resistance increase. In 1.6 Ah graphite/LMO 18650 cells, 2.1 wt % TMSP reduces Mn deposition on the anode by 95.2% and increases capacity recovery from 90.5% to 95.1% after storage at 60 °C for 7 days. The cells also retain 80.2% of their initial capacity after 500 cycles at 1 C and 45 °C. These results establish the suppression of Mn crosstalk as an effective strategy for improving the high-temperature durability of graphite/LMO batteries.

items.title: Flexible and Bridge-Free CuI Mutual Capacitive Arrays for Machine Learning-Assisted Three-Dimensional Spatial Interactive Interfaces
items.abstract: Abstract Flexible transparent human–machine interfaces (HMIs) are fundamentally bottlenecked by the brittleness of conventional indium tin oxide (ITO), the mechanical vulnerability of photolithographic bridged structures, and the complex hardware shielding required to suppress capacitive crosstalk. Herein, we propose a hardware-algorithm co-design strategy featuring a bridge-free double-sided (BFDS) mutual capacitive sensor array based on magnetron-sputtered p-type γ-CuI thin films. By employing a simplified floating-electrode readout scheme, the transparent flexible array not only captures high-fidelity two-dimensional (2D) tactile signals (signal-to-noise ratio of 268.5 ± 5.6) but also unlocks highly sensitive three-dimensional (3D) proximity perception (0–5 cm) driven by fringing electric fields. To overcome the global spatial crosstalk intrinsically induced by the unshielded hardware, a customized lightweight Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) is integrated. The CNN robustly decodes the complex nonlinear capacitance matrices, achieving an overall test accuracy of 86.2%. Furthermore, the CuI/PET structure exhibits good robustness over 10,000 extreme bending cycles (radius of 2.5 mm), where the grain-boundary scattering serves as a strain-release mechanism while preserving a continuous percolating conductive network. This work demonstrates that algorithmic compensation can relax stringent hardware shielding constraints, paving a novel avenue for ultra-simplified, touchless, and intelligent wearable electronics.

items.title: Ag Nanowire/Mo2CTx Transparent Electrodes with Chemically Tunable Work Function for Near- and Shortwave-Infrared Photodetectors
items.abstract: Abstract Transparent electrodes that simultaneously combine low sheet resistance, broadband infrared transparency, and tunable interfacial energetics are critically needed for emerging infrared optoelectronics, yet are rarely achieved within a single solution-processable architecture. Here, we report a hybrid transparent electrode composed of a percolative Ag nanowire network overcoated with Mo2CTx MXene nanosheets (Ag/MX). In this architecture, Ag nanowires provide an efficient conductive scaffold, while the Mo2CTx overlayer bridges interwire junctions, smooths the surface, and governs the device-facing interfacial electronic structure. The resulting electrodes exhibit a low sheet resistance of 18.84 Ω/sq together with a transmittance of 82% at 1550 nm and an average transmittance of 80.84% over 1500–2500 nm. More importantly, two distinct surface-modification routes enable chemically tunable work-function states: polyethyleneimine lowers the work function through interfacial dipole formation, whereas UV/Ozone treatment raises it through oxygen-enriched surface termination and mild surface oxidation of the Mo2CTx overlayer. These chemically distinct low and high work function states allow the common AgNW/Mo2CTx (Ag/MX) electrode architecture to meet different carrier-selective requirements in quantum dot short-wave-infrared and organic near-infrared photodetectors. This work establishes a chemically tunable transparent-electrode platform for cross-material infrared photodetection and provides a strategy for integrating infrared transparency, electrical transport, and carrier-selective interfacial energetics within a common electrode architecture.

items.title: Analog Spin–Orbit Torque Switching in Vertically Graded Pt/Co–Re Heterostructures for Neuromorphic Computing
items.abstract: Abstract Achieving gradual, analog magnetization switching in spin–orbit torque (SOT) devices is essential for neuromorphic computing. In perpendicular magnetic anisotropy (PMA)-based SOT devices, gradual switching can arise from domain nucleation, domain-wall propagation, and pinning, and controlling it through materials design remains a key goal. This study demonstrates that a vertically graded cobalt (Co)–rhenium (Re) alloy region, formed through a simple Co/Re multilayer design, enables analog SOT switching in Pt/Co–Re heterostructures. Microstructural and compositional analyses confirm that annealing transforms the discrete multilayer into a depth-dependent alloy with tunable gradient direction and magnitude, controlled by adjusting the Re layer thickness distribution. Increasing the Co/Re bilayer repetition number up to 3 yields a pronounced sigmoid-like transfer characteristic plausibly explained by the sequential reversal of sub-regions with distributed local switching thresholds, with only a small change in the effective PMA energy. We demonstrate stable, bidirectional long-term potentiation and depression under repeated pulse stimulation across Re compositions of 30–70%. System-level validation using a multilayer perceptron on MNIST (modified National Institute of Standards and Technology) Digits, Fashion-MNIST, and MNIST Characters datasets shows test accuracies within 1.21 percentage points of the ideal sigmoid baseline, with MNIST Digits accuracy varying by 0.24 percentage points across the full compositional range.

items.title: Interfacial Polymerization Using Acyl Chloride-Functionalized Porphyrin Comonomers toward Robust PA-66 with Type I/II Dual Photodynamic Antibacterial Durability
items.abstract: Abstract The growing threat of bacterial contamination and antibiotic resistance urgently requires functional antibacterial textiles. Photodynamic antibacterial approaches relying on reactive oxygen species (ROS) provide a promising alternative to achieve safe and long-term antimicrobial protection. Herein, a fabrication strategy was developed to construct intrinsically photodynamic antibacterial polyamide 66 (PA-66) yarns via interfacial polymerization. Acyl chloride-modified porphyrin (TCPP-Cl4), acting as a ternary monomer, was covalently grafted onto PA-66 molecular chains via interfacial polymerization. Subsequent drawing, spinning, and twisting yielded functional TCPP-Cl4-PA-66 yarns that preserved the favorable mechanical performance and thermal stability of PA-66. Physically blended TCPP/PA-66 yarns were also prepared as reference samples. Compared with TCPP/PA-66 yarns, the covalent anchoring process effectively reduced photosensitizer leaching and improved ROS generation capacity. As a result, TCPP-Cl4-PA-66 yarns achieved antibacterial efficiencies of 97.4 ± 1.3% against Staphylococcus aureus (S. aureus) and 94.0 ± 2.8% against Escherichia coli (E. coli). Furthermore, this covalent immobilization also endowed the yarns with favorable washing resistance, maintaining stable photodynamic antibacterial activity against both strains after multiple washing cycles. Interwoven fabrics fabricated from TCPP/PA-66, TCPP-Cl4-PA-66, and cotton yarns also exhibited desirable photodynamic antibacterial performance. This work provides a facile strategy for constructing photodynamic antibacterial textile materials with good stability.

items.title: A TiVCrMoC3 MXene-Based Sustained-Release Vancomycin Nanoplatform Mitigates Septic Arthritis through Modulation of Bacterial Acetate Metabolism
items.abstract: Abstract Acute septic arthritis caused by bacterial infection is a common and serious orthopedic disease. The formation of bacterial biofilms severely limits antibiotic penetration, rendering conventional therapy ineffective and short‑acting. In this study, we developed a novel nanodrug delivery system by loading vancomycin onto high‑entropy TiVCrMoC3 MXene (VCM@NPs). Featuring a sheet‑like porous structure, this material enables efficient drug loading via electrostatic interactions and sustains release in the weakly acidic infection microenvironment, achieving a cumulative release of 67% over 20 days. In vitro, VCM@NPs exhibited potent bactericidal activity against Staphylococcus aureus, with complete colony eradication by day 5, and markedly disrupted biofilm architecture, as shown by electron and confocal microscopy. In a rat septic arthritis model, a single intra‑articular injection of VCM@NPs effectively inhibited bacterial growth, alleviated joint inflammation, and improved cartilage and bone damage. By day 10, OARSI scores in the VCM@NPs group were significantly lower than those in the free vancomycin group, and micro‑CT analysis revealed increased bone volume and trabecular thickness, confirming sustained therapeutic efficacy. Notably, mass spectrometry imaging demonstrated that VCM@NPs reprogrammed the joint metabolic microenvironment by suppressing the bacterial acetate metabolic pathway, thereby destabilizing biofilms—a mechanism that, to the best of our knowledge, has not been previously reported in the context of nanoparticle-mediated modulation of this pathway. Collectively, this study offers a new nanodrug delivery strategy that integrates sustained release with biofilm disruption, holding promise for clinical translation in septic arthritis.

items.title: Structural and Esaki-Diode-like Electrical Properties of PLD-Grown 2D MoS2 Film on MBE Grown AlN/Si(111) Heterostructures
items.abstract: Abstract MoS2 thin films were synthesized via pulsed laser deposition (PLD) onto AlN/Si(111) templates, where the AlN buffer layers (110 and 200 nm thick) were grown by molecular beam epitaxy. We achieved excellent MoS2 thickness uniformity (≈3 monolayers) and confirmed the conformal coverage of the PLD-grown films by Raman mapping. Transmission electron microscopy analysis confirmed the epitaxial character of the AlN film and the presence of an ultrathin aluminum oxynitride layer on its surface. Following X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy analysis, oxygen impurities were confirmed in the bulk AlN film as well. Heterojunctions between the ultrathin MoS2 film and AlN, investigated by current–voltage characterization of vertical diode structures, exhibit Esaki-diode-like behavior with a negative-resistance zone. A diagram of the energy bands and Fermi levels in the heterostructure composed of the thick oxygen-doped AlN film sandwiched between the MoS2 and Si electrodes was proposed, and the observed Esaki-diode-like current–voltage characteristic was attributed to electron tunneling from the oxygen impurity band in the AlN film into the valence band of the degenerate p-MoS2 film.

items.title: Organic Upconversion Devices for NIR–II Biometric Sensing and Imaging Enabled by an Isomerically Engineered Narrow-Bandgap Quinoidal Polymer
items.abstract: Abstract The limited availability of organic donor materials absorbing beyond 1000 nm fundamentally limits the development of solution-processed photodetectors and upconversion devices (UCDs) in the second near-infrared (NIR-II) window. Herein, we report DPP-TbT, a narrow-bandgap alternating copolymer realized through isomeric engineering of the thiophene backbone. By employing a thieno[3,4-b]thiophene (TbT) quinoidal donor fused to a diketopyrrolopyrrole (DPP) acceptor, the absorption onset is extended to ∼1300 nm, enabling intrinsic NIR-II photon harvesting. When blended with the benchmark non-fullerene acceptor Y6 to form bulk-heterojunction photodetectors, the DPP-TbT:Y6 system achieves a specific detectivity exceeding 1011 Jones at 1064 nm with a linear dynamic range (LDR) of 68 dB. Monolithic integration of this photodetector with a quantum-dot light-emitting diode further yields a UCD that directly transduces 1064 nm excitation into visible emission with a turn-on voltage of ∼2 V, a luminance of 3741 cd m–2, and a luminance-LDR of 60 dB. We further demonstrate real-time heart-rate monitoring via photoplethysmography, high-resolution biological imaging (5080 ppi), and visualization of hidden information through a 1000 nm long-pass filter. This work establishes isomeric engineering as a rational strategy for accessing ultra-narrow bandgaps and advancing low-cost, wearable NIR-II visualization and biometric sensing systems.

items.title: Organic Spacer Cation Engineering Enhances the Electroluminescence of Full-Color PeLEDs
items.abstract: Abstract Quasi-two-dimensional (quasi-2D) perovskites have great potential in pure-blue perovskite light-emitting diodes (PeLEDs). Nevertheless, disordered multi-n phase distribution gives rise to inhomogeneous quantum confinement, accompanied by high charge-transport barriers, which severely restrict the performance of pure-blue devices. This paper proposes a universal dual-functional modification strategy, which achieves efficient pure-blue PeLEDs by partially replacing phenethylammonium bromide (PEABr) with 2-methoxyethylammonium bromide (MOAmBr). Due to the smaller steric hindrance of MOAmBr and its strong interaction with the perovskite framework, it can effectively reduce the interlayer spacing of quasi-2D perovskites and regulate the distribution of phases, thereby enhancing quantum confinement and achieving a blueshift and high-purity electroluminescence (EL). At the same time, MOAmBr reduces the carrier injection barrier, improves charge migration, and inhibits internal recombination losses of the device. The optimized pure-blue PeLED achieves a peak external quantum efficiency (EQE) of 6.8% at 469 nm. Additionally, this universal strategy is successfully applied to green and red PeLEDs, achieving significant EQE values of 21.69 and 17.29% at 506 and 660 nm, respectively. This work provides a simple and versatile cation engineering method for constructing high-performance full-spectrum quasi-2D PeLEDs.

items.title: High-Performance Planar Ni/Si Photothermoelectric Photodetectors Enabled by MnO2 Nanosheets
items.abstract: Abstract Photodetectors are the key component of modern communication systems, surveillance applications, robotics, and scientific research. The photothermoelectric effect offers opportunity to fabricate broadband and self-driven photodetectors utilizing thermally energized charge carriers. Unfortunately, photothermoelectric photodetectors are facing the challenge of large dark current, leading to low detectivity, linear dynamic range, and on–off ratio. Herein, we design a planar Ni/n-Si device structure with the help of a monolayer of MnO2 nanosheets for contact engineering. The demonstrated device shows a broadband detection range from 200 nm to MIR with an external quantum efficiency of 263.6%, a photoresponsivity of 455.1 mA W–1, a detectivity of ∼7.25 × 1012 Jones, and an on–off ratio of ∼103 at 0 V. Additionally, the device shows an unprecedented bias-assisted photoresponsivity and external quantum efficiency of 21.56 A W–1 and 13,363%, respectively, with 200 nm illumination at –10 V. The nanosheet-based contact engineering provides a powerful strategy to fabricate self-powered photodetectors with high photoresponsivity, external quantum efficiency, and broadband detection from the solar blind region to the MIR spectrum.

items.title: Inhibition of Oxidative Activity by Photo-induced Surface Hydroxyl Groups in Bismuth Titanium Oxide Photocatalysts Detected by Single-Molecule Fluorescence Imaging
items.abstract: Abstract The surface structure of semiconductor photocatalysts plays a critical role in the extraction of charge carriers during photocatalytic reactions. However, the surface structures of many photocatalysts are dynamic under catalytic conditions, which makes identifying photo-induced changes and their effect on photocatalytic activity challenging. Herein, we use super-resolution, single-molecule fluorescence imaging to map the spatial distribution of catalytically active regions and quantify the changes in activity of those regions for photocatalytic oxidation in bismuth titanium oxide (Bi4Ti3O12) nanoplates. Individual nanoplates varied widely in both activity and stability, reflecting significant heterogeneity among a single synthesis batch of photocatalyst particles. We observed that while the nanoplates are more active around the perimeter of the basal facet, those perimeter regions decrease in activity at the same relative rate as the rest of the basal facet, indicating a spatially uniform degradation mechanism. Through ensemble structural characterization of the nanoplates after irradiation, we identified surface hydroxyl groups as the photo-induced feature. Our results indicate that surface hydroxyl groups introduce hole trap states that increase charge recombination at the surface of the nanoplates, leading to the observed decrease in activity. Surprisingly, we identified nanoscale features that do not begin with high activity but exhibit a slower rate of activity loss, leading to regions with greater activity relative to the rest of the basal facet at the end of imaging. Our findings highlight the importance of not only understanding how different nanoscale features influence catalytic activity but also how these features evolve over time, which dictates catalyst stability.

items.title: Integration of Charged Peptide Amphiphiles within Lipid Nanoparticles (LNPs) for Enhanced Targeted mRNA Delivery
items.abstract: Abstract Lipid nanoparticles (LNPs) play a pivotal role in mRNA-based therapy; however, achieving targeted delivery remains challenging. We developed an LNP platform integrating peptide amphiphiles (PAs) to exploit their dual bioactivity and electrostatic tunability. Two PAs, cationic C16TAT (derived from a cell-penetrating peptide) and anionic C16HA2 (based on an endosomolytic peptide), were co-assembled into LNPs. In vitro, C16TAT/LNPs significantly enhanced mRNA delivery across multiple cell lines via improved cellular uptake. Due to the potent charge-modifying capacity of C16HA2, C16HA2/LNPs exhibit spleen-selective tropism in vivo, achieving &gt;100-fold higher mRNA expression in the spleen than in the liver. While the commonly used surface-conjugated TAT-PEG-LNPs enhanced transfection in vitro, their in vivo performance was inferior relative to the C16TAT/LNP system due to the lack of stability, highlighting the advantage of PA integration. Critically, effective tissue targeting required substantial LNP charge alteration (pKa and zeta potential), which was achievable with C16HA2 but not C16TAT, likely due to the former’s higher aggregation tendency. Dual PA-PEG modifications may improve spleen targeting but required formulation optimization. This work establishes a simple PA/lipid co-assembly approach as a robust method for modulating LNP tropism, advancing the rational design of targeted mRNA delivery systems.

items.title: Polarized 3D Bicontinuous bcu Covalent Organic Frameworks with Accessible Octa-Sites for High-Efficiency Oxygen Electrocatalysis
items.abstract: Abstract Three-dimensional (3D) covalent organic frameworks (COFs) are potential metal-free electrocatalysts for the oxygen reduction reaction (ORR) due to their inherent porosity and potential for fully exposed active sites. However, their practical application is severely hindered by inefficient electron transport along the extended framework and the resultant high kinetic barriers. Herein, we report a series of highly crystalline and non-interpenetrated 8-connected body-centered cubic (bcu) COFs featuring eight unstacked catalytic nodes per unit cell for ORR. By integrating redox-active azobenzene (Azo) units into the linkages, we successfully bridge the gap between electronic conductivity and catalytic activity. The incorporated Azo moieties not only narrow the bandgap but also serve as electron reservoirs, facilitating rapid electron shuttling to the imine-based active sites. Consequently, the optimal DZPy-COF achieves a remarkable half-wave potential of 0.77 V under alkaline conditions, coupled with a high turnover frequency (0.03 s–1) and enhanced capacitance (13.7 mF cm–2). Theoretical calculations reveal that the Azo units polarize the framework, lowering the energy barrier for intermediate formation, which is the rate-determining step in conventional 3D COFs. This work underscores the efficacy of leveraging high-valency topologies combined with redox-active linkages to overcome electron transport limitations in crystalline porous catalysts.

items.title: A Graphene Oxide-Based Tribo-Piezoelectric Hybrid Sensor for Armed Swimming Action Recognition
items.abstract: Abstract Limb movement analysis provides a convenient and effective approach for physiological safety monitoring and motion standardization assessment of personnel working in humid, wading, or underwater environments.
