However, in wet and wading environments, the existing wearable flexible sensors generally suffer from several limitations such as insufficient sensitivity, rapid performance degradation, and poor environmental stability. In this paper, we propose a corrosion-resistant tribo-piezoelectric hybrid sensor (CRTPHS) primarily composed of an intrinsically corrosion-resistant fluorinated graphene oxide film with a micro-truncated pyramid array structure (MFGOF) and gold-coated polydimethylsiloxane-barium zirconate titanate (PDMS-BZT). The CRTPHS exhibited a sensitivity of up to 1.86 V/N, a response time of 106 ms, a peak power density of 1.98 mW/m2, and stable output performance after 50,000 cycles. In corrosion resistance tests, the CRTPHS retained a sensitivity of 1.27 V/N and excellent underwater sensing capability even after 3 days of seawater immersion. By integrating a lightweight random forest (RF) algorithm, the CRTPHS enabled recognition of five simulated armed-swimming motion states, achieving an average cross-subject accuracy of 99.25% ± 0.07% under leave-one-subject-out cross-validation (LOSO-CV). This study not only provides a novel fabrication method for developing corrosion-resistant self-powered sensors but also offers a new strategy for intelligent posture recognition in corrosive seawater environments.

items.title: Ion-Conductive Elastomers with Enhanced Mechanical Performance and Electrical Conductivity via a Nano-Synergistic Transport Mechanism
items.abstract: Abstract Flexible ion-conductive elastomers have emerged as promising materials for wearable humidity sensors owing to their excellent stretchability and efficient ion transport capability. However, simultaneously achieving high ionic conductivity and excellent mechanical performance remains a significant challenge, primarily because the incorporation of high loadings of ionic components often induces solvation effects within polymer networks and compromises their mechanical stability. To address this challenge, we developed an ion-conductive elastomer with enhanced mechanical robustness and efficient ion transport capability by constructing a hydrogen-bond-anchored micro/nanostructured conductive network. Specifically, amino-functionalized SiO2 serves not only as a nanoreinforcing phase but also as a “bridging node” for ion transport through multiple hydrogen-bond anchoring interactions with polyurethane chains, enabling the formation of a continuous micro/nanoscale ionic conductive network while preserving the structural stability of the polymer matrix. The resulting ion-conductive elastomer exhibits high ionic conductivity (1.4 × 10–2 S/m), high tensile strength (2.17 MPa), and recyclability, achieving an effective synergy between mechanical performance and ion transport properties. Based on a humidity-induced ion transport mechanism, the fabricated flexible humidity sensor demonstrates rapid, stable, and reversible responses over a broad relative humidity range. This work provides a new material design strategy for developing high-performance, sustainable, and flexible ion-conductive polyurethane-based wearable humidity sensors.

items.title: Chemically Active Interfaces Enable Modular Manufacturing of DLP 3D Printed Hydrogel Electronics
items.abstract: Abstract Hydrogel-based flexible sensors are promising for wearable electronics, while digital light processing (DLP) printing enables customized device fabrication. However, DLP manufacturing remains largely limited to monolithic structures because freshly printed hydrogels lack sufficient mechanical stability for constructing curved or enclosed architectures. Here, a modular manufacturing strategy is developed by enabling post-printing polymerization through a sustained radical-generation system comprising Cu2+, lignosulfonate (LS), and ammonium persulfate (APS). Unlike conventional photoinitiated systems that become inactive after light exposure, the Cu2+–LS complex maintains a dynamic Cu2+/Cu+ redox cycle in the dark, continuously activating APS to generate radicals. Consequently, independently printed hydrogel modules undergo interfacial polymerization and reconstruct a continuous covalent network, enabling assembled hydrogels to exhibit bulk-like load-bearing performance with failure occurring outside the assembled interface. The Cu–LS system also introduces mobile ions, imparting intrinsic ionic conductivity for strain sensing without conductive fillers. Using this approach, ring-integrated and kirigami-patterned wearable sensors are fabricated through modular assembly. A fingertip-mounted device achieves 99% accuracy in classifying ten sign-language gestures and enables real-time intelligent wheelchair control. This work converts hydrogel interfaces from inactive boundaries into active reconstruction sites, offering a versatile route to the modular fabrication of mechanically integrated soft electronics.

items.title: Interface-Engineered Electrochemical CO2 Reduction to Formate Coupled with Enzymatic Dihydroxyacetone Production
items.abstract: Abstract While the electroreduction of CO2 to high-value chemicals provides a revolutionary strategy for achieving sustainable development, the direct synthesis of multi-carbon products remains a prominent challenge. Herein, an integrated strategy that combines renewable electrochemical carbon dioxide reduction reactions (eCO2RR) with enzyme cascades for the high-value-added production of dihydroxyacetone is proposed. Specifically, bismuth nanocatalysts were doped with sulfur to modulate the surface electronic structure, leading to the significantly accelerated formation of *HCOO intermediates. Consequently, a 94.7% formate Faradaic efficiency was attained at 300 mA cm–2, and good long-term catalytic stability was achieved. Moreover, a 4 cm2 membrane electrode electrolyzer was employed with a 0.1 M KHCO3 neutral electrolyte to concentrate the formate product and protect the downstream enzymes from the alkaline electrolyte. The cofactor NADH was directly regenerated using a copper foam electrode, driving an enzymatic cascade to convert formate to 2.77 g L–1 dihydroxyacetone without external carbon supplementation. This work presents a DHA synthesis method, which is solely electricity-driven and involves the direct reaction of CO2 and H2O, without requiring any externally supplied cofactors or stoichiometric reductants. By exploiting the fine selectivity and efficiency of enzyme catalysis, this formate-mediated pathway maximizes carbon utilization and significantly expands the chemical space accessible to carbon dioxide.

items.title: Nanofiber Density Is a Higher-Order Architectural Regulator of Multidimensional Cardiomyocyte Maturation
items.abstract: Abstract Insufficient maturation of cardiomyocytes (CMs) remains a major challenge in cardiac tissue engineering. While electrospun nanofibers offer biomimetic topographical and mechanical cues, conventional high-density fiber architectures impose excessive mechanical constraints that restrict mechanotransduction and limit CM maturation. Here, we employed a suspended, aligned electrospun polycaprolactone (PCL) nanofiber platform to investigate how fiber density—categorized as low (LD; 15.89 ± 1.84 μg/cm2), medium (MD; 85.81 ± 12.74 μg/cm2), and high (HD; 404.90 ± 59.10 μg/cm2)—modulates the maturation of neonatal rat cardiomyocytes (NRCMs). The MD substrate was identified as the optimal configuration, effectively balancing topographical guidance with a permissive mechanical microenvironment for NRCM maturation. Compared with the HD substrate, NRCMs on MD substrates exhibited enhanced structural maturation, with a greater aspect ratio (5.65 ± 1.15) and sarcomere length (1.92 ± 0.17 μm). These structural improvements were accompanied by enhanced gap junction formation and improved electromechanical function, including a 4.03-fold higher contraction displacement and a 4.01-fold faster calcium decay rate. Furthermore, the MD substrate promoted metabolic maturation, evidenced by a 2.08-fold increase in mitochondrial membrane potential and a 2.42-fold higher ATP production. The LD substrate exhibited an intermediate maturation phenotype between MD and HD groups. Mechanistically, the maturation-promoting effects of the MD substrate were associated with increased YAP phosphorylation and cytoplasmic retention, together with enhanced PI3K–Akt signaling, all of which were attenuated by high-density fiber packing. This "Goldilocks effect" establishes fiber density as a critical architectural determinant of CM maturation and highlights optimization of this parameter to regulate mechanosignaling as an effective strategy for engineering functionally mature cardiomyocytes.

items.title: Microfluidic Production of Mangiferin-Loaded Liposomes Enables Gut–Joint Axis Modulation for Early Osteoarthritis Intervention
items.abstract: Abstract Microfluidic nanomanufacturing provides a controllable and scalable strategy for improving the oral delivery of poorly bioavailable natural compounds. Herein, mangiferin-loaded liposomes (Lip@MG) were fabricated using an in-house-developed continuous microfluidic platform integrated with a high-efficiency micromixer and evaluated as a gut–joint axis-oriented intervention for early knee osteoarthritis (KOA). Compared with the conventional batch method, microfluidic synthesis produced Lip@MG with a more uniform spherical morphology, a clearly defined bilayer structure, and a narrower particle size distribution. By adjusting the flow-rate ratio, Lip@MG with tunable particle sizes from 207.8 to 118.6 nm, reduced polydispersity, and stable negative zeta potentials of up to approximately –35 mV was obtained. In vitro, Lip@MG exhibited favorable cytocompatibility and enhanced chondrocyte viability. Transcriptomic analysis, qRT-PCR, and western blot further indicated that Lip@MG attenuated LPS-induced inflammatory responses in chondrocytes, at least partly by suppressing NF-κB signaling and inhibiting p65 phosphorylation. In an anterior cruciate ligament transection-induced KOA mouse model, oral Lip@MG administration alleviated cartilage degeneration, increased cartilage thickness from 132 to 215 μm, reduced the OARSI score from 2.5 to 1.5, increased subchondral bone mineral density by 27%, and restored colonic barrier integrity, as reflected by a 65% reduction in the colonic histopathological score. Full-length 16S rRNA gene sequencing revealed that Lip@MG reshaped KOA-associated gut dysbiosis by partially restoring the Firmicutes/Bacteroidetes balance and enriching potentially beneficial taxa. These findings demonstrate that microfluidically manufactured Lip@MG is a promising nutritional nanocarrier for microbiota-centered early KOA intervention through coordinated regulation of intestinal homeostasis and joint degeneration.

items.title: Sequence-Engineered Multifunctional Peptide Nanozyme Gel for Catalytic Microenvironment Regulation in Diabetic Infected Wounds
items.abstract: Abstract Chronic diabetic wounds are characterized by persistent infection, redox imbalance, and dysregulated enzymatic activity, yet current biomaterials largely function as passive dressings, with limited capacity to actively intervene in the stalled healing cascade. Here, we report a sequence-programmed peptide nanozyme that encodes multiple enzyme-mimetic activities within a single supramolecular framework for adaptive microenvironment regulation. By mimicking the coordination motifs of natural hydrolases and superoxide dismutase, a de novo peptide sequence, C7-RD(S)HHEEH, was rationally engineered to encode integrated nitrogen/oxygen metal-binding sites. The incorporation of a side-chain–modified serine enhances coordination adaptability, while glutamate residues facilitate catalytic functionality. Upon Cu2+ coordination, the peptide self-assembles into a nanozyme exhibiting hydrolase (HYD)-, oxidase (OXD)-, peroxidase (POD)-, and superoxide dismutase (SOD)-like activities within a unified framework, thereby enabling coordinated regulation of enzymatic debridement, antibacterial defense, and redox homeostasis. Incorporated into a sprayable gelatin hydrogel, the nanozyme provides conformal wound coverage while maintaining excellent biocompatibility and sustained catalytic functionality. In a diabetic bacteria-infected wound model, the nanozyme gel significantly accelerates wound closure, enhances angiogenesis and collagen deposition, and restores tissue regeneration. Our work demonstrates that rational peptide sequence design can encode complex, multimodal catalysis into synthetic nanozymes, offering a programmable approach for active regulation of pathological microenvironments in chronic wound therapy.

items.title: Atomic Resolution Microscopy Reveals Cluster, Charge Transport, and Diffusion Metrics in Guest:Host Blend Films
items.abstract: Abstract Quantitatively determining the 3D arrangement of guest molecules in a guest:host emissive layer remains a challenge, particularly for beam-sensitive organic materials. By extracting 3D coordinates from depth-sectioned HAADF–STEM stacks of Ir(ppy)2(acac):TCTA and Ir(ppy)3:TCTA vacuum-deposited guest:host blend films, we enable direct access to molecular-scale morphology in beam-sensitive materials. We find that guest aggregation is significantly stronger than expected from random distributions, with the difference diminishing only at high concentrations. Coupling these morphologies to master equation transport modeling reveals that aggregation alters transport pathways and reduces mobility. Additionally, thermal motion of guest molecules between the image frames provides an estimate of molecular diffusion, linking structural and dynamic behavior.

items.title: Conductive Composite-Based Wearable Sensors for Sports Science: Intelligent Data Analysis and Emerging Applications
items.abstract: Abstract Wearable sensors enable continuous acquisition of physiological, biochemical, and biomechanical signals during exercise, providing data to support sports performance assessment, training regulation, fatigue monitoring, and rehabilitation interventions. However, signal reliability and multidimensional data analysis under complex motion conditions remain constrained by device functionality. Conductive composites can improve sensor flexibility, interfacial conformability, and signal acquisition performance, while artificial intelligence (AI) enables movement pattern recognition, state assessment, and outcome prediction from complex data. Their integration is advancing wearable systems toward multimodal sensing and intelligent analysis. Guided by application needs in sports, this review summarizes emerging applications of wearable sensing technologies enabled by conductive composites and AI. First, the relevance to sports science and the data characteristics of physiological, biochemical, and biomechanical signals are introduced. The functional characteristics, representative applications, and major limitations of conductive polymer, carbon-based, MXene, and hydrogel composites are then summarized. Regarding algorithms, the fundamental principles of supervised learning, unsupervised learning, deep learning (DL), and large language models (LLMs) are discussed, with comparisons of their capabilities in feature extraction, temporal modeling, and multisource data analysis, as well as their input data requirements. On this basis, advances in the application of these systems to sports performance and sport-specific movement monitoring, exercise-induced fatigue monitoring and assessment, sports injury identification and evaluation, and intelligent monitoring of sports rehabilitation are reviewed followed by a discussion of current challenges and future directions. Through the coordinated integration of material design, signal acquisition, and intelligent analysis, wearable systems are expected to enable continuous, reliable, and individualized assessment of exercise-related states, with further applications in real-time feedback, risk alerts, and training decision support, providing a technological foundation for scientifically informed training, sports rehabilitation, and individual health management.

items.title: End-to-End Biomanufacturing of Extracellular Vesicles
items.abstract: Abstract Extracellular vesicles (EVs) have emerged as next-generation, multispecific, and multifunctional agents across medicine, biotechnology, veterinary science, cosmetics, and nutrition. Their delivery efficiency of therapeutic cargo surpasses that of conventional carriers, and their capacity to simultaneously transport internal cargo and activate multiple recipient cells gives them a therapeutic versatility that no other platform can match. Translating this potential into real-world products depends on integrating process design with product characterization, a link that has not yet been systematically established for EV manufacturing. The functionality of an EV is inseparable from how it is made. EV composition is shaped at every stage of production, from the biology of the producer cell, to upstream microenvironmental stressors, to the operational parameters of downstream isolation and purification. Each of these variables influences the final product quality and functionality, which means that process design is, in effect, product design. While many guidelines, including minimal information for studies of extracellular vesicles (MISEV) and quality by design (QbD), have been reported, they operate at different levels: MISEV ensures the validity of EV characterization, whereas QbD defines how a manufacturer designs, controls, and releases a product. Currently, however, there is no link between them to provide an integrative framework. This manuscript, therefore reviews and proposes a framework for context-of-use–dependent EV biomanufacturing, in which biomanufacturing and bioprocessing parameters are deliberately matched to the intended application. By linking specific process conditions to resultant EV characteristics, and by fine-tuning upstream and downstream operations accordingly, bespoke EVs can be produced for defined therapeutic, diagnostic, or industrial purposes rather than made as a single generic product. Together, this work offers essential guidance for producing EVs at scale and for designing end-to-end bioprocesses that can be tailored to the diverse needs of future EV-based products.

items.title: Band Structure-Engineered Nanopatterned MoS2/Graphene Heterostructures for Low-Noise Broadband Photodetection
items.abstract: Abstract Integrating two-dimensional (2D) heterostructures is a promising strategy for high-performance optoelectronics; however, achieving high sensitivity and broadband response while maintaining low-noise operation remains challenging. Here, we report a nanoporous molybdenum disulfide (MoS2)/graphene heterostructure phototransistor fabricated via block copolymer-assisted self-assembly and material-selective etching, which provides a scalable and reproducible approach for large-area fabrication. By employing a precise etching sequence using O2 plasma for graphene and XeF2 gas for MoS2, we successfully realize a periodic nanohole array while preserving interfacial integrity. The resulting nanoporous architecture induces bandgap opening in graphene and introduces a high density of edge states, which enhances trap-assisted photogating in the phototransistor and significantly amplify the photocurrent. As a result, the device exhibits a high photoresponsivity of 24.58 AW–1 and a specific detectivity of 2.33 × 1011 Jones under 405 nm illumination. Notably, the device demonstrates a robust photoresponse in the mid-infrared (MIR) region (≈11 µm), extending beyond the intrinsic bandgap limitation of MoS2 and enabling detection capability spanning from the visible to the MIR regime, compared with previously reported MoS2-based heterostructures operating over narrower spectral ranges. Temperature-dependent measurements confirm that this MIR response originates from genuine optical carrier generation rather than bolometric effects. Furthermore, the nanoporous graphene suppresses excessive dark current via bandgap opening and edge-induced states, enabling improved signal-to-noise characteristics. These results establish nanoporous 2D heterostructures as an effective strategy for ultra-broadband and low-noise photodetection.

items.title: Hierarchical Biomimetic Engineering of Transition Metal Dichalcogenide-Based Composites for Electromagnetic Attenuation: Structure-Behavior-Function Relationships and Design Rules
items.abstract: Abstract Transition metal dichalcogenide (TMD)-based composites are increasingly investigated for microwave absorption and electromagnetic interference shielding, yet their attenuation response cannot be explained by composition alone. The spatial arrangement of nanosheets, pores, interfaces, and conductive domains governs wave entry, polarization relaxation, carrier transport, and internal dissipation. Biomimetic materials are nevertheless commonly classified by their resemblance to flowers, nacre, honeycombs, or biological networks, making it difficult to compare structures that perform similar physical roles. Accordingly, a structure-behavior-function (SBF) relationship is used to reassess the field. TMDs are considered adjustable building units whose phase, defects, surface chemistry, and assembly can be tailored while restacking, limited conductivity, and structural instability remain practical constraints. Five recurring strategies are examined: porous architectures that modify wave propagation, heterogeneous interfaces that redistribute charge, oriented channels that direct carrier transport, through-thickness gradients that regulate impedance, and multilevel structures that couple these processes. Reported absorption and shielding results are compared to determine where these structural interpretations are supported and where commonly used descriptors, including filler loading, total porosity, and interface density, remain insufficient. The resulting design rules are function-dependent because high total shielding, strong microwave absorption, and absorption-dominated shielding require different balances among conductivity, polarization, and impedance matching. Quantitative descriptors, multiscale modeling, data-assisted design, reproducible manufacturing, and device-level validation are identified as priorities for moving biomimetic TMD composites beyond morphology-led optimization.

items.title: Scalable Melt-Spun Polyethylene/Boron Nitride Fabric Integrating Radiative and Nonradiative Cooling Effects for Personal Thermal Management
items.abstract: Abstract With the escalating global energy crisis and environmental challenges, radiative cooling textiles have emerged as a promising energy-free thermal management solution. However, existing cooling fabrics primarily focus on enhancing optical properties like solar reflectance and infrared emissivity, often neglecting the critical role of nonradiative heat dissipation (conduction and convection) while also facing challenges in scalability, durability, and comfort. To address these limitations, this study presents a scalably manufactured polyethylene/boron nitride (HDPE/BN) composite fabric fabricated via industrial melt spinning and weaving. By uniformly incorporating BN sheets into HDPE fibers, the composite fabric achieves enhanced solar reflectivity (86%) and mid-infrared emissivity (89.3%) due to the high refractive index, efficient Mie scattering, and intrinsic infrared absorption features of BN. More importantly, it exhibits enhanced in-plane thermal conductivity (7.73 ± 0.18 W·m–1·K–1) while maintaining breathability, complementing the nonradiative cooling effects. Experimental results demonstrate that the fabric provides temperature reductions of 3.7 °C (daytime) and 2.7 °C (nighttime) in simulated building cooling tests, and 3.9 °C (daytime) and 1.6 °C (nighttime) in simulated human skin tests. This work highlights the importance of integrating optical and thermal management properties, providing a scalable manufacturing route of high-performance personal cooling textiles for practical applications.

items.title:
<scp>l</scp>
                    -Cysteine-Functionalized MXene Porous Scaffold-Based Phase Change Films for Efficient Thermal Management
items.abstract: Abstract Phase change materials (PCMs) hold great promise for thermal management, yet their low thermal conductivity and liquid leakage severely hinder practical applications. Herein, we designed a high-enthalpy phase change composite film (LMAP) based on l-Cysteine-functionalized MXene (l-MXene) and aramid nanofibers (ANFs). l-cysteine was bonded to MXene via covalent and coordination bonds, and further crosslinked with ANF through hydrogen bonds to form layered aerogel films with a porous scaffold structure, which was subsequently impregnated with polyethylene glycol (PEG). The unique porous layered architecture of LMAP-20 achieved a PEG loading of 86.71%, a phase-change enthalpy of 169.33 J/g, and a tensile strength of 17.26 MPa for favorable energy storage performance. Moreover, l-MXene nanosheets endowed LMAP-50 with a high thermal conductivity of 1.58 W/(m·K), which enabled outstanding thermal management and reduced the operating temperature of the LED chip by 21.4 °C. These results suggest that the l-MXene/ANF porous scaffold holds great potential for fabricating phase change composites with high thermal conductivity and suppressed leakage, which could be applied for efficient thermal management in advanced electronic devices.

items.title: Dual-Scale Hollow-in-Porous PVDF Composite Films Integrating Broadband Reflectance and Fire Safety for Secure Passive Daytime Radiative Cooling
items.abstract: Abstract Passive daytime radiative cooling (PDRC) has emerged as a promising zero-energy thermal management technology for building energy conservation. However, the inherent porosity of polymeric cooling materials renders them highly flammable, which facilitates rapid flame spread and poses severe safety hazards in practical applications. To address these challenges, this study proposes a design strategy of “dual-scale optical and multifunctional chemical integration”, successfully fabricating a dual-scale hollow-in-porous polyvinylidene fluoride (PVDF) composite film that elegantly integrates broadband reflectance with exceptional fire safety. Specifically, hollow core-shell hybrid fillers (ZIF-8@PA@SiO2) were synthesized by etching ZIF-8 templates with phytic acid (PA), followed by uniform encapsulation within a SiO2 shell. These fillers were subsequently incorporated into a PVDF matrix via a phase-inversion process, yielding a hierarchical dual-scale hollow-in-porous architecture. Benefiting from enhanced Mie scattering induced by this structural design, alongside the synergistic molecular vibrations of polar Si–O–Si and C–F bonds, the resulting film delivers an outstanding solar reflectance of 92.3% and a high infrared emissivity of 94.8%. Under outdoor conditions, the composite achieves a sub-ambient temperature drop of 12.7 °C, while under simulated conditions, it exhibits a temperature reduction of 19 °C relative to the bare substrate. The corresponding cooling powers reach 109.3 and 130.7 W m–2 during the day and night, respectively. Crucially, the incorporation of ZIF-8@PA@SiO2 drastically bolsters the material's flame retardancy. Compared to the pristine substrate, the peak heat release rate (pHRR) and total heat release (THR) are curtailed by 52.8 and 52.4%, respectively. This facile and highly effective fabrication strategy paves the way for the secure and practical architectural deployment of PDRC materials.

items.title: An Environmentally Benign and Cost-Effective Modified Graphene Oxide/Sodium Alginate-Based Gel Electrolyte for Practical Quasi-Solid-State Zinc-Ion Batteries
items.abstract: Abstract Quasi-solid-state zinc-ion batteries (ZIBs) have attracted extensive attention owing to their intrinsic safety, low cost, and environmental sustainability. Sodium alginate (SA), as a natural polysaccharide, is a promising gel electrolyte matrix for sustainable ZIBs. However, the practical application of SA-based gel electrolytes is limited by insufficient ionic conductivity, unstable electrode/electrolyte interfaces, and uncontrolled Zn deposition. To address these problems, a modified graphene oxide/sodium alginate-based gel electrolyte (TCGSA) was prepared by incorporating TiO2/CaCO3 co-modified graphene oxide (TCGO) and erythritol (ER) into the SA matrix. The synergistic interaction among TCGO, ER, and SA was conducive to the transport of Zn2+ and the homogenization of interfacial ion flux, and the ionic conductivity of TCGSA was 23.8 mS·cm–1. Specifically, the polar TiO2-containing groups in TCGO provided additional Zn2+ interaction sites, while the hydrogen-bonding network formed by ER and SA enhanced the structural stability of the gel electrolyte and inhibited interfacial side reactions. When the TiO2 content in TCGO was 3.3 wt %, the Zn||MnO2 full cell assembled by the TCGSA gel electrolyte delivered a maximum capacity of 483 mAh·g–1 at 0.1 A·g–1 and retained 60.92% of its initial capacity after 1900 cycles at 2 A·g–1. Meanwhile, the Zn||Zn symmetric cell exhibited stable cycling for over 1200 h. The cost of the TCGSA pouch cell was relatively low (only $0.026 mAh–1) according to the estimation of raw material prices, and it was a potential candidate for the large-scale production of low-cost and environmentally friendly quasi-solid-state ZIBs.

items.title: Laser-Fabricated Ordered Tri-Level Hemispherical Microstructures for Flexible Pressure Sensors with Ultrahigh Sensitivity over a Wide Linear Range
items.abstract: Abstract The rapid advancement of embodied intelligence and soft robotics demands flexible pressure sensors that simultaneously achieve high sensitivity, a broad linear response range, and excellent long-term stability. However, the inherent compression hardening effect of soft materials imposes a fundamental trade-off between sensitivity and linear range, severely limiting their practical applicability in complex dynamic environments. Inspired by the hierarchical tactile perception mechanism of human skin and guided by Archard’s contact theory, we propose a piezoresistive sensor incorporating an ordered tri-level hemispherical microstructure array. The sensing layer, composed of a graphite powder/multiwalled carbon nanotubes/polydimethylsiloxane (GP/MWCNT/PDMS) conductive composite, is patterned via a rapid, scalable, and mask-free three-dimensional (3D) dynamic focusing laser processing technique. Finite element analysis (FEA) guides the optimization of geometric parameters, confirming that the tri-level configuration exhibits the highest compressibility and the greatest rate of contact area change among single-level, dual-level, and tri-level designs. The sensor operates through a graded deformation mechanism: under low pressure, the smallest hemispheres deform first to rapidly increase contact area, under medium pressure, the intermediate hemispheres engage to sustain sensitivity; under high pressure, the largest hemispheres provide structural support, ensuring continuous contact area expansion over a broad pressure range. Consequently, the sensor achieves an ultrahigh sensitivity of 12.8 kPa–1 over a wide linear range of 0–369 kPa (R2 = 0.998), with fast response/recovery times (20/21 ms) and excellent cycling stability (15,000 cycles). Beyond single-point sensing, we further construct a 4 × 4 sensor array that successfully discriminates spatial pressure distributions, as demonstrated by recognition of “M”-shaped and “U”-shaped loading modules. Practical applications include precise monitoring of finger joint bending angles and real-time plantar pressure distribution during walking and running, and shape-resolved tactile imaging, highlighting its great promise for applications in embodied intelligence, wearable health monitoring, human-machine interaction, and related fields.

items.title: Efficient and Stable Red QLEDs via 4-TBP-Doped Hole Transport Layer Engineering
items.abstract: Abstract The insufficient charge carrier mobility in the hole transport layer (HTL) and the energy level mismatch with the emissive layer have long been critical factors limiting the electroluminescence performance and carrier balance of quantum dot light-emitting diodes (QLEDs). To address this issue, we employed 4-tert-butylpyridine (4-TBP) as a dopant in poly[(9,9-dioctylfluorenyl-2,7-diyl)-co-(4,4′-(N-(4-sec-butylphenyl)diphenylamine))] (TFB) as the HTL. By modulating the highest occupied molecular orbital energy level of TFB and enhancing the hole mobility, 4-TBP doping effectively reduces the hole injection barrier and suppresses interfacial charge accumulation. The optimized TFB:4-TBP HTL significantly improves hole injection efficiency in red QLEDs, leading to a decrease in turn-on voltage from 1.74 V to 1.65 V and an increase in external quantum efficiency (EQE) from 22.21 to 26.47%. Moreover, at an initial luminance of 1000 cd m–2, the QLED with the TFB:4-TBP HTL reaches a T95 operational lifetime of 11,708.67 h, which is 2.4 times longer than that of the undoped one. 1.22- and 1.37-fold improvements in EQEmax are obtained for green and blue QLEDs, respectively. This strategy demonstrates that 4-TBP doping, combined with interface engineering, provides an effective method to achieve efficient and stable hole transport, offering new insights for carrier balance control in solution-processed QLEDs.

items.title: Microneedle Patch with Dual Control of Temperature and Drug-Release for Synergistic Chemo-Photothermal Therapy of Melanoma
items.abstract: Abstract Microneedles (MNs) combining chemotherapy and photothermal therapy offer a smart strategy for melanoma treatment but are hindered by the inadequate control of hyperthermia temperature and drug release. In this study, a novel MN patch consisting of a backing layer and porous needle tips was developed. The backing layer is made of the poly(N-isopropylacrylamide-acrylamide) (PNA) hydrogel. The needle tips are made of ethoxylated trimethylolpropane triacrylate, and their pores are loaded with PNA hydrogel containing both chemotherapeutic drug doxorubicin and photothermal agent polydopamine. Leveraging the thermochromic properties of the backing layer, the MN patch can autonomously regulate the temperature of needle tips to lower critical solution temperature of PNA (around 43 °C) upon near-infrared laser irradiation, without the need for external temperature control devices. Combined with the thermosensitive volume change of PNA in needle tips, the MN patch enables on-demand drug release. In vivo anti-melanoma experiments demonstrated a potent tumor-killing efficacy, with a tumor suppression rate of 89.2%. This innovative MN patch integrating temperature self-regulation and on-demand drug release presents a promising alternative for melanoma therapy.

items.title: Matrix Stiffness Controls Lipid Homeostasis in Human Corneal Endothelial Cells via a Piezo1-PI3K/AKT-mTOR-PPARγ Mechanotransduction Axis
items.abstract: Abstract Substrate stiffness is a critical mechanical cue that regulates cellular behaviors, yet its role in governing lipid homeostasis of human corneal endothelial cells (HCECs) remains poorly understood. Here, we developed a polyacrylamide hydrogel platform with tunable stiffnesses (25, 50, and 100 kPa) covering the pathophysiological range of Descemet’s membrane to investigate stiffness-dependent lipid metabolic reprogramming in HCECs. All hydrogels exhibited excellent transparency (&gt;95%) and good biocompatibility. We found that soft substrates (25 kPa) promoted substantial accumulation of neutral lipids and free cholesterol in HCECs. Mechanistically, soft substrates upregulated SREBP1 and its target genes to enhance fatty acid synthesis while suppressing CPT1-mediated fatty acid oxidation, and simultaneously upregulated LDLR and SREBP2 to promote cholesterol uptake and synthesis while downregulating the LXRα-ABCA1/ABCG1 axis to impair cholesterol efflux. Notably, PPARγ emerged as a key regulator of stiffness-dependent lipid homeostasis; its expression was positively correlated with substrate stiffness, and pharmacological activation of PPARγ reversed soft substrate-induced lipid accumulation. Furthermore, the Piezo1-PI3K/AKT-mTOR signaling axis was identified as an upstream mechanotransduction pathway mediating stiffness-regulated PPARγ expression. Analysis of transcriptomic datasets from Fuchs endothelial corneal dystrophy (FECD) patients revealed dysregulation of lipid metabolism genes consistent with our findings. Together, these results demonstrate that substrate stiffness governs HCEC lipid homeostasis through a Piezo1-PI3K/AKT-mTOR-PPARγ mechanotransduction cascade, and that matrix softening promotes abnormal lipid accumulation by reprogramming fatty acid and cholesterol metabolic networks. Our findings establish a mechanistic link between the mechanical microenvironment and lipid metabolism in corneal endothelial cells, providing insights into FECD pathogenesis and a theoretical framework for designing stiffness-tuned biomaterials for corneal endothelial regeneration.

items.title: Efficient Hydroxymethanesulfonate Electrosynthesis from CO2 and Sulfite over CuPd1 Single-Atom Alloys
items.abstract: Abstract Electrochemical C–S coupling of CO2 and sulfite (SO32–) offers a sustainable alternative for hydroxymethanesulfonate (HMS) synthesis, yet its electrocatalytic selectivity remains far from satisfactory. Here, CuPd1 single-atom alloys (CuPd1-SAA) are developed as a highly efficient catalyst for HMS electrosynthesis, delivering an exceptional Faradaic efficiency of 56.8% and an HMS yield rate of 301.5 mmol h–1 g–1 in an MEA electrolyzer, together with outstanding electrolysis stability for over 200 h of electrolysis. Mechanistic investigations reveal the critical Cu-Pd1 synergy in driving CO2 reduction to *CHOH and C–S coupling of *CHOH with *SO3 for selective HMS generation.

items.title: Mie Scattering-Enhanced Fluorinated Polyether Ether Ketone Nanofibrous Films for Efficient Radiative Heat Dissipation
items.abstract: Abstract This study develops a high-performance radiative cooling (RC) composite film based on electrospinning fluorinated polyether ether ketone, incorporating titanium dioxide (TiO2) and hexagonal boron nitride (h-BN) as functional fillers to achieve exceptional spectral selectivity with a solar reflectance of 96.51% and mid-infrared emissivity of 95.12%. The three-dimensional porous fibrous network endows the film with outstanding RC performance, achieving a maximum sub-ambient temperature reduction of 14.63 °C under direct sunlight and a temperature reduction of 8.66 °C relative to the bare vehicle model in small-scale outdoor vehicle tests, thereby validating the significant cooling advantage of the electrospinning film under real-world service conditions. The synergistic effect of the porous fibrous network and intrinsically low-surface-energy matrix imparts self-cleaning functionality to the film (water contact angle of 151.46° and sliding angle of approximately 5°), while solar reflectance degradation remains below 3% after the aging test, demonstrating long-term outdoor service reliability. EnergyPlus building energy simulations confirmed that the film achieved annual energy savings exceeding 6% in tropical arid cities, with positive net energy savings across the vast majority of global climate regions. This film provides a comprehensive design paradigm for high-performance multifunctional RC materials, with broad application prospects for low-carbon building energy conservation and outdoor thermal management.

items.title: Sn@C Composite with an Ultra-high Initial Coulombic Efficiency via Interfacial Engineering for Sodium-Ion Battery Anodes
items.abstract: Abstract Tin (Sn)-based anodes are attractive candidates for sodium-ion batteries due to their high theoretical capacity and low operating potential. However, their practical viability is severely constrained by drastic volume changes, unstable solid–electrolyte interphase (SEI) formation, and intrinsically low initial Coulombic efficiency (ICE). Herein, an interfacial regulation strategy to enhance the ICE and cycling stability of Sn-based anodes is proposed. That is, we construct Sn-MOF-derived Sn@C composites with submicron Sn particles uniformly confined in a conductive carbon matrix via hydrothermal synthesis and subsequent pyrolysis. This architecture yields an exceptional ICE of 96.4% (725/752 mA h g–1 at 0.1 A g–1), far surpassing that of commercial Sn powder (77.9%). Mechanistic investigations reveal a reversible stepwise alloying pathway from Sn to Na9Sn4 and subsequently to Na15Sn4, while the carbon matrix promotes a thin, uniform NaF-rich SEI that curbs electrolyte decomposition and Na+ loss. In situ EIS-DRT analysis further corroborates the progressive reduction of interfacial resistances during sodiation–desodiation. As a result, the anode sustains 378 mA h g–1 after 500 cycles at 1 A g–1. A Sn@C-900∥Na3V2(PO4)3 full cell can deliver an energy density of 188 W h kg–1 and retain 107 mA h g–1 over 400 cycles, underscoring the practical feasibility of this high-ICE Sn@C anode.

items.title: Microneedle-Based Oral Mucosal Vaccines: Mechanisms, Challenges, and Emerging Strategies
items.abstract: Abstract Oral mucosal vaccination is a minimally invasive and highly acceptable strategy that can trigger both local and systemic immunity. However, its progress toward clinical use is hindered by salivary washout, the multilayered epithelium, and a tolerance-prone immune environment. Microneedles offer a promising way to overcome these barriers. They deliver antigens beneath the oral surface, place them directly in immune-responsive tissues, and can remain operational in the dynamic, enzyme-rich oral cavity. Recent research shows that microneedles enable precise antigen deposition, stabilize fragile vaccine components, and provide controllable release patterns. Studies using both model antigens and clinically relevant targets suggest that oral microneedle vaccination can induce systemic IgG, mucosal sIgA, and tissue-resident cellular responses. Distal mucosal immune responses have also been observed. These distal responses are consistent with the common mucosal immune system (CMIS), although direct evidence of CMIS-dependent lymphocyte trafficking remains limited. The co-delivery of immunostimulatory materials, adjuvants, or nanoparticle carriers further enhances antigen presentation and helps counteract oral immune tolerance. Despite these advances, several challenges remain. These include clarifying the early immune events in oral tissues, identifying adjuvants suited to the oral environment, and ensuring safety, stability, and user acceptability for clinical translation. Overall, current evidence positions microneedles as a versatile and promising platform for mucosal vaccination. Continued integration of oral immunology with formulation and microneedle design will be essential for moving these systems toward real-world application.

items.title: Bias-Switchable ZnO/AlScN Heterojunction for Self-Powered UV Photodetection and Neuromorphic Learning
items.abstract: Abstract The convergence of ultraviolet (UV) communication and neuromorphic computing demands multifunctional devices that integrate high-speed photodetection with synaptic learning, yet the intrinsic mismatch between fast photoresponse and slow memory retention poses a fundamental challenge for monolithic integration. Here, we report a dual-mode UV optoelectronic device based on a ZnO/AlScN heterojunction, in which flexible switching between a self-powered photodetection mode and a neuromorphic mode is achieved through bias modulation. In mode I, operating at zero bias, the device exploits the type-II band alignment and built-in electric field of the heterojunction to realize a rapid response to 365 nm UV illumination, exhibiting a pA-level dark current, an on/off ratio of ∼ 4.2 × 103, rise/decay times of 279/64 ms, a responsivity of 101.06 mA/W, and a specific detectivity of 1.15 × 1012 Jones. It also demonstrates UV optical communication based on ASCII encoding. In mode II, operating under a 1 V bias, enhanced carrier separation together with oxygen-vacancy-induced persistent photoconductivity (PPC) in ZnO enables a series of neuromorphic behaviors, including excitatory postsynaptic current, paired-pulse facilitation, the transition from short-term to long-term memory, memory-forgetting characteristics, and Pavlovian associative learning. Our findings demonstrate the potential of the ZnO/AlScN heterojunction as a versatile two-terminal platform integrating self-powered UV detection and neuromorphic learning, enabled by interfacial band engineering and bias-controlled oxygen-vacancy dynamics for dual-mode switching. This strategy offers an approach for developing multifunctional optoelectronic devices for UV communication, biomimetic visual perception, and neuromorphic information processing.

items.title: Multiamino Polydiacetylene-Mediated Interfacial Engineering of Boron Nitride Nanosheet/Polyimide Composites for Low-Dielectric Thermal Management
items.abstract: Abstract The rapid advancement of high-frequency and highly integrated semiconductor devices urgently calls for dielectric materials that combine high thermal conductivity, low dielectric constant, and excellent thermal stability. Herein, multiamino polydiacetylene-functionalized boron nitride nanosheets (BNNS@MAPDA) have been incorporated into a MAPDA-containing polyimide matrix to improve filler–matrix interfacial coupling. The functionalized nanosheets exhibit high aspect ratios, few lattice defects, high yields, and excellent dispersion in the PI-MAPDA matrix. At a filler loading of only 7.5 wt %, the PI‑MAPDA/BNNS@MAPDA‑7.5 composite film achieves an in‑plane thermal conductivity of 1.67 W m–1 K–1, representing a 422% enhancement over pristine PI‑MAPDA. Benefiting from the ultralow polarizability of fluorinated groups and the strengthened interfacial coupling, the nanocomposite simultaneously maintains a low dielectric constant of 2.20 and a low dielectric loss tangent (tanδ) of 0.0066 at 1 MHz, alongside a volume resistivity of 9.7 × 1011 Ω cm. The density functional theory (DFT) calculations reveal that MAPDA functionalization enhances interfacial affinity and energy transfer, while molecular dynamics (MD) simulations elucidate its influence on thermal conductivity and dielectric properties. The Hashin–Shtrikman (HS) model analysis further confirms the positive role of interface regulation in thermal conductivity enhancement. MAPDA-mediated interphase engineering, through multisite anchoring to BNNS and strong chemical affinity with the PI matrix, provides an effective route to promote interfacial heat transfer while suppressing interfacial polarization at low filler loading. This material provides a promising solution for advanced electronic insulation and packaging applications by successfully addressing the challenge of combining low dielectric constant and high thermal conductivity in microelectronic systems.

items.title: Accelerated Discovery of Zn(II) Therapeutic Coordination Polymers (TCPs) for Controlled Drug Release
items.abstract: Abstract Therapeutic Coordination Polymers (TCPs) are a distinct class of nonporous drug-release materials in which tunable release kinetics arise from degradation of metal-ligand coordination bonds. Here, we report a high-throughput (HT) screening workflow that significantly accelerates TCP discovery by enabling parallel evaluation of 192 reaction conditions across four nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs: Diclofenac, Ibuprofen, Indomethacin, Naproxen) and six bis-imidazole or methyl-imidazole linkers (biim-4, biim-5, biim-6, biim-8, biim-4m, biim-6m). This approach yielded 15 crystalline zinc-based materials, including 13 TCPs and 2 metallocycles, with 12 representing previously unreported structures. The workflow offers a generalizable platform to expand the accessible chemical space for TCP formation and to broaden the range of compatible drug candidates. Among the linkers investigated, biim-4m emerged as particularly effective, forming TCPs with all four NSAIDs (ZnDiclo4m, ZnIbu4m, ZnIndo4m, ZnNap4m). These materials exhibited sustained drug-release kinetics in simulated body fluids, with intrinsic dissolution rates several orders of magnitude slower than those of their corresponding sodium salt forms. To evaluate the influence of the polymeric framework, a discrete Zn(II)-diclofenac-methylimidazole complex was synthesized to model a monomeric coordination unit. Dissolution studies showed significantly faster release from the monomeric complex compared to its polymeric counterpart, underscoring the functional advantage of the extended TCP architecture. Cell viability assays demonstrated biim-4m-derived TCPs were well tolerated below 50 µM relative to the native drugs. Overall, this work presents a scalable and versatile strategy for TCP discovery, highlights the structural features that contribute to sustained drug release, and supports the development of coordination polymer-based therapeutics with tunable performance.

items.title: Construction of Single-Atom Cobalt in Ordered Mesoporous Metal–Organic Frameworks for Boosting CO2 Conversion
items.abstract: Abstract Constructing single-atom transition-metal-implanted mesoporous metal–organic frameworks (MOFs) for CO2 conversion is of great importance for achieving carbon neutrality, yet remains a formidable challenge. This work presents a modular optimization of cerium-based metal–organic frameworks by incorporating Co single atoms with ordered mesopores (OMCU). These periodically arranged mesopores in OMCU were fabricated by synergistically combining the Hofmeister effect with a soft-template structure-oriented strategy. Mechanistic investigations reveal that the Co single atoms could not only accelerate photogenerated electron participation in CO2 conversion but also lower the energy barrier by promoting the formation of a new intermediate, *OCHO, along a specific reduction pathway, as directly observed by in situ Raman and operando ATR-IR spectroscopy. Density functional theory calculations corroborate that Co atoms favor the generation of *OCHO-related intermediates, omitting the high energy input for CO2·– formation and resulting in outstanding CO2 reduction performance, which is equivalent to a 10.84-fold enhancement in CO generation rate compared to that of the pristine MOF in the presence of TEA and bipyridinium ruthenium. This work provides an effective strategy through the construction of active cobalt sites within ordered mesoporous cerium-based MOFs for modulating the key intermediates in CO2 photoreduction.

items.title: Intranasal Mitochondria-Targeted Rosmarinic Acid Selenium Nanoparticles Restore Mitochondrial Function and Attenuate Dopaminergic Neurodegeneration in Parkinson’s Disease
items.abstract: Abstract Parkinson's disease (PD) is a progressive neurodegenerative disorder characterized by dopaminergic neuronal loss, mitochondrial dysfunction, oxidative stress, and α-synuclein pathology, highlighting the need for mitochondria-targeted neuroprotective strategies. Here, we developed a mitochondria-targeted intranasal nanotherapeutic system comprising rosmarinic acid (RA)-loaded selenium nanoparticles (RASNPs) surface-functionalized with triphenylphosphonium (TPP)-conjugated chitosan (TCS-RASNPs) to enhance nose-to-brain delivery and improve mitochondrial function. TCS-RASNPs exhibited a spherical morphology, a uniform particle size distribution (140.13 ± 0.40 nm), a narrow polydispersity, and a positive surface charge (33.7 ± 0.75 mV), indicating good colloidal stability. Spectroscopic characterization confirmed successful RA loading and surface functionalization. Moreover, TCS-RASNPs enhanced antioxidant activity and sustained drug release compared with free RA and unmodified RASNPs. In neuronal cells, TCS-RASNPs significantly enhanced neuronal survival, reduced apoptosis, attenuated intracellular and mitochondrial reactive oxygen species (ROS) generation, and improved mitochondrial membrane potential under 1-methyl-4-phenylpyridinium (MPP+)-induced neurotoxicity. Confocal microscopy further confirmed efficient mitochondrial localization of TCS-RASNPs. Pharmacokinetic and biodistribution studies demonstrated prolonged retention of RA and significantly higher brain RA levels following intranasal administration. In 1-methyl-4-phenyl-1,2,3,6-tetrahydropyridine (MPTP)-induced Parkinsonian mice, TCS-RASNPs increased tyrosine hydroxylase (TH) expression, reduced α-synuclein (SNCA) expression, and normalized oxidative stress biomarkers in the substantia nigra pars compacta (SNpc) and striatum (STR) regions. Together, these findings demonstrate that TCS-RASNPs facilitate mitochondrial targeting and nose-to-brain delivery, thereby representing a promising nanotherapeutic approach for the management of PD.

items.title: Phage Cocktail-Mediated Ultrasensitive Real-Time Electrochemical Whole-Cell Detection of Klebsiella pneumoniae on a SPCE
items.abstract: Abstract Rapid and selective detection of pathogenic bacteria is essential for timely clinical diagnosis and environmental surveillance. In this work, we report a bacteriophage-assisted electrochemical sensing platform for the selective detection of Klebsiella pneumoniae using an Er2O3/Co3O4/Au/polyethylenimine (PEI)-modified screen-printed carbon electrode (SPCE). The hierarchical nanocomposite was engineered to provide high surface area, enhanced charge transfer kinetics, and abundant functional sites for efficient phage immobilization. PEI served as a cationic linker to facilitate electrostatic attachment of lytic bacteriophages while maintaining their biological activity and host specificity. Upon target recognition, phage–bacteria binding at the electrode interface produced pronounced impedance changes due to interfacial blocking and altered electron transfer dynamics. The developed biosensor exhibited high selectivity for Klebsiella pneumoniae over nontarget bacteria and could distinguish live from dead bacteria. The sensor showed a wide linear detection range of 10–107 CFU/mL with a low detection limit of 7.36 CFU/mL and good repeatability with an RSD of ∼1.17%. The real-world applicability of the sensor was tested using aquarium water samples and demonstrated good performance, with recovery percentages ranging from ∼91.71 to 96.26%. This work establishes a robust nano–bio hybrid interface strategy that integrates rare-earth/transition metal oxide electrocatalysts with phage biorecognition on disposable SPCE platforms. The developed system shows strong potential for point-of-care pathogen monitoring in clinical, environmental, and food safety applications.

items.title: Asymmetric Janus Patch Integrating Antifouling and Wet-Adhesive Functions for Infected Wound Repair
items.abstract: Abstract The wet, dynamic, and bacteria-contaminated microenvironment of infected wounds creates conflicting demands for stable wound-facing adhesion and outward antifouling protection. To address these demands, we developed an asymmetric Janus hydrogel-film patch (JP-TA/Fe) with a coordination-stabilized bilayer interface. The patch consisted of a dense nonadhesive layer containing silk fibroin/tannic acid (SF/TA) and an adhesive hydrogel layer containing polyacrylic acid/recombinant collagen/tannic acid (PAA/rhCol/TA). TA-Fe3+ chelation was introduced at the bilayer interface through a facile process to strengthen interlayer bonding and maintain bilayer structural integrity during hydration and mechanical deformation. The outward-facing SF/TA layer provided mechanical support and an antifouling barrier, whereas the wound-facing hydrogel layer exhibited favorable fluid-uptake capacity and maintained stable tissue adhesion. Benefiting from this asymmetric design, the patch exhibited robust wet-tissue adhesion, pH-responsive TA release, asymmetric antifouling and adhesive properties, antibacterial activity, biofilm-disrupting performance, and efficient reactive oxygen species (ROS)-scavenging capacity. In a rat full-thickness skin incision model and a Staphylococcus aureus-infected full-thickness skin defect model, JP-TA/Fe promoted stable wound closure, reduced bacterial burden, and accelerated collagen remodeling and epidermal regeneration. This study presents a structurally stable Janus wound patch with spatially differentiated functions, providing a multifunctional material platform for infected wound repair.

items.title: A Microscopic View of Protein Soft and Reactive Landing on Flexible Polyethylene Glycol Surfaces
items.abstract: Abstract The interaction of proteins with polymer surfaces is central to understanding biomaterial compatibility and developing advanced deposition techniques. In this work, we investigate the collision dynamics of lysozyme and neurotensin with polyethylene glycol (PEG) surfaces in the vacuum using the reactive force field (ReaxFF). These simulations mimic the soft and reactive landing processes encountered in electrospray ionization (ESI)-, matrix-assisted laser desorption/ionization (MALDI)- and cluster ion beam-based preparative mass spectrometry approaches. Various PEG structures, including vertically aligned chains and amorphous configurations, with or without surface chain terminations, were considered. Collision velocities ranging from 1 to 6 km/s were employed to explore structural preservation, energy transfer, and chemical bond formation between the biomolecules and the PEG. For lysozyme (∼14 kDa), where 1 km/s corresponds to approximately 74 eV, our results show that PEG acts as a soft, cushion-like substrate, effectively dissipating impact energy and preserving protein structure under most conditions. Notably, covalent bond formation was observed only at high velocity (≥5 km/s) in the amorphous PEG structure lacking surface chain terminations. The findings indicate that PEG offers a promising medium for preserving protein integrity during deposition, maintaining the capacity to build protein multilayers, and potentially facilitating controlled protein desorption in solvents when desired. Even though defining an exact energy threshold would require a more detailed investigation, our simulations also constitute a proof-of-principle that the molecular fragments also transferred in iBEAM may act as mediators to induce protein grafting at relatively low velocity (3 km/s).

items.title: Vertical van der Waals Graphene/h-BN/SnS2 Top-Floating-Gate Memory for Optoelectronic Storage and Neuromorphic Computing
items.abstract: Abstract Nonvolatile memories based on two-dimensional (2D) van der Waals (vdW) heterostructures have attracted considerable attention because of their atomic-scale thickness, low energy operation, and prolonged data storage capability. However, most reported vdW floating-gate memories employ a bottom-floating-gate configuration, which often leads to a limited on/off ratio due to charge leakage and substrate-induced disturbance. Herein, a top-floating-gate memory based on a graphene (Gr)/h-BN/SnS2 vdW heterostructure is demonstrated, in which the top graphene layer serves as the charge-trapping layer. The device exhibits excellent nonvolatile memory performance, including an on/off ratio of 106, a memory window of 50.8 V, a low standby current of 1 pA, and an extrapolated retention time of 10 years. Owing to the low hole-tunneling barrier between SnS2 and h-BN, the device achieves more than 50 progressively modulated conductance levels under a weak optical pulse of 0.74 nW·mm–2. Moreover, stable long-term potentiation and depression characteristics can be regulated by optical and electrical pulses. Based on these synaptic behaviors, a three-layer multilayer perceptron neural network using the floating-gate memory achieved a classification accuracy of 96% for handwritten digit recognition using the Modified National Institute of Standards and Technology (MNIST) dataset. This work presents a top-floating-gate architecture for 2D-material memories, providing a feasible strategy for future logic-in-memory and neuromorphic computing applications.

items.title: Tuning Exciton Dynamics in Asymmetric Molecular Acceptors by End-Group Modulation Enables Efficient All-Small Molecule Organic Solar Cells
items.abstract: Abstract Asymmetric small-molecule acceptors have been recognized as a pivotal component in the development of organic solar cells (OSCs). Here, we report the design and synthesis of two cost-effective asymmetric molecular acceptors, SM-11 and SM-12, featuring a simple coumarin–thiophene scaffold linked to different electron-acceptor end groups, such as dicyanoindanone and 3-ethylrhodanine units, respectively. This strategic variation precisely controls the absorption properties, molecular dipole moments, energy levels, and binding energies, thus effectively mitigating intramolecular charge transfer effects beneficial for OSCs. In binary OSCs with CA-CO as the donor, the achieved power conversion efficiencies (PCEs) were 11.73% (SM-11) and 6.78% (SM-12), respectively. The broader absorption profile, higher exciton generation/dissociation efficiency, along with lower binding energy of SM-11 account for the performance enhancement. Furthermore, integrating SM-11 into a ternary blend with CA-CO:Y7 further enhanced the PCE to 15.58%, outpacing the binary reference CA-CO:Y7 device (12.17%). The enhanced PCEs stem from the alteration of end-group functionalization in the small molecules, which accelerates exciton dissociation and charge transfer in the ternary system, promoting favorable blend morphology and efficient guest-to-host energy transfer.

items.title: Thermosensitive Hydroxybutyl Polyvinyl Alcohol Hydrogel for Vaginal Delivery of Progesterone Microcrystals to Treat Endometrial Hyperplasia
items.abstract: Abstract Endometrial hyperplasia (EH), a common precursor lesion to endometrial carcinoma, represents a major gynecological challenge. Current noninvasive vaginal treatments are severely hampered by poor retention and inadequate mucosal adhesion. Herein, we developed a novel thermosensitive hydroxybutyl polyvinyl alcohol (HBPVA) hydrogel for efficient localized vaginal delivery of progesterone. By grafting hydrophobic hydroxybutyl groups onto the hydrophilic PVA backbone, the resulting HBPVA hydrogel exhibited good flowability at 4 °C and a rapid sol-gel transition at 37 °C. Progesterone microcrystals were directly incorporated into the HBPVA solution via simple physical mixing, yielding a stable formulation (Pro@HBPVA) without the need for organic solvents or purification. The thermosensitive hydrogel, once gelled at body temperature, leveraged its abundant surface hydroxyl groups to achieve superior mucoadhesion compared to commercial F127 hydrogel (mucosal adhesion duration &gt;10 times that of the F127 control). Ex vivo fluorescence imaging revealed that the fluorescein-labeled HBPVA hydrogel was retained in the vaginal tract 4-fold longer and at significantly higher levels than a fluorescein sodium solution. Furthermore, the HBPVA formulation enabled preferential uterine accumulation with prolonged therapeutic exposure (&gt;24 h). In an estrogen-induced EH rat model, Pro@HBPVA demonstrated superior therapeutic efficacy to intramuscular progesterone oil injection (positive control), effectively reducing uterine wet weight, restoring endometrial thickness and apoptosis balance, suppressing excessive endometrial angiogenesis and proliferation, and attenuating local inflammation to levels comparable to healthy controls. Collectively, with proven biocompatibility, this mucoadhesive platform offers an effective and noninvasive strategy for EH treatment.

items.title: Hybrid Membrane-Coated Nanoplatform Enables Pyroptosis-Driven Photothermal Immunotherapy via Synergistic STING/TLR4 Activation
items.abstract: Abstract The immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment (TME) remains a major barrier to effective cancer immunotherapy, largely due to deficient activation of innate immune pathways and insufficient immune cell infiltration. To address this issue, we developed a hybrid biomimetic nanoplatform (CL8-BO NPs + CLPS) that encapsulates a near-infrared photothermal agent (L8-BO) and the Toll-like receptor 4 (TLR4) agonist lipopolysaccharide, respectively, and is surface-functionalized with a mixed macrophage–red blood cell membrane, with the two components used in synergy. Upon 808 nm laser irradiation, L8-BO generated localized hyperthermia, inducing gasdermin D-dependent pyroptosis, which released cytosolic DNA and damage-associated molecular patterns to activate the stimulator of interferon genes (STING) pathway. Concurrently, released lipopolysaccharide engaged TLR4 signaling, potentiating innate immune activation. In a subcutaneous 4T1 breast carcinoma model, intratumoral administration of CL8-BO NPs followed by laser irradiation remodeled the immunosuppressive TME by promoting dendritic cell maturation, enhancing intratumoral CD8+ cytotoxic T lymphocyte infiltration by 5-fold, and suppressing regulatory T cells and myeloid-derived suppressor cells. The combination therapy inhibits tumor growth by over 90%. This nanoplatform provides a promising strategy for converting “cold” tumors into “hot” tumors through photothermal–triggered pyroptosis and synergistic STING/TLR4 activation in a localized delivery model.

items.title: Carbon–ITO Composite Electrodes with Silver Leaf Current Collectors for Efficient Perovskite Solar Cells
items.abstract: Abstract Developing vacuum-free and potentially scalable top electrodes is essential for the practical deployment of perovskite solar cells (PSCs). Here, a hybrid carbon-based composite electrode is developed by incorporating carbon black and colloidal indium tin oxide (ITO) nanoparticles into a commercial carbon paste, followed by lamination of a silver (Ag) leaf as a highly conductive current collector. The resulting carbon–ITO/Ag architecture exhibits substantially improved electrical properties, achieving a low sheet resistance of 0.11 Ω sq–1 and a conductivity enhanced by approximately three orders of magnitude relative to pristine carbon electrodes. Morphological analysis reveals that carbon black improves particle packing and film compactness, while ITO colloids promote the formation of additional conductive pathways within the carbon network. When integrated into ambient-processed PSCs, the optimized electrodes deliver improved charge collection and reduced resistive losses, yielding a champion power conversion efficiency of 19.64%. In addition, the optimized CCB-ITO/Ag electrode, which forms a denser carbon network and more conformal contact with the Ag leaf current collector, maintained approximately 90% of its initial efficiency, compared with ∼85% for C-ITO/Ag, after 2000 h (∼83 days) of aging under continuous dark storage at 25 °C and 2% RH. Improved performance retention demonstrates the beneficial effect of the hybrid carbon architecture on electrode stability while preserving efficient charge transport. This hybrid carbon-ITO/Ag strategy provides a practical, vacuum-free route toward conductivity-enhanced carbon electrodes for high-performance PSCs and offers a promising platform for potentially scalable device fabrication.

items.title: Deconstructing the Nanoscale Electromechanical Response of Mixed Conductors
items.abstract: Abstract Piezoresponse force microscopy (PFM) techniques, which probe nanoscale electromechanical coupling, are often difficult to interpret. For ferroelectric mixed conductors useful for computation elements, this becomes more difficult due to non-piezoelectric electromechanical effects. The measured PFM signal can have tip-local and nonlocal contributions associated with multiple coupling mechanisms, and it is often unclear what material property is truly being probed. Here, using antimony sulfide (Sb2S3) as a model system, an emerging phase change material for optical and electrical memory and computation elements, we show that the PFM signal can be separated into a fast, capacitive contribution, and a slow, ionic contribution whose time-domain characteristics match well with diffusion-controlled kinetics. This ionic contribution, rather than ferroelectric switching, leads to electromechanical hysteresis in Sb2S3, with no clearly measurable ferroelectric switching effects. Uniquely, electromechanical behavior has a very clear spatial contrast that is decoupled from surface topography, showing that the signal arises from surface charging that reflects bulk-like properties and allowing a self-consistent interpretation in terms of dielectric behavior. This protocol establishes a clear interpretation of a non-piezoelectric signal, often mischaracterized as an indication of the ferroelectric state. Additionally, because all electromechanical experiments show a strong, low-frequency electric relaxation in crystalline Sb2S3 while the response of glassy Sb2S3 is static, we conclude that the crystalline phase of Sb2S3 is a mixed conductor, while the amorphous phase remains strictly insulating.

items.title: Supramolecular Pulley Effect Enabling Highly Stretchable Transparent Electrodes
items.abstract: Abstract Silver nanowires (AgNWs) are promising materials for stretchable transparent electrodes (STEs) due to their high aspect ratio, excellent electrical conductivity, and optical transparency. However, the flexibility of AgNW-based STEs is often constrained by the significant modulus mismatch between the rigid AgNWs and soft polymer substrates. Herein, we introduce acrylated polyrotaxane (PRA) between the AgNW network and a polyurethane (PU) substrate, resulting in a highly stretchable and transparent electrode. The pulley effect of the acrylated polyrotaxane helps alleviate stress concentration at the AgNW–PU interface. Therefore, the network structure of AgNWs can remain relatively intact even under large tensile strains. The resulting composite electrode combines a transmittance of about 86.8%, a sheet resistance of 47 Ω·sq–1, and a stretchability of up to 130%. The as-prepared AgNWs/PRA/PU electrode demonstrates great potential for applications in stretchable electroluminescent devices and electrophysiological signal monitoring. This study offers a straightforward and effective strategy for developing high-performance stretchable electrodes, presenting a viable pathway for next-generation electronic devices.

items.title: Cu/Ce Bimetallic Porphyrin MOFs with Enhanced Charge Transfer for Efficient Photocatalytic–Photothermal Sterilization
items.abstract: Abstract A series of bimetallic CuxCey (x = 1–5, y = 10 – x) metal-organic frameworks (MOFs) were prepared via a solvothermal method. Results reveal that the coordination between Cu2+ and the central N atoms of the porphyrin ring is consistent with partial metallation of the porphyrin macrocycle and alters excited-state and charge-transfer behavior, which contributes to the enhanced photocatalytic bactericidal activity. The Cu/Ce bimetallic sites alter the excited-state and charge-transfer behavior of the framework, which may facilitate the generation of reactive oxygen species (ROS), including singlet oxygen (1O2), while the photothermal effect derived from TCPP ligands contributes to bacterial inactivation. Under visible light irradiation (0.2 W cm–2, λ ≥ 420 nm) for 15 min, the optimized Cu2Ce8 achieves a bactericidal rate of over 99.99% against Escherichia coli (E. coli), and the bactericidal rate remains above 90% after 4 recycling cycles.

items.title: Synergistic O2 Activation and H2O Dissociation Triggered by Spatially Proximal Frustrated Lewis Pairs on Hydroxylated Indium Oxide for Boosted Photocatalytic H2O2 Generation
items.abstract: Abstract Efficient activation of O2 and H2O at active sites is the core prerequisite for high-performance photocatalytic H2O2 generation, yet current photocatalytic systems are severely restricted by spatially separated sites-induced blocked proton transfer/intermediate coupling and competitive substrate activation among different active sites. Herein, frustrated Lewis pairs (FLPs) are rationally engineered on the hydroxylated indium oxide (In2O3–x(OH)y) surface, where spatially proximal Lewis acid (LA) and Lewis base (LB) sites are integrated to realize synergistic photocatalysis. The electron-deficient LA sites efficiently adsorb and activate O2 through a Pauling-type adsorption configuration. The proximal LA/LB sites cooperatively facilitate H2O adsorption and O–H bond cleavage. Following H2O dissociation, the resulting surface In–OH species can participate in a water-assisted proton exchange process, providing a plausible pathway for proton transfer to oxygen-derived intermediates. Through the spatially coordinated activation of O2 and H2O, the proximal LA/LB sites facilitate interfacial proton transfer and promote the coupling of O2 reduction intermediates with protonic species, thereby enhancing H2O2 formation. Benefiting from the aforementioned dual-site synergistic effect, the optimized In2O3–x(OH)y catalyst exhibits a photocatalytic H2O2 production rate in pure water that is nearly three-fold higher than those of control samples with sole LA or LB active sites. This work successfully extends the spatial synergistic mechanism of FLPs toward efficient photocatalytic H2O2 synthesis, which provides a feasible strategy and insights for the rational design of high-performance bifunctional photocatalysts.

items.title: High-Throughput Fabrication of Large-Area Optical Glass Microlens Arrays by Roll-to-Plate Hot Embossing
items.abstract: Abstract Microlens arrays (MLAs) play an essential role in advanced optical systems, especially in applications such as three-dimensional imaging and augmented reality. However, the mass production of large-area MLAs on optical glass substrates remains challenging due to limitations in replication area and manufacturing efficiency inherent in conventional plate-to-plate (P2P) hot embossing. To enable the fabrication of large-area optical glass MLAs with high efficiency and consistency, this study proposes a novel roll-to-plate (R2P) hot embossing technology designed to achieve high-throughput production while addressing critical challenges in microstructure replication, including embossing-induced surface defects, unsatisfactory forming accuracy, and excessive manufacturing costs for large-area optical microstructures. A combined computational and experimental approach was employed to systematically investigate the glass filling behavior during the R2P embossing process. The parametric effects on MLA filling uniformity were quantitatively evaluated through designed factorial experiments. Optimal processing parameters were subsequently identified, enabling the successful fabrication of glass MLAs with high precision and exceptional surface consistency. This study thus demonstrates R2P hot embossing as a promising and economically attractive solution for the fabrication of advanced glass-based optical systems.

items.title: Facet- and Size-Related Electrical Conductivity and Piezocatalytic Behaviors of Co3O4 Crystals from Lattice Deviation
items.abstract: Abstract Size-tunable Co3O4 cubes (136 and 276 nm), cuboctahedra (168 and 240 nm), and octahedra (180 and 258 nm) have been hydrothermally synthesized. Synchrotron X-ray diffraction (XRD) analysis suggests best fitting of peaks into bulk and surface layer lattice components for all the samples. Fast Fourier transform (FFT) processing of high-resolution transmission electron microscopy (HR-TEM) images shows a regular array of lattice points in the interior bulk but significant spot distortion in the surface layer. The surface lattice deviation patterns are distinct for different particle morphologies. Their band gaps can vary with particle size and shape. For the smaller crystals, an octahedron is electrically highly conductive, but a cube is nearly insulating from representative single-particle measurements. Cuboctahedra and octahedra also show higher piezoelectric responses than cubes do. Regardless of the particle shape, the smaller crystals are clearly more piezocatalytically effective at dye degradation than the larger ones. Active species generated in piezocatalysis have been identified. Lattice deviations from crystal shape control is a good way to enhance material properties.

items.title: Dual-Mode Memristors with Controlled Cluster Dynamics for High-Performance Neuromorphic Computing
items.abstract: Abstract In the process of realizing brain-like information processing based on artificial synapses, the conductive filament (CF) model has become an intensively studied topic. Its significant attraction stems from its ability to emulate the dynamic evolution of synaptic connection strengths in biological systems. However, owing to its inherent geometrical structural defects, traditional CF exhibits significant uncontrollability during its growth and dissolution processes, severely limiting the stability and accuracy of its synaptic function simulation. To address this limitation, a synaptic device was constructed in this study that features a dual-active-layer composed of polyvinylpyrrolidone (PVP): graphene-oxide quantum dots (GO QDs), and polyvinyl alcohol (PVA). The thin PVA active layer enables compliance-current-controlled regulation of dendritic conductive filaments, resulting in volatile switching at low compliance currents and nonvolatile switching at higher compliance currents, thereby enabling compliance-current-controlled dual-mode operation. Ag ions originating from the electrochemically active Ag electrode migrate into the active layer driven by the external electric field and are reduced in situ around the GO QDs in the PVP:GO QDs nanocomposite layer, forming uniformly distributed and controllable silver clusters (Ag-C), resulting in enhanced device stability and improved synaptic emulation capability. The proposed mechanism is consistent with the voltage-dependent SEM/EDS observations and previously reported charge-trapping characteristics of GO QD-containing materials. Experimental results confirmed that diverse synaptic behaviors can be realized in the device. Meanwhile, a neural-network simulation based on its synaptic characteristics demonstrated its excellent performance (94.0%) in learning and inference tasks. Such performance further highlights the potential of the device for constructing reliable neuromorphic computing architectures.

items.title: First Evidence and Role of γ -Fe2O3 Seeds in Low-Temperature-Processed Sn-Doped Hematite Photoanodes
items.abstract: Abstract Sn doping is an effective strategy to improve the photoelectrochemical response of hematite photoanodes, but its activation typically requires high-temperature treatments that can degrade conductive substrates and limit device integration. Considering photoelectrochemical water splitting as a case study, this work investigates the mechanism of photoelectrochemical activation of Sn-doped hematite-based photoanodes by oxidative annealing of thin metallic Fe–Sn alloy films at a low temperature.
