X-ray absorption spectroscopy, Raman spectroscopy, grazing-incidence X-ray diffraction, and electron paramagnetic resonance reveal that while hematite is the main crystalline phase, poorly ordered γ-Fe2O3 seeds selectively form in Sn-containing films annealed at 450 °C and progressively transform into Sn-doped α-Fe2O3 at higher annealing temperatures. Under solar illumination in 1 M KOH, photoanodes annealed at 450 °C exhibit photocurrent density (≈480 μA/cm2) and onset potential (≈0.9 V vs RHE) comparable to those obtained after annealing at a higher temperature (750 °C). Sn K-edge X-ray absorption spectroscopy identifies Sn4+ in local Sn–Fe coordination environments consistent with incorporation into the hematite lattice. The γ-Fe2O3 domains may act as transient Sn reservoirs, accommodating Sn beyond the hematite solubility limit and promoting the formation of well-ordered, photoactive Sn-doped α-Fe2O3 nanocrystals, while limiting SnO2 segregation at an Sn/(Fe + Sn) atomic ratio of approximately 3 at %. Control films deposited under an oxygen atmosphere contain a lower γ-Fe2O3 fraction and show poor activity, indicating that low-temperature activation arises not from Sn addition alone but requires oxidation-driven restructuring of the metallic Fe–Sn precursor. The γ-Fe2O3 seeds represent structural fingerprints of a synthesis pathway that enables efficient Sn incorporation and low-thermal-budget fabrication of hematite photoanodes for solar water splitting.

items.title: Electronic Structure Modulation and Electrochemically Induced Reconstruction of Ni-Doped Fe Oxyhydroxides for Overall Water Splitting
items.abstract: Abstract Structurally analogous metal oxyhydroxides such as NiFeOOH and CoFeOOH lie at the pinnacle of the oxygen evolution reaction (OER) volcano plot for alkaline water electrolysis. However, stabilization of a single FeOOH phase is inherently challenging because of the small thermodynamic energy differences among FeOOH polymorphs and the phase selection being governed by crystallization kinetics. Herein, we report a heterovalent Ni doping strategy to stabilize β-FeOOH structural morphology and enhance the local electric field, thereby tuning its electronic conductivity to promote OER activity. Moreover, Ni doping alters the interfacial structure in an optimal OH– ionic environment by lowering the reaction energy barriers at Fe active sites with a significantly lower adsorption free energy of 3.56 eV for the *OOH intermediate. Under cathodic polarization, NFO24/CFC undergoes in situ reconstruction, transforming bulky α-Fe2O3 NCs into hydroxylated rich FeOOH-like thin nanosheets. This structural evolution generates abundant active sites and facilitates charge-transfer kinetics, thereby accounting for its superior hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) activity. Consequently, NFO6/CFC delivers a high anodic current density with an OER overpotential of 355 mV, while NFO24/CFC exhibits superior HER performance with an overpotential of 272 mV at a current density of 10 mA cm–2 in alkaline media. Furthermore, the two-electrode assembly using NFO6/CFC∥NFO24/CFC operates at a cell voltage of 1.87 V to drive overall water splitting and demonstrates long-term stability of 24 h at 10 mA cm–2 in alkaline conditions.

items.title: Biochar-Augmented Semi-interpenetrating Network Hydrogel for Multifunctional Applications
items.abstract: Abstract Developing multifunctional integrated composites is crucial for next-generation flexible wearable devices. In this study, a multifunctional composite hydrogel was fabricated by incorporating biochar (BC) and polypyrrole (PPy) based on sodium alginate (SA) and polyacrylamide (PAM) to simultaneously enhance mechanical performance, deformation sensing capability, and electromagnetic interference (EMI) shielding effectiveness. The results demonstrated that the synergistic effect of BC and PPy improved the strength and toughness of the hydrogel, which was attributed to the strong interfacial interactions between the fillers and the polymer network, including hydrogen bonding, π–π stacking, and electrostatic interactions. Also, the stability of electrical signal response and attenuation of electromagnetic waves of the composite hydrogel were enhanced by the three-dimensional conductive network formed by BC and PPy. Among all composite hydrogels, the composite hydrogel containing 30 wt % BC exhibited the optimal overall performance with a tensile strength of 0.20 MPa, a tensile modulus of 0.056 MPa, an elongation at break of 874.26%, a tensile toughness of 0.58 MJ·m–3, and an EMI shielding effectiveness of 29.50 dB. The composite hydrogel developed in this study integrates structural stability, strain-sensing capability, and EMI shielding performance, providing a strategy for the design of multifunctional flexible wearable devices.

items.title: Stomata-Inspired Composite Films for All-Climate Dynamic Thermal Management in High-Humidity Environments
items.abstract: Abstract Passive daytime radiative cooling faces two fatal challenges in high-humidity environments: radiative transmission attenuation in the atmospheric window in summer and overcooling caused by static high emissivity in winter. Existing technologies can only solve one of these problems and cannot achieve all-climate adaptation. Inspired by the dynamic transpiration regulation mechanism of plant stomata, we have fabricated a humidity-responsive cellulose-hydrogel composite film, which autonomously adjusts the pore size of the porous structure via moisture adsorption–desorption to selectively modulate near-infrared reflectance. This film achieves a solar reflectance of 92.0% and an infrared emissivity of 96.1%. At high temperatures, it triggers a synergistic evaporative–radiative cooling effect, realizing a 15.6 °C sub-ambient temperature drop and effectively offsetting the cooling performance degradation caused by high humidity; at low temperatures, the material suppresses its radiative cooling power by reducing its solar reflectance. With excellent mechanical properties and weather resistance, it provides a novel design paradigm for all-climate intelligent thermal management in high-humidity regions.

items.title: Nonreciprocal Transport in Superconducting Diodes via Tailored Antidot Geometries
items.abstract: Abstract The superconducting diode effect (SDE) offers a transformative path toward dissipationless nonreciprocal electronics, yet a unified framework for controlling its microscopic origins remains elusive. Here, we demonstrate precision engineering of the SDE in niobium films by tailoring the geometry of asymmetric micrometer-sized antidots. By decoupling transport responses under in-plane and out-of-plane magnetic fields, we identify a dual-mechanism regime: low-field rectification is governed by surface-barrier asymmetry (edge flux pinning), while high-field performance is driven by the intrinsic geometric landscape of the antidots (bulk flux pinning). Supported by time-dependent Ginzburg–Landau (TDGL) simulations and a robust analytical model, we establish a predictive design principle that links pinning topology to diode efficiency. These results provide a scalable strategy for developing tunable superconducting rectifiers, offering a critical building block for next-generation cryogenic logic and quantum information processing.

items.title: Surface-Active Hydrogen Coverage Engineering Enables Selective Electrochemical Hydrogenation of Nitrobenzene over a CoFe Catalyst
items.abstract: Abstract Electrocatalytic hydrogenation of nitroarenes to aromatic amines is significant, but selectivity control remains challenging. Herein, a series of CoFe non-precious catalysts are prepared on carbon cloth via a facile constant-current deposition method. The optimal CoFe catalyst features a 3D honeycomb-like porous structure with a high electrochemically active surface area and enhanced mass transfer, delivering the highest cathodic current density and the most positive onset potential. At –1.2 V vs Hg/HgO, the nitrobenzene (NB) conversion approaches 100%, with the aniline (AN) yield and selectivity both exceeding 95%, demonstrating outstanding NB electroreduction (NBER) performance. In-situ Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR) confirms the reaction pathway NB → NSB → PHA → AN. Theoretical calculations reveal that CoFe optimizes the electronic structure to modulate the surface coverage of active hydrogen (*H) from water dissociation, thereby promoting the hydrogenation reaction while efficiently suppressing the competing hydrogen evolution reaction. Coupling this cathode with 5-hydroxymethylfurfural (HMF) oxidation to produce 2,5-furandicarboxylic acid (FDCA) gives a higher energy utilization efficiency and economic returns than the conventional system that coupled with the oxygen evolution reaction. This work demonstrates a promising strategy for upgrading both nitroaromatic and biomass-derived substrates via green electrosynthesis, offering a viable route toward the energy-efficient and economically attractive co-production of fine chemicals.

items.title: Silver-Cluster and Polyoxometalate-Incorporated Metal-Organic Frameworks for Electrochemical Nitrite Sensing and Capacitive Energy Storage
items.abstract: Abstract In this work, four new polyoxometalate-based metal-organic frameworks (POMOFs), namely [Ag10HCl2(dtb)8(PMo12O40)3]·2H2O (JOU-42-Mo), [Ag10HCl2(dtb)8(PW12O40)3]·2H2O (JOU-42-W), [Ag4Cl(dtb)2PMo12O40]·2H2O (JOU-43-Mo), and [Ag4(OH)(H2O)2(dtb)2PW12O40] (JOU-43-W) (dtb = 4,4′-(1,4-phenylene)bis(4H-1,2,4-triazole)), constructed from silver clusters and Keggin-type polyoxometalates (POMs), were synthesized via a solvothermal strategy. Single-crystal X-ray diffraction analyses reveal that these compounds consist of two structural families. The JOU-42 series features a three-dimensional (3D) fcu-type framework assembled from decanuclear Ag clusters, generating tetrahedral and octahedral cages for the confinement of POM guests, whereas the JOU-43 series adopts a 2D + 2D → 3D interpenetrated architecture containing one-dimensional channels for POM encapsulation. The combination of redox-active POM clusters and accessible Ag sites endows these POMOFs with enhanced electrochemical sensing performance toward nitrite (NO2–). Among them, JOU-42-Mo exhibits the best NO2– sensing performance, achieving a wide linear detection range of 20–30,000 μmol L–1 and a low detection limit of 3.88 μmol L–1, together with excellent selectivity, reproducibility, and stability. Furthermore, the POMOF electrodes display promising capacitive energy storage characteristics, demonstrating the multifunctional potential of Ag-cluster-based POMOFs.

items.title: From Hydrogels to Cosmetic Contact Media: Honeycomb-Structured Reusable Textile Electrodes for Wearable TENS
items.abstract: Abstract Textile-integrated electrodes are promising for wearable transcutaneous electrical nerve stimulation (TENS), but their practical use is limited by high dry skin-electrode impedance, mechanical instability, and insufficient durability after washing and deformation. Here, we report reusable screen-printed textile electrodes based on thermoplastic polyurethane/carbon composites and a stretchable honeycomb architecture for low-impedance skin-interfacing TENS applications. Three carbon skin-contact layers: graphite (G), carbon black (CB), and graphite/carbon black hybrid (G:CB) were integrated with a silver current-delivery layer and transferred onto an elastic polyamide/elastane textile. The honeycomb design significantly improved electromechanical stability, reducing strain-induced resistance changes by approximately one order of magnitude under tensile loading. Under 1000 cycles of 20% strain, CB-based electrodes showed the highest stability, with a final relative resistance increase of 52.1% and an absolute resistance below 0.5 Ω. After 10 washing cycles, resistance increased but remained partially recoverable by post-treatment heat pressing, indicating reconfiguration of the conductive network within the thermoplastic matrix. All carbon-based layers were noncytotoxic toward L929 fibroblasts in an indirect MTT assay. Scanning electron microscopy (SEM) and contact profilometry revealed filler-dependent surface morphologies, with surface roughness decreasing from CB and reaching the lowest values for G. In vivo skin-electrode impedance measurements showed that dry interfaces were strongly influenced by surface contact conditions, whereas hydrogel, glycerin-based cream, and oil-in-water (O/W) emulsion substantially reduced impedance across 0.1–200 Hz. Importantly, low impedance was retained after washing and cyclic deformation when a contact medium was used. These results highlight a synergistic design strategy combining material composition, stretchable architecture, and interface engineering to enable robust, reusable textile electrodes for wearable electrotherapy. Notably, the demonstrated compatibility with simple, nonspecialized contact media suggests that common cosmetic formulations can effectively serve as impedance-reducing interfaces, opening a practical pathway toward accessible, user-friendly TENS systems without reliance on dedicated hydrogel electrodes.

items.title: The Impact of Oxide Transport Layers and Active Layer Composition on the Energy Band Alignment of the Frontier Orbitals in Non-Fullerene Acceptor Organic Solar Cells
items.abstract: Abstract The PM6:Y7 blend is a leading system for non-fullerene acceptor organic photovoltaics (OPV), achieving power conversion efficiencies (PCEs) above 16%. In bulk heterojunction architectures, it is typically combined with transition-metal-oxide transport/extraction layers to enable efficient energy-level alignment and charge transport toward the electrodes. However, accurate determination of the frontier orbital band alignment across the device interfaces remains challenging and is the subject of ongoing debate. This work aims to map the energetic landscape within an inverted OPV device architecture by investigating how variations in the PM6:Y7 donor-to-acceptor mass ratio (1:1, 1:2, and 2:1) affect device performance and assessing the role of the oxide transport/extraction layers (MoO3 and ZnO). By combining valence band photoemission and X-ray absorption spectra relative to the Fermi level, we map the frontier orbital alignment between the blend active layer and the charge transport/extraction layers. Moreover, by exploiting the element selectivity of X-ray absorption spectroscopy, we are able to follow the evolution of the Y7 acceptor LUMO level in the blends with different compositions. We observe a nonlinear behavior in the acceptor LUMO level with the blend composition and find that the 1:1 blend exhibits a relative maximum, reflecting a maximized effective donor–acceptor dipole interaction. Combining this trend with the optimal 1:1–1:2 composition window, identified from band alignment analysis, suggests that stronger molecular dipole interactions in the PM6:Y7 1:1 blend can promote a favorable electronic structure for efficient charge extraction and reduced recombination effects. These findings are consistent with the PCE trend resulting from our device measurements, providing a general framework for correlating frontier-orbital alignment with device performance and guiding the design and optimization of OPV architectures beyond the specific system investigated here.

items.title: Unraveling Structure and Spectroscopic Signatures of Pt/γ-Al2O3 via an Artificial Intelligence-Enabled Simulation Framework
items.abstract: Abstract Supported subnanometer clusters have attracted significant attention in catalysis. Yet, it is challenging to resolve their structural evolution, particularly in the presence of adsorbates. Here, we present an artificial intelligence (AI)-enabled simulation framework that integrates machine learning force field (MLFF) construction, molecular dynamics (MD) simulations, and ML-assisted infrared (IR) and X-ray absorption near-edge structure (XANES) spectra analysis to investigate the restructuring of supported subnanometer clusters. Using Pt10/γ-Al2O3(110) as a model system, we explored the CO-induced restructuring of the cluster under different conditions. The simultaneous machine learning (ML)-spectra elucidate a strong interplay among adsorbate coverage, cluster restructuring, and cluster-support interaction. This work sheds light on the complex dynamics of supported subnanometer clusters that is extendible to other systems.

items.title: Issue Editorial Masthead
Issue Publication Information
Entropy-Driven Phase Transition in Polymer-Grafted Nanoparticle Blend Films and Associated Gloss and Dielectric Breakdown Strength
items.abstract: Abstract While polymer-grafted nanoparticle (PGNP) mixtures having brush layers with different chemistry undergo phase separation as in ordinary homopolymer blends, knowledge of the underlying phase behavior of such “hybrid” blends currently does not exist theoretically or even empirically. Entropic effects in PGNPs arising from the chain-end tethering constraints of the brush layers reduce the number of configurational states of the polymer segments, compared to their corresponding free chain homopolymer blend, greatly reducing the gain in entropic free energy of mixing (–TΔSmix). However, the enthalpic driving force for phase separation for χ(Τ) &gt; 0, ΔHmix ∼ χ(Τ), is also lowered by reduced unfavorable segmental brush/brush physical contacts, a situation that makes estimation of the overall free energy of mixing, ΔG = ΔHmix – TΔSmix, difficult. The phase stability of miscible polymer blends is normally dominated by a large enthalpic (relative to entropic) contribution to ΔG, so that observations of competitive entropy/enthalpy effects on blend phase behavior are limited to systems having relatively small ΔHmix, i.e., 0 &lt; χ(Τ) Ν &lt; 2. With this general thermodynamic relationship in view, we designed a binary PGNP blend system comprising end-grafted polymer brush layers on silica nanoparticles having nearly balanced entropic/enthalpic interactions. Specifically, we synthesized poly(methyl methacrylate-silica) (PMMA-SiO2) and poly(styrene-acrylonitrile (AN-14%)-silica (PSAN-SiO2) PGNPs and cast blend films that exhibited a reversible and compositionally tunable U-shaped lower critical solution temperature (LCST) phase behavior. In contrast, the corresponding free chain PMMA/PSAN homopolymer blend films under the same conditions were fully miscible. As in a phase-separating homopolymer blend, phase separation in the PGNP blend film leads to spontaneous (spinodal) surface pattern formation, wherein the ratio of the in-plane to out-of-plane phase separation scale, λ/h, is constant. Furthermore, a shift in miscibility based on an asymmetry in the grafted chain length ratio of PGNPs can be compensated by an equivalent asymmetry in the PGNP blend ratio. Practical properties relevant to colloidal paints and coatings, including gloss (sheen) and dielectric breakdown strength (EBD) for capacitive energy storage, are measured. Single-phase PGNPs show high gloss (sheen) and high EBD, while the phase-separated PGNP blend films have low gloss and low EBD, effects that could be exploited for the design of numerous optical and flexible solid-state electrical power devices.

items.title: Achieving Rapid, Nonbuffered Nerve Agent Hydrolysis with Alkali-Loaded MOFs: Insights from KWW Kinetic Modeling
items.abstract: Abstract Nerve agents, a class of extremely toxic chemical warfare agents, pose a severe threat, making their rapid degradation an urgent necessity. Zirconium-based metal-organic frameworks are promising catalysts for hydrolyzing organophosphorus nerve agents, but their practical application is severely hampered by the reliance on external alkaline buffers to regenerate active sites. Furthermore, conventional kinetic models are inadequate for fully describing the time-dependent catalytic behavior. Herein, we report a general strategy to overcome these limitations by constructing a built-in alkaline microenvironment within nanoflower-like zirconium-based metal-organic frameworks (denoted as MOFF/Mg-n) through loading magnesium methoxide. In this dual-component system, the Zr6 nodes function as catalytic centers while the loaded Mg(OMe)2 serves as a consumable alkaline reservoir. Under the tested conditions (Zr6:DMNP = 1:2), the optimized catalyst MOFF/Mg-2 exhibits a significantly shortened hydrolysis half-life of only 2.8 min toward nerve-agent simulant dimethyl 4-nitrophenyl phosphate (DMNP) under nonbuffered conditions, while MOFF/Mg-4 can hydrolyze DMNP almost completely within 20 min. To gain deeper insight into the kinetic behavior of this complex system, we successfully applied the Kohlrausch-Williams-Watts (KWW) stretched-exponential model, which provided an excellent fit of the experimental data and yielded two key parameters of the characteristic rate constant and the stretching exponent, for quantitative performance evaluation. This work demonstrates that constructing a built-in alkaline microenvironment is a feasible and powerful strategy for achieving efficient, nonbuffered nerve agent degradation, paving a new route for practical decontamination in real-world scenarios. Moreover, the successful application of the KWW model provides a robust empirical kinetic framework for designing and evaluating high-performance decontamination catalysts for complex surface reactions. The system operates as a reusable MOF scaffold with a replenishable alkaline reservoir, enabling sustained performance through simple re-impregnation of Mg (OMe)2.

items.title: Dynamic Covalent Nanoparticle Network Enabling Shrinkage-Resistant and Closed-Loop Recyclable Microcellular Ethylene Copolymer Foams
items.abstract: Abstract Thermoplastic elastomer foams have attracted considerable attention owing to their lightweight nature, flexibility, and processability. However, their widespread application is limited by unstable cellular structures, severe post-foaming shrinkage, and poor recyclability. In this work, epoxy-functionalized ethylene copolymer (EGMA) was employed as the matrix, and a dynamic covalent network containing B–O bonds was constructed through the ring-opening reaction between 3-aminophenylboronic acid (APBA) and epoxy groups. Hydroxyl-rich SiO2 nanoparticles were further introduced to establish a dynamic nanoparticle network, yielding a thermoplastic elastomer foam with enhanced foamability, dimensional stability, and recyclability. The synergistic effect of the dynamic covalent network and SiO2 nanoparticles significantly improved the modulus, creep resistance, and melt stability of the elastomer. Under the optimized foaming condition of 80 °C and 20 MPa, a microcellular foam with an average cell size of 8.94 μm and a cell density of 3.73 × 1010 cell/cm3 was obtained. Compared with E-A and E-Si foams, the E-A-Si foam exhibited outstanding dimensional stability, retaining 94.09% of its original volume after 24 h. The dynamic B–O bonds enabled moderate topological rearrangement during foaming, promoting uniform nucleation and suppressing cell rupture. After foaming, SiO2 nanoparticles participated in a dynamic nanoparticle network through B–O–Si linkages, which effectively restricted stress relaxation and chain retraction, thereby stabilizing the cellular structure and reducing post-foaming shrinkage. Moreover, the E-A-Si foam maintained an intact cellular morphology and excellent elastic recovery after two closed-loop refoaming cycles. This work provides a new strategy for developing thermoplastic elastomer foams with high dimensional stability and closed-loop recyclability.

items.title: Design Strategy of T 1-Weighted MRI Contrast Agents for High Relaxivity Based on a Self-Folding Macromolecular Architecture
items.abstract: Abstract Conjugation of gadolinium chelates to macromolecular nanoplatforms has emerged as a promising strategy for developing high-performance contrast agents for T1-weighted MRI. However, conventional macromolecular gadolinium-based contrast agents (GBCAs) typically achieve limited enhancement of longitudinal relaxivity merely by tethering Gd chelates to macromolecular platforms to slow their global rotational motion. Here, we present a rational design strategy based on a self-folded macromolecular contrast agent (SMCA), formed through intramolecular self-folding of a single amphiphilic polymer chain incorporating a minimized amount of Gd chelate. The SMCA forms a nanosized micellar structure with a hydrophobic core and a hydration shell, while positioning the Gd chelates at the core–shell interface. Experimental results suggest that the rigid architecture of SMCA may contribute to relatively slow global motion, while the PEG shell may restrict segmental dynamics, potentially contributing to the enhanced longitudinal relaxivity. Systematic structural modulation, including control of the degree of polymerization and hydrophilic chain length, enables enhanced relaxivity while ensuring renal clearance. The optimized Gd-DOTA-conjugated SMCA exhibits a longitudinal relaxivity of 31.5 mM–1 s–1 at 0.47 T, representing an 8.5-fold increase over clinically used Gd-DOTA. In a proof-of-concept MRI study, SMCA enhances strong and long-lasting vascular contrast even at one-eighth of the Gd-DOTA dose, yielding a 2.7-fold higher peak signal intensity while maintaining favorable clearance. This work would contribute to establishing mechanistic guidance for designing next-generation macromolecular GBCAs with high relaxivity and ensured safety.

items.title: Aggregation-Induced Photodegradable and Hydrolyzable Photosensitizer for Cu64 Positron Emission Tomography/Photoacoustic Imaging-Guided Phototherapy Nanoplatforms with Controllable Performance
items.abstract: Abstract Radio imaging and optical imaging offer complementary advantages for biomedical diagnosis. However, the photosensitizers used in imaging must be degraded to reduce phototoxicity during phototherapy. Herein, we report a novel dicyanomethylene-based near-infrared photosensitizer (PS) that self-degrades via multiple pathways, including hydrolysis, aggregation-induced photodegradation, and oxidation by hypochlorous acid. To meet diverse theranostic requirements, the degradation behavior and performance of the PS were systematically regulated through co-assembly with three carriers. First, co-assembly with DSPE-PEG2000 produced a nanosystem that is stable to laser irradiation and water during multimodal diagnosis, and labeling with 64Cu enabled dual-mode photoacoustic and radio signal imaging. Second, co-assembly with PLGA-PEG5000 reduced the photodegradation rate by enabling complete degradation through hydrolysis, thereby facilitating deep-tumor phototherapy. Third, complexation with cucurbit[8]uril (CB[8]) selectively inhibited the hydrolytic properties of the photosensitizer, thereby reducing its phototoxicity through photodegradation and oxidative degradation pathways when superficial tumors are subjected to phototherapy. The phototherapeutic efficacy of the designed nanosystems was validated in a subcutaneous 4T1 tumor-bearing mouse model. The results demonstrated effective tumor inhibition with minimal phototoxicity, confirming the suitability of the developed system for safe phototherapy. Overall, this work presents a rational strategy for tuning photosensitizer degradation pathways to balance imaging performance, therapeutic efficacy, and biosafety, providing a versatile platform for multimodal theranostic applications.

items.title: Extending Self-Assembled Monolayer Interface Engineering to Carbon-Based Perovskite Solar Cells
items.abstract: Abstract Printable carbon-based perovskite solar cells (C-PSCs) offer a low-cost and durable photovoltaic platform but remain limited by poor interfacial charge extraction and substantial nonradiative recombination at the perovskite/carbon junction suppressing open-circuit voltage (VOC). While phosphonic acid–based self-assembled monolayers (SAMs) are widely used in p–i–n devices, their application in mesoscopic carbon architectures remains unexplored. Here, we report a simple post-treatment based on the molecular self-assembled monolayer MeO-2PACz to address these bottlenecks in triple-mesoscopic TiO2/ZrO2/carbon architectures. MeO-2PACz treatment modulates the perovskite/carbon interface, improving energy-level alignment and passivating undercoordinated Pb2+ sites. Transient photocurrent and transient photovoltage analyses show accelerated charge extraction and extended recombination lifetimes. Consequently, the SAM-treated devices achieve enhanced VOC (0.90 V), fill factor (70.7%), and a champion power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 14.7%, along with suppressed hysteresis and improved stability, retaining 98% of initial PCE after 2400 h under controlled humidity without encapsulation.

items.title: Hierarchical MCTS-Guided Bayesian Optimization for Co-designing Formulation and Processing of Thermosetting Polymers with Balanced Performance
items.abstract: Abstract Optimizing the properties of thermosetting polymers presents an inherent challenge due to the high-dimensional formulation-processing parameter space and the trade-offs between thermomechanical properties. In this contribution, we propose a hierarchical Monte Carlo tree search (MCTS)-guided Bayesian optimization (BO) framework to enable the simultaneous design of both the composition and curing protocols of epoxy resins as a major class of thermosetting polymers. A sigmoid-based weighting strategy is introduced to encode application-driven performance thresholds into the objective function, guiding the optimization toward coordinated multi-property improvement. With only 30 experiments across four iterative rounds, the framework optimizes both the formulation and curing protocols to yield a performance-enhanced epoxy resin that simultaneously meets all four target thresholds. This balanced performance cannot be achieved by any of the initial samples, an equal-weight baseline, or commercial and literature-reported systems. Furthermore, interpretable machine learning analysis combined with targeted experimental validation quantitatively resolves the relative importance of formulation and processing parameters, indicating that composition variables dominate overall property trends while their synergistic interactions produce non-linear effects on glass transition temperature. The findings demonstrate that the hierarchical MCTS-guided BO framework offers an efficient strategy for navigating complex formulation-processing spaces, and the interpretable analysis provides a quantitative basis for understanding structure–property relationships in thermosetting polymers.

items.title: Deep-Blue Hot Exciton Emitters Approaching the BT.2020 Standard: Spiro-Fluoreno-Imidazole Acceptors with Twisted D–π–A Architectures
items.abstract: Abstract Achieving deep-blue electroluminescence with high efficiency and color purity that meets the BT.2020 standard remains a major challenge for organic light-emitting diodes. Here, we report two D–π–A emitters, SFIA-1 and SFIA-2, based on a spiro-fluorene-imidazole acceptor (A) and a 10H-spiro(acridine-9,9′-fluorene) donor (D). By strategically introducing a para-phenylene bridge, the molecules adopt highly twisted conformations. Experimental and theoretical analyses further reveal CT-dominated, hybridized local-excited and charge-transfer states. Both emitters exhibit wide optical band gaps (&gt;3.3 eV). A negligible singlet–triplet energy gap of 0.01 eV, combined with a moderate spin–orbit coupling, activates an efficient high-lying reverse intersystem crossing “hot exciton” channel. As a result, the SFIA-1-doped device achieves a maximum external quantum efficiency (EQE) of 7.53% with an electroluminescence peak at 425 nm, while SFIA-2 delivers an electroluminescence peak at 420 nm with Commission Internationale de l'Éclairage coordinates of (0.159, 0.043), closely aligned with the BT.2020 blue light standard. Furthermore, the non-doped devices based on SFIA-1 and SFIA-2 exhibit maximum EQEs of 6.29 and 10.89%, respectively. Therefore, SFIA-2 was utilized as a host for PO-01-TB, tCzphB-Ph, and Ir(mphmq)2(tmd) emitters, yielding maximum EQEs of 30.47, 24.09, and 15.57%, respectively. These results demonstrate a molecular design strategy for ultra-deep-blue hot-exciton materials and high-performance hosts that reconciles the trade-off between exciton utilization efficiency and color purity.

items.title: Surface-Localized Hydrogen Manganese Oxide Polyethersulfone Membranes for Selective Lithium Capture under Recirculating Flow
items.abstract: Abstract Selective lithium recovery from multication aqueous streams requires translating the high selectivity of lithium-ion-sieve powders into macroscopic materials without compromising the accessibility of their ion-exchange sites. Here, hydrogen manganese oxide (HMO) was localized at the surface of a commercial polyethersulfone (PES) membrane through an adhesive polydopamine (PDA) interlayer, providing direct access to the active phase while preserving the porous membrane architecture. Microscopy and surface analyses confirmed the formation of an HMO-rich interfacial layer, and the resulting PES–PDA–HMO membrane exhibited a Langmuir maximum uptake of 35.6 ± 0.7 mg Li g–1 HMO, corresponding to approximately 91% of the experimentally measured capacity of the free HMO powder (39.1 ± 0.2 mg g–1). Under closed-loop recirculating flow, Li+ uptake approached equilibrium within 6 h and was accompanied by proton release, while X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy directly confirmed Li incorporation into the HMO-containing surface. Lithium removal remained similar across recirculation flow rates of 10–150 mL min–1 under the closed-loop configuration, whereas increasing the HMO surface loading from 5.8 to 8.7 mg cm–2 increased Li+ removal from 68 ± 2 to 99 ± 3% at an initial concentration of 50 ppm. After five adsorption–regeneration cycles using lactic acid at pH 2.1, the membrane retained 90 and 85% of its initial removal performance at 25 and 250 ppm Li+, respectively, with no detectable Mn release. Importantly, selectivity was preserved under severe multication competition: in a solution containing 50 ppm Li+ and 250 ppm each of Co2+, Ni2+, and Mn2+, Li+ removal remained 65 ± 3%, whereas removal of the competing divalent ions remained near 1%. These results demonstrate that interfacial localization of HMO can preserve its ion-exchange functionality after macroscopic immobilization while enabling selective, regenerable lithium capture under dynamic aqueous conditions.

items.title: Coral-Inspired Thermodynamically Stable-Phase Core-Shell Strategy Enables α-Al2O3@SiO2 Aerogels with Thermal Stability up to 1500 °C and Superhydrophobicity
items.abstract: Abstract Alumina aerogels have attracted great interest for extreme thermal insulation. However, traditional alumina aerogels inevitably undergo severe structural degradation above 1000 °C due to the metastable-to-α phase transformation, which fundamentally limits their ultrahigh-temperature applications. In nature, red coral constructs its robust porous skeleton directly from calcite, the thermodynamically stable polymorph of CaCO3, thereby achieving exceptional long-term structural durability. Inspired by this “thermodynamically stable-phase construction” wisdom, we herein propose a thermodynamically stable-phase core-shell (TSC) strategy that employs thermodynamically stable α-Al2O3 nanoparticles as building blocks. The in situ sol-gel growth of a methyl-containing SiO2 shell on the nanoparticle surfaces directly yields three-dimensional continuous α-Al2O3@SiO2 core-shell aerogels (SAAs). The resulting SAAs exhibit outstanding ultrahigh-temperature thermal stability, retaining a non-collapsed porous skeleton with a high specific surface area retention of 23.6% after calcination at 1500 °C in air for 2 h. They also display excellent superhydrophobicity, with a water contact angle as high as 163.0° and a rolling angle as low as 2.9°. Furthermore, the SAAs deliver remarkable thermal insulation performance, exhibiting a room-temperature thermal conductivity of only 0.0394 W·m−1·K−1. When exposed to a 1300 °C butane torch flame for 120 s, a merely 4-mm-thick SAAs plate registers a cold-side temperature rise of only 141 °C. Molecular dynamics simulations reveal that the SiO2 shell acts as an efficient physical and diffusion barrier, effectively suppressing sintering neck formation and atomic diffusion between particles, thereby preserving the nanostructure at extreme temperatures. This work not only provides a coral-inspired stable-phase construction pathway toward lightweight ceramic aerogels for extreme environments but also establishes a general approach for constructing sintering-resistant nanostructures based on thermodynamically stable-phase nanoparticles via core-shell engineering.

items.title: Crosslinking Temperature-Regulated Topological Confinement of Amorphous PEO Electrolytes for High-Performance Sodium-Metal Batteries
items.abstract: Abstract Poly(ethylene oxide) (PEO) is a promising solid-state polymer electrolyte (SPE), but its room-temperature crystallization leads to low ionic conductivity, limiting its application. Semi-interpenetrating networks (semi-IPNs) represent an effective strategy for suppressing PEO crystallization. Previous studies have overlooked the influence of crosslinking temperature on the network topology. Here, we report a crosslinking temperature-regulated topological confinement of amorphous PEO electrolyte achieved by initiating the photopolymerization of ethoxylated trimethylolpropane triacrylate (ETPTA) at 80 °C. The resulting homogeneous network effectively confines the amorphous phase of PEO while retaining local freedom for Na+ transport. When the mass ratio of PEO to ETPTA is 60:40 (P-E40H), the material exhibits optimal comprehensive electrochemical performance, demonstrating a high room-temperature ionic conductivity of 0.173 mS cm–1, a high Na+ transference number of 0.59, high voltage stability of 4.72 V, and an elongation at break of 160.05%. Molecular dynamics simulations indicate that the uniform network allows Na+ to adopt a solvation structure dominated purely by PEO. The capacity retention ratios of Na3V2(PO4)3|P-E40H|Na cell are 92.9% (1 C, 400 cycles) and exhibits a specific capacity of 64.05 mAh g–1 at 5 C. This work demonstrates that crosslinking temperature is an effective processing parameter for tuning the network topology of semi-IPN electrolytes, offering a simple and efficient structural regulation strategy for high-performance solid-state sodium-metal batteries.

items.title: Directional Control of Nonthermal Photocurrents Driven by Optical Spin Angular Momentum
items.abstract: Abstract Controlling the flow of electricity in metallic circuits with light is a key goal for future optoelectronics. In this work, we demonstrate all-optical generation and directional control of non-thermal drift photocurrents driven by the transfer of spin optical angular momentum to the electron gas of a plasmonic gold wire. We attribute this phenomenon to the Inverse Faraday Effect and show that the current's direction can be precisely reversed at a subwavelength scale by tailoring the incident light's polarization or laser beam position. A bespoke polarization modulation technique is employed to unambiguously separate ultrafast drift currents from the ubiquitous photothermal background. We further reveal a collaborative mechanism where macroscopic thermal gradients, acting as a driving force, are used to extract and remotely detect the locally-generated nanoscale photocurrents. This robust control and detection scheme paves the way for reconfigurable, all-optical nanocircuitry capable of ultrafast on-chip processing.

items.title: Switchable Anomalous Valley Hall Effect in Bilayer Mg(FeN)2
items.abstract: Abstract Achieving the controllable anomalous valley Hall effect (AVHE) is crucial for valleytronics but remains challenging for bilayer altermagnetic systems. Here, bilayer Mg(FeN)2 is proposed as a stacking-dependent platform for a switchable AVHE. The AA stacking of bilayer Mg(FeN)2 exhibits altermagnetism due to the broken TP(t) symmetry, while the AB stacking is a conventional antiferromagnet protected by TP(t) symmetry. Interestingly, interlayer sliding between AA-1 and AA-2 configurations reverses the out-of-plane ferroelectric polarization and consequently switches the layer-dependent valley polarization. Reversing the magnetic configuration changes the spin occupation of valleys, leading to an opposite Hall voltage signal. Thus, a valleytronic device is constructed for the nonvolatile control of the AVHE. For AB-0 configuration, an external electric field can break layer equivalence and induce layer-dependent valley polarization. Switching the electric field direction or magnetic configuration enables the polarity reversal of the Hall response. This work provides a feasible route for electrically and magnetically controllable AVHE in altermagnets.

items.title: Thermally Transformed ZnC8H4O4 Nanocrystals for Enhanced Sodium-Ion Storage
items.abstract: Abstract Metal-organic terephthalates composed of earth-abundant elements are promising low-cost and structurally tuneable anodes for sodium-ion batteries, yet their electrochemical behavior, particularly in newly developed compounds, remains insufficiently understood. We report monoclinic nanocrystalline ZnC8H4O4 (ZnTP-2), prepared through the controlled thermal transformation of a hydrated zinc terephthalate precursor, ZnC8H6O5 (ZnTP-1), containing residual terephthalic acid (ZnTP-1@TPA). This transformation involves TPA sublimation and framework dehydration, producing ZnTP-2 with fine crystals of approximately 50–150 nm, increased surface area, and a higher concentration of oxygen-related defect sites compared with ZnTP-1@TPA. ZnTP-2 delivers a reversible Na-ion storage capacity of 222.7 mAh g–1 after 80 cycles at 50 mA g–1, approaching its theoretical capacity and indicating highly efficient utilization of the terephthalate redox framework. It also retains 110 mAh g–1 after 500 cycles at 1000 mA g–1, with a relatively low charge-transfer resistance of 11.5 Ω, demonstrating improved electrochemical stability and rate performance compared with conventional metal-organic terephthalate anodes. Electrochemical kinetic analyses reveal Na-ion diffusion coefficients between 10–14 and 10–12 cm2 s–1, with the differences discussed in terms of apparent, Warburg-related and bulk/chemical diffusion processes. UV–vis analysis reveals a lower optical band gap for ZnTP-2 (2.74 eV) than for ZnTP-1@TPA (3.36 eV), with DFT calculations on idealized molecular models of hydrated and dehydrated zinc terephthalates supporting a similar trend. Full-cell examination provides proof of concept for its applicability.

items.title: Multifunctional Integration in Aerogels: Recent Progress and Prospects in Simultaneous Thermal Insulation and Microwave Absorption
items.abstract: Abstract The rapid development of science has led to an increasing demand for lightweight and high-performance composite materials. Aiming at the dual requirements of thermal insulation and microwave absorption in the field of aerospace, this paper first clarifies the mechanism of heat insulation and microwave absorption. Secondly, five representative bifunctional aerogel systems are introduced. This paper mainly focuses on the recent research progress of the thermal insulation and microwave absorption bifunctional composite aerogels. Finally, challenges and future perspectives of the current thermal insulation and microwave absorption composite integrated aerogels are discussed.

items.title: Oxygen-Vacancy-Engineered Robust Ferroelectricity in Epitaxial-Strain-Free SrTiO3 Films
items.abstract: Abstract SrTiO3 (STO), a typical quantum paraelectric material, has been extensively investigated for the stabilization of ferroelectric order through external perturbations. However, conventional approaches typically rely on epitaxial strain or external field excitation, limiting their suitability for epitaxial-strain-free and low-stress device architectures. Here, we demonstrate an epitaxial-strain-independent route to robust ferroelectricity in STO enabled by interfacial oxygen-vacancy engineering. By introducing a La0.5Sr0.5MnO3 (LSMO) bottom electrode with strong oxygen affinity, interfacial oxygen redistribution is promoted during epitaxial growth, resulting in significant oxygen-vacancy accumulation in the adjacent STO layer. The engineered oxygen vacancies drive local symmetry breaking and stabilize polar nanoregions in fully relaxed STO epitaxial films. Consequently, STO grown on the LSMO buffer layer exhibits robust room-temperature ferroelectricity with a remanent polarization of 14 μC/cm2, achieved without conventional epitaxial strain engineering. These findings establish interfacial oxygen-vacancy engineering as a viable strategy for inducing ferroelectricity in STO-based heterostructures and provide a possible route for designing emergent functionalities.

items.title: Green Manufacturing of High-Performance Multilayered Boron Nitride Composites via Modulus-Contrast-Assisted Stack Pressing
items.abstract: Abstract Controlling the in-plane orientation of two-dimensional nanosheets during repeated forming remains challenging because deformation can become nonuniform through the film thickness. Here, alternating 60 and 80 wt % boron nitride nanosheet/thermoplastic polyurethane (BNNS/TPU) layers were used to introduce a moderate modulus contrast during water-based stack pressing and were compared with homogeneous 70 wt % films having the same nominal average filler content. Repeated pressing increased BNNS alignment in both architectures, while the binary film exhibited a slightly narrower SEM-derived angular distribution after six total pressing operations. The binary film reached an in-plane thermal conductivity of 17.85 W m–1·K–1, a through-plane thermal conductivity of 0.22 W m–1 K–1, a tensile strength of 17.48 MPa, and a thermal anisotropy ratio of approximately 81. Under the present point-heating configuration, its hotspot temperature was 5.7 °C lower than that of the unitary film at 60 s. Idealized linear-elastic finite-element analysis qualitatively illustrates modulus-dependent stress and strain partitioning but does not model interfacial damage or nanosheet rotation. Fabrication of 400 × 400 mm films further demonstrates large-area batch-processing feasibility.

items.title: T7 Ribonucleic Acid Polymerase-Triggered CRISPR/Cas13a and Branched HCR Cascade Amplification with Machine Learning for SERS Detection of Cardiac Troponin I
items.abstract: Abstract Cardiac troponin I (cTnI) serves as a critical biomarker of acute myocardial infarction (AMI). Its serum level is extremely sparse, and the clinical cut-off value reaches merely 0.2 ng mL–1. This poses a significant challenge, requiring highly sensitive analytical techniques for reliable quantification. This study proposes a powerful surface-enhanced Raman scattering (SERS) sensing strategy integrating multistage signal amplification and machine learning to enhance detection performance. By combining T7 RNA polymerase, CRISPR/Cas13a, branched hybridization chain reaction (bHCR), and Fe3O4@COF@Ag magnetic substrate, the strategy constructs an efficient “recognition–amplification–signal output” closed loop for cTnI detection. Experimental results demonstrate that the platform has a linear calibration range of 0.1–104 pg/mL for cTnI, with an estimated limit of detection (LOD) of 0.1 pg/mL, holding promise for future AMI-related biomarker analysis. It also shows excellent selectivity against common serum interferents, good reproducibility (intra-batch RSD = 2.87%, inter-batch RSD = 7.96%), and reliable recovery (100.1%–110%) in human serum samples. Based on Raman signals, the k-nearest neighbor (kNN) classifier demonstrated high accuracy in classifying cTnI concentration levels, while the artificial neural network (ANN) model exhibited strong quantitative predictive performance with an R2 of 0.9997. This platform overcomes the limitations of conventional cTnI assays in terms of sensitivity and signal amplification efficiency, providing a promising analytical platform for future AMI-related biomarker studies.

items.title: Strain-Resilient Integrated Conductive Elastomer with Stable Conductivity via Grafting and Blending for Flexible Sensing and Self-Adhesive Dry Electrocardiogram Monitoring Electrode
items.abstract: Abstract Integrated conductive elastomers have attracted significant attention for their potential in flexible wearable electronics, electrocardiogram (ECG) monitoring, and other fields due to their unique combination of elasticity and electrical functionality. Conventional flexible conductors often suffer from environmental instability, such as solvent leakage in gels, or conductivity degradation under mechanical deformation in filler-based elastomers. To realize practical applications in flexible electronics, conductive elastomers must possess stable conductivity under stretching, as well as superior deformability and resilience. Moreover, addressing the trade-off between electrical performance and mechanical properties of conductive elastomers is still challenging. In this study, the solid polymer electrolyte (SPE) polyethylene glycol (PEG) was incorporated into a butyl acrylate (BA) elastomer via grafting and blending to fabricate integrated conductive elastomers. Furthermore, based on the multi-bond network (MBN) concept, 1-vinylimidazole (VI) was copolymerized into the butyl acrylate elastomer backbone to form Zn2+-VI coordination, which further enhanced the mechanical properties of the conductive elastomer. The PEGMA chains grafted onto the BA ensure excellent compatibility between P(BA-co-VI)-g-PEGMA/Zn2+ and the blended free PEG chains, thereby inhibiting phase separation and facilitating Li+ transport. Consequently, a transparent integrated conductive elastomer was obtained with a stable conductivity as high as 1.60 × 10–2 S m–1, which is comparable to that of a pure PEG-Li+ system. Its conductivity can remain near 1.5 × 10–2 S m–1 even under an extremely large strain of 1000%. The resulting elastomer exhibited an extremely high elongation at break exceeding 1800% and outstanding resilience, showing a residual strain of only 130% after five cycles at 1000% strain and rapid recovery within 30 min. Furthermore, the conductive elastomer demonstrated remarkable stability and sensitivity in strain sensing, while also serving as a dry electrode for high-quality ECG signal collection, highlighting its considerable potential for flexible sensing technologies and health monitoring.

items.title: Ultrathin and Anti-friction Janus Bioelectrodes for Imperceptible Electrochemical Sweat Analysis
items.abstract: Abstract Skin-like electrochemical sweat biosensors hold great promise for non-invasive and unobtrusive health monitoring, yet their real-world application is severely hindered by poor durability under repeated skin friction, stretching, and sweat erosion. Here, we report a versatile Janus bioelectrode design that simultaneously achieves ultralow thickness, high stretchability, and exceptional anti-friction performance for reliable sweat sensing. The Janus architecture prepared by sequential screen printing and thermal annealing, provides strong interfacial adhesion with strain-insensitive conductivity. The resulting ultrathin electrodes (∼20 µm) survive over 1600 s of Radio Corporation of America (RCA) abrasion and 500% tensile strain without significant degradation in conductivity or electrochemical stability. We further functionalized the Janus bioelectrodes into a durable three-electrode system for uric acid (UA) sensing. As a proof of concept, we attached the tattoo-like sensor onto a human forearm to enable real-time, wireless monitoring of sweat UA during both aerobic and anaerobic exercise. The sensor printed directly onto a T-shirt survived prolonged use and daily laundry cycles. This work establishes a general strategy for creating ultrathin, durable electrochemical biosensors that resist motion artifacts and friction, paving the way for robust and imperceptible electrochemical sweat analysis.

items.title: Biomimetic Cell-Membrane-Guided Precision Delivery of Gold Nanoclusters for Targeted Alleviation in Acute Lung Injury
items.abstract: Abstract Acute lung injury (ALI) and its severe sequela, acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS), remain life-threatening conditions with high morbidity and mortality. However, effective targeted therapeutics for ALI are still lacking. Biocompatible gold nanoclusters (AuNCs) with intrinsic immunomodulatory activity have shown a promising application in ALI alleviation, but their clinical potential is constrained by insufficient accumulation at pulmonary lesion sites following systemic administration. To overcome this critical barrier, we developed two biomimetic delivery platforms by encapsulating TAT peptide-protected gold nanoclusters (TAT-AuNCs; designated as TA) with natural cell membranes that derived from either lung bronchial epithelial cells (TA@CMVs-MLE) or M1-polarized macrophage (TA@CMVs-M1M), respectively. Both nanoplatforms displayed excellent biosafety profiles and achieved substantially enhanced pulmonary accumulation and better therapeutic outcomes than free TA in lipopolysaccharide (LPS)-induced ALI mice, after intravenous administration. Nevertheless, TA@CMVs-M1M achieved markedly superior therapeutic outcomes than TA@CMVs-MLE, although their efficiency in delivering TA to the lungs was comparable. Mechanistic studies indicated that TA@CMVs-M1M can be selectively taken up by inflammatory macrophages and has an ability to neutralize proinflammatory cytokines, which is not possessed by TA@CMVs-MLE. Therefore, TA@CMVs-M1M exhibited a superior attenuation on inflammatory lung injury. These results demonstrated that the M1 macrophage membrane not only enables AuNCs to achieve precise targeting of pneumonia lesions but also possesses inherent inflammatory cytokine neutralization capabilities, which can synergize with the transcriptional inhibitory activity of AuNCs on inflammatory cytokines to enhance the targeted alleviating of ALI. Thus, this work establishes a translatable nanotheranostic strategy that merges natural immune-cell tropism with intrinsic AuNCs pharmacology for next-generation ALI management.

items.title: Molecular Architecture of Covalent Adaptable Network Additives Governs Their Integration into Melt-Processed Polyamide 6
items.abstract: Abstract Covalent adaptable networks (CANs) are predominantly developed as bulk thermoset matrices, while their use as dynamically crosslinked functional phases within melt-processed thermoplastics remains largely unexplored. Here, phosphorus-containing CANs (P-CANs) with systematically varied molecular architectures are employed as macromolecular additives in polyamide 6 (PA6) to establish relationships between network structure, dynamic response, dispersion, retention, and melt processability. Transitioning from a rigid small-molecule-derived network to flexible polyphosphonate architectures shifted the glass-transition temperature from 160 to –5 °C and markedly altered stress relaxation and deformation under processing conditions. These architecture-dependent differences translated directly into thermoplastic integration: the rigid P-CAN formed larger phosphorus-rich domains and exhibited greater phosphorus retention, whereas the most flexible network appeared more uniformly dispersed, lowered processing resistance, and promoted shear-thinning behavior. The resulting balance between dispersion and retention enabled kilogram-scale twin-screw compounding and continuous film extrusion of homogeneous PA6 composites containing 5–10 wt % flexible P-CAN. Despite low final phosphorus contents (∼0.25–0.60 wt %), incorporation of the P-CANs increased limiting oxygen index, promoted char formation, and reduced microscale heat release. These results demonstrate that CAN molecular architecture provides a tunable design parameter for controlling the integration and functional performance of dynamically crosslinked polymeric additives in melt-processed thermoplastics.

items.title: High-Extinction-Coefficient Donor Engineering Enables High-Performance Photothermal Cocrystals
items.abstract: Abstract Organic charge-transfer cocrystals have emerged as promising candidates for photothermal conversion, yet current design strategies predominantly focus on intermolecular charge-transfer interactions or nonradiative decay pathways, with less attention paid to the fundamental prerequisite of absorbance. Here, we propose a high-extinction-coefficient donor engineering strategy to boost photothermal conversion. A charge-transfer cocrystal (BNQ) was constructed from DtBuCzB—a donor with a high molar extinction coefficient (5.81 × 104 L mol–1 cm–1)—and the classical acceptor TCNQ. The BNQ cocrystal exhibits a well-ordered 2:1 alternating columnar packing structure with close π–π interactions and C–H···N hydrogen bonds, leading to a narrow optical bandgap of 1.04 eV and broad-spectrum absorption extending to 1198 nm. Under 808 nm laser irradiation, BNQ achieves an outstanding photothermal conversion efficiency of 95.1% and an ultrafast heating rate (130 °C within 10 s), substantially outperforming previously reported TCNQ-based cocrystals. As a practical demonstration, BNQ-incorporated polyurethane foam delivers an average solar-driven water evaporation rate of 1.84 ± 0.03 kg m–2 h–1 under 1-sun illumination with excellent operational stability. This work establishes donor extinction coefficient engineering as a simple yet powerful design strategy for developing next-generation photothermal cocrystals and provides a design parameter for the rational screening of component monomers.

items.title: High- k Gate Dielectrics for Organic Field-Effect Transistors: Interfacial Engineering, Performance Optimization, and Scalable Flexible Electronics
items.abstract: Abstract Organic field-effect transistors (OFETs) are promising platforms for flexible, wearable, biointegrated, and large-area electronics owing to their mechanical compliance, solution processability, low-temperature fabrication, and molecular tunability. However, their practical application requires low-voltage operation, low power consumption, high operational stability, and scalable manufacturing, which are strongly influenced by the gate dielectric and its interface with the organic semiconductor. High-k gate dielectrics can increase gate capacitance and enhance electrostatic control, enabling low-voltage operation. However, a higher dielectric constant does not necessarily lead to better device performance, as strong polarization, surface polarity, interfacial trapping, dipolardisorder, remote phonon scattering, leakage, ion migration, and dielectric–semiconductor incompatibility can impair charge transport and device reliability. This Review presents a performance-oriented and interface-centered overview of high-k gate dielectrics for OFETs. We first classify high-k dielectric systems into inorganic oxides, molecularly engineered polymers, organic–inorganic hybrids and composites, and all-organic composite/multilayer structures, highlighting their polarization mechanisms, advantages, limitations, and structure–property relationships. We then discuss how dielectric properties and interfaces affect carrier mobility, threshold voltage, switching characteristics, charge injection, leakage current, hysteresis, and operational stability. Particular attention is given to interface engineering strategies, including surface modification, buffer layers, multilayer architectures, molecular design, composite construction, and defect/passivation control. We further discuss long-term reliability under electrical, thermal, mechanical, and environmental stresses, as well as emerging dielectric systems, low-temperature and scalable fabrication, large-area uniformity, process integration, and commercialization challenges. Finally, we summarize key design considerations for balancing high capacitance, low leakage, interfacial compatibility, mechanical robustness, environmental stability, and scalable processability. By integrating dielectric design, interface engineering, device physics, reliability, and manufacturing, this Review provides guidelines for developing low-voltage, stable, and scalable OFETs for next-generation flexible electronics.

items.title: Three-Dimensional-Printed Lithium-Doped Conductive Carbon@Hydroxyapatite Scaffolds for Coordinated Neurovascular-Osseous Regeneration
items.abstract: Abstract The repair of critical-sized bone defects remains a formidable clinical challenge, where coordinated neurovascular reconstruction is important for effective bone regeneration. Accordingly, this study aimed to develop a three-dimensional (3D)-printed hydroxyapatite (HAp) scaffold integrating a polydopamine (PDA)-derived conductive carbon interface with Li+ release, and to evaluate its neural-, vascular-, and osteogenic-related effects in vitro and its bone-regenerative performance in vivo. A lithium-containing, hydrothermally carbonized HAp scaffold (HAp@C/Li) was fabricated through 3D printing, Li+-assisted dopamine coating, and hydrothermal carbonization. Material characterization confirmed a PDA-derived carbon coating with measurable local surface conductivity and Li+ release characterized by an early release phase followed by a gradual plateau. In vitro experimental results revealed that HAp@C/Li possessed excellent cytocompatibility. It effectively promoted neurite outgrowth of dorsal root ganglion (DRG) neurons, migration and tube formation of human umbilical vein endothelial cells (HUVECs), as well as osteogenic differentiation of bone marrow mesenchymal stem cells (BMSCs). In vivo evaluation in a rat femoral condyle defect model showed favorable bone repair, collagen deposition, vascular remodeling, and neural-associated tissue responses, with significantly higher BMD at 8 weeks, whereas BV/TV did not differ significantly from that of the HAp group. Collectively, these results indicate that the HAp@C/Li scaffold provides a promising therapeutic strategy for the clinical repair of critical-sized bone defects.

items.title: In Situ Activated Bi2WO6 Nanosheets with Fast-Response and Self-Bleaching Electrochromism for Automotive Antiglare Rearview Mirrors
items.abstract: Abstract Trailing vehicle headlight glare critically endangers nighttime driving safety, with electrochromic devices (ECDs) being the most promising solution. Nevertheless, commercial organic electrochromic materials face high cost and irreversible degradation, whereas inorganic alternatives exhibit slow response and severe memory effect, severely restricting their application in antiglare rearview mirrors. Herein, we report the electrochromic behavior of thin bismuth tungstate (T-BWO) nanosheets synthesized via a facile hydrothermal method. A unique in situ activation process is discovered, accompanied by (19.7 ± 1.8)% leaching of surface Bi atoms and a transient dark transition state, which endows the activated T-BWO with exceptional electrochromic performance: an ultralow working voltage window of –0.6/0.3 V, ultrafast coloration/bleaching times of (0.81 ± 0.06)/(0.55 ± 0.04) s, a high coloration efficiency of (148.3 ± 7.8) cm2 C–1, and reasonably fast self-bleaching under open-circuit conditions. The assembled T-BWO-based self-bleaching ECD delivers a moderate optical modulation (ΔR) of (37.8 ± 1.7)% and excellent cycling stability (86% performance retention after 900 cycles). This work not only introduces a novel high-performance inorganic electrochromic material but also provides a new design paradigm for functional ECDs toward practical automotive antiglare applications.

items.title: Bamboo-Inspired Homogeneous Porous Aerogel via Gas Foaming Assisted by Freeze-Drying for High-Sensitivity Flexible Pressure Sensors
items.abstract: Abstract Flexible piezoresistive sensors are pivotal in personalized healthcare. However, simultaneously achieving high sensitivity and a broad linear range remains a formidable challenge owing to rapid structural densification of porous materials. Inspired by the multiscale composite structure of bamboo, this study addresses the existing challenge by proposing a novel MXene aerogel sensor, reinforced by compounding cellulose nanofiber (CNF) and bamboo cellulose. By leveraging a uniform conductive network constructed on CNF (simulating bamboo parenchyma cells to disperse the vascular bundles) and the supporting effect of the bamboo cellulose skeleton (mimicking vascular bundles to provide support), premature collapse is effectively resisted. Moreover, inspired by the hollow cell cavity structure of bamboo, a stable porous architecture is constructed via gas foaming and freeze-drying, enabling it to effectively reconcile the inherent trade-off between sensitivity and the detection range. The sensor exhibits a high sensitivity of 148.29 kPa–1 (0–15 kPa) and a wide effective working range extending up to 100 kPa. This superior electromechanical performance enables the precise detection of full-spectrum physiological signals ranging from subtle pulse waveforms to large-scale joint movements and facilitates assistive rehabilitation for post-stroke finger therapy via human–computer interaction. Augmented by a support vector machine algorithm, the sensor has a wireless sleep monitoring capability and achieves a high classification accuracy of 96.5% in identifying distinct breathing states. The proposed sensor demonstrates significant application potential in next-generation intelligent home health management systems.

items.title: Surface and Electronic-Structure Regulation of NiCrPt-LDH for Ampere-Level Methanol-Assisted Hydrogen Production in Alkaline Seawater
items.abstract: Abstract Substituting the anodic oxygen evolution reaction (OER) with the methanol oxidation reaction (MOR) provides an energy-saving route for alkaline seawater electrolysis, but it demands bifunctional electrodes that efficiently facilitate both anodic MOR and cathodic hydrogen evolution reactions (HER) in chloride-containing alkaline media. This work reports a surface and electronic-structure regulation strategy for a low-Pt (0.86 wt %) NiCrPt-LDH electrode constructed on nickel foam via a single-step hydrothermal route. The NiCrPt-LDH electrode integrates an open nanosheet framework, a defect-enriched metal–oxygen surface environment, and a super-hydrophilic/-aerophobic interface, which requires only 74, 146, and 228 mV to deliver 100, 500, and 1000 mA cm–2 for HER, respectively, with 1380 h of stability at 500 mA cm–2. Its Pt-mass-normalized HER activity is much higher than that of commercial Pt/C. For MOR in methanol-containing alkaline seawater, NiCrPt-LDH reaches 100 mA cm–2 under an applied potential of 1.401 V vs RHE. The NiCrPt-LDH (+) || NiCrPt-LDH (–) electrolyzer outputs 100 mA cm–2 at an operating voltage of 1.477 V, underscoring the potential of low-platinum, surface-engineered bifunctional LDH electrodes for methanol-assisted hydrogen production in alkaline seawater electrolysis.

items.title: Dual-Microstructure Configuration Design Enabling Highly Sensitive Biotemplated Flexible Capacitive Pressure Sensors
items.abstract: Abstract Flexible capacitive pressure sensors (FCPSs) that resolve subtle pressure are central to soft robotics and human health monitoring. Their sensitivity is affected by microstructures incorporated at the interface between the electrode and dielectric layers, but fabricating fine artificial microstructures typically requires costly techniques. Biological templates offer a cost-effective way to form these microstructures, yet biotemplated FCPSs have remained limited in sensitivity. Efforts to improve sensitivity have predominantly focused on microstructure geometries, whereas the microstructure configuration in the sensor has not been well-studied. Here, we establish design insights for microstructure configurations through simplified computational analysis, revealing that amplifying the effective interelectrode distance variation rate and effective permittivity variation rate within the structured region is the key to enhancing overall sensitivity. Following this insight, we propose a dual-microstructure configuration that increases the air fraction within the structured region, leading to the amplified effective permittivity variation rate. Both computational and experimental assessments demonstrate that the dual-microstructure configuration outperforms conventional ones in sensitivity, with the fabricated sensor achieving the highest sensitivity of 4.3 kPa–1 among all the reported biotemplated FCPSs using the same dielectric materials (Table S1), along with a fast response/recovery time of 46/20 ms, a low detection limit of 1.2 Pa, and stable operation over 7500 cycles. These performance attributes enable the sensor for applications in robotic hand tactile sensing for soft objects and real-time physiological signal monitoring. Consequently, the proposed dual-microstructure configuration offers a generalizable pathway to enhance the sensitivity of biotemplated FCPSs, promoting the development of high-performance, cost-effective flexible pressure sensors.

items.title: Synergistic Coordination Regulation and Nanofiller-Guided Ion Transport in a Polyacrylamide Gel Electrolyte for Highly Reversible Aqueous Zn Metal Anodes
items.abstract: Abstract Despite their safety and cost advantages, aqueous zinc-ion batteries remain limited by the instability of Zn metal anodes, including nonuniform deposition, dendrite growth, and parasitic reactions. A PAM/CMC-Na/CNTs (PCC) hydrogel electrolyte is constructed by incorporating sodium carboxymethyl cellulose (CMC-Na) and carbon nanotubes (CNTs) into a polyacrylamide (PAM) matrix. The –COO– and –OH groups of CMC-Na regulate the local coordination environment of Zn2+ and suppress water-related side reactions, while CNTs reinforce the gel network and improve interfacial contact. PCC exhibits an ionic conductivity of 24.16 mS cm–1 and an apparent Zn2+ transference number of 0.791. These transport characteristics, together with interfacial analyses, are consistent with more uniform Zn deposition. Zn//Zn symmetric cells cycle stably for over 2300 h at 1 mA cm–2 with an areal capacity of 1 mAh cm–2 and for approximately 550 h at 5 mA cm–2 with a capacity of 5 mAh cm–2. Zn//Cu cells achieve an average Coulombic efficiency of 99.94%, while Zn//MnO2 full cells retain 81.64% capacity after 700 cycles at 1 A g–1. A high-loading Zn//MnO2 pouch cell further demonstrates favorable energy-storage performance. This work presents a strategy for designing hydrogel electrolytes that integrate coordination regulation, homogenized ion transport, and mechanical robustness.

items.title: Correction to “ZnBr2-Assisted Br-Rich Regulation of Blue-Emitting CsPbBr3 Nanoplatelets Synthesized at Low Temperature”
An Organic–Inorganic Hybrid Memristor with Trap-Assisted Hopping for Synaptic Plasticity and Artificial Nociceptor
items.abstract: Abstract Neuromorphic hardware demands artificial synaptic devices that mimic biological synapses. Achieving multifunctional emulation of synaptic plasticity and nociceptive behavior in a single, highly stable, low-power device remains a major challenge. In this report, zinc oxide nanoparticles (ZnONP) are synthesized via a surfactant-assisted sol–gel method. These are incorporated into an organic small-molecule matrix of 6,13-bis(triisopropylsilylethynyl)pentacene (TP) to fabricate a solution-processed organic–inorganic hybrid memristor. The as-fabricated hybrid memristor mimicked artificial synaptic behavior at a low operating voltage (&lt;±1 V) while demonstrating high stability with retention exceeding 105 s in ambient atmosphere. The TP/ZnONP-based memristor has illustrated both short-term and long-term synaptic plasticity, facilitating the exemplification of learning and memory functions of biological synapses. The memristor has been found to exhibit pain-perception-related nociceptive behavior, including protective responses to excessive stimulation and self-recovery, closely resembling that of biological nociceptors. The device exhibits neurapraxia-like responses with a recovery time of only 40 s. The experimentally obtained synaptic characteristics are further employed in a device-aware fully connected artificial neural network, yielding a handwritten digit recognition accuracy of 97.9%. Various investigations on the dynamics of charge transport have revealed trap-assisted hopping through transient localization, which is induced by shallow and deep traps. The integration of artificial nociception and pattern recognition in a highly stable low-power synaptic device demonstrates the potential of the hybrid memristor for multifunctional neuromorphic hardware.

items.title: Biomimetic Liquid Diodes Across Materials and Scales for Directional Liquid Transfer
items.abstract: Abstract The last decade has witnessed remarkable advancements in liquid diode, evolving from fundamental research to cutting-edge applications such as microfluidics, thermal management, and wearable electronics. However, how material characteristics and structural scales mediate liquid transport on liquid diodes has yet to be fully clarified to date. In this study, we develop a Crassula muscosa inspired liquid diode (CMLD) with superior material adaptability and structural scale adaptability spanning three orders of magnitude. Such a liquid diode endows a cross-material, and cross-scale unidirectional liquid transfer from microscale to macroscale. The mechanisms underlying the role of the wettability, viscosity and structure scale in regulating the liquid transfer kinetics including transfer distance, transfer velocity and liquid rectification, are clearly demonstrated. By combining experimental observation, numerical simulation, and building a theoretical retention force model, the liquid transfer and pinning mechanisms governed by asymmetric reentrant structures are systematically elucidated, which enables superior robustness for unidirectional liquid transfer of continuous flows with various flow rates. These results provide a robust framework for coupling material characteristics and structural scales to achieve controllable unidirectional liquid transfer, laying a solid foundation for the practical implementation of liquid diode-based technologies.

items.title: Magnetic Fe/Cu Metal–Organic Frameworks-Derived Trilayer Cathode for Enhanced Enrofloxacin Degradation in Heterogeneous Electro-Fenton via Synergistic Radical and Nonradical Pathways
items.abstract: Abstract Heterogeneous electro-Fenton (HEF) technology represents a promising eco-friendly strategy for wastewater remediation. However, sluggish Fe(III)/Fe(II) cycling and reliance on a single hydroxyl radical (•OH) pathway limit its overall catalytic efficiency and oxidant utilization. Herein, a bifunctional trilayer cathode (Fe8Cu2@C-GF/ACF) was fabricated by integrating activated carbon fiber (ACF) with a magnetic Fe/Cu metal–organic frameworks-derived layer grown on graphite felt. This architecture spatially couples H2O2 electrogeneration with immediate activation, maximizing the effective utilization of generated oxidants. Furthermore, Cu incorporation thermodynamically accelerates Fe(III)/Fe(II) cycling. The bimetallic synergy facilitates the simultaneous generation of radical (•OH) and nonradical (1O2) species. Quenching and EPR analyses confirmed these dual pathways collectively accelerate enrofloxacin (ENRO) degradation. The system achieves excellent mineralization across a broad initial pH range (3.0 to 9.0). Crucially, effective operation at neutral pH eliminates the need for chemical adjustment. Specifically, treating 100 mg L−1 ENRO at initial pH 7.0 and 18 mA cm−2 yielded a 75.6% mineralization degree. Degradation intermediates were elucidated via DFT calculations and UPLC-QqQ-MS analysis. Finally, the cathode exhibits high stability and low metal leaching. Its intrinsic magnetic recoverability prevents secondary solid waste and promotes practical material reuse for sustainable water treatment.

items.title: Dynamic Energy-Dissipating Interface Design Reconciles Thermal Performance with Interfacial Reliability
items.abstract: Abstract Highly filled thermal interface materials (TIMs) are essential for reliable heat dissipation in high-power electronics, yet restricted polymer chain mobility and reduced interfacial conformability make it difficult to achieve high thermal conductivity, strong adhesion, and crack-growth resistance simultaneously. We propose a dynamic energy-dissipating interface (DEDI) strategy that coordinates favorable interfacial affinity, stable chemical anchoring, and dynamic bulk energy dissipation to improve interfacial stability and crack resistance in highly filled TIMs. γ-Methacryloxypropyl trimethoxysilane (γ-MPS) provides stable chemical anchoring at the substrate interface, while urethane-associated polar interactions contribute to favorable interfacial affinity. Reversible disulfide and hydrogen-bond interactions within the bulk network promote deformation accommodation and mechanical energy dissipation. Surface-modified Al2O3/ZnO hybrid fillers form a multiscale network that provides efficient heat-transfer pathways. The resulting PSM-60-1.2 exhibits a thermal conductivity of 3.88 W·m−1·K−1, an adhesion strength of 4.25 MPa, and an adhesion energy of 3080.04 J·m−2. Combined experimental and finite-element analyses support coordinated interfacial stabilization, bulk energy dissipation, and enhanced thermomechanical deformation accommodation. After 100 thermal shock cycles between −40 and 150 °C, PSM-60-1.2 shows a 6.0 °C increase in maximum steady-state temperature, compared with 16.2 °C for the commercial thermally conductive adhesive, with less interfacial cracking and low-viscosity liquid infiltration. The DEDI design offers a molecular strategy for combining high thermal conductivity, high adhesion energy, and long-term thermomechanical reliability in highly filled TIMs.

items.title: Promoting Glycine Electrosynthesis from Nitrate and Oxalic Acid over Co–Cu Dual-Site Metal–Organic Frameworks
items.abstract: Abstract Electrochemical coreduction of nitrate (NO3–) and oxalic acid to glycine (ENOG) provides a sustainable alternative to conventional glycine production but remains limited by sluggish reactant activation, inefficient C–N coupling, and competing reaction pathways. Herein, a dual-site metal–organic framework, CoTAPc-BPDA-Cu, is developed as an efficient and robust cathode catalyst for ENOG. Operando spectroscopic measurements and theoretical calculations reveal the cooperative effect of Cu–Co dual sites in promoting OA-to-*C2H2O3 conversion, *NO3 reduction to *NH2OH, *C2H2O3-*NH2OH coupling to *C2H3NO3, and subsequent *C2H3NO3 hydrogenation for selective glycine formation.
