Moreover, by integrating cathodic ENOG over the CoTAPc-BPDA-Cu catalyst with an anodic glycerol oxidation over the PbO2 catalyst in a two-electrode electrolyzer, we achieve a glycine Faradaic efficiency of 78.3% and a glycine yield rate of 629.3 mmol h−1 g−1, while enabling the gram-scale production of high-purity glycine.

items.title: 3D Printed Sandpile-Shaped Photothermal Evaporator Based on Thiol-Ene Click Chemistry for Efficient Water Evaporation
items.abstract: Abstract The interface evaporation technology driven by solar energy has received widespread attention due to its advantages of being clean, pollution-free, and low in energy consumption. However, the cumbersome preparation process of existing high-efficiency evaporators hinders their large-scale promotion and application. Furthermore, we find that the inclined slope of the sandpile has the geometric condition of “forced reflection,” and the incident light can form reciprocating reflection between adjacent sandpiles, greatly improving the light capture efficiency and providing a structural basis for achieving efficient evaporation. Inspired by this, we construct a sandpile-shaped photothermal evaporator with different array densities by digital light processing (DLP) 3D printing technology with thiol-ene click chemistry reactions, using pentaerythritol tetrakis(3-mercaptopropionate) (PETMP) and poly(ethylene glycol) diacrylate (PEGDA) and molybdenum disulfide (MoS2) as photothermal materials to achieve integrated molding of the evaporator. Through structural optimization, the 3 × 3 array structure exhibits the best evaporation performance, with an evaporation rate of 1.91 kg m–2 h–1 and an evaporation efficiency of 90.9% at one solar intensity. When used for photocatalytic degradation of dye wastewater, the degradation efficiency of dyes can reach 86%. In addition, using a 3 × 3 array evaporator to treat salt-containing dye wastewater can cause directional salt collection due to the temperature difference between the top and bottom. After 5 complete evaporation and collection cycles, the average salt collection capacity of the evaporator can still be maintained at 0.593 g, with a salt collection rate of 158.34 mg m–2 h–1. This biomimetic photothermal evaporator provides a solution for the recycle and high purification of salt-containing dye wastewater.

items.title: Vicinal Functional-Group Engineering in Defect-Engineered MOFs for One-Step Ethylene Purification
items.abstract: Abstract The development of C2H6-selective adsorbents offers a promising strategy for energy-efficient C2H4 purification from C2H6/C2H4 mixtures. However, the similar physicochemical properties of C2H6 and C2H4 make it challenging to achieve preferential adsorption of C2H6. Herein, we propose a vicinal functional-group engineering strategy to construct C2H6-recognition domains, enabling efficient one-step C2H4 purification from C2H6/C2H4 mixtures. The adjacent functional groups on the modulators are introduced close to the defect sites of MOFs, constructing synergistic electrostatic-confinement microenvironments for C2H6 recognition. The fluorinated-defective MOF (UiO-66-(CF3)2) exhibits C2H6 preferential adsorption with an uptake of 2.2 mmol/g at 298 K and 100 kPa. Breakthrough experiments further confirm the dynamic separation performance of UiO-66-(CF3)2, achieving high-purity C2H4 (&gt;99.99 %) with a productivity of 12.67 L/kg. Theoretical calculations further reveal that the adjacent functional groups in the ligands would induce electrostatic potential redistribution and confined pore structures, strengthening C2H6 adsorption on defective MOF over C2H4. This work establishes a vicinal functional-group engineering strategy for constructing synergistic electrostatic-confinement microenvironments toward C2H6 recognition in MOFs.

items.title: Constructing Continuous Proton Channels through One-Dimensional Confined Nanofillers for High-Performance H2/O2 Fuel Cells
items.abstract: Abstract Establishing continuous proton transport pathways alongside robust interfacial interactions remains a critical bottleneck for organic–inorganic composite proton exchange membranes (PEMs). Herein, we report a rationally designed hybrid nanofiller (SUC@PHNTs) that integrates the long-range orientational order of one-dimensional (1D) halloysite nanotubes (HNTs) with the high-density proton-hopping sites of the metal-organic framework UiO-66-(COOH)2 (UC) and zwitterionic surface grafts. Subsequently when dispersed in a sulfonated poly(ether ether ketone) (SPEEK) matrix, this 1D confined architecture bridges discrete UC domains into interconnected, continuous proton-conducting channels, effectively reducing proton transport tortuosity. Specifically, the S/SUC@PHNTs-3.0% membrane delivered 174.72 mS cm–1 (80 °C, 100% RH), corresponding to a 35.21% increase relative to pristine SPEEK. In an H2/O2 single-cell test, the membrane delivered a maximum power density of 793.29 mW cm–2, substantially exceeding that of SPEEK. Moreover, the voltage decay rate over 150 h of continuous operation was merely 0.42 mV h–1, indicative of excellent long-term operational stability. Overall, these results establish that the 1D confined nanofiller design strategy provides a promising technological pathway toward high-performance PEMs.

items.title: Regulating the Activity and Product Selectivity of Electrocatalytic Glycerol Oxidation by Changing the Au Loading on Ni2.86Te2/NF
items.abstract: Abstract Electrocatalytic glycerol oxidation reaction (GOR) has attracted much attention recently in the production of high-value-added chemicals coupled with water electrolysis for energy-saving hydrogen production due to its mild reaction conditions, green and harmless, and lower onset potential than the oxygen evolution reaction (OER) in water electrolysis. However, under alkaline conditions, glycerol is prone to generate low-value-added C1 products, and the selectivity for C3 products is a significant challenge. In this work, we successfully regulated the activity and product selectivity of electrocatalytic glycerol oxidation by changing the Au loading on Ni2.86Te2/NF. The results showed that the selectivity of Au/Ni2.86Te2/NF-3 for glyceric acid (GLA) was 72.41%, and its GOR performance and selectivity were superior to those of recently reported catalysts. An appropriate Au loading results in favorable changes in Au distribution and surface electronic structure, which are associated with improved GOR activity and GLA selectivity.

items.title: Structured Filler-Enabled Pore-Interface Engineering in Polydimethylsiloxane for Passive Radiative Cooling
items.abstract: Abstract Passive radiative cooling (PRC) materials require efficient solar scattering, high thermal emissivity, and mechanical compliance, yet constructing hierarchical pore-interface architectures that simultaneously enhance particle scattering, interface scattering, and flexibility within a single polymer system remains challenging. Here, we report a structured filler-induced pore-interface engineering strategy for flexible PRC films. Carboxymethyl cellulose (CMC) and silane-modified SiO2 nanoparticles were electrostatically assembled into a spatially organized CMC@SiO2 filler, which simultaneously acts as a scattering unit and a pore-forming scaffold. Upon incorporation into polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS), the structured filler induces hierarchical pore architectures with SiO2-decorated pore walls, generating coupled particle-scattering and pore-interface scattering pathways. The Finite-Difference Time-Domain simulations reveal that the multiscale architecture broadens solar scattering across the 0.25–2.5 μm range through enhanced refractive-index contrast and multiple-scattering effects. Benefiting from the coupled contribution of SiO2 scattering centers, hierarchical pore interfaces, and the intrinsic mid-infrared (MIR) emissivity of PDMS, the resulting film achieves a solar reflectivity of 94.6% and a MIR emissivity of 95.2%. The film delivers a maximum sub-ambient cooling of 7.1 °C under direct sunlight. Building energy simulations further predict an average annual cooling-energy reduction of 10.4% across representative climate zones in China. This work establishes a structured filler-enabled hierarchical pore-interface engineering strategy that integrates scattering enhancement, porous architectures, and polymer flexibility, offering a general route toward scalable and high-performance PRC materials.

items.title: Controlled Interfacial Electronic Coupling in Chemical Vapor Deposition-Grown WSe2 Monolayers on Au(111)
items.abstract: Abstract We report on the controlled growth and interface engineering of high-quality WSe2 monolayers on Au(111) using ambient-pressure chemical vapor deposition (CVD) combined with comprehensive surface-sensitive characterization in ultrahigh vacuum (UHV). The as-grown films exhibit a selenium buffer layer, which enables the formation of a weakly coupled WSe2 phase at the metal interface, as revealed by scanning tunneling microscopy (STM) and low-energy electron diffraction (LEED). Annealing in UHV removes the selenium buffer layer and leads to the emergence of a pronounced moiré superstructure and a transition toward a strongly coupled WSe2 phase. Furthermore, this transformation is accompanied by pronounced modifications of the electronic structure, including phase-dependent changes in the valence band structure observed by angle-resolved photoelectron spectroscopy (ARPES), a hybridization-induced metallization measured by scanning tunneling spectroscopy (STS), and a significant decrease in the work function determined by field emission resonance (FER) and ultraviolet photoemission spectroscopy (UPS). Density functional theory (DFT) calculations confirm strong WSe2–Au hybridization and the presence of the mid-gap states for the strongly coupled phase, whereas the Se8 buffer layer weakens the interaction of WSe2 with Au, so that its electronic structure is close to that for the freestanding system. Our results demonstrate that growth-induced interface chemistry provides a powerful handle to tune the electronic coupling in WSe2/Au(111), establishing a direct link between interfacial structure and electronic properties in metal–transition metal dichalcogenide (TMD) interfaces.

items.title: Robust Thermal Stability, Flame Retardancy, and Weather Resistance Cross-Linked Cellulose Aerogel toward High-Performance Passive Radiative Cooling
items.abstract: Abstract The frequent occurrence of high temperatures has driven the development of green passive cooling technologies. Traditional passive radiative cooling materials have single performance, insufficient weather resistance and structural stability, and are unable to adapt to outdoor multifunctional thermal management. In this study, cellulose nanofibers were used as the substrate, and silica and methyltrimethoxysilane were incorporated to prepare a composite aerogel. Tests show that the optimal sample has excellent radiation cooling, heat insulation, flame retardancy, hydrophobicity, and sound absorption performance. With a solar reflectance of 93.5% and a mid-infrared emissivity of 94.3%, it provides a maximum outdoor temperature reduction of 15.7 °C. Its minimum thermal conductivity reaches 0.034 W m–1 K–1, offering excellent thermal insulation performance. The total heat release and the rate of heat release were significantly reduced, and flame retardancy was greatly improved. In addition, the sample exhibits a water contact angle of 137.2°, endowing it with favorable self-cleaning properties. The average sound absorption coefficient reaches 0.78 in the broadband range of 1000–6300 Hz, and the noise reduction performance is superior to that of commercial materials. This multifunctional composite aerogel overcomes the performance limitations of traditional materials and offers new insights into the development and application of outdoor integrated thermal management functional materials.

items.title: Hierarchical Functionalized Lignin Interfaces Regulate Water Transport in Low-Coating-Content Bio-Based Polyurethane-Coated Urea
items.abstract: Abstract Bio-based polyurethane coatings are promising for controlled-release fertilizers, but their release performance at low coating contents is often limited by rapid surface wetting and water transport through the coating membrane. Here, we constructed a hierarchical lignin-based interface on castor-oil-derived polyurethane-coated urea to regulate water–coating interactions. Lignin micro/nanospheres were sequentially functionalized with polydopamine and octadecyltrichlorosilane and introduced at the outer polyurethane interface during the final coating stage. Thermodynamic calculations and spectroscopic analyses were consistent with interfacial chemical coupling between polydopamine-associated functional groups and residual isocyanate groups in the polyurethane coating. The resulting interface increased the apparent water contact angle from 87.4° to 157.2°, weakened the calculated adsorption of water, and reduced water-vapor permeability through the coating. Under a nominal total coating-material input of approximately 3 wt %, the cumulative nitrogen release within 10 days decreased from 56% for bio-based polyurethane-coated urea (BCU) to 20% for OTS-LMNPs@PDA-modified bio-based controlled-release urea (SBCU), while the time required to reach 80% nitrogen release increased from 20 to 49 days. This enhanced release performance was associated with reduced surface wetting, lower water affinity, and slower water transport across the modified coating, which collectively delayed water penetration, urea dissolution, and subsequent nitrogen diffusion. These results demonstrate that lignin-based interfacial modification provides an effective strategy for regulating water transport and improving the controlled-release performance of low-coating-content bio-based polyurethane fertilizers.

items.title: Dicationic Porous Poly(Ionic Liquid)s with Hydrogen Bond Donors for Efficient Catalytic Conversion of CO2 under Mild Conditions
items.abstract: Abstract The formation of cyclic carbonates by coupling CO2 with epoxides offers a practical way of upgrading the surplus CO2 that has accumulated in the atmosphere, and thus helps to mitigate global warming. Because CO2 is intrinsically robust thermodynamically and sluggish kinetically, however, this transformation usually demands harsh conditions. Herein, a family of porous poly(ionic liquid)s denoted bAm-PIL-x (bAm = bis-amide) was constructed by radical copolymerization of an imidazolium-based ionic liquid monomer (tVIm-IL) and a quaternary ammonium-based ionic liquid monomer (tQAm-IL) in the presence of N,N'-methylenebisacrylamide as the cross-linker. These polymers combine a moderate specific surface area, pores spanning several size regimes, and a pronounced affinity for CO2, which makes them well suited to both capturing and converting CO2. Applied to the coupling of CO2 with epoxides under solvent-free, metal-free, and cocatalyst-free conditions, bAm-PIL-2 delivered excellent performance at a mild 80 °C and 1.0 bar. The catalyst was readily regenerated and recycled, and it accepted a wide range of epoxide substrates. Density functional theory (DFT) calculations together with in situ infrared spectroscopy were used to probe how the catalyst, the epoxides, and CO2 interact, and on this basis a plausible reaction mechanism for the cycloaddition is proposed. The present findings offer meaningful guidance for designing highly efficient catalysts for CO2 conversion.

items.title: High-Performance SrLiAl3N4:Eu2+ Red Phosphor via Alloy Precursor Synthesis for Laser-Driven and Wide-Gamut Displays
items.abstract: Abstract In this work, the alloy-precursor solid-state synthesis strategy (AS-method) is employed to fabricate high-performance SrLiAl3N4:Eu2+ phosphors. This approach effectively suppresses the oxidation of Eu2+ to Eu3+ compared to conventional solid-state synthesis (S-method). The resultant optimization of the local structure not only enhances the structural rigidity but also modulates the surrounding chemical pressure at different activator sites. This site-selective regulation leads to spectral narrowing and a blue shift in the emission. The optimized phosphor exhibits an external quantum efficiency (EQE) of 52.38%, a value that ranks among the highest reported for the SLA-based phosphors. Furthermore, it demonstrates an ultrahigh saturation threshold of 90.69 W/mm2 under blue laser excitation, surpassing most reported red phosphors. When applied in white LEDs, it achieves 104% of the NTSC color gamut. Thus, this phosphor indicates great potential for applications in both laser-driven and high-color-gamut displays.

items.title: Modelling and Emulation of Afferent-Like Excitatory–Inhibitory Spiking Using Ovonic Threshold Devices for Neuromorphic Oscillatory Computing
items.abstract: Abstract Spike-based computing has attracted increasing attention for efficient information processing, creating demand for neuromorphic hardware capable of generating and processing spikes. Ovonic threshold switching (OTS) devices are promising spiking neurons because their threshold-switching behavior and negative differential resistance enable compact spike-generation circuits, while their scalability supports dense integration. However, a circuit-level design framework linking defect dynamics with conduction behavior remains lacking. Here, we experimentally demonstrate an intensity-tuned artificial neuron based on a GeAsTe OTS device integrated with a resistor-capacitor (RC) circuit. The neuron shows a non-monotonic excitatory–self-inhibitory response with applied voltage, phenomenologically analogous to excitatory–inhibitory behavior in biological neurons. The spiking frequency initially increases and then decreases beyond an inflection voltage point. This transition arises intrinsically from competition between RC charging dynamics and conductive filament retention in the OTS device, rather than from a separate inhibitory pathway. The neuron achieves a spiking frequency of up to 1.6 MHz. The behavior is supported by simulations using a dynamical model for diffusive filament-based memristors, accounting for resistance changes from filament formation and rupture. Furthermore, a physics-informed compact SPICE model combining defect-state transitions and filament evolution reproduces OTS switching and predicts neuron dynamics under varying temperatures, internal resistances, and circuit conditions. Finally, circuit simulations of a coupled OTS neuron network demonstrate vertex coloring with phase convergence within approximately 5 μs, highlighting the potential of this framework for compact, energy-efficient brain-inspired computing.

items.title: IMAN: An Integrated Colorimetric Sensor for Direct Detection of PD-L1 on Extracellular Vesicles in Lung Cancer Diagnosis
items.abstract: Abstract Lung cancer is a leading cause of cancer mortality, yet early diagnosis remains difficult, highlighting the need for sensitive, noninvasive methods. Extracellular vesicles (EVs) and their surface proteins (e.g., PD-L1) are promising biomarkers; nevertheless, current EV detection requires time-consuming purification, sophisticated instrumentation, and long measurement protocols, resulting in high expenses and operational difficulties. This study developed an integrated colorimetric sensor, IMAN, based on a strategy of “Immunomagnetic Microbeads (IM) capture + Aptamer(Apt) recognition + Nanozyme (N) catalysis”. IMAN employs magnetic beads modified with antibodies against CD9 and CD81 to directly capture EVs from serum, eliminating the need for time-consuming prior isolation; combined with a one-step colorimetric readout, the entire workflow can be completed with only ∼40 min of hands-on time, requiring no complex instrumentation. The PD-L1 protein on the EV surface is specifically recognized by a nanoparticle-bound nucleic acid aptamer. Signal generation is achieved through the catalytic oxidation of 3,3',5,5'-tetramethylbenzidine (TMB) by a platinum-gold bimetallic nanozyme (Pt@Au). The facile IMAN colorimetric method demonstrated a relatively broad dynamic range (107–1010 particles/mL), high specificity (unaffected by 100 pg/mL soluble PD-L1 in serum), and reproducibility (relative standard deviation, RSD = 9.1%). Analysis of clinical serum samples revealed significantly elevated EV-PD-L1 levels in patients with lung cancer compared with healthy donors and patients with benign nodule (p &lt; 0.01). Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis yielded areas under the curve (AUC) of 0.849 for distinguishing patients with lung cancer from healthy donors and 0.860 for distinguishing patients with lung cancer from patients with benign nodules, which are superior to those of the conventional serum biomarkers CEA and Cyfra21-1. By addressing the cost, complexity, and slow response of current methods, IMAN offers a simple, cost-effective platform for direct EV surface protein detection without complex instrumentation, providing a novel tool for the noninvasive lung cancer diagnosis.

items.title: Improvement of Photocatalytic and Nanomechanical Properties of GaN Nanowires via Core-Shell Surface Modification
items.abstract: Abstract The practical implementation of photocatalytic water splitting for sustainable hydrogen production is largely limited by the efficiency of the oxygen evolution reaction at the photoanode. Gallium nitride is a promising material for photoanode fabrication, provided that suitable nanostructuring strategies are applied to enhance its efficiency and stability. Here, we report the functionalization of gallium nitride nanowires with a 5 nm-thick titanium dioxide layer of and a 10 nm biomimetic polydopamine coating, resulting in a 1.9-fold (190%) increase in the anodic photocurrent, as demonstrated by chronoamperometry. We provide a detailed explanation of this enhancement based on electrochemical impedance spectroscopy and a series of optical studies. The observed decrease in photoluminescence intensity (60–90%) and shortening of carrier lifetimes from 0.17 to 0.07 ns correlate with the improved photocatalytic performance. Moreover, the 50% reduction in the band-to-band to defect emission ratio and the analysis of exciton recombination pathways show the role of defect-related and surface recombination processes in determining the photocatalytic activity of the nanowires. The enhanced photocatalytic performance is further attributed to shell deposition, which induces surface-state passivation, band realignment, and the quantum-confined Stark effect. Concurrently, changes in strain distribution are confirmed by increased heterogeneity of the GaN E2high phonon mode frequency distribution, expressed by an increase in the standard deviation from 0.09 up to 0.17 cm–1 and linewidth broadening from 3.2 up to 3.4 cm–1, as observed by Raman spectroscopy. Additionally, we show that the nanomechanical properties of the nanowires are significantly improved after shell deposition, by the elimination of pop-in events, enhanced elastic recovery, and an increase in Young’s modulus from 12 to 37 GPa. Finally, we point out opportunities for further optimization of similarly functionalized nanowire systems to achieve even higher efficiencies and support emerging applications.

items.title: Metal–Organic Framework@Polysulfone Composite Beads for Air Filtration of Postharvest Pathogenic Fungal Spores
items.abstract: Abstract Phytopathogenic fungal infections pose a persistent threat to postharvest fruit quality and food security worldwide, with resistant strains increasingly limiting the efficacy of conventional fungicides. This study explored metal–organic frameworks (MOFs) as an emerging class of antifungal materials and examined their potential for air-based decontamination in storage environments. Among the zinc- and copper-based frameworks tested, HKUST-1 and ZIF-8 demonstrated exceptionally broad-spectrum antifungal activity, completely inhibiting mycelial growth of Penicillium expansum, Penicillium citrinum, and Colletotrichum gloeosporioides, while maintaining strong inhibition of Botrytis cinerea and Mucor piriformis. To enable practical deployment, the most active MOFs were incorporated into polysulfone composite beads via phase inversion, preserving their antifungal properties while offering a processable and scalable format. In vitro assays revealed that these MOF@PSF beads substantially suppressed both mycelial growth and spore germination, with HKUST-1@PSF and ZIF-8@PSF composites reducing conidial viability to near-complete levels. Mechanistic studies revealed that HKUST-1 primarily acts through substantial copper ion release (≈19 ppm), leading to pronounced metabolic inhibition, whereas ZIF-8 operates via reactive oxygen species (ROS) generation. Evaluation in a dual-chamber air-filtration prototype demonstrated remarkable performance: both composites reduced airborne spore transfer by 95.2–96.7% for P. expansum and by 99.4–99.6% for B. cinerea, effectively preventing contamination of the clean chamber and protecting the stored produce. These findings establish MOF@PSF composite beads as bioactive filtration materials that combine physical spore capture with intrinsic antifungal action, offering a residue-free route to limiting fungal dissemination during postharvest storage.

items.title: Thermo-responsive Ionizable Xanthone Bolaamphiphiles for Dynamic Self-Assembly into Nanovesicles Enabling Enhanced Intracellular Drug Release and Tumor Growth Inhibition
items.abstract: Abstract Stimuli-responsive supramolecular nanocarriers capable of controlled drug release have emerged as promising alternatives to conventional chemotherapy; however, the development of structurally defined small-molecule systems exhibiting thermo-responsive behavior within biologically relevant temperature ranges remains challenging. Herein, we report a series of ionizable xanthone-based bolaamphiphiles (X1–X3) engineered to undergo temperature-triggered self-assembly in aqueous media. Systematic modulation of oxyethylene-chain density revealed that X3 exhibits a sharp and reversible lower critical solution temperature (LCST) transition within the physiological temperature window (35–40 °C), leading to the formation of stable nanovesicular assemblies. The resulting X3 nanovesicles accommodate doxorubicin (DOX) with an encapsulation efficiency of ∼25% and a drug-loading content of 11% while maintaining good colloidal stability under physiologically relevant conditions. X3-DOX nanovesicles exhibit progressive thermoresponsive drug release near physiological temperature, which is further enhanced under mild hyperthermia, together with an additional acid-responsive release behavior associated with protonation of the piperazine units (apparent pKa ≈ 4.5). Cellular studies performed in 4T1 breast cancer and A549 lung cancer cells demonstrated enhanced intracellular drug accumulation, superior cytotoxicity, and effective suppression of multicellular tumor spheroids compared with free DOX. Furthermore, the nanoformulation exhibited excellent hemocompatibility, favorable biodistribution characteristics, and efficient systemic clearance. In a 4T1 tumor-bearing mouse model, X3-DOX induced remarkable tumor-growth inhibition with minimal systemic toxicity. These findings establish thermo-responsive xanthone-based nanovesicles as a versatile supramolecular platform for controlled anticancer drug delivery and provide a molecularly defined strategy for developing stimuli-responsive nanomedicines.

items.title: Synergistic Interfacial Engineering in V2C MXene Heterostructures for Enhanced Nano-aluminum Reactivity
items.abstract: Abstract Nano-aluminum (nano-Al) is a high-energy-density material with exceptional reactivity, making it promising for aerospace and military applications. Reducing particle size increases the active surface area and interfacial mass diffusion, but intrinsic agglomeration and dense alumina shells hinder diffusion. Conventional additives often reduce reactivity. Here, we modulate nano-Al interfacial diffusion through synergistic interactions in a V2C MXene heterostructure. The self-assembly of nano-Al on MXene suppresses agglomeration, while fluorine-containing terminations etch the alumina shells. The heterostructure also forms metal oxide contact layers that promote solid-phase thermite reactions. These effects increase the peak heat flow in air to 107.6 W g−1, 3.5 times that of pristine nano-Al. Solid-phase reactions complete energy release before Al melting, minimizing energy loss. The composite shows larger flame areas and a lower minimum ignition concentration (≥5 wt %). Adjusting the heating temperature reduces the total combustion duration by 88.9% and increases the dynamic pressure. This versatile fabrication process enables tunable performance for diverse operational environments.

items.title: Sustainable Thermoplastic Thermal Interface Adhesive Derived from Poly(lipoic acid) and Boron Nitride for Efficient Electronic Thermal Management
items.abstract: Abstract The escalating power density of electronics demands thermal interface materials (TIMs) that simultaneously offer high thermal conductivity, strong adhesion, and environmental sustainability. Conventional thermally conductive adhesives (TCAs) face inherent trade-offs among these properties, often relying on non-recyclable thermosets. Here, we present a sustainable thermoplastic TCA composed of a poly(lipoic acid) (polyLA)-based dynamic polymer matrix integrated with polyvinylpyrrolidone-modified hexagonal boron nitride (BN@PVP). The polyLA matrix incorporates catechol moieties and reversible Fe3+-carboxyl/catechol coordination bonds, creating a dynamically reconfigurable network. This design yields an adhesive (LD50Fe100) with high toughness (1.52 MJ m–3), and strong lap shear adhesion (884 kPa on PMMA and 1210 kPa on steel). The dynamic bonds enable room-temperature self-healing (93.1% efficiency) and robust recyclability. At a BN@PVP loading of 40 wt %, the composite (BN@LD50Fe100) achieves a thermal conductivity of 1.2 W m–1 K–1 while maintaining enhanced mechanical properties. LED chip heat dissipation experiments demonstrate a 4 °C lower operating temperature compared to devices without a TIM, with stable thermal performance over multiple cycles. This work provides a promising material strategy to overcome the traditional trade-offs in TCAs, offering a path toward repairable, reusable, and efficient thermal management solutions for advanced electronic packaging.

items.title: Interfacial Kinetic Matching in Amorphous Fe2O3/Crystalline Cu2O Enables Efficient Nitrate-To-Ammonia Electrosynthesis
items.abstract: Abstract Electrochemical nitrate (NO3–) reduction to ammonia (NH3) is a promising route for simultaneous nitrate remediation and sustainable NH3 synthesis, yet remains challenged by sluggish multistep hydrogenation kinetics. Here, we report an amorphous Fe2O3/crystalline Cu2O catalyst (a-Fe2O3/c-Cu2O), in which ultrasmall Cu2O nanocrystallites are uniformly dispersed in an amorphous Fe2O3 matrix. The resulting a-Fe2O3/c-Cu2O interface induces strong electronic interaction and complementary catalytic functions. The pH-dependent potential analysis shows that a-Fe2O3/c-Cu2O maintains a highly alkaline interfacial microenvironment, while stepwise kinetic measurements reveal favorable kinetic matching between NO3– activation and subsequent NO2– hydrogenation. In situ spectroscopic studies reveal a tandem catalytic pathway in which NO3– is first activated on c-Cu2O to form NO2–, followed by transfer to adjacent a-Fe2O3 sites for hydrogenation to NH3. Consequently, a-Fe2O3/c-Cu2O achieves an NH3 Faradaic efficiency of 92.4% and an NH3 yield rate of 6.25 mmol h–1 mg–1, and sustains stable operation for 100 h in a membrane electrode assembly electrolyzer. This work offers a viable strategy for promoting nitrate-to-ammonia electrosynthesis through amorphous/crystalline interfacial engineering.

items.title: Microstructured Ionic Polymer-Based Multifunctional Iontronic Skin for Pressure Sensing, Object Recognition, and Underwater Environmental Monitoring
items.abstract: Abstract Skin-like iontronic sensors capable of multifunctional sensing and reliable operation hold strong potential for next-generation wearable electronics, human–machine interfaces, and underwater technologies. However, simultaneously achieving high sensitivity and multifunctionality within a single platform remains a significant challenge. Here, we report a multifunctional iontronic skin based on a microstructured ionic polymer (MSiP) composed of PVDF and [EMIM]+[BF4]– ion pairs. The MSiP is fabricated through mask-less photolithography to create highly ordered micropillar arrays with a diameter of 30 μm, a height of 5 μm, and an interspacing of 20 μm. The iontronic skin is constructed by sandwiching the MSiP layer between flexible PDMS/PEDOT:PSS electrodes, where pressure-induced migration of highly mobile [BF4]– ions, as revealed by molecular dynamics simulations, facilitates electrical double-layer formation at the MSiP/electrode interface, resulting in enhanced capacitive response. Moreover, finite-element simulations reveal that the microstructured architecture effectively concentrates local stress, increases the effective contact area, and amplifies structural deformation during compression, thereby accounting for the exceptional pressure sensitivity of the MSiP sensor. As a result, the sensor achieves an ultrahigh pressure sensitivity of 833 kPa–1, a highly linear response (R2 = 0.98), and excellent durability over 20,000 loading–unloading cycles. Its remarkable sensitivity enables the detection of pressures as low as 3 Pa. Furthermore, integration with a robotic arm enables the development of a tactile robotic interface platform capable of real-time object grasping, lifting, and releasing in response to tactile forces applied to the sensor surface. The sensor can also be attached to the human body to monitor physiological signals and various body movements. Beyond tactile sensing, when combined with machine learning, the sensor can accurately distinguish objects ranging from soft cloth to rigid steel bottles, achieving a high classification accuracy of 95–97%. The iontronic sensor also demonstrates underwater sensing, including monitoring of depth (0–35 cm), temperature (20–80 °C), and salinity (0–8 ppt). This work presents a versatile iontronic platform that enables high-performance multifunctional sensing for wearable electronics, intelligent robotics, human–machine interfaces, and underwater environmental monitoring.

items.title: Toward Robust InP Laser Lift-Off: Energy-Dependent Absorption Shift and Self-Absorption under Single-Pulse 1064 nm Irradiation
items.abstract: Abstract Heterogeneous integration of InP on silicon is essential for the next generation of electronic systems by enabling high-performance photonics and radio frequency devices. Near-infrared Laser Lift-Off (LLO) is a promising route to enable the cost-effective transfer of InP-based device layers onto Si platforms. However, its underlying mechanisms remain poorly understood. To clarify these laser-material interactions, we investigate an InP/InGaAs heterostructure under single-pulse 1064 nm irradiation. Through microstructural characterization and coupled optical-thermal simulations, we reveal that the LLO process deviates fundamentally from the conventional sacrificial layer decomposition model. Instead, we identify an energy-dependent transition driven by highly localized transient melting and dynamic optical property changes. At moderate energies, rapid atomic intermixing and phosphorus depletion occur within a short-lived liquid phase, followed by epitaxial recrystallization that preserves macroscopic structural integrity. At higher energies, thermally induced bandgap shrinkage in the nominally transparent InP strongly enhances direct 1064 nm absorption. This initiates a positive feedback loop of thermal runaway, shifting the dominant energy absorption from the InGaAs sacrificial layer toward the InP layer and causing catastrophic ablation. These findings suggest that the onset of InP self-absorption imposes a critical high-energy constraint on the LLO process, rather than the sacrificial-layer decomposition threshold alone, providing a mechanistic framework for understanding and optimizing InP layer transfer.

items.title: Integrated Droplet Microfluidic Platform for Single-Spheroid Photothermal Nanotherapy and Morphology-Driven Response Prediction
items.abstract: Abstract Photothermal therapy (PTT) is a promising cancer treatment modality, but its evaluation remains limited by the lack of physiologically relevant and quantitatively controlled in vitro platforms. Here, we present a droplet-based microfluidic platform that enables single-spheroid formation, programmable nanoparticle delivery, and in situ laser irradiation with real-time thermal monitoring. The platform enables temperature multiplexing within a single experiment, allowing construction of single-spheroid dose–response relationships and the definition of a temperature-based inhibitory metric (IT50). This provides a direct and physically meaningful quantification of photothermal efficacy. In parallel, a label-free, spheroid morphology-based machine learning approach predicts treatment response across cell types, nanoparticle incubation conditions, and therapeutic regimes while preserving intrinsic single-spheroid variability. Despite a limited dataset size and biological heterogeneity, the system achieves robust and reproducible predictive performance. Overall, this work establishes a scalable and versatile microfluidic framework for quantitative photothermal nanotherapy screening, integrating controlled thermal dosing, 3D tumor models, and morphological data-driven analysis within a single-spheroid platform.

items.title: Bubble-Guided Self-Healing Superhydrophobic Surfaces with Dual-Mode In Situ Visual Monitoring
items.abstract: Abstract Superhydrophobic surfaces exhibit great application potential ranging from sophisticated droplet manipulation to aerospace and other fields, owing to their unique properties such as liquid repellent, anti-corrosion, anti-icing, drag reduction, and so on. However, maintaining the stability of the solid–liquid interface remains a major challenge: the instability of the three-phase line caused by the collapse of the air layer during dynamic transport and the degradation of surface function caused by the retention of micro–nano contaminants seriously undermine its durability. In nature, rice leaves possess oriented microgroove architectures for unidirectional droplet transport, while submerged photosynthetic plants continuously generate bubbles to sustain intact solid–air–liquid (SAL) composite layers. Inspired by these merits, we propose a directional confinement–transport strategy, in which the microcolumn structure achieves dynamic compensation of the interfacial air layer through precise submillimeter bubble manipulation and establishes a cooperative stabilization of “structural confinement–air self-replenishment”. The surface demonstrates exceptional self-cleaning and no loss transport behaviors, vastly expanding its applicability in extreme environments. In addition, we construct a monitoring system based on interfacial chemical reactions, which enables in situ visual monitoring of the surface wetting state and can restore its superhydrophobicity on demand. In essence, this approach not only benefits the development of the superhydrophobic field, but also provides valuable theoretical foundations and practical guidance for constructing multifunctional stable interfaces, thereby propelling the field toward practical applications.

items.title: Slide-Ring Hydrogel Networks Cross-Linked by Movable Cucurbit[8]uril/Macromer Host-Guest Complexes
items.abstract: Abstract For traditional covalently cross-linked hydrogels, achieving both stiffness and toughness is generally difficult, owing to the fixed cross-linking points and the lack of dynamic response. Introducing movable cross-linking points into the network has proven to be an effective strategy to overcome this limitation. However, most existing approaches rely on pseudopolyrotaxane architectures based on cyclodextrin (CD) and polyethylene glycol (PEG), which require complicated synthesis. In this study, slide-ring hydrogels were conveniently synthesized via free radical polymerization of acrylamide (AM) and acrylic acid (AA) monomers, employing a supramolecular complex of azobenzene guest-modified telechelic macromers (Acr-Azo-PEG20K-Azo-Acr) and cucurbit[8]uril (CB[8]) as movable cross-linkers. Benefiting from the introduction of dynamic host–guest cross-linking, these hydrogels possess movable cross-linking points that can effectively dissipate energy and distribute stress during deformation, thereby significantly enhancing the mechanical properties through the pulley effect. By tuning the cross-linker content, solid content, and monomer structure, the material properties could be precisely optimized. Furthermore, posttreatment with ferric citrate (FeCA) allowed the introduction of Fe3+ dynamic coordination cross-linking into the acrylic-based slide-ring hydrogels, achieving a simultaneous 3-fold increase in tensile strength and an approximately 4-fold increase in toughness while maintaining high ductility and excellent fatigue resistance. The use of macromer/CB[8] complexes as movable cross-linkers offers a new strategy for high-performance hydrogels and lays a solid foundation for their future applications.

items.title: Manganese-Coordinated Rhein Hydrogel as a Vaccine Adjuvant for Synergistically Enhanced Humoral and Cellular Immunity
items.abstract: Abstract Manganese ions (Mn2+), which act as agonists of the cGAS-STING pathway, hold considerable promise as vaccine adjuvants. However, free Mn2+ is rapidly cleared after injection, making it difficult to sustain local immune stimulation. In this study, we exploited the coordination between Mn2+ and rhein, a naturally occurring anthraquinone small molecule, to construct a novel injectable Rhe@Mn hydrogel through one-step self-assembly. Within the hydrogel, densely packed supramolecular nanofibers intertwine to form a three-dimensional network, and energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDS) confirmed the uniform distribution of Mn along the nanofibers. Rheological testing showed that the Rhe@Mn hydrogel had favorable viscoelasticity and structural stability. In vitro studies, the Rhe@Mn hydrogel retained the STING-agonist activity of Mn2+ and effectively promoted antigen uptake by DCs and their maturation. In vivo, the hydrogel formed an antigen depot at the injection site, enabling sustained antigen release for up to 10 days. It also efficiently recruited immune cells, including DCs and macrophages, thereby establishing a local immune microenvironment enriched in antigen-presenting cells. After a single immunization, the Rhe@Mn hydrogel vaccine increased the abundance of germinal-center B (GC B) cells in lymph nodes by approximately 3.7-fold, significantly enhanced antigen-specific humoral and cellular immune responses, and established durable immune memory. This study provides a facile, functionally integrated platform for adjuvant-antigen co-delivery in subunit vaccines.

items.title: Type-III Porous Liquid ZIF-8/Perfluorodecalin for O2 Delivery and CO2 Removal: Stability, Sorption, and Transport Monitored by In Situ EPR Spectroscopy
items.abstract: Abstract Perfluorodecalin (C10F18) is a well-known gas carrier for chemical and biomedical applications. Being an inert and stable liquid, it is capable of dissolving and releasing large volumes of O2 and CO2. In this work, we propose a route for enhancing its functional properties furthermore by designing a type-III porous liquid (PL) composed of C10F18 and metal–organic framework ZIF-8. Using spin probes encapsulated in ZIF-8, we employ in situ electron paramagnetic resonance (EPR) spectroscopy to investigate the stability of this PL and the adsorption, transport, and desorption of O2 and CO2 in practical conditions. The prototypical flow system with EPR detection was designed to demonstrate the controllable sorption cycles of ZIF-8/C10F18 PL. The exceptional stability and appealing functional properties of this PL pave the way for its future chemical and biomedical applications.

items.title: Synergistic Effects of Thermally Engineered Defect-Rich Structures in Renewable Nanocarbons for Enhanced Electrochemical Performance
items.abstract: Abstract The electrochemical performance of conventional hard carbons remains constrained by their limited surface activity and insufficient interlayer spacing for efficient sodium storage. Here, we report a microstructurally engineered carbon derived from waste passenger tyres, exhibiting tunable defect density, interlayer spacing, and pore distribution through controlled carbonization between 700 and 1500 °C. The thermally driven reconstruction of sp2/sp3 domains induces a hierarchical framework featuring short-range ordered graphene nanodomains embedded within disordered carbon matrices, generating abundant closed and open pores that synergistically facilitate ion transport and adsorption. The optimized carbon produced at 1300 °C delivers a first-cycle reversible capacity of approximately 282.1 mAhg–1, retains approximately 278.5 mAh g–1 after 100 cycles at 10 mA g–1, and exhibits sustained high-current cycling stability over 500 cycles. Detailed micromechanistic analysis reveals that the enhanced sodium storage originates from the coupling of enlarged interlayer spacing (≈0.38–0.40 nm) and optimized Raman-active disorder with the internal pore architecture, enabling coexisting diffusion-controlled intercalation and surface-induced capacitive processes. This work establishes a framework for defect-controlled microstructural engineering of tyre-derived carbons, providing mechanistic insight into the pore–defect–graphite interplay and offering a sustainable pathway for converting end-of-life rubber waste into high-performance anode materials for next-generation sodium-ion batteries.

items.title: Defect and Ion-Migration Regulation in MAPbI3 Memristors via ZIF-67 Modification toward Stable Resistive Switching and Neuromorphic Computing
items.abstract: Abstract High-performance resistive random-access memory (RRAM) based on organic–inorganic hybrid perovskites remains limited by intrinsic vacancy defects and uncontrolled ion migration, which usually induce random conductive filaments (CFs) formation and poor device stability. Herein, a defect-engineering strategy is proposed by using a cobalt-based zeolitic imidazolate framework (ZIF-67) as a multifunctional additive to synergistically regulate the MAPbI3 film through Co ion incorporation and ligand-assisted defect passivation. Structural, morphological, optical/electrical, and conduction analyses reveal that the introduction of ZIF-67 improves film quality by enlarging grains and reducing grain boundaries, while regulating Pb-vacancy-related defect states and introducing a stronger Co–I bond. These effects suppress disordered vacancy migration and promote stable CFs formation during resistive switching (RS). Consequently, the Cu/ZIF67-MAPbI3/p-Si device exhibits enhanced RS performance, including a high resistance ratio (&gt;103), low operating power consumption (≈1.01 mW), endurance over 2300 cycles, and improved switching uniformity with reduced coefficients of variation for both high-resistance state and low-resistance state. Benefiting from its continuously tunable conductance, the device successfully emulates synaptic plasticity behaviors, including paired-pulse facilitation (PPF), spike-timing-dependent plasticity (STDP), and long-term potentiation/depression (LTP/LTD). Moreover, an experimentally calibrated multilayer perceptron achieves Modified National Institute of Standards and Technology (MNIST) handwritten digit recognition with an accuracy of 97.54% and a last loss of 3.35%, demonstrating the potential of ZIF67-MAPbI3-based RRAM device for artificial synapses and neuromorphic computing.

items.title: Tailoring Viscoelasticity by Carbon Filler Dimensionality toward High-Impact-Resistant Polydiborosiloxane Composites
items.abstract: Abstract The development of lightweight and flexible materials with high-impact-resistant performance remains a critical challenge under dynamic loading conditions, including precision instruments, electronics, and military defense systems. Herein, carbon fillers with distinct dimensionality are incorporated into polydiborosiloxane (PDBS) to construct composites with tunable viscoelastic behavior and excellent impact resistance. Increasing filler dimensionality not only retains the specific shear-stiffening viscoelastic behavior of PDBS but also significantly enhances the energy-dissipation capability and impact-resistant performance of the composites. Notably, the composite with large-size graphene achieves a high impact-force attenuation rate of 92.2% under low strain-rate impact while maintaining a strength of 48.8 MPa and a toughness of 24.2 MJ/m3 under high strain-rate impact. This work highlights the critical role of filler dimensionality in tailoring the viscoelasticity toward high-impact-resistant composite materials, thereby offering potential for efficient protection under dynamic loading conditions.

items.title: Anharmonic Shear Vibration of Electrostatic Layers Leads to Low Thermal Conductivity in Bi2O2Se
items.abstract: Abstract Bi2O2Se is among the best n-type oxide thermoelectric materials with low lattice thermal conductivity and shows a robust ferroelectric state at room temperature in reduced dimensions. Herein, we have combined experimental and theoretical studies to comprehend this elusive congruence of low lattice thermal conductivity (κlat) and an incipient ferroelectric state. We have experimentally measured the κlat of Bi2O2Se in the 10–300 K temperature range, which showed that temperature–dependent κlat deviates from the usual T–1 dependence. Density functional theory-based calculation of phonon dispersion reveals that the low κlat in Bi2O2Se primarily originates from the anharmonic lattice vibration and the presence of low-frequency optical phonons, which strongly interact with the longitudinal acoustic phonons and suppress their dispersion along Γ-A and Γ-X directions in the Brillouin zone. Our study reveals that the lowest frequency optical phonons at ∼25.7 and ∼66.5 cm–1 involve a shear interlayer vibration that can promote distortion in the Bi–O bond length and displacement of Se atoms. We propose that these vibrational modes can dynamically break the centrosymmetric configuration in the reduced dimension, leading to the experimentally observed ferroelectricity in ultrathin nanosheets or flakes of Bi2O2Se as reported in the literature. We have corroborated the presence of these low-frequency phonons using low-temperature heat capacity measurement and temperature–dependent Raman spectroscopy.

items.title: Enhanced Performance of Protonic Ceramic Electrolysis Cells via Transient Sinterlayer Engineering
items.abstract: Abstract Protonic ceramic electrolysis cells (PCECs) are a promising technology for efficient hydrogen production at intermediate temperatures (500–600 °C), but their commercialization is hindered by fabrication challenges. In particular, the high-temperature sintering required to densify barium cerate–zirconate electrolytes promotes barium volatilization, leading to phase decomposition and degraded performance. Here, we introduce a transient sinterlayer processing strategy in which a thin (∼1 μm) surface coating is applied atop the electrolyte before sintering. During high-temperature processing, the sinterlayer suppresses electrolyte decomposition, promotes densification and grain growth, and is ultimately incorporated into the perovskite lattice, yielding a chemically uniform perovskite electrolyte. Three sinterlayer compositions (CeO2, La2O3, and La2Ce2O7) were evaluated for BaCe0.7Zr0.1Y0.1Yb0.1O3–δ electrolytes. La2O3 provided the greatest benefit by enhancing grain growth, preserving dopant distributions, and substantially improving stability upon exposure to boiling water, although degradation under CO2-containing conditions at 550 °C remained evident. Integrated into complete electrolysis cells, La2O3 sinterlayers increased current density by 67.2% at 1.3 V and 600 °C while improving Faradaic efficiency from 78.8 to 85.0% relative to a bare cell. These results establish transient sinterlayers as an effective fabrication strategy for high-performance PCECs.

items.title: A High-Brightness, Low-Energy-Spread Au Needle Point Electron Source Nanocold-Cathode Adapted to Low-Power Photoelectric Coexcitation
items.abstract: Abstract To address the requirements of vacuum electronic and optoelectronic device applications for next-generation low-power-consumption, high-brightness, low-energy-spread, and tunable electron sources, the pursuit of high-efficiency metal nanocold-cathodes with plasmon-enhanced properties in specific waveband emerges as one of potent solutions. In this study, by screening and comparing the cathode materials and structures, we propose a high-brightness, low-energy-spread Au needle nanocold-cathode point electron source adapted to low-intensity photoelectric coexcitation. The experimental results demonstrate sensitivity to excitation light and outstanding electron emission performance of this point electron source: under the coexcitation of an electrostatic field below ∼1.25 V μm–1 and a supercontinuum-spectrum laser with average intensity of ∼24 W cm–2, the source achieved an emission current of 130 nA, improving by one order of magnitude when compared to the field emission current (∼13 nA) under pure electrostatic field excitation. As the laser excitation intensity increased, its effective work function decreased from 5.1 to 2.7 eV, resulting in a significant reduction of the excitation threshold for electron emission. Benefiting from the plasmon-enhanced light-harvesting effect, the cathode exhibits high sensitivity and selectivity to the wavelength and polarization of the incident light. In the 532–675 nm plasmon resonance band, the emission current exceeds 225 nA at an average excitation intensity of only 7.05 W cm–2, ∼17 times the pure electrostatic field emission current. Meanwhile, the plasmon relaxation preferentially populates high-energy electrons and suppresses the energy spread broadening induced by the space charge effect, thereby achieving a high reduced brightness of 6.89 × 109 A m–2 sr–1 V–1 and a low-energy spread of approximately 0.5 eV. This low-power photoelectric coexcitation scheme greatly relaxes the requirements on the excitation source, providing a route for the miniaturization and integration of vacuum optoelectronic point electron sources.

items.title: Architecting Co-continuous PVDF Composites via Multi-material 3D Parallel Printing for Enhanced Piezoelectricity and Wearable Sensing
items.abstract: Abstract Flexible piezoelectric composites have attracted considerable attention for self-powered sensing; however, achieving efficient electromechanical response while maintaining structural integrity under repeated deformation remains challenging. Herein, a structure-driven multi-material 3D parallel printing strategy is developed to construct polyvinylidene fluoride (PVDF)-based piezoelectric composites with a co-continuous dual-phase architecture. In this design, ionic liquid (IL)-modified PVDF serves as the piezoelectric phase, where the IL promotes β-phase formation and dipole orientation, while carbon nanotubes (CNTs)-reinforced PVDF provides a conductive phase for electrical signal collection. Unlike conventional stacked configurations, the parallel-printed architecture enables continuous integration of the piezoelectric and conductive phases, providing intimate interfacial contact and a mechanically interconnected structure. The resulting structural continuity facilitates stress transfer during mechanical deformation and contributes to a stable electromechanical response. Kelvin probe force microscopy measurements further reveal an interfacial potential difference of 85.6 mV, indicating distinct interfacial electrical characteristics between the two phases. The optimized sensor delivers an output voltage of 0.55 V at 5 N, a sensitivity of 439.77 mV/N in the low-force regime, and a response time of 28 ms, together with excellent mechanical stability. Finite element analysis and experimental results demonstrate that the enhanced piezoelectric response is closely associated with the continuous deformation and effective stress transfer enabled by the parallel architecture. The sensor further exhibits reliable performance in human-motion monitoring and human–machine interaction. This work establishes multi-material 3D parallel printing as a structure-engineering approach for integrating piezoelectric and conductive phases and provides a versatile route toward high-performance flexible piezoelectric sensing devices.

items.title: Amino-Terminated Ti3C2T x MXene Prepared via Ammonia Treatment Boosts Efficiency and Stability of Perovskite Solar Cells
items.abstract: Abstract Defect-mediated non-radiative recombination and progressive material degradation impose fundamental limits on the power conversion efficiency (PCE) and operational durability of perovskite solar cells (PSCs). To address this issue, we synthesized amino-terminated Ti3C2Tx MXene (denoted as A-MXene) nanosheets through LiF/HCl etching and subsequent ammonia post-treatment and incorporated them into PSCs. Characterization results reveal that ammonia treatment modifies the surface/interlayer chemistry of Ti3C2Tx and introduces amino-related nitrogen species, accompanied by increased interlayer spacing, reduced lateral flake dimensions, and enhanced dispersibility. In PSCs, A-MXene regulates both Pb- and I-related chemical environments, improves perovskite crystallization, suppresses non-radiative recombination, and promotes interfacial hole extraction. Consequently, the A-MXene-modified device delivers a PCE of 23.49%. Moreover, the encapsulated device retains 94.9% of its initial PCE after 720 h of uninterrupted 1-sun illumination at 85 °C in a N2 atmosphere. These findings establish ammonia-treated MXene as a versatile additive capable of concurrently governing defect chemistry and charge transport, thereby enabling high-efficiency, stable PSCs.

items.title: Preconstructed Electrolyte Interphase Enables Stable Commercial V2O5 Cathodes for Aqueous Zinc-Ion Batteries
items.abstract: Abstract Aqueous zinc-ion batteries (AZIBs) show great potential for large-scale energy storage on account of their exceptional safety, low cost, and environmental friendliness. As a representative cathode for AZIBs, commercial vanadium pentoxide (c-V2O5) still suffers from critical bottlenecks including severe vanadium dissolution, sluggish Zn2+ diffusion, and intensive interfacial side reactions in aqueous electrolytes. Herein, a novel electrochemical pretreatment strategy is developed to in-situ construct a uniform, compact ∼3 nm amorphous electrolyte interfacial layer (EIL) with an organic–inorganic composite structure on the surface of c-V2O5 in an organic lithium-ion battery system, which breaks through the limitations of unstable and inhomogeneous interfacial layers formed in conventional aqueous systems. The EIL exerts multifunctional effects by suppressing vanadium dissolution, accelerating ion diffusion, and inhibiting side reactions, endowing the modified electrode with a high initial Coulombic efficiency of 98.3%, outstanding cycling stability (180 mAh g–1 after 5000 cycles at a current density of 1 A g–1), and enhanced rate capability. This work could provide guidance for optimizing cathode materials of AZIBs through rational electrolyte interface engineering in the future.

items.title: A Geometrically Tunable Cardiovascular Shunt for the Individualized Care of Neonates with Congenital Heart Defects
items.abstract: Abstract Congenital heart defects (CHDs), particularly single-ventricle anomalies such as hypoplastic left heart syndrome (HLHS), require early surgical intervention using fixed-diameter vascular shunts. However, current shunts are incapable of adapting to the physiological changes of infant growth, often leading to hemodynamic imbalance and elevated mortality risk. Here, we report a geometrically tunable cardiovascular shunt lined with a photoresponsive hydrogel based on methacrylated dextran (DexMA) and dithiothreitol (DTT). This dual-stage crosslinked hydrogel system enables minimally invasive modulation of the inner lumen diameter in response to external blue light. We optimized the hydrogel composition to achieve both mechanical robustness (Young’s modulus ≈ 8.5 kPa) and light-induced deswelling, allowing for lumen expansion up to 39% with high stability over one month. In vitro studies confirmed excellent cytocompatibility, hemocompatibility, and minimal immune activation. Prototype annular shunts demonstrated precise, programmable diameter increases (15–18%) corresponding to computational models of infant growth. This dynamic, photoresponsive platform is a critical advance toward implantable materials for personalized cardiovascular interventions and a significant step toward growth-accommodating pediatric medical devices.

items.title: Prepressed Liquid Metal Fabric with Strain-Insensitive Conductance for Wearable Bioelectronics
items.abstract: Abstract The development of flexible conductors with high electrical conductivity, flexibility, and electromechanical stability is important for reliable signal transmission in wearable electronics. Here, we report a patternable liquid metal (LM) fabric with strain-insensitive performance, fabricated using a highly elastic knitted fabric (KF) as the substrate and a gallium-based liquid metal as the conductive coating. A patterned poly(3,4-ethylenedioxythiophene)(styrene sulfonate) (PEDOT:PSS) intermediate layer was introduced to enhance the interfacial adhesion and facilitate the selective deposition of LM on the textile substrate. In addition, pre‑oxidation of the LM followed by a prepressing treatment further promotes the permeation of liquid metal into the knitted fabric, thereby improving the stability of electrical conductivity. Benefiting from the pore structure of the fabric and the strong interfacial combination of liquid metal and PEDOT:PSS, this composite fabric achieves a strain capacity of 200% with low resistance variations, and the resistance change rates are 18.6% for longitudinal stretching, 20.4% for 45° diagonal stretching, and 24.8% for transverse stretching. When stretched by 100% along three distinct directions (transverse, longitudinal, and 45°), the resistance change rate remains below 5% in all cases, demonstrating excellent multidirectional strain-insensitive conductivity. Moreover, after 1000 cyclic stretching cycles under a 30% strain, the resistance fluctuation still stays within 3%. The resulting fabric exhibited excellent conductivity stability when applied to conductors, Joule heating, electrocardiogram (ECG), and near field communication (NFC), demonstrating its potential for next‑generation wearable electronics.

items.title: RES NPs/GelMA Sustained-Release Cryogel Modulates Macrophage Arachidonic Acid Metabolism and Angiogenic Microenvironment Promoting Diabetic Wound Healing
items.abstract: Abstract Refractory chronic diabetic wounds severely impair quality of life. Their delayed healing is mainly driven by impaired angiogenesis and persistent inflammation caused by infection and excessive ROS. Resveratrol (RES) has anti-inflammatory and pro-angiogenic effects, but its clinical use is limited by poor solubility and low bioavailability. Here, we developed a dual-mechanism sustained-release system for RES to promote diabetic wound healing. RES was converted into nanoparticles (RES NPs) to improve cellular uptake and bioavailability, then encapsulated in GelMA cryogel microspheres (CMS) for injectable, sustained release. This system downregulated NF-κB signaling, reduced ROS, and suppressed pro-inflammatory cytokines and COX2, thereby inhibiting arachidonic acid metabolism and promoting macrophage polarization from M1 to M2. Meanwhile, AMPK activation restored endothelial cell function, enhanced angiogenesis, and supported new vessel formation. Overall, this strategy accelerated high-quality wound repair in diabetic conditions.

items.title: Nanostructure-Enabled Apparent Slip through Dynamic Hydration Reorganization
items.abstract: Abstract Dynamic transport across solid–liquid nanointerfaces is commonly interpreted through equilibrium wettability, although increasing evidence suggests that interfacial hydration rather than contact angle governs nanoscale liquid motion. However, how hydration reorganizes under ionic and hydrodynamic perturbations at strongly hydrophilic nanostructured interfaces remains poorly understood. Here, we demonstrate that dendritic silica nanostructures create a hydration-rich interphase whose dynamic mechanical state can be programmed by electrolyte concentration, flow, and biomolecular adsorption. Contact-angle measurements, density functional theory calculations, and overtone-resolved quartz crystal microbalance with dissipation monitoring reveal that intermediate ionic strengths maximize near-surface acoustic loading without a proportional increase in dissipation, while increasing flow induces a flow-dependent enhancement in model-derived apparent mobility. The response is strongest at higher overtones and persists after bovine serum albumin adsorption, demonstrating that the adaptive hydration state survives the formation of a complex protein–water interphase. Rather than reflecting the classical hydrophobic slip, the observations identify a dynamically reconfigurable hydration layer that decouples equilibrium wettability from interfacial mechanics. These findings establish hydration-layer reconfigurability as a general mechanism governing liquid mobility at hydrophilic nanostructured interfaces and provide a design framework for nanofluidic transport, antifouling materials, separation membranes, and interfacial biosensing technologies.

items.title: Biodegradable Starch/Gelatin/PAM Hydrogel Electrolyte for Wide-Temperature Flexible Zinc-Ion Batteries
items.abstract: Abstract The booming development of flexible wearable electronics requires safe, deformable, and sustainable aqueous zinc-ion batteries (AZIBs). Liquid electrolytes suffer leakage, zinc corrosion, and dendrite growth, while the recently reported hydrogel electrolytes fail to balance biodegradability and mechanical stretchability. Herein, we developed a fully biodegradable biomass dual-network hydrogel electrolyte fabricated via free-radical copolymerization of starch, gelatin, and acrylamide (AM) with ZnSO4 salts. Benefiting from abundant hydrogen-bond networks formed by renewable biomass skeletons, the tailored hydrogel effectively immobilizes free water to construct a water-poor interfacial microenvironment, simultaneously suppressing dendrite proliferation and electrolyte leakage. The hydrogel delivers an outstanding low-temperature tolerance and favorable ionic conductivity of 23.76 mS cm–1 (–20 °C) and contributes to accelerating redox reaction kinetics and improving the reversibility of the Zn plating/stripping process. Therefore, the assembled Zn||sodium vanadate battery delivers a high capacity of 350 mAh g–1 at 1.0 A g–1 with 100% Coulombic efficiency and 83% capacity retention over 700 cycles. Impressively, within a broad temperature window of 0–55 °C, the pouch cell could work under repeated bending states, and the hydrogel is fundamentally degraded within 20 days in natural soil. It provides a facile strategy for flexible and sustainable AZIBs with high performance.

items.title: Growth Kinetics of Gallium Selenide on Graphene: Bridging Atomistic and Mesoscale Processes
items.abstract: Abstract Achieving uniform, wafer-scale thin layers and heterostructures remains a major challenge in the synthesis of two-dimensional (2D) semiconductors, which requires precise control of growth parameters and atomic-level insight into surface interactions. We combine density functional theory (DFT) and kinetic Monte Carlo (KMC) simulations to investigate the early stages of 2D gallium selenide (GaSe) growth on graphene and determine how GaSe domain morphology, growth rate, and nucleation density depend on the atomic fluxes and substrate temperature. The presence of Ga on the substrate is key to promoting GaSe nucleation, while a sufficiently high Se flux is required to enable 2D GaSe growth and suppress accumulation of Ga clusters. The DFT-informed KMC simulations also reveal a trade-off between the growth rate and morphology, showing that increasing the flux of Ga relative to Se promotes faster growth of GaSe and increases the surface roughness. In contrast, high substrate temperatures promote edge healing and favor the formation of compact triangular domains. These results identify a narrow window of experimental conditions for 2D GaSe growth on graphene.

items.title: Hansen Solubility-Guided Design Optimization of Biopolymer–Drug Compatibility for Photodynamically Antimicrobial Biomaterials
items.abstract: Abstract Designing polymeric nanocarriers for hydrophobic therapeutics requires an understanding of polymer–drug interactions and their dependence on polymer molecular weight. Herein, poly(butylene succinate) (PBS) oligomers (αPBS) with tunable molecular weights were prepared via controlled microwave-assisted alcoholysis to investigate the relationships among molecular weight, solubility behavior, and curcumin encapsulation. Experimental solubility mapping revealed substantial deviations between experimentally determined and conventionally predicted Hansen solubility parameters (HSPs) in the oligomeric regime, highlighting the limitations of group-contribution methods for low-molecular-weight polyesters. The PBS oligomer with a M̅n of approximately 2,000 g/mol (αPBS6) exhibited experimental HSP values of δD = 17.0, δP = 7.3, and δH = 7.1 MPa½. Despite borderline-to-unfavorable HSP-derived compatibility with curcumin (RED ≈ 1.04 and χ ≈ 1.21), αPBS6 exhibited high curcumin encapsulation, demonstrating that HSP-derived parameters alone do not directly predict encapsulation efficiency. Curcumin-loaded αPBS nanoparticles (Cur@PBS6) had an average diameter of 232 ± 1.5 nm, a high loading capacity (8.54–9.10%), and good colloidal stability. Their loading capacity exceeded those of commercial PBS (6.36%), PBSA (6.64%), and PLA (2.75%) systems, indicating that molecular-weight modification and nanoparticle formation conditions contribute to curcumin incorporation. Spectroscopic analyses suggested reduced curcumin aggregation following encapsulation, which preserved its photoactivity and promoted reactive oxygen species generation under blue-light irradiation. Moreover, Cur@PBS6-incorporated electrospun poly(lactic acid) fibers exhibited photodynamic antibacterial activity under blue-light irradiation (450 nm, 0.3 W/cm2, 60 min), achieving bacterial killing efficiencies of 94.2% against Escherichia coli and 98.1% against Staphylococcus aureus. These findings demonstrate that experimentally determined HSPs provide a complementary framework for evaluating molecular-weight-dependent polymer–drug interactions, while nanocarrier performance is collectively governed by molecular weight, crystallinity, formulation condition, and other physicochemical factors.

items.title: Cross-Dimensional Percolation and Metastructure-Assisted Highly Efficient Electromagnetic Interference Shielding Films
items.abstract: Abstract Increasing electromagnetic interference (EMI) issues make shielding materials urgent in need. However, designing a thin/lightweight material with high shielding effectiveness (SE over 100 dB) by facile and scalable technologies with high production accuracy is still challenging. Herein, excellent shielding composite films are successfully prepared through sequential scalable positive pressure filtration, accurate inkjet printing, and facile transferring. From mass ratio optimization of 1D silver nanowires to 2D MXene, a skeleton with maximum inner free space and fast electron and phonon transport channels through cross-dimensional percolation is produced for internal multiple reflection absorption. To further increase EMI SE, graphene-based mesh metamaterials are theoretically calculated and accurately printed with controlled conductivity for impedance matching as the top layer. Facile inkjet printing succeeds in balancing print accuracy and conductivity control by advanced ink formulation. Finally, under multiple attenuation mechanisms verified through complex permittivity analysis in both frequency domain and real space (conductive loss, dipole polarization, and various interfacial polarizations), EMI SE of 102.31 dB in X-band is achieved. Integrating different attenuation technologies in a single material system of multidimensions inspires further designing shielding materials with increasingly strict requirements like multiband compatibility with special frequency enhancement.

items.title: Inducing Tunable Volatile Analog Switching in Nanocomposite-Based MAPbBr3 Perovskite Memristors for Synaptic Emulation
items.abstract: Abstract Metal halide perovskites (MHPs) are promising candidates for memristive applications owing to their mixed ionic-electronic conductivity, yet their inherent instability and tendency toward abrupt resistive switching remain critical barriers to neuromorphic implementations. Here, we present a nanocomposite strategy in which MAPbBr3 nanocrystals are synthesized in situ within a nickel acetate matrix through a one-step, annealing-free, and glovebox-free process, enabling ambient-stable memristive devices. By modulating the perovskite volume fraction, the ionic-electronic dynamics are tuned, inducing a transition from abrupt, nonvolatile digital switching in polycrystalline MAPbBr3 to gradual, volatile analog switching in the nanocomposite. Impedance spectroscopy and photophysical analyses attribute this transition to a shift from ion migration-driven switching in the bulk material to interfacial charge trapping and detrapping in the nanocomposite. The resulting volatile memristors emulate key synaptic functionalities, including short- and long-term plasticity, paired-pulse facilitation, and spike-dependent weight modulation, with stable performance over 1000 cycles under ambient conditions. Exploited in a reservoir computing framework, the nanocomposite memristor achieves ∼89% classification accuracy on noisy digit patterns with a linear readout, rising to 98% with a deeper network. This scalable, solution-processed approach offers a viable route to analog memristors for neuromorphic and edge computing.

items.title: Accelerated Charge Transfer Kinetics and Byproduct Suppression in Surface-Tailored LiNi0.83Mn0.05Co0.12O2 Cathode at –40 °C
items.abstract: Abstract In extreme-environment applications such as military, aerospace, and polar research, batteries capable of reliable operation at ultralow temperatures are urgently needed. Current low-temperature battery research has largely focused on electrolyte optimization, while cathode material design remains relatively underexplored. LiNi0.83Mn0.05Co0.12O2 cathodes, however, suffer from sluggish interfacial charge-transfer kinetics and accelerated parasitic reactions at –40 °C. Here, a simple polypyrrole (PPy) surface coating is demonstrated to simultaneously enhance the rate capability and cycling stability of LiNi0.83Mn0.05Co0.12O2 at –40 °C. The π-conjugated PPy coating improves electronic transport while stabilizing the surface/interfacial chemical environment, thereby reducing the kinetic barrier for interfacial charge transfer, suppressing excessive interphase growth, and facilitating Li+ transport. Consequently, the PPy-coated cathode delivers 103.1 mAh g–1 at 1C and retains 78.7% of its capacity over 300 cycles at –40 °C. Furthermore, a practical 1.6 Ah lithium-metal pouch cell delivers 75% of its nominal energy at –40 °C and maintains 92.2% capacity retention after 50 cycles. This work highlights cathode interfacial engineering as an effective complement to electrolyte optimization for developing high-rate and long-life LiNixMnyCo1–x–yO2-based lithium-metal batteries under extreme cold.

items.title: Gas Phase Multizone Synthesis and Localized Deposition of Pt/In Core−Shell Nanoparticles and Their Photothermoelectric Application
items.abstract: Abstract Multizone synthesis and localized deposition of bimetallic nanoarchitectures remain major challenges in additive manufacturing at the nanoscale, particularly when control over nanoarchitecture and localized functionality is required. Here, a multizone gas-phase electrodeposition strategy for the simultaneous synthesis and localized deposition of Pt/In core−shell nanoparticles through coupled vapor-phase encapsulation and electrostatic confinement is reported. In contrast to previous gas-phase electrodeposition studies that primarily focused on metallic and metal-oxide nano- and microarchitectures, the present work extends the process to bimetallic core−shell nanoarchitectures as functional nanoscale building blocks. Spark-generated Pt nanoparticles interact in flight with transported In vapor, enabling ligand-free Pt/In encapsulation before deposition. By controlling the In vapor supply through the evaporation temperature, two distinct nanoarchitectures are obtained: centric Pt-core/In-shell nanoparticles (evaporation temperature 750 °C) and eccentric core−shell nanoparticles (evaporation temperature 900 °C) with asymmetric shell distribution. In-flight particle collection reveals that the asymmetry initiates during high-temperature formation and becomes more pronounced during cooling after deposition. The charged Pt/In core−shell nanoparticles are selectively deposited into predefined Si micro-openings and linear patterns. The eccentric Pt/In structures exhibit broadened visible-light absorption and generate a measurable photo-thermoelectric response under illumination at 532 nm. The polarity reversal strongly supports the thermoelectric origin of the response. This approach establishes gas-phase electrodeposition as a route toward localized bimetallic core−shell nanoarchitectures for optothermal and thermoelectric applications.

items.title: Interface-Engineered Proton-Gated Oxide Transistors with Multitimescale Synaptic Plasticity
items.abstract: Abstract Ion-gated transistors that mimic biological synapses are essential for energy-efficient neuromorphic hardware capable of adaptive learning and sensory processing. However, achieving both high-speed operation and stable memory in silicon-compatible platforms remains challenging due to the trade-off between ionic mobility and retention characteristics. In this work, we developed proton-gated synaptic transistors composed of an electron-beam (EB)-deposited SiO2 electrolyte and a sputtered WO3 channel.
