A low film density with the oxygen deficiency of EB-deposited SiO2 enables gate-controlled proton intercalation and deintercalation, producing versatile synaptic plasticity of continuously modulating the WO3 channel conductance. The devices exhibit a wide time response range (pulse widths from 100 ms to 50 μs) and a large dynamic range (&gt;103) with a retention time of ∼18 s, successfully emulating short-term plasticity and nociceptor-like sensory behaviors such as threshold spiking, relaxation, and sensitization. They also achieve ∼90% image recognition accuracy and a low power consumption of ∼200 fJ for a single synaptic event. Furthermore, an introduction of a thin Al2O3 layer between the electrolyte and channel effectively suppresses proton back-diffusion, extending the retention time to ∼860 s. This also results in high recognition accuracy across a wide range of pulse widths, from subseconds to submilliseconds. By integrating two transistors with different retention times into a “one-transistor–one-synapse” architecture, we further demonstrated hardware-level temporal control of synaptic plasticity that enables event-driven learning, forgetting, and memory without altering input stimuli. These results indicate that all-oxide proton-gated transistors incorporating interface engineering provide a neuromorphic platform that enables highly flexible designs with excellent synaptic characteristics.

items.title: Porosity-Tunable Zn-0.5Mg Triply Periodic Minimal Surface Scaffolds Enable Immune-Osteogenic Coupling for Customized Bone Regeneration
items.abstract: Abstract Bone defects remain a clinical challenge due to the limited regenerative capacity of native bone and the lack of biodegradable implants capable of actively regulating the healing microenvironment. Current metallic scaffolds often suffer from an intrinsic trade-off among mechanical properties, degradation behavior, and bioactivity, limiting their therapeutic efficacy in load-bearing bone regeneration. Herein, porosity-tunable Zn-0.5Mg scaffolds with a triply periodic minimal surface (TPMS) structure are fabricated via selective laser melting. By systematically varying scaffold porosities (40, 60, and 80%), the coordinated regulation of mechanical properties, degradation performance, and ion release is achieved. The incorporation of Mg into Zn-0.5Mg enhances mechanical strength and stabilizes degradation behavior, while increasing the porosity accelerates Zn and Mg ion release in a controllable manner. Importantly, the co-released ions promote macrophage polarization, thereby establishing an immunoregulatory microenvironment favorable for bone regeneration. In a rabbit femoral condyle defect model, the implantation of Zn-0.5Mg scaffolds with high porosity (80%) enhanced bone ingrowth into interconnected pore networks and accelerated new bone formation over 14 weeks, without inducing systemic toxicity. Overall, this study establishes a porosity-tunable and immune-osteogenic coupling strategy in biodegradable Zn-0.5Mg scaffolds, offering a generalizable design for customizable and bioactive bone implants.

items.title: Strong D–A Interactions and π–π Interfaces Enable Efficient Hydrogen Evolution in S -Scheme D–A type Conjugated Polymer/g-C3N4 Heterojunctions
items.abstract: Abstract Polymer heterojunctions (PHJs) have emerged as a promising approach for solar-to-hydrogen conversion, owing to their tunable electronic structures and potential for efficient charge separation. A critical factor in achieving high photocatalytic performance lies in the rational design of photocatalysts with well-matched energy levels and effective carrier separation pathways. In this study, we designed and synthesized two S-scheme heterojunctions composed of donor–acceptor (D–A) type linear conjugated polymers integrated with g-C3N4 nanosheets for photocatalytic hydrogen evolution (PHE). The polymers were constructed using 10-methyl-10H-phenothiazine as a constant donor unit, while two different electron acceptors, dibenzothiophene-S,S-dioxide (BTDO) and dithieno[3,2-b:2′,3′-d]thiophene-S,S-dioxide (DTTDO), were employed to yield the polymers SOPTZ and DTPTZ, respectively. Among them, SOPTZ, incorporating the BTDO acceptor with higher electron affinity, provided a stronger driving force for intramolecular charge transfer (ICT) and separation. When composited with g-C3N4 nanosheets, the phenothiazine-based polymer formed a strong π–π conjugated heterointerface. The resulting S-scheme heterojunction induced band bending and an internal electric field (IEF), which synergistically enhanced charge separation while maintaining strong redox capability. As a result, the SOPTZ/g-C3N4-30 composite achieved a remarkable hydrogen evolution rate (HER) of 56.34 mmol g–1 h–1 under visible-light irradiation without any additional cocatalyst, significantly outperforming the DTPTZ/g-C3N4-10 catalyst. This work provides valuable insight into the rational construction of high-performance S-scheme PHJs for efficient PHE activity.

items.title: Redefining a Scalable β-Ga2O3/SiC Heterogeneous Material Platform via MOCVD-Assisted Ion-Cutting Technology
items.abstract: Abstract Heterointegration has emerged as a key developmental pathway for the continuous progress of microelectronics technology in the post-Moore era. However, there exists an urgent demand for practical and universally applicable approaches to realize high-quality heterogeneous integrated materials. In this study, MOCVD-assisted ion-cutting technology, which combines ion-cutting and homoepitaxy technology, is proposed for fabricating a β-Ga2O3-on-SiC heterointegrated material with excellent electrical and thermal transport performance. Benefiting from the excellent crystal quality, the β-Ga2O3 thin film exhibits a high effective Hall mobility of 31.9 cm2 V–1 s–1 at a relatively high apparent Hall carrier concentration of 3.6 × 1018 cm–3 and a thin film thermal conductivity of 13.0 +1.7/–1.8 W m–1 K–1. The atomically abrupt β-Ga2O3/SiC heterointerface constructed by hydrophilic bonding and stepwise annealing interface engineering yields an exceptional interfacial thermal conductance of 147 +23/–20 MW m–2 K–1, in which elastic phonon scattering with energies of 56 meV dominates the thermal transport. This proposed method offers a versatile and scalable solution for the development of next-generation semiconductor devices, showcasing enormous potential to revolutionize the microelectronics technology by enabling the fabrication of diverse heterointegrated materials with superior electrical and thermal characteristics.

items.title: A Multifunctional Sacrificial Plasticizer in PEO-Based Electrolytes for Improved Ionic Transport Properties and a Robust Solid-Electrolyte Interphase
items.abstract: Abstract Poly(ethylene oxide) (PEO)-based electrolytes have attracted extensive attention owing to their excellent lithium-salt-solvating capability and favorable mechanical flexibility. However, the practical application of PEO-based electrolytes is severely hindered by poor ionic transport properties and unstable interfaces between the electrolytes and electrodes. To address these challenges, a flexible organic molecule, 2-(2-(butylthio)–5-(methoxymethyl)–3-methylcyclohexa-2,5-dien-1-yl)–2,2-difluoro-1-phenylethanone (DFAPCS), was rationally designed and synthesized for preparing the PEO/LiTFSI/DFAPCS (PLD) composite electrolyte with a highly homogeneous structure. Such a DFAPCS additive, which contained methoxy (–OCH3) groups and thioether (–S–) linkages, imposes steric hindrance, polar interactions, and conformational disturbances on PEO chains. Such effects disrupted PEO ordered packing and reduced crystallinity to boost ionic conductivity. In addition, the DFAPCS additive possessed a low lowest unoccupied molecular orbital (LUMO) energy level, enabling it to preferentially undergo electrochemical decomposition for the formation of a robust solid-electrolyte interphase (SEI) enriched with LiF, Li2O, and LixSx components. As a result, the PLD electrolyte exhibited a significantly enhanced ionic conductivity of 8.06 × 10–4 S cm–1 at 60 °C, a higher lithium-ion transference number of 0.58, and an expanded electrochemical stability window of 4.6 V. The Li//Li symmetric cell demonstrated excellent long-term stability, achieving an ultra-long cycling lifespan of 4000 h at a current density of 0.1 mA cm–2. The LiFePO4-based full cell delivered outstanding rate capability and cycling performance, maintaining stable operation for 1000 cycles at 1 C with a capacity retention of 66.9% and an average Coulombic efficiency as high as 99.88% after prolonged cycling.

items.title: Multifunctional Surface Modulation of CsPbI3 Nanocrystals Enables Stable and Efficient Quantum Dot Solar Cells
items.abstract: Abstract All-inorganic CsPbI3 perovskite quantum dots (PQDs) represent a class of highly promising materials for next-generation photovoltaics. However, their stability is hindered by surface structural defects—primarily arising from dynamic ligand detachment—which severely compromise the stability of both the PQDs and their resulting thin films. In this study, we implement a multifunctional surface modification (MSM) strategy by introducing mono-butylammonium tetrafluoroborate (MBT) molecules to selectively passivate these surface vacancies. This approach not only stabilizes the PQD structure but also facilitates enhanced interdot electronic coupling, resulting in films with significantly reduced defect densities and improved energetic uniformity. Consequently, the MSM-treated device achieves a PCE of 15.5%, a substantial improvement over the 13.5% recorded for control devices, while exhibiting superior environmental stability. This work provides mechanistic insights into surface stabilization of CsPbI3 PQDs through a multifunctional surface modulation strategy, enabling enhanced performance and stability of PQD solar cells.

items.title: A Coassembled PTAA:BPDT Molecular Blend Hole-Transport Layer Enables Efficient and Stable Inverted Perovskite Single‑Crystal Solar Cells
items.abstract: Abstract Perovskite single-crystal (SC) solar cells promise superior charge transport and lower bulk defect densities than their polycrystalline counterparts, yet they suffer from poor interfacial contact, high surface trap densities, and limited operational stability. The interfacial delamination remains a critical barrier to the operational stability of SC photovoltaics. This is primarily due to the hydrophobic and weakly interacting nature of conventional hole-transport layers (HTLs) such as PTAA in inverted solar cells. Here, we overcome these limitations by blending PTAA with a dual-functional small molecule, biphenyl-4,4-dithiol (BPDT). Spectroscopic and theoretical studies reveal that BPDT forms noncovalent secondary interactions, thereby enabling π-electron delocalization with the PTAA’s aromatic rings, rendering the HTL more hydrophilic and shifting its Fermi level closer to the valence band (enhanced p-type character). The exposed thiol groups of BPDT strongly coordinate to Pb2+ at the perovskite SC surface, establishing a chemically anchored, mechanically robust interface. Using FA0.95Cs0.05PbI3 single crystals grown by inverse temperature crystallization on the PTAA:BPDT blend, the HTL exhibits markedly enhanced interfacial adhesion and long-term durability. The strong interfacial bonding suppresses delamination, enabling devices to retain 90% of their initial efficiency after 1000 h of maximum power point tracking under 50–60% relative humidity. This stability enhancement is accompanied by improved photovoltaic performance, with a champion power conversion efficiency of 24.85%, compared with 22.95% for pristine PTAA. This molecular blending strategy resolves the long-standing trade-off between efficiency and stability in perovskite single-crystal photovoltaics.

items.title: A Dual-Scale Porous Architecture with Anisotropic Mechanoluminescence for Flexible Sensing
items.abstract: Abstract Mechanoluminescence (ML) materials, which convert mechanical stimuli into optical signals, hold great promise for applications in flexible sensing and human–machine interfaces. However, conventional dense or randomly porous composite structures often suffer from uniform stress distribution, limited emission intensity, and a lack of directional selectivity. In this work, we propose and fabricate a dual-scale porous copper-doped zinc sulfide/polydimethylsiloxane (ZnS:Cu/PDMS) composite architecture featuring both micron-sized pores and aligned through-holes. Finite element analysis, mechanical characterization, and force–light synchronized measurements reveal that the dual-scale architecture promotes stress redistribution and strengthens the ML response, particularly under radial compression. Compared with dense and single-scale porous counterparts, the dual-scale porous composite exhibits enhanced ML intensity and sensitivity, together with a distinct direction-dependent luminescent response under axial and radial loading. Leveraging this anisotropic emission, its potential in various application scenarios is demonstrated, including bimodal flexible sensing, programmable pattern display, and direction-dependent information encoding. This study provides an effective structural design strategy for developing advanced ML materials and devices with high performance and directional recognition capabilities.

items.title: Two-Dimensional Indium Selenide for Next-Generation Photodetection: Interface Engineering, Device Architectures, and Emerging Applications
items.abstract: Abstract Two-dimensional (2D) indium selenide (InSe) has emerged as a compelling semiconductor platform for next-generation photodetection because of its thickness-tunable bandgap, high carrier mobility, and strong light–matter interaction. Moreover, its nonlinear, ferroelectric, piezoelectric, and polarization‑related functionalities can be modulated by phase, layer number, stacking configuration, and device architecture. This Review summarizes the recent advances in InSe-based photodetectors through a structure–property–performance framework. We first discuss the crystal structures, thickness-dependent band evolution, and preparation strategies of InSe and then compare representative device architectures including single-InSe channels, van der Waals heterostructures, ferroelectric-gated devices, asymmetric Schottky contacts, optical microcavities, and plasmonic/metasurface contact designs. Particular attention is paid to contact engineering, interface regulation, dark-current suppression, carrier-extraction acceleration, and polarization-selective detection, which have become central routes for improving sensitivity, speed, stability, and multifunctionality. Recent applications in optical sensing, broadband and polarization-resolved imaging, flexible and wearable electronics, neuromorphic vision, and secure optical communication are further reviewed. Finally, the remaining challenges associated with wafer-scale growth, defect control, environmental stability, standardized benchmarking, complementary metal–oxide–semiconductor (CMOS)-compatible integration, and system-level deployment are critically discussed. By emphasizing both recent progress and unresolved bottlenecks, this Review aims to provide a clearer roadmap for developing practical, high-performance InSe-based optoelectronic technologies.

items.title: Micro–Macro Synergistic Engineering of Metal-Organic Framework-Intercalated GO Membranes for Efficient Solar-DrivenWater-Electricity Cogeneration
items.abstract: Abstract Solar-driven interfacial evaporation and thermoelectric cogeneration present sustainable pathways to address global water and energy scarcity. Among various photothermal materials, 2D graphene oxide (GO) membrane evaporators have attracted considerable attention. However, they suffer from restricted water transport and poor heat localization, leading to unsatisfactory evaporation performance. Herein, we report a micro–macro synergistic engineering strategy to construct ZIF-8-intercalated GO composite membranes with a central macroscopic perforation (GO-MOF30-1.5) for efficient solar water-electricity cogeneration. At the microscale, the intercalation of ZIF-8 nanoparticles expands the interlayer spacing, creates abundant light-trapping sites, and enhances both water transport and photothermal conversion. At the macroscale, the central hole eliminates the “evaporation dead zone”, improves thermal convection, and accelerates vapor escape. Benefiting from this hierarchical design, the optimized GO-MOF30-1.5 membrane achieves a broadband solar absorptance of 86.21% under one sun. Consequently, it delivers a high evaporation rate of 1.53 kg m–2 h–1 with an outstanding evaporation efficiency of 91.91%. The membrane also exhibits excellent salt tolerance and long-term cycling stability. When coupled with a thermoelectric module, the system produces a stable open-circuit voltage of 135 mV under one sun, which can be amplified to 308 mV by connecting three units in series. Outdoor tests further demonstrate a daily freshwater yield of 3.75 L m–2 and a continuous voltage output of 218 mV (two units in series). This micro–macro synergistic optimization strategy offers a feasible approach for decentralized water purification and electricity supply in remote or off-grid locations, showing great promise for environmentally friendly and sustainable growth.

items.title: Visible-Light-Driven Hematite–Titania Janus Micromotors for Programmable Cargo Manipulation with Magnetically Triggered Release
items.abstract: Abstract Programmable cargo manipulation is essential for microrobotic systems intended for targeted delivery, microscale assembly, and lab-on-a-chip applications. However, achieving autonomous cargo capture, guided transport, and on-demand release within a single light-driven platform remains challenging because cargo capture and release are often coupled to the same propulsion mechanism. Here, we report visible-light-driven hematite–titania (α-Fe2O3/TiO2) Janus micromotors that decouple cargo capture and cargo release through photocatalytically generated phoretic interactions and magnetic actuation. Under blue-light illumination, the micromotors exhibit autonomous propulsion with speeds up to 8.5 μm s–1 while operating at a low hydrogen peroxide concentration of only 0.5% (v/v). The micromotors enable repeated cargo pickup, transport, selective collection from mixed particle populations, and on-demand cargo release, while a single micromotor can simultaneously transport more than 15 silica microparticles. Importantly, magnetic-field-induced micromotor reorientation triggers cargo release without interrupting propulsion or altering the chemical environment. Numerical simulations support the proposed phoretic cargo-capture mechanism, while high-speed imaging and repeated release experiments provide complementary evidence for the magnetically triggered cargo-release strategy and its high repeatability. By independently controlling cargo capture and cargo release through complementary photocatalytic and magnetic mechanisms, this work establishes a versatile strategy for programmable microscale cargo manipulation.

items.title: Sub-Monolayer Core-Shell Engineering of PbS Quantum Dots for High-Efficiency, High-Radiance Solution-Processed Short-Wave Infrared Light-Emitting Diodes
items.abstract: Abstract Short-wave infrared (SWIR) light-emitting diodes (LEDs) are indispensable for next-generation biomedical imaging and optical communication systems. Colloidal quantum dots (QDs) provide a versatile material platform for SWIR optoelectronics owing to their low-temperature solution processing, bandgap tunability, and compatibility with diverse substrates. However, realizing high-performance LEDs from narrow-bandgap QDs is hindered by the intrinsic efficiency–radiance trade-off in conventional architectures. Advanced blend device architectures, while enabling strong carrier confinement and high peak external quantum efficiencies (EQEs) at low current densities, suffer from pronounced efficiency droop and limited radiance under high injection. To address these challenges, we introduce sub-monolayer core–shell engineering within a binary QD blend framework. Through in situ cation exchange, epitaxial CdS shells of sub-ångström thickness were precisely grown on PbS cores, enabling independent tuning of shell coverage for both matrix (M) and emitter (E) QDs. This strategy simultaneously enhances surface passivation and preserves efficient matrix-to-emitter charge transfer. Optimized shell engineering achieved a peak EQE of 8.08% and a maximum radiance of 16.26 W sr–1 m–2, representing 12% and 55% improvements, respectively, over state-of-the-art binary blend designs. Furthermore, operational stability was extended 3.5-fold relative to shell-free controls. This simultaneous optimization of efficiency, brightness, and durability establishes a viable pathway toward high-performance, solution-processed SWIR light sources for practical applications.

items.title: NIR-Activated ROS/NO Cascade Nanocomposite Rewires Bacterial Redox Defense for Synergistic Eradication of Pseudomonas aeruginosa Wound Infection
items.abstract: Abstract Pseudomonas aeruginosa wound infections remain difficult to eradicate because biofilm formation and bacterial redox-adaptive defenses weaken antibacterial efficacy and delay tissue repair. In this study, we reported a near-infrared (NIR)-activated reactive oxygen species (ROS)/ nitric oxide (NO) cascade nanocomposite, UCeSi-L@CA, designed to amplify oxidative/nitrosative antibacterial stress while promoting infected wound healing. UCeSi-L@CA was constructed from Ce6-loaded mesoporous silica-coated upconversion nanoparticles, with L-arginine conjugated through surface carboxyl groups and cinnamaldehyde loaded into the mesopores. Upon NIR irradiation, upconversion nanoparticles activated Ce6 to generate abundant ROS. Cinnamaldehyde exerted direct antibacterial activity and inhibited glutathione-mediated ROS scavenging, thereby sustaining ROS accumulation and weakening bacterial antioxidant defense. The accumulated ROS further triggered NO production from L-arginine, establishing a ROS/NO cascade in which ROS and NO cooperatively damaged bacterial membranes, enhanced lipid peroxidation, and induced efficient bacterial killing. Beyond antibacterial activity, NO also contributed to infected tissue repair. In vitro, UCeSi-L@CA + NIR showed excellent killing against planktonic P. aeruginosa, effectively inhibited biofilm formation, eradicated bacteria within established biofilms, and suppressed biofilm regrowth. In the P. aeruginosa-infected wound model, UCeSi-L@CA + NIR markedly reduced local bacterial burden, attenuated infection-associated inflammation, accelerated wound closure, and promoted tissue repair, with favorable biocompatibility in vitro and in vivo. This nanocomposite presents a non-antibiotic nanotherapeutic strategy integrating NIR-triggered ROS generation, cinnamaldehyde-mediated GSH-defense inhibition, and L-arginine-derived NO release for treating refractory biofilm-associated wound infections.

items.title: Dual-State Tumor-Activated RNA Delivery for Tumor-Selective and Precision Therapy
items.abstract: Abstract RNA therapeutics hold transformative potential for precision oncology; however, their systemic application remains constrained by a fundamental tradeoff between prolonged circulation stability and efficient intracellular activation. Conventional polyethylene glycol (PEG)-based carriers provide antifouling protection but lack tumor responsiveness, resulting in limited tumor accumulation and suboptimal gene expression. In this study, we developed a nanosystem, the dual-state tumor-activated RNA platform (D-STAR), which enables a dynamic transition from a stealth circulatory state to an activated transfection state through stepwise environmental alternation by recognizing a narrow pH window. At physiological pH, D-STAR maintains a negative surface potential to minimize nonspecific interactions and extend its blood circulation. Within the tumor microenvironment and endo-/lysosomal compartments, progressive protonation induces charge reversal and strengthens cationic activation, thereby enhancing tumor retention, cellular uptake, and cytoplasmic mRNA release. The systemic administration of D-STAR enabled tumor-selective mRNA expression with limited off-target organ distribution and markedly enhanced intratumoral reporter activity compared with PEG-based controls. The therapeutic delivery of human neutrophil elastase mRNA suppressed tumor growth and prolonged survival in a CT26 syngeneic model without systemic toxicity. Collectively, D-STAR establishes a dual-state adaptive RNA delivery framework that decouples systemic stability from activation potency, thereby offering a generalizable strategy for context-responsive precision RNA therapeutics.

items.title: Iron Site Evolution in Fe-MFI Zeolite under Thermal Treatment: Spectroscopic Insights and Acetone Vapor Interactions
items.abstract: Abstract Iron-containing MFI zeolites (Fe-MFI) and purely siliceous MFI were compared to assess the structural and electronic effects of iron incorporation. Powder X-ray diffraction confirms that the MFI framework is preserved after Fe introduction during synthesis. UV–vis and 57Fe Mössbauer spectroscopy show that iron is mainly present as Fe3+ in distorted [5]/[6]-coordinated and octahedral environments. In the as-synthesized material, Fe3+ accounts for ∼88% of the total iron, accompanied by a minor Fe2+ fraction (13%). After calcination, Fe2+ is fully oxidized to Fe3+ and redistributed nearly equally between distorted and octahedral sites. Nitrogen physisorption indicates a moderate loss of microporosity due to the partial pore occupation by FeOx species. Overall, Fe incorporation generates dispersed Fe3+ centers and small extra-framework FeOx species that subtly modify the structural and electronic properties of the MFI zeolite. These powders were incorporated into a membrane for acetone vapor detection, the Fe-MFI membrane showing a stronger and more distinct response to acetone exposure than the pure MFI membrane. In summary, this study establishes Fe-MFI membranes as promising active materials for acetone vapor interaction, providing a robust proof-of-concept for future gas-sensing applications. The key novelty of this work is the direct correlation between the calcination-induced redistribution of iron sites and the resulting vapor-sensing performance of the membrane.

items.title: Stage-Associated Efficacy of Systemically Administered Neural Stem Cell-Derived Exosomes in Ischemic Stroke through the Prevention of Cx43 Degradation
items.abstract: Abstract Ischemic stroke pathology is highly dynamic, making the optimal timing for biological interventions highly elusive. This study investigated the stage-associated therapeutic efficacy of neural stem cell-derived exosomes (NSC-Exos) for cerebral ischemia–reperfusion. The in vivo evaluations identified a restricted therapeutic window closely associated with the temporal evolution of the ischemic microenvironment. Early exosome intervention (4 or 24 h post-ischemia) significantly reduced infarct volume, restored blood–brain barrier integrity, and improved neurological functional recovery. In contrast, delayed administration (48 h) failed to reduce the mortality rate and provide meaningful neuroprotection. To examine the molecular basis of this time dependence, we integrated temporal proteomic profiling of the ischemic penumbra with small RNA sequencing of NSC-Exos. The analytical and functional data suggest that early NSC-Exo delivery transfers miR-9-5p to suppress Nedd4 expression, thereby restoring the Connexin 43 protein pool and stabilizing the astrocytic network to halt initial microenvironmental collapse. Collectively, this study underscores the critical importance of intervention timing and provides a potential translational strategy for utilizing NSC-Exos as a targeted, stage-specific therapy in acute ischemic stroke.

items.title: Direct Regeneration of Spent Graphite Electrodes Using an Organic Solvent-Free Approach: Evaluation of Aqueous- and Rapid Thermal Processing-Assisted Black Mass Delamination
items.abstract: Abstract Sustainable recycling of graphite anodes is critical for enabling closed-loop lithium-ion battery manufacturing, yet most direct recycling methods rely on organic solvents and corrosive acid treatments that increase costs and environmental impacts. Herein, we evaluate an organic solvent-free, direct recycling strategy that combines aqueous graphite recovery with boric acid-assisted regeneration. Water-based delamination of graphite black mass was investigated using two representative commercial end-of-life graphite anodes and a commercially manufactured uncycled graphite anode. The effectiveness of aqueous separation of the black mass from the Cu current collector was investigated along with rapid thermal processing (RTP), which has been proposed to improve graphite recovery through binder degradation. Both methods resulted in effective graphite recovery despite impurities originating from ceramic-coated separators, Ti-containing additives, and current collector corrosion. However, delamination of RTP-treated spent anodes was more difficult than pristine anodes, requiring pre-RTP washing and ultrasonication for efficient graphite recovery. Boric acid treatment followed by calcination at 1050 °C increased the degree of graphitization for all spent graphite samples while removing residual surface species and trapped lithium. Electrochemical testing showed that the regenerated graphite largely recovered its capacity and electrochemical activity, although residual metallic impurities may limit long-term cycling stability. Overall, aqueous delamination combined with boric acid-assisted regeneration provides an effective and more sustainable route for graphite recycling by eliminating organic solvents and strong mineral acids while preserving favorable structural and electrochemical properties. This process offers a promising pathway for scalable, environmentally responsible recovery of graphite from end-of-life lithium-ion batteries.

items.title: Advanced Thermoelectric Power Modules Employing n -Type Ag2Se Synthesized via a Sustainable Route
items.abstract: Abstract Thermoelectric (TE) Ag2Se was synthesized via an energy-efficient, solution-based chemical synthesis route with microwave-assisted heating and compacted by sustainable cold pressing. Structural and TE transport property analyses confirmed a highly crystalline microstructure that promotes high electrical conductivity, a large Seebeck coefficient, and low thermal conductivity, yielding a peak TE figure of merit (ZT) of ∼0.85 at room temperature. To evaluate device-level performance, Ag2Se was employed as the n-type TE leg in modules paired with Sb1.5Bi0.5Te3 (ZT ∼1.1 at 325 K) as the complementary p-type TE leg. Both rigid and flexible modules, each containing 58 thermocouple pairs, were fabricated and benchmarked against a commercial TEC1-12706 module. The rigid module exhibited more than four times the maximum power output of the commercial reference, highlighting the promise of Ag2Se for low-temperature TE power applications. Cooling performance tests demonstrated the critical influence of electrical configuration. Series-connected rigid modules achieved the lowest cold-side temperatures at lower input power, reaching ∼2 °C at 18 W, comparable to or exceeding the cooling performance of the commercial device. In contrast, parallel-connected modules exhibited stronger initial cooling but were hindered by excessive current draw, Joule heating, and thermal instability, preventing stable saturation. Increasing input power would enhance cooling performance until saturation limits were reached. These results emphasize the importance of module architecture and thermal management for optimizing TE device performance. Overall, this work establishes Ag2Se as a promising alternative to conventional Bi-Sb-Te-based n-type materials, demonstrating versatility in both rigid and flexible TE modules for energy harvesting and cooling technologies.

items.title: Wet-Adhesive Hydrogel Patch for Sustained Oral Ulcer Treatment
items.abstract: Abstract Oral ulcers are a common mucosal disorder that causes persistent pain and significantly impairs quality of life for patients. Current therapeutic approaches, including sprays and commercial patches, provide only temporary relief, as the complex, dynamic, and moist oral environment hinders prolonged retention and drug efficacy. Here, we report the rational design of a multifunctional hydrogel adhesive that integrates poly(acrylic acid) (PAA) for hydrogen bonding, polyamidoamine-epichlorohydrin (PAE) for electrostatic interactions with mucosal surfaces, and poly(methyl methacrylate) (PMMA) for swelling resistance. The resulting hydrogel exhibits an instant wet tissue adhesion strength of ∼40 kPa and enhances adhesion after prolonged immersion in phosphate-buffered saline (PBS). Remarkably, it retains high adhesion strength under extreme conditions, such as hypertonic and strongly acidic environments. When loaded with dexamethasone acetate, the hydrogel enables controlled drug release, significantly improving therapeutic outcomes in a rat oral ulcer model. By ensuring prolonged retention and effective drug delivery, this hydrogel patch offers a promising strategy for enhancing oral ulcer treatment.

items.title: Ionic-Liquid-Based Engineering of MOF Membranes: Tuning from H2- to CO2-Selective
items.abstract: Abstract Reprogramming the transport preference of crystalline membranes offers a useful strategy for adapting a single membrane platform to different gas-separation tasks. Herein, we report ionic liquid (IL) engineering of pure ZIF-8 membranes to switch H2/CO2 transport from H2- to CO2-preferential behavior. A continuous ZIF-8 membrane was first fabricated on an anodic aluminum oxide support by cathodic deposition, followed by the loading of an IL of type 1-butyl-3-methylimidazolium bis(trifluoromethylsulfonyl)imide ([BMIM][TFSI]). The compact, well-intergrown, and crystalline ZIF-8 membrane was preserved after IL incorporation, and vibrational spectroscopy provided evidence for molecular interactions between confined [BMIM][TFSI] and the ZIF-8 framework. Gas-permeation measurements revealed that increasing IL loading decreased both H2 and CO2 permeances, indicating an increased transport resistance caused by partial pore occupation. However, the H2 permeance decreased significantly more rapidly than the CO2 permeance. The H2/CO2 selectivity decreased from 3.6 for the pristine ZIF-8 membrane to approximately 0.3 at 15 vol % ionic-liquid loading, corresponding to a CO2/H2 selectivity close to 3. The separation reversal originates from the combined effects of IL-induced pore narrowing and preferential CO2 affinity. This work demonstrates that confined ILs can reprogram adsorption–diffusion coupling in MOF membranes and provides a route toward process-adaptive gas-separation membranes.

items.title: Muscle-Inspired Micro/Nanofiber Composites via Flow-Assigned Hierarchical Alignment
items.abstract: Abstract Plastic accumulation and microplastic exposure have increased the demand for renewable lightweight materials. Lignocellulosic fibers are promising alternatives for acoustic diaphragms, paper-based packaging, and automotive interiors. However, their practical application is limited by the inherent trade-off between low density and mechanical performance, with most high-strength composites relying on densification or additional reinforcing phases that compromise lightweight characteristics. Here, inspired by the multiscale alignment of human muscle, we develop an oriented lignocellulose micro/nanofiber composite (O-LMU) through a flow-field-assisted assembly strategy. This approach enables the construction of a highly ordered multiscale fiber architecture coupled with optimized nanoscale interfaces. Multiscale simulations reveal that optimized interfacial interactions and hierarchical fiber alignment promote hydrogen-bond network reconstruction, mitigate stress concentration, and facilitate efficient load transfer within the fiber network. Therefore, O-LMU achieves a low density of 0.71 g·cm–3, a specific strength of 205 kN·m·kg–1, a tensile stiffness of 2245 kN·m–1, and a toughness of 394 J·m–2. Notably, O-LMU exhibits a specific strength that is 2.4 times that of the lignocellulosic nanofiber film. The material can be recycled by aqueous disintegration and biodegrades under natural soil conditions. This work establishes a structure-driven strategy for designing lightweight, strong, and sustainable lignocellulosic materials beyond conventional densification-based reinforcement approaches.

items.title: Pendant Engineering of Covalent Organic Frameworks for Photocatalytic Hydroperoxide Production
items.abstract: Abstract Covalent organic frameworks (COFs) have attracted much attention for their potential in photocatalytic hydrogen peroxide (H2O2) production. However, traditional COFs often suffer from sluggish charge transfer kinetics and a lack of highly electron-localized sites for O2 adsorption, leading to inefficient photocatalytic activity. Herein, we report a pore-channel electronic engineering strategy that introduces highly electron-localized cores into the pore channels of COFs by the regulation of heterocyclic pendants. The cores located in the channel of COFs acted as electron-rich active sites, enabling enhanced charge separation for photocatalytic H2O2 production. The polar furan groups were introduced onto the cores, further forming a powerful built-in electric field and hydrogen bond network within the channels, thereby accelerating the transport of electrons and protons. The furan-grafted COF (O-COF) showed a photocatalytic H2O2 production rate of 15,378 µmol h–1 g–1, with a yield 1.5–2.4 times higher than that of its counterparts. This work provides a valuable reference for the precise electronic regulation of pore channels in COFs to enhance photocatalytic performances.

items.title: Self-assembled Carbon Nanotube/Extracellular Matrix Hydrogel as a Promising Matrix for Organoid Growth and Functional Maturation
items.abstract: Abstract Organoids are three-dimensional, self-organized structures derived from tissue-specific cells that recapitulate key architectural and functional features of native tissues in vitro. Current organoid culture systems primarily rely on tumor-derived Matrigel, which suffers from batch-to-batch variability, high cost, and safety concerns, thereby limiting reproducibility and clinical translation. Notably, existing natural and synthetic polymeric hydrogels have not simultaneously supported efficient organoid formation and functional maturation comparable to Matrigel. Here, we present an improved composite hydrogel composed of carbon nanotubes (CNTs) and porcine small intestinal submucosa extracellular matrix (SIS-ECM) as a versatile and biologically active promising alternative matrix for organoid culture. We demonstrate its broad applicability by successfully culturing adult stem cell-derived mouse intestinal organoids (mIOs), human intestinal organoids (hIOs), and human embryonic stem cell-derived vascular organoids (hVOs). Organoids grown within the CNT-SIS-ECM hydrogel exhibited formation efficiency, structural integrity, and functional maturation comparable to, and in certain aspects exceeding, those cultured in Matrigel, underscoring their advantages for transplantation-oriented applications. Mechanistic investigations revealed that CNT incorporation provides instructive bioactive cues that promote organoid development, including upregulation of high mobility group box 1 (Hmgb1), which enhances mIO proliferation and differentiation. Additionally, CNTs augment the WNT signaling pathway, thereby facilitating hVO growth and vascular maturation. Together, these findings establish the CNT/SIS-ECM composite hydrogel as a promising matrix alternative that supports organoid formation and maturation across multiple lineages, offering a practical platform for organoid-based research and tissue regeneration.

items.title: Molecular Functionalization Tunes Twist Angles of MoS2 Moiré Superlattices for Surface-Enhanced Raman Scattering
items.abstract: Abstract In the quest for surface-enhanced Raman spectroscopy (SERS) substrates without noble metals, transition-metal dichalcogenides (TMDs) have emerged as an important class of alternatives. In this regard, molybdenum disulfide (MoS2)-based SERS substrates have been extensively studied; however, their moiré superlattices (with controlled twist angles) could be potent candidates for significant signal enhancement. Here, we employed a molecular functionalization method using 4-aminothiophenol (4-ATP) as a linker to tune the twist angles of MoS2 moiré superlattices. Transmission electron microscopy (TEM) and Raman spectroscopy experiments confirmed the formation of moiré patterns in 4-ATP functionalized MoS2 (4ATP-MoS2), with reduced twist angles in contrast to pristine MoS2 superlattices. Furthermore, we used 4ATP-MoS2 moiré superlattices as SERS substrates to probe molecules, such as rhodamine 6G, rhodamine B, methylene blue, and crystal violet. We observed significant enhancement of Raman signal intensity (on the order of 105) for all the molecules. Interestingly, pristine MoS2 did not show any significant enhancements of the SERS signals. We attribute the enhancement to the moiré interface-induced charge transfer from MoS2 to the probe molecules through 4-ATP, thereby increasing the Raman signals. This strategy could open possibilities to design moiré superlattices for improved SERS substrates and light–matter interactions.

items.title: Enhanced Reliability and Neuromorphic Functionality of a-IGZO-Based Memristors via N2 Annealing-Induced Vacancy Modulation
items.abstract: Abstract Amorphous indium–gallium–zinc oxide (a-IGZO)-based memristors have attracted considerable attention for neuromorphic computing applications owing to their structural uniformity, amorphous-phase stability, CMOS compatibility, and oxygen-vacancy-mediated resistive switching characteristics. However, uncontrolled oxygen-vacancy concentrations can lead to unstable charge transport and switching variability, limiting reliable device operation. In this work, post-deposition N2 annealing was employed to regulate the oxygen-vacancy-related defect states of Pd/HfO2/a-IGZO/HfO2/Pd memristors. The a-IGZO layer was annealed in an N2 atmosphere at 300–600 °C, and the resulting changes in material properties, resistive switching behavior, and synaptic characteristics were systematically investigated. XPS and XRD analyses indicated that N2 annealing decreased the relative oxygen-deficient/defect-related O 1s component while maintaining the amorphous nature of the a-IGZO layer. Among the investigated conditions, the 500 °C-annealed device exhibited the most stable switching behavior, with reduced variation, improved retention and endurance characteristics, and reliable analog conductance modulation. Conduction mechanism analysis revealed that the optimized device maintained stable space-charge-limited current conduction, whereas excessive vacancy reduction at 600 °C promoted a premature transition toward the trap-filled-limit regime, resulting in degraded switching stability. Furthermore, the optimized device successfully emulated long-term potentiation/depression and paired-pulse facilitation, and its measured synaptic characteristics were validated through ANN-based MNIST pattern recognition and PPF-driven neuron circuit simulation. These results demonstrate that N2 annealing-induced oxygen-vacancy engineering is an effective strategy for improving the reliability and neuromorphic applicability of a-IGZO memristors.

items.title: Contrasting Oxygen and Chlorine Evolution Selectivity in Tunnel and Layered MnO2 Electrocatalysts
items.abstract: Abstract Controlling competing oxygen and chlorine evolution is a key challenge in chloride-containing electrolysis, particularly under neutral saline conditions relevant to seawater electrolysis. Here, two phase-pure MnO2 polymorphs with contrasting crystallographic frameworks, α-MnO2 and δ-MnO2, were synthesized through surfactant-free routes and evaluated under comparable conditions. Tetragonal α-MnO2 with a 2 × 2 tunnel framework preferentially promoted oxygen evolution, whereas layered δ-MnO2 favored chlorine evolution. X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy revealed no detectable chlorine signal for α-MnO2 after chlorine evolution, while δ-MnO2 exhibited pronounced chloride-associated surface modification. Electron paramagnetic resonance spectroscopy and density functional theory calculations further revealed distinct defect characteristics and substantially different oxygen-vacancy formation tendencies between the two frameworks. These observations suggest that framework-dependent defect formation influences chloride-associated surface chemistry and contributes to the contrasting oxygen and chlorine evolution selectivity. Importantly, the selectivity trend was retained when the MnO2 phases were integrated onto iridium-ruthenium-based dimensionally stable anodes. These results demonstrate that contrasting crystallographic frameworks and their associated defect characteristics can markedly alter anodic selectivity and provide a structural basis for designing selective electrodes for chloride-containing electrochemical systems.

items.title: Sequential-Photocuring-Assisted Transformation of Planar Multilayer Structures into Curved Geometries
items.abstract: Abstract The integration of functional electronic structures into curved geometries remains challenging, as conventional approaches rely on post-shaping or adhesive-assisted assembly that separate structure formation from shape definition. Here, we present a sequential-photocuring-assisted fabrication strategy that transforms planar multilayer structures into curved forms within a single material system. A wavelength-selective acrylate–epoxy resin is designed to create a deformable intermediate state under visible light, followed by a fixation-enabled final state through UV-triggered curing. A gradient-like curing strategy, involving time-dependent evolution of conversion during sequential irradiation, allows controlled partial epoxy conversion and provides both processability and subsequent reactivity. The second curing step induces simultaneous interfacial bonding and structural stiffening, enabling adhesive-free integration and fixation of the mold-imposed geometry. A multilayer patch antenna operating at 28 GHz is fabricated and transformed from planar to curved geometry while maintaining its performance. This approach provides a material-based framework for integrating planar-fabricated structures into three-dimensional form factors without thermoforming or adhesives.

items.title: Sporoderm-Removed Particles Enhance Oxaliplatin Immunochemotherapy against Colorectal Cancer and Mitigate Neurotoxicity via Dual-Directional PINK1/Parkin Mitophagy
items.abstract: Abstract Oxaliplatin (OXA) is a widely used and effective first-line chemotherapeutic agent for colorectal cancer. However, its therapeutic benefits are often constrained by limited antitumor immune activation and dose-limiting peripheral neurotoxicity. Here, we report that sporoderm-removed particles from Ganoderma lucidum spores (RGLS), a naturally derived bioactive particulate system, orchestrate bidirectional regulation of PINK1/Parkin-mediated mitophagy to simultaneously enhance OXA efficacy and mitigate neurotoxicity. Sporoderm removal remodeled the particle biointerface, improved the hydrophilicity of RGLS, and facilitated the release of bioactive constituents in gastrointestinal fluids, thereby increasing their bioavailability. In tumor tissues, RGLS cooperated with OXA to intensify mitochondrial dysfunction and excessive mitophagy, leading to increased tumor cell death and amplified immunogenic cell death, as indicated by enhanced calreticulin exposure and HMGB1 release. This immunogenic remodeling promoted dendritic cell maturation, increased intratumoral infiltration of CD4+ and CD8+ T cells, and attenuated OXA-induced PD-L1 upregulation, collectively converting immune-cold tumors into immune-hot phenotypes. In contrast, in dorsal root ganglia, RGLS restored OXA-impaired PINK1/Parkin-dependent mitochondrial quality control, reduced mitochondrial reactive oxygen species accumulation, and protected neurons from chemotherapy-induced injury, thereby alleviating peripheral neuropathy. These findings establish sporoderm removal as a biointerface-modulation strategy for transforming Ganoderma lucidum spores into multifunctional therapeutic particles and highlight RGLS as a promising adjuvant platform to improve the therapeutic index of OXA-based colorectal cancer chemotherapy.

items.title: Hydrophilic Zinc Metal-Organic Frameworks with Optimized Lewis Acid Centers for Enhanced Photocatalytic Performance
items.abstract: Abstract Water-stable metal–organic frameworks (MOFs) have emerged as promising porous materials for addressing water pollution challenges, owing to their tailorable structures and unique active sites. However, the regulatory role of metal centers with fully or partially filled d orbitals in interfacial behaviors during advanced oxidation processes remains insufficiently understood, posing a critical barrier to the development of efficient decontamination systems. In this study, we rationally designed and fabricated a series of MOF materials featuring ordered π-conjugated skeletons. These MOFs were constructed using 2-aminoterephthalic acid as the ligand, incorporating diverse metal nodes (Zn, Ti, and Co), and engineering hydrophilic or hydrophobic channels. The tetracycline (TC) degradation efficiencies of these MOFs under visible-light irradiation were systematically compared. By correlating the degradation results with structural characteristics elucidated via X-ray diffraction (XRD), Brunauer-Emmett-Teller (BET) surface area analysis, and X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS), combined with photoelectrochemical measurements, the influence of different metal centers on charge separation efficiency was comprehensively evaluated. The findings reveal that the Zn-MOF exhibits exceptional photocatalytic performance, which originates from the closed-shell d10 electronic configuration of Zn2+. This unique electronic structure confines electrons within the organic linker, effectively suppressing the recombination of photogenerated electron–hole pairs. Furthermore, the incorporation of Zn2+ centers prolongs the lifetime of photoexcited electrons and optimizes the ligand-to-metal charge transfer (LMCT) process, thereby significantly enhancing photocatalytic activity. Radical trapping experiments identified superoxide radicals (•O2−), photogenerated electrons (e−), and holes (h+) as the dominant reactive species involved in the TC degradation process. This work highlights the potential of water-stable MOFs with suppressed charge recombination for applications in various photochemical processes beyond water treatment.

items.title: Roll-to-Roll Fabrication of Large-Area Electrochromic WO3 Films via Slot-Die Coating and Intense Pulsed Light Processing
items.abstract: Abstract Electrochromic tungsten oxide (WO3) films are promising candidates for flexible smart window applications. However, realizing large-area WO3-based electrochromic devices fabricated by low-temperature solution processing remains challenging. Here, we report a roll-to-roll (R2R)-compatible strategy for the fast fabrication of electrochromic WO3 films by synergistically combining an ultrafast intense pulsed light (IPL) process with trace Pt additives acting as light absorbers. Pt-incorporated WO3 (WO3-Pt) films were coated onto flexible substrates and subsequently treated within 10 ms using intense broadband irradiation from a xenon flash lamp. Structural, optical and chemical analyses indicate that the IPL process promotes the photothermal modification of WO3, while the Pt additive significantly enhances photothermal heating efficiency and electronic conductivity of the WO3 films. When integrated into electrochromic devices, the IPL-treated WO3-Pt (WO3-Pt-IPL) films exhibit high optical contrast, accelerated switching kinetics, and enhanced cycling stability compared to bare and IPL-treated WO3 films without Pt. The electrochromic device based on WO3-Pt-IPL film exhibited the highest optical contrast of 61.5% at 550 nm and a coloration efficiency (CE) of 139 cm2 C–1, whereas the devices based on bare WO3, WO3-Pt, and WO3-IPL films showed lower optical contrast values of 55.5%, 59.7%, and 59.3%, respectively, with CE values of around 80 cm2 C–1. In addition, the WO3-Pt-IPL device maintained nearly constant bleached and colored transmittance over 1500 cycles, demonstrating markedly improved cycling stability compared with the other device configurations. We further demonstrate large-area fabrication of WO3 films via R2R slot-die coating combined with IPL processing, achieving excellent spatial uniformity. This approach enables energy-efficient and scalable production of flexible metal oxide films and provides a feasible pathway for tuning charge transport and electrochromic properties in electrochromic materials.

items.title: Issue Editorial Masthead
Issue Publication Information
Biomembrane-Camouflaged Stents: Promising Strategies for Advanced Coronary Interventions
items.abstract: Abstract Coronary stent implantation remains a cornerstone therapy for coronary artery disease, yet current stent technologies continue to face limitations including acute and late thrombosis, delayed re-endothelialization, chronic inflammation, and in-stent restenosis. These complications largely arise from the nonphysiological interface between the implanted device and the injured vascular microenvironment. Biomembrane-camouflaged stents have recently emerged as a promising strategy to engineer biologically instructive blood-contacting surfaces by integrating natural or artificial membrane systems onto stent platforms. In this review, we summarize recent advances in three major biomembrane-based strategies for coronary stent functionalization: cell membrane-camouflaged stents, liposome-camouflaged stents, and exosome-camouflaged stents. Biomimetic cell membrane coatings retain native bioactive signals that collectively facilitate immune evasion, thromboresistance, and vascular healing. Liposome-based coatings are tunable artificial biomembrane reservoirs for the localized delivery of anticoagulants, anti-inflammatories, nitric oxide releasers, antiproliferatives, and gene therapies. Exosome-functionalized stents further enable bioactive intercellular communication by transferring endogenous regulatory cargos that modulate endothelial regeneration, macrophage polarization, smooth muscle cell phenotype, oxidative stress, and neointimal remodeling. We further discuss fabrication approaches, biological mechanisms, preclinical evidence, translational barriers, and future design principles for these platforms. Although challenges remain in coating durability, sterilization, long-term storage, manufacturing reproducibility, and clinical validation, biomembrane-camouflaged stents represent a compelling direction for next-generation coronary intervention by transforming conventional stents from passive mechanical scaffolds into active regulators of vascular repair.

items.title: Robust Anomalous Hall Effect in Epitaxial Cubic D03-Fe3Ge Nanoplates Grown via Chemical Vapor Deposition
items.abstract: Abstract Iron-based ferromagnetic materials have emerged as a promising system for spintronics due to their high Curie temperatures and the significant anomalous Hall effect (AHE) driven by Berry curvature. While there have been investigations into the epitaxial growth of nonlayered iron-based ferromagnetic materials, the realization of high-quality single crystal thin films continues to be a formidable obstacle. Meanwhile, issues such as grain boundary scattering further hinder their characterization and application. Here, we report the first chemical vapor deposition synthesis of single-crystalline cubic D03-Fe3Ge nanoplates. This compound represents a substantial departure from the conventional hexagonal phases typically observed in the Fe–Ge system. Structural characterizations confirm the cubic lattice and the stoichiometric purity of the crystals. Structural analysis identifies a strong epitaxial effect, resulting in a giant compressive strain of ∼4.16% at the interface that relaxes gradually toward the surface. The second-harmonic generation signals might further reveal that such interfacial strain disrupted the inherent centrosymmetry of the cubic phase. Superconducting quantum interference device magnetometry shows robust room-temperature ferromagnetism and clear magnetic anisotropy. Magneto-transport measurements reveal a robust AHE that remains stable at temperatures far exceeding the room temperature. The scaling observed between the anomalous Hall resistance and longitudinal resistance strongly suggests that this effect is dominated by the intrinsic Berry curvature mechanism. Furthermore, density functional theory calculations reveal that the huge epitaxial strain induces band reconstructions and creates dense spin–orbit coupling gaps near the Fermi level, effectively doubling the anomalous Hall conductivity to match our experimental observations.

items.title: Reprotonation Kinetics Engineering of Aramid Nanofiber Hydrogel Electrolytes for Aqueous Zinc-Ion Batteries
items.abstract: Abstract Aqueous zinc-ion batteries are promising next-generation energy-storage systems owing to their intrinsic safety and cost-effectiveness. However, dendrite formation and parasitic reactions at Zn metal anodes limit long-term cycling stability. Here, aramid nanofiber (ANF) hydrogel electrolytes are engineered by controlling the acid identity and solution pH during reprotonation. These variables regulate reprotonation kinetics, thereby shaping hydrogen-bond formation, molecular ordering, and the through-thickness morphology of the ANF network. The selected ANF hydrogel electrolyte exhibits a Young’s modulus of 1.1 MPa while maintaining an ionic conductivity of 30.8 mS cm–1. Its mechanically robust and ionically conductive network promotes compact Zn deposition and resists dendrite penetration. Consequently, Zn||Zn symmetric cells sustain stable plating/stripping for over 2000 h at 1.0 mA cm–2 with an areal capacity of 1.0 mAh cm–2. Compared with conventional glass-fiber-based cells, Zn||hydrated vanadium oxide full cells also exhibit improved high-rate capacity retention and retain over 88% of their initial capacity after 2000 cycles at 1.0 A g–1. These findings establish reprotonation kinetics as a practical design parameter for balancing mechanical robustness, ion transport, and interfacial stability in hydrogel electrolytes for durable aqueous zinc-ion batteries.

items.title: Hierarchical Lead-Free Cs–Cu–I Multilayers Fabricated by Vacuum Molten Salt Deposition for Hydrochromic and Spectrally Multiplexed Optical Encryption
items.abstract: Abstract Optical security labels are the front line of product authentication, yet mainstream photoluminescent tags emit a static, single-color signal that is easily replicated. Lead-free ternary copper halides of the Cs–Cu–I system combine nontoxicity and air stability with bright luminescence arising from self-trapped excitons. In solution processing, the lack of solvent orthogonality makes it difficult to stack CsCu2I3 and Cs3Cu2I5 layers within a single device. Here, we adapt the molten salt evaporation concept, previously developed for lead-halide perovskite photovoltaics, to the Cs–Cu–I system through a vacuum molten salt deposition strategy. Premixed CsI and CuI form a homogeneous molten source that mitigates the disparate volatilities of the two precursors and enables compositionally coupled evaporation. Phase-selective X-ray diffraction, X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy, and optical characterization confirm that the 1:2 and 3:2 sources yield the targeted one-dimensional (1D) CsCu2I3 and 0D Cs3Cu2I5 films, respectively. Because the process is solvent-free, the two phases can be deposited sequentially between transparent PDMS spacers to form an encapsulated PDMS/CsCu2I3/PDMS/Cs3Cu2I5/PDMS core, and adding a spatially patterned, unencapsulated Cs3Cu2I5 dynamic layer on top yields an integrated label that combines three independent security primitives. First, macroscopic transparency provides physical stealth, revealing nothing to the naked eye. Second, spectral gating with 325 nm excitation and a 510 nm long-pass filter unmasks the yellow CsCu2I3 pattern beneath the intense blue Cs3Cu2I5 emission. Third, moisture triggers a reversible 0D-to-1D phase conversion of the dynamic layer that executes a localized bit-flip in the optical code. A standalone unencapsulated Cs3Cu2I5 film and the integrated label remain stable for 200 days in ambient air, the dynamic layer withstands 20 hydration–dehydration cycles, and the encapsulated core withstands 20 days of water immersion. By combining solvent-free, phase-selective deposition with multistimulus optical encoding, this work provides a lead-free multilayer platform for optical encryption.

items.title: Harnessing a Light-Activated Ruthenium(II) Complex Self-Delivery Nanoplatform for Tumor–Organelle Cascade-Targeted Immunotherapy via Type II Immunogenic Cell Death
items.abstract: Abstract Immunogenic cell death (ICD) converts immunosuppressive “cold” tumors into immunogenic “hot” ones, yet ICD inducers with precise tumor–organelle cascade targeting and spatiotemporal controllability remain largely unexplored. Herein, we report a self-delivery nanoplatform (ER-Ru NPs) constructed via the self-assembly of well-defined tumor–endoplasmic reticulum (ER) cascade-targeting ruthenium(II) complexes. The intrinsic amphiphilicity enables self-assembly of the ruthenium(II) complexes into stabilized nanoparticles with efficient tumor accumulation properties via biotin-mediated active targeting, without any exogenous carriers. Following cellular internalization, the released ruthenium(II) complex monomer specifically accumulates in the ER to generate a cleaved Ru–H2O anticancer agent and in situ reactive oxygen species (ROS) upon red-light irradiation. The robust ROS burst triggers severe ER stress via activation of the PERK/eIF2α pathway, leading to the release of damage-associated molecular patterns and the type II ICD induction. Notably, this cascade-targeted ICD activation strategy enhances not only tumor specificity but also the immunogenicity of dying tumor cells, achieving effective primary tumor ablation in the 4T1 models and simultaneously suppressing distant tumors through dendritic cell maturation, cytotoxic T-cell infiltration, and memory T-cell generation. This study offers a paradigm for photoactivatable, self-delivery ICD inducers with cascade targeting, holding substantial promise for clinical translation in precision cancer immunotherapy.

items.title: Enhancing Proton Conductivity in the Ce0.9Gd0.1O2–δ Electrolyte for Low-Temperature SOFCs via Surface Doping with a Cobalt Oxide Redox Mediator
items.abstract: Abstract Developing oxide electrolytes with high ionic conductivity (∼0.1 S cm–1) at temperatures below 600 °C is essential for next-generation solid oxide fuel cells. However, current electrolyte materials rarely meet this benchmark, primarily because of limitations inherent in bulk doping and high-temperature sintering. To overcome this challenge, we demonstrate a surface engineering strategy that involves controlled cobalt doping onto the acid-etched surface of gadolinium-doped ceria (Ce0.9Gd0.1O2–δ, GDC), thereby constructing a Co3+/Co2+ redox mediator. The 3 mol% cobalt-surface-doped GDC (GDC-Co3) electrolyte exhibits optimal ionic transport behavior, achieving an ionic conductivity of 0.153 S cm–1 at 500 °C and a 30% improvement over pristine GDC (0.118 S cm–1), while simultaneously reducing the activation energy from 0.64 eV to 0.36 eV. X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) and multi-wavelength Raman spectroscopy reveal that Co2+/Co3+ redox pairs are introduced onto the surfaces of GDC particles through doping with different Co(II)/GDC molar ratios. The formation of a Schottky junction, as evidenced by a rectifying effect, effectively prevents electron leakage across the electrolyte. Electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS), combined with distribution of relaxation times (DRT) analysis, indicates that ionic conductivity is strongly correlated with electronic conductivity. These results collectively support a mechanism where surface-localized Co2+/Co3+ redox pairs act as mediators for the Ce4+/Ce3+ couples in GDC, establishing favorable surface pathways for proton transport via an alternating interstitial proton-hydrogen hopping process. The accompanying reduction in electrode polarization resistance suggests that accelerated interfacial reaction kinetics may also contribute to the improved cell performance, alongside enhanced proton transport. This work presents an innovative surface engineering approach that significantly enhances proton transport in fluorite oxide materials, with important implications for low-temperature solid oxide electrochemical devices.

items.title: Polymerization-Pathway-Dependent Zwitterionic Hydrogels for Time-Gated Information Encryption and Irreversible Optical Erasure
items.abstract: Abstract Chameleon-like adaptive coloration inspires dynamic information camouflage, yet translating temporally programmable optical behavior into synthetic soft materials remains challenging. Here, we develop a zwitterionic pVS hydrogel for time-gated information encryption, decryption, and irreversible optical erasure. The system uses the established alkali-responsive fluorescence of VPES-derived units as the optical basis, while the SBMA-rich zwitterionic network suppresses swelling and preserves pattern fidelity. Spatially separated UV- and thermally initiated polymerization pathways generate domains with distinct initial emission states and alkaline-response trajectories within the hydrogel, allowing polymerization history to function as an intrinsic optical key. Quantitative kinetic analysis reveals progressive fluorescence convergence between the UV- and thermally initiated domains, with the red-emission contrast decreasing from 0.667 to 0.012 during prolonged alkaline treatment and preventing subsequent recovery of QR-code readability after acid treatment. This convergence establishes an operational time window for information security: short alkaline exposure produces a recoverable encrypted state, whereas excessive exposure permanently eliminates the optical contrast required for QR-code recognition, resulting in irreversible information self-destruction. This work provides a kinetically controlled hydrogel strategy for transient information protection and time-limited optical authentication.

items.title: Polarization Modulation in Core–Shell Halloysite Nanotubes@Sulfides for Broadband Electromagnetic Wave Absorption
items.abstract: Abstract Polarization modulation is an effective approach for developing electromagnetic wave (EMW) absorbing materials. However, it is still a challenge to enhance the polarization performance of composites by adjusting the components. Herein, a series of core–shell halloysite nanotubes (HNTs)@sulfides are synthesized via one-step hydrothermal treatment. The sulfide-modified composites have excellent dielectric loss and polarization loss, resulting in favorable EMW absorption performance. Among them, HNTs@MoS2 has an effective absorption bandwidth (EAB) of up to 6.02 GHz at a thickness of 2.12 mm. This paper proposes a technical strategy for achieving polarization modulation to develop efficient EMW absorbing materials.

items.title: Manipulation of the Nanoarchitecture of Porous Media Determines Water Mobility: NMR Experiments using Metal–Organic Framework (MOF)-Functionalized Track-Etched Solid-State Nanochannels (SSNs)
items.abstract: Abstract Transport in hierarchically porous membranes depends on pore organization at the mesoscale, yet how this organization shapes local dynamics remains poorly understood. Herein, we employ single-sided nuclear magnetic resonance (SS-NMR) to probe the in situ diffusion dynamics of water within solid-state nanochannels (SSNs) functionalized with UiO-66 metal–organic framework (MOF). We systematically compare two distinct synthetic protocols: a one-pot (OP) interfacial growth and a counter-diffusion (CD) method. By deconvoluting the NMR signal attenuation, we isolate a minor slow diffusion component corresponding to intraparticle micropores and a dominant fast diffusion component representing interparticle constructional porosity. Our results show that OP growth produces large particle agglomerates and poorly connected pores with narrow bottlenecks, forcing water along highly tortuous paths. Furthermore, leveraging the pH-responsive surface charge of UiO-66, we find that water mobility in the well-connected CD nanoarchitecture varies measurably with pH, consistent with a surface-charge effect, whereas OP membranes show a weaker, nonmonotonic variation, consistent with dominant geometric obstruction. These findings link nanochannel architecture directly to local water mobility and identify constructional porosity as a structural parameter to consider in MOF-based nanofluidic membranes.

items.title: Controlled Edge-Mediated Photoelectrochemical Thinning and Patterning of Transition Metal Dichalcogenides
items.abstract: Abstract Transition metal dichalcogenides (TMDs) are widely investigated for electrochemical and photoelectrochemical energy conversion applications, yet the oxidation processes that govern their stability in reactive electrolytes remain poorly understood. Here, we systematically compare dark electrochemical and illuminated photoelectrochemical anodic etching and thinning of mechanically exfoliated MoS2, WS2, MoSe2, and WSe2 flakes as a function of applied potential, electrolyte pH, irradiance, and oxidation time. In the dark, oxidation initiates at defect-rich flake edges and produces lateral etching without appreciable basal-plane thinning. The oxidation peak potentials exhibit significantly different pH dependences for sulfide- and selenide-based TMDs, revealing chalcogen-dependent oxidation chemistry and kinetics. Under illumination, an additional oxidation regime emerges at lower anodic potentials, in which multilayer n-type MoS2, WS2, and MoSe2 undergo vertical thinning with minimal lateral etching, whereas no thinning is observed for p-type WSe2. This observation, together with strong suppression of thinning by sacrificial hole acceptors, indicates that photogenerated holes accumulated in the upper layers of n-type TMDs drive a photoelectrochemical self-oxidation process. Tuning the bias, irradiance, and oxidation time enables controlled conversion of initially nonuniform multilayer flakes into homogeneous few-layer structures, while focused laser excitation yields spatially localized thinning and patterning. In addition to elucidating stability windows and oxidation mechanisms of TMD photoelectrodes, these results provide a versatile strategy for controllably tuning the thickness and morphology of layered semiconductors.

items.title: La Doping Imparts Bifunctional Interfacial Catalysis for Dehydrolactonization of 1,6-Hexanediol
items.abstract: Abstract The dehydrolactonization of 1,6-hexanediol (1,6-HDO) to ε-caprolactone (ε-CL) requires a catalyst capable of cooperatively catalyzing two distinct half-reactions, namely dehydrogenation and cyclization. However, conventional catalysts lack the electronically asymmetric sites needed to drive both steps efficiently. Herein, a bifunctional Cu+–Ov–Ce3+ interfacial frustrated Lewis pair (FLP) is constructed by loading Cu onto La doping CeO2. La doping introduces additional oxygen vacancies (Ov) and Ce3+ species, thereby enriching the Ov–Ce3+ sites. Systematic characterizations (XPS, EPR, XAS, TPD, in situ FTIR) combined with DFT calculations reveal that Cu+ sites are responsible for α-H elimination to form 6-hydroxyhexanal (6-HA), whereas the cyclization reaction is driven by the FLP composed of Ov–Ce3+ and adjacent lattice oxygen. La incorporation lowers the energy barrier and enhances FLP formation. Under optimized conditions (3 wt % La, 280 °C, weight hourly space velocity of 1.5 h–1), a ε-CL yield of 61.17% is achieved with good stability over 120 h. From these findings, the interfacial bifunctional mechanism is clearly elucidated, and a defect engineering strategy for decoupling interfacial components is demonstrated, providing a rational approach to the design of multifunctional catalysts for tandem reactions.

items.title: Interface Engineering of Hydrated Tungsten Oxide via Carbon Nitride for Durable Electrochromic Energy Storage
items.abstract: Abstract Electrochromic smart windows demand high optical contrast, fast switching, long-term durability, and charge-storage functionality, yet hydrated tungsten oxides suffer from restricted ion transport and structural degradation during repeated ion insertion/extraction. Here, we present a carbon nitride-driven phase transformation strategy for a durable energy-storing electrochromic hydrated tungsten oxide. Under mild hydrogen annealing, orthorhombic WO3·H2O nanoplates containing an optimized 10 wt % carbon nitride (CNx) selectively transform into predominantly hexagonal WO3·0.33H2O nanorods (∼80%), accompanied by a relatively minor orthorhombic fraction (∼20%). The CNx promotes structural rearrangement while providing nitrogen-rich Li+-interactive sites that regulate interfacial ion transport and improve electrochemical reversibility. Supported by density functional theory, impedance, diffusion, and postcycling analyses, the optimized WHX-CNx10% film shows favorable Li+ insertion, improved charge-transfer kinetics, and excellent structural retention. The air spray-coated film in 3-electrode system delivers 57% optical modulation at 650 nm, coloration/bleaching times of 2.9/0.6 s, stable cycling over 20,000 cycles, and an areal capacitance of 16.9 mF/cm2. A 5 × 5 cm2 device further exhibits optical modulation of 52% at 650 nm with a coloration efficiency of ∼156 cm2/C. These results establish CNx-mediated phase and interface engineering as an effective route toward scalable, durable, and energy-storing electrochromic smart windows.

items.title: ROS-Responsive Hydrogel for Spatiotemporal Cascade Regulation of Ferroptosis and Fibrosis for Myocardial Protection
items.abstract: Abstract Myocardial infarction (MI)-induced cardiac injury is mainly divided into two phases: the acute necrotic phase and the repair phase. Given the distinct therapeutic requirements of each phase—salvaging dying cardiomyocytes and reducing infarct size in the acute phase, while achieving controlled fibrosis to promote effective ventricular remodeling in the repair phase—we designed an ROS-responsive hydrogel co-delivery system (Met/Anti-34a@Gel) loaded with metformin (Met) and Anti-34a liposomes (Anti-34a Lip) to achieve precise regulation of both the acute and repair phases of MI. In the highly oxidative stress microenvironment following MI, the hydrogel gradually degrades and releases Met and Anti-34a Lip in a stage-specific manner. Met improves mitochondrial function, inhibits oxidative stress and ferroptosis, thereby effectively salvaging cardiomyocytes in the acute phase. Anti-34a Lip modulates the differentiation behavior of cardiac fibroblasts, suppressing excessive fibrosis and promoting favorable ventricular remodeling in the repair phase. Echocardiography revealed that Met/Anti-34a@Gel preserved left ventricular ejection fraction (EF) and fractional shortening (FS) at 72 h post-MI, reduced serum MDA levels in the acute phase, and maintained EF at approximately 60.92 ± 8.37% with a lower collagen I/III ratio at 4 weeks, collectively demonstrating both acute cardioprotection and long-term anti-fibrotic remodeling. In this combined therapeutic strategy, the early mitochondrial protection and anti-ferroptosis effects establish a favorable tissue and functional foundation for subsequent precision anti-fibrotic therapy, while the later anti-fibrotic treatment further consolidates the early protective effects. The two actions synergistically form a positive feedback loop, ultimately achieving sustained long-term cardiac functional improvement.

items.title: Digitally Printed Gold Nanoelectronics for Tap-to-Detect Electrochemical Biosensing and Chemical Sensing
items.abstract: Abstract Printed electrochemical sensors offer a promising route toward decentralized diagnostics and environmental monitoring, but their practical use remains constrained by complex electrode fabrication and instrument-dependent readout. Here, we present a tap-to-detect sensing platform that couples digitally printed gold nanoparticle nanoelectronics with a battery-free near-field communication (NFC) potentiostat. Single-pass digital materials deposition enables direct fabrication of ready-to-use AuNP working/counter electrodes and AgNP reference electrodes on a flexible polyimide substrate, producing mechanically robust and electrochemically reliable devices. The NFC potentiostat provides smartphone-based wireless voltammetric readout with performance comparable to a commercial potentiostat. As proof of versatility, the printed AuNP electrode is applied to two distinct sensing modes: the thiol-mediated aptamer functionalization enables label-free HER2 biosensing with a detection limit of 4.87 pg mL–1 and successful analysis in spiked human serum, while the intrinsic Au–As interaction enables direct As(III) detection with a detection limit of 42.5 ng mL–1, without additional electrode modification. This digitally printed, smartphone-readable gold nanoelectronic platform provides a scalable pathway toward portable electrochemical sensing for healthcare and environmental applications.

items.title: Hollow Silica Nanoparticles with Tunable Morphology and Porosity
items.abstract: Abstract Hollow silica nanoparticles (HSNPs) are promising nanomaterials for applications such as antireflection coatings, catalysis, and gas separation membranes. Their hollow cores and tunable porosity provide a unique combination of a low refractive index, a high surface area, and selective transport properties. However, precise control of the structure of HSNPs remains challenging because the formation pathways are highly sensitive to synthesis conditions. We systematically examine the influence of poly(acrylic acid) (PAA), tetraethyl orthosilicate (TEOS), and ammonia concentrations on particle morphology to gain insight into the mechanisms governing the formation of HSNPs. Distinct regimes of nanospheres, nanochains, and aggregates are identified, with the core size and shell thickness of nanospheres independently governed by the concentrations of PAA and TEOS. Increasing the PAA/TEOS ratio promotes the formation of nanochains with higher aspect ratios and increased porosity.
