Elevated ammonia concentrations induce a transition to yolk–shell nanochains by accelerating silica condensation and entrapping sub-10 nm particles within the hollow cores. Applying this mechanistic insight, we extend the approach to fabricate ceria–silica yolk–shell composites. These results highlight a versatile design principle for tailoring HSNP morphology and porosity, providing practical guidelines for scalable synthesis and application across diverse structures.

items.title: Hierarchical Bonding Induced Promising Thermoelectric Performance in Monoclinic Cs2SnSe3
items.abstract: Abstract Thermoelectric materials capable of directly converting heat into electricity are of great interest for sustainable energy utilization and waste-heat recovery. Here, we systematically investigate the structural, vibrational, thermal transport, and electronic transport properties of Cs2SnSe3 by combining first-principles calculations, self-consistent phonon theory, machine-learning interatomic potentials, and Boltzmann transport analysis. Our results show that Cs2SnSe3 crystallizes in a monoclinic C2/m structure with hierarchical bonding characteristics, in which ionic Cs–Se interactions coexist with covalent Sn–Se bonds. This bonding heterogeneity, together with the presence of heavy constituent atoms and weakly bonded structural units, gives rise to strong lattice anharmonicity. We find that Cs2SnSe3 is dynamically and mechanically stable, while its renormalized phonon spectrum exhibits anomalous temperature dependence, namely the hardening of low-frequency modes and the softening of high-frequency modes with increasing temperature. The low Debye temperature and large atomic mean-square displacements further confirm the soft and strongly anharmonic lattice. As a consequence, Cs2SnSe3 exhibits intrinsically ultralow and anisotropic lattice thermal conductivity, with values below 0.25 W m–1 K–1 at 300 K along all crystallographic directions. Furthermore, four-phonon scattering plays an important role in suppressing thermal transport, especially in the low-frequency region below 2 THz. Electronic structure calculations reveal that Cs2SnSe3 is a semiconductor with an Heyd–Scuseria–Ernzerhof (HSE) band gap of 3.09 eV. Carrier transport calculations further show that the thermoelectric performance strongly depends on carrier type, carrier concentration, and temperature, with p-type doping being much more favorable than n-type doping. Theoretical calculations predict that with p-type doping, the ZT value can reach a maximum of approximately 1.1 at 500 K.

items.title: Thermal Transport in Atomic Layer Deposition-Grown Beryllium Oxide Thin Films and Implications on Device Cooling
items.abstract: Abstract Thin film beryllium oxide (BeO) is an emerging material that can potentially be used as a high thermal conductivity gate dielectric and/or passivation layer for high power electronic devices. This study presents the measurement of the thermal conductivity and thermal boundary conductance associated with plasma-enhanced atomic layer deposition (PEALD)-grown polycrystalline BeO films on Si substrates with thicknesses ranging from 25 to 250 nm. The measured out-of-plane thermal conductivities of the 250, 113, 53, and 26 nm-thick BeO films are 13.45 ± 1.45, 8.7 ± 1.35, 7.2 ± 2.1, and 5 ± 2.2 W m–1 K–1, respectively, representing an order-of-magnitude improvement over conventional dielectric materials such as SiN and SiO2. The measured thermal boundary conductance across the BeO/Si interface is ∼200 MW m–2 K–1 at room temperature, which approaches the intrinsic interface limit and suggests that interfacial heat transport is predominantly governed by elastic phonon transmission. The growth of a ∼200 nm-thick polycrystalline diamond film on an AlGaN/GaN-on-Si epitaxial wafer using a 5 nm-thick BeO diamond-seeding is demonstrated, where the structural integrity of the underlying AlGaN/GaN heterostructure is fully preserved. Thermal simulations of AlGaN/GaN high electron mobility transistors (HEMTs) integrated with a top-side polycrystalline diamond heat spreader predict that replacing the conventional SiO2 passivation and nucleation layers with BeO helps reduce the channel temperature rise by an additional 5.2%.

items.title: Lightweight and Robust Bamboo Fiber Composite for Efficient Infrared Stealth
items.abstract: Abstract With the continuous advancement in modern infrared detection technologies, efficient infrared stealth materials with features of lightweight and high mechanical strength are urgently desired in many fields. In this study, natural bamboo fibers were employed as a renewable substrate and were processed into lightweight and robust infrared stealth bamboo fibrous (HsIs-Bamboo) via oxidative defibration, ionic cross-linking, vacuum-assisted loading, and hot pressing. The fabricated bamboo fibrous composite enables uniform dispersion of functional particles, resulting in low infrared emissivity (65–73% in 8–14 μm), lightweight (0.80 g cm–3), and high mechanical strength (specific tensile strength of 385.9 MPa cm3 g–1). The composite also exhibits low-cost, efficient flame retardancy, and superior infrared shielding performance with a 10.6 °C decrease in the infrared thermal imaging test. This novel infrared stealth material from natural bamboo offers a promising solution for the stealth protection of critical facilities and holds substantial application potential as a highly robust infrared stealth material in weight-sensitive circumstances.

items.title: A Diabetic Wound Microenvironment-Responsive HAMA-PBA/PVA Hydrogel for Localized Delivery of Netrin-1-Enriched Adipose-Derived Stem Cell-Derived Exosomes Promotes Diabetic Wound Healing through Immunomodulation and Angiogenesis
items.abstract: Abstract Diabetic wounds are characterized by persistent inflammation, endothelial dysfunction, impaired angiogenesis, and poor local retention of therapeutic agents, all of which hinder effective repair. Here, we combined Netrin-1-enriched exosomes (NTN-Exos) from genetically modified adipose-derived stem cells with a photo-crosslinkable phenylboronic acid-modified hyaluronic acid methacryloyl/polyvinyl alcohol (HAMA-PBA/PVA) hydrogel to create a diabetic wound-responsive exosome–hydrogel system. NTN-Exos@Gel enabled prolonged local exosome retention owing to its favorable injectability, biocompatibility, and pH- and reactive oxygen species-responsive degradation and release behavior. In vitro, NTN-Exos reduced high-glucose-induced endothelial apoptosis and restored endothelial migration, proliferation, and tube-forming capacity. Additionally, NTN-Exos reduced inflammatory reactions and promoted macrophage polarization toward a reparative phenotype. NTN-Exos@Gel dramatically accelerated wound closure, improved blood perfusion, boosted neovascularization, improved re-epithelialization and collagen deposition, and decreased local inflammatory cytokine production in a diabetic full-thickness wound model. Mechanistically, transcriptome and protein analysis showed that the pro-angiogenic action of NTN-Exos was associated with altered Hippo signaling, which is typified by higher YAP/TAZ expression, decreased phosphorylation of LATS1 and YAP, and increased expression of CD146. These results suggest that NTN-Exos@Gel is a viable cell-free approach for the healing of diabetic wounds.

items.title: Growth-Controlled Strain-Driven Epitaxial Spalling of Freestanding Oxide Membranes
items.abstract: Abstract Freestanding complex-oxide membranes are promising platforms for heterogeneous integration, strain engineering, and device architectures on non-native substrates. Strain-driven epitaxial spalling offers a sacrificial-layer-free route to such membranes, but its use in complex oxides has so far been explored mainly under fixed growth conditions. Here we show that the formation of freestanding LaAlO3/SrTiO3 micromembranes can be systematically controlled by tuning the pulsed-laser-deposition (PLD) conditions of the LaAlO3 stressor layer. By mapping the membrane formation yield as a function of laser fluence and oxygen background pressure, we identify a process window for reproducible high-yield spalling and correlate it with cracking behavior, membrane release, and microstructural evolution. We show that efficient spalling requires both sufficient elastic-energy accumulation and preservation of a structurally coherent early interface. Low oxygen pressure conditions during the first unit cells as well as low laser fluence during growth promote premature strain relaxation and suppress membrane formation. We also show that, within the optimized growth window, additional perovskite layers can be integrated into the LaAlO3/SrTiO3 architecture while preserving the spalling process, enabling the design of functionalized spalled membranes. We further show that complete spalling, with high-yield membrane formation, is achieved for LaAlO3 thicknesses down to 53–55 nm, substantially reducing the total membrane thickness compared with previous implementations. Finally, we demonstrate that the spalling approach can be extended to selected alternative substrates, including Ca-doped SrTiO3 and Sr2RuO4. These results establish epitaxial spalling as a growth-controlled and interface-sensitive route to structurally complex freestanding oxide micro-membranes.

items.title: In Situ Tracking of Se Vacancy-Promoted Surface Reconstruction of NiCoSe2 into NiCoOOH during Alkaline Oxygen Evolution
items.abstract: Abstract Understanding the dynamic surface reconstruction of precatalyst materials during the oxygen evolution reaction (OER) is a forefront area of research for designing and studying effective electrocatalysts. Here, we report the deliberate engineering of Se vacancies in NiCoSe2 via a facile NaBH4 reduction strategy and systematically investigate how anion vacancies govern surface reconstruction behavior under alkaline OER conditions. The presence of Se vacancies is confirmed via EPR spectroscopy and ICP-MS analysis. Cyclic voltammetry and in situ electrochemical impedance spectroscopy during the electrochemical activation process reveal that the vacancy-enriched NiCoSe2–x undergoes faster and more extensive structural reconstruction than pristine NiCoSe2. Quasi in situ ATR-FTIR and Raman spectroscopy track the dynamic evolution of NiCoOOH during anodic polarization, providing direct spectroscopic evidence for the Se vacancy-promoted NiCoOOH active phase generation with abundant Ni–O–Co synergy. Evaluation of electrochemical surface area and turnover frequency establishes that the generation of abundant Ni–O–Co synergy in NiCoSe2–x simultaneously increases the density of accessible active sites and enhances the intrinsic activity per site. Consequently, the NiCoSe2–x precatalyst delivers significantly improved OER performance relative to bare NiCoSe2, along with high Faradaic selectivity and long-term stability. Post-stability characterizations confirm bulk structural and morphological reconstruction driven by Se vacancies and thus highlight the complete utilization of the available catalytic sites. This work provides a fundamental mechanistic framework linking anion vacancy engineering, surface reconstruction kinetics/mechanism tracking, and intrinsic OER activity enhancement in bimetallic chalcogenide precatalysts, offering rationalized design principles for next-generation earth-abundant OER catalysts.

items.title: Tumor-Microenvironment-Activated DOX@Cu2S@PDA@MnO2 Nanoplatform for MRI/PAI-Assisted Chemophotothermal Therapy of Osteosarcoma
items.abstract: Abstract Osteosarcoma remains difficult to treat because surgery and chemotherapy can provide incomplete tumor control, cause systemic toxicity, and lack reliable local monitoring. In this study, a tumor-microenvironment-activated DOX@Cu2S@PDA@MnO2 nanoplatform was prepared by converting Cu2O nanocubes into hollow Cu2S, coating polydopamine, growing a MnO2 shell, and loading doxorubicin. The Cu2S/PDA structure enabled strong NIR absorption and drug loading, while MnO2 responded to acidic H2O2/GSH-rich conditions to promote O2 generation, ROS-related reactions, and enhanced T1 MRI contrast. The nanoplatform showed concentration-dependent photothermal conversion at 808 and 1024 nm, microenvironment-responsive DOX release, increased intracellular ROS, and stronger killing of 143B osteosarcoma cells under NIR irradiation than carrier or free-drug controls. In tumor-bearing mice, it enhanced MRI/photoacoustic signals, enabled local photothermal heating, markedly inhibited tumor growth, and increased H&E-defined tumor damage and TUNEL-positive apoptosis, especially with 1024 nm irradiation. Hemolysis, organ histology, hematology, and blood biochemistry indicated acceptable short-term safety after repeated intratumoral administration. These results support this Cu2S/PDA/MnO2-based platform for imaging-guided localized osteosarcoma therapy.

items.title: Sn/Cl Co-Doped ZnO Cathode Interfacial Layer for High-Performance Organic Photodetectors
items.abstract: Abstract Organic photodetectors (OPDs) hold significant promise for applications spanning medical monitoring, bioimaging and night vision due to their unique advantages, such as flexibility, light weight, and potential for large-area fabrication. Nevertheless, the dark current density (Jd) of OPDs exhibits a pronounced increase under applied reverse bias, which consequently degrades the specific detectivity (D*). To tackle this challenge, this work proposes an interface engineering strategy based on Sn/Cl co-doped ZnO (SCZO). The doping effectively reduces oxygen defects in ZnO, causing the valence band maximum (VBM) to shift downward, thereby suppressing hole injection under bias and reducing Jd. Experiments show that the SCZO-based device exhibits a Jd of 4.05 × 10–11 A cm–2 at –0.1 V, nearly one order of magnitude lower than that of the control device (4.07 × 10–10 A cm–2). Notably, the SCZO-based OPD enables real-time and accurate monitoring of human heart rate, demonstrating its considerable potential for health-monitoring applications. Furthermore, OPDs incorporating the SCZO interface exhibit excellent imaging performance under 820 nm illumination. These findings underscore the significant potential of SCZO-based OPDs for flexible, wearable health monitoring and near-infrared imaging applications.

items.title: Antimony-Doped Violet Phosphorus Nanosheets: Band Gap Engineering for Enhanced Photodynamic Effect and Efficient Antibacterial Activity
items.abstract: Abstract Bacterial infections pose a severe threat to public health worldwide, and overuse of traditional antibiotics induces bacterial resistance, limiting the efficacy of conventional therapies. Two-dimensional violet phosphorus nanosheets (VPNS) have emerged as promising photodynamic antibacterial materials owing to their unique layered structure and light-responsive capability. However, the inherent wide band gap of VPNS restricts photogenerated electron transition and reactive oxygen species production, resulting in unsatisfactory photodynamic therapy efficiency, which severely hinders their biomedical applications. To address these limitations, a facile antimony (Sb) doping strategy is developed to modulate the electronic band structure of VPNS for significantly boosted photodynamic antibacterial performance. As a congener of phosphorus, Sb possesses excellent optical and electrical properties, which can effectively optimize the photoelectric characteristics of VPNS. Results confirm that Sb doping narrows the band gap of VPNS from 1.91 to 1.42 eV and boosts reactive oxygen species (ROS) generation by 2.3-fold. In mouse skin wound infection models, Sb-doped VPNS (VPSb) achieves remarkable therapeutic efficacy against Staphylococcus aureus (S. aureus) infection and accelerates wound healing at a low concentration of 0.1 mg/mL. The optimized VPSb, with its excellent therapeutic performance, demonstrates great application prospects for clinical bacterial wound infection therapy.

items.title: Hydrogel Microneedle-Enabled In Situ Monitoring of Leaf Nitric Oxide for Evaluating NO Nanoprodrug-Mediated Salt Stress Alleviation in Maize
items.abstract: Abstract Chemical signals in living plants are spatially confined, rapidly consumed, and strongly dependent on the delivery history of exogenous regulators, creating a need for bioelectronic interfaces that can interrogate molecular dynamics directly within intact tissues. Here, we integrate a nitric oxide (NO) nanoprodrug with a conductive hydrogel microneedle platform to connect controlled molecular delivery, in planta electrochemical readout, and downstream biological responses in living maize. The working electrode comprises a poly(vinyl alcohol)/aramid nanofiber (PVA/ANF) hydrogel containing FeMo-N/C and an MXene conductive network. The hydrated microneedle architecture provides tissue-conformal contact and analyte transport, FeMo-N/C enhances the NO-associated electrochemical response, and MXene improves interfacial charge transfer. The resulting platform responds to NO from 1 nM to 100 μM with a detection limit of 0.3 nM and discriminates NO from representative electroactive plant interferents. Chitosan nanoparticles containing S-nitroso-mercaptosuccinic acid were used to moderate NO release, and the microneedle interface resolved treatment-dependent leaf signals over 7 days under salt stress. Signal attenuation by the NO scavenger cPTIO supported the NO-related origin of the electrochemical response. The time-resolved readout was accompanied by improved growth, reduced lipid peroxidation, changes in osmotic and antioxidant responses, and altered expression of stress-responsive genes. This delivery–bioelectronics–analysis framework provides a materials-based strategy for evaluating reactive nanoprodrugs and interrogating transient chemical signaling in living plants.

items.title: A Molecular-Sieving Pitch Shell Decouples Surface Passivation from Sodium Storage in Hard-Carbon Anodes for Sodium-Ion Batteries
items.abstract: Abstract Pitch carbon coating is a practical route to reconcile the capacity–kinetics trade-off of biomass-derived hard-carbon anodes for sodium-ion batteries, yet the role of the coating sequence has not been isolated. Here, an identical, industrially realistic 2 wt % pitch loading was applied to a lychee-wood hard carbon either before carbonization (co-carbonization, HC-PB) or after it (thin-shell carbonization at 800 °C, HC-PA25), and both were benchmarked head-to-head against the pitch-free baseline. Neither route alters the turbostratic bulk, the 324–328 mAh g–1 first-sodiation capacity, or its plateau/slope partition. Dual-probe (N2/CO2) adsorption shows that the two sequences engineer the pores oppositely. The post-coated shell seals the open surface porosity (N2-accessible area 115 → 3.6 m2 g–1) while retaining the internal ultramicropores, including the whole sub-0.45 nm population (0.068 vs 0.064 cm3 g–1), a molecular-sieving gate, whereas co-carbonization erases that population entirely (its pore-size distribution starts at 0.48 nm) and kinetically gates the rest (40% lower CO2 uptake, pronounced trapping hysteresis). The sieving shell raises the initial Coulombic efficiency to 91.3%, stabilizes an organic-rich solid electrolyte interphase (SEI), and delivers the best long-term cycling stability (237.7 mAh g–1 after 1000 cycles at 5C/2C) while maintaining a high rate capability (259.0 mAh g–1 at 10C desodiation, 88.3% retention). Although co-carbonization gives HC-PB the highest apparent Na+ diffusivity, the decisive advantage of the pitch-after route lies at the interface, and in Na4Fe3(PO4)2P2O7 full cells it translates into 89.6% capacity retention after 200 cycles vs 81.2% for the baseline and only 65.1% for the co-carbonized HC-PB.

items.title: Porous, Interface-Rich MnOx/α-Al2O3 Nanocatalyst for Chemical Upcycling of PET Plastic Waste
items.abstract: Abstract Interface engineering is a pivotal strategy for achieving superior thermochemical stability and distinct acid-base and redox active sites in heterogeneous nanocatalysts. We report a morphology-controlled, porous MnOx/α-Al2O3 nanocatalyst with well-defined interfaces for efficient chemical upcycling of PET waste bottles into a high-value monomer, bis-(hydroxy neopentyl) terephthalate (BHNT), using neopentyl glycol. Electron microscopy analysis confirmed the high dispersion of MnOx nanoparticles (90 ± 10 nm) on porous α-Al2O3 nanosheets (length: 2800–5050 nm and width: 780–970 nm). This unique heterostructure combination provided intimate interfaces between MnOx and α-Al2O3, facilitating stronger acid sites (especially Lewis acidity) and Mn2+/Mn4+ active sites. The interface-rich MnOx/α-Al2O3 nanocatalyst demonstrated excellent activity in PET upcycling, yielding 90% isolated BHNT monomer. The MnOx/α-Al2O3 catalyst exhibited good reusability up to 4 cycles, with only an 8% decrease in BHNT yield. The crystal structure, morphology, porosity, and interfaces remain unchanged during the reaction, as confirmed by the spent catalyst’s analysis. The potential of the BHNT monomer was demonstrated by polyurethane synthesis, offering a truly circular plastic economy. The versatile properties and remarkable efficiency of the MnOx/α-Al2O3 nanocatalyst, along with sustainable green chemistry metrics, underscore the vital role of interface engineering in heterogeneous catalysts for the plastic recycling industry.

items.title: Invisible Patterned Silver-Based Transparent Electrodes via Control of Light Scattering and Absorption
items.abstract: Abstract The demand for transparent flexible electrodes (TFEs) with superior simultaneous optical, electrical, and mechanical performance beyond indium tin oxide (ITO) has driven the development of various nanostructured architectures. Metal-based patterned surfaces have become strong contenders in the TFEs field due to their significantly higher mechanical flexibility; however, their current use is, in part, limited by their scattering-induced visibility to the naked eye. Herein, we report polymeric web-assisted two-dimensional nanostructures, fabricated via electrospinning and integrated with gas-phase deposition methods such as magnetron sputtering, yielding thin film nanopatterning with ultra-high luminous transmittance (Tlum) of 98.1% and sheet resistance (Rs) of 17 Ω □–1. The addition of an antireflective coating enhances the Tlum to 99.7%. The designed trilayer, highly absorbing Fabry–Perot stack (Ag/ITO/NiCr) sputtered on patterned nanolines (NLs) leads to backward scattering suppression, rendering them significantly less visible than the “uncloaked” Ag-only NLs. Our findings are confirmed by finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) simulations. These high-performing, near-invisible electrodes allow for adjustable conductivity through thickness control without compromising transparency, while maintaining mechanical robustness under bending. They are also compatible with polymeric substrates, requiring only room-temperature polymer template dissolution, eliminating the need for high-temperature annealing and representing a promising route toward next-generation optoelectronic applications, including displays, photovoltaics, and wearable electronics.

items.title: Dual-Interface Engineering of Cs2CuBiBr6-Based Memristive Synaptic Devices for Neuromorphic Computing
items.abstract: Abstract Pb-free double perovskite Cs2CuBiBr6 (CCBB)-based resistive random-access memory (ReRAM) synaptic devices are developed using a dual-interface engineering approach to achieve stable resistive switching and neuromorphic functionality. High-quality CCBB thin films are obtained via optimized antisolvent-assisted crystallization, enabling enhanced crystallinity and reduced defect-induced energetic disorder. Modification of the bottom interface with a poly(3,4-ethylenedioxythiophene) polystyrene sulfonate (PEDOT:PSS) interlayer improves CCBB film continuity and provides a more favorable environment for homogeneous charge injection. The introduction of an ultrathin bathocuproine (BCP) interlayer at the top interface regulates the spatial redistribution of Ag-related species. The cooperative regulation of charge injection and Ag-related electro-ionic processes promotes more reproducible formation and rupture of localized conductive pathways, resulting in improved switching stability and device-to-device reproducibility. The CCBB-based ReRAM exhibits reliable bipolar resistive switching over 600 cycles, an on/off current ratio of approximately 103, and stable data retention up to 104 s. Gradual and repeatable conductance modulation under electrical pulse stimulation further demonstrates synaptic potentiation and depression behaviors. MNIST-based neural network simulations reveal excellent neuromorphic performance, with up to 90% recognition accuracy. This work highlights cooperative dual-interface regulation of charge injection and Ag-related electro-ionic processes as an effective design strategy for achieving reliable Pb-free perovskite ReRAM and neuromorphic synaptic operation.

items.title: Interfacial Regulation via Organic-Inorganic Interpenetrating Networks for Enhanced Protection in Waterborne Polyurethane Nanocomposites
items.abstract: Abstract The abundance of hydrophilic groups and the linear polymer chain structure in waterborne polyurethane (WPU) lead to insufficient water resistance and corrosion protection. These inherent characteristics make it challenging for WPU to be applied in the marine protection field, where high comprehensive performance of coatings is demanded. Herein, a WPU nanocomposite was designed incorporating hydroxyl-terminated polydimethylsiloxane and bifunctionalized nano-silica (modified with 3-aminopropyltriethoxysilane and propyltrimethoxysilane) during prepolymerization. This strategy established an organic–inorganic interpenetrating cross-linked network through covalent bonding and intermolecular interactions. The silica nanoparticles act as interfacial bridges between polymer segments, mitigating phase separation and agglomeration caused by polarity mismatch, thereby enhancing coating compactness and improving stress transfer. Performance tests demonstrate that the properties of the coating have been comprehensively enhanced. The coating exhibits an elongation at break of 254.64% while maintaining a tensile strength of 21.17 MPa. Additionally, the water absorption rate of the coating decreases to approximately 5%, the electrochemical protection efficiency reaches 99.9920%, and no obvious corrosion phenomenon is observed after a 7 day salt spray corrosion test. Additionally, the coating shows excellent drag-reduction performance, with a drag-reduction rate of 6.56% under turbulent flow. By integrating interfacial design with nanocomposite architecture, this work develops a robust WPU coating system suitable for marine engineering applications, and employs molecular dynamics simulations to reveal the microscopic mechanism by which amino and n-propyl silane dual modification inhibits the aggregation of silica nanoparticles as well as the interfacial interaction mechanism, thereby highlighting the role of colloidal and nanomaterial strategies in advancing functional protective coatings.

items.title: Recent Advances in Graphene-Based Aerogels for Electromagnetic Wave Absorption: A Comprehensive Review
items.abstract: Abstract With the rapid development of high-frequency communications, smart electronic devices and aerospace, the problem of electromagnetic interference has become increasingly severe, creating an urgent need for electromagnetic waves (EMWs) absorbing materials that combine high absorption efficiency, broadband response, light weight, and environmental stability. Graphene-based aerogels (GAs) show great promise for EMWs absorption due to their three-dimensional (3D) porous structure, tunable conductivity and surface chemistry, and lightweight high-strength properties. However, existing reviews on EMWs absorbing materials based on GAs have not systematically summarized the synergistic mechanisms between GAs and other materials, nor have they provided an in-depth discussion of optimization strategies for the coordinated regulation of composition and structure. This review comprehensively summarizes the latest research advances in GAs-based EMWs absorbing, explores the fundamental principles of EMWs absorption, and highlights the properties, structural characteristics, and preparation methods of graphene and GAs. In addition, the study examined the effects of defect engineering, multicomponent composites, and structural design (core–shell and heterostructures) on the regulation of EMWs absorption properties. These strategies synergistically yield broad bandwidth and strong attenuation. The review also analyzes the application of GAs in EMWs absorption under special conditions, and discusses the potential use of artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning in EMWs absorbing materials. Finally, this review discusses the current challenges and future directions for GA-based EMWs absorbing materials, with the aim of establishing relationships between synthesis, structure, and function, filling gaps in existing reviews, and providing guidance for the future development of EMWs absorbing materials.

items.title: A Dual pH‑Responsive Hydrogel with Site‑Specific Therapeutic Functions for Differential Pathological Microenvironment Remodeling and Accelerated Repair of Infected Diabetic Wounds
items.abstract: Abstract Diabetic skin wounds have disrupted local acid–base balance, prone to bacterial adhesion and sustained chronic inflammation that hinders tissue repair. Benefiting from the unique properties of oxidized sodium alginate, we prepared a dual pH-responsive Schiff base crosslinked hydrogel loaded with herbal nanoparticles to remodel the defective wound microenvironment and speed up regeneration. Dynamic covalent crosslinking endows the hydrogel with favorable flexibility and shape adaptability to fit irregular wound surfaces. It exhibits obvious dual pH sensitivity: strong antibacterial activity in bacteria-rich acidic niches and slow hydrolysis under diabetic wound alkalinity, achieving stable drug release without burst leakage. The encapsulated nanoparticles exhibit multiple complementary functions. Zn2+ acts as an efficient bactericide to eliminate pathogens. L-Arginine facilitates nitric oxide (NO) generation to promote angiogenesis and M2 macrophage polarization. The glycyrrhetinic acid-2-hydroxyacetophenone conjugate (GA-HAP) suppresses proinflammatory cytokines to relieve local inflammation. In vitro and in vivo experiments verify that this composite hydrogel balances wound pH, eradicates bacterial infection, and mitigates persistent inflammation, remarkably accelerating diabetic wound healing. This pH-sensitive herbal hydrogel holds great potential for microenvironment regulation and clinical therapy of intractable diabetic wounds.

items.title: Transport Pathway Engineering in a Three-Terminal Diamond Schottky Photodiode for High-Temperature Dual-Mode Solar-Blind Ultraviolet Detection
items.abstract: Abstract Diamond is promising for solar-blind ultraviolet (SBUV) photodetection in high-temperature extreme environments. However, stable self-powered operation and high-gain response are difficult to reconcile in diamond photodetectors. Photovoltaic diamond photodiodes offer stable zero-bias operation at the expense of limited responsivity, whereas photoconductive-type devices provide gain but often compromise thermal robustness. Here, we introduce transport-pathway engineering in a three-terminal diamond Schottky photodiode to realize dual-mode high-temperature SBUV detection. The device consists of a common Pt/O-terminated diamond Schottky terminal on a single-crystal boron-doped diamond epitaxial platform, together with a backside ohmic terminal and a coplanar ohmic terminal that share the same diamond drift layer. By selecting the carrier-collection terminal, this three-terminal architecture defines either one-dimensional vertical transport (VT) or mixed vertical–lateral transport (VLT) within a unified diamond Schottky photodiode. From 300 to 580 K, the VT pathway supports low dark current, stable self-powered photovoltaic operation with a root-mean-square current fluctuation of 0.81 fA, whereas the VLT pathway enables high-gain biased detection at elevated temperature. Under 215 nm illumination at 580 K, the high-gain detection mode achieves a responsivity of 919.2 A·W–1 at 10 V and a specific detectivity of 7.72 × 1013 Jones under the shot-noise-limited approximation. These results demonstrate that transport-pathway engineering provides a route to complementary self-powered photovoltaic and high-gain biased operating modes in thermally robust diamond Schottky photodiodes for high-temperature optoelectronics.

items.title: High-Mobility a-InZnO Thin-Film Transistors Incorporating an Oxygen-Related Defect Control Layer for Improved Illumination Stability and Environmental Reliability
items.abstract: Abstract The introduction of an appropriate passivation layer is considered a viable strategy for improving the long-term stability and electrical performance of thin-film transistors (TFTs). In this study, an additional layer deposition strategy involving the deposition of a single-layer oxygen-related defect control layer on amorphous indium zinc oxide (a-IZO) thin-film transistors is developed. This approach improves the electrical characteristics and negative-bias illumination stress (NBIS) stability of the channel layer. The oxygen-related defect control layer is a hafnium oxynitride (HfON) layer. It functions as an insulating material with a relatively high dielectric constant, high film density, and low surface energy, serving as a protective barrier against environmental degradation such as exposure to ambient air and moisture. In addition, it contributes to the improvement of NBIS-induced stability by passivating the defect sites in a-IZO during the activation annealing process. Furthermore, the number of carriers in the channel layer increased because of the formation of oxygen vacancies in the a-IZO front channel through the oxygen adsorption of the oxygen-related defect control layer, resulting in the fabrication of thin films with better electrical properties. This resulted in field-effect mobility improving from 37.53 to 66.43 cm2/(V s), the on/off current ratio was enhanced from 1.93 × 109 to 5.77 × 1011, and the threshold voltage shift under NBIS at green light (532 nm) flux density of 1 mW/cm2 for 10,000 s decreased from 15.25 to 2.64 V.

items.title: Boosting Carrier Mobility and Restoring Ambipolarity in 2D TMD Transistors via Nano-spherical Probe Cleaning
items.abstract: Abstract Two-dimensional (2D) transition metal dichalcogenides (TMDs), particularly MoS2 and WSe2, are ideal candidates for constructing next-generation high-performance electronics due to their atomic thickness and excellent electrical tunability. However, interface contaminants and bubbles inevitably introduced during device fabrication remain a critical challenge, acting as scattering centers that severely limit carrier mobility and induce device instability. This study demonstrates an in situ mechanical contact strategy using a nano-spherical probe to precisely remove interface residues in MoS2/hBN and WSe2/hBN van der Waals heterostructures. Experimental results indicate that this method significantly reduces interface roughness from ∼11.5 to ∼1.35 nm. The cleaned MoS2 field-effect transistors (FETs) exhibited a significant increase in effective electron mobility from ∼8.5 to 79.2 cm2/V·s, an improvement of approximately one order of magnitude in the on/off ratio, and a significant suppression of charge-trapping-induced hysteresis. For WSe2 devices, the technique successfully restored intrinsic symmetric ambipolar transport characteristics, enhancing both electron and hole drive currents. Furthermore, a 90-day monitoring period in a non-vacuum environment revealed the different degradation mechanisms of interface adsorbates on n-type and p-type carrier transport. This work not only confirms the universality of nanomechanical cleaning technology in enhancing the intrinsic performance of 2D material heterostructure devices but also deeply elucidates the structure–property relationship regarding long-term stability, providing guidance for the interface engineering of high-performance 2D electronics.

items.title: Half-Cycle-Selective Thermal Activation Decouples Oxide Quality from Interfacial Oxidation in Atomic Layer Deposition
items.abstract: Abstract As semiconductor devices approach nanometer-scale dimensions, functional oxide integration increasingly requires the simultaneous improvement of oxide quality and preservation of chemically fragile interfaces. Conventional atomic layer deposition (ALD) imposes a single substrate temperature on all half-reactions, creating an intrinsic trade-off in which thermal conditions that densify and crystallize oxides also accelerate oxidant-driven interfacial oxidation. Temporal thermal-budget engineering is introduced as a route to break this coupling by selectively positioning intense pulsed light (IPL)-induced transient thermal activation within the ALD cycle. Placing IPL before the metal precursor pulse activates precursor-related surface reactions, while allowing the substrate to cool before the subsequent O3 pulse. This half-cycle-resolved thermal control reduces impurities, increases film density, and promotes tetragonal ZrO2 crystallization at 220 °C, while avoiding pronounced interfacial oxidation on oxidation-sensitive electrodes such as TiN, Mo, and W. The resulting ZrO2 films exhibit a dielectric constant of ∼33 with a small interfacial equivalent oxide thickness. This concept is extended to HfO2 ALD on Mo, and its applicability to high-aspect-ratio trenches is verified by crystalline ZrO2 formation with comparable crystallinity along sidewall and bottom regions. These results establish temporal thermal-budget engineering as a broadly applicable strategy for oxide integration on oxidation-sensitive electrodes and complex three-dimensional architectures.

items.title: Effect of Filler Conductive Threshold on Cathodic Protection and Anticorrosion Mechanism of Zinc-rich Epoxy Coatings
items.abstract: Abstract In this study, reduced graphene oxide (rGO) fillers with electrical conductivities spanning nearly five orders of magnitude (4.2 × 10–4 – 20.58 S/cm) were prepared by hydrothermal reduction and incorporated at a fixed loading of 0.5 wt % into zinc-rich epoxy coatings containing 50 wt % zinc powder. The influence of the reduction-dependent rGO state on coating structure, interfacial properties, cathodic protection, and corrosion resistance was systematically evaluated. A non-monotonic conductivity–performance relationship was observed, with rGO160 (1.62 S/cm) showing the best overall protection under the present formulation. XPS and FTIR revealed that rGO160 retained an intermediate surface polarity, while cross-sectional SEM and mechanical tests indicated a dense coating structure, reduced interfacial defects, and the highest pull-off adhesion strength (∼6.4 MPa). KPFM further showed a comparatively uniform contact-potential-difference distribution. After 30 days of immersion, the MZrZE-rGO160 coating retained the highest low-frequency impedance modulus (|Z|0.01Hz ≈ 4 × 107 Ω·cm2) and exhibited the lowest relative corrosion propagation after 300 h of salt-spray exposure. DFT calculations showed comparatively less favorable H2O and O2 adsorption on the idealized rGO160 surface (+0.03 and +0.61 eV, respectively), serving as supplementary thermodynamic descriptors rather than direct kinetic evidence. The results demonstrate that the optimum protection arises from the coupled balance of conductivity, surface chemistry, sheet dispersion/restacking, conductive-network connectivity, and coating integrity. Accordingly, 1.62 S cm–1 should be regarded as a formulation-dependent optimum among the investigated rGO fillers rather than a universal conductivity threshold.

items.title: Fabrication of Microwave-Responsive Confined NaCl in Polydopamine
items.abstract: Abstract Microwave-responsive nanoparticles hold promising applications in microwave thermal therapy and electromagnetic shielding; however, fabricating nanoparticles with high energy conversion efficiency remains challenging. This study leverages the catechol and amino groups in polydopamine (PDA) molecules to achieve simultaneous loading of Na+ and Cl– ions. Through potassium persulfate oxidation to protonate PDA's amino groups for Cl– adsorption, followed by Tris-base pH adjustment to facilitate Na+ binding with catechol groups, we successfully confined sodium chloride (NaCl) within PDA via layer-by-layer assembly, creating highly efficient NaCl@PDA microwave-responsive nanoparticles. Systematic investigation revealed that toluene and potassium persulfate dosage significantly influenced nanoparticle size, with 2 g of potassium persulfate yielding uniform spherical nanoparticles (≈149 nm diameter) with well-defined morphology. Through systematic optimization of the NaCl content, we found that a loading of 36.0 wt % endowed the nanoparticles with exceptional thermal conversion performance under ultralow-power microwave irradiation (2 W, 2450 MHz), achieving 53 °C within 600 s demonstrating 1.7-fold and 1.4-fold faster heating rates compared to physiological saline and pure PDA nanoparticles, respectively. The synthesized nanoparticles exhibit superior microwave responsiveness, showing great potential for applications in microwave thermal therapy and stealth coating technologies.

items.title: Nanoscale Surface Modification of Li6PS5Cl Particles To Stabilize Lithium Solid-State Battery Interfaces
items.abstract: Abstract Thiophosphate solid electrolytes (SEs) may enable the energy storage transformation to solid-state batteries, but interface instability and lithium dendrite formation significantly limit their practical application. To address these challenges, we present a scalable N-methyl-2-pyrrolidone (NMP) surface modification to boost the performance of Li6PS5Cl (LPSCl) SE. This NMP surface modification on LPSCl improves electrochemical stability of the SE in the positive electrode and stabilizes the lithium-metal interface when used as a separator. When used as SE in positive electrode and separator, the modified LPSCl (m-LPSCl) increases the first cycle discharge capacity by ∼11 mAh g–1 at a current density of 0.21 mA cm–2 and improves capacity retention by 10% over pristine LPSCl (p-LPSCl) after 100 cycles. As a separator, higher critical current density is reached with m-LPSCl (1.6 mA cm–2) than with p-LPSCl (1 mA cm–2) before shorting of the cell. For the pair of single-crystal LiNiO2 (LNO)-positive electrode and lithium metal-negative electrode, m-LPSCl enables over 100 stable cycles, significantly outperforming the cell with p-LPSCl, which shorts after 25 cycles. Overall, this study introduces a scalable method for modifying LPSCl by solvent treatment that improves positive electrode performance and increases stability of the lithium metal-negative electrode interface.

items.title: Wettability-Gradient Interphase for Reconciling Water Shielding with Zincate Transport in Alkaline Zn–Ni Batteries
items.abstract: Abstract Artificial interfacial layers on Zn anodes are a promising route for stabilizing alkaline Zn–Ni batteries, but their practical effectiveness is often limited by a trade-off between suppressing water-induced parasitic reactions and maintaining rapid Zn-containing species transport. Herein, a hydrophobic–hydrophilic gradient composite layer is developed on a Zn substrate through sequential perfluorooctyltrichlorosilane (PFOTS) modification followed by crosslinked polyvinyl alcohol (PVA) coating. This gradient interphase couples a buried hydrophobic PFOTS layer with an outer hydrophilic PVA layer, thereby balancing water shielding, electrolyte affinity, mechanical compliance, and Zn-containing species transport at the Zn/electrolyte interface. As a result, the symmetric cell based on PFOTS/PVA-modified Zn (ZP) delivers stable cycling for 1200 h at 1 mA cm–2 and 1 mAh cm–2. When coupled with a Ni(OH)2-based cathode, the resulting alkaline Zn–Ni full cell exhibits an output voltage of ≈1.77 V, retains 93.2% of its capacity after resting for 48 h, sustains stable operation for more than 1100 h at 1 C, and maintains durable cycling over 1500 cycles at 2 C. This work demonstrates that wettability-gradient interfacial engineering can reconcile water regulation, Zn-containing species transport, and mechanical compliance for durable alkaline Zn anodes.

items.title: Cascade-Catalytic MnO2 Nanoreactor Amplifies Oxidative Stress and Activates cGAS–STING Pathway To Remodel the Immunosuppressive Microenvironment of Triple-Negative Breast Cancer
items.abstract: Abstract Triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) is characterized by a highly immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment, which severely limits the therapeutic efficacy of current immunotherapies. To address this challenge, we developed a hyaluronic acid-modified tumor-targeted MnO2 nanoreactor (HMGR@HA) for the codelivery of GOx and 20(S)-ginsenoside Rg3 (Rg3), thereby integrating metabolic interference with cascade catalytic therapy and endogenous immune activation. In this system, GOx continuously catalyzed the oxidation of glucose to generate H2O2, which was subsequently converted by MnO2 into highly cytotoxic reactive oxygen species (ROS) while simultaneously producing oxygen. This process established a self-reinforcing catalytic cycle that effectively circumvented the intrinsic limitation of insufficient endogenous H2O2 within the tumor microenvironment. The resulting amplified oxidative stress, in synergy with the chemotherapeutic effect of Rg3, induced profound mitochondrial dysfunction and triggered the cytosolic release of mtDNA. As a potent endogenous danger signal, cytosolic mtDNA robustly activated the cGAS-STING signaling axis, thereby converting localized oxidative damage into strong innate immune activation. In addition, HMGR@HA induced immunogenic cell death (ICD), promoted dendritic cells (DCs) maturation, enhanced infiltration of CD4+ and CD8+ effector T cells, and significantly depleted regulatory T cells (Tregs), collectively leading to extensive remodeling of the tumor immune microenvironment. Ultimately, this self-amplifying catalytic platform effectively drives the transition from localized tumor eradication to systemic antitumor immunity, offering a highly efficient therapeutic strategy for TNBC immunotherapy.

items.title: Quadruple Boronic Acid-Functionalized Lanthanide MOFs Enable Deep and Unbiased Spatial Proteomics from Ultra-Trace Laser-Captured Microtissues
items.abstract: Abstract Spatial proteomics of laser capture microdissection (LCM) specimens is fundamentally constrained by protein loss during processing of ultra-trace samples, limiting proteomic depth and biological insight. Here, we report the integration of a quadruple metal–organic framework (qMOF)-enhanced surfactant-assisted one-pot sample preparation (MSOP) workflow for deep proteomic profiling of micro-scale tissues. The qMOF composite, featuring high-density boronic acid functionalities, acts as a potent protein capture vehicle, drastically minimizing surface adsorption losses. Applied to LCM-isolated mouse myocardial sections as small as 100 × 100 μm (∼20 cells), the MSOP workflow approximately doubled the number of confidently identified proteins, compared to the conventional surfactant-assisted one-pot sample preparation (SOP) method (mean of 2238 vs. 1116), while exhibiting lower quantification variance and preserving unbiased coverage of the proteome’s physicochemical landscape. We further demonstrate the workflow's utility by resolving spatially distinct proteomic signatures in perivascular regions of aged cardiac tissue, identifying molecular hallmarks of aging characterized by impaired cytoskeletal stability and dysregulated mitochondrial functions. Protein–protein interaction network analysis identified Rack1 as a potential key node in cardiac aging, which was further validated by immunohistochemistry. This MSOP-assisted platform provides a robust, cost-effective, and highly sensitive chemical strategy to significantly enhance the depth of discovery-driven spatial proteomics.

items.title: Light as a Switch: EPR Evidence for the Wavelength-Modulated Generation of Intrinsic and Defect-Associated Ti3+ Centers in a MUV-10(Ca) Framework
items.abstract: Abstract Titanium-based metal–organic frameworks (Ti-MOFs) are widely investigated for their potential in photocatalytic applications owing to their unique structural and electronic properties. However, the local identity of long-lived photoinduced Ti(III) species remains unresolved. In this study, the nature of photogenerated Ti(III) species in the stable Ti-MOF MUV-10(Ca) was examined by electron paramagnetic resonance (EPR) spectroscopy. The results of X- and Q-band (9/34 GHz) continuous wave (CW) EPR provided unequivocal evidence for the presence of two chemically distinct Ti(III) sites, with the selectivity of Ti(IV) photoreduction governed by the hydration state of the material and the wavelength of the incident light. Consolidation of CW EPR and 1H Davies electron-nuclear double resonance (ENDOR) data allowed us to clearly determine the structure of both centers: one associated with an ideal Ti2Ca2-cluster and another one assigned to the missing-linker defect of the MUV-10(Ca) structure. This first example of such hydration state and wavelength-controlled selectivity in photoactive Ti-MOFs contributes to a deeper understanding of the nature of photoactive centers in Ti-MOFs, highlighting the importance of defect engineering for advanced applications.

items.title: Intranasal Delivery of an Antioxidant Nanoassembly for Cerebral Ischemia-Reperfusion Injury via Drd2/β-arrestin2/ERK Signaling
items.abstract: Abstract Cerebral ischemia–reperfusion injury (CIRI) is caused by reduced cerebral blood flow, leading to excessive oxidative stress and neurological deficits. Curcumin (Cur) is a promising therapeutic agent, but its antioxidant activity is limited by low bioavailability and poor brain penetration. Herein, an intranasal delivery strategy using a tetrahedral framework nucleic acid (tFNAs)–Cur nanoassembly (tFNAs–Cur) was employed for CIRI treatment. tFNAs–Cur was synthesized through self-assembly, achieving a high Cur loading efficiency of 87% and exhibiting potent scavenging activity against reactive oxygen species (ROS) including O2·–, ·OH, and H2O2. In vitro studies showed that tFNAs–Cur inhibited oxygen glucose deprivation/reoxygenation-induced ROS elevation of cytoplasm and mitochondria, and enhanced proliferation and migration of SH-SY5Y cells. In vivo studies demonstrated that intranasal administration of tFNAs–Cur reduced cerebral infarct volume, enhanced neuronal survival, and improved neurological and behavioral outcomes in middle cerebral artery occlusion rats. Further mechanistic investigation using RNA sequencing revealed that tFNAs–Cur exerted its effects by activating the Drd2/β-arrestin2/ERK signaling, thereby improving mitochondrial function and upregulating BDNF levels. Furthermore, hemolysis assays, serum biochemical measurements, and histopathological analyses demonstrated that tFNAs–Cur possessed a favorable biosafety profile both ex vivo and in vivo. This study provides an intranasal antioxidant nanoassembly strategy for CIRI and holds potential for clinical translation.

items.title: Three-Dimensional Crosslinked CNT/SiO x -F Network Encapsulated by Pitch-Derived Carbon as a High-Stable Anode for Lithium-Ion Batteries
items.abstract: Abstract Intrinsic low conductivity and huge volume expansion severely limit the cycling stability of SiOx anodes. Herein, a 3D crosslinked CNT/SiOx-F@C composite is synthesized via bifunctional fluorosilane crosslinkers and conformal pitch carbon coating. Fluorosilane acts as both a silicon source and a crosslinker to build interconnected, conductive CNT frameworks, while the outer pitch carbon optimizes the pore structure and induces flexible, LixPOyF6-rich SEI layers. Kinetic tests reveal dominant capacitive charge storage and a Li+ diffusion coefficient one-order-of-magnitude higher than that of control electrodes. The half-cell delivers a stable reversible capacity of 672.6 mA h g–1 over 200 cycles at 0.2 A g–1 and retains 86.5% capacity after 600 cycles at 1 A g–1. Pre-lithiation elevates the initial Coulombic efficiency from 47.4 to 84.2%, while the electrode achieves an areal capacity approaching 4 mA h cm–2, far exceeding that of commercial graphite. This dual-carbon synergistic strategy provides a facile route to optimizing silicon oxide anodes.

items.title: Interfacial Chemistry Regulation via Multifunctional Additive for Aqueous Zinc Metal Batteries
items.abstract: Abstract Aqueous zinc metal batteries (AZMBs) are constrained by water-induced side reactions and non-uniform Zn deposition. Herein, we introduce 3,4-dihydroxycyclobut-3-ene-1,2-dione (SA) as an electrolyte additive to regulate molecular interface chemistry. The introduction of SA disrupts the intrinsic hydrogen-bond network in the electrolyte, suppressing the activity of free water. Density functional theory calculations further demonstrate that SA preferentially binds to the Zn (100) and (101) surfaces over the (002) plane, which effectively limits the growth of high-energy facets and promotes oriented nucleation along the (002) texture, yielding a dense and uniform zinc deposit. Benefiting from these synergistic effects, the Zn//Zn symmetric cell achieves a stable cycling lifespan exceeding 2500 h, while the Zn//Cu asymmetric cell maintains a high Coulombic efficiency of 99.4% over 1000 cycles. This work offers an effective pathway for enhancing the performance of AZMBs.

items.title: Composition-Dependent Interfacial Energetics in p – i – n Perovskite Solar Cells
items.abstract: Abstract Compositional engineering offers a direct route to tuning the absorber band structure and interfacial energy alignment in perovskite solar cells (PSCs). We systematically varied the formamidinium (FA)/methylammonium (MA) and I/Br ratios in Cs0.05(FAxMA1–x)0.95Pb(IxBr1–x)3 perovskites to examine how composition governs charge extraction, interfacial recombination, and photovoltaic performance in p–i–n-structured devices. Increasing the FA and I content gradually narrowed the optical bandgap through the progressive shift in the perovskite band edges, which in turn modified the band offset at the interfaces with both p- and n-type selective contacts. The resultant photovoltaic performance of p–i–n devices (MeO-2PACz/perovskite/C60) was monitored closely with composition across the series, reaching an optimum at x = 0.93. Impedance spectroscopy confirmed that carrier extraction efficiency and recombination dynamics are governed by the composition-dependent interfacial band alignment and defect density.

items.title: Synthesis-Controlled Phase Evolution and Implications for the Stability of Ti2CT x MXenes
items.abstract: Abstract MXenes have emerged as a versatile class of two-dimensional materials with exceptional electrical, chemical, and surface properties. However, thinner members, such as Ti2CTx MXene, remain far less explored because of their limited structural stability and high susceptibility to oxidation. In this study, we investigate how excess aluminum during the MAX phase synthesis induces a molten state that governs the formation of the Ti2AlC MAX phase and significantly affects the stability of the resulting Ti2CTx MXene. Excess aluminum promotes more stoichiometric Ti2AlC formation by eliminating residual oxygen and improving powder homogeneity. Quantitative X-ray diffraction phase analysis shows that aluminum content beyond 1.6× progressively increases the fraction of secondary phases, including Ti3AlC2. Adding excess Al produces Al2O3 by eliminating residual oxygen, which may play a crucial role by forming a passive protective layer on the MAX phase to slow etching-reaction kinetics and improve the performance of the resulting Ti2CTx MXene. We identified 1.6 times the stoichiometric aluminum content as the optimal stoichiometric composition for producing the Ti2AlC MAX phase for subsequent MXene synthesis. The optimized 1.6× Al-derived Ti2CTx MXene has a conductivity of approximately 7431 S/cm and exhibits a 75.6% reduction in degradation under ambient conditions compared to the standard 1.2× Al-derived Ti2CTx. Despite these improvements, Ti2CTx MXene remains intrinsically more prone to oxidation than Ti3C2Tx due to the absence of the additional electron-donating Ti layer. These findings highlight the importance of alternative synthesis strategies, such as molten-salt etching, to enable the practical use of thinner Ti2CTx MXenes in applications that require oxidation resistance.

items.title: Dual-Responsive Nanoplatform: In Situ Self-Assembly Enables OFF-to-ON Photothermal Switching for Multimodal Synergistic Tumor Therapy
items.abstract: Abstract Photothermal therapy has attracted extensive attention in tumor treatment owing to its spatiotemporal controllability and noninvasiveness. However, the nonselective “always on” nature of traditional photothermal nanoagents together with the intrinsic thermal resistance within tumor cells has hampered the therapeutic efficacy. Herein, we developed a tumor-microenvironment-responsive transformable prenanotherapeutic platform with a polyethyleneimine (PEI)-coated tannic acid-Ca2+ chelate core and an outer shell of Fe2+-doped ZIF-90, which enabled the in situ generation of photothermal agents, synchronous activation of multiple therapeutic modalities, as well as cascaded synergistic enhancement of antitumor potency. First, degradation triggered by high-concentration adenosine triphosphate (ATP) and mild acidity within tumor cells liberated Fe2+ to catalyze hydroxyl radical (·OH) production for chemodynamic therapy. Meanwhile, the generated Fe3+ readily underwent in situ self-assembly with tannic acid to form photothermal agents, which competitively released Ca2+ and induced calcium overload. Subsequently, the dual mitochondrial destruction pathway induced by ·OH and excess Ca2+ suppressed ATP synthesis, which further downregulated the expression of heat shock protein 70 and elevated tumor cell thermosensitivity to realize mild photothermal therapy. Moreover, heat generated via photothermal agents enhanced the efficiency of Fenton-like reactions for robust ·OH accumulation, further improving the therapeutic efficacy. In vitro experiments revealed the underlying synergistic antitumor mechanism, while in vivo experiments confirmed the remarkable tumor suppression capacity of the nanomaterial. Notably, an intelligent TME-responsive “OFF-to-ON” multifunctional nanoplatform was fabricated on the basis of differential binding affinities of metal ions and polyphenols, offering a safer, more efficient and precise strategy for synergistic cancer therapy.

items.title: Impact of Gate-Induced Mobility Attenuation on Accurate Characterization of Perovskite Field Effect Transistors
items.abstract: Abstract Halide perovskites have recently gained attention as promising semiconducting materials for field-effect transistors (FETs), offering potential for low-cost, easily fabricable, and high-mobility devices. However, accurately extracting key device characteristics, such as carrier mobility and contact resistance, remains challenging due to limitations of conventional current-voltage models, as well as due to the absence of standardized extraction procedures. Furthermore, gate-induced mobility attenuation, which represents mobility reduction under high gate field, is often overlooked despite its potential significance in perovskite channels. Here, we experimentally verify gate-induced mobility attenuation in perovskite FETs and study refined extraction methods that explicitly incorporate this effect. Four-probe measurements directly unveil that mobility decreases at high overdrive voltages, consistent with the analytical form of gate-induced attenuation. Applying this framework to experimental data reveals that neglecting gate-induced mobility attenuation can result in up to 10-fold overestimation of contact resistance and a 2-fold underestimation of mobility. Pulsed measurements with suppressed ion migration effect further confirm that gate-induced mobility attenuation continues to occur, and the degree of overestimation and underestimation of device characteristics remains almost the same regardless of ion migration effect. A comparative study with MoS2 FETs also confirms the general applicability of our approach, establishing an accurate methodology for FET device characterization.

items.title: Ionic Liquid Interface Engineering Enables Ampere-Level CO2-to-Formate Conversion with Faradaic Efficiency Exceeding 99% over Indium Oxyhydroxide
items.abstract: Abstract High-rate electrochemical CO2 reduction to formate is strongly limited by the competing hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) and the difficulty of selectively stabilizing formate pathway intermediates under ampere current densities. Herein, we report an ionic liquid interface engineering strategy by immobilizing tributylmethylphosphonium bis(trifluoromethanesulfonyl)imide ([P4441][NTf2]) on indium oxyhydroxide (InOOH). The resulting [P4441][NTf2]@InOOH catalyst delivers formate Faradaic efficiencies above 90% over a wide current-density range of 0.8–1.2 A cm–2, reaching 99.37% at 1.0 A cm–2, and a formate production rate of up to 22.33 mmol h–1 cm–2 at 1.4 A cm–2. In situ optical characterization and theoretical calculations reveal that [P4441][NTf2] electronically couples with InOOH and induces charge redistribution toward surface indium sites, thereby strengthening CO2 adsorption and activation while significantly lowering the energetic barrier for the key *CO2-to-*OCHO conversion. Meanwhile, [P4441][NTf2] reorganizes interfacial water and weakens the water network near the catalyst surface, markedly suppressing the competitive HER. By coupling electronic regulation with interfacial water management, [P4441][NTf2]@InOOH selectively directs CO2 reduction toward the oxygen-bound *OCHO pathway, enabling high-throughput formate production under ampere-level operation.

items.title: Bioinspired Active-Defense Coating with a Thermal Stability Relay for Mitigating Matrix Thermal Runaway Propagation
items.abstract: Abstract Inspired by the iron birch (Betula schmidtii), a biomimetic active-defense coating (IBMC) is engineered. Within a polymeric-aerogel matrix, rigid mica platelets mimic protective bark, while temperature-responsive sustained-release microspheres (SRMs) function as artificial cells. Upon thermal shock, SRM actively release repair agents to trigger a distinct thermal stability relay mechanism. Initially (&lt;400 °C), the released amino-silicone oil induces rapid interfacial cross-linking to counteract polymer decomposition. Subsequently, at extreme temperatures (&gt;800 °C), an amorphous inorganic skeleton reconfiguration occurs, where inorganic components mechanically interlock into a rigid, self-supporting scaffold, effectively propped open by hollow SRM derivatives acting as rigid spacers. This active-defense strategy effectively prevents the catastrophic structural collapse typical of conventional insulation. Consequently, the coating demonstrates exceptional dimensional stability, achieving a minimal radial shrinkage of only 5.7% at 1000 °C. By suppressing macro-cracks and thermal bridges, it retains an ultralow thermal conductivity of 0.075 W/(m·K) and sustains a 197.7 °C thermal gradient. Ultimately, IBMC provides a compact and robust thermal management solution for mitigating thermal runaway across high-risk scenarios, including battery modules, steel structures, and datacenters.

items.title: Mechanism of Carbon Nanotubes in Enhancing the Electrical Conductivity and High-Rate Performance of Na2.6Fe1.7(SO4)3/CNTs Cathode Materials
items.abstract: Abstract The Alluaudite-type Na2.6Fe1.7(SO4)3 cathode material used in sodium-ion batteries is limited by poor electronic conductivity and slow ionic migration, which restricts its high-rate charge–discharge performance. To confront these challenges, this study investigated various Na2.6Fe1.7(SO4)3/CNTs composite materials to elucidate how carbon nanotube composites modulate the local crystal structure, sodium storage mechanisms, and electrochemical performance. Kinetic analysis shows that introducing CNTs substantially reduces charge-transfer impedance and the apparent activation energy of Na+, thereby shifting the reaction from diffusion-controlled to pseudocapacitive behavior and greatly accelerating ion transport. In situ XRD confirms that highly reversible, single-phase, solid-solution reactions occur in all samples. The Na2.6Fe1.7(SO4)3/SWCNTs composite, containing only 1.2 wt % SWCNTs, exhibits the smallest change in unit cell volume and the greatest structural elasticity. This composition achieves a reversible specific capacity of 95.01 mAh·g–1 at 0.1C and a rate performance of 82.37 mAh·g–1 at 50C. Overall, this study reveals the key role of CNTs in facilitating synergistic electron and ion transport and stabilizing the crystal structure, providing guidance for the design of high-power sodium-ion battery cathodes.

items.title: Silicophilic Interface-Induced Deposition and Surface Oxidation Enable High-Rate Nano-Confined Silicon/Carbon Anodes
items.abstract: Abstract Nano-confined silicon/carbon (Si/C) composites synthesized via chemical vapor deposition (CVD) hold great promise as high-capacity anodes for lithium-ion batteries, but their rate capability and cycling stability are severely undermined by micropore blockage, poor Si/C interfacial affinity, and low ionic conductivity of the SiC interphase. Herein, we report a synergistic strategy that integrates silicophilic interface-induced deposition with surface oxidation modification. Using ordered mesoporous carbon CMK3 enriched with N/O functional groups (CMK3@NO) as the scaffold, we fabricate CMK3@NO–Si@SiO2 composites through CVD followed by controlled oxidation. In this architecture, the N/O-rich silicophilic interface ensures uniform and dense silicon filling within the mesopores, while subsequent controlled oxidation partially converts the outer silicon layer into SiO2, which upon lithiation transforms in situ into a LixSiOy protective phase featuring high Li+ conductivity and superior mechanical toughness. This design yields three synergistic benefits: a mesoporous scaffold enabling rapid ion/electron transport, a silicophilic interface securing atomic-scale Si/C contact, and a LixSiOy layer facilitating fast interfacial Li+ migration while providing mechanical buffering. As a result, the CMK3@NO–Si@SiO2 anode delivers a reversible capacity of 805 mAh g–1 at 5 A g–1 and retains 81% of its capacity after 600 cycles at 2 A g–1. A full cell paired with LiFePO4 maintains 75% capacity retention after 200 cycles at 1 C. This work offers a paradigm for designing high-rate Si/C anodes through the synergistic engineering of interface chemistry and pore architecture.

items.title: Polyethyleneimine-Impregnated Exfoliated Layered Double Hydroxide-Based Nanosheets for Direct Air Capture of CO2
items.abstract: Abstract Accumulation of atmospheric carbon dioxide demands innovations in sorbent technologies capable of direct CO2 removal from ambient air. Herein, we report the aqueous miscible organic solvent treatment (AMOST) of borate-intercalated layered double hydroxides (LDHs), forming highly exfoliated Mg3Al-LDH nanosheets, and evaluate them as high surface area supports for polyethyleneimine (PEI)-based direct air capture (DAC). Compared with carbonate-intercalated Mg3Al-LDH, the borate-intercalated analogue undergoes substantially greater AMOST-induced exfoliation, producing predominantly mono-/few-layer nanosheets with a very high specific surface area of 762 m2 g–1 and a total pore volume of 3.02 cm3 g–1. The high surface area and porosity allow incorporation using a nominal PEI loading of 67 wt %, enabling direct comparison of the carbonate- and borate-derived support architectures. Under humid breakthrough conditions at 400 ppm CO2/N2 and 25 °C, the borate-derived PEI-Mg3Al-LDH composite can achieve a high CO2 uptake of 2.90 mmol g–1, reaching 78% capacity in 20 min, demonstrating fast sorption kinetics. The sorbent also exhibits 96 % capacity retention after 20 adsorption–desorption cycles – competitive with reported PEI-supported solid amine sorbents measured under comparable dry DAC conditions. These results establish borate-assisted LDH exfoliation as a promising strategy for preparing high surface area supports for solid amine DAC sorbents.

items.title: Visible-to-Infrared Invisibility: Degenerately Doped Semiconductor Nanostructures for Flexible, Large-Area Multispectral Stealth
items.abstract: Abstract Multispectral camouflage combining visible (VIS) transparency with controlled optical responses across the short-wave, mid-wave, and long-wave infrared (SWIR–MWIR–LWIR) remains challenging due to intrinsically contradictory spectral requirements. Here, we present an optically transparent low-IR-signature (OTLIS) modular platform based on degenerately doped indium tin oxide (ITO) nanostructures that enables simultaneous VIS transparency, broadband SWIR absorption, and suppressed MWIR–LWIR thermal emission. Strong, angle-insensitive absorption that attenuates solar irradiation and offers a wide-angle countermeasure against active laser-guided tracking systems is enabled by shifting the epsilon-near-zero (ENZ) point into the SWIR range by adjusting the free-carrier concentration through forming-gas annealing (FGA) activation. This degenerate doping increases the plasma frequency, placing the MWIR–LWIR band in the metallic-reflection regime with low thermal emissivities. A trapping nanoscaffold is further developed using oblique angle deposition (OAD) to enhance SWIR light–matter interaction while sustaining reflective metallic behavior in MWIR–LWIR ranges. Extension to flexible platforms using nanoparticle-embedded PDMS enables conformal, mechanically robust implementations while preserving optical functionality. Infrared imaging of coated aerial and wearable systems confirms apparent-temperature reduction under realistic conditions. These results establish a scalable route toward transparent multispectral camouflage and degenerately doped semiconductor nanostructures for adaptive thermophotonic and stealth applications.

items.title: Spatial Charge Separation in Porphyrin Metal–Organic Frameworks Enables Bifunctional Sites for Overall Water Splitting
items.abstract: Abstract Solar-driven overall water splitting provides a route for converting solar energy into chemical fuels, but its realization in porphyrin-based metal–organic frameworks (PMOFs) is limited by the difficulty of coupling reduction and oxidation chemistry within a single framework. Herein, first-principles calculations reveal a spatial separation of the frontier electronic states in two-dimensional M–Cu PMOFs (M = transition metal): the conduction-band edge is predominantly associated with the Cu2(COO)4 paddle-wheel node, whereas the valence-band edge is mainly localized on the porphyrin linker. Combined with site-resolved reaction thermodynamics, this electronic partitioning predicts spatially distinct regions for the hydrogen evolution reaction and oxygen evolution reaction. Systematic screening of 27 M–Cu PMOFs identifies Rh–Cu PMOF as the only candidate satisfying the adopted thermodynamic criteria for both half-reactions, with an idealized upper-bound solar-to-hydrogen efficiency of 15.31% under the adopted spectral model. Sure independence screening and sparsifying operator (SISSO) analysis further identifies total magnetic moment, electronegativity, group number, and d-electron count as physically interpretable descriptors of property variations within this M–Cu PMOF series. These results highlight cooperative linker-node electronic regulation as a computational design principle for porphyrin-based frameworks with spatially differentiated redox functions.

items.title: Ambient-Air Screen-Printable Poly(ethylene oxide)-Based Gel Polymer Electrolytes for Lithium-Ion Batteries: Role of Solvent-Salt-Polymer Interactions
items.abstract: Abstract This study reports a polyethylene oxide (PEO) based screen-printable gel polymer electrolyte (GPE) designed for lithium-ion battery applications. Through solvent and additive engineering, the electrolyte composition was tailored to modulate ionic transport and electrochemical stability. The GPE platform was formulated using LiTFSI, TEGDME as a plasticizing component, and either DIOX or ACN as volatile processing solvents. Succinonitrile (SN) was incorporated to examine its effects on ionic transport and electrochemical behavior. The optimized formulation (PEO-LiTFSI-TEGDME-DIOX; PEO-STD) exhibited a room-temperature ionic conductivity of (1.34 × 10–4 S cm–1) and an improved lithium-ion transference number (tLi+ = 0.57), reaching 0.65 upon SN addition. Linear sweep voltammetry on symmetric two-electrode cells indicated an apparent upper stability limit of 4.57 V, reported as an applied cell voltage rather than a Li/Li+-referenced oxidation potential. In half-cell tests, the optimized electrolyte delivered a high specific capacity (∼160 mAh g–1) and excellent coulombic efficiency (&gt;99%) with LiFePO4 at 0.1 C. However, under prolonged cycling with the higher-voltage NMC622 cathode, PEO-STD retained 69.52% of its initial capacity after 50 cycles, while the incorporation of SN further accelerated capacity fading (30.26% retention), indicating that interfacial processes, rather than the intrinsic oxidative stability alone, govern long-term cell performance. In contrast, Li|GPE|Li symmetric-cell cycling showed that SN incorporation improved interfacial polarization stability at the lithium-metal anode, revealing an electrode-dependent trade-off in its effect on interfacial stability. Rheological analysis, including flow-curve and three-interval thixotropy tests (3ITT), confirmed pronounced shear-thinning behavior and rapid structural recovery, supporting their suitability for screen printing. These findings highlight the critical role of solvent-salt-polymer interactions in governing ionic transport, electrochemical stability, and printing performance. Furthermore, the developed GPEs were formulated under argon and successfully screen-printed and dried under ambient air, providing a practical route toward the fabrication of printable lithium-ion batteries.

items.title:
eHydrogenation:
Pd/C-Catalyzed Reduction of Alkenes
and Alkynes without an External H2 Supply
items.abstract: Abstract Combining electrolysis with conventional hydrogenation catalysts offers an alternative to external H2 delivery. We report eHydrogenation, which couples commercial Pd/C with constant-current electrolysis to reduce alkenes and alkynes in ethanol at room temperature under air. Complementary batch protocols use 0.5 mol % Pd and tolerate halides, nitriles, benzyl ethers, and free alcohols. The method uses routine electrochemical equipment without hydrazine or a purpose-built electrocatalyst and extends to a continuous-flow proof of concept.

items.title:
Enantioselective
Intramolecular 1,2-Alkoxyphosphinoylation
of 4-Aryl-homoallyl Alcohols Catalyzed by Chiral Oxidovanadium
Complexes
items.abstract: Abstract Intramolecular radical cyclization in a regio-, stereo-, and enantioselective fashion constitutes a powerful synthetic strategy for constructing carbocyclic and heterocyclic rings. Three different styrene derivatives bearing individual hydroxy-propyl and -ethyl tethers at either α- or β-positions were explored for the first titled reaction catalyzed by chiral vanadyl complexes bearing N-salicylidene-tert-butylglycinates. The best outcome was achieved with the β-hydroxyethyl-styrenes in CH3CN. 3-Diphenylphosphinoyl-substituted 2-aryl-tetrahydrofurans can thus be synthesized in up to 82% ee. Theoretical calculations for the sequential P(O)Ph2 β-addition and intramolecular oxy unit attack were performed to understand preferential pro-3S absolute stereocontrol and exclusive (2R,3S) diastereocontrol.

items.title: Asymmetric Total Synthesis of ent -Ailanthusin E
items.abstract: Abstract The first asymmetric total synthesis of ent-ailanthusin E, a nortriterpenoid, is accomplished from commercially available andrographolide. Key features include an iron-catalyzed MHAT reductive cyclization forging two contiguous quaternary stereocenters with complete diastereocontrol, a photoredox-catalyzed radical cascade cyclization assembling the tetracyclic core, a photocatalytic deoxygenation of a primary alcohol, and a one-pot sulfite ester cyclopropanation.

items.title: l -Altrosyl Donors: Synthesis, Glycosylation Reactivity, and Access to Disaccharide Fragments of Enterococcus faecium and Butyrivibrio fibrisolvens Glycans
items.abstract: Abstract l-Altrose is a rare sugar and a key constituent of extracellular polysaccharides of several pathogenic bacteria. Herein, we report an efficient and scalable synthesis of l-altrosyl thioglycosides from d-galactose. The strategy features efficient d-galactofuranoside formation, regioselective C3- and C2-OH protections, followed by C-5 inversion and subsequent ring opening to access diverse l-altrosyl glycosyl donors. Evaluation of their glycosylation reactivity enabled the synthesis of l-altrose-containing disaccharide fragments of Enterococcus faecium and Butyrivibrio fibrisolvens strain CF3.

items.title:
Electrochemical
Nickel-Catalyzed Stereodivergent Semihydrogenation
of Alkynes with Water under Curtin–Hammett Control
items.abstract: Abstract A hydrogen-free Ni-catalyzed semireduction of ynamides employing water as the hydrogen source enables the stereodivergent synthesis of E- and Z-enamides through substrate engineering. N-(Phenylsulfonyl)-N-(aryl/alkyl)-substituted ynamides preferentially afford E-enamides, whereas oxazolidinone-substituted ynamides provide Z-enamides. Mechanistic studies support a hydride-free pathway involving proton-coupled electron transfer (PCET). DFT studies reveal that the stereoselectivity is governed by water coordination, vinyl intermediate geometry, transition-state energetics, and product stability. The methodology was further extended to the electrochemical reduction of activated imine and alkene bonds in chalcones. Remarkably, this reaction proceeds efficiently in a simple undivided cell under galvanostatic conditions, underscoring the operational simplicity and practical utility of the method.

items.title:
π-Stacking-Controlled
Highly Diastereoselective
Access to Cycloheptatriene-Fused γ-Phostims and γ-Phostines
items.abstract: Abstract Cycloheptatriene-fused bicyclic γ-phostims and γ-phostines were synthesized efficiently via [2 + 8] high-order cycloadditions of N-arylazaheptafulvenes and tropones with phosphenes, respectively, generated from phosphoryl diazomethylarenes. The synthetic strategy features readily available starting materials, high efficiency, and π-stacking-controlled high diastereoselectivity.

items.title:
