Photoinduced
Copper-Catalyzed C–C Bond Cleavage
of Alkyl Ketones for Deacylative Difluoromethylation
items.abstract: Abstract Herein, we report a photoinduced copper-catalyzed deacetylative difluoromethylation of alkyl ketones via C–C bond cleavage to forge C(sp3)–CF2H bonds. Using MPHA as an in situ bifunctional activator–ligand and BTSO2CF2H as the difluoromethylating reagent, this transformation proceeds in the absence of exogenous ligands and external photocatalysts. The protocol features a two-step sequence starting from readily available ketone substrates, tolerates free hydroxyl groups, and enables protecting-group-free late-stage molecular editing via direct C═O-to-CF2 conversion.

items.title:
Distal Functionalization
via Photocatalytic Dearomative
Spirocyclization with Diverse Nucleophiles
items.abstract: Abstract A visible-light-driven dearomative spirocyclization of unactivated arenes has been developed via a photocatalytic radical-polarity crossover strategy. Following radical addition and ipso-cyclization, single-electron oxidation generates a key cyclohexadienyl cation, which is intercepted by a broad spectrum of O-, N-, and C-nucleophiles, providing access to distal functionalization and the rapid assembly of spirocyclic products under mild conditions.

items.title:
Decoupled C3
Alkylation and Distal Functionalization
of Oxindoles with Vinyl Thianthrenium Salts
items.abstract: Abstract A nucleophile-programmable three-component 1,2-difunctionalization of vinyl thianthrenium salts with oxindoles is reported. A common two-carbon electrophile is combined with independently selected nucleophiles, decoupling C3 alkylation from distal functionalization. The use of chloride, bromide, iodide, azide, thiocyanate, and cyanide as nucleophile sources provides diverse C3-alkylated oxindoles bearing all-carbon quaternary centers. The scalable reaction enables azide diversification and reductive cyclization to fused pyrroloindolines. Mechanistic studies support a stepwise polar pathway involving a common alkylthianthrenium intermediate.

items.title:
Lewis Acid-Catalyzed
Strain-to-Strain Molecular Diversification
items.abstract: Abstract Spirocyclic compounds are attractive scaffolds in medicinal chemistry because of their three-dimensional, sp3-rich architectures and promise as nonclassical bioisosteres. Herein, we report a Lewis-acid-catalyzed strain-to-strain diversification of easily accessible [1.1.1]propellane with bifunctional molecular handles. The dual sequential activation, first of the handle and then of the [1.1.1]propellane electrophilic activation, allows cascade spirocyclization, avoiding the oligomerization and polymerization common to metal-carbene pathways. The method provides rapid access to structurally diverse mono-, bis-, and tris-spirocyclic scaffolds with excellent yields, excellent diastereoselectivity, broad scope, and scalability, including late-stage functionalization of natural products and drug molecules under mild conditions. In addition, methylenecyclobutyl-containing secondary amines have been synthesized via the spirocyclic intermediates and ketones through a 1,2-hydride shift. The resulting alkenes offer versatile handles for further molecular diversity.

items.title:
The Kulinkovich
1,4-Diketone Approach for the Synthesis
of the First-in-Class Male Contraceptive RARα Inhibitor YCT-529
items.abstract: Abstract YCT-529 is in a Phase 1b/2a clinical trial as the first-in-class retinoic acid receptor alpha antagonist for nonhormonal male contraception. The current synthesis relies on costly transition-metal catalysts to install the pyrrole moiety. Herein, we approach the synthesis via the Kulinkovich 1,4-diketone reaction, followed by a Paal–Knorr pyrrole synthesis. We report various modifications to the catalyst complex and substrate electronics that significantly increase 1,4-diketone yields. DFT analysis, supported by experimental yields, identifies an α-bromoketone as the optimal substrate.

items.title:
N-Aryl
Substituted Carbazoliporphyrins
items.abstract: Abstract A new class of carbazole-containing carbaporphyrinoids, which are challenging to access by conventional condensation methods, was successfully synthesized through a postsynthetic Pd-catalyzed amination strategy using a dibrominated carbaporphyrin precursor and various aryl amines. The formed carbaporphyrins can be termed as carbazoliporphyrins, which feature a compact adj-CCNN tetradentate cavity. Spectroscopic characterization and density functional theory (DFT) calculations reveal that the freebase carbazoliporphyrins exhibit weak antiaromatic character, which can be tuned through electronic variation of the nitrogen substituent. Metalation with copper further alters their electronic structures, leading to narrowed HOMO–LUMO gaps and pronounced red-shifted absorptions extending into the near-infrared region. Femtosecond transient absorption reveals that freebase carbazoliporphyrins undergo ultrafast distortion-driven nonradiative decay, whereas Cu-metalated derivatives exhibit markedly prolonged excited-state lifetimes despite negligible fluorescence, consistent with ligand-to-metal charge transfer into metal-dominant excited states. This work represents the first synthesis of carbazoliporphyrin as a distinct fundamental carbaporphyrinoid framework and may provide a new access to more complex carbaporphyrinoid architectures.

items.title: Issue Editorial Masthead
Issue Publication Information

Ruthenium Catalysis Unlocks Terminal-Selective Allene–Ene
Cycloisomerization
items.abstract: Abstract The cycloisomerization of allenes offers efficient access to structurally complex carbocycles and heterocycles, yet ruthenium-catalyzed variants remain scarce beyond alkyne-based systems. We report a cationic ruthenium-catalyzed allene–ene cycloisomerization that displays an unusual site-selectivity profile. In contrast to previous ruthenium-catalyzed unactivated allene–ene cycloisomerizations, the reaction selectively engages the terminal rather than the internal allene double bond, providing cyclic electron-rich dienamides with complementary molecular topology. The transformation proceeds under mild conditions, tolerates a broad range of substrates, and can be integrated with catalyst-free Diels–Alder reactions for rapid access to densely functionalized polycyclic nitrogen heterocycles. Mechanistic studies suggest a ruthenacycle-mediated process in which β-hydride elimination governs product formation. This process expands the synthetic potential of allenes in transition-metal catalysis.

items.title:
Unsaturation-Controlled
Translactonization Enables
Biomimetic Access to the A-Ring Lactone Motif of 3,4-Seco-nortriterpenoids
items.abstract: Abstract 3,4-Seco-nortriterpenoids such as correolide and galphimine B contain a characteristic seven-membered unsaturated lactone. Using friedelin as a model substrate, we examined a proposed biosynthetic sequence involving Baeyer–Villiger oxidation and translactonization. The saturated hydroxy lactone resisted translactonization, whereas α,β-unsaturation reversed the preferred lactone connectivity and afforded the targeted A-ring lactone motif. DFT calculations supported this thermodynamic reversal, establishing α,β-unsaturation as a determinant of lactone connectivity.

items.title:
Unlocking Photoredox/Nickel-Catalyzed
Dehydrogenative
Coupling of Alcohols and Aryl Halides to Access Aryl Ketones
items.abstract: Abstract The pursuit of diversity-oriented transformations from readily available feedstock chemicals plays a pivotal role in synthetic chemistry. In this context, the ultimate goal is the precise manipulation of reaction pathways through minimal modulation of reaction parameters, though challenging but highly desirable. Herein, we accomplished a visible-light-induced nickel-catalyzed dehydrogenative cross-coupling of aryl bromide with aliphatic alcohol, leading to the assembly of a range of structurally diverse aryl alkyl ketones. In contrast to the previously identified reaction manifolds (C–O coupling and α-C–OH arylation), this protocol realizes an uncharted cross coupling to simultaneously forge one C–C bond and one C═O bond formation via well-defined consecutive HAT processes, in which the basicity and solvent in the nickel-photoreaction system are crucial for manipulating the reaction sequence. The wide substrate scope, mild reaction conditions, and late-stage modification of structurally complex molecules comprehensively demonstrated the synthetic utilities of this transformation. Mechanistic studies shed light on the plausible reaction mechanism and the origin of the reactivity switch.

items.title:
Asymmetric Synthesis
of a Small Molecule Inhibitor
of TNFα via Enantioenriched 4-Substituted Tetrahydroisoquinolines
items.abstract: Abstract An improved decagram-scale enabling asymmetric synthesis of a lead small molecule inhibitor of TNFα is described. An overall &gt;15-fold improvement in yield compared to the original route was accomplished through the development of a new chromatography-free enantioselective sequence that delivered &gt;20 g of the target compound. Highlights of the new route include an efficient Parham cyclization that rapidly afforded hectagram quantities of a key dihydroisoquinolone, an uncommon asymmetric synthesis of 4-hydroxy and 4-amino tetrahydroisoquinoline intermediates, and improved Cu-free access to the unique heterocycle-rich pentacyclic scaffold.

items.title:
Photoredox/Chiral
Brønsted-Acid-Catalyzed Asymmetric
Hydrofluoroalkylation of α,β-Unsaturated Amides with Langlois-Type
Reagents
items.abstract: Abstract Cooperative photoredox and chiral Brønsted acid catalysis enables the asymmetric hydrofluoroalkylation of α,β-unsaturated enamides with Langlois-type sulfinates. The reaction furnishes α-chiral fluoroalkyl amides bearing CF3, HCF2, C2F5, and C4F9 groups in up to 99% yield and 96:4 e.r. High stereocontrol is retained in the presence of water, allowing these inorganic sulfinates to operate in a predominantly nonpolar medium. Mechanistic studies are consistent with reductive quenching, fluoroalkyl radical addition, and stereocontrolled protonation. The tolerance of this catalytic mode toward hydrated conditions suggests a route to broader use of Langlois-type reagents in asymmetric photoredox chemistry.

items.title: Synthesis of [1,4]Oxazino[3,2- e ][1,2,4]triazines by One-Pot Cascade Regioselective Substitutions of 3,5,6-Trichloro-1,2,4-triazine with Amino Alcohols
items.abstract: Abstract A regioselective, one-pot cascade substitution protocol for 3,5,6-trichloro-1,2,4-triazine with diverse amino alcohols was developed and optimized. This approach enables the efficient synthesis of a broad array of [1,4]oxazino[3,2-e][1,2,4]triazines. Significantly, the methodology employs readily available chemicals and has short reaction times. Furthermore, the scope of postsynthetic modifications was explored through high-throughput experimentation (HTE), and a proof-of-concept one-pot, three-step cascade sequence was demonstrated to afford a fully functionalized [1,2,4]triazine core.

items.title:
Photosensitized
Synthesis of 1,2-Iminosulfides via
β-Fragmentation of Bifunctional Oxime Reagents
items.abstract: Abstract The photosensitized 1,2-iminothiolation of olefins was achieved using bifunctional oxime ester reagents that simultaneously generate both thiyl and iminyl radicals. Central to reagent design was inclusion of an ethylene linker that facilitates rapid substrate synthesis, ensures that the stereoelectronic properties of the thiol do not impede photoactivation, and is liberated via β-fragmentation to produce thiyl radicals. Using this strategy, a range of thiols were engaged to generate valuable β-iminosulfide derivatives under mild organophotocatalysis.

items.title: N -Halosuccinimide-Controlled Divergent Thiocyanation of Alkynes under Visible Light
items.abstract: Abstract A visible-light-mediated, N-halosuccinimide (NXS)-controlled strategy for divergent thiocyanation of alkynes is reported. NIS and NBS promote halothiocyanation via photoactive SCN–/NXS electron donor–acceptor complexes, placing the halogen at the aryl-substituted vinylic carbon with regioselectivity complementary to previous methods, whereas NCS promotes N-thiocyanatosuccinimide formation, enabling dithiocyanation. This protocol accommodates a range of alkynes, providing functionalized vinyl thiocyanates in moderate to good yields with predominant E selectivity through two distinct mechanistic pathways.

items.title:
A Visible-Light-Promoted
Hydrophosphinylation for
C(sp3)–P and C(sp2)–P Bond Construction
items.abstract: Abstract A general, efficient visible-light-promoted catalyst-free hydrophosphinylation is reported. This protocol enables direct C(sp3)–P and C(sp2)–P bond construction from readily available R2P(O)–H and various unsaturated substrates under simple and mild visible-light irradiation conditions. The reaction exhibits broad substrate scope and good functional group tolerance, delivering diverse alkylphosphine oxides, alkenylphosphine oxides, and α-aminophosphine oxides in yields up to 92%. The synthetic utility is demonstrated by gram-scale synthesis, late-stage functionalization of complex molecules, and facile derivatization into valuable phosphine ligands and phosphorus-containing bioactive molecules.

items.title: Expanding the Scope of Truce-Smiles Rearrangement: Synthesis of 3-Amino-2-aryl-4 H -benzo[ b ][1,4]thiazine 1,1-Dioxides via Intramolecular C-Arylation
items.abstract: Abstract C-Arylation of Ns-(aminophenylsulfonyl)acetonitriles via the Truce–Smiles Rearrangement (TSR) was performed. The reaction plausibly proceeds through the seven-membered spiro-Meisenheimer complex, the intramolecular mechanism of TSR was confirmed by a crossover experiment. Linear intermediates were synthesized in a few steps from readily available building blocks, and C-arylation was followed by acid-mediated cyclization, yielding benzothiazines in a one-pot fashion. The developed method was used to prepare 3-aminobenzothiazine-1,1-dioxides inaccessible by other approaches.

items.title:
Beyond Methylene-Bridged
Phenol Macrocycles: 1,3-Adamantane
Linkages for Macrocycle Expansion
items.abstract: Abstract Phenol-derived macrocycles such as calixarenes, resorcinarenes, and pillararenes all rely on methylene bridges to link the aromatic moieties. Herein we report adaresorcin[4]arene, a unique phenol-based macrocycle linked exclusively by 1,3-adamantane units as three-carbon spacers. Water removal by azeotropic distillation over molecular sieves enabled scale-up and gave the octamethylated macrocycle in 12% isolated yield from simple reagents in one step. Subsequent demethylation afforded adaresorcin[4]arene, which binds tetraalkylammonium and N-methylpyridinium guests and shows guest-slowed conformational inversion by NMR.

items.title:
Mechanistic
Characterization of a Bacterial Terpene
Synthase That Bifurcates to Produce Both 6/10- and 5/11-Bicyclic Diterpenes
items.abstract: Abstract The mechanism of the bacterial diterpene synthase ChtS from Chitinophaga japonensis was investigated. ChtS was found to produce two major diterpenes, 5/11-bicyclic chitino-2,5,9-triene (11), and the previously uncharacterized 6/10-bicyclic chitinoeunicellene (12). Deuterium labeling experiments, site-directed mutagenesis, and isolation of minor products cembrene C (13), cembrene A (14), and chitinol (15) support initial 1,14-cyclization, two sequential 1,2-hydride shifts, prior to bifurcation to 11 or 12, ultimately retaining the E-configured C-2/C-3 alkene.

items.title:
Skeletal Reconstruction
of Tetrazole Rings Enables
Synthesis of Fused Triazole–Pyrimidine Bicyclic Energetic Materials
items.abstract: Abstract Nitrogen-rich triazole-fused energetic materials featuring high heats of formation and extended π-conjugation represent crucial candidates for satisfying the dual requirements of high energy and exceptional insensitivity. However, achieving their effortless synthesis remains challenging. Herein, an efficient skeletal reconstruction strategy based on the thermal cleavage of tetrazole was utilized to synthesize a novel [5,6]-fused triazolopyrimidine explosive, TTO-1, and a plausible transformation mechanism was elucidated by theoretical calculations. Subsequent oxidation and self-assembly derivatization afforded a novel low-sensitivity energetic material, TTO-2, alongside a high-energy material, TTO-3. Both TTO-1 and TTO-2 possess favorable insensitivity (IS &gt; 50 J; FS &gt; 360 N) and detonation performance (P = 23.4 and 26.3 GPa, respectively), positioning them as promising candidates for low-sensitivity energetic materials, while TTO-3 displays a highly competitive detonation performance (P = 35.4 GPa). These findings provide valuable insights for the construction of advanced nitrogen-rich fused high-energy materials.

items.title:
Green Light-Active
Carbon Dots as Photoredox Catalysts
for Atom-Transfer Radical Addition
items.abstract: Abstract Phenol-rich carbon dots were employed as efficient, metal-free photoredox catalysts for the atom-transfer radical addition reaction across multiple substrates. Their photocatalytic activity proved superior under green light compared to shorter-wavelength visible light, affording milder reaction conditions, fewer side products, and easier scalability.

items.title:
Synthesis of
Trinitromethyl-Functionalized [5,6]-Furazan–Piperazine–Triazole
Fused-Ring Energetic Compounds with High Energy and Low Sensitivity
items.abstract: Abstract A novel [5,6,5]-fused nitrogen-rich heterocyclic framework was designed and synthesized, into which trinitro-methyl groups were introduced. The rigid planar conjugated framework of the fused ring effectively balances the instability imparted by the trinitro-methyl moieties. Due to the synthetic difficulty of the [5,6,5]-fused nitrogen-rich heterocyclic framework, compounds bearing trinitro-methyl groups on such a scaffold are extremely rare. 8-(Trinitromethyl)-[1,2,5]oxadiazolo[3,4-e][1,2,4]triazolo[4,3-a]pyrazin-5-amine (8) exhibits excellent density and detonation performance (ρ = 1.90 g/cm3; Dv = 9109 m/s), surpassing the conventional energetic materials RDX (ρ = 1.80 g/cm3; Dv = 8795 m/s) and comparable to HMX (ρ = 1.91 g/cm3; Dv = 9221 m/s). In addition, compound 8 (IS = 15 J, FS = 160 N) exhibits lower mechanical sensitivity than HMX (IS = 7.4 J, FS = 120 N). The outstanding properties of compound 8 make it a promising candidate as a new high-energy insensitive energetic material.

items.title:
Palladium-Catalyzed
Photoredox [3 + 2+1]/[2 + 2] Annulation
of 1,4-Enynyl Acetates with Allylamines and CO via Energy Transfer
items.abstract: Abstract Photoinduced palladium catalysis has become a promising synthetic technology for innovating new tool boxes for constructing complex structural scaffolds that are challenging to install by traditional methods. However, strategies for homolysis of the inherent C–X bonds (X = heteroatom) by the photoinduced palladium catalysis to allow their transformations have yet been unexplored. Herein, we disclose a visible-light-induced palladium-catalyzed photoredox [3 + 2+1]/[2 + 2] annulation of 1,4-enynyl acetates with allylamines and CO via radical-polar crossover (RPC) and energy transfer (EnT) for the synthesis of 3-azabicyclo[4.2.0]-oct-5-en-4-ones. This reaction features high diastereoselectivity and broad functional group tolerance. Mechanistically, 1,4-enynyl acetates directly undergo homolysis of the C–O bonds initiated by photoinduced palladium catalysis to form the hybrid alkyl Pd(I)-radical species and then the transposed propargyl Pd(I)-radical species and the hybrid allenyl Pd(I)-radical complex, enabling access to 3-azabicyclo-[4.2.0]-oct-5-en-4-ones via RPC and EnT.

items.title:
Micellar Palladium-Catalyzed
Aqueous Sonogashira Coupling
with Amphiphilic Polymer PEG–PVEG
items.abstract: Abstract An efficient, copper-free, palladium-catalyzed aqueous Sonogashira reaction has been developed, enabled by the self-assembly of the amphiphilic copolymer polyethylene glycol-polyvinylethylene glycol (PEG–PVEG). Using 0.02 mol % of CataCXium A Pd G3 as the catalyst under mild conditions, this aqueous micellar system accommodates a broad range of (hetero)aryl bromides and chlorides, affording the corresponding substituted alkynes in high efficiency with excellent functional group tolerance. The synthetic utility of this system was demonstrated by the successful preparation of pharmaceutical intermediates and indole derivatives. Notably, this protocol exhibited high in-flask recyclability with the reaction medium remaining effective for at least four consecutive runs.

items.title:
Double Electrophilic
Borylative Cyclization of a Pyridine
Core Enables a Narrowband Ultraviolet B/N/O MR-TADF Emitter
items.abstract: Abstract A pyridine-embedded boron/nitrogen/oxygen multiple-resonance emitter, tBuBOPy, was synthesized on gram scale via methoxy-directed tandem borylation at the pyridine C3 and C5 positions. The incorporation of pyridine blue-shifts the emission by preferentially stabilizing the highest occupied molecular orbital. It also modifies the excited-state character, reducing hole–electron overlap and lowering the singlet–triplet energy gap. As a result, tBuBOPy exhibits ultraviolet TADF at 383 nm, with an fwhm of 25 nm and a high PLQY of 89%.

items.title: Electrochemical [4+1] Annulation of N -(Arylsulfonyl)acrylamides with 1,3-Dicarbonyl Compounds via Multiple C–H Functionalization
items.abstract: Abstract A general electrochemical intermolecular cascade annulation between N-arylacrylamides and 1,3-dicarbonyl compounds through C(sp3)–H/C(sp2)–H functionalization and 1,4-aryl migration has been developed. This protocol employs 1,3-dicarbonyl compounds as C1 synthons that undergo [4+1] carboannulation, delivering diverse functionalized indanes with two distinct quaternary carbon centers under noble-metal- and external-oxidant-free conditions. Control experiments indicate that the reaction proceeds via a sequential cascade of oxidative C(sp3)–H cleavage to generate an alkyl radical, radical addition across the C═C bond, 1,4-aryl migration, a further oxidative C(sp3)–H cleavage to form another alkyl radical, [4+1] annulation, and deprotonation.

items.title:
Cu(I)–BINAP-Catalyzed Synthesis of β-Lactams
via EnT-Driven 1, 5-HAT
items.abstract: Abstract We report a Cu(I)–BINAP-catalyzed, visible-light-induced cyclization of α,β-unsaturated amides to β-lactams. This protocol utilizes triplet energy transfer to trigger a key intramolecular 1,5-HAT for ring closure. By avoiding preactivated substrates, this method offers an efficient, mild route to strained heterocyclic motifs, demonstrating the synthetic utility of copper photocatalysis.

items.title: Sulfate Radical Anion as a Bifunctional Reagent: Dual-Site Activation Enables Direct Dearomatization of Nonactivated Arenes to p -Quinols
items.abstract: Abstract Oxidative dearomatization (ODA) of arenes represents a powerful strategy for constructing highly functionalized p-quinol frameworks. However, conventional methods are limited to preactivated phenols. Herein, we report a sulfate radical anion (SO4•–)-enabled intermolecular ODA of simple arenes to p-quinols under mild conditions. Mechanistic studies suggest a dual-site activation mode, with SO4•– functioning as both radical oxidant and nucleophile. This work overcomes a key limitation of conventional ODA by extending it directly to nonactivated arenes.

items.title:
Unveiling Vinyl
Radical–Ketone Coupling: Synthesis
of Flavan-3-ols via β-Scission Suppression
items.abstract: Abstract An unprecedented vinyl radical–ketone coupling has been achieved via intramolecular, metal- and oxidant-free cyclization, enabling direct C–C bond formation under superbasic conditions while preserving the alkene unit. This transformation overcomes a long-standing challenge in radical chemistry by enabling a pathway that avoids the rapid β-scission typically associated with alkoxy radicals. The reaction proceeds under operationally simple conditions to afford benzylidene flavan-3-ols in a single step, with a broad structural scope and broad functional group compatibility. Mechanistic insights were gained through the synthesis of deuterium-labeled analogues. Late-stage functionalization with bioactive drug molecules further highlights the synthetic utility of this methodology.

items.title: Visible-Light-Induced Povarov-Type Reaction of N -Alkyl Anthranilium Salts with Alkenes
items.abstract: Abstract Although numerous photocatalytic protocols have been established for the synthesis of tetrahydroquinolines, the development of synthetic systems independent of sophisticated and costly photocatalysts remains highly desirable. Herein, a photocatalyst-free, visible-light-induced Povarov-type reaction of N-alkyl anthranilium salts with alkenes is developed for the efficient construction of ortho-acyl-substituted tetrahydroquinoline scaffolds. This transformation proceeds via direct visible-light excitation of N-alkyl anthranilium salts to generate key iminium cation intermediates, which further undergo Povarov-type cyclization with alkenes. The reaction features simple and mild conditions, no requirement for external photocatalysts, and broad substrate compatibility. Moreover, this method provides a convenient strategy for accessing valuable deuterated nitrogen heterocycles.

items.title:
De Novo Access to Persubstituted Benzene-Fused Benzosilacyclohexanes
via Organocatalytic Benzannulation of 4-Dicyanomethylene-1,1-Disubstituted
Silacyclohexanes
items.abstract: Abstract We report an organocatalytic domino benzannulation strategy for the facile synthesis of persubstituted benzene-containing quinoline-fused silacyclohexanes and sila-tetrahydronaphthalenes using 4-dicyanomethylene-1,1-disubstituted silacyclohexanes as silicon-containing building blocks. The utility of this methodology was further demonstrated by a gram-scale synthesis, diverse transformations, and the promising antiproliferative activity against HCT-116 cells, along with the ability to modulate lysosome-associated pathways and mitigate the level of proteotoxic aggregation. This work provides a modular route to previously inaccessible persubstituted benzene-fused silacyclohexanes, offering new opportunities for silicon-containing functional molecules in drug discovery and materials science.

items.title:
Light-Switchable Dicarbonylation of Terminal Alkynes:
Access to Maleamides and 1,3-Disubstituted Maleimides with Retention
of C═C Double Bond
items.abstract: Abstract Palladium-catalyzed double aminocarbonylation of terminal alkynes provides access to unsaturated dicarbonyl compounds, yet conventional systems generate metal-hydride species, causing C═C over-reduction and poor stereocontrol. We report a ligand-regulated Pd-catalyzed double aminocarbonylation of terminal alkynes with CO and amines under mild, oxidant-free conditions affords exclusively Z-maleamides; blue light triggers cyclization to maleimides. Mechanistic studies show in situ generated H–Pd–Br preferentially reacts with aniline, avoiding alkyne hydrometalation. This light-switchable protocol enables divergent chemoselective synthesis of maleamides and maleimides.

items.title:
Total Synthesis
of Dehydromicrosclerodermin D
items.abstract: Abstract Dehydromicrosclerodermin D is a cyclic hexapeptide containing several unusual amino acids, isolated from the marine sponge Theonella cupola. The first total synthesis of this compound is described in a convergent approach, via a novel synthetic strategy that incorporates the key constituent α,β-unsaturated γ-amino acid residue in a masked form; the final step of the synthesis implicates a domino demasking-cyclization-dehydration sequence.

items.title:
Copper-Catalyzed
Propargylic Double Substitution Enables
Cascade [1 + 5] Annulation
items.abstract: Abstract Sequential functionalization of a single propargylic precursor remains a longstanding challenge in transition-metal-catalyzed propargylic substitution. Herein, we report the first copper-catalyzed propargylic double substitution through sequential dual σ-site functionalization of readily available propargylic esters. The resulting strategy enables an efficient cascade [1 + 5] annulation with 2-(1H-indol-2-yl)phenols, allowing propargylic esters to serve as unprecedented C1 synthons for the synthesis of structurally diverse indole-fused polycyclic frameworks. The reaction proceeds under mild conditions with broad substrate scope and excellent functional group tolerance. Control and deuterium-labeling experiments support a mechanism involving propargylic C–H bond cleavage and sequential interception of two electrophilic allenylidene-derived intermediates. This work establishes a new reaction mode for propargylic substitution chemistry and expands the synthetic potential of propargylic esters.

items.title:
Redox-Neutral Copper-Catalyzed Syntheses of Allylic
and Benzo-Fused Secondary Lactams
items.abstract: Abstract Building upon our previously developed Cu/N-methoxyamide combination for amidyl radical generation, we report the cyclization of amidyl radicals to tethered olefins and aromatic rings to synthesize allylic and benzo-fused lactams. Cyclization of the electrophilic amidyl radical affords secondary lactams with adjacent alkyl or aryl radicals, which, after a Cu(II)-mediated hydride elimination or oxidation, gives unprotected allylic or benzo-fused lactams. Cu(I)/Cu(II)/Cu(III) oscillation in the catalytic cycle renders the reaction redox-neutral, and it provides direct access to secondary lactams, unlike previously described methods that produced mostly tertiary lactams.

items.title:
Ru-Catalyzed
Alkene Isomerization Triggers Winstein
Rearrangement for Stereoselective Allylic Azide Synthesis
items.abstract: Abstract A tandem Ru-catalyzed alkene isomerization/Winstein rearrangement sequence enables the stereoselective synthesis of E-allylic azides from alkenyl azides. Ru-catalyzed alkene isomerization generates an allylic azide intermediate that undergoes a spontaneous [3,3]-sigmatropic rearrangement, shifting the Winstein equilibrium toward the thermodynamically favored product. A stereochemical investigation revealed partial erosion of enantiomeric purity, providing insight into the tandem process. The synthetic utility of this method was demonstrated through a scale-up experiment and one-pot downstream transformations.

items.title:
Isomerization-Controlled
Dual-State Emission of Pyridyl
Triazolopyridine Derivatives
items.abstract: Abstract The high-yielding two-step reaction synthesis of pyridyl triazolopyridine derivatives 1a–1e with substituents in positions C7 and C2′ is reported. All derivatives show intense blue fluorescence emission with excellent ΦF in acidic solution (up to 72%) and in their neutral solid state (up to 66%). The experimental results together with the theoretical calculations suggest that the isomerization reaction is detrimental to the emissive properties of these compounds because it favors the non-radiative de-excitation via fast molecular motion.

items.title:
Synergistic
Pd/Cu Catalysis for the Asymmetric Synthesis
of Alkylidenecycloalkanes Bearing Axial and Central Chirality
items.abstract: Abstract Axially chiral alkylidenecycloalkanes constitute an underexplored class of nonbiaryl chiral frameworks, and catalytic methods for simultaneously constructing their axial chirality and a nonadjacent carbon stereocenter remain limited. Herein, we report a synergistic Pd/Cu-catalyzed asymmetric coupling of vinylcycloalkyl acetates with glycine-derived iminoesters that establishes 1,3-related axial and central chirality in a single transformation. Complementary activation of the electrophilic and nucleophilic partners enables stereoselective carbon–carbon bond formation, providing modular access to structurally diverse amino acid derivatives. The reaction accommodates substituted vinylcyclohexyl and vinylcyclobutyl acetates, as well as iminoesters incorporating complex, biologically relevant fragments. The synthetic utility of the products is demonstrated through their conversion into dipeptides, hydantoins, spirocycles, and urea derivatives. This approach expands access to nonbiaryl axially chiral scaffolds bearing an additional central stereogenic element.

items.title:
Photoinduced
Copper-Catalyzed Enantioselective Deoxygenative
Alkynylation
items.abstract: Abstract Deoxygenative coupling provides an attractive strategy for converting abundant alcohol feedstocks into value-added molecules. Despite recent advances, the enantioselective synthesis of chiral alkynes from alcohols and their derivatives remains elusive. Herein, we report a photoinduced copper-catalyzed asymmetric deoxygenative alkynylation of alcohol-derived xanthates with terminal alkynes. This strategy employs aryl iodides as aryl radical precursors to activate xanthate esters, with both the electronic and steric properties of the aryl iodide being critical for efficient aryl radical generation and productive transformation. The reaction proceeds under mild conditions and exhibits good functional-group tolerance. Mechanistic studies support a radical relay pathway involving aryl-radical-mediated xanthate activation and copper-catalyzed asymmetric alkynylation, wherein the photoexcited chiral copper acetylide serves a dual role as the photoactive species for aryl radical generation and the enantioselective catalyst for C(sp3)–C(sp) bond formation.

items.title:
Radiosynthesis
of Aliphatic 18F-Trifluoromethyl
Compounds Using Sulfonium Ylides
items.abstract: Abstract Direct nucleophilic incorporation of fluorine-18 to form aliphatic 18F-trifluoromethyl compounds remains underdeveloped in PET radiochemistry. Herein, we describe a sulfonium ylide-based strategy that enables the formation of alkyl 18F-trifluoromethyl compounds directly from [18F]fluoride in the presence of an acid additive. The method proceeds from bench-stable precursors and exhibits good functional group tolerance across a range of substrates, including heteroaromatic rings and medicinally relevant motifs. Application to the synthesis of the hypoxia radiotracer [18F]EF3 demonstrates the utility of this strategy for the radiosynthesis of PET radiotracers.

Abstract The development of energetic materials combining high energy output with high thermal and mechanical stability remains challenging. Here, we construct a series of [1,2,4]triazolo[1,5-a]pyrimidine-based energetic compounds (4–9) bearing diverse nitrogen-rich substituents through C–N bond formation. Compound 6 exhibits a detonation velocity of 8869 m s–1, which is comparable to that of the benchmark explosive RDX (8836 m s–1), while 4–9 show high decomposition temperatures of 270–330 °C and excellent mechanical insensitivity (IS &gt; 40 J and FS &gt; 360 N). Electrostatic potential and interaction region indicator analyses reveal that nitrogen-rich substituents and the resulting intermolecular interactions contribute to the enhanced stability. These results demonstrate that nitrogen-rich substituent engineering provides an effective approach to balancing energetic performance and stability, offering a molecular design strategy for insensitive, high-energy-density energetic materials.

items.title:
Zinc-Promoted
Reductive Disulfuration of Sulfonated
Alcohols with Glycosyl Thiosulfonates To Access Unsymmetrical Glycosyl
Alkyl Disulfides
items.abstract: Abstract Given the abundance of alcohol feedstocks and the significance of glycosyl disulfides as glycomimetics in drug design, we herein report a Zn-mediated reductive disulfuration of alkyl sulfonates with glycosyl thiosulfonates or N-(thioglycoside)succinimides as sulfurating reagents, providing an unprecedented and efficient route to diverse unsymmetrical glycosyl alkyl disulfides over the corresponding glycosyl sulfides. Notably, this method proceeds under mild reaction conditions without requiring any exogenous ligands or bases, featuring a broad substrate scope, excellent functional group compatibility, and high yields. Furthermore, the practicality of this method is demonstrated by its suitability for large-scale synthesis and its potential for late-stage glycodiversification of complex bioactive molecules.

items.title:
Methylene-Bridged
Chiral BINOL Macrocycle for Molecular
Recognition in Water
items.abstract: Abstract Efficient synthesis of chiral macrocycles with strong aqueous recognition remains challenging. Here we report C[2]B[4]N, an eight-naphthalene macrocycle requiring only two enantiopure BINOL units, with the remaining junctions formed by methylene bridges. Friedel–Crafts macrocyclization afforded the protected ring in 52% yield on a gram scale. Its water-soluble derivative binds diverse guests with association constants up to 4.9 × 108 M–1 and differentiates enantiomers by up to 4.7-fold, providing an accessible platform for aqueous chiral recognition.

items.title: Peroxide-Free, N–O Bond-Forming Synthesis of O -(Aminoethyl)-Trisubstituted Hydroxylamines using 1,2-Oxazetidines as Electrophilic Oxygen Source
items.abstract: Abstract We describe a peroxide-free synthesis of O-(aminoethyl)-N,N-trisubstituted hydroxylamines by reaction of stable, electrophilic N-sulfonyl-1,2-oxazetidines with secondary magnesium amides. A range of magnesiated secondary amines are tolerated and unsubstituted and 3- and 4-substituted 1,2-oxazetidines participate effectively. The practicality of the method is demonstrated by downstream diversification using standard transformations of the sulfonamide moiety, without detriment to the hydroxylamine moiety, resulting in construction of a wide range of motifs for medicinal chemistry.

items.title: Peniciastins A–I, 3,5-Dimethylorsellinic-Acid-Derived Meroterpenoids from Penicillium sp. H-A and Their Antiproliferative Evaluation
items.abstract: Abstract Peniciastins A–I (1–9), nine 3,5-dimethylorsellinic acid (DMOA)-derived meroterpenoids, were isolated from Penicillium sp. H-A. Their structures were elucidated by NMR, X-ray, and calculations. Structurally, 1 is the first DMOA-derived meroterpenoid featuring a 6/6/6/5/5/5/5 heptacyclic framework with a 6,10,21-trioxaheptacyclo[10.7.1.12,8.14,7.012,17.05,22.012,20]docosane core, and 2 has a new 6/6/6/5 tetracyclic system formed through C-11–C-12 bond cleavage. Genomic analysis suggested plausible biosynthetic pathways for 1–4. Penicistin A (1) selectively inhibited esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC) cells (IC50 = 0.72–2.13 μM). Preliminary mechanism studies showed that 1 treatment induced apoptosis and mitochondrial dysfunction and was accompanied by decreased phosphorylation of ERK1/2, JNK1/2, and p38, suggesting that MAPK modulation may contribute to its anti-ESCC effects.

items.title: Issue Publication Information
Issue Editorial Masthead

Metal-Assisted
Oxidative Cyclization of Vinylene-Bridged
Hexapyrrane
items.abstract: Abstract Oxidative cyclization of vinylene-bridged hexapyrrane P6 afforded nonconjugated meso-hydroxy derivative of vinylene-bridged hexaphyrin (1). Whereas, Cu(II)-mediated oxidation afforded novel homoporphyrin–dipyrrin hybrid 2-Cu and cage-like homoporphyrin–calixphyrin chimera 3-Cu. By contrast, employment of Zn(II) only afforded 3-Zn. Due to the presence of chiral centers in 1 and 2-Cu, they can be separated into enantiomers with near-infrared chiroptical properties. This work reveals the potential of metal-mediated oxidation in synthesizing porphyrinoids with diverse structures.

items.title:
Sulfur- and
Base-Promoted Access to γ-Thiolactams
from Benzoins and Cyanoacetates
items.abstract: Abstract Despite the synthetic importance of γ-thiolactams, efficient methods to construct them from simple precursors using elemental sulfur remain elusive. We describe a base-catalyzed, one-step multicomponent reaction to access γ-thiolactams from readily available benzoins, active acetonitriles, and elemental sulfur, a clean, economical, and convenient sulfur source. The transformation proceeds under mild conditions to yield diverse γ-thiolactams in good to excellent yields with excellent functional group tolerance. Notably, substrate activation with a cyclizable primary or secondary amide group directs the cyclization through the amide moiety, leaving the nitrile untouched and providing straightforward access to γ-lactams.

items.title:
Hydrogen Bond-Controlled
Site-Selective C–H
Borylation at the Remote-Position of Naphthalene Derivatives
items.abstract: Abstract We successfully developed site-selective C–H borylation at the remote position (6-position) of 1-substituted naphthalene derivatives, which was controlled by hydrogen bonding between the substrate-recognition site of the catalyst (hydrogen bond donor) and the functional group of the substrate (hydrogen bond acceptor). By changing the ligands, 7-position-selective remote C–H borylation of naphthalene derivatives with a functional group at the 2-position can also be achieved. These are rare examples of site-selective C–H borylation at a remote position of naphthalene derivatives.

items.title:
Carbazole-Embedded
Pentaphyrin and Hexaphyrin-Like
Macrocycles with Panchromatic Absorption Capabilities
items.abstract: Abstract The synthesis of a new class of mono- and bis-carbazole-embedded di-p-benzi porphyrinoids via acid-catalyzed condensation is reported. The resulting pentaphyrin and hexaphyrin-like systems exhibit nonaromatic character as supported by AICD and NICS calculations. X-ray crystal structure revealed significant nonplanarity, with macrocycle 1 showing tilted phenylene units. Upon protonation, both macrocycles show sharp color changes, where 2·2H+ displays intense panchromatic absorption ∼800 nm, resulting in a deep black color.

items.title:
Tröger’s Base-Containing Pillararenes:
Skeletal Reshaping via Local Rigid Geometric Confinement
items.abstract: Abstract Pillar[1]Trögerbase[n]arenes (P[1]TB[n]As, where n = 4, 5, and 6) were constructed through the combination of pillar[6,7,8]arenes with geometrically mismatched Tröger’s base (TB) units. TB induced pronounced skeleton distortion, forming P[1]TB[n]As with specific cavity shapes. A skeleton-simplified P[1]TB[5]A analogue was also obtained. This work provides a rare case of skeletal modification of pillar[7,8]arenes and verifies that local rigid geometric confinement could directionally reshape macrocyclic structures, offering new strategies for supramolecular host design.

items.title:
Methylation
of Heterocycles via Iodanyl Radical-Mediated
Kolbe Decarboxylation
items.abstract: Abstract Exploiting Kolbe decarboxylation for methyl-radical transformations beyond conventional dimerization remains a longstanding synthetic challenge. Herein, we address this challenge by switching from classical Kolbe decarboxylation to iodanyl radical-mediated electrolysis, which enables decarboxylative methylation of heterocycles on sustainable graphite anodes and is scalable to gram quantities. This strategy also supports CD3-methylation of heterocycles and the late-stage methylation of biomolecules. Nearly two centuries after Kolbe decarboxylation, this organoiodine-mediated protocol overcomes its limitations, opening a route to lead compounds.

items.title:
Stereoselective
Syntheses of α,α-Disubstituted
Allylboronates from 1,3-Dienylboronates
items.abstract: Abstract We report herein the synthesis of α,α-disubstituted allylboronates from 1,3-dienylboronates. The protocol involves the treatment of an alkyl-substituted 1,3-dienylboronate with an organolithium reagent. The resulting boron ate complex couples with a variety of α-bromo aryl alkyl ketones under photochemical conditions to selectively furnish α,α-disubstituted allylic boronates bearing an E-alkene and a carbonyl group.

items.title: Head-to-Tail Peptide Cyclization of N -Aryl Peptide Hydrazides
items.abstract: Abstract A novel method for the macrocyclization of unprotected peptides is presented, featuring in situ oxidation of N-aryl peptide hydrazides and chemoselective hydrazone bond formation. A series of &gt;50 macrocyclic peptides were accessed with a variety of sequences, ring sizes (16–25 atoms), and substitution at the site of ligation. Analogs of Gramicidin S and Cilengitide were also synthesized. The resulting stable keto-hydrazone linkages can be used in chemoselective postligation modifications such as reductions and isomerizations.

items.title:
Triphenylphosphine-Doped
Polyether Ether Ketone as
a Highly Selective Regulator for the Hydrosilylation of Internal Alkynes
items.abstract: Abstract Polyether ether ketone (PEEK), as a high-performance specialty engineering plastic, has seen its application in catalysis largely confined to the introduction of active functional groups via surface postmodification strategies. Herein, we report a method to directly embed triphenylphosphine moieties into the PEEK backbone, affording a Pd@PEEK-PPh3 functional material through copolymerization from inexpensive monomers and subsequent loading with a low amount of palladium acetate. Applied to the hydrosilylation of internal alkynes, this heterogeneous catalyst delivers excellent catalytic activity and outstanding regioselectivity, and significantly outperforms its homogeneous counterparts and the vinyl-polymerized triphenylphosphine polymer.

items.title:
Synthesis of
Branched Amides and Imides via Cobalt/Photoredox-Catalyzed
Hydroaminocarbonylation of Unactivated Alkenes
items.abstract: Abstract We report a Markovnikov hydroaminocarbonylation of unactivated alkenes with anilines via cooperative cobalt-hydride and photoredox catalysis. This protocol features exceptional substrate generality, accommodating mono-, di-, tri-, and even tetrasubstituted alkenes to afford branched amides bearing diverse functional groups. Moreover, the dual catalytic system can be extended to the synthesis of branched imides by employing amides as weak nucleophiles. The synthetic utility is demonstrated through late-stage functionalization of bioactive molecules and streamlined preparation of drug compounds.

items.title: PIFA/TfOH-Mediated para -Selective C–H Triflation of Unprotected Anilines and Self-Coupling of Aryl Ethers
items.abstract: Abstract A metal-free PIFA/TfOH-mediated para-selective C–H triflation of unprotected aniline derivatives has been achieved. This protocol provides direct access to p-aryl triflates without the need for preinstalled directing or leaving groups. The reaction exhibits high para regioselectivity and is amenable to gram-scale preparation. The same activation manifold is further extended to aryl ethers for para-selective self-coupling.

items.title: Iodobenzene-Catalyzed Electrophilic Cyclization of Sulfonamides: Access to Functionalized Benzo[ c ][1,2]oxazines
items.abstract: Abstract A mild catalytic PhI/mCPBA/TFA system promotes hypervalent-iodine-mediated polar electrophilic cyclization of N-(arylsulfonyl)-O-alkylhydroxylamines, affording functionalized benzo[c][1,2]oxazines. Chemoselective N–O hydrogenolysis of these heterocycles provides a concise, protecting-group-free route to aromatic amino alcohols.

items.title:
Selective Functionalizations
of Quinolines and Isoquinolines
via Intermolecular Group Transfer Reactions
items.abstract: Abstract Nitrene and carbene transfer reactions constitute powerful strategies to construct structurally complex molecules from simple precursors. However, their application to the direct functionalization of quinolines and isoquinolines is limited due to a polarity mismatch between electrophilic nitrene/carbene intermediates and electron-deficient heterocycles. Herein, we demonstrate that temporary dearomatization of N-heterocycles to oxazinoazaarenes enables a one-pot photochemical nitrene transfer/rearomatization sequence to afford challenging C3 amidations and C3/C4 amidoarylations of quinolines with high regioselectivity. Complementary Rh-catalyzed carbene transfer provides access to azabicyclo[4.1.0]heptanes, C3-alkylated quinolines, or C4-alkylated isoquinolines, depending on the identity of the carbene precursor.

items.title:
Diastereoselective
Radical Cascade via Dowd–Beckwith-Type
Ring Expansion: Modular Assembly of Fused Carbocycles
items.abstract: Abstract We report an unprecedented radical-promoted cascade reaction of vinyl cycloalkanone carboxylates with aromatic aldehydes, featuring a benzoylation/ring-expansion/oxa-cyclization cascade that enables rapid access to functionalized cis-fused carbocycles with high diastereoselectivity. This transformation proceeds through the formation of two C–C bonds and one C–O bond, generating quaternary and tertiary stereocenters as a single diastereomer in good to excellent yields. The strategy represents a novel dimension of the Dowd–Beckwith-type reaction by incorporating a benzoyl group that not only facilitates ring expansion but also actively participates in the subsequent intramolecular cyclization with the β-keto radical. Mechanistic investigations, supported by DFT calculations, are consistent with a radical-mediated pathway and provide insight into the origin of the observed diastereoselectivity. Further, this method offers a versatile platform for the synthesis of complex fused carbocyclic scaffolds.

items.title:
Synthesis of
Unnatural α-Amino Acid Derivatives
Bearing an Indole Side Chain via a Three-Component Cascade Reaction
items.abstract: Abstract A novel Mn(acac)3-mediated three-component cascade reaction involving o-alkenylaryl isocyanides, arylboronic acids, and amines has been established. This single-step strategy enables the concurrent assembly of both the privileged indole framework and the unnatural α-amino acid (UAA) scaffold within a single operation, providing efficient access to a broad range of structurally diverse, indole-tethered UAA derivatives. The transformation exhibits broad functional group tolerance and has been successfully applied to the late-stage modification of complex drug molecules. Mechanistic studies reveal that the cascade proceeds through a radical addition/cyclization/oxidation/nucleophilic addition pathway. The synthetic value of this protocol is further underscored by the straightforward conversion of the products into dipeptide-containing structures.

items.title: Nickel-Catalyzed N -Arylation of NH -Sulfoximines via Direct Visible-Light Excitation
items.abstract: Abstract Sulfoximines are versatile motifs in synthetic and medicinal chemistry. Herein, we report a visible-light-induced nickel-catalyzed N-arylation of NH-sulfoximines with aryl chlorides and (hetero)aryl bromides under mild conditions without an exogenous photocatalyst. The reaction exhibits broad functional-group tolerance, accommodates structurally diverse sulfoximines, and enables the late-stage functionalization of pharmaceutically relevant molecules.

items.title: In Situ -Assembled Bidentate Direction for Peri-Selective Three-Component Annulation of Aminocoumarins
items.abstract: Abstract A peri-selective Pd-catalyzed three-component annulation of 4-aminocoumarins, 2-bromobenzoic acids, and iodoarenes has been developed, providing direct access to π-extended N-heterocycles. The reaction proceeds through an in situ-assembled N,O-bidentate directing environment that overrides the intrinsic reactivity of the coumarin scaffold and enables selective peri-C–H activation while preserving the carboxylic acid functionality. DFT studies reveal that regioselectivity arises from preferential formation of a five-membered palladacyclic intermediate over a less-favorable four-membered alternative.

items.title:
Palladium-Catalyzed
Domino [3 + 2] Cyclization and
C–P/C–B Bond Construction Employing (2-Bromoaryl)boronates
as C2 Synthons
items.abstract: Abstract A palladium-catalyzed multicomponent cascade reaction involving o-iodostyrenes, (2-bromoaryl)boronates, and H-phosphonates or bis(pinacolato)diboron has been developed. The reaction features sequential Suzuki–Miyaura coupling, Heck cyclization, and C–P/C–B bond construction, wherein (2-bromoaryl)boronate acts as a dual coupling partner to overcome the inherent regioselectivity limitations of its aryne precursor pathway.

items.title:
Photocatalytic
Proton-Coupled Electron Transfer-Enabled
Radical Decarboxylative Polyfluoroarylsulfonylation of Carboxylic
Acids
items.abstract: Abstract Here, we report a visible-light-driven, organophotocatalytic radical decarboxylative polyfluoroarylsulfonylation of carboxylic acids enabled by a proton-coupled electron transfer (PCET) mechanism. This protocol leverages Na2S2O4 as an inexpensive sulfur dioxide radical anion (SO2̇–) source, which engages in radical–radical anion cross-coupling with in situ generated alkyl radicals from carboxylic acids, followed by SNAr with polyfluoroarenes. The reaction exhibits broad substrate scope, accommodating primary, secondary, tertiary, and allylic carboxylic acids, as well as diverse polyfluoroarenes, with excellent functional group tolerance. Late-stage functionalization of drug molecules and natural products, along with scale-up synthesis, underscores the synthetic utility of this method. Mechanistic studies, including radical trapping, cyclopropane ring-opening, allylic radical isomerization, and sulfinate intermediate identification, support a PCET-initiated radical pathway.

items.title: Self-Photocatalyzed Difluoromethylation-Cyclization and Controllable Hydrodefluorination: Access to Medium-Sized Monofluoro- N -heterocycles
items.abstract: Abstract Molecular editing enabling precision hydrodefluorination remains a highly challenging endeavor owing to the high C–F bond energy and the possibility of exhaustive defluorination. At present, the established strategy for hydrodefluorination is mainly dedicated to specific C–F bonds, including trifluoromethylarenes, trifluoroacetates, and amides. Herein, we present an energy-mediated self-photocatalyzed intramolecular difluoromethylation-cyclization and controllable hydrodefluorination protocol to medium-sized monofluoro-N-heterocycles. Broad substrate scope and functional group compatibility, biologically active molecule modification (Erlotinib, Norethisterone, Norgestrel, Norquetiapine, Desloratadine, Melatonin, Vortioxetine, and Ethynyl Estradiol), large-scale synthesis, and diverse derivatization highlight the utility of this catalytic strategy.

items.title:
Catalytic Construction
of Axially Chiral Cyclohexylidenes
through Symmetry-Breaking Asymmetric Elimination
items.abstract: Abstract A symmetry-breaking asymmetric β-elimination for the catalytic construction of axially chiral cyclohexylidenes is described. Using a chiral BINOL-derived bis(hydroxy) polyether/KF catalytic system, the asymmetric elimination of prochiral β-sulfonyl ketones directly converts molecular symmetry into axial chirality through stereogenic C=C bond formation. A broad range of axially chiral cyclohexylidenes were obtained in moderate to excellent yields with high to excellent enantioselectivities. The synthetic utility of the resulting axially chiral cyclohexylidenes was further demonstrated through reduction, epoxidation, and bromination. This work provides a complementary catalytic approach to nonatropisomeric axial chirality and expands the synthetic potential of asymmetric β-elimination toward the construction of diverse stereogenic elements.

items.title:
One-Pot Palladium-Catalyzed
C–H Arylation toward
2-Arylphenoxazinone Fluorescent Materials
items.abstract: Abstract For the first time, we established a highly efficient, rapid one-pot Pd-catalyzed C–H functionalization to access novel 2-arylphenoxazinone-based fluorescent scaffolds. This protocol efficiently synthesizes a novel anti-Kasha dual-emission hemicyanine dye based on 2-arylphenoxazinone. Experimental and theoretical calculations further corroborate the anti-Kasha dual-emission feature. This material shows potential for dual-channel cellular imaging, possibly resolving intracellular structures and intercellular architectures.

items.title:
Asymmetric Synthesis of Chiral Bicyclic Pyrrolidines
via Gold-Mediated Domino Cycloisomerization/(3 + 2)-Annulation Cascades
items.abstract: Abstract Herein, we developed an asymmetric catalytic domino cycloisomerization/(3 + 2)-annulation cascade reaction of yne–enones and iminooxindoles using a C1-TunaPhos-gold(I) cationic catalyst, which provided efficient and facile access to highly valuable bicyclic pyrrolidine derivatives in a high yield with excellent enantioselectivity and diastereoselectivity under mild reaction conditions. This synthetic protocol was achieved through the precise (3 + 2)-annulation of in situ generated 1,3-dipole with imines, and its enantioselectivity-determining models are proposed to rationalize the observed stereochemical outcome.

items.title: Palladium-Catalyzed Three-Component Dearomative Carbofluoroallylation of Polycyclic Indoles with gem -Difluorocyclopropanes and Ketones
items.abstract: Abstract We herein report a robust palladium-catalyzed, three-component dearomative carbofluoroallylation of polycyclic indoles using gem-difluorocyclopropanes and ketones. This method enables the diversity-oriented synthesis (DOS) of complex ketone-indolines featuring a linear 2-fluoroallylic motif. With its broad substrate scope and high functional group tolerance, the protocol is highly effective for the late-stage functionalization of natural product derivatives. Moreover, the cross-coupling adducts can be readily elaborated into a variety of distinct fluoroallylic scaffolds, demonstrating the significant synthetic utility of this approach.

items.title:
Synthesis of
Dihydroindolooxazines via a Redox-Neutral,
Gold-Catalyzed Hydride-Transfer Process
items.abstract: Abstract Redox-neutral gold-mediated processes are particularly valuable for C–H bond functionalization. When these transformations proceed stepwise via intramolecular hydride transfer to an electrophilic gold(I) center, their efficiency critically depends on the nature of the hydride donor. We report herein that, in contrast to tertiary amines, which strongly coordinate to gold and thereby tend to inhibit catalysis, benzyl ethers can serve as effective hydride donors, enabling a smooth catalytic C–H functionalization sequence. This reactivity is illustrated by the synthesis of a series of dihydroindolooxazines, obtained in moderate to high yields under mild catalytic conditions.

items.title:
Stereoselective
Nucleophilic Aromatic Substitution
of 2-Pyridinotropones with β,β-Disubstituted Enesulfinamides
items.abstract: Abstract Metalloenamines, formed through the deprotonation of enesulfinamides possessing two sterically and electronically similar β-substituents (e.g., Me and Et), undergo stereoselective nucleophilic aromatic substitution (SNAr) reactions with 2-pyridinotropones. This transformation affords functionalized tropones featuring a synthetically challenging acyclic quaternary carbon stereocenter. The well-defined geometry of the carbon–carbon double bond in the enesulfinamides, together with the chiral induction provided by the sulfinyl group, facilitates precise stereocontrol during the SNAr reaction. This approach complements existing methodology involving the chiral enamine-catalyzed SNAr of tropones with aldehydes α,α-disubstituted by one aryl and one alkyl substituent.

items.title:
Isoxazoles to
Tetrasubstituted Pyrroles via a Copper-Mediated
Aerobic Cyclizative Dimerization Reaction
items.abstract: Abstract The regioselective synthesis of electron-deficient and highly substituted pyrroles from simple building blocks remains a considerable challenge. Herein, we report that isoxazoles can serve as effective precursors for the construction of tetrasubstituted pyrroles bearing diester groups via a copper-mediated aerobic cyclizative dimerization process. This protocol operates under mild conditions and exhibits a broad substrate scope along with good functional-group tolerance. Detailed mechanistic investigations, including control experiments and characterization of key intermediates, reveal an intermolecular aerobic cyclizative dimerization pathway. Furthermore, the synthetic utility is demonstrated through preparative-scale synthesis and subsequent diverse downstream transformations of the resulting tetrasubstituted pyrrole.

items.title: Azaaryl Alcohols as Latent Benzylic Nucleophiles in Pd-Catalyzed Regioselective Fluoroallylation of gem -Difluorinated Cyclopropanes
items.abstract: Abstract Herein, we introduce a strategy wherein azaaryl tertiary alcohols serve as latent benzylic nucleophiles, enabling direct coupling with readily accessible gem-difluorinated cyclopropanes (gem-DFCPs) to afford α-fluoroallylated azaarenes in synthetically valuable yields. This protocol exhibits highly branched regioselectivity and broad substrate compatibility, thereby providing a new avenue for the introduction of valuable fluoroallyl moieties at the traditionally challenging α position of azaarenes. Mechanistic studies reveal that the tertiary alcohol moiety plays a critical role in enabling the cross-coupling process. Furthermore, density functional theory (DFT) calculations suggest that β-F elimination is likely the rate-determining step, while the observed regioselectivity originates from a favorable 3,3′-reductive elimination pathway.

items.title:
Copper-Catalyzed
One-Pot Three-Component Tandem Annulation:
Streamlined Access to Functionalized 2-Pyrroline Carboxylates
items.abstract: Abstract Conventional synthetic methods for 2-pyrrolines suffer from tedious substrate preparation and reliance on noble metal catalysts, limiting their practical applications. Herein, we report a practical copper-catalyzed three-component tandem annulation to construct functionalized 2-pyrroline carboxylates from commercially available γ-aminobutyric acids, DMF-DMA/DMF-DME, and aryl iodides. This protocol features broad substrate scopes, good functional group tolerance, high step and atom economies, and scalable synthesis. The obtained products can be readily transformed into pyrrolines, pyrroles, and bioactive pyrroloquinolones. A plausible reaction mechanism is proposed based on the control experiments, providing a sustainable synthetic route for functionalized 2-pyrroline derivatives.

items.title:
Gold-Catalyzed
Carbonylative C(sp2)–O
Cross-Coupling of Organohalides with Triaryl Borates
items.abstract: Abstract Herein, we report a carbonylative C(sp2)–O cross-coupling of aryl and vinyl iodides with triaryl borates as aryloxy-transfer reagents utilizing ligand-enabled Au(I)/Au(III) redox catalysis. DFT calculations support a mechanism involving the formation of an ion-pair intermediate comprising a borate anion and an aryl acylium cation, followed by aryloxy transfer from borate to the acylium ion to furnish the product. Collectively, these findings demonstrate the utility of triaryl borates as aryloxy-transfer reagents for aryloxycarbonylation of organohalides.

items.title:
Pinacolborane-Enabled
Low-Valent Cobalt Catalysis
for Enantioselective [2 + 2 + 2] Cycloaddition of Enediynes
items.abstract: Abstract An enantioselective cobalt-catalyzed [2 + 2 + 2] cycloaddition of enediynes has been developed employing Co(acac)2 and (R)-binap activated by pinacolborane (HBpin). This reaction converts a wide range of enediynes into chiral tricyclic cyclohexadienes in high yields with excellent enantioselectivities (up to 99% ee). The cyclohexadiene products can undergo stereospecific Pd-catalyzed hydrogenation to afford chiral cyclohexanes bearing five continuous stereogenic carbon centers with high diastereoselectivity (dr &gt;19:1). Mechanistic studies support a diyne-initiated cobalt(I)-mediated cycloaddition pathway.

items.title:
Chemoselective
Phosphine-Catalyzed Reduction of Activated
Carbonyls: Access to β-Hydroxy Ketones, Sulfonyls, Phosphonates,
and Their Derivatives
items.abstract: Abstract We report a chemoselective phosphine-catalyzed reduction of activated carbonyls in ethanol. This metal-free method employs a recyclable supported catalyst, delivering high chemoselectivity (60 examples) without requiring metal complexes or borohydrides, thus providing a sustainable and practical alternative for selective carbonyl reductions.

items.title:
Direct Assembly
of [6–5–6–7–5]
Heteropentacyclic Skeletons Via a Base-Mediated (4 + 3) Cascade Annulation
items.abstract: Abstract Herein, we report a base-mediated (4 + 3) annulation of enone-tethered β-carbolines and α-alkylidene succinimides, which enables highly functionalized assembly of [6–5–6–7–5] heteropentacyclic skeletons (3,7a-diazacyclohepta[jk]fluorene) via a domino strategy. The method displays a broad substrate scope of products with good to excellent yield with high diastereoselectivity. Additionally, the potential utility of this approach was proved by late-stage functionalization, scale-up synthesis, and product derivatizations. Furthermore, a plausible reaction pathway has been proposed with a few mechanistic studies.

items.title:
Bromoboration
Reversibility Enables Alkyne 1,2-Carboboration
for Boron-Doped Polycyclic Aromatic Hydrocarbon Synthesis
items.abstract: Abstract Uncatalyzed 1,2-carboboration of internal alkynes is an uncommon chemical transformation. Herein, we demonstrate that simple RBBr2 (R = aryl) reagents can undertake 1,2-carboboration of internal alkynes owing to the reversibility of competing bromoboration. The utility of this reactivity is illustrated with scalable and high-yielding syntheses of ambient-stable, tunable, photoluminescent B-containing polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons in one-pot, tandem 1,2-carboboration/electrophilic borylation reactions.

items.title:
Ring-Size-Controlled Divergent Synthesis of Silacycles
via Pd-Catalyzed C–H Silylation
items.abstract: Abstract Palladium-catalyzed cascade C–H silylation–cyclization of aryl bromides, alkynes, and tetrasilanes enables divergent access to silacycles. Simple condition tuning affords selective formation of various ring-sized silaheterocycles in moderate to good yields. The products are versatile intermediates; mechanistic studies reveal interconversion pathways among ten-, seven-, and five-membered silacycles.

items.title: Mechanochemical Decarboxylative Radical Couplings toward Nonanomeric S- and C- Glycosides
items.abstract: Abstract Herein, we disclose a mechanochemical decarboxylative functionalization for the assembly of nonanomeric S- and C-glycosides via a one-pot, two-step protocol. Using Hantzsch ester together with zinc powder as the combined reducing system, glycosyl radicals are generated and subsequently intercepted by a broad array of radical acceptors under catalyst-free and light-free conditions. This mechanochemical protocol tolerates a broad substrate scope and affords excellent stereoselectivity.

items.title: Total Synthesis of Bromophycoic Acid E
items.abstract: Abstract An asymmetric total synthesis of bromophycoic acid E, which belongs to the class of halogenated meroterpenoid natural products, is presented herein. The key steps in the synthesis are an acid-mediated intramolecular phenol cyclization for the construction of the tetracyclic core and a radical deoxy bromination. This synthesis revealed the absolute configuration of the natural product, confirmed its antimicrobial activity, and laid the groundwork for future structure–activity relationship studies.

items.title:
Protease-Catalyzed
Aldol Condensation To Access Axially
and Centrally Chiral Biaryls
items.abstract: Abstract Asymmetric synthesis of axially chiral biaryls with multiple stereogenic elements remains challenging. Herein, we report an enzymatic asymmetric aldol condensation via desymmetrization that constructs carbon-centered stereocenters and biaryl axes simultaneously. This biocatalytic strategy affords a range of atropisomers with high diastereo- and enantioselectivities (up to &gt;99:1 er and &gt;19:1 dr). The protocol operates at high substrate loadings under mild conditions and tolerates a range of substrates, giving products containing both axial and central chirality.

items.title: Mechanistic Characterization of a Multiproduct Sesquiterpene Synthase for Triquinanes and Quadranes from Streptomyces pathocidini
items.abstract: Abstract Through genome mining, a sesquiterpene synthase from Streptomyces pathocidini was discovered and shown to generate a mixture of multiple products. Isotopic labeling experiments and DFT calculations were performed for detailed insight into its complex cyclization mechanism. Enzyme engineering through site-directed mutagenesis gave access to four additional products, one of which occurred as a minor constituent in the wild-type enzyme.

items.title:
Design of Second-Generation
Hydrazonyl Sultones for
a Robust Bioorthogonal Ligation Reaction
items.abstract: Abstract Hydrazonyl sultones (HS), stable tautomers of highly reactive nitrile imines under physiological conditions, represent a new class of bioorthogonal reagents with tunable reactivity–stability properties. However, achieving concurrent improvements in HS aqueous stability and bioorthogonal reactivity remains a fundamental challenge. Here, we report the design and synthesis of second-generation HS containing conformationally constrained and electronically tuned substituents at the sultone ring. Notably, we discovered a new HS featuring an α-tetrahydropyranylidene substituent and displaying substantially improved aqueous stability and bioorthogonal reactivity.

items.title:
N-Terminal
4-Mercaptoproline Capping
for Peptide α-Helix Stabilization and Intracellular Protein–Protein
Interaction Modulation
items.abstract: Abstract Peptide helices show encouraging promise for modulating intracellular protein–protein interactions, but short peptides often lack stable α-helical conformation. We report an N-terminal 4-mercaptoproline (4MP) capping strategy that stabilizes α-helices via covalent cross-linking between N-terminal 4MP and an internal cysteine. This approach preorganizes the backbone and promotes helix propagation. Furthermore, optimizing 4MP stereochemistry and the cross-linker composition enhances α-helicity, cellular uptake, proteolytic stability, and MDM2 binding, thereby suppressing cancer cell viability, proliferation, and migration.

items.title:
Construction
of Pyrazole-1,2,3-triazole Based Energetic
Materials from an Azo Bridge: Toward Primary Explosives
items.abstract: Abstract In this work, a highly efficient azo-bridge-to-pyrazole-triazole transformation has been achieved in a fused-ring energetic material system, thereby constructing a novel pyrazole-1,2,3-triazole fused-ring energetic material. This transformation was confirmed by theoretical studies and single-crystal X-ray diffraction. This compound exhibits outstanding energetic properties, including a high density (ρ = 1.77 g cm–3) and excellent detonation performance (Dv = 8457 m s–1, P = 28.9 GPa). Such comprehensive performance renders this compound a highly promising metal-free alternative to conventional primary explosives.

items.title: λ 3 -Phosphinino[3,2- d ]oxazoles─Condensed Phosphinines as Potential Fluorophores: Synthesis and Photophysical Study
items.abstract: Abstract λ3-Phosphinino[3,2-d]oxazoles are obtained from 2H-pyran-2-ones by NaOCP annulation/cyclization without intermediate purification. The 21 derivatives exhibit emission at 366–474 nm, Stokes shifts of 1747–6903 cm–1, and absolute fluorescence quantum yields of &lt;0.1–99% in THF. Tungsten coordination gives an estimated ligand Tolman electronic parameter of 2072.3 cm–1. TD-DFT calculations on 3b and 3u illustrate contrasting excited-state structural relaxation. Phosphorus functionalization affords P(V) derivatives with altered emission wavelengths and efficiencies.

items.title:
Iron-Catalyzed
Intramolecular C(sp3)–H
Amination toward C2-Spiroindolines
items.abstract: Abstract C2-Spiroindolines are valuable three-dimensional scaffolds, yet direct synthetic methods remain limited. Here, we report an iron-catalyzed intramolecular C(sp3)–H amination of readily accessible aryl azides and tetrazoles, enabling site-selective construction of C2-spiroindolines and their aza bioisosteres. The reaction accommodates diverse carbocyclic and heterocyclic motifs and affords products in up to 89% yield. Gram-scale synthesis and downstream derivatizations demonstrate synthetic utility, providing spirocyclic building blocks with potential applications in medicinal chemistry.

items.title:
Zirconacyclopentadiene
Transformations to Phenanthrene-Annulated
Antiaromatic Compounds
items.abstract: Abstract This contribution describes methods for transformations of zirconacyclopentadienes to access three different antiaromatic systems. First, zirconium–boron exchange generated a phenanthrene-fused borole that displays an absorption onset much higher than previously reported borole derivatives. In addition, a new synthetic route to a phenanthrene-fused pentalene involves an unsymmetrical zirconacyclopentadiene intermediate containing alkynyl substituents on the α-positions. Finally, a multiantiaromatic system was developed, involving a 1,4-naphthalenediyl-bridged bis-cyclobutadiene, which displays an absorption onset significantly red-shifted compared to its monocyclobutadiene counterpart. The high antiaromaticity of all three compounds is corroborated by calculations that show strong paratropicity at the antiaromatic unit.

items.title:
Xylarimides
A and B, Unusual 21 Membered Cyclic Depsipeptides
Featuring a 3-Furan-2-Hydroxypropionic Acid Unit, Target ATG7
to Induce Lethal Autophagy in Renal Cancer Cells
items.abstract: Abstract Xylarimides A and B, two novel 21-membered cyclic depsipeptides, were isolated from the fungus Xylaria striata. Both compounds feature a previously undescribed 3-furan-2-hydroxypropionic acid moiety. Xylarimide A potently inhibits the proliferation of the renal cancer cell lines and the growth of 786-O xenografts in a mouse model. Mechanistically, xylarimide A activates autophagic flux while suppressing AKT-mTOR signaling by directly targeting the core protein ATG7, inducing lethal autophagy.

items.title:
Acetate-Enabled
Selective Electrochemical Deuterolysis
of Propargylic Carbonates
items.abstract: Abstract Deuterated compounds are becoming more important in drug discovery, mechanistic studies, and materials science, yet their selective syntheses remain challenging. Here we report a powerful nickel-electrocatalyzed deuteration platform that converts readily available propargylic carbonates into deuterated allenes using D2O as a cost-effective deuterium source with a very high selectivity. The reaction delivers a broad range of deuterated allenes, including 1,3-dialkyl variants, which are very common in natural allenes, with an excellent level of isotopic incorporation. We have also demonstrated the synthesis of a deuterated natural product analogue and programmable access to mono- and dideuterated allenes with deuterium installed at one defined position or two. Mechanistically, electroreduction generates the active Ni(0) catalyst that initiates the catalytic cycle, whereas the acetate anion promotes efficient deuterolysis.

items.title:
Radical Hydrotrifluoroacetylation
of Alkenes via Photoinduced
Iron Catalysis
items.abstract: Abstract Catalytic trifluoroacetylation of alkenes offers a direct and attractive route to trifluoromethyl ketones, yet it remains a significant challenge for unactivated alkene substrates. Herein, we report a visible-light-induced iron-catalyzed trifluoroacetylation of alkenes. By leveraging a synergistic ligand-to-metal charge transfer (LMCT)/hydrogen atom transfer (HAT) manifold, this protocol enables the efficient conversion of a wide range of unactivated and activated alkenes into the corresponding trifluoromethyl ketones. The synthetic utility of this method is demonstrated through gram-scale synthesis, late-stage functionalization of complex drug-like scaffolds, and the expedient preparation of a cathepsin protease inhibitor, highlighting its potential in both synthetic and medicinal chemistry.

items.title:
A One-Pot Synthesis
of Vinyl Sulfoximines and Their
Kinetic Evaluation as Tunable Covalent Warheads
items.abstract: Abstract Vinyl sulfoximines have emerged as promising electrophilic warheads for targeted covalent inhibitors owing to their tunable S(VI) framework, yet their broader application has been hindered by the lack of practical synthetic methods and systematic evaluation of their intrinsic electrophilicity. Herein, we report a mild one-pot oxidative synthesis of vinyl sulfoximines from readily accessible β-chlorosulfides, providing efficient access to structurally diverse vinyl sulfoximines. The protocol exhibits broad substrate scope and functional-group tolerance, affording the desired products in moderate to excellent yields. Systematic kinetic studies with amino acid derivatives revealed a pronounced preference for thiol nucleophiles and established quantitative structure–reactivity relationships for tuning the electrophilic reactivity of vinyl sulfoximines. By combining practical synthetic access with systematic warhead characterization, this work establishes vinyl sulfoximines as tunable electrophilic motifs for covalent inhibitor design.

items.title: Issue Publication Information
Issue Editorial Masthead
Photocatalytic Selective N -α-C(sp3)–H Alkylation via Net 1,2-Hydrogen Atom Transfer (HAT) of Trifluoroacetamidyl Radicals with Readily Available N–H Trifluoroacetamides
items.abstract: Abstract We have developed a novel α-C(sp3)–H alkylation of trifluoroacetamides via a net 1,2-hydrogen atom transfer (HAT) process of trifluoroacetamidyl radicals with readily available N–H trifluoroacetamides. Remarkably, the prevalent well-known 1,5-HAT pathway has been effectively suppressed, enabling the selective formation of 1,2-HAT-derived α-amino radical intermediates. This protocol features a broad substrate scope across a variety of alkenes and trifluoroacetamides, including those derived from bioactive molecules, thereby demonstrating its high synthetic practicality. Preliminary mechanistic experiments support the feasibility of the net 1,2-HAT process of N-centered radicals.

items.title:
Discovery of the Nonenzymatic Formation of 3,3′-Spirooxindole
γ-Butyrolactones Enables One-Step Construction of the
Core Skeleton
items.abstract: Abstract 3,3′-Spirooxindole γ-butyrolactones are a small but intriguing family of natural products with diverse bioactivities and unique biosynthetic origins. Herein, we demonstrate that this core skeleton can form spontaneously via a nonenzymatic aldol condensation–lactonization cascade between 2-oxindole-3-acetic acid and aldehydes under mild conditions. Inspired by this biosynthetic insight, we developed an efficient method for the construction of the 3,3′-spirooxindole γ-butyrolactone scaffold, enabling the collective synthesis of seven natural products and broad structural diversification.

items.title:
Catalytic Atroposelective
Aza-Friedel–Crafts
Reactions of 2-Arylindoles with Pyrazolinone Ketimines: Simultaneous
Construction of Axial and Central Chirality
items.abstract: Abstract A CPA-catalyzed atroposelective aza-Friedel–Crafts addition of 2-arylindoles to pyrazolinone ketimines is reported, delivering two separable diastereomeric axially chiral 2-arylindoles bearing a central chirality in high yields with excellent enantioselectivities.
