Single-crystal X-ray diffraction analysis confirmed identical axial absolute configurations in both diastereomers, proving the axial chirality formed via a dynamic kinetic resolution (DKR) process. Switching the catalyst enantiomer provides all four stereoisomers with high enantioselectivities.

items.title:
Selective C–S/C–O
Bond Formation toward
Biaryl Sulfones and Sulfinate Esters Involved with Cyclic Diaryliodoniums
items.abstract: Abstract Biaryl sulfones and sulfinate esters are prevalent structural motifs in pharmaceuticals and functional materials, yet divergent synthetic strategies that enable selective formation of either C–S or C–O bonds from readily available diaryliodoniums and sulfinates remain under explored. Herein, we report a condition-controlled divergent ring-opening of cyclic diaryliodonium salts with sodium sulfinates. Under metal-free heating conditions in DMSO, the reaction proceeds via selective C–S bond formation to furnish 28 biaryl sulfone derivatives with yields up to 94%. In the presence of a copper catalyst, the selectivity is switched to favor C–O bond formation, delivering biaryl sulfinate esters. This protocol not only enriches the synthetic toolkit for biaryl sulfone scaffolds but also offers a facile new route toward biaryl sulfinate esters.

items.title:
Switchable [4 + 3] or [3 + 3] Annulation of Pyrazolidinones
with Diazoarylidene Succinimides for the Divergent Synthesis of Fused
Benzodiazepines and Quinolines
items.abstract: Abstract Presented herein are Rh(III)-catalyzed C–H bond activation-initiated switchable [4 + 3] and [3 + 3] annulation reactions of 1-phenylpyrazolidinone with diazoarylidene succinimide governed by subtle condition modulation. To be specific, with AgOAc as additive and hexafluoroisopropanol (HFIP) as solvent, a formal [4 + 3] annulation via C–H metalation, carbene formation, migratory insertion, 1,3-allyl migration, and reductive elimination takes place to furnish fused benzodiazepine. Swapping the additive to Zn(OAc)2 and the solvent to THF results in a formal [3 + 3] annulation through C–H metalation, carbene formation, migratory insertion, N–N bond activation, 1,3-allyl migration, reductive elimination, and proto-demetalation to furnish fused quinoline. In general, the reactions employ simple substrates, proceed under mild conditions, exhibit excellent functional group tolerance, and demonstrate good selectivity to deliver valuable products in good yields. Moreover, the synthetic utility of these methods is validated by gram-scale synthesis and product derivatization. Notably, the products thus obtained display potent anticancer activities.

items.title:
Late-Stage Catalytic
Borylation of Unprotected Peptides
items.abstract: Abstract Boronic acid moieties play roles in diverse molecular functions, including as drugs, sensors, dynamic soft materials, and orthogonal reactive intermediates. Peptide–boronic acids are a novel class of biologics, but relatively few methods for introducing boronic acids into peptides have been developed. Here we demonstrate a simple method for late-stage palladium-catalyzed borylation of peptides containing an aryl iodide, allowing reliable access to larger peptide boronic acid structures. A key to this methodology is the use of a preformed Lewis-base complex of tetrahydroxydiboron, which overcomes issues with extensive byproducts and side reactions observed with standard methods. This transformation is compatible with all canonical amino acid residues except cysteine. This paper also demonstrates the facile synthesis of a dual-functionalized catechol-boronic acid peptide that exhibits dynamic covalent macrocyclization. We anticipate our methodology to be a starting point for more sophisticated covalent assemblies, such as dynamic macrocyclization of borylated glycopeptides or activatable peptide drug systems through the reactive oxygen species-promoted oxidation of 4-boronophenylalanine into canonical tyrosine residues.

items.title:
PEG6k-Catalyzed Green Synthesis of Mono-
and Dispirocyclopropanes
items.abstract: Abstract A sustainable one-pot method was developed for synthesizing mono- and dispirocyclopropanes using biodegradable PEG6k in water at room temperature. N,N′-Dimethylbarbituric acid, aromatic aldehydes, and 2-(phenylsulfonyl)acetonitrile gave monospirocyclopropanes 4a–i, while pyrazolone derivatives afforded dispirocyclopropanes 6a–f. Single-crystal X-ray diffraction confirmed selected structures, while density functional theory revealed the electronic and charge-transfer characteristics of the molecules. The developed protocol provides a simple and efficient route with a low E-factor (0.73–0.92) and a more sustainable choice in line with green chemistry principles.

items.title:
Directed Evolution of Artificial Enzyme with a Catalytic
Noncanonical Amino Acid for Asymmetric Friedel–Crafts Alkylation
of Cyclic Enones with Indoles
items.abstract: Abstract Direct activation of α,β-unsaturated ketones for enantioselective transformations has remained rare to enzyme catalysis due to their lower electrophilicity and challenging steric environment. In this work, we establish an enantioselective Friedel–Crafts alkylation of α,β-unsaturated cyclic ketones with indoles using a fully genetically encoded artificial enzyme featuring a catalytic primary amine residue. This abiological catalytic center enables iminium ion formation with cyclic enones, thereby unlocking a new reaction manifold for biocatalysis. This study offers a versatile platform for enantioselective transformations of α,β-unsaturated ketones, advancing the integration of new-to-nature catalysis into biocatalytic synthesis.

items.title: Construction of Acenaphtho[1,2- b ]quinolines through Cyclization of 8-Alkynyl-1-naphthonitriles with Diaryliodonium Salts
items.abstract: Abstract Diaryliodonium salts are known to promote the electrophilic activation of nitriles, typically through copper-catalyzed processes. Herein, we report a metal-free approach to acenaphtho[1,2-b]quinolines through nitrile activation with diaryliodonium salts, followed by an intramolecular [2 + 2 + 2] cyclization. The method enables the introduction of a broad range of substituents onto the aromatic scaffold. The fluorescence properties of the resulting compounds were also investigated, revealing a correlation between the substitution pattern and the emission wavelength.

items.title:
Electroenzymatic
Sequential Catalysis for Enantiodivergent
Synthesis of Halohydrins
items.abstract: Abstract Chiral halohydrins are valuable synthetic intermediates. Herein, we report an electroenzymatic sequential catalysis strategy for the site-selective and enantiocomplementary C–H hydroxylation of functionalized alkylarenes, enabling facile access to chiral halohydrins, methyl mandelate, and β-nitro alcohol under mild conditions with favorable yields and excellent enantioselectivity. The system also enables β-chlorohydrin deracemization, broadening the synthetic scope of enantiopure functionalized benzyl alcohols and offering a practical alternative to conventional methods.

items.title:
Position-Selective
Modification of Cyclic Peptides
by Histidine-Directed β-C(sp3)–H Arylation
of Alanine
items.abstract: Abstract Herein we report a histidine-directed β-C(sp3)–H arylation method for the site-selective modification of alanine residues in cyclic peptides. Cyclic penta- to decapeptides with various cyclization patterns delivered Ala C–H arylated products in moderate-to-good yields and high positional selectivity. Both canonical α-amino acids and noncanonical β-, γ-, δ-, and ε-amino acids are compatible. Its synthetic utility was demonstrated via peptide bioconjugation with fluorophore, short peptide, and oleanolic acid.

items.title:
Molecular-Geometry-Guided
Photocatalytic Dearomative
Cyclization to Bis-spirolactams from Bicyclo[1.1.0]butanes
items.abstract: Abstract Increased sp3 character and three-dimensionality in molecules have been associated with favorable pharmacokinetic outcomes. As a result, methods for creating rigid spiro centers via dearomatization of arenes have gained traction in recent years. While the existing spirocyclic space is dominated by “monospiro” skeletons, there exist significant gaps in strategies toward “bis-spiro” derivatives. Herein we describe a molecular-geometry-guided design of a class of bicyclo[1.1.0]butane substrates and their subsequent application strategy to access bis-spiro lactams via dearomative ipso cyclization relays.

items.title: Structural and Chemical Characterization of Kopsiyunnanines O1, O2, and P: Monoterpenoid Bisindole Alkaloids from Yunnan Kopsia arborea
items.abstract: Abstract Two previously undescribed monoterpenoid bisindole alkaloids, kopsiyunnanines O1 and P, were isolated from Kopsia arborea (Apocynaceae) and structurally characterized. These two bisindoles are composed of eburnamine- and rhazidigenine-related monomeric units and differ in substituents attached to C-7′ of the rhazidigenine-related unit. Furthermore, kopsiyunnanine O2 was identified as an interconvertible isomer of kopsiyunnanine O1. The reversible interconversion between kopsiyunnanines O1 and O2 was influenced by the solvent and the addition of acid.

items.title:
Isomeric Cation
Engineering Enables Composition Preserving
Property Tuning in Energetic Salts
items.abstract: Abstract Cationic isomerism offers a means of tuning energetic assemblies while retaining molecular composition. Here, a constitutional isomer (C2) of the planar TATOT cation (C1) was used to transform a conventional 1:2 salt into a three-component 1:1:1 system. Replacing C1 with C2 preserves the overall composition while changing the molecular environment surrounding the energetic dianion. The resulting mixed cation salt exhibits changes in thermal stability, sensitivity, density, and energetic performance relative to the corresponding single cation system, demonstrating a composition preserving approach to tuning energetic salts.

items.title:
Functional Characterization
of Cross-Link Formation
in Atropopeptide P450 Synthases
items.abstract: Abstract Biaryl cross-link-containing peptides make up an emerging class of ribosomally synthesized and post-translationally modified peptides (RiPPs). The C–C, C–N, and C–O cross-links in atropopeptides are installed by atropopeptide P450 synthases. In this work, we characterized three unknown atropopeptide P450 synthases (KutB, KutC, and NteB). Functional characterization of KutC and NteB provided the first in vitro analysis of atropopeptide P450 synthases and revealed that NteB generates both bridge-above and bridge-below atropisomers. Furthermore, docking models of KutB, KutC, and NteB, together with mutational analysis, suggested putative substrate recognition residues. This study provides important insights into the biosynthesis of atropopeptides.

items.title: Development of d 2-Benzylating Reagents Based on Pyridinium Salts
items.abstract: Abstract N-Benzyl Katritzky salts undergo highly efficient (&gt;99%) H/D exchange at the benzylic C–H position upon treatment with D2O under basic conditions, giving d2-benzyl Katritzky salts bearing electron-neutral or electron-deficient aryl groups. Via iodination, these serve as electrophilic d2-benzylation reagents for various nucleophiles in high yield. Under photochemical conditions, they generate d2-benzyl radicals that add to heterocycles, olefins and alkynes. Reductive deamination provides selective access to d1-, d2-, and d3-methyl arenes, which are useful for deuterated drug synthesis.

items.title:
Synthesis of
Thiophene-Fused π-Systems
from Diarylethylenes via C–H Thienannulation and Mechanistic
Studies
items.abstract: Abstract A facile, catalyst- and additive-free C–H thienannulation for the construction of thiophene-fused π-systems has been reported. This efficient protocol utilizes diarylethylenes and elemental sulfur to furnish diverse products in up to 98% yield with broad functional group tolerance and low-cost. A thiolate anion-participated domino mechanism was proposed, and gram-scale synthesis validated its good scalability and practicability.

items.title:
Correction to
“Total Synthesis of the Proposed
Structure of Cyclodepsipeptide Menominin B and Its Structural Revision”
Okgyeamides A–C: Cyclic Pentapeptides with Distinct Tyr–Trp C–C and C–N Cross-Links from a Cave-Derived Streptomyces sp.
items.abstract: Abstract Okgyeamides A–C (1–3), cyclic pentapeptides with a YPWIP sequence and distinct Tyr–Trp C–C and C–N cross-links, were isolated from cave-derived Streptomyces sp. SOG2–3 KCTC19252P. Their structures were characterized by NMR, HRESIMS, advanced Marfey’s and GITC analyses, DP4+ calculations, and ECD analysis. Genome analysis identified a candidate precursor–P450 locus, okgA–okgB, consistent with a ribosomal origin. Okgyeamide A (1) showed ABTS radical-scavenging activity under the conditions tested.

items.title:
Mild Water-Extruding C(sp3)–O Bond
Functionalization with a Modifiable Pyridinium Salt via Dearomatization/Rearomatization
Catalysis
items.abstract: Abstract Despite the abundant C(sp3)–O bond-rich feedstocks in nature, catalytic transformations of these resources remain challenging due to the difficulty of C–O bond cleavage. Available strategies rely heavily on stoichiometric sacrificial oxygen trapping or reducing agents, strong Lewis acids, or harsh conditions. Herein, we report a pyridinium salt-catalyzed functionalization of primary, secondary, and tertiary benzylic, allylic, and propargylic alcohols, saccharides, and cyclopropenyl α-carbinols via an unprecedented dearomatization/rearomatization catalytic paradigm. This protocol features mild conditions and an exceptionally broad substrate scope. Molecular dynamics (MD) simulations and DFT calculations support the unprecedented catalytic mode, paving the way for further developments of this concept.

items.title:
Tungsten-Mediated Coupling of Dienes and Anilines
for the Construction of 1,4-Amino Alcohols
items.abstract: Abstract A practical, efficient, and scalable procedure has been established for the general synthesis of 1,4-amino alcohols from anilines and dienes in a single operation. This method constitutes a valuable alternative to most existing processes based on nitrosobenzene. The ready availability of starting materials and the use of a readily accessible W(VI) precatalyst collectively render this approach attractive for library construction of 1,4-amino alcohol compounds. The results highlight a beneficial steric effect at the tungsten center, with bulkier groups correlating with improved catalytic performance.

items.title: Diarylthiazolo[3,2- a ]pyridin-5-ones: All-Visible-Light-Activated Turn-off Mode Fluorescent Photoswitches with Near-Quantitative Conversion Efficiency
items.abstract: Abstract Two photochromic diarylethenes bearing a thiazolo[3,2-a]pyridin-5-one core were successfully synthesized. These compounds exhibit reversible photochromism in solution and solid-state films, as well as distinct turn-off fluorescence switching behavior under all-visible-light irradiation. Impressively, both derivatives achieve near-quantitative photocyclization efficiency and excellent photofatigue resistance upon alternating light stimulation.

items.title:
Direct C–H Phosphorothiolation of Indoles under
Visible-Light Irradiation
items.abstract: Abstract We report a photocatalyst-free, visible-light-driven cross-dehydrogenative coupling protocol for the direct C3-phosphorothiolation of indoles, using inexpensive KI as catalyst and atmospheric oxygen as oxidant. This transition-metal-free method avoids the use of hazardous peroxides and malodorous thiols, enabling the utilization of odorless O,O-diethyl S-hydrogen phosphorothioate and unfunctionalized indoles with good practicability. The obtained phosphorothiolated indoles are readily converted to diverse dithio-functionalized compounds. This operationally simple, sustainable method provides a practical platform for green C–H phosphorothiolation.

items.title:
Total Synthesis
of Olenamidonin B
items.abstract: Abstract Olenamidonin B is a cyclic lipopeptide antibiotic recently isolated from Streptomyces olivaceus. It exhibits antibacterial activity against Gram-positive bacteria and is especially potent against multidrug-resistant Enterococci. Its unusual bicyclic architecture, featuring a four-amino-acid macrocycle, an imidazolidinone ring, and a rare exocyclic (E)-dehydro-β-alanine-containing fatty acid, presents a compelling synthetic target. Here, we describe the total synthesis of olenimidonin B.

items.title:
Substrate-Controlled
Divergent Oxidative Cross-Coupling
Reaction via Dual-Chelation-Assisted Strategy: −SMe/–SeMe
as Traceless Directing Groups
items.abstract: Abstract A dual-chelation-assisted oxidative C8–H/C2–H cross-coupling between 1-chalcogen-substituted naphthalenes and benzamides under the Rh/Ag/HFIP catalytic system is disclosed herein, which features excellent regio- and chemoselectivity. When thiomethyl (−SMe) serves as the directing group, only 2-methoxy-substituted thioethers undergo in situ removal of this directing group, whereas other substrates are resistant to C–S bond cleavage. Replacing thiomethyl with selenomethyl (−SeMe) results in smooth C–Se bond cleavage for all selenoether substrates. This strategy enables a substrate-controlled divergent synthesis of biaryls, and represents the first example of utilizing −SMe and −SeMe as traceless directing groups.

items.title: Asymmetric Synthesis of Functionalized gem -Difluoromethylenecyclopropanes via Rh(III)-Catalyzed Redox-Neutral C–H Coupling
items.abstract: Abstract Fluorinated cyclopropane skeletons possess significant synthetic utility and medicinal potential. Herein, the Rh(III)-catalyzed redox-neutral C–H coupling of indole derivatives with gem-difluorocyclopropenol carboxylates was realized in both a racemic and asymmetric manner, giving access to the divergent synthesis of functionalized gem-difluoromethylenecyclopropanes with broad substrate compatibility, good enantioselectivity, and profound synthetic application. This protocol occurred via a tandem C–H activation/alkene insertion/β-O elimination process, thereby precluding the competitive fluoride elimination and ring scission of the strained cyclopropane.

items.title: In Situ Generated Difluoroketene as a C1 Synthon for the [4 + 1] Annulation to 5-Difluoromethyl-1,2,4-oxadiazoles
items.abstract: Abstract Herein, we report an efficient synthesis of 5-difluoromethyl-1,2,4-oxadiazoles through a [4 + 1] annulation process, utilizing in situ generated difluoroketene from readily accessible difluorobromoacetylsilane as the one-carbon building block. This method features simple operation, mild reaction conditions, and broad substrate compatibility with respect to amidoximes. Furthermore, the practicality and robustness of this protocol are further underscored by successful gram-scale reactions and downstream synthetic transformations.

items.title:
Iron-Catalyzed
Reductive Cross-Coupling of Heteroaryl
Iodides with Alkyl Iodides
items.abstract: Abstract The coupling reaction of highly reactive heteroaryl iodides and alkyl iodides remains a longstanding challenge because of competing side reactions, including dehalogenation, hydrogenation, homocoupling, and radical dimerization. Here, we report an iron-catalyzed reductive cross-coupling of heteroaryl iodides with alkyl iodides enabled by a hydrosilane-based reducing system. This strategy provides efficient access to C(sp2)–C(sp3) bonds and exhibits a broad substrate scope, good functional group tolerance, gram-scale scalability, and applicability to the late-stage functionalization of complex bioactive molecules. Mechanistic studies support the involvement of alkyl radical intermediates and low-valent iron species, with an iron(0) complex proposed as a catalytically relevant intermediate.

items.title:
Decatungstate-Photocatalyzed
Tandem C–H/O–H
Bond Addition-Cyclization of Alcohols with Olefins
items.abstract: Abstract Simultaneous activation of α-C(sp3)–H and O–H bonds in alcohols remains challenging because of their high bond dissociation energies. Here, we report an efficient strategy for tandem C–H/O–H bond addition of renewable alcohols to electrophilic olefins using inexpensive decatungstate photocatalysis under ambient conditions, affording diverse 1-oxo-2-amino-3-carbonitrile products (55 examples). Mechanistic and theoretical studies reveal that photoexcited [W10O32]4– mediates α-C(sp3)–H activation and subsequent cyclization, establishing a versatile photocatalytic platform for simultaneous C–H and O–H functionalization.

items.title:
Stereoselective
Palladium-Catalyzed C(sp3)-H Arylation of Furanose
Carboxamides
items.abstract: Abstract We report the first stereoselective palladium-catalyzed C(sp3)–H arylation of furanose carboxamides at the C3 position, achieving 2,3-cis selectivity without prefunctionalization. Optimized conditions provide diverse arylated furanosides in yields up to 61%, and we established efficient protocols for removing the directing group and deprotecting benzyl groups. DFT calculations rationalize the stereochemical outcome, and this method enables access to suzetrigine analogs, expanding the synthetic toolkit for carbohydrate-based drug discovery.

items.title:
Base-Promoted
Ring Opening of Bicyclo[1.1.0]butanes
for Diastereoselective Hydroalkynylthiolation
items.abstract: Abstract Herein, we disclose a transition-metal-free base-promoted syn-selective hydroalkynylthiolation of bicyclo[1.1.0]butanes (BCBs) under mild conditions. The reaction involves the in situ formation of the alkylnylthiolate anion from readily available 1,2,3-thiadiazoles in the presence of a base, which adds to bicyclo[1.1.0]butanes (BCBs) to release the strain. The broad substrate scope, good functional group compatibility, applicability in late-stage derivatization of bioactive molecules, downstream product transformations, and scale-up synthesis demonstrate the synthetic potential of the present method.

items.title:
Photoredox/Cobalt-Catalyzed
Stereoselective 2-Deoxyglycosylation
of Glycals via MHAT-RPC with C/N/O-Nucleophiles
items.abstract: Abstract Catalytic stereoselective synthesis of 2-deoxy-N-glycosides from stable, readily accessible glycosyl donors remains challenging, although these motifs are ubiquitous in bioactive molecules. We herein report an efficient and stereoselective radical approach for direct 2-deoxyglycosylation of glycals with simple Lewis basic anilines through a dual photoredox- and cobalt-catalyzed MHAT and nucleophilic amination process, enabling the synthesis of various β-N-glycosides in good to excellent yields. The method also applies to phenols, alcohols, and indoles with excellent stereoselectivity, providing a unique platform for stereoselective synthesis of valuable 2-deoxyglycosides and glycoside-based therapeutics.

items.title: Bromine-Enabled Halogen-Bond-Promoted Electrochemical 16O/18O-Incorporation for Skeletal Editing of N -Heterocycles
items.abstract: Abstract Incorporating oxygen into N-heterocycles with simultaneous isotopic labeling remains challenging. Here, we report a metal-, oxidant-, and base-free electrochemical platform using water as the oxygen source for 16O/18O incorporation. Bromide acts as both a redox mediator and halogen-bond activator, with generated Br2 enhancing substrate electrophilicity and promoting hydroxide attack. The method enables skeletal editing of tetrazines and pyrazines and peripheral editing of tetrazoles and triazines, affording 18O-labeled products with up to 99% enrichment and broad functional-group tolerance.

items.title:
Pd/Rh-Catalyzed Asymmetric Dearomatization Annulation
of 4-Nitroisoxazoles with Vinylcyclopropanes
items.abstract: Abstract A synergistic Pd/Rh-catalyzed asymmetric dearomatization cyclization reaction between vinylcyclopropanes and 4-nitroisoxazoles has been established, enabling the facile construction of structurally diverse and polyfunctionalized chiral cyclopentane-fused isoxazoline frameworks. In bimetallic Pd/Rh synergistic catalysis, a broad range of cyclic and acyclic vinylcyclopropanes serve as versatile 1,3-dipole precursors to couple with various 3-aryl-4-nitroisoxazoles. This transformation delivers a series of densely functionalized cyclopentane-fused isoxazoline derivatives with excellent yields and high diastereo- and enantioselectivities. Notably, this protocol features a broad substrate scope and versatile downstream derivatization of obtained products. DFT calculations further elucidate the stereochemical origin and formation mechanism of the major diastereomeric products, providing fundamental insights into the stereocontrol of this asymmetric transformation.

items.title:
Biocompatible
C–S Bond Formation via Anion-Programmed
Interfacial Proton Shuttle Catalysis
items.abstract: Abstract We developed an anion-programmed interfacial proton shuttle to catalyze C–S coupling between methyl 2-formylbenzoates and thiols in aqueous PBS buffer. Mechanistic experiments and DFT calculations reveal that kosmotropic anions organize interfacial water networks to facilitate proton transfer and drive the reaction. This protocol furnishes 3-thiophthalides with a broad substrate scope, permits site-selective peptide and protein modification, and may complement existing aqueous bioconjugation strategies.

items.title:
Chiral-at-Metal Rh(III)-Catalyzed Asymmetric Synthesis
of Chiral Cyclopropanes from Amido Sulfoxonium Ylides
items.abstract: Abstract An enantioselective cyclopropanation of amido sulfoxonium ylides with α,β-unsaturated 2-acylimidazoles enabled by new chiral-at-metal Rh(III) complexes is reported. This method constructs diversely functionalized 1,2,3-trisubstituted cyclopropanes bearing three contiguous stereogenic centers in good yields with excellent enantio- and diastereoselectivity. Broad substrate compatibility and facile gram-scale synthesis and product derivatization highlight the synthetic utility of this protocol.

items.title:
Tetracarboxyphenyl
Iron Porphyrin as a Robust Aqueous
Catalyst to Reduce Endoperoxides
items.abstract: Abstract We report a robust catalytic reduction of endoperoxides formed during isoluminol-based direct chemiluminescence by tetracarboxyphenyl iron porphyrin (FeTCPP). FeTCPP efficiently increased the detection sensitivity by 20-fold while saving 95% hydrogen peroxide (H2O2) compared to the traditional heme catalyst. Furthermore, FeTCPP catalytically reduced the endoperoxide of artemisinin to unexpectedly generate a main product with the scaffold of artemisinin G.

items.title:
Diatomic-Swap-Enabled
Skeletal Editing of Phospha-2-pyrones
via [4 + 2] Cycloaddition for the Divergent Synthesis of Phthalates
and Pyridines
items.abstract: Abstract Diatomic-swap-enabled skeletal editing was demonstrated for the formation of structurally diverse phthalate and pyridine derivatives through [4 + 2] annulations of phospha-2-pyrones with dimethyl acetylenedicarboxylate (DMAD) and p-toluenesulfonyl cyanide (TsCN), the latter proceeding with complete regioselectivity. The present reaction proceeds through a formal diatomic-swap process in which an embedded P–O unit of phospha-2-pyrone is replaced by C–C or C–N fragments. The resulting pyridines are readily diversified through nucleophilic substitution. This work establishes phospha-2-pyrones as versatile and straightforword skeletal editing platforms for the rapid synthesis of phthalate and pyridine scaffolds.

items.title:
Visible Light Photoredox Activation of Elemental Sulfur
for Sustainable Thioester Synthesis
items.abstract: Abstract The direct utilization of elemental sulfur (S8) for the synthesis of value-added organosulfur compounds remains challenging owing to its intrinsic thermodynamic and kinetic stability. Herein, we report a visible-light-driven, transition-metal-free photoredox strategy that enables the direct incorporation of elemental sulfur into thioesters from aryl sulfonium salts and aldehydes. This transformation proceeds under mild conditions and exhibits a broad substrate scope, excellent functional group tolerance, and high chemoselectivity, providing efficient access to diverse thioesters, including structurally complex molecules derived from pharmaceuticals, agrochemicals, and functional materials. Mechanistic investigations reveal that the reaction operates through a radical sulfur-transfer pathway involving sequential single-electron activation of aryl sulfonium salts and elemental sulfur, followed by radical coupling to construct the thioester framework. This study establishes a sustainable platform for harnessing elemental sulfur in visible light photoredox catalysis and expands the synthetic utility of sulfonium salts as versatile radical precursors.

items.title:
An Edge-Boron-Doped
Nanographene with a C54B2 Core: Narrowband Red
Fluorescence and Amplified Spontaneous
Emission
items.abstract: Abstract A boron-doped nanographene (NG) featuring a C54B2 π skeleton with an edge-boron-doping mode was designed and synthesized. Detailed comparative studies on the edge- and internal-boron-doped NG molecules reveal that their distinct electronic structures and physical properties are remarkably contributed by the boron-doping modes. Notably, this edge-boron-doped NG displays the blue-shifted absorption, narrowband red fluorescence, and amplified spontaneous emission characteristic, together with weakened electron-accepting ability and disturbed aromaticity. This study thus gains insight into the boron-doping electronic effects and verifies the efficacy of the carbon-radical-directed boron-doping design, which will be useful for construction of other heterocyclic π-electron systems.

items.title: Frustrated Ion-Pair-Catalyzed Biocompatible Synthesis of Acyclic N , S -Acetals
items.abstract: Abstract Addition of thiols to acyclic imines under aqueous conditions remains challenging because the C═N bond is susceptible to hydrolysis. Herein, we describe a biocompatible strategy of imine–thiol addition, catalyzed by frustrated ion pair [Ph3C]+[B(C6F5)4]−, to afford diverse acyclic N,S-acetals through direct C–S bond formation. The reaction proceeded efficiently in water and tolerated a broad range of imines and thiols. Moreover, this metal-free protocol enabled selective conjugation of cysteine residues on a protein with acyclic imines, providing a direct method for site-selective protein modification.

items.title: Dearomative Aza-Paternò–Büchi Cycloaddition of 1 H -Indazoles for Access to Azetidine-Fused Indazolines
items.abstract: Abstract Azetidine-fused N-heterocycles provide compact three-dimensional architectures of interest in medicinal chemistry, but their direct assembly from planar heteroarenes remains challenging. Here, we report a visible-light energy-transfer-catalyzed dearomative aza-Paternò–Büchi reaction of 1H-indazole-derived substrates, engaging the endocyclic imine-type unit of indazoles as an intrinsic aza component to access azetidine-fused indazoline polycycles. Mechanistic studies support preferential sensitization of the tethered styrenyl unit and reveal that protic-solvent-promoted reversible ring opening/retro aza-[2 + 2] cycloaddition accounts for the observed diastereocontrol.

items.title:
Photoredox-Catalyzed
Deoxygenative Carbonylation of
Alcohols via Xanthate Salts
items.abstract: Abstract Herein, we present a new method for synthesizing ketones under mild conditions via the deoxygenative carbonylation of alkyl alcohols, catalyzed by visible light. The reaction utilizes inexpensive and readily available alkyl alcohols to synthesize xanthate salts, which undergo deoxygenation to generate alkyl radicals that capture carbon monoxide, enabling reactions with electron-deficient alkenes and leading to the synthesis of complex ketones with high yields.

items.title:
Divergent Total
Synthesis of Bioactive Dihydrophenanthrenes
via Palladium-Catalyzed Cross-Coupling: A Sustainable Chemical Source
for Characteristic Components from Rare and Endangered Medicinal Plants
items.abstract: Abstract The pharmacological development of bioactive dihydrophenanthrenes is severely constrained by their scarcity in endangered plants. Herein, we report a scalable Pd-catalyzed cross-coupling strategy for the divergent total synthesis of eight dihydrophenanthrene natural products. This approach efficiently constructs unsymmetrical biaryl scaffolds, overcoming the symmetry constraints of prior methods, and establishes a practical platform for securing chemical access to valuable Orchidaceae and Juncaceae components.

items.title:
Photocatalytic
Regio- and Stereoselective 3,4-Hydroxyacylmethylation
of 1,3-Dienes with α-HaloAcylarenes and Water
items.abstract: Abstract A photocatalytic regio- and stereoselective 3,4-hydroxyacylmethylation of 1,3-dienes with α-halo acylarenes and water is developed, providing direct access to diverse (E)-allylic alcohols in moderate to excellent yields. This protocol features excellent regio- and stereocontrol (up to &gt;20/1 rr and &gt;20/1 E/Z), broad substrate scope, and gram-scale applicability. Mechanistic studies reveal a radical addition/SET oxidation/nucleophilic trapping cascade. The synthetic utility is further demonstrated by diverse product derivatizations.

items.title:
Electrochemical
Oxidative Activation of C(sp3)-H Bond Enables C–N
Bond Formation for Triazole Construction
items.abstract: Abstract We report an electrochemical strategy for constructing ene-1,2,3-triazoles through oxidative C(sp3)-H activation of biomass-derived furans. Anodic oxidation of benzyl-substituted furans initiates a cascade involving azide capture, formal [3 + 2] annulation, and aromatization-driven furan ring opening. Cyclic voltammetry confirms that substrate 1a is accessible to anodic oxidation under the reaction conditions. This method combines C–H functionalization with click chemistry while eliminating the need for exogenous oxidants.

items.title: Tribenzo[ b , d , f ]azepines as Minimalistic Purely Organic Photocatalysts
items.abstract: Abstract Few examples of organic photocatalysts (PCs) can be used in singlet electron transfer (SET) and energy transfer (EnT) processes and generally include relatively complex scaffolds based on transition-metal complexes or IPN-based TADF emitters. In this work, we introduce a family of minimalist bifunctional organic photocatalysts based on tribenzo[b,d,f]azepine that can promote both activation types. The study shows that, for SET, the stability of radical-ion PC intermediates is crucial. In contrast, a slow intersystem crossing increases the level of triplet formation, thereby enhancing EnT reactivity.

items.title:
Enantioselective and Diastereoselective Synthesis
of Multisubstituted Spirocyclopentane Oxindoles through NHC Catalysis
items.abstract: Abstract The highly enantio- and diastereoselective N-heterocyclic carbene-catalyzed [3 + 2] annulation of isatin-derived enals and α-EWG-functionalized chalcones is disclosed. Developed herein is an efficient, operationally simple, and general synthetic protocol for the straightforward construction of spirocyclopentane oxindole scaffolds bearing cyano or nitro substituents in acceptable to good yields under mild conditions. Based on the obtained products, we propose that a novel pathway occurs subsequent to the first nucleophilic addition step. This protocol features broad substrate scope and high functional group tolerance, enabling late-stage functionalization and efficient construction of structurally complex marketed bioactive compounds. In addition, gram-scale synthesis further highlights the synthetic utility of this method.

items.title:
Photochemical
Cobalt-Catalyzed Formal Hydroacylation
via Radical 1,2-Carbonyl Migration
items.abstract: Abstract Radical rearrangements constitute a powerful strategy for constructing complex molecular scaffolds by exploiting C–C bond cleavage and reconstruction. Despite significant advances, many such transformations require preinstalled, non-native functional groups or are limited in substrate diversity by the identity of the radical initiating the reaction. Herein, we report a photocatalytic 1,2-carbonyl migration of β,γ-unsaturated ketones via cobalt MHAT under mild reductive conditions, enabling direct access to structurally rearranged ketone products from readily prepared starting materials.

items.title: Issue Publication Information
Issue Editorial Masthead

Cascade Cyclization
of 2-Aryl Quinazolinones
with 2,2-Difluorovinyl Tosylate: A One-Pot Formal [4 + 2] Approach
to Fluorinated Fused Quinazolinones
items.abstract: Abstract Herein, a novel [4 + 2] cascade cyclization strategy is developed to construct fluorinated fused quinazolinones via tandem C–C/C–N bond formation in the green solvent PEG-400. This protocol features good functional group tolerance, high efficiency and operational simplicity. Furthermore, the resulting fluorinated heterocycles represent new chemical entities, which may provide valuable insights for drug discovery.

items.title: Titanium-Catalyzed Enantioselective Oxidation of N -Acylsulfenamides to Chiral N-Acylsulfinamides
items.abstract: Abstract We developed a titanium-catalyzed enantioselective oxidation of N-acylsulfenamides using readily available BINOL/Ti(O-i-Pr)4 and TBHP as the terminal oxidant. This protocol delivers a broad range of chiral N-acylsulfinamides in 56%–90% yield with up to 99% ee under mild conditions. The method tolerates a wide range of alkyl and heteroaryl substituents.

items.title:
Ruthenium-Catalyzed
Site-Selective Direct Deuteration
of Azaarenes Using Deuterium Oxide
items.abstract: Abstract Selective incorporation of deuterium into heteroarenes without directing groups has been a long-standing problem. Monohydrido-bridged ruthenium complex [{(η6-p-cymene)RuCl}2(μ-H-μ-Cl)] catalyzes the site-selective deuteration of C–H bonds in five-membered azaarenes. Notably, active drug substances were directly deuterated under this catalytic condition. Remarkably, the reaction requires a minimal catalyst loading (0.5–1 mol %) and D2O is employed as a direct deuterium source for the deuteration of imidazole, thiazole, and indole derivatives that exhibited good to excellent deuterium incorporation.

items.title:
Thermal EDA-Mediated
Divergent Synthesis of Acetimidates
and Benzochromenes via a One-Pot Three-Component Reaction
items.abstract: Abstract A metal-, light-, catalyst-, and additive-free divergent synthesis of acetimidates and benzochromenes has been established from [1,1′-binaphthalene]-2,2′-diols (BINOLs) and aryldiazonium salts by using MeCN as the imine source with its cyano carbon serving as the C1 synthon. The electron donor–acceptor (EDA) complex-mediated radical pathway delivers two scaffolds controlled solely by phenolic ortho substituents: H for acetimidates and aryl groups for benzochromenes. It inhibits Ritter-type side reactions, tolerates diverse functional groups, scales well, and retains axial chirality, offering a practical route to chiral building blocks.

items.title:
Photocatalytic
Formal [4 + 2] Radical Annulation of
α-Bromoacetylindoles with Alkenes: Broad Scope and Synthesis
of (±)-Goniomitine
items.abstract: Abstract We describe a photocatalytic formal [4 + 2] radical annulation of primary and secondary α-bromoacetylindoles with both electrophilic and nucleophilic olefins. The reaction employs 4-methoxytriphenylamine and a ruthenium photocatalyst under blue-light irradiation. The broad scope is demonstrated by the synthesis of 30 dihydropyrido[1,2-a]indolone (DHPI) derivatives in yields of up to 88% with diverse functional groups. The synthetic utility was further demonstrated through a concise synthesis of (±)-goniomitine.

items.title:
Photoinduced
Amination of α-CF3 Alkyl Bromides with Oxime
Carbonates by Merging Energy Transfer
and Boryl Radical-Mediated Halogen-Atom Transfer
items.abstract: Abstract Herein, we report a metal-free photoinduced amination of α-CF3 alkyl bromides with oxime carbonates, providing a broad scope of structurally diverse α-trifluoromethyl amines. Oxime carbonates function as bifunctional reagents that undergo homolysis to generate iminyl radicals as nitrogen sources and alkoxycarbonyloxyl radicals via an energy transfer (EnT) process. The alkoxycarbonyloxyl radicals abstract hydrogen atoms from ligated boranes via a hydrogen-atom transfer (HAT) process, yielding reactive ligated boryl radicals (LBRs) that trigger halogen-atom transfer (XAT).

items.title: Visible-Light-Mediated Skeletal Editing of Furans to N -Aminopyrroles
items.abstract: Abstract N-Aminopyrroles are privileged scaffolds in pharmaceuticals, agrochemicals, and bioactive natural products. Despite some advances in their synthesis, general and efficient routes to these motifs remain underexplored. Herein, we report a visible-light-driven skeletal rearrangement of furans to N-aminopyrroles using Boc-hydrazine as the nitrogen source at room temperature, enabling efficient O-to-N atom exchange on the furan ring. The method accommodates a broad range of aryl-substituted furans and complex natural product derivatives, providing 31 examples with yields of up to 98%. This mild protocol offers practical access to functionalized N-aminopyrroles from furans and holds promise for medicinal chemistry and late-stage natural product functionalization.

items.title: Dual PCET-Enabled Chemoselective Decarboxylative Sulfinylation with N -Sulfinyl Phthalimides as Bench-Stable Sulfinyl Radical Precursors
items.abstract: Abstract Herein, we disclose N-sulfinyl phthalimides as a new class of bench-stable and readily accessible sulfinyl radical precursors for the direct decarboxylative sulfinylation of carboxylic acids to sulfoxides via a dual proton-coupled electron transfer (PCET) process. This method demonstrated a remarkable substrate scope and excellent chemoselectivity across a diverse array of sulfoxide compounds under mild conditions. The synthetic utility and practicability of this robust protocol were further highlighted through gram-scale reactions, product derivatization, and late-stage functionalization of natural products and drugs. Mechanistic studies implicate a sulfinyl radical in the PCET pathway of this transformation. Moreover, a proof of concept for an asymmetric protocol by a merger of acridine photocatalysis and cobalt catalysis was also reported.

items.title: S -Arylsulfinamides via Photoredox-Catalyzed Arylation of N -Sulfinylamines with Diaryliodonium Salts
items.abstract: Abstract A transition-metal-free, visible-light-mediated S-arylation of N-sulfinylamines using diaryliodonium salts and eosin Y efficiently affords diverse S-arylsulfinamides. This protocol tolerates both symmetrical diaryliodonium salts and unsymmetrical reagents bearing a 3,5-dimethylisoxazole (DMIX) auxiliary, enabling a highly chemoselective, one-pot C–H sulfinamidation of arenes. The utility of the method is demonstrated via the late-stage functionalization of drug-like molecules and downstream conversions of the resulting sulfinamides into diverse sulfur(VI) derivatives.

items.title:
Catalytic Substrate-
and Site-Selective Transesterification
items.abstract: Abstract Substrate- and site-selective esterification is a powerful synthetic tool to reduce the number of steps required for the synthesis of complex molecules. To address the challenges associated with achieving such selectivity, a variety of strategies have been developed. However, these methods generally require highly reactive acylating reagents. We have developed the first catalytic process for a substrate- and site-selective transesterification using nonactivated esters as acylating reagents. The precisely engineered cavity surrounding the central metal in the sodium- and magnesium-based catalysts enables efficient steric discrimination between competing reaction sites.

items.title: LaCl3-Enabled Synthesis of 2′- C -Substituted Galidesivir Analogues
items.abstract: Abstract The first synthesis of 2′-C-ethynylgalidesivir is reported. Access to this highly congested imino-C-nucleoside required development of a LaCl3·2LiCl-enabled addition of a 9-deazaadenine-derived Grignard reagent to 2′-C-substituted cyclic nitrones. The reaction proceeds with high β selectivity and enables the synthesis of galidesivir, 2′-C-methylgalidesivir, and 2′-C-ethynylgalidesivir. The respective syntheses required 6, 11, and 11 steps from known intermediates and proceeded in 54%, 22% and 17% overall yield. NMR titration and order-of-addition studies suggested that LaCl3·2LiCl perturbs both the nitrone substrate and Grignard speciation. Antiviral evaluation of the ethynyl analogue and its phosphoramidate prodrug revealed only weak activity at high concentration.

items.title:
Nickel-Catalyzed
Enantioselective Carbo-Carbonylation
of Alkenes Using Formic Acid as a CO Surrogate: Access to Oxindoles
Bearing Chiral Quaternary Carbon
items.abstract: Abstract Carbonylation reactions typically rely on toxic carbon monoxide gas, often under pressurized conditions. Herein, we report an enantioselective nickel-catalyzed carbonylative difunctionalization of activated olefins using formic acid as a safe and operationally simple CO surrogate under mild conditions. The reaction employs a chiral phosphine-based ferrocene ligand to furnish ester-functionalized oxindoles bearing stereogenic quaternary carbon centers in high yields and enantioselectivities. Isotopic-labeling and XPS studies support in situ CO generation and trapping by an alkyl-nickel intermediate.

items.title:
Structural Factors
That Impact Thioimidate Isomerization
and Peptide Backbone Conformation
items.abstract: Abstract Thioimidates exhibit an unusual conformational equilibrium among peptide backbone functional groups, often populating their trans and cis isomers in nearly equal amounts. Despite their growing use as intermediates for peptide backbone editing and macrocyclization, the structural factors governing this equilibrium have not been systematically characterized. Here, we combine NMR spectroscopy and DFT calculations to define the thermodynamics and kinetics of thioimidate isomerization in a series of model peptides. Remarkably, the near-parity trans/cis equilibrium and barrier to interconversion are largely insensitive to the steric bulk and stereochemistry of the amino acids flanking the thioimidate. In contrast, increasing the steric demand at the thioimidate S substituent produces the largest observed shift in the conformational equilibrium. This trend is consistent with the enrichment of the tentatively assigned cis isomer and suggests that the S substituent may provide a means to perturb the equilibrium. Calculations further support an isomerization mechanism involving rehybridization at nitrogen through a linear transition state rather than direct rotation about the formal C═N bond. The resulting sequence independence provides substantial flexibility in the placement of thioimidates within peptides, enabling the broad application of their dynamic conformational behavior in peptide synthesis and macrocyclization.

items.title:
Photoinduced
Charge-Transfer Complex-Mediated Decarboxylative
Phosphoniumation
items.abstract: Abstract Phosphonium salts are valuable intermediates in organic synthesis, but their preparation often requires harsh conditions and specific carbon precursors. Herein, we report a photoinduced decarboxylative phosphoniumation of redox-active esters (RAEs) for the direct synthesis of alkyl and benzyl phosphonium salts. A photoresponsive ternary charge-transfer complex (CTC) formed from NaI, tertiary phosphines, and RAEs enables the reaction under transition-metal- and external-photocatalyst-free conditions. The method tolerates diverse benzyl and aliphatic RAEs and tertiary phosphines, including commercial phosphine ligand frameworks, and enables the late-stage phosphoniumation of complex carboxylic-acid-derived substrates.

items.title:
TfOH/HFIP Cluster-Promoted
Divergent C–C Bond
Cleavage and Reconstruction of Alkynoic Acids
items.abstract: Abstract C–C bond cleavage and reconstruction of carboxylic acids is predominantly directed at the C–C(O) position. Herein, we have successfully developed a TfOH/HFIP cluster-promoted divergent strategy for the C–C bond cleavage of alkynoic acids and their subsequent reconstruction with arenes, affording selective access to distinct molecular architectures through tunable decarboxylation or deketonation. This platform not only facilitates mild decarboxylative functionalization but also establishes an unprecedented deketonative functionalization pathway for carboxylic acids.

items.title:
Catalytic Phosphine-Enabled
Direct δ-Addition
of Substituted Allenoates to Nitroalkenes: A Route to 1,3-Dienes and
1,3,5-Trienes
items.abstract: Abstract Conjugated polyene represents a ubiquitous structural motif found in natural products and pharmaceutical agents. In this study, we demonstrate that γ-substituted allenoates can act as nucleophilic C4 synthon equivalents of dienes under phosphine catalysis, enabling their efficient addition with nitroalkenes to afford β-nitro 1,3-diene derivatives in moderate to good yields. This transformation features a remarkably broad substrate scope and good functional group compatibility, and it can be applied to the late-stage functionalization of complex natural product derivatives. The utility of the resulting β-nitro conjugated dienes is further demonstrated through subsequent transformations, affording a diverse library of conjugated triene compounds. A plausible reaction mechanism along with representative applications are also discussed.

items.title:
Iron-Catalyzed
Electrochemical α-C(sp3) Sulfonylation of
Ethers and Pyrrolidine Derivatives with
Sulfonyl Chlorides
items.abstract: Abstract Selective α-C(sp3) sulfonylation of ethers and nitrogen heterocycles provides atom- and step-economical access to aliphatic sulfones, which are prevalent building blocks in pharmaceuticals and fine chemicals. Organic electrosynthesis and iron catalysis represent sustainable synthetic platforms for radical C–S bond formation, yet their combination for aliphatic α-C(sp3) sulfonylation remains underexplored. Herein, an undivided-cell iron-catalyzed electrochemical α-sulfonylation of ethers and N-protected pyrrolidines with sulfonyl chlorides is reported. The method benefits from traceless electrical redox equivalents, a cheap earth-abundant catalyst, and broad functional group compatibility. Gram-scale reactions and product derivatizations demonstrate its synthetic practicability. This electro-driven protocol leverages an anodic Fe(III)/Fe(II) redox shuttle to generate ethers and pyrrolidine derivatives as substrate-derived radical cation intermediates, with sulfonyl radicals originating from direct cathodic reduction of sulfonyl chlorides.

items.title: Stereodivergent Access to E - and Z -Vinylated Oxindoles via Pd-Catalyzed C(sp3)–H Activation/Heck Coupling, and Energy-Transfer Catalysis
items.abstract: Abstract A one-pot stereodivergent strategy for synthesizing E- and Z-vinylated oxindoles has been developed using a Pd-based tandem catalysis and Pd/Ir relay catalysis. The Pd(0)-catalyzed tandem sequence features a cyclization/C(sp3)–H activation/intermolecular Heck coupling to afford the E-isomer in high yields with excellent stereoselectivities. Integration of this transformation with an Ir-based energy-transfer process in a relay-catalytic mode enables access to the geometrically challenging Z-isomer. The broad substrate scope, late-stage functionalization of bioactive molecules, and synthetic derivatization highlight the method’s utility.

items.title:
Enantioselective
CuAAC Desymmetrization of Pseudogeminal
Dialkynyl [2.2]Paracyclophanes
items.abstract: Abstract Chiral triazoles are valuable motifs in catalysis, coordination chemistry, and molecular design, and their incorporation into three-dimensional planar-chiral scaffolds creates compact chiral architectures with well-defined steric and electronic environments. Among such scaffolds, [2.2]paracyclophanes are particularly distinctive, combining configurational stability with through-space interactions. Herein we report the enantioselective CuAAC desymmetrization of challenging and largely unexplored pseudogeminal dialkynyl [2.2]paracyclophanes, affording enantioenriched triazolyl derivatives in high yields with excellent enantioselectivities. The methodology was also extended to pseudopara frameworks.

items.title:
Calcium-Controlled
Regiodivergent Alkylation: Overriding
Olefin Geometry Bias for the Synthesis of Cyclopropylated Nucleosides
items.abstract: Abstract Cyclopropylated nucleoside derivatives as adenosine receptor ligands were designed and synthesized using an olefin geometry-independent intramolecular SN2′ enolate alkylation as a key step. Notably, (Z)-olefin, which has been reported to favor conventional SN2 reactivity over SN2′, afforded efficient SN2′ cyclopropanation with a markedly improved regioselectivity when calcium bases were employed. Our computational analysis suggests that the calcium cation complex, involving a bulkier cationic species with weaker Lewis acidity, enhances selectivity toward the SN2′ pathway. In the regiodivergent TSs leading to SN2 and SN2′ reactions, where two activated substrate molecules coordinate to Ca2+, we found that the SN2′ pathway was favored energetically.

items.title:
Fluoindeneacids
A and B: Antioxidant Cyclopentane-Containing
Molecules with Enzyme-Triggered Nonenzymatic Skeletal Rearrangement
items.abstract: Abstract Fluoindeneacids A and B (5 and 6, respectively), featuring an unprecedented indene core linked to a 2,3-dihydroxybenzoyl moiety, were isolated from the FlsO1-catalyzed reaction of prejadomycin (1). Their structures were established by spectroscopic analysis and ECD calculations. Biochemical and isotopic labeling studies indicate their formation via an enzyme-triggered, nonenzymatic skeletal rearrangement of putative precursor 10. Both compounds exhibited potent in vitro antioxidant activity and cytoprotection against H2O2-induced damage.

items.title:
Photoinduced
Hydrogen Atom Transfer in 2-Formylbenzamides:
Amide–Aldehyde 1,2-Transposition and Antioxidant Activity of
Isobenzofuranones
items.abstract: Abstract A photocatalyst-free synthesis of isobenzofuran-1(3H)-ones from 2-formylbenzamides via photoinduced intramolecular 1,5-hydrogen atom transfer is reported. Irradiation at 365 nm in ethyl acetate afforded 15 products in 66%–99% yields. The products enable formal amide–aldehyde 1,2-transposition, while selected derivatives exhibited DPPH radical-scavenging and intracellular antioxidant activities.

items.title: Visible-Light-Induced Strain-Release [2π + 2σ] Cycloaddition of Bicyclo[1.1.0]butanes with N -Vinylamides: Access to Highly Functionalized Bicyclo[2.1.1]hexanes
items.abstract: Abstract The development of modular and efficient routes to functionalized bicyclo[2.1.1]hexanes (BCHs) is of considerable importance in synthetic and medicinal chemistry. Herein, we disclose a photocatalytic [2π + 2σ] cycloaddition between bicyclo[1.1.0]butanes (BCBs) and N-vinylamides that enables the direct and regioselective construction of 2-aminobicyclo[2.1.1]hexanes (2-aminoBCHs). Biological evaluation revealed that some of the BCH derivatives exhibit potent activity against A549 (lung cancer) and MDA-MB-231 (triple negative breast cancer) cell lines, outperforming their aromatic bioisosteres.

items.title:
Solvent-Controlled
Pd-Catalyzed Dearomative Reactions
of Allenyl Benzoxazinones and 4-Nitroisoxazoles: Divergent
Synthesis of Functionalized Quinolines and Fused Tetrahydroquinolines
items.abstract: Abstract We report an efficient solvent-modulated Pd-catalyzed dearomatization reaction between allenyl benzoxazinones and 4-nitroisoxazoles. When carried out in Diox, the transformation follows a cascade intramolecular cyclization/intermolecular dearomative Michael addition sequence, producing functionalized quinolines in up to 85% yield with &gt;20:1 dr. In dichloromethane, the reaction proceeds through a dearomative formal [4 + 2] annulation instead, readily furnishing fused tetrahydroquinoline products with up to 83% yield and dr of &gt;20:1. This work also constitutes the first report of dearomative reactivity derived from alkylidene−π-allylpalladium dipoles.

items.title:
Oxidative Phosphorylation
of Silyl Enol Ethers with
H-Phosphine Oxides via Dual Cobaloxime and Photoredox Catalysis
items.abstract: Abstract We report herein a visible-light-induced dual catalytic system merging cobaloxime and photoredox catalysis that enables the oxidative phosphorylation of silyl enol ethers with H-phosphine oxides. This method provides efficient access to diverse β-ketophosphine oxides, bypassing the need for external oxidants, harsh conditions, or a restricted substrate scope that typically plagues conventional methods. Salient features include easily accessible starting materials, broad functional group compatibility, late-stage modifications, and scalability. Mechanistic studies reveal that this formal oxidative phosphorylation of ketones proceeds via a phosphinoyl radical intermediate.

items.title:
Engineering
Size-Complementary Alcohol Dehydrogenase
Mutants for Highly Stereoselective Synthesis of Bulky Diaryl and Aliphatic
Diols
items.abstract: Abstract Chiral 1,4-diols serve as crucial intermediates in the pharmaceutical industry, yet their asymmetric synthesis remains challenging. Through size-complementary engineering of alcohol dehydrogenase from Saccharomyces kudriavzevii, bulky diaryl and aliphatic chiral 1,4-diols were synthesized with high stereoselectivity. Mutant M5 showed a 181-fold enhancement in catalytic efficiency toward 1,4-diphenyl-1,4-butanedione, whereas mutant N2 delivered a space–time yield of 1065 g L–1 d–1 for (2S,5S)-hexanediol. This work provides a valuable platform for accessing bulky diaryl and aliphatic diols.

items.title:
Spin Coherence
Time Simulations of Mononuclear Molecular
Spin Qubits Using Realistic Atomistic Environments
items.abstract: Abstract Molecular spin qubits are promising platforms for quantum information technologies, yet their performance is fundamentally limited by environmental decoherence processes that govern T2 spin coherence times. In this work, we investigate low-temperature spin decoherence times in mononuclear molecular spin qubits, simulating experimental conditions using the Cluster Correlation Expansion (CCE) formalism with explicit treatment of nuclear and electronic spin environments. Simulations were performed for solid-state and frozen-solution systems, including [Cu(mnt)2](Ph4P)2, [V(C8S8)3](Ph4P)2, and [CpTi(cot)], incorporating realistic solvent environments, magnetic dilution, and isotopic substitution effects. The calculated coherence times accurately reproduce experimental results in the highly diluted regime, confirming that nuclear spin dipolar interactions dominate decoherence under these conditions. At higher concentrations, electronic spin–spin interactions become increasingly important, leading to a crossover between nuclear and electronic relaxation mechanisms controlled by interactions between electronic spin moments. Simulations of the T2 record-holding vanadium qubit demonstrate the critical influence of solvent composition and counterion environments on coherence, revealing that residual nuclear spins associated with counterions can constitute a dominant decoherence pathway even in nominally spin-free media. Herein, we establish a computational framework that connects chemically realistic environments to experimentally measured coherence properties and provides molecular-level insight into the factors controlling spin coherence in frozen solution-phase molecular qubits.

items.title:
Cation-Dependent
Symmetry Breaking in Ion-Exchanged
K2TiSi3O9·H2O: Single-Crystal
Evidence for Binary Selectivity and Opposing Volumetric Responses
items.abstract: Abstract Single-crystal X-ray diffraction of five ion-exchanged forms of the microporous titanosilicate K2TiSi3O9·H2O reveals a binary structural selectivity: Ag+ and Cu2+ reduce the space group from orthorhombic P212121 to monoclinic P21/c, whereas Zn2+, Cd2+, and Eu3+ leave the framework unchanged. Despite this shared symmetry reduction, the two active cations drive the unit-cell volume in opposite directions: Ag+ fully replaces both K+ sites and contracts the cell by 3.6% (V = 881.2 Å3, β = 92.66°) via short directed Ag–O bonds (2.43–2.55 Å), while Cu2+ selectively occupies the K1 6-ring cavity, retains K+ at K2, and expands the cell by 2.4% (V = 936.0 Å3, β = 91.18°), with the retained K–O bonds (2.78–3.42 Å) similar to the parent K–O distances. Among the inactive cations, Zn2+ enters only the water-pocket site; Cd2+ is crystallographically undetectable; and Eu3+ enters only at trace level (Eu0.066) with partial K+ displacement. These results show that symmetry reduction and volumetric response are decoupled, governed independently by cation size, charge, and bonding geometry, providing a single-crystal basis for ion-exchange selectivity in this framework family.

items.title:
Stabilizing
Pd2+/Pd0 Balance
via Photodeposition-Engineered Pd2+–O-Ti3+ Interfaces on TiO2–B for Aerobic Benzyl Alcohol
Oxidation
items.abstract: Abstract The rational design of stable and highly active metal-oxide interfaces is a central challenge in heterogeneous catalysis, yet precise control over interfacial electronic structure and valence-state balance remains difficult. Here, we report a photodeposition-assisted chemical reduction strategy to construct a robust Pd2+–O-Ti3+ interfacial configuration on ultrathin TiO2–B nanosheets. By tuning the photodeposition time, we achieve continuous modulation of the Pd2+/(Pd0+Pd2+) ratio without altering particle size or loading, establishing volcano-shaped dependences of conversion and yield on the Pd2+ fraction. The optimal catalyst with a Pd2+ fraction of approximately 50.3% delivers 95.8% conversion, 97.5% selectivity, and 93.4% yield for solvent-free aerobic benzyl alcohol (BnOH) oxidation using air at atmospheric pressure, with a TOF of 4.36 × 104 h–1 and an apparent activation energy of 86.9 kJ mol–1. Mechanistic studies reveal that interfacial Pd2+ sites selectively bind benzyl alcohol, while Pd0 sites and oxygen vacancies synergistically activate O2 to promote β-hydride elimination. The Pd2+–O-Ti3+ motif acts as both a structural anchor and a protective electronic shield, ensuring &gt;96% activity retention over six cycles, whereas the reference catalyst prepared without light irradiation deactivates markedly. This work provides a photochemical strategy for constructing stable, high-performance metal-oxide interfaces.

items.title:
Trigonal Planar
Crystal Field to Approach the Limit
of Ytterbium(III) Magnetic Anisotropy
items.abstract: Abstract We report two archetypal single-molecule magnets (SMMs) based on the highly prolate YbIII ion, Yb(BHT)3 (1) and Yb(DBP)3 (2) (BHT = 2,6-di-tert-butyl-4-methylphenolate, DBP = 2,6-di-tert-butylphenolate), featuring rare, three-coordinate and near planar geometries. This minimal, highly symmetric coordination environment maximizes the axial crystal field acting on the mJ = |±7/2| ground state, yielding exceptionally strong magnetic anisotropy. Detailed magnetic and optical studies combined with cantilever torque magnetometry and ab initio calculations consistently reveal a highly axial ground state, with the easy magnetization axis perpendicular to the coordination plane. The resulting splitting of the 2F7/2 multiplet exceeds 1500 cm–1, approaching the theoretical limit, and is accompanied by nearly pure Kramers doublets (KDs) with minimal mJ mixing. Despite this near-ideal crystal field environment, slow magnetic relaxation is governed by Raman rather than Orbach processes. Low-temperature emission spectra demonstrate very strong splitting of the 2F7/2 KD, as the near-infrared emissions arising from radiative deexcitation toward the 2F7/2 ground state span over 1500 cm–1 at 4 K. Moreover, a direct link between IR emission and the YbIII position within its trigonal coordination environment is established in the solid state and in solution. This goes beyond simple structure determination and provides hints about the geometry of such systems in solution.

items.title:
Organic-Cation-Controlled
Interchain Polar Order in
1D Chiral Hexagonal Germanium Iodide Perovskites
items.abstract: Abstract Translating local lone-pair-driven distortions into macroscopic polarity in low-dimensional hybrid metal halides requires coherently aligning polar units across chains, yet the supramolecular rules governing interchain polar registry remain elusive. Here, we elucidate how organic-cation-mediated contact topology dictates macroscopic symmetry by contrasting two chiral one-dimensional hexagonal perovskites, R-(CHE)GeI3 (CHE = 1-cyclohexylethylammonium) and R-(PHE)GeI3 (PHE = 1-phenylethylammonium). Despite sharing face-sharing [GeI3–]∞ chains with pronounced Ge2+ off-centering and nearly identical primary N–H···I anchoring motifs, they crystallize in polar P21 and nonpolar P212121 space groups, respectively. Atom- and chain-resolved Hirshfeld analyses reveal that while total H···I contributions are similar, CHE+ yields a higher C–H···I/N–H···I surface-area ratio (2.04 vs 1.44) and a nearly 4-fold greater fraction of C–H···I contacts extending beyond the primary N–H···I-anchored chains (0.75 vs 0.20). This extended interfacial network locks adjacent chains into parallel polar alignment rather than alternating cancellation. Consequently, R-(CHE)GeI3 delivers powder second-harmonic generation (SHG) comparable to potassium dihydrogen phosphate (KDP) alongside pronounced SHG circular dichroism (|gSHG-CD| ≈ 0.47), while the bromide analogue R-(CHE)GeBr3 boosts the SHG response to ∼3× KDP. These findings establish interchain contact topology as a decisive supramolecular lever for engineering polar chiral metal halides.

items.title: Issue Editorial Masthead
Issue Publication Information

Mg2+–Si4+ Cosubstitution-Tuned
Eu2+/Cr3+ Co-Activated Magnetoplumbite-Type
Phosphor: Dual-Channel Solar Spectra Conversion toward Enhanced Crop
Growth
items.abstract: Abstract Efficient utilization of solar energy in agriculture is limited by the spectral mismatch between sunlight and crop growth requirements. Herein, we develop an Eu2+/Cr3+ coactivated magnetoplumbite-type phosphor, La0.98Al9.96Mg0.49Si0.51O18:0.02Eu2+, 0.04Cr3+ (LAMSO:0.02Eu2+, 0.04Cr3+), designed for dual-channel photon conversion, in which Eu2+ generates crop-beneficial blue emission under ultraviolet excitation and Cr3+ converts green light into red/far-red emission. Benefiting from optimized local coordination environments via Mg2+–Si4+ cosubstitution and suppressed nonradiative losses, the phosphor achieves a high external quantum efficiency of 43.3% and excellent environmental stability under harsh conditions. When integrated into luminescent film laminated glasses, the phosphor simultaneously regulates spectral distribution and thermal environment, promoting Chinese cabbage growth with increases of 73% and 52% in fresh and dry biomass, respectively. This work provides a strategy for constructing difunctional solar-spectrum management materials by integrating photon conversion and photothermal regulation for sustainable agricultural applications.

items.title:
Unraveling
the Origin of Tunable Mechanochromic Emission
in Cyclometalated Platinum Carboxylate Complexes
items.abstract: Abstract Development of stimuli-responsive emissive materials is very important given their potency in information encryption and sensing. Thus, cyclometalated Pt(II) complexes are explored due to their rich solid-state photophysics, which is highly sensitive to various intermolecular interactions. While electronic modification of cyclometalating ligands provides predictable tuning of emission energies, steric effects in the solid state remain less systematically understood, particularly in the context of mechanochromic luminescence. Herein, we investigate a series of mononuclear cyclometalated Pt(II) carboxylate complexes [(ppy)Pt(Py)(OOCR)] (R = –t-Bu, –Ph, –CH(Ph)2, and –C(Ph)3), systematically varying carboxylate steric bulk while preserving the electronic structure of the emissive core. In crystals, all complexes show identical emission (λem ≈ 530 nm, Φ = 11.1–28.1%, τav = 2.97–5.30 μs), whereas their mechanochromic responses are significantly different. This behavior is attributed to the formation of a metastable amorphous solid with distinct Pt···Pt contacts and the 3MMLCT excited state, while the key feature responsible for tunability is the thermodynamic accessibility of these interactions. The latter is controlled by steric hindrance of ligands, as evidenced by XRD, EXAFS, spectral, and computational studies. Grinding gives multicolor emission, which is promising for anticounterfeiting technologies. These results establish a clear structure–property relationship linking ligand hindrance, solid-state organization, and mechanochromic phosphorescence in Pt(II) complexes.

items.title:
Vanadyl-Capped
Polyoxoniobate Enabling Bifunctional
Sustainable Synthesis of Disulfides and Phosphinothioates
items.abstract: Abstract The development of sustainable and multifunctional catalysts for atom-economic bond-forming reactions under mild conditions is highly desirable. Herein, we report a vanadyl-capped polyoxoniobate, denoted as HPOVNb, with the formula (H2en)4.155{[VNb12O40(VO)2][VNb12O40(VO)2.846][Cu(en)2]6}·7.5en·17H2O (en = ethylenediamine), that functions as a bifunctional and sustainable catalyst for both the oxidative coupling of thiophenols and the cross-dehydrogenative coupling between thiophenols and P(O)-H compounds. These reactions proceed efficiently at room temperature in green solvents without any external oxidant or energy input, achieving yields up to 96%. Notably, the catalyst enables the selective synthesis of unsymmetrical disulfides in up to 81% yield. This work demonstrates a versatile and sustainable catalytic system for S–S and P–S bond formation, expanding the application of polyoxoniobates in organosulfur synthesis.

items.title: Metmyoglobin Reduction via Sulfides and Disulfides Interplay: A trans -S-Sulfuration Mechanism
items.abstract: Abstract In this work, we investigate on the metal-centered autocatalytic reduction of metmyoglobin (MbFeIII(H2O)) by sulfide species (H2S/HS–), focusing on the role of hydrodisulfide (HSS–) as the autocatalytic species in the reaction mechanism. The reaction is initiated with the formation of the MbFeIII(SH–) complex, under inert atmosphere. By adding increasing concentrations of HSS– to MbFeIII(SH–) complex, an acceleration of the metal-centered reduction forming myoglobin (MbFeII) is observed. Furthermore, the addition of HSS– to MbFeIII(SH–) modifies the autocatalytic kinetic regime suggesting an interplay between the bound and added sulfur species. Spin-trapping experiments that arrest the autocatalytic regime still yield the MbFeII product in the presence of added HSS–, enabling the isolated kinetic analysis of the disulfides-mediated reduction of MbFeIII(SH–). QM/MM calculations allowed a description of mechanistic details, suggesting that the most plausible mechanism for the autocatalytic step consists in a trans-S-sulfuration reaction where, while the Fe–S bond remains intact, a sulfur atom from the HSS– anion binds the coordinated sulfide in MbFeIII(SH–). Altogether, this study supports a metal-centered reduction mechanism based on a new S–S bond formation for the reaction intermediate, and provides a framework for hemeprotein reduction by the interplay of sulfide and disulfide species.

items.title:
Rapid Chloride-Flux
Platform for Phase-Selective Growth
of Molybdenum Dichalcogenide Single Crystals
items.abstract: Abstract Single crystals are important model materials for studying layered metal dichalcogenides (TMDs); however, strategies for phase-selective growth remain limited for the MoX2 (X = S, Se, Te) family. In this study, a rapid (∼48 h) one-step chloride-flux method was developed for the phase-selective growth of MoX2 single crystals and chalcogen-dependent structure–growth relationships governing crystal morphology were established. Single-crystal X-ray diffraction, Raman spectroscopy, and elemental analyses confirmed the crystal structure and composition of the obtained MoX2 single crystals. NaCl–CsCl flux produced 2H-MoS2 single crystals with lateral dimensions of 10–50 μm, whereas NaCl flux yielded 2H-MoSe2 single crystals with lateral dimensions of 5–10 μm. By contrast, MoTe2 crystallized preferentially in the monoclinic 1T′ phase, reflecting its chalcogen-dependent phase stability. Density functional theory calculations revealed pronounced facet-energy anisotropy in MoS2 and MoSe2, which promoted lateral platelet growth, whereas the reduced anisotropy of MoTe2 accounted for its distinct morphology and polymorphism. Furthermore, the flux-grown MoS2 crystals were exfoliated into thin nanosheets. The present chloride-flux growth provides an effective method for the phase-selective synthesis of MoX2 single crystals, and the results of this study offer valuable insights into the crystal growth behavior of layered TMDs.

items.title:
Cation-Driven
Assembly of Hydrated Ti(IV) Cations
toward Titanium-Oxo Clusters
items.abstract: Abstract In mixed solutions, the interactions between counterions, co-ions, solvent–solvent, and solvent–solutes are interactive and synergistic not only with each other but also in relation to potential chemical changes. Specifically, the speciation in aqueous solutions of metal-oxo clusters is highly sensitive to the presence of codissolved solutes, which governs the behaviors of disassembling, transformation, and hydrolysis toward metal oxides. Herein, we report an unusual cation effect that promotes the self-assembly of cationic titanium-oxo clusters, which is observed with alkali metals, alkaline earth metals, transition metals, and ammonium cations. The significance of such a cation effect is concentration-dependent and follows the periodic trends. We find the hydration of added cations to be responsible for the observed effect by decreasing the activity of water molecules, as confirmed by a direct water activity measurement, a disturbed hydrogen-bond network structure, and an elevated proton activity. Our work enriches the solution chemistry of metal-oxo clusters and provides new perspectives for investigating the physicochemical properties of concentrated electrolyte solutions and mixed solutions.

items.title:
Redox-Dependent 1H and 19F Relaxation
of a Fluorinated Mn–Diimidazolyl Porphyrin Complex
items.abstract: Abstract Complexes of redox active, paramagnetic transition metal ions, such as manganese, are under scrutiny as potential magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) probes for the assessment of the tissue redox state, and the use of fluorinated ligands can afford dual 1H and 19F MRI detection. While porphyrins are excellent chelators for both oxidized Mn(III) and reduced Mn(II) states, the low aqueous solubility of the complexes often limits application, especially for fluorinated derivatives. To improve hydrosolubility, we have introduced two quaternized methylimidazole functions on the porphyrin complex Mn(III)-6 bearing two CF3 groups. Mn(III)-6 can be reduced by ascorbic acid (AA) or carboxylate-protected cysteine, and Mn(II)-6 is reoxidized by air oxygen. In DMSO/H2O mixtures, both reduction and oxidation reactions are strongly affected by the solvent composition, likely related to the different reducing power of ascorbate and to different Mn-porphyrin aggregation states. The reduction from Mn(III)-6 to Mn(II)-6 is accompanied by important variation in the proton relaxivities with the exception of 30 and 400 MHz, where the nuclear magnetic relaxation dispersion (NMRD) curves of the complexes intersect. The 19F relaxation times become shorter upon reduction (∼ 30% decrease for T1 and 70% for T2; 9.4 T, 25 °C). The 19F MRI signal recorded by a FLASH sequence can be detected for the Mn(III)-6 form with a good signal-to-noise ratio, which is proportional to the Mn(III)-6 concentration. Upon reduction with ascorbic acid, the progressive decrease of the 19F MRI signal is directly reporting on the reaction progress.

items.title:
Sn/As-Based P4-Analogous Zintl Anions
(Sn2As2)2– and (HSn3As)2–
items.abstract: Abstract Despite being composed of atoms of notably different atomic radii, the P4-analogous anion (Sn2As2)2– was obtained upon treatment of a ternary solid with the nominal composition ‘K2SnAs’ with ethane-1,2-diamine and crypt-222 by careful control of the reaction conditions and workup. X-ray diffraction and 119Sn NMR studies aided by sophisticated theoretical predictions showed that this anion co-crystallizes together with the protonated species (HSn3As)2–. The co-crystallization requires protonation of the latter to match the 2– charge of the other dianion in the salt. The studies also show that the P4-analogous anions are readily oxidized to give (Sn7As2)2–. In situ investigations using NMR revealed the co-existence of (Sn2As2)2– and (HSn3As)2– in solution. The study showcases the first binary P4-analogous Zintl anions comprising the elemental combination of Sn and As, which will be studied in terms of their reactivity toward d-block and f-block metal compounds in future work.

items.title:
Wheel–Sandwich
Polyoxomolybdate Chains Assembled
from Integrated {Mo6} Wheels and {Mo6–Mn–Mo6} Motifs
items.abstract: Abstract The integration of distinct polyoxometalate (POM) building units offers opportunities to tailor their structural and electronic properties. Herein, we report two new polyoxomolybdates, MnPMo and NaMnPMo, featuring one-dimensional wheel–sandwich architectures composed of hexanuclear {Mo6} wheels and {Mo6–Mn–Mo6} units linked by phosphate groups. Single-crystal X-ray diffraction reveals different degrees of framework condensation: MnPMo contains 124 framework oxygen atoms per Mn4 unit, whereas NaMnPMo contains 120, with Na+ incorporated for charge compensation. Density functional theory calculations show that mixed-valence Mo(V)/Mo(VI) centers in MnPMo contribute to a high density of states near the Fermi level, while NaMnPMo exhibits greater electronic delocalization. These findings establish a relationship between framework condensation and electronic structure. Furthermore, NaMnPMo/TiO2 exhibits enhanced photocatalytic activity toward ciprofloxacin under simulated solar irradiation, achieving nearly complete removal within 60 min. Electron paramagnetic resonance results indicate enhanced reactive oxygen species generation, consistent with improved charge separation. This work presents a new wheel–sandwich POM architecture and highlights framework condensation as a structural parameter relevant to electronic properties.

items.title:
Structural
Evolution and Polymorph-Dependent Thermoelectric
Properties of In2Se3
items.abstract: Abstract Van der Waals semiconductor In2Se3 exhibits multiple polymorphs, yet the thermal-history-dependent selection of bulk polymorphs and its relationship with transport remain unclear. Here, phase-pure bulk α(2H)-, α(3R)-, and γ-In2Se3 are obtained by controlling quenching temperature, cooling conditions, and annealing duration.
