Ex situ annealing of bulk ingots reveals staged retained-phase evolution from α(2H) through a transient α(3R)-enriched state to γ-In2Se3, consistent with Ostwald’s rule of stages. At 673 K, the estimated α(3R) fraction in the initially α(2H) sample reaches approximately 74–78% after 2–3 h and subsequently decreases as γ-In2Se3 develops. For the two α polymorphs, the room-temperature electrical conductivity along the ∥ specimen direction increases from 2 S m–1 for α(2H)-In2Se3 to 86 S m–1 for α(3R)-In2Se3. Despite its lower carrier concentration, α(3R)-In2Se3 exhibits a substantially higher estimated mobility of 20.9 cm2 V–1 s–1, compared with 0.20 cm2 V–1 s–1 for α(2H)-In2Se3. The thermal conductivity along the same direction decreases from 3.19 to 2.70 W m–1 K–1, consistent with the lower measured sound velocities and lower calculated low-frequency phonon group velocities of α(3R)-In2Se3. These results connect thermal-history-dependent polymorph selection with electronic and phonon transport in bulk In2Se3.

items.title:
Directional
Te3 Polyanion Connectivity
in Layered In2Te5: Linear Dichroism and Polarization-Dependent
Effective Second-Harmonic Generation
items.abstract: Abstract Directional polyanion connectivity provides a structural perspective on optical anisotropy in layered materials. Here, we investigate the structural, electronic, and optical properties of In2Te5. Crystallographic analysis identifies distinct Type-A and Type-B Te3 motifs with preferential connectivity along the b-axis. First-principles calculations show that Te3-associated sites contribute 70.24% of the integrated projected density of states within 0.2 eV below the valence-band maximum, with per-atom enrichment factors of 1.86 and 2.59 for Type-A and Type-B sites, respectively, relative to the framework Te. Polarized Raman spectroscopy and optical measurements establish pronounced anisotropy, including broadband linear dichroism with an effective-absorptance ratio of 1.47–1.49 over 350–808 nm. Calculated absorption spectra reproduce the preferred b-axis polarization direction, although quantitative discrepancies remain. Furthermore, effective second-harmonic generation (SHG) measurements on four flakes (13–75 nm) reveal parallel-channel maxima close to the b-axis. These findings support a structure–electronic–optical correlation underlying linear dichroism and reveal a related crystallographic preference for effective SHG.

items.title:
Dynamics of
an Excess Electron in Two IL-Based Extraction
Systems
items.abstract: Abstract Excess electrons generated in the extraction system during spent fuel reprocessing remain poorly understood. Ab initio molecular dynamics (AIMD) simulations have already been utilized to study excess electrons in ionic liquids (ILs), but have never been employed to investigate extraction systems. To bridge this gap, AIMD simulations were employed to investigate the dynamics of an excess electron in two IL-based extraction systems. For the DCH18C6/C2MIM/NTF2 system in the presence of an excess electron, three interesting processes that have different system compositions, electronic structures, and spectra can be identified. During the electron localization process (0–250 fs), the excess electron localizes onto one anion to form NTF22–•, leading to blue shifts in spectra. In the bond breakage process (250–700 fs), one N–S bond in the NTF22–• breaks, and in the radical diffusion process (700–3000 fs), no reaction can be observed. In contrast, in the Cyphos 101-IL/Toluene system, no localization of the excess electron can be identified. This research not only supports prior experiments, but also provides additional details regarding electron localization and bond breakage, which are absent in previous experimental investigations. More importantly, it highlights the importance of further research, as new transient species, reactions, and mechanisms might be discovered.

items.title:
Noncentrosymmetric
Crystal Structure of the Oxyfluoride
PbBiTi4O10F Driven by Cooperative Pb/Bi and
O/F Ordering
items.abstract: Abstract Mixed-anion chemistry provides unique opportunities for controlling crystal structures through the interplay of chemically distinct anions and cations. Here, we report a newly synthesized oxyfluoride, PbBiTi4O10F, in which Pb2+ and Bi3+, despite their similar chemical characteristics, exhibit long-range cation ordering. Combined synchrotron X-ray and neutron powder diffraction analyses reveal a noncentrosymmetric monoclinic structure with space group Cm, in which Pb/Bi cation ordering is coupled with selective O/F anion occupation. The absence of inversion symmetry is independently confirmed by second-harmonic generation. Bond-valence analysis identifies the origin of this coupling. In the centrosymmetric C2/m structure, Pb and Bi share a common crystallographic site whose coordination environment is unfavorable for both cations: Bi is underbonded, whereas Pb is overbonded relative to their formal valences. The symmetry reduction to Cm splits this site into two crystallographically distinct sites and relieves both bond-valence mismatches simultaneously. It places the two cations in more favorable coordination environments and generates an anion site that is too weakly bonded to accommodate O2– but is well suited to F–. These results indicate that the noncentrosymmetry arises from cooperative cation–anion ordering rather than substantial local structural distortions. The present study demonstrates that selective anion occupation in mixed-anion compounds can provide an additional driving force for cation ordering even when conventional differences in cation size or valence are insufficient, offering a strategy for designing noncentrosymmetric structures.

items.title:
Polymorphism
and Dimensionality in Rhodium Chalcogenide
Nanocrystals
items.abstract: Abstract Rhodium chalcogenides have rich crystal chemistry and offer opportunities in catalytic chemical transformations, quantum phenomena and devices, and biological applications. However, their solution phase chemistry, particularly the synthesis of specific phases with well-defined dimensionality, remains nascent. Here, we report a colloidal strategy to access multiple air-stable 5–30 nm nanocrystals of binary rhodium chalcogenides, including Rh0.78Se (P63/mmc), 2D (P3̅m1) RhTe2, 3D (Pa3̅) RhTe2, and Rh3Te8 (R3̅). We demonstrate how the choices of precursors and injection (Tinj) and growth temperatures (Tgrowth) enable their phase selective synthesis. Analyses by powder X-ray diffraction and electron microscopy verify the compositions and phase purities of the different nanocrystalline samples. Density functional theory calculations confirm the metallic character of the binary rhodium chalcogenides and unveil the relative stabilities of different RhCh2 polymorphs (Ch = Se, Te). For example, we find that the synthesized trigonal 2D (P3̅m1) and cubic pyrite-type 3D (Pa3̅) phases of RhTe2 are metastable compared to a yet unobserved orthorhombic (Pnma) phase. This study unlocks the phase- and dimensionality-selective synthesis of rhodium chalcogenide nanocrystals and provides a foundation for exploring their structure-dependent properties.

items.title:
Synthesis
and Isonitrile-Induced Isomerization of
Manganese Pnictaketenes
items.abstract: Abstract Metal pnictaketenes (M–ECO; E = P, As) are known to readily decarbonylate to afford terminal metal pnictogenido complexes; however, alternative reactivity modes of these complexes remain comparatively unexplored. Herein, we report the synthesis of manganese(II) phosphaketene and arsaketene complexes supported by a tris(carbene)borate ligand through salt metathesis of a manganese(II) chloride precursor with the corresponding sodium salts of 2-pnictaethynolate anions, [Na(1,4-dioxane)x][OCE] (E = P, As). Single-crystal X-ray diffraction confirms κ1-E coordination of the phosphaketene and arsaketene ligands. The manganese arsaketene complex represents the first structurally characterized example a κ1-As-bound arsaketene supported by a 3d metal. Attempts to induce decarbonylation by heating or photolysis did not afford tractable products. However, treatment with isonitriles led to an isonitrile-induced linkage isomerization of the manganese pnictaketenes to give the corresponding manganese pnictaethynolate complexes (Mn–OCE). The linkage isomerization is supported by FT-IR spectroscopy, X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy, chemical derivatization with triisopropylsilyl triflate, and density functional theory calculations, which indicate that the phosphaethynolate isomer is thermodynamically favored. These results demonstrate that coordinated pnictaketenes can undergo linkage isomerization on a transition metal center, expanding the known reactivity of such complexes.

items.title:
Stimuli-Responsive
Viologen-Based Coordination Supramolecular
Isomers Modulated by π-Stacking Interactions
items.abstract: Abstract Supramolecular isomerism provides a useful platform for correlating molecular packing with physicochemical properties, yet packing-induced isomers remain uncommon because coordination modes and intermolecular interactions are difficult to control. Herein, regulation of intermolecular π-stacking between monodentate, highly conjugated PhSQ ligands affords a pair of viologen-based copper(II) isomers, CuCl2(PhSQ)2 (1 and 2; PhSQ = N-(4-sulfophenyl)─4,4′-bipyridinium). Single-crystal X-ray diffraction reveals that 1 forms a supramolecular organic framework through π-stacking interactions, whereas 2 adopts a densely packed architecture composed of A-B-style supramolecular chains. Isomer 1 exhibits pronounced photochromic and thermochromic responses, while 2 shows no discernible color change under comparable stimuli. Isomer 1 also displays higher structural stability, stronger light and thermal responsiveness, significantly enhanced absorbance, and a photothermal conversion efficiency of 31.58%, compared with 25.03% for 2. These contrasting properties are attributed to differences in the types and strengths of intermolecular weak interactions, especially the more abundant π-stacking interactions in 1, highlighting the importance of packing modes in the rational design of stimuli-responsive supramolecular materials.

items.title:
The Structural
Twist of His1 Residue in Cu-ATCUN Metallopeptides:
A Rule Breaker on Redox Activity
items.abstract: Abstract The Amino-Terminal Copper and Nickel (ATCUN) motif (H2N-Xxx-Zzz-His) is renowned for forming exceptionally stable, 4N square-planar Cu(II) complexes that are typically “redox-silent” due to their inability to effectively coordinate Cu(I). This study demonstrates a “structural twist” where the characteristic redox inactivity of the canonical ATCUN motif is bypassed strategically incorporating a histidine residue at the N-terminal position (His1). Through a comparative analysis of three peptides, NH2-ADHV-Am (canonical), NH2-HDHV-Am (modified), and Ac-HDHV-Am (acetylated), we investigated the impact of the His1 residue on Cu(I/II) coordination, thermodynamic stability, and catalytic Reactive Oxygen Species (ROS) production. Spectroscopic and thermodynamic data reveal that while both NH2-ADHV-Am and NH2-HDHV-Am form stable 4N Cu(II) complexes at physiological pH, the presence of His1 in the latter sequence increases its affinity for Cu(I) by approximately 1 order of magnitude. This modification also enables the formation of transient “histamine-like” coordination intermediates involving the terminal amine and the His1 imidazole nitrogen, which could act as structural bridges to promote the Cu(II/I) transition. Consequently, NH2-HDHV-Am effectively promotes ascorbate-mediated ROS generation, exhibiting a catalytic activity halfway between the redox-silent canonical motif and the highly reactive acetylated control. These findings redefine the structural boundaries for peptide-mediated catalysis, identifying the N-terminal residue’s chemical nature as a key parameter for transforming inert copper reservoirs into tunable generators of oxidative species.

items.title:
Revisiting
Pearson’s HSAB Principle: The Hardness
of Cations and Anions from Atomic Polarizabilities
items.abstract: Abstract The hard–soft acid–base (HSAB) principle is among the most useful tools to rationalize chemical reactivity, establishing that hard acids tend to associate with hard bases, while soft acids tend to associate with soft bases. The hard/soft nature of acids and bases can be quantified using absolute hardness (η), which was defined by Pearson as η = (I – A)/2, where I and A are the ionization potential and electron affinity, respectively. We found that this definition results in anomalies for some ions across the periodic table (i.e., La3+ and Ce3+ have significantly different η values of 15.4 and 8.4 eV, respectively, but similar coordination chemistry). This prompted us to propose an alternative definition of η based on the electric dipole polarizability (α) and the radius of the ion, estimated from the maxima of the radial distribution functions (⟨r⟩) obtained with relativistic CCSD(T) calculations: η = ⟨r⟩2/α. We show that this simple relationship affords coherent η values for cations across the periodic table, overcoming the anomalies observed with Pearson’s definition. Furthermore, this definition allows calculating η values for anions and other species for which electron affinities are not readily available, offering a useful tool to rationalize chemical reactivity across different areas of chemistry.

items.title: Heptacoordinated Antimony(V) Cations
items.abstract: Abstract Heptacoordinated pnictogen cations are quite rare, and structurally characterized Sb(V) cations have remained elusive. Here, we report on the synthesis, isolation, and structural characterization of salts containing two heptacoordinated Sb(V) cations, i.e., [(ppy)3Sb–X]+ (X = F; [1–F]+, X = CH3; [1–CH3]+, ppy = 2-(2-pyridyl)phenyl). Fluorination of neutral [(ppy)3Sb] (1) followed by treatment with BF3·OEt2 afforded [1–F][BF4], while methylation of 1 followed by counteranion exchange furnished [1–CH3][PF6]. In the solid state, [1–F]+ adopts a pentagonal-bipyramidal (PBP) geometry, whereas [1–CH3]+ adopts a tricapped-tetrahedral (TCT) one. Density functional theory (DFT) calculations for the [(ppy)3Sb–X]+ ([1–X]+) series revealed that the PBP structure is more stable for X = F, Cl, and Br, whereas the TCT structure is more stable for X = CF3, H, and CH3. Calculated fluoride ion affinity (FIA) and pyridine affinity (PyA) of simplified [Ph3Sb–X]+ models revealed substituent-dependent Lewis acidity and donor-binding-site preferences that broadly correlate with the PBP/TCT preferences of [1–X]+. These results suggest that substituent X influences the relative stability of the PBP and TCT structures in the heptacoordinated [1–X]+ series.

items.title:
Synthesis
and Crystal Structure of a Tb(III)-MOF and
Its Luminescent Sensing for Erythromycin, Tetracycline, and 3,5-Dinitrosalicylic
Acid
items.abstract: Abstract A new MOF {[Tb2(L)3(H2O)2]·H2O·0.5CH3OH}n (1) was synthesized using rare earth metal Tb3+ and organic ligand 4,4′-dioxoacetic acid diphenylsulfone (H2L) via solvothermal reaction. Single-crystal X-ray diffraction experiments showed that 1 is three-dimensional. Additionally, the detailed fluorescence sensing properties of 1 were studied, where 1 effectively sensitizes the characteristic emission of Tb3+ through the antenna effect. Notably, 1 can recognize erythromycin (ERY), tetracycline (TC), and 3,5-dinitrosalicylic acid (DNSA) in water, exhibiting significant quenching effects, with detection limits of 1.92 × 10–8 M, 2.73 × 10–7 M, and 2.21 × 10–7 M, demonstrating high selectivity and sensitivity. Based on these findings, a fluorescent test strip was developed for real water sample detection of ERY, TC, and DNSA. 1 demonstrated stable luminescence over a wide pH range and excellent water stability, making it suitable for various environmental conditions. The possible fluorescence quenching mechanism was also discussed. Time-resolved luminescence decay and XPS characterizations reveal distinct quenching pathways that are not dominated merely by the inner filter effect: dynamic collision quenching for ERY, synergistic competitive absorption and photoinduced electron-transfer effects for TC, and ground-state intermolecular interactions coupled with selective quenching of short-lived defect sites for DNSA.

items.title:
When Counterions
Fall into Place: Alkali Effects on
f-Element Polyoxomolybdate Crystallization and Speciation
items.abstract: Abstract Speciation and crystallization of f-elements with polyoxomolybdate (POMo) ligands have been scarcely studied compared to analogous tungstate POMs. Here we investigate polyoxomolybdate complexes with trivalent lanthanides (LnIII) in solution and the solid state to detail the interplay between the f-elements, POM ligand, and counterions. Alkali counterions play a decisive role in shaping the solid-state structure and solution-state behavior of POM complexes, including the Ln-POMo reported here. A family of Ln(PMo11O39)211– compounds with charge-balancing K+ and Cs+ counterions were synthesized across the lanthanide series, with 16 total structures determined by single-crystal X-ray diffraction, complemented by bulk solid characterization. Combined solid-state and solution-state studies enabled direct comparison of structural trends and revealed a countercation-dependent solution-state speciation. While K+ analogues exhibit consistent parallel arrangement of POM units in the crystalline lattice, Cs+ derivatives adopt distinct packing modes, including both parallel and perpendicular orientations. These structural differences are reflected in various lattice organizations and intercluster interactions, highlighting the role of larger alkali cations in directing long-range assembly. Moreover, solution-state 31P nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) spectroscopy and small-angle X-ray scattering (SAXS) reveal that the countercation (Li+, Na+, K+, Rb+, and Cs+ studied) directly impacts assembly and dynamic equilibria among the aqueous species PMo11O397–, Ln(PMo11O39)4– and Ln(PMo11O39)211–, prior to crystallization.

items.title:
Design, Synthesis,
and Crystal Structure of Naturally
Occurring Arsenic-Based Materials: A Sustainable Approach toward Photocatalytic
Dye Degradation, Catalytic Solvent-Free Organic Transformations, Electrochemical
and Theoretical Studies
items.abstract: Abstract A naturally occurring arsenic-based mineral, i.e., lammerite, Cu3As2O8, has been successfully synthesized in the laboratory by employing a hydrothermal technique, and its sustainable approach toward photocatalytic dye degradation and catalytic solvent-free organic transformations has been explored along with electrochemical studies. Single-crystal X-ray diffraction studies reveal that it crystallizes in monoclinic symmetry with a = 5.3938(6) Å, b = 11.6233(15) Å, c = 5.0804(7) Å, β = 111.74(6)°, V = 295.86(71) Å3, SG: P21/c, and Z = 2. The building unit comprises [AsO4] tetrahedral, [CuO5] trigonal bipyramidal, and [CuO4] square planar units. [AsO4] and [CuO5] are connected to each other through a bridging oxide linkage to form a [CuAsO8]n unit. Further, [CuO4] is connected to the [CuAsO8]n unit to form Cu3As2O8. The material served as an efficient photocatalyst for the complete degradation of the methylene blue (MB) dye, although the degradation efficiency was enhanced by approximately 2-fold upon addition of 0.1 mL of 6% H2O2. The SEM and TEM studies revealed multilayered, porous, nanosized particles with enhanced surface-active area. The radical scavenger experiment confirms that the hydroxyl radical is responsible for the dye degradation. Electrochemical studies confirm the quasi-reversible electron transfer process of the Cu2+/Cu+ and Cu+/Cu0 redox system. Further, the synthesized lammerite exhibited promising catalytic efficiency toward a solvent-free Knoevenagel condensation reaction by varying different electron-withdrawing and -donating substituents.

items.title:
Triply Bonded
Zero-Valent Heavy Alkaline Earth Metals
(Ae = Ca, Sr, Ba) in Group 9 Carbonyl Anion Complexes
items.abstract: Abstract The involvement of (n – 1)d orbitals in covalent interactions with main-group elements has recently reshaped the fundamental understanding of bonding in heavy alkaline earth metals (Ae = Ca, Sr, Ba), particularly in terms of coordination modes, bond strength, and bond order. Herein, we report an unusual class of Group 9 carbonyl anion complexes, AeM(CO)3– (M = Co, Rh, Ir), featuring direct Ae-transition metal interactions with pronounced multiple-bond character. Comprehensive structural searches reveal that the global minimum structures of these complexes adopt C3v-symmetric geometries with a 1A1 ground electronic state, in which the Ae center occupies a terminal position and forms an exceptionally short Ae–M bond along the principal axis. Detailed bonding analyses indicate that the Ae–M interaction can be described as a formal triple bond, comprising a dominant σ component, supplemented by weaker π contributions involving donation from d orbitals of the transition metal into vacant orbitals of Ae. These interactions give rise to an unusual zero-valent description of the heavy alkaline earth metals and establish high-order Ae–transition-metal bonding, leading to remarkably short Ae–M distances within carbonyl frameworks.

items.title:
Half-Sandwich
Scandium Complexes Bearing Heterocycle-Fused
Ligands for the (Co)Polymerization of Styrene
items.abstract: Abstract Half-sandwich scandium complexes have been demonstrated to be efficient catalyst precursors for the (co)polymerization of styrene. In this study, we synthesized a series of half-sandwich scandium complexes bearing indole- and benzothiophene-fused cyclopentadienyl ligands with various substituents. With [Ph3C][B(C6F5)4] as a cocatalyst, all the scandium complexes exhibited considerable catalytic activity toward styrene polymerization. Notably, among the indole-fused ligand systems, catalytic activity increased as the steric bulk of the substituent decreased. This trend contrasts with previous reports, in which bulkier ligands generally afforded higher catalytic activities for half-sandwich scandium complexes. Furthermore, the scandium-based catalytic system bearing an indole-fused ligand also served as an efficient catalyst for the copolymerization of styrene with either ethylene or butadiene, producing high-molecular-weight copolymers containing highly syndiotactic styrene–styrene sequences (&gt;99% rrrr). 1H and 13C NMR analyses reveal a random microstructure of ethylene-styrene copolymers and the block microstructure of butadiene-styrene copolymers with 1,4-enriched polybutadiene sequences (&gt;90% 1,4-). The block microstructure of the butadiene–styrene copolymers was further confirmed by kinetic studies and atomic force microscopy (AFM), while tensile stress–strain measurements were performed to evaluate the mechanical properties of selected butadiene–styrene copolymers.

items.title:
Phase Stability
of Hexacelsian Initially Formed as
Low-Crystalline Spherical Particles
items.abstract: Abstract Hexacelsian, a layered polymorph of BaAl2Si2O8, is attractive for high-temperature applications but eventually transforms into celsian, the stable polymorph without a layered structure. In this study, spherical BaAl2Si2O8 precursors were prepared by spray pyrolysis. The as-prepared precursor was identified as low-crystalline hexacelsian with a spherical morphology. Upon heat treatment, crystalline hexacelsian formed exclusively over a wide temperature range. Notably, hexacelsian persisted even after heat treatment at 1300 °C for 136 h and 1500 °C for 181 h, conditions under which celsian formation has been reported for clay-derived and conventionally mixed precursors. X-ray diffraction, solid-state nuclear magnetic resonance, electron diffraction, and Rietveld refinement showed that the specimens calcined at 1000 °C consisted of mixed α- and β-hexacelsian phases, whereas the calcined specimen at 1500 °C was assigned to the β-phase. Mechanistic investigations indicate that the overall composition, together with the mixing state of Ba, Al, and Si achieved by spray pyrolysis, contributes to the stabilization of hexacelsian. Furthermore, compact specimens prepared from the spherical precursor exhibited reduced preferred orientation of platy hexacelsian grains compared with those derived from platy clay-based precursors. Thus, spray-pyrolyzed spherical precursors offer a useful route for improving the phase stability and processing characteristics of hexacelsian.

items.title:
A Multielectron
Macromolecular Ruthenium–Bipyridine
Electrolyte for Redox Flow Batteries
items.abstract: Abstract Renewable power sources offer a compelling path to decarbonized electricity generation, but their inherent intermittency often mismatches real-world demand. Efficient, scalable energy storage is therefore essential to capture surplus generation and deliver power on demand. Redox flow batteries (RFBs) are particularly attractive for grid applications, yet their practical energy density is frequently limited by the narrow electrochemical stability window of aqueous electrolytes and by predominantly one-electron redox chemistries. Here we report the synthesis and electrochemical characterization of a macromolecular ruthenium complex soluble in organic solvents that undergoes a reversible three-electron redox process. Cyclic voltammetry and galvanostatic charge–discharge measurements confirm multielectron accessibility and stable cycling behavior. Notably, the complex retains electrochemical performance over 100 charge–discharge cycles, highlighting the promise of multielectron, macromolecular redox couples in organic electrolytes as a strategy to increase RFB energy density.

items.title:
Bowl-Shaped
Indenofluoranthenes: Organoselenium Functionalization
and Titanium Coordination
items.abstract: Abstract Indeno[1,2,3-cd]fluoranthene (iFLA) is known as one of the smallest π-segments of fullerene C60. However, its intrinsic chemical reactivity remains largely unexplored. Herein, we report a regioselective 1,4-functionalization of iFLA, affording an ethylene-bridged di(n-butyl)indeno[2,1-a]fluorene derivative (iFL). The crystallographic analysis confirmed the bowl-shaped geometry. The further oxidation of the ethylene bridge by benzeneseleninic anhydride (PhSeO)2O provided the corresponding diketone together with an elusive intermediate bearing an organoselenium functionality. This provides mechanistic insights into the (PhSeO)2O-mediated oxidation process. The diketone was further converted in situ into an N,N-chelating di(imino) ligand to generate a 12-electron octahedral coordinate d0-complex through a one-pot protocol. These methods would be applicable to diversify fullerene-inspired π-segments with functional groups containing main group elements.

items.title:
Assembly of
Uranyl-Containing Isopolyoxotungstate
for Visible-Light-Driven Photocatalytic Synthesis of Quinazolinones
items.abstract: Abstract Introducing uranyl into isopolyoxotungstates offers significant opportunities for enriching the structures and properties of polyoxometalates, yet it remains a formidable challenge. Herein, a novel dimeric uranyl-containing isopolyoxotungstate, Na3[H2N(CH3)2]4H5[(UO2)(H2O)(H2W11O38)]2·10H2O (U2W22), was synthesized using Na2B4O7·10H2O as both a buffer and mineralizer, and DL-tartaric acid as a key auxiliary reagents. Single-crystal X-ray structure analysis revealed that U2W22 features a fascinating “S”-shaped sandwich framework, in which two UO22+ units are connected to two {W11} subunits through eight bridging oxygen atoms. Notably, U2W22 exhibits outstanding photocatalytic performance in the visible-light-driven synthesis of quinazolinones via the condensation of o-aminobenzamides and aldehydes under an oxygen atmosphere. This work provides a viable strategy for constructing uranyl-containing isopolyoxotungstates and demonstrates their promising potential in photocatalytic organic transformations.

items.title:
Pressure-Induced
Symmetry Breaking and Polarity in
the van der Waals Magnet CrSBr
items.abstract: Abstract The van der Waals magnet CrSBr has emerged as a fascinating platform for exploring coupled structural, magnetic, and electronic phenomena. Yet, the evolution of its crystal symmetry and electronic states under pressure and temperature remains unresolved. To elucidate this, we employ low-temperature single-crystal X-ray diffraction, Raman scattering, and photoluminescence measurements under hydrostatic pressures of up to 12 GPa, complemented by first-principles calculations. We observe a cascade of pressure-induced structural transitions from the orthorhombic Pmmn to the monoclinic P21/m phase at ≈1.5 GPa, followed by the emergence of a polar orthorhombic Pmm2 phase at ≈6.5 GPa. The change in symmetry is accompanied by phonon anomalies and a direct-to-indirect band gap crossover. Our results demonstrate pressure as a knob to engineer structure, symmetry, and electronic properties in CrSBr in a coupled manner.

items.title:
Selective
Oxidation of Cellulose to Carboxylated Cellulose
Catalyzed by a Recyclable Keggin-Type Polyoxometalate H6PMo9V3O40 with O2: An
Insight into Mechanism by DFT and Experimental Study
items.abstract: Abstract In this work, we have developed a sustainable and efficient catalytic system for the selective oxidation of the C6 hydroxyl groups of cellulose to carboxyl groups, utilizing a trivanadium-substituted Keggin-type phosphomolybdate (H6PMo9V3O40) as the catalyst and molecular oxygen (O2) as the terminal oxidant. Under the optimal conditions (120 °C, 8 h, 0.3 g catalyst, 1 MPa O2), our H6PMo9V3O40/O2 system achieved a carboxyl content of 1.02 mmol/g, which is comparable to that of the well-established TEMPO-mediated oxidation system (0.8–1.2 mmol/g). The catalyst exhibited outstanding stability and reusability, maintaining essentially unchanged activity over eight consecutive cycles without any regeneration treatment. Density functional theory calculations established a detailed catalytic cycle, revealing that the two proton-coupled-electron-transfer steps with activation energy barriers of 47.57 and 37.93 kcal mol–1 are the rate-determining bottleneck region. The thermodynamic driving force for the whole reaction is calculated to be −96.21 kcal mol–1. Kinetic analysis indicates that the reaction rate exhibits pseudozero-order kinetics. Our catalytic system successfully introduces negatively charged carboxylate groups on the cellulose surface, which generates strong electrostatic repulsion that effectively loosens the tightly bundled elementary fibrils of corn stalks, and effectively promotes the subsequent defibrillation into micro/nanofibrils upon ultrasonication.

items.title:
Electron-Driven
Ag Migration and Interfacial Growth
in ZIF-8/α-Ag2WO4 Heterostructures
items.abstract: Abstract ZIF-8/α-Ag2WO4 heterostructures were designed to investigate electron-driven Ag evolution at MOF–semiconductor interfaces. In situ electron microscopy revealed structural integration and preferential Ag nanoparticle growth on ZIF-8 under irradiation. Interfacial charge redistribution is proposed to mediate this process, offering opportunities for catalytic, sensing, and antimicrobial applications.

items.title:
Temperature-Dependent
Stereoselectivity Switch in
the Lithium-Catalyzed ROP of rac-Lactide: Interplay of a Flexible
Cation−π Interaction, Ligand Fluxionality, and Donor-Arm
Architecture
items.abstract: Abstract Precise control over the stereochemistry of polylactide (PLA) is crucial for tailoring its properties, yet achieving a temperature-driven switch between heteroselectivity and isoselectivity in the ring-opening polymerization (ROP) of racemic lactide (rac-LA) remains challenging. Herein, we report a rare example of a temperature-driven stereoselectivity switch: complex 1 affords heterotactic PLA (Pr = 0.79) at room temperature but produces isotactic PLA (Pm = 0.78) at −50 °C. Combined VT-NMR, DOSY, single-crystal X-ray diffraction, kinetic experiments, control experiments, and DFT studies reveal that the ligand backbone is inherently flexible, endowing this series of lithium complexes with fluxionality in solution, and that a flexible cation−π interaction in complex 1 is involved in its temperature-dependent conformational/coordination reorganization. Comparative VT-NMR studies of complexes 1, 4, 6, and 7 further reveal the structural origin of this switching. The trityl-containing complexes 1, 6, and 7 each exist as two distinguishable species in solution, but their temperature responses depend markedly on the side arm length: the species ratio remains essentially unchanged for complexes 6 (shortest) and 7 (longest), whereas it changes nonlinearly for complex 1 (intermediate). The tert-butyl analogue 4 shows no distinguishable species and only peak broadening upon cooling. These results indicate that the switching arises from the synergy among the intrinsic ligand fluxionality, the flexible cation−π interaction, and the donor-arm structure, which are appropriately matched only in complex 1. This work provides a strategy for designing switchable stereoselective catalysts by exploiting this synergy.

items.title:
Photochromic
POM–Lanthanide Hybrids and Their
Composite Hydrogels for Wearable Strain Sensing and Information Encryption
items.abstract: Abstract Organic–inorganic hybrid photochromic materials (OIHPMs) have attracted considerable attention owing to their rapid and reversible color changes upon light stimulation. In this paper, three Wells–Dawson-type P2W18-lanthanide–organic hybrid complexes (Ln = Eu, Ho, Nd) were hydrothermally synthesized: {[Eu(L)2(H2O)3][H3P2W18O62]} (1); {[Ho(L)2(H2O)3][H2P2W18O62]}·(L)·H2O (2); {[Nd2(L)4(H2O)6][P2W18O62]2}·(L)6·14H2O (3). They exhibit reversible photochromism upon UV irradiation, attributed to photoinduced electron transfer from POM oxygen donors to pyridine nitrogen acceptors. These complexes were incorporated into a sodium alginate/sulfobetaine methacrylate/polyacrylamide (SA/(AM-SBMA)) semi-interpenetrating hydrogel, yielding ASW composite hydrogels with enhanced mechanical properties and ionic conductivity. The hydrogels function as flexible strain sensors for real-time human motion monitoring. The Eu3+ complex shows characteristic red fluorescence dynamically quenched upon photochromism. The materials were further applied in inkless printing, QR code encryption, fingerprint anticounterfeiting, and photochromic PMMA films. This work provides a versatile strategy for multifunctional POM-based smart materials in wearable sensing and information security.

items.title:
Mixed Ionic-Electronic
Conductivity in K3W2N5 and the Nonconductive
K2WN2O
items.abstract: Abstract We report on the synthesis of the novel alkali tungsten nitride K3W2N5 and the alkali tungsten oxonitride K2WN2O. Both compounds were synthesized in bulk using the ammonothermal method at 873 K with autogenous pressures between 100 and 175 MPa. The compounds feature zweier chains, ∞1[WNON2/2]2– in K2WN2O and zweier double chains, ∞1[W2N2N6/2]3– in K3W2N5. Temperature-dependent PXRD data revealed an anisotropic thermal expansion along the direction of the anionic chains in both compounds. The compounds are semiconductors with band gaps between 2.14 and 2.24 eV determined by UV/Vis measurements and supported by DFT calculations. Electrochemical impedance spectroscopy measurements revealed K2WN2O to be an insulator and mixed ionic-electronic conductivity in K3W2N5, which makes K3W2N5 the first tungsten nitride-based ionic conductor.

items.title:
Lewis Acidic
Pentafluoroorthotellurato Germanes and
the Structural Characterization of the Germylium Ion [GePh3]+
items.abstract: Abstract The properties of the strong Lewis acid Ge(OTeF5)4 are investigated experimentally and quantum-chemically and compared to other germanes with electron-withdrawing ligands. It readily forms the octahedral germanate [NEt4]2[Ge(OTeF5)6] upon reaction with two equivalents of [NEt4][OTeF5]. Additionally, germanes with the formula RxGe(OTeF5)4–x with R = Me, Ph and x = 3, 2, 1 have been characterized. Ph3GeOTeF5 was utilized to generate the germylium ion [GePh3][Al(OTeF5)4] by –OTeF5 abstraction with one of the strongest Lewis acids available─Al(OTeF5)3.

items.title:
Programmable Synthesis of Monodisperse Multimetallic
Alloy Nanoparticles
items.abstract: Abstract Multimetallic alloy nanoparticles (MMANPs) exhibit excellent properties, yet developing general colloidal routes toward monodisperse MMANPs is still challenging due to multidimensional synthetic complexity. Herein, we demonstrate a generalized Two-NP conversion strategy for the colloidal synthesis of a library of uniform MMANPs, in which parent precursor NPs with well-defined structures are clearly identified that can accommodate various metallic atoms throughout multistep transformation. This study defines two pivotal criteria for eligible parent precursors, verifying colloidal monometallic Pt, Au, and Pd NPs, as well as their bimetallic derivatives, as ideal candidates. The differential competency and rich diversity of parent precursors allow us to design a variety of rational synthetic routes, which enables that the versatile synthesis of MMANPs, including over 200 monodisperse Pt-based ternary-to-senary alloy nanocubes, to be theoretically achieved (the constituent metals studied include Pt, Au, Pd, Fe, Co, Ni, Rh, Ag, Cu, Mn, and Sn). Benefiting from the structural inheritance of parent precursor NPs, 64 representative monodisperse MMANPs with controllable constituent elements, morphology, and size are readily produced. We propose a mechanism-driven synthesis paradigm that replaces empirical screening with a reliable precursor-oriented synthetic methodology, enabling the programmable fabrication of diverse MMANPs.

items.title:
Assessing
the Reactivity of Cobalt(II) Amide Co(TMP)2 toward Unsaturated
Organic Molecules
items.abstract: Abstract Typically regarded as strong Brønsted bases with low nucleophilicity, TMP metal amides (TMP = 2,2,6,6-tetramethylpiperidide) find widespread application in deprotonative metalation chemistry. While most examples employ s-block metal amides, Co(TMP)2 has also emerged as a powerful metalating reagent for the cobaltation of pyridines and fluoroarenes. Herein, we investigate the ability of this Co(II) metal amide to undergo insertion reactions into its Co–N bonds by assessing its reactivity toward a range of heterocumulenes and unsaturated organic molecules. Excellent stoichiometric control was achieved in reactions toward phenyl isocyanate, diphenyl ketene, and carbon dioxide, where one or two of the TMP groups can undergo insertion. Contrastingly, extending these studies to 4-methylacetophenone revealed the preference of this metal amide to act as a base to form the relevant enolate complex. The reactivity of Co(TMP)2 toward phenyl isocyanate, benzonitrile, and 4-methylacetophenone was contrasted with that of the classical Co(II) amide Co(HMDS)2, which shows, in most cases, a diminished nucleophilic power and lower selectivity.

items.title:
A Recyclable
Ni(II) Metal–Organic Framework
as a Catalyst for Imine Synthesis via Acceptorless Dehydrogenative
Coupling and Oxidative Self-Condensation of Benzylamine
items.abstract: Abstract A new Ni(II) metal–organic framework (MOF), IITG-12 (IITG: Indian Institute of Technology Guwahati), was solvothermally synthesized in mixed solvents (acetonitrile and water). The as-synthesized MOF was thermally activated, followed by solvent exchange with methanol to obtain the activated MOF, namely IITG-12a. The catalytic potential of IITG-12a was explored for imine synthesis via two distinct pathways, which included oxidative coupling of benzyl alcohol and aniline derivatives through acceptorless dehydrogenation and oxidative self-condensation of benzylamine. For oxidative coupling reaction, optimal conditions are 3 mol % IITG-12a loading, KOtBu as base, toluene as solvent, 115 °C, and 8 h, with 83% isolated yield. For oxidative self-condensation of benzylamine, the optimized conditions were established as 100 °C, 24 h, under an O2 atmosphere under a solvent-free medium, delivering a yield of 96%. Both catalytic systems demonstrated a broad substrate scope with diverse functional group tolerance. The catalyst, IITG-12a, exhibited remarkable recyclability over four consecutive cycles. The stability of the catalyst after the catalytic reactions was examined via different characterization techniques. The mechanistic pathways for both transformations were studied through control experiments and reported literature analysis. This work represents the introduction of a new MOF single crystal and its catalytic applications for sustainable imines syntheses via two distinct pathways.

items.title:
In Situ Cyanide-to-Bipyridine
Coordination-Sphere
Reconstruction of [Fe(CN)6]3– into Surface-Confined
Fe(bpy)32+ on Nafion/Carbon Soot for Selective
Electrocatalytic Nitrite Oxidation and Sensing
items.abstract: Abstract A simple electrochemical strategy is introduced for the in situ synthesis of a surface-confined tris(2,2′-bipyridine)iron(II), [Fe(bpy)3]2+, complex through coordination-sphere reconstruction (CSR) of hexacyanoferrate(III), [Fe(CN)6]3–. The process involves an electrochemically driven cyanide-to-bipyridine ligand exchange directly on a Nafion/carbon soot (Nf-CS)-modified electrode, thereby avoiding conventional multistep solution-phase synthesis. Cyclic voltammetry, Raman spectroscopy, Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy, UV–vis spectroscopy, high-resolution mass spectrometry, and electrochemical quartz crystal microbalance measurements collectively confirm the formation of surface-confined [Fe(bpy)3]2+ and provide evidence for transient Fe2+/Fe3+ intermediates during CSR. A selective Prussian Blue test further confirms CN– release, supporting the proposed ligand-exchange mechanism. The resulting GCE/Nf-CS@[Fe(bpy)3]2+ electrode exhibits remarkable electrocatalytic activity toward nitrite oxidation, with a sensitivity of 150 μA mM–1, approximately 10-fold higher than that of chemically synthesized [Fe(bpy)3]2+-based electrodes. The electrode also demonstrates a low overpotential, excellent operational stability, and negligible fouling. Coupling with batch injection analysis enables rapid, selective, and reproducible nitrite determination in serum, urine, saliva, spinach, and wastewater samples, with recoveries of 98–101%. This new approach provides a versatile platform for developing a variety of surface-confined molecular electrocatalysts and functional inorganic materials for real-time applications.

items.title: Probing the Structures, Electronic Properties, and Bonding Patterns of RbOn–/0 and CsOn–/0 ( n = 4–7) by Photoelectron Spectroscopy and Theoretical Calculations
items.abstract: Abstract This study combines anion photoelectron spectroscopy with density functional theory calculations to explore the geometric structures, electronic structures, and bonding properties of RbOn–/0 and CsOn–/0 (n = 4–7). The measured spectra exhibit a clear size-dependent evolution: as the number of oxygen atoms increases, all features shift progressively toward higher binding energies. Theoretical analysis reveals that RbOn– and CsOn– have similar structures. They can be described as polyoxide units electrostatically stabilized by alkali metal cations, with structural motifs that follow systematic trends: [O2]−–M+–[O2]− (n = 4), [O3]−–M+–[O2]− (n = 5), [O2]−–M+–[O2]2– (n = 6), and [O3]−–M+–[O2]2– (n = 7). These results confirm that electrostatic interactions dominate the bonding between alkali metal cations and oxygen-rich units, and the polarization effects become more pronounced with the increase of cluster size. The neutral RbOn and CsOn clusters undergo pronounced structural reorganization compared with their corresponding anionic structures yet largely retain the same basic framework as their anionic counterparts.

items.title:
Electrochemical
Acetonitrile Release from Dinitrogen-Derived
Rhenium Imido Complexes through Proton-Coupled Electron Transfer
items.abstract: Abstract The oxidation of rhenium(III) azavinylidene complexes that originate from the reductive splitting of dinitrogen enables the stepwise conversion of N2 to nitriles. We here report the development of an electrochemical protocol and the experimental and computational examination of the reaction mechanism. Electrolysis of N2-derived {ReIII–N═CHCH3} azavinylidene complexes in the presence of chloride and NEt3 affords MeCN nearly quantitatively and the respective ReIV 3-electron oxidation products in yields around 50%. The lower yields in the Re product can be attributed to degradation processes of the supporting pincer ligands. The first oxidation is coupled to chloride addition. Subsequent proton-coupled electron transfer (PCET) affords the nitrile product as a net 2-electron oxidation of the nitrogenous ligand. The overoxidation to rhenium(IV) originates in a large potential inversion upon restoration of rhenium(III) as an inherent feature to the mechanism.

items.title:
Hydrometallogel-Templated,
Plasmonic Au Nanoparticle
Assemblies for NIR-Activated H2 Release from Ammonia-Borane
items.abstract: Abstract The addition of [Au(acac)(PMe3)] (acac = acetylacetonate) to orotic acid affords the mononuclear complex [Au(N-orotate)(PMe3)] (1) and the dinuclear species [{Au(PMe3)}2(μ-O,N-orotate)] (2), with the crystal structures of two polymorphs of complex 2 fully elucidated by X-ray diffraction studies. Remarkably, complex 1 undergoes ultrasound-induced supramolecular self-assembly in water to form a robust Au(I) hydrometallogel (1-hyd), whereas 2 lacks the capacity to gelate due to coordination-induced suppression of intermolecular hydrogen bonding. The hydrometallogel acts as both a soft template and an in situ gold precursor, enabling the formation of densely packed, belt-like assemblies of plasmonic Au nanoparticles (1-hyd-Au NPs) upon mild and short thermal treatment. These anisotropic nanoarrays display strong interparticle coupling, yielding a broad, red-shifted localized surface plasmon resonance (LSPR) absorption centered at ca. 650 nm with substantial NIR absorption. Under 808 nm excitation, the system exhibits efficient photothermal conversion accompanied by the generation of localized plasmonic hot spots. Exploiting this dual activation mode, 1-hyd-Au NPs photocatalyse the methanolysis of ammonia-borane, delivering significantly enhanced H2 release relative to purely thermal conditions. The results demonstrate that hydrometallogel-templated Au assemblies provide an effective and modular platform for NIR-driven plasmonic catalysis, integrating supramolecular templating with strong light-matter interactions to boost the dehydrogenation of chemical hydrogen carriers.

items.title:
Comparative
Study of Dihydrogen, Tetrel, and Metal
Bonds in Complexes of C3H4 Isomers with MH and
MH2 (M = Li, Na, Be, and Mg)
items.abstract: Abstract In this manuscript, the interactions of metal hydrides, MH and MH2 (M = Li, Na, Be, and Mg), with the C3H4 isomers cyclopropane (CP) and propyne (P) were investigated using quantum chemical calculations at the MP2/aug-cc-pVTZ level of theory. The molecular electrostatic potential (MEP) results showed that each isomer exhibits distinct behavior and participates in different types of interactions with specific characteristics. The interaction patterns differ markedly between the MH and MH2 hydrides. For the MH monomers, Structure A is stabilized by a tetrel bond (TB), while Structure C is characterized by the simultaneous presence of dihydrogen bond and metal bond interactions (DHB–MB). In contrast, the corresponding MH2 monomers form TB complexes in Structure A but are stabilized exclusively by metal bond (MB) interactions in Structure C. By comparison, cyclopropane participates only in DHB complexes, giving rise to Structure B.The interaction energy (ΔEintCP) and thermodynamic calculations highlighted that the stability of the complexes follows the order C &gt; B &gt; A. They also indicated that complex formation is governed by an exothermic process. Moreover, ΔG was negative only for Structure C, indicating that the formation of these complexes is thermodynamically favorable under the specified gas-phase conditions at 298 K and 1 atm

items.title:
Fluorination-Associated
Symmetry Transformation and
Band-Gap Widening in Antimony Tellurite-Based Birefringent Crystals
items.abstract: Abstract Balancing a wide optical band gap with large birefringence remains challenging for ultraviolet (UV) birefringent crystals. Herein, two antimony tellurite-based compounds, centrosymmetric (CS) Sb2O(TeO3)2 and noncentrosymmetric (NCS) SbTeO3F, were synthesized and compared to investigate fluorination-associated structural and optical regulation. Sb2O(TeO3)2 crystallizes in the CS space group P1̅ and features a layered framework of [SbO4], [SbO5], and [TeO3] units connected through Sb–O–Te linkages. In contrast, SbTeO3F adopts the NCS space group P212121, in which terminal Sb–F coordination accompanies changes in Sb coordination and Sb–Te–O framework connectivity. SbTeO3F exhibits improved UV transparency, shifting the absorption edge from 394 to 304 nm and increasing the experimental band gap from 3.15 to 4.08 eV. Both compounds retain large birefringence values of 0.29 and 0.30 at 546 nm, respectively. SbTeO3F also exhibits a measurable powder second-harmonic generation (SHG) response of approximately 0.6 times that of potassium dihydrogen phosphate (KDP, KH2PO4). First-principles calculations suggest that the band gap widening is related to modified band-edge electronic states, whereas large birefringence is associated with anisotropic lone-pair-active Sb3+ and Te4+ units. These findings highlight the potential of fluorination-associated structural regulation for improving UV transparency while preserving large birefringence in antimony tellurite-based crystals.

items.title:
Organic Cation-Directed
Tuning of Structure and Optical
Band Gap of One-Dimensional Hybrid Sb(III) Iodides
items.abstract: Abstract Sb(III)-halide perovskite-related structures are environmentally benign alternatives to traditional lead-based perovskites. Here, we report three hybrid Sb(III) iodides: (H2BDA)SbI5, (H2PDA)SbI5, and (H2CDA)SbI5, where H2BDA, H2PDA, and H2CDA represent 1,4-butanediammonium, 1,5-pentanediammonium, and trans-1,4-cyclohexanediammonium cations, respectively. These compounds exhibit one-dimensional zigzag chains of [SbI6]3– octahedra separated by organic cations. Temperature-dependent X-ray diffraction and calorimetry reveal thermally reversible phase transitions for (H2BDA)SbI5 at 368 K upon heating and at 363 K upon cooling, while (H2PDA)SbI5 undergoes a transition at 428 K in the heating scan and at 424 K in the cooling scan. Specifically, (H2BDA)SbI5 undergoes a monoclinic (P21/n) to monoclinic (P21/m) phase change, while (H2PDA)SbI5 changes from orthorhombic (P212121) to orthorhombic (Pnma) at high temperatures. In contrast, (H2CDA)SbI5 does not show any detectable transition within the studied temperature range. The optical band gaps are in the 2.0–2.3 eV range, with (H2CDA)SbI5 exhibiting a significantly wider gap compared to the other two analogs, attributed to pronounced distortion of the Sb–I framework, particularly increased Sb–I–Sb tilting. Additionally, (H2BDA)SbI5 exhibits a broad, Stokes-shifted emission centered at 720 nm and extending to 1200 nm. The broad emission is attributable to self-trapped excitons, making this system a potential light-emitting material.

items.title:
Generation
and Reactivity of Nickel(III)–Oxyl
Complex
items.abstract: Abstract Transition-metal terminal-oxido species are important reactive-oxygen intermediates involved in many biological and abiological oxidation reactions. In contrast to the large number of transition-metal oxido complexes of Group 5 to 8 elements in the periodic table, terminal oxygen complexes of Group 9 to 11 elements are very rare due to the existence of the “oxo-wall” between Group 8 and 9 elements. Herein, we demonstrate the generation of a nickel(III)-oxyl complex 2Cl using a diphenol supporting ligand via the reaction of the nickel(II) precursor complex 1Cl with m-chloroperbenzoic acid in CH2Cl2 at a low temperature. The terminal oxygen atom of 2Cl was confirmed to originate from m-CPBA using an 18O-labeled derivative. 2Cl exhibited a paramagnetic 1H NMR spectrum, indicating a triplet ground state (S = 1). DFT calculations supported the electronic structure of 2Cl as a nickel(III)-oxyl structure having a triplet ground state. 2Cl also exhibited an intense near-IR absorption band at 1090 nm, which was assigned to a charge transfer from the phenolate moiety of the supporting ligand to the Ni–O moiety based on TD-DFT calculations. Furthermore, 2Cl showed electrophilic reactivity in the sulfoxidation of thioanisole derivatives and induced C–H bond activation via a hydrogen atom abstraction mechanism.

items.title:
From K4SrP2S8 to
Na4SrP2S8: Alkali-Metal Cation Substitution
Induces Noncentrosymmetric Structure and Moderate Second Harmonic
Generation
items.abstract: Abstract Designing sulfide compounds with noncentrosymmetric structures is an important approach for the development of functional materials. We present the successful preparation of an unreported quaternary sulfide, Na4SrP2S8, through high-temperature solid-state synthesis. Na4SrP2S8 crystallizes in the noncentrosymmetric tetragonal space group P4̅n2. Alongside a wide direct band gap of 3.78 eV, the material shows a moderate phase-matchable second-harmonic generation response reaching 0.58 × AgGaS2─a combination that ensures excellent resistance to two-photon absorption. First-principles calculations reveal that the nonlinear optical (NLO) performance is predominantly governed by the synergistic covalent interactions within the high-dipole-moment [PS4] and [NaS4] units (specifically the S–P and Na–S bonds), while the Sr-related ionic interactions contribute negligibly. Overall, this study validates alkali-metal cation substitution as a promising strategy for constructing noncentrosymmetric chalcogenides, and also provides a promising structural prototype for high-performance infrared NLO materials.

items.title: Issue Editorial Masthead
Issue Publication Information

One-Dimensional
Semi-Rigid Bis(1H-Benzimidazole)-Functionalized
Reduced Phosphomolybdate Complexes with Distinct Bridging Metal Assemblies
for Electrochemical Sensing of Trace Cr(VI)
items.abstract: Abstract Rational development of polyoxometalate-based metal–organic complexes (MOCs) for enhanced electrochemical sensing performance in wastewater remains a significant challenge in environmental remediation. Two reduced phosphomolybdate-based MOCs functionalized with a semirigid bis(1H-benzimidazole) ligand, (H2bbix)2[Mn(H2O)3]2{Mn[P4Mo6O31H7]2}·6H2O (1) and (H2bbix)2[Co(H2O)2][Na(H2O)]2{Co[P4Mo6O31H7]2}·6H2O (2) (bbix = 1,4-bis(benzimidazol-1-ylmethyl)benzene), were hydrothermally synthesized. Single-crystal X-ray diffraction reveals adjacent {Mn[P4Mo6O31H7]2}8– polyoxoanions are linked by homometallic {[Mn(H2O)3]2}4+ ions to form 1D inorganic chains in 1. Meanwhile, 2 features 1D chains assembled from {Co[P4Mo6O31H7]2}8– clusters and heterometallic {[Co(H2O)2][Na(H2O)]2}4+ units. The 3D supramolecular frameworks of 1 and 2 are constructed from these 1D chains and protonated [H2bbix]2+ cations via intermolecular hydrogen bonds. Both compounds display excellent reversible redox properties and favorable electrochemical sensing toward trace Cr(VI). 2 exhibits significantly superior performance with a lower limit of detection (LOD) of 38.9 nM (2.01 ppb) and a higher sensitivity of 0.445 mA·μM–1 than that of 1 (LOD: 52.8 nM (2.74 ppb), sensitivity: 0.327 mA·μM–1). Mechanistic studies indicate that the synergistic effects of reduced {Co[P4Mo6O31H7]2}8– clusters, the heterometallic Co–O–Na bridge, and the bbix ligand in 2 collectively accelerate electron-transfer kinetics and mass transport. This study establishes a design strategy for high-performance electrochemical Cr(VI) sensing materials by modulating reduced phosphomolybdate structures, providing new insights for aqueous trace Cr(VI) detection.

items.title:
Near-Infrared Emitting Cu(I) Cluster-Based Metal–Organic
Frameworks with Thermally Activated Delayed Fluorescence
items.abstract: Abstract Reaction of 4-methylpyrimidine-2-thione (Hmpymt) with excess CuCl or CuCN at 150 °C gave two [Cu6(mpymt)6] cluster-based metal–organic frameworks {(CuCl)4[Cu6(mpymt)6]}n (1) and {(CuCN)4[Cu6(mpymt)6]·2Me2CO}n (2). The solid-state structures of 1 and 2 consisted of three-dimensional frameworks in which quasi-hexagonal [Cu6(mpymt)6] units are connected by [Cu4Cl4] units in 1 and [CuCN]n chains in 2. Compounds 1 and 2 exhibited strong near-infrared emission (λem = 737 and 744 nm) with photoluminescence quantum yields of 18.4% and 25.2% at ambient temperature, respectively. Fitting of the temperature-dependent lifetimes yielded model-derived singlet–triplet energy gap estimates of 0.060 and 0.077 eV for 1 and 2, respectively, with model-derived thermally activated delayed fluorescence contributions of approximately 72% and 66% at 300 K. The corresponding room-temperature emission lifetimes were 3.60 and 4.85 μs. A near-infrared phosphor-converted light-emitting diode device fabricated from 2 demonstrated promise for night-vision and potential near-infrared imaging applications.

items.title:
Nanoscale
Polyoxometalate-Based Cu-Aminotriazole Complexes
with Cooperative Acid–Base Sites for the Baeyer–Villiger
Oxidation Reaction
items.abstract: Abstract The development of efficient, stable, and recyclable heterogeneous catalysts is the key to enabling greener Baeyer–Villiger (B–V) oxidation processes. In this work, a new polyoxometalate-based metal–organic complex (POMOC) with both Lewis acidic sites and basic –NH2 groups, [Cu3(atrz)8(H2O)2(PW12O40)2] (denoted as 1-SC in its single-crystal form, atrz = 4-amino-1,2,4-triazole), was successfully synthesized. To address the limited accessibility of active sites in the nonporous POMOC material, micro- and nanosized catalysts with average particle sizes of 0.5 μm (1-0.5 μm) and 60 nm (1-60 nm) were obtained through dry ball milling and solvent-assisted ball milling of 1-SC, respectively. In the B–V oxidation reaction of cyclohexanone using O2 as the oxidant and benzaldehyde as the sacrificial agent, all prepared catalysts exhibited high catalytic activities. Notably, the nanoscale catalyst 1-60 nm demonstrated the best performance (99% conversion) due to the enhanced exposure of active sites. Furthermore, a synergistic catalytic mechanism was proposed, wherein the Cu(II) center, the [PW12O40]3– anion, and the –NH2 group cooperatively facilitated the B–V oxidation reaction via a proton-coupled electron transfer pathway. This work not only provides a facile approach for fabricating efficient and recoverable POMOC-based heterogeneous catalysts but also offers new insights into constructing green oxidation catalytic systems with acid–base multifunctional active sites.

items.title:
Rational Design
of Cu–O–Mo Dual Sites
with Fast Electron Transfer for Enhanced Photocatalytic Amines with
Alcohols to Imine
items.abstract: Abstract Solar-light-driven imine synthesis from aniline and benzyl alcohol requires selective C–OH bond activation and C═N stabilization. Enhancing efficiency relies on precise spatial control of catalytic sites, making the achievement of high activity and selectivity a persistent challenge. Here, we synthesized a dual-metal-site catalyst, [Cu2(4,4′-bipy)(Mo2O8)·2.75H2O]n (CuMo-MOF), featuring Cu and Mo centers bridged by μ-oxo groups with an average Cu···Mo distance of 3.3527 Å. The structurally defined framework provides distinct Cu/Mo coordination environments and facilitates substrate access and electron transfer, thereby enabling cooperative catalytic reactivity. Notably, the CuMo-MOF exhibits excellent photocatalytic activity (100% selectivity for imine and &gt;99.9% conversion of aniline) for the coupling of amines with alcohols under 10 W LED illumination (λ = 420–425 nm) and retains high activity over five cycles. In situ IR spectroscopy reveales an enhanced C═O stretching band on CuMo-MOF, indicating that the Cu–O–Mo fragment facilitates benzyl alcohol oxidation. Control experiments and DFT calculations reveal the detailed oxidation pathway and the synergistic effect of dual active sites. Mo sites govern benzyl alcohol adsorption and formation of ·O2–, and Cu sites mediate benzyl alcohol oxygenation as the rate-determining step. This work provides an alternative solar-driven catalytic platform for the sustainable production of value-added chemicals.

items.title:
Incorporating
Co-Encapsulated N-Doped Carbon
Nanotube with Zn Phthalocyanine: Accelerated Water Dissociation Kinetics
for Hydroxylamine Electrosynthesis
items.abstract: Abstract Electrocatalytic nitrite (NO2–) reduction to hydroxylamine (NH2OH) under ambient conditions is regarded as a sustainable way to simultaneously enable pollutant abatement and value-added chemical synthesis; however, the intrinsically sluggish kinetics and competing over-reduction to ammonia necessitate the rational exploration of robust electrocatalytic systems. Herein, we report the anchoring of zinc phthalocyanine (ZnPc) molecules onto bamboo-like nitrogen-doped carbon nanotubes encapsulating metallic cobalt nanoparticles (Co-NCNT) for selectively converting NO2– to NH2OH. The resulting ZnPc/Co-NCNT electrocatalyst achieves a considerable NH2OH yield of 0.25 mmol h–1 mgcat–1 and a high Faradaic efficiency of 64.32% at −0.3 V vs RHE, significantly outperforming its monocomponent counterparts. Mechanistic investigations reveal that the Co-NCNT facilitates charge transfer and lowers the water dissociation barrier, securing efficient active hydrogen (*H) supply to drive the hydrogenation processes. Furthermore, the practical viability of this system is demonstrated by constructing a Zn–NO2– battery, which concurrently generates NH2OH while delivering a peak power density of 7.22 mW cm–2. This study underscores the efficacy of synergistically integrating molecular catalysts with functional carriers for selective NO2– electroreduction to NH2OH.

items.title:
Structure,
Luminescence Properties, and DFT Theoretical
Study of Bidentate Ligand Samarium Complexes
items.abstract: Abstract Three new luminescent matrix materials, Sm(oct-ala)3phen, Sm(oct-phe)3phen, and Sm(oct-ser)3phen, were prepared by in-solution synthesis method. The molecular structure, fluorescence properties, and thermal stability of the samarium complex were characterized. The results indicate that the introduction of 1,10-phenanthroline (phen) as the second ligand significantly extends the ultraviolet absorption range of the samarium complexes to 200–350 nm. In addition, the introduction of the phen ligand leads to a 30% increase in the molar extinction coefficient of the samarium complexes, providing a 22-fold improvement in the luminescence lifetime. Further morphological observations under a PLM reveal that Sm(oct-ser)3phen has the characteristics of spherulites, while cubic crystal grains are observed via SEM, which has been rarely reported in the family of amino acid–based rare earth complexes. And it was found that samarium complexes emit light that changes color from orange-red to cyan-blue at high temperatures. Theoretical calculations confirm that Sm–N and Sm–O are weak coordination bonds, and the energy gap of the samarium complexes is 3.5 eV, categorizing them as wide bandgap materials. These samarium complexes have excellent optical and thermal properties, making them very promising for applications in luminescent probes and optoelectronics.

items.title:
Supramolecular
Polymers of Chiral and Achiral Rhodium
and Iridium Complexes of N-Confused Porphyrin
items.abstract: Abstract A series of rhodium(III) and iridium(III) complexes of N-confused porphyrin (NCP) was synthesized and characterized by spectroscopic, electrochemical, and XRD methods. The results were analyzed and corroborated by DFT calculations. Insertion of the metal ions was carried out in the presence of primary alcohols (EtOH, n-PrOH), affording diamagnetic chiral square-pyramidal complexes, H NCPM(Acyl), bearing a C-bonded apical acyl ligand. By exploiting H-bonding between the apical ligand and 2-NH, in the solid state, the complexes formed 1-D polymeric chains composed of homochiral (for rhodium(III)) or heterochiral (for iridium(III)) monomers. The optical activity of these molecules in solution was established by CD for HPLC-separated enantiomers. Redox properties were studied by electrochemical and spectroelectrochemical methods. Relatively low first oxidation potentials of the NCP complexes of both metals allowed facile reaction with I2 as an oxidant and a source of the anionic ligands. The paramagnetic six-coordinated H NCPMI2 complexes formed in the solid state 1-D polymeric chains bridged by I2, interacting by halogen bonding with axial iodides. Analysis of the electronic structures of these complexes using EPR and DFT calculations revealed a predominantly π-radical character of the metal(III) complexes rather than tetravalent rhodium or iridium NCP species.

items.title: Redox and Excited-State Modulation in Porphyrin Photosensitizers Controls H 2 Evolution at pH 7
items.abstract: Abstract While ligand design for photocatalytic hydrogen evolution has attracted much attention, replacing rare elements with more abundant ones in molecular photosensitizers without losing photocatalytic efficacy remains challenging. The key is to obtain appropriate ground-state redox potentials and excited-state properties. We report a series of four new tetraanionic tin(IV)-porphyrin complexes bearing electron-donating or electron-withdrawing substituents and, compared to their zinc(II) analogues, systematically probed the influence of electronic effects on photocatalytic properties. Tin(IV) complexes proved more electron-poor than their Zn(II) analogues, resulting in distinct photocatalytic behavior. Under green light irradiation in pH 7.0 water/acetonitrile mixtures with a cobaloxime catalyst and a triethanolamine donor, the electron-rich octamethyl-substituted photosensitizer [Sn-MeP]4– achieved the highest photocatalytic turnover number of 430 molH2/molPS after 20-h irradiation and a maximum photocatalytic turnover frequency of 35 h–1 in the Sn series. Conversely, under identical conditions, the electron-poorest zinc(II) complex [Zn–F16P]4– yielded the best performance (photocatalytic turnover number of 850 and photocatalytic turnover frequency of 59 h–1). Notably, both series in this study operated via a reductive quenching pathway. This work establishes critical structure–property relationships and provides new insights into tuning excited-state redox chemistry in molecular photocatalytic systems based on earth-abundant elements.

items.title:
A Lanthanum
Polyoxometalate–Organic Framework
with Abundant Intrinsic Proton Sources Enabling Ultrahigh Proton Conduction
items.abstract: Abstract Intrinsic proton sources and hydrolytic stability are two important elements of efficient proton-conducting materials for enhancing proton conductivity and reduced dependence on external environment. Herein, we report a lanthanide polyoxometalate–organic framework prepared using edta as a chelator, with coordinated and lattice water molecules acting as intrinsic proton sources. The material exhibits high proton conductivity even at 40% relative humidity and 298 K, retaining 2.6 × 10–4 S cm–1 with only a 4.6-fold decrease from the value of 1.19 × 10–3 S cm–1 at 95% relative humidity. This demonstrates weak humidity dependence, a key advantage over materials requiring conditions near saturation. At 373 K and 95% relative humidity, the conductivity reaches 1.76 × 10–2 S cm–1. Our findings offer a viable design for proton conductors that depend on internal water reservoirs.

items.title:
Encapsulation of Nitrogen-Rich Imidazole/Pyrazole
in an Indium-Based Metal–Organic Framework for Organic Iodide
Adsorption
items.abstract: Abstract Nitrogen-rich organic small molecules are frequently incorporated into porous materials to improve their adsorption performance. To investigate the effect of nitrogen-rich imidazole/pyrazole compounds encapsulated within metal–organic frameworks (MOFs) on organic iodide adsorption, 2-methylimidazole, 1-vinylimidazole, and pyrazole were separately incorporated into the pores of SHF-61 via the thermal diffusion method, yielding SHF-61-based composites (namely, 2-MI@SHF-61, Vlm@SHF-61, and Pyr@SHF-61). These composites exhibited remarkable static CH3I adsorption capacities of 1421, 1290, and 1149 mg/g at 75 °C, representing 2.40-, 2.18-, and 1.94-fold enhancements relative to pristine SHF-61. Likewise, their static C2H5I adsorption capacities at 75 °C were increased by 3.33-, 2.28-, and 2.05-fold, respectively. Noteworthily, the static organic iodide adsorption capacities of SHF-61-based composites surpass those of most previously reported MOF-based adsorbents. Further analysis of the adsorption mechanism of SHF-61-based composites toward organic iodides revealed that the adsorption process involves the formation of I3– anions through charge-transfer interactions as well as N-methylation/ethylation reactions. Our study demonstrates that the encapsulation of nitrogen-rich imidazole/pyrazole compounds within MOFs effectively enhances the organic iodide adsorption performance of materials, providing valuable guidance for the rational design of high-performance organic iodide adsorbents.

items.title: An Amine-Decorated Porous rht -Type Cu-MOF with Multi-CO2-philic Sites for High CO2 Uptake Capacity
items.abstract: Abstract We report an amine-decorated porous rht-type Cu-MOF (HNUST-18) that has multi-CO2-philic sites (CuII OMSs, triazine rings and NH groups) and shows a high CO2 gas uptake capacity (27.3 mmol g–1, 273 K under 30 bar) with effective separation for CO2–CH4 (CO2–N2) mixtures under dynamic conditions at 298 K. Theoretical calculations verify that NH groups and triazine rings have significant synergistic effects to enhance CO2 binding affinity.

items.title:
Trans-Picolinate
Functionalization of a Cyclen-Based
Chelator Enables Complexation of Large Radiometals for Cancer Theranostics
items.abstract: Abstract The development of chelators with diverse coordination properties is essential for expanding the radiometals available for imaging and targeted therapy. We investigate the metal-binding behavior of DO2A-2PA, a trans-picolinic acid-functionalized cyclen chelator, with isotopes of lanthanum (133/155La/natLa), actinium (225Ac), lead (203Pb/212Pb/natPb), and lutetium (117Lu/natLu). Metal complexes were characterized in solution by 1H NMR spectroscopy (natLa3+, natPb2+, and natLu3+) and in the solid state by X-ray crystallography (natLa3+, natPb2+). The solid-state structures revealed a 10-coordinate La3+ complex, whereas Pb2+ engaged only six donor atoms and resided deeper within the cyclen cavity, consistent with shorter M-NDO2A distances in [Pb(H4DO2A-2PA)]2+. Solution-state NMR studies showed fluxional behavior for La3+, Pb2+, and Lu3+ complexes, supported by variable-temperature experiments. Radiolabeling studies demonstrated efficient, quantitative, and ambient-temperature incorporation of [225Ac]Ac3+ and [133/135La]La3+, with the resulting radiocomplexes exhibiting high kinetic inertness in vitro. Although quantitative [203Pb]/[212Pb]Pb2+ labeling was achieved with DO2A-2PA, performance did not exceed DOTAM, and incorporation of [177Lu]Lu3+ remained inefficient even at elevated temperatures. Overall, these results identify DO2A-2PA as a promising chelator for large, hard radiometals particularly [225Ac]Ac3+ and [133/135La]La3+ while underscoring that increased donor-atom density does not universally enhance coordination performance for softer radiometals such as [203Pb]/[212Pb]Pb2+.

items.title:
Enhanced Properties
and Stability of Block-MOFs for
Electrochemical Reduction through Tuning the Defective Sites
items.abstract: Abstract The poor electrical conductivity and insufficient active sites of MOFs severely restrict their electrocatalytic applications. Herein, tannic acid (TA), a polyhydroxy molecule, was used to etch the surface of MIL-101(Fe). The hydroxyl groups chelate with exposed Fe sites to stabilize active centers and improve electrocatalytic durability. Among TA-modified MIL-101(Fe) samples with different reaction durations, MIL-101(Fe)-1h delivers nearly full conversion, high Faradaic efficiency, and excellent selectivity for electrochemical nitrobenzene hydrogenation. Control experiments confirm that the TA-etching strategy creates abundant active sites, enhances stability, and modulates the local microenvironment for boosted catalytic performance.

items.title:
Two-Dimensional
Silver-Alkynyl Framework Based on
Tetraalkynylporphyrin for Visible-Light-Driven Photocatalysis
items.abstract: Abstract The rational construction of crystalline two-dimensional metal–organic frameworks (2D MOFs) sustained exclusively by metal–carbon (M–C) bonds remains a significant challenge. Herein, we report a 2D silver-alkynyl framework, Ag-Por-MOF, assembled at room temperature from 5,10,15,20-tetrakis(4-ethynylphenyl)porphyrin (H2-TEPP) and silver(I) triflate (AgOTf). The material adopts a layered structure built from tetranuclear silver clusters bridged by Ag–C≡C linkages, with charge neutrality achieved without additional counterions, as supported by Ag K-edge XAS/EXAFS analysis, elemental analysis, and theoretical simulation. The framework exhibits broad visible-light absorption, pronounced photoinduced charge separation, and pronounced reactive oxygen species (ROS) generation capability under ambient illumination. The synthesis is readily scalable to the gram level without loss of crystallinity or porosity. As a heterogeneous photocatalyst, Ag-Por-MOF enables visible-light-driven oxidative cyclization of o-phenylenediamines and aldehydes to afford 2-substituted benzimidazoles with high efficiency (up to 97% yield), excellent functional-group tolerance, and robust recyclability over five consecutive cycles. This work provides a viable route toward M–C bond-based 2D frameworks for sustainable photocatalysis.

items.title: Pyrrolo[3,2- b ]pyrrole Dicarboxylate Linkers Enable Topological Diversity and Tunable Luminescence in Zr6-Based Metal–Organic Frameworks
items.abstract: Abstract Aryl-substituted pyrrolo[3,2-b]pyrrole dicarboxylate linkers with distinct substitution patterns were designed to construct Zr6-based metal–organic frameworks (SIFE-8–14) with controllable topology and photophysical properties. The 2,5-substituted linear linkers form conventional fcu-topology MOFs and exhibit aggregation-caused quenching (ACQ). In contrast, 1,4-substituted analogues display aggregation-induced emission (AIE), assembling into either disordered fcu frameworks or a rare 2,6-connected pcu net (SIFE-14). Modulator engineering triggers the fcu-to-pcu structural transition, confirmed by 3D microelectron diffraction. Remarkably, SIFE-14 achieves a photoluminescence quantum yield (PLQY) of 2%, representing up to a 4-fold enhancement relative to the fcu-type analogues (0.5–0.7%). Benefiting from its excellent water resistance and thermal stability, SIFE-14 can serve as a highly sensitive fluorescent probe for Cr3+ in aqueous media via a significant fluorescence quenching effect. It exhibits excellent reliability (R2 = 0.996) with a detectable Cr3+ concentration as low as 25 × 10–5 M. This work establishes pyrrolo[3,2-b]pyrrole as a versatile building block that enables simultaneous topological control and luminescence tuning in Zr-MOFs, offering a new design paradigm for high-performance luminescent framework materials.

items.title:
Excited-State
Dynamics of Platinum(II) Complexes with
Flexible Lewis Pair Ligands
items.abstract: Abstract Excited-state dynamics of platinum(II) complexes coordinated with stimuli-responsive flexible Lewis pair (FlexLP) and 4,4′-di-tert-butyl-2,2′-bipyridine (tBu2bpy), 1,2-bis(diphenylphosphino)ethane (dppe), or triphenylphosphine (PPh3) ligands were investigated by ultrafast transient absorption spectroscopy. Spectroscopic studies reveal that the platinum(II) bipyridine complex exhibits faster intersystem crossing (ISC) and triplet excited-state decay than the complexes with phosphine ligands, attributed to the higher contribution of charge-transfer (CT) and metal character in the excited states. The triplet excited-state lifetimes of the complexes are also influenced by the conformation of the FlexLP ligands, with the closed-form complexes showing longer lifetimes than the open-form complexes.

items.title:
N-Heterocyclic
Carbene-Supported Metaphosphoric
Acids as Tunable Anionic Oxygen-Donor Ligands
items.abstract: Abstract Anionic oxygen-donor ligands play a central role in coordination chemistry, yet the development of new, modular ligand families remains limited. Herein, we report a series of N-heterocyclic carbene (NHC)-supported metaphosphoric acids (NHC→PO3H) spanning three distinct carbene structures. These compounds are prepared on gram scale via NHC phosphorylation followed by ester cleavage, affording air- and water-stable metaphosphate esters and oxoacids. Single-crystal X-ray diffraction and density functional theory reveal closely related structures across the series, featuring conserved C–P bonding. Protonation affords well-defined (NHC→PO3H2)+ species; characterization of a representative example reveals contraction of the C–P bond, consistent with enhanced carbene–phosphorus interaction. In aqueous solution, these metaphosphoric acids behave as monoprotic oxoacids with tunable Brønsted acidity spanning more than three pKa units (pKa = 4.07–7.14). The chemical behavior of these ligands is further demonstrated by carbene-dependent reactivity in phosphoanhydride formation and by coordination to Cu(I), yielding discrete dicopper and tetracopper complexes supported by μ2-η1:η1 and μ3-η1:η1:η1 binding modes, respectively. Two corresponding dicopper(I) complexes are competent precatalysts for aerobic oxidation of benzyl alcohol to benzaldehyde. Together, these results establish NHC–metaphosphates as an accessible and tunable class of anionic oxygen-donor ligands with adaptable structural, electronic, and coordination properties.

items.title:
Low-Temperature
Magnetism of Rare-Earth Orthophosphates
items.abstract: Abstract Rare-earth orthophosphates, REPO4, are highly insulating materials in which localized 4f moments interact through a phosphate framework, providing a model system for weak cooperative magnetism in the absence of itinerant electrons. Here, we report a systematic study of single and mixed rare-earth orthophosphates spanning the lanthanide series, Y, and Sc. Susceptibility and magnetization measurements reveal a progression from weakly paramagnetic behavior in the light rare-earth compositions to large low-temperature moments and antiferromagnetism in the heavier members. High-temperature Curie–Weiss analysis yields effective moments that follow the expected free-ion trends, while SmPO4 and EuPO4 deviate because of Van Vleck contributions and low-lying excited multiplets.
