The onset and strength of magnetic order are determined by moment and structure, with TbxGd(1–x)PO4 compositions showing enhanced ordering temperatures associated with the composition and xenotime structure. Structural analysis indicates that xenotime provides shorter, more regular RE–O coordination and a more linear RE–O–P exchange segment than monazite, supporting enhanced superexchange. Within the mixed Tb–Gd series, the highest ordering temperature, TN = 3.1 K, occurs for Tb0.5Gd0.5PO4, exceeding those of both parent compounds. These results establish REPO4 as a benchmark family for understanding how localized 4f moments, crystal-field anisotropy, and structure-dependent exchange combine to produce low-temperature magnetic order.

items.title:
Bond-Dissociation
Energies to Probe Pyridine Electronic
Effects on Organoplatinum(II) Complexes and Their Organogold(III)
Analogues: Decoupling Bond Length, Bond Strength, and Trans Influence
items.abstract: Abstract Understanding how metal centers modulate ligand electronic effects is essential for rationalizing the reactivity of organometallic complexes. Herein, we report a systematic investigation of pyridine electronic effects in cationic cyclometalated platinum(II) complexes, [(N^C^N)Pt(pyrR)]PF6, bearing para-substituted pyridines spanning a broad range of donor abilities. Metal–ligand bond strengths were quantified experimentally through gas-phase critical energies (E0) obtained by tandem mass spectrometry and RRKM kinetic modeling and compared with DFT-calculated bond-dissociation energies (BDEs). While Pt–NpyrR bond lengths and coordination-induced 1H NMR shifts proved largely insensitive to ligand electronics, E0 values correlated closely with the pKa of the pyridinium ions, establishing E0 measurements as a sensitive probe of ligand donor strength. Energy decomposition analysis revealed that Pt–NpyrR bonding is dominated by electrostatic interactions and σ-donation, with only a minor contribution from π-backdonation due to sterically enforced pyridine twisting. Comparison with the isoelectronic Au(III) series [(C^C)Au(NHC)(pyrR)]PF6 showed similar M–NpyrR interaction energy despite distinct bonding characters, with increased Pauli repulsion offsetting the greater covalency of Au–NpyrR. QTAIM and IBSI analyses demonstrated that the Au–Ctrans bond is intrinsically weaker than its Pt analogue. These results highlight the value of combining experimental thermochemistry with theoretical descriptors to disentangle metal and ligand electronic effects.

items.title:
A DFT/TD-DFT
Study of Self-Assembled Carborane Metallacycles
as Tunable Third-Order Nonlinear Optical Platforms: Synergistic Evolution
of Dimensionality and Topology in Structure–Property Relationships
items.abstract: Abstract Coordination-driven self-assembly provides a modular route to functional supramolecular materials, yet the relationship between architectural parameters and third-order nonlinear optical (NLO) response remains largely unexplored. Here, DFT/TD-DFT investigations are performed on carborane-based assemblies spanning a 0D building block 1, 1D linear scaffolds 2–3, and 2D metallacycles 4–7 with rectangle (C2), triangle (C3), and square (C4) topologies. Dimensionality and topology emerge as independent but synergistic variables governing the second hyperpolarizability (γ). Progression from 0D/1D to 2D enhances γave by up to 13.8-fold, from 87.1 × 10–36 esu (1) to 1199.1 × 10–36 esu (7), through cyclic conjugation and multidirectional charge transfer. Within the 2D series, high-symmetry C3 and C4 topologies yield near-isotropic in-plane γ tensors (γxxxx ≈ γyyyy), whereas the C2 rectangle confines the response along its long axis despite the largest longitudinal component. The γave order 7 &gt; 5 &gt; 6 &gt; 4 therefore reflects the synergy of framework symmetry and corner-unit conjugation rather than molecular size. Frequency-dependent calculations confirm that these trends persist under dynamic optical conditions. These findings establish design principles for 2D metallacyclic NLO platforms and higher-symmetry architectures, providing predictive guidelines for the rational construction of next-generation (3D polyhedral frameworks) NLO materials via coordination-driven self-assembly.

items.title:
A Coupled
Cluster Study of the Electronic Structure,
Double Aromaticity, and π–π Stacking Interactions
of a C8 Carbon Ring
items.abstract: Abstract Recent experimental advances in the synthesis and characterization of carbon rings have stimulated renewed interest in their unusual structures and electronic properties. Here, we provide a detailed analysis of the electronic structures of three low-lying isomers of the C8 ring using high-level coupled-cluster methods. The ground-state minimum is a singlet polyynic structure with C4h symmetry, featuring alternating single and triple bonds. It possesses σ- and π-antiaromaticity, resulting in overall antiaromatic character. In contrast, the singlet D4d crown-shaped structure exhibits σ- aromaticity and π-antiaromaticity, leading to net antiaromaticity. The triplet D4h minimum adopts a cumulenic structure characterized by σ-antiaromaticity and π-aromaticity, giving rise to an overall aromatic character consistent with Baird’s rule. Furthermore, the C8 ring readily forms a stable π–π stacked structure, in which the interactions give rise to four nondegenerate excited states that correlate with a monomer excited state, forming two pairs of near-degenerate states. These results reveal the intricate interplay between σ- and π-aromaticity in carbon rings and provide further insights into the electronic structure and π–π stacking interactions of C8, highlighting the complexity of aromaticity in carbon-based molecular systems.

items.title:
Centimeter-Scale Ethyltriphenylphosphonium Manganese(II)
Halide Single Crystals as Thermally Robust Green Phosphors for White
LEDs
items.abstract: Abstract Lead-free manganese(II) halide hybrids are promising phosphors for solid-state lighting, but the effect of halide substitution within a fixed organic-cation framework remains insufficiently resolved. Here, centimeter-scale ETP2MnCl4 and ETP2MnBr4 single crystals were grown at room temperature by antisolvent diffusion using ethyltriphenylphosphonium (ETP) as the organic cation. Single-crystal X-ray diffraction and powder X-ray diffraction identified zero-dimensional structures composed of isolated [MnX4]2– tetrahedra separated by ETP cations. Both compounds exhibited Mn2+-centered green emission under blue-compatible excitation. ETP2MnCl4 and ETP2MnBr4 emitted at 518 nm with a fwhm of 43 and 520 nm with a fwhm of 44 nm. ETP2MnBr4 reached a photoluminescence quantum yield (PLQY) of 64.0%, compared with 28.1% for ETP2MnCl4, and retained 73.9% of its room-temperature PL intensity at 390 K. In phosphor-converted WLEDs, the chloride formulation delivered a luminous efficacy of 102.54 lm·W–1, whereas the bromide formulation achieved a CRI of 84.4. The matched-cation comparison shows that chloride-to-bromide substitution preserves the basic emission mechanism but changes local distortion, Mn2+-Mn2+ separation, optical-gap response, decay kinetics, electron–phonon coupling descriptors, and thermal performance. These results provide a composition-guided basis for selecting lead-free Mn2+ halide phosphors according to efficiency, color temperature, color rendering, and operating-temperature requirements.

items.title:
Sulfur Vacancy-Engineered ZnIn2S4 Nanosheets Integrated with CoS1.097 for Enhanced Visible
Light-Driven Nitrogen Photofixation
items.abstract: Abstract Herein, S-scheme heterojunction photocatalysts integrating sulfur vacancy-engineered ZnIn2S4 (Sv-ZnInS) with CoS1.097 (CoS) were successfully synthesized via a simple hydrothermal reaction. The formed CoS/Sv-ZnInS heterostructures exhibited considerably high catalytic activity toward visible light-driven photocatalytic nitrogen (N2) fixation. Notably, the optimized 3CoS/Sv-ZnInS sample achieved an ammonia yield of 18.18 ± 0.39 mg·L–1 after 1 h of visible-light illumination, which was an approximately 2.4-fold enhancement relative to pristine Sv-ZnInS. The S-scheme charge separation and transfer pathway was elucidated via in situ irradiated X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy, noble-metal loading, and band structure analysis. The underlying N2 photofixation mechanism was systematically investigated using density functional theory calculations and in situ diffuse reflectance infrared Fourier transform spectroscopy. The results revealed that N2 photofixation over the 3CoS/Sv-ZnInS catalyst occurred via a multistep proton-coupled electron transfer. Our findings indicate that S-scheme CoS/Sv-ZnInS heterojunctions may offer a viable route toward visible light-driven photocatalytic N2 fixation.

items.title:
Relativistic
Effects Support Atomic Segregation in
the Pseudobinary System Ca(Ag,Au)2
items.abstract: Abstract The pseudobinary system CaAg2–CaAu2 exhibits unusual atomic ordering associated with the distinct electronic and bonding characteristics of Au compared to Ag. These characteristics are strongly influenced by the substantially greater influence of relativity on Au. Although both CaAg2 and CaAu2 crystallize in the KHg2 type of structure, this type was not observed in the ternary system. Instead, two new ternary phases Ca3Ag5–xAu1+x (x = 0.78–2.48), adopting the hexagonal Fe2P-derivative Zr3Cu4Si2-type structure (hP9) and Ca3Ag1–xAu5+x (x ≈ 0.05), crystallizing in the orthorhombic Y3ZnAu5 type (oS72) were identified. Structure analyses reveal pronounced, composition-dependent Ag/Au ordering. Au–Au contacts are largely avoided in the Ag-rich intermediate, whereas an extended Au–Au bonding network develops in the Au-rich phase. Density functional theory calculations, complemented by chemical bonding and semiempirical analyses, confirm that such ordering is energetically favored over the tested alternative ordered arrangements. The observed atomic arrangements arise from the interplay of relativistically enhanced Au bonding characteristics and electron transfer from the formal cation Ca to the Ag/Au sublattice. These findings highlight the importance of relativistic effects on Au bonding, electron transfer from Ca, and geometric packing in governing Ag/Au ordering and structure selection.

items.title:
Pressure-Induced
Luminescence Enhancement Retained
after Decompression in a Gadolinium-Based Metal–Organic Framework
items.abstract: Abstract Luminescent metal–organic frameworks (MOFs) are emerging as versatile platforms for molecular sensing, yet their emissive performance is often compromised by guest-induced quenching. However, strategies aiming to reactivate such luminescence-quenched states remain limited to date. Here, we demonstrate that high-pressure engineering provides an effective approach to address this challenge in the stored triclinic phase of Gd-MOF. After a compression–decompression cycle up to 16 GPa, the material exhibits an approximately 6-fold luminescence enhancement when quenched to ambient conditions, while largely retaining its broadband framework-related emission profile. In situ synchrotron X-ray diffraction results reveal an irreversible isostructural transition in the pressure range of ∼4–7 GPa, accompanied by abnormal framework softening, a volume collapse of ∼10.33 Å3 (∼3.38%), and pronounced anisotropic lattice compression. The structural transition and subsequent hysteretic recovery indicate that the initial framework environment is not fully restored after pressure release. Together with the moderate luminescence enhancement observed during compression, these results suggest that pressure-induced modification of the pore-guest environment may contribute to the enhanced emissive state, while retained framework distortion may provide an additional contribution. This work identifies high-pressure treatment as a feasible strategy for converting guest-sensitive porous frameworks from quenched states into more emissive states.

items.title: Achieving High-Sensitivity and High-Selectivity Nitric Acid Vapor Sensors at Room Temperature: A Mixed-Ligand Cu2I2(P-( m -Tol)3)2(4VP)2 Cluster
items.abstract: Abstract Nitric acid (HNO3) vapor is highly corrosive and hazardous yet developing room-temperature chemiresistive sensors for its sensitive and selective detection remains challenging. Herein, we report a mixed-ligand copper iodide cluster, Cu2I2(P-(m-Tol)3)2(4VP)2, as a molecularly engineered sensing material for HNO3 vapor detection. The incorporation of complementary phosphine and pyridine ligands simultaneously enhances the structural stability of the copper(I) iodide framework and provides accessible recognition sites for acidic gas molecules. The chemiresistive sensor exhibits excellent HNO3 sensing performance at room temperature, delivering a high response of 925% toward 100 ppm of HNO3, low theoretical limit of detection of 235 ppb and limit of quantitation of 784 ppb, rapid response/recovery times of 13/8.8 s, as well as outstanding selectivity, humidity tolerance and cycling stability. Density functional theory calculations reveal that HNO3 are anchored on the cluster surface via cooperative dual-site adsorption involving an O–H···I hydrogen-bond-like interaction and an O···H–C interaction with the 4VP ligand. The cooperative adsorption mode induces interfacial charge redistribution, accompanied by electron transfer from the n-type cluster to HNO3 molecules, thereby modulating the electrical resistance. This work establishes a molecular-level relationship between ligand regulation, acidic gas recognition, and chemiresistive response, providing a rational strategy for cluster-based sensors for highly corrosive gas detection.

items.title:
Thia-Aza Pyridinophane
Chelators for Copper Coordination
and 64Cu Radiolabeling Studies
items.abstract: Abstract A new macrocyclic ligand, 3-thia-7-aza-1,5(2,6)-dipyridinacyclooctaphane, has been synthesized and functionalized to produce a family of nitrogen/sulfur–based chelators with tunable donor environments. Alkyl and picolyl derivatives were obtained through selective N-alkylation of the secondary amine site with methyl, isopropyl, and picolyl substituents, and a tridentate macrocyclic NNS analogue was also prepared by N-deletion. The coordination chemistry of these ligands toward Cu(II) and Cu(I) was investigated, and the copper complexes were characterized using X-ray crystallography, UV–vis, cyclic voltammetry (CV), EPR or NMR, and elemental analysis (EA). Acid dissociation constants and metal complex stability constants were determined by UV–Vis spectrophotometric titrations, providing insight into the ligands’ coordination ability. Radiolabeling with 64Cu revealed that while the isopropyl-functionalized complex exhibited moderate radiolabeling efficiency, the picolyl analogue achieved quantitative 64Cu incorporation, underscoring its potential for PET imaging applications.

items.title:
Interplay
between Sn(IV) N-Confused Porphyrin
Dianionic and Trianionic Forms Elucidated by Experiment and Theory
items.abstract: Abstract In this report, we present the formation and the X-ray crystal structure of the [SnIVNCP(3-)Py2](SnCl3) complex upon direct metalation of the H2NCP(2-) ligand (NCP = 5,10,15,20-tetraphenyl-N-confused porphyrin) with a large excess of SnCl2 in pyridine in dry anaerobic conditions. Reaction of this complex with dry and wet (NBu4)Cl results in the formation of the anionic [SnIVNCP(3-)Cl2]− and neutral SnIVNCP(2-)Cl2 complexes, respectively, indicating the ability to manipulate the electronic structure of the NCP ligand by stabilizing the external NH proton in part via the formation of a hydrogen bond. Similarly, reaction of the [SnIVNCP(3-)Py2]+ cation with (NBu4)OH or water results in the formation of [SnIVNCP(3-)(OH)2]− and SnIVNCP(2-)(OH)2 complexes, respectively. UV–vis-NIR and magnetic circular dichroism (MCD) spectroscopies are indicative of a significantly larger Qx-Qy energy gap for the NCP(2-) core compared to the NCP(3-) ionic form. Density Functional Theory (DFT) calculations confirm that a much smaller difference between ΔHOMO and ΔLUMO values for the NCP(2-) ligand (ΔHOMO is the energy gap between Gouterman’s “a1u” and “a2u” MOs, and ΔLUMO is the energy gap between Gouterman’s “eg(x)” and “eg(y)” MOs) is responsible for quenching of the magnetic orbital moment of the Qx-band in all NCP(2-)-containing complexes, reflected in MCD signal magnitudes. Time-Dependent DFT (TDDFT) calculations on all complexes correlate well with the experimental data and reveal specific spectroscopic signatures of the NCP(2-) and NCP(3-) systems as a function of the axial ligands and intermolecular hydrogen bond.

items.title:
Confinement Functionalization of Pd/UiO-66 for Steering
Non-Thermal Plasma Catalysis toward CO2 Deep Hydrogenation
to CH4
items.abstract: Abstract Nonthermal plasma (NTP) coupled with catalysts for the conversion of CO2/H2O into value-added chemicals presents an effective pathway for carbon resource recycling. However, when H2O is used as a sustainable hydrogen source, plasma-driven CO2 hydrogenation is largely limited by electron quenching and poor control over reaction depth, typically leading to CO as the dominant product. Herein, we report a confinement functionalization strategy for steering NTP-catalytic CO2/H2O conversion toward deep hydrogenation by dispersing Pd nanoparticles (Pd NPs) within the plasma-stable pores of UiO-66 and on its external surface. This material is applied for the first time in NTP catalytic CO2 hydrogenation using H2O as the hydrogen source. The optimized 2.5% Pd/UiO-66 catalyst delivers a CH4 selectivity of 52.45% and a CH4 formation rate of 2.82 mmol·g–1·h–1, which is 752.70 and 6.36 times higher than those of the plasma-only and pristine UiO-66 systems, respectively. Mechanistic studies reveal that confined Pd NPs not only promote the activation of CO2 and H2O-derived hydrogen species, but also enrich interfacial electrons and increase the surface collision probability of plasma-excited species, thereby facilitating *CO retention and subsequent hydrogenation toward CH4. This work provides a sustainable strategy for selective CO2 methanation using H2O as the hydrogen donor.

items.title:
Lanthanide
Grafting Modulates Radiative and Nonradiative
Energy Dissipation in a Defect-Rich In-MOF for Dual-Functional Luminescence
Sensing and Electromagnetic Wave Absorption
items.abstract: Abstract The dual threats of Cr(VI) water pollution and electromagnetic interference demand multifunctional materials integrating fluorescence sensing with electromagnetic wave absorption (EMA). Herein, Eu3+ and Tb3+ ions were postsynthetically anchored onto a defect-rich In-MOF to construct Eu@In-MOF and Tb@In-MOF with integrated luminescence sensing and microwave absorption functionalities. The characteristic f-f emissions of the lanthanide-functionalized frameworks arise from ligand-mediated sensitization and radiative transitions, while microwave attenuation is associated with dipolar/interfacial polarization, magnetic loss, and impedance matching. The composites exhibit selective fluorescence quenching toward Cr(VI), with detection limits of 7.56 ppb for CrO42– using Eu@In-MOF and 8.39 ppb using Tb@In-MOF. Mechanistic studies indicate that fluorescence quenching involves competitive light absorption and coordination-induced electronic perturbation, accompanied by static and dynamic quenching processes. In the X-band, Tb@In-MOF achieves a minimum reflection loss of −41.26 dB and an effective absorption bandwidth of 3.0 GHz. DFT calculations, together with spectroscopic and electrochemical characterization, reveal that lanthanide coordination regulates the local electronic environment and interfacial charge-transfer behavior of the framework, providing a structural basis for the enhanced polarization-related dielectric response. These results demonstrate that lanthanide coordination enables the coexistence of luminescence sensing and microwave attenuation within an In-MOF platform, providing a strategy for multifunctional MOF-based materials.

items.title:
Narrowing
the pH-Dependent HER Activity Gap via Synergistic
Heteronuclear Dual-Single-Atom Sites and Compressive Strain in Sub-1.6
nm High-Entropy Alloy Clusters
items.abstract: Abstract Developing electrocatalysts capable of narrowing the pH-dependent activity gap in hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) and revealing its mechanism remains a key challenge. Herein, we developed a facile and surfactant-free NaBH4 coreduction strategy for the rapid synthesis of sub-1.6 nm RuPtNiCuCo high-entropy alloy nanoclusters with a near-theoretical-maximum mixing entropy on presynthesized hollow nitrogen-doped carbon (RuPtNiCuCo-HEA/HNC). Detailed structural characterizations, combined with a series of in situ spectroscopic and isotopic experiments, collectively reveal that the ability of RuPtNiCuCo-HEA/HNC to narrow pH dependence originates from the synergistic effect between its heteronuclear Ru–Pt dual single-atom active sites and the compressive strain. This synergy promotes the formation of hydrogen-down water (OH2↓), accelerating interfacial water dissociation while balancing the adsorption and desorption of OH* and H* to enable rapid hydrogen release, thereby reducing the pH-dependent activity gap. Specifically, the RuPtNiCuCo-HEA/HNC exhibits low overpotentials (14, 27, and 9 mV at 10 mA cm–2) and delivers mass activities that are 8.11-, 3.54-, and 19.39-fold those of Pt/C in alkaline, neutral, and acidic electrolytes, respectively. Moreover, RuPtNiCuCo-HEA/HNC in an anion exchange membrane water electrolyzer (AEMWE) can operate continuously for over 260 h at 1 A cm–2, significantly outperforming RuPt/HNC and Pt/C.

items.title: Redox Behavior of Heme Embedded in Mycobacterium tuberculosis Bacterioferritin Protein Shell: Impact of Axial Ligands and Non-heme Iron
items.abstract: Abstract While higher organisms synthesize only heme-free ferritin, pathogenic bacteria such as Mycobacterium tuberculosis (Mtb) express both heme-bound and heme-free analogues. The synthesis of multiple types of ferritin in these bacteria and the roles of heme(s) and conserved axial Met52 in heme-bound bacterioferritin remain a mystery. Though the redox chemistry of heme embedded in bacterioferritin seems crucial, reports on its reduction potential (Em,7) are scarce. Here, the reduction potential and kinetics of heme reduction were obtained to understand its redox behavior in detail. A transient profile for heme reduction and subsequent reoxidation suggests the role of heme as an intrinsic electron relay station in Mtb bacterioferritin. Presence of O2 and non-heme iron impacts heme reduction and detection of transient reduced-heme species. Substitution of axial Met52 affects heme binding and reduction kinetics. Em,7 of heme in wild-type bacterioferritin was found to be unusually negative, which further decreased upon Met52 substitution or incorporation of non-heme iron. These findings, in conjunction with crystallographic analyses, explain the natural preference for Met52. This work establishes the direction of electron flow from reductants to the mineral core via heme and may explain the advantages that bacterioferritin provides to Mtb under limited iron/O2 levels in human macrophages and lungs to meet the iron requirements.

items.title: Enhancing Hole Utilization via PHI-NiO x p–n Heterojunctions for C–H Bond Activation
items.abstract: Abstract Efficient photocatalysis C–H bond activation under mild conditions remains a long-standing challenge due to the limited charge separation efficiency and insufficient utilization of photogenerated carriers. Herein, a poly(heptazine imide) (PHI) and NiOx p–n heterojunction (PHI-NiOx) is engineered to induce interfacial charge redistribution and construct a built-in electric field, enabling directional charge transfer and enhanced hole utilization. As a result, the optimized catalyst achieves efficient visible-light-driven oxidation of toluene to benzaldehyde, delivering a production rate of 1245 μmol g–1 h–1, which is 10 times higher than that of pristine PHI. Kinetic isotope effect and radical trapping experiments confirm that C–H bond cleavage is the rate-determining step and proceeds via a hole-dominated oxidation pathway. Mechanistic studies combining in situ spectroscopy and density functional theory calculations demonstrate that the heterojunction facilitates charge separation, accelerates interfacial charge transfer, and lowers the energy barrier of the key dehydrogenation step. This work highlights the critical role of interface engineering in modulating charge dynamics and reaction pathways, providing a versatile strategy for designing high-performance photocatalysts for selective organic transformations under mild conditions.

items.title:
Uranyl Chloride
Transformations under Atmospheric
Conditions
items.abstract: Abstract While the speciation of the uranyl cation (UO22+) in chloride solutions is fairly well understood, spectroscopic characterization and investigation of the analogous solid-phase species are lacking. We report here the transformation of solid uranyl chloride hydrate complexes in air starting from UO2Cl2(H2O); this transition is characterized by the formation of five successive solid phases: (UO2)4O2Cl4(H2O)6·4H2O, two polymorphs of UO2Cl2(H2O)3, (UO2)4O2Cl4(H2O)6·2H2O, and (UO2)2(OH)2Cl2(H2O)4. Each phase in this system produces distinct morphologies and unique spectroscopic signatures. Extensive hydrogen-bonding networks stabilize these complexes, which lead to sensitivity to atmospheric water and a deliquescent behavior that drives some phase transformations. Lengthening of the uranyl bond and bending of this structural unit as a result of coordination to μ2-OH and μ3-O hydrolytic bridging ligands are characterized using single-crystal X-ray diffraction, Raman spectroscopy, and density functional theory modeling with good agreement between techniques. A dimeric complex, (UO2)2(OH)2Cl2(H2O)4, represents the stable, terminal phase after months of aging in air, suggesting a structural stability of polynuclear uranyl chloride complexes over monomeric solids. Characterization of these compounds supports the identity of monomeric and polynuclear aqueous uranyl species through investigation of these molecular solid analogs with greater implications for environmental speciation of the uranyl cation.

items.title:
Two-Step Fabrication of PtCo Nanodendrites for Superior
Electrocatalytic Oxidation of Ethylene Glycol and Glycerol in an Alkaline
Electrolyte
items.abstract: Abstract Three-dimensional (3D) nanodendrites (NDs) have garnered significant attention for electrocatalytic oxidation due to their high surface area and abundant active sites. However, the controllable synthesis of these structures remains a challenge. Furthermore, the electrocatalytic oxidation of complex polyols, such as ethylene glycol and glycerol, is still inadequately explored in fuel cell applications. In this study, we present a controllable strategy for the stepwise synthesis of PtM (M = Co, Ni, Fe) NDs. The alloying of oxophilic metals with Pt not only reduces the amount of Pt required but also enhances catalytic performance through synergistic effects. Among them, PtCo NDs demonstrates remarkable mass activities of 10120 and 8051 mA mgPt–1 for ethylene glycol and glycerol oxidation reactions (EGOR and GOR), respectively. The corresponding specific activities are 12 and 9 mA cm–2. Meanwhile, PtCo NDs maintains mass activities of 3141 and 1025 mA mgPt–1 after 4000 s of chronoamperometric (CA) testing, outperforming PtNi NDs, PtFe NDs, Pt NDs, and commercial Pt/C catalysts. This study offers a promising strategy for the controlled synthesis of Pt-based bimetallic nanocatalysts aimed at enhancing polyol electrocatalysis efficiency.

items.title:
Interfacial
Ion Association Governs Selective and
Regenerable Samarium Recovery by a β-Diketonate Ionic
Liquid
items.abstract: Abstract Following chemical precipitation, naphthenic-acid extraction for deep Al removal can coextract substantial Sm, generating an Al-rich process stream for investigating selective lanthanide transfer. Here, we report a quaternary ammonium β-diketonate ionic liquid, [N1888][TTA], that selectively recovers Sm from simulated and industrial feeds. Extraction proceeds through ion association at a weakly solvated interface rather than classical ion exchange. At equilibrium, the organic-phase [N1888][TTA]/Sm molar ratio was 4:1; after six sequential contacts, the Sm loading reached 5.9 g·L–1 and the ratio decreased to approximately 3.5:1. Raman and UV–Vis titration show that SmL4 dominates under ligand excess, whereas higher metal loading promotes lower-ligand-number species. EXAFS fitting resolves two Sm–O contributions with effective coordination numbers of approximately 5.6 and 1.7, consistent with an eight-coordinate Sm center. Theoretical calculations and free-energy analysis further support the proposed extraction pathway. Compared with HTTA, [N1888][TTA] combines stronger Sm extraction with easier stripping. The regenerated extractant retained its extraction and separation performance over five cycles. Following sodium oxalate precipitation and calcination, an Sm2O3-rich oxide product was obtained from the real process feed in 85.6% yield. These results establish a molecular basis for linking ion association and Sm coordination speciation to reversible extraction and stripping in β-diketonate ionic liquid media.

items.title:
Bifunctional
Electrocatalyst (HER/UOR) Derived from
Keplerate-Type Polyoxometalate for Energy-Saving Hydrogen Production
items.abstract: Abstract The development of energy-saving hydrogen production technology coupled with the hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) and urea oxidation reaction (UOR) is critical for addressing the energy crisis and environmental contamination. Herein, we report a bimetallic electrocatalyst of Ni/Mo2C nanoparticles coated on N-doped carbon layers (Ni/Mo2C@NC), derived from a facile one-step pyrolysis of the precursor containing a Keplerate-type polyoxometalate (Mo153) and nickel acetate with dicyandiamide (DCA) as the carbon/nitrogen source. Ni/Mo2C@NC shows outstanding bifunctional electrocatalytic activity, requiring overpotentials of 161 and 192 mV to drive 10 mA cm–2 for HER in basic and acidic electrolytes, respectively, with the corresponding Tafel slopes of 86 and 84 mV dec–1. For UOR, a relatively low potential of 1.407 V is required to achieve 10 mA cm–2 with a Tafel slope of 46 mV dec–1. When employed in a two-electrode urea electrolysis cell, merely 1.458 V can drive 10 mA cm–2, substantially lower than that required for water splitting, including HER and OER. Moreover, Ni/Mo2C@NC demonstrates good, long-term durability exceeding 24 h for both HER and UOR. This work can provide design-assistant insights using POMs for energy-saving hydrogen production.

items.title:
Pressure-Induced
Phase Stability and Superconductivity
of Ruthenium Borides
items.abstract: Abstract Ruthenium borides have garnered significant attention due to their diverse configurations, intriguing electronic structures, and promising applications. By combining first-principles calculations with crystal-structure searches, we systematically investigate the Ru–B system over the pressure range of 0–400 GPa. The results show that RuB and RuB2 remain thermodynamically stable across the entire pressure range, whereas RuB3 is metastable at ambient pressure and becomes thermodynamically stable above approximately 100 GPa. Among the considered phases, P-6m2-RuB3 exhibits the highest calculated superconducting critical temperature (Tc) of 7.70 K at 0 GPa. Under compression, its Tc evolves nonmonotonically: it first decreases to 3.06 K at 180 GPa, then increases to 6.75 K at 200 GPa, and finally decreases to 4.45 K at 213.7 GPa. Above 213.7 GPa, P-6m2-RuB3 is predicted to transform into P21/m-RuB3, where Tc drops to 0.58 K and decreases further under compression, accompanied by weakened electron–phonon coupling and changes in Ru–B and B–B bonding. Finally, pressure–temperature phase diagrams for RuB, RuB2, and RuB3 are constructed within the quasiharmonic approximation. Increasing boron content promotes the formation of boron-rich frameworks, thereby enhancing structural stability, modifying the electronic structure, and tuning Tc. These findings provide guidance for the design of novel superconducting materials.

items.title:
Non-FCC Kernel
Geometry and Multicenter Bonding in
Au23(SR)17 Nanoclusters: Structural Isomerism
and Cohesion Descriptors for the Au Skeleton
items.abstract: Abstract Atomically precise structures provide molecular-level platforms for correlating metal-kernel geometry, ligand-shell topology, and electron delocalization in thiolate-protected gold nanoclusters. Here, Au23(SR)17 is used to examine structural isomerism and bonding descriptors associated with nonface-centered-cubic (non-FCC) Au-kernel geometry. Guided by the grand unified model and the ring model, five Au23(SR)17 isomers were constructed and compared with crystallographically determined Au23(SCTMS)17, denoted Au23–Iso1. All predicted structures are local minima with no imaginary harmonic frequencies. Among the predicted structures, Au23–Iso2 is lowest in energy, but remains 0.43 eV above Au23–Iso1 at the Perdew–Burke–Ernzerhof level. PBE0 and Tao–Perdew–Staroverov–Scuseria single-point calculations preserve the Au23–Iso1 &lt; Au23–Iso2 &lt; Au23–Iso3 order. The calculated ultraviolet–visible spectrum of Au23–Iso2 shows a broadly similar multiband profile to the reported spectra of unresolved Au23(SPh-tBu)17 and Au23(S-c-C6H11)17 clusters; however, the peak-deviation analysis does not favor Au23–Iso2 over the crystallographic Au23(SCTMS)17 spectral reference. Bonding and descriptor analyses identify a non-FCC kernel in Au23–Iso1, three clearly retained ADNDP-localized 4c–2e features and a threshold-sensitive fourth candidate, a distinct kernel–surface contact distribution, and the largest whole-skeleton cohesion descriptor in the selected isomer set.

items.title:
Thermochemistry
and Tunneling Enhance the PCET Reactivity
of Ni and Cu Complexes With Redox-Active Ligands
items.abstract: Abstract Herein, we report the synthesis, characterization, and reactivity of Cu-acetate and Ni-acetate complexes bound by tridentate redox-active ligands capable of reaching three molecular oxidation states. The reduced complexes ([XMOAc]2–) were characterized by single-crystal X-ray diffraction analysis, depicting metal-acetate cores stabilized by intramolecular H-bonding interactions. Cyclic voltammetry measurements indicate that [XMOAc]2– can be reversibly oxidized to [XMOAc]– and [XMOAc], and that the reduction potentials varied depending on the ligand substitution. The oxidation of [XMOAc]2– to [XMOAc]– and [XMOAc] was accomplished using 1 and 2 equiv of ferrocenium, respectively. The proton-coupled electron transfer reactivity of the oxidized complexes was analyzed in detail. Thermochemical analysis determined that the [XMOAc] species had higher affinities toward H atom equivalents than [XMOAc]–, and that the systems with electron-withdrawing groups were more prone to undergo reductive protonation. The kinetics for the reactions of [XMOAc]– and [XMOAc] with TEMPOH (1-hydroxy-2,2,6,6-tetramethylpiperidine) showed that the [XNiOAc]– complexes depict enhanced reaction rates. These findings contradict our thermochemical analysis (i.e., complexes with higher thermodynamic tendency to accept H atoms usually react faster) and are explained by tunneling effects. Further analysis of the PCET reactions provided further evidence that nonthermodynamic factors govern the PCET reactivity of the Ni-semiquinone oxidants.

items.title:
Investigation
into the Existence of Sr3Sn2S7 via
Exploratory Synthesis
items.abstract: Abstract During our investigation of A3B2Q7 compounds (A = Sr–Ba; B = Si–Sn; Q = O–Te), we solved the mystery of the Sr3Sn2S7 crystal structure. Although Sr3Sn2S7 shares the 3:2:7 stoichiometry with other compounds in the family, it crystallizes in a distinct, new centrosymmetric structure type. Sr3Sn2S7 adopts the monoclinic C2/m space group, with lattice parameters a = 23.207(2) Å, b = 7.9768(8) Å, c = 17.216(3) Å, β = 132.1738(17)°, and Z = 8, rather than the predicted Pbam space group. Unlike previously reported A3B2Q7 compounds, Sr3Sn2S7 is composed of rare SnS5 trigonal bipyramids as well as SnS4 tetrahedra, forming SnS4–SnS5 chains within the crystal structure. Density functional theory (DFT) calculations revealed that the new material is a semiconductor with a calculated band gap of 1.10 eV, while its red color is indicative of a larger gap of 1.8–2.0 eV.

items.title:
Contrasting
Biological Behavior of Deep Red Luminescent
Ru(II) and Ir(III) Complexes Bearing Phosphonium Pendants
items.abstract: Abstract Four luminescent complexes based upon heteroleptic complex formulas [Ru(bipy)2(L)]n+ or [Ir(tmq)2(L)]n+ (where bipy = 2,2′-bipyridine; tmq = 2,6,7-trimethyl-3-phenylquinoxaline) are reported. These complexes are functionalized via an ancillary 2-(2-pyridinyl)-4-quinolinecarboxamide ligand to incorporate either a pendant alcohol group (LOH) or a triphenylphosphonium cation (LTPP). All complexes were characterized using a range of spectroscopic and analytical techniques: multinuclear NMR, IR, UV–vis and luminescence spectroscopies, HRMS, and cyclic voltammetry. Photophysical studies describe the red phosphorescent nature of the complexes and show that the Ru(II) species are longer wavelength emitters (λem = 719 and 724 nm) compared to the Ir(III) species (λem = 641 and 643 nm); the Ru(II) complexes are weaker emitters in aerated solvent (ϕ &lt; 0.1%) compared to the Ir(III) species (ϕ = 3.5 and 3.9%). A range of biological studies were conducted on the complexes: antiproliferative activity, cyto- and photocytotoxicity assays, quantification of cell uptake, cell cycle and reactive oxygen species assays, cell imaging using confocal fluorescence microscopy and wound healing assays. The Ir(III) complexes reveal markedly enhanced antiproliferative and light-activated activity compared to the Ru(II) analogues, primarily driven by higher cellular uptake and efficient intracellular accumulation. Quantitative colocalization analysis confirmed enhanced mitochondrial targeting for [Ir(tmq)2(LTPP)]2+.

items.title: CdTe x S1– x Alloy Nanoplatelets with Decoupled Absorption and Emission
items.abstract: Abstract Achieving homogeneous CdTexS1–x alloy nanoplatelets (NPLs) remains a significant challenge owing to disparate chalcogen precursor reactivity and large anion size and orbital mismatch. In this study, homogeneous CdTexS1–x alloy NPLs with various compositions were synthesized by using chalcogen precursors with comparable incorporation kinetics. The resulting alloy NPLs exhibit an unusual optical response, where the excitonic absorption peak initially red-shifts upon sulfur incorporation and subsequently becomes pinned with increasing sulfur content, while photoluminescence red-shifts continuously. This behavior is in stark contrast to conventional CdSexS1–x alloy NPLs, where both absorption and emission progressively blue-shift with increasing sulfur incorporation. The decoupled absorption and emission behavior was found to arise from Te-dominated valence-band pinning, while alloying-induced carrier localization further enhanced photoluminescence efficiency and prolonged exciton lifetimes. This work provides new insights into unconventional band-edge evolution in low-dimensional semiconductor alloys.

items.title:
Mixed Thiolate/Alkoxide
Antimony Cages for Reversed-Bilayer
Vesicle Self-Assembly and Dye Protection in Organic Media
items.abstract: Abstract A new two-step synthesis produces moisture-stable antimony and arsenic dithiothreitol cages. Single crystal analysis reveals that the Sb compounds self-assemble into reversed bilayers in the solid state. Together with DLS, TEM, fluorescence microscopy, encapsulation studies, and spectroscopic measurements, these results are consistent with pnictogen-bond-directed vesicle formation in organic media. The Sb assemblies more efficiently encapsulate and protect rhodamine B than the arsenic analogue or a topological mimic that lacks pnictogen-bonding capability. This work provides a synthetically accessible tool for partitioning organic media to allow for orthogonal reactivity.

items.title:
Halogen-Driven
Tetrahedral Distortion Enables Tunable
White-Light Emission and Scintillation Properties in Hybrid Zinc Halides
items.abstract: Abstract Organic–inorganic hybrid zinc halides have emerged as promising luminescent materials for solid-state lighting and radiation detection owing to their facile synthesis, tunable crystal structures, and rich photophysical behaviors. Herein, we report two hybrid zinc halides, (C5H14N2)ZnCl4·0.5H2O (Cl4) and (C5H14N2)ZnBr4·H2O (Br4), wherein halogen substitution from Cl– to Br– successfully achieves tunable white-light emission with color coordinates of (0.23, 0.25) for Cl4 and (0.26, 0.29) for Br4, originating from the synergistic contribution of singlet and triplet excited states. Benefiting from the favorable crystal-field environment of the bromide host, Mn2+ ions are further introduced into the Br4 lattice via an N-ion-doping strategy. The incorporated Mn2+ activators endow Br4 with prominent radioluminescence under X-ray excitation, and the optimized Br4:0.6Mn2+ exhibits a light yield of 16900 photons/MeV and a detection limit of 1.28 μGyair/s. Further, a spatial resolution of 7.6 Lp/mm is achieved in X-ray imaging based on the flexible Br4:0.6Mn2+@PDMS films. This work establishes a straightforward anion engineering strategy to simultaneously realize white photoluminescence and efficient X-ray scintillation within a single hybrid zinc halide system, providing a facile route toward multifunctional luminescent materials for white-light illumination and high-performance X-ray imaging.

items.title:
A Supramolecular
Symmetry-Breaking Strategy for Enhanced
Circularly Polarized Luminescence, High-Temperature Phase Transition,
and Piezoelectric Response in Chiral Manganese(II) Halides
items.abstract: Abstract Circularly polarized luminescence (CPL) has attracted intense interest for applications in 3D displays, optical data storage, and quantum information processing. Chiral organic–inorganic hybrid metal halides (HOMHs) have emerged as promising CPL materials owing to their structural tunability, facile solution processability, and tunable photoluminescence, yet they often suffer from small luminescence dissymmetry factors (glum) and limited functionality. Herein, we report a pair of enantiomeric host–guest compounds, [18-crown-6]2[(R/S)-C3H12N2][MnCl4] (R-Mn and S-Mn; (R/S)-C3H12N2 = (R/S)-propane-1,2-diammonium), via a supramolecular assembly strategy. The resulting two-in-one structures feature strong N–H···O hydrogen bonds that lock the chiral cations and reduce the crystal symmetry from the C2 phase of the previously reported compound without 18-crown-6 to the lowest-symmetry P1 space group. R/S-Mn exhibits CPL with |glum| = 2.6 × 10–2, more than 10 times higher than the previously reported value of 2 × 10–3. Moreover, both compounds display a reversible high-temperature solid–solid phase transition at 405 K and a measurable piezoelectric coefficient of 11 pC/N. DFT calculations reveal that the band edges and emissive states are dominated by the [MnCl4]2– units. Meanwhile, the organic cations do not contribute to the electronic transitions, indicating that the CPL arises from the chiral environment of the two-in-one supramolecular cations surrounding these nonchiral emissive centers. This work demonstrates supramolecular symmetry breaking as an effective design principle for integrating enhanced CPL, thermal responsiveness, and piezoelectricity into a single multifunctional chiral hybrid metal halide system.

items.title:
Vacancy-Mediated
Oxide-Ion Conduction in the Palmierite-like
Layers of Ba6Nb2Na2V2O17
items.abstract: Abstract Various hexagonal perovskite derivatives have recently been demonstrated to exhibit high oxide ion conductivity, with their conductivity properties repeatedly being linked to palmierite-like (P-L) structural layers. Here, we report an investigation into the crystal structure and electrical properties of the hexagonal perovskite derivative Ba6Nb2Na2V2O17. Ba6Nb2Na2V2O17 exhibits oxide ion conductivity, with a total conductivity of 1.8 × 10–6 S cm–1 at 650 °C under an atmosphere of flowing dry N2. Unlike other oxide ion conducting hexagonal perovskite derivatives, Ba6Nb2Na2V2O17 is shown not to feature interstitial oxygen, mixed coordination polyhedra, or isolated polyhedra. Regardless, oxide ion conductivity is still enabled by the P-L structural motif. These results hence further emphasize the utility and versatility of P-L layers in the context of ionic conductivity. Our atomistic modeling reveals a distinct vacancy-mediated oxide-ion conduction pathway, predominantly involving the O1 and O2 sites of the P-L layer.

items.title:
Construction
of Insensitive Energetic Coordination
Complexes as Promising Combustion Promoters for Ammonium Perchlorate
items.abstract: Abstract Herein, a novel energetic ligand, ammonium 2-cyano-2-nitroacetamide (ANCA), was synthesized. Based on this ligand, five new energetic coordination complexes (ECCs-1 to ECCs-5) were prepared using Li+, Na+, K+, Rb+, and Cs+ as the respective metal centers. The crystal structures, thermal stabilities, mechanical sensitivities, and catalytic activities toward the thermal decomposition of AP were systematically investigated. The densities of these complexes range from 1.573 to 2.643 g·cm–3, increasing with the atomic number of the metal center. All complexes exhibit excellent thermal stability, with decomposition temperatures ranging from 237 to 253 °C, and are insensitive to mechanical stimuli, with impact sensitivities exceeding 40 J and friction sensitivities exceeding 360 N. Notably, ECCs-3 demonstrated the best catalytic performance toward the thermal decomposition of AP, reducing the high-temperature decomposition peak temperature by 129 °C. Ignition tests further confirmed that the ECCs-3, ECCs-4, and ECCs-5 formulations exhibited excellent combustion behavior, with ECCs-5 producing the brightest flame. These results indicate that the as-prepared insensitive energetic coordination complexes are promising multifunctional combustion promoters for solid propellants.

items.title:
Photoactive
Heterometallic Assemblies Based on Dinuclear
Clathrochelate Metalloligands and a ZnII–Porphyrin/RuII–Metallacycle
items.abstract: Abstract A modular self-assembly strategy combining a RuII-metallacycle of ZnII-porphyrins with three different dinuclear boron-capped clathrochelate metalloligands bearing two hexacoordinate metal ions in the center (either ZnII/ZnII or mixed-valence FeII/FeIII cores) affords a new family of discrete photoactive heterometallic sandwich-like assemblies. The assemblies are formed quantitatively in solution and fully characterized by UV–Vis, IR, and NMR spectroscopy, DOSY, and single-crystal X-ray diffraction. The nature of the intercomponent photoinduced process depends critically on the identity of the clathrochelate connector: in the ZnII/ZnII-containing assembly, excitation of the clathrochelate unit results in quantitative energy transfer to the ZnII-porphyrin platform; in the FeII/FeIII-containing assembly, the ZnII-porphyrin singlet excited state is completely quenched by the mixed-valence iron core. These results demonstrate that the photoinduced intercomponent process can be switched simply by varying the metal identity within the clathrochelate connector, while retaining the same overall supramolecular architecture, offering a new design principle for photoactive multicomponent inorganic assemblies.

items.title:
XBe6Au62+ (X = Si,
Ge): Electron-Sharing Covalently Bonded Planar Hexacoordinate Silicon
and Germanium Atoms
items.abstract: Abstract Examples of planar hexacoordinate molecular systems are scarce in the literature, particularly for the covalently bonded planar hexacoordinate group 14 elements. In the previously reported such systems, three bonds were covalent in nature, and the remaining three bonds were predominantly supported by electrostatic interactions. Here, we report that the global minimum of the 20-valence electronic XBe6Au62+ (X = Si, Ge) clusters has a D6h-symmetric star-like structure featuring planar hexacoordinate silicon and germanium (phX) atoms, which are strongly covalently bonded to the Be6 ring through three σ and one π-electron-sharing bonds. Additionally, electrostatic interactions also contribute considerably to the stabilization of the phX clusters. These clusters show high stability against dissociation and kinetic stability against distortion from planarity. The stability of phX species can be attributed to the electronic stabilization (2π + 6σ double aromaticity) and the optimal geometrical match between the planar X center and the peripheral Be6Au6 ring, making them promising candidates for experimental realization. We have further explored the possibility of blocking the reactivity of phX by [10]cycloparaphenylenes ([10]CPP), forming a viable host–guest complex while maintaining the novel electronic and structural integrity of phX motifs.

items.title:
Near-Infrared
Photothermally Enhanced Oxidation of
Amines by Modified MXene Composites
items.abstract: Abstract MXenes are two-dimensional nanomaterials with strong near-infrared (NIR) absorption and high photothermal conversion capability. However, their catalytic applications in the NIR region have been constrained by insufficient catalytic activity and the intrinsically low photon energy in this spectral range. To break this bottleneck, (3-aminopropyl)triethoxysilane is used to covalently modify titanium carbide MXene (Ti3C2TX) to obtain aminated NH2–Ti3C2, which is further electrostatically assembled with catalytically active transition-metal-substituted Keggin-type polyoxometalates (POMs), affording POMs@NH2–Ti3C2 composites. Under NIR irradiation, these catalysts generate the localized photothermal effect around the catalytic centers, efficiently driving the oxidation of tetrahydroquinoline derivatives. The precise synergy between photothermal and catalytic centers enables near-unity product selectivity, suppressing byproduct formation and thus minimizing organic solvent waste. Under photothermal conditions, the system achieves a turnover frequency as high as 154.3 h–1, far surpassing that of conventional external heating at the same temperature and outperforming most non-noble-metal and even noble-metal catalysts. This work not only expands the photothermal applications of POM-based composites but also demonstrates a feasible strategy for driving green catalytic transformations using light as a remote heat source, offering new insights into the synergistic development of energy-input saving and separation-process minimization for fine chemical synthesis.

items.title: Rational Design of Tridentate NNN Zn(II) Catalysts: Ligand-Assisted Synthesis of Trisubstituted s -Triazines via Dehydrogenative Coupling of Primary Alcohols with Amidines and Biguanides
items.abstract: Abstract s-Triazines are important N-heterocycles used in pharmaceuticals, sensors, and optoelectronic devices, but their synthesis typically relies on prefunctionalized substrates and harsh conditions. In this study, we synthesized a series of well-characterized zinc complexes, confirmed by various spectroscopic methods, which serve as catalysts for the dehydrogenative coupling of alcohols with amidines and biguanides to produce 2,4,6-trisubstituted s-triazines. This eco-friendly catalytic method offers a sustainable route to s-triazines, with H2, H2O, and NH3 as the main small-molecule byproducts and eliminates the need for stoichiometric oxidants. The technique has been successfully tested with 77 substrates, including both aliphatic and aromatic primary alcohols, amidines, and biguanides. Additionally, the synthesis of several functional triazines featuring fluorescent dyes, organic linkers, and bioactive molecules demonstrates the efficiency of our catalytic system. Mechanistic investigations supported by DFT studies suggest that the catalyst functions via a metal–ligand cooperative mechanism, involving reversible aromatic and nonaromatic states of the pyridyl-hydrazone backbone, substrate activation, hydrogen transfer, and stabilization of key intermediates, with the ligand playing a crucial role in bond formation.

items.title:
Neutron Diffraction
Directly Locates an Interstitial
Hydride in a Ni–Ag Superatomic Nanocluster
items.abstract: Abstract Interstitial hydrides can modulate the electronic and geometric structures of atomically precise metal nanoclusters (NCs). Direct crystallographic localization of hydrides in heavy-metal nanoclusters remains challenging by single-crystal X-ray diffraction (SCXRD). Here, dithiophosphate-to-diselenophosphate ligand exchange produced [Ni(H)Ag19{Se2P(OiPr)2}12] (1x) and [NiAg20{Se2P(OiPr)2}12] (2). The ligand exchange enabled the growth of high-quality single crystals suitable for neutron diffraction. The neutron structure of 1x (1o) directly locates the hydride in an interstitial μ4-NiAg3 cavity, providing the first direct neutron-crystallographic localization of a Ni–H motif in a superatomic nanocluster. The result supports the metallic-hydrogen description for a first-row-transition-metal-centered superatom. Comparison with the hydride-free analogue shows hydride-induced distortion and expansion of the Ag12 core together with changes in optical response. These findings provide an experimental structural benchmark for Ni-centered hydride superatoms and establish neutron diffraction as a direct probe of interstitial hydrogen in heavy-metal nanoclusters.

items.title:
Alkyne Cyclotrimerization
Catalyzed by Bimetallic
Fe(II) Complexes with Low-Basicity Urea-Derived Ligands
items.abstract: Abstract Catalytic cyclotrimerization of alkynes by iron complexes would be an important reaction for the preparation of useful building blocks. It would be important to broaden the ligand scope, but the reactions can be catalyzed only when a lower-valent Fe(0) or Fe(I) is used or when Fe(II) is coordinated to strongly basic ligands. Here, we describe how bimetallic Fe(II) complexes with urea-derived ligands can catalyze the cyclotrimerization of alkyne despite the relatively lower basicity. Treatment of H2NMe2[NNNN] with a half-equivalent of {FeMes2}2 formed a bimetallic Fe(II) complex, {NMe2[NNNN]Fe}2 (Fe1), and the catalytic cyclotrimerization of phenylacetylene was achieved under mild conditions. The reaction exhibited an approximately half-order dependence on Fe1 and an apparent substrate order of ca. 1.5 under initial-rate conditions, although deviations from a simple 1.5-order rate law were observed. The Eyring plot exhibited a moderately negative ΔS‡ = −7.82 cal/mol·K, while the negative slope in the Hammett analysis implicated the electron-deficient transition state. The combined kinetic studies are consistent with the formation of a monomeric active species prior to the rate-determining step. Finally, both reaction rates and isomer ratios improved when the substituents were replaced with more donating, sterically bulkier Et or nPr groups, {NEt2[NNNN]Fe}2 (Fe2) and {NnPr2[NNNN]Fe}2 (Fe3). Overall, this study demonstrates how Fe(II) complexes with lower-basicity ligands successfully catalyze alkyne cyclotrimerization reactions and can control the isomer ratios.

items.title:
Pyrazinephosphonate-Bridged Dysprosium(III) Cyclic
Coordination Clusters
items.abstract: Abstract Noncentered paramagnetic metal rings are widely regarded as ideal prototypes for exploring one-dimensional magnetic systems. Herein, we report the synthesis of three giant hollow hexagons, Dy6, Dy24a, and Dy24b. Dy6 hexagon is assembled from a single pyrazinyl hydrazone ligand, without ring-expanding agents. The coalescence of the pyrazinephosphonate and C2-symmetric di-o-vanilloyl hydrazones enables access to two hexagonal nuts, Dy24a and Dy24b, with large cavities, in which six hydrazone ligands capture 18 DyIII ions to construct the outer hexagons, while the pyrazinephosphonate ring-expanding agents fix the inner hexagons, enabling high metal center density. Replacing the key pyridyl group of the hydrazone ligand with a pyrazinyl group transforms Dy24a into Dy24b. The structural changes substantially influence the zero-field single-molecule magnet behavior. This work demonstrates the feasibility of building giant noncentered paramagnetic metal rings and precisely tuning their size and shape, thereby paving new avenues for the design and synthesis of advanced materials.

items.title:
Metal-Node Engineering Enables Tunable Photocatalytic
Benzylamine Oxidation Coupled with H2 Production in MOFs
items.abstract: Abstract The precise modulation of the electronic structure in bimetallic metal–organic frameworks (BMOFs), achieved by altering their metal nodes, critically governs their photocatalytic performance. However, how altering the metal nodes in BMOFs regulates the inherent structure–performance relationship remains unclear. Here, a series of CoM-HHTP with similar crystal structures (M = Ni, Cu, and Fe; HHTP = 2,3,6,7,10,11-hexahydroxytriphenylene) were integrated with CdS nanorods, yielding CdS@CoM-HHTP heterojunctions, which exhibited tunable performance in photocatalytic benzylamine coupling and hydrogen evolution. Among them, CdS@Co0.75Fe0.25-HHTP exhibits the best catalytic performance, with a hydrogen evolution rate of 55.29 mmol g–1 h–1 and a benzylamine conversion rate of 63.76%. The experimental results show that substitution of the second metal (M = Ni, Cu, and Fe) effectively modulates the electronic configuration of Co and significantly regulates the ability of BMOFs to extract photogenerated electrons from CdS, thereby enabling tunable photocatalytic activity. This study substantiates that modulation of the secondary metal node is pivotal for achieving synergistic regulation of both the active-site electronic structure and the photocatalytic performance.

items.title:
Photolytic
Release of CS2 from Bis(trityl)trithiocarbonate
Using Green Light
items.abstract: Abstract Reaction of Ph3CSH with 1 equiv of Na{N(SiMe3)2} in THF, followed by addition of excess CS2 and 1.2 equiv of 18-crown-6, results in formation of the mono(trityl) trithiocarbonate, [Na(18-crown-6)(THF)2][Ph3CSCS2] (1a), which was isolated in high yield after workup. Reaction of 1a with 1 equiv of Ph3CCl in pyridine results in formation of the bis(trityl) trithiocarbonate, Ph3CSC(S)SCPh3 (2). Compounds 1a and 2 were characterized by NMR spectroscopy and X-ray-crystallography, and their ultraviolet–visible (UV–vis) spectra were simulated with TD-DFT calculations. Photolysis of 2 using a green LED lightstrip for 6 h results in formation of CS2, Ph3CSSCPh3, Ph3CH, and 9-phenyl-fluorene as the major products. CS2 is formed in 85% yield in this reaction. For comparison, we also evaluated the CS2-releasing properties of bis(benzyl) trithiocarbonate, PhCH2SC(S)SCH2Ph (3). Photolysis of 3 in CD2Cl2 for 26 h, using a medium-pressure Hg lamp, results in formation of CS2 in 50% yield. Also formed in the reaction are toluene, bibenzyl, PhCH2SCH2Ph, PhCH2SSCH2Ph, PhCH2SH, and PhCH2SCH2SCH2Ph, along with a large number of unidentified products. The identities of the major products were confirmed by comparison of the reaction mixture spectra with the 1H and 13C{1H} NMR spectra of authentic materials. We attribute the lower CS2 yield of 3 vs 2 to the lower stability of the benzyl radical vs the trityl radical, highlighting the importance of stable radical formation in the photo-uncaging of molecular cargo.

items.title:
Tuning Hydrogen
Evolution Pathways through Ligand
Design and Proton Sources for Mixed-Ligand Cobalt(II) Catalysts
items.abstract: Abstract In the pursuit of an effective molecular catalyst for electrocatalytic proton reduction, herein, we have reported two mixed-ligand-based cobalt(II) complexes, namely, [Co(L)(Bpy)Cl](ClO4) (1) and [Co(L)(dmBpy)Cl](ClO4) (2) (where L = 4-methoxy-N-((1-methyl-1H-benzo[d]imidazol-2-yl)methyl)-N-(pyridin-2-ylmethyl)aniline, Bpy = 2,2/-bipyridine, and dmBpy = 4,4/-dimethyl-2,2/-bipyridyl). Both complexes are well characterized using different spectroscopic and analytical techniques, including single-crystal X-ray diffraction for structure elucidation. The introduction of two methyl groups into complex 2 was aimed at elucidating the electronic effects of these substituents on the electrochemical properties of the complex and determining their impact on its electrocatalytic hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) performance. The electrocatalytic HER studies were performed using acetic acid and trifluoroacetic acid (TFA) as weak and strong proton sources, respectively, in an acetonitrile medium. The mechanism has been drawn based on experimental observations and the reported literature. This study shows the effect of the strength of two proton sources along with the electronic effect of ligands on the mechanism being followed by them. The involvement of cobalt hydride was confirmed by the electrochemical reduction of styrene to ethylbenzene. Postcatalytic studies confirmed the molecular integrity of both complexes, confirming the homogeneous nature of the catalysts.

items.title:
A 3D POM-Based
Supramolecular Framework Hosting a
Hexahedral Cage via Hydrogen Bonds for Room-Temperature Oxidative
Desulfurization
items.abstract: Abstract To address the environmental challenges posed by sulfur-containing emissions, the development of efficient catalysts for oxidative desulfurization is highly desirable. Herein, a new [β-Mo8O26]4–-based Co-complex, {[Co(4-pbba)(H2O)5]2(β-Mo8O26)(4-pbba)}·6H2O (Mo8-pbba-Co, 4-H2pbbaBr2 = 1,1′-(1,4-phenylene-bis(methylene))-bis (pyridine-4-carboxylic-acid)dibromo), was obtained by a hydrothermal reaction of Na2MoO4·2H2O, Co(OAc)2·4H2O and 4-H2pbbaBr2. Mo8-pbba-Co represents the first 6-connected 3D polyoxometalate (POM)-based supramolecular framework constructed from [Co(4-pbba)(H2O)5] units and [β-Mo8O26]4– clusters, featuring unique centrosymmetric hexahedral cage-like units {O2(OW)6} formed via hydrogen-bonding interactions. Mo8-pbba-Co exhibits remarkable catalytic activity for oxidative desulfurization at room temperature using H2O2 as an oxidant, achieving 99% conversion and 99% selectivity for CEES in just 6 min, and 98% conversion and 97% selectivity for MPS within 45 min. Mechanistic investigations elucidate a synergistic catalytic effect between the [β-Mo8O26]4– cluster and Co2+ sites, where hydroxyl radicals (•OH) are identified as the key reactive oxygen species. Furthermore, Mo8-pbba-Co demonstrates outstanding recyclability, offering a promising pathway for the development of efficient desulfurization catalysts under mild conditions.

items.title:
The ELEFANT Concept for Extended Low-X-ray-Contrast
Electron-Precise Frameworks with Adaptive Noradamantane-Like Topologies
items.abstract: Abstract A persistent structural challenge in ternary Ge/As compounds is that X-ray crystallography cannot reliably distinguish germanium and arsenic due to their near-identical electron counts, complicating site assignments and composition determination. We developed a systematic approach linking composition, valence electron count, and structural connectivity to arrive at chemically meaningful structure descriptions, demonstrated here by 11 new compounds: AxGe8+xAs16–x (A = Na, K, Rb), Rb1.7Ge2.7As3.3, NaGe3As3, Na2Ge3As3, Na6Ga6Ge6As12, K0.6Ge2.6P3.4, Rb0.7Ge2.7P2.3, NaSi3As3, and Na2Ge7As7. We introduce the ELEFANT concept (Extended Low-X-ray-contrast Electron-precise Frameworks with Adaptive Noradamantane-like Topology) to describe A–(Tr)–Tt–Pn compounds containing noradamantane-like substructures. All structures share a common (5)+1-ring motif, enabling calculation of the valence electrons per 12 framework atoms (VE/12FA) and the bond-to-lone-pair ratio (B/LP). These parameters define structure groups, reveal electronic boundaries, and constrain framework connectivity. DFT calculations predict semiconducting behavior for all compounds, consistent with transport and impedance measurements. By connecting stoichiometry, bonding, and topology, ELEFANT provides a unified framework for understanding, validating, and modifying A–Tt–Pn semiconductors through controlled substitution of chemically similar elements such as Ga, Ge, and As.

items.title:
Phosphide-Mediated
Hydrogen Evolution by a Well-Defined
Molecular Model for Amorphous Cobalt Phosphide Surfaces
items.abstract: Abstract Cobalt phosphide is a promising non-noble metal electrocatalyst for the electrocatalytic production of hydrogen gas, although the mechanism by which it operates at its amorphized surfaces is not well understood. In this work, we report a highly stable cobalt phosphide cluster, Co3(μ3-P)(CO)6(CNArDipp2)3 (ArDipp2 = 2,6-(2,6-(iPr)2C6H3)2C6H3), which is a competent catalyst for electrocatalytic hydrogen evolution (HER) under acidic conditions and serves as a functional model system for amorphous cobalt phosphide surfaces. The active catalyst was identified as being the protonated cluster [Co3(μ3-PH)(CO)6(CNArDipp2)3]+, which was isolated and fully characterized. Additionally, P-functionalized derivatives were found to have impeded or absent catalytic activity, implicating the phosphide atom as playing a crucial role in the catalytic mechanism. This work suggests that the phosphide anions on heterogeneous cobalt phosphide surfaces serve as important mediators of proton delivery, analogous to the well-established importance of Lewis basic moieties in molecular and biological hydrogen evolution catalysts.

items.title:
Dual Lanthanide
(Eu–Tb) Doped 2D MOFs with
Tunable Multicolor Emission for Fluorescence Sensing
items.abstract: Abstract Due to their unique luminescence properties, long lifetimes, and large Stokes shifts, lanthanide metal ions (Ln3+) serve as an important metal source for the construction of fluorescent MOFs. In this study, two isostructural two-dimensional lanthanide metal–organic frameworks, CUST-528 and CUST-529, were reported. Under solvothermal conditions, these frameworks were successfully synthesized using the ligands 2,4,6-tri(2-pyridinyl)-1,3,5-triazine (TPTZ) and 2-bromoterephthalic acid (2-BrTA), along with Eu(NO3)3·6H2O and Tb(NO3)3·6H2O. The PXRD patterns indicated that CUST-528 and CUST-529 maintained their crystalline structure and exhibited good stability in an aqueous environment for 10 days. In the fluorescence sensing experiments, the two crystals exhibited good detection capability, selectivity, and sensitivity toward NOR, Fe3+, Cr2O72–, and TNP, respectively. By adjusting the mass ratio of Eu3+ to Tb3+, a series of dual-lanthanide emissive EuxTb1–x-MOF materials were successfully developed. Eu0.6Tb0.4-MOF was further applied to ratiometric and hydrogel-based visual sensing of norfloxacin. During the detection process, a systematic investigation of the possible mechanisms of fluorescence quenching was conducted.

items.title: Issue Editorial Masthead
Issue Publication Information

Super-Rapid
Dissemination of the Fundamentals of Inorganic
Chemistry: “Synthesis Notes”

Quasicrystal
Formation, Composition, and Stability
in the Yb–Au–Sn and Yb–Au–Al Systems:
A Comparative Study
items.abstract: Abstract Yb-based icosahedral quasicrystals (iQCs) can exhibit intermediate-valence behavior. Here, we revisit the Yb–Au–Sn and Yb–Au–Al systems, which host iQCs with average Yb valences of approximately 2.18 and 2.8, respectively. Particular emphasis was placed on the formation conditions, compositions, thermodynamic stability, and relationship to related periodic approximant crystals (ACs). i-YbAuSn, Yb13.6Au64.8Sn21.6, can only be obtained by solution growth from melts containing 4–6 at. % Yb and melts incongruently at ∼510 °C to form the 2/1 AC Yb14.2Au63.5Sn22.3. In contrast, i-YbAuAl, Yb15.8Au53.5Al30.7, is accessible only as a metastable phase by arc melting Yb-rich compositions (∼17 at. % Yb). The phase remains kinetically stable up to ∼400 °C. The 1/1 AC YbAuAl melts congruently and occurs in two structural variants: Yb13.6Au56.2Al30.2, featuring an (Au,Al)4 tetrahedron at the center of the Tsai-cluster building unit, and Yb14.0Au54.7Al31.11, in which the central tetrahedron is partially (∼10%) replaced by a single Yb atom. It is proposed that thermodynamically stable Yb-based iQCs (such as i-YbAuSn, i-YbAgIn, and i-YbCd) are characterized by a low Yb average valence (close to 2). In contrast, iQCs in which Yb exhibits a substantially higher average valence (&gt;2.4), such as i-YbAuAl, appear to be metastable.

items.title:
Site-Selective
Cation–Anion Cosubstitution
Rewires Na+ Transport in NASICON-Type Na3V2(PO4)2F3 Cathodes
items.abstract: Abstract NASICON-type Na3V2(PO4)2F3 is a promising cathode for sodium-ion batteries owing to its robust three-dimensional framework and high operating voltage. However, the strong Coulombic attraction imposed by the highly electronegative F– ions suspended above and below the diffusion channels, together with the ordered arrangement of Na+ ions, severely restricts the mobility of Na+. Herein, we propose a trace cation–anion cosubstitution strategy by introducing Li+ into Na+ sites and substituting Cl– for F– to synergistically regulate the local diffusion environment. The large-radius Cl– doping expands the lattice and widens the diffusion channel, while the Li+ ions act as a “pillar” to reinforce the framework. Meanwhile, such cosubstitution reduces the electrostatic attraction between pendant F– and Na+ and disrupts the ordered Na+ arrangement, thereby constructing favorable pathways for Na+. The optimized cathode exhibits reduced polarization and improved kinetics, delivering a high reversible capacity of 125.1 mAh g–1 at 0.1C, an excellent rate capability of 97.1 mAh g–1 at 15C, and 90.1% capacity retention after 1000 cycles. Density functional theory (DFT) calculations confirm the reconstructed electrostatic environment and favorable Na+ transport pathways. This work offers a new paradigm for enhancing the reaction kinetics of polyanionic cathodes.

items.title:
Low-Alloying
Entropy Engineering Stabilizes Cubic
GeSe for Enhanced Thermoelectric Performance
items.abstract: Abstract The thermoelectric potential of orthorhombic GeSe is markedly constrained by its pronounced intrinsic covalent bonding alongside low structural symmetry. Here, we report a high-entropy alloying strategy using AgSnSbTe3 to activate the latent thermoelectric potential of GeSe by stabilizing a high-symmetry cubic phase. Incorporating a minimal fraction of AgSnSbTe3 triggers a lattice phase transformation from orthorhombic GeSe, which features covalent bonding, to a cubic structure governed by metavalent bonding. Compared with conventional I–V–VI2 alloying approaches that typically require high dopant concentrations, the high-entropy AgSnSbTe3 enables efficient phase engineering at significantly lower composition levels. The elevated configurational entropy markedly expands the solid solubility of constituent elements, inhibits phase segregation, and promotes the persistence of a uniform, single-phase cubic solid solution across a broad temperature range. The stabilized cubic GeSe exhibits significantly weakened chemical bonding, reduced cation vacancy formation energy, enhanced band degeneracy, increased lattice anharmonicity, and multiscale defect structures, which together allow electrical and thermal transport properties to be optimized synergistically. As a result, (GeSe)0.75(AgSnSbTe3)0.25 achieves a peak zT of 0.92 at 723 K, representing a substantial improvement over pristine GeSe. This work demonstrates that entropy-driven alloying with AgSnSbTe3 provides an effective and general strategy to stabilize high-symmetry cubic phases and boost thermoelectric performance in low-symmetry chalcogenide systems.

items.title: Topochemical Conversion of Ti3AlC2 to Ti3C2T x MXene via Kinetically Accelerated Microwave Etching and Targeted Byproduct Purification
items.abstract: Abstract Achieving high synthesis throughput without sacrificing the structural integrity of two-dimensional (2D) Ti3C2Tx MXenes remains a primary challenge, as conventional minimally intensive layer delamination (MILD) requires prolonged etching (∼24 h) that induces surface degradation and nonstructural carbon defects. Herein, we demonstrate a rapid microwave-assisted (MW) etching strategy combined with targeted sulfuric acid (H2SO4) byproduct purification to produce highly crystalline Ti3C2Tx MXenes within 1 h of total process time (120 °C MW etching for 30 min; 100 °C H2SO4 washing for 30 min). Avrami-Erofe’ev kinetic modeling reveals that MW irradiation reduces the apparent activation energy (Ea) to 25.51 ± 0.73 kJ mol–1 (R2 = 0.9976)─approximately 54% lower than the conventional HF etching benchmark (55.2 kJ mol–1)─significantly accelerating topochemical conversion. X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) and energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDS) confirm that this accelerated kinetic regime effectively suppresses acidic overetching, yielding a lower relative C–C defect ratio (47.25%) while fully preserving the Ti–C framework. Furthermore, postpurification with 3 M H2SO4 completely removes insoluble crystalline Li3AlF6 byproducts. The resulting predominantly single- to few-layer delaminated MXene nanosheets assemble into flexible freestanding films with an outstanding electrical conductivity of 2.64 × 103 S cm–1. This work establishes a scalable kinetic pathway for high-speed, defect-minimized manufacturing of 2D MXenes.

items.title: Anion-Exchange Strategy for the Optimization of Cu2MnS2-xSe x Nanostructures toward Bifunctional Electrocatalysis in Alkaline Water Splitting
items.abstract: Abstract The catalytic performance of multicomponent chalcogenides is highly dependent on their anionic composition, yet the role of controlled sulfur–selenium exchange in regulating electrocatalytic activity remains largely unexplored. Herein, a series of Cu2MnS2-xSex (0 ≤ x ≤ 2) catalysts were synthesized through a hydrothermal anion-exchange strategy, enabling systematic tuning of the chalcogen environment. Selenium (Se) incorporation induced lattice distortion and electronic redistribution within the Cu–Mn chalcogenide framework, leading to enhanced charge transport and increased accessibility of catalytic sites. Among all compositions, a two-electrode electrolyzer assembled using the Cu–Mn–Se (CMSe-5) multiphase system exhibited the best bifunctionality, requiring a low overall cell potential of 1.67 V to acquire 10 mA/cm2 current density, with excellent long-term stability in alkaline media. Fascinatingly, the equal chalcogen ratio Cu–Mn–S–Se (CMSSe-4) reveals very close performance with CMSe-5. The superior activity is attributed to the synergistic interaction between sulfur and selenium, which effectively modulates the electronic structure and facilitates adsorption and desorption of reaction intermediates. These findings demonstrate that precise anion engineering offers an effective pathway for optimizing multimetal chalcogenides and provides valuable insights for the development of high-performance, earth-abundant electrocatalysts for sustainable alkaline water electrolysis.

items.title:
Exploring
the Role of the Coordinated 2-Hydroxypropyl
Arm in [Ln(HP-DO3A)]: Determining Equilibrium Properties, Prototropic
Exchange, Solid-State and Solution Structures
items.abstract: Abstract [Gd(HP-DO3A)] represents the neutral macrocyclic analogue of the negatively charged [Gd(DOTA)]−. Its structure is analogously based on SAP and TSAP geometries. Solid-state X-ray structures of [Ln(HP-DO3A)] (Ln= La(III) and Lu(III)) were acquired. [La(HP-DO3A)] crystals displayed a single molecule in the asymmetric unit endowed with a TSAP structure without coordinated water. Conversely, [Lu(HP-DO3A)] showed two molecules, both with a coordinated water molecule and SAP geometry. New results on the [Eu(HP-DO3A)] solution structure and prototropic exchange were gained by acquiring the 1H NMR spectra in water and in the presence of different buffers at variable temperatures and pH. The difference in the prototropic exchange at the −OH function of the two isomers was assessed. The lower log KEuLH-1 for the −OH function of the SAP diastereomer appears to be the determinant for speciation at basic pH as well as for faster prototropic exchange. Moreover, it was shown that the buffer components affect proton exchange as they can compete with OH– from water dissociation as proton-acceptor partners in base catalysis. This finding was well evident in the CEST response of [Eu(HP-DO3A)] in the presence of bicarbonate/carbonate anions. Furthermore, a new saturation transfer signal at about 2.7 ppm was detected that has been ascribed to a weakening or partial displacement of the OH-bearing arm from the coordination sphere of the Eu(III) ion upon formation of a ternary complex with the carbonate anion in the presence of a large molar excess of the buffer.

items.title:
Strain-Engineered
Heterointerfaces of Bimetallic Sulfides
for the Alkaline Hydrogen Evolution Reaction
items.abstract: Abstract Efficient non-noble-metal catalysts are vital for the alkaline hydrogen evolution reaction (HER), where slow H2O dissociation at the cathode markedly surges the overpotential in water splitting. Herein, we developed Cu2S nanorod arrays on Cu foam (CF) under wet-chemical conditions, which were further subjected to electrodeposition as a function of time (30, 60, and 90 s) to create heterointerfaces of urchin-like CoS-Cu2S/CF structures. These nanorod arrays/urchin interfaces demonstrated elongated strain (∼5.83%) at CoS/Cu2S surfaces. When these catalysts were assessed for HER in 1 M KOH, CoS-Cu2S-60/CF delivered a low overpotential of 232 mV at 10 mA·cm–2 with a Tafel slope of 113 mV·dec–1. The CoS-Cu2S-60/CF overpotential (232 mV) was lower by 283 and 146 mV than those of CF (515 mV) and Cu2S/CF (378 mV), respectively. After the post-HER studies, the overpotential at 10 mA·cm–2 was decreased to 138 mV, and potentiostatic stability revealed an increase in current densities, because of the elongated strain of 5.89%. Post-structural and chemical analyses revealed the presence of Cu2+ states from the in situ formed CuO-Cu2S interfaces. This phenomenon promotes strong Jahn–Teller distortion, and the eg bonds thus elongated, contributing to increased strains and effectively absorbing protons, thereby accelerating H2 production.

items.title:
Unraveling
the Dominant Role of Chlorine Vacancies
in a BiOCl-Based Photocatalyst for Decabromodiphenyl Ether Debromination
items.abstract: Abstract Vacancy engineering is a powerful strategy to tune photocatalyst’s performance, but the divergent roles of different vacancies in photocatalytic reactions remain unclear. Herein, we systematically investigate the impacts of oxygen vacancies (VO) and chlorine vacancies (VCl) on visible-light-driven decabromodiphenyl ether (BDE209) debromination over a BiOCl-based iodine-chlorine solid-solution photocatalyst.
