A VO-enriched solid-solution catalyst (BiOCl0.8I0.2-VO) exhibited superior photoelectric properties, such as a broader light absorption range and higher photocurrent density, whereas VCl-enriched BiOCl0.8I0.2-x-VCl showed longer carrier lifetimes. Despite its weaker photoelectric response, BiOCl0.8I0.2-x-VCl achieved a much higher photocatalytic reaction rate for BDE209 debromination. After 50 min of photoreaction, ∼90% of BDE209 was removed, while the removal percentage was only 40% for BiOCl0.8I0.2-VO. The specific surface area-normalized rate constant in the BiOCl0.8I0.2-x-VCl was ∼8-fold superior to BiOCl0.8I0.2-VO. Also notably, BiOCl0.8I0.2-x-VCl exhibited a shorter induction period for BDE209 degradation than that for BiOCl0.8I0.2-VO. Further investigations revealed that VCl lowered the C–Br bond activation energy barrier and enabled efficient debromination with fewer photogenerated electrons. This work clarifies the divergent roles of VO and VCl in BiOCl for BDE209 debromination and photoelectric properties, offering insights into the rational design of vacancy-engineered photocatalysts for brominated pollutant remediation.

items.title:
Cu–S–Zn Bridging Bonds and Sulfur-Vacancy-Induced
Electron Delocalization in CuS/ZnS Heterojunction for Stable and Enhanced
CO2 Photoreduction
items.abstract: Abstract Due to uncontrollable hole accumulation and intrinsic electron localization, photocorrosion and inefficient CO2 activation severely restrict the photocatalytic properties of transition-metal sulfides (TMS). Herein, a hierarchical microbelt-like CuS/ZnS heterojunction [Vs-CuS(001)/ZnS] with Cu–S–Zn bridging bonds and sulfur vacancies (Vs) was designed to overcome these limitations. The well-matched interatomic S–S and Zn–Zn distances on the CuS(001) and ZnS(111) facets (∼3.80 vs. ∼3.82 Å) provide structural basis for constructing atomic-level heterointerface. Experimental and theoretical results confirm that this crystallographic compatibility drives the formation of an atomically intimate interface via Cu–S–Zn bonding, further reinforced by Vs-induced unsaturated anchoring sites. Such a heterointerface facilitates hole extraction from CuS to ZnS, fundamentally suppressing photocorrosion. Concurrently, the hierarchical microstructure provides abundant accessible active sites and shortened charge diffusion pathways. Additionally, density functional theory calculations reveal that the incorporation of Vs induces electron delocalization around Cu sites, promoting π back-donation of Cu 3d electrons into the antibonding orbitals of CO2 for its activation. Benefiting from these synergistic effects, the optimal Vs-CuS(001)/ZnS-3 achieves a high CO production rate of 19.3 μmol g–1 h–1 with high stability. This work establishes a synergistic strategy that modulates interfacial, electronic, and geometric structures for designing durable and efficient TMS-based photocatalysts.

items.title:
DMF-Driven
Modulation of Coordination Geometry and
SMM Performance in Dinuclear Dysprosium(III) Complexes
items.abstract: Abstract Given the favorable nature of pentagonal-bipyramidal coordination geometry in achieving high-performance dysprosium(III)-based single-molecule magnets (SMMs), an equatorial pentadentate chelator of pyridyl-2,6-diacetylbis(salicylhydrazone) (H4Pdas) was employed in this study. The attempted replacement of Cl– in [Et3NH][Dy(H2Pdas)Cl2] by Ph3SiO– in various solvents with different bases gave two Dy(III) complexes, namely, [Dy2(H2Pdas)2(OSiPh3)2]·CH2Cl2 (Dy2) and [Dy2(H2Pdas)2(DMF)2(OSiPh3)2] (Dy2-DMF). Both Dy2 and Dy2-DMF have similar dinuclear skeletons with their two Dy(III) ions linked by a pair of H2Pdas2– linkers in a μ2-η1:η5 bridging mode. The major difference between Dy2-DMF and Dy2 is that there is one more DMF molecule for each Dy(III) ion in Dy2-DMF than in Dy2, which leads to pentagonal bipyramidal and triangular dodecahedral Dy(III) coordination geometries for Dy2 and Dy2-DMF, respectively. These structural differences between Dy2 and Dy2-DMF resulted in their different SMM performances with energy barriers of 51(1) and 31.8(3) K for Dy2 and Dy2-DMF, respectively. It demonstrated that the additional coordination of DMF in the dinuclear complex significantly tunes the structural parameters such as coordination geometry and bond angles, consequently influencing the magnetic anisotropy and SMM performance, which was further rationalized by CASSCF-SO theoretical calculations.

items.title:
Coordination
Chemistry of a Hybrid N/S Macrocyclic
Framework: PyN2S Chelators toward Stabilization of 64Cu(II/I)
in PET Imaging Applications
items.abstract: Abstract In recent efforts to develop optimal 64Cu chelators with ideal thermodynamic stability and high kinetic inertness, focus has shifted to the common problem of reduction-induced demetalation of 64Cu(I). The most common approach to remedy this issue is to make the reduction of 64Cu(II) to 64Cu(I) inaccessible, with anionic ligands comprising hard Lewis bases like carboxylates. However, an alternative approach has been to focus on the stability of the 64Cu(I) species, most commonly achieved by incorporating soft sulfur donors, such as thiols or thioethers, into the chelator framework. Herein, we present a novel copper chelator, PyN2S, comprising both N and S donors, allowing for an N3S binding mode. Five new ligands are introduced, and their coordination chemistry with copper is explored. Thermodynamic stability constants with Cu2+ and Zn2+ are presented, as well as solution and solid-state characterization of the Cu(II) complexes. Finally, the radiochemistry of the PyN2S ligands with 64Cu was explored, including both in vitro characterization and in vivo biodistribution in mice. Overall, the PyN2S framework has demonstrated promising stability for both Cu(II) and Cu(I), and quantitative radiolabeling with 64Cu was achieved, while in vivo biodistribution revealed the highest uptake in renal clearance pathway organs.

items.title:
Interface-Enhanced
Thermal Localization in Ce-Doped
Biphasic Nb2O5 via Oxygen Vacancies and Hot-Carrier
Transport for Solar Evaporation
items.abstract: Abstract Defect and interface engineering were jointly introduced into Nb2O5 through Ce doping to enhance broadband light harvesting and hot-carrier transport for solar-driven interfacial evaporation. Ce incorporation induces oxygen vacancies, reconstructs the local Nb–O framework, and triggers the formation of a low-mismatch T/ζ biphasic interface with directional strain. This coupled structure generates a positive thermal-conductivity window absent in the single phases, together with higher hot-carrier concentration, longer low-frequency phonon lifetime, and more continuous local vibrational coupling. Finite-element simulations further reveal faster thermal-field buildup and stronger interfacial heat localization in the biphasic structure. As a result, Nb–Ce3.0 exhibits the highest thermal conductivity of 1.532 W m–1 K–1, a surface temperature of 62.3 °C with bulk water remaining at ≈33.4 °C, and evaporation rates of 1.343, 4.022, and 6.525 kg m–2 h–1 under 1, 3, and 5 sun, respectively, while maintaining effective seawater desalination.

items.title: Cation-Size-Controlled Structural and Magnetic Ground State Transitions in Co2+-Based Honeycomb-Derived Oxides Na0.5 RE 0.5Co2TeO6 ( RE = La, Nd, Sm, Eu, Tb, Dy, Yb, and Y)
items.abstract: Abstract Honeycomb lattices containing spin–orbit-entangled Co2+ ions with effective Jeff = 1/2 moments provide promising platforms for enhancing strong quantum fluctuations and thus realizing potential quantum spin-liquid states. Here, we report a series of honeycomb-derived tellurates, “Na0.5RE0.5Co2TeO6” (NRECTO, RE = La, Nd, Sm, Eu, Tb, Dy, Yb, and Y). The increased size mismatch between Na+ and RE3+ drives an orthorhombic-to-hexagonal structural transition for NRECTO, accompanied by reconstruction in the connectivity of the [Co2TeO6]2– double-rutile chains and transformation in hexagonal channel topologies. High-resolution synchrotron X-ray diffraction and neutron powder diffraction reveal that both structures retain similar three-dimensional Co2+ topologies derived from AAA-stacked buckled honeycomb layers. Magnetic measurements revealed that orthorhombic NLaCTO exhibits a long-range antiferromagnetic order below 13 K, as confirmed by DC and AC susceptibility and a λ-type heat-capacity anomaly, whereas hexagonal NYCTO exhibits glassy magnetic freezing below 11 K, characterized by frequency-dependent AC susceptibility and slow spin dynamics. Despite comparable Co2+–O–Co2+ exchange pathways and Co-topologies are retained in both structures, their contrasting magnetic behavior demonstrates that subtle structural differences can strongly reshape the magnetic energy landscape. These results establish chemical-unit substitution as an effective strategy for controlling magnetism in Co2+-based honeycomb oxides.

items.title:
Complex Structural Evolution and Compressibility of
β-Cu2V2O7 under Pressure
items.abstract: Abstract The structural response of β-Cu2V2O7 to compression was investigated by synchrotron single-crystal X-ray diffraction up to 12.6 GPa using helium as a highly hydrostatic pressure-transmitting medium and complemented by density-functional theory calculations. Compared with previous studies using 4:1 methanol–ethanol, the present experiments reveal a different pressure-induced structural evolution and significantly lower compressibility. Instead of the previously reported β → γ transition, β-Cu2V2O7 transforms from monoclinic β (C2/c) to a previously unreported monoclinic β′ (C2/m) phase at 0.3 GPa, followed by two triclinic polymorphs, γ′ (P1̅) at 3.3 GPa and γ″ (P1̅) at 8.4 GPa. These transitions involve increased Cu and V coordination numbers, substantial volume collapses, and enhanced framework connectivity. Accordingly, the bulk modulus increases from 54 GPa for the β phase to approximately 103 GPa for the highest-pressure polymorph. Experimental equations of state agree closely with ab initio calculations, which further show that the competing polymorphs have small enthalpy differences, helping explain the complex pressure-induced polymorphism. Differences between the present and the previously reported structural sequences are discussed in terms of the possible effects of experimental and intrinsic factors, although the available data do not establish a specific origin for the discrepancy.

items.title:
Dynamic Electronic
Structure of the FeMoco Enables
Mechanistic Coupling between N2 Binding and H2 Evolution in Nitrogenase
items.abstract: Abstract The mechanistic coupling of N2 binding and H2 evolution through reductive elimination from the E4 intermediate constitutes a critical step in the nitrogenase catalytic cycle. Despite extensive mechanistic investigations, how the Fe centers within the FeMoco cofactor dynamically reorganize their local electronic structures to facilitate this coupled process remains unresolved. Here, using density functional theory (DFT) combined with intrinsic atomic orbital/intrinsic bond orbital (IAO/IBO) and natural bond orbital (NBO) analyses, we uncover the electronic structure evolution of FeMoco along the coupled N2-binding/H2-evolution reaction coordinate. Comparative analyses of reaction energetics, with appropriate transition states, support an “intermediate” mechanism over purely “associative” or “dissociative” pathways, revealing a key intermediate E4(H2N2) in which N2 and H2 are simultaneously coordinated to the same Fe center. Detailed molecular-orbital analyses demonstrate that the coupled reaction is enabled by highly synchronized electronic reorganization across neighboring Fe centers, which dynamically redistribute electron density to stabilize concurrent H2 release and N2 activation. In particular, cooperative Fe–Fe electronic coupling allows the reactive Fe site to adapt its local bonding interactions. These findings provide an electronic-level rationale for the functional necessity of the multinuclear FeMoco architecture and reveal how orchestrated electronic flexibility within the cluster governs the critical mechanistic step of nitrogenase catalysis.

items.title:
Host–Guest
Inclusion Self-Assembly of Zero-Dimensional
Metal Halides for Enhanced Photocatalytic Amine Coupling
items.abstract: Abstract The practical application of zero-dimensional (0D) organic–inorganic hybrid metal halides in photocatalysis is hindered by their poor stability, rapid charge-carrier recombination, and low surface reactivity. Herein, we report a host–guest self-assembly strategy for constructing two 0D anionic metal halides with enhanced photocatalytic activity, [(L1)2⊂(ZnCl4)2–3] (C1) and [(L1)2⊂(MnCl4)2–3] (C2), by one-pot reaction of an anthracene-pyridine-based cationic cavity ligand (L13+·3Br–) with ZnCl2 and MnCl2·4H2O, respectively. Single-crystal X-ray diffraction reveals that both compounds feature discrete tetrahedral [MX4]2– cores yet exhibit distinct lattice packing modes; notably, in C1, the anionic cluster is anchored via C–H···Cl hydrogen bonds rather than direct encapsulation. The host–guest inclusion systems of discrete metal halides exhibit optical band gaps of 2.19–2.27 eV, with observable charge separation. Under 455 nm blue-light irradiation, C2 demonstrates exceptional photocatalytic performance in benzylamine coupling (TOF of 492.66 h–1), achieving 71–99% conversion across 10 substrates and about 90% activity retention after five cycles, while C1 shows lower activity (TOF of 463.58 h–1). EPR spectroscopy and quenching experiments uncover a radical-based synergistic mechanism. These results show that host–guest self-assembly affords stable 0D metal halide photocatalysts and that metal-center exchange significantly affects catalytic activity.

items.title:
Photoresponsive
Ruthenium(II) Isomeric Switches in
Solution: Leveraging Asymmetry in Ligand Design for Precision in Photoactivated
Chemotherapy
items.abstract: Abstract Ligand orientation is emerging as a powerful, underexploited lever for tuning the photoreactivity of Ru(II) complexes, although its mechanistic basis remains unclear. Herein, we report a systematic isomeric series, [RuII(ptpy)(N^N)(DMSO)]2+ (ptpy = 4′-phenyl-2,2′:6′,2″-terpyridine), based on unsymmetrical picolylamine/picolylimine N^N donors, alongside the bpy-based reference complex [3]. Crystal structures of four geometrical isomers ([1]AMD, [2]AMD, [1]IMD, [2]IMD) pinpoint how donor placement, which possibly could reshape the excited-state behavior. Visible-light irradiation in acetonitrile triggers clean DMSO photosubstitution, yet the amine and imine platforms diverge sharply in outcome, giving ∼3:2 vs. 1:3 Npy-cis-MeCN:Npy-trans-MeCN product ratios. Strikingly, isomers wherein −NH2 /═NH- trans to DMSO react substantially faster despite virtually invariant Ru–DMSO bond lengths across the series, showing that kinetic control arises in the excited state, not from ground-state structural perturbation. Light drives reversible switching between geometrical isomers via a plausible common pentacoordinate intermediate, revealing previously unrecognized structural flexibility in this ligand class. TDDFT calculations assign the 1MLCT absorptions and rationalize the photosubstitution-induced red shift to selective access to dissociative 3MC states, identifying this excited-state pathway as the origin of rate differences and a predictive design principle. Collectively, these findings establish ligand orientation as a rational, structure-based handle for engineering Ru(II) excited-state reactivity, positioning this thermally robust, visible-light-responsive scaffold as a promising PACT platform.

items.title:
Synthesis
and Characterization of the Nitrosonium
Borosulfates (NO)[B(SO4)2] and (NO)[B(S2O7)2]
items.abstract: Abstract The solvothermal reaction of boron oxide and oleum (65% SO3) in the presence of nitrosonium cations resulted in the formation of the first nitrosonium borosulfates. By careful adjustment of the initial boron content as well as the reaction temperature, we achieved the selective synthesis of two distinct borosulfates featuring S–O–S and B–O–S bridges, respectively. (NO)[B(S2O7)2] crystallizes homeotypically to A[B(S2O7)2] (A = NH4, K) in space group Cc (no. 9, Z = 8, a = 11.3824(6) Å, b = 14.6067(7) Å, c = 13.6858(6) Å, β = 95.128(2)°) and contains molecular [B(S2O7)2]− anions. In addition, one-dimensional, SiS2-analogue chains are present in (NO)[B(SO4)2], which crystallizes in space group Pccn (no. 56, Z = 4, a = 9.0046(2) Å, b = 9.0780(3) Å, c = 7.4462(2) Å) homeotypically to A[B(SO4)2] (A = NH4, K). Vibrational spectroscopy confirms both structural models, including the presence of S–O–S bridges. Thermal analysis revealed the transformation of S–O–S bridges in (NO)[B(S2O7)2] to B–O–S bridges in (NO)[B(SO4)2]. The charge-to-radius ratio of the cation was identified as structure-directing parameter for [B(SO4)2] chains.

items.title:
Integration over Assembly: A Single-Material Approach
to Dynamic and Self-Erasing Optical Encryption
items.abstract: Abstract The evolution of optical encryption demands materials that not only conceal information but also enable sophisticated control over its lifecycle. However, increased functionality requires more complex material compositions or device architectures. To circumvent this trade-off, here we report a conceptual and practical evolution from a dual-material binary architecture relying on external erasure to a single-material ternary system featuring intrinsic self-erasure. In the binary design, pristine (C6H8N3)CdCl3 serves as a nonemissive background, while the two addressable states are provided by its N,N-dimethylformamide (DMF)-activated derivative (i.e., (C6H8N3)CdCl3–DMF, green afterglow) and its Mn2+-doped counterpart (no afterglow). This configuration enables dynamic “1/0” readout and selective information erasure upon exposure to water mist. More critically, the Mn2+-doped compound alone functions as a self-contained, multiresponsive unit, manifesting three addressable states under 254 nm irradiation: an initial red state, an HCl-switched green state, and a solvent-induced “off” state. Exploiting these three discrete states affords compact ternary encryption. Furthermore, the latter two states inherently constitute a built-in self-erasure mechanism, enabling complete pattern disappearance without any external intervention. This progression─from combinatorial assembly to integrated functionality─offers a blueprint for designing streamlined, high-capacity optical security platforms.

items.title:
Systematic
Exploration of the Ternary Dy–Ir–Sn
System with Magnetic Property Investigation
items.abstract: Abstract The ternary Dy–Ir–Sn system phase equilibria at 800 °C were investigated with a goal of identifying novel phases. Samples were prepared by arc-melting and subsequent annealing and then characterized using scanning electron microscopy, powder X-ray diffraction, and single-crystal X-ray diffraction. To streamline the exploratory process, a scalable, high-throughput framework was developed to automate the summary of crystallographic data, which aids the systematic exploration of ternary intermetallic systems and provides a reproducible methodology for exploratory materials characterization. The newly identified intermetallic phases were further investigated using density functional theory (DFT) to probe their electronic structures, alongside magnetic characterization to elucidate their magnetic ground states. We report four novel ternary compounds: DyIrSn (ZrNiAl-type), Dy26Ir9.25Sn7.75 (Sm26Co11Ga6-type), Dy4Ir7Sn6 (U4Re7Si6-type), and Dy3Ir2.5Sn3.5 (Lu3Co2In4-type). Magnetic measurements were done on pure samples of bulk polycrystalline DyIrSn and Dy26Ir9.25Sn7.75, revealing antiferromagnetic- and ferrimagnetic-like behavior, respectively, with both inverse susceptibilities and Curie–Weiss fits consistent with a trivalent Dy3+ moment. In DyIrSn, there is an AFM-like transition near TN= 7.25 K, with a second anomaly near T2 = 4.9 K. Dy26Ir9.25Sn7.75 shows ZFC-FC irreversibility below 40 K, likely due to magnetic ordering.

items.title:
High Proton
Conduction in a Hydrogen-Bonded Co(II)
Framework through Pendant Carboxylic Acid-Decorated 1D Channels
items.abstract: Abstract A two-dimensional Co(II) metal–organic framework, FCG-7 (FCG = Framework Chemistry Group of CSIR-CSMCRI), containing pendant carboxylic acid (−COOH) groups was rationally constructed to investigate the role of intrinsic proton-donating sites in solid-state proton transport. Crystallographic study divulged a hydrogen-bonded layered framework in which the uncoordinated −COOH groups project toward one-dimensional channels, providing accessible sites for interaction with guest water molecules. The activated framework (FCG-7a) exhibits good hydrolytic and thermal stability, a lower water contact angle of 48.6°, and a proton conductivity of 1.25 × 10–3 S cm–1 at 80 °C and 95% relative humidity (RH). The low activation energy (0.22 eV) is in agreement with a predominantly Grotthuss-type proton-hopping mechanism. Proton transport is strongly humidity-dependent, with conductivity increasing approximately 1600-fold from 60% to 95% RH at 80 °C, highlighting the participation of confined water molecules in establishing extended hydrogen-bonding pathways. To evaluate the contribution of pendant −COOH groups, a structurally analogous framework, FCG-10, lacking pendant carboxylic acid functionality, was prepared through a molecular-scissoring strategy. FCG-10a exhibits a lower conductivity of 3.5 × 10–4 S cm–1 under identical conditions. These results highlight a structure-guided strategy wherein accessible acidic sites and water-mediated hydrogen-bonding networks promote proton transport in crystalline frameworks

items.title:
Fluoride-Enabled
Assembly of Iron–Hydrogen-Bonded
Frameworks as Bifunctional Lewis Acid–Base Catalysts for Knoevenagel
Condensation
items.abstract: Abstract The development of recyclable heterogeneous catalysts that enable efficient organic transformations without solvents is important for sustainable chemical synthesis. In this work, two new fluoride-mediated metal–hydrogen-bonded organic frameworks (M-HOFs), labeled as JOU-40 and JOU-41, were successfully synthesized. Single-crystal X-ray diffraction reveals that both M-HOFs feature [Fe3F11]n chains that are extended into three-dimensional supramolecular networks through O–H···F hydrogen bonds. The resulting frameworks integrate Lewis-acidic iron centers and basic fluoride sites within a confined porous environment, enabling efficient Lewis acid–base catalysis. As heterogeneous catalysts, JOU-40 and JOU-41 efficiently promote the solvent-free Knoevenagel condensation of benzaldehyde with malononitrile, affording &gt;99.00% conversion and selectivity. The catalyst also exhibits good substrate compatibility across a range of substituted aldehydes. More fascinatingly, kinetic analyses reveal that the reaction can be described by the Avrami nucleation–growth model, highlighting the coupled contributions of chemical conversion and product crystallization. Density functional theory (DFT) calculations demonstrate that the adjacent Fe3+ and F– sites activate the two reactants and facilitate C═C bond formation, providing a molecular-level basis for the observed catalytic activity. This work offers new design insights for developing highly efficient, stable, and recyclable catalytic systems for solvent-free Knoevenagel condensation.

items.title:
High-Entropy
MnFeCoNiZn-ZIF Couples Interfacial Hole
Transfer with Water Oxidation Kinetics in Metal Oxide Photoanodes
items.abstract: Abstract Photoelectrochemical water oxidation is constrained by inefficient interfacial hole transfer and sluggish oxygen evolution kinetics in semiconductor photoanodes. Here, a high-entropy MnFeCoNiZn zeolitic imidazolate framework (HEZ) cocatalyst was constructed on BiVO4 by in situ potentiostatic electrodeposition. The ultrathin, structurally disordered HEZ layer integrates compositionally diverse metal sites with an electronically coupled semiconductor/cocatalyst interface. Raman and X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy reveal pronounced interfacial electronic redistribution and valence-state regulation of the multimetallic centers, while photoluminescence and modulated photocurrent/photovoltage measurements reveal reduced radiative recombination and accelerated interfacial hole transfer. Density functional theory calculations further show that Zn incorporation into MnFeCoNi-ZIF lowers the free-energy requirement of the key *O-to-*OOH step from 1.28 to 0.95 eV and produces a more balanced oxygen-evolution free-energy profile. Consequently, HEZ-BiVO4 delivers a photocurrent density of 6.23 mA cm–2 at 1.23 V versus the reversible hydrogen electrode, an applied-bias photon-to-current efficiency of 1.91%, a bulk charge-separation efficiency of 99.6%, and a surface charge-injection efficiency of 95%. The photoanode retains 94% of its initial photocurrent after 10 h. Extension of HEZ modification to Fe2O3 and WO3 demonstrates a transferable strategy for coupling interfacial charge management with multimetallic water-oxidation catalysis.

items.title:
High-Throughput
Synthesis and Screening of Cyclometalated
Iridium Complexes for Antibacterial Applications
items.abstract: Abstract The discovery of novel antibiotics to address the rise of antimicrobial resistance is an increasingly pressing issue for global health. In recent years, transition-metal complexes have gained attention as potential antibacterial agents. We herein describe a new methodology to generate novel cyclometalated iridium compounds with bidentate Schiff ligands in a high-throughput combinatorial approach, alongside the expansion of an existing approach using bidentate pyridine-triazole ligands, with the aim of finding new metalloantibiotics. A total of 552 new complexes were synthesized and evaluated. Variety in the libraries was introduced by including three cyclometalating phenylpyridine ligands, demonstrating that the synthesis can tolerate both electron-rich and electron-poor metal scaffolds while using mild and biologically compatible conditions. Screening of the crude reaction mixtures in a direct-to-biology approach revealed a number of highly active complexes against Gram-positive bacteria, which was confirmed by resynthesis and further testing of lead compounds. This approach widens the scope of metal complex combinatorial chemistry, enabling rapid exploration of the chemical space involving cyclometalated iridium complexes.

items.title:
Local Ligand-Framework
Evolution Prior to Long-Range
Antiferromagnetic Ordering in NiPS3
items.abstract: Abstract Two-dimensional van der Waals antiferromagnets have emerged as a promising platform for low-dimensional spintronics. NiPS3 is a representative system because of its negligible stray fields and ultrafast spin dynamics. However, the relationship between local structural evolution and the establishment of long-range antiferromagnetic order remains incompletely understood. Here, we investigate the temperature-dependent magnetostructural evolution of NiPS3 using anisotropic magnetization measurements, neutron powder diffraction, variable-temperature powder X-ray diffraction Rietveld refinement, Raman spectroscopy, and maximum entropy method electron density reconstruction. Anisotropic magnetization and its temperature derivatives reveal a broad, orientation-dependent magnetic response over approximately 157–164 K. Neutron diffraction detects additional intensity near the magnetic (010) reflection at 150 K, whereas no comparable magnetic Bragg feature is resolved at 160 or 166 K under the present measurement conditions, indicating that the higher-temperature magnetic response is not accompanied by resolvable long-range magnetic Bragg scattering. Structural refinements, Raman spectroscopy, and electron density analyses further identify complementary local structural, vibrational, and electronic responses within the 162–164 K portion of this broad magnetic response interval. Together, these results place the local structural response within the upper part of the magnetic-response interval and before the development of resolvable long-range antiferromagnetic order at lower temperatures. These findings provide an experimental framework for examining magnetostructural evolution and ligand-mediated tuning of magnetism in layered antiferromagnets.

items.title: Structural Evolution and Bonding Analysis of Heterotrinuclear Carbonyl Clusters TiNi2(CO) n – ( n = 3–5)
items.abstract: Abstract A series of heterotrinuclear carbonyl clusters TiNi2(CO)n– (n = 3–5) have been produced by a laser sputtering supersonic cluster ion source and probed by a velocity-map photoelectron imaging spectrometer. Theoretical calculations have been executed to probe the structures and assist the experimental spectral assignments. At n = 3, an intriguing trigonal pyramidal Ti–Ni–Ni–C motif is formed with two μ2-bridging CO ligands and one μ3-bridging CO ligand, which is retained in the most stable structures of larger clusters. For n = 4 and 5, the additional CO ligands are separately bound to each Ni atom in a terminal coordination mode. C–O bond activation is found to increase systematically with the binding motif of metal–CO coordination: terminal &lt; μ2-bridging &lt; μ3-bridging coordination. The present findings elucidate the bonding mechanism in the heteronuclear metal clusters at the molecular level and provide microscopic insights into metal–CO interactions in heterometallic systems.

items.title:
Halide-Regulated
Dual Emission and Thermochromism
in Zero-Dimensional Phosphonium Metal Halides
items.abstract: Abstract Temperature-responsive luminescent materials have attracted considerable attention for optical sensing and dynamic anticounterfeiting. However, designing thermochromic luminescent materials with pronounced color variation and well-defined emission mechanisms remains challenging. A series of zero-dimensional dual-emissive complexes, (2-NpPPh2Bn)2M2X6 (2-NpPPh2Bn = benzyl(naphthalen-2-yl)diphenylphosphonium; M = Zn, X = Cl (1); M = Zn, X = Br (2); M = Cd, X = Cl (3); M = Cd, X = Br (4)), are constructed. At room temperature, these complexes exhibit single-band blue emission at 399 nm, which evolves into dual-band white emission centered at 417 and 557 nm upon cooling to 80 K. Variable-temperature lifetime measurements and theoretical calculations reveal the 417 nm band originates from halide-to-ligand charge transfer (XLCT) dominated self-trapped exciton luminescence (1.479 μs), while the 557 nm band is attributed to intraligand charge transfer (ILCT)-mediated phosphorescence (17.249 ms). Halide substitution from Cl to Br reverses the relative intensity of the two emission bands. Complex 3 exhibits the pronounced yellow afterglow at 80 K. The orthogonal responses to temperature, UV excitation, and afterglow decay time enable a multilevel dynamic information encryption system. Functionalized phosphonium countercation and halide substitution cooperatively regulate XLCT/ILCT competition, offering a strategy for designing multiresponsive luminescent materials with tunable emission mechanisms.

items.title:
ANb2(PS4)2(S2)2 (A = K, Rb)
Synthesized by Metal Oxide–Boron–Chalcogen
(MOBQ) Method: Featuring [Nb2S8(S2)2] Dimers and [PS4] Tetrahedra for Infrared
Nonlinear Optical Properties
items.abstract: Abstract NbnSm clusters containing S–S and Nb–Nb bonds are promising as infrared nonlinear optical (IR NLO) functional motifs, yet their study in the thiophosphate system remains scarce. Here, ANb2(PS4)2(S2)2 (A = K (1), Rb (2)) were synthesized by the metal oxide–boron–chalcogen (MOBQ) solid-state routine, and their structures feature a three-dimensional double-helical tunnel framework costructed by alternately connected [Nb2S8(S2)2] dimers and [PS4] tetrahedra. Both compounds exhibit narrow band gaps (1.59 and 1.58 eV), large birefringences (0.20 and 0.21 @ 2.1 μm), second-harmonic generation (SHG) responses, and photocurrent responses. Theoretical calculations indicate that their weak SHG response originates from the multidirectional cancellation of dipole moment vectors at the microscopic scale. This work enriches the IR NLO research on Nb-based thiophosphates and clarifies the application potential and structural limitations of Nb-based sulfides in the NLO field.

items.title:
Tuning the
Raman/Orbach Relaxation Ratio in Co2IIIDyIII Single-Molecule Magnets through
Acetate-to-Nitrate Substitution
items.abstract: Abstract To precisely regulate Orbach and Raman processes in polynuclear complexes, four novel Co2IIILnIII complexes with the molecular formula of [Co2IIILn(HL)2{(py)2CO2}(OAc)3]·2CH3CN·1.5H2O (Ln = Tb (1Tb), Dy (2Dy), and Ho (3Ho); (py)2CO2H2 = the gem-diol form of di-2-pyridyl ketone(dpk); OAc– = acetate) and [Co2IIIDy(HL)2{(py)2CO2}(OAc)2(NO3)]·2CH3OH·H2O (4Dy) have been obtained. The main difference between 1Tb–3Ho and 4Dy is that one μ1-κ1-O,O′-OAc– ligand coordinates with LnIII in 1Tb, 2Dy, and 3Ho, while one μ1-κ1-O,O′-NO3– coordinates with DyIII in 4Dy. Alternating current (ac) susceptibility studies revealed that 1Tb and 3Ho show field-induced slow magnetic relaxation signatures, while 2Dy and 4Dy both exhibit field-induced single-molecule magnet behavior. Additionally, the Raman/Orbach ratios are about 18 for 2Dy and about 5480 for 4Dy, indicating that the relative weighting of the Raman and the Orbach relaxation channels can be markedly modulated by OAc–/NO3– substitution. Ab initio calculations analyzed the difference in the magnetic relaxation behavior of 2Dy and 4Dy and revealed that the directions of the main magnetic axes of DyIII are sensitive to the coordinated OAc–/NO3– ions, namely, the main magnetic axis of DyIII in 2Dy is almost parallel to the Dy1–O2 bond, while the axis of DyIII in 4Dy deviates from all Dy–O bond directions.

items.title:
Hexagonal
Phase Stabilization and Multiferroicity
in (Tm,Yb,Lu,In,Sc)FeO3 High-Entropy Ceramics
items.abstract: Abstract Geometric ferroelectrics hexagonal RFeO3 (h-RFeO3) has emerged as a prominent class of single-phase multiferroic materials, exhibiting magnetoelectric coupling by the spin–lattice coupling mechanism. However, stabilizing the hexagonal structure for RFeO3 remain challenging. Herein, we report the synthesis of stabilizing the pure hexagonal structure of (Tm,Yb,Lu,In,Sc)FeO3 high-entropy ceramics through the incorporation of (Tm,Yb,Lu,In,Sc) at the R-site via solid-state sintering without precursors. The samples retained polar hexagonal structure up to a ferroelectric transition temperature above 1373 K. The samples exhibit complex magnetic anomalies, including antiferromagnetic transition (TN ∼ 232 K) and spin reorientation behavior (TSR ∼ 156 K) based on comparison with established h-RFeO3 systems. Furthermore, significant coupling between magnetic and dielectric degrees of freedom or magnetoelectric coupling effect was observed, as evidenced by a dielectric anomaly near the spin reorientation temperature. Remarkably, periodic modulation of polarization by applied periodic magnetic fields was achieved at 2 K. The findings highlight the potential of the high-entropy strategy for designing novel multiferroic materials and provide new insights into magnetoelectric coupling in high-entropy systems.

items.title:
A Sodium-Based
Microporous Metal–Organic Framework
Built on 2 Tetranuclear Clusters for Size-Dependent Sorting of Hexane
Isomers
items.abstract: Abstract The construction of alkali metal-based metal–organic frameworks (AMOFs) with permanent porosity represents a notable challenge. Here we report a novel sodium-based MOF, designated HIAM-113, built on tetranuclear Na4 clusters and a tetracarboxylate linker. HIAM-113 features high structural robustness and one-dimensional channels that are optimal for size-sieving separation of hexane isomers.

items.title:
Modulation
of Mixed-Cation Lead Halide Crystal Structures
and Properties by Changing Small Size Cation
items.abstract: Abstract Mixing of organic cations is a promising strategy for extending the diversity of hybrid lead halides and tuning their properties. Most famous examples of this approach are multilayered Ruddlesden–Popper and Dion-Jacobson perovskites and three-dimensional (3D) MPDA2APb4Br13 perovskitoids (MPDA = N-methylpropanediammonium, A = methylammonium, formamidinium, ethylammonium, and dimethylammonium). We show that the 3D perovskitoid structure is no longer stable when imidazolium (IM+) and guanidinium (GA+) are used, but instead two- and one-dimensional structures are formed, respectively, and the stoichiometry changes to MPDA2IM3Pb4Br15 and MPDA6GA6Pb7Br30Br2. Most interestingly, MPDA2IM3Pb4Br15 comprises unprecedented layers composed of the corner-sharing PbBr6 octahedra organized into tetrameric units with IM+ located in the perovskite cages. It undergoes a transition from the high-temperature P21/c phase to the low-temperature P21/n phase associated with the dielectric anomaly. The MPDA6GA6Pb7Br30Br2 structure is composed of corner-sharing PbBr6 octahedra arranged into chains, and its crystal structure remains trigonal, P-3C1, in the entire temperature range studied. Optical studies show that different structural motifs strongly affect band gaps and emission properties of these compounds. In particular, MPDA6GA6Pb7Br30Br2 exhibits very stable broadband greenish-yellow emission, while MPDA2IM3Pb4Br15 exhibits both narrowband emission (attributed to free excitons (FEs) and bound excitons (BEs)) and self-trapped (STE) broadband emission, a thermally activated population transfer from STE to FE + BE, and strong thermochromism.

items.title:
Synthesis
and Structural Characterization of Three
Lithium Dithiophosphates: Li3PO2S2·11H2O, Li3PO2S2·H2O, and Li3PO2S2
items.abstract: Abstract Solid-state batteries require electrolytes with high Li-ion conductivity, together with good interfacial and chemical stability. Oxythiophosphate-type solid electrolytes appear to achieve such a balance, but their chemistry remains little investigated. Here, we report the low-temperature aqueous synthesis of lithium dithiophosphate undecahydrate, Li3PO2S2·11H2O, and its dehydration pathway to the monohydrate Li3PO2S2·H2O and to the anhydrous phase Li3PO2S2. Li3PO2S2·11H2O crystallizes in the P212121 space group, isostructural to the parent compound Na3PO2S2·11H2O. Upon annealing at 100 °C, a monohydrate forms with a C2cm structure solved ab initio from XRPD and PND data. Further dehydration at 200 °C yields anhydrous Li3PO2S2, which adopts a Pbca structure isostructural to the Na analog. Solid-state NMR spectroscopy confirms dominant (PO2S2) units in the hydrate and reveals partial transformation to (PO3S)/(PO4) units upon annealing. Li3PO2S2·11H2O exhibits a room-temperature ionic conductivity of ∼10–5 S cm–1. The ionic conductivities of Li3PO2S2·H2O and Li3PO2S2 are lower: σ = 8.7 × 10–8 S·cm–1 and 2.6 × 10–8 S·cm–1 (at 110 °C), with activation energies of ∼0.70 and ∼0.69 eV, respectively. These findings expand the oxythiophosphate structural family with new hydrated and anhydrous phases, providing a basis for tuning O/S composition and Li-ion transport through targeted cation substitution.

items.title:
Sb2TeO7: A Chiral Antimony Tellurite
with Phase-Matchable Second-Harmonic Generation
items.abstract: Abstract Noncentrosymmetric (NCS) structures are uncommon among compositionally simple inorganic solids, even when their constituent polyhedra are locally asymmetric. Here, we establish the binary tellurite Sb2TeO7 as a chiral NCS crystal that adopts the orthorhombic space group P212121 (No. 19). Stereochemically active trigonal-pyramidal [TeO3] units bridge two types of distorted Sb–O zigzag chains into a three-dimensional framework, preventing cancellation of the local asymmetric distortions. The structure was obtained through prolonged oxidative solid-state treatment and validated by single-crystal and powder X-ray diffraction. Sb2TeO7 exhibits high thermal stability up to approximately 800 °C and well-balanced nonlinear optical properties. It possesses a wide transparent window from 299 nm to 5.75 μm, a suitable birefringence of 0.106 at 546 nm, and a moderate phase-matchable second-harmonic generation (SHG) response (1.36 × KDP at 1064 nm). Although the SHG response is moderate relative to optimized tellurites, these results demonstrate that an NCS framework and optical anisotropy can be realized in a binary antimony tellurite when the constituent polyhedra assemble cooperatively.

items.title:
Self-Activation
and Dynamic Surface Reconstruction
of Metal–Organic Frameworks Enable Durable Oxygen Evolution
Reaction
items.abstract: Abstract Metal–organic frameworks (MOFs) have emerged as prospective oxygen evolution reaction (OER) electrodes, yet their activity is contingent upon irreversible reconstruction into metal oxyhydroxides (MOOH), resulting in structural degradation and compromising long-term durability. Here, we report a self-supported Co-BPM/NF electrode (BPM = 4,4′-dihydroxybiphenyl-3,3′-dicarboxylic acid) that undergoes self-activation and dynamic surface reconstruction during OER. In situ spectroscopic investigations combined with electrochemical analysis reveal dynamic transformation between the initial MOF skeleton and the surface CoOOH active phase under operating potentials. This dynamic surface reconstruction accelerates charge-transfer kinetics while preserving structural integrity. The resulting electrode delivers 100 mA cm–2 at an overpotential of 387 mV while maintaining stable operation for 300 h and 4000 cycles. This work proposes self-activation combined with dynamic surface reconstruction as a strategy to achieve durable MOF electrocatalysts.

items.title:
Crystal Structure
and Bioinspired Reactivity of an
Ambient-Stable Mononuclear Copper(III)-Azide Complex
items.abstract: Abstract The synthesis, stabilization, and structural characterization of high-valent copper complexes are critical for understanding biological and chemical oxidation processes and for developing new catalytic transformations. Herein, we report the ambient generation of a novel terminal mononuclear CuIII–N3 complex supported by a dicarboxamide ligand, H2L (H2L = N,N′-(2,6-diisopropylphenyl)-2,6-pyridinedicarboxamide). The electronic and structural features of the terminal azide ligand play a crucial role in controlling the stability and reactivity of the CuIII-complex. The high-valent complex [(L)CuIII(N3)] (2) was prepared from Bu4N[(L)CuII(N3)] (1) through a one-electron oxidation process. Both complexes 1 and 2 were characterized by X-ray crystallography and UV–vis, 1H/13C NMR, FT-IR, and EPR spectroscopies, and ESI-MS. The single-crystal X-ray structure of 2─a rare example of a crystallographically characterized mononuclear CuIII–N3 complex─revealed shortened Cu–N bond distances (Cu–Navg. = 1.878(2) vs 1.972(1) Å). Fascinatingly, 2 performed direct azidation of very strong C–H bonds in hydrocarbons (e.g.; cyclohexane). We found that complex 2 drives hydrocarbon azidation via hydrogen atom abstraction or basicity-driven PCET and a subsequent radical-capture mechanism. 2 also exhibited aldehyde deformylation, and phenol and phosphine oxidation reactions. Our results found a very interesting new class of metal oxidant with diverse bioinspired reactivity profile.

items.title:
Multi-Emission
Regulated by Coordination Bonding and
Protonation in Chiral Hybrid Zinc(II) Halides for Circularly Polarized
Luminescence and Anticounterfeiting
items.abstract: Abstract Luminescent hybrid metal halides (HMHs) have emerged as promising platforms for circularly polarized luminescence (CPL); however, their rational design remains challenging due to the limited understanding of the relationship between structural chirality and the luminescence dissymmetry factor (glum). Herein, using chiral 2,2′-bipyridine-based enantiomers and by modulating the synthesis pathways, two pairs of chiral Zn(II) hybrids ([Zn(R/S-L)3][ZnBr4] (R-HH-1/S-HH-1) and [H2R/S-L][ZnBr4] (R-HH-2/S-HH-2)) were synthesized. In R-HH-1/S-HH-1, [Zn(R/S-L)3] node adopts Λ- and Δ-enantiomorphic configurations, R-HH-1/S-HH-1 exhibited blue fluorescence and green room-temperature phosphorescence (RTP). The luminescence of R-HH-2/S-HH-2 is dominated by green self-trapped exciton (STE) emission. Importantly, these two pairs of chiral HMHs have high glum values; especially, the glum values of R-HH-2/S-HH-2 are +12.23 × 10–3 and −11.68 × 10–3, improved by the hierarchical chiral hydrogen-bonding networks. Meanwhile, these HMHs exhibit photochromic properties for anticounterfeiting. This work provides an approach for the design of high-performance chiroptical HMHs.

items.title:
Photoswitching in P-Centered Biradicaloid–
and Tetraradicaloid–Group 4 Metallocene Hybrids
items.abstract: Abstract Biradical(oid)s are key intermediates in the formation and cleavage of chemical bonds, and their application as molecular switches is of particular interest. In contrast, tetraradical(oid)s remain far less explored, although they may, for example, consist of two biradical(oid) units. Herein, we report the synthesis of phosphorus-centered bi- and tetraradicaloids coordinated to group 4 metallocene fragments of titanium and zirconium. The target compounds were obtained via ring-expansion reactions of metallocene-substituted isonitriles with one or two equivalents of the biradicaloid [P(μ-NTer)]2, affording group 4 metallocene complexes bearing one or two bridged P-centered, five-membered heterocyclic biradicaloid units. These systems function as mono- and double-molecular switches, respectively, each based on a biradicaloid motif. Upon irradiation with light (638 nm), the biradicaloid heterocycles undergo transannular bond formation in one or both five-membered heterocyclic biradicaloid units, resulting in the generation of housane-type species. The photoinduced switching behavior as well as CO2 activation were investigated in solution by NMR and UV/Vis spectroscopy. Quantum-chemical calculations were further performed to examine the design of the isonitrile ligands, the mechanism of their insertion reactions, and the electronic structure and photoswitching behavior, supporting the experimental findings.

items.title:
Red-Light-Driven
Ru(II) Photocatalysts Enable Dual
Oxidation of NADH and Glutathione in Living Cells
items.abstract: Abstract Intracellular photocatalysis has emerged as a promising strategy to disrupt cancer redox homeostasis, yet most photoredox systems remain limited by oxygen dependence and deactivation by intracellular thiols, particularly glutathione (GSH). Here we report PEGylated Ru(II) terpyridine complexes that function as visible-light photocatalysts, and catalytically oxidize both NADH and GSH through complementary Type I and Type II pathways. The complexes exhibit broad visible-light absorption, aqueous stability, and activity in biologically relevant media. Stern–Volmer quenching experiments and electrochemical studies are consistent with excited-state electron transfer from NADH and GSH, while ROS studies reveal singlet oxygen, superoxide, and hydrogen peroxide during catalysis. Unexpectedly, glutathione enhances rather than suppresses photocatalytic activity, supporting its participation in catalyst turnover. NADH oxidation is maintained in oxygen-limited solution. In cancer cells, red-light irradiation disrupts the intracellular NAD+/NADH balance, depletes glutathione, and amplifies oxidative stress, resulting in selective photocytotoxicity. Comparative studies further reveal that intracellular performance depends not only on catalytic efficiency in solution but also on catalyst photostability and accessibility to cellular redox pools. Together, these findings establish terpyridine-based Ru(II) photocatalysts as an effective strategy for disrupting intracellular redox balance and provide new insight into glutathione-assisted photocatalysis in biological systems.

items.title:
Terminal Atom
Effects on Magnetic Relaxation Rates
in Uranium(V) “Single-Molecule Magnets”
items.abstract: Abstract The success of lanthanide-based single-molecule magnets (SMMs) has not yet been matched by their actinide counterparts, despite large calculated barriers to magnetic relaxation. Existing studies often conclude that standard multiconfigurational methods cannot accurately predict the magnetic relaxation barrier, but these models represent only a static picture of magnetic relaxation. Here, we perform the first ab initio calculations of spin-phonon coupling and magnetic relaxation in actinide SMMs, studying [UV(TrenTIPS)(E)] (TrenTIPS = N(CH2CH2NSiPr3i)3), with the terminal atom systematically varied across E = N, O, F, P, S, Cl, Br. We find that changing E strongly modifies U-E bonding, crystal field splitting, and wave function composition; however, these static descriptors do not predict low-temperature magnetic relaxation. All complexes relax through the two-phonon Raman mechanism, with low-energy phonon pathways revealed through the Raman rate integrand. The [UV(TrenTIPS)(F)] complex relaxes faster despite a large excited state energy gap, while [UV(TrenTIPS)(P)] shows that the overall relaxation rate reflects the combined contributions from the Raman rate integrand. Our results demonstrate that Ueff is not an appropriate metric for assessing these systems and that spin-phonon coupling and phonon availability, rather than static electronic structure descriptors alone, are central to understanding magnetic relaxation in this family of actinide complexes.

items.title:
Enhanced Antithermal
Quenching of Hybrid Pb(II)- and
Bi(III)-Based Metal Halides for Phosphor-Converted Light-Emitting
Diodes
items.abstract: Abstract Two complexes, [(BrPhen)PbCl2] (1) and [(BrPhen)2BiCl3] (2), were solvothermally assembled by utilizing 3,8-dibromo-1,10-phenanthroline (BrPhen). 1 suffers 36.9% luminescence quenching at 150 °C, while 2 maintains high thermal stability with just 8.2% emission loss. The anti-TQ performance of 2 is comparable to those of several reported inorganic luminescent materials. In addition, phosphor-converted LED devices were fabricated, which exhibit stable light emission under high-power operation.

items.title:
Metastable
Adducts as a Route to Silver Thiolate Processing
on the Way to New Thiorenes: Structural, Spectroscopy, and Computational
Data
items.abstract: Abstract Metal–organic chalcogenides (MOCs) represent an emerging class of organic–inorganic compounds that exhibit remarkable semiconductor and luminescent properties that can be finely tuned by varying the organic ligands. In this work, we investigate previously unreported polymeric silver thiolates, [Ag(S-ArF)]n (where ArF = a polyfluorinated aryl group). We demonstrate that the recrystallization of these compounds from pyridine and its derivatives (py-R) affords crystalline 1D coordination polymers (CPs) based on [(py-R)Ag(S-ArF)]n chains. Through this approach, we prepared 17 novel complexes, which were structurally characterized by single-crystal X-ray diffraction (SCXRD). A majority of these complexes (14 of 17) are infinite, ribbon-like polymers formed by the lateral association of two [(py-R)Ag(S-ArF)]n chains. These structures predominantly feature argentophilic interactions ranging from infinite Ag···Ag chains to isolated dimers. Furthermore, quantum chemical calculations predict semiconducting behavior for these materials. Notably, bulk [(py-R)Ag(S-ArF)]n MOCs slowly lose their coordinated pyridine molecules, yielding polymeric [Ag(S-ArF)]n that adopts a 2D structure analogous to the [Ag(S-Ph)]n (“thiorene”) network. Finally, the practical utility of the prepared complexes is demonstrated in the design of novel photoluminescent coatings based on [Ag(S-ArF)]n thin films.

items.title:
Chemical Origins
of Line Broadening in the f–f
Transitions of a Molecular Yb(III) Complex
items.abstract: Abstract Lanthanide molecular complexes are promising platforms for quantum information science (QIS), where narrow optical line widths are essential for coherent light–matter interaction. Rational design of such color centers requires understanding how the chemical environment sets the line width, yet predictive modeling of lanthanide electronic structure remains challenging. Here we compute the energy gaps and line widths of f–f optical transitions in a model Yb(III) solvate, Yb(2Me–THF)3Cl3, using CASSCF/NEVPT2 and compare them with high-resolution absorption spectra. We simulate broadening by scanning the PES along all 150 normal modes and by conformational sampling of the ligand environment. The simulated envelopes reproduce the main features of the experimental spectrum and can be decomposed into contributions from individual nuclear motions. Our analysis shows that the broadening is set by fluctuations of the ligand field and is dominated by low-frequency collective motions of the first coordination sphere. We further find that 4f energy gaps are highly sensitive to the Yb-ligand bond distances, and that oscillator strength varies nonmonotonically with geometry, so that brighter transitions need not be broader. These results suggest that spectral broadening in molecular Yb(III) absorbers may be reduced by ligand designs that fix the first coordination sphere and limit conformational freedom.

items.title:
Structural
Dimensional Regulation in Organic Copper(I)
Chloride Family based on Same Building Unit
items.abstract: Abstract Systematic dimensional regulation of low-dimensional metal halides remains challenging for establishing clear dimension–property relationships because changes in dimensionality are often accompanied by variations in chemical composition or inorganic building units. Herein, we realize systematic dimensionality regulation across 0D (DMP)2Cu2Cl6, 1D (DMP)Cu2Cl4, and 2D (DMP)Cu2Cl4 through a solvent-mediated structural engineering strategy, while preserving the same organic cation and local [Cu2Cl6] dimer building unit. This homologous series enables a more direct correlation between framework connectivity and structural and photophysical properties, including Cu···Cu contacts, band gaps, and photoluminescence associated with self-trapped excitons. The three compounds exhibit distinct Cu···Cu contacts and emission profiles, highlighting the influence of structural dimensionality and local coordination environments on their photoluminescence behavior.

items.title:
Mechanistic
Insights into Nicotinamidase by CoII EPR Spectroscopy
items.abstract: Abstract Nicotinamidases catalyze the metal-dependent hydrolysis of nicotinamide in the NAD+ salvage pathway in most nonmammalian organisms. Their essential role in pathogenic bacteria, but not mammals, has made them an attractive target for new antibiotic treatments. Most of the characterized nicotinamidases rely on a ZnII active site for catalysis, which has limited spectroscopic studies of these enzymes. Herein, we employ CoII-substitution as a spectroscopic probe to investigate the mechanism of nicotinamidase from the pathogen Streptococcus pneumoniae (SpPncA). The CoII-substituted enzyme features a spin S = 3/2 EPR signal with resolved hyperfine splitting consistent with a five-coordinate metal center. Analysis of a conserved second-sphere Asp9 residue via site-directed mutagenesis reveals an unexpected role in maintaining the geometry of the metal coordination site through an extended network of electrostatic interactions. Characterization of substrate, intermediate, product, and inhibitor-bound complexes demonstrates that subtle changes in the ligand impact the rhombicity of the EPR spectrum. Leveraging these spectroscopic features, we characterize a catalytically relevant thioester intermediate formed during turnover with nicotinamide for the first time. Together, these results provide new mechanistic insights into nicotinamidase catalysis.

items.title:
Regio- and
Stereoselective Dimerization of Arylalkynes
Mediated by a Transient Zinc Radical
items.abstract: Abstract Vinyl radicals are crucial intermediates in synthetic chemistry that readily undergo a range of well-established transformations, such as hydrogen atom transfer and cyclization. Herein, we report a distinct reaction mode in which vinyl radicals, generated from the attack of a transient zinc radical on an alkyne, are diverted toward selective dimerization to form a diene. Reaction of the dizinc compound (DIPPNacnacZn)2 (DIPPNacnac = [(DIPPNCMe)2CH]−; DIPP = 2,6-iPr2C6H3) with 1-phenylpropyne under UV irradiation affords a (Z,E)-2,5-dizincated-2,4-hexadiene derivative with high regio- and stereoselectivity. This transformation is also applicable to a variety of substituted 1-arylpropynes, yielding the corresponding diene products, although replacement of the methyl group with bulkier substituents (e.g., tert-butyl and trimethylsilyl) directs the reaction pathway toward 1,2-addition of the Zn–Zn unit across the alkyne. Mechanistic investigations involving radical trapping and radical clock experiments support a pathway initiated by the addition of a zinc radical to the alkyne, generating a β-zincated vinyl radical intermediate that subsequently undergoes selective dimerization. Complementary density functional theory calculations further elucidate the mechanistic details and the origins of selectivity in this reaction.

items.title:
Reconstructing
the Hydrogen-Bonded Network on an IrNi
Sponge for the Alkaline Oxygen Evolution Reaction
items.abstract: Abstract Precise regulation of the interfacial hydrogen-bonded network is critical for enhancing both electrocatalytic activity and long-term stability in the oxygen evolution reaction (OER). Herein, we successfully construct a flexible, metallic fibrous IrNi sponge that effectively reshapes the hydrogen-bonded network, thereby improving alkaline OER performance. The resulting IrNi sponge achieves a low overpotential of 270 mV at 200 mA cm–2 and maintains this current density for over 100 h in 1.0 M KOH, significantly outperforming the Ni sponge and IrO2/Ni sponge. When integrated as the anode in an anion exchange membrane water electrolyzer, the system achieves 0.5 A cm–2 at 1.65 V and exhibits remarkably stable operation for 500 h. Mechanistic investigations reveal that the in situ-generated Lewis acid sites (Irδ+) within the IrNi sponge reinforce the interfacial hydrogen-bonded network. This strengthened network facilitates OH– diffusion and lowers the energy barrier of the rate-determining step (*O → *OOH), thereby markedly enhancing the OER activity. This work underscores the importance of Lewis acid sites in regulating the hydrogen-bonded network and offers a viable design strategy for achieving high-current-density, durable catalysts for water electrolysis.

items.title: Cyanide Photodissociation from the Site-Differentiated [4Fe-4S]1+ Cluster of Pyrococcus furiosus Ferredoxin Characterized by EPR and 13C/15N ENDOR
items.abstract: Abstract Ferredoxin (Fd) from the hyperthermophilic archaeon Pyrococcus furiosus (Pf), Pf-Fd, functions in electron transfer, serving to transfer an electron from various oxidoreductases to an H2-evolving, membrane-bound hydrogenase. The [4Fe-4S] cluster of Pf-Fd is coordinated by three cysteine residues and the carboxylate group of an aspartate residue. Recently, we have found that several such site-differentiated [4Fe-4S]1+ clusters are photoactive, inspiring us to investigate the photoreactivity of the site-differentiated [4Fe-4S]1+ cluster in Pf-Fd. We show here through X-band EPR and 13C/15N Q-band ENDOR studies that visible-light irradiation of the cyanide-bound [4Fe-4S]1+ cluster of Pf-Fd, Pf-Fd-CN, at 12 K results in photodissociation of the cyanide anion, which geminately recombines only upon annealing to 150 K. In addition, this work revisits our previous CW 13C/15N ENDOR studies of Pf-Fd-CN with pulsed-ENDOR techniques. Of particular note, we definitively determine the absolute sign of the 13C hyperfine coupling with the PESTRE pulsed-ENDOR protocol and from this draw inferences about Fe valence localization within the cyanide-bound cluster.

items.title:
Unconventional
Antiferromagnets - Beyond Conventional
Antiferromagnets
items.abstract: Abstract Antiferromagnets are an important class of magnetically ordered materials due to compensation of the magnetic moments. They are increasingly important for emerging spintronic technologies, as they can enable greater data density, faster devices, and new functionality. Traditionally, the magnetic-moment compensation arises from symmetry constraints (translation and inversion). Recently, several new paradigms enabling the development of antiferromagnets have emerged and are discussed in this Viewpoint. These include compensated ferrimagnets, altermagnets, and artificial/synthetic antiferromagnets as well as antiferromagnetically ordered ferri- and ferromagnets, as they offer additional pathways to discover new antiferromagnets with new phenomena and technologically important attributes. Additionally, the magnetic ordering Néel temperature, TN, is frequently reported as the maximum temperature in the susceptibility, χ(T), data; however, the maximum temperature in the d[χ(T)T]/dT data (so-called Fisher specific heat) is in better agreement with the specific-heat determined TN and is preferred.

items.title:
Enhancing
the Hydrogen Evolution Performance of WC
via Microstructure Engineering
items.abstract: Abstract Tungsten carbide (WC) is considered an ideal electrode material for hydrogen evolution reactions (HER) due to its platinum-like d-band density of states (DOS) at the Fermi level. However, achieving high performance for HER always requires modifying WC by doping or compositing, which results in a complicated process and complex samples. This study proposes constructing microstructures in WC via a one-step high pressure and high temperature (HPHT) method to modify the HER activity. The locally distorted lattice is captured in WC under 1 GPa and 600 °C (WC-1–600), which delivers optimal HER performance of 106 mV and 125 mV at 10 mA cm–2 in acidic and alkaline electrolytes, respectively. It is only about 44.2% and 69.8% of pure WC (WC-initial) in acidic and alkaline electrolytes, respectively. It can operate stably for more than 70 and 100 h under acidic and alkaline electrolytes. The excellent HER performance of WC-1–600 is attributed to that the distorted lattice rearranging the surface electron distribution, reducing the adsorption ability of H atoms, and promoting the reaction dynamics of HER. The findings offer a new insight into optimizing catalyst performance by microstructure engineering through HPHT technology applications in electrocatalysis research.

items.title:
Engineering
Interface and Orientation to Construct
BNNS/LM Heterostructures with High Thermal Conductivity and Electrical
Insulation for Improved Phonon Transport
items.abstract: Abstract The synergistic optimization of high thermal conductivity and electrical insulation is a key challenge in thermal interface materials (TIMs). Conventional ceramic-based composites are inherently incapable of reconciling the contradictory demands of thermal conduction, electrical insulation, and low brittleness, while liquid metal fillers are plagued by poor interfacial compatibility and the risk of leakage. To address these issues, a synergistic strategy integrating molecular interfacial modification and microstructural alignment is developed to construct boron nitride nanosheets (BNNS)/liquid metal (LM) heterostructures. Using H2O2-assisted chlorosulfonic acid intercalation, h-BN is efficiently exfoliated and hydroxylated. Thiomalic acid (TMA) serves as a bridge, achieving uniform LM anchoring on BNNS and preventing LM leakage at a high loading of 42 wt %. A pressure-induced orientation is further applied to vertically align BNNS/LM hybrids, generating preferentially oriented and interconnected thermally conductive networks. The resulting composite exhibits an out-of-plane thermal conductivity of 17.76 W m–1 K–1, while maintaining good electrical insulation with an electrical resistivity exceeding 6 × 109 Ω m. LED tests show that this material reduces LED chip temperature by 16.7 °C compared to a commercial thermal pad. This cross-scale synergistic strategy provides a material design solution that combines high thermal conductivity and electrical safety for thermal management of high-power-density electronic devices.

items.title:
Tuning the
Photoinduced Magnetic Coupling in Terbium
Porphyrazines: The Effect of Thiadiazole Electron-Withdrawing Groups
and an Asymmetric Secondary Coordination Environment
items.abstract: Abstract Modulating intramolecular magnetic interactions between localized 4f electrons and delocalized photoexcited macrocyclic π-systems (J–L interaction) provides a strategy for designing magneto-optical materials. However, the effects of ligand electronic structure and asymmetric coordination environments remain poorly understood. Here, we report the synthesis and magneto-optical properties of an asymmetric terbium(III) complex featuring a thiadiazole electron-withdrawing group (EWG)-containing porphyrazine ligand and an acetylacetonate ligand, [TbTTDPz(acac)(DMF)(H2O)]. Variable-temperature, variable-field magnetic circular dichroism (VTVH-MCD) spectroscopy at the Q-band confirms parallel-type J–L coupling. A comparative analysis with the symmetric [TbPc(cyclen)]Cl analogue suggests that the asymmetric environment contributes to reduced ligand-centered orbital angular momentum (Lz(π) = 1.5), while the thiadiazole substitution enhances the J–L interaction (ΔJL = 1.5 cm–1). Multiconfigurational and DFT calculations demonstrate that explicitly including acac π orbitals in the active space is essential for accurately evaluating Lz(π) and ΔJL, as its highest occupied orbital resides in close energetic proximity to the TTDPz HOMO, facilitating hybridization. Spatial distribution analyses reveal that the thiadiazole EWG creates an electropositive core, forcing the excited-state LUMOs to contract inward. This maximizes spatial overlap with the lanthanide center to enhance the J–L interaction. Thus, modifying the primary π-framework and the asymmetric secondary coordination environment enables systematic tuning of J–L interactions.

items.title: Issue Publication Information
Issue Editorial Masthead

Stabilization
of Diatomic Interhalogens by Lewis Bases
items.abstract: Abstract Computational studies reveal significant stabilization of diatomic interhalogen complexes BrCl, ICl, IBr with respect to complexes with homonuclear dihalogens both in the gas phase and in nonaqueous solutions. This opens an easy pathway for the synthesis of interhalogen complexes by mixing halogens in the presence of Lewis bases. The approach was experimentally verified by the synthesis of a series of interhalogen complexes with HMTA (IBr, ICl, BrCl) and pyridine (IBr, ICl) directly from elemental halogens. The IBr·HMTA and (IBr)2·HMTA complexes were structurally characterized by single-crystal X-ray diffraction. The remaining complexes were identified by powder X-ray diffraction.

items.title:
Synergistic
Assembly of High-Symmetry Motifs Enhances
Nonlinear Optical Response in the Chromium-Based Thiophosphates ACrP2S7 (A = K, Rb, Cs)
items.abstract: Abstract Transition-metal chalcogenides represent promising candidates for nonlinear optical (NLO) materials, yet Cr-based ones remain largely unexplored owing to the challenge of simultaneously achieving suitable electronic structures and noncentrosymmetric structures. Herein, we report the reactive flux assisted solid-state synthesis of a series of thiophosphates ACrP2S7 (A = K, Rb, Cs) and systematically investigate their structural chemistry and optical properties. All compounds crystallize in the polar monoclinic space group C2 and feature a layered structure composed of distorted [CrS6] octahedra and [P2S7] dimers, which cooperatively construct low-symmetric [CrP2S11] motifs. Structural analysis reveals that the polar structure can be derived from the centrosymmetric CrPS4 through symmetry breaking via insertion of A+ ions. The band gaps of ACrP2S7 are tunable in the range of 1.22–1.27 eV, and the second-harmonic generation measurements confirm that ACrP2S7 represents the first Cr-based chalcogenide exhibiting significant NLO activity (0.3–0.8 × AgGaS2). This work suggests that Cr-based thiophosphates can also be explored as promising infrared NLO materials.

items.title:
Coordination-Site
Engineering of Porphyrin COFs for
Laser Ignition and Combustion Catalysis of Ammonium Perchlorate
items.abstract: Abstract Rapid laser ignition and efficient subsequent combustion require distinct additive properties, yet integrating both into a single material remains challenging. Here, a Cu/Co-coordinated porphyrin-based covalent organic framework (Cu/Co-Tapp-Phen-COF) was constructed to combine photoresponse with AP decomposition catalysis. The framework was synthesized from premetalated Cu-Tapp, followed by postsynthetic Co coordination at the Phen sites. Metal incorporation modifies the framework’s electronic environment while preserving its ordered structure. Cu/Co-Tapp-Phen-COF exhibits enhanced O2•– generation under 808 nm irradiation and promotes AP thermal decomposition, lowering its high-temperature decomposition peak from 431.1 to 350.6 °C and the apparent activation energy from 224.14 to 144.50 kJ mol–1, accompanied by earlier gas evolution. AP/Cu/Co-Tapp-Phen-COF achieves an ignition delay of approximately 3.5 ms and a combustion duration of 2.08 ± 0.05 s. Mechanistic analysis indicates that photoinduced O2•– contributes to laser ignition, while metal-coordinated sites promote AP thermal decomposition and subsequent combustion. These findings demonstrate that coordination-site engineering is an effective strategy for integrating photoresponse and combustion catalysis within a single COF.

items.title:
Modulation
of Mechanical Properties in Ti3AlC2 via B Substitution
and Charge-Compensation-Induced
Carbon Vacancies
items.abstract: Abstract Tuning the intrinsic bonding and mechanical behavior of MAX phases is crucial for tailoring their performance. In this work, a series of Ti3AlC2–xBx MAX phase ceramics were fabricated via spark plasma sintering, and we systematically investigated the effects of B substitution on their crystal structure, bonding characteristics, and mechanical properties through a combination of experiments and theoretical calculations. B substitution creates local electronic imbalance within the M–X layers, which in turn promotes carbon vacancy formation via charge compensation process. The interplay between B incorporation and Cv formation induces further structural relaxation and charge redistribution. As a result, the resistance to elastic failure and plastic deformation failure is enhanced by 27.6% and 76.0%, respectively, under the synergistic influence of M–X bonds and Cv. However, under high B concentrations, excessive Cv accumulation destabilizes the Ti3C2 layers and drives the formation of Ti2AlC. Overall, this work systematically unravels how B substitution modifies the Ti3AlC2 structure, offering valuable insights into the regulation of X-site chemistry and bonding in MAX phases.

items.title:
Correction
to “Revisiting the Cocktail Effect
in High-Entropy Layered Double Hydroxides: Linear Additivity Rather
than Emergent Behavior”

Murine Aβ4–x Peptides Retain
High-Affinity Redox-Silent Cu2+ Binding
items.abstract: Abstract β-Amyloid peptides N-truncated at Phe4 (Aβ4–x) contain an amino-terminal Cu- and Ni-binding (ATCUN) motif that can form high-affinity, redox-silent Cu2+ complexes. Human Aβ4–40/42 is present in the brains of individuals with and without Alzheimer’s disease, and soluble Aβ4–9 can be generated by neprilysin proteolysis of Aβ1–40/42 in vitro. These observations led to the proposal that Aβ4–x may be functional Cu2+-binding peptides. Because amyloid precursor protein is constitutively expressed in mammals, this study assessed whether murine Aβ4–x peptides retain the properties of the human analogues. Cu2+ coordination, binding affinity, and redox activity were compared for murine and human Aβ4–9 and Aβ4–16. The murine peptides formed Cu2+ complexes with spectroscopic parameters closely matching those of the human peptides. Competitive binding against glycylglycylhistidine gave conditional Cu2+ dissociation constants at pH 7.4 of 3–4 fM for murine Aβ4–x and 8–10 fM for human Aβ4–x. All Cu(Aβ4–x) complexes were redox-silent in an aminophenyl fluorescein/ascorbate assay. Thus, murine Aβ4–x has the chemical capacity required for a Cu2+-binding role if generated in vivo. However, because endogenous murine Aβ4–x has not been detected in wild-type mice, the present findings challenge the support for a broadly conserved physiological role for Aβ4–x in mammalian Cu2+ handling.

items.title:
Pillared-Layer
Heterometallic Zn/Cd MOF for Natural
Gas Upgrading and C3–C4 Hydrocarbon Recovery
items.abstract: Abstract Developing stable adsorbents for the separation of light hydrocarbons from natural gas is critical for methane purification and high-value C3/C4 hydrocarbon recovery. Herein we report a stable heterometallic Zn/Cd pillared-layer MOF (LIFM-268) featuring a doubly interpenetrated structure with unique hourglass-shaped Zn2Cd node. LIFM-268 exhibits outstanding thermal and chemical stability. Gas adsorption measurements reveal that its adsorption uptakes, isosteric heats of adsorption, and adsorption selectivities for C2–C4 hydrocarbons all far exceed those of CH4, following the order n-C4H10 &gt; C3H8 &gt; C2H6 &gt; CH4. Crucially, dynamic breakthrough experiments using ternary and quinary simulated natural gas confirm that LIFM-268 can directly produce high-purity methane while efficiently capturing C3/C4 components. The material demonstrates excellent recyclability over five adsorption–regeneration cycles. Furthermore, theoretical simulations elucidate that the superior separation performance arises from abundant strong host–guest interactions, specifically C–H···O and C–H···π forces between long-chain alkanes and the framework built from aromatic ligands and trinuclear metal nodes. This work provides a promising adsorbent candidate for industrial natural gas upgrading and offers structural insights into the design of heterometallic MOFs for light hydrocarbon separation.

items.title:
Nanoceria
as an Acid–Base Catalyst for Interfacial
Hydrolysis of Sulfonylureas: A Combined 31P MAS NMR and
DFT Study
items.abstract: Abstract Understanding coordination-driven bond activation at metal oxide interfaces is essential for predicting the chemical stability of complex organic molecules. Here, we demonstrate that nanoceria efficiently drives the spontaneous, dark hydrolysis of sulfonylureas (amidosulfuron, metsulfuron-methyl, and nicosulfuron) via surface acid–base chemistry under ambient conditions. By combining liquid chromatography–mass spectrometry (LC-HRMS) with density functional theory (DFT) calculations, we show that the degradation proceeds through urea N–C bond cleavage. While the experimental identification of the degradation products confirms the overall hydrolytic pathway, DFT calculations are used to provide unique insights into the specific mechanism, proposing that the reaction is initiated by lattice-oxygen nucleophilic attack leading preferentially to sulfonyl-side N–C bond cleavage. Crucially, solid-state 31P MAS NMR spectroscopy using a trimethylphosphine oxide probe explicitly mapped the distribution and strength of surface Lewis and Brønsted acidic sites (oxygen vacancies and bridging hydroxyls). This provides a molecular-level link between ceria defect structures and their unique interfacial reactivity, highlighting the potential of tailored ceria surfaces to drive spontaneous chemical transformations without external energy inputs.

items.title:
pH-Guided
Design of Cu(II) Phosphonopropionate Coordination
Polymers: Synthesis, Structures, Proton Conductivity, and Catalytic
Properties
items.abstract: Abstract A series of new Cu(II) phosphonopropionate coordination polymers (CPs) was obtained from reaction of CuCl2 and H3PPA (3-phosphonopropionic acid) in water under reflux conditions at different pH values (2, 3, 4, and 6). The resulting compounds, formulated as [Cu(μ4-HPPA)(μ-H2O)]n (Cu@pH2), [Cu(μ4-HPPA)(H2O)]n (Cu@pH3), [Cu(μ5-HPPA)]n (Cu@pH4), and [Cu2(PPA)(OH)]n·3nH2O (Cu@pH6), were isolated as stable microcrystalline solids and fully characterized. The crystal structures of the first three compounds were solved from laboratory powder X-ray diffraction data. Their pH-guided structural differences are related to coordination modes of the bridging or terminal water ligand (or its absence), as well as to bridging modes of μ4-HPPA2–/μ5-HPPA2– blocks, resulting in 2D layers with 4,6L26, sql, or 5,5L4 topologies. Proton transport properties of the obtained compounds were investigated, revealing the highest proton conductivity for Cu@pH6 (1.2 × 10–3 S·cm–1 at 90 °C and 95% relative humidity), with proton transport occurring predominantly through a water-mediated Grotthuss-type mechanism. In addition, Cu(II) phosphonopropionates were screened as efficient catalysts in the mild oxidation of cycloalkanes and propane. The effects of different reaction parameters, substrate scope and selectivity features were investigated. The present study expands the family of Cu(II) phosphonate CPs and highlights the prospective use of these compounds in proton conduction and catalysis.

items.title:
Kinetic Studies
of Oxidative Addition to Well-Defined
[Pd0(NHC)(PhC≡CPh)] Complexes (NHC = N-Heterocyclic
Carbene)
items.abstract: Abstract The kinetics of oxidative addition (OA) of 4-chlorobenzotrifluoride to a well-defined Pd0-NHC complex, [Pd(IPr)(PhC≡CPh)], has been investigated using electrochemical techniques. The influence of the concentration of the substrate and added amounts of the weakly coordinating ligand on kobs have been studied. The resulting OA product has been isolated and full characterized and is a dimeric species. Additionally, evidence supports a “cocktail-type” catalysis and the reductive elimination of the NHC ligand from the Pd center as a possible decomposition pathway. Finally, the influence of eight different NHC ligands on the oxidative addition has been evaluated.

items.title:
Correction
to “Solvation Ion Volumes from Solution
Densities”

Site-Dependent
Crystal Fields of Nd3+,
Er3+, and Yb3+ in the Chalcogenide Perovskite
BaZrS3: Spectroscopic and Magnetic Signatures from Embedded-Cluster
CASSCF/NEVPT2 Calculations
items.abstract: Abstract BaZrS3 doped with Nd3+, Er3+, or Yb3+ shows structured near-infrared emission whose interpretation requires distinguishing the local coordination environments. Embedded-cluster CASSCF/NEVPT2 calculations with spin–orbit coupling in the complete 4fn configuration space compare Nd3+, Er3+, and Yb3+ in six-coordinate Zr-site and eight-coordinate Ba-site models, and breathing-coordinate scans quantify the sensitivity to the local Ln–S distance. Validation on Cs2NaLnCl6 shows that the complete state space brings the Er3+4I13/2 and 4I11/2 energies to within 0.5% of experiment, where the highest-multiplicity restriction leaves larger, multiplet-dependent errors.
