The two sites give comparable ground-multiplet widths but contrasting level patterns: the Zr-site ligand field is dominated by rank-four terms and the Ba-site field by rank-two terms, with opposite responses to the local bond length. Published low-temperature emission data are compatible with a Zr-like environment for the dominant Er3+ and Nd3+ emitters and, tentatively, a contracted Ba-like environment for the broadest Yb3+ population; ground-doublet g-tensors and susceptibilities provide discriminants for EPR and magnetometry, and restricted-active-space calculations calibrated on Er3+ in LaCl3 show that, within the static electronic models, the electric-dipole strength of Er3+ and Yb3+ is symmetry-suppressed at the Zr site whereas the Ba-site ions acquire a forced electric-dipole channel of comparable or larger strength.

items.title:
Ionic Association
in LaCl3·7H2O/MgCl2·6H2O Mixed Molten Salt
Hydrates and Their Contributions to Dehydration and Energy Conservation
items.abstract: Abstract The dynamic solvation structures of concentrated electrolyte systems, especially mixed molten salt hydrates (MSHs), govern their thermal properties and dehydration pathways. The multilevel coordination geometries formed by cations, anions, and water molecules in MSHs directly determine thermal stability and dehydration reactivity. Herein, we characterize the dehydration process of LaCl3·7H2O/MgCl2·6H2O mixed MSHs via combined experimental measurements and first-principles simulations. Three mixed molar ratios are investigated: n(MgCl2·6H2O):n(LaCl3·7H2O) = 5:1 (denoted Mg5La1), 1:1 (Mg1La1), and 1:5 (Mg1La5). Raman spectroscopy, thermogravimetric-differential scanning calorimetry (TG-DSC), vacuum in situ high-temperature X-ray powder diffraction (XRD), and ab initio molecular dynamics (AIMD) based on density functional theory (DFT) are integrated to unravel ion–ion interaction mechanisms and structural evolution during dehydration. Experimental results confirm distinct ionic association modes among La3+, Mg2+, and Cl– in mixed MSHs, which cannot be observed in single-component LaCl3·7H2O or MgCl2·6H2O melts. Elevated temperature breaks intermolecular water hydrogen bonds and increases Cl– coordination numbers around La3+; both La3+ and Mg2+ capture free Cl– to form heteronuclear bridging aggregates, which alter dehydration thermodynamics and kinetics. Coordination interactions between La3+, Mg2+, and Cl– collectively lower the dehydration onset temperature and reduce total dehydration heat absorption. All mixed MSH samples exhibit lower dehydration temperatures than single-component LaCl3·7H2O or MgCl2·6H2O. In situ vacuum XRD verifies that crystalline anhydrous LaCl3 and MgCl2 initially form at 150 °C for Mg1La5 mixtures. DSC results demonstrate that the dehydration enthalpy of Mg1La5 is merely 75% relative to that of LaCl3·7H2O on a per-unit-mass basis. The coordinated heteronuclear La–Cl–Mg cluster structure suppresses MgCl2 hydrolysis by consuming free Cl– and inhibiting HCl release, which mitigates MgO impurity formation. This structural regulation strategy provides a feasible route for low-temperature, hydrolysis-free preparation of mixed anhydrous LaCl3/MgCl2.

items.title: Caffeinated- N -Heterocyclic Carbene Ligand at Play in a Molecular H2-Evolving Cobalt Electrocatalyst
items.abstract: Abstract In this work, we implemented a proton-responsive caffeine wingtip at the strong sigma-donor N-heterocyclic carbene (NHC) ligand in a new cobalt complex C-2 for the hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) with various proton sources. The NHC ligand is expected to boost the hydricity of the Co–H bond for the reaction with H+. In parallel, the proton-responsive functionality of the caffeine wingtip should help in shuttling protons to the catalytic center to facilitate the formation of the Co–H bond and H2 and thereby should improve the rate of the HER. Cyclic voltammetry (CV) and controlled potential electrolysis (CPE) experiments using CH3CO2H, Et3NHBF4, and CF3CO2H as proton sources showed that C-2 was an efficient HER catalyst, achieving maximum turnover frequency (TOFmax) values in the range of 2592–13,270 s–1, Faradaic efficiency (FE) values of 75–90% at the overpotential range of 0.40–0.73 V, and turnover number (TON) values of 81–216. Detailed CV analyses highlighted some key mechanistic insights into the electron- and proton-transfer steps involved in the C-2-based catalytic cycles with acid substrates. Overall, the work supports the possibilities of HER catalyst design using biosourced ligand motifs such as caffeine and many other nucleobases with Earth-abundant transition metals.

items.title:
Molecular
Engineering of Dysprosium Complexes for
Tunable Magnetic Anisotropy and Luminescent Thermometry
items.abstract: Abstract Harnessing and tailoring spin dynamics at the molecular level is pivotal for advancing quantum information technologies and multifunctional materials. While α-diimine–Dy(III) β-diketonates have been extensively explored, β-diimine ligands remain largely unexplored as a ligand-field platform for modulating magnetic anisotropy and magneto-optical response in Dy(III) β-diketonates. Herein, we investigate β-diimine coligands as a tunable ligand-field platform in Dy(III) β-diketonate complexes, [Dy(dbm)3(bik-Et)] (1), [Dy(dbm)3(bik-Me)] (2), and [Dy(acac)3(bik-Et)] (3), where bik-R = bis(1-R-1H-imidazol-2-yl)methanone. Single-crystal X-ray diffraction reveals DyO6N2 coordination in distorted square antiprismatic (1, 3) and triangular dodecahedral (2) geometries, leading to distinct anisotropy-axis orientations. All complexes exhibit zero-field slow magnetic relaxation, and ab initio CASSCF/SINGLE_ANISO calculations reproduce Kramers doublet splitting and show qualitative correlations between coordination structure, electronic anisotropy, and relaxation pathways. Temperature-dependent photoluminescence demonstrates that these complexes function as luminescent thermometers with high relative sensitivity up to 2.98% K–1. Together, these results establish β-diimine coordination as a complementary ligand-field platform for modulating coordination geometry, Kramers-doublet structure, magnetic anisotropy, relaxation behavior, and luminescent thermometry in Dy(III) β-diketonate single-ion magnets.

items.title:
Carbon Dot
Composites Exhibiting Time-Dependent Phosphorescence
Color and Circularly Polarized Room-Temperature Phosphorescence
items.abstract: Abstract Time-dependent phosphorescence color (TDPC) materials offer a temporal dimension for information encryption, but integrating circularly polarized luminescence (CPL) into TDPC systems to achieve circularly polarized room-temperature phosphorescence (CPRTP) remains challenging. Herein, we obtain three carbon dot-based composites (RG-CDs, GB-CDs, and YG-CDs) that simultaneously exhibit TDPC and CPRTP via pyrolysis of boric acid, arginine, and selected organic dyes. After turning off a 365 nm UV lamp, RG-CDs change from red to green, GB-CDs from green to blue, and YG-CDs from yellow to green. Time-resolved phosphorescence spectra and lifetime measurements confirm that these dynamic behaviors originate from multiple emissive centers with distinct decay rates. Leveraging the synergy of TDPC and CPRTP, we demonstrate multilevel anticounterfeiting and dynamic information encryption. This work establishes a promising platform for designing carbon dot-based chiroptical systems with time-dependent optical signatures.

items.title:
Systematic
Inorganic Promoter Screening over MOF-Derived
Fe@C Catalysts for CO2 Hydrogenation to Long-Chain Hydrocarbons
items.abstract: Abstract CO2 hydrogenation to liquid hydrocarbons (C5+) via the reverse water–gas shift/Fischer–Tropsch (RWGS-FTS) tandem route represents a compelling strategy for carbon-neutral e-fuel production. Iron-based catalysts are intrinsically bifunctional for this chemistry, yet secondary inorganic promoter selection beyond potassium remains largely empirical. Here, we construct a 30-member inorganic promoter library (including noble metals, transition metals, alkaline earth metals, rare-earth lanthanides, post-transition metals, and nonmetals) coimpregnated with potassium onto a MIL-100(Fe)-derived carbon-encapsulated iron catalyst (Fe@C) and evaluate them under identical conditions. Promoter identity decisively governs iron phase evolution: high-performing promoters (Pr, Pt, Co, Mg(acetate)) facilitate the formation of Hägg carbide (χ-Fe5C2) alongside magnetite (Fe3O4), while RWGS-selective promoters (Sn, Bi, Mo, N) stabilize cementite (Fe3C). Among all tested elements, praseodymium emerges as the most effective non-noble promoter, delivering C5+-hydrocarbon performance comparable to the platinum benchmark at equal nominal loading. Complementary characterization establishes three recurring structural prerequisites for high C5+ productivity: well-dispersed nanoparticles, CO2/H2 adsorption at moderate-strength basic sites, and the Fe3O4–Fe5C2 phase combination. Notably, the promoter precursor anion (acetate, nitrate, or carbonate) is associated with substantial, cation-dependent differences in iron-phase composition and particle dispersion, identifying promoter salt chemistry as an important catalyst-design variable.

items.title:
Beyond Structural
Analogy: Electronic and Functional
Divergence in Isostructural Zr, Hf, and Th Metal–Organic Frameworks
items.abstract: Abstract Zr(IV), Hf(IV), and Th(IV) exhibit closely related coordination chemistry and can form structurally analogous materials, underpinning the widespread use of Zr as a nonradioactive surrogate for Th(IV). Here we demonstrate that such structural analogy does not necessarily extend to electronic and functional properties through a comparative study of three isostructural M6-ADC (M = Zr, Hf, and Th;ADC = 9,10-anthracenedicarboxylate) metal–organic frameworks. Despite their nearly identical framework structures, Th6-ADC exhibits optical and electronic characteristics distinct from its Zr and Hf analogues, including distinctive red coloration, extended visible-to-near-infrared absorption, and a pronounced ligand-centered radical signature. These electronic differences are further manifested in their functional behavior, with Th6-ADC displaying substantially enhanced photothermal conversion under near-infrared irradiation. These results reveal a clear divergence between structural and electronic similarity among Zr-, Hf-, and Th-based frameworks.

items.title:
Hierarchical Assembly of Gold Nanoclusters Mediated
by Kinetic Aggregation of Amphiphilic Amino Acid for Generation of
Enhanced Emission and Tunable CPL-Activity
items.abstract: Abstract Hierarchical assembly of coinage-metal nanoclusters constitutes an important strategy for constructing optical materials with advanced luminescent performance and chiroptical activities. However, it remains intractable to rationally design and direct the hierarchical assembly process that leads to the desired functionalities. Herein, hierarchical assemblies of 6-aza-2-thiothymine-protected gold nanoclusters (ATT-AuNCs) are constructed by coassembling with an amphiphilic amino acid (Fmoc-Arg) whose aggregates serve as reservoirs to control the assembly kinetics. In the presence of a proper amount of Fmoc-Arg higher than its critical aggregation concentration, dynamic coassembly can be observed, which gives rise to tassel-like and hydrangea-like aggregates. Thermodynamic and kinetic spectral analyses verify that the controlled release of Fmoc-Arg and subsequent association with ATT-AuNCs are involved in the hierarchical assembly mechanism. Moreover, the obtained tassel-like and hydrangea-like aggregates exhibit enhanced emission and chiroptical activity. By introducing rhodamine B to construct a FRET system, the emission color as well as CPL can be bathochromically shifted. The tunable optical properties endow ATT-AuNCs/Fmoc-Arg systems with potential applications in anticounterfeiting. The dynamic assembly of nanoclusters described herein controlled by the reservoir of aggregated amphiphiles represents a feasible strategy for constructing hierarchical assemblies with excellent performance.

items.title:
Multinuclearity
Effect of Yb(III) Complexes as Sensitizers
for Near-Infrared-to-Visible Triplet–Triplet Annihilation Upconversion
items.abstract: Abstract NIR-to-visible upconversion (UC) has garnered substantial attention owing to its promising applications in biomedicine and solar energy conversion. Although organo-Yb(III) complexes as photosensitizers can overcome the threshold of large anti-Stokes shifts in NIR-to-visible UC based on triplet–triplet annihilation (TTA), improving the quantum yields remains a formidable challenge. Herein, focusing on the Yb3+-complex/Rubrene coupling that emits yellow light (λem = 560 nm) under NIR excitation (980 nm), we systematically investigate the multinuclearity effect induced by three Yb(III) complex sensitizers, namely, binuclear [Yb2(Salen)2(H2Salen)Cl2(MeOH)2] (Yb-1), trinuclear [Yb3(Salen)3(HSalen)(OH)2] (Yb-2), and tetranuclear [Yb4(Salen)4(NO3)2(CO3)(DMF)2] (Yb-3). The progression from binuclear to tetranuclear architecture systematically enhances 980 nm absorbance, suppresses nonradiative loss, and improves energy transfer efficiency, culminating in a maximal upconversion intensity for tetranuclear Yb-3 (absorbance = 28.6 M–1cm–1, UC energy transfer efficiency = 4.0%, relative intensity 1.67 times larger than Yb-1 and 1.25 times large than Yb-2). This work provides key insights for the rational design of high-performance Yb3+-complex/Rubrene TTA-UC systems.

items.title:
Nanoparticle-Promoted
and Nanoparticle-Suppressed
Behavior of Pd/C Catalytic Systems Revealed by a Digital Assistant
for Electron Microscopy Data Quantification
items.abstract: Abstract Various transition metal particles on assorted carbon supports form the family of metal-on-carbon (M/C) catalysts, which are of particular importance for the chemical industry and laboratory research. Obtaining comprehensive information about the structure of these materials at different scales is essential for developing new synthesis methods, identifying potential applications, and predicting M/C properties. Although electron microscopy is a convenient method for the direct visualization of supported metal particles, the locality and specificity of such analysis can limit the establishment of relationships between the observed nanostructure and catalytic properties. This paper introduces an approach for converting local microscopy data into quantitative structural metrics for catalytic studies. A series of palladium-on-graphite (Pd/C) materials was synthesized and characterized using a digital assistant for rapid image processing, enabling a multiparametric description of the nanoscale phase through metal surface density and particle distribution parameters. Applied to Mizoroki–Heck and transfer hydrogenation reactions, these descriptors revealed nanoparticle-promoted and nanoparticle-suppressed catalytic behavior, highlighting an alternative perspective on evaluating the role of nanoscale phases in supported metal catalysts. Rather than replacing traditional structural and mechanistic approaches, this method was shown to complement them, expanding electron microscopy applications in catalytic system design.

items.title:
Bi3+/Mn2+ Codoping Regulates
Chloride Vacancies and Self-Trapped Excitons in Cs2ZrCl6 Scintillators
items.abstract: Abstract Lead-free zirconium-based halide scintillators are promising for X-ray detection and imaging owing to their structural stability, defect tolerance, and solution processability. Aliovalent doping can regulate the excited states of vacancy-ordered halide scintillators, but may also generate charge-compensating defects that promote nonradiative recombination. Here, Bi3+/Mn2+ codoping is used to control the defect and excitonic states of vacancy-ordered Cs2ZrCl6. Bi3+ substitution induces local lattice distortion and introduces Bi3+-associated excitation and radiative-decay pathways, while simultaneously increasing the tendency for chloride-vacancy formation. Temperature-dependent photoluminescence, Raman spectroscopy, and thermoluminescence measurements show that Mn2+ redistributes the trap population, suppresses deep-trap-mediated losses, and stabilizes lattice-coupled self-trapped excitons. Density functional theory calculations support an interstitial Mn2+-based charge-compensation configuration that reduces the thermodynamic tendency for chloride-vacancy formation in the Bi3+-doped lattice. Consequently, the photoluminescence quantum yield increases from 34.8% to 84.12%, and the optimized scintillator exhibits a light yield of 56,840 photons MeV–1, a detection limit of 2.84 μGy s–1, and stable radioluminescence under continuous irradiation. A multilayer flexible screen further achieves a spatial resolution of 30 lp mm–1 and enables curved-surface and underwater X-ray imaging. These results demonstrate how coupled aliovalent substitution and charge compensation regulate defect formation and self-trapped-exciton recombination in Cs2ZrCl6 scintillators.

items.title:
Immobilization
of a Carboxylated Iridium(III) Complex
on NH2-UiO-66: A Robust MOF-Based Photosensitizer
for Photodynamic Therapy
items.abstract: Abstract Photodynamic therapy (PDT) represents a promising noninvasive approach for cancer treatment; however, its therapeutic efficacy is often constrained by hypoxia within the tumor microenvironment, particularly in the highly oxygen-dependent Type II PDT system. In this study, a nanocomposite photosensitizer IrbpyCONH@UiO-66 was developed by conjugating an iridium(III) complex (IrbpyCOOH) with an amino-functionalized zirconium-based metal–organic framework NH2-UiO-66 via an amidation reaction. The material was thoroughly characterized using TEM, SEM, IR, XPS, and elemental mapping, as well as absorption and emission spectroscopy. The nanocomposite IrbpyCONH@UiO-66 retained the photosensitizing properties of IrbpyCOOH as a photosensitizer. Using DPBF and DHR 123 as probes for 1O2 and O2•–, respectively, both IrbpyCOOH and IrbpyCONH@UiO-66 were confirmed as dual Type I/II photosensitizers, generating both 1O2 and O2•– under 420/520 nm light, while the MOF NH2-UiO-66 did not produce ROS under 520 nm. In vitro assays conducted on HeLa, A549, and MKN45 cells demonstrated that the nanocomposite not only showed improved biocompatibility but also enhanced intracellular ROS generation, leading to superior phototoxicity. In vivo experiments further revealed that IrbpyCONH@UiO-66 effectively suppressed MKN45 tumor growth without causing notable tissue damage. These findings highlight that nanocomposite formation significantly enhances PDT efficiency against cancer cells.

items.title:
PNNH–Ru-Catalyzed
Highly E-Selective
Semi-Hydrogenation of Alkynes Using MeOH as a Hydrogen Donor
items.abstract: Abstract Herein, we describe the selective semi-hydrogenation of alkynes utilizing methanol as a safe and readily accessible hydrogen donor, catalyzed by a newly developed PNNH–Ru complex. This approach offers a practical and attractive alternative to traditional hydrogenation methods that depend on pressurized H2 gas. A wide range of alkynes are smoothly converted into (E)-alkenes in high yields, exhibiting excellent stereoselectivity under relatively mild reaction conditions. Detailed kinetic investigations combined with mechanistic analysis reveal that an active ruthenium dihydride species is generated in situ, which plays a pivotal role in driving the transfer hydrogenation process. The presence of both the base and methanol is essential for converting the pre-catalyst into the catalytically active dihydride species. The excellent selectivity observed in the reaction is attributed to the Z–E isomerization of the initially generated alkene, which is promoted by the in situ-formed ruthenium dihydride complex. The method tolerates diverse functional groups, including electron-rich and electron-poor substituents such as halides, esters, and heterocycles, delivering products with high efficiency and stereoselectivity. The reaction proceeds efficiently on a gram scale, highlighting its practical utility.

items.title:
Cu(I) Halide
Cluster Scintillators’ Radiographic
Imaging of Energetic Materials
items.abstract: Abstract X-ray imaging is vital for the nondestructive inspection of energetic materials, enabling internal structural analysis and defect detection through the deep penetration of X-rays. Scintillators with different emission characteristics were investigated for X-ray imaging performance. Herein, we report five Cu(I) halide cluster scintillators with tunable emissions across the visible region. Among them, Cu4I4(C72H60P4) exhibits a low X-ray detection limit of 19.19 nGy s–1 and a high light yield of 49,011 photons MeV–1, together with excellent thermal and environmental stability. These scintillators enable high-resolution imaging of cracks, compositional inhomogeneity, and thickness variations in energetic materials. Scintillators with different emission colors were further used to image four energetic material pellets with different compositions, all yielding clear internal images. This work provides an economical and environmentally friendly approach for the nondestructive inspection of energetic materials.

items.title:
One-Pot Synthesis of Oxidation-Resistant Silica-Coated
Iron Nanoparticles via Ultrasonically Assisted Citrate Modification
items.abstract: Abstract This study presents a facile, one-pot aqueous coating strategy to synthesize oxidation-resistant silica-coated iron (Fe/SiO2) core–shell nanoparticles under ambient conditions. Citrate-mediated reduction produced metallic Fe cores, with citrate ions and a thin native surface oxide layer acting as interfacial modifiers that promote SiO2 nucleation and eliminate the need for intermediate washing. Ultrasonication-assisted SiO2 encapsulation via a sol–gel process yielded Fe/SiO2 nanoparticles comprising a metallic Fe core (50.4 ± 15.1 nm in diameter) and a SiO2 shell (14.1 nm thick), as confirmed by transmission electron microscopy and energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy. Magnetic measurements demonstrated that the saturation magnetization of bare Fe nanoparticles decreased from 105.9 to 39.7 emu g–1 after 72 h in water owing to oxidation, whereas that of Fe/SiO2 nanoparticles remained at 84.6 emu g–1 compared with an initial value of 86.4 emu g–1. X-ray diffraction confirmed the preservation of the metallic α-Fe (body-centered cubic) phase, demonstrating that the SiO2 shell served as an effective diffusion barrier against oxidation. By providing a facile and eco-friendly route to protect metallic nanomaterials robustly, this study opens new avenues for their practical applications in advanced magnetic sensors, biosensors, catalysis, and magnetic separation.

items.title:
Engineering
Cu–Co Active Sites in CdIn2S4 for Selective
CO2 Photoreduction
to CH4
items.abstract: Abstract Single-metal doping in photocatalysts can lead to a trade-off between activity and product selectivity. Here, Cu–Co codoping was introduced into CdIn2S4 to regulate the electronic structure and surface reaction properties. The Cu–Co codoping modulates sulfur vacancy concentration, introduces impurity states, and generates surface active sites. These structural modifications broaden visible-light absorption and facilitate charge separation and transfer. The Cu–Co active sites enhance CO2 adsorption and promote the formation of bridging M–C–O–M intermediates, thereby directing CO2 reduction toward CH4 formation. With a selectivity of 99.55%, the optimized catalyst produces CH4 at a rate of 116.58 μmol·g–1·h–1 under visible-light irradiation.

items.title:
From “Dual-Cluster
Coexistence” to One-Dimensional
Chains: Anion-Regulated Assembly of Copper(I)-Iodide Supramolecular
Clusters for Enhanced Photocatalysis
items.abstract: Abstract The self-assembly of ionic copper(I) iodide clusters is hard to control due to the diverse Cu–I coordination modes. We propose an electrostatically driven strategy to direct distinct architectures within the same ligand system by simply varying the counteranion. A cavitand-like ligand based on a triphenylamine pyridinium salt was designed. Solvothermal assembly with Br– and PF6– anions afforded two anionic supramolecular clusters:Br– induced the formation of an anionic cluster (denoted HUBU-4, [(L1)3+2·(Cu6Br1.47I7.53)3–]·(Cu5Br0.66I7.34)3–) featuring a “dual cluster coexistence” motif, whereas PF6– directed the formation of a one-dimensional cluster chain (HUBU-5, [(L1·PF6–)2+·(Cu5I7)2–]∞). DFT calculations and photophysical/electrochemical measurements show that HUBU-5 has a narrower optical band gap, a smaller HOMO–LUMO gap, and stronger electronic transition capability than HUBU-4. (optical band gaps: 1.49 eV for HUBU-5 vs 1.62 eV for HUBU-4). Photocatalytic evaluation indicated that both clusters possess high activity for the copper(I)-catalyzed azide–alkyne cycloaddition (CuAAC) reaction under mild conditions, with a modest performance enhancement observed for the one-dimensional chain architecture. By simply changing the counteranion, this study achieves topological regulation of anionic copper(I) iodide clusters from 0D to 1D, revealing the structure-directing role of anions and offering an alternative design strategy for ionic supramolecular clusters.

items.title:
Ligand Symmetry
Modulates Singlet–Triplet Energy
Gap for Tunable Luminescence Temperature Sensing Performance
items.abstract: Abstract The influence of reverse intersystem crossing on temperature response is a highly intriguing research topic for TADF materials. In this work, we report three isostructural Cu(I) coordination polymers featuring ligands with different symmetries. We tailor their singlet–triplet energy gap to systematically investigate its impact on temperature-responsive properties.

items.title:
Metal Composition Controls the Confined Reorientation
of Nitride Clusters in Endohedral Metallofullerenes
items.abstract: Abstract The composition of encapsulated metal clusters plays a critical role in determining their confined motion within the fullerene cages. Here, we investigate the temperature-dependent structural behavior of mixed-metal MSc2N@C80 (M = Nd, Ho) in NiOEP (Ni(II) octaethylporphine) cocrystals using variable-temperature single-crystal X-ray diffraction. Despite the distinct temperature-dependent behavior of the C80 cages, both MSc2N clusters exhibit similar highly restricted librational reorientation upon heating. This behavior contrasts with the larger-amplitude spinning-top-like and tumbling-like reorientations observed for analogous M3N@C80 clusters with different metal compositions (Sc3N, M2ScN, and M3N, where M is a lanthanide). The results demonstrate that the metal composition and distribution within the encapsulated cluster dictate the degree of restricted librational reorientation, providing new structural insight into the interplay between metal composition, cage dynamics, and confined molecular motion in endohedral metallofullerenes.

items.title:
Technetium
Uptake by Ferrous Hydroxide and Ferrous
Hydroxychloride: Influence of Host Phase Coordination Environments
items.abstract: Abstract The safe disposal of high-level radioactive waste (HLW) in deep geological repositories requires understanding how radionuclides interact with Fe(II)-bearing secondary phases formed during steel canister corrosion. This study investigates the redox and coordination behavior of 99Tc(VII), a long-lived and radiotoxic fission product, upon reaction with ferrous hydroxide and ferrous hydroxychloride under anoxic, alkaline conditions. Batch uptake experiments showed that both Fe(II)-bearing phases rapidly and effectively immobilize 99Tc, independent of ionic strength, and no compelling localized accumulation of Tc precipitate could be detected by scanning electron microscopy-energy dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (SEM-EDXS). Tc K-edge X-ray absorption near-edge structure (XANES) spectroscopy revealed that technetium prevails as Tc(IV), implying that Fe(II) oxidation occurred concomitantly with pertechnetate reduction. Furthermore, extended X-ray absorption fine structure (EXAFS) spectroscopy indicated that Tc occurs primarily as dimers or as a mixture of monomeric and dimeric species, and ruled out significant TcO2·nH2O formation. The number of detected next-nearest Fe atoms pointed to Fe and Tc octahedra sharing edges at the solid/solution interface, forming either Tc surface-sorbed species or Tc surface-incorporated species. In the latter species, Tc substitutes for structural Fe at the mineral surface, the local excess charge resulting from the substitution of a divalent by a tetravalent cation being possibly balanced by anions present at the solution side. Overall, findings suggest that during the long-term evolution of a nuclear waste repository system, the formation of Fe(OH)2 and β-Fe2(OH)3Cl as canister corrosion products represents a sink capable of efficiently immobilizing 99Tc, preventing its spread in the far-field.

items.title: Lewis Acid Modification of Binding Modes of bis -Diazophoranimide Ligands at Lithium
items.abstract: Abstract The uncatalyzed hydrophosphination of diazoesters with secondary phosphines affords bis-diazophoranimide ligands. Deprotonation provides Li–N2O2-tetradentate complexes with 5,6,5-chelation. These bifunctional ligands coordinate one equivalent of HB(C6F5)2 to a N atom remote from the lithium prompting a geometry change to a 6,5,5 binding mode and dimerization. A second equivalent of HB(C6F5)2 alters chelation, restoring 5,6,5 binding with two B–N bonds adjacent to phosphorus. The energetics of these bonds are examined computationally.

items.title:
Multi-B-Site
Cation Engineering in Stable Thiocyanate-Templated
Layered Double-Perovskite Halides
items.abstract: Abstract Hybrid organic–inorganic perovskite halides offer a versatile structural platform owing to their flexible bonding nature. Beyond organic-cation engineering, halide-site engineering using molecular anions has recently emerged as an effective approach to alter the perovskite bonding network; however, accessible compositional and structural diversity remains limited. Here, we report, for the first time, hybrid layered Ag–Bi double perovskites, MA4AgBiX4(SCN)4 (X = Br, I), in which incorporation of thiocyanate (SCN–) at the halide-site reduces perovskite dimensionality. While the previously reported single-metal-cation compound, MA2PbI2(SCN)2, offers a unique van der Waals-coupled structural platform, its rapid decomposition, limited compositional space, and lack of bromide analogue hindered further development. First-principles calculations suggest that the structural instability of the lead-based bromide analogue arises from a bromide-induced lifting of the axial SCN ligand and resultant increased interlayer hydrogen-bond distance. Transitioning to an Ag–Bi architecture mitigates this destabilizing effect, as Ag+ (4d105s0) possesses isotropic s-orbital character and enhanced angular flexibility compared to Pb2+ (6s26p0) with a stronger orientational preference. This strategy yields a full range of solid solutions with band gaps tunable from 1.95 to 2.30 eV. The resulting materials, particularly the bromide-rich phases, exhibit markedly increased environmental robustness, demonstrating that multi-B-site cation design can expand the structural diversity of stable pseudohalide-based hybrid perovskites.

items.title:
Holistic Optimization
of Li- and Mn-Rich Cathodes
from Precursor Coprecipitation to Mechanochemical Calcination
items.abstract: Abstract Li- and Mn-rich layered oxide (LMR) cathodes offer high capacity through both transition metal and oxygen redox but remain limited by voltage/energy fade and sluggish high-rate kinetics. Here, we develop a holistic process–structure–performance optimization strategy for enhanced LMR cathodes by controlling conditions for coprecipitation, calcination, and mechanochemical treatment. First, ammonia concentration and pH were tuned to regulate complexation and precipitation kinetics, yielding precursors with improved particle-size uniformity and structural crystallinity. Second, calcination temperature was optimized to balance layered crystallinity against grain coarsening and strain accumulation, identifying 900 °C as the structural optimum. Third, ball milling the precursor with a lithium source further reduced the primary particle size, significantly enhancing the rate capability. These results evidence the effectiveness of the integrated optimization of precursor chemistry, calcination control, and mechanochemical treatment for improved Li+ insertion kinetics toward high-power LMR cathodes.

items.title:
Ultrawide
NIR-II Emission Regulation of Ni2+ in SrGa12O19 Based on a Crystal-Field Engineering
Strategy
items.abstract: Abstract Near-infrared II light (NIR-II, 1000–1700 nm) is highly desirable for deep-tissue bioimaging, nondestructive testing, and night vision, but it remains challenging to realize simultaneously tunable emission peak and bandwidth within a single-activator system. Ni2+ with a 3d8 configuration is a promising broadband NIR-II activator ion whose emission originates from crystal-field-dependent d-d electron transitions. Nevertheless, the currently reported Ni2+-activated phosphors are largely limited with spectral tunability (full width at half-maximum, fwhm &lt;200 nm). Herein, a series of SrGa12O19:Ni2+ phosphors with NIR-II emission are prepared that exhibit an emission peak at 1180 nm originating from the 3T2g → 3A2g electron transition. Through designing Al3+-Ga3+ cation substitution strategy, the local coordination environment and crystal-field strength around Ni2+ are controllably modulated, driving a progressive redshift of the emission peak from 1180 to 1350 nm and a pronounced fwhm broadening from 222 to 566 nm, ultimately affording an ultrabroadband NIR-II emission. Furthermore, a prototype phosphor-converted light-emitting diode (LED) is fabricated, demonstrating promising applications in night vision. This crystal-field engineering strategy substantially extends the tunable range of the emission peak and fwhm for Ni2+-activated phosphors and provides guidelines for optimizing transition-metal-activated NIR luminescent materials.

items.title:
Tetraisopropyl
Titanate-Catalyzed Esterification Mechanism
for the Synthesis of 1,2-Cyclohexanedicarboxylates
items.abstract: Abstract Titanates (e.g., Ti(OiPr)4) serve as green, noncorrosive catalysts for synthesizing the new plasticizer bis(2-ethylhexyl) cyclohexane-1,2-dicarboxylate (DEHCH). However, the structural evolution of the Ti center and the microscopic mechanism remain elusive, hindering industrial process optimization. Herein, we used density functional theory (DFT), coupled with Atoms-in-Molecules (AIM) topological analysis and charge decomposition analysis (CDA), to investigate the diesterification mechanism. The reaction proceeds via four steps: alcoholysis/ligand exchange (ΔG = 36.46 kJ·mol–1); nucleophilic attack of the isooctyloxy group to form a tetrahedral intermediate (ΔG = 65.05 kJ·mol–1); proton transfer to form a tetrahedral geminal diol (ΔG = 36.46 kJ·mol–1); and intramolecular dehydration (ΔG = 156.28 kJ·mol–1). The lower ΔG of alcoholysis relative to the hydrolysis side reaction (48.27–69.74 kJ·mol–1) effectively mitigates water-induced catalyst deactivation. Notably, the Ti atom preferentially activates the isooctyloxy oxygen over the carboxylic carbonyl oxygen, dominating the subsequent nucleophilic attack. AIM and CDA results further reveal dynamic coordination behavior: the Ti center flexibly interconverts between geometries resembling a five-coordinate trigonal bipyramid and a six-coordinate regular octahedron, activating the carboxylic carbonyl oxygen via formation of a partial covalent Ti–O bond. These results suggest that an excess of 2-ethylhexanol (2-EH) not only promotes the desired esterification but also suppresses hydrolysis-induced catalyst deactivation.

items.title:
Tuned 4,7-Methoxy-Derivatized
DAPhen Ligands with
Enhanced Selectivity for Am/Eu and An/Np Separations
items.abstract: Abstract We report the synthesis and evaluation of two CHON-compliant 4,7-dimethoxy-1,10-phenanthroline-2,9-dicarboxamide (DADOMePhen) ligands: an aromatic variant, Et-Tol-DADOMePhen (1), and an aliphatic analogue, TCH-DADOMePhen (2). Solvent extraction under SANEX conditions shows that ligand 1 has good Am/Eu selectivity in an optimal window of 0.1–0.5 M HNO3, achieving a maximum SFAm/Eu of 108.2 at 0.5 M HNO3, the highest reported for a lipophilic ligand of pure DAPhen-type molecular architecture to date. This performance inverts conventional acidity dependence: electron-donating methoxy substituents enhance metal–ligand covalency at low acidity but make the ligand susceptible to protonation at higher concentrations. Coordination and fluorescence studies indicate a 1:2 metal-to-ligand stoichiometry; single-crystal diffraction reveals the structure of ligand 1. Quantum-chemical calculations establish that methoxy groups tune electrostatic potential and frontier orbitals, strengthening bonding relative to parent Et-Tol-DAPhen. Beyond Am/Eu partitioning, ligand 1 may enable actinide/neptunium separations: at 0.1 M HNO3, calculated SFAm/Np, SFPu/Np, SFU/Np, and SFTh/Np reach 436, 1690, 9766, and 1953, respectively, reflecting mismatch between the dioxo Np(V) monocation and the ligand. This work establishes 4,7-methoxy derivatization as a design strategy to tune DAPhen-based extractant selectivity and introduces a ligand that could be useful for specialized low-acidity actinide/neptunium or lanthanide separations.

items.title:
Dynamic Luminescence
Color Tuning and Afterglow Modulation
in Sb3+-Doped 0D Hybrid Perovskite (3-AMB)2CdCl4 Through Controlled Energy Transfer
items.abstract: Abstract The development of advanced luminescent materials with tunable emission properties and multidimensional information encoding capabilities has become increasingly promising for next-generation optoelectronic devices and anticounterfeiting technologies. Herein, we reported a novel zero-dimensional (0D) organic–inorganic hybrid metal halides (OIHMHs), (3-AMB)2CdCl4 ([3-AMB]+ = methyl 3-aminobenzoate), and demonstrated how Sb3+ doping enables dual-mode luminescence engineering. Photoluminescence studies revealed excitation-wavelength-dependent color tuning: under 345 nm excitation, emission evolves from blue to orange, while 365 nm excitation yields color variation ranging from deep blue through white to pale yellow. Remarkably, the host exhibits 6 s room-temperature phosphorescence (RTP). The Sb3+ doping enables tunable yellow Sb3+-STEs delayed fluorescence, and achieves time-resolved color switching from yellow to green simultaneously. This work established a paradigm for engineering multifunctional luminescent materials, offering transformative potential for advanced optical encryption and intelligent anticounterfeiting technologies.

items.title: Cavity-Forming Cofacial Porphyrin Dimers via Cooperative Zn 2+ Binding: Structure, Formation Pathways, and Host Properties
items.abstract: Abstract Porphyrins bearing four 2,2′-bipyridine ligands linked through acetylene or diacetylene spacers, ZnPor(C2bpy)4 and ZnPor(C4bpy)4 were designed to self-assemble into cavity-containing cofacial dimers through Zn2+ coordination. Electrospray ionization mass spectrometry confirmed the formation of [(ZnPor(Cnbpy)4)2Zn4]8+ (n = 2, 4). For ZnPor(C2bpy)4, Bayesian Markov chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) analysis of through-space 1H NMR chemical shift changes identified a cofacial dimer as the probable solution structure. Titration of the porphyrins with Zn(OTf)2 produced highly sigmoidal changes in their UV–Vis absorption spectra. Spectral deconvolution by multivariate curve resolution–alternating least-squares, followed by Bayesian MCMC equilibrium analysis, identified the most probable intermediate distributions and supported a stepwise pathway involving side-by-side (J-type) porphyrin dimers before formation of the final cofacial (H-type) dimer. The cavities exhibited spacer-dependent guest selectivity: ZnPor(C2bpy)4 encapsulated electron-deficient aromatic guests through π–π stacking, whereas ZnPor(C4bpy)4 accommodated 4,4′-bipyridine and 4,4′-dipyridylacetylene through ditopic axial coordination. r2SCAN-3c geometry optimizations were consistent with the proposed binding modes. These results establish Bayesian MCMC analysis as a powerful approach for resolving multiparameter systems, including multicomponent supramolecular assemblies, while explicitly accounting for uncertainty.

items.title:
Formation-pH-Dependent
Structural Difference as a
Significant Control on Ferrihydrite Transformation Behaviors
items.abstract: Abstract Ferrihydrite (Fhy) is a metastable iron (oxyhydr)oxide whose transformation into more stable crystalline phases is an important manifestation of its reactivity. However, whether nominally identical 2-line Fhy samples retain formation-dependent differences in short-range structure and how these differences control subsequent phase transformation behavior remain poorly understood. Here, Fhy was synthesized at different pH levels to establish formation-pH-dependent variations in the structure and phase transformation. Although all products were identified as 2-line Fhy by conventional X-ray diffraction, low-pH Fhy contained more hydroxyl-related components and exhibited lower structural order, while the local Fe coordination environments varied with the formation pH. These structural differences strongly affected the subsequent transformation. Under aqueous conditions, Fhy formed at pH 3.0 showed a greater tendency toward dissolution-mediated transformation to goethite, whereas Fhy formed at higher pH values generally yielded a greater relative proportion of hematite. Under nonaqueous conditions, the greater hydroxyl content of low-pH Fhy facilitated dehydroxylation and promoted hematite formation at a lower temperature and shorter reaction time. These results demonstrate that the formation pH leaves a persistent structural imprint on Fhy that governs hydroxylation degrees, Fe coordination environments, and phase transformation pathways. This work establishes formation-controlled short-range structures as a vital determinant of the transformation behavior of metastable materials.

items.title:
Aromatic Ring-Enhanced Pore-Space-Partitioned Metal–Organic
Frameworks for Selective Separation of Saturated Hydrocarbons
items.abstract: Abstract Light saturated hydrocarbons are difficult to separate efficiently because of their similar physicochemical properties, and metal–organic frameworks (MOFs) with tailor-made pore environments promising adsorbents for precise separation. Here, three aromatic ring-enhanced pore-space-partitioned MOFs (SNNU-304–306) were constructed by integrating thieno[2,3-b]thiophene-2,5-dicarboxylic acid (TDC) with tripyridyl partitioners of different aromatic frameworks and N-site characteristics. Modular variation of the partitioners within the same Ni-TDC framework tunes the cage geometry and local aromatic environment, enabling differentiated recognition of C1–C3 hydrocarbons. SNNU-306 exhibits the highest C2H6 and C3H8 uptakes, with C2H6/CH4 and C3H8/CH4 ideal adsorbed solution theory (IAST) selectivities of 34.1 and 1398.6 at 298 K. More importantly, dynamic breakthrough experiments show that SNNU-304 gives the longest separation time for C2H6/CH4, while SNNU-306 exhibits the longest separation time for C3H8/CH4, demonstrating the targeted regulation of different saturated-hydrocarbon separation requirements by different aromatic partitioners. For the ternary C3H8/C2H6/CH4 mixture, the CH4 purity reaches up to 99.96%. Grand Canonical Monte Carlo (GCMC) simulations reveal that different aromatic partitioners regulate host–guest interactions, thereby enabling differentiated hydrocarbon recognition. These results show that aromatic ring enhancement and pore-space partitioning synergistically transform pacs-MOFs into modularly tunable molecular-recognition systems, offering a strategy for the task-specific design of porous materials for saturated-hydrocarbon separation.

items.title:
Dynamic Balance
between Heptamolybdate and Octamolybdate:
Controlled Syntheses of Ag46 and Ag48 Nanoclusters
and Their Transformation via pH-Regulated Ligand Exchange
items.abstract: Abstract The integration of polyoxometalates (POMs) as structural templates for noble metal nanoclusters (NCs) represents a cutting-edge strategy to achieve atomic-level precision in cluster synthesis, but the relationship between polyoxometalates and overall structures of assembled NCs and their transformations often are not clear due to significant complexity coming from transient intermediates and coexisting species. Herein, we report the trifluoroacetic acid (TFA)-mediated controlled syntheses and pH-regulated induced structural transformation of silver NCs: [(Mo7O24)@Ag46(CyhS)28(CF3COO)10(CH3CN)4]•2COOCF3–•2CH3CN and [(Mo8O28)@Ag48(CyhS)24(CF3COO)16(CH3CN)4]•7.5CF3COOH (abbreviated as Ag46 and Ag48). Both clusters feature core–shell architectures with molybdenum-based POMs ([Mo7O24]6– and [Mo8O28]8–) acting as anionic templates directing the assembly of Ag shells. The structural evolution from Ag46 to Ag48 was achieved via pH-regulated ligand exchange, highlighting the dynamic balance between POM cores of different sizes, Ag shell coordination geometry, and TFA’s dual role. This work advances the frontier of hybrid NC-POM systems, offering insights into cluster transformation mechanisms and programmable synthesis.

items.title: Triplet Resting States Govern E / Z Selectivity and Chemoselectivity in Carbene-Pincer Cobalt-Catalyzed Alkyne Semihydrogenation
items.abstract: Abstract Rigid, electronically tunable carbene-based pincer ligands constitute a highly promising platform for controlling selectivity in cobalt-catalyzed alkyne semihydrogenation, but the influence of catalyst spin-state characteristics on Z/E selectivity and over-reduction remains poorly understood. Herein, we compare the mechanistic pathways governing Z-selective, E-selective, and overhydrogenation of alkynes catalyzed by the mono(carbene)-based pincer cobalt complex [(PCNHCP)Co(N2)]+. The observed chemoselectivity between Z-selective semihydrogenation and overhydrogenation is found to be primarily from the energy difference between the two triplet resting states─B2triplet and A2triplet, which has not ever been reported. The β-hydride elimination transition state, TSB5-4_Esinglet, lies at a high energy of 17.5 kcal/mol, rendering the E-selective pathway kinetically inaccessible. Steric and electronic analyses indicate that the coordinated E-alkene in the β-hydride elimination step experiences greater steric hindrance and less πC═C → π*carbene electron-transfer stabilization than the Z-alkene, thereby suppressing β-hydride elimination. Comparative analysis reveals that the carbene ligand preferentially stabilizes the singlet state relative to the triplet state in these Co systems, and the stabilizing effect of the carbene ligands can be accumulated across multiple carbene units.

items.title:
Cyclopentadienyl
in Cp2Hf Complexes Is
No Longer a Spectator Ligand: Reactions of a Hafnacyclocumulene Complex
with Ketones
items.abstract: Abstract The interaction of five-membered hafnacyclocumulene complex 1Hf with ketones was investigated. The reaction outcome depends on the conditions and the ketone substituents. Under UV irradiation, insertion can be halted at one or two ketone molecules inserted into Hf–C bonds, affording hafnadihydrofuran 2Ph or the nine-membered dioxahafnacyclocumulene 3Fl. Under thermal conditions, the reaction of 1Hf with ketones revealed, for the first time, ketone insertion into one or two Cp–Hf bonds of the metallocene moiety. In the reaction with benzophenone, the corresponding insertion product 4Phb was isolated, and its structure was confirmed by SC-XRD. Products resulting from the insertion of benzophenone or fluorenone into the Cp–Hf bonds of the metallocene fragment of the hafnacyclocumulene were also characterized. A ketone insertion mechanism into the Cp–Hf bonds was proposed based on quantum chemical calculations at the DLPNO–CCSD(T)/Def2-TZVP//r2-SCAN-3c/Def2-TZVP level of theory. The calculation results revealed that the ketone undergoes insertion via η1-type of Cp–Hf bond. Furthermore, benzophenone and fluorenone also insert into the Cp–Hf bonds of hafnocene diphenolates by the same manner. The results obtained allow understanding the general deactivation mechanism in metallocene catalytic processes under interaction with carbonyl compounds.

items.title:
Impact of the Metal–Ligand Bonding Nature on
Electronic States of {Fe(NO)2}9/10–{Fe(NO)2}9/10 RREs Unraveled by the Combined X-ray
Spectroscopic Analyses: Relevance to DNIC-Mediated Translational Functionality
items.abstract: Abstract Probed by the combined X-ray spectroscopic techniques (N K-edge/Fe L-edge XAS, Fe K-edge HERFD–XANES, Kβ1,3 mainline, VtC Kβ2,5 XES) and DFT computation, the qualitative/quantitative assignment of Fe/NO oxidation states in dinuclear dinitrosyl iron complexes (DNICs) suggests that the balance between NO– → Fe π-donating and Fe → •NO π-backbonding interactions in the [Fe(NO)2] unit(s) is modulated by the ionicity-covalency competition within the Fe–ER(2) bonds for a series of [ER(2)]−-bridged {Fe(NO)2}9/10–{Fe(NO)2}9/10 RREs (E = S, N, O). With the delicately ligand-controlled NO–/•NO equilibrium in the [Fe(NO)2] unit, the biomimetic activity governed by {Fe(NO)2}9/{Fe(NO)2}10 DNICs echoes their electronic/spectroscopic features, which not only uncovers molecular identity in complex environments but also decodes the reported H2S/NO communication, degradation/repair of [Fe–S] clusters, and translational functionality for NO-to-[N2O2]2–-to-N2O and NO-to-HNO/NO– transformations.

items.title:
Hierarchical
Heterometallic Coordination Underpins
Alkali Tolerance in a Zr–Cu Hydroxamate Framework
items.abstract: Abstract Chemical robustness in heterometallic metal–organic frameworks depends on the strength and organization of chemically distinct coordination bonds. We report SUM-71, a three-dimensional Zr–Cu hydroxamate framework integrating Zr–O/Cu–O rods with Cu–N cross-links. Its characteristic powder X-ray diffraction peaks persist after 24 h in common solvents, aqueous media spanning pH 2–14, and near-saturated NaOH (ca. 20 M); measurable microporosity also persists after acid and alkaline treatment. Cluster density functional theory calculations find endothermic water substitution at all modeled sites and greater thermodynamic resistance at rod-forming interactions than at Cu–N cross-links. In 0.1 M KOH, SUM-71/nickel foam retains a nearly unchanged composite-electrode polarization response after 500 cycles, with SUM-71 diffraction peaks remaining detectable. These results highlight differentiated coordination roles as a strategy for exceptional static alkali tolerance.

items.title:
Cobalt as
an Anchor: Acetate and Nontrigonal Phosphorus
Ligand-Assisted Hydroboration
items.abstract: Abstract Replacing precious metals with earth-abundant alternatives remains a vital challenge in sustainable catalytic systems. Herein, the synthesis and catalytic application of a cobalt(II) acetate complex with a tridentate, dianionic urea-based ligand bearing a nontrigonal phosphorus center are reported. The Co(II) complex was fully characterized, including by single-crystal X-ray diffraction to confirm the direct coordination of the Co(II) center to the nontrigonal phosphorus. Catalytic studies reveal that this complex promotes the hydroboration of aldehydes, ketones, styrene, and phenylacetylene using pinacolborane under mild conditions. The system operates with catalyst loadings as low as 0.1 mol % for aldehydes and 0.5 mol % for ketones at room temperature and displays high selectivity toward aldehydes. Experimental and computational mechanistic studies indicate that the Co(II) center does not serve as the locus of B–H bond activation, with no evidence for catalytically active boryl or hydride species. Instead, density functional theory suggests that the strongly coordinated acetate ligand serves to activate pinacolborane during catalysis, positioning the BH group near the electrophilic phosphorus center. These findings demonstrate the potential role of ligand-centered chemistry in first-row transition-metal catalysis and open new directions for the design of cooperative ligand platforms beyond traditional metal-centered pathways.

items.title: Ditopic Bis(Pyridinium Amidate) Ligands with N , N - and O , O -Bidentate Bonding Sites: Oxygen-Coordinated Alkali Metals Systematically Impact the Reactivity of the N-Bound Palladium Center
items.abstract: Abstract Alkali metal (AM) salts are widely used as bases or additives in homogeneous catalysis, yet the influence of the AM cation itself is often overlooked. Here, we demonstrate that AM binding to the backbone of a bis(pyridinium amidate) (bisPYA) ligand affects the reactivity of the coordinated palladium center. Specifically the ortho-pyridinium bisPYA ligand adopts an N,N′-bidentate bonding mode to PdX2 fragments with X = MeCN(BF)4 (3), Cl (4), or OAc (5). When exposed to AM carbonates, the dicarbonyl backbone of the bis(amidate) ligand coordinates in an O,O′-bidentate fashion to the AM to form stable and crystalline complexes of the type [AM(bisPYA-PdOAc2)2]+ with AM = Li (6a), Na (6b), K (6c), Rb (6d), and Cs (6e). The stability of these AM adducts decreases according to competitive binding and dilution experiments along the series Li+ &gt; Na+ &gt; K+ &gt; Rb+ &gt; Cs+. In agreement with this trend, rates of electrophilic cyclometalation involving C–H bond activation of the pyridinium N–CH3 group correlate with the stability of the adducts, thus providing valuable insights relevant to understanding specific AM effects in transition metal catalysis and offering opportunities to remotely tune the electron density of catalytic centers in this bisPYA and related ligand classes.

items.title: Issue Publication Information
Issue Editorial Masthead

Ligand Local
Rigidity as a Quantitative Descriptor
of Lanthanide Size Selectivity
items.abstract: Abstract Separation of the rare-earth elements relies on the small, monotonic contraction in the ionic radius across the trivalent lanthanide series. Ligand preorganization is a powerful strategy for amplifying this size difference, but within the N,O-tetradentate ligand family examined here, it approaches a structural ceiling as the most preorganized scaffolds become fully fused. Here, using density functional theory, we introduce cavity rigidity as a quantitative framework for lanthanide size selectivity and define local rigidity (LR) as the resistance of the ligand cavity to the compression required for metal binding. The LR reflects both the intrinsic stiffness of the ligand framework and the extent to which the cavity must deform upon coordination. Across the N,O-tetradentate ligands examined, the computed La/Lu size selectivity increases linearly with LR. The same relationship is observed for five additional lanthanide pairs with larger ionic radius differences producing steeper slopes. Within this ligand family, the results point to two routes for increasing thermodynamic size selectivity: increasing the framework stiffness or increasing the equilibrium donor separation.

items.title:
Quantifying
Base-Dependent Lewis Acidity in Substituted
Boranes through DFT and Machine Learning
items.abstract: Abstract The dependence of Lewis acidity on the interacting base is established. Here, density functional theory calculations and machine-learning analysis quantify substituent effects and base dependence within a combinatorial library of 816 trisubstituted boranes constructed from 16 substituents. Interactions with five probe bases (H2O, NH3, C5H5N, PMe3, and Cl–) yield 3927 calculated adduct formation free energies in dichloromethane. Electron-withdrawing substituents generally enhance borane Lewis acidity, whereas electron-donating substituents attenuate it. The magnitude of these effects varies with the base, producing changes and occasional reversals in relative acidity rankings. PMe3 shows the strongest dependence on substituent identity among the investigated bases. Weak linear correlations between isolated-borane global hardness and adduct formation free energy indicate limited predictive power for this single descriptor. Random forest models describe the computed trends, while SHAP analysis identifies the summed Hammett σp parameter, the borane–base frontier orbital energy gap, and borane electrophilicity as the most influential descriptors in the model. These results provide a quantitative map of substituent effects and the transferability of relative borane acidity rankings across the investigated bases.

items.title:
Rationalizing
the Solvent-Driven “Venus Flytrap”
Mechanism in Argentivorous Molecules
items.abstract: Abstract This computational study examines the dynamic, thermodynamic, and electronic factors governing the selective “Venus flytrap” mechanism of argentivorous molecules and the different responses of Ag+ and Zn2+ in solution. Three independent 250 ps molecular dynamics replicas were performed for each of Ag+@TCA(4-OMe), Zn2+@TCA(4-OMe), and free TCA(4-OMe). Both cations approach the cyclen ring, but only Ag+ induces collective and sustained folding of the four aromatic side arms, with Ag-N coordination and cavity closure occurring as temporally coupled processes. Thermodynamic calculations in CH3CN indicate opposite conformational preferences: folded Ag+ complexes are favored over their unfolded structures by 24.31–30.52 kcal mol–1, whereas unfolded Zn2+ complexes are favored over their folded structures by 85.90–102.29 kcal mol–1. The differential solvation contribution associated with complex formation is much less favorable for Zn2+, particularly in the folded structures. Energy decomposition analysis (EDA) and EDA-NOCV indicate that Zn2+ has a stronger intrinsic metal–host interaction, dominated by orbital Zn-N coordination, whereas electrostatics is the largest attractive contribution in the Ag+ complexes. Folding increases the magnitude of ΔEint more strongly in relative terms for Ag+ than for Zn2+ (23.5% and 5.4%, respectively), mainly through electrostatic stabilization. Independent Gradient Model (IGM) and QTAIM analyses show more extensive participation of the aromatic cavity in the Ag+ series, while Voronoi deformation density (VDD) indicates more pronounced electron-density redistribution in the Zn2+ coordination region. The Ag+-selective conformational response reflects the balance between solvation, receptor adaptation, and the distinct metal–host interactions established by each cation.

items.title:
An MOF-Based
Composite with the Applications in Anticounterfeiting
and Fluorescence Detection for 4-Nitrophenol in Water and Extracts
of Rice, Soil, and Plant
items.abstract: Abstract Toxic 4-nitrophenol (4-NP) poses risks to human health and the ecological environment, whose detection is of significance. A 3D metal–organic framework of [Zn(tr)(OAc)] (Zn-tr) (Htr = 1H-1,2,4-triazole; OAc– = acetate) and its Rh6G@Zn-tr (Rh6G = rhodamine 6G) composite were presented. Zn-tr is topologized as a (3,4,6)-connected 3,4,6T56 topological {3.72}2{32.4.73}{32.4.76.86} network. Ratiometric fluorescence Rh6G@Zn-tr sensor exhibits a high sensitivity to 4-NP with a linear relationship of I365/I554 = −0.01745C4-NP + 1.03741 (I365/I554 is the ratio of the emission intensities at 365 and 554 nm; C4-NP = 4-NP concentration) within C4-NP = 0–40 μM and limit of detection = 0.48 μM. Rh6G@Zn-tr sensing 4-NP will not be interfered by common ions and some analogues, showing high anti-interference. Rh6G@Zn-tr can accurately sense 4-NP in lake water and some environmental extracts, showing high reliability. ASCII binary code defined by blank and Rh6G@Zn-tr hydrogel in a 4 × 8 array can encrypt or decrypt information. With the two-tier secret keys of 4-NP and 254 nm UV light, a QR code becomes readable by a smartphone and returns the encrypted information. This work provides a visual fluorescence 4-NP detection method and an anticounterfeiting platform by designing an allochroic MOF-based composite.

items.title:
Molecular Dynamics
Analysis of Early Activation Events
in the Cannabinoid Type 2 Receptor Reveals a Putative Water-Mediated
Allosteric Pathway
items.abstract: Abstract The cannabinoid receptor type 2 (CB2R) is a therapeutically relevant class A G protein-coupled receptor implicated in neuroinflammation, pain modulation, and immune regulation. However, the molecular events by which agonist binding promotes CB2R activation remain incompletely understood. Here, we investigated the conformational dynamics of AM12033-bound CB2R using four independent 1 μs all-atom molecular dynamics simulation replicas initiated from the agonist-bound inactive-like crystal structure. Principal component analysis and free-energy landscape reconstruction showed that CB2R samples active-like conformational states characterized by partial outward displacement of TM6, disruption of the TM3–TM7 interaction, and rearrangement of the NPxxY microswitch. A free-energy minimum displayed close structural similarity to the experimentally determined active CB2R–Gi complex, with a Cα RMSD of 1.71 Å. However, the persistence of the internal DRY interaction and the incomplete transition of the Trp2586.48 toggle switch indicate that the receptor predominantly populates a preactive or partially activated ensemble rather than a fully active G protein-bound state. A water-mediated Trp2586.48–water–water–Asp802.50 bridge formed reproducibly in three of four independent replicas after the activation-related transition and was associated with increased receptor-core hydration, activation-related microswitch populations, and shortened or rewired allosteric communication pathways from the toggle-switch region. These findings suggest that agonist-bound CB2R can sample active-like conformations before G protein engagement and support a putative role for a water-mediated allosteric pathway in early CB2R activation.

items.title:
Acetylation
of YajL Preserves Its Protective Enzymatic
Activity against Stress-Induced Glycolytic Byproducts
items.abstract: Abstract The E. coli protein YajL and its human homologue DJ-1 catalyze the inactivation of reactive carbonyl species that result from high glycolysis rates. Left unchecked, these reactive carbonyl species have the potential to induce protein damage. Proteomics studies have shown that YajL is post-translationally acetylated at lysine 142 when glycolytic rates are high, but the functional significance of this modification is unclear. To determine the impact of acetylation on YajL activity, we cotranslationally incorporated acetylated lysine into YajL using genetic code expansion and conducted kinetic activity assays. We found that acetylated YajL retains function and may possess kinetic advantage over the unmodified form. Additionally, we found that lysine 142 is susceptible to modification by a reactive carbonyl substrate that YajL targets, but acetylation of this residue prevents this potentially damaging modification.

items.title:
Recombinant
Protein Expression and Purification in
the Era of Artificial Intelligence: Bridging Classical Biochemistry
and Molecular Engineering
items.abstract: Abstract Recombinant protein production has evolved from an empirical biochemical procedure into a predictive engineering discipline that brings together molecular genetics, host biology, biophysics, synthetic biology, and artificial intelligence. The production of proteins, particularly complex classes such as membrane receptors, multidomain assemblies, intrinsically disordered regulatory proteins, and glycoproteins, demands expression environments that synchronize transcriptional load, translational kinetics, folding trajectories, and post-translational modifications (PTMs). Advances in synthetic biology, coupled with omics-guided host engineering, enable fine-tuning of several of these interconnected processes. In parallel, cell-free protein synthesis platforms offer programmable, decoupled environments that enable the production of structurally intricate, aggregation-prone, or cytotoxic proteins. These developments reposition recombinant protein science as a cohesive, predictive, and highly tunable platform capable of producing proteins with high structural integrity and functional fidelity. Despite remarkable technological progress, a cohesive framework that integrates host selection, construct engineering, purification strategies, and computational design around the specific requirements of the target protein has remained elusive. Here, we present a protein-centric perspective on recombinant protein production, linking the molecular determinants of folding, translational kinetics, PTMs, and cellular stress responses to rational decisions throughout the production pipeline. By synthesizing advances in expression platform engineering, purification technologies, biophysical quality assessment, artificial intelligence, synthetic biology, and systems-level optimization, we highlight how recombinant protein production is evolving from a largely empirical practice into a predictive engineering discipline. We further discuss unresolved challenges associated with structurally complex proteins and outline emerging opportunities that are poised to redefine the future of protein biomanufacturing, structural biology, and therapeutic development.

items.title:
Stabilizing
Full-Length PYY for Native Y1R/Y2R Dual
Agonism
items.abstract: Abstract Peptide agonists that engage multiple G protein-coupled receptors provide a framework for orchestrating discrete but complementary signaling pathways within a single molecular entity. Peptide YY (PYY) is an endogenous 36-residue multiagonist of the neuropeptide Y receptor (YR) family. Full-length PYY(1–36) activates both Y1R and Y2R, coupling Y1R-dependent pancreatic and glucoregulatory signaling with Y2R-dependent satiety pathways. This native dual agonism is rapidly uncoupled by the ubiquitous dipeptidyl peptidase-4 (DPP4), which removes the N-terminal dipeptide to yield PYY(3–36), a Y2R-selective ligand with markedly reduced Y1R activity. Thus, DPP4 hydrolysis alters the receptor pharmacology of PYY rather than merely shortening peptide lifetime. Here, we report chemically stabilized PYY analogues that are refractory to DPP4 while retaining potent agonism at both Y1R and Y2R. Preservation of this native dual agonism was not achieved by introducing 2-aminoisobutyric acid (Aib) at the penultimate N-terminal residue. Although Aib is widely used to protect GLP-1 and GIP receptor agonists from DPP4, it results in PYY derivatives with diminished receptor activity at the Y1R. N-terminal alkylation afforded a minimally perturbative strategy to block DPP4 recognition while maintaining the full-length PYY(1–36) functional pharmacophore. Structure–activity studies define N-terminal features required for dual-receptor potency and identify a lipidation site that retains receptor activity while producing an HSA-dependent potency shift consistent with albumin association. Together, these protease-stable PYY(1–36) analogues expand the chemical framework for preserving native multireceptor pharmacology in DPP4-sensitive peptides and for engineering long-acting therapeutic analogues.

items.title:
Oncogenic Cysteines
Create Peroxide-Sensitive Regulatory
States That Impair GAP-Mediated Shutoff in KRAS
items.abstract: Abstract Covalent KRAS-G12C inhibitors exploit an acquired cysteine in the nucleotide-binding P-loop, and prior work established that oxidation can limit inhibitor engagement. Here we asked whether peroxide-dependent cysteine chemistry also affects GAP-mediated KRAS shutoff. Using purified KRAS variants, chemoselective sulfenic- and sulfinic-acid probes, intact-protein mass spectrometry, nucleotide-displacement and exchange assays, multiple-turnover phosphate-release assays, and multireplica molecular dynamics simulations, we compared WT-KRAS, G12C, G13C, and selected C118S backgrounds. G12C-containing variants accumulated strong BTD-trappable sulfenic-acid signal that persisted after C118 substitution, supporting C12 as its principal source. DiaAlk profiling identified a substantial C118-associated sulfination component and residual C118-independent labeling in G13C. GDP-bound simulations identified differences in phosphate proximity and local ion association, providing structural context for the distinct chemical profiles. Nucleotide-displacement responses were variant- and treatment-dependent, and detectable SOS1-mediated exchange persisted. For the functional assay, KRAS peroxide pretreatment was followed by complete catalase-mediated peroxide removal before GAP-334 addition. The GAP-dependent apparent phosphate-release slope increment was markedly reduced in G12C and G13C, whereas WT retained a substantial response. This differential response persisted after normalization to each variant’s own untreated GAP increment. The simplest interpretation is that cysteine oxidation and accompanying structural changes impair GAP responsiveness in these oncogenic variants. These findings identify a peroxide-sensitive dimension of KRAS regulation without assigning the functional effect to a single oxidation species or elementary catalytic step.

items.title:
Efficient G-Quadruplex
RNA Resolution Mediated
by Dimeric Suv3 Helicase
items.abstract: Abstract G-quadruplexes (G4) are stable secondary structures that can impede DNA replication, transcription, and translation. Although the human mitochondrial helicase Suv3 (SUPV3L1) is essential for RNA unwinding in mitochondrial RNA decay pathways, its involvement in resolving G4-RNA remains poorly characterized. Here, we demonstrate that dimeric Suv3 binds G4-RNA with nanomolar affinity, independently of ATP and irrespective of a 3′ overhang. However, efficient catalytic resolution of G4-RNA by Suv3 requires both ATP hydrolysis and a minimum 3′ single-stranded overhang of approximately 12 nucleotides to serve as a loading dock. Our findings support a translocation-based mechanism whereby efficient G4 resolution is initiated by the binding of Suv3 to G4-RNA with a long 3′ overhang, and this interaction triggers ATP hydrolysis, subsequent enzyme translocation, and G4 unfolding. We further show that dimeric Suv3 is markedly more effective than its monomeric counterpart in resolving G4-RNA, particularly under physiologically relevant mitochondrial salt conditions. Structural modeling supports that dimeric Suv3 functions as an asymmetric complex, with one of the subunits together with the C-terminal tails interacting with the G4 core structure, while the other subunit tethers the long 3′ overhang to enhance enzymatic efficiency and processivity. Together, these results establish Suv3 as a mitochondrial G4-RNA resolvase and provide a mechanistic framework for understanding how Suv3 dysfunction is linked to aberrant RNA processing in mitochondria and disease.

items.title:
Synthesis and
PEGylation Strategy for Bradykinin-Potentiating
Peptides from Animal Venoms
items.abstract: Abstract Polyethylene glycol (PEG) conjugation is one of the most established bioconjugation strategies and is FDA-approved due to its low toxicity, high solubility, extended circulation time, and low immunogenicity. In this study, we synthesized and PEGylated three venom-derived peptides: TsHpt-I17–25 (KETNAKPPA) from Tityus serrulatus scorpion venom, Lmr-BPP-9 (WPPRPQIPP) from Lachesis muta rhombeata snake venom, and Bj-BPP-10c (ENWPHPQIPP) from Bothrops jararaca snake venom, and evaluated their biological activities in vitro and in vivo. Peptides were obtained by solid-phase synthesis, purified by HPLC, and characterized by mass spectrometry and Tricine-SDS-PAGE. PEGylation was performed using mPEG-aldehyde, and ACE inhibitory activity in vitro was assessed for PEGylated and non-PEGylated forms. In vitro, Lmr-BPP-9 (IC50 = 5.19 ± 0.2 μg/1.56 ± 0.05 μM) and Bj-BPP-10c (IC50 = 13.59 ± 2.14 μg/4.08 ± 0.18 μM) showed significant ACE inhibition, whereas TsHpt-I17–25 was inactive. Notably, PEGylated peptides displayed no ACE inhibitory activity and were not tested in vivo. In vivo, the synthetic peptides Lmr-BPP-9 and Bj-BPP-10c did not reduce blood pressure, possibly due to proteolytic degradation or structural alterations during synthesis. Conversely, TsHpt-I17–25 unexpectedly induced a hypertensive response. In conclusion, our findings demonstrate both the therapeutic promise and the challenges of developing venom-derived peptides as drug leads. While PEGylation can enhance peptide stability, it may compromise biological activity, especially in small peptides. Future efforts should explore alternative conjugation strategies to preserve functionality while improving pharmacological properties.

items.title: Visualization of CryoEM Hydrogen Peaks in the Photosystem II Reaction Center P 680 Chlorophyll Pair
items.abstract: Abstract X-ray crystallography reports only on the electron density (ED) distribution in molecules, and neutron crystallography only describes the distribution of nuclei. CryoEM visualizes both simultaneously and thus can provide unique information about the electronic structures of molecules that neither of its competitors can do alone. Hydrogen peaks in CryoEM maps are an order of magnitude larger than those in X-ray crystallographic maps. This makes it possible to visualize them in CryoEM maps even when they are not fully resolved from the peaks of the heavy atoms to which they are bonded. Here, I report the results obtained when the methods I have developed for locating the hydrogen peaks were applied to photosystem II (PSII) reaction center P680 chlorophyll pair (A404/D404), its protein ligands (D1-H198 and D2-H197), and flanking residues (I192-G204 of the D1 subunit and T191-A202 of D2) in a CryoEM map having a resolution of 1.71 Å. Hydrogen peaks were found at all the chemically expected locations except for two. First, the orientations of the two methylene hydrogen peaks of the vinyl substituent on A404 were found to differ from those of the same vinyl methylene hydrogens of all the other chlorophylls in PSII. They were orthogonal to the expected plane instead of being in-plane. Second, in the backbone I192O–H195N hydrogen-bonding (HB) pair, the hydrogen peak was found to be next to D1-I192O, rather than D1-H195N, which indicates that this hydrogen atom is part of a carboxyl-imide hydrogen bond rather than a carbonyl-amide hydrogen bond.

items.title:
N-n-Propylnorapomorphine
Inhibits Huntingtin
Aggregation and Lipid Membrane Interactions
items.abstract: Abstract Aggregation of mutant huntingtin (HTT) contributes to Huntington’s disease (HD) pathogenesis. Lipid membranes strongly influence this process and can also be damaged by membrane-associated HTT species. N–n-propylnorapomorphine (NPA), an aporphine-derived dopamine agonist, was identified in a polydiacetylene (PDA)-based screen for compounds that reduce HTT-exon1-induced perturbation of lipid vesicles. Here, thioflavin T fluorescence assays, ex situ and in situ atomic force microscopy (AFM), lipid-vesicle binding assays, and supported-lipid-bilayer imaging were used to determine how NPA affects HTT aggregation and membrane interactions. In bulk solution, NPA reduced β-sheet-rich fibril formation in a dose-dependent manner, with high concentrations nearly abolishing fibril growth. AFM imaging further showed that NPA suppresses fibril formation while altering the oligomer morphology and heterogeneity. NPA also destabilized preformed HTT fibrils and suppressed the surface-mediated aggregation of an HTT-derived peptide. Importantly, NPA retained inhibitory activity in the presence of lipid vesicles that either suppressed or accelerated HTT aggregation. NPA reduced HTT association with lipid vesicles in a dose-dependent manner and markedly decreased HTT-induced disruption of supported brain lipid bilayers. Collectively, these observations are consistent with NPA acting at multiple, potentially connected stages of the HTT aggregation pathway by altering early assemblies, destabilizing fibrils, and reducing the formation or persistence of membrane-active species. The present data do not distinguish whether these effects arise from a single shared binding mode or from interactions with multiple HTT conformational states. Although its dopamine agonist activity may limit direct therapeutic application, NPA provides a useful proof-of-concept scaffold for compounds targeting both HTT aggregation and membrane-associated toxicity.

items.title: Issue Publication Information
Issue Editorial Masthead

Amyloid-β42 Drives Collagen-Independent
Activation of Discoidin Domain Receptor 2 in Alzheimer’s Disease
items.abstract: Abstract Discoidin domain receptor 2 (DDR2), a receptor tyrosine kinase (RTK) family member, plays a pivotal role in collagen-mediated signaling, influencing several key cellular processes. In Alzheimer’s disease (AD), DDR2 expression and activity are significantly upregulated. While collagens, the endogenous ligands of DDR2, either remain unchanged or are downregulated in AD-like conditions, Amyloid-beta 42 (Aβ42) has been found to activate DDR2 noncanonically in the absence of collagen. Additionally, DDR2 naturally translocates to the nucleus in the neuroblastoma cell line SH-SY5Y, and the nuclear pool of DDR2 further increases in the presence of Aβ42, suggesting a novel pathological role for DDR2 in AD. The E113K mutant of DDR2, where the collagen-binding site has been compromised, fails to get activated by collagen, whereas Aβ42 could still activate it. Furthermore, the DDR2 inhibitor WRG-28 effectively inhibits Aβ42 induced phosphorylation of the protein. We have modeled the ectodomain of DDR2 in silico, extending it through the transmembrane helix and subsequently docked the Aβ42 pentamer to provide a structural hypothesis for elucidating the mechanistic basis of Aβ-mediated kinase activation. Additionally, we analyzed WRG-28 binding by forming a ternary complex among DDR2, Aβ42, and WRG-28. Our structural analyses offer key insights into the molecular mechanisms governing DDR2 activation by Aβ42 and its inhibition by WRG-28 in the AD cell model, providing a foundation for targeted therapeutic strategies.

items.title:
From Monomer
to Mesh: The Biochemical Maturation of
Gel-Forming Mucin Glycoproteins
items.abstract: Abstract Secreted mucin glycoproteins, which form the scaffolds of the mucus hydrogels coating tissue epithelia, are among the most complex molecules in nature. Mucin protein backbones are typically more than 5000 amino acids in length, become stapled into domain folds by over 100 disulfide bonds, and contain thousands of potential sites for O-glycosylation. The glycans added to these sites vary in chemical composition, length, and degree of branching, producing mucins with diverse biochemical and biophysical properties. In addition to this chemical complexity, structural heterogeneity arises via hinges between domains, long segments of natively disordered polypeptide, and intrinsic glycan flexibility.
