By retaining the standard P3M decomposition, P3MaZe preserves the systematic accuracy controls associated with the real-space cutoff, the Ewald splitting, the mesh spacing, and the charge assignment procedure, while replacing the conventional multigrid Poisson solver by a constrained correction problem. The method is validated for molten NaCl and simple point-charge flexible water (SPC/Fw). Values of the potential, structural, translational, collective, and rotational dynamical observables are in quantitative agreement with those obtained with established electrostatic methods, including real-space P3M, and Ewald summation. We further show that, for the linear, time-independent Poisson operator considered here, the constrained correction problem is algebraically equivalent to a direct Poisson solve initialized by a chronological extrapolation of the mesh potential, a connection not previously established for MaZe-based approaches. This result identifies the precise mechanism through which acceleration of the iterative long-range solve is achieved, and we exploit it systematically through higher-order predictors to further improve convergence, while retaining the expected linear scaling with system size. Because the underlying extrapolation is independent of the constrained-dynamics formalism, it can, of course, also be used directly to accelerate conventional iterative real-space Poisson solvers.
items.journal: Journal of Chemical Theory and Computation

items.title:
Can DFT-Trained
Neural Network Potentials Reproduce
Structure, Solvation, and Water-Exchange Properties in Aqueous Magnesium
Solutions?
items.abstract: Abstract Magnesium ions play an essential role in many biological processes but remain challenging to model in biomolecular simulations. Despite considerable scientific effort, classical force fields fail to simultaneously reproduce key structural, thermodynamic, and kinetic solution properties, likely due to their inability to explicitly account for quantum many-body effects. Here, we develop and systematically benchmark MACE neural network potentials (NNPs) for aqueous MgCl2 solutions, trained on revPBE-D3/zd and revPBE0-D3/zd density functional theory reference data, and assess their ability to reproduce a broad range of experimental solution properties including the structure of the first hydration shell, diffusion coefficient, activity derivative, water-exchange rate, and mechanism as well as solvation free energy. Both NNPs accurately reproduce the octahedral structure of the first hydration shell, ion-pairing properties, and diffusion coefficients. Combining the NNPs with transition path sampling and other enhanced sampling techniques allows us to capture the rare event of water exchange in the first hydration shell of Mg2+, revealing a dissociative exchange mechanism. Transition interface sampling yields exchange rates within 1 order of magnitude of experiment, representing a substantial improvement over classical dissociative force fields. In contrast, the NNP-derived solvation free energy significantly underestimates the experimental value, revealing a limitation of the present local NNP architecture for describing ion solvation thermodynamics. Our results demonstrate that DFT-trained NNPs can accurately describe Mg2+ hydration structure, diffusion, ion pairing, and exchange kinetics while highlighting limitations of local NNP architectures and the importance of long-range electrostatic contributions to achieve quantitative agreement with experimental ion solvation free energies.
items.journal: Journal of Chemical Theory and Computation

items.title:
Cavity Quantum
Electrodynamic Nuclear–Electronic
Orbital Complete Active Space Configuration Interaction
items.abstract: Abstract Polaritons offer the possibility of modifying chemical properties through the strong coupling of molecules to photons confined in optical cavities. From a first-principles perspective, understanding how these strong light–matter interactions cause chemical changes requires quantum mechanical descriptions of electrons, nuclei, and photons. Herein, we develop the ab initio cavity quantum electrodynamic nuclear–electronic orbital complete active space configuration interaction (QED-NEO-CASCI) method, in which electrons, specified nuclei, and cavity photons are all treated quantum mechanically. Using this method, we are able to describe hydrogen tunneling under vibrational strong coupling and geometry changes in a hydrogen-bonded complex coupled to a cavity. Under vibronic strong coupling, we observe features in the polaritonic absorption spectrum that correspond to Raman active transitions outside a cavity. We also develop the real-time variant, denoted time-dependent configuration interaction (QED-NEO-TDCI). This method allows us to simulate nonadiabatic hydrogen tunneling dynamics and observe the real-time quantum mechanical transfer of energy between the molecule and cavity photons. These methods provide the ab initio foundation for studying correlated electronic–nuclear–photonic chemical physics.
items.journal: Journal of Chemical Theory and Computation

items.title:
Δ-HGPR: A Hierarchical Gaussian Process
Framework for Active-Learning Δ-Potentials
items.abstract: Abstract Δ-learning, which uses machine learning to represent only the difference between a high-accuracy reference and a lower-accuracy base calculator, is a promising route to high-fidelity molecular dynamics (MD) with limited training data, but it has lacked a unified protocol combining hierarchical descriptors with well-defined equilibrium sampling. We propose Δ-HGPR (hierarchical Gaussian process regression for Δ-learning), a framework for learning difference potentials, and its MD instantiation, Δ-HGPR-MD. The framework combines (i) a difference potential written as an additive radial (inverse-distance) term plus a many-body machine-learning correction, determined by a single regularized least-squares fit; (ii) the ensemble force standard deviation as an active-learning indicator with an automatically scaled threshold; and (iii) a difference potential held fixed within each round so that equilibrium NVT sampling is well-defined in both exploration and production. The many-body term of Δ-HGPR-MD uses smooth overlap of atomic positions (SOAP) descriptors with random Fourier features (Δ-HGPR-RFF). On a toy system whose difference potential contains a 1/r contribution beyond the cutoff of the local descriptor, the many-body term alone reproduces none of this force, however many features it is given, whereas the hierarchy recovers 99% of it, with a reach set by the cutoff of its radial term. In MD, the hierarchy reproduces about 80% of the shift of the ion-pair distribution toward the reference, while the many-body term alone leaves it where the base places it. On malonaldehyde and the Zundel cation H5O2+ with three base calculators, Δ-HGPR-RFF removes barrier errors of up to 0.1 eV under one protocol, giving free-energy barriers statistically indistinguishable from DFT; free-energy perturbation shows that the error contributed by the learned correction is below 0.01 eV on average in every case. For H5O2+with ANI-2x, whose dynamics collapse without correction, it recovers the Zundel geometry and a barrier and transition count consistent with DFT.
items.journal: Journal of Chemical Theory and Computation

items.title:
Investigation of
Magnetic Properties in Exchange Coupled
Radical-Nickelocene Complexes by Adopting a Generalized Spin Hamiltonian
items.abstract: Abstract Magnetic interaction between an isotropic spin center and a strongly anisotropic partner presents a unique challenge in molecular magnetism, as the interplay between local anisotropy and exchange pathways often defies conventional Heisenberg exchange. In this work, we address this complexity by investigating a series of nitronyl-nitroxide radicals coupled to nickelocene through polyene spacers of increasing length. Both density functional theory and wave function based multireference approaches are adopted to investigate the nature of isotropic exchange in these systems. To resolve the limitations of standard spin models, we employ a mapping approach based on an effective Hamiltonian derived from CASSCF + NEVPT2 spin–orbit eigenstates. By treating the system’s low-lying electronic structure through this extended framework, we explicitly account for the significant mixing between the ground and first excited spin states which is found to be responsible for an anomalous increase in the axial zero-field splitting (D). We find that increasing the model space to include antiferromagnetic states recovers the full zero-field splitting while enabling finite anisotropic exchange contributions to be extracted. By establishing a systematic distance dependence for these interactions, this work provides a rigorous framework for navigating the nontrivial coupling mechanisms in complex organic–inorganic spin architectures.
items.journal: Journal of Chemical Theory and Computation

items.title:
Electron Spin Decoherence due to Hindered Rotation
in Donor-Bridge-Acceptor Linked Molecules
items.abstract: Abstract Extraordinarily broad line widths for the magnetic field effects (MFEs) on radical pair recombination in rigid oligoaromatic donor-bridge-acceptor molecules have been successfully simulated by the full-hybrid Monte Carlo (MC) MD simulation, in which modulation of the exchange coupling due to hindered rotation is directly calculated. It has been demonstrated that the single-site Liouville equation gives nearly identical results at general diffusional rotation times (&lt; a few nanoseconds) if the effective exchange coupling and singlet–triplet dephasing rate constants are estimated from the electron-only MC simulation of spin coherence. Furthermore, the single-site model is applicable to multinuclear simulations of the so-called low-field effect, which is due to the coherent superposition of the degenerate zero-field eigenstates. These findings ensure MD-assisted spin dynamics simulations with high accuracy and fewer computational resources.
items.journal: Journal of Chemical Theory and Computation

items.title:
SPectroscopy Informed
Configurational Enhanced Sampling
(SPICES)
items.abstract: Abstract We present a new enhanced-sampling scheme for obtaining the underlying conformer starting from a spectrum: the SPectroscopy Informed Configurational Enhanced Sampling (SPICES) method. SPICES is driven by a history-dependent biased molecular dynamics, in which the biases are governed by spectral information rather than by energetic considerations. The performance of SPICES is hence rather insensitive to the target conformer’s relative energy compared to the global minimum structure. Furthermore, it does not require pretraining or prior knowledge of the system. We have critically assessed the performance of SPICES and demonstrated that it can identify the correct conformer of our test system, diphenylalanine (FF), among the 400 stable conformations in 22 spectral calculations (median value). We also show that SPICES is robust to noise in the experimental spectrum and to small discrepancies between theory and experiment.
items.journal: Journal of Chemical Theory and Computation

items.title:
Mixed Quantum/Classical
Theory for Fine-Structure
Inelastic Transitions in the Scattering of 2Π Molecule
with Structureless Target
items.abstract: Abstract Mixed Quantum/Classical Theory (MQCT) offers an efficient alternative for computing molecular scattering cross sections, scaling favorably with the size of the basis as compared to the exact close-coupling methods. In this work, the MQCT framework is extended to the rotationally inelastic scattering of 2Π molecules with structureless targets, using the Ar + NO (X2Π) system as a benchmark. The time-dependent equations of motion are solved for independent MQCT trajectories by treating the translational motion classically and the electronic and rotational motions quantum mechanically. This formalism naturally incorporates electronic nonadiabatic couplings, enabling calculations of state-to-state cross sections across all possible transitions, including pure rotational excitation, transitions between spin–orbit manifolds and between the individual states of Λ-doublet components. For validation purposes, these are compared against exact full-quantum calculations using HIBRIDON package. Good quantitative agreement is observed, with complicated quantum interference effects successfully reproduced, specifically capturing major features of the Λ-doublet propensity.
items.journal: Journal of Chemical Theory and Computation

items.title:
Augmented Roothaan-Hall
Hessian Applied to Spin-Restricted
Open-Shell Density Functional Theory
items.abstract: Abstract We generalize the augmented Roothaan–Hall (ARH) Hessian formalism to the self-consistent field (SCF) optimization of spin-restricted open-shell (RO) wave functions, encompassing high-spin, low-spin, and two-determinant electronic states. A detailed ARH formulation is presented. We demonstrate that ARH is a highly efficient optimization algorithm for rapidly identifying accurate SCF solutions, primarily owing to its systematic construction of an effective Hessian, particularly in the case of Euclidean quadratic energy functions. The ARH is built upon a universal energy formulation, including grid-based integration, for spin-restricted closed-shell, spin-unrestricted, and RO density functional theory (DFT), thereby unifying and simplifying their numerical implementation. The performance of the present method is evaluated using two benchmarking studies. First, for a series of iron–sulfur clusters exhibiting different spin states, which represent notoriously challenging SCF problems, the ARH algorithm demonstrates superior convergence efficiency relative to L-BFGS and truncated Newton methods, requiring much fewer RO-SCF iterations to achieve convergence. Second, the ARH approach tends to avoid convergence to higher-energy stationary points in two-determinant RO-SCF calculations for singlet excited states of selected photoactive compounds. Finally, an application of the ARH-based RO-SCF is illustrated by an investigation of the mechanistic origin of the spin-crossover phenomenon in a Ni(II)-porphyrin complex utilized as a contrast agent.
items.journal: Journal of Chemical Theory and Computation

items.title:
DeepHartree: A
Poisson-Coupled Neural Field for One-Shot
Density Functional Theory
items.abstract: Abstract Linear-combination-of-atomic-orbital (LCAO) density functional theory (DFT) incurs steep costs when it constructs Coulomb terms and iterates the self-consistent field (SCF) equations. Matrix-learning approaches can bypass parts of this workflow, but their outputs inherit the dimensions and conventions of a fixed orbital basis. We introduce DeepHartree, a Poisson-coupled neural field that connects continuous real-space prediction to LCAO electronic structure. An E(3)-equivariant network predicts the Hartree potential, and the Poisson equation converts this potential into electron density. Atom-centered Gaussian fields resolve the near-nuclear region, while a molecule-level correction enforces the electron count. Analytical Gaussian integrals and numerical quadrature connect the predicted fields to the Kohn–Sham matrix. One diagonalization provides estimates of frontier orbital energies and the occupied subspace, and yields the density matrix used to evaluate energy components and initialize SCF. Mean molecular weighted normalized mean absolute errors (wNMAEs) are 0.110% for QM9 and 0.199% for VQM24 on PySCF level-0 grids, increasing to 1.366% and 2.218%, respectively, on level-3 grids. Models trained on def2-SVP densities transfer without retraining to def2-TZVP and def2-QZVP, retaining total-energy accuracy and occupied-subspace agreement. The Hybrid method combines finite differences and first-order automatic differentiation with analytical Gaussian integrals and multilevel quadrature to accelerate field-to-matrix conversion. It achieves near-linear density-matrix construction in both alkanes and PEG chains. For the 1004-atom PEG chain, this construction is 8.75-fold faster than full AD and 7.34-fold faster than converged GPU4PySCF SCF. Without fine-tuning, the QM9 model attains a total-energy MAE of 9.437 meV atom–1 on 1000 larger OE62 molecules. Across the three basis sets, DeepHartree initialization reduces mean QM9 SCF iteration counts by 15.3–15.6%. For a 620-atom organic cage, it reduces total SCF wall-clock time by 12.9%, including initialization. These results establish continuous electrostatic fields as an accurate and scalable interface between machine learning and LCAO DFT.
items.journal: Journal of Chemical Theory and Computation

items.title:
Predicting Ternary
Complex Stability through Binding
Free-Energy Calculations in the Geometric Route
items.abstract: Abstract Molecular glue-induced targeted protein degradation is a powerful emerging therapeutic modality that exploits the ubiquitin-proteasome degradation pathway to break down proteins associated with disease proliferation. At the structural level, degradation proceeds through the formation of a ternary complex induced by small molecules between the target protein and an E3 ligase. Unlike PROTACs, molecular glues do not require a chemical linker and tend to stabilize preexisting native protein–protein interactions. Computational screening of novel glues is challenging, in large part due to the complexity and high degree of cooperativity involved in the formation of the ternary complex interface. Here, we present a rigorous Molecular Dynamics-based simulation protocol that uses Umbrella Sampling to calculate the ternary complex binding free energy. The protocol follows a geometric thermodynamic cycle with conformational and Boresch-style orientational restraints to drive the system from bound to unbound. Our framework successfully predicts the effect of single-point interface mutations on the relative stability of the CK1α-lenalidomide-CRBN ternary complex (R2 = 0.95 compared to experimental binding affinities). We also study a series of systems related to the BRD4 degraders IBG1 and IBG3, which recruit the DCAF16 E3 ligase. We rank various complexes engaging DCAF16 by their binding free energies and achieve an ordering that is consistent with the trends observed in biophysical assays. Of particular note is our ability to assert the reliance of BRD4 selectivity on a single interfacial glycine residue, which alternative, reduced-sampling MM/GBSA or HADDOCK scoring methodologies fail to achieve. Overall, our protocol shows promise as a generalizable approach to ranking ternary complexes by thermodynamic stability, potentially aiding in the identification of potent new degraders.
items.journal: Journal of Chemical Theory and Computation

items.title:
An Always-Accepting
Algorithm for Transition Path
Sampling
items.abstract: Abstract We present a one-way shooting algorithm for transition path sampling that accepts every proposed trajectory while sampling the correct transition path ensemble for systems with overdamped stochastic dynamics. The method combines an always reactive path generation scheme with a reweighting procedure that corrects the bias introduced by unit acceptance, improving efficiency by avoiding rejected trajectories. We show its performance on CO2 hydrate formation, where the enhanced efficiency enables the sampling of crystalline channels under conditions inaccessible to conventional algorithms.
items.journal: Journal of Chemical Theory and Computation

items.title:
Accelerating Lead
Optimization Away from Anti-Targets:
Navigating the Structural Complexity of Promiscuous ADMET Proteins
items.abstract: Abstract The development of a small molecule suitable for clinical use involves optimization of ligand binding to an identified target protein but also frequently the reduction of binding to a variety of anti-target proteins known to pose translational risk. These anti-targets, often referred to as ADMET proteins, often contain large, highly flexible binding sites, leading to promiscuous binding of small molecules. This property often frustrates efforts to execute structure-based design against these anti-targets. Here, we demonstrate the application of a combination of induced fit docking and free energy perturbation to structurally enable several of the most common anti-targets: cytochrome P450 isoforms 3A4 and 2D6, the hERG ion channel, and PXR. Crucially, the enforcement of a consensus binding mode across a congeneric series allowed for the efficient exploration of a wide range of receptor conformational space. Results are presented for both public retrospective datasets and prospective application in active drug discovery programs.
items.journal: Journal of Chemical Theory and Computation

items.title:
A High-Performance
Mesoscale Molecular Dynamics Framework
for Polar Ordering in Dipolar Liquid Crystals
items.abstract: Abstract Polar ordering in liquid crystals arises from the interplay between molecular anisotropy and long-range dipole–dipole interactions, making molecular dynamics simulations of formation kinetics computationally demanding due to the cost of evaluating these interactions. Here, we develop a high-performance mesoscale molecular dynamics framework for efficient large-scale simulations of dipolar liquid-crystal systems. The framework incorporates GPU- and DCU-accelerated algorithms for efficiently computing anisotropic Gay-Berne forces and long-range dipole–dipole interactions, and supports generalized Gay-Berne particles carrying an arbitrary number of embedded dipoles with freely assignable positions and orientations. The algorithm employs a multithreaded parallelization strategy with adaptive optimization, yielding significant speedups on heterogeneous computing platforms. We validate the framework against representative ferroelectric and antiferroelectric systems, faithfully reproducing known phase behavior while maintaining computational efficiency. This work provides a versatile molecular dynamics framework for investigating polar ordering and its formation kinetics across a wide range of liquid-crystal systems and dipolar assemblies.
items.journal: Journal of Chemical Theory and Computation

items.title:
Performance of
Neuroevolution Potentials for the Ionic
Liquid [Emim][Ac]: A Systematic Benchmark of Four Density Functionals
items.abstract: Abstract Machine-learned force fields (MLFFs) based on Neuroevolution Potential (NEP) models were developed for the ionic liquid 1-ethyl-3-methylimidazolium acetate ([Emim][Ac]) using first-principles reference data generated with four density functionals: PBE-D3, RPBE-D3, optB88-vdW, and SCAN+rVV10. Using a unified training protocol, the resulting NEP models were systematically benchmarked against structural, thermophysical, transport, and hydrogen-bond-network properties, including radial distribution functions (RDFs), coordination numbers, neutron total scattering profiles, density, viscosity, ionic conductivity, and thermal conductivity. Spearman correlation analysis and weighted composite scoring were further used to establish a property-oriented evaluation framework for MLFF assessment and selection. The results reveal a pronounced dependence of NEP performance on the density functional used to generate the reference data. Although all four models reproduce the dominant local structural features of [Emim][Ac], appreciable differences emerge in medium-range structural ordering and transport properties. The PBE-D3-based NEP provides the most accurate overall description of structural properties, whereas the optB88-vdW-based NEP yields the closest agreement with experimental transport properties, particularly viscosity and ionic conductivity. Analysis of the hydrogen-bond network further reveals systematic relationships among hydrogen-bond populations, residence times, free-ion fractions, and ion transport. These results demonstrate that, for [Emim][Ac], the exchange–correlation functional used for reference-data generation influences the physical fidelity and property-specific performance of the resulting NEP models.
items.journal: Journal of Chemical Theory and Computation

items.title:
Mapping Collective
Electron-Density Rearrangements
at Oil–Water Interfaces Using Optimal Transport
items.abstract: Abstract The electronic and spectroscopic properties of aqueous hydrophobic interfaces continue to be a topic of active research. One such open question is rooted in the origin of the apparent negative charge of oil droplets. Here, we deploy an information-theoretic optimal transport approach dubbed VIPER-CT (Voronoi-Informed Partitioning of Electron Redistribution for Charge Transfer), to construct the electronic T-matrix derived from the real-space electron density determined from first-principles simulations of an extended decane-water interface, sampled using neural-network-based Deep Potential Molecular Dynamics. This matrix operationally separates directional interphase charge transfer (CT) from intraphase density rearrangements. While decane-water molecular clusters of various sizes show small net CT from decane to water, the extended interface displays a systematic opposite electronic asymmetry, yielding a net CT from water to the hydrocarbon phase producing an average surface charge density of ∼0.003 e– nm–2 on the oil phase. This imbalance is accompanied by much larger intraphase self-polarization, particularly within the hydrocarbon phase, demonstrating that collective many-body polarization dominates the interfacial electronic response.
items.journal: Journal of Chemical Theory and Computation

items.title:
Uncertainty Quantification
for Free Energy Calculations
by Generalized Hierarchical Bayesian Inference
items.abstract: Abstract Free energy calculations are routinely used to study molecular processes inaccessible to unbiased molecular dynamics, but their utility ultimately depends on knowing when and how much their predictions can be trusted. Uncertainty estimation is therefore essential for distinguishing genuine physical features of a free energy profile from artifacts arising from limited simulation data or inadequate sampling. Gaussian processes have emerged as a powerful framework for reconstructing free energy profiles together with predictive uncertainties. However, existing implementations typically condition on fixed hyperparameters and observation noise, preventing predictive uncertainties from adapting to the information content of the simulation data. Here, we develop a generalized hierarchical Gaussian process framework that accounts for these neglected sources of uncertainty. Applications to umbrella sampling and extended Lagrangian metadynamics of peptide-lipid membrane interactions demonstrate that the resulting uncertainty estimates track reconstruction errors across a wide range of sampling and data conditions.
items.journal: Journal of Chemical Theory and Computation

items.title:
MARS: Machine-Learned
Force Field Framework for Automated
Conformational Sampling, Vibrational Spectroscopy, and Microsolvation
items.abstract: Abstract We present MARS, an open-source Python package for automated conformational ensemble generation, infrared spectrum prediction, and explicit microsolvation of molecular systems. Built on JAX for GPU acceleration and automatic differentiation, MARS is carried out with machine-learned force fields (MLFFs), including SO3LR and MACE, with a four-phase conformational sampling workflow combining metadynamics, multitemperature molecular dynamics, and genetic algorithms. The package provides automated vibrational mode classification using Wilson B-matrix projections and functional group identification via graph-based pattern matching. We benchmark MARS on chemically diverse systems, including alkanes, halogenated aromatics, amino acids, peptides, drug-like molecules, phosphamides, host–guest complexes, and microsolvated biomolecular models. Semiempirical quantum-chemical methods have until now provided the practical state of the art for automated conformational sampling. Our benchmarks show that modern MLFFs can improve upon this paradigm by combining greater accuracy for high-level relative conformer energies with lower computational cost and more favorable scaling with molecular size. IR benchmarks against experimental gas-phase spectra additionally show performance comparable to quantum-chemical methods, with chemically interpretable mode assignments. Applications to alanine peptides, proline/β-cyclodextrin inclusion complexes, alanine dipeptide, and 2-methoxycyclohexanone further demonstrate that MARS captures conformational reorganization, noncovalent binding motifs, solvent-induced stability shifts, and spectroscopic signatures. These results establish MARS as a transferable and accessible platform for ensemble-based molecular modeling with machine-learned potentials. MARS is freely available at github.com/tcpunilu/mars.
items.journal: Journal of Chemical Theory and Computation

items.title:
Incorporating Anharmonicity
of Selected Modes into
Fermi’s Golden Rule Rate Calculations for Large Molecular Systems
items.abstract: Abstract Properties of photofunctional materials are governed by nonadiabatic transitions, and theoretical methods to predict reaction rate constants for nonadiabatic transitions are desired. Fermi’s golden rule (FGR) is one of the most useful approaches for computing rate constants. In particular, FGR combined with the harmonic approximation to the potential energy surface (PES) is widely used, since it requires only geometry optimizations and Hessian calculations for the initial and final states. However, real PESs are inherently anharmonic, and such anharmonicity can affect the rate constant by altering vibrational energy levels and wave functions. In this study, we propose a method for computing rate constants that incorporates anharmonicity into the conventional harmonic-approximation framework. In this method, only a subset of important modes is treated anharmonically, whereas the remaining modes are treated harmonically. We applied the proposed method to two systems: the T1 → S0 nonradiative decay process of 4-pyrone molecule, and the S1 → T1 intersystem crossing process of 3-(9,9-dimethylacridin-10(9H)-yl)-9H-xanthen-9-one (ACRXTN) molecule. The calculation for 4-pyrone revealed that the rate constant decreases by 3 orders of magnitude compared with the harmonic rate when anharmonicity of all vibrational modes is taken into account, indicating the importance of considering the anharmonicity when calculating the rate constant. In addition, it was found that the fully anharmonic rate constant can be reproduced by considering the anharmonicity of only two vibrational modes. Further analysis based on the sum-over-states formalism revealed that this decrease in the rate constant originates from a reduction in the overlaps between the initial- and final-state vibrational eigenfunctions. It was also found that this decrease in the rate constant does not appear unless the anharmonicity of multiple vibrational modes is taken into account simultaneously, even though coupling between vibrational modes is not considered. The application to ACRXTN showed that the anharmonicity associated with dihedral torsional modes has little influence on the rate constant. Comparison of these results revealed that the anharmonicity of vibrational modes with high Huang–Rhys factors and high frequencies, or those whose harmonic frequencies are different between initial and final states, has an impact on the rate constant. The proposed method is expected to be useful for the theoretical design of new photofunctional materials.
items.journal: Journal of Chemical Theory and Computation

items.title:
Reconstructing
All-Electron Densities and Static Structure
Factors from General Pseudopotentials
items.abstract: Abstract Electron densities provide valuable information, such as atomic charges and static structure factors, but all-electron densities can be computationally expensive to obtain. This work presents a method to approximate all-electron densities from pseudopotential electronic structure calculations, called the Valence Electrons Plus Independent Cores (VEPIC) model. For each pseudopotential in the calculation, a pseudocore is defined, and this is added to the ab initio pseudovalence density. Electron densities obtained this way yield accurate static structure factors, as well as atomic charges and dipoles from the Hirshfeld and Minimal Basis Iterative Stockholder methods, compared with those from all-electron calculations. While the total density of this model matches the all-electron density in the valence region, the model lacks core polarization, which is present in the Projector Augmented Wave (PAW) method, making the VEPIC model an intermediate between the Independent Atom Model (IAM) and the PAW model in terms of accuracy. It is also intermediate between the two in terms of computational complexity, as it only requires the pseudovalence density, unlike PAW, which additionally requires processing every pseudovalence wave function in the system.
items.journal: Journal of Chemical Theory and Computation

items.title:
Correlating Metal-Water Interactions and Double-Layer
Capacitance at Gold and Silver: Revisit of Single-Crystal Experiments
Using a Unified Theoretical Model
items.abstract: Abstract We quantify how metal identity and crystallographic orientation shape the electrical double layer (EDL) and differential capacitance (Cdl) in weakly adsorbing electrolytes. The concentration-dependent Cdl curves of Ag(110), Ag(100), Ag(111), and Au(110) in aqueous KPF6, are quantitatively analyzed using the density-potential functional theory (DPFT). The comparative analysis results in four key findings. First, in accordance with conventional understanding, Cdl is dominated by the diffuse layer and is identical for Ag and Au electrodes near their respective potential of zero free charge (pzfc) at the same low electrolyte concentrations. Second, the Cdl sequence of Ag(110)&gt;Ag(100)&gt;Ag(111) at their pzfc at the same higher electrolyte concentration is attributed to facet-dependent water adsorption. Third, under same solution conditions, Ag(110) shows a higher Cdl peak and smaller peak-to-peak spacing than Au(110), reflecting differences in short-range metal-water interaction, metal-ion interaction and electron spillover at the metal surface. Fourth, partial desolvation under strong interfacial fields further reshapes the ionic distribution and lifts the Cdl curves away from the pzfc. Overall, these results map macroscopic capacitance fingerprints onto microscopic EDL structure within a unified DPFT framework.
items.journal: Journal of Chemical Theory and Computation

items.title:
Force Fields and
Simulation Engines: Lessons Learned
from Porting Amber ff14SB and ff19SB to GROMACS
items.abstract: Abstract The GROMACS molecular dynamics simulation package has historically supported a number of molecular mechanics force fields, including Amber. Force fields have evolved over time and continue to do so through refinement of existing interactions and the definition of additional ones to more faithfully match real-world experiments and higher-level quantum chemistry calculations. Although users have provided a number of conversions of newer Amber force fields over the years, the two most recent Amber protein force fields, ff14SB and ff19SB, had not previously been officially ported to GROMACS. A technical challenge is that ff19SB introduces residue-specific backbone dihedral energy correction maps (CMAPs), which required new support in GROMACS for residue-aware force-field preprocessing and topology generation. Unlike older force fields such as CHARMM27, in which CMAPs are parameterized using only atom types, ff19SB extends this scheme with additional amino-acid typing. Here, we describe how we ported and validated the Amber ff14SB and ff19SB force fields for use with GROMACS as AMBER14SB and AMBER19SB, respectively. The ported force fields reproduce the Amber reference topologies exactly, with per-interaction energies matching to within the single-precision floating-point limit (&lt;10–7 kJ/mol). To achieve this level of consistency between Amber and GROMACS, we resolved discrepancies in their handling of fundamental constants, parameter precision, and improper-dihedral atom ordering logic. In long unrestrained ubiquitin simulations, the converted ff19SB reproduces the conformational free-energy profile obtained with the native Amber implementation. This work provides the first official port of an Amber force field to GROMACS in more than a decade, improving feature parity between the two simulation packages. We provide a reproducible porting and validation procedure that can be used for modified variants and future versions of Amber force fields.
items.journal: Journal of Chemical Theory and Computation

items.title:
Differentiable
OPLS Force-Field Parameterization for
Ionic Electrolytes and High-Throughput Application to Lithium-Ion
Batteries
items.abstract: Abstract The rational design of lithium-ion battery (LIB) electrolytes is severely impeded by the vast chemical space of solvent–salt combinations and the inefficiency of empirical trial-and-error approaches. Molecular dynamics (MD) bridges microscopic solvation structures and macroscopic physicochemical properties, but classical force fields (FFs) often lack accuracy for multicomponent electrolytes. To address this, we develop an automated differentiable OPLS-AA FF parametrization workflow tailored for ionic electrolytes. It employs topology-guided atom typing to reduce parameter redundancy and optimizes Lennard-Jones parameters via the DMFF framework. A uniform charge-scaling scheme approximates condensed-phase charge transfer and polarization. Density serves as the structural/thermodynamic fitting target, while ionic conductivity provides the independent transport benchmark, ensuring balanced accuracy. Rigorous convergence tests establish a standardized protocol with ∼100,000-atom systems and 35–40 ns NVT trajectories for reliable transport property calculations. Furthermore, high-throughput simulations of over 10,000 formulations─encompassing 67 solvents and 15 lithium salts─are performed on Tianqiong, a special-purpose supercomputer for molecular dynamics simulations that has been validated to deliver numerically equivalent results to GPUs with superior efficiency. A comprehensive data set is generated covering five key electrolyte properties. The t-SNE visualization reveals partial clustering of distinct salt chemistries, continuous property gradients as functions of salt concentration and temperature, and internal physical self-consistency across the measured electrolyte parameters while simultaneously identifying solvent components as another critical performance determinant. The accurate, transferable FF and the rich data resource establish a robust foundation for future data-driven design of ionic electrolytes.
items.journal: Journal of Chemical Theory and Computation

items.title:
Localized and Delocalized
Nonadiabatic Vibronic Models
Unravel Chiroptical Trends and Design Principles in Symmetric π
Conjugated Macrocycles
items.abstract: Abstract The chiroptical response of π-conjugated macrocycles assembled from repeating chromophores can be remarkably intense, yet how it scales with ring size, and what controls it, remains only partly understood. Here we investigate a series of axially chiral diethynylspirobifluorene macrocycles, (Pn)-DESn (n = 2, 3, 4; D2, D3 and D4 symmetry), combining accurate nonadiabatic quantum dynamics with two complementary linear vibronic coupling Hamiltonians: a delocalized model, whose diabatic states span the whole macrocycle, and a localized, exciton-like model built from the excitations of the individual fragments. Both reproduce the experimental one-photon absorption and electronic circular dichroism (ECD) spectra and reveal that nonadiabatic interactions, conical intersections and (pseudo-)Jahn–Teller couplings govern their shapes; a hierarchical representation of the Hamiltonian keeps the simulations tractable, even for (P4)-DES4, with more than 500 vibrational modes. A simple symmetry analysis bridges the two pictures, tracing every coupling back to the single excited-state gradient of the monomer and partitions the magnetic transition dipole into an intrinsic contribution, from the strained monomer and an extrinsic, excitonic one. This decomposition rationalizes the observed trends explaining why the ECD grows super-linearly with ring size. As a result, the response crosses over from strain-dominated chirality in (P2)-DES2 to excitonic chirality in (P4)-DES4 at a nearly constant dissymmetry factor. Crucially, the excitonic rotatory strengths form a nearly conservative couplet whose oppositely signed branches partly cancel, and their splitting (0.12–0.16 eV) is comparable to the width of the vibronic progressions. The intrinsic band shape of the monomer, not the splitting alone, therefore sets how much ECD survives. We translate these findings into geometric, excitonic and vibronic design principles for g-factor improved symmetric chiral macrocycles, suggesting that our proposed computational approach can be a fast screening tool for new designed macrocycles before synthesis.
items.journal: Journal of Chemical Theory and Computation

items.title:
Data-Driven Complete
Basis Set Limit Estimates from
a Minimal Auxiliary Basis
items.abstract: Abstract Quantum chemistry calculations are often performed using atom-centered basis sets, which are chosen to balance accuracy and cost. While they are systematically improvable, the total energy converges slowly with basis set size toward the complete basis set (CBS) limit. Common extrapolation methods require several intermediate-quality calculations to afford an estimate of the CBS energy. We propose a minimal complementary auxiliary basis set (CABS) baseline to estimate the CBS energy from a single quantum chemistry calculation in a minimal basis set via kernel ridge regression (KRR), which is more efficient than both direct and Δ-machine learning and 40× faster than triple-ζ single-point calculations. The spatial and alchemical gradients from minimal basis and minimal CABS are more accurate than double-ζ (DZ) calculations. We show that KRR on standard molecular representations can be improved by approximating atom-wise local kernels using Chebyshev polynomials, which allows us to train KRR models 10×–50× times faster on moderate compute resources, thereby enabling a data-driven approach toward the mean-field CBS, combining physical baselines capturing leading-order effects with data-efficient machine learning models.
items.journal: Journal of Chemical Theory and Computation

items.title:
Multiplicative
Error Analysis: A Scale-Invariant View
of TDDFT Two-Photon Absorption Benchmarks
items.abstract: Abstract Two-photon absorption (2PA) strengths span several orders of magnitude, yet time-dependent density functional theory (TDDFT) benchmark studies have commonly relied on raw-scale mean absolute errors and linear regression statistics. Such statistics can be dominated by the most intense transitions and do not distinguish systematic multiplicative bias, typical fold error, dynamic range reproduction, and rank preservation. Here, published TDDFT 2PA benchmarks based on coupled-cluster references are reanalyzed by using a scale-invariant, multiplicative framework. For the most widely used benchmark set [J. Chem.Theory Comput. 2022, 18, 1046], it is shown that the five strongest transitions, representing only approximately 10% of the data, account for up to 65.5% of the total raw absolute error. Consequently, raw-scale metrics assign disproportionate weight to a small number of intense transitions and may obscure method performance across the remainder of the intensity range. Across several benchmark sets, the analysis further reveals that similar raw-scale errors can arise from qualitatively different error structures. The multiplicative analysis goes beyond previously recognized qualitative trends by resolving them into directly comparable and interpretable components. These results demonstrate that neither individual raw-scale metrics nor their combinations provide a sufficient basis for identifying a reliable or generally recommended functional, and they support a multidimensional, scale-invariant assessment of 2PA benchmarks. The same framework may also be useful for other properties for which multiplicative errors provide a more appropriate description than additive deviations such as oscillator strengths, kinetic and radiative rate constants, and equilibrium constants.
items.journal: Journal of Chemical Theory and Computation

items.title: Rationale‐Guided and Iterative Learning for Redesigning a Highly Enantio‐ and Chemoselective Flavin‐Dependent Phenolic Hydroxylase
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Flavin‐dependent monooxygenases (FDMOs) can catalyze C─H hydroxylation of phenolic compounds, yet the scope of their application has never been challenged beyond the hydroxylation of simple substrates nor explored for the ability to achieve selective hydroxylation. FDMO hydroxylation is often poorly controlled, yielding unstable, multiply hydroxylated products. Here, we used a mechanistic insight‐guided iterative learning workflow to redesign the active site of p ‐hydroxyphenylacetate hydroxylase to expand its capability for chemo‐ and enantioselective control in the synthesis of ( R )‐norepinephrine. Within only three rounds of an engineering campaign, a DISD_LG variant that switched from ( S )‐ to ( R )‐selective hydroxylation was obtained with excellent enantioselectivity (97.6%ee ( R )). This variant also produced markedly fewer multiply hydroxylated products (<5% relative amount in the product mixture), indicating significant improvement in chemoselective control. The kinetic resolution was performed at a 20‐mL scale (4 mM racemic substrate) and ( R )‐norepinephrine was obtained with 48.8% isolated yield and 96.2%ee ( R ). The molecular mechanisms underlying the enantio‐ and chemoselective control achieved by the DISD_LG variant were elucidated using molecular dynamics simulations. This work presents an enzyme engineering workflow to achieve kinetic resolution in combination with a controllable degree of hydroxylation, the aspects previously overlooked or underemphasized in FDMOs.

items.title: Pronounced Visible‐Light Cryptochirality Detection of Various Terpenoids via Helical Polyaromatic Capsules
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Cryptochirality refers to molecular chirality with undetectable/absent circular dichroism (CD) bands. Whereas there have been several host compounds capable of binding cryptochiral biosubstrates for their analysis, those with guest‐induced CD activity in the visible region remain quite rare so far. We herein report the host‐guest interaction‐based CD analysis of various terpenoids using two different, helical polyaromatic capsules under ambient aqueous conditions. When one molecule of CD‐inactive monoterpenoid, (–)‐carvone, is quantitatively encapsulated within a CD‐inactive capsule bearing a spheroidal cavity, the resultant host‐guest complex displays pronounced CD bands in the range of 350–430 nm with a relatively high absolute molar circular dichroism value (i.e., |Δ ε | >80 M −1 cm −1 at ∼390 nm), derived from the guest‐induced host helicity. The chirality of other cryptochiral mono/sesquiterpenoids is also detected with similar efficiency (∼30–90 M −1 cm −1 ). The enantiomeric excess (%ee) of d/l ‐mixtures of monoterpenoids can be determined with the helical cavity via comparative CD analysis. By the use of another larger capsule, di‐ and triterpenoids also induce its intense CD bands (up to ∼130 M −1 cm −1 ) in the visible region upon encapsulation. The present study highlights the potential application of helical polyaromatic hosts to the facile cryptochiral analysis of a broad range of biosubstrates with intense CD output.

items.title: Topological Regioisomerism Enables Triplet–Triplet Energy‐Transfer for Reversible Dual Delayed Fluorescence–Phosphorescence Multicolor Afterglow
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Achieving concurrent thermally activated delayed fluorescence (TADF) and room‐temperature phosphorescence (RTP) afterglow in purely organic systems remains elusive owing to limited control over triplet dynamics, competing decay pathways and unclear operational mechanisms. Reversible TADF/RTP modulation within a single host‐guest system is challenging, hindering advances in color‐ and lifetime‐tunable afterglow materials. To achieve this, we utilized regioisomerism as a structural topology control parameter in a host‐guest platform to modulate triplet‐triplet energy transfer (TTET), enabling the transition from exciplex TADF to dual TADF‐RTP afterglow. The optimized system exhibits TADF‐associated delayed emission with an intensity‐weighted apparent lifetime of 617 ms, along with persistent RTP and ∼6.5‐9.5 s afterglow. Temperature‐dependent modulation of I TADF / I RTP ratio enables reversible cryogenic afterglow color evolution from yellow to orange and red through thermally regulated exciton redistribution.

items.title: Irradiation‐Wavelength‐Tuned Stepwise [2+2] Cycloaddition of Indolylphenylpropenone Derivatives as a Platform for Light–Mechanical Energy Conversion
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Cyclobutane motifs are widely present in natural products, and [2+2] cycloaddition provides a facile route for synthesizing four‐membered rings. However, controlling the regio‐ and stereo‐selectivity of cycloaddition remains a great challenge. In topo‐photochemical reaction, the prearrangement of the reactant molecules can place the atoms at specific positions in the products. In this work, irradiation‐wavelength‐controlled, stepwise photo‐induced topo‐[2+2] cycloaddition of indolylphenylpropenone derivatives was achieved in crystals. Under blue light, one kind of monocyclobutane was produced via the cycloaddition of the vinyl groups; for ( E )‐1‐(5‐bromo‐1 H ‐indol‐1‐yl)‐3‐(3,5‐difluorophenyl)prop‐2‐en‐1‐one ( PEOBr 5 F 35 ), this process proceeded via a single‐crystal‐to‐single‐crystal transformation. Upon subsequent irradiation with 365 nm light, the monocyclobutane product underwent a second‐step [2+2] cycloaddition between C = C bonds on five‐membered heterocyclic ring in indole, converting into a bicyclobutane product. Such catalyst‐free dearomatization of indole via [2+2] cycloaddition provide a facile and green strategy for constructing cyclobutane‐fused heterocyclic architectures. Driven by [2+2] cycloaddition, the molecular crystals exhibited obvious macroscopic mechanical motion.

items.title: A Scalable Presodiation Strategy Enabling Dry‐Air‐Processable Hard Carbon Anodes for High Energy Sodium‐Ion Batteries
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Hard carbon (HC) anodes hold promise for sodium‐ion batteries but are plagued by low initial Coulombic efficiency (ICE) stemming from irreversible sodium sequestration. Chemical presodiation offers a direct route to compensate this deficit, yet its translation to high‐loading electrodes is crippled by sluggish mass transport and air sensitivity of the sodiated product, a barrier to scalable manufacturing. Here, we break this impasse by synchronizing acoustic field enhanced transport with in situ interfacial engineering. Ultrasound‐driven microconvection and cavitation overcome diffusion limitations within thick electrodes, delivering ∼100% ICE within one minute, approximately twice as fast as conventional immersion. A five second quenching in sodium difluoro(oxalato)borate constructs a B/F‐rich hybrid interphase that not only passivates the highly reactive sodiated surface against dry‐air degradation, retaining >79% ICE after 6 h exposure, but also selfregulates subsequent solid‐electrolyte interphase evolution, suppressing impedance growth and stabilizing charge transfer kinetics. Practical pouch cells deliver 76% capacity retention over 700 cycles at 0.5 C/1 C and exhibit superior wide‐temperature adaptability from −40°C to 55°C. By resolving the coupled bottlenecks of kinetic inhomogeneity and environmental instability, this work establishes a scalable, dry‐air‐compatible presodiation paradigm that bridges the gap between laboratory innovation and industrial battery manufacturing.

items.title: Photocatalytic 1,2‐Boron Migrative Alkene Homologation to Access 1,3‐Difunctionalized Alkenes
items.abstract: ABSTRACT In contrast to well‐established methods for vicinal di‐functionalization of alkenes, remote di‐functionalization is much more challenging and has achieved limited success. Herein, we disclose a visible light photocatalytic boron‐directed alkene homologation with alkyl halides activated by a traceless tert ‐butylsulfonyl (Bus) leaving group. The reaction produces a myriad of 1,3‐difunctionalized alkenes under mild conditions with excellent functional group tolerance. β‐Elimination of the Bus group not only drives the contra‐thermodynamic 1,2‐boron migration, but also regenerates a C─C double bond, thus transforming the sulfone‐based alkyl halide into a vinylidene precursor, rather than a traditional alkyl source. The synthetic utility of this method is well demonstrated by gram‐scale synthesis, downstream transformations, and the formal total synthesis of 24‐fluoro‐25‐hydroxyvitamin D 3 analogues. This work represents a very rare example of one‐carbon homologation of ubiquitous alkenes, thus establishing a new strategic paradigm for chemical synthesis.

items.title: Reconfiguring Interfacial Electrochemical Potential for Boosting Sodium‐Ion Transport in Composite Solid Electrolytes
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Sluggish ion transport kinetics between the ceramic and polymer phases remain a key challenge in composite solid electrolytes (CSEs), primarily due to a severe interfacial barrier arising from their intrinsic physicochemical incompatibility. Herein, molecular design‐enabled electronic structure engineering is proposed to reconfigure the interfacial electrochemical environment at the Na 3 Zr 2 Si 2 PO 12 –poly(ethylene oxide) interface, based on a dual‐axis screening guided by the electron‐donating capability and molecular electronic asymmetry. By grafting different functional trimethoxysilanes from a targeted library onto the ceramic surface, the effect of the interfacial electrochemical potential on Na‐ion transport is investigated, revealing a strong negative correlation with the ionic conductivity of CSEs. The CSE with the optimal grafting molecule (phenyltrimethoxysilane) reduces the potential mismatch by 87% and lowers the Na‐ion migration barrier, thereby boosting Na‐ion conductivity by two orders of magnitude. All‐solid‐state sodium‐metal batteries using this CSE show boosted electrochemical performance with a high capacity of 91.8 mAh g −1 delivered at 5 C and retain ∼99% of their initial capacity after 500 cycles at 2 C. This work establishes a screening framework for reducing interfacial potential mismatch and addressing the long‐standing ion‐transport bottleneck across ceramic–polymer interfaces in CSEs.

items.title: Engineering Amino‐Induced p‐π Conjugation for Electronic Regulation of Li + Transport in PVDF‐Based Solid‐State Electrolytes
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Sluggish Li + transport in poly(vinylidene fluoride) (PVDF)‐based solid polymer electrolytes (SPEs) arises from restricted polymer segmental motion and persistent Li + ‐FSI − association, while conventional fillers provide limited regulation of the local electronic and coordination environments. Herein, amino‐functionalized UiO66‐NH 2 is introduced into a PVDF/lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide (LiFSI) electrolyte to construct electronically active composite SPEs (U6NP). The electron‐donating ─NH 2 groups induce p‐π conjugation, redistribute the linker electron density, and strengthen ligand‐to‐metal charge transfer (LMCT)‐related electronic coupling between the organic linkers and Zr‐O clusters. This electronic reconstruction, together with amino‐associated modulation of local O‐centered coordination environments, reshapes the electrostatic landscape, weakens Li + ‐FSI − interactions, and facilitates Li + migration. U6NP delivers a room‐temperature ionic conductivity of 2.41 × 10 −3 S cm −1 , a Li + transference number of 0.56, and an oxidative stability of 4.42 V. More importantly, Li||U6NP||LiNi 0.8 Co 0.1 Mn 0.1 O 2 (NCM811) cells with a cathode loading of 21.5 mg cm −2 retain 98.51% after 120 cycles at 0.05 C. The Li||U6NP||NCM811 pouch cell delivers 136.6 mAh g −1 initially and 120.9 mAh g −1 after 100 cycles. This work establishes ─NH 2 ‐induced p‐π conjugation‐enhanced LMCT as an effective strategy for electronically active MOF‐reinforced PVDF electrolytes toward high‐loading solid‐state lithium metal batteries.

items.title: Frontispiece: Isolated Ir–Se Sites in Nickel Selenide for Glyoxal‐Mediated Ethylene Glycol Oxidation to Formate and PET Upcycling
Synthesis of Enones and Enals From Alkenes via Alkenyl Thianthrenium Salts
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Herein, we show the stereoselective conversion of alkenes into enones and enals. Alkenyl thianthrenium salts are used as a readily accessible pool of stereodefined alkenyl electrophiles that can be engaged in two types of carbonylative Pd‐catalyzed three‐component coupling reactions. Using alkyl zinc species generated in situ from alkyl iodides, enones can be accessed via a carbonylative Negishi coupling. In the presence of triethylsilane, enals can be generated via reductive carbonylation.

items.title: Coking–Crosslinking Competition Shapes Alveolar Hard Carbon Formation From Heterogeneous Precursors for Wide‐Temperature Sodium Storage
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Competing with lithium‐ion technology on cost and resource abundance requires sodium‐ion batteries to use hard‐carbon anodes produced from abundant, inexpensive feedstocks without sacrificing structural control. Yet the natural and residual feedstocks that meet these requirements are typically chemically heterogeneous. Competing transformations among their constituent fractions before high‐temperature treatment make the carbonization pathway and carbon architecture difficult to predict and direct. Here, controlled fraction removal and reintroduction reveal a new mechanism whereby coking‐crosslinking competition selects the carbonization pathway. Surface coking blocks oxygen access and suppresses bulk crosslinking, whereas low‐temperature pre‐purification removes coking‐prone fractions, preserving an oxygen‐accessible skeleton that forms alveolar hard carbon (AHC). Operando x‐ray diffraction (XRD)/Raman and synchrotron x‐ray absorption near‐edge structure (XANES) establish that the low‐potential plateau arises from reversible formation of highly reduced sodium species within confined pores. AHC‐120@15‐1400 delivers 388.3 mAh g −1 with 91.3% initial Coulombic efficiency (ICE), retains 94.3% capacity after 10 500 cycles at 4 A g −1 , and operates from −25°C to 45°C. A 1.2 Ah pouch cell retains 82.5% capacity after 1,000 cycles, while the route lowers cradle‐to‐gate material‐resource impact by 35.6% relative to commercial hard‐carbon production. Controlling coking‐crosslinking competition establishes a pathway‐selective design principle for converting heterogeneous carbon resources into durable, wide‐temperature sodium‐storage carbons.

items.title: Cofactor‐Inspired Second‐Sphere Engineering of Artificial Metalloenzymes for Neutral Ammonia Synthesis
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Constructing artificial metalloenzymes with precisely positioned metal centers and tailored second‐sphere microenvironments remains challenging in replicating the hierarchical catalytic functions of natural enzymes. Here, we report a cofactor‐inspired second‐sphere engineering strategy to construct an artificial nanozyme, CuS 1 /CN, featuring atomically defined [3Cu−1S] motifs selectively anchored to ultrasmall Cu clusters (∼0.73 nm) within a mesoporous nitrogen‐doped carbon framework. This architecture establishes enzyme‐like catalytic compartmentalization without compromising active‐site accessibility: exposed Cu sites mimic nitrate reductase for nitrate activation and water dissociation, while adjacent [3Cu−1S] motifs function as cofactor‐like centers that orchestrate interfacial hydration, facilitating proton‐coupled electron transfer and hydrogen relay during downstream hydrogenation. The engineered second‐sphere microenvironment overcomes the intrinsic *NO 2 ‐to‐*NO 2 H bottleneck and shifts the rate‐determining step to *NH 2 O‐to‐*NH 2 OH conversion with a substantially reduced energy barrier. Consequently, CuS 1 /CN enables highly efficient and selective ammonia electrosynthesis under neutral conditions at industrially relevant current densities with long‐term stability. Its integration into a Zn−NO 3 − battery further enables simultaneous nitrate conversion and electricity generation. This work establishes cofactor‐inspired second‐sphere engineering as a general strategy for designing artificial enzymes with programmable catalytic microenvironments beyond conventional active‐site engineering.

items.title: In Situ Product Separation Suppresses Self‐Poisoning in 2‐Butanol Electrooxidation
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Replacing the oxygen evolution reaction with the electrooxidation of 2‐butanol (SBA) offers an energy‐efficient route to co‐production of hydrogen and methyl ethyl ketone (MEK), yet achieving selective MEK formation while maintaining sustained operation remains challenging because of sluggish anodic kinetics and product accumulation. Here, we integrate alloy‐catalyst engineering with reaction–rectification to address these coupled catalytic and process‐level limitations. A self‐supported PdAu/NF anode exploits Pd–Au ligand interactions to regulate the adsorption of SBA, surface hydroxyl species and MEK, thereby suppressing C─C bond cleavage and facilitating product desorption. The optimized PdAu/NF catalyst delivers 300 mA cm − 2 at 0.74 V versus RHE. Despite weakened MEK adsorption, accumulated MEK and MEK‐derived intermediates inhibit SBA oxidation on PdAu and hydrogen evolution on Pt. At the process level, membrane‐free PdAu/NF||Pt/NF electrode arrays are integrated with reaction–rectification, enabling continuous MEK removal, recovery and SBA recycling. This in situ product separation mitigates product accumulation and its inhibitory effects, enabling continuous electrolysis at 14 A with a cell voltage of approximately 1.3 V over 10 h. The integrated system produces MEK with 99% purity while simultaneously generating hydrogen, highlighting the potential of coupling molecular‐level catalyst regulation with process‐level product management for MEK and hydrogen co‐production.

items.title:
Mechanocatalytic Upcycling of Diverse Plastic Wastes via an Fe/SiO
                    <sub>2</sub>
                    Catalyst
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Upcycling plastic waste into high‐value chemicals is an attractive pathway for the sustainable development of human society. Here, we demonstrate the mechanocatalytic conversion of polyethylene, polypropylene, polystyrene, polyester, and their mixtures into valuable hydrogen (H 2 ) and methane (CH 4 ) gases on an iron (Fe) species‐dispersed silica (SiO 2 ) catalyst, achieving almost 100% conversion under mild conditions. During the mechanocatalytic process, Fe species from the milling balls were anchored to the surface of pristine SiO 2 nanoparticles, forming the Fe/SiO 2 catalyst. Simultaneously, the Fe and Si sites in the Fe/SiO 2 catalyst synergistically facilitate the C─H bond activation and C─C bond cleavage pathways, enabling a favorable dehydrogenation‒cracking‒hydrogenation process to produce commercially valuable H 2 and CH 4 . Notably, this catalytic system also exhibits exceptional versatility in processing mixed plastic wastes without requiring prior sorting, while maintaining robust cycling stability. No expensive components, toxic chemicals, or energy‐intensive thermal conditions are needed.

items.title: Iron‐Catalyzed Regioselective Amidation of Pyridines via Zincke Imine Intermediates
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Achieving precise site‐selective functionalization of pyridines is highly desirable in synthetic and medicinal chemistry. Herein, we present an operationally simple iron‐catalyzed protocol for accessing C3‐amidated pyridines. The reaction harnesses an in situ‐generated Fe–acylnitrenoid that interacts with Zincke imines, which serve as temporarily dearomatized forms of pyridines. The reaction exhibits broad substrate scope across C2‐, C3‐, C4‐, or disubstituted pyridine substrates. This approach was also successfully implemented in a telescoped one‐pot procedure by directly employing pyridines. Mechanistic and computational studies revealed that a high‐spin Fe(III)–imidyl radical would be the key amidating species.

items.title: An Oxidative Twist to the Interrupted Pummerer Reaction: Unlocking Inaccessible Aryl Sulfonium Salts
items.abstract: ABSTRACT The interrupted Pummerer reaction is a time‐honored and enduringly versatile tool in organic synthesis, and has recently found widespread application in the preparation of aryl sulfonium salts. However, the classical interrupted Pummerer protocol suffers from long‐standing intrinsic limitations: (a) The key reactants, sulfoxides, are rarely commercially available; (b) the use of harsh electrophilic activator often leads to limited functional‐group tolerance. To address these issues, we have herein developed a Selectfluor‐mediated oxidative interrupted Pummerer variant, which is applicable to synthetic C─H functionalization, allowing approaches to a range of aryl sulfonium salts, including thianthrenium, dibenzothiophenium, and phenoxathiinium frameworks. The present strategy circumvents the use of electrophilic activator and directly utilizes sulfides as starting materials, thereby enabling the scope to be expanded to unprotected amine‐containing arenes.

items.title: Trigonal Prismatic Coordination Field‐Induced d‐Orbital Splitting Enables σ Electron Activation for Efficient Polysulfide Conversion in Li–S Batteries
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Understanding the electron‐transfer pathways and the mechanism in facilitating polysulfide conversion is crucial for the rational design of catalysts in lithium–sulfur batteries. Herein, we designed an NbSe 2 model catalyst to investigate the electron‐transfer pathways at sublayer transition metal cation sites through coordination field modulation, and revealed the relationship between electron transfer and catalytic efficiency. Moreover, the σ *– σ and π *– σ electron transfer channels at transition metal sites are identified in terms of the coordination field theory and hybrid orbital theory, where the σ *– σ channel exhibits higher electron transfer efficiency and therefore enhances the adsorption and conversion role of transition metal sites in polysulfides. The designed trigonal prismatic NbSe 2 exhibits a reversible capacity up to 799 mAh g −1 at a high rate of 5 C, and the battery maintains stability under ultra‐high sulfur loading, achieving a capacity retention rate as high as 95.85%. From an electronic perspective, this work reveals the role of coordination fields on catalytic activity, providing new insights for the rational design of catalysts in metal–S batteries.

items.title: Spatial Electrostatic Complementarity in MOF Pores Enables Selective Recognition of Closely Related Fluoromethanes
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Trace purification of chemically similar gases is particularly challenging when molecular size and kinetics offer little contrast and conventional affinity descriptors provide conflicting guidance. Trifluoromethane (CHF 3 ) removal from monofluoromethane (CH 3 F) exemplifies this problem: CH 3 F has the greater dipole moment, and CHF 3 is more polarizable. Here, to our knowledge, we report the first adsorptive removal of trace CHF 3 from CH 3 F and demonstrate electrostatic complementary recognition (ECR) in interpenetrated anion‐pillared MOF pores. Localized, directional negative‐potential sites from TiF 6 2– pillars and surrounding electropositive pyridyl C─H domains complement the 1H/3F electrostatic pattern of CHF 3 while geometrically frustrating the inverse 3H/1F pattern of CH 3 F. All other benchmark adsorbents showed an overall preference for CH 3 F, whereas both TIFSIX frameworks achieved a reversal of adsorption preference toward CHF 3 under trace‐relevant conditions. TIFSIX‐Cu‐dpt, featuring a more focused and directional ECR environment, adsorbed 18.5 cm 3 /g of CHF 3 at 0.1 kPa. Neutron diffraction, adsorption thermodynamics, and molecular simulations support a spatially complementary multipoint binding mode. Fixed‐bed breakthrough of a binary feed containing 1000 ppm CHF 3 produced CH 3 F with >99.999% purity relative to CHF 3 at 320 L/kg. These results show how spatial electrostatic complementarity can translate subtle molecular differences beyond conventional scalar descriptors into selective adsorption.

items.title: Photocatalytic Disruption of Concurrent Redox Axes Elicits Convergent Redox Collapse
items.abstract: ABSTRACT The interconnected antioxidant systems of cancer cells, centered on the glutathione and thioredoxin axes, constitute a promising therapeutic vulnerability. However, simultaneous disruption of both axes by dual‐inhibitor regimens is hampered by pharmacokinetic asynchrony. Herein, we report squaraine‐based photocatalysts as a single‐agent modality that concurrently disrupts these interconnected antioxidant systems in cancer cells. Upon 635 nm light irradiation, IITC depletes intracellular NADPH and GSH through photocatalytic oxidation coupled with type I/II photosensitization. NADPH depletion deprives the reductive coenzyme of thioredoxin reductase in the thioredoxin axis, while glutathione oxidation collapses the central antioxidant axis. Consequently, IITC ablates both antioxidant axes concurrently and exerts potent phototherapeutic anticancer activity in vitro and in vivo. Importantly, during phototherapy IITC undergoes self‐immolation into nontoxic degraded fragments, thereby avoiding phototoxicity post‐treatment. This self‐eliminating, metabolism‐targeted photocatalytic strategy establishes a new avenue for safe and efficient cancer phototherapy.

items.title: Robust Tetrazine‐Bridged Binuclear Iridium(III) Complex Featuring Tunable Conformational Dynamics for Efficient Photothermal Conversion
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Developing near‐infrared photothermal materials with outstanding conversion efficiency and high photostability remains a critical challenge for small‐molecule systems. We report a unique donor‐acceptor platform based on a binuclear iridium(III) architecture featuring a bridging electron‐deficient 1,2,4,5‐tetrazine ligand. The complex exhibits strong and broad absorption up to 1200 nm in solution and 1500 nm in the solid state, significantly outperforming other metal complexes. Temperature‐ and solvent‐dependent 1 H NMR coupled with X‐ray diffraction suggest the ‘butterfly‐like’ conformational behavior of the complex, while theoretical calculations identify low‐energy charge‐transfer transitions from cyclometalated cores to the tetrazine moiety as the origin of the exceptionally high absorbance and efficient non‐radiative relaxation. This facilitates robust photothermal activity across three different excitation wavelengths (635, 808, 980 nm), delivering an excellent conversion efficiency of 94.9% at 808 nm (acetone solvate) along with long‐term stability over multiple cycles (CHCl 3 /CH 2 Cl 2 ‐derived phase), uniquely tunable through crystal packing engineering. When applied to cellulose paper, the complex drives solar‐to‐thermal water evaporation with an efficiency of 86.6%. This high performance is accompanied by exceptional photostability under prolonged irradiation, ranking the developed material among the most competitive systems reported. Overall, this work establishes bridging 1,2,4,5‐tetrazines and crystal engineering as powerful tools for designing high‐performance organometallic photothermal materials.

items.title: A Phosphonium Relay for Integrated Cleavage‐to‐Cyclization of Cyclic Peptides
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Head‐to‐tail macrocyclization of peptides is typically performed through stepwise workflows that separate resin cleavage, isolation of linear intermediates, and subsequent cyclization, largely due to incompatible activation requirements for each transformation. Here we report a phosphonium‐mediated relay that unifies these steps within a single activation node. In this design, an electrophile‐activated phosphonium species promotes cleavage from standard 2‐chlorotrityl chloride (2‐CTC) resin and is proposed to enable in situ formation of a C ‐terminally activated intermediate for intramolecular amidation. The strategy directly couples cleavage to cyclization on standard peptide supports without auxiliary linkers, intermediate purification, or high‐dilution cyclization conditions. The method is compatible with diverse peptide sequccnces and functional handles and can be integrated into a closed‐loop automated workflow for end‐to‐end synthesis, with advantages for hydrophobic substrates by avoiding isolation of poorly soluble linear intermediates such as Vespid chemotactic peptide 5f . Process‐level benchmarking against side‐chain anchoring further demonstrated favorable process metrics and gram‐scale scalability. This work establishes a linker‐free cleavage‐to‐cyclization strategy and provides a practical framework for integrated and automation‐compatible cyclic peptide synthesis.

items.title: Photo‐Induced Multi‐Physical Field Synergy for Direct Natural Seawater Electrolysis
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Direct natural seawater electrolysis offers a sustainable route for green hydrogen production, yet severe performance degradation stemming from irreversible interfacial precipitation hinders its practical application. Herein, a photo‐induced multi‐physical field synergy strategy is developed to dynamically regulate interfacial OH − transfer and eliminate cathode pH self‐amplifying polarization. A plasmonic photo‐responsive electrode constructed via ultrathin amorphous MoO 3 coating on PtMo alloy nanoparticles is fabricated to integrate photo‐induced asymmetric electric field (PAEF) and localized photothermal field (PLPF). Such a well‐designed core‐shell structure delivers a record‐high industrial current density of 8 A cm −2 at low overpotential (433 mV) in alkaline seawater. In situ characterizations and spectroscopic analyses verify that the dual fields optimize the electric double‐layer ion distribution and drive microscale thermal convection, accelerating OH − dissipation. Benefiting from the above, the engineered light‐responsive catalytic system exhibits a low overpotential of 232 mV at 100 mA cm −2 in natural seawater, alongside anti‐precipitation ability, and maintains stable operation over 100 h (6.2% decay). A photo‐assisted asymmetric electrolyzer achieves a low cell voltage of 2.27 V at 0.5 A cm −2 for seawater splitting, which realizes effective green hydrogen generation under fluctuating natural solar light (normalized ramp‐following ratio > 0.9).

items.title: One Carbon Matters: Conformational Bending Stabilizes Ferroelectric Nematic Order and Enables Domain‐Modulated Antiferroelectric Smectic C Order
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Molecular design of ferroelectric nematics has primarily focused on optimizing highly polar rigid mesogenic cores, whereas the role of flexible aliphatic segments in regulating molecular conformation and polar ordering remains insufficiently understood. Here, we show that exchanging the positions of a methylene group and the ether oxygen within the linkage between a polar rigid core and an aliphatic tail (Ar‐O‐CH 2 ‐ versus Ar‐CH 2 ‐O‐) reshapes the molecular conformational landscape and profoundly influences the stability of the ferroelectric nematic (N F ) phase. Molecules with a stronger preference for bent, pear‐like effective geometries exhibit significantly enhanced N F stability, accompanied by reduced splay and bend elastic constants in the apolar nematic phase, and lower apparent activation barriers for dipolar reorientation. Further elongation of the flexible segment introduces competing packing motifs and gives rise to a domain‐modulated antiferroelectric smectic C (SmC AF ) phase. These findings establish conformational bending as a molecular‐shape parameter for controlling hierarchical ferroelectric and antiferroelectric liquid‐crystalline order, bridging the design principles of conventional bent‐core layered ferroelectrics with emerging rod‐like fluid ferroelectric materials.

items.title: Revisiting the Role of Dynamic Linkages in Polymer Compatibilization Using Diazirine–Anhydride Conjugates
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Small‐molecule crosslinkers can compatibilize mixed plastics through reactive extrusion, providing a potential solution to extant challenges in polymer recycling. Existing studies have prioritized the use of crosslinker molecules that incorporate dynamic linkages between reactive warheads; however, the absolute requirement for these dynamic groups remains unproven, and previous comparisons of static versus dynamic crosslinkers employed molecules with vastly different C–H insertion efficiencies. In this study, we employed chemistry‐explicit reaction molecular dynamics simulations, small‐molecule surrogates of interface reactions, phase morphology studies, and mechanical analysis to explicitly test hypotheses around the value of dynamic linkages. Using rationally designed, reactivity‐matched pairs of dynamic and static crosslinkers, we found the presence of dynamic anhydride linkages did not generally improve compatibilization efficacy. Instead, dynamic exchange enabled reorganization of compatibilizing hetero‐crosslinks into non‐compatibilizing homo‐crosslinks over time, while facilitating other undesirable reactivity pathways. Our findings indicate compatibilization performance is dictated by physicochemical control over crosslinker distribution, rather than dynamic bonding, and that the kinetics of dynamic exchange must be tightly regulated to avoid undermining compatibilization. We anticipate that these findings will guide the development of improved crosslinker reagents for polymer compatibilization and other materials applications.

items.title: Anionic Lone‐Pair‐Like Electrons Induced Ultra‐Low Lattice Thermal Conductivity and High Thermoelectric Performance
items.abstract: ABSTRACT The traditional lone‐pair electron strategy primarily reduces lattice thermal conductivity ( κ L ) by enhancing anharmonic lattice vibrations. However, this mechanism has long been considered to exist only in specific cations with ns 2 electron configurations (e.g. Sb 3+ , Bi 3+ ), severely restricting the broader applicability of this lone‐pair‐based approach. In this study, CuInSnSe 4 is successfully synthesized via atomic cross‐substitution from the diamondoid CuInSe 2 , wherein the Se atoms exhibit an anionic lone‐pair‐like electronic behavior, revealing a new approach to reducing κ L that differs from conventional cation‐based mechanisms.
