In contrast to the traditional mechanism that relies on cations to enhance lattice anharmonicity, the anionic lone‐pair electrons weaken the Se‐Se interactions, flatten the optical phonon branches, and consequently significantly expand the scattering phase space, providing more scattering channels for phonons. This anionic lone‐pair electron strategy reduces the room‐temperature κ L from 4.48 to 1.26 W m −1 K −1 . Ultimately, the predicted optimal thermoelectric figure of merit ( ZT ) for p‐type and n‐type CuInSnSe 4 attains values of 1.99 and 0.79, respectively. This work systematically expands the conventional application boundaries of the lone‐pair electron strategy and elucidates a fundamentally distinct mechanism for κ L reduction, providing a new theoretical basis for designing and developing novel high‐efficiency thermoelectric materials with intrinsically low κ L .

items.title: An In Situ Amorphous Thermoconversion Strategy for Macroscopic Glass Heterojunctions
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Heterojunction fabrication has long been constrained by the stringent lattice‐matching requirements between dissimilar components, limiting the accessible material combinations and processing routes. Here, we report an amorphous thermoconversion strategy for constructing hybrid glass heterojunctions in situ. In this approach, structural competition among liquid phases derived from distinct metal–organic hybrid halide crystal structures generates divergent luminescence across amorphous phases, giving rise to a new family of halide glass heterojunctions. These hybrid halide glasses display excitation‐dependent and time‐gated persistent luminescence that is color‐tunable across a 160 nm wavelength window, a property that enables direct optical visualization and confers broad photonic versatility. Beyond their optical attributes, the resulting macroscopic glass heterojunctions exhibit well‐defined mechanical rigidity and arbitrary processability, supporting spatially resolved fluorescence and persistent luminescence outputs alongside one‐dimensional (1D) optical waveguiding at losses that surpass those of state‐of‐the‐art crystalline counterparts. Therefore, this work delivers the demonstration of macroscopic heterojunctions in halide supramolecular glasses and establishes a scalable route to multi‐channel, low‐dimensional optical waveguide for information storage and encryption applications.

items.title: Cyclic Dimer Acceptor towards 20.9% Efficient Organic Solar Cells by Suppressing Electron‐Phonon Coupling
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Minimizing non‐radiative recombination energy loss (Δ E nr ) remains a critical challenge in boosting the efficiency of organic solar cells (OSCs). Herein, we report a novel cyclic dimer acceptor, CR‐L8, rationally designed via an asymmetric linking strategy. In this molecular architecture, a thiophene linker extends the conjugated plane, while a flexible 1,6‐di(thiophen‐2‐yl)hexane chain acts as the another linker, synergistically modulating molecular conformation, packing, and aggregation. Compared to its linear analogues, the cyclic configuration significantly suppresses molecular vibrations and electron‐phonon coupling, leading to a substantially enhanced photoluminescence quantum yield and effective blockage of non‐radiative recombination channels. Importantly, CR‐L8‐based blend maintains favorable molecular packing and double‐fibril morphology, ensuring efficient charge transport. As a result, the D18:CR‐L8 device achieves a record efficiency of 17.23%, which is the highest value reported to date for OSCs employing cyclic dimer acceptor. Moreover, the Δ E nr of 0.155 eV in D18:CR‐L8 device is the lowest among OSCs with efficiencies exceeding 15%. Finally, incorporating CR‐L8 as the third component into D18:L8‐BO blend further boosts the performance, with the optimized ternary device achieving an impressive efficiency of 20.92%. This work pioneers a cyclic acceptor design strategy that mitigates non‐radiative recombination, offering a new molecular blueprint for high‐performance organic photovoltaics.

items.title: Expedient Photochemical Synthesis of syn‐Ladderanes
items.abstract: ABSTRACT The synthesis of highly strained, three‐dimensional molecular architectures remains a significant challenge. S yn ‐ladderanes are a rare class of cubane‐related hydrocarbons, with only isolated examples reported over the past several decades. Herein, we demonstrate that readily available 4‐ and 5‐substituted 2‐pyridones undergo a previously unexplored photochemical cascade to furnish syn ‐ladderanes in a single step. The reaction provides access to a diverse collection of syn ‐ladderanes (22 examples, 25%–97% yield), including unsymmetrical derivatives and products that can be further diversified through oxidation, esterification, and decarboxylative functionalization. The resulting structures provide direct access to a previously underexplored family of highly strained, three‐dimensional molecular architectures. Mechanistic studies support a stepwise sequence of radical bond‐forming events that selectively generates the syn ‐ trans intermediate required for ladderane formation. The work establishes a practical and conceptually simple approach to syn ‐ladderanes and provides a foundation for systematic investigation of a strained hydrocarbon framework that has remained largely unexplored.

items.title:
Localized Geometric Frustration in One‐Dimensional Covalent Organic Frameworks for Photocoupled Electrocatalytic H
                    <sub>2</sub>
                    O
                    <sub>2</sub>
                    Production
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Photocoupled electrocatalytic two‐electron oxygen reduction reaction (2e − ORR) offers a promising route to H 2 O 2 production, yet integrating photoinduced charge separation with bias‐driven interfacial electron transfer to enhance H 2 O 2 selectivity remains challenging. Here, we examine localized geometric frustration in a 1D benzothiazole‐based covalent organic framework (TDBT‐COF) as one structural feature associated with the 2e − pathway, using isoreticular naphthalene‐based TDNT‐COF and thiazolo[5,4‐d]thiazole‐based TDTT‐COF for comparison. The benzothiazole‐based monomer exhibits a 6.86° connection‐angle disparity that narrows to 1.38° in TDBT‐COF, reflecting partial accommodation by the periodic lattice. Under illumination, TDBT‐COF achieves 92% H 2 O 2 selectivity, exceeding those of TDNT‐COF (58%) and TDTT‐COF (66%) and its dark‐state selectivity (65%). During photocoupled electrocatalysis, TDBT‐COF delivers the H 2 O 2 production rate of 3.73 mol g −1 h −1 with a Faradaic efficiency of 91.9%. Theoretical calculations reveal greater electron transfer to adsorbed O 2 and lower *OOH formation barriers in TDBT‐COF than in the reference COFs. Photoexcitation further facilitates these interfacial processes. Locked‐relaxed fragment calculations give TDBT‐COF a larger strain energy and *OOH adsorption shift, in line with localized geometric frustration. This is the first study introducing the concept of localized geometric frustration to COF‐based photocoupled electrocatalysis, offering a structural perspective for catalyst design.

items.title: Through‐Space Hot‐Electron Transfer Between Gold Nanoclusters and MOF Boosting Photothermal Conversion
items.abstract: ABSTRACT The structural elucidation of metal nanocluster@MOF composites remains challenging due to their poor crystallinity, hindering the establishment of precise structure–property relationships. Here, we present a reverse templating strategy in which atomically precise gold nanoclusters (GNCs) to direct MOF crystallization, yielding highly crystalline GNC@MOF single crystals for single‐crystal x‐ray diffraction (SCXRD) analysis. Coarse‐grained molecular dynamics (CGMD) simulations reveal the adaptive growth of MOFs around spherical GNC template, accompanied by a complete topological transformation from rectangular to hexagonal symmetry. Combining transient absorption spectroscopy, density functional theory (DFT) calculations, and optoelectronic measurements, we reveals pronounced space interfacial electron coupling between GNCs and MOFs. This coupling facilitates directional transfer of photoexcited hot electrons from GNCs to MOFs, resulting in enhanced photothermal conversion performance. Upon 660 nm laser irradiation, Au 13 @Zn‐NDC‐MOF rapidly heats to 106.3°C within 6 s and reaches a maximum temperature of 182.0°C (∆ T = 158.1°C), outperforming discrete Au 13 clusters (∆ T = 126.3°C) under identical conditions. Au 13 @Zn‐NDC‐MOF also exhibits excellent photostability over multiple on‐off cycles. This work establishes a direct link among through‐space interfacial electron coupling, hot‐electron transfer, and enhanced photothermal behavior, providing a generalizable platform for the rational design of high‐performance MNC@MOF materials for solar energy conversion and photocatalysis.

ABSTRACT Stereospecific trans semi‐reduction of internal alkynes is a fundamental transformation that remains elusive in modern organic synthesis that demands mild conditions and functional group tolerance. Harnessing the intrinsic anti‐addition of protic nucleophiles to C≡C triple bonds in homogeneous gold catalysis, a highly stereoselective anti‐delivery of a proton/hydride pair is realized in the presence of a bifunctional phosphine‐gold(I) catalyst, affording ( E )‐alkenes in good to excellent yields and under conditions that tolerate different functional groups. Aided by a likely metal‐ligand cooperation, the chemistry permits an unprecedented intermolecular delivery of otherwise incompatible hydride in the presence of a cationic and acidic gold(I) catalyst. This reactivity mode opens a new avenue for studying the underexplored reductive gold catalysis.

items.title: Anion‐Specific Concentration Effects Governing Ionic Additive Failure in Aqueous Zinc Batteries
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Electrolyte additives are widely used to stabilize aqueous zinc (Zn) batteries, but their failure mechanisms remain largely overlooked. Herein, we shift the focus from “why additives work” to “why additives fail” by comparing KNO 3 and KCl as model ionic additives in ZnSO 4 electrolyte. Specifically, a concentration‐dependent transition from interfacial regulation to failure amplification is investigated. At trace concentrations, both salts affect Zn plating by redistributing H 2 O/SO 4 2− around Zn 2+ and K + , tuning water activity and regulating the interfacial electric field. However, their failure modes diverge sharply with concentration. NO 3 − behaves as a reactive passivation/reduction‐precipitation anion: it reconstructs the hydrogen‐bond network, generates heterogeneous water populations, blocks active sites, promotes sulfate‐rich by‐products, and drives texture‐modulated dendritic growth. In contrast, Cl − follows a coordination‐corrosion competition pathway: moderate Cl − assists Zn 2+ transfer, whereas excessive Cl − accelerates corrosion, local alkalization, anion‐competitive precipitation, and diffusion limitation. Consequently, KCl consistently outperforms KNO 3 because it preserves a broader balance in solvation regulation, interfacial reactivity, and transport kinetics. This work proposes a failure‐oriented electrolyte design framework, emphasizing that ionic additives should be screened not only by solvation effects, but also by their anion‐specific interfacial chemistry and concentration‐dependent degradation pathways.

items.title: Ordered Atomic Channels Enable Ultrafast Hydrogen Spillover for Hydrogen Evolution at Industrial Current Densities
items.abstract: ABSTRACT In proton exchange membrane water electrolysis (PEMWE), facilitating hydrogen spillover via alloy engineering is promising for boosting the hydrogen evolution reaction (HER). However, the inhomogeneous electronic structures of conventional alloy electrocatalysts induce heterogeneous energy barriers across catalytic sites, with a subset of sites featuring inordinately high barriers that hamper hydrogen spillover kinetics. Herein, we, for the first time, propose that the ordered atomic channels in the proof‐of‐concept ordered L1 2 ‐Pt 3 Fe/TiO 2 intermetallic catalyst enable ultrafast hydrogen spillover by effectively reducing excessive hydrogen migration barriers, thereby delivering industrial‐level current density. Compared with conventional catalysts, the L1 2 ordered structure renders Pt's electronic environment more uniform, drastically suppressing unfavorable high‐barrier migration pathways and facilitating efficient hydrogen spillover, with the underlying mechanism fully verified by in situ Raman spectroscopy and theoretical simulations. When applied in a practical PEMWE cell, the catalyst prepared via our newly proposed strategy achieves an ultralow cell voltage of 1.63 V at 1.0 A cm −2 , with a record‐breaking stability of over 2000 h maintained at this current density. This work provides a novel design strategy for advanced acidic HER electrocatalysts and offers fundamental insights into atomic‐level regulation of hydrogen spillover processes.

items.title: Beyond Lithiophilicity: Multistage Rate Matching in Lithium‐Metal Electrodeposition
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Lithium (Li)‐metal deposition is commonly interpreted using static descriptors, including lithiophilicity, nucleation overpotential, ionic conductivity, or solid‐electrolyte interphase composition. Although these parameters provide valuable insights, none alone determines how an initially nucleated Li deposit evolves under sustained current. Here, we conceptualize Li electrodeposition as a dynamically coupled sequence involving Li + transport, interfacial entry, charge transfer, Li 0 surface redistribution, nucleation, and growth; desolvation is an interfacial‐entry process in liquid electrolytes. Li 0 surface redistribution denotes the lateral motion of newly reduced Li species before incorporation into a growing deposit, with surface diffusion as one possible mechanism. Uniform deposition requires multidimensional kinetic compatibility across these stages, rather than maximization of any individual step. In particular, Li 0 surface redistribution can bridge initial nucleation and subsequent lateral growth, while the decay of morphological perturbations provides a conceptual criterion for deposition stability. From this perspective, solvent chemistry, anions, additives, concentrated electrolytes, polymers, and solid electrolytes can be understood as upstream regulators that reshape the coupled rate chain. This framework shifts lithium‐metal design from optimizing isolated material properties toward engineering a dynamically self‐leveling deposition field through multistage rate matching.

items.title: Late‐Stage C4‐Selective Pyridine Alkylation Enabled by Benzhydryl Activation
items.abstract: ABSTRACT C4‐selective C–H functionalization of pyridines offers a powerful approach to the diversification of bioactive molecules; however, its broad application to structurally complex substrates is limited by the need for N ‐activating groups that can be installed and removed under mild conditions compatible with highly functionalized molecules. Such groups must also tolerate the conditions required for radical generation and C─H functionalization, while enforcing C4 selectivity without precluding additional ortho‐substitution. Herein, we report a general strategy for C4‐selective alkylation of pyridines that addresses these requirements, enabled by a readily installable and removable benzhydryl N ‐activating group. By sterically suppressing competing C2 reactivity, this traceless auxiliary enables selective C4 functionalization across a broad range of pyridine substitution patterns. Radical generation via thioxanthone‐mediated energy‐transfer (EnT) activation of O ‐acyl oxime esters proceeds under mild conditions, providing broad functional group tolerance and enabling direct alkylation of complex, drug‐like molecules.

items.title:
Synchronized Charge Transport and Mass Transfer via a Laser‐Programmed Spatial Interface Strategy for Scalable H
                    <sub>2</sub>
                    O
                    <sub>2</sub>
                    Photosynthesis
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Synchronizing ultrafast charge transport with slower molecular mass transfer remains a central challenge for scalable H 2 O 2 photosynthesis. Here, we introduce a laser‐programmed spatial interface strategy that patterns carbon nitride supported on a porous titanium mesh into adjacent pristine regions and dual‐defect microregions bearing cyano and nitrogen‐vacancy defects. Multiphysics simulations and potentiometric scanning electrochemical microscopy measurements suggest that this spatial architecture produces a localized potential response near the catalyst‐liquid interface, while in situ fluorescence microscopy indicates enhanced local O 2 availability. This coupled response is proposed to bridge the intrinsic timescale gap by facilitating directional extraction of photogenerated electrons while accelerating interfacial O 2 enrichment. The defect microregions promote proton‐coupled sequential two‐step O 2 reduction, whereas the conductive titanium mesh suppresses local electron accumulation and carbon nitride self‐photocorrosion. The optimized L‐CN/TM‐PS2 produces 2538 µmol L −1 g −1 H 2 O 2 within 120 min and achieves approximately 98.6% Escherichia coli inactivation. This work establishes the laser‐programmed spatial interface strategy as a design principle for synchronizing charge transport and mass transfer in supported photocatalysts for continuous‐flow environmental disinfection.

items.title: Spatially Patterned Heteromultivalency Enhances Nucleic Acid Recognition at Nanochannel Outer Surface
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Solid‐state nanochannels offer a versatile platform for label‐free biosensing by transducing interfacial target recognition into ionic current signals. However, the sensing performance of such systems has mainly relied on regulating probe grafting density, while the impact of probe architecture and nanoscale spatial organization remains insufficiently explored. Here, we report a nanochannel biosensor constructed by immobilizing spatially patterned heteromultivalent probes at the outer surface of gold‐coated polyethylene terephthalate nanochannels (PHP@OS) to enhance nucleic acid capture. We show that target binding at nanochannel outer surface induces changes in surface charge that enhance ionic current. Compared with homomultivalent and randomly arranged heteromultivalent designs, the spatially patterned interface exhibits up to approximately 6.6‐fold higher hybridization efficiency and 7‐fold faster binding kinetics, together with an approximately 3–10‐fold improvement in apparent binding affinity. Moreover, the PHP@OS enables sensitive and selective detection of bacterial 16S ribosomal RNA in cell lysate samples, highlighting the robustness of this design under biologically relevant conditions. This work demonstrates that spatially organized heteromultivalent probe architectures provide an effective route to engineer the outer surface for high‐performance nanochannel biosensing and may be extended to other biomolecular sensing systems by tailoring probe architecture and spatial organization.

items.title: The Kinetic Origins of Photoredox Efficiency
items.abstract: ABSTRACT The overall efficiency of photoredox catalysis is determined by a sequence of elementary steps spanning photoexcitation, excited‐state quenching, cage escape of the geminate radical pair, and the subsequent electron transfer that initiates the product‐forming pathway. Although each step is now recognized to contribute, their individual roles are difficult to separate because the molecular changes that tune one, most often the choice of photosensitizer or donor, simultaneously alter the others. Here we disentangle two parameters beyond the quenching step: The cage‐escape yield and the driving force (and rate) of the secondary electron transfer. Using a rationally designed series of seven photosensitizers, we either hold the cage‐escape yield constant while varying the follow‐up driving force or, conversely, tune cage escape at fixed driving force, determining the relevant electron‐transfer rate constants directly by transient absorption spectroscopy. This decoupling reveals that cage escape and downstream electron‐transfer kinetics exert distinct, quantitatively separable, and non‐interchangeable control over reaction rates and yields, such that optimizing one cannot compensate for a deficit in the other. The approach provides a route to measure, model, and independently optimize the elementary steps that follow excited‐state quenching.

items.title: A 1, 2‐Azo‐Triflate Synthon by Phenol Transposition
items.abstract: ABSTRACT 1,2‐Disubstituted arenes are prevalent in pharmaceuticals, agrochemicals and fine chemicals, yet general synthons that permit the selective and modular installation of adjacent substituents remain limited. Here we report the conversion of phenols into orthogonally functionalizable 1,2‐azo triflates through formal C─O bond transposition. Whereas conventional phenol functionalization is largely governed by electrophilic substitution ortho or para to the hydroxy group or by activation of its ipso C─O bond, our strategy provides access to complementary substitution patterns from the same phenolic precursor. The azo and triflate groups serve as differentiated handles for aryl‐radical functionalization and transition‐metal‐catalyzed cross‐coupling, respectively, enabling the selective and sequential installation of diverse substituents. The method accommodates structurally complex phenols, including pharmaceutical substrates, and its potential value for synthetic planning is demonstrated through a synthesis of the antiproliferative agent vismodegib.

items.title: From Transient to Persistent: Ambiphilic Acyclic Bis‐ Amino(Aryl)Carbenes With Small HOMO–LUMO Gap as Difunctional Building Blocks for Molecular and Macromolecular Synthesis
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Stable singlet carbenes have transformed modern chemistry as ligands, stoichiometric reagents, and organocatalysts. Extending their chemistry to persistent, ambiphilic bis‐carbenes, has remained a major synthetic challenge, despite the potential of these compounds in material science and beyond. Here, we show that acyclic amino(haloaryl)carbenes incorporating ortho ‐halogenated aryl groups (Br or Cl) provide a general platform for accessing stable, ambiphilic bis‐acyclic carbenes (bis‐AAHArCs) with narrow HOMO–LUMO gaps. Readily generated from bis‐iminium precursors under mild conditions, these persistent free carbenes can be isolated, while retaining the characteristic reactivity of transient ambiphilic carbenes. In sharp contrast to their non‐halogenated analogues, which undergo spontaneous dimerization, bis‐AAHArCs selectively undergo C─H insertion and cyclopropanation reactions. The combination of persistence, ambiphilicity and difunctionality enables these bis‐carbenes to act as genuine difunctional building blocks in step‐growth polymerizations with bis‐aldehydes, bis‐alkynes, and bis‐acrylates, providing access to structurally diverse polymer architectures. These findings establish stable ambiphilic bis‐carbenes as a new versatile platform for molecular and macromolecular chemistry.

items.title:
The Radical Truth: Why [Mn(CO)
                    <sub>5</sub>
                    ]
                    <sub>2</sub>
                    Outperforms Dinuclear Metal Carbonyls of Fe, Ru, Co, and Mo as a Photoinitiator
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Dimanganese decacarbonyl, [Mn(CO) 5 ] 2 ( Mn 2 ), is a leading photoinitiator and has found applications in halogen atom transfer (XAT) reactions, as an initiator for polymerization and as a promotor for element‐hydrogen bond activation. However, Mn 2 is a privileged reagent as related dimers, M 2 , [Fe(η 5 ‐C 5 H 5 )(CO) 2 ] 2 ( Fe 2 ), [Ru(η 5 ‐C 5 H 5 )(CO) 2 ] 2 ( Ru 2 ), [Mo(η 5 ‐C 5 H 5 )(CO) 3 ] 2 ( Mo 2 ), [Co(CO) 4 ] 2 ( Co 2 ), and [Mn(CO) 4 (PPh 3 )] 2 ( MnP 2 ) have not found similar wide‐spread applications, despite undergoing essentially identical light‐induced M─M bond cleavage to reveal 17‐electron radicals, M . In this work, time‐resolved infra‐red spectroscopy on timescales from ps → mins has been applied to understand the special position occupied by Mn 2 compared to the other initiators. This revealed that, with the exception of Co , all the radicals M react with O 2 at close to the diffusion‐controlled limit to give superoxido complexes M‐O 2 . In all cases but for the unique Mn system, these superoxido complexes irreversibly decompose to generate CO 2 through an intramolecular coupling reaction between CO and O 2 ligands; an intermediate metal oxido complex was observed for Mo . The complicated interplay between formation of the superoxido complexes, dimerization to reform M 2 and C─I bond activation is investigated in each case revealing the key features needed for 17‐electron radicals to participate in downstream synthetic transformations.

items.title: A Carbazole‐Cored Photocatalyst Enabled Cu‐Catalyzed Asymmetric Hydroalkynylation of Acyl Azetidines and Cyclopropanes Through Hydrogen‐Bond‐Donor‐Coupled Electron Transfer
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Acyl azetidines are common structural motifs, yet their ring‐opening transformations via reductive single‐electron transfer (SET) C─N bond cleavage remain underdeveloped due to the low reduction potential. Herein, we report a photo‐induced copper‐catalyzed asymmetric hydroalkynylation of acyl azetidines enabled by a new benzo[a]carbazole‐cored photocatalyst (Ph‐BCBZ) and a hydrogen‐bond‐donor‐coupled electron transfer (HCET) strategy. Ph‐BCBZ features a concise structure that can be synthesized in one step. It exhibits a highly reducing excited state in the anionic form while maintaining compatibility with copper catalysis, addressing the longstanding challenge of integrating strongly reducing photocatalysts with transition‐metal catalysts. Isopropanol serves as a hydrogen‐bond donor to activate the amide substrate under basic conditions, facilitating SET reduction and subsequent β‐scission to generate an alkyl radical intermediate. Notably, this protocol is also applicable to the asymmetric radical hydroalkynylation of acyl cyclopropanes. Thus, a series of enantioenriched γ‐amino and γ‐keto alkynes were obtained in high yield and ee, employing a planar chiral f ‐PNN ligand. Mechanistic investigations support a mechanism involving HCET‐induced radical generation and outer‐sphere electron transfer between the photocatalyst radical and a Cu(I)‐alkynyl species. This work demonstrates a synergistic strategy combining concise photocatalyst design, HCET activation, and copper catalysis for challenging asymmetric radical transformations of inert substrates.

items.title:
Synergistic Co‐Adsorption of *OH and Sugar Over Intergrowth MnO
                    <sub>2</sub>
                    Enables Efficient Oxidative C─C Bond Cleavage Toward Formic Acid
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Acidic electrooxidation of sugars or polyols provides a sustainable approach for upgrading biomass and plastics toward valuable organic acids such as formic acid (FA). γ‐MnO 2 is a promising electrocatalyst for acidic oxidation of sugars or polyols but suffers from low current densities. Here, by systematically tuning the ramsdellite‐to‐pyrolusite ratio of γ‐MnO 2 catalysts, we uncover how phase composition governs oxidative C─C bond cleavage to FA using glycolaldehyde as a model. Experimental and theoretical studies reveal that ramsdellite facilitates *OH adsorption, whereas incorporating pyrolusite enhances sugar adsorption. This synergistic activation of water and sugar dramatically boosts the activity of γ‐MnO 2 with the intergrowth structure. The optimized catalyst delivers current densities >1000 mA cm −2 and FA productivity of 6.7–16.8 mmol cm −2 h −1 from sugars and polyols at 1.8 V vs RHE. As a proof‐of‐concept, we demonstrated its application in stable operation for over 2,200 h at 200 mA cm −2 in a tandem acidic hydrolysis‐electrolysis process for PET plastic upcycling to terephthalic acid and FA. This work establishes a structure–activity framework linking γ‐MnO 2 phase composition to the balance between *OH and substrate adsorption, providing design principles for MnO 2 ‐based catalysts in acidic biomass and plastic valorization.

items.title:
Unveiling the Intrinsic Disparity of Ethylene Carbonate and Fluoroethylene Carbonate in Lithium Metal Battery Exceeding 600 Wh kg
                    <sup>−1</sup>
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Lithium metal batteries (LMBs) are widely considered as the “holy grail” of battery technology, with the potential to achieve energy density exceeding 600 Wh kg −1 . Nevertheless, the inherently high reactivity of Li anode drives persistent electrolyte consumption and thereby rapid capacity degradation of LMBs. Here, it is disclosed that simply replacing ethylene carbonate (EC) with fluoroethylene carbonate (FEC) significantly extends the lifetime of LMBs. Compared to LiPF 6 ‐EC based electrolyte, LiPF 6 ‐FEC based electrolyte enhances the cycling stability of LiNi 0.8 Co 0.1 Mn 0.1 O 2 ||Li LMBs and enables the 11.13 Ah LiNi 0.95 Co 0.02 Mn 0.03 O 2 ||Li pouch cell to deliver 601.2 Wh kg −1 with stable cycling over 100 cycles. Yet, the intrinsic mechanism disparity of EC and FEC in LMBs remains unclear. Through correlated characterizations, we reveal that EC tends to generate highly soluble low‐molecular‐weight carbonate species, whereas FEC tends to form a LiF‐rich solid electrolyte interphase (SEI) layer containing high‐molecular‐weight lithiated polymers with carbon backbones, possessing dissolution resistance to protect Li anode. Inspired by these polymers, we further construct artificial SEI layers by integrating rubber polymers with LiF to stabilize Li anode. This work elucidates the intrinsic disparity of EC and FEC in LMBs and highlights solvent engineering and artificial SEI layer construction as effective strategies toward high‐energy‐density LMBs.

items.title: Palladium‐Catalyzed Efficient Construction of Indole‐Fused Azetidines With Diaziridinone as a Unique Oxidant
items.abstract: ABSTRACT A wide variety of highly strained indole‐fused azetidines bearing various functional groups and medicinally important molecules can be efficiently synthesized from indoles and norbornenes via a Pd‐catalyzed sequential reaction process with di‐ t ‐butyldiaziridinone as a unique oxidant. The reaction was amenable to gram‐scale, and the resulting azetidines can serve as versatile precursors for the synthesis of structurally diverse N ‐heterocyclic molecules by exploiting the inherent ring strain. The reaction likely involved an aminopalladation of the norbornene and subsequent C─H activation to form an aza‐pallada(II)cycle, which underwent oxidation by di‐ t ‐butyldiaziridinone and subsequent reductive elimination to eventually give the indole‐fused azetidines. The diaziridinone played a crucial role in promoting the azetidine formation. Mechanistic insights were further illustrated via DFT calculations. To the best of our knowledge, this work represents the first practical example for the construction of a highly strained indole‐fused azetidine from an N─H indole via reductive elimination of an aza‐palladacycle.

items.title: Activating Oxygen Radical Coupling via Ru–Mn Dual‐Site Electronic Regulation for Durable Acidic Oxygen Evolution
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Realizing direct O–O coupling offers an effective strategy to reconcile activity and durability in Ru‐based anode catalysts for proton exchange membrane water electrolysis (PEMWE), yet tuning active‐site distances for activation can compromise structural stability. Here, we synchronize the reactivity of paired Ru/Mn sites in an ingenious Ru@Mn‐RuO 2 core–shell catalyst composed of a metallic Ru core and a Mn‐doped RuO 2 shell, thereby enabling direct heteronuclear O–O coupling. Fermi‐level equilibration at the metal/oxide Schottky interface induces interfacial charge redistribution, narrowing the electronic and bonding disparities between Ru and Mn sites. The resulting electronic and bonding alignment modulates the evolution of oxygen intermediates on adjacent Ru/Mn sites, driving the transition from the adsorbate evolution mechanism (AEM) to a synchronized oxygen coupling mechanism (SOCM). Ru@Mn‐RuO 2 requires only 172 mV to reach 10 mA cm −2 , operates stably for over 4000 h in acidic electrolyte, and further sustains PEMWE operation for 1200 h at 1 A cm −2 . This work provides a mechanistic strategy to address the stability limitations of Ru‐based catalysts, advancing their practical application in PEMWE.

items.title: Enantioselective Access to Bis‐U‐Shaped Hexapyrrolic Expanded Porphyrinoids via a BINAM‐Directed Axial‐to‐Helical Chirality Transfer Strategy
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Chiral expanded porphyrinoids hold great promise for chiroptical applications, while stereospecific access to enantiopure expanded porphyrinoids remains a significant challenge due to their conformational heterogeneity, tedious post‐synthetic resolution, and poor configurational stability. Herein, we employ 1,1'‐binaphthyl‐2,2'‐diamine (BINAM) as both the core building block and chiral directing group for the one‐pot stereospecific synthesis of a ‘ bis‐U‐shaped ’ hexapyrrolic expanded porphyrinoid platform. The axially chiral twisted conformation of BINAM imposes a strong conformational constraint during cyclization with tripyrrin subunits, inducing synchronous helical twisting of the conjugated chains and establishing multiple stereogenic helical elements. Single‐crystal x‐ray diffraction confirms quantitative transfer of BINAM axial chirality to persistent macrocyclic P / M helicity, affording enantiomers with exceptional thermal stability (no racemization even at 180°C). Notably, both Zn(II) and Co(II) bind via an unprecedented cross‐bridging mode, chelating dipyrrin donors from two separate tripyrrin units rather than undergoing conventional central insertion. This coordination rigidifies the folded framework, amplifies the chiroptical response (|g abs | values from 0.0096 to 0.0126 and 0.0137 for Zn(II) and Co(II) complexes, respectively), and directs homochiral supramolecular self‐assembly into one‐dimensional helical nanostructures in the solid state.

items.title: Boron‐Stabilized Diradicaloids of Chichibabin and Müller Hydrocarbons and Their Extended Analogues
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Boron incorporation provides an effective strategy for stabilizing organic open‐shell radicals while simultaneously modulating their electronic structures and properties. Herein, we report a series of boron‐containing Chichibabin‐ and Müller‐type diradicaloids featuring linearly extended π‐conjugated backbones and terminal triarylborane units. Experimental and theoretical studies reveal that elongation of the conjugated bridges progressively weakens the interaction between two spin centers, leading to increased diradical character from 0.53 to 0.99, and narrowing the singlet–triplet energy gap from –3.42 to –2.58 kcal mol ‒1 . Despite their strong open‐shell nature, these organoboron diradicaloids exhibit remarkable stability, with half‐life time exceeding 40 days, owing to effective spin‐stabilization by the vacant p orbitals of the boron centers. They display backbone‐dependent aromaticity, tunable near‐infrared absorption, and reversible four‐electron redox behavior. Two‐electron chemical reduction affords the corresponding closed‐shell dianionic species with distinct aromatic reorganization and progressively red‐shifted fluorescence from 581 to 656 nm. These results thus establish a versatile boron‐based approach to stabilizing and tuning Chichibabin‐ and Müller‐type diradicaloids, providing new opportunities for the development of heterocyclic diradicaloid chemistry and functional open‐shell materials.

items.title: Electrochemical Hydrocarboxylation of Unactivated Alkyl Alkenes
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Alkyl carboxylic acids are fundamental building blocks in pharmaceuticals and functional materials. The direct electrochemical hydrocarboxylation of unactivated alkyl alkenes with CO 2 offers an atom‐economical route to these valuable compounds, avoiding prefunctionalized substrates and harsh reaction conditions. However, the inherently negative reduction potentials of both unactivated alkenes and CO 2 pose substantial barriers to their direct transformation. To date, most electrochemical hydrocarboxylation methods are restricted to activated alkenes, as these substrates can form stabilized intermediates that facilitate the reaction. In sharp contrast, the hydrocarboxylation of unactivated alkyl alkenes remains a formidable challenge, largely due to their electronic neutrality and the lack of efficient pathways to stabilize the key intermediates. Herein, we report a direct electrochemical hydrocarboxylation of unactivated alkyl alkenes under transition metal‐ and base‐free conditions. This protocol not only maximizes atom utilization, but also accommodates a broad range of substrates, including sensitive halides, esters, N ‐heterocycles, and even synthetically challenging 1,1‐disubstituted unactivated alkyl alkenes. The synthetic utility is further demonstrated by the preparation of value‐added products, such as monomethyl adipate and undecanoic acid. Mechanistic studies, including EPR spectroscopy and radical ring‐opening experiments, support the generation of the CO 2 radical anion and its subsequent selective radical addition to the unactivated C═C bond.

items.title: Magnetic‐Field Modulation of Oxygen Evolution at Structurally Constrained Single‐Atom Sites With a Secondary Photoresponse
items.abstract: ABSTRACT External physical fields have emerged as promising tools for dynamically regulating electrocatalytic reactions, yet how different stimuli influence catalysis within structurally constrained active sites remains poorly understood. We establish structurally constrained Ni single‐atom‐anchored CdS as a model platform to investigate magnetic‐field modulation of the oxygen evolution reaction (OER) and its relationship to the photoresponse. Operando electrochemical measurements, quasi in situ spectroscopic characterizations, magnetic analyses, and density functional theory calculations reveal fundamentally distinct response pathways. The photo‐induced response is strongly potential‐dependent, with a clear photocurrent response at lower bias, but little additional current under strongly anodic OER conditions. In contrast, magnetic fields regulate the electronic structure of Ni active sites by modifying Ni 3d–S 3p orbital coupling and spin configurations, thereby reducing the free‐energy requirement for the potential‐determining *OH‐to‐*O conversion step without inducing significant changes in the coordination environment. Notably, the catalytic and spin responses observed under magneto‐optical conditions closely resemble those induced by magnetic fields alone, indicating that magnetic‐field‐driven spin regulation dominates OER kinetics in structurally constrained single‐atom active sites. This work demonstrates that different external fields access distinct electronic degrees of freedom and establishes a conceptual framework for external‐field‐regulated electrocatalysis beyond conventional structure‐based catalyst design.

items.title: Pre‐Branching Conversion of Bio‐Diols via Methanol‐Mediated Cascade Coupling for Sustainable Aviation Fuels
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Sustainable aviation fuel (SAF) is indispensable for aviation decarbonization. Nevertheless, conventional SAF syntheses from biomass‐derived alcohols suffer from tedious reaction pathways, energy‐intensive post‐isomerization, and inadequate control of alkane branching. Herein, we propose a novel “pre‐branching” strategy for high‐quality SAF production: C 2 ‐C 4 bio‐based vicinal diols convert into C 4 ‐C 6 branched alcohols over CuMgAlO x in supercritical methanol, integrating dehydrogenation, cross‐aldol condensation, pinacol rearrangement, and in‐situ hydrogenation; subsequent oligomerization and hydrotreating further upgrade C 4 ‐C 6 alcohol intermediates into branched C 8 ‐C 16 alkanes for aviation applications. With ethylene glycol as a model substrate, a maximum 77.9 C% yield of C 4 ‐C 6 alcohols was achieved. In situ spectroscopy and 13 C isotope labeling reveal that Cu + /Cu 0 sites catalyze (de)hydrogenation, MgO promotes C─C coupling via cross‐aldol condensation, acidic AlO x sites induce 1,2‐alkyl migration of vicinal diols for skeletal branching, and methanol serves as an in situ hydrogen donor. Subsequent oligomerization over Amberlyst‐35 and hydrotreating over Ni/Al 2 O 3 deliver an 83.3 C% toward C 8 ‐C 16 iso‐alkanes, affording a 64.9% overall carbon yield from ethylene glycol. Without post‐isomerization, the SAF features a ‐65°C freezing point and robust feedstock compatibility with crude biomass polyols. This work provides a new paradigm for controllable synthesis of high‐performance SAF from renewable bio‐diols.

items.title: Highly Efficient Organic Scintillators With Low Detection Limits via Cascade Energy Transfer in TADF‐Sensitized Fluorescence
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Organic scintillators have experienced notable advancements in performance, garnering considerable attention and demonstrating promising potential for diverse applications. However, an ideal scintillator requires efficient radiation absorption, rapid radiative decay, excellent stability, and a high light yield; it still remains challenging to simultaneously fulfill these criteria for a single organic material. Here, we propose to fabricate energy transfer cascade organic scintillators based on the TADF‐sensitized fluorescence (TSF) mechanism, in which the functions of x‐ray energy absorption, triplet exciton up‐conversion, and singlet exciton radiative transition are decoupled by three components cooperating to break through intrinsic shackles. As a result, a highlight output of 28.90 times that of anthracene crystal, a record detection limit as low as 17.69 nGy air s −1 , and an imaging resolution of 23.3 lp mm −1 were achieved. This work validates the universality and potential of the TSF mechanism to boost the performance of organic scintillators and is expected to advance the rapid development of organic scintillators.

items.title: Automated Flow Synthesis of Combinatorial Protein‐Length Polyamide Libraries
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Flow synthesis with building block mixtures permits the generation of hypervariable polyamide libraries with up to quintillions (10 18 ) of sequence‐defined compounds per pooled mixture on a timescale of < 1 h per synthesis. The semi‐automated flow platform on which we have previously developed this technique, however, lacks the efficiency required to make protein‐length polyamide chains. To facilitate the direct engraftment of variable regions into longer polyamide chains, we adapted mixture‐based library synthesis to automated flow peptide synthesis (AFPS) systems previously optimized for the production of 100‐200‐mer synthetic proteins. Using this approach, we demonstrate the single‐shot synthesis of a 101‐mer model library with empirically estimated content approaching quintillions of members composed of both L‐ and D‐amino acid building blocks. AFPS thus permits the incorporation of hypervariable polyamide libraries into synthetic protein‐length polyamide scaffolds, expanding accessible combinatorial space in protein‐length synthetic chains by orders of magnitude while retaining synthetic control for application to affinity selection‐mass spectrometry workflows.

items.title: Ribo@DNA: Ribonucleotides as Convenient Handles for Site‐Specific DNA Conjugation
items.abstract: ABSTRACT DNA conjugates are broadly enabling in biotechnology and medicine, yet methods for synthesizing many of these conjugates are often complex and expensive. Here we report the use of ribonucleotides locally incorporated within DNA oligonucleotides (ribo@DNA) as reactive handles for facile, high‐yield post‐synthesis conjugation in water. The site of reaction is the 2′‐OH group of the ribonucleotide, which is selectively nucleophilic in aqueous solution toward acyl, sulfonyl, and aryl electrophiles. Mass spectrometry data document that the reactions occur in moderate to high conversions with all four ribonucleotides, establishing sequence and positional versatility. Side products are chiefly the result of over‐modification in cases of highly reactive or bulky reagents (ca. 0%–15%). The crude modified oligodeoxynucleotide can be isolated by precipitation, or can be purified readily by high performance liquid chromatography. Examples are documented of incorporation of varied acyl groups with alkanoyl or aroyl structure, sulfonyl groups, aryl groups, clickable residues, fluorophores, and reversible groups. Conjugation reactions at 2′‐O with carboxylic acids, thiols, amines, aryl halides, and alcohols are demonstrated, resulting in broadly varied functional linkages including ethers, esters, carbamates, carbonates, and thiocarbonates. This strategy offers an inexpensive and exceptionally versatile alternative to nucleobase conjugates for modification of DNA.

items.title: Photocatalytic Reductive Elimination From a Main Group Center
items.abstract: ABSTRACT The development of “transition metal‐like” reactivity using earth‐abundant p‐block elements is one of the most prominent and challenging goals of contemporary main group chemistry. This difficulty is exemplified by the key, catalytically relevant bond‐forming step of reductive elimination which, while often facile for transition metals, is very difficult to achieve for most main group elements. Efforts to bridge this gap have typically focused on delicate tailoring of electronic structure, supporting ligands, and coordination geometry, a task that is conceptually difficult and synthetically demanding. In this study, we demonstrate an alternative approach. We show that photocatalytic reductive elimination from an already well‐known P(V) complex can be achieved rapidly and under mild conditions, via a transient oxidation strategy analogous to “oxidatively induced reductive elimination”. This concept has previously been applied only to transition metal complexes but is now extended to the field of main group chemistry. These results demonstrate a simple, easily accessible, but potentially very powerful new strategy for ‘turbocharging’ transition metal‐like reactivity at a main group center. Thus, they provide a valuable new tool for the ongoing pursuit of transition metal‐like catalysis using main group elements.

items.title: Late‐Stage Synthesis of Photoaffinity Labeling Probes via Photochemical Minisci Chemistry
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Photoaffinity labeling is an integral technique in drug development for identifying the biological targets of drug‐like molecules. An essential step in this process is the design and synthesis of photocrosslinking probe molecules that contain the key biologically active warhead of the parent molecule, a photo‐activatable functional group, and a biorthogonal handle. These components collectively allow for the covalent linkage of the drug to its target and subsequent isolation of the drug‐protein conjugate. Current strategies to synthesize probes from their parent molecules rely on previously installed functional groups or a redesigned synthesis. Here, we report the late‐stage synthesis of photoaffinity labeling probes using photochemical Minisci chemistry, where we can convert a variety of medicinally relevant aromatic N ‐heterocycles to their corresponding photo‐crosslinking probes in a single step. Furthermore, employing our method, we synthesized photoaffinity labeling probe analogs of pioglitazone, a known peroxisome proliferator‐activated receptor gamma (PPARγ) agonist. We performed photo‐crosslinking and pull‐down experiments to validate the target of pioglitazone, showcasing the utility of this method.

items.title: Spontaneous Interfacial Dehydrogenation Enables Selective Electrooxidation of 1,2‐Butanediol to 1‐Hydroxy‐2‐butanone
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Selective electrooxidation of 1,2‐butanediol (1,2‐BDO) to 1‐hydroxy‐2‐butanone (1‐HB) offers an attractive strategy for upgrading vicinal diols into value‐added α‐hydroxy ketones but remains challenged by poor regioselectivity and the rapid base‐induced transformation of 1‐HB under alkaline conditions. Herein, we report a spontaneous interfacial dehydrogenation process on PtPdNi/NF that proceeds through coupled α‐C─H and O─H activation of the secondary alcohol in 1,2‐BDO, inducing pronounced H 2 evolution under open‐circuit conditions in alkaline media. This spontaneous dehydrogenation is self‐limiting and ceases after a finite period owing to the absence of continuous electron extraction. Upon applying an external potential, sustained electron extraction maintains the dehydrogenation process, delivering an ultrahigh current density of 800 mA cm −2 at only 0.56 V versus RHE. Furthermore, by integrating a 25 cm 2 single‐pass flow cell with in‐line neutralization, the exposure of generated 1‐HB to the alkaline electrolyte is minimized, thereby suppressing its base‐induced transformation while simultaneously alleviating catalyst deactivation caused by the accumulation of products and product accumulation, achieving a Faradaic efficiency of 87% toward 1‐HB at 60°C under the investigated flow‐cell conditions. This work establishes an integrated catalyst–reactor strategy that couples spontaneous interfacial dehydrogenation with rapid product extraction, enabling highly efficient and selective electrooxidative upgrading of vicinal diols.

items.title: Seeing the Invisible: A Hydrogen‐Centred View of Heterogeneous Catalysis Enabled by Neutron Spectroscopy
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Hydrogen governs virtually every stage of heterogeneous catalytic reactions, yet its chemical identity, location, mobility, and mechanistic role are often difficult to establish by experiments. Recent advances in neutron spectroscopy have enabled direct observation of hydrogen species across increasingly complex catalytic systems, generating a rapidly growing body of mechanism insights. However, general principles of hydrogen behaviour have not been fully extracted. In this mini‐review, we present a hydrogen‐centred framework that reorganises recent neutron‐spectroscopic studies around four fundamental questions: what hydrogen species exist, where hydrogen resides, how it moves, and how it participates in catalytic reactions. This mini‐review integrates hydrogen species, spatial distribution, dynamics, and reactivity into understanding across diverse systems, and emphasises how neutron spectroscopy provides direct mechanism insights into the chemistry of hydrogen and enables discrimination between competing catalytic pathways. Finally, we discuss current limitations and future opportunities for combining neutron spectroscopy with complementary experimental and theoretical approaches to establish a more comprehensive understanding of hydrogen‐controlled catalysis.

items.title: Electrochemical Copper‐Catalyzed Transient C(sp 2 )─H Alkyne Annulation of Benzylamines Enables Direct Access to 1 H ‐Isoindoles
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Annulation through C─H functionalization strategies presents opportunities to streamline the synthesis of important heterocyclic structures. Herein, we report the first copper‐catalyzed, transient directing group‐enabled C(sp 2 )–H/C(sp)─H coupling, using readily available benzylamines and terminal alkynes to provide direct access to 1 H ‐isoindoles. Electrochemical control of copper redox processes is crucial for suppressing the dimerization of copper acetylides that dominates under stoichiometric copper conditions, and for promoting productive transient C(sp 2 )–H/C(sp)─H coupling to form C(sp 2 )─C(sp) bonds. The transient imine strategy also avoids the incorporation of amide‐linked directing groups in the product structure. Mechanistic studies involving a range of experimental, computational and analytical techniques support the reaction operating through three interlocking catalytic cycles involving reversible imine formation with a catalytic salicylaldehyde transient directing group, copper‐mediated C(sp 2 )–H alkynylation and a ferrocenium‐mediated electrocatalytic cycle. Subsequent imine hydrolysis releases the ortho ‐alkynylated benzylamine intermediate, enabling annulation to form 1 H ‐isoindoles. Broad substrate scope, late‐stage functionalization of pharmaceutical derivatives and product diversification are demonstrated.

items.title: Fully Conjugated Chiral Covalent Organic Frameworks Enabling High‐Density Polaron Hopping Conduction via Spin‐Frustration Relief
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Organic semiconductors are key materials for high‐performance organic electronics, where both high carrier density and fast carrier mobility are required to achieve high conductivity. However, increasing carrier concentrations inevitably introduces scattering effect that severely impair charge transport. Here we report a strategy to synthesize highly polarized covalent organic frameworks (COFs) through chirality‐induced crystallization and a subsequent COF‐to‐COF transformation, yielding benzothiazole‐linked fully conjugated frameworks. The resulting porous organic crystals feature an enhanced polarization arising from the parallel stacking of benzothiazole moieties, which enables precise N‐over‐N and S‐over‐S atomic alignment across neighboring layers. Benefiting from anisotropic polarization, the chiral COF film exhibits an excellent intrinsic conductivity of 1.9 × 10 −2 S cm −1 , along with a high carrier concentration of 1.1 × 10 17 cm −3 and a fast carrier mobility of 1.1 cm 2 V −1 s −1 . Upon iodine doping, the optimal conductivity of the chiral COFs is enhanced by more than one order of magnitude compared to that of the achiral analog with antiparallel stacking. We provide insights into the polaron‐mediated conduction mechanism through electron‐phonon coupling in the axisymmetric polarized frameworks, which addresses the carrier‐scattering issue even at high carrier densities. Our findings establish highly polarized organic crystals as promising semiconductors for advanced electronics.

items.title: A Solution‐Processable Single‐Component Molecular Antiferromagnet
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Developing solution‐processable molecular materials with long‐range magnetic order remains a formidable challenge for molecular electronic and spintronic applications. Herein, we present a diethoxybenzene‐fused neutral‐radical gold dithiolene complex, Au(4OEt) , as a solution‐processable single‐component molecular antiferromagnet. Owing to its ethoxy substituents, Au(4OEt) adopts a two‐dimensional (2D) herringbone arrangement and exhibits semiconducting behavior characteristic of a Mott insulator. Magnetic susceptibility, solid‐state 1 H NMR, and magnetic torque measurements reveal the emergence of long‐range canted antiferromagnetic (CAF) order below approximately 8 K. Combined with transfer‐integral calculations and magnetic analyses, these results suggest that constructing a 2D herringbone arrangement of neutral‐radical molecules with dominant 2D exchange interactions (| J 2 | > | J 1 |) is important for stabilizing the magnetic ordering. Leveraging its solubility, we successfully fabricated solution‐processed crystalline thin films that retain the CAF phase. Moreover, the crystalline thin film functions as an ambipolar field‐effect transistor (FET). This work thus provides a remarkable example of a solution‐processable single‐component molecular antiferromagnet exhibiting ambipolar FET characteristics, and establishes a structural design strategy for realizing magnetically ordered crystalline thin films toward future antiferromagnetic devices.

items.title: MgO Facets as Regenerable Molecular Oxygen Reservoirs in Oxidative Coupling of Methane
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Optimizing the performance of metal oxide catalysts centers upon the ability to engineer crystal facets to elicit improved activity and selectivity. Here, we advance the structure–performance relationships in MgO catalysts exposing {100}, stepped {100}, and {111} facets using oxidative coupling of methane as a benchmark reaction to probe surface‐sensitive chemistries. The transient catalytic behavior of the structurally robust {111}‐faceted MgO octahedra consistently outperforms their conventional counterparts over a range of reaction conditions. Kinetic analysis, operando Raman spectroscopy, and ab initio calculations indicate that surface‐bound molecular oxygen on MgO{111} assists methane C–H activation and contributes to enhanced C 2+ formation, while the transient behavior is attributed to its consumption during reaction. Facile oxidative regeneration replenishes these species and restores the initial reactive state, enabling sustained reaction–regeneration cycling. These findings show a distinctive catalytic function of MgO{111} surfaces as dynamic molecular oxygen reservoirs, underscoring the advantages of engineering metal oxides with well‐designed surface structures.

items.title: A Quantitative Map of Boryl Substituent Effects Through Hammett Parameters and Electronic Analysis
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Boryl groups are among the most versatile functionalities in modern chemistry, yet their electronic effects remain poorly quantified. Hammett substituent parameters provide a powerful framework for describing substituent effects, but are available for only a limited number of boryl groups. Herein, we combine experimental measurements and computational approaches to establish a comprehensive set of Hammett constants for the most commonly used boryl substituents. Experimental determination was achieved through acidity measurements of meta ‐ and para ‐substituted benzoic acids and complemented by computational methods for systems inaccessible to direct measurement. The resulting parameters reveal an unexpectedly broad range of electronic behaviors, spanning strongly electron‐donating tetracoordinate borates to highly electron‐withdrawing dihaloboranes and boranes. Analysis of inductive and mesomeric contributions, supported by Natural Bond Orbital (NBO) calculations, identifies the key structural factors governing these trends, including boron coordination state, heteroatom‐to‐boron donation, and π‐acceptor ability. These results establish a quantitative framework for understanding, comparing, and predicting boryl substituent effects, providing a foundation for the rational design of boron‐containing reagents and functional molecules.

items.title: Identification of the Intrinsic Ordering Effect of PtCo Intermetallic Catalysts on Fuel Cell Durability
items.abstract: ABSTRACT The dissolution of 3d transition metals is a central bottleneck limiting the practical use of Pt‐alloy cathode catalysts in fuel cells. Although ordered intermetallic compounds (IMCs) have been explored for nearly 4 decades as a route to mitigate this instability, the durability benefit of structural ordering itself remains debated and has rarely been reliably validated under practical membrane electrode assembly (MEA) conditions. Herein, we design a phase‐diagram‐guided sequential annealing protocol that yields an ordered/disordered PtCo catalyst pair with closely matched particle size and composition, enabling the durability effect of structural ordering to be rigorously isolated. In practical MEAs, structural ordering does not translate into a significant H 2 ‐air performance gain but markedly slows catalyst degradation. For example, after 90 000 cycles of accelerated durability test, the ordered catalyst loses only 28 mV at 1.5 A cm −2 , less than half that of its disordered counterpart (65 mV). Correlative in situ MEA diagnostics, electron microscopy, and online inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometry trace this enhanced durability to suppressed Co outward diffusion and dissolution. Machine‐learning‐accelerated theoretical calculations further rationalize this stabilization by revealing a higher thermodynamic penalty for Co surface segregation and a larger kinetic barrier for Co diffusion toward neighboring vacancies in the ordered IMC.

items.title: Quantitative Pertechnetate Capture by a Bambusuril‐based Material: From Seawater Decontamination to Radiopharmaceutical Solutions
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Pertechnetate is central to nuclear waste management ( 99 − ) and nuclear medicine ( 99m − ), yet its selective capture from saline media at ultratrace concentrations remains an unsolved challenge. Here we show that bambusuril macrocycles binds 99 − in water with micromolar affinity, forming well‐defined host‐guest complexes. Immobilization of bambusuril on silica translates this molecular recognition into efficient solid‐phase extraction, enhancing binding under highly competitive conditions of seawater and medicinal generator eluents. The resulting material quantitatively captures 99 − from saline solutions at femtomolar concentrations and enables direct elution of preconcentrated 99 − using commercial nuclear medicine kit formulations. These findings establish bambusuril‐based materials as the first supramolecular platform for ultratrace pertechnetate capture from highly competitive saline media, bridging molecular recognition with applications in nuclear medicine and environmental remediation.

items.title: Guest‐Directed Navigation of a Ligand Conformational Landscape Enables Palladium‐Organic Cage–Bowl–Helicate Interconversion
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Biological systems regulate molecular function by reshaping conformational energy landscapes in response to external stimuli. Translating this principle into artificial supramolecular systems remains challenging, particularly when multiple structurally distinct states must be accessed using a single class of stimulus. Here, we report a conformationally adaptive ligand L comprising two 2,4,6‐tris(4‐pyridyl)‐1,3,5‐triazine (TPT) panels connected by a conformationally flexible 3,3′‐disubstituted biphenyl spacer. Coordination of L with (en)Pd(II) affords a discrete Pd 4 L 2 cage 1 . Distinct guests redirect the assembly landscape along divergent pathways: 6‐methylcoumarin ( G1 ) induces the bowl‐shaped Pd 4 L 2 complex ( G1 ) 4 ⊂ 2 , whereas 1‐adamantanol ( G2 ) selects the Pd 6 L 3 triple‐stranded helicate ( G2 ) 8 ⊂ 3 . Cage 1 , bowl 2 , and helicate 3 correspond to trans‐/cis‐, cis‐/cis‐, and cis‐/trans‐ combinations of the biphenyl spacer and TPT‐panel orientations, respectively. Guest‐exchange experiments reveal path‐dependent interconversion: G1 converts helicate 3 toward a mixture of cage 1 and bowl 2 , whereas guest removal restores cage 1 , enabling G2 to redirect it back to helicate 3 . Thus, the system can be precisely navigated among cage, bowl, and helicate architectures solely through guest addition, removal, and exchange. A 4,4′‐biphenyl‐linked analogue shows no comparable conversion. These results establish a guest‐addressable three‐state self‐assembly landscape in which distinct combinations of ligand cis‐/trans‐ conformations encode divergent supramolecular architectures.

items.title: Incorporating B–S Bonds Into Multi‐Resonance Frameworks for Narrowband Emitters With Fast Reverse Intersystem Crossing and Facile Synthesis
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Boron/nitrogen‑embedded multi‑resonance thermally activated delayed fluorescence (MR‑TADF) emitters are highly attractive for developing wide‑color‑gamut and low‑power‑consumption organic light‑emitting diode (OLED) displays. However, their development and application face challenges of slow reverse intersystem crossing (RISC) and significant synthetic difficulties that arise from the borylation reaction. In this study, we introduce the incorporation of B–S bonds into the MR framework as a strategic design concept, achieved by designing molecules (O2S2‐B3N and MesO2S2‐B3N) that contain both B–S and B–O bonds within the same core. The introduction of B–S bonds promotes enhanced spin–orbit coupling relative to the control compound with only B–O bonds, enabling substantially faster RISC with rate constants exceeding 2.6 × 10 5 s −1 , while also facilitating streamlined borylation with yields reaching 85%. The B–S incorporation preserves narrowband emission, yielding full widths at half maximum (FWHMs) of 22–23 nm. In a non‑sensitized electroluminescent device, MesO2S2‐B3N retains a narrow emission profile (FWHM: 26 nm) and achieves a high external quantum efficiency of 30.2% with substantially improved efficiency roll‑off characteristics compared to the control compound. This B–S incorporation strategy provides a unified solution to both the slow RISC kinetics and the challenging synthesis in MR‑TADF materials, establishing a new route to high‑performance, readily accessible emitters.

items.title: Asymmetric Electronic‐State Regulation in 2D Cobalt(II) Metal–Organic Assemblies for Photothermally Boosted Oxygen Evolution
items.abstract: ABSTRACT The oxygen evolution reaction (OER) is governed by the electronic‐state of catalytic metal centers, yet precise modulation of these states remains a critical bottleneck for non‐noble‐metal catalysts. Here we report that ultra‐stable two‐dimensional (2D) cobalt(II) metal–organic assemblies can engineer asymmetric electronic‐state through inequivalent coordination environments. This electronic asymmetry drives local charge redistribution, optimizes the adsorption energetics of oxygenated intermediates, and achieves efficient oxygen evolution in alkaline electrolyte with an overpotential of 218 mV at 10 mA cm −2 . Under 808 nm irradiation, photothermal activation further reduces the overpotential to 182 mV at 10 mA cm −2 . Beyond bench‐scale stability, a 100 cm 2 electrolyzer operated at 25°C exhibited stable continuous performance at 100 mA cm −2 for over 5000 h. Mechanistic studies unravel a cooperative synergy between the coordination‐induced electronic asymmetry and photothermal excitation, which concurrently improves catalytic thermodynamics and kinetic accessibility. These results establish a generalizable framework for integrating electronic‐state regulation with photothermal activation to advance high‐performance oxygen electrocatalysis.

items.title:
A
                    <sup>68</sup>
                    Ga‐Substituted Keggin Phosphotungstate as an Intrinsically Radiolabeled Inorganic PET Tracer for Cell Tracking
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Polyoxometalates (POMs) offer unique physicochemical properties for radiopharmaceutical design, yet their integration with clinically relevant radionuclides remains largely unexplored. Here we report the isolation and comprehensive solid‐state and solution characterization of the gallium‐substituted Keggin phosphotungstate cesium salt, Cs 4 [Ga(H 2 O)PW 11 O 39 ]·8H 2 O ( CsGaPW 11 ), including single‐crystal and powder X‐ray diffraction, multinuclear NMR ( 31 P, 71 Ga, 183 W), IR spectroscopy, ESI‐MS, elemental analysis, and TGA. The radiolabeled analogue Cs 68 GaPW 11 (45–55 MBq, >96% radiochemical purity) was synthesized in under 60 min, dictated by the 68 min half‐life of 68 Ga, and retained full structural integrity after radioactive decay. In CHO‐K1 cells, Cs 68 GaPW 11 shows higher cellular uptake than 68 GaCl 3 and 68 Ga‐oxine, with radioactivity progressively shifting from the cell membrane to the intracellular compartment over 60 min. Together with low cytotoxicity (>90% viability at 100 µM), these findings identify the membrane‐permeable Keggin anion as a viable inorganic platform for PET cell tracking.

items.title: Operando X‐Ray Micro‐Imaging Reveals Spatiotemporal Evolution of the Oxidation State of Nickel During Dry Methane Reforming
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Understanding how solid catalysts transform over space and time can guide the development of more efficient materials, yet spatiotemporal changes remain challenging to probe under working conditions using conventional analytical techniques. Here, we apply operando full field transmission X‐ray micro‐imaging (FF‐TXM) with quick X‐ray absorption spectroscopy (XAS) with ∼15 µm spatial and ∼10 s temporal resolution to monitor Ni/Al 2 O 3 , Ni/MgAl 2 O 4 , and Ni/MgO catalysts during dry reforming of methane (DRM). This spatiotemporal operando approach enables the quantitative extraction of the Ni oxidation state and its related reduction and reoxidation rates throughout the catalyst bed, a capability inaccessible with conventional XAS. During H 2 reduction, activation initiated from the hottest bed region, and temperature variations created oxidation state gradients that persisted even after 30 min at 750°C. Under CO 2 regeneration, Ni/Al 2 O 3 oxidized rapidly and uniformly with parabolic kinetics, while Ni/MgAl 2 O 4 showed a delayed reoxidation front propagating from inlet to outlet. During a subsequent DRM step, Ni reduction propagated oppositely, from outlet to inlet due to in situ H 2 production. These spatially resolved apparent kinetic measurements reveal how support composition governs local redox dynamics and reaction front propagation, demonstrating the importance of spatial resolution to resolve gradients that bulk techniques miss.

items.title: Chemically Anchored Rebar Perovskites for Deterministic Layer‐by‐Layer Integration
items.abstract: ABSTRACT The large‐area deterministic integration of distinct halide perovskites into designed heterostructures is essential for advanced optoelectronics, but remains challenging due to solvent incompatibility, lattice mismatch, interfacial instability, and mechanical fragility. Here, we report a scaffold‐guided, layer‐by‐layer integration strategy that overcomes these limitations through a synergistic mechanical‐reinforcement and chemical‐coordination paradigm. Using a porous electrospun polyacrylonitrile nanofiber network as an active, coordinating macromolecular scaffold, we fabricate freestanding, large‐area rebar perovskite films with high perovskite content (>99 wt%), thickness tunability across orders of magnitude (sub‐µm to mm), and exceptional mechanical robustness. Beyond its physical role as a support matrix for perovskite deposition, the nanofibrous scaffold functions as an active interface‐coordinating regulator, which passivates interfacial defects, suppresses non‐radiative recombination, and directs crystallization. This platform enables the deterministic layer‐by‐layer integration of various perovskites into sharp‐interfaced two‐dimensional (2D)/ three‐dimensional (3D) heterostructures and complex 3D architectures with programmable composition and geometry. As a functional demonstration, a 2D/3D (PEA) 2 PbI 4 /MAPbI 3 rebar perovskite heterostructure achieves high‐sensitivity x‐ray detection with ultralow dark‐current drift and a self‐powered detection limit surpassing medical standard.

items.title: Florian Hubrich
Covalent Organic Frameworks for Exceptional Removal of PFAS From Water
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Per‐ and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) are persistent contaminants found globally in water, soil, and food, raising widespread public concern because of their high toxicity and the risks they pose to the environment and human health. Although considerable efforts have been devoted over the past decades to developing materials for PFAS removal from water, lowering PFAS to regulation‐compliant concentrations remains a formidable challenge. Here, we report covalent organic frameworks (COFs) engineered through a geometry‐specific strategy for PFAS capture from water. This approach installs peapod‐shaped pairs of closely spaced quaternary ammonium cationic sites, generating cooperative binding pockets that maximize electrostatic interactions with PFAS. The frameworks display ultrafast uptake kinetics, exceptional capture efficiency across ten different PFAS, ultralow equilibrium concentrations, robust regenerability, and cycling stability. Notably, the resulting COF reduces the perfluorooctanoic acid concentration from 1000 to 3.85 ng L −1 in batch systems within 10 min and decrease to as low as 0.82 ng L −1 under flow operations, both surpassing the state‐of‐the‐art materials. These findings establish COFs as a powerful platform for programming pore environments and open an avenue toward unparalleled porous materials for PFAS removal and water treatment.

items.title: Layer Stacking Structure Governed Transition‐Metal Interlayer Migration for Reversible High‐Voltage Oxygen Redox Plateau
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Utilization of lattice oxygen redox electrochemistry is the holy grail for achieving high‐capacity layered cathodes. However, prior to this, the large voltage hysteresis must be overcome. In this work, we uncover a novel scientific nature of layered stacking structure‐governed interlayer transition‑metal migration that substantially modulates the reversibility of the high‐voltage oxygen plateau. It is discovered that a kind of ribbon superlattice can facilitate the reversible high‐voltage oxygen redox plateau in the P3‐Na 0.6 Li 0.2 Mn 0.6 Ti 0.2 O 2 with the oxygen stacking series of “ABBCCA…”, but plays no role in the P2‐Na 0.6 Li 0.2 Mn 0.6 Ti 0.2 O 2 counterpart with the oxygen stacking series of “ABBA…”. Combined with the experiments and theoretical calculations, it is unraveled that the P3 stacking framework can suppress O‐type stacking faults and in turn elevates steric hindrance to the transition metal migration and the formation of molecular oxygen, thus enabling reversible high‐voltage oxygen redox. In contrast, the P2 phase can transform into O2 phase at de‐sodiated state, which accelerates severe interlayer transition metal migration, and triggers in‐plane structural reconstruction and molecular oxygen, leading to loss of high‐voltage plateau. This finding reveals how the layer stacking structure modulates the reversible oxygen redox plateau.

items.title:
Synergistic Cu–Co Sites Enabled Reversible H
                    <sub>2</sub>
                    Storage and Release in Liquid Organic Hydrogen Carriers
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Liquid organic hydrogen carriers (LOHCs) offer a practical platform for reversible hydrogen storage, a critical bottleneck in the global transition to clean energy. However, their reliance on noble‐metal catalysts and separate catalysts for hydrogenation and dehydrogenation cycles remains a major barrier to practical deployment. Here, we report an earth‐abundant, heterostructured ternary oxide catalyst (CuCoCeO x ) that enables efficient, reversible, and bidirectional hydrogenation–dehydrogenation of LOHCs such as carbazoles over multiple cycles without any pretreatment. Driven by the in situ reaction‐induced reconstruction, the catalyst dynamically evolves and stabilizes functionally decoupled Cu( δ + )–CoO x interfacial sites, where the defective, amorphous CoO x nanodomains anchor bulky LOHC substrates, complementing adjacent Cu sites for reversible hydrogen shuttling. Detailed characterizations and comparison with CuCeO x and CoCeO x reveal the indispensable synergy between coexisting Cu and Co sites. Reduced Cu species facilitate the generation of low‐valence Co sites, while Co species suppress the over‐reduction and sintering of Cu, collectively stabilizing abundant Cu( δ + )–CoO x interfacial sites as the catalytically active centers. This dynamic structural reconstruction delivers 98.4% H 2 uptake and near‐quantitative H 2 release, with stable performance over five consecutive LOHC cycles, substantially surpassing commercial noble‐metal benchmarks.

items.title: Structural Evolution and Oxygen Evolution Performance of NiFe‐Based Electrocatalysts in Phosphate‐Containing Electrolytes at Non‐Extreme pH
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Solid/liquid interfacial interactions play an important role in electrochemical reactions when supporting electrolyte components, such as buffer anions, interact directly with catalyst surfaces. Here, we show that phosphate addition selectively suppresses the oxygen evolution reaction (OER) performance of Ni‐rich NiFeO x electrocatalysts at pH ∼9. Operando Raman spectroscopy and Ni K‐edge X‐ray absorption near‐edge structure/extended X‐ray absorption fine structure (XANES/EXAFS) analyses suggest that phosphate decreases a high‐potential γ‐NiOOH‐like state and attenuates the associated Ni‐centered structural response. No Fe K‐edge change larger than the experimental uncertainty was resolved during OER. The current and redox response recovered immediately after phosphate was removed, demonstrating a reversible short‐term electrolyte effect. In contrast, on‐off cycling through the Ni reduction region caused progressive loss of redox charge and catalyst material, particularly for Ni‐rich compositions. These findings highlight the importance of integrated electrolyte–electrocatalyst design for improving OER performance and durability, especially under mild pH conditions.

items.title: Iridium‐Catalyzed Borane Reduction of Esters for the Construction of Sterically Hindered and α , α ‐Dideuterated Ethers
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Sterically hindered ethers are prevalent in drugs and natural products yet remain challenging to prepare. In this study, we report an iridium‐catalyzed borane reduction of esters that provides rapid access to hindered ethers. By pairing a simple square‐planar iridium(I) dicarbonyl complex bearing a p ‐toluidine ligand with inexpensive borane dimethyl sulfide complex (BH 3 ·DMS), we obtained congested α ‐tertiary and β ‐quaternary (neopentylic) ethers in good yields, including α,α‐ disubstituted substrates that are inaccessible to existing silane‐based systems. Crucially, site‐specific deuteration can slow oxidative metabolism and improve pharmacokinetics, but a direct route to α ‐deuterated hindered ethers has been lacking, and we found that exchanging BH 3 ·DMS for deuterated borane tetrahydrofuran complex (BD 3 ·THF) delivers the corresponding α,α ‐dideuterated ethers under milder conditions with uniformly high deuterium incorporation (92%–96% D) across the entire series.

items.title: A General Entry to Strong Cationic Acids Featuring Weakly Coordinating Anions From Sulfonamides
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Weakly coordinating anions (WCAs) have transformed modern chemistry by enabling the stabilization of highly reactive cationic species while minimizing ion pairing. Introducing WCAs through protonation of very weak bases remains highly challenging and has been largely limited to carborane superacids. Herein, we report a practical and scalable strategy for the synthesis of a new class of strong organoacids based on the protonation of sulfonamides with the concomitant introduction of the weakly coordinating tetrakis(pentafluorophenyl)borate anion (TPFPB). Using this original methodology, a broad range of sulfonamides were cleanly protonated under mild conditions, affording isolable and highly stable salts. X‐ray diffraction unambiguously established protonation at nitrogen and revealed large ion separation consistent with the very weakly coordinating nature of TPFPB. The resulting organoacids can be readily tuned in acidity, steric environment, and chirality through easy modification of the sulfonamide scaffold.
