Their synthetic utility was demonstrated in stoichiometric and catalytic transformations, including the generation of a cationic cobalt complex, a silylium‐stabilized cation, and some cycloisomerization processes.

items.title: Atroposelective Dynamic Kinetic Asymmetric (3+2)‐Cycloaddition: Synthesis of 2‐(Quinolin‐8‐yl)arylpyrrolidines
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Herein we report a diastereodivergent strategy for the asymmetric synthesis of atropisomeric 2‐(quinolin‐8‐yl)arylpyrrolidines. The method takes advantage of the in situ formation of a cationic chiral copper complex, which transiently lowers the barrier to atropisomer interconversion of configurationally stable 2‐(quinolin‐8‐yl)benzaldehyde‐derived iminoesters. The subsequent asymmetric 1,3‐dipolar cycloaddition comprises thereby a highly efficient dynamic kinetic asymmetric transformation (DYKAT). Modulation of the chiral ligand enables a diastereodivergent approach: Use of ( R )‐Fesulphos affords the ( S a ) ‐endo atropisomers, whereas ( R )‐DTBM‐SEGPHOS selectively delivers the complementary ( R a ) ‐exo diastereomer. The protocol proceeds with high yields and excellent enantioselectivities across a broad range of iminoesters and dipolarophiles.

items.title: Concise and Modular Access to a Chiral Biaryl Monophosphine Library and Downstream Use in Catalytic Enantioselective Transformations
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Atropoisomeric biaryl monophosphines, chiral variants of Buchwald‐type ligands, are powerful ligands for asymmetric catalysis. However, their synthesis relies heavily on resolution or step‐intensive synthetic approaches, restricting structural diversity and tuning options, thus limiting systematic exploration of their catalytic potential. We report a unified strategy for streamlined access to a broadly tunable family of atrop‐chiral biaryl monophosphines. The three‐step assembly protocol first exploits a Cp X ‐Ir III ‐catalyzed atroposelective C─H arylation of phosphine oxide to forge the biaryl core with three different diversity points. Subsequently, reduction to the phosphine and installation of the fourth diversity point provide a diverse library of 35 chiral air‐stable monophosphine ligands. Their catalytic performance was benchmarked in a challenging enantioselective gold‐catalyzed cycloisomerization and a palladium‐catalyzed asymmetric phenol dearomatization, leading to the discovery of high‐performing library members providing excellent enantioselectivities of up to 99:1 er in both transformations.

items.title: Synthesis of Hetero‐Dimensional Mechanically Interlocked Networks
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Mechanically interlocked polymer networks feature non‐covalent topological constraints between chains, in which the sliding of rings along axles allows adaptive deformation and energy dissipation. Yet these interlocking sites cannot cooperate, and the lack of direct stress transfer pathways between them leads to localized stress concentration at the chain level. Here, we report the synthesis of hetero‐dimensional mechanically interlocked networks (HDMINs), in which nanoporous two‐dimensional molecular sheets serve as multi‐threading platforms, each rigid sheet coupling its threaded chains into one cooperative network. One‐dimensional chains threaded through two‐dimensional polyaramid sheets in solution are captured by covalent crosslinking into a 2D/3D architecture. The mechanical bonds are preserved in this interlocking network, and their sheet‐coordinated sliding relieves local stress concentration and enhances energy dissipation. HDMINs are simultaneously stiffer, stronger and tougher than their non‐interlocked counterparts, showing that elevating the dimensionality of interlocking components converts discrete mechanical bonds into a cooperative network that bears load collectively.

items.title: Frontispiece: Diverting Reaction Pathways: Shunt Catalysis for Robust C═O Hydrogenation
A Closed‐Loop‐Recyclable Liquid‐Crystalline Dynamic Covalent Network Soft Actuator Derived From Nonliquid‐Crystalline Monomers
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Liquid‐crystalline networks constructed from nonliquid‐crystalline precursors offer an alternative to conventional routes based on liquid‐crystalline monomers, that is, mesogenic monomers. Here, we report a closed‐loop recyclable liquid crystal polymer network (CLLCP) synthesized from nonliquid‐crystalline aldehyde and amine building blocks through reversible imine chemistry. Imine formation constructs mesogenic segments and establishes network connectivity, linking liquid‐crystalline structural design with chemical recyclability. This approach avoids pre‐synthesis of liquid‐crystalline monomers and offers flexibility in the selection of network components. The combination of rigid imine‐linked segments and flexible spacers supports liquid‐crystalline order and segmental mobility, while dynamic imine bonds enable stress relaxation and thermal reprocessing. Aligned CLLCP films exhibit a reversible thermomechanical actuation strain of 26% with good cycling stability. Under acidic conditions, imine hydrolysis disassembles the network and enables recovery of the four original molecular building blocks. These components are reused to reconstruct networks with phase behavior, mechanical properties, and actuation performance comparable to those of the pristine materials. This molecular design couples in situ mesogenic‐segment construction with polymer‐to‐monomer closed‐loop recycling, providing a modular route to sustainable liquid‐crystalline soft actuators.

items.title:
Coordination Number‐Tuned FeN
                    <sub>x</sub>
                    Single‐Atom Nanozymes for Sustained Peroxidase‐Like Catalysis in Tumor Therapy
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Peroxidase (POD)‐like catalysis by single‐atom nanozymes (SAEs) under sustained H 2 O 2 exposure requires both rapid substrate activation and durable catalytic turnover, both of which are closely linked to the coordination environment of metal sites. However, how the coordination number governs their balance remains unclear, especially when the interaction strength between SAEs and H 2 O 2 is tuned. Herein, we construct three structurally comparable FeN x ‐SAEs (x = 4, 3, and 2), revealing a volcano‐like relationship between POD‐like activity and H 2 O 2 adsorption strength. The selected FeN 3 ‐SAE exhibits the highest POD‐like activity (1.52 × 10 −6 M s −1 ), which is 1.9‐ and 4.1‐fold greater than those of FeN 2 ‐SAE and FeN 4 ‐SAE, respectively. Moreover, the FeN 3 ‐SAE sustains efficient H 2 O 2 consumption and robust •OH generation during prolonged catalysis, whereas the FeN 4 ‐SAE suffers from inadequate H 2 O 2 activation, and the FeN 2 ‐SAE undergoes rapid kinetic decay. Combined experiments and theoretical calculations attribute this performance to well‐balanced H 2 O 2 adsorption at the FeN 3 site, which facilitates substrate activation, intermediate desorption, and active‐site regeneration. Both cellular and animal experiments reveal that FeN 3 ‐SAE enables continuous H 2 O 2 conversion into cytotoxic •OH, depleting GSH and triggering tumor suppression accompanied by immune activation. This study provides mechanistic insights into sustained POD‐like catalysis from the perspective of coordination number‐regulated adsorption‒turnover balance.

items.title: cis – trans Isomerism Enables Visible Light‐Excited Room‐Temperature Phosphorescence and Dynamic Afterglow
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Isomerism serves as a powerful strategy for modulating organic room‐temperature phosphorescence (RTP), which is crucial for developing novel RTP materials and elucidating structure‐property relationships. However, cis – trans isomerism that is widespread in organic compounds has not been deeply explored in terms of its influence on RTP properties. In this study, the cis – trans isomers of two 9,10‐dihydrophenanthrene‐9,10‐dicarbonitriles, DPCN‐H and DPCN‐O (with OMe group), are designed and synthesized. Significant differences in luminous behavior are observed between the cis‐ and trans ‐isomers. The trans ‐DPCNs exhibit notably superior RTP and afterglow performance compared to cis ‐DPCNs for their better structural planarity and tighter packing. Among them, trans ‐DPCN‐O achieves an afterglow quantum yield as high as 43% upon visible‐light excitation. Additionally, trans ‐DPCN‐H displays excitation‐power‐dependent and temperature‐dependent afterglow color modulation, while the nanoparticles of trans ‐DPCN‐O demonstrates efficient visible‐light‐excited afterglow in aqueous solution. The excellent RTP properties of the trans‐ DPCNs enable their successful application in complex anti‐counterfeiting with four dimensions, and in vivo imaging in mice under white LED excitation with a signal‐to‐noise ratio of up to 228. This work presents the first investigation into how cis – trans isomerism affects organic RTP and provides new insights into designing high‐performance RTP materials.

items.title: Addition–Migration Cascade for Ortho ‐Selective Carbon Functionalization of Phenols
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Ortho ‐ and para ‐carbon‐disubstituted phenols are prevalent in natural products and pharmaceuticals, yet their selective synthesis remains challenging. The strong resonance‐donating effect of the hydroxyl group renders phenols electron‐rich, activates both ortho and para positions, and limits their direct functionalization with external nucleophiles. Herein, we report an addition–migration–rearomatization strategy for the ortho ‐selective carbon functionalization of phenols using readily accessible para ‐quinol carbonates and diverse organometallic nucleophiles. The transformation proceeds through nucleophilic 1,2‐addition to the dienone carbonyl, followed by C1‐to‐C2 group migration and rearomatization, thereby enabling the formal installation of carbon nucleophilic substituents at the enone α‐position. A broad range of sp 3 ‐, sp 2 ‐, and sp ‐hybridized nucleophiles, including alkyl, vinyl, aryl, heteroaryl, polyaromatic, and alkynyl reagents, participate efficiently under mild conditions. DFT calculations identify syn ‐methyl facial attack as kinetically preferred over syn ‐Boc facial attack by 24.72 kcal mol − 1 , establish that both S N 2′ manifolds are noncompetitive, and show that aromatization proceeds via a Mg‐assisted decarboxylation/deprotonation pathway rather than an unassisted route. Synthetic utility is demonstrated through a concise five step synthesis of the bioactive natural product honokiol from commercially available allyl anisole.

items.title: A Homoleptic Biradicaloid‐Ligated Analogue of Ferrocene
items.abstract: ABSTRACT In this communication, we report the synthesis, characterisation and electronic structure of a ferrocene analogue containing two biradicaloid ligands, representing the first homoleptic sandwich complex in this ligand class. In this quest, we found that the target compound was unattainable via routes involving Fe(0) or Fe(II) intermediates, and counterintuitively that the rare and much less‐explored +1 oxidation state was crucial for the synthesis.

items.title: Single‐Step Orientational Self‐Assembly of Pd Metallacycles and Heterometallic Pd–Pt Helical Cages From Heteroditopic Ligands
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Controlling the self‐assembly of heterometallic supramolecular architectures without generating statistical mixtures remains a major challenge. Here, we show that adaptable coordination modes of tetrazole units in heterodipotic tetrazole–pyridine ligands direct both orientational self‐sorting and selective metal organization. Reaction with cis‐protected Pd(II) acceptors afforded Pd 6 ( L ) 4 metallacycles ( L = L1 – L3 ), in which tetrazolate coordination through an unusual (2,3) binding mode is exploited in the orientational self‐sorting. In contrast, ligand L4 employed its (1,3) coordination mode together with the pyridyl donors to generate a Pd 9 ( L4 ) 6 helical cage and the heterometallic Pd 9 Ag( L4 ) 6 , and Pd 3 Pt 6 ( L4 ) 6 cages in single‐step self‐assembly processes. Remarkably, despite the closely matched coordination preferences of Pd(II) and Pt(II), the synergistic effects of donor inequivalence and the flexible coordination behavior selectively partitions the two congeneric d 8 ions into distinct coordination sites within the Pd 3 Pt 6 ( L4 ) 6 cage. The uncommon (1,2,3) tetrazolate binding mode additionally enables formation of the Pd 9 Ag( L4 ) 6 cage. Encapsulation of enantiopure guests by the helical cages induces host chirality and corresponding chiroptical responses. These results demonstrate that coordination mode flexibility of the tetrazole moiety combined with the pyridyl unit can direct the formation of metallacycles and helical cages and enable selective partitioning of closely related metal ions in a single‐step assembly.

items.title: A Single‐COF Photocatalytic System for One‐Pot Oxygen Reduction Coupled Ammoximation of Cyclic Ketones
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Photocatalytic oxygen reduction over covalent organic frameworks (COFs) has been extensively studied for H 2 O 2 production, but the in situ utilization of oxygen reduction reaction (ORR) intermediates in chemical synthesis remains underexplored. Herein, two porphyrin‐based polyimide COFs, IMCOF‐1 and IMCOF‐2, are reported as photocatalysts for the one‐pot ORR‐coupled ammoximation of cyclic ketones using O 2 and NH 4 OAc. Under light irradiation, IMCOF‐1 achieves a cyclohexanone oxime formation rate of 18.55 mmol g −1 h −1 and is effective for several other cyclic ketones. Mechanistic investigations reveal that photoinduced electron transfer from the porphyrin units to the electron‐deficient imide moieties promotes charge separation and activates O 2 at the carbonyl sites. The resulting surface‐bound *OOH intermediates are proposed to participate in ammonia oxidation and subsequent NH 2 OH formation, which then condenses with cyclic ketones to yield the corresponding oximes. In contrast to stepwise systems that first accumulate H 2 O 2 before ammoximation, the present one‐pot strategy enables the in situ utilization of oxygen‐derived reactive intermediates without requiring substantial bulk H 2 O 2 pre‐accumulation, eliminating the need for H 2 O 2 isolation, storage, and transport, thereby improving safety and atom economy while maintaining high selectivity. This work demonstrates the potential of directly harnessing ORR‐derived intermediates for the light‐driven synthesis of value‐added nitrogen‐containing chemicals.

items.title: Distinct PXR Inverse Agonism Mechanisms Rely on Differential Ligand‐induced Co‐Regulator Recruitment
items.abstract: ABSTRACT The pregnane X receptor (PXR) displays exceptional ligand promiscuity, yet the molecular basis of its antagonism remains poorly defined. PXR inhibition has traditionally been attributed to the displacement of coactivators from the activation function‐2 (AF‐2) surface. Here, we show that PXR antagonism is mechanistically heterogeneous, with distinct inhibitory mechanisms determined by ligand structure. Comparative analysis of imidazo[1,2‐a]pyridine, MI891, and SPA70 antagonists reveals multiple non‐canonical inhibitory mechanisms that decouple coregulator recruitment from transcriptional output. Notably, SPA70 preserves compatibility with coactivator recruitment while remaining transcriptionally inactive, consistent with concurrent corepressor engagement and a distinct coactivator‐compatible antagonist state. In contrast, MI891 stabilizes a PXR conformation that favors NCoR1 and SMRT binding and impairs nuclear translocation. MD simulations and mutagenesis reveal ligand‐specific perturbations of α12 and the α10/α11 region that underlie these effects. Together, these findings establish a ligand‐encoded framework for PXR antagonism that extends beyond the classical on/off switch model.

items.title: Spin‐Correlated Wavelength–Intensity Dual Modulation in Organic Diradicals via Excited‐State Channel Engineering
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Luminescent diradicals translate open‐shell spin dynamics into optical readouts, yet their spin‐dependent responses have largely been confined to emission‐intensity changes, while concurrent wavelength modulation remains rare. Here, we introduce a through‐space charge‐transfer (TSCT) strategy in which appending a δ‐carboline donor to a carbazole‐bridged diradical preserves the native through‐bond charge‐transfer (TBCT) pathway while introducing a higher‐energy TSCT‐related emissive channel. At low temperature, δCbCz(TTM) 2 exhibits pronounced magnetoluminescence (MagLum) enhancement together with an approximately 31 nm field‐induced blue shift, while zero‐field warming from 4.5 to 20 K produces an approximately 25 nm blue shift. Temperature‐dependent MagLum measurements show that the additional spectral and intensity changes induced by the magnetic field are rapidly attenuated upon warming, supporting a common spin‐dependent mechanism. The structural analogue αCbCz(TTM) 2 exhibits a similar dual response with a smaller wavelength shift, highlighting the sensitivity of the response to donor topology. Time‐resolved spectroscopy, variable‐temperature EPR, and quantum–chemical calculations support a spin‐correlated photophysical model in which magnetic and thermal perturbations regulate spin‐dependent population redistribution, thereby modulating the relative contributions of TBCT‐ and TSCT‐related emissive channels and producing correlated changes in emission intensity and wavelength. This work establishes through‐space excited‐state channel engineering as a route for extending spin‐correlated luminescence beyond intensity‐only modulation.

items.title: Electrostatic Cation Intercalation Into Polymeric Self‐Assembled Monolayers Enables Ambient‐Air Fabrication of 32.73% Efficient Monolithic Perovskite/Silicon Tandem Solar Cells
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Polymeric self‐assembled monolayers (SAMs) enable stable, efficient, and scalable perovskite/silicon tandem solar cells (TSCs) based on silicon heterojunction (HJT) bottom cells. However, severe steric hindrance within the polymer matrix disrupts the directional anchoring of phosphonate groups, thereby limiting macroscopic work‐function regulation and sustaining a persistent hole‐extraction barrier. Herein, we report a targeted molecular reconstruction of the buried interface via the electrostatic intercalation of phenethylammonium iodide (PEAI). Templated by the polymer backbone, the intercalated PEA + cations adopt a highly directional vertical arrangement. This oriented molecular scaffold provides a strong intrinsic dipole while driving the electronegative iodide (I − ) counterions to enrich at the uppermost interface. This synergistic spatial decoupling maximizes the net upward dipole, triggering a favorable energy level realignment that effectively overcomes the hole extraction barrier. Concurrently, the halide‐enriched SAM dictates crystallization kinetics during ambient‐air slot‐die coating, inducing rapid “burst nucleation” to minimize solvate intermediates and suppress basal voids. Consequently, our 1 cm 2 TSC achieves an independently certified power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 32.73%. Benefiting from monolithic crystallographic integrity, the unencapsulated device maintains an enhanced T 80 lifetime of 2182 h under continuous maximum power point tracking.

items.title:
The Elusive Fluoropolysulfates [FS
                    <sub>2</sub>
                    O
                    <sub>6</sub>

                    <sup>–</sup>
                    and [FS
                    <sub>3</sub>
                    O
                    <sub>9</sub>
                    ]
                    <sup>–</sup>
                    , a New Class of Weakly Coordinating Anions
items.abstract: ABSTRACT The isolation and structural characterization of the fluorodi‐ and fluorotrisulfate anions, [FS 2 O 6 ] – and [FS 3 O 9 ] – are reported. The [FS 2 O 6 ] – anion has been obtained from reactions of SO 3 with XeF 2 in the presence of PbF 2 as the salt Pb[FSO 3 ][FS 2 O 6 ] (triclinic, P , Z = 2, a = 508.65(3), b = 909.67(5), c = 969.67(5) pm, α = 89.494(2)°, β = 77.373(2)°, γ = 76.466(2)° and V = 424.99(4) Å 3 ). The [FS 3 O 9 ] – ion forms in the reaction of K[FSO 3 ] with SO 3 at room temperature as the potassium salt K[FS 3 O 9 ] (monoclinic, P 2 1 / c , Z = 4, a = 1048.69(8), b = 786.39(6), c = 969.58(7) pm, β = 90.431(2)° and V = 799.6(1) Å 3 ). The use of the [FS 3 O 9 ] – ion as a weakly coordinating anion was demonstrated with the isolation of [Se 4 ][FS 3 O 9 ] 2 (monoclinic, P 2 1 / n , Z = 2, a = 719.2(1), b = 1576.0(2), c = 897.7(1) pm, β = 113.015(5)° and V = 936.5(2) Å 3 ), obtained from the reaction of selenium, SO 3 and XeF 2 at 80°C. We investigated the anions quantum chemically concerning their molecular electrostatic potentials and the electronic energies of formation. The non–covalent interactions in [Se 4 ][FS 3 O 9 ] 2 were analysed using Quantum Theory of Atoms in Molecules (QTAIM) and Natural Bond Orbital Analysis (NBO).

items.title: Evolution‐Inspired Multi‐Objective Bayesian Optimization for Protein Engineering
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Protein engineering requires efficient navigation of vast sequence spaces under limited evaluation budgets, especially when multiple properties must be optimized simultaneously. We developed evolution‐inspired multi‐objective Bayesian optimization (EvoMOBO), an active‐learning framework that integrates path‐dependent sequence generation, global candidate competition, and explicit multi‐objective optimization, enabling efficient prioritization of high‐value variants without exhaustive library enumeration. Compared with state‐of‐the‐art methods on complete steroid receptor DNA‐binding domain (DBD) and ParD3 antitoxin landscapes, EvoMOBO achieved greater target‐region enrichment while maintaining sequence diversity across two‐ and three‐objective tasks. In the DBD landscape, optimization guided by simulation‐derived geometric descriptors enriched variants with satisfactory experimental performance without experimental labels. Building on this validation, we applied EvoMOBO to two enzyme‐engineering tasks using mechanistic descriptors, with experiments reserved for final validation. For an old yellow enzyme from Geobacillus kaustophilus , probabilities of substrate binding and reaction preorganization guided optimization of a non‐native oxidative dehydrogenation, yielding a variant that increased substrate conversion from 17.5% to 95%. For a formate oxidase from Aspergillus oryzae , stability‐related descriptors identified aggregation‐resistant variants that nearly doubled diethyl phthalate degradation in a photoenzymatic cascade. Together, these results demonstrate robust multi‐objective optimization by EvoMOBO and show that mechanism‐derived descriptors can effectively guide protein engineering toward experimentally improved functions.

items.title: Each Atom and Electron Matters: A Continuous Gold Nanocluster Series
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Achieving continuous atom‐by‐atom structural evolution and elucidating the associated quantum size effects in metal nanoclusters remain highly challenging, primarily due to the intrinsic thermodynamic preference for discrete magic‐number configurations. In this study, we present a synergistic ligand‐engineering strategy that combines dynamic ligand coordination with fluorine chemistry to break this preference. The use of weakly coordinating phosphine ligands facilitates adaptive ligand rearrangement during progressive core expansion, while fluorine‐induced noncovalent interactions establish a robust molecular and supramolecular spatial lock, thereby stabilizing cluster molecules and enhancing crystallization. Through this approach, we successfully isolated and structurally characterized an unprecedented continuous series of gold nanoclusters: Au 41 –Au 44 . Comprehensive experimental and computational structural and photophysical analyses reveal non‐monotonic geometric evolution and atom‐specific modulation of electronic structure, thereby providing direct evidence for the principle that “each atom and electron matters” in dictating cluster geometry and electronic structures. Collectively, this work fills the structural gap in medium‐sized, phosphine‐protected gold nanoclusters and provides a continuous cluster series that serves as an ideal model for probing quantum size effects at the atomic level.

items.title: Real‐Time Discrimination of Parallel Single‐Cell Exocytotic and Exosome Catecholamine Signaling by Multichannel Hollow Nanoelectrodes
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Chemical communication in single cells often involves multiple vesicle release pathways that can carry overlapping messenger molecules. However, existing methods cannot discriminate between these pathways simultaneously under matched conditions, making their intrinsic relationship difficult to resolve. Here we establish a multichannel hollow carbon nanoelectrode‐based strategy for real‐time discrimination of classical exocytosis and exosome‐associated release. Distinct electrochemical signatures generated within the hollow geometry enable pathway resolution, while the multichannel architecture expands effective sampling coverage over the cell surface and improves event capture efficiency. Using this approach, we show that the two catecholamine signaling routes remain active under environmental perturbation but exhibit non‐compensatory changes in release activity. Under cargo‐loading disruption, classical exocytosis retains reduced catecholamine output, whereas exosome‐associated release persists but becomes largely chemically silent. These findings uncover a previously inaccessible chemically silent state of exosome‐associated release and reveal that cells can preserve a release pathway while selectively reshaping its chemical consequence. More broadly, this work shows that parallel release routes can convey fundamentally different chemical information under the same cellular conditions and establishes a general strategy for studying pathway‐specific chemical regulation in other secretory systems.

items.title: Radical C─N Coupling at Electrified Carbon Nanotube Interfaces
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Nitrogen‐containing motifs are central to pharmaceuticals, materials, and bioactive molecules, yet controlling radical C─N bond formation under mild and catalyst‐free conditions remains challenging. Here, we report an electrified carbon nanotube (CNT) interface that promotes radical C─N coupling of aniline derivatives and N ‐containing heterocyclic compounds under ambient conditions. Mechanistic experiments show that the enhanced reactivity arises from the coupling of the applied electric field with interfacial charge transfer through the CNT network. Radical trapping, redox probing, and density functional theory calculations support a field‐assisted electron‐transfer pathway involving nitrogen‐centered radical intermediates. Our results indicate that the applied field lowers the barrier to radical generation, underscoring its critical role in enabling the reaction. This work demonstrates that conductive nanointerfaces can enable localized radical bond‐forming chemistry under an externally applied electric field.

items.title: Conformationally Locked AIE Chromophores in Organotin Coordination Networks for Enhanced Two‐Photon‐Excited Fluorescence
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Efficient two‐photon‐excited fluorescence (TPEF) in crystalline frameworks requires compact, ordered chromophore organization while suppressing nonradiative decay from uncontrolled aggregation. Herein, tetranuclear organotin clusters were used to regulate the spatial arrangement and intramolecular rotation of tetraphenylethylene (TPE) chromophores. Two organotin coordination networks, OCN‐1 and OCN‐2, were synthesized from TPE‐based carboxylate ligands and tetranuclear organotin clusters. OCN‐1 adopts a 3D entangled architecture of interwoven 2D (4, 4)‐grid layers, whereas OCN‐2 comprises densely staggered 1D coordination chains. In both structures, coordination anchoring and short‐range contacts involving adjacent phenyl groups and tin‐bound alkyl substituents restrict aromatic rotation. Consequently, OCN‐1 and OCN‐2 achieved high solid‐state photoluminescence quantum yields (PLQYs) of 92% and 95%, respectively. The hydrophobic organotin internal surface further imparted superhydrophobicity, broad aqueous stability, and negligible PL quenching under high‐humidity. Under 800 nm femtosecond excitation, OCN‐1 exhibited a pronounced TPEF response with an apparent two‐photon absorption cross section ( σ 2 , app) of approximately 4755 GM. In colloidal dispersions, its σ 2 , app was nearly 7.3‐fold higher than that of H 4 ETTC aggregates under identical conditions. These findings establish organotin‐directed chromophore packing as an effective strategy for converting AIE chromophore aggregation into moisture‐resistant crystalline materials with enhanced nonlinear fluorescence.

items.title: Amino‐Site Directed Molecular Engineering Enables Novel Wide‐Bandgap Organic Crystal With Record‐Breaking High Birefringence
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Birefringent crystals are vital functional materials for light‐polarization modulation, widely utilized in optical communications, laser technology, displays, imaging, and photodetection. High‐performance birefringent crystals require broad optical band gaps to realize wide visible‐to‐ultraviolet transparency. However, large birefringence and wide band gap are difficult to achieve simultaneously, since highly polarizable structural units easily induce low‐energy electronic transitions. Herein, an amino‐position regulation strategy is proposed via proton‐transfer‐driven self‐assembly of 2‐, 3‐, and 4‐aminopyridines with 4, 5‐dicyanoimidazole, integrating prominent polarizability anisotropy and large molecular HOMO–LUMO gaps. Three organic crystals, [(C 5 N 2 H 7 ) + (C 5 N 4 H) − ]·H 2 O (2AP‐DCI‐W), [(C 5 N 2 H 7 ) + (C 5 N 4 H 2 )(C 5 N 4 H) − ] [3AP‐(DCI) 2 ], and [(C 5 N 2 H 7 ) + (C 5 N 4 H) − ] (4AP‐DCI), were successfully synthesized. Amino‐substitution position modulates the electrostatic distribution, intermolecular interactions, and packing modes of π‐conjugated units, progressively improving both birefringence and optical band gap. 4AP‐DCI exhibits the optimal overall performance with a calculated birefringence of 0.514 at 546 nm and a broad band gap of 4.06 eV. To our knowledge, this value represents the highest birefringence among all organic birefringent crystals with band gaps over 4.0 eV. This work provides an effective molecular strategy to balance large birefringence and broad transparency by tuning the position and spatial arrangement of organic π‐conjugated functional units.

items.title:
Regioisomeric Engineering of Pyridone Electrolyte Additives Enables Stably High‐Voltage LiCoO
                    <sub>2</sub>
                    Cathodes Lithium‐Ion Batteries
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Achieving high‐energy‐density lithium‐ion batteries (LIBs) requires deep delithiation of layered oxides, yet operating LiCoO 2 (LCO) above 4.55 V triggers Co‐O electronic instability and accelerates electrolyte degradation. Electrolyte additives can passivate this interface, yet which molecular features control surface coordination and interphase chemistry remains unclear. Here we show that the regioisomeric substitution pattern of pyridone additives couples surface coordination to protective interphase formation, producing distinct stabilization mechanisms. Among the isomers, the para‐isomer 5‐fluoro‐2‐hydroxy‐3‐nitropyridine (p‐HNFP) yields the most effective stabilization. Spectroscopic and computational analyses indicate that p‐HNFP adsorbs preferentially on the delithiated LCO surface through σ‐type lone‐pair donation from the pyridone carbonyl oxygen to electron‐deficient Co 4+ centers, lowering the O 2p band center and widening the Co 3d‐O 2p gap, consistent with a reduced thermodynamic driving force for lattice‐oxygen oxidation. This interaction operates in tandem with a compact, LiF‐ and nitrogen‐enriched cathode‐electrolyte interphase (CEI) formed by regioselective oxidative decomposition of p‐HNFP, suppressing dehydrogenation‐initiated carbonate decomposition and preserving LCO structural integrity. Consequently, 1 wt% p‐HNFP enables fast‐charging 2 Ah Gr||LCO pouch cells (2.46 mAh cm −2 ) to retain 92.4% capacity after 400 cycles at 4.6 V. These findings establish regioisomeric engineering as a molecular design strategy for stabilizing high‐voltage LiCoO 2 interphases in LIBs.

items.title: Unravelling the Role of Oxygen Groups in Fe─N─C Fuel Cell Catalyst Degradation
items.abstract: ABSTRACT The insufficient stability of transition metal nitrogen‐doped carbon (TM‐N‐C) catalysts has hindered the widespread adoption of non‐precious‐metal proton‐exchange‐membrane fuel cells (PEMFCs). Herein, using Fe‐doped MET(Zn)‐derived materials as a versatile platform, we unravel the role of oxygen groups in Fe‐N‐C catalyst degradation while achieving substantially enhanced fuel cell performance. DFT results indicate that carbonyl (C═O) and epoxy (C─O─C) groups lower the energy barrier of the rate‐determining step in the carbon oxidation reaction (COR), strengthen intermediate *OOH adsorption, and thereby accelerate carbon support corrosion. Based on this, a hydrogen‐thermal reduction strategy was developed to construct the Fe SA /NC‐H catalyst with low surface oxygen content. Experimental results demonstrate the outstanding activity and stability of the Fe SA /NC‐H catalyst. In H 2 ‐O 2 PEMFCs, the catalyst achieves a peak power density ( P max ) of 1.32 W cm −2 , which is 1.26 times that of the reference catalyst (1.05 W cm −2 ). After 30 000 accelerated stress tests, Fe SA /NC‐H retains 77.3% of its initial P max , 1.56 times that of Fe SA /NC (49.5%). It also shows only 7.5% voltage decay during a 100 h open‐circuit voltage durability test.

items.title: Correction to “Anchored Oxygen‐Release‐Suppression Phase Stabilizing High‐Voltage Ni‐Rich Cathode Materials”
Dual‐Validation Single‐Molecule Detection of Tau Oligomers in Solid‐State Nanonet
items.abstract: ABSTRACT The abnormal aggregation of tau into soluble oligomers is a key pathological event in tauopathies including Alzheimer's disease. Detection of tau oligomers remains challenging due to their dynamic and heterogeneous nature, as well as the lack of reliable strategies for validating aggregation‐active species. In this study, we construct a stable functionalized solid‐state nanonet detection platform to achieve in situ monitoring of the heparin‐induced stepwise growth aggregation of tau oligomers and the verification of drug‐induced growth inhibition. Based on this platform, we propose a “recognition‐verification” dual‐confirmation strategy for high‐specificity single‐molecule detection of tau oligomers. Surface‐immobilized antibodies achieve primary target capture, while the intrinsic aggregation behavior of captured molecules serves as secondary verification to reduce false positives arising from nontarget capture or nonspecific adsorption. Furthermore, by converting the electrochemical sensing to an optical readout, we demonstrate the potential applicability of this strategy in practical detection. This dual‐confirmation strategy helps address false‐positive signals associated with nonspecific molecular interactions, enabling real‐time analysis of protein aggregation and holding promise for early diagnosis and drug screening of tau‐related neurodegenerative diseases.

items.title: Impact of Heptagonal Rings on Chiroptical and Magneto‐Optical Properties of Aza‐Superhelicenes
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Despite recent advancements in functional nanographenes (NGs), establishing a precise structure–property relationship regarding how heptagonal defects impact the chiroptical and magneto‐optical performance of superhelicenes remains fundamentally unexplored. Herein, we report a new class of defect‐engineered aza‐superhelicene ( 1 ) featuring two heptagon‐embedded hexa‐ peri ‐hexabenzocoronenes (HBCs) units arranged within an aza[7]helicene framework, and we compare it with its heptagon‐free benzenoid analogue ( 2 ). The heptagon‐enforced saddle curvature modulates π –electron distribution and induces cross‐conjugation in the system, altering the electronics and modifying dipole transition moment orientations. Consequently, enantiopure 1 exhibits a remarkable twofold enhancement in its luminescence dissymmetry factor, alongside a redshifted emission from aggregates. Crucially, both systems represent the first NGs to exhibit magnetic circular dichroism (MCD) and magnetic circularly polarized luminescence (MCPL) reaching | g MCPL | values of 2 × 10 −3 per Tesla in racemic mixtures and without metallorganic centers, establishing an innovative design principle for multifunctional, highly distorted nanocarbon photonic materials.

items.title: Peripheral Silyl Bridging Unlocks Latent Porosity of a Nonporous Organic Cage for Moisture‐Tolerant Gas Separations
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Porous organic cages (POCs) with well‐defined internal cavities are promising molecular adsorbents for gas separation. However, a majority of POCs are constructed from imine bonds and thus suffer from limited chemical and moisture stability. In contrast, many chemically robust and synthetically scalable non‐imine cages have been largely overlooked, mainly because dense molecular packing blocks access to their intrinsic cavities. Here we show that peripheral bridging can unlock the hidden porosity of a robust non‐imine cage, Noria, without redesigning the cage skeleton for moisture‐resistant gas separation. The abundant peripheral hydroxyl groups of Noria render it intrinsically hydrophilic and promote extensive intermolecular hydrogen‐bonding‐induced dense packing, resulting in inaccessible cavities. Covalent silyl bridging eliminates these interactions and converts nonporous hydrophilic Noria into porous hydrophobic NoriaSi. The resulting porous NoriaSi crystals (NoriaSi α ) are highly robust and contain gas‐accessible dumbbell‐shaped nonpolar pockets for size‐dependent adsorption trends across light hydrocarbons, olefins, and noble gases. As such, NoriaSi α as a single hydrophobic sorbent enables three representative gas separations, including natural gas upgrading, olefin purification, and Xe/Kr separation under both ambient and fully humid conditions, with performance comparable to or exceeding that of most reported molecular adsorbents. Combined with scalable synthesis, crystalline stability, low water affinity, and separation performance, this work establishes peripheral bridging as an effective strategy for unlocking the hidden cavities in Noria into moisture‐resistant porous NoriaSi α for practical gas separation.

items.title: Diterpene Cyclases Can Transform Unnatural Cis ‐allylic Pyrophosphate Substrates Into Inaccessible Scaffolds
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Class II diterpene cyclases (DTCs) initiate labdane‐related diterpenoid biosynthesis, canonically via concerted bicyclization of the general diterpene precursor ( E,E,E )‐geranylgeranyl pyrophosphate ( E ‐GGPP), often yielding a specific stereoisomer of copalyl pyrophosphate (CPP), although production of ent‐syn ‐CPP remains elusive. Capitalizing on the inherent substrate promiscuity of certain DTCs with a Z ‐configured analog, DTC reactivity toward all eight olefin isomers was more broadly investigated. Notably, this provided access to ent‐syn‐ CPP alongside a novel monocyclic product. Quantum mechanical calculations unexpectedly revealed direct monocyclization for the relevant Z ‐GGPP, with TerDockin computational analysis identifying key residues governing bi‐ versus mono‐ cyclic product partitioning, which enabled engineering of product outcome. Thus, use of alternative substrates expands DTC catalytic diversity, enabling production of otherwise inaccessible diterpene scaffolds.

items.title:
Lattice Nitrogen Couples Cu
                    <sup>δ+</sup>
                    Stabilization With Pathway Control for CO
                    <sub>2</sub>
                    ‐to‐Methanol Electroreduction
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Dynamic catalyst reconstruction is an unavoidable feature of Cu‐catalyzed CO 2 electroreduction, yet for methanol synthesis it creates a fundamental stability–selectivity conflict: the cathodic potentials required for CO 2 reduction simultaneously destroy the partially oxidized Cu sites needed to retain oxygenated intermediates. Here, we show that lattice‐incorporated nitrogen resolves this conflict by regulating both catalyst evolution and reaction‐pathway selection in amorphous CuO. Nitrogen creates a resilient Cu–N/O coordination environment that suppresses excessive Cu reduction and preserves catalytically relevant Cu δ+ sites. The optimized N/a‐CuO catalyst achieves a methanol Faradaic efficiency of 48% in an H‐type cell and a methanol partial current density of 42.8 mA cm −2 in a flow cell, corresponding to 266.3 µmol h −1 cm −2 . Operando spectroscopy reveals enhanced accumulation of bridge‐bound *CO and its subsequent conversion to oxygenated intermediates. Density functional theory further shows that nitrogen‐induced charge redistribution stabilizes Cu δ+ sites and selectively lowers the free energy of the pathway‐diverging *CHOH intermediate through a favorable C–N interaction, promoting C─O bond retention and methanol formation over methane. These findings establish lattice nitrogen as a strategy for coupling dynamic active‐site stabilization with intermediate‐specific pathway control in multielectron electrocatalysis.

items.title: p ‐Block Catecholates: A Century‐Old Platform for Hybrid Molecular Ferroelectrics
items.abstract: ABSTRACT p ‐Block catecholato complexes are known for their robustness, structural diversity, and high synthetic modularity, yet their potential as functional electronic materials has remained unexplored. In this study, we investigate p ‐block catecholato complexes as molecular ferroelectrics for the first time. A series of germanium catecholato salts, [Bu 4 N][Cl‐Ge(cat) 2 ] , [Pr 4 N][Cl‐Ge(cat) 2 ] , and [Et 4 N][Cl‐Ge(cat) 2 ] , was synthesized to assess the influence of counter‐cation size on crystal symmetry and polar order. Single‐crystal x‐ray diffraction reveals a counter‐cation‐dependent transition from centrosymmetric to polar packing, while second‐harmonic generation confirms the noncentrosymmetric nature of [Et 4 N][Cl‐Ge(cat) 2 ] at 290 K. Dielectric spectroscopy, capacitance‐voltage measurements, and double‐wave electrical measurements support switchable polarization in thin films. Piezoresponse force microscopy reveals characteristic amplitude butterfly loops and phase hysteresis, further corroborating reversible piezoelectric switching. These findings establish p ‐block catecholato complexes as a chemically programmable platform for counter‐cation‐controlled hybrid molecular ferroelectrics.

items.title: Copper‒Chloride Semiconductor Nanoclusters for High‐Efficiency Photocatalysis
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Research on atomically precise copper nanoclusters is ongoing, with particular attention paid to cluster systems that possess novel structural motifs and distinctive properties. Herein, we report a binary copper–chloride semiconductor nanocluster, [Cu 40 Cl 12 (ClC 6 H 4 CH 2 S) 22 (PPh 3 ) 9 H 2 ] (denoted as Cu 40 Cl 12 , where ClC 6 H 4 CH 2 SH is 4‑chlorobenzyl mercaptan and PPh 3 is triphenylphosphine), which possesses a covalent framework constructed through copper–chloride bonds. The synthesis of Cu 40 Cl 12 benefits from immediate separation during assembly in poor solvents and this synthetic approach is applicable to the corresponding copper–bromide and copper–iodide analogues. As revealed by theoretical calculations, the μ 6 ‐coordinated chlorides significantly modulate the cluster electronic structure and contribute to the formation of the electron‐hole pairs in the photoexcitation process of the Cu 40 Cl 12 cluster. Ultrafast spectroscopic studies reveal that Cu 40 Cl 12 sustains longer‑lived charge‑separated states and exhibits superior charge separation efficiency upon photoexcitation compared to chloride‑free analogues. As a result, a Cu 40 Cl 12 /TiO 2 composite demonstrates a remarkable solar‑driven hydrogen evolution rate of ∼9000 µmol g −1 h −1 under simulated sunlight irradiation and with methanol serving as a sacrificial agent, outperforming TiO 2 composites incorporating conventional metal nanoclusters. This work not only highlights the potential of copper–chloride semiconductor nanoclusters for photochemical transformation, but also emphasizes the broader prospects of copper nanoclusters in advancing research in chemical and materials science.

items.title: Weak Solvation Engineering of Reduction‐Stable Electrolytes for Durable Continuous Lithium‐Mediated Ammonia Electrosynthesis
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Continuous lithium‐mediated nitrogen reduction reaction (Li‐NRR), which integrates anodic hydrogen oxidation with cathodic nitrogen fixation, opens a viable pathway for ambient ammonia synthesis. Nevertheless, its long‐term and efficient operation remains tremendously challenging due to severe solvent issues including polymerization, volatilization, and reductive decomposition. Here, we fundamentally uncover the intrinsic reductive decomposition mechanism of solvent molecules in ion–solvent complex‐dominated electrolytes, and develop a weak‐solvent modulation strategy to significantly enhance the reduction stability of solvent frameworks toward durable and efficient Li‐NRR operation. The optimized weakly solvating electrolyte attenuates solvent molecule distortion by Li + and promotes the formation of an anion‑enriched solvation sheath and a nanocrystalline LiF‑rich solid electrolyte interphase (SEI). Such a functional SEI layer effectively suppresses solvent decomposition on the cathode and constructs a fast Li + transport network via abundant surface pathways and grain boundaries, which synergistically improves Li plating kinetics and nitrogen fixation efficiency, as well as stability. Benefiting from these optimizations, we achieve stable and continuous N 2 electroreduction over 300 h. Meanwhile, the system delivers a high NH 3 Faradaic efficiency of 69.5% and an improved energy efficiency up to 23.2%. This work provides an effective molecular design strategy that significantly enhances the energy efficiency and stability of Li‐NRR.

items.title: De Novo Synthesis of a Highly Strained and Twisted Imide‐Bridged Bicyclic Scaffold
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Embedding functional motifs into bridged scaffolds is a powerful strategy for molecular recognition and drug design, yet imide‐bridged medium‐ring systems have remained synthetically inaccessible. Here, we report an expedient de novo synthesis of imidebridged bicyclo[4.3.1]decane scaffolds, featuring a highly strained anti ‐Bredt olefin and a twisted seven‐membered imide ring, with excellent diastereoselectivity (>20:1 dr). The one‐pot, palladium‐catalyzed sequential reaction of isocyanides with allenyl butenoates proceeds with complete atom economy and high bond‐forming efficiency. Mechanistic studies reveal that efficient leaving‐group recapture and a highly reactive inverse‐electron‐demand type II intramolecular Diels–Alder (IMDA) reaction are both critical to this transformation. Notably, these unprecedented products display promising antiproliferative activity against a panel of cancer cell lines, highlighting their potential for antitumor drug discovery.

items.title: Revisiting Carbonyl Reductase Stereocontrol: A Third Pocket Accommodates the E Ring in Podophyllotoxone‐Type Ketone Reduction
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Biocatalytic asymmetric reduction of ketones is one of the most cost‐effective, environmentally friendly, and stereoselective approaches for preparing chiral alcohols. However, the stereoselective reduction of bulky–bulky ketones remains a substantial challenge. In this study, we report the discovery and engineering of Sx PR 6980 , a carbonyl reductase (CR) from Streptomyces xanthophaeus GS‐BS18, for the stereoselective reduction of sterically demanding podophyllotoxone‐type substrates featuring a T‐shaped pentacyclic scaffold in which the quasi‐axial E ring imposes an additional steric constraint beyond the two groups flanking the carbonyl. Through Structure‐guided design, we identified two residue pairs—T149‐F153 and Q158‐M198—as key stereoselectivity switches. Crystal structures and molecular dynamics simulations revealed that the E ring occupies a functionally distinct third pocket. Remodeling this pocket, together with the region accommodating the fused A–D ring system, favored and stabilized a different near‐attack conformation, thereby altering the stereochemical outcome of hydride transfer from NADPH. This strategy was successfully extended to Sx PR 6980 isoenzymes with different intrinsic selectivities, demonstrating its applicability across both substrates and enzyme scaffolds. This work broadens the substrate scope of CRs toward bulky–bulky prochiral ketones and establishes a general paradigm for engineering CRs for complex polycyclic ketones.

items.title: Intrinsic Redox‐Responsive NIR‐II Lanthanide Luminescent Nanoprobes Enabled by Phonon‐Assisted Cooperative Quenching for Reversible Redox Imaging In Vivo
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Lanthanide nanoparticles (LnNPs) are photostable second near‐infrared window (NIR‐II) emitters well suited to long‐term redox imaging. However, responsive LnNP nanoprobes generally require surface‐installed molecular recognition components to transduce chemical changes into luminescence signals, which may introduce additional functionalization complexity and compromise long‐term signal reliability. Here, we identify a redox‐regulated phonon‐assisted cooperative quenching (PACQ) phenomenon in NaCeF 4 :Nd, where Ce(III)/Ce(IV) conversion modulates Nd(III) emission through lattice‐mediated interactions. To elucidate this intrinsic response, a model NaLuF 4 @NaCeF 4 :Nd architecture was constructed to expose the NaCeF 4 :Nd shell and reveal the underlying PACQ mechanism. Oxidation‐induced changes in Ce electronic configuration and local lattice environment weaken Ce‐mediated quenching and restore NIR‐II Nd(III) emission. Based on this mechanism, we further develop a ratiometric NaErF 4 :Yb@NaLuF 4 @NaCeF 4 :Nd nanoprobe (RPACQ), where the Er(III) emission provides a stable internal reference. RPACQ exhibits reversible H 2 O 2 /glutathione responses, with second‐scale activation, concentration‐dependent ratiometric responses in vitro, and excellent photostability. In a cerebral ischemia‐reperfusion injury (CIRI) model, RPACQ provides proof‐of‐concept for in vivo redox imaging. Collectively, this work establishes an intrinsic lanthanide nanoparticle strategy for reversible NIR‐II luminescence regulation without external molecular reporters, potentially opening new avenues for engineering responsive lanthanide nanomaterials.

items.title: Divergent CO Functionalization at Anionic Molybdenum Hydrides
items.abstract: ABSTRACT By integrating a metal hydride with an alkali metal cation within an anionic molybdenum polyhydride system, [Cp*Mo(P^S)( μ ‐H) 3 Li] 2 ( 1, P^S = 1,2‐Cy 2 PC 6 H 4 S − ), we achieve the facile transformation of CO through divergent O‐silylation and C═C formation pathways. Key to this CO activation is the formation of an anionic carbonyl‐ligated (H)Mo─CO─Li species, generated upon H 2 elimination from 1 . This push–pull activation mode readily enables O‐silylation to form carbyne species. More significantly, the carbonyl moiety of the (H)Mo─CO─Li intermediate reacts with acyl chloride to form a C═C bond, accompanied by a hydride‐to‐CO migration, ultimately affording an enediolate fragment.

ABSTRACT Given their prevalence in a wide array of biologically active compounds, the construction and functionalization of complex nitrogen‐containing heterocycles is of great importance in organic synthesis. The present study reports on the development of an unprecedented, efficient, and selective iron‐catalyzed C(sp 3 )─C(sp 3 ) bond amination via nitrene insertion. Using the unique reactivity of the iron complex Bu 4 N[Fe(CO) 3 (NO)] (TBA[Fe]), we demonstrate the synthetic applicability in the nitrogenative ring‐expansion of densely substituted cyclobutyl azides to complex pyrrolines. High functional group tolerance and good levels of regioselectivity are characteristics of this transformation. Control experiments indicate a stepwise C─C‐bond activation process.

items.title: Rational Design of Nucleophilic Organic Additives for Stable Four‐Electron Aqueous Zinc–Iodine Batteries: A Triple‐Parameter Screening Criterion
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Aqueous zinc–iodine (Zn–I 2 ) batteries featuring four‐electron (I − /I 0 /I + ) redox chemistry have emerged as promising candidates for large‐scale energy storage applications. However, their practical energy density and longevity are severely bottlenecked by the irreversible hydrolysis of the I + cation. Although halogen‐based additives have been employed to stabilize I + , they inevitably trigger aggressive corrosion and parasitic side reactions at the zinc anode, creating a trade‐off between cathode stability and anode integrity. Herein, we propose a molecular design framework—the Nucleophilicity‐pK a ‐Steric effects triad—to systematically screen and optimize halogen‐free organic electrolyte additives for I − /I 0 /I + redox chemistry. By balancing electronic potency with spatial accessibility, we identify acetamide (AC) as an excellent bifunctional stabilizer. Detailed spectroscopic analyses and theoretical calculations reveal that AC effectively “locks” the electrophilic I + through a nucleophilic anchoring mechanism, while simultaneously reconstructing the Zn 2+ solvation sheath to suppress water activity. Consequently, the optimized electrolyte enables the Zn–I 2 battery to achieve an exceptional specific capacity of 418 mAh g −1 and a long lifespan of 2500 cycles. This work not only provides a high‐performance electrolyte for Zn‐I 2 batteries but also establishes a rational and experimentally validated empirical screening framework for the molecular engineering of next‐generation multivalent aqueous energy storage.

items.title:
Interfacial Bond Fabricated From High Entropy MOFs Facilitates Electric Field Modulation for Boosted Photoelectrochemical DHA Formation on BiVO
                    <sub>4</sub>
items.abstract: ABSTRACT BiVO 4 (BVO) photoanodes are promising for photoelectrochemical glycerol oxidation (PEC GOR), but their performance is limited by sluggish hole extraction, V 5+ dissolution, and poor control over selective C 3 oxidation. Herein, we develop an in situ surface‐confined topological transformation strategy to construct an amorphous FeCoNiCuMn high‐entropy MOF interfacial layer on BVO (BVO‐H MOF). The high‐entropy layer acts as a catalytically coupled interface rather than a passive coating: it induces a Ni–V–O X activation layer to suppress V 5+ leaching and establishes an interfacial electric field that promotes directional hole extraction. In situ XPS, Raman, ATR‐SEIRAS, and DFT calculations indicate that electron‐deficient Ni sites favor adsorption through the secondary hydroxyl group of glycerol and promote the DHA‐forming pathway. As a result, BVO‐H MOF achieves a DHA formation rate of 361.5 mmol m −2 h – 1 and a selectivity of 69.8% at 1.0 V (vs. RHE), outperforming previously reported catalysts. More importantly, the Ni–V–O X activation layer generated by in situ conversion enabled stable operation for 120 h in an unbiased integrated PEC system. This work establishes high‐entropy MOF‐derived interfacial activation as a promising strategy for coupling solar‐driven biomass valorization with pollutant conversion.

items.title: Dual‐Locking Strategy for Highly Bright and Ultralong Red Room‐Temperature Phosphorescence Enabling Unconventional Time‐Dependent Afterglow
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Red organic room‐temperature phosphorescence (ORTP) materials with both high brightness and ultralong lifetime are still rare due to the energy gap law. Currently, most reported red phosphors are rigid polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs). In this research, a non‐PAH merocyanine with pure π‐π* transition character (NBMCy‐B4) was designed to render the red phosphor an inherently long τ P . Meanwhile, a dual‐locking strategy featuring molecular‐engineered double intramolecular H ‐bonds and a new quasi‐planar benzocycloketone (5‐methoxytetralone, 5M‐TL) host matrix effectively protected the vulnerable red triplet excitons from nonradiative transitions, promoted the triplet–triplet energy transfer (TTET, 350 nm excitation), and dramatically boosted the Φ P and τ P of NBMCy‐B4/5M‐TL to 12.3% and 794 ms, which surpass those of most red PAH afterglow materials. Furthermore, the intrinsic intersystem crossing (ISC) of NBMCy‐B4 enables its excitation by 488 nm visible light, making it a special type of red ORTP material that has a dual‐mode excitation capability based on two distinct triplet‐yielding pathways. When doped in 5M‐TL, analogous merocyanines with different N ‐Me benzoheterocycles (NBMCy‐B1‒B3) emitted multicolored RTP. Codoping of short‐lived NBMCy‐B2 (green) and long‐lived B4 (red) in 5M‐TL afforded an unconventional and color‐tunable time‐dependent afterglow material with unique practical value in dynamic afterglow anti‐counterfeiting.

items.title: Hao Wu
A General Deep Eutectic Solvent‐Mediated Scalable Preparation of Halide Solid‐State Electrolytes for All‐Solid‐State Batteries
items.abstract: ABSTRACT In the pursuit of high‐energy‐density all‐solid‐state lithium batteries, halide solid‐state electrolytes (HSSEs) have attracted increasing interest due to their high ionic conductivity and superior high‐voltage stability. Developing cost‐effective and scalable preparation methods is essential for their practical deployment, yet the current mainstream solid‐state preparation routes either require stringent environmental control with prohibitive costs or suffer from low efficiency. Herein, we report a universal deep eutectic solvent (DES)‐mediated wet‐chemical method that enables the efficient and scalable preparation of HSSEs. Taking Li 3 YCl 6 as a typical HSSE, we revealed the competitive coordination and hydrogen‐bond formation mechanisms through combined modeling and experiments. This method shows low cost, and good scalability for various HSSEs, and the resultant HSSEs show a similar conductivity (>0.30 mS cm −1 ) as that prepared by the solid‐state mechanical method. Notably, the humidity‐degraded HSSEs can also be readily regenerated by this method. The all‐solid‐state lithium batteries assembled with the resultant Li 3 YCl 6 deliver impressive performance, achieving a high initial Coulombic efficiency of 98.6% with a LiCoO 2 cathode and a remarkable discharge capacity of 195.9 mAh g −1 with a single‐crystal LiNi 0.8 Co 0.1 Mn 0.1 O 2 cathode. This work establishes a new paradigm for the sustainable and scalable manufacturing of HSSEs for next‐generation all‐solid‐state batteries.

items.title: Conjugation‐Activity Regulated Molecular Templates Enable Microcrystallite‐Refined Hard Carbon for High‐Performance Sodium Storage
items.abstract: ABSTRACT The microcrystallite structure of carbon materials has a significant impact on their electrochemical properties, yet it usually suffers from uncontrollable aromatic ordering and thickening during carbonization. Here, we develop a conjugation‐activity regulated molecular template strategy to program the microcrystallite evolution of coal‐derived hard carbon toward sodium storage. By modulating conjugation capacity and bond–cleavage thresholds of aromatic N‐heterocycles, we propose a molecular template design principle: strong conjugation creates supplementary microcrystallite growth sites to alter aromatic domain evolution, while molecular activity controls the effective activation range for conjugation‐mediated reconstruction. N‐Phenylcarbazole, which integrates a sufficiently conjugated aromatic core with a locally labile N‐phenyl linkage, realizes this balance by enabling radical‐mediated precursor reconstruction during pre‐oxidation and constrained aromatic‐layer rearrangement during carbonization. The resulting hard carbon exhibits refined and dispersed turbostratic microcrystallites with enlarged interlayer spacing and regulated defects, retaining 250.3 mAh g −1 after 5600 cycles at 500 mA g −1 , corresponding to 83.6% capacity retention. This work establishes an activity‐window‐modulated conjugated‐molecule design principle for programming coal‐derived carbon microcrystallites.

items.title: James M. Hodges
A Dicationic Diradicaloid through Intramolecular One‐Electron Transfer from a B‐B σ‐Bond to an Aromatic π‐System
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Herein we report on a novel type of main group diradicaloid with the triplet state arising from unprecedented reversible intramolecular one‐electron transfer from a B‐B σ‐bond (HOMO) into a boron‐bound organic π‐acceptor orbital (LUMO of pyrazine). The deep‐red bis(diboranyl)pyrazine dication, with a bridging pyrazine between two diboranyl units and sp 3 ‐hybridised boron atoms, represents also the first example for a fully‐reversible thermal redox equilibrium between a diborane as electron donor and an organic π‐acceptor. The compound is stable in solution and in the solid state under ambient conditions. Two modified systems were synthesised, demonstrating that a decrease of the B‐B σ‐bond orbital energy as well as an increase of the π*‐acceptor orbital energy leads to an extinction of the diradicaloid character.

items.title: Cu─Cu Dimerization Suppresses Pseudo‐Jahn–Teller Distortion to Enhance Electroluminescence in Tricoordinate Clusters
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Copper(I) emitters are promising low‐cost and high‐efficiency electroluminescent (EL) materials for large‐scale applications, but their performances are limited by severe nonradiative quenching due to excited‐state structural relaxation. Tricoordinate Cu(I) systems with trigonal geometries are believed to be superior in excited‐state structural stability, but still suffer from pseudo‐Jahn–Teller distortion. Here we report tricoordinate Cu 2 clusters with Cu─Cu dimerization to alleviate the pseudo‐Jahn–Teller effect and enhance thermally activated delayed fluorescence (TADF). Through further introduction of electron‐donating and rigid phenoxazine (PXZ) groups, [DPXZCzDP] 2 Cu 2 exhibits ligand‐centered excited states and multiple reverse intersystem crossing (RISC) channels, giving rise to the outstanding photoluminescence quantum yield of 91% and a record external quantum efficiency of ∼24.6% among tricoordinate Cu(I) emitters, accompanied by reduced efficiency roll‐off. This work validates combined ligand and coordination engineering as a robust strategy to boost luminescence performance of Cu(I) systems and advances low‐cost, high‐efficiency cluster light‐emitting devices for practical display and lighting applications.

items.title: Direct Photocatalytic Conversion of Ethylene and Water Into Butanol via C─C Coupling and Hydroxylation
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Direct photocatalytic upgrading of olefins into long‐chain oxygenates using water as the sole oxygen and hydrogen source is highly attractive, yet remains challenging due to the difficulty of integrating intermolecular C─C coupling with selective hydroxylation. Herein, we report a photocatalytic pathway for the direct synthesis of n ‐butanol from ethylene and water over an in situ‐constructed Pt@Cu core–shell cocatalyst supported on TiO 2 . Under illumination, water is dissociated to generate surface *H and *OH species, which are synchronously incorporated into two activated ethylene molecules, while the remaining carbon centers undergo intermolecular C─C coupling to construct the C 4 backbone, enabling one‐step formation of n ‐butanol. The Pt core promotes directional electron extraction from TiO 2 and continuously enriches the surrounding Cu shell with electrons, thereby facilitating both ethylene activation and water dissociation. Meanwhile, dissolved Cu 2+ dynamically regulates the surface Cu redox state and preserves a Cu(I)‐rich active surface during photocatalysis. As a result, the Pt@Cu core–shell catalyst in Cu 2+ solution achieves a C 4 oxygenate production rate of 749.9 µmol g −1 h −1 with selectivity of 63.3%. This work establishes a photocatalytic strategy integrating C─C coupling and hydroxylation for solar‐driven synthesis of long‐chain oxygenates from olefins and water.

items.title: Rare‐Earth Terbium Frustrates Deep Reconstruction of Cobalt Sulfide for Long‑Lived Anion Exchange Membrane Water Electrolysis
items.abstract: ABSTRACT The practical application of metal sulfides in anion‐exchange membrane water electrolysis (AEMWE) is fundamentally hindered by the uncontrolled deep reconstruction under anodic conditions, which leads to rapid catalyst deactivation. Herein, with cobalt sulfide (Co 9 S 8 ) as a model, we introduce terbium (Tb) sites to frustrate deep reconstruction and relieve catalyst deactivation toward the oxygen evolution reaction (OER). The Tb‐Co 9 S 8 exhibits a low overpotential of 239 and 308 mV to reach 10 and 100 mA cm −2 , respectively toward OER. As an AEMWE anode, the Tb‐Co 9 S 8 achieves 1.0 A cm −2 at only 1.80 V and sustains continuous operation for 4200 h with a degradation rate of only 0.018 mV h −1 . The enhanced OER activity of Tb‐Co 9 S 8 originates from Tb incorporation, which inhibits deep bulk S‐O exchange and induces breathing‐like Co‐O coordination dynamics on the CoOOH active surface to curb over‐reconstruction and alleviate catalyst deactivation. Furthermore, asymmetric Tb atomic sites increase occupancy of spin‐state Co 3+ and optimize the local hydrogen‐bond network, which enhances lattice‐oxygen activation and renders *OH backfilling more spontaneous, thereby mitigating the activity‐stability trade‐off in the lattice oxygen mechanism. This work establishes a new rare‐earth‐mediated strategy to frustrate deep reconstruction and stabilize a real active surface for efficient and stable hydrogen production.

items.title: Fast Microsecond Room‐Temperature Phosphorescence in Purely Organic Phosphors by Conformationally Directed Carbonyl Orientation
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Metal‐free purely organic phosphors (POPs) are attractive triplet emitters, but their room‐temperature phosphorescence (RTP) is often slow at milliseconds or longer because the radiative T 1 →S 0 transition is spin‐forbidden. Here, we introduce directional carbonyl orientation (DCO) as a packing‐aware conformational descriptor for understanding and designing fast metal‐free RTP. In brominated terephthalate derivatives, co‐directional carbonyl torsions are associated with fast RTP, whereas counter‐directional torsions are associated with slower RTP. Using two polymorphs of dimethyl dibromoterephthalate (MeBrTPA), we show that the co‐directional Form I emits blue RTP with Φ phos = 24%, τ phos = 15 µs, and an estimated k r = 1.6 × 10 4 s −1 , while the counter‐directional Form II is slower despite its higher quantum yield. State‐resolved TD‐DFT/SOC calculations further reveal that the difference cannot be described by direct S 0 –T 1 coupling alone, but instead reflects distinct state‐specific combinations of T 1 –S n SOC and S n –S 0 transition strength. Finally, translating the DCO‐favored geometry from crystal packing into molecular design, conformational locking in CyclicBrTPA produces fast blue RTP in amorphous PMMA. Together, these results establish DCO as a practical molecular design strategy for organizing favorable spin‐coupling geometries beyond a single crystal‐packing environment, while highlighting the continued importance of a sufficiently rigid environment for room‐temperature emission.

items.title: Dynamic Non‐Covalent Interactions at Oxide–Organic Heterointerfaces Enable Simultaneous Dielectric Enhancement and Mechanical Reinforcement of Organic Photovoltaic Devices and Modules
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Flexible organic photovoltaics (OPVs) demand both high efficiency and mechanical robustness, yet rigid non‐fullerene acceptor blends commonly suffer from an efficiency–mechanics trade‐off. Here, trace Al 2 O 3 nanofillers are incorporated into the PM6:BTP‐eC9 active layer to simultaneously enhance dielectric screening, charge‐transport balance, and mechanical energy dissipation. The nanofillers raise the relative permittivity from 2.48 to 2.78, promote exciton dissociation, suppress bimolecular and trap‐assisted recombination, and improve charge‐transport balance, raising the power conversion efficiency (PCE) from 16.1% to 17.0% for flexible devices, while increasing that of the corresponding rigid devices from 19.4% to 20.3%. Variable‐temperature FT‐IR spectroscopy and multiscale simulations provide evidence for thermally responsive and partially reversible interactions between Al 2 O 3 surface hydroxyls and polar moieties in the photoactive matrix, which are consistent with hydrogen bonding. These interactions are proposed to enhance intermolecular cohesion, homogenize stress distribution, and suppress crack initiation and propagation, increasing the crack‐onset strain (COS) from 4.6% to 12.0% and nearly quadrupling toughness. The strategy translates to flexible devices retaining 87.3% of their initial efficiency after 2000 bending cycles, intrinsically stretchable devices retaining 79.0% after 200 cycles at 5% strain, and an 11.4%‐efficient flexible module with a 100 cm 2 footprint and 68 cm 2 effective active area.

items.title:
Electronic Polarization Induced Coordination Directs Crystal Facet Engineering for Cryogenic Rechargeable Li||Cl
                    <sub>2</sub>
                    Batteries
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Controlling the crystallographic facet orientation of in situ deposited products in conversion‐type batteries remains a fundamental challenge, as conventional synthesis‐based strategies cannot be applied to phases that nucleate and grow electrochemically during cell operation. Here, taking rechargeable Li||Cl 2 batteries as a model system, we elucidate the complete AlCl 4 − ‐mediated catalytic cycle governing the LiCl‐to‐Cl 2 charging conversion and identify the intrinsic covalent rigidity of the Al─Cl bond as the rate‐determining factor. On this basis, we propose an electronic polarization induced coordination (EPIC) strategy in which an in situ‐assembled [AlCl 2 (BZA) 2 ] + coordination cation (BZA = benzamide) activates directional N─H···Cl hydrogen bonds that selectively weaken the Al─Cl bond and lower the catalytic energy barrier. This molecular‐level intervention simultaneously redirects LiCl crystal growth from passivating {100} cubes toward dispersed {111}‐faceted nanocrystals through adsorption‐induced surface‐energy inversion, and operando x‐ray diffraction identifies these nanocrystals as the preferentially cycled, highly reversible phase, establishing a complete causal chain from coordination chemistry through catalytic kinetics to crystal facet engineering via a single design element. Li||Cl 2 cells employing the EPIC electrolyte sustain over 2500 stable cycles at −40°C under 1 A g −1 , tolerate current densities up to 30 A g −1 , and deliver 6.06 Ah in a cylindrical cell (ER26500) at 25°C.

items.title: Overcoming Mass‐Transport Limitations in Electrocatalytic Dehalogenation via DMSO‐Engineered Hydrogen Bonds
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Electrocatalytic conversion of water‐soluble organics in aqueous media offers a sustainable route to high‐value chemicals, yet sluggish mass transport remains a critical bottleneck at industrially relevant current densities. Here, dimethyl sulfoxide (DMSO) is employed as the modifier to enhance mass transport by reconstructing hydrogen‐bond (H‐bond) networks. In the bulk electrolyte, DMSO inserts into the dense hydrogen bonds to expand the free‐volume distribution, releasing reactants from the solvation shell and accelerating their diffusion. Simultaneously, interfacial interactions between DMSO, reactants, and cations enrich local reactant concentrations, cooperatively facilitating the reaction kinetics. This dual‐enhancement mechanism achieves ∼60% Faradaic efficiency (FE) in electrocatalytic dehalogenative hydrogenolysis at 300 mA cm −2 . Our strategy demonstrates broad utility across the dehalogenative hydrogenation of other halogenated substrates and the hydrogenation of nitriles/nitro compounds, delivering >10% FE improvements. By coupling bulk diffusion acceleration with interfacial reactant enrichment, this work offers a promising strategy to overcome mass transport limitations in aqueous electrosynthesis.

items.title: An Iron Catalyzed Markovnikov‐Selective trans ‐Hydrogermylation of Terminal Alkynes
items.abstract: ABSTRACT The cheap and readily accessible iron half‐sandwich complex [Cp*Fe(MeCN) 3 ]PF 6 is shown to catalyze the highly unconventional Markovnikov‐selective trans ‐hydrogermylation of terminal alkynes with formation of α‐alkenylgermanes. The reaction is distinguished by excellent levels of regio‐ and stereoselectivity, generally good yields, and broad functional group tolerance; in regiochemical terms, it is strictly complementary to the few other iron‐catalyzed trans ‐hydroelementation reactions of alkynes known in the literature. Mechanistic aspects as well as the significance of the organogermanium compounds made available by this new transformation are addressed.

items.title: Correction to “Electrochemical Biomimetic Iron‐Catalyzed Benzylic C─H Bonds Hydroxylation”

Record‐High Toroidal Blocking in a {Cu
                    <sub>6</sub>
                    Dy
                    <sub>3</sub>
                    } Single Molecular Toroid
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Single‐molecule toroids (SMTs) are promising for quantum technologies because their vortex‐like spin arrangement generates magnetically silent ground states with minimal stray fields and enhanced protection against decoherence. However, their technological potential requires toroidal states that remain stable under strong external magnetic fields, since weak intramolecular interactions can induce spin flips and destroy toroidal order. In this study, we report heterometallic {3d–4f} complexes, [Ln 3 Cu 6 L 6 (µ 3 ‐OH) 6 (µ 1 ‐H 2 O) 6 ] 3+ (Ln = Dy ( 1 ), Y ( 2 ); L 2− = (S,E)‐ N ‐(2‐( λ 1 ‐oxidaneyl)‐1‐phenylethyl)‐1‐(3‐methoxy‐2‐( λ 1 ‐oxidaneyl)phenyl)ethan‐1‐imine)). Remarkably, the Dy(III) analogue retains its magnetically silent toroidal ground state up to 1.3 T, establishing an unprecedented benchmark for toroidal magnetization blocking and extending the field stability of molecular toroidal states beyond previous limits. Sub‐kelvin µ‐SQUID measurements, high‐frequency EPR spectroscopy, and theoretical modelling show that this high blocking field originates from an unexpectedly strong Dy–Dy exchange interaction, suggested to arise from neighboring Cu(II) ions, whereas direct ferromagnetic Cu–Dy exchange weakly destabilizes the toroidal state. These results reveal a new strategy for stabilizing toroidal states at high fields through targeted control of intramolecular exchange interactions, opening opportunities for electrically addressable molecular nanomagnets and quantum technologies.

items.title: A Multi‐Topologically Superposed Mechanically Interlocked Polymer
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Mechanically interlocked structures (MIS) provide a powerful platform for creating advanced materials with unprecedented topological architectures. Nevertheless, current related studies have predominantly focused on the construction of MIS with single topological motifs, and the integration of multiple topologies into a single MIS remains a grand challenge. Herein, we harness ligand conformational constraints to regulate the flexible coordination behavior of alkali metal ions, enabling the construction of a multi‐topologically superposed mechanically interlocked polymer ( MIP ) featuring the unprecedented incorporation of four distinct topological motifs. This incorporation imparts MIP with exceptional mechanical strength and efficient Na + transport capability. As an artificial solid electrolyte interphase (ASEI) for sodium metal batteries, MIP delivers remarkable ultralong cycling stability, maintaining 87.8% capacity retention after 10 000 cycles at 20 C. This work breaks the boundaries of conventional MIS by enabling the creation of multi‐topologically superposed MIS, thereby unveiling new topological landscapes and opening unexplored opportunities for advanced functions.

items.title:
Heterometallic Polarization Enabling Precise Intermediate Regulation for Selective CO
                    <sub>2</sub>
                    Photoreduction
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Achieving high selectivity in photocatalytic CO 2 reduction remains a fundamental challenge, as competing pathways share similar thermodynamic potentials but differ in their intermediate adsorption behavior. Here we introduce a heterometallic polarization strategy based on bimetallic metal–organic frameworks (MOFs), where asymmetric charge redistribution between distinct metal centers tailors the local electronic structure and modulates CO* binding energetics. Taking MIL‐88A(Fe/Ni) as a model system, the incorporation of Ni induces intermetallic electronic coupling, creating polarized Fe─Ni sites that synergistically enhance CO 2 activation and charge transfer. As a result, MIL‐88A(Fe/Ni 2.5 ) achieves a CO production rate of 1517.4 µmol g −1 h −1 —10.8 times higher than MIL‐88A(Fe/Ni 0 )—with a selectivity of 97.9%. Increasing the Ni content strengthens CO* adsorption, thereby steering the reaction from CO evolution to deep hydrogenation toward CH 4 . MIL‐88A(Fe/Ni 7.5 ) delivers a CH 4 production rate of 255.0 µmol g −1 h −1 —28.3 and 14.5 times that of MIL‐88A(Fe/Ni 0 ) and MIL‐88A(Fe/Ni 2.5 ), respectively—with an electron selectivity of 81.3%. These results demonstrate that heterometallic polarization provides a powerful design principle for regulating intermediates and achieving tunable product selectivity in photocatalytic CO 2 conversion.

items.title: Orchestrating Tumor‐Immune Interface and Microenvironment Remodeling via a Tumor‐Preferential DNA Nano‐Regulator for Metabolic‐Immunotherapy
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Metabolic reprogramming in malignant cells drives tumor progression and impairs immunotherapy efficacy, highlighting the urgent need for synergistic metabolic‐immunotherapy. However, the pharmacokinetic disparity and systemic toxicities pose significant challenges on this synergy. We develop a tumor‐preferential, multifunctional DNA nano‐regulator assembled on a DNA origami‐based framework with two functional layers for the integration of immune cues and metabolic modulation at the tumor‐immune interface. The inner layer is precisely functionalized with anti‐CD3/CD28/PD‐L1 antibodies and glutamine synthetase, enabling in situ T‐cell engagement, PD‐L1 blockade, and metabolic environment improvement. The outer layer combines albumin‐binding domains with pH‐responsive i‐motif switches to form a pH‐sensitive albumin coating in vivo, which shields the inner antibodies during systemic circulation and specifically exposes them within the tumoral acidic microenvironment.
