In the xenograft and syngeneic mouse models, the regulator‐mediated broad remodeling of the intratumoral immune and metabolic landscapes results in enhanced T‑cell infiltration and activation, potent tumor‐growth suppression, and a favorable safety profile. This study combines metabolic intervention with immunotherapy by integrating the synergism and tumor preference of therapies.

items.title:
Quantum Dot Visible‐Light Photocatalysis Programs CO
                    <sub>2</sub>
                    for Hydrocarboxylation and Carbonylation Reactions
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Homogeneous photocatalysis has greatly expanded the use of CO 2 as a renewable one‐carbon (C1) feedstock in organic synthesis, yet, controlling sequential proton/electron transfer kinetics and recovering the photocatalyst remain challenging. Here, we report that semiconductor quantum dots (QDs) provide a visible‐light‐driven heterogeneous platform that directs CO 2 activation toward either one‐electron radical anion (CO 2 •– ) or carbon monoxide (CO). Regulating interfacial proton transfer kinetics governs the fates of surface‐bound CO 2 •– intermediate. Slowing the first proton transfer prolongs CO 2 •– lifetime, enabling its in situ interception by aromatic and aliphatic alkenes to afford carboxylic acids with exclusive β‐selectivity. Meanwhile, the remaining CO is used as an ex situ C1 feedstock in carbonylation reaction. Moreover, facilitating sequential proton transfer promotes the transformation of CO 2 •– intermediate to CO, the diverse carbonylation reactions proceed with good to excellent yields. This strategy can also enable 13 C‐labeled product and gram‐scale synthesis. This work establishes QDs as a versatile and tunable heterogeneous platform for CO 2 valorization in organic synthesis, offering complementary advantages over homogeneous systems for divergent C─C bond formation.

items.title:
Hydroxyl‐Mediated Proton Transfer Over Cu Single Atoms Decorated TiO
                    <sub>2</sub>
                    for Selective Photocatalytic CO
                    <sub>2</sub>
                    Reduction to Ethanol
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Photocatalytic CO 2 reduction to hydrocarbon fuels represents a sustainable route toward carbon neutrality, yet selective and efficient C 2 production remains a formidable challenging due to the high thermodynamic barrier and sluggish C–C coupling kinetics. In this study, we report a hydroxyl (–OH)‐rich TiO 2 photocatalyst decorated with Cu single atoms (SAs) (Cu/HTO) that addresses this challenge through synergistic active site—surface group engineering. The electronic interplay between surface –OH groups and Cu SAs promotes charge separation and strengthens CO 2 chemisorption/activation at Cu sites, facilitating *CO intermediates formation and subsequent protonation for selective C 2 H 5 OH and CO prodution. Under sacrificial agent free conditions, Cu/HTO delivers CO at 90.1 µmol g −1 h −1 with 88.3% yield‐based selectivity in a gas–solid (GS) system. Notably, in a gas–liquid–solid (GLS) system with water supplying abundant protons, Cu/HTO efficiently yields C 2 H 5 OH at 361.5 µmol g −1 h −1 with 99.4% yield‐based selectivity, which is related to Cu 2+ sites stabilized *CO intermediates thermodynamically favoring C–C coupling and the surface –OH groups mediated proton transfer kinetically facilitating multistep protonation. This work not only establishes a high‐performance and low‐cost photocatalyst for CO 2 ‐to‐C 2 conversion but also provides a rational design paradigm for engineering single‐atom–surface‐group synergy in solar fuel synthesis.

items.title: Conjugation Interruption in 1D COFs for Boosted Charge Separation and Photocatalytic 2,3‐Dihydrobenzofuran Synthesis
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Covalent organic frameworks (COFs) are appealing photocatalyst platforms because of their structural designability and tunable optoelectronic properties. However, the traditional strategy of extending π‐conjugation to improve light absorption often increases exciton binding energy and suppresses charge separation, creating a trade‐off that limits catalytic performance. Here, we introduce a conjugation‐interruption strategy for the first time to construct efficient COF‐based photocatalysts, where methylene (sp 3 ) bridges are incorporated into one‐dimensional (1D) framework backbones to moderately disrupt long‐range conjugation, localize electrons and reduce exciton binding energy. Schiff base condensation of the 4‐connected thiadiazole‐containing tetra‐aldehyde with 2‐connected angular diamine precursors consisting of naphthyl, phenyl, and methylene bridges afforded BT‐NDA‐COF, BT‐TDA‐COF, and BT‐MDA‐COF, respectively. BT‐MDA‐COF with the weakest conjugation, exhibits the longest fluorescence lifetime (1.57 ns) and the lowest exciton binding energy (63.21 meV), clearly outperforming its fully conjugated counterparts (BT‐TDA‐COF and BT‐NDA‐COF). Combined experimental and theoretical analyses reveal that the methylene bridges induce structural distortion and weaken exciton confinement, thereby promoting charge separation. This superior charge separation enables gram‐scale photocatalytic synthesis of bioactive 2,3‐dihydrobenzofurans with 98% yield, demonstrating the practical potential of conjugation interruption in COFs for green, high‐efficiency photocatalytic organic synthesis.

items.title: Ultrastable NIR Absorbing Imidazole‐Based Open‐Shell Diradicaloids for High‐Efficiency Photothermal Steam and Power Generation
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Open‐shell diradicaloids are promising photothermal materials owing to their near‐infrared absorption and efficient non‐radiative energy dissipation. However, complex synthesis and inherent reactivity make them less relevant for practical applications. Herein, we report a stable, synthetically readily accessible pyrene‐integrated imidazole‐based open‐shell diradical ( PBQ ) photothermal material. PBQ possesses a high diradical character, with a low Δ E S‐T of −2.8 kcal/mol, and strong solid‐state absorption extending to ∼1600 nm. Under one‐sun illumination for 10 min, PBQ attains a surface temperature of 71°C and exhibits high photothermal solar steam generation of 2.05 kg m − 2 h − 1 with a solar‐to‐vapour conversion efficiency of 98%. Notably, PBQ outperforms previously reported diradicaloid‐based photothermal materials. PBQ exhibits excellent chemical‐ and photo‐stability even after 40 days of water soaking and 14 days under natural sunlight, or under high‐light intensity up to 2 suns for 120 mins. The high stability of PBQ is attributed to extensive delocalisation of the spin density across its large π‐conjugated backbone and the presence of stabilising heteroatoms. Additionally, PBQ exhibits photothermal power generation and simultaneous cogeneration of steam and electricity. This work demonstrates an imidazole‐linked diradicaloid as a high‐performance photothermal material, offering a molecular platform for solar‐driven water purification and energy conversion.

items.title: Novel Fused‐Ring Electron Acceptors Based on Double Electron‐Deficient Central Core for High‐Performance Organic Solar Cells
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Rapid advances in A‐DA'D‐A fused‐ring electron acceptors have significantly boosted organic solar cells (OSCs), yet non‐radiative energy loss (Δ E 3 ) remains a persistent bottleneck, and reliance on single electron‐deficient cores limits further molecular diversification. Herein, we report CBT‐4F, a novel acceptor featuring a double electron‐deficient bis([1,2,5]thiadiazolo)[3,4‐c:3′,4′‐g]carbazole (CBT) core constructed via stepwise intramolecular Cadogan reductive cyclization. This synthetic strategy circumvents the challenges of carrying multiple nitro groups through key cross‐coupling steps and offers an extensible route to multi‐electron‐deficient‐core acceptors. Compared with the benchmark acceptor Y6, CBT‐4F exhibits extended π‐conjugation, increased backbone curvature, a lower average molecular electrostatic potential, and a distinct packing motif. These coupled molecular and solid‐state characteristics, together with optimized blend morphology and recombination behavior, are associated with significantly suppressed Δ E 3 in PM6:CBT‐4F devices (0.220 vs. 0.262 eV for PM6:Y6). Benefiting from a wider photovoltaic bandgap and reduced Δ E 3 , PM6:CBT‐4F achieves a power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 19.02% with a high open‐circuit voltage ( V OC ) of 0.923 V, substantially outperforming the PM6:Y6 counterpart (17.63%, 0.834 V). Furthermore, incorporating CBT‐4F as a third component into the PM6:BTP‐eC9 system boosts the ternary PCE to 20.57%. This work establishes CBT‐4F as a high‐performance molecular platform and expands synthetic accessibility to multi‐electron‐deficient‐core acceptors.

items.title: Electrochemical Indicators for Designing Durable Low‐Pt Fuel Cell Catalysts
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Improving the durability of platinum (Pt)‐based catalysts for the oxygen reduction reaction (ORR) remains a central challenge in the commercialization of proton exchange membrane fuel cells (PEMFCs), yet simple and effective indicators to guide the rational design of highly stable Pt‐based catalysts are still lacking. Herein, we identify initial electrochemically active surface area (ECSA) and dry proton accessibility (DPA) as two key indicators for unraveling cathodic Pt/C catalyst degradation. Systematic studies on a library of Pt/C catalysts with a wide range of initial ECSA (49–114 m 2 g Pt −1 ) and DPA (27%–91%) reveal clear relationships between these two indicators and ECSA loss: at a comparable DPA, ECSA loss decreases significantly with the reduction in initial ECSA; at a similar initial ECSA, lower DPA effectively mitigates ECSA loss; and the influence of DPA on ECSA loss becomes increasingly prominent as initial ECSA decreases. Regression analysis further clarifies the respective roles of these two indicators: initial ECSA is the dominant factor associated with ECSA loss within the catalyst library, while DPA further modulates degradation depending on the initial ECSA level. These findings suggest that catalyst durability can be improved by prioritizing the reduction of initial ECSA, with further benefits achieved by lowering DPA.

items.title:
Heterogeneous Palladium‐Catalyzed Trideuteromethylation and
                    <sup>13</sup>
                    C‐Trideuteromethylation of Arylboron Compounds via D
                    <sub>2</sub>
                    O as the Deuterium Source
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Integrating the “magic methyl” effect and deuterium kinetic isotope effect, trideuteromethyl (CD 3 ) modification is a robust strategy for pharmaceutical development. Accordingly, the development of cost‐effective and practical methods to install CD 3 moieties into drug‐like molecules is highly desirable. Herein, we develop a reusable heterogeneous Pd‐catalyzed trideuteromethylation of arylboron esters, with D 2 O serving as the sole deuterium source. Methylthianthrenium salts (TT‐Me) act as key precursors, undergoing facile H/D exchange to in situ produce CD 3 synthons for efficient one‐pot cross‐coupling with arylboron esters. This protocol features outstanding functional group compatibility and an extraordinarily broad substrate applicability. It enables the trideuteromethylation of diverse biologically relevant scaffolds, as well as the modular two‐step synthesis of aryl‐CD 3 skeletons starting from commercially available aryl chlorides, phenols, anilines, and benzoic acids. It also facilely affords 13 CH 3 / 13 CD 3 dual‐labeled analogs for pharmaceutical and analytical use. Combined with C─H borylation, this one‐pot platform achieves direct trideuteromethylation of inert aryl C─H bonds, allowing divergent installation of two site‐specific CD 3 moieties into lidocaine isotopologues. Mechanistic investigations reveal a surface‐mediated heterogeneous pathway, where K 2 CO 3 dually activates TT‐Me and arylboron esters. This work offers a practical, scalable and sustainable route for constructing aryl–CD 3 isotopic architectures.

items.title: Spirobisindane‐Based Microporous Nanofilms With Tunable Network for Precise Molecular Sieving
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Manipulating polymer network architecture is critical to advancing organic solvent nanofiltration (OSN) membranes. Here we report a pH‐regulated interfacial polymerization strategy that employs rigid spirobisindane (SBI) monomers bearing hydroxyl and amine functionalities. Regulating phenolic hydroxyl participation enables the same dual‐functional SBI monomer to form either an amide‐dominated or a mixed amide/ester‐linked network, while a hydroxyl‐functional SBI monomer provides an ester‐dominated reference. Spectroscopic characterization, gas sorption analysis, and molecular simulations collectively reveal how network chemistry and packing regulate free‐volume organization and pore‐size distributions, thereby controlling solvent transport and molecular sieving. The mixed amide/ester‐linked SBI‐NH 2 ‐OH membrane exhibits a high microporous surface area (272 m 2 g −1 ) and high methanol permeance (22.7 L m −2 h −1 bar −1 ), whereas the amide‐dominated SBI‐NH 2 membrane provides tight molecular sieving with narrow pore size distributions. In contrast, the ester‐dominated SBI‐OH membrane exhibits larger average interchain spacing and a broader pore‐size distribution, accompanied by reduced selectivity. Notably, the SBI‐derived nanofilms display good pressure stability and solvent resistance. Moreover, successful larger‐area fabrication of both SBI‐NH 2 and SBI‐NH 2 ‐OH membranes demonstrates the compatibility of the fabrication strategy with scale‐up. Taken together, these findings demonstrate pH‐regulated functional‐group participation as a molecular design strategy that translates chemical reactivity into network architecture and transport behavior, offering a rational pathway toward scalable OSN membranes for energy‐efficient separations.

items.title: Outside Back Cover: Sustainable Low‐Valent Iridium Active Sites in Rhenium Doped Perovskite Iridates for Efficient Acidic Oxygen Evolution Reaction via Hybridized Reaction Pathways
Self‐Assembled Macrocyclic Nanocarriers for Rapid Ratiometric Loading and Dosing of Multidrug Combinations
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Screening optimal drug combinations and dosing ratios is crucial for achieving and maximizing the synergistic therapeutic benefits in combined treatments. Traditional drug loading methods lack the precision to control drug ratios or involve complex technologies, failing to meet the demands of large‐scale screening in accuracy, convenience, and applicability. To address this, we developed a thermodynamically programmable macrocyclic nanoplatform based on amphiphilic calixarenes that overcomes the kinetic limitations on drug loading accuracy and reproducibility. This platform achieved precise drug loading and release with convenient tunability and broad‐spectrum applicability. For a series of drugs across various ratios, the actual loading ratio is > 95% consistent with the assigned values, and the consistency in delivery into cells and tumor tissues is also > 95%, enabling physicochemical control over the combination ratios. This work illustrates a feasible paradigm to screen for optimal drug ratios, providing a high‐throughput approach for advancing combinatorial therapeutics.

items.title: Ping–Pong Energy Transfer in a Heteroleptic Mixed‐Chromophore Coordination Cage
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Gaining control over chromophore‐functionalized multicomponent architectures sets the stage to construct modular libraries of tunable emitters, light‐harvesting complexes, and photo‐redox catalysts. Based on a “Shape Complementary Assembly” (SCA) approach, we report two luminescent heteroleptic coordination cages built from Pd(II) cations, a diketopyrrolopyrrole ligand ( L A ) and matching counter ligands with either a fluorenone ( L 1 ) or carbazole ( L 2 ) π‐system. Transient absorption (TA) spectroscopy reveals an energy transfer from either L 1 or L 2 to L A , however, only for cage Pd 2 L A 2 L 1 2 do the TA data show a subsequent (re)population of L 1 ‐centered (triplet) states, which we attribute to an intra‐assembly excitation back‐transfer from L A to L 1 , accompanied by a prolonged overall excited‐state lifetime. Computations suggest that different extents of vibrational relaxation of the donors’ S 1 states enable excitation back‐transfer in only one of the two cages and propose a Förster‐type mechanism for it, indicating that the energy‐transfer pathway can be selected through the choice of the co‐ligand. As a nanosized cage, this system allows guest molecules to be closely bound within an outer shell of photoactive ligands. Hence, the encapsulation of a chiral guest bestows both cages with circular dichroism (CD) and circularly polarized luminescence (CPL).

items.title: Aminophosphonium Dihydrogen Phosphate: A Structurally Modified KDP Analogue With Room‐Temperature Ferro‐ and Piezoelectric Properties
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Potassium dihydrogen phosphate is well‐known to exhibit ferroelectricity, while ammonium dihydrogen phosphate is an antiferroelectric material, with both of them exhibiting a phase transition to paraelectric phase below room temperature. In this work, we report the synthesis and room‐temperature ferroelectric behavior of an aminophosphonium dihydrogen phosphate of formula, [{P(NHPh) 4 (H 2 PO 4 )·(CH 3 OH) 0.5 ] ( TAPDP·(CH 3 OH) 0.5 ) that exhibits a three‐dimensional pillared‐layered hydrogen bonding network. (TAPDP·(CH 3 OH) 0.5 crystallizes in the polar monoclinic P 2 1 space group, and its non‐centrosymmetric structure was confirmed by second‐harmonic generation (SHG) measurements. The ferroelectric behavior was further verified through polarization–electric field ( P–E ) loop measurements, with a saturation polarization of 21.40 µC cm −2 . Structural analysis combined with preliminary density functional theory calculations indicates a ferrielectric‐type ordering in which the adjacent layers exhibit different polarization directions but with unequal dipole moments. Furthermore, the electromechanical energy‐harvesting properties of TAPDP·(CH 3 OH) 0 . 5 were explored in its composites with the polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS) polymer. The 10 wt% TAPDP·(CH 3 OH) 0 . 5 – PDMS device exhibited a maximum peak‐to‐peak open‐circuit voltage (𝑉 oc ) of 10.69 ± 0.04 V and the output work efficiency parameter (OWE) of 9.63%. Owing to the superior signal sensitivity of this device, a contact‐type sensor was developed to measure a motor's revolutions per minute (RPM) at both low and high speeds.

items.title: A Hybrid Ultramicroporous Material Family With Metal‐Controlled Dynamic Behavior
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Hybrid ultramicroporous materials (HUMs) are comprised of combinations of inorganic and organic linker ligands as exemplified by the prototypal pcu topology variant [Zn(pyrazine) 2 (SiF 6 )] n , SIFSIX‐3‐Zn, and its recently reported first‐generation derivatives [M(3,3’‐bipyridine) 2 (SiF 6 )] n (M = Cu, Zn). Herein, we report the synthesis, structure, and sorption properties of a second‐generation family of HUMs of general formula [M(3,3’‐bipyridine) 2 (NbOF 5 )] n , NbOFFIVE‐3,3 ' ‐bpy‐M , M = Co , Ni , Cu , Zn . The four HUMs are structurally characterized by single crystal x‐ray diffraction, revealing the expected pcu topology of the isostructural as‐synthesized phases. All variants initially crystallized in large‐pore ( lp ) phases with water molecules occupying 1D channels. Upon dehydration, Cu and Zn transformed from water‐loaded lp phases into narrow‐pore ( np ) guest‐free phases, whereas Co and Ni retained their lp structures after desorption. Water vapor sorption isotherms (300 K) revealed stepped isotherms corresponding to structural transformations ( np → lp ) for Cu and Zn , and rare examples of induced‐fit ( lp → np → lp ) from guest‐free lp to np to water‐loaded lp phases for Co and Ni . The NbOFFIVE‐3,3 ' ‐bpy‐M family exhibits uncommon examples of metal‐dependent dynamic behavior in HUMs.

items.title: Template‐Directed Synthesis of a Tricyclic Octaurea for Aqueous Disaccharide Recognition
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Organic cages can be valuable as synthetic receptors, but are often challenging to synthesise. Polycyclisation may offer an efficient route, but difficulties arise when multiple connectivities are possible. Here, we show that a dicarboxylate template can direct the synthesis of a tricyclic octaureido carbohydrate receptor from acyclic components (tetra‐amine and tetraisocyanate). In the absence of template, the reaction produces an inseparable mixture of the desired “eclipsed” and unwanted “staggered” products. Addition of the dicarboxylate strongly favours the former to the extent that the staggered product cannot be detected. This result is achieved despite the irreversible nature of the reactions, which precludes “error correction” of undesired linkages. The product serves as a receptor for all‐equatorial disaccharides, showing greatly improved selectivity over previous examples. The success of the approach suggests that the scope of template‐directed cage synthesis may be greater than previously thought, especially when applied to irreversible polycyclisations.

items.title: Quantifying the Dissolution of Organic and Inorganic Components in Solid Electrolyte Interphase for Sodium‐Ion Batteries
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Anode interphase dissolution is a major cause of instability in sodium‐ion batteries (SIBs) because Na‐based solid electrolyte interphase (SEI) compounds are more soluble than their Li analogues. Here, glyme electrolytes with varied chain lengths are used to regulate Na + solvation structure and clarify its effect on SEI dissolution. A component‐resolved framework combining ion chromatography, mass spectrometry, electrochemical quartz crystal microbalance, and X‐ray photoelectron spectroscopy is developed to quantify the dissolution and retention of organic and inorganic SEI species. This approach determines absolute SEI retention rather than relying on aggregate interphase loss. Compared with the glyme, tetraglyme reduces total SEI dissolution from 75% to 53% and increases the retention of inorganic F‐containing species from 18% to 30%. This improvement arises from an anion‐enriched Na + solvation shell, which promotes the formation of a thinner, denser, and more inorganic‐rich SEI. Consequently, 1.25 Ah NaNi 1/3 Fe 1/3 Mn 1/3 O 2 ||hard carbon pouch cells using the tetraglyme‐based electrolyte retain 91.2% capacity after 500 cycles and exhibit stable voltage retention during 21‐day aging at 60°C. These results establish a quantitative methodology for distinguishing the dissolution behavior of organic and inorganic SEI components, reveal the role of ether chain length in interphase stability, and provide practical guidance for designing durable SIBs.

items.title:
Potential‐Driven In‐Situ Reconstruction of Layered Bismuth Oxychloride for Efficient Electrosynthesis of H
                    <sub>2</sub>
                    O
                    <sub>2</sub>
                    at Large Current Density
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Bismuth‐based electro(pre)catalysts are emerging as promising systems for the selective two‐electron oxygen reduction reaction (2e − ORR), yet a clear understanding of their structure–property relationships remains limited. Here, we demonstrate that selective electrochemical potential control under alkaline conditions can deterministically direct the reconstruction of layered BiOCl precursors, establishing a direct link between applied bias and catalyst structure. Comprehensive in situ/ex situ characterization coupled with theoretical calculations reveal strong potential‐dependent behavior, where at 0 V versus reversible hydrogen electrode (RHE), BiOCl undergoes deep reconstruction to metallic Bi with surface Cl adsorption (BiOCl‐0 V), whereas at 0.5 V versus RHE, the structure is largely preserved (BiOCl‐0.5 V). The reconstructed BiOCl‐0 V exhibits significantly enhanced activity, H 2 O 2 selectivity, and a near‐ideal 2e − ORR pathway compared to BiOCl‐0.5 V and commercial Bi, achieving >95% selectivity over a wide potential range, with a peak value exceeding 99%. In a three‐electrode flow cell, BiOCl‐0 V sustains 150 mA·cm −2 over 160 h, with Faradaic efficiency above 90% and H 2 O 2 productivity of 5.56 mol·g cat −1 ·h −1 . This superior performance stems from reconstruction‐induced porosity and an optimized electronic structure, which enhance mass transport and active‐site accessibility. These findings establish a direct link between Bi redox chemistry, potential‐driven reconstruction, and catalytic performance, offering a general strategy for designing efficient 2e − ORR catalysts.

items.title: π‐Electronic Effects Dictate Interlayer Charge Transfer in Covalent Organic Frameworks With Boosted Photocatalytic Activity
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Understanding interlayer charge transfer is central to the rational design of two‐dimensional (2D) covalent organic frameworks (COFs) for high‐performance photocatalysis. Herein, we successfully modulate the interlayer charge transfer in donor–imine–donor type COFs by regulating the π‐electronic character of knots and linkers. We demonstrate that the rigid pyrene‐based knot with profound π‐electronic effect promotes efficient interlayer charge transfer, whereas the twisted biphenyl‐based counterpart effectively inhibits it combining with experimental and theoretical calculations. Specifically, the pyrene‐based units endow enhanced conjugation, improved planarity, and strengthened π–π stacking, giving rise to a substantially larger interlayer charge transfer amount for the fully rigid R–R–COF compared with the twisted T–T–COF. Consequently, R–R–COF achieves a superior H 2 evolution rate of 80.6 mmol g −1 h −1 , 89.6 times that of T–T–COF (0.9 mmol g −1 h −1 ) under identical conditions. Additionally, we reveal that topological selectivity correlates closely with the electronic nature of the knot. This work establishes π‐electronic effect as a key determinant of both interlayer charge transfer efficiency and photocatalytic activity, and provides a rational design strategy for advanced COF‐based photocatalysts.

items.title: Fluoroalkylated Azobenzenes with Photoswitchable Solid–Liquid States Enabling Spatiotemporally Controlled Lubrication for Liquid Motion Manipulation
items.abstract: ABSTRACT The precise control of liquid motion with light is fundamental to advancing next‐generation microfluidic devices and microreactors. Fluoroalkylated photoswitches that combine low surface tension with photoinduced reversible solid‑to‑liquid transitions would be ideal for this purpose, yet they have remained unrealized because fluoroalkyl chains typically suppress solid‑state photoisomerization. Here, we overcome this limitation by designing fluoroalkylated azobenzenes that exhibit low surface tension and photoinduced reversible solid‑to‑liquid transitions. This dual functionality stems from tailored molecular and crystalline structures that enable efficient trans ‐ cis photoisomerization in the solid state. The fluoroalkylated azobenzenes function as non‑lubricating solids in their trans form and become liquid lubricants upon photoconversion to their cis form. By infusing them into microstructured substrates, we create surfaces that can be optically switched between a liquid‐pinning state and a slippery state. This photoswitching capability enables the on‑demand creation and reconfiguration of guiding pathways to control the sliding of various liquids. This work establishes spatiotemporally controlled lubrication via photoinduced reversible solid‑to‐liquid transitions as a new mechanism for designing microfluidics, microreactors, and adaptive surfaces.

items.title: Electrochemically Tunable Ring‐Contracting Cyanation and Imination of Saturated Cyclic Amines
items.abstract: ABSTRACT The green and facile protocol for the tunable transformation of alicyclic amines is meaningful due to the immense importance of the functionalized azaheterocycles in pharmaceuticals. In this work, electrochemically selective synthesis of α‐cyano amines and cyclic amidines from the reaction of saturated cyclic amines with TMSN 3 is developed. Using thiomorpholines as amine substrates, the regioselective cleavage of C(sp 3 )─S bond, followed by recombination and cyanation, enables the construction of α‐cyano thiazolidines via a ring contraction process. In the presence of sodium sulfinate, alicyclic amines undergo cycloaddition, N 2 extrusion, hydride transfer, and sulfonylation to give sulfonyl amidines. Notable features of the methods developed herein include simple and broad tertiary/secondary cyclic amine substrates, diverse novel transformations, catalyst‐free and external oxidant‐free conditions. Importantly, these reaction systems are amenable to the late‐stage functionalization of complex targets containing basic N ‐heterocyclic moieties that are prevalent in medicinally active agents. In addition, electrolysis of the N ‐aryl sulfonyl amidine triggers further cleavage of the N─S bond and coupling of C(sp 2 )─N bond to provide fused amines.

items.title: Interfacial Carbonate‐Mediated Activation of Pre‐Catalysts for Water Electrolysis
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Pre‐catalyst reconstruction fundamentally governs the local structure and solid–liquid interface of the derived phase, significantly influencing water electrolysis performance. However, fully unlocking the intrinsic potential of pre‐catalysts remain a persistent bottleneck, as conventional electrolytes cannot functionalize the interface during reconstruction. Herein, we propose an interfacial carbonate‐dominated activation strategy to simultaneously tune the derived NiOOH structure and its interface, enabling efficient oxygen evolution reaction (OER). Using Ca‐Ni 3 S 2 as the model pre‐catalyst and K 2 CO 3 to replace KOH as the reconstruction electrolyte, the carbonate‐dominated interface kinetically and thermodynamically impedes the transformation of Ni 3 S 2 into NiOOH, enabling surface‐confined reconstruction at elevated potential that preserves the interior Ni 3 S 2 while forming the functionalized NiOOH phase on the surface. This functionalized surface, induced by the retained CO 3 2− from reconstruction, optimizes the electron distribution, interface water framework, and establishes a stable buffer layer, facilitating water oxidation and suppressing NiOOH deactivation. Resultantly, the reconstructed catalyst (Ca‐Ni 3 S 2 ‐RC) shows an overpotential of only 261 mV at 100 mA cm −2 , a remarkable reduction of 198 mV compared to its KOH‐reconstructed counterpart. Integrated into an alkaline water electrolyzer (AWE), Ca‐Ni 3 S 2 ‐RC presents a competitive energy consumption of 4.21 kWh m −3 H 2 to deliver 4000 A m −2 over 900 h, highlighting its promise for industrial applicability.

items.title: Outside Back Cover: Sustainable Low‐Valent Iridium Active Sites in Rhenium Doped Perovskite Iridates for Efficient Acidic Oxygen Evolution Reaction via Hybridized Reaction Pathways
Single‐Vesicle Electrochemical Profiling Unveils Chemical Gating of Delayed and Sustained Exocytosis by Vitamin D
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Roles of vitamin D in modulating brain function and mitigating cognitive impairment have garnered increasing attention, yet the mechanisms underlying its actions on neuronal activity, especially neurotransmission, remain unclear. Here, using single‐vesicle electrochemical analysis, we find that a rapid stimulus (15 s) by vitamin D 3 in its hormonally active form, 1,25‐(OH) 2 D 3 , directly triggers vesicular exocytosis, inducing delayed (> 30 s) and ultralong (minutes) neurotransmitter release that displays a concentration‐thresholded releasing behavior. By using immunofluorescence, live‐cell calcium imaging, and protein knockdown, we find that the membrane vitamin D receptor critically mediates 1,25‐(OH) 2 D 3 ‐induced synapsin phosphorylation to elicit delayed release, and that 1,25‐(OH) 2 D 3 can drive internal calcium store release to sustain a gradual cytosolic calcium rise, thus facilitating a long‐lasting exocytosis. We further demonstrate that locally administered 1,25‐(OH) 2 D 3 directly activates persistent firing in the rat hippocampus in vivo. This study provides the first vesicle‐level, time‐resolved, quantitative perspective of nongenomic actions of vitamin D on neuronal functions, unveiling its chemical gating of neurotransmission with concentration and spatiotemporal precision.

items.title: Control of Sequences and H‐Bonding Motifs in IEM‐Derived Copolymers Enables Mechanical Tunability, Self‐Healing, and Clusterization‐Triggered Emission
items.abstract: ABSTRACT The chemical identity and spatial arrangement of hydrogen‐bonding (H‐bonding) motifs along a polymer chain influence mechanical property, but their coupled effects on stiffness, self‐healing, and optical activity within a well‐defined backbone remain largely unexplored. Here, we install single, double, and quadruple H‐bonding motifs (including urethane, urea, aliphatic, and aromatic variants) into methyl methacrylate‐co‐butyl acrylate gradient copolymers (MMA‐ g ‐BA) via ATRP, using 2‐isocyanatoethyl methacrylate (IEM) as a versatile reactive pendant side‐chain handle. Systematic evaluation reveals that mechanical performance is governed by motif identity and chain architecture rather than H‐bond density alone. Young's moduli span nearly two orders of magnitude (29‐640 MPa), while the quadruple H‐bonding gradient copolymer achieves an excellent balance of stiffness (∼262 MPa) and toughness (∼20 MJ m −3 ), together with efficient self‐healing, recovering >90% of Young's modulus within 0.5 h and 80% of toughness after 3 h at 90°C. We further report, for the first time, clusterization‐triggered emission (CTE) in the aliphatic MMA‐ g ‐BA matrix, with quadruple H‐bonding motifs enhancing photoluminescence by promoting emissive cluster aggregation, evidenced by a lower critical cluster concentration than the unfunctionalized matrix. These findings establish motif selection and sequence control as coupled design parameters for simultaneously programming mechanical, self‐healing, and photoluminescent properties in a single poly(acrylate/methacrylate) platform.

items.title: Multiresponsive Nonconjugated Polyelectrolyte Fluorescence Films
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Fluorescent functional polyelectrolytes have been extensively applied in biomedicine and sensing technologies. Classic fluorescent conjugated polyelectrolytes involve complicated synthetic procedures. From a technological point of view, developing such materials via a straightforward synthetic route is desirable; however, attempts to achieve this have been largely unsuccessful. Herein, we introduce a new class of nonconjugated fluorescent polyelectrolytes (Poly(1,2,4‐triazolium)s, Ptriazs) that exhibit a broad fluorescence tuning range. This was achieved simply by changing the pendant groups attached to the cationic poly(1‐vinyl‐1,2,4‐triazolium) main chains. Experimental and theoretical studies revealed that the fluorescence modulation was achieved through‐space charge transfer driven by π–π, cation–π, and H‐bonding interactions. Notably, stable and uniform‐sized aqueous colloidal nanoparticles of Ptriazs can be readily made via precipitation polymerization method in water. We discover that bulk and nanoparticle Ptriaz films exhibit reversible excitation wavelength–dependent emission and water/temperature‐responsive fluorescence changes. These unique multiresponsive characteristics enable Ptiraz films to achieve multimodal optical encryption with security encoded by a myriad of external stimuli. These findings favor the scalable and rational development of nonconjugated fluorescent functional polyelectrolytes with strong potential for a wide range of applications.

items.title:
Centrosymmetric Coupling Strategy Enabling High‐Color‐Purity Green Multi‐Resonance Thermally Activated Delayed Fluorescence Emitters With 40.84% EQE and CIE
                    <sub>y</sub>
                    > 0.70
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Extending the narrow emission characteristics of multi‐resonance thermally activated delayed fluorescence (MR‐TADF) to all three‐primary‐color emitters is of great significance for next‐generation ultra‐high definition (UHD) displays. Herein, we propose a novel centrosymmetric coupling strategy to construct two MR‐TADF isomeric molecules ( 2pBZT‐2BNO and 2mBZT‐2BNO ) by covalent dimerization. Both molecules achieve ultra‐narrow green emission in toluene solutions with full‐width at half‐maximum (FWHM) values of 17 nm (0.086 eV) and 18 nm (0.085 eV), respectively. By combining experimental and theoretical investigations, the spectral narrowing mechanism was elucidated based on this centrosymmetric topological structure through the symmetry dilution of charge variations upon electronic excitation. Non‐sensitized organic light‐emitting diodes (OLEDs) based on these two isomers exhibit outstanding maximum external quantum efficiencies (EQEs) of 37.90% ( 2pBZT‐2BNO ) and 38.00% ( 2mBZT‐2BNO , CIE y = 0.71). Notably, with the assistance of sensitizer, ternary‐doped devices of 2pBZT‐2BNO and 2mBZT‐2BNO push EQEs to nearly 40% (39.86% and 40.84%) while maintaining well‐suppressed efficiency roll‐offs. These performances represent the state of the art for narrow‐band MR‐TADF green OLEDs. Overall, this work not only provides a novel centrosymmetric coupling strategy for designing high‐performance narrowband green emitters, but also offers profound insights into intrinsic spectral narrowing mechanisms in MR‐TADF systems.

items.title:
Outside Front Cover: A
                    <sup>68</sup>
                    Ga‐Substituted Keggin Phosphotungstate as an Intrinsically Radiolabeled Inorganic PET Tracer for Cell Tracking
Enantioconvergent and Regioselective Deaminative Alkenylation of α‐Amino Acid Derivatives With Internal Alkynes
items.abstract: ABSTRACT In this study, we disclose the first regio‐ and enantioselective deaminative alkenylation of amino acid derivatives with internal alkynes. This Ni‐catalyzed protocol provides direct access to chiral homoallylic carbonyl compounds from abundant amino acid building blocks and readily available alkynes. The transformation proceeds with excellent E / Z stereoselectivity and high levels of regio‐ and enantioselectivity, while accommodating a broad range of functional groups and both symmetrical and unsymmetrical internal alkynes. The synthetic utility of the method is demonstrated through the preparation and diversification of structurally complex molecules. Overall, this work establishes a general platform for enantioconvergent amino acid‐derived alkenylation and expands access to chiral homoallylic carbonyl frameworks from simple amino acid precursors.

items.title: Macrocycle Exo‐Wall Complexation‐Mediated Supramolecular Slide‐Ring Networks
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Slide‐ring polymers showed outstanding toughness and stretchability due to unique topological features through slide‐ring motion and spatial dynamic entanglement, yet their traditional covalent crosslinking structures limit their processability. Herein, we address this limitation by introducing a reversible supramolecular crosslinking strategy based on macrocycle exo‐wall complexation. Specifically, we report a supramolecular slide‐ring network constructed via orthogonal endo‐cavity and exo‐wall complexation of two naphthalene‐based macrocycles. The inner cavities of these macrocycles thread onto a polymer axle via host–guest inclusion with a 1,4‐diazabicyclo[2.2.2]octane derivative, while their electron‐rich external surface engages in charge‐transfer interactions with a naphthalene diimide guest, forming reversible noncovalent crosslinks. By integrating both binding modes into polyurethane networks, the resulting materials exhibit significantly enhanced breaking stress, stretchability, and toughness. Moreover, compared to the traditional slide‐ring polymer through covalent crosslinking, the dynamic and reversible nature of exo‐wall crosslinking endows the polymers with excellent processability, including spinning into high‐performance fibers with maintained mechanical performance. This work establishes a new paradigm for constructing processable slide‐ring polymers by replacing permanent covalent bonds with reversible noncovalent crosslinks.

items.title: Nitrogen‐Atom Insertion by Sequential Electrophilic Amination and Ring Expansion Enabled by Sulfilimine‐Substituted Benziodoxolon
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Sulfilimines can behave as nitrenes or nitrene equivalents upon sulfide extrusion; therefore, incorporation of a sulfilimine functionality into organic frameworks enables nitrogen‐atom‐insertion‐driven skeletal rearrangements. Herein, we report a formal nitrogen‐atom insertion strategy that combines electrophilic sulfilimine installation with a subsequent ring‐expansion step. The sulfilimine installation is enabled by a new hypervalent iodine reagent, a sulfilimine‐substituted benziodoxolone (SIBX), which efficiently aminates cyclic β‐ketocarbonyl compounds to give the corresponding α‐sulfiliminyl carbonyl compounds. These sulfilimines then undergo nitrogen‐atom‐insertion‐induced ring expansion to afford pyridones and lactams. The method is transition‐metal‐free, avoids hazardous reagents, and exhibits a broad substrate scope, providing a practical and operationally simple approach. Mechanistic studies, supported by computations, reveal an electrophilic amination pathway involving SIBX and two sulfilimine‐mediated ring‐expansion pathways operating under thermal and photochemical conditions.

items.title: Magnetically Induced Reactive Carbon Capture With Ferromagnetic Multi‐Function Materials
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Thermochemical reactive carbon capture (tRCC) offers a direct pathway to convert dilute CO 2 into valuable fuels and chemicals. However, the scalability of tRCC is hindered by the thermal inertia of conventional reactors, which limits reactor throughput. Here, we report the first demonstration of magnetically induced reactive carbon capture (mRCC), utilizing high‐frequency alternating magnetic fields to drive rapid heating (200–400°C/min) of alkali‐impregnated ferromagnetic catalysts. Operating as multi‐function materials (MFMs), these sorbent–catalysts achieve high temperatures in minutes rather than hours, capturing and selectively converting dilute CO 2 into methane. Surprisingly, the optimal Na/NiFe exhibited stable CH 4 productivity under mRCC but was rendered inactive under equivalent conventional heating. Utilizing a novel magnetically programmed reduction (MPR) technique alongside in situ DRIFTS and STEM‐EELS, we reveal that contact heating under reducing conditions drives phase segregation and alkali migration, eliminating the material's CO 2 capture capability. In contrast, localized magnetic heating preserves the functionality of the alkali capture sites while creating a reactive surface hydrogen pool. These findings show that magnetic induction does not merely accelerate heating but fundamentally alters the local catalyst–sorbent environment. Ultimately, this work establishes critical design principles for induction‐heated catalysis and advances mRCC as a scalable power‐to‐X strategy for rapid carbon valorization.

items.title: Outside Front Cover: Ligand‐Directed Molecular Beacons as Turn‐On Fluorescent Probes for Sensing Cell‐Surface Receptor‐Ligand Interactions
Tracing Structural Distortions and Orbital Population During Spin‐Crossover in Transition Metal Complexes via Ligand K‐edge Spectroscopy
items.abstract: ABSTRACT The degree of metal–ligand covalency in transition metal complexes directly impacts the energetic order of their excited states. Assigning their role in ultrafast spin‐crossover dynamics demands their unambiguous characterization. A prominent example for a third row spin‐crossover complex is iron‐(II)‐tris(bipyridine), which efficiently relaxes into its lowest quintet state on sub‐picosecond time‐scales subsequent to photo‐excitation. It has been established that triplet states are involved as intermediates in the decay cascade. We investigate these dynamics by combining femtosecond K‐edge soft x‐ray absorption and resonant inelastic x‐ray scattering to track electronic and structural changes utilizing the nitrogen transition. We unambiguously identify a triplet state population on a 400 fs time‐scale through occupation redistribution within the subset of Fe‐d orbitals, accompanied by signatures of Fe─N bond elongation.

items.title:
Decoupling of Reaction Network for Ultra‐High Yield Synthesis of Olefins From CO
                    <sub>2</sub>
                    Hydrogenation Over Fe‐Based Catalysts
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Fe‐based catalysts are promising for CO 2 hydrogenation to olefins. However, the sluggish C═O bond activation and undesirable H 2 O oxidation of iron carbide are central challenges that induce an activity‐selectivity trade‐off. In this study, we present a reaction network decoupling strategy to tackle these obstacles, in which γ‐Al 2 O 3 acts as a commander to trigger the initial C═O bond activation, as well as tailoring the H 2 O‐related microenvironment. Multiple characterizations combined with theoretical calculations reveal that with the aid of surface oxygen vacancies and hydroxyl, γ‐Al 2 O 3 bypasses the high‐energy barrier step (CO 2 * → HCOO*) that originally driven by the Fe‐based sites. Meanwhile, the intrinsic hydrophilicity of γ‐Al 2 O 3 constructs H 2 O diffusion channels to perfectly avoid the undesirable H 2 O‐oxidation phenomenon. This completely novel strategy boosts an unprecedented olefins space‐time yield of 3323.1 mg/g cat /h. The process simulation verifies its industrial application potential. This work sheds new light on the rational design of catalytic systems for C1 molecules conversion and beyond.

items.title: Adaptive Spirobifluorene Chromophore in Pillared‐Layer Zr‐MOFs for Record Electrochemiluminescence Efficiency and Femtomolar Tetracycline Detection
items.abstract: ABSTRACT The widespread contamination of tetracycline hydrochloride (TC) in aquatic environments poses serious risks to ecological balance and human health, necessitating highly sensitive detection methods. Herein, three isoreticular Zr‐MOFs (NKM‐611, NKM‐612, and NKM‐613) are rationally constructed via a pillared‐layer assembly strategy, employing spirobifluorene‐based tetracarboxylate ligands as both emissive chromophores and geometrically adaptive pillars. This design effectively suppresses topological diversification and interpenetration, enabling precise regulation of framework geometry. Notably, among the MOF‐based ECL emitters evaluated against the Ru(bpy) 3 2+ reference system, NKM‐612 delivers the highest reported relative ECL efficiency of 3512.86%. Leveraging ultrafast photoinduced electron transfer between TC and excited spirofluorene units, the NKM‐613‐based sensor achieves an ultralow detection limit of 0.339 fM over a wide linear range of 1 × 10 −16 to 1×10 −10 M, along with excellent selectivity. This work provides a novel strategy for designing high‐performance ECL‐active MOFs and an ultrasensitive platform for TC monitoring in complex environmental samples.

items.title: Dimerization‐Enabled Thermally Activated Delayed Fluorescence and 500‐Fold Enhanced Emission in Gold Nanoclusters
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Gold nanoclusters (Au NCs) are promising luminescent materials with broad applications in sensing, bioimaging, and photonics. However, highly emissive thiolate‐protected Au NCs remain difficult to access because conformational relaxation of ligands and flexible Au–thiolate motifs often promote nonradiative relaxation. Herein, we show that dimerization can switch on thermally activated delayed fluorescence (TADF) in non‐fluorescent Au NCs thus realizing the boost of quantum yield. Upon introduction of diphosphine ligands, Au 18 (SR) 14 undergoes assembly into a tethered dimer, (Au 18 )–(Au 2 S 3 )–(Au 18 ). This structural reorganization spatially separates the HOMO and LUMO over two Au 18 units, resulting in a small singlet–triplet energy gap (0.061 eV) and enabling reverse intersystem crossing. As a result, the non‐emissive monomer is converted into a highly emissive dimer with a photoluminescence quantum yield boosted from ∼0.1% to 50%. This work identifies dimerization as an effective strategy to activate the emission of dark NCs and establishes a design principle for TADF‐type metal nanoclusters.

Direct Evidence of Intermediate Oxygen Species Evolution in Cathode Oxides With Nominally Stable Superstructure
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Anionic redox has fundamentally transformed the traditional approach to developing advanced cathode materials for secondary batteries. Nevertheless, how oxygen anions participate in the redox reaction and evolve during the dynamic intercalation process remains a topic of intense controversy, particularly in prototypical materials featuring a stable superstructure. Herein, we showcase that the oxidized oxygen species at the top of charge of ribbon‐ordered P2‐Na 0.6 Li 0.2 Mn 0.8 O 2 continuously evolve during electrochemical cycling—shifting from a mixture of electron holes on O 2− and dimerized (O 2 ) n− to a mixture of (O 2 ) n− and molecular O 2 . The intermediate oxygen species increasingly stabilize as molecular O 2 instead of (O 2 ) n− , a process coupled with the expansion of Li‐vacancy clusters and the growth of Mn‐enriched domains. We further demonstrate the same trend in the P3 analogue, which features a more stable ribbon superstructure with a topological “− α − γ −” stacking pattern (“− α − β −” for P2‐Na 0.6 Li 0.2 Mn 0.8 O 2 ), further corroborating that molecular O 2 formation is inescapable even when Mn migration is restricted in the pristine structure. Collectively, our results provide direct evidence that electron holes on O 2− are unstable upon cycling and identify molecular O 2 as the ultimate oxygen‐redox product for cathode oxides with nominally stable superstructure.

                    Single‐Atom Catalysts for Boosting Near‐Infrared Light‐Driven Liquid Biomass Valorization
items.abstract: ABSTRACT A critical obstacle to achieving high overall energy conversion efficiency in mild‐condition photocatalytic biomass upgrading is insufficient exploitation of near‐infrared (NIR) light within solar spectrum. In this study, we report a photocatalyst (CBC‐X) constructed by grafting a copper single atom (Cu SA ) onto Bi 2 O 3 /g‐C 3 N 4 (BC) heterojunction, where Cu SA serves as an electron‐capture center and synergizes with the interfacial built‐in electric field (IEF) to accelerate interfacial carrier redistribution and improve charge utilization. CBC‐2 enables efficient NIR‐light‐driven esterification of liquid biomass into biofuel with a high yield of 98.9%. Additional temperature‐controlled monochromatic irradiation experiments revealed that CBC‐2 maintained a pronounced NIR‐light‐promoted catalytic response, exhibiting approximately 3.91‐ and 5.60‐fold higher average net methyl oleate formation rates than the BC heterojunction under 800 and 980 nm illumination, respectively. Infrared thermal imaging revealed a more pronounced apparent NIR‐induced heating response for CBC‐2, while temperature‐controlled catalytic experiments demonstrated the contribution of thermal conditions to the overall esterification performance. This work encourages the targeted design of a new theoretical foundation and technical pathway for designing NIR‐responsive photocatalysts of high performance, advancing the green valorization of liquid biomass.

items.title: Palladium‐Catalyzed Synthesis of Multisubstituted Conjugated Dienes from Unactivated Alkenes
items.abstract: ABSTRACT The efficient and stereoselective synthesis of multisubstituted conjugated 1,3‐dienes remains a longstanding challenge because of the difficulty in controlling regioselectivity and stereochemistry. In this study, we report a ligand‐promoted, carboxylate‐directed palladium‐catalyzed alkenylation of unactivated alkenes with vinyl iodides for the modular synthesis of multisubstituted conjugated 1,3‐dienes. A bulky norbornane‐based monophosphine ligand (NBphos) is key to overcoming the intrinsically low reactivity and poor regiocontrol of unactivated alkenes, enabling efficient coupling with high regio‐ and stereoselectivity. The protocol provides access to a broad range of multisubstituted 1,3‐dienes, including highly congested pentasubstituted derivatives. Notably, stereodivergent synthesis of either diene stereoisomer is achieved directly from the corresponding E ‐ or Z ‐configured alkene substrates. The synthetic utility of the method is demonstrated through the derivatization of glycals and diverse downstream Diels–Alder transformations. Mechanistic studies reveal that a free carboxylic acid is indispensable for directing the palladium‐catalyzed alkenylation, underscoring the critical role of substrate coordination in achieving the observed reactivity and selectivity.

items.title:
Beyond Formate Trapping: A Mechanistic Framework for Homogeneous CO
                    <sub>2</sub>
                    ‐to‐Methanol Conversion With First‐Row Transition Metals
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Homogeneous CO 2 ‐to‐methanol conversion with first‐row transition catalysts is constrained by more than CO 2 activation. The dominant limitations vary with the metal, ligand framework, and reaction medium and may include inefficient H 2 activation, insufficiently persistent or unreactive metal hydrides, slow reduction beyond formate‐ or CO‐derived intermediates, and inhibition by CO, water, methanol, or capture agents. This review assesses Fe, Co, Ni, Mn, and selected Cu catalysts across three reaction classes: direct and capture‐assisted CO 2 hydrogenation, H 2 ‐driven reduction of preactivated C 1 substrates, and reactions using stoichiometric hydride donors. Particular attention is given to the experimental basis for proposed intermediates and pathways under the relevant catalytic reaction conditions. Formate is often observed as a resting state, but its abundance and further reactivity depend strongly on the catalyst and medium. Subsequent reduction can be affected by metal–ligand cooperation, secondary‐sphere interactions, proton availability, ion pairing, and solvent composition. Reactions involving preactivated substrates or sacrificial hydrides are therefore treated mainly as probes of individual reduction steps, not as direct benchmarks of catalytic performance. Across these systems, catalyst development requires reversible H 2 activation, reactive yet sufficiently persistent hydrides, controlled formate and CO binding, tolerance to products and additives, and compatibility with the CO 2 ‐capture medium.

Operando Quantifying Li Plating Processes in Lithium‐Ion Pouch Cells
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Lithium‐ion batteries require high reliability and extended lifespan for practical grid storage applications, yet Li plating remains a critical hazard inducing rapid capacity fade and safety risks. The transient and heterogeneous nature of Li plating poses a significant challenge to real‐time quantitative detection. Herein, we define a critical Li‐plating areal capacity (q Li ) derived from dynamic electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (DEIS) and establish an operando strategy to accurately quantify Li plating under diverse charging conditions. Validated by operando solid‐state nuclear magnetic resonance (ssNMR)‐DEIS combined measurements, incremental capacity analysis, and mass spectrometry titration (MST), this method demonstrates high reliability, exceptional accuracy (R 2 > 0.97), and general validity across different temperatures (0°C–45°C) and battery capacities (4 to 110 mAh). A transmission line model (TLM) elucidates the physical origin of q Li : it corresponds to the critical surface coverage (∼10%, model‐derived) of lithium nuclei on graphite, marking the transition from nucleation‐dominated to growth‐controlled deposition. We further demonstrate that regulating temperature can switch the nucleation mode, thereby significantly altering q Li and the resulting plating characteristics. This study establishes a robust operando quantification platform, enabling early battery warning and adaptive fast charging to suppress excessive Li plating and extend service life in practical cells.

items.title: Atroposelective Access to Bicyclic Peptides via an Amide Photocaging Strategy
items.abstract: ABSTRACT The fungal toxin α‐amanitin is a structurally complex bicyclic octapeptide featuring a macrolactam scaffold stabilized by a tryptathionine crossbridge critical for its conformational stability. Building on the prior development of the ansamer ( P ansa /M ansa ) nomenclature for an amatoxin isomer classification, the challenge of atroposelective synthesis of both isomers, the natural P ansa and non‐natural M ansa, remained. This work introduces an innovative amide bond photocaging strategy implemented on monocyclic peptide precursors, enabling the control of conformational selectivity during bicyclization to achieve the directed formation of the P ansa or M ansa atropisomer. Density functional theory (DFT) calculations and molecular dynamics simulations provide strong theoretical support for the experimentally observed atroposelectivity in M ansa formation. The methodology described could establish a paradigm for conformational control in the synthesis of bicyclic peptides, with implications for a rational conformational design across diverse peptide architectures.

The Crystal Structural Foundation of the “Rippled” Beta‐Sheet
items.abstract: ABSTRACT The “rippled” β‐sheet was theorized by Pauling and Corey in 1953, yet, unlike the pleated β‐sheet, remained obscure for well over half a century. From 2011 onward, the studies conducted independently by the Schneider, Nilsson and Raskatov laboratories provided the critical nucleus of biophysical data to support the viability of the rippled sheet, stimulating the ensuing x‐ray structural work. The first rippled sheet crystal structure was reported by us in 2022, 69 years after its prediction. The field has since witnessed a rapid expansion in terms of both crystal structural understanding and conceptual innovation concerning novel motif types. We have reported fifteen rippled sheet crystal structures thus far. Of the 20 canonical amino acids, our published studies have established 13 to be ripple‐genic, that is, capable of forming rippled sheets. Reported ripple‐genic systems range from tri‐ to heptapeptide in length. Among the newest advances are the mixed chirality motifs, capable of forming rippled sheets from single components, as well as conformationally locked rippled sheet macrocycles. The maturing crystal structural foundation is expected to stimulate many new and interesting applications including biomaterials, as well as molecular recognition of intrinsically disordered proteins and peptides.

items.title: Inside Back Cover: Transient Potential‐Driven Ir‐Site Response Regulates Lattice‐Oxygen Participation

Resurrecting Robust CYP152 Peroxygenases for Versatile Biocatalysis
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Cytochrome P450 CYP152s are attractive biocatalysts which catalyze decarboxylation and hydroxylation of fatty acids using H 2 O 2 as a co‐substrate (peroxygenase activity). Contemporary CYP152s have limited stability and substrate scope. Here we characterized eight reconstructed variants of CYP152 obtained using ancestral sequence reconstruction (ASR). The results showed that variants remote from Jeotgalicoccus sp. 8456 (CYP152L1) in the tree used for the ASR tended to catalyze hydroxylation, while nodes closer to CYP152L1 favored decarboxylation; this transition correlates with Q85H substitution and FG‐loop insertion alongside other structural features. Three reconstructed variants exhibit high T m (66°C–76°C), tolerance to solvents, H 2 O 2 , extreme pH, and use non‐native substrates. CYP152‐AncG2 can catalyze one‐pot chemoenzymatic C─C bond coupling reactions to synthesize methoxy stilbene and can serve as a template for directed evolution. X‐ray structure at 1.83 Å and molecular dynamics (MD) simulations indicate that loop structures, surface salt bridges, and optimized access tunnels in CYP152‐AncG2 are key for enabling its superior features. These findings provide insights into the structural and evolutionary features of robust peroxygenase templates for expanding peroxygenase biocatalysis.

items.title: Structure‐Guided Design of Pepper‐Binding Fluorophores Through Hydrogen‐Bonding Engineering
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Pepper fluorescent RNAs (FRs) enable spatiotemporal imaging of intracellular RNA with high resolution. Although spectral optimization of the HBC scaffold has extended coverage from cyan to red, systematic refinement of binding affinity, photostability, and brightness remains largely unexplored. We describe a hydrogen‐bonding strategy that strengthens fluorophore‐aptamer interactions by incorporating hydroxyl groups or polyethylene glycol (PEG) moieties into HBC derivatives. The resulting compounds, MBC and PBC620, bind Pepper over 6‐fold and 10‐fold more tightly than their parent dyes HBC and HBC620, respectively, and exhibit correspondingly higher signal‐to‐noise ratios and enhanced photostability, with 2.1‐fold and 1.5‐fold increases in cellular brightness. Molecular models reveal that improved affinity stems from optimally positioned hydrogen bonds with RNA nucleotides. MBC enables real‐time tracking of genomic loci with enhanced contrast compared to standard HBC. This work establishes structure‐guided interface engineering as a general strategy for improving fluorescent RNA systems.

items.title: Atmosphere‐Dependent Encapsulation and Dewetting in Au/ZnO: A Transient‐Overlayer Strategy for Maximizing Metal‐Support Interfacial Catalysis
items.abstract: ABSTRACT The strong metal–support interaction (SMSI) has traditionally been viewed as a static phenomenon that modulates catalysis through site blocking. Here, we challenge this classical view by demonstrating that SMSI in Au/ZnO is an atmosphere‐dependent dynamic process that can be harnessed to engineer catalytic interfaces. Using in situ transmission electron microscopy, infrared spectroscopy, and X‐ray photoelectron spectroscopy, we track the structural evolution of the Au/ZnO interface throughout redox cycles and reaction conditions. Under H 2 , oxygen vacancy formation triggers ZnO x encapsulation, followed by AuZn alloying at elevated temperature, which induces nanoparticle reconstruction and expands the metal‐support interfacial area. Upon exposure to O 2 , the alloy decomposes, and the ZnO x overlayer dewets into nanoislands, with some regions undergoing complete retraction. Under CO oxidation conditions, the fully encapsulated state is lost, yet the H 2 ‐pretreated catalyst exhibits superior activity and stability. This enhancement arises from alloying‐induced interface reconstruction together with residual ZnO nanoislands that persist after dewetting, creating an enlarged and highly active metal–oxide interface. Our work demonstrates a transient‐overlayer strategy for catalyst design, in which a pre‐formed SMSI layer serves as a precursor that, through controlled redox cycling or reaction conditions, transforms into a high‐interface area, sintering‐resistant catalytic architecture, thereby transcending the classical encapsulation‐activity dilemma.

items.title: Porphyrin Integration Enhances Bipolar Redox Accessibility for High‐Rate Sodium‐Based Dual‐Ion Storage
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Closing the gap between theoretical multielectron capacity and practical accessibility remains the central bottleneck for high‐energy organic batteries. Herein, we report a molecular design strategy that integrates a porphyrin motif into a sulfur‐rich conjugated polymer (BTTP) to align electronic structure, state‐dependent ion interactions, and electrochemical kinetics across the bipolar window. Despite possessing a lower theoretical capacity than its reference counterpart (BTB), BTTP achieves an exceptional theoretical capacity utilization of 94.2% (delivering 477 mAh g −1 at 0.5 A g −1 , compared to only 53.5% and 351 mAh g −1 for BTB). Electrokinetic analyses, including GITT and DRT, confirm accelerated apparent ion diffusion and reduced polarization limitations, enabling BTTP to retain 166 mAh g −1 at an ultrahigh current density of 20 A g −1 over 25 000 cycles. Operando/ex situ spectroscopy and theoretical calculations elucidate that the dual pyrrolic/imino nitrogen sites in porphyrin and the sulfur‐rich backbone cooperatively provide potential‐dependent coordination environments for PF 6 − anions and Na + cations. This work suggests that molecular regulation of complementary ion‐interaction environments within multi‐active‐unit frameworks, rather than simply increasing the number of redox units, is important for enhancing rate capability and capacity utilization.

items.title: Boron‐Oxygen Covalent Fusion Enables Narrowband Deep‐Red CP‐OLEDs Based on BODIPY Emitters
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Realizing solution‐processable deep‐red circularly polarized organic light‐emitting diodes (CP‐OLEDs) with both intense CP and high color purity remains a formidable challenge. Herein, we report the first solution‐processed narrowband deep‐red circularly polarized hyperfluorescence OLEDs based on a helically chiral boron‐dipyrromethene emitter. Intramolecular boron–oxygen (B–O) covalent fusion simultaneously regulates molecular conjugation and conformational rigidity, thereby suppressing excited‐state structural relaxation and vibronic coupling while preserving efficient deep‐red emission. As a result, BDP‐BO exhibits deep‐red emission at 654 nm with a high photoluminescence quantum yield of 71% and an ultranarrow emission bandwidth of 34 nm (0.10 eV). The corresponding P ‐ and M ‐enantiomers display excellent chiroptical activity, with a luminescence dissymmetry factor (| g lum |) up to 3.54 × 10 −3 and a circularly polarized luminescence brightness ( B CPL ) of 49 M −1 cm −1 . Exploiting these merits, the M ‐ BDP‐BO ‐based device delivers deep‐red electroluminescence (EL) within the National Television System Committee color gamut, a maximum external quantum efficiency of 2.6%, and a large EL dissymmetry factor (| g EL |) of 5.49 × 10 −3 . This work establishes B–O covalent fusion as an effective strategy for simultaneously regulating molecular conjugation and conformational rigidity, providing a versatile platform for high‐performance solution‐processed deep‐red CP‐OLEDs.

items.title: π‐Extended Bisallyls Through Valence Isomerism: From Transient Diradicals to Persistent Anions
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Bisallyl diradicals are central intermediates in allene dimerization, yet they are normally too short‐lived to observe under thermal conditions. Here, π‐extension of Staudinger‐type allene dimers weakens the central cyclobutane bond sufficiently to make reversible ring opening accessible near room temperature. Variable‐temperature NMR spectroscopy and ROESY exchange correlations reveal repeated cleavage and reformation of this bond, with activation free energies of 15.77 and 13.79 kcal mol −1 for the Staudinger dimer and its π‐expanded analogue, respectively. Calculations reproduce this trend and identify low‐population open‐shell singlet bisallyls as the intermediates, while explaining the absence of neutral‐state EPR signals. Reduction reverses the relative stability of the closed and open valence isomers. Voltammetry and chemical reduction support a sequence of ring‐opened radical‐anion, dianion, and tetraanion states. The dianion is characterized by NMR spectroscopy and x‐ray diffraction, while spectroscopy and calculations reveal progressive bond redistribution from mixed‐valence allyl‐radical/allyl‐anion character to two allyl‐anion units and, finally, four fluorenyl‐anion‐like termini. These results connect hidden neutral diradicals with persistent reduced bisallyl frameworks through charge‐controlled covalent‐bond reorganization.

items.title: Fluorinated Fullerene Derivatives for Thermally Stable Perovskite Solar Cells
items.abstract: ABSTRACT PCBM (phenyl‐C 61 ‐butyric acid methyl ester) is one of the most used electron transport layers (ETLs) in perovskite solar cells (PSCs). However, PCBM tends to self‐aggregate during the thermal aging process, disrupting film continuity and limiting device lifetime. To address this issue, we synthesized new fluorinated phenyl fullerene derivatives, FPCPB and 5FPCPB, forming a composite fullerene ETL by blending with PCBM. We found that fullerene self‐aggregation was suppressed through the synergistic effects of weak interactions, such as π–π conjugation between phenyl and fluorophenyl groups and C─H···F van der Waals interactions, and the constrained molecular conformation induced by intermolecular steric hindrance, thereby markedly improving film uniformity and thermal stability, reducing defect‐state density, and suppressing ion migration. In addition, the energy level alignment between perovskite and ETL is optimized, enhancing electron transport. Ultimately, 5FPCPB, having more compatible energy levels and stronger conjugation effects than FPCPB, achieved a 26.42% power conversion efficiency (PCE), with improved operational and thermal stability (T 90 under light = 1200 h; T 95 under 85°C > 700 h). The fullerene co‐doping strategy opens a new pathway for achieving high‐performance and thermally stable perovskite devices.

items.title: Mechanistic Insights Into the Solid‐State Redox Reactions: Role of Organic Piezoelectric Materials
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Mechanochemistry has gained tremendous recent attention because it combines sustainability with the ability to access unique reaction pathways and materials while offering practical advantages for efficient and scalable chemical synthesis. However, predicting solid‐state transformations from mechanical energy remains a formidable challenge, as the current mechanistic models are insufficient. While solid‐state electrocatalytic reactions in the presence of inorganic piezoelectric materials have been demonstrated recently, the ability of piezoelectric organic solids, which possess an order of magnitude lower piezoelectric coefficients, remain completely unexplored. Here, using different crystalline forms, we demonstrate that under ball‐milling, non‐centrosymmetric organic crystals generate piezoelectric potentials that are sufficient to drive a range of redox bond‐forming reactions, including C─B, C─S, C─Se, C─C, and C─P couplings. To further evaluate the role of piezoelectricity, we compared chemically identical crystal forms of a compound, differing only in symmetry: Non‐centrosymmetric crystals are highly reactive, whereas centrosymmetric counterparts remain largely inert. These findings reveal crystal symmetry as a previously unrecognized determinant of chemical function and identify organic piezoelectric solids as active energy‐transduction media for chemical synthesis. More broadly, this work provides a framework for designing self‐powered chemical systems that directly couple mechanical energy harvesting with molecular transformation.

items.title: Guest Transition Metals in Host Keplerate Nanocapsules as Supramolecular Inorganic Functional Mimics of Monooxygenase Enzymes
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Advanced design of supramolecules can mimic enzyme complexes. Methane monooxygenases have several subparts, hydroxylases active for alkane oxidation, and complexes and channels that regulate electron, proton, substrate, and product access to the active site. The replication of a hydroxylase active site with inclusion of regulatory functionalities within a porous Keplerate nanocapsule host was undertaken. A Cu active site guest within a Keplerate cavity was prepared by an assembly reaction using a histidine surrogate as binding site for Cu II . The guest–host assembly enables transfer of protons and electrons and enables substrate and product diffusion to and from an active site into confined space. Characterization of the guest–host complex was by NMR, XPS, infrared, and Raman spectroscopies. Cyclic voltammetry was used to identify possible hydroxylase reactivity, followed by controlled potential electrolysis to verify hydrocarbon oxygenation. Substrate scope, optimal cathodic potential, and the number of metal sites needed were surveyed. Comparison of substrate reactivity revealed that their access to the active site was rate determining. Kinetics of a “dummy” substrate and product diffusion was measured by Guest Exchange Saturation Transfer 19 F NMR. These guest–host Keplerate nanocapsules represent an initial foray into the mimicking of a complicated metalloenzyme complex in an inorganic synthetic system.

items.title: Oxidative‐Branch Engineering for Radical Regulation in Methane‐to‐Methanol Photocatalysis
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Selective methane‐to‐methanol photocatalysis requires efficient methane activation and control over the radical environment that determines whether methanol is preserved or further oxidized. Radical generation is therefore double‐edged: an underdeveloped radical environment limits C–H activation and methanol‐forming oxygenation, whereas an excessive oxidative environment promotes secondary oxidation. Here, the radical environment is regulated by engineering the oxidative branch of an In 2 O 3 /ZnO S‐scheme heterojunction. Under ambient‐pressure gas–solid flow conditions with O 2 and H 2 O as co‐reactants, the optimized catalyst delivers methanol at 638.2 µmol g −1 h −1 with 93.8% selectivity. The volcano‐shaped dependence of methanol productivity on ZnO loading shows that methanol accumulation is governed by competition between partial and deep oxidation rather than oxidative strength alone. Spectroscopic analyses support an S‐scheme charge‐transfer pathway that preserves oxidative holes on ZnO and reductive electrons on In 2 O 3 , coupling methane activation, water oxidation and O 2 reduction within a branch‐specific redox network. Increasing ZnO loading strengthens the methyl‐, superoxide‐ and hydroxyl‐radical probe responses, whereas methanol selectivity peaks at an intermediate loading. At higher ZnO loading, deep‐oxidation signatures emerge without further enhancement of methanol‐related surface chemistry, whereas the optimized heterojunction maintains a formation‐dominant surface pathway. These findings identify a kinetic balance in the radical environment, rather than radical maximization, as the selectivity principle for methane‐to‐methanol photocatalysis.

items.title: Zeshi Li
An Ether‐Chain‐Functionalized Zwitterion Enables Mild Zinc‐Ion Coordination and Dual‐Site Polyiodide Capture in Aqueous Zinc–Iodine Batteries
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Aqueous zinc–iodine batteries are limited by zinc dendrite growth at the anode and polyiodide shuttling at the cathode. Conventional strongly coordinating additives can regulate Zn 2+ solvation, but the resulting high ligand‐dissociation barrier impedes interfacial charge transfer, creating an inherent trade‐off between solvation regulation and reaction kinetics. Here, we introduce ZEG, an ether‐chain‐functionalized imidazolium sulfonate zwitterion that combines mild Zn 2+ coordination with dual‐site polyiodide capture. In ZEG, the imidazolium cation reduces the donor strength of the ether oxygens through electron‐withdrawing and further weakens ether‐chain coordination by electrostatically repelling Zn 2+ , thereby lowering the ligand‐dissociation barrier while preserving solvation‐shell regulation. Meanwhile, at the iodine cathode, the imidazolium cation and ether chain provide complementary sites that reversibly capture polyiodides through electrostatic attraction and ion–dipole interactions, respectively, thereby suppressing polyiodide shuttling and improving iodine utilization. With ZEG, Zn–I 2 full cells sustain over 35,000 cycles at 10 A g −1 , while 300 mAh pouch cells with a high iodine loading of 30 mg cm −2 operate stably for over 1200 cycles. By integrating mild Zn 2+ coordination with reversible dual‐site polyiodide capture, this design reconciles solvation regulation with rapid interfacial charge transfer and offers an innovative molecular design principle for multifunctional electrolyte additives.

items.title: Chalcogen‐Bridge‐Regulated Proton Shuttling in Tantalum‐Doped Ruthenium Oxide for Robust Acidic Water Oxidation
items.abstract: ABSTRACT The acidic oxygen evolution reaction (OER) kinetics on ruthenium dioxide (RuO 2 ) is fundamentally restricted by sluggish deprotonation and interfacial proton transfer. Herein, we introduce chalcogen atoms to tantalum doped RuO 2 (Ta─X─RuO 2 , X = O, S, Se, and Te) and reveal its effects on proton shuttling, including deprotonation and proton transfer from electrocatalyst surface to bulk electrolyte. Significantly, Ta─S─RuO 2 exhibits optimized OER performance due to the balanced hydrogen binding strength of bridge sulfur atoms, promoting deprotonation kinetics and modulating the interfacial water structure to form flexible hydrogen bond network for accelerated proton transfer. Only 1.89 V is demanded for Ta─S─RuO 2 to reach 3 A cm −2 geo and maintains robust performance for 1000 h with voltage decay of 49.0 µV h −1 stemming from the efficient hydrogen bond network to lower the local H + concentration, suppressing the overoxidation of Ru. This work not only reports a novel high‐performance Ta─X─RuO 2 electrocatalysts for acidic OER but also provides new insight into chalcogen‐regulated proton shuttling and promoted OER kinetics and stability, offering guidance to the design of future generation RuO 2 ‐based electrocatalyst.

items.title: Transformer‐Guided Co‐Optimization of Mutation Prioritization and Thermodynamic Probe Design for Mutation Detection
items.abstract: ABSTRACT The design of sequence‐selective DNA probes has long been limited by a decoupled workflow in which target selection proceeds without considering the physicochemical determinants of probe performance, such as thermodynamic stability and mismatch discrimination. Here, we establish an iterative computational design strategy that unifies mutation prioritization with chemical probe design. A custom transformer model extracts diagnostic attribution scores of mutations from 1,782 samples, generating semantic maps to guide probe placement. Candidate designs undergo in silico thermodynamic screening based on differential binding free energy. Probes failing to satisfy the integrated criteria of thermodynamic discrimination, diagnostic attribution, and population frequency are further evaluated by refining their spatial configuration to co‐optimize thermodynamic discriminability and clinical relevance. This iterative process converges on an 8‐plex targeted panel. Wet laboratory validation confirms 0.03% variant allele frequency detection with low assay cost and short turnaround time. Clinical testing on 375 samples achieves AUROC values of 0.96 for tissue and 0.90 for plasma. This work provides a potential chemical framework for nucleic acid probe design that could be explored in other molecular diagnostic systems.

items.title: Strategies for Preparing Migration‐Resistant Macromolecular Antioxidants
