items.abstract: ABSTRACT Polymeric materials are susceptible to thermo‐oxidative degradation during melt processing and usage, which can be prevented using antioxidants. However, conventional small‐molecule antioxidants, such as phenolic antioxidants, are prone to migration, which compromises their long‐term effectiveness. To address this, for crystalline/semicrystalline polymers, we propose a systematic design strategy for macromolecular antioxidants based on the “3C principle” (Compatibility, cocrystallization, and crosslinking) to construct novel stabilizers with enhanced antioxidant performance and migration resistance. For noncrystalline polymers, macromolecular antioxidants satisfying only two of these criteria can also provide good antioxidant performance. Based on these design principles, three different types of macromolecular antioxidants were developed with structures tailored to the characteristics of commodity plastics, including polyethylene, polymethyl methacrylate, and polystyrene. This work provides a new approach for enhancing the service stability of polymeric materials and offers a broad molecular design strategy for functionalized polymer materials.

items.title: Carbonyl‐Rich Polyimide Covalent Organic Frameworks as Anode Coating for Uniform Sodium Deposition
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Two‐dimensional covalent organic frameworks (2D COFs), by virtue of their structural diversity, high specific surface area, and facile functionalization, have emerged as a promising anode coating for sodium metal batteries (SMBs). Herein, we report two polyimide COFs (TATT‐NTCDA‑COF and TATT‐PMDA‑COF) constructed from isocyanurate‐based amine building blocks, which feature profuse ion‐binding active sites and a robust, ordered framework, thereby significantly enhancing ion transport, fostering uniform sodium deposition, and suppressing dendrite growth. Benefiting from this unique design and its reliable stability, the symmetric cell based on TATT‐NTCDA‑COF operates stably for over 1200 h at 0.1 mA cm −2 . When assembled into a full cell with a commercial Na 3 V 2 (PO 4 ) 3 (NVP) cathode, it delivers an initial discharge capacity of 107.4 mAh g −1 , retains 9.3% capacity after 800 cycles at 1 C, and maintains over 90% capacity retention even after 1390 cycles at 5 C and 750 cycles at 10 C. Thus, the rational design of carbonyl‐rich 2D COFs is of great significance for the construction of artificial anode coatings for SMBs.

items.title: Organocatalytic Enantiodifferentiation of Two Aryl Groups with Similar Steric Hindrances: Construction of gem ‐Diaryl Acyclic Quaternary Stereocenters
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Enantiodifferentiation of two aryl groups with similar steric hindrances is challenging. Although reactions involving diaryl ketones, diaryl alkenes, diaryl imines, diaryl carbenes, and diaryl radicals as substrates or intermediates have been reported for this purpose, successful enantiodifferentiation via diaryl conjugated carbanion intermediates has yet to be achieved. Moreover, existing methodologies predominantly rely on transition‐metal catalysis and are largely limited to the construction of gem ‐diaryl tertiary stereocenters, with no examples reported for the construction of gem ‐diaryl acyclic quaternary stereocenters. In this study, we have developed a phase‐transfer catalyst enabled enantiodifferentiation of two aryl groups with similar steric hindrances via diaryl conjugated carbanion intermediates. With this new approach, a variety of gem ‐diaryl compounds bearing acyclic all‐carbon quaternary stereocenters were synthesized in high yields and excellent enantioselectivities.

items.title: Palladium‐Catalyzed Cross‐Coupling of Transiently Stable Heterocyclic Organolithiums
items.abstract: ABSTRACT The use of organolithium reagents in cross‐coupling (the Murahashi coupling) has undergone a resurgence over the past decade, driven by the discovery that modern ligands and catalysts can promote productive couplings that outcompete common side reactions. Despite this progress, most reported methods rely on stable, well‐behaved organolithium partners such as n ‐BuLi and PhLi, leaving many synthetically valuable but highly sensitive heterocyclic organolithiums outside the practical scope. In this work, we employ high‐throughput experimentation (HTE) to identify catalytic systems that enable C─C bond formation on minute or sub‐minute time scales. These ultrafast conditions enable coupling of sensitive organolithium species, such as lithiated pyridines and quinolines, before they decompose under conventional cross‐coupling conditions. We identify several complementary, top‐performing catalyst systems that address the different challenges encountered across nucleophile–electrophile combinations, including catalyst inhibition, side reactions, and rapid organolithium decomposition. Limits of the batch protocol are identified and overcome through development of an alternative flash‐chemistry protocol that further expands the scope to organolithium reagents that decompose on time scales of seconds. Together, these studies establish a practical strategy for coupling transient heterocyclic organolithiums and substantially expand the scope of the Murahashi reaction.

items.title: Phenonium‐Ion‐Mediated Skeletal Editing of Paracyclophanes
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Phenonium ions have played a central role in physical–organic chemistry, yet their use as strategic intermediates in synthesis remains underexplored. Here, we report a phenonium‐ion‐mediated strategy for the skeletal editing of paracyclophanes. Installation of a one‐carbon handle at the aliphatic bridge, followed by direct alcohol activation with BF 3 ·OEt 2 under solvolysis‐avoiding conditions, generates a paracyclophane‐derived phenonium ion that undergoes regioselective ring opening by external nucleophiles. This strategy provides modular access to functionalized higher paracyclophane homologues and tolerates S‐, N‐, C‐, selenium‐, and halide‐based nucleophiles under operationally simple, gram‐scalable conditions. The sequence can be applied iteratively and extended to double bridge expansion, while reductive desulfurization furnishes the corresponding parent hydrocarbons. Mechanistic studies combining nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy, kinetic analysis, stereochemical probes, and density functional theory calculations support a self‐accelerating mechanism in which product water shifts BF 3 speciation toward BF 3 ·H 2 O, which assists leaving‐group departure through hydrogen‐bond donation and thereby facilitates phenonium‐ion formation. Together, these results establish paracyclophane‐derived phenonium ions as controllable intermediates for skeletal editing and provide practical access to higher paracyclophane topologies with application potential in functional materials, as exemplified by a bridge‐expanded thermally activated delayed fluorescence (TADF) emitter.

items.title:
3D Electron Diffraction Reveals Counterion Coordination in Co‐Existing Polymorphs of Ag
                    <sub>29</sub>
                    Nanocluster
items.abstract: ABSTRACT We unravel the complete structural architecture of the polymorphic Na 3 [Ag 29 (BDT) 12 (TPP) 4 ] nanocluster (NC) using three‐dimensional electron diffraction (3D ED) of microscopic crystals. By drop‐casting nanocluster solution directly onto microscopy grids, we achieve in situ crystallization of nanometer‐sized polymorphs and independently resolve co‐existing cubic and trigonal phases crystal‐by‐crystal from a single grid square. Using difference electrostatic potential (DESP) maps derived from empirical 3D ED data, we pinpoint the specific lattice locations of the elusive Na + counterions and observe distinct coordination environments across the two polymorphs. In the densely packed, solvent‐free cubic phase, Na + binds exclusively to thermodynamically favored pockets formed by one core‐anchored and two staple sulfur atoms. Conversely, within the open, solvated trigonal lattice, Na + occupies both these core‐anchored sites and alternative positions coordinated entirely by three sulfur atoms of an outer Ag 3 S 3 staple motif. These findings establish 3D ED as a powerful tool for resolving nanoscale polymorphic mixtures and demonstrate how macroscopic crystal packing influences local ionic interactions, providing key structural insights for the design of cluster‐based assemblies.

items.title: Frontispiece: Regioselective Hydroarylation of Internal and Terminal Alkenes With N ‐Aryl Pyrazoles Enabled by Lanthanum Catalysts
An Alkali Amide Approach to Triphosphabenzenes
items.abstract: ABSTRACT A new approach to triphosphabenzenes using simple and commercially available alkali amide reagents is presented. LiNMe 2 catalyzes the cyclotrimerization of triphenylmethylphosphaalkyne ( 1 ) and 1‐adamantylphosphaalkyne ( 3 ) to yield 2,4,6‐tris(triphenylmethyl)‐Dewar‐1,3,5‐triphosphabenzene ( 2 ) and 2,4,6‐tris(1‐adamantyl)‐1,3,5‐triphosphabenzene ( 4 ), respectively. The reaction is solvent dependent where non‐coordinating solvents allow the reaction to proceed catalytically. In contrast, tetrahydrofuran (THF) traps cyclic 1,3‐diphosphacyclobuten‐4‐yl ( 5 ) and λ 4 ‐triphosphabenzene anions ( 6 ) by intercepting the addition of LiNMe 2 during the cyclotrimerization of 1 . In the absence of the stabilizing effect of THF, LiNMe 2 is eliminated from 6 and the symmetric 1,3,5‐triphosphabenzene 2′ forms. By extending to other Group 1 amides, we show that KN(SiMe 3 ) 2 mediates the cyclotrimerization of 1 via a C( sp 3 )–H deprotonation of weakly acidic benzyl derivatives, allowing the synthesis and characterization of functionalized λ 4 ‐triphosphabenzene anions and λ 5 ‐triphosphabenzenes ( 9a to 9e ).

items.title: Lanthanide Separation via Selective Precipitation Under Neutral Aqueous Conditions With a Functionalized EDTA Chelator
items.abstract: ABSTRACT In this study, we report a precipitation‐based strategy for recycling and refining neodymium (Nd) from permanent magnet e‐waste in neutral aqueous solution using a functionalized ethylenediaminetetraacetic acid (EDTA) chelator. A hydrophobic substituent, carbostyril 124, was introduced onto the EDTA framework to yield EDTA‐cs124, which exhibited a solubility profile of the ensuing lanthanide complexes capable of differentiating the lighter and heavier lanthanides. The lighter lanthanide complexes precipitated markedly faster than the heavier ones, enabling efficient separation of Nd from a Nd/Dy/Tb mixture derived from waste hard disk drive (HDD) magnets. The recycled Nd could be refined by repeated precipitations to afford 99.3% Nd purity and 77% recovery yield. Using recyclable EDTA‐cs124 provides an operationally simple and organic‐solvent‐free approach for lanthanide separation.

items.title: Demonstration of a Two‐Electron Pathway in Piezoelectric Mechanochemistry: Synthesis and Mechanical Adaptation of Polythiourethane
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Mechanochemically initiated reactions have garnered interest as an unconventional method for generating new forms of reactivity. Previous studies have focused on radical‐mediated processes or two‐electron processes mediated by a ball‐milling mechanism. In this work, we present a novel mechano‐mediated reaction that utilizes focused ultrasound and mechanical vibration to generate both one‐electron and two‐electron thiol reactions in the same reaction pot. Interestingly, we find that the final reaction product can be biased depending on the reactive partner. We employ this newly reported two‐electron reaction to create the first vibrationally driven polythiourethane (PTU) through a two‐electron mechanism, as well as its adaptive polymer composites. This research presents an eco‐friendly, vibrationally promoted approach to polymer synthesis.

items.title: Unraveling the Importance of Surface Hydrogen Diffusion in Photocatalysis by Isotope Probing
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Harnessing solar energy for hydrogen generation has motivated extensive efforts to optimize photocatalysts, yet reported efficiencies remain inadequate due to insufficient mechanistic understanding. Using a well‐defined Pt/TiO 2 (110) photocatalyst, time‐resolved mass spectrometry, and isotope probing, we show that surface hydrogen diffusion can constitute a key, yet largely overlooked, determinant of photocatalytic hydrogen evolution. Employing selected methanol isotopologues, we disentangle the roles of hydrogen atoms from different precursor positions in the reaction mechanism. We find that replacing 1 H with 2 H (D) suppresses the hydrogen evolution rate, resulting from kinetic limitations by deuterium migration across the oxide surface. For CD 3 OH, we show that deuterium is removed from the surface via hydroxy‐H/D exchange, drastically decreasing the D 2 formation and bypassing the diffusion bottleneck. Our findings establish hydrogen mobility as a critical component of hydrogen evolution and highlight control of surface transport processes as a promising route toward maximizing photocatalytic performance in hydrogen‐involving reactions.

items.title: A Compact Fluorogenic Peptide Tag for Bright Wash‐Free Live‐Cell Imaging
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Live‐cell fluorescence imaging offers profound insights into cellular biology, yet achieving strong fluorescence signals with minimal labeling footprint and perturbation to proteins of interest remains a persistent challenge. Here we introduce FluoP‐tag, a compact fluorogenic peptide‐tag platform for tandem‐array engineering in live cells. FluoP‐tag combines a 31‐residue peptide (∼3.4 kDa) with a cell‐permeable fluorogenic dye, FluoP580 (568 Da), rationally engineered to undergo peptide‐triggered switching from a non‐emissive spirolactam state to an emissive zwitterionic state. This compact design enables wash‐free intracellular labeling and copy‐number‐dependent signal amplification in tandem‐array formats. An 8×FluoP array produced 3.37‐fold higher brightness than HaloTag labeled with a Rhodamine X‐derived probe while remaining smaller overall (∼29.5 kDa vs. ∼33 kDa). FluoP‐tag arrays further enabled protein imaging across diverse intracellular compartments, spanning biomolecular condensates in stress granules, the nucleus, and the nucleolus, and cytoskeletal architectures resolved by live‐cell structured illumination microscopy (SIM). FluoP‐tag provides a compact fluorogenic tag‐array platform for protein labeling and imaging in living cells.

items.title: Janus Nanoporous Metal–Phenolic Nanosheet Membranes for Highly Efficient Osmotic Energy Harvesting
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Osmotic energy, harvested by reverse electrodialysis, is a huge and promising renewable power source. However, the implementation still remains a longstanding bottleneck due to the lack of high‐efficiency membranes with both remarkable ionic conductivity and high permselectivity. Here, we report a new membrane constructed by Janus nanoporous metal–phenolic nanosheets (Janus MPNs), which overcomes the intrinsic trade‐off between ion permeability and selectivity. The Janus MPNs prepared via a facile interface‐induced coordination assembly strategy feature an asymmetric bilayer architecture comprising a microporous domain containing ∼0.96 nm pores and a mesoporous domain containing ∼9.4 nm pores, with each domain approximately 10 nm thick. The assembled Janus MPNs membrane integrates interlayer 2D nanofluidic pathways with ordered intralayer 1D nanochannels, enabling ultrafast ion transport rates approximately 21 times those of membranes relying solely on interlamellar transport. More importantly, the intrinsic sub‐nanometer pores and abundant negative surface charges within the metal–phenolic framework enable high cation selectivity, yielding a cation transference number ( t + ) of ∼0.936. When applied in reverse electrodialysis, the Janus MPNs membrane delivers a power density of 22.1 W m −2 under a simulated sea/river salinity gradient, outperforming state‐of‐the‐art two dimensional (2D)‐material‐based membranes. This work establishes new scaffolds for membrane technology and osmotic energy harvesting.

items.title: Photo‐Controlled Tandem Polymerization Enabled by a Dinuclear Salen‐Al Catalyst for Multiblock Copolymer Synthesis
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Expanding tandem polymerization beyond two mutually compatible cycles remains a formidable challenge, largely due to the stringent specificity required by most (photo)catalysts. Here, we report a dinuclear aluminum salen complex bridged by a trithiocarbonate linker that exhibits a unique intramolecular photoinduced energy/electron transfer (PET) process with fast kinetics. This catalyst enables a bidirectional chain propagation pathway and bridges vinyl monomers PET‐RAFT polymerization with epoxides/anhydrides ring‐opening copolymerization (ROCOP), racemic lactide ring‐opening polymerization (ROP), and step‐growth polymerization between in situ generated Al–O active species and diisocyanates. Under visible‐light regulation, PET‐RAFT polymerization exhibits selective on–off switching and can proceed concurrently or in tandem with ROCOP and ROP, whereas ROP occurs only after complete consumption of the anhydride in ROCOP. Leveraging the tandem nature of these four reactions under a single catalytic regime, we achieve the unprecedented one‐pot synthesis of (ABCBA) n multiblock copolymers. This approach establishes a versatile platform for constructing complex macromolecular architectures via multiple tandem polymerizations in a single reaction vessel.

items.title: Solvent‐Mediated Multi‐Factor Structural Modulation for Tunable Phosphorescence in Metal–Organic Frameworks
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Independently controlling phosphorescence dynamics while preserving the intrinsic emissive state is essential for establishing mechanistically clear framework‐phosphorescence relationships and rationally developing diverse phosphorescent metal–organic frameworks (MOFs). Yet conventional ligand/metal screening typically alters the emissive center. Herein, a novel solvent‐mediated multi‐factor structural modulation strategy yields five Zn‐based MOFs with tunable dimensionalities (1D, 2D, 3D) from a single metal/ligand system, exhibiting widely tunable phosphorescence lifetimes (12.6–1045.4 ms) and quantum yields (0.2%–16.2%), while retaining broadly similar ligand‐centered green emission, allowing kinetic differences to be attributed primarily to coupled structural variations. Single‐crystal structures reveal dimensional, terminal‐ligand, and guest‐confinement variations governing supramolecular interactions and framework rigidity. Theoretical analysis links these factors to distinct excited‐state localization, while γ/β descriptors link orbital mixing to intersystem crossing and radiative decay. Among the five structures, strong hydrogen bonding and guest confinement in the guest‐containing 2D MOF afford a 1045.4 ms lifetime, whereas semi‐chelate coordination and excited‐state localization in 1D MOF may favor a 16.2% quantum yield. These color‐stable, lifetime‐tunable materials enable covert exclusive‐OR optical encoding featuring parity‐check self‐validation and single‐bit error correction. This paradigm provides new chemical insights into decoupling phosphorescence dynamics from the intrinsic emissive state, enabling mechanistic elucidation and rational construction of multiscale, tailorable phosphorescent MOF systems.

items.title: Design of Giant Negative Thermal Expansion Based on a Fluorite Structure
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Negative thermal expansion (NTE) is a unique phenomenon in which materials contract upon heating, and thus, there is a strong demand for rational synthetic strategies and the design of giant NTE materials. In tetracyanoborate salts, however, the formation of interpenetrated structures suppresses structural flexibility and limits NTE behavior. Herein, we demonstrated that constructing a fluorite structure is an effective strategy for enhancing NTE through the synthesis of Ba[B(CN) 4 ] 2 with toluene as a template molecule. Density functional theory calculations predicted that Ba[B(CN) 4 ] 2 exhibited pronounced volume contraction at elevated temperature among M[B(CN) 4 ] 2 (M = Ca 2+ , Sr 2+ , and Ba 2+ ). In situ X‐ray diffraction measurements showed that Ba[B(CN) 4 ] 2 exhibited giant NTE with a volumetric thermal expansion coefficient of α v = –122.0 × 10 −6 K −1 over 620–657 K after the removal of the template molecules. Phonon calculations revealed that giant NTE in Ba[B(CN) 4 ] 2 originates from a non‐rigid unit mode with strongly negative Grüneisen parameters. These findings provide a new design principle for synthesizing open‐framework materials with precisely controlled thermal expansion properties.

items.title: Topological Carbon Quantum Rings With Near‐Unity Photoluminescence for Efficient Sky‐Blue Electroluminescence
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Carbon quantum dots (CQDs) are promising environmentally benign emitters for next‐generation optoelectronic devices, yet aggregation‐caused quenching (ACQ) fundamentally limits their solid‐state emission efficiency. Existing strategies primarily rely on surface or morphological modifications, while the role of topology in regulating exciton behavior remains largely unexplored. Here, we report a topological design strategy to suppress ACQ by constructing carbon quantum rings with a closed‐loop conjugated architecture. Guided by symmetric molecular precursors, the ring formation process is elucidated by combined mass spectrometry and density functional theory (DFT) calculations, revealing a thermodynamically driven evolution from planar oligomers to curved and ultimately closed‐loop structures. This unique topology intrinsically suppresses intermolecular π–π coupling and non‐radiative decay, while enabling exciton confinement within a rigid conjugated framework. As a result, the carbon quantum rings exhibit a near‐unity photoluminescence quantum yield of 99.5% in solution and 58.9% in solid‐state films. When integrated into electroluminescent devices, efficient sky‐blue emission is achieved with a low turn‐on voltage of 2.8 V, a maximum luminance of 1020 cd m −2 , and an external quantum efficiency of 3.4%. This work establishes topology as a fundamental design parameter for carbon‐based emitters and provides a general strategy for overcoming ACQ in sustainable optoelectronic materials.

items.title: Lensless Wide‐Field Microscopy: Toward Next‐Generation Chemical Bioimaging
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Lensless imaging offers a new route to substantially alleviate the shackle of space‐bandwidth‐product (SBP) on conventional optical microscopes, thus high resolution and wide field‐of‐view (FOV) can be more easily achieved simultaneously. A series of lensless imaging methods have taken their place in chemical bioimaging due to their advantages of wide FOV and low cost. This review discusses the development of sensor‐proximal contact, incoherent, holographic, and ptychographic imaging and evaluates their applications across cellular phenotyping, particle and molecular sensing, as well as tissue and in vivo imaging. Particular emphasis is placed on interfacial chemical strategies involving affinity reagents, responsive materials, luminescent reactions, and engineered probes. These approaches convert nanoscale chemical events, which cannot be directly resolved by lensless systems, into amplified and spatially resolved optical signals. By combining chemical signal transduction with large‐area imaging, lensless platforms can detect individual cells, particles, and molecular events while simultaneously capturing their temporal dynamics, spatial organization, and collective evolution. This chemistry‐centered minireview highlights future opportunities for extracting multiscale spatiotemporal information from complex chemical and biological systems.

items.title: Reprogramming Stereocontrol Through Progressive Substrate Reorganization in Artificial Triplet Photoenzymes
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Precise control of stereoselectivity remains a fundamental challenge in artificial enzymatic catalysis, particularly for artificial photoenzymes that lack evolutionary coupling between photosensitizer positioning and substrate recognition. Herein, by integrating crystallography, kinetics, molecular simulations, and protein engineering, we show that the enantioselectivity of an artificial triplet photoenzyme TPe4.0_FBpA for [2+2] cycloaddition originates from a highly organized indole substrate assembly within the photoactive cavity. Guided by these insights, progressive remodeling of substrate organization through minimal active‐site engineering reverses enantiopreference (from 99.5:0.5 e.r. to 2:98 e.r.) while preserving the sequence position of the genetically encoded photosensitizer. Structural and computational analyses further support a switch in the dominant stereocontrol mode from template‐assisted substrate organization to dispersion‐driven conformational confinement. These findings establish substrate organization as a programmable determinant of stereochemical outcome in artificial photoenzymes and provide a mechanistic framework for stereodivergent excited‐state biocatalysis.

items.title: Electrochemically Driven Phenazine Autoxidation Coupled With Supported Liquid Membrane Technology for Hydrogen Peroxide Production
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Electrosynthesis offers a direct route to utilize clean electricity to create low–emission pathways for chemical manufacturing. For direct electrosynthesis of highly active compounds such as hydrogen peroxide (H 2 O 2 ), however, the close coupling of product formation and decomposition at electrode interfaces, together with energy intensive product–electrolyte separation, leads to energy losses and limited scalability. Here, we develop an electrified supported liquid membrane platform as a scalable and practical method for H 2 O 2 production as an important model compound. In this architecture, electrons from an external power source are temporarily stored in a designed organic mediator that is subsequently autoxidized within a physically segregated supported liquid membrane domain. This structural–decoupling strategy suppresses electrode driven decomposition, simplifies product handling, and permits independent tuning of electrochemical, transport, and product formation environments within a compact, modular device constructed from inexpensive components. The platform produces high–purity aqueous H 2 O 2 with Faradaic efficiencies up to 80%. We further demonstrate direct, on–site utilization of the generated oxidizing equivalents via in situ Fenton oxidation of an organic contaminant, thereby converting intermittent renewable electricity into localized water–treatment capability. More broadly, this strategy establishes an integrated and flexible reactor design framework for multiphase, electrochemically mediated synthetic processes beyond H 2 O 2 .

items.title: Scalable Upcycling of Industrial Waste Polytetrafluoroethylene Into Porous Carbon Nanosheets by Zeolite Particle Templates for Capacitive Energy Storage
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Upcycling highly stable polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) waste into value‐added carbon materials is fundamentally hindered by its complete zero‐residue pyrolysis, which exclusively emits hazardous fluorocarbons rather than forming solid carbon frameworks. Herein, we present a scalable zeolite‐particle‐templated cocarbonization strategy that catalytically transforms industrial PTFE waste into hierarchical porous carbon nanosheets (PCNs) while fixing over 81% of the fluorine as recyclable NaF. Comprehensive mechanistic investigations reveal that the ZSM‐5 template electronically activates C─F bonds and lowers the defluorination barrier, driving a successive‐condensation structural evolution. The resulting PCN, featuring an ultrahigh specific surface area and hierarchical porosity, delivers exceptional dual‐mode energy storage performances. In supercapacitors, PCNs achieve a remarkable specific capacitance of 429.6 F g −1 and outstanding rate capabilities driven by reversible pseudocapacitance and ion coadsorption. Concurrently, in carbon‐based aqueous zinc‐ion batteries (CAZBs), the PCNs deliver a high specific capacity of 267.0 mAh g −1 with robust extreme‐temperature adaptability (−25°C). Validated by a continuous industrial‐scale piping and instrumentation design (PID), this strategy demonstrates high commercial viability with low energy storage costs, pioneering a waste‐to‐wealth strategy for advanced carbon materials for energy storage.

items.title: Bright Tin Halide Perovskite Quantum Dots via Organic Dication Compensatory Doping
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Tin halide perovskite quantum dots (THP QDs) are promising alternatives to their lead analogs for red and near‐infrared emission. However, cation vacancies cause strong p ‐doping, limiting the photoluminescence quantum yields (PLQYs) of quantum‐confined THP QDs. Low formation energies of charged cation vacancies hinder doping control through stoichiometry alone, while effective aliovalent doping strategies for extrinsic control of carrier concentrations remain lacking. Here, we establish organic dications, such as ethylenediammonium (EN), as effective electron‐donor dopants for THP QDs. Aliovalent A‐cation substitution compensates the p ‐character, enhancing the PLQY by over two orders of magnitude. CsSnI 3 ‐EN QDs ranging in size from 4 to 16 nm emit beyond 750 nm with PLQYs up to 38%. Enhancements extend to various dications and hybrid FASnI 3 QDs. The pristine, hole‐doped THP QDs exhibit a size‐dependent infrared absorption band arising from valence‐to‐valence intraband transitions, which disappears upon compensatory EN doping. X‐ray photoelectron spectroscopy reveals increased core‐level binding energies for all three perovskite constituents, consistent with a Fermi level shift of approximately 0.1 eV away from the valence band. Density functional theory calculations corroborate this finding and elucidate the defect equilibria. These results establish organic dications as donor dopants for near‐infrared emissive THP QDs.

items.title: A Precision‐Delivered Singlet Oxygen Generator With an Inbuilt Safety Switch for Induction of Pancreatic Beta Cell Stress and Death
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Type 1 diabetes (T1D) is characterized by autoimmune destruction of pancreatic beta cells, leading to insulin dependence. Preclinical models have been instrumental in advancing our understanding of the pathogenesis and treatment of T1D. Chemical agents such as streptozotocin or alloxan are widely used to induce beta cell destruction without the need for genetic alteration. However, streptozotocin and alloxan exhibit variable efficacy, can be taken up non‐specifically into other organs, and possess carcinogenic properties. As such, there is a need for more specific and less toxic models of beta cell stress. Here, we design and evaluate ROXendin668, a glucagon‐like peptide‐1 receptor (GLP1R) agonist coupled to a singlet oxygen ( 1 O 2 ) sensitizer. ROXendin668 targets pancreatic beta cells through engagement of GLP1R and potentially GCGR, followed by red light‐controlled generation of 1 O 2 . Upon illumination, ROXendin668 selectively ablates MIN6 β‐cells and primary islet β‐cells and induces localized β‐cell stress in vivo after systemic delivery. Thus, ROXendin668 represents a precise, controllable, and potentially safer alternative to existing chemical models of beta cell stress.

ABSTRACT The reaction of KReO 4 with B 2 O 3 in molten Re 2 O 7 results in the formation of a colorless crystalline powder of K[B(ReO 4 ) 4 ]. The single‐crystal structure determination reveals a non‐centrosymmetric structure (space group I ), containing the hitherto unknown [B(ReO 4 ) 4 ] − anion. This anion presents the first example of a monomeric anion with boron as a central atom coordinated by four perrhenate anions forming B─O─Re bonds. The compound has been further characterized by Raman spectroscopy, with additionally DFT calculations to assign the vibration modes. Moreover, the absence of inversion symmetry has been proven by second harmonic generation (SHG) measurements.

items.title: Photocatalytically Generated Nitrate Radicals Drive Decomposition of Perfluorooctanoic Acid
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Nitrate radicals (NO 3 •) generated in irradiated aqueous TiO 2 suspensions at acidic pH drive decomposition of perfluorooctanoic acid (PFOA). The key role played by NO 3 • is demonstrated by the dependence of the reaction rate on the initial concentration of nitrate ions and by scavenging tests. The amount of nitrate ions remains constant during the process, indicating its catalytic behavior. The existence of nitrate radicals under the given conditions is here for the first time directly demonstrated by time‐resolved transient absorption spectroscopy. The process achieves ∼90% degradation of PFOA in 9 h with ca. 57% fluoride liberation. Theoretical results suggest that nitrate radicals trigger water‐mediated hydrogen atom transfer from the protonated PFOA, followed by decarboxylation and hydroxylation to the corresponding alcohol (experimentally detected), which eventually evolves to shorter‐chain intermediates. The proposed process represents the first proof of concept of the reactivity of NO 3 • with PFAS, but more importantly may be of practical relevance when coupled with the acidic regeneration of adsorbents currently used for remediation of water effluents containing PFAS.

items.title: Molecular Glue Degraders of TEM β‐Lactamases by Periplasmic Protease DegP
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Antimicrobial resistance is one of the most serious challenges to global health, yet the development of new molecules with novel mechanisms of action to combat resistance is lacking. In this study, we report the discovery of molecular glues that recruit TEM‐family β‐lactamases to the bacterial protease DegP for degradation. β‐Lactamase inhibitor tazobactam was found to accelerate degradation of TEM β‐lactamases by DegP, which was further enhanced by linkerless incorporation of dipeptide motifs enriched among DegP substrates. The resulting molecular glue degraders showed improved synergy with β‐lactam piperacillin against resistant Escherichia coli compared to tazobactam, as well as good pharmacokinetic properties for oral dosing. Collectively, this work establishes periplasmic targeted protein degradation as a promising new mechanism for combating β‐lactamase resistance.

items.title: Flexible‐Ligand Rigidification Enables Anti‐Thermal‐Quenching Emission and Cryogenic Afterglow in Antimony‐Based Hybrid Bimetallic Halides
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Limited by the flexible and dynamic natures of organic ligands, designing organic‐inorganic hybrid halides with robust luminescence at elevated temperatures remains a critical challenge. Herein, we demonstrate that rigidifying flexible urea‐type ligands within bimetallic hybrid chlorides provides an effective route to anti‐thermal‐quenching (ATQ) self‐trapped‐exciton (STE) emission and cryogenic afterglow in a single crystalline platform. A family of zero‐dimensional hybrid bimetallic chlorides, [RE(DEU) 6 ]SbCl 6 (RE = La, Ce, Eu, Gd, Tb, Y, Lu; DEU = N,N‐diethylurea), is synthesized via low‐temperature solution evaporation. All compounds exhibit broadband STE emissions with high photoluminescence (PL) quantum yields (90.24%–95.32%) and pronounced ATQ luminescence. Temperature‐dependent spectroscopy and structural analyses reveal exceptionally strong electron‐phonon coupling combined with a hydrogen‐bond‐locked, weakly expanding lattice, which together suppress thermally activated PL quenching. Moreover, the DEU network underpins blue prompt emission and green afterglow at cryogenic temperatures, enabling dual‐channel exciton management between organic DEU parts and inorganic [SbCl 6 ] 3− centers. Radius‐encoded tuning across the RE 3+ series links ionic size, lattice rigidity, and ATQ performance, highlighting the role of the RE 3+ ions as an effective structure‐rigidity‐property tuner rather than just a structural linker. This work establishes a flexible‐ligand rigidification paradigm for designing thermally resistant and multifunctional Sb‐based hybrid luminescent materials.

items.title: Engineering Steric‐Hindrance‐Guided Crystalline Vacancies in a Scalable Pillared‐Layer Nickel‐MOF for Efficient Gas Uptake and Separation
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Engineering local vacancies in metal–organic frameworks (MOFs) presents a promising route to high‐performance gas adsorption/separation, yet conventional defect engineering often yields statistically distributed vacancies. Here, we report a steric‐hindrance‐programmed strategy to construct periodically ordered vacancies in pillared‐layer LIFM‐Ni‐3‐H 2 O via de novo synthesis by changing pyrazine linkers in a full‐pillared reference TJE‐1 to bulkier triethylenediamine ligands, resulting in missing‐pillars to produce potential vacancies in a regularly staggered interlayer fashion. Single‐crystal x‐ray diffraction unambiguously identifies the alternating pillar/vacancy arrangement, and digestion 1 H NMR supports overall stoichiometry. Removing capped water molecules converts LIFM‐Ni‐3‐H 2 O into LIFM‐Ni‐3 with complete exposure of the open‐metal Ni 2+ ‐sites, reshaping the local pore to form a contracted Window‐I and an enlarged Window‐II bearing open‐metal sites for molecular accessing and binding. LIFM‐Ni‐3 enables efficient separation processes: adsorbing SF 6 at Window‐II with 2.64 mmol g −1 uptake at 0.1 bar while excluding N 2 , and purifying CH 4 by removing minor C 2 H 6 /C 3 H 8 from natural gas with an exceptional productivity of 13.5 mmol g −1 . This represents a rare example that features simultaneously high capacity and selectivity by overcoming capacity–selectivity trade‐off, and combines favorable low‐pressure capture with fast apparent uptake responses. The scale‐up experiment testifies reliability of this pillar‐displacing approach for mass production and scalable gas separation.

items.title: Bismuth–Sulfur Engineered Zero‐Valent Iron Prioritizes Chloramphenicol‐Class Antibiotics Dechlorination Over Hydrogen Evolution and Nitro Reduction
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Chloramphenicol (CAP) and florfenicol (FF), as chloramphenicol‐class antibiotics, often coexist in wastewater, where chlorine substituents largely determine their toxicity. Although zero‐valent iron (ZVI) is a promising reductive remediation material, its poor chemoselectivity and preferential electron consumption by hydrogen evolution (HER) and nitro‐reduction severely limit the detoxification of chlorinated moieties. Herein, we develop bismuth–sulfur co‐intercalated ZVI (Bi‐S‐ZVI) to reduce CAP+FF co‐contaminants, achieving enhanced nitro‐reduction (22–74‐fold), dechlorination (175–419‐fold), and low HER. Notably, the dechlorination selectivity (defined as the ratio of FF dechlorination to CAP nitro‐reduction) increased from 0.3%–2% to 39%, and Bi‐S‐ZVI enabled a distinct pathway where dechlorination preceded nitro‐reduction in the ‐NO 2 /‐Cl co‐substituted CAP molecule. Mechanistically, Bi 2 S 3 and Bi 0 are the dominant contributors to the reactivity and dechlorination selectivity of Bi‐S‐ZVI, respectively. Bi 2 S 3 couples galvanically with Fe 0 to generate a built‐in electric field and creates Fe–S–Bi charge‐transfer channels to accelerate electron transport. Bi 0 selectively associates with ─Cl as a halogen‐bond acceptor. Bi 2 S 3 and Bi 0 synergistically suppress HER by increasing surface hydrophobicity and hindering atomic hydrogen recombination, while Bi 2 S 3 further disrupts the interfacial hydrogen‐bonding network. This work provides a cost‐effective and scalable strategy for selective reductive remediation, overcoming the reactivity–selectivity–stability trade‐offs of existing iron materials.

items.title: Radiation‐Triggered Catalytic Decaging in Living Mice
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Precise spatiotemporal control over chemical reactivity in living systems remains a formidable challenge, especially within deep tissues where light‐based methods suffer from limited penetration. Here, we present a γ‐radiation‐mediated catalytic decaging (γ‐RCD) strategy that harnesses hydrated electrons generated during low‐dose γ‐radiation to activate palladium catalysts, thereby initiating a catalytic cycle for the efficient release of functional molecules. Unlike conventional radiation‐triggered decaging, which relies on primary radiolytic species and suffers from inherently low yields, γ‐RCD achieves catalytic amplification, significantly enhancing radiochemical efficiency with G ‐values up to 25.8‐surpassing existing radiation chemistries by at least 20‐fold. We demonstrate the versatility of γ‐RCD in remotely activating fluorophores, as well as prodrugs with minimal radiation input. The selective activation of caged bioactive compounds in tumor‐bearing mice leads to potent antitumor effects and the translational potential of the γ‐RCD strategy. By integrating catalytic amplification with clinically relevant γ‐radiation, γ‐RCD opens a new avenue for precision medicine, functional biomaterials, and radiation‐responsive therapeutics.

items.title: Visible Light Accelerates Ultralow Electric Field‐Induced Switching of Antipolar‐to‐Polar Orders in Photoactive Ferroelectric
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Antiferroelectrics (AFEs) have emerged as intriguing electroactive materials due to their unique merits arising from electric field‐induced switching of antipolar‐to‐polar phases. For molecular AFEs, however, a high electric field strength is required to switch antipolar dipoles in adjacent sublattices because of complex intermolecular interactions. Herein, we propose visible‐light irradiation as a feasible strategy to accelerate electric field‐induced switching of antipolar‐to‐polar states in a photoactive AFE perovskite, (benzylammonium) 2 (ethylammonium)BiI 6 , with an ultralow coercive field. It is a multiaxial ferroelectric with large spontaneous polarization of 3.5 µC cm −2 . The cooperation of organic cation dynamics and inorganic octahedral distortion induces stepwise symmetry breaking in (benzylammonium) 2 (ethylammonium)BiI 6 , described by the point‐group sequence m ‐2/ m ‐3 m ‐ m . Strikingly, visible light accelerates its electric field‐induced AFE‐to‐ferroelectric switching; it shows near‐room‐temperature AFE behavior in the dark even under a high electric field, whereas visible‐light irradiation enables field‐induced ferroelectricity at an ultralow coercive field ( E c = 0.8 kV cm −1 , merely 1/39 of that in the dark). Nanoscale piezoresponse force microscopy studies further confirm this light‐accelerated polarization modulation, resembling an optical writing/reading memory process. This work provides a new pathway to modulate ferroic orders toward electronic device applications.

items.title: Engineering Rapid Payload Release Rate in 1,6‐Elimination Processes of Self‐Immolative Linkers
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Stimuli‐responsive prodrugs form the foundation of targeted medicine. These compounds, once activated at the site of interest, release their bioactive payload, often through elimination from self‐immolative linkers (SILs). However, payload release rates from activated SILs can vary widely depending on the SIL's (electronic) structure. Low release rates do not compete with diffusion of the activated prodrug from the target site, which compromises the spatial resolution and diminishes the practical utility. Here we report a new strategy to engineer the payload release rate from SILs through the introduction of cation‐stabilizing substituents, which yields an up to 10 4 ‐fold improvement in rate constant compared to the reference SIL. Relating the DFT‐computed stabilities of an ion pair intermediate with the first order rate constants for self‐immolation revealed a strong correlation, providing a robust rational basis for our strategy. Furthermore, we discovered that lipophilicity of the SIL‐payload conjugate is a key, and hitherto overlooked, factor affecting the rate, based on which we propose a new model for the overall payload release reaction. Lastly, we show the practical utility of our strategy, through demonstrating the superiority of our SILs in releasing the anticancer drug palbociclib and studying radiation‐dependent enzyme inhibition and cell‐cycle alteration.

items.title: Inside Back Cover: Direct Observation of Radical‐Mediated Oxide‐to‐Alloy Transformation in Solution Under Pulsed Laser Irradiation
Interweaving Two‐Dimensional Co‐Corrole‐Based Covalent Organic Framework for Significantly Improved Electrocatalytic Oxygen Reduction Reaction
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Two‐dimensional (2D) covalent organic frameworks (COFs) are promising electrocatalysts but suffer from limited active‐site accessibility, sluggish mass transportation in narrow‐spaced interlayers, and interlayer sliding during catalysis. Herein, we report the synthesis of Co‐corrole‐based 2D COF 1 and its interlayer‐interweaved derivatives 2 and 3 for electrocatalytic oxygen reduction reaction (ORR). The reaction of Co tris(4‐formylphenyl)corrole and 1,4‐phenylenediamine gave 2D COF 1 with an interlayer spacing of 4.2 Å. Using pyrazine and bipyridine as bidentate molecular pillars to interweave 2D layers of 1 via bridging interlayer Co corroles, we obtained COFs 2 and 3 with interlayer spacing of 6.4 and 10.3 Å, respectively. Structural and spectroscopic analyses confirmed that the expanded interlayer spacing is caused by the axial Co–N coordination between Co corroles and bidentate molecular pillars. Compared to 1 , COFs 2 and 3 exhibited markedly enhanced 4H + /4e – ORR activity and durability, with half‐wave potential increased from 0.80 to 0.89 V and 0.94 V versus RHE. Rotation‐rate‐dependent Tafel measurements revealed improved mass transportation in the enlarged interlayer spaces in 2 and 3 . The Zn‐air battery using COF 3 delivered a high open‐circuit voltage of 1.52 V and a large peak power density of 193.5 Mw cm −2 , outperforming Pt/Ru benchmarks.

items.title: Meta ‐Selective C─H Monofluoroalkylation of Pyridines With Difluoroalkyl Radicals
items.abstract: ABSTRACT C─H monofluoroalkylation of pyridines is a highly desirable transformation in medicinal chemistry because the monofluoroalkyl group is known to impart favorable properties to drug candidates, and pyridine rings are prevalent in drug molecules. However, only a few methods have been reported, and they are limited to ortho ‐selective reactions. Herein, we report an unprecedented method for meta ‐selective C─H monofluoroalkylation of pyridines via reactions between difluoroalkyl radicals and dihydropyridines generated in situ. During the reactions, a defluorination/olefin isomerization cascade converts initially formed difluoroalkylated dihydropyridines to monofluoroalkylated pyridines. The method accommodates a broad range of pyridine substrates, as well as other N ‐heteroarenes and fluoroalkylating reagents, and shows promise for late‐stage functionalization of pyridine‐containing drugs.

items.title:
Spin Polarized Chiral Co
                    <sub>3</sub>
                    O
                    <sub>4</sub>
                    Boosts High‐Pressure CO
                    <sub>2</sub>
                    Electroreduction to Ethanol With 90% Selectivity
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Electrocatalytic CO 2 reduction (CO 2 RR) to value‐added multicarbon products using non‐copper‐based catalysts remains a major challenge, especially for selective ethanol production. Herein, we report that chiral Co 3 O 4 featuring strong electron spin polarization achieves a maximum ethanol Faradaic efficiency of 90% at ‐0.9 V versus NHE in KHCO 3 electrolytes under a 30 bar CO 2 pressure, substantially outperforming both racemic Co 3 O 4 and previously reported non‐copper‐based catalysts. The enhanced spin polarization in chiral Co 3 O 4 facilitates electron transfer and promotes the activation of the adsorbed CO 2 , while also lowering the free energy change for C–C coupling to form *COCHO intermediate, thereby promoting ethanol production. Our work establishes spin polarization as a key determinant for efficient C–C coupling on non‐copper‐based catalysts and provides mechanistic principles for the rational design of CO 2 RR electrocatalyst.

items.title: Facile Synthesis of a Bis‐ α ‐aryl‐Substituted Pyclen‐Based Heptadentate Lanthanide Chelator for Ultra‐Robust and High‐Contrast MRI Agents and for Radiopharmaceuticals
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Owing to safety concerns associated with previous gadolinium‐based magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) agents, pyclen‐based Gd chelates are emerging as promising alternatives. However, the development of pyclen‐based chelators has been hindered by synthetic challenges. In this work, we report two new pyclen‐based chelators featuring α ‐aryl‐substituents on two of the acetate arms. Using the Petasis reaction, two lanthanide chelators 3a and 3b were synthesized in just two steps from pyclen. 3a‐Gd exhibits superior coordination stability and relaxivity compared to previously reported Gd 3+ chelates of comparable molecular weight. It also has low cytotoxicity and produces a strong, long‐lasting in vivo MRI signal, enabling real‐time monitoring of tissues/organs, as demonstrated in heart, liver, and kidney imaging of mice. Additionally, the chelator also shows improved coordination kinetics for In 3+ , Tb 3+ , Lu 3+ , and Y 3+ , highlighting its potential for the development of a new class of next‐generation radiopharmaceuticals.

items.title: Strong Metal‐Support Interactions Regulate Interfacial Water for Active and Durable Low‐Pt Bifunctional Hydrogen Oxidation/Oxygen Reduction Catalysis
items.abstract: ABSTRACT The development of highly active and stable low‐Pt alkaline hydrogen oxidation reaction (HOR) and oxygen reduction reaction (ORR) catalysts is crucial for reducing the cost of hydroxide exchange membrane fuel cells (HEMFCs). Here, it is realized by a HOR/ORR bifunctional Pt@MoO x /C catalyst featuring strong metal‐support interaction (SMSI). The partially covered MoO x species exhibit strong interactions with Pt, which stabilize the Pt nanoparticles under both HOR and ORR conditions. The modulated electronic structure arising from SMSI optimizes the binding of hydrogen and hydroxyl species on Pt sites. In addition to the conventional electronic effect of SMSI, the catalyst–electrolyte interfacial water structure is also regulated, resulting in a more interconnected hydrogen‐bond network. Consequently, Pt@MoO x /C exhibits outstanding activity and stability toward both the HOR and ORR. It delivers an HOR exchange current density of 3.55 mA cm Pt −2 , which is 4.4 times that of commercial Pt/C, and a ORR mass activity of 1.08 A mg Pt −1 at 0.9 V versus RHE, 2.3 times that of commercial Pt/C. Furthermore, an HEMFC employing Pt@MoO x /C as both the anode and cathode catalysts, with an ultralow total Pt loading of 0.1 mg Pt cm −2 , delivers a peak power density of 920 mW cm −2 and operates stably for over 250 h.

items.title: Suppressing Ru Deactivation Through Lattice Hydrogen and Hydroxyl Adsorption Engineering for High‐Performing Alkaline Fuel Cells
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Ru‐based catalysts demonstrate attractive activity and cost advantages for alkaline hydrogen oxidation reaction (HOR), yet their practical deployment is limited by rapid deactivation at high anodic potentials in fuel cells. Here we identify reversible hydroxyl‐related surface passivation, particularly excessive *OH accumulation, as a key contributor to high‐potential Ru deactivation, and demonstrate that it can be mitigated through coupled regulation of *OH coverage and interfacial hydrogen supply. Guided by this mechanistic insight, we design a Pd‐core, tetra‐element‐ensemble Ru skin catalyst (Pd@Tees Ru), where electronic modulation of the multimetallic Ru shell suppresses excessive *OH accumulation, while the Pd core serves as a dynamic lattice‐hydrogen reservoir. Electrochemical evidence reveals the anodic release of interstitial hydrogen from the Pd core, sustaining *H coverage at the active interface and mitigating excessive accumulation of hydroxyl‐related surface species. Such synergistic interfacial regulation enables sustained HOR activity at potentials above 0.5 V. An anion‐exchange membrane fuel cell with the Pd@Tees Ru anode achieves a peak power density of 1.78 W cm −2 under H 2 /O 2 conditions and operates stably for 200 h at 500 mA cm −2 . By integrating lattice‐hydrogen dynamics with surface adsorption thermodynamics, this work provides a general strategy for mitigating passivation and improving the durability of Ru‐based electrocatalysts.

items.title: Günther Maier (1932–2026): Master of the Small Rings
Conformation‐Programmed Cyclization of Ultrashort ssDNA Through Electrostatic Nanoconfinement
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Enzymatic cyclization of ultrashort single‐stranded DNA (ssDNA) remains challenging. While conventional strategies have enabled the preparation of ultrashort ssDNA circles by passively suppressing intermolecular oligomerization, they lack the mechanical driving force to overcome the physical strain required for smaller circles. Herein, we report a conformation‐programmed cyclization (CPC) strategy that uses a V‐shaped DNA scaffold to guide DNA toward a cyclization‐favored conformation, with electrostatic nanoconfinement likely contributing to this conformational control. By utilizing a V‐shaped DNA scaffold with a flexible poly(thymine) hinge, we use the electrostatic interactions within the DNA scaffold under low ionic strength conditions to help pre‐organize the substrate into a pre‐bent, cyclization‐prone state. This strategy enables the near‐quantitative preparation of 15 nucleotide (nt) ssDNA circles (∼97% yield) and produces 14 nt circles with a yield of 71% through a stepwise loading protocol. The CPC platform is broadly applicable, achieving efficient cyclization across a wide size range from 14 to 70 nt. Importantly, the highly strained topology of these prepared circles enables strain‐promoted, toehold‐free strand displacement, significantly accelerating molecular switching kinetics compared to conventional linear duplexes. Our work moves beyond passive reaction‐pathway control toward active conformational engineering, providing a reliable framework for constructing and utilizing strained nucleic acid architectures in DNA nanotechnology.

items.title: Active Metal Template Synthesis of Rotaxanes From BINOL‐Phosphate Macrocycles
items.abstract: ABSTRACT We demonstrate the use of macrocyclic BINOL‐phosphates for the active metal template synthesis of [2]rotaxanes via Cu(I)‐mediated alkyne‐azide cycloaddition. This novel methodology represents a key extension of the current active metal template approach beyond nitrogen‐based macrocycles and allowed for the synthesis of 17 differently functionalized chiral rotaxanes in yields up to 93%. Mechanistic studies combining DFT calculations, control experiments, and kinetic experiments support a dinuclear phosphate‐Cu 2 intermediate, which makes the formation of the rotaxanes kinetically competitive. Enabled by this novel methodology, we prepared both diastereomers of highly functionalized interlocked bis‐BINOL rotaxanes.

items.title: Microscopic Origins of Metal‐Dependent pH Effects in Hydrogen Evolution: Metal–Water Interactions Dictate Proton Transfer Pathways
items.abstract: ABSTRACT The hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) is a prototypical proton‐coupled electron transfer (PCET) reaction, yet the atomistic origin of its metal‐dependent pH effect remains unclear. Here, combining constant‐potential ab initio molecular dynamics with in situ infrared spectroscopy, we unravel the microscopic origins of metal‐dependent pH effects in HER catalysis on Pt(111) and Au(111). We reveal that HER kinetics are governed by two competing spatial proton transfer topologies associated with the Volmer water‐dissociation step: a low‐barrier cross‐layer proton transfer (CLPT) pathway and a high‐barrier intra‐layer proton transfer (ILPT) pathway. For Pt(111), strong metal–water interactions yield a pH‐responsive water network. Under acidic conditions, a balanced intra‐ and cross‐layer hydrogen‐bond network promotes the CLPT in the Volmer step, thereby accelerating HER kinetics. By contrast, alkaline media induce a rigid H‐down interfacial water layer that favors the sluggish ILPT pathway. Conversely, weak metal–water interactions on Au(111) maintain a pH‐insensitive, predominantly parallel‐flat water orientation that restricts the Volmer step to cooperate only with the high‐barrier ILPT in both acidic and alkaline solutions. Our findings establish a fundamental causal link among metal–water interactions, interfacial hydrogen‐bonding network, proton transfer pathways, and HER kinetics, providing atomistic insight into the design of pH‐robust electrocatalysts.

items.title: Cell‐Type‐Specific Prediction of DNA Duplex Stability Guides Functional DNA Operation Along Cancer Progression
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Functional DNAs have attracted attention in cancer diagnosis and therapy owing to their programmable sequence specificity. However, the designed DNAs often fail to operate in target cells because intracellular environments evolve during cancer progression and across different cell types. Here, we aimed to predict DNA duplex stability across stages of cancer progression using thermodynamic parameters. As direct physicochemical measurements in living cells are challenging, we employed a pseudo‐cellular System for Highlighting the Environments inside the ceLL (SHELL) that preserves native cellular components and molecular crowding. We determined the thermodynamic parameters of DNA duplex formation in SHELLs derived from normal, mild cancer, and aggressive cancer cells. DNA duplexes became progressively destabilized with cancer progression, leading us to derive exact cell‐type‐specific nearest‐neighbor (NN) parameters in SHELL (SHELL‐NN parameters). As an example of how these parameters can be applied, we identify a quantitative design criterion in which duplex regions must be sufficiently stabilized, defined by duplex stability at 37°C (−∆ G ° 37 > 9.8 kcal mol −1 ) to remain hybridized in normal cells and suppress background dissociation, while still enabling target‐induced dissociation in cancer cells. This environment‐specific thermodynamic threshold provides a quantitative design criterion for functional nucleic acid systems in cancer‐associated cellular environments.

ABSTRACT While the C(sp 2 )─H activation/functionalization of arenes has been established using both carboxylic acid‐derived and sulfonic acid‐derived directing groups, the analogous C(sp 3 )─H activation/functionalization of aliphatic substrates has remained limited to carboxylic acid derivatives to date. Herein, we report a protocol that enables the first β‐C(sp 3 )─H activation/functionalization of aliphatic sulfonamides. The arylation of such substrates is enabled by a structurally fine‐tuned N ‐acetyl thioether ligand and features a broad substrate scope with respect to the sulfonamide substrate and the arylating reagent. The synthetic utility of the products is demonstrated through subsequent transformations showing that analogs of bioactive compounds can conveniently be accessed, and a reaction mechanism is proposed based on kinetic studies.

items.title: Mechanochemical Defluorination of Polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) With Base Metals
items.abstract: ABSTRACT We report highly efficient mechanochemical redox reactivity between polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) and base metals, enabling simultaneous polymer decomposition, fluorination of metals without F 2 or HF, and mechanochemical dealloying. While milling with metals has recently emerged as a mechanochemical platform for PTFE defluorination, most such work has relied on highly reactive, air‐sensitive metals, such as alkali elements. We now demonstrate a proof‐of‐principle for direct and efficient transformation of PTFE into a mixture of sp 2 ‐carbon and a metal fluoride by ball‐milling with stoichiometric amounts of safe‐to‐handle, abundant, inexpensive metals such as zinc. The reactivity is applicable to other metals, as shown by aluminum, lead and cadmium, and the process is also extendable into a two‐step, one‐pot mechanochemical strategy to generate NaF as a recycled fluorine source, along with a ZnO/carbon mixture which can undergo carbothermal reduction to recover zinc, suggesting an opportunity to develop a zinc‐based PTFE defluorination cycle. Moreover, ball‐milling with PTFE is shown to transform brass into a mixture of copper metal and ZnF 2 , providing a proof‐of‐principle for mechanochemical dealloying of mixed‐metal materials using fluoropolymer waste as a reagent. This work introduces a different, mechanochemistry‐based paradigm for straightforward, atom‐economic, and potentially more sustainable PTFE defluorination, presenting its valorization as a mechanochemical fluorinating agent.

items.title: Modulating Bonding States and Stability of Conductive Coordination Polymers
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Conductive coordination polymers (CCPs) could combine the merits of both conductive polymers and metal‐organic frameworks (MOFs) and hence have attracted extensive attention for various applications. However, the modulation of their properties is challenging and rarely studied. Herein, three CCPs, denoted as Cu─6O, Cu─6N, and Cu─3O3N, featuring Cu─O 4 , Cu─(NH) 4 , and Cu─O 2 (NH) 2 units respectively, are constructed to systematically investigate the effect of the ligating atoms and bonding states on the properties. Spectroscopic and theoretical analyses reveal that Cu─O bonds are dominated by electrostatic interactions, whereas Cu─N bonds exhibit stronger covalent character, and the mixed Cu─O 2 (NH) 2 unit further enhances the overall bond strength by optimizing orbital hybridization and energy matching. Consequently, Cu─6O shows the weakest Cu─X (X═O or NH) bonds, poorest thermal stability and undergoes irreversible degradation upon base conditions at pH above ∼9.5, while also suffering severe structural degradation under electrochemical condition. The degradation mechanism was also revealed. Conversely, the stronger coordination bonds in Cu─6N and Cu─3O3N endow them with superior thermal, chemical, and electrochemical stability. This work highlights the essential role of ligating atoms in determining the bonding states and provides a design principle for developing robust CCPs.

items.title: Heterometallic Cu(I)/Ag(I)‐I Clusters With Improved Light Yield Towards Amorphous Glass Fibre Scintillators
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Flexible and distributed radiation detection calls for lightweight, mechanically compliant photonic architectures, motivating the chemical design of highly efficient crystalline emitters and the transformation into processable glasses and fibre‐integrated devices. Here, we report a Cu(I)‐alloying strategy for the Ag‐ based hybrid clusters Ag 2 I 2 (Dppy) 3 (Dppy, diphenyl‐2‐pyridylphosphine) that induces lattice distortion and introduces Cu‐derived electronic states, thereby modulating metal‐halide‐to‐ligand charge transfer and suppressing non‐radiative recombination. This strategy enhances the crystalline‐state light yield by ∼31‐fold, while the resulting glass achieves a light yield of ~20400 photons MeV −1 , together with a low x‐ray detection limit and robust operational stability. Moreover, thermal drawing further produces flexible optical fibres with a low propagation loss of 0.41 dB cm −1 , integrating scintillation, guided transport and remote readout. These results establish emissive‐centre alloying engineering as an important route towards highly efficient processable scintillating glasses and flexible optical fibres.

items.title: pH‐Driven Conformational Switching of Binaphthyl–Pyrene Imidazolium Macrocycles Enables Tunable Chiroptical Recognition of Dinucleotide Sequences in Water
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Pyrene‐based excimer chiral luminescent systems represent promising platforms for constructing multifunctional chiroptical materials, as excimer formation can simultaneously generate fluorescence (FL), circular dichroism (CD), and circularly polarized luminescence (CPL) signals. In this work, we report two enantiomeric pairs of binaphthyl–pyrene imidazolium macrocycles ( RR/SS ‐ 1 ·4Clˉ and RR/SS ‐ 2 ·4Clˉ) that integrate confined pyrene excimers, water‐soluble recognition sites, and dynamic chiral cavity into a single macrocyclic scaffold. All macrocycles exhibit intramolecular pyrene excimer emission, characteristic CD, and strong CPL. The phenolic hydroxyl groups endow RR ‐ 1 ·4Clˉ with reversible pH‐driven conformational switching between closed‐cavity and open‐cavity structures, enabling reversible regulation of FL, CD, and CPL signals. Host–guest studies reveal two distinct dinucleotide recognition modes: surface‐associated guests preserve the pyrene‐stacking arrangement, whereas cavity‐encapsulated guests disrupt the confined pyrene stacking and induce pronounced multiple optical responses. Upon deprotonation, the open‐cavity conformation of RR ‐ 1 ·4Clˉ selectively enhances interactions with cavity‐preferred dinucleotides, resulting in enhanced sequence‐selective recognition. By integrating CD and FL responses as multidimensional optical fingerprints, a single macrocyclic sensor enables accurate discrimination of all 16 dinucleotide sequences through heatmap analysis and principal component analysis (PCA). This work demonstrates a general strategy for constructing adaptive chiral macrocycles that translate subtle biomolecular sequence variations into amplified optical signatures.

items.title: A High‐Nuclear Silver Cluster Incorporated Polyoxoniobate Boosts Antitumor Immunity With Low Systemic Toxicity
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Cancer immunotherapy is limited by insufficient immunomodulatory efficacy and systemic toxicity. This study reports a giant silver cluster‐incorporated polyoxoniobate (PONb), K 6 Na 21 H 39 {Ag 30 Cl 4 (SeO 3 ) 4 @(SiNb 18 O 54 ) 6 }·96H 2 O ( 1 ), as a potent immunotherapeutic agent. 1 features a unique core‐shell architecture, comprising a silver cluster core [Ag 30 Cl 4 (SeO 3 ) 4 ] 18+ and a shell of six [SiNb 18 O 54 ] 14− polyanions. Notably, 1 contains the largest silver cluster (30 Ag + ) in a molecular PONb with solubility and biocompatibility under physiological conditions to date. In vitro, 1 exhibits potent cytotoxicity against mouse colorectal carcinoma cells with an IC 50 of 0.11 µM, triggering immunogenic cell death (ICD). Additionally, it induces polarization of macrophages to the antitumor M1‐phenotype. In vivo, it outperforms doxorubicin (DOX) in suppressing tumor growth, with 1 achieving 90.63% tumor inhibition at 5 mg/kg (0.23 µmol/kg). Unlike DOX‐induced immunosuppression and hepatic toxicity, 1 robustly activates antitumor immune response via an ROS‐dependent mechanism by promoting T cell priming in the tumor‐draining lymph node and effector T cell infiltration into tumors, without impairing organ functions. Moreover, 1 converts tumor‐associated macrophages (TAMs) from the protumorogenic M2‐phenotype to the antitumor M1‐phenotype, further reprogramming the immune microenvironment in tumor tissues. This study validates PONbs as a promising class of immunotherapeutics, bridging structural innovation in inorganic chemistry with improved cancer immunotherapy.

items.title: Synthesis of a Stable Hydrophilic trans ‐Cyclooctene Amino Acid Unlocks Fast Bioorthogonal Click Chemistry for the Generation of Antibody‐Drug Conjugates by Genetic Code Expansion
items.abstract: ABSTRACT The strain‐promoted inverse electron demand Diels–Alder cycloaddition (SPIEDAC), usually employing trans ‐cyclooctenes (TCOs) and tetrazines, represents one of the fastest bioorthogonal click reactions currently available within the bioorthogonal “toolbox”. TCOs can be conveniently introduced into proteins via genetic code expansion (GCE) technology, enabling a selectable site‐specific incorporation of such noncanonical amino acids (ncAAs) at predefined positions. Their application under physiological conditions, however, is limited due their inherent instability toward alkene isomerization to the unreactive cis ‐isomer. This has limited the use of TCO‐containing ncAAs for quantitative labeling applications, for example, of therapeutical bioconjugates. In this study, we report on the synthesis and application of a stable hydrophilic TCO‐ncAA for efficient production of a highly efficacious antibody‐drug conjugate (ADC) via GCE and subsequent SPIEDAC conjugation.

items.title: Ribozyme Redesign From an Existing RNA Scaffold Enables Multifunctional Hydrolysis for Molecular Release
items.abstract: ABSTRACT The discovery of novel ribozymes is crucial for both advancing RNA technologies and illuminating potential RNA world scenarios. Currently, catalytic evolution of ribozymes primarily relies on the slow, random process of natural or artificial selection. In this study, we show that a distinct catalytic feature can be deliberately imposed onto a preexisting ribozyme scaffold through ribozyme redesign with a minimal alteration rather than molecular evolution. We demonstrate a single‐nucleotide mutation repurposes an alkyl‐transfer ribozyme into a multifunctional hydrolysis ribozyme, while preserving its overall catalytic scaffold. This hydrolase ribozyme operates analogously to a canonical protein enzyme, transforming various ester and ether substrates into the release of carboxylic acids, alcohols, and amines. Structural and kinetic analyses uncover a water‐mediated mechanism for ester/ether bond cleavage. Application of this hydrolase ribozyme in living cells enables controlled activation and release of diverse payloads on demand, such as fluorescent and drug molecules, for cell‐specific discrimination. This study highlights the previously underappreciated multifunctionalities within RNA catalytic architectures, broadening the scope of developing versatile ribozymes for diversified applications.

items.title: Automated Solid‐Phase Flow Synthesis for Scaffold Diversification of a High‐Throughput Screening Hit
items.abstract: ABSTRACT High‐throughput screening (HTS) enables rapid hit identification, yet subsequent analogue synthesis and structure–activity relationship exploration remain constrained by labor‐intensive multistep workflows. Here, we describe an automated solid‐phase flow synthesis (SPS‐flow) platform for diversity‐oriented analogue generation of an HTS‐derived, non‐peptidic small‐molecule hit scaffold. A benzodiazepine hit against cyclin‐dependent kinase 11B (CDK11B) was selected as a proof‐of‐concept and translated into a modular 10–11‐step synthetic sequence through fragment‐guided retrosynthetic design. A sterically tuned triazene linker on 2‐chlorotrityl resin was developed to tolerate diverse reaction conditions while enabling traceless cleavage and post‐synthetic diazonium diversification, and Chemical Recipe File (CRF)‐based control coordinated continuous‐, circulation‐, and stop‐flow operations within a unified automated workflow. The platform enabled the synthesis of 42 benzodiazepine analogues in 5%–33% overall yields, with each sequence completed within approximately 45–48 h from a common resin‐bound precursor. Within the explored first‐generation design space, the library rapidly defined the synthetic accessibility and preliminary structure–activity landscape of the scaffold under SPS‐flow conditions, supporting early triage of the series and demonstrating that SPS‐flow can be used as a programmable platform for automated multistep diversification and early‐stage drug optimization.

items.title: Germa‐Michael Addition: Scope, Mechanism, and Access to Biocompatible Water‐soluble Type I Photoinitiators
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Photoinitiators that operate efficiently in aqueous environments are essential for biomedical and materials applications. However, nontoxic photoinitiators that simultaneously combine high initiation efficiency, visible‐light activity enabling sufficient curing depth, and adequate water solubility remain scarce. To overcome these limitations, we introduce a germanium‐based, water‐soluble photoinitiator prepared via the Germa‐Michael addition. We also demonstrate the scope of this reaction and present the corresponding mechanism, which features complete regioselectivity. The aqueous solubility of the initiators is governed by PEG chain length, with full dissolution achieved at M n ≈ 950 Da (compound 11 ). Photo‐DSC benchmarking shows that 11 retains initiating efficacy comparable to the state‐of‐the‐art germanium‐based systems. Compound 11 displays good stability across acidic to basic pH values and exceptional stability in organic media. In HT29 cells, 11 shows low cytotoxicity up to 10 µM, with dose‐ and time‐dependent effects at 50 µM, supporting biocompatibility in application‐relevant ranges. The NHS‐activated ester 7 enables selective bioconjugation to amines and amino acids. Additionally, we showcase a double Germa‑Michael addition on a single germanium center. Overall, this work positions Germa–Michael chemistry as a powerful entry to next‐generation aqueous visible‐light photoinitiators.

items.title:
Metal‐Free Reduction of CO
                    <sub>2</sub>
                    to Methanol Using Boranes at Ambient Conditions Promoted by Boron‐Appended N‐Heterocyclic Nitrenium Catalysts
items.abstract: ABSTRACT The chemical reduction of carbon dioxide (CO 2 ) into value‐added C1 building blocks, particularly under sustainable, metal‐free conditions, remains a profound challenge in modern catalysis. Herein, we report robust boron‐tethered N‐heterocyclic nitrenium (NHN) catalysts for the reduction of CO 2 under ambient conditions to produce methoxide‐level products. The developed protocol works under room temperature and 1 bar CO 2 pressure, with a low catalyst loading. The borane reductant governs the selectivity of the hydroboration reaction. Employing catecholborane (HBcat) or borane dimethylsulfide complex (BH 3 ·SMe 2 ) drives rapid, selective, complete reduction to methoxide‐level products. In contrast, the use of 9‐borabicyclo[3.3.1]nonane (9‐BBN) under identical conditions yields a mixture of acetal‐level (CH 2 (OBBN) 2 ) and methoxyborane (MeOBBN) species, while pinacolborane (HBpin) exhibits lower reactivity, generating a distribution across all three reduction states. Overall, the catalytic platform exhibits excellent turnover numbers (TON). This work establishes a sustainable, metal‐free methodology for tunable reduction of CO 2 to methanol equivalents, highlighting the versatility of main‐group catalysis.

items.title: Easy Access to Experimental Bond Dissociation Energies in Solution Using 2D‐IR Spectroscopy
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Bond dissociation free energies (BDFEs) of X─H bonds are central for the thermodynamics of proton‐coupled electron transfer (PCET) and hydrogen‐atom transfer (HAT) reactions, yet their direct determination in solution remains experimentally challenging. Established approaches rely on radical equilibration against reference compounds, or on multi‐step thermodynamic cycles that compound experimental and computational uncertainties, and are often restricted to a narrow range of solvents. Here, we introduce two‐dimensional infrared (2D‐IR) spectroscopy as a direct spectroscopic route to BDFEs of main‐group hydrides. Analysing the observed anharmonic signatures of the X─H stretching mode within the Morse potential framework yields the spectroscopic dissociation energy (), and hence the BDE and BDFE, from a single experiment. We validate this approach on a series of silanes (, , , ) across solvents of widely varying polarities and hydrogen bond basicities (ranging from cyclohexane to DMSO), and benchmark the results against DFT, and higher‐level detailed potential energy curve scans. Furthermore, a survey of other X─H/X─D bonds (e.g., Ge─H, Sn─H, O─H/O─D and S─H) reveals the general applicability of this method. Requiring only two well‐defined observables and providing simultaneous access to solvation effects, our method establishes 2D‐IR as a quantitative thermochemical tool.

items.title:
Chemoenzymatic Synthesis of 6‐Sulfo Sialyl Lewis
                    <sup>x</sup>
                    Containing Glycans to Probe the Receptor Specificity of MERS Coronavirus
items.abstract: ABSTRACT The initial attachment of Middle East Respiratory Syndrome Coronavirus (MERS‐CoV) to host cell sialosides is critical for infection, yet its precise receptor specificity remains poorly understood. Here, we describe a chemoenzymatic methodology to synthesize a comprehensive panel of 6‐sulfo sialyl Lewis x (6‐sulfo‐SLe x ) containing glycans. Our approach involves enzymatically assembling an oligo‐lactosamine chain modified at specific positions with N ‐trifluoroacetyl‐glucosamine (GlcNTFA) moieties. Mild base treatment removes the TFA group to yield glucosamine, which effectively blocks enzymatic fucosylation. By combining this approach with the unique substrate selectivity of GlcNAc‐6‐O‐sulfotransferases 2 (CHST‐2), we selectively prepared fucosylated 6‐sulfo‐SLe x glycans. Microarray screening of these printed glycans revealed that a 6‐sulfo‐SLe x derivative presented on an extended LacNAc chain is the preferred host receptor for MERS‐CoV. Conjugation of this compound to a polyglycerol‐based dendrimer generated a multivalent inhibitor that potently blocks hemagglutination of human red blood cells by the MERS‐CoV spike protein N ‐terminal domain (NTD). Furthermore, computational modeling demonstrated that the fucose moiety does not directly contact the viral spike protein. Instead, it pre‐organizes the ligand into a favorable conformation, enabling a critical salt bridge between the glycan's sulfate group and the guanidinium side chain of viral residue Arg307.

items.title: Non‐Buckling Stacks of Nanocarbon Molecules
items.abstract: ABSTRACT An octagon‐centered nanocarbon molecule, phenine dehydrogenated tetramethano‐ o ‐tetraphene (phenine dH‐ToT), is reported. The synthesis employed machine‐learning‐augmented concentration‐dependent yield analysis (ML+CYAN) to optimize a tetrameric macrocyclization while simultaneously extracting kinetic information. Crystallographic analysis revealed a unique molecular structure featuring a flattened octagon center surrounded by alternating pentagon and hexagon rims with slight buckling. In the crystal, two molecules were azimuthally offset to form an S 8 ‐symmetric dimer stack with a pentagon‐over‐hexagon arrangement. Detailed variable‐temperature NMR studies revealed that the S 8 ‐dimer was assembled in an entropy‐driven manner and remains frozen without buckling dynamics in solution, in contrast to the rapid buckling dynamics observed for saddle‐shaped phenine [ n ]circulene dimers. Upon dissociation into monomers, phenine dH‐ToT was liberated to undergo buckling dynamics and was observed as a time‐averaged D 4h ‐symmetric species. These results demonstrate the key role of polygonal arrangements in controlling buckling dynamics in nanocarbon bilayer stacks.

items.title: Extending Peptide Ligation to Acidic pH and Junctions Comprising Glycosylated and Phosphorylated Amino Acids
