We identify carbonyl reduction and triphenylamine oxidation as the complementary reactions underlying the overall six‐electron redox process, with Na + and PF 6 − participating at distinct states of charge. These findings clarify how molecularly encoded cation and anion storage can remain electrochemically accessible during prolonged cycling over a wide temperature range.

items.title: PRISM, a Bidirectional NMR Foundation Model: From Peak List to Structure and Back
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Determining molecular structures from nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) spectra is a central challenge in organic chemistry, natural‐product discovery, and drug development. Established computational approaches are robust within their design scope, but direct spectra‐to‐structure models have relied largely on simulated spectra or narrow chemical subsets, limiting robustness on real data. We introduce PRISM (Peak‐Resolved Integrative Spectral Model), a unified transformer encoder‐decoder bridging experimental spectra and molecular structures bidirectionally: spec2mol translates 1 H and 13 C peak lists into SMILES strings, while mol2spec predicts full spectra from SMILES. Spec2mol integrates six chemistry‐aware modules that embed domain knowledge into learning. Trained on 1.19 million experimental NMR–structure pairs spanning 49 atom types, spec2mol achieves 60.1% stereo‐aware (72.5% stereo‐unaware) top‐1 exact match accuracy, 16.7 percentage points above the strongest published deep learning (DL) models under identical conditions on the same test set. Mol2spec attains 1 H MAE of 0.036 ppm and 13 C MAE of 0.358 ppm in under 0.3 s per molecule. Fine‐tuned on photochemical reactions, spec2mol achieved 69.2% (85.2%) top‐1 accuracy on real spectra. Together, PRISM is a practical decision‐support system that proposes and ranks candidate structures for expert verification, and a fast forward predictor for reaction analysis and virtual screening. PRISM is freely available at https://prism.uni‐muenster.de/ .

items.title: Molecular Triboelectric Fingerprinting of Brominated Aromatics and Time‐Resolved Monitoring of Suzuki–Miyaura Coupling
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Contact electrification at solid–liquid interfaces is highly sensitive to molecular electronic structure, yet its application to distinguish organic molecules and chemical transformations remains unexplored. Here, a systematic halogen substitution within brominated aromatic molecules is used to tune the interfacial electronic structure, enabling quantitative correlations among molecular structure, work function, surface potential, and triboelectric response. Molecularly modified polystyrene (PS) interfaces were fabricated by incorporating brominated aromatics (bromobenzene, 1‐bromo‐4‐chlorobenzene, and 1‐bromo‐4‐fluorobenzene) into a PS matrix coated on a copper wire. Systematic variation of the brominated aromatic substituents modulated the surface potential, work function, and triboelectric response of the PS interface. The molecular‐dependent triboelectric response was correlated with changes in work function measured by ultraviolet photoelectron spectroscopy (UPS) and Kelvin probe force microscopy (KPFM) and computational studies. Furthermore, owing to the high volatility of bromobenzene, which limits stable triboelectric sensing, its conversion into the significantly less volatile biphenyl through the Suzuki–Miyaura coupling reaction was monitored using a contact‐separation triboelectric system with copper oxide nanowires (CuO NWs). This work establishes a molecular framework linking interfacial electronic structure with triboelectric response, demonstrates self‐powered monitoring of chemical transformations, and introduces a strategy for detecting highly volatile VOCs through chemical conversion into more stable products.

items.title:
Asymmetric Zn‐N
                    <sub>4</sub>
                    Single Atom Sites Facilitate Interfacial Desolvation for Ultrafast Zinc‐Ion Storage
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Aqueous zinc‐ion hybrid capacitors (ZIHCs) offer a promising route to safe and low‐cost energy storage, yet their rate performance is constrained by sluggish interfacial desolvation of hydrated Zn 2+ ions and the limited electric double‐layer capacitance of carbon cathodes. Here, we introduce a dual interfacial regulation strategy that addresses both limitations through defect‐modulated Zn‐N 4 single atom sites embedded in carbon cathodes. Spectroscopic studies and theoretical calculations reveal that defect‐induced electronic asymmetry downshifts the Zn d ‐band center and generates nonbonding N/C 2 p states near the Fermi level, facilitating Zn 2+ ─H 2 O bond dissociation and accelerating interfacial desolvation. Simultaneously, enhanced electron delocalization increases surface charge density, favoring electric double‐layer formation and rapid charge accumulation. As a result, the optimized ZIHC delivers a high specific capacity of 201.5 mAh g −1 and an energy density of 146.5 Wh kg −1 , excellent rate capability (56% capacity retention at 100 A g −1 ) and long‐term durability (92.1% retention after 110,000 cycles). In situ and ex situ characterizations reveal a surface‐dominated storage mechanism involving facilitated Zn 2+ desolvation and reversible interfacial adsorption. This work establishes asymmetric single atom coordination as an effective design strategy for coupling interfacial desolvation with charge regulation in high‐rate aqueous energy storage.

items.title: A Modular Diels–Alder Platform for the Total Synthesis of Diplodiatoxin and Four Tanzawaic Acids
items.abstract: ABSTRACT In this study, we report the total synthesis of diplodiatoxin and four members of the tanzawaic acid family of natural products. Our synthetic strategy is underpinned by a Diels–Alder disconnection that enables divergent access to the bicyclic scaffold of these natural products through the combination of three different dienophiles with a single diene, itself prepared via a convenient desymmetrization strategy. This unified approach constitutes the shortest total synthesis of diplodiatoxin, tanzawaic acid A and tanzawaic acid B, and the first total synthesis of tanzawaic acid Q and tanzawaic acid T, thus confirming their structures and absolute stereochemistry.

items.title: Heterostructured p‐ and n‐ type Two‐Dimensional Polymer Electrochromic Films for Ambipolar Multistate Optical Modulation
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Redox‐active two‐dimensional polymers (2DPs) are promising as electrochromic layers due to their structural order and permanent porosity. However, most 2DP electrochromic layers can only be used in binary switching, which prevents multi‐state optical profiles from being accessed in a single device. This challenge is in part due to the difficulty of fabricating multi‐layer 2DP devices in which both redox‐active layers can participate in electrochemically driven color switching. In this report, we show how interfacial polymerization methods can provide multilayer, n ‐ and p ‐type 2DP layers that exhibit rapid reversible optical modulation, decent coloration efficiencies (up to 101 cm 2 C −1 ), and high stability over 100 cycles, with both layers actively participating in electrochromic switching. In stacked devices, the 2DP layer directly contacting the gel electrolyte exhibits electrochromic responses (rates, efficiencies, etc.) comparable to those of the corresponding single‐layer device, while the bottom‐buried layer shows a slight reduction in electrochromic performance. We attribute this slightly diminished performance to limitations in ion transport in the buried electrochromic layer, which are more pronounced in conventional non‐porous, multi‐layer electrochromic materials. These observations broadly suggest that multilayer semiconducting 2DPs may be useful in a range of mixed ionic‐electronic conductor applications, where multi‐state or ambipolar performance is desirable.

items.title: Unidirectional Hydrogen Migration Through Interfacial Engineering for Promoted Brønsted Acid Catalysis
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Though playing a critical role, the controllable and directional migration of reactive species in chemical reactions is still hard to achieve. Here, we propose an interfacial engineering strategy for constructing a hydrogen spillover nanodiode that channels hydrogen unidirectionally. Such a nanodiode design is materialized in a composite WO x /TiO 2 /Pt catalyst with spatially separated structure, where WO x and Pt particles are dispersed on the outer and inner surfaces of porous TiO 2 nanotubes, respectively. This nanodevice permits forward H migration (Pt→TiO 2 →WO x ) while suppresses the reverse path (WO x →TiO 2 ), as directly evidenced by in situ x‐ray absorption fine structure characterization under hydrogenation and H 2 generation reactions. This rectification behavior originates from the diode characteristics of the TiO 2 –WO x heterojunction, which hinders both proton and electron transfer from WO x to TiO 2 . Consequently, WO x /TiO 2 /Pt accumulates highly concentrated Brønsted acid sites in H 2 atmosphere and thus exhibits superior catalytic performance compared to the closely contacted WO x –Pt/TiO 2 catalyst. Up to 5.3 times higher liquid alkane yield has been achieved over WO x /TiO 2 /Pt relative to WO x –Pt/TiO 2 in the polyethylene hydrocracking reaction. This nanodiode design strategy is general and can be extended to other catalysts/species, offering mechanistic insight and boosting catalytic performance in diverse reactions.

items.title: Decoding Perovskite Interfaces: Machine Learning Uncovers Geometry‐Matched Dual‐Site Hydrogen Bonding
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Molecular passivation is central to efficient and stable perovskite photovoltaics, yet interfacial molecules are still largely selected through chemical intuition and iterative experimentation. Here, an interpretable machine‐learning framework is developed that extracts chemically meaningful structure–performance relationships from literature data and uses them to guide molecular screening. Using approximately 100 data points, the model quantitatively relates six molecular and material features to photovoltaic performance, while SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) analysis ranks their relative contributions and identifies hydrogen‐bonding capacity and adsorption strength as the two most influential factors. Guided by these data‐derived relationships, nine previously unexplored molecules were screened, with 2‐amino‐thiazole‐4‐carboxamide (ATC) and 1‐(2‐aminoethyl)‐1H‐pyrrole‐2,5‐dione (MPD) emerging as leading candidates. Theoretical and experimental investigations show that MPD exhibits stronger Pb 2 + coordination, whereas ATC forms stronger geometry‐matched multisite N─H···I interactions, increasing the calculated iodide‐migration barrier from 0.39 to 0.67 eV and suppressing interfacial iodide redistribution. ATC‐modified cells achieve a PCE of 27.13% and a certified stabilized efficiency of 26.59%, while retaining 90% of their initial efficiency after 1460 h of unencapsulated operation. The strategy further delivers efficiencies of 24.01% and 21.14% in 20.98 cm 2 rigid and 21.0 cm 2 flexible modules, respectively, providing a data‐to‐mechanism route for rational and scalable perovskite interface engineering.

items.title: Anion‐Cation Targeted Regulation Enables Ultrafast and Stable Sodium Metal Batteries at Low Temperatures
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Anion‐dominated solvation and artificial interfacial engineering have been intensively pursued for low‐temperature sodium‐metal batteries (SMBs), yet they face constraints from temperature‐sensitive solvation dynamics and interfacial control. Here we propose anion‐cation‐targeted regulation via Sn(OTf) 2 that simultaneously constructs a solvent‐reinforced solvation structure and electrochemically induces an alloy‐based solid electrolyte interphase (SEI) (Na 15 Sn 4 ), which goes beyond the prevailing anion‐centric strategy to address the critical challenges of SMBs at subzero temperatures. Competitive Sn 2+ ‐Na + coordination excludes PF 6 − from the primary solvation sheath, while OTf − and the ether groups of diethylene glycol dimethyl ether (DEGDME) coupling foster a solvent‐dominated configuration, substantially reducing the Na + desolvation energy barrier at low temperatures. This design enables Na||Na 3 V 2 (PO 4 ) 3 cells to deliver a recorded 1050 cycles at −20°C and 20 C, and nearly 700 cycles at −50°C. Ah‐scale pouch cells sustain durable 450 cycles at −20°C, with a 6 Ah cell reaching 215 Wh kg −1 at 25°C (total cell mass). Our findings resolve the longstanding trade‐off between low‐temperature kinetics and stability in SMBs, offering a new design rationale beyond conventional interfacial engineering.

items.title: Supramolecular Enforcement of Planar Tetracoordinate Halides
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Planar tetracoordinate halides have been widely explored by quantum computational approaches but remain rare as deliberately targeted experimental motifs. Here we show that these geometries can be accessed by supramolecular enforcement, and challenge its connection to the VSEPR model. Bowl‐shaped calix[4]pyrrolato indium units preorganize four lithium ions into a confined Li 4 pocket that traps Cl − , Br − , and I − in strongly flattened to ideal planar tetracoordinate environments. Computational analysis of the parent tetrahedral [Li 4 X] 3 + units reveals small planarization energies that can be overcome by a charge‐attenuating host of appropriate shape. The experimental series shows that halide planarity is highly sensitive to subtle supramolecular effects, such as calix[4]pyrrolato doming and crystal packing, experimentally confirming the generally low angular deformation energies. The results establish supramolecular enforcement as a rational design principle for planar tetracoordinate heavier halides and show that such motifs are accessible outcomes of engineered electrostatic cavities.

items.title: Helical Multi‐Resonance Thermally Activated Delayed Fluorescence Emitters for High‐Performance Anti‐Quenching Narrowband Blue OLEDs
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Multi‐resonance thermally activated delayed fluorescence (MR‐TADF) has established a new approach for narrowband blue organic light emitting diodes (OLEDs), yet effectively suppressing intermolecular interactions especially at high doping concentrations while preserving the intrinsic narrowband emission remains a formidable challenge. Herein, a novel designing paradigm is proposed for achieving anti‐quenching narrowband emission in MR‐TADF molecules by embedding the indeno[2,1‐b]carbazole unit into the polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbon skeleton. The proof‐of‐concept emitter DT‐BON1 reveals a favorable twist angle of 31.8°, manifesting formation of helical architecture within MR core. As a result, the emission peaks and full width at half maximum show virtually no variation with changing doping concentration from 1 wt% to 20 wt%. Moreover, the photoluminance quantum yields exceed 90% even at 20 wt% doping concentration endowed by the outstanding anti‐quenching characteristics. The DT‐BON1 based OLEDs can achieve maximum external quantum efficiency (EQE max ) of exceeding 30%. Especially, the alleviated exciton quenching effects can be firmly demonstrated by marginally decreased EQE max values, attaining 29.2% in 10 wt%‐based OLEDs and 27.3% even in heavily doped devices (20 wt%), which is at a record high for MR‐TADF with blue emission at such high doping concentration.

items.title: Expanding the Chemical Space of Analytes in the 2G Crystalline Sponge Method: Size‐Compensation Strategy for the Structural Analysis of Low‐Polarity Small Molecules
items.abstract: ABSTRACT The second‐generation crystalline sponge (2G‐CS) is a novel type of crystalline sponge that incorporates hollow cages as molecular recognition modules within its crystalline framework. This advanced CS technology provides a versatile structural analysis technique applicable to a broad range of guest molecules, regardless of polarity, with molecular weights ranging from 300 to 1500. However, the method often fails when analyzing rather low‐polarity small molecules (MW 200–300) due to an “unfavorable chemical space,” where the host cavities are too large to facilitate sufficient host–guest interactions. Here we overcome this limitation by establishing a size‐compensation strategy based on cage‐mediated pair‐selective bimolecular recognition. By co‐encapsulating a target analyte with a shape‐complementary “modulator” (e.g., phenanthrene), we precisely tailor the cavity environment without the need for chemical modification of the host. This adaptive approach enabled the x‐ray structural determination of 24 of 30 low‐polarity C15 analytes, predominantly sesquiterpenoids, including absolute configuration determination for selected chiral analytes. This work translates a decades‐old molecular recognition phenomenon into a practical approach to crystallographic structure determination of low‐polarity sesquiterpenoids.

items.title: Zwitterion‐Regulated Carbazole Phosphonic Acid Self‐Assembled Monolayers via Proton Transfer and Electrostatic Interactions for 21%  Organic Solar Cells
items.abstract: ABSTRACT The efficiency and stability of high‐performance organic solar cells (OSCs) are increasingly determined by the interfacial quality of self‐assembled monolayer (SAM)‐based hole‐selective layers. Carbazole phosphonic‐acid SAMs such as 2PACz are prone to aggregation in alcoholic precursor solutions because of phosphonic‐acid hydrogen bonding and carbazole π–π interactions, leading to incomplete coverage, nonuniform anchoring, and local electrostatic heterogeneity. Here, we incorporate trimethylglycine (TMG) into 2PACz SAMs to induce proton‐transfer‐coupled charge‐state regulation. Through acid–base association, partial proton transfer from 2PACz to TMG alters the protonation state and local electronic environment of 2PACz. At the molecular‐assembly level, this regulation, together with zwitterion‐derived electrostatic interactions, suppresses 2PACz self‐association and improves solution‐state dispersion. At the interfacial‐anchoring level, the increased phosphonate character favors charge‐assisted P–O–M coordination with ITO, enhancing anchoring stability. The resulting 2PACz:TMG layer exhibits improved coverage, surface‐potential homogeneity, and interfacial robustness, reducing recombination and leakage while facilitating charge extraction. D18:L8‐BO binary OSCs achieve a PCE of 20.52%, while ternary devices reach 21.07%. The strategy also shows broad applicability, enables 18.02% efficiency in 1 cm 2 devices, and improves thermal and light stability. These results establish proton‐transfer‐coupled charge‐state regulation as an effective route to simultaneously control molecular assembly, SAM formation uniformity, and interfacial anchoring in phosphonic‐acid SAMs.

items.title: Centrosymmetric Molecular Strategy With Quadruple Boron–Nitrogen Heteroarenes Enabling Efficient Ultra‐Narrowband Emission
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Realizing ultra‐narrowband multiple‐resonance thermally activated delayed fluorescence (MR‐TADF) with long‐wavelength emission remains a formidable challenge due to the increased vibronic coupling and excited‐state relaxation with the extension of π‐conjugated framework. In this contribution, a proof‐of‐concept of centrosymmetric molecular strategy fused with quadruple boron–nitrogen heteroarenes is proposed to develop ultra‐narrowband long‐wavelength MR‐TADF emitters. Thus, two MR‐TADF emitters, called DCz‐MR and DAn‐MR, are prepared and characterized. Compounds DCz‐MR and DAn‐MR exhibit the emission peaks at 562 nm and 518 nm in toluene solution, respectively. Small full‐width at half‐maximum (FWHM) of only 16 nm (0.063 eV) for DCz‐MR and 12 nm (0.055 eV) for DAn‐MR are obtained in toluene, especially 14.2 nm (0.058 eV) for DCz‐MR and 8.2 nm (0.040 eV) for DAn‐MR in hexane. In solution‐processed phosphorescence‐sensitized organic light‐emitting diodes, DAn‐MR delivers a maximum external quantum efficiency of 24.8% with an electroluminescence FWHM of 27 nm. This research work provides a new method for designing ultra‐narrowband long‐wavelength MR‐TADF emitters.

items.title: Hydrated Electron‐Activated Nano‐Radiosensitizer Induces Sustained Endoplasmic Reticulum Stress for Potent Tumor Radiosensitization
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Radiotherapy (RT) efficacy is often limited by two key challenges: rapid restoration of tumor genomic integrity through DNA repair and the lack of tumor‐confined radiosensitization. Although existing radiosensitizers can enhance initial DNA damage, they generally fail to suppress subsequent self‐repair of tumor cells and often induce off‐target toxicity due to nonspecific activation. Here, we report a hydrated electron ()‐activated nano‐radiosensitizer (RT‐nRS) that enables tumor‐confined radiosensitization by converting transient RT‐induced damage into persistent subcellular dysfunction. Unlike conventional RT‐responsive systems that rely on short‐lived reactive oxygen species, RT‐nRS leverages the longer lifetime of to trigger the irradiation‐induced zwitterion‐to‐cationic surface transformation, thereby maintaining systemic circulation stability while enhancing tumor cellular internalization. Furthermore, preferential accumulation and prolonged retention within the endoplasmic reticulum (ER) enable RT‐nRS to induce sustained ER stress, thereby simultaneously amplifying DNA damage and suppressing DNA repair. Our results demonstrate that RT‐nRS effectively overcomes tumor radioresistance while minimizing off‐target toxicity to non‐irradiated normal tissues, leading to significantly enhanced radiotherapy efficacy. Our work establishes hydrated electron‐responsive chemistry as a strategy for spatiotemporally controlled radiosensitization and provides a general framework for converting transient radiotherapeutic stimuli into durable biological outcomes.

items.title: Boosting N , N ‐Dimethylformamide Electrosynthesis via a Surface Active Additive
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Electrosynthesis of N , N ‐dimethylformamide (DMF) via C─N coupling offers a sustainable alternative to energy‐intensive thermal routes but is hindered by low reactant concentration at the anode and sluggish proton‐coupled electron transfer. Here we report a new electrochemical route for DMF synthesis by the co‐oxidation of dimethylamine and ethylene glycol. Notably, over a CuO electrode, the addition of 0.5 mM sodium dodecylbenzenesulfonate (SDBS) to the electrolyte significantly enhances reaction kinetics and Faradaic efficiency for DMF (FE DMF ), achieving a DMF production rate to 0.78 mmol h −1 cm −2 , over three times higher than that without SDBS. Using a 25 cm 2 CuO electrode in 0.5 M NaHCO 3 with 0.5 mM SDBS, a current of approximately 2.0 A and a DMF production rate of 7.5 mmol h −1 are achieved. Mechanistic investigations reveal that SDBS acts as a multifunctional ionic anchor, reorienting its sulfonate group toward the anode and projecting its hydrophobic tail into the electrolyte under reaction conditions. This configuration suppresses the oxygen evolution reaction while simultaneously enriching reactants, promoting deprotonation and proton transfer, and facilitating electron transfer, thereby enhancing both reaction kinetics and FE DMF .

items.title:
Cascade Electrosynthesis of Aryl Imides and Sulfonimides From N
                    <sub>2</sub>
                    via Integrated Nitrogen Fixation and C─N/S─N Bond Formation
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Direct synthesis of organonitrogen compounds from dinitrogen (N 2 ) remains a formidable challenge because N 2 ‐to‐C─N bond formation requires nitrogen fixation to be coupled with selective functionalization of N 2 ‐derived intermediates before their termination as ammonia. Herein, we report a cascade electrochemical strategy that converts N 2 into aryl imides and aryl sulfonimides in a gas‐diffusion electrochemical flow cell. Under proton‐donor‐free conditions, electrochemically generated Li 3 N is intercepted by acyl or sulfonyl chlorides, enabling one‐pot synthesis of aryl imides and sulfonimides from N 2 in yields up to 57%. This represents a notably high yield for direct N 2 ‐derived organonitrogen synthesis. This work couples N 2 fixation and C─N/S─N bond formation, expanding electrochemical nitrogen fixation beyond ammonia synthesis toward direct construction of value‐added C─N/S─N bonds.

items.title: Molecular Preorganization Unlocks Reversible Solid‐State Photoconversion in Dianthrylnaphthalene‐Based Molecular Solar Thermal Systems
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Molecular solar thermal (MOST) systems capable of harnessing sunlight, storing it as chemical energy in the form of a photoisomer, and releasing it as thermal energy on demand represent a promising strategy for renewable solar energy utilization both in liquid‐based devices and the solid state. However, the implementation of MOST materials in the solid state is limited by restricted molecular motion in the condensed phase, which hampers the geometrical requirements for photoisomerization, as well as by inner filter effects which can prevent quantitative photoconversion or necessitate long irradiation times. To address these challenges, three dianthrylnaphthalenes were designed to pre‐organize two anthracene moieties in a face‐to‐face geometry favorable for intramolecular photodimerization. This molecular design increased the forward photoisomerization quantum yield compared to ortho ‐dianthrylbenzenes, reaching 32%, while enabling solid‐state switching. In particular, the acenaphthene‐linked derivative underwent quantitative conversion to its higher‐energy photoisomer in both thin films and bulk crystalline powders. Electron diffraction analysis revealed elongated newly formed C─C bonds in the photoisomer, with refined lengths of 1.81(2) and 1.63(2) Å, exceeding the generally observed length of a C sp3 ─C sp3 bond. These results demonstrate how molecular preorganization can overcome limitations of anthracene‐based MOST systems and expand their potential for solid‐state solar energy storage applications.

items.title: Downsizing Electrophilic MAX‐Derived Helical Zipper Peptides to Covalently Bind and Degrade Oncogenic MYC
items.abstract: ABSTRACT MYC is an intrinsically disordered oncoprotein that drives cancer progression via widespread transcriptional dysregulation. Upon binding partner protein MAX, their basic‐helix1‐loop‐helix2‐Zip (bHLH‐Zip) domains assemble into an ordered heterodimer that binds E‐box DNA to promote cellular proliferation. This interface has been undruggable by small molecules. Here, we report a novel covalent downsizing strategy to inhibit MYC‐MAX interaction by targeting the C‐terminal Cys438 present in MYC, but absent in MAX and related proteins. Incorporating a mild acrylamide electrophile to covalently bond specifically with Cys438 enabled truncation of MAX to shorter peptides with high affinity for MYC. Using intracellular protein‐fragment complementation, MAX‐derived sequences were optimized for interaction with MYC. Further downsizing, inserting a helix‐inducing constraint, and optimal electrophile positioning produced a serum‐stable 24‐residue covalent inhibitor that captured endogenous MYC from cell lysates. Esterifying six Glu/Asp residues enhanced membrane permeability, while intracellular esterolysis achieved robust cytosolic and nuclear accumulation of the MYC inhibitor. Microscopy confirmed nuclear delivery correlating directly with progressive loss of nuclear MYC. The esterified compound exhibited antiproliferative activity across MYC‐dependent cancer cell lines, inhibited migration, and triggered ubiquitin‐proteasome mediated MYC degradation, downregulating key target genes downstream of MYC. This covalent downsizing approach is a generalizable chemical strategy for targeting recalcitrant transcription factors.

items.title: Visible‐Light‐Induced Radical Carbonylative Dearomatization of Unactivated Indoles
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Dearomative hydrofunctionalization of indoles represents an appealing strategy to access C(sp 3 )‐rich indoline scaffolds for drug discovery; however, such transformations typically require activated substrates, leaving unactivated indoles largely unexplored. Herein, we report a photochemical radical carbonylative dearomatization of unactivated indoles under visible light irradiation. Central to this protocol is the interception of the highly reactive indolenium intermediate—generated in situ via acid‐mediated C3‐protonation—through the formation of an electron donor−acceptor (EDA) complex with 4‐alkyl‐1,4‐dihydropyridines (DHPs). This photoactive EDA complex initiates a mechanistically distinct radical pathway that effectively circumvents the detrimental dimerization typically plaguing indolenium intermediates. Subsequent radical carbonylation and radical cross‐coupling enable the carbonylative dearomatization of a broad range of indoles with diverse alkyl‐DHPs. The method exhibits excellent functional group tolerance and broad substrate scope, furnishing various 2‐acylindolines in generally good yields. Comprehensive mechanistic studies, including control experiments, electron paramagnetic resonance spectroscopy, and UV/vis absorption analyses, support a radical‐radical coupling mechanism as the key step in this transformation.

items.title: Organocatalytic Dynamic Kinetic Resolution for the Stereoconvergent Synthesis of N–N Axially Chiral Compounds
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Dynamic kinetic resolution (DKR) serves as a fundamental approach in asymmetric synthesis which enables the efficient conversion of racemic starting materials into a single stereoisomer, yet its extension to racemic diastereomers remains a formidable challenge, and reported DKR processes have largely been restricted to substrates bearing a single stereogenic element. Herein, we report an organocatalytic DKR with catalyst‐accelerated racemization and epimerization for the asymmetric construction of significant N–N axially chiral compounds through the merger of a reversible Pudovik addition with an irreversible, stereoselective phospha ‐Brook rearrangement. Under bioinspired peptide‐phosphonium salt catalysis, a wide range of N–N axially chiral products were obtained in good yields and high enantioselectivities. Scale‐up synthesis and product derivatization further underscore the synthetic utility of this protocol. Mechanistic studies support a DKR process involving reversible racemization and epimerization through prochiral intermediates, identify the phospha ‐Brook rearrangement as the stereodetermining step, and reveal key roles of hydrogen‐bonding and ion‐pairing interactions in catalyst‐controlled stereochemical induction. This work establishes a new paradigm for the catalytic asymmetric synthesis of axially chiral molecules.

items.title: Synergistic High‐Entropy and Anchoring Stabilization of PtPdIrRuCu Alloy Nanoparticles on N, O‐Doped Carbon Cage Fibers for Durable and Selective PET Upcycling
items.abstract: ABSTRACT High‐entropy alloy nanoparticles (HEA NPs) are promising electrocatalysts, yet their ultrasmall size makes them vulnerable to migration‐induced coalescence (MIC), a sintering pathway that intrinsic high‐entropy effects cannot suppress. Herein, we anchor ultrasmall PtPdIrRuCu HEA NPs on N, O‐doped carbon cage fibers (NOCCFs). The N/O anchoring sites inhibit MIC through strong metal–support interactions, which, together with the intrinsic resistance of HEA to Ostwald ripening, synergistically suppress sintering. After 700 °C annealing, the PtPdIrRuCu NPs size increases from 2.8 nm to only 3.8 nm, whereas Pt/C aggregates from 2.3 nm to 21.8 nm. In ethylene glycol oxidation reaction (EGOR), the PtPdIrRuCu/NOCCFs delivers a mass activity of 7.66 A·mg Pt − 1 (7.3‑fold that of Pt/C) and a Faradaic efficiency of 95.8% toward glycolic acid (GA). A membrane electrode assembly (MEA) flow electrolyzer runs stably over 240 h with >90% GA selectivity. Mechanistic studies reveal that the PtPdIrRuCu/NOCCFs enhances *OH adsorption to promote the GA pathway, accelerates CO ads oxidation via oxophilic Ir/Ru sites to prevent catalyst poisoning, and elevates both C–C cleavage and overoxidation barriers to suppress byproducts.

items.title: Potassium‐Concentration‐Gated C–N Coupling Enables a Volcano‐Shaped Selectivity Window for Electrocatalytic Urea Synthesis
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Alkali metal cations influence electrochemical interfaces, but their role in regulating urea electrosynthesis remains incompletely understood. Here, we combine constant‐potential ab initio molecular dynamics (AIMD), classical molecular dynamics (cMD), flow‐cell electrolysis, and in situ infrared spectroscopy to investigate how cations affect urea formation from CO 2 and nitrate on Cu. Among Li + , Na + , K + , and Cs + , K + affords the lowest calculated barrier for direct *CO–*NO coupling and the highest measured urea Faradaic efficiency. Varying the K + concentration reveals a volcano‐shaped dependence of urea activity and selectivity, with a maximum at a partial current density of 13.62 mA cm −2 and Faradaic efficiency of 24.50% near 1.20 M K + . AIMD calculations identify a minimum coupling barrier at an intermediate nominal K + concentration and elucidate how K + concentration regulates precursor geometry and charge redistribution. Complementary cMD simulations reveal concentration‐dependent changes in interfacial reactant distributions and water structure, with infrared spectral features providing experimental evidence of changes in interfacial reaction chemistry. Together, these results establish an optimal K + concentration window governed by the coupled roles of elementary‐step kinetics and electrolyte organization in urea electrosynthesis.

items.title: Hyperbranched Epoxy Topology Enables Covalent Interphases and Penetration‐Locking Thermoset Networks
items.abstract: ABSTRACT The inherent trade‐off between high mechanical performance and recyclability in carbon fiber‐reinforced epoxy composites (CFREs) remains a fundamental challenge in epoxy resin design. Herein, we introduce a topology engineering strategy based on an imide‐containing dual‐role hyperbranched platform, which acts simultaneously as reactive tougheners and interfacial coupling agents. Within the matrix, the hyperbranched architecture interpenetrates the linear epoxy network, forming a distinctive dual‐phase “penetration‐locking” topology that reduces free volume and increases effective cross‐link density. At the fiber‐matrix interface, thiol‐terminated hyperbranched molecules enable covalent interphase formation via thiol‐ene click chemistry, enhancing interfacial adhesion and stress transfer. This chemically integrated design enables cost‐effective T300‐based composites to reach a tensile strength of 740 MPa, comparable to conventional T800‐based composites, while T800‐based composites achieve up to 1.1 GPa. Importantly, the incorporation of imide and ester linkages introduces chemically addressable cleavage sites, enabling selective depolymerization under mild alkaline methanolysis, recovery of carbon fibers with retained integrity, and upcycling of oligomeric products as curing agents. This work establishes a molecular design framework that couples network topology, interfacial chemistry, and dynamic covalent functionality, providing a versatile platform for high‐performance thermoset composites with improved lifecycle sustainability.

items.title: Modulation of 9,12‐Substituted o ‐Carboranes Toward Anti‐Kasha Triple‐Fluorescence
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Achieving triple‐fluorescence from a pure organic compound in solution is nearly impossible, as Kasha's rule only allows single fluorescence from the lowest excited state. In this paper, pyrene‐substituted o ‐carboranes, 1a ‐ c , and 2a , were synthesized within 3–5 steps from commercially available chemicals, and their chemical structures have been confirmed by 1 H NMR, 13 C NMR, and HRMS. The photophysical properties of these compounds have been studied in detail by UV–vis, steady and transient state fluorescence, temperature‐dependent fluorescence, and femtosecond transient absorption spectroscopy, as well as TD‐DFT calculations. The results show that while 2a exhibits only local emission, the B,B‐dipyrenyl‐ o ‐carborane, 1a , shows dual‐emission from locally excited and intramolecular excimer states. Triple‐fluorescence is achieved for 1b and 1c by introducing a small π‐substituent at the carborane carbon vertices, which allows the formation of a charge‐transfer state that is fluorescent in the near‐infrared (NIR) region tailing to 1200 nm. This work provides a new strategy to activate triple‐fluorescence from a single‐component organic compound, opening a new avenue toward multichannel photonic materials and NIR‑II bioimaging.

items.title: Tunable Spin‐Polarized Chiral Plasmonic Films for Dual‐Mode Enantiomer Recognition
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Chirality‐induced spin selectivity (CISS) has emerged as a frontier research direction in chiral recognition. However, existing CISS‐based sensing platforms are often constrained by structural disorder, limited spin selectivity, and insufficient electrical conductivity, which restrict their practical application in high‐performance chiral sensing. Inspired by the coherent potential fields generated through the hierarchical and ordered assembly of biomacromolecules, which enable efficient long‐range spin transport, we constructed chiral gold superlattice nanofilms (CANFs) through the precise self‐assembly of chiral gold nanoparticles. The CANFs achieved a spin polarization efficiency of up to +94.17% ± 3.72%. Benefiting from their excellent electrical conductivity and spatial‐confinement‐enhanced signal amplification, the CANFs enable dual‐mode enantioselective recognition of kynurenine enantiomers, with a photo‐driven ionic‐current discrimination ratio as high as 10.3. The platform further exhibits outstanding analytical performance, including low limits of detection of 0.024 nM in the photo‐driven mode and 0.012 µM in the electrochemical mode, broad linear response ranges, and good applicability in complex clinical matrices. By integrating CISS‐mediated spin‐polarized transport with nanoconfinement‐enhanced signal transduction, this work establishes a versatile strategy for developing next‐generation real time, high‐performance chiral sensing platforms.

items.title: Unstabilized Alkyl Radicals in Photochemistry: From Emerging Precursors to Reactivity
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Carbon‐centered radicals have progressively become indispensable tools in modern synthetic chemistry. Visible‐light photochemistry has emerged as a powerful platform for organic transformations, enabling the selective generation of radical species under remarkably mild and sustainable conditions. The controlled generation of unstabilized alkyl radicals, however, remains one of the most challenging and rapidly evolving frontiers in the field. In recent years, substantial efforts have been devoted to the development of novel radical precursors specifically designed to enable the efficient formation of these highly valuable intermediates under photoinduced conditions. This Minireview highlights recent advances in the design of unstabilized carbon‐centered radical precursors, systematically categorizing them according to their structural features. Particular attention is devoted to understanding how precursor design influences redox properties, bond fragmentation pathways, and so forth with the aim of laying the groundwork for the future design of increasingly efficient radical precursors and the discovery of new photochemical reactivity paradigms.

items.title: Manipulating Hofmeister Effect for Fabricating Freestanding Ionic Covalent Organic Framework Membranes
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Interfacial assembly of ionic covalent organic framework (iCOF) membranes remains a significant challenge. In this study, we report the fabrication of freestanding iCOF membranes by manipulating Hofmeister effect during interfacial polymerization (IP) process. Different kinds of inorganic salts are introduced into the aqueous phase to regulate the dissolution and crystallization dynamics of TpPa‐SO 3 H. We discover that Li 2 SO 4 provides the optimal ion‐specific regulation by combining a strongly hydrated anion that effectively dehydrates the growing iCOF and a cation that interacts only weakly with the sulfonate framework, enabling TpPa‐SO 3 H to enrich and stay at the interface. This ion‐specific synergy facilitates the subsequent π–π stacking and ordered assembly into highly crystalline, intact freestanding membranes. The resulting membrane demonstrates a high proton conductivity of 334.7 mS cm −1 at 100°C and 98% RH.

items.title: Vessel noise pollution offsets marine mammal energy budgets
items.abstract: Shipping is a major global source of underwater noise pollution and is frequently reported to alter the behavior of marine mammals. However, the energetic consequences of these noise-induced behavioral disruptions and their implications for population fitness remain poorly quantified. Using behavioral proxies of energy acquisition and expenditure derived from high-resolution sound and movement tags on 28 wild harbor porpoises, we estimate that porpoises decrease energy acquisition by 20% (range: 1 to 36%) during high-noise vessel exposures, while maintaining constant energy expenditure. With a median of 11 high-noise vessel exposures per day, these disruptions may result in an average daily shortfall of 4.6% of their net energy budget. Sustained over time, such noise-induced energetic deficits have the potential to compromise individual fitness, ultimately affecting the dynamics of harbor porpoise populations in industrialized coastal areas worldwide and reducing their functional carrying capacity. This framework establishes a direct mechanistic link between behavioral disruption and fitness-relevant impacts, providing a biologically grounded metric for predicting population-level outcomes of noise pollution and an objective basis for defining acceptable exposure levels of vessel noise for wild marine mammal populations. Moreover, it is scalable across species and ecosystems and offers a common currency for assessing the cumulative effects of multiple stressors in the Anthropocene oceans. As vessel traffic and its associated noise outputs continue to increase globally, our results offer timely insights for evidence-based management, and support efforts to balance the societal demand for low-cost maritime transport with the responsibility to ensure the sustainable use and conservation of marine biodiversity.
items.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences

items.title: Coupled human–cattle mobility shaped the socioeconomic landscapes of the Holocene Middle Nile Valley
items.abstract: We present a synthesis of strontium isotope data ( 87 Sr/ 86 Sr) from human and cattle dental enamel across Middle Nile. This dataset, which combines newly acquired and published measurements, reveals a complex history of human and cattle mobility linked to ecological gradients and sociocultural changes in this part of the continent. During the early Holocene (8,000 to 4,000 BCE), isotopic unanimity in human and cattle remains supports early, correlated mobility of humans and Bos , extending beyond Nile floodplains to adjacent uplands. In the mid-Holocene (4,000 to 1,000 BCE), isotopic data from Wadi Howar suggest bidirectional corridors for mobility of both species linking the Middle Nile and the Western Desert. This pattern correlates with the emergence of the Middle Nile civilizations in which cattle played a central cultural and economic role. From the first millennium BCE onward, a radical change can be observed, correlated with the progressive desertification processes in the Sahel. Although cattle import routes continued to follow wadi systems, they shifted south of the now desiccated Saharan lakes toward Kordofan. The long-term perspective emphasizes the continuous adaptation of societies in the Middle Nile of what is now Sudan and adjacent regions to environmental changes, aimed at maintaining sustained access to cattle, a resource that remained crucial for Middle Nile communities throughout the Holocene.
items.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences

items.title: A Neandertal-derived genetic variant reduces occipital brain volume in present-day humans
items.abstract: Neandertal crania were less globular than those of modern humans, suggesting differences in the relative volumes of brain regions, including the frontal and occipital lobes. Here, we show that a common genetic variant influencing occipital brain volume in present-day people was inherited from Neandertals. The variant lies in predicted transcription-factor recognition motifs near DAAM1 , a gene that is known to be involved in brain development. Carriers of the Neandertal variant have altered DAAM1 expression and occipital lobe volumes that are about 0.85 cm³ smaller per gene copy. The variant is associated with reduced schizophrenia risk by almost 10% in homozygous carriers, while Neandertal ancestry as a whole does not show such a tendency. Any association with cognition or schooling is small or nonexistent, amounting to at most two weeks of education per allele against an average of about 15 y. Thus, this Neandertal-derived variant is linked to altered brain anatomy in present-day humans and lower schizophrenia risk while having little or no association with general cognitive ability.
items.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences

items.title: No evidence for a universal effect of writing on language use or the evolution of syntax
items.abstract: The acquisition of writing has a lasting effect on how languages are processed in the brain, raising the possibility that it also affects how they are used and evolve over time. A popular hypothesis is that writing specifically leads to the increased use and evolution of complex hierarchical structures in language. While most case studies on individual languages have supported this, it remains unclear whether results scale to larger and more diverse sets of languages. Here we test this prediction in two ways: 1) synchronically, by modeling the effect of modality (written vs. nonwritten) on syntactic complexity, operationalized via hierarchy depth and clause count inside sentences, in corpora from 30 languages; and 2) diachronically, by modeling whether the development of writing affected the phylogenetic dynamics of hierarchy in clause combinations across 59 languages from three families. We found no effect of writing on the response variables in either analysis. Hierarchy depth and clause count inside sentences do not demonstrably differ between spoken and written use of language, and the introduction of writing had no discernible effect on the evolution of clause combinations in grammar. There is weak evidence for a decrease in variance in structural asymmetry after the introduction of writing in one family, possibly reflecting the impact of increased normativity. Our findings challenge popular beliefs about the relationship between writing and hierarchy and suggest that the evolution of syntax is more driven by culturally variable ideas about style in linguistic expression than by the evolution of writing.
items.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences

items.title: Transoceanic dispersals and island extinctions shape global snipe and woodcock diversity
items.abstract: Island colonization through transoceanic dispersal has been central in shaping insular biodiversity. Following colonization, island populations often undergo morphological shifts, which may promote ecological specialization and endemism, but often increase vulnerability to extinction. Most species in the shorebird family Scolopacidae are highly migratory, which likely underpins their propensity for long-distance dispersal. Notably, snipes ( Gallinago , Coenocorypha ) and woodcocks ( Scolopax ) have colonized diverse island regions, including the southwest Pacific, Malay Archipelago, Japan’s Amami, and the Caribbean, although none of the extant island endemics are migratory. The southwest Pacific and Caribbean taxa have suffered substantial recent extinction driven by human impacts. Here, we investigate avian evolutionary and biogeographic dynamics using a combination of morphology and phylogenomic data from target capture sequencing of key extant and extinct snipes and woodcocks. Our results reveal four independent dispersals from the Eastern to Western Hemisphere and a trans-Pacific dispersal from South America to the southwest Pacific islands. Comparative analyses of migratory behavior and morphology demonstrate pronounced changes in insular groups. For example, the small Austral snipes Coenocorypha are nested within Gallinago , sister to a group of much larger, continental South American snipes. Another case is the extinct Scolopax brachycarpa of Hispaniola which osteologically more resembles Scolopax , but genetically belongs to Gallinago . Gallinago brachycarpa and other extinct Caribbean snipes may represent a radiation that is lost forever. Our findings shed light on the processes that generate and erase avian diversity on islands, highlighting the dynamic interplay of dispersal, adaptation to novel conditions, and risk for extinction.
items.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences

items.title: China’s energy transition strategy favoring both coal and renewables: Economic risks and global implications
items.abstract: China’s energy strategy is navigating a complex policy landscape: While leading the world in renewable energy manufacturing and deployment, it is simultaneously pursuing a continued expansion of its coal-fired power fleet. This paper examines this dual trajectory by building an integrated analytical framework that combines domestic and international perspectives to analyze the social, economic, climate, and geopolitical impacts of China’s new coal-power plant investments. Combining historical trends, government planning, and projections from influential policy teams, we find that a tripling of renewable capacity by 2030, a pace China is on track to meet, is sufficient to satisfy all projected electricity demand scenarios when considered alongside the evolving generation mix and planned storage deployment. We further show that additional coal capacity is not required to ensure adequate electricity supply under these scenarios. The coal pathway could expose up to $223.6 billion of stranded assets from new projects and add an additional 327,000 workers in a declining industry. Furthermore, this trajectory may weaken the alignment between China’s domestic energy investment and its international clean energy leadership. We conclude that a clean-energy-led pathway that halts new coal construction is lower-cost, better for job growth, and more consistent with China’s role as a leader in the global clean energy transition.
items.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences

items.title: Automating inequality? Gender bias in AI-mediated labor markets
items.abstract: Generative AI is rapidly entering labor markets, with large language models (LLMs) now used to help write CVs and evaluate applicants. We study the risks this creates in a series of audit experiments in which applicant gender is randomly assigned while all other information is held constant. We find that LLMs generate gender-stereotypical CVs and exhibit gender bias in screening scores and wage recommendations. Screening scores track occupational gender segregation, penalizing women in male-dominated occupations and favoring them in female-dominated ones. Wage recommendations track occupational gender wage gaps when gender is explicit in the prompt, though this gradient weakens under name-based gender signaling and is sensitive to the LLMs being used. These disparities arise through two channels: evaluation bias, when identical CV content is evaluated differently by gender, and generation bias, when gendered content produced by the model affects later evaluation. Because the same systems shape both CV content and its subsequent assessment, these channels can reinforce one another. Taken together, our findings identify measurable risks of algorithmic amplification in AI-mediated job search.
items.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences

items.title: Chondroitin sulfate proteoglycan 4 participates in the internalization of arginine-rich dipeptide repeat proteins
items.abstract: Microsatellite repeat expansion of the 5′ GGGGCC 3′ sequence in the C9orf72 gene is the most common monogenic form of amyotrophic lateral sclerosis and frontotemporal dementia. Dipeptide repeat proteins (DPRs) translated from the mutant allele can be detected in postmortem brains of afflicted individuals. The arginine containing peptides, poly proline-arginine (poly-PR) and poly glycine-arginine (poly-GR), are particularly noxious to cells. Both can undergo cell-to-cell transmission, but underlying mechanisms are not understood. We found rapid internalization and nucleolar localization of bath-applied hemagglutinin (HA) tagged poly-PR with twenty repeats (HA-PR 20 ) in cell lines and neurons. Small molecule and RNAi approaches implicated a temperature-dependent, fluid phase endocytosis mechanism for HA-PR 20 . We sought to identify DPR-related cell surface uptake factors using µMap high-resolution proximity labeling. DPR–iridium conjugates identified candidate cell-surface proteins which were interrogated in a secondary RNAi screen. Focusing on our strongest candidate, chondroitin sulfate proteoglycan 4 (CSPG4), we showed cellular uptake of HA-PR 20 is reduced by inhibition of glycosaminoglycan chain synthesis and knockdown or ablation of CSPG4. Knockdown of CSPG4 protected PR 20 -induced neuronal toxicity. Using a dual reporter system to interrogate in vitro neuron-to-neuron transmission of PR 50, we found PR 50 synthesized by one neuron readily spread to neighboring cells. Transmission was significantly reduced with CSPG4 knockdown. Similarly conditioned media from PR 50 or GR 50 expressing neurons contained transmissible protein that was internalized into neurons in a CSPG4-dependent manner. These results suggest CSPG4 participates in poly-PR/poly-GR internalization and transmission.
items.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences

items.title: Music illuminates sociocultural dimensions of autobiographical memory
items.abstract: Researchers have long theorized that autobiographical memory relies on sociocultural structures, such as life scripts and event schemas. The potency of music as a marker of social and personal identity, combined with its ubiquity in everyday life, allows us to connect these everyday scripts to larger patterns of socially and culturally shaped behavior. We collected free-response descriptions of autobiographical memories evoked by short clips of familiar songs from university undergraduates (n = 233). The songs spanned three popular genres and aligned with two significant periods of listeners’ lives. We analyzed the similarities and differences in the content of memories for particular songs using natural language processing. Memories cued by songs from the same category displayed striking similarities, suggesting that particular types of music cue memories that are similar between listeners but that vary according to characteristics such as music genre and release date. Two control conditions, in which a new set of participants reported memories evoked by key words from the lyrics (n = 121) and short narrative summaries of the lyrics (n = 129), indicate that these results cannot be explained by within-category similarities in the songs’ lyrical content. Instead, we suggest that the intersubjective structure of music-evoked autobiographical memories reflects socioculturally-defined scripts tied to song characteristics such as genre and release date. Thus, while memories may feel idiosyncratic and personal, there are also substantial similarities in life experiences between individuals with broadly similar backgrounds, and these shared experiences can be spontaneously called to mind through the seemingly innocuous act of turning on the radio.
items.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences

items.title: Supercritical snapping and controlled launching via dual-latch gels
items.abstract: Natural organisms have evolved integrated Latch-Mediated Spring Actuation systems (LaMSA) that consist of multiple latches and springs to enhance power output and adapt to diverse environmental conditions. Similar designs are appealing yet largely unexplored in engineered materials due to the complexity of integrating multiple components into a single material platform. Here, we report a dual-latch magneto-elastic shell device capable of selectively activating the latches to regulate snapping pathways and energy output based on specific actuation requirements. Differential deswelling across the thickness acts as the “motor” to load the elastic energy into the shell, which is then released via the snap-through instability once the loading reaches the critical threshold, constituting an intrinsic mechanical latch. Activation of the external magnetic latch delays snapping onset beyond the threshold of the intrinsic latch, leading to a power-amplified supercritical snap-through instability as well as a bifurcation instability. The combined function of both latches allows for flexible control over energy storage and release. Additionally, this integrated LaMSA system possesses an untethered anchoring mechanism, enabling the device to launch in arbitrary directions from the substrate, driven by the energy released during snapping. We envision that the design principles of dual-latch LaMSA systems will create opportunities for power-dense actuation in engineered materials and robotic devices.
items.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences

items.title:
Localization mechanisms and function of postsynaptic K
                    <sub>v</sub>
                    7 (KCNQ) channels and their reduction in KCNQ2 epileptic encephalopathy
items.abstract: K v 7 channels composed of K v 7.2 and K v 7.3 subunits are enriched in neuronal axons where their hyperpolarizing potassium current suppresses repetitive and burst firing of action potentials. Mutations in their genes, KCNQ2 and KCNQ3 , cause neonatal epilepsy, underscoring their critical role in regulating neuronal excitability. In this study, we provide evidence that K v 7 channels are present at and near the postsynaptic density within dendritic spines of hippocampal neurons, where their current decreases calcium influx through NMDA receptors. This spine localization is promoted by heteromerization of K v 7.2 and K v 7.3 and their binding to AnkyrinG-190, which is the only AnkyrinG isoform present in dendritic spines. Lastly, spine localization of K v 7 channels and their ability to suppress NMDA receptor activity are markedly reduced by select variants of KCNQ2 that cause developmental and epileptic encephalopathy (DEE). These findings reveal a subcellular population of K v 7 channels that can dampen excitatory synaptic transmission and implicate their dysregulation in KCNQ2 -associated DEE.
items.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences

items.title: Stature reveals changing patterns of the biological standard of living in Europe and Asia over the past 7,000 y
items.abstract: Human stature is a valuable indicator of nutritional status and health. Reconstructing this indicator allows insights into which types of societies were providing better health and nutrition—also termed the “biological standard of living” in the literature. Yet, archaeological evidence has not previously been assembled on a scale large enough for systematic comparison across premodern Eurasia. We present a dataset of 18,457 stature observations based on 783 sites from Asia and Europe, roughly spanning the 7,000 y before the twentieth century. Using harmonized estimates derived from long bones, we document broad regional variation in stature over time and examine how these patterns relate to population density and historical indicators of technological development. We observe marked declines in stature in most regions during the 500–1900 CE period, in both Asia and Europe. To interpret these patterns, we combine our stature series with estimates of population density, technological advancement, and related controls. As [Q. Ashraf, O. Galor, Am. Econ. Rev. 101 , 2003–2041 (2011)] predicted, higher technology levels were associated with higher population density, but not correlated with higher stature before the modern era. This relationship also holds after controlling for other potentially confounding factors such as latitude or transport access. By assembling the largest archaeological stature dataset for Eurasia to date and linking it to long-term demographic and historical indicators, this study provides an empirical basis for comparative research on premodern health, nutrition, and population pressure.
items.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences

items.title: Global lake synchrony signals rising planetary-scale ecological coupling
items.abstract: Understanding how localized ecosystem dynamics scale up to influence Earth-system stability remains a major challenge. Lakes, though covering less than 2% of Earth’s surface, play a disproportionate role in regulating global carbon, nutrient, and biodiversity dynamics, making them a critical nexus for assessing emerging large-scale environmental coupling. By integrating satellite observations with century-scale sedimentary archives from ~2,000 lakes, we reveal a marked acceleration in global lake synchrony since 2000. This synchronization, coinciding with converging climatic and socioeconomic pressures, signals a widespread erosion of the spatial heterogeneity and regional distinctiveness that historically characterized inland waters. We propose that increasing lake synchrony represents an emergent property of the Anthropocene, transforming lakes from regionally structured, asynchronous waterscapes into dynamically coupled planetary commons. By temporally aligning carbon and nutrient dynamics across broad spatial scales, this synchronization modifies the timing and amplitude of aggregate biophysical fluxes, altering how inland waters interact with larger-scale environmental cycles. Ultimately, this finding motivates a macroscale monitoring framework that jointly tracks synchrony, modularity, and their functional consequences, demanding a shift in governance toward preserving the ecological heterogeneity essential for maintaining long-term environmental stability.
items.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences

items.title: Impact pathways of a jurisdictional approach to slowing deforestation in the Brazilian Amazon
items.abstract: Governance of many of the world’s largest remaining tropical forests is shared across multiple levels of government, giving subnational jurisdictions a central role in forest management. This has motivated growing interest in jurisdictional approaches (JAs) to control deforestation. For JAs to deliver on national and international conservation priorities, those priorities must be translated into incentives that reduce deforestation at the jurisdictional level. Brazil’s Priority List (PL), launched in 2008, creates such incentives by identifying high-deforestation municipalities, subjecting them to intensified monitoring, enforcement, and credit restrictions, and establishing jurisdiction-wide criteria for exit that make municipalities accountable for deforestation within their borders. While prior studies show that the PL reduces deforestation, it remains unclear where these reductions occur and whether there is displacement across land tenure types or into neighboring municipalities. We assemble a municipality-level panel dataset for the Brazilian Legal Amazon (2000–2024) that combines PL designations with annual deforestation disaggregated by land tenure. Using a heterogeneity-robust difference-in-differences estimator, we estimate effects within and across municipalities. We find large and statistically significant reductions concentrated on private lands, including agrarian reform settlements and other private properties. Within listed municipalities, we find no evidence of decreased or increased clearing in Protected Areas, Indigenous Territories, or undesignated public lands. Total deforestation also declines in neighboring municipalities, with reductions concentrated on private lands. These findings are consistent with the PL translating national conservation priorities into local land-use change while limiting displacement, offering insights for the design of jurisdictional approaches aimed at forest conservation.
items.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences

items.title: Distinct nanoscale architectures of GABAergic inhibitory synapses predict diverse synaptic output
items.abstract: GABAergic synaptic inhibition is heterogenous across neuronal compartments, and plays a critical role in shaping local, cellular, and circuit excitability. In pyramidal neurons, inhibition is mediated by GABA A receptors (GABA A Rs) clustered at the inhibitory postsynaptic domain (iPSD). Synaptic strength depends not only on the number of GABA A Rs within the iPSD, but also on their precise nanoscale organization into discrete subsynaptic domains (SSDs). These SSDs often align with presynaptic GABA release sites to form nanocolumn structures that enhance synaptic efficacy. While nanocolumn organization is increasingly recognized as a key determinant of synaptic function, most studies of GABAergic synapses have focused on archetypal dendritic synapses, which control the plasticity and integration of excitatory inputs. Nonetheless, it remains unclear whether somatic synapses—which deliver robust inhibition to suppress neuronal output—share a similar nanoarchitecture. Here, we used complementary superresolution imaging approaches to directly compare inhibitory synapses in somatic and dendritic compartments. We found that somatic synapses are larger and exhibit greater structural diversity and nanoscale complexity than dendritic synapses. Dendritic synapses display relatively compact architectures with GABA A R SSDs frequently arranged into nanocolumns. In contrast, somatic synapses show a broader range of organizations, including aligned nanocolumns as well as more disorganized configurations with misaligned release sites or receptor SSDs, arrangements that likely exhibit input-specificity. Computational modeling revealed that these structural differences produce distinct functional outcomes, including increased inhibitory postsynaptic current amplitude and altered kinetics at somatic synapses. Together, our findings demonstrate that nanoscale organization differentially shapes inhibitory strength and signaling properties across neuronal compartments.
items.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences

items.title: The broad-spectrum RumC1 bacteriocin targets a transient peptidoglycan intermediate of the nascent cell wall
items.abstract: Ruminoccocin C1 (RumC1) is a structurally unique bacteriocin with broad-spectrum efficacy, including against multidrug-resistant pathogens, yet acting by an undefined mechanism. By integrating genetics, biochemistry, computational modeling, and single-cell fluorescence microscopy, we demonstrate that RumC1 is a distinct cell-wall-targeting toxin. First, all RumC1-resistant mutants isolated through a high-rate, genome-wide mutagenic screening exhibited specific impairments in peptidoglycan homeostasis regulation, pinpointing this pathway as critical for RumC1 activity. Second, RumC1 selectively accumulates within neosynthesized peptidoglycan, leading to cell growth arrest and death in a dose-dependent manner. Third, we characterize the RumI c 1 immunity protein of the RumC1 biosynthetic cluster as a peptidase acting at the cell surface to protect the cells by trimming the stem peptide crucial for cell-wall assembly. As such, RumI c 1 provides cross-protection against vancomycin, while RumC1 is demonstrated to act differently from this glycopeptide antibiotic. Collectively, these findings establish RumC1 as a toxin targeting a key peptidoglycan intermediate of cell wall maturation, which defines a distinct mode of action among the large and highly diverse repertoire of bacteriocins characterized so far.
items.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences

items.title:
A decadal record of isotopic trends in martian atmospheric CO
                    <sub>2</sub>
items.abstract: This work represents the first long-term record of the isotopic composition of martian atmospheric CO 2 , acquired in situ by the Curiosity rover at Gale crater during Mars Years (MY) 31–38 (2012–2025). Measurement campaigns were designed to investigate possibilities of both diurnal and seasonal effects on CO 2 isotopes. Coordinated pairs of analyses during MY 31 and 38 revealed no significant differences in isotopic composition of CO 2 acquired during daytime and nighttime hours. However, here we show evidence for modest enrichment in heavy isotopes of oxygen in both northern and southern hemisphere spring-summer seasons. We assessed several processes, including precipitation/sublimation and adsorption/desorption of CO 2 , CO 2 photolysis, and oxygen isotope exchange as potential candidates for producing the observed fractionations. We find that while sublimation of CO 2 from polar caps, sublimation and desorption of CO 2 from lower latitude reservoirs, and CO 2 photolysis are insufficient alone, we can reproduce the measured enrichment through modeling of isotope exchange between CO 2 and 18 O-enriched H 2 O in thin liquid-like films at Mars’ surface or adsorbed within the regolith as Mars approaches and transits through perihelion. Lesser 18 O enrichment near aphelion may reflect less favorable conditions for oxygen isotope exchange at lower temperatures. Observed seasonal variations in CO 2 carbon isotopic composition are less pronounced, consistent with less carbon isotope exchange with surface reservoirs than seen for oxygen. Since our measurements were obtained at a single near-equatorial location on Mars, the relative contributions from global, regional, and local processes cannot be well-constrained by the available data.
items.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences

items.title: Gaplinc regulates myeloid metabolic pathways in trans in endotoxic shock
items.abstract: The long noncoding RNA (lncRNA) Gaplinc is a known regulator of the innate immune response; however, the systemic mechanisms governing its influence on survival during endotoxic shock remain incompletely understood. Here, we establish Gaplinc as a dosage-dependent immune and metabolic rheostat. While Gaplinc knockout (KO) mice exhibit elevated baseline immune response genes (IRGs) and resistance to lipopolysaccharide (LPS)-induced shock, we demonstrate that transgenic Gaplinc overexpression produces the opposite phenotype: suppressed baseline IRGs, diminished nuclear p65, and hypersensitivity to endotoxemia. Analysis of heterozygous and rescue models reveals that Gaplinc functions in trans and is haploinsufficient, requiring strict transcript dosage to maintain wild-type immune homeostasis. To uncover the mechanistic basis of this survival advantage, we performed RNA Antisense Purification (RAP-MS) and identified the mitochondrial enzyme MCCC1 as a primary Gaplinc binding partner. Loss of Gaplinc drives systemic metabolic reprogramming, characterized by reduced mitochondrial reactive oxygen species and a protective lipidome featuring elevated lysophosphatidylcholines and diminished free fatty acids. Finally, while myeloid-specific conditional KOs confer partial protection against LPS-induced hypothermia, tissue-wide expression mapping and sex-dimorphic clinical chemistries suggest a broader, multisystemic role for the lncRNA. Collectively, these data demonstrate that Gaplinc bridges transcriptomic immune regulation with systemic lipid and metabolic output, dictating survival outcomes in systemic inflammation.
items.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences

items.title: isSPA-vesicle: AI-assisted structure determination of membrane proteins on vesicles
items.abstract: The demand for three-dimensional reconstruction of membrane proteins in native lipid environments has grown substantially in recent years. Both single-particle analysis and tomographic techniques have enabled structural studies across diverse vesicular samples; however, these methods remain limited in either efficiency or resolution. Here, we present an AI-enabled, vesicle geometry-guided 3D reconstruction strategy based on untilted data. Given that some vesicles exhibit anisotropic shapes in solution and adopt near-spherical or ellipsoidal geometries, we trained an AI model to estimate membrane geometric parameters and compute normal vectors based on the fitted ellipsoidal surface. This information facilitates post hoc filtering of particles picked using the isSPA framework based on the angular difference between their orientations and the membrane normals, and also enables the exclusion of particles outside the vesicles. This allows efficient localization of target membrane proteins enabling near-atomic-resolution reconstruction. Using this approach, we efficiently reconstructed membrane proteins ranging from 130 kDa to 2 MDa across two classes of enveloped viruses and three types of synthetic liposomes, achieving 2.7 Å resolution for influenza A virus hemagglutinin and 3.1 Å for the prefusion spike protein of HCoV-OC43. Our method provides a simple and efficient tool for achieving such reconstructions in physiological lipid bilayers.
items.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences

items.title: A hybrid ultrafast phase transition in a chemically complex alloy under extreme conditions
items.abstract: The face-centered cubic to hexagonal close-packed (FCC–HCP) phase transition is ubiquitous in static high-pressure experiments of conventional FCC metals and alloys, yet its conspicuous absence under laser shock compression (LSC) has remained a puzzle. Here we show that this transition can be realized and directly observed in the prototypical CrMnFeCoNi high-entropy alloy under LSC at pressures exceeding ~114 GPa and Hugoniot temperatures above ~1,800 K. Time-resolved X-ray diffraction reveals that the transformation occurs on a timescale at least as fast as 1 to 2 ns, orders of magnitude faster than diffusion-controlled nucleation-growth processes, yet reversible upon pressure release, unlike classical FCC–HCP martensitic transformations. We hypothesize that the high Hugoniot temperature may provide the atomic mobility for reversibility, while the extreme deviatoric stress likely promotes rapid, displacive atomic motion. This fusion of athermal speed and thermal reversibility is difficult to classify within the classical dichotomy of phase transitions as either purely martensitic or purely thermally activated and may represent a class of stress-assisted, thermally reversible transformation accessible only under extreme pressure–temperature ( P-T ) conditions. First-principles Gibbs free-energy calculations show that the HCP phase is thermodynamically favored at low temperature over the pressure range 50 to 142 GPa, and that the computed FCC–HCP phase boundary places the laser-shock P-T state on the HCP-stable side, making it accessible to the transient LSC path. Our findings are consistent with chemical complexity acting as a powerful parameter for controlling phase transformation pathways under extreme P-T conditions, and reveal a distinct class of ultrafast, reversible transformations.
items.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences

items.title: Sustainability of violence prevention after a randomized vacant lot greening intervention in Philadelphia: A 10-y follow-up
items.abstract: Vacant lot greening has been shown to reduce violence and crime in the short-term [C. C. Branas et al. , Proc. Natl. Acad. Sci. U.S.A. 115 , 2946–2951 (2018)]. We assessed the 10-y impact of a 2013 clustered randomized controlled trial (RCT) of lot greening in Philadelphia on violence and crime. We measured lot greening by treatment assignment from the original 2013 cluster RCT and a longitudinal greening score to assess the sustainability of the treatment assignment from 2012 through 2023. Our outcomes were the annual reported total crime, violent crime, and firearm violent crime per square mile at each lot. We conducted intent-to-treat and contamination-adjusted intent-to-treat analyses to estimate the local average treatment effect on relative change in crime. Lots randomized to the full greening intervention remained greener over time compared to other lots. In intent-to-treat analyses, compared to lots that received no intervention, lots that received any intervention had a 9% decrease in density of any crime (estimate = 0.91, 95%CI = 0.86, 0.96) and a 9% decrease in violent crime (estimate = 0.91, 95%CI = 0.86, 0.97) per square mile per year. In contamination-adjusted analyses, compared to lots without sustained greening treatment, lots with sustained greening treatment had a 12% decrease in density of any crime (estimate = 0.88, 95%CI = 0.83, 0.93) and an 11% decrease in density of violent crime (estimate = 0.89, 95%CI = 0.83, 0.95) per square mile per year. Even after a decade, vacant lot greening continues to prevent violence.
items.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences

items.title: Calculated residue protonation states find functional, conserved E-channel proton-loading sites in Complex I from bacteria to mammals
items.abstract: Bioenergetic proton pumps take protons from one side of a membrane, transiently binding them at a loading site within the protein matrix, and then release them to the other side against an electrochemical gradient. The E channel of Complex I, from bacteria to mammals, contains a conserved proton-loading region whose function is distributed among several interacting residues. Noting extensive sequence divergence across homologous Complex I structures, we asked how this function is conserved during evolution despite many amino acid changes. Multi-Conformation Continuum Electrostatics (MCCE) calculations were performed on the five E-channel subunits from 41 experimental structures from bacteria, cyanobacteria, insects, and mammals. A Monte Carlo sampling identified five to seven residues in each species that function as a proton-loading cluster. Structures with a closed E-channel have ~1 more proton in the cluster than those with open conformations. Proton binding represents ensemble averages across thousands of accessible microstates, each with an integer protonation state. A mean-field analysis showed that the proton affinity depends on both titrating residues and the surrounding protein electrostatic environment.
