These findings provide insights into the molecular mechanisms driving host–microbe coevolution and highlight the evolutionary forces shaping microbial specialization within host–symbiont relationships.
items.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences

items.title: In This Issue
items.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences

items.title: Rapid soil degradation of a cross-linked, semicrystalline polyethylene-like polyester produced by Colletes bees
items.abstract: Polyethylene (PE)-like polyesters have long been investigated as biodegradable alternatives to conventional polyolefins but degrade poorly despite possessing hydrolyzable esters due to high crystallinity and hydrophobicity. Bees of the genus Colletes line their nests with a PE-like polyester that shows no environmental accumulation despite decades of nesting in dense aggregations, suggesting rapid biodegradability. This work provides a comprehensive characterization of Colletes inaequalis polyester and demonstrates its rapid degradation under ambient environmental conditions. Colletes polyester is completely insoluble in trichlorobenzene or toluene at elevated temperatures, indicating cross-linking despite originating from macrocyclic lactones that lack obvious cross-linkable functionality. Small molecules extracted from the network match the Dufour’s gland secretion but lack macrolactone, indicating complete monomer conversion. Although its repeat unit resembles amorphous, network-like plant cutin, Colletes polyester is highly crystalline ( X c = 60%), with PE-like orthorhombic packing and T m = 75 °C, indicating a much lower cross-link density. Composition analysis of nest linings collected 0 to 11 mo after construction reveals significant degradation, with polyester content falling from 73 to 40 wt% within 4 mo in ambient soil. Esterase activity against the model substrate p-nitrophenylbutyrate is observed in both newly constructed and 4-mo aged linings, which may accelerate environmental degradation. Crystallites also lack higher-order spherulitic or lamellar structure, possibly due to cross-linking, which may promote degradation by leaving more esters exposed to cleavage. This PE-like polyester is shown to degrade rapidly in the environment, offering a template for next-generation biodegradable PE-like polymers.
items.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences

items.title: Ancient genomes from Mendoza, Argentina, trace the dynamics of colonial urban formation in the Southern Cone of the Americas
items.abstract: European colonization introduced abrupt changes into the Americas. These included the introduction of infectious diseases, forced labor and displacement of Indigenous and African individuals, European settlement, and the imposition of caste regimes. However, the role of these forces in reshaping communities across different regions remains debated. This is especially true in the Virreinato del Río de la Plata (the territories of present-day Argentina, Bolivia, Uruguay, Paraguay, and Brazil), which is less studied than other regions such as the United States, the Caribbean, and Mexico. We investigated how these forces shaped the colonial societies of Mendoza in the Cuyo region (Central-Western Argentina) by sequencing ancient DNA of 28 individuals (17th to 19th centuries) excavated from churches associated with different social strata, recovering 22 mitochondrial genomes, and genome-wide data of 15 individuals. By performing paleogenomic analyses contextualized by burial site, we detected admixture among Indigenous, European, and African populations, with ancestry partially structured by church and burial location. Exceptions to this pattern indicate social mobility and flexible social classifications beyond genetic ancestry. The European-related ancestry aligns with Southern European migration, while African-related ancestry shows affinities to Western-Central Africa. The Indigenous-related ancestry shows highest affinity to precontact populations from Cuyo, supporting local genetic continuity across the colonial period. Additionally, uniparental markers reflect sex-biased dispersal and admixture. These findings reveal often-neglected African contributions to the city’s formation and illustrate how caste, labor, and migration shaped colonial urban societies. Our work provides a scalable model for interrogating caste regimes, social mobility, and admixture in understudied regions of the Americas.
items.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences

items.title: Heme signatures in mineralized red blood cells within vascular canals of a 115-million-year-old dinosaur bone
items.abstract: Detection of endogenous biomolecules in vertebrate fossils remains controversial because labile compounds degrade quickly and are highly susceptible to contamination. Here, we present data on the preservation of heme-derived tetrapyrroles, and vascular canal-constrained ellipsoidal microstructures, inferred to be red blood cells, in limb bones of Aratasaurus museunacionali , a 115-million-year-old theropod dinosaur. High-performance liquid chromatography–mass spectrometry identified parent and diagenetically altered heme B as the principal tetrapyrroles of bone extract, contrasting the chlorophyll and bacteriochlorophyll porphyrin signatures of the surrounding matrix supporting an endogenous origin. Separate spatially resolved analyses by Raman spectroscopy and transmission electron microscopy confirmed the ellipsoid microstructure localization of i) porphyrin signals of heme and ii) key elements of heme (Fe, N, and C) and mineral stabilizing hausmannite (Mn 3 O 4 ), respectively. These results demonstrate blood-derived biomolecules in mineralized red blood cells of a dinosaur.
items.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences

items.title: Designing school choice for diversity in the San Francisco Unified School District
items.abstract: More than 65 years after the Brown v. Board of Education ruling that school segregation is unconstitutional, public schools across the United States are again experiencing rising segregation. In districts like San Francisco, efforts to implement district-wide choice policies have largely failed to reverse these trends. Since 2019, we have collaborated with the San Francisco Unified School District to design a student assignment policy meeting the district’s goals of diversity, predictability, and proximity. We use optimization techniques to develop policies restricting choice to zones. We compare these to district-wide choice policies by estimating a choice model using historical application data and simulating assignment. Our results show multiple policies can reduce school segregation while preserving varying degrees of proximity, choice, and predictability. Zone-based policies with reserves reduce the concentration of racial minority students in high-poverty schools and maintain proximity, but reduce choice. District-wide choice with reserves and distance-based priority can further reduce segregation, but at the cost of predictability. Tradeoffs are necessary as no policy dominates another policy. In addition, we show that spatial segregation indices capture average patterns in these tradeoffs but miss important variation revealed by our simulation framework. Our work informed the design and approval of a zone-based policy in San Francisco in 2020, and supports ongoing policy implementation.
items.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences

items.title: Environmental forcing, individual repeatability, and mother–daughter resemblance shape the phenology of a long-lived seabird
items.abstract: Climate change and variability push species to shift their distributions and phenology to track their climatic niche. Predicting population responses requires identifying the environmental cues that trigger reproduction, their fitness consequences, and the intrinsic factors that shape individual breeding decisions. In long-lived species with deferred breeding, extrinsic (environmental) and intrinsic (individual/maternal) factors may interact in shaping responses to environmental change, but direct empirical evidence remains scarce. We use 2065 breeding events collected over 22 y on a wide-ranging seabird, the Scopoli’s Shearwater. We quantify the effects on population mean laying date of a large-scale climatic index (wNAO) associated with oceanographic conditions. We assess how individual breeding experience and mother–daughter resemblance contribute to among-female differences in reproductive timing, and evaluate the consequences for breeding success (BS) and adult survival. Average laying date was earlier under negative phases of wNAO, indicating a plastic response at the population level. Individual repeatability in the relative laying date (RLD) was high ( R = 0.50) irrespective of experience, indicating consistency among females. Using 142 mother–daughter cases, daughters’ RLD resembled those of their mothers, a covariance that may reflect genetic inheritance, maternal effects, or shared environment. Early laying was associated with higher BS and survival, translating into an annual fitness advantage. Differences in survival and BS across individuals were more evident during the first observed breeding attempts. Together, these results support a scenario in which plasticity shifts the population mean breeding date in response to climatic variation, while persistent traits generate differential fitness among individuals.
items.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences

items.title: A causal account of the neural origins of mental fatigue
items.abstract: Successful goal-directed behavior often requires the exertion of effortful cognitive control processes, but it remains unclear why engaging in cognitive control is experienced as effortful and induces fatigue. Here, we tested the hypothesis that sustained activation in the dorsolateral prefrontal cortex (DLPFC)—a neural substrate of cognitive control—causally induces motivational fatigue via the accumulation of prefrontal glutamate metabolites. For this purpose, we combined brain stimulation with spectroscopy imaging to assess how increasing DLPFC excitability during an effortful mental task changes the motivation for mental effort and glutamate concentrations. We found that stimulating the DLPFC during mental effort exertion improved mental performance at the cost of increased posteffort motivational fatigue, suggesting a causal role of DLPFC activation for inducing fatigue. On the neural level, DLPFC activation during effortful cognition also increased prefrontal concentrations of glutamate, which statistically explained the fatigue-induced lower motivation for mental effort. A corresponding analysis of combined glutamate–glutamine (Glx) concentrations revealed converging effects. Together, these findings provide causal evidence that enhanced DLPFC activation contributes to fatigue via neurochemical changes, supporting neuro-metabolic accounts of fatigue and offering new insights into why demanding cognitive tasks are perceived as effortful.
items.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences

items.title:
CD8
                    <sup>+</sup>
                    regulatory T cells limit immunopathology but impair viral clearance in Hantaan virus infection
items.abstract: In hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome (HFRS) caused by Hantaan virus (HTNV), virus-specific CD8 + T cells mediate both viral clearance and immunopathology. Here, we characterized a CD8 + regulatory T cell (Treg) subset restricted by HLA-E (and its murine ortholog Qa-1) in HFRS patients and in a murine HTNV infection model. CD8 + Tregs (CD122 + Eomes + CD49d lo KIR + ), a subset substantially enriched for HLA-E-restricted T cells, were significantly reduced in peripheral blood of HFRS patients and displayed a terminally differentiated profile with elevated expression of KLRG-1, NKG2A, CTLA-4, and Fas-L, correlating with disease severity. Two HTNV glycoprotein-derived nonapeptides that bound Qa-1 were identified. Following immunization with the identified HTNV peptides and subsequent HTNV challenge, wild-type (WT) mice showed attenuated renal immunopathology, whereas D227K knock-in mice (with disrupted Qa-1-CD8/TCR interaction) showed enhanced viral clearance in the spleen and kidney but exacerbated renal immunopathology. Mechanistically, Qa-1-restricted CD8 + Tregs from WT mice suppressed effector CD8 + T cell proliferation in a peptide-specific, CD8/TCR-dependent manner via enhanced TGF-β secretion. Strikingly, D227K mutation dichotomously reshaped Treg phenotype: bulk polyclonal CD8 + Tregs displayed compensatory upregulation of inhibitory receptors (NKG2A, CTLA-4, PD-1) and TGF-β, whereas epitope-specific CD8 + Tregs showed impaired antigen-specific suppressive function and attenuated TGF-β production. Collectively, these findings indicate that HLA-E/Qa-1-restricted CD8 + Tregs can restrain immunopathology during HTNV infection, potentially at the cost of delayed viral elimination. Modulation of this axis may provide insights for therapeutic strategies in HFRS and related viral hemorrhagic fevers.
items.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences

items.title: Thermal ecology drives alternate responses to rising temperatures in Caribbean anoles
items.abstract: Rapidly rising temperatures threaten populations of ectothermic animals worldwide, with the greatest impacts predicted in the tropics—hotspots for biodiversity. Ectotherms can respond to warming through two primary compensatory responses: behavioral thermoregulation, which buffers exposure to extreme temperatures; and heat tolerance increases via plasticity, adaptation, or both. The relative contribution of these responses is predicted to depend on ecological context, but whether these principles can anticipate organismal responses to contemporary warming remains largely untested. Here, using a decadal resurvey of anole lizards from Hispaniola, Jamaica, and Puerto Rico, we show that simple principles of thermal ecology can reliably anticipate organismal responses to rising temperatures. Species occupying thermally heterogeneous open/edge habitats, such as dry forests, behaviorally thermoregulate and have shown little to no increase in heat tolerance over the past decade. By contrast, species from thermally homogeneous closed-canopy environments are poor thermoregulators and have increased their heat tolerance by 2 °C, on average, over the same period. Seasonal comparisons, acclimation experiments, and laboratory-rearing experiments indicate that contemporary increases in heat tolerance likely reflect contributions from rapid evolutionary change and physiological plasticity. Thermal ecology, not phylogenetic or spatial proximity, is the key factor driving responses to rising temperatures. Our results consistently link organismal responses to habitat complexity and thermoregulatory behavior; we suggest that these factors are key to predicting how ectotherms respond to climate warming.
items.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences

items.title: 3D confinement reshapes RNA folding and enhances circularization in the Zika virus
items.abstract: Many RNA molecules function within confined environments, but the effect of confinement on RNA folding remains poorly understood. Proximity ligation experiments reveal altered long-range contacts in confined vs. unconfined states, yet they do not explain how spatial constraints give rise to these differences. Here, we develop a physical modeling approach that incorporates proximity ligation data into coarse-grained molecular dynamics simulations to reconstruct RNA 3D structures under confinement. We test our model on the ∼ 11 kb genome of the Zika virus, comparing the folding in virions (confined) and in cells (unconfined). We observe that the probability of contact between two regions of the genome vs. linear distance follows different scaling laws in the confined and unconfined cases, in agreement with proximity ligation experiments. We find that genome circularization—an interaction that regulates replication in Zika—occurs more frequently under confinement in both experiments and simulations. Our model reveals that the formation of long double-stranded stems through stacking confers local nematic liquid crystalline order to the RNA, and predicts pseudoknot topologies consistent with those seen in crystallographic structures of shorter RNAs. These results provide insight into the mechanism through which confinement alters the ensemble of 3D structures accessible to a long RNA molecule.
items.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences

items.title: Kinome profiling enabled development of a LATS1/2 inhibitor with wound healing potential
items.abstract: System-level mapping of kinase inhibitors’ polypharmacology can uncover opportunities for drug repurposing and identify starting points for medicinal chemistry campaigns aimed at novel targets. Here, we describe a large-scale profiling of 257 kinase inhibitors that revealed domains of promiscuity, a broad region of uninhibited targets and discrete pockets of selectivity. Focusing on a subcluster enriched for AGC group kinases and using the AKT inhibitor AT-7867 (an antiproliferative agent) as a starting point, we employed scaffold hopping and property-based optimization to discover NCGC-6782, a LATS1/2 inhibitor with robust proproliferative activity. In biochemical and cell-based assays, NCGC-6782 inhibited LATS1/2 activity, reduced YAP phosphorylation, and promoted rapid YAP nuclear translocation and transactivation of YAP-target genes. Kinome-wide profilings demonstrated good in vitro selectivity and exquisite chemoproteomic and kinetic selectivity. In vivo, NCGC-6782 exhibited favorable pharmacokinetic (PK) profiles following intraperitoneal (IP), intravenous (IV), or oral (PO) dosing, leading to rapid inhibition of YAP-phosphorylation in murine liver samples. Transcriptomics and proteomics following NCGC-6782 revealed upregulation of YAP-dependent genes (4 h) followed by activation of cell cycle programs (24 h). Consistently, NCGC-6782 accelerated proliferative regeneration in both cell-based and in vivo wound healing models of full-thickness excisional skin injury, significantly shortening wound-closure time without evidence of systemic toxicity. Altogether, we describe an optimized, potent, and selective LATS1/2 kinase inhibitor with desirable drug-like properties and broad potential for regenerative medicine applications following acute injury of nonproliferative, postmitotic tissues.
items.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences

items.title: On-site, subannual climate records decouple Neolithic expansion from climate instability
items.abstract: How the life of prehistoric people was influenced by climate change and extreme events often remains elusive. Finding appropriate spatiotemporal scales is the major challenge for studies with socioenvironmental questions. This challenge can be overcome by sourcing climatic information from archaeological sites, alongside traces of human agency. For instance, extreme cold-events have been proposed as causing a standstill in early farming expansion across the Mediterranean 8600-8000 years ago. However, there is no immediate (local/short-term) evidence of such events and how they might have influenced people’s lives, nor have previous records been sufficiently resolved to test this robustly. Here we statistically assess the influence of on-site and short-term extremes on human decision-making hypothesized by long-term climate records. Using the largest dataset yet of high-resolution temperature archives in mollusks, we test whether early farmers would have been exposed to extreme cold-events, compromising their subsistence by reducing harvest yields. This immediate agricultural risk is argued to have prevented the spread of new settlements and thus delayed the vigorous expansion that followed, one of prehistory’s fastest known dispersals. Direct comparison of paleotemperature and subsistence data from the same archaeological contexts shows no winter cooling of the magnitude proposed for this period, and no strong relationship between climate and subsistence. Our study reveals how a major scale mismatch in climate-society research can be resolved at the site level, integrating climatic variability on the subannual timescale crucial to farming, and provides a direct, local empirical test of a long-assumed climate impact.
items.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences

items.title: Lifetime stressor exposure is associated with altered trust formation and social learning in dynamic interactions
items.abstract: Although trust is fundamental to social interactions, how lifetime stressor exposure relates to the cognitive processes underlying trust remains poorly understood. Using the Stress and Adversity Inventory (STRAIN) to assess cumulative lifetime stressor exposure, combined with an adaptation of the repeated trust game and computational modeling (Hierarchical Gaussian Filtering), we investigated how stressors experienced over the life course relate to three core aspects of trust dynamics—initial trust formation, learning about others’ intentions, and adaptation to changes in trustworthiness—in 168 adults. Greater lifetime stress was associated with stronger negativity biases, lower initial trust, and heightened uncertainty about others’ intentions, increases that were general rather than specific to partner type. These more pessimistic priors were not accompanied by poorer reading of partners: Higher lifetime stress was associated with greater differentiation between prosocial and selfish trustees, driven by reduced investment in the selfish trustee alone. Computational analyses further indicated greater belief volatility, consistent with faster model-implied updating of perceived trustworthiness. These findings provide novel evidence that lifetime stress is associated with a profile consistent with recalibration, rather than a degradation, of the cognitive mechanisms underlying trust, with potential consequences for relationship formation and social functioning. They also provide a computationally grounded framework for understanding associations between adversity and social cognition and generate testable predictions for future experimental work.
items.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences

items.title: Paradoxical effects of opioids in suppression of colonic motility
items.abstract: Opiates slow colonic transit and cause constipation, effects traditionally attributed to suppression of excitatory cholinergic neurons through μ (MOR), δ (DOR), or κ (KOR) opioid receptors on myenteric neurons. However, the cellular mechanisms mediating opioid-induced constipation remain incompletely defined. We found that spontaneous enteric nitrergic motor inputs to mouse colon were reduced by opioid receptor agonists, leading to increased phasic contractions of colonic muscles, an effect abolished by pretreatment with tetrodotoxin, L-NNA, or apamin (in distal colon). Increased contractions in response to opioids are not easily explained by suppression of excitatory neural inputs, and spontaneous cholinergic motor inputs to colon were not suppressed by the MOR agonist Endomorphin-1 (EM-1). Consistent with these effects, MOR were expressed by many nitrergic neurons, and EM-1 reduced the asynchronous activity of nitrergic myenteric neurons during the period of tonic inhibition and the synchronized activity occurring normally just before neurogenic contractions. In addition to increasing phasic contractions, EM-1 enhanced Ca 2+ transients in interstitial cells of Cajal, depolarized membrane potentials of circular muscle cells, effects equivalent to the effects of tetrodotoxin. These are effects consistent with suppression of tonic inhibition. We also found that anterogradely propagating neurogenic contractions in intact colon were suppressed by receptor-specific MOR, DOR, and KOR agonists. Together, these observations demonstrate that opioid agonists suppress inhibitory rather than excitatory motor inputs to colonic muscles. Suppression of inhibitory motor inputs precludes the precisely timed cessation of enteric inhibition that causes poststimulus depolarization and peristaltic contractions.
items.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences

items.title: Active immunotherapy against IL-1β restores tissue repair under chronic inflammation
items.abstract: Chronic inflammation driven by sustained interleukin-1 beta (IL-1β) signaling disrupts the resolution phase of tissue repair by orchestrating dysregulated immune activity. As a key upstream mediator, IL-1β prolongs the activation of pro-inflammatory myeloid cells and establishes an environment that prevents the transition to tissue repair. Here, we developed an active immunotherapy against IL-1β using the self-assembling peptide nanofiber Coil29, which elicits robust and specific IL-1β-targeted immune responses in both wild-type and diabetic mice, without inducing systemic immunosuppression. In a chronic wound model, the therapy accelerated re-epithelialization and enhanced overall tissue regeneration, outperforming anti-IL-1β monoclonal antibodies. This therapy suppressed macrophage activity, promoted their M2-like polarization, enhanced pro-healing cytokine secretion and enriched the injury site with anti-IL-1β antibodies. In vitro, we found that antibodies from immunized mice reprogrammed M1 macrophages toward an M2-like phenotype, suggesting that antibody-mediated modulation of IL-1β activity may drive the enhanced wound re-epithelization seen in immunized animals. Altogether, these findings highlight a targeted, regenerative therapy for the healing of chronic wounds.
items.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences

items.title: Transcranial magnetic stimulation to the dorsolateral prefrontal cortex modulates single-neuron activity in humans
items.abstract: Transcranial magnetic stimulation (TMS) to the dorsolateral prefrontal cortex (dlPFC) is an established treatment for depression, yet the fundamental question of how cortical stimulation influences single neurons in deep brain circuits critical for mood regulation remains unanswered. Using a rare opportunity to record from intracranial microelectrodes while TMS was delivered in four neurosurgical patients, we evaluated the responses of 185 single neurons. Artifact cleaning enabled single-neuron spikes to be resolved as early as 8 ms after stimulation. We found that single-pulse TMS to the left dlPFC elicited time-locked firing responses in 46% of neurons (26% facilitated only, 19% suppressed only, 1% both). These responses occurred within deep bilateral cortical and subcortical structures, including the putamen and thalamus. Single-pulse TMS tended to facilitate spiking in striato-thalamic putative inhibitory neurons from ~8 ms, peaking at ~80 to 100 ms, and decaying until ~600 ms. In contrast, putative excitatory neurons and limbic areas were suppressed with a slower time course lasting to ~1,000 ms. TMS-evoked potentials recorded from intracranial depth macroelectrodes to quantify network activity revealed that the modulation of responsive neurons was positively correlated with cortico-striato-thalamic network activity and anticorrelated with limbic network activity in one participant with sufficient network and unit sampling. These results suggest that dlPFC TMS recruits a high percentage of neurons spanning cortical and subcortical brain regions bilaterally. The recruitment pattern selectively involves increasing the firing rate of inhibitory neurons in executive control networks while suppressing limbic excitatory drive, providing a candidate cellular mechanism for how cortical stimulation modulates distributed brain networks.
items.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences

items.title: Binding sites as dynamic hubs of coevolution encoded information flow
items.abstract: The relationship between evolution and allostery is inherently intertwined. While structural studies have elucidated allosteric mechanisms, the extent to which evolutionary sequence information encodes these dynamic networks remains underexplored. Here, we introduce Sequence-based GNM-TE, a framework that integrates coevolutionary information with Gaussian Network Model (GNM) based Transfer Entropy (TE) calculations. This approach translates evolutionary constraints, shaped by both structural and functional requirements, into functionally meaningful allosteric dynamic information. Across 29 cases, we identify binding sites as dynamic hubs of collective information transfer and reveal mode-dependent, directional information flows between these sites. These findings overall indicate that evolutionary constraints embed the architecture of allosteric regulation within protein sequences, preserving binding site communication within layered dynamic ensembles that enable robust functional control and adaptation.
items.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences

items.title: TLR7-independent control of retroviral infection
items.abstract: Development of effective immune responses against any pathogen requires efficient activation of the innate immune system followed by induction of an appropriate adaptive immune response using specific signaling pathways tailored to each infection. The sole innate immune receptor implicated in the induction of adaptive immunity to retroviral infection is Toll-like receptor 7 (TLR7). We have found that germinal center responses, neutralizing antibody production, and clearance of murine leukemia virus (MLV) infection in BALB.J and C57BL/6N (B6N) mice occurs in the absence of TLR7 signaling. This suggests that a previously unknown alternative sensing pathway exists for the activation of protective immune responses upon retroviral infection. Genetic crosses indicate that the ability to control retroviral infection in the absence of TLR7 signaling is determined by the same recessive mechanism in both B6N and BALB.J mice, suggesting that TLR7-independent responses do not result from a gain-of-function of an alternative pattern recognition receptor. Additionally, we observed that TLR7-deficient BALB.J mice produce neutralizing antibodies against mouse mammary tumor virus (MMTV) infection, indicating that this alternative sensing pathway is active against retroviruses of multiple genera. Finally, we determined that the alternative sensing pathway is also independent of both MyD88 and STING signaling. The ability of mice of two genetic backgrounds to control retroviral infection in the absence of TLR7 signaling provides a valuable tool for the identification of an additional mechanism of retrovirus control. The dissection of this pathway has the potential to alter our understanding of the requirements for the stimulation of antigen-specific neutralizing immunity.
items.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences

items.title: Rising temperatures, shifting population: Changes in children’s ambient heat exposure in China
items.abstract: The frequency and intensity of heat waves are increasing, but how these trends translate to changes in the ambient heat to which children are potentially exposed (hereafter, exposures) is not well established. One complicating factor is that it is not only extreme temperatures that change over time, but also the geospatial distribution of children. Another limitation in our understanding is that existing studies often summarize exposure as person-time accumulated above a temperature cutoff, a quantity that confounds the choice of cutoff, the duration of individual exposure, and the share of the population affected. Our study addresses these gaps by developing a double-dual-distributional framework that jointly considers two types of geospatial and temporal distributions (ambient temperatures and child populations) and two types of heat exposure thresholds, namely intensity (heat levels) and duration (hourly exceedance). To illustrate, we assessed potential exposures—the ambient heat conditions experienced—among 250 million children in China, comparing the 1989–1991 and 2019–2021 periods. We found that children’s average annual exposure to moderate or stronger heat increased by 385 h, and the share exposed to strong heat for at least 12% of hours rose from 8.1% (24.9 million) to 23.7% (59.1 million). Both rising temperatures and shifts in child population distributions contribute materially to increased heat exposures in China, a finding that suggests the need for forecasts of children’s potential heat exposures to consider shifting child population distributions.
items.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences

items.title: Molecular basis of quorum-sensing signal transduction by CqsS and its inhibition by CqsA, the autoinducer synthase
items.abstract: Vibrio bacteria possess multiple quorum-sensing systems, each of which conveys information into the cell concerning the cell density and species composition of the vicinal community. Germane to the present work is the CqsA-CqsS quorum-sensing pathway that vibrios use for intragenus communication. CqsA is the synthase for the autoinducer ( S )-3-hydroxytridecan-4-one (CAI-1), and CqsS, a bifunctional two-component kinase-phosphatase, is the CAI-1 receptor. Here, we determine the cryo-EM structures of the full-length Vibrio harveyi CqsS dimer in the apo- and ATPγS-bound states. Our structures reveal the molecular basis for the initiation of the phosphorylation cascade, which we support through biochemical and genetic analyses. Autophosphorylation of CqsS occurs in cis at the conserved histidine residue (H1), whereas phospho-transfer to the conserved aspartate residue (D1) in the C-terminal receiver domain occurs in trans . By coexpressing CqsS and CqsA to capture CqsS bound to CAI-1, we unexpectedly find a tight interaction between the CqsS intracellular domain and CqsA. In the complex, the CqsS H1 residues are positioned away from the catalytic cavity, and CqsS kinase activity is inhibited. Cryo-EM analysis, focused on the transmembrane domain of CqsS in this complex, reveals the presence of two CAI-1 molecules. CAI-1 binding induces an obvious movement of transmembrane helix 6, disrupting its extension into the cytosol, providing a structural basis for how CAI-1 binding in the periplasm is coupled to signal transduction into the cytoplasm. Together, our findings advance the understanding of CqsS-CAI-1-mediated quorum-sensing signal transduction, an activity that underpins the coordination of group behaviors in vibrios.
items.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences

items.title: The limits of scaling in aggregation-driven patterning of cell collectives
items.abstract: Robust development requires maintaining correct proportions as overall size varies. What controls and limits this scaling remains poorly understood due to the complex interplay of mechanical and biochemical embryonic factors. Combining confinement of dissociated embryonic presomitic mesoderm cells with imaging and chemical perturbations, we identified cell aggregation as the initial event in de novo posterior pole formation. Using a continuum model based solely on cell–cell attraction, we quantitatively map how the time available for aggregation-driven patterning limits the maximum scalable system size. Small systems allow rapid, robust pattern scaling, whereas coarsening dynamics substantially delay scaled patterns in large systems. Our experiments quantitatively confirm these predicted scaling regimes. Together, our results reveal a developmental time–size tradeoff governing the scaling of aggregation-driven patterns.
items.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences

items.title: Nonadiabatic dynamics of the ferroelectric soft mode
items.abstract: Most microscopic descriptions of structural dynamics assume the Born–Oppenheimer separation, where electrons adjust adiabatically to ionic motion. When this separation breaks down, electronic and lattice degrees of freedom can evolve on different timescales, giving rise to new physical phenomena beyond the adiabatic limit. Here, we use time-resolved, phase-sensitive second-harmonic generation and pump–probe reflectivity to reshape the ferroelectric free-energy landscape of SnTe while separately tracking polar order and coherent lattice motion. When photoexcitation transiently suppresses the double-well barrier, polarization dynamics become strongly nonlinear, while the coherent phonon dynamics remain harmonic. This decoupling cannot be described by a single adiabatic coordinate for the electronic polarization and ionic positions. We provide a unifying physical description for the nonadiabatic dynamics of the ferroelectric mode and the mixed displacive/order–disorder nature of SnTe based on a separation of scales for the renormalization of the ferroelectric stiffness.
items.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences

items.title: Using high-frequency data to quantify how urban nature affects air temperature and energy consumption
items.abstract: Globally, cities account for 78% of energy consumption and 70~75% of greenhouse gas emissions. Using spatially explicit data on urban vegetation, water bodies, and buildings, combined with extensive daily observations of air temperature and electricity consumption for the subtropical megacity of Shenzhen, China, this study shows that urban nature contributes to urban cooling, reducing energy consumption and associated greenhouse gas emissions. We found that green and blue spaces in the city’s built-up area had a pronounced influence on air temperature, ranging from a cooling effect of 1.27 °C to a warming effect of 0.29 °C, with the cooling effect being dominant over the course of a year. The cooling effect was greatest at moderate temperatures (~20 °C) and was lower on hotter days. We identified a temperature threshold of 16 to 18 °C above which urban nature produces measurable reductions in cooling energy demand. We found that residential electricity consumption was more temperature-sensitive than nonresidential electricity consumption. For the study year of 2021, the net electricity savings from urban nature was 1.5 billion kWh. This reduction in energy consumption translated to almost one million tons of avoided CO 2 emissions, which was 4.65-times the sequestration capacity of the city’s terrestrial vegetation and equivalent to the annual emissions of over 223 thousand people using global average annual per capita carbon emissions.
items.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences

items.title: Intratumoral cDC1–T cell clusters serve as sites of local costimulation to enhance CTL-mediated tumor rejection
items.abstract: T cells are essential for antitumor immunity, but their ability to eliminate tumors depends on interactions with type 1 conventional dendritic cells (cDC1s). cDC1s are known for cross-presenting tumor-derived antigens in lymph nodes to prime T cells, but their role within tumors remains less well understood. Here, we use a tumor array model to investigate how cDC1–T cell interactions influence immune responses and tumor fate. We show that the spatial distribution of both cDC1s and T cells determines whether a tumor can be rejected. We defined three immunotypes based on the spatial distribution of T cells and cDC1s: T cell–inflamed/dendritic cell-inflamed (TC-In/DC-In) tumors, where T cells and cDC1s coinfiltrate the tumor; T cell–inflamed/dendritic cell-excluded (TC-In/DC-Ex) tumors, where T cells infiltrate but cDC1s remain at the periphery; and T cell–excluded/dendritic cell-excluded (TC-Ex/DC-Ex) tumors, which lack both cDC1 and T cell infiltration. TC-In/DC-In tumors are most likely to undergo rejection, whereas TC-In/DC-Ex tumors persist despite T cell infiltration. Within TC-In/DC-In tumors, cDC1s interact directly with T cells, upregulate costimulatory molecules, and sustain effector T cell responses, while cDC1s in TC-In/DC-Ex tumors express higher migration-associated genes, suggesting they may exit the tumor. We further show that chemokine modulation, particularly through CXCL9, CCL5, and XCL1, can reshape immune infiltration patterns to promote intratumoral cDC1–T cell clustering and improve tumor rejection. These findings reveal an important role of cDC1 in sustaining effective antitumor immunity and highlight spatially organized cDC1–T cell clusters as critical hubs for local T cell activation.
items.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences

items.title: Afforestation reshapes wildfire activity across global temperate biomes
items.abstract: In temperate ecosystems, afforestation is rapidly expanding as a flagship climate mitigation strategy. Yet its impact on wildfires remains poorly understood, raising concerns that establishing planted forests over nonforest areas may intensify wildfire activity under increasingly fire-prone climatic conditions. Here, we combine land-use change data, fire activity records, climatic and anthropogenic covariates to quantify how afforestation alters fire occurrence and burned area across 67,248 patches distributed throughout global temperate biomes using satellite records starting in 2001. We found that, on average, afforestation increased fire occurrence by 26% and burned area by 23% in global temperate regions. However, these effects differed markedly among biomes. Wildfire responses ranged from a near-threefold increase in fire occurrence in Temperate Conifer Forests and a 38% increase in Mediterranean Woodlands biomes to an 18% reduction in the Temperate Grasslands, Savannas, and Shrublands biome. In Temperate Broadleaf and Mixed Forests, afforestation reduced fire occurrence but increased burned area, indicating a shift toward less frequent but larger wildfires following the conversion to planted forest. These contrasting, biome-specific responses show that the consequences of afforestation on wildfire activity may depend strongly on ecological and regional context. The strong variability at biome-scale questions the premise that tree planting provides consistent climate mitigation benefits across all landscapes, and highlights the need to evaluate afforestation initiatives alongside regional disturbance regimes. Our findings indicate that wildfire risk should be explicitly accounted for when assessing the long-term effectiveness of afforestation as a climate mitigation strategy in a warming world.

items.title: At long last, BchE gets its day in the sun

items.title: Pericyte contraction generates angiostatic effect via cell force–dependent activation of TGFβ
items.abstract: Pericytes are phenotypically plastic and capable of switching between contractile and proliferative phenotypes, similar to vascular smooth muscle cells. The intimate interaction of contractile pericytes with endothelial cells (ECs) is essential to the maturation, quiescence, and stability of the capillary and microvascular endothelium. However, the mechanistic link between pericyte contraction and vascular stability is unknown. It is known that TGFβ has dual pro- and antiangiogenic effects depending on the downstream Smad signaling. Here, we show that R-Ras-mediated contractility in pericytes activates TGFβ by integrin-dependent, actomyosin-generated cell traction force. This TGFβ activation, in turn, promotes the quiescence of ECs via the ALK5-Smad2/3 axis of the TGFβ pathway in ECs, but not the Smad1/5 axis of the TGFβ pathway. Furthermore, pericyte-targeted deletion of Rras in mice resulted in impaired pericyte contractility and a significant reduction of Smad2/3 phosphorylation in ECs, accompanied by increased tumor angiogenesis and vessel deformation in the skeletal muscle. These observations suggest that pericytes use the cell force to maintain the quiescence of the endothelium by elevating the local bioavailability of active TGFβ. Our findings provide a mechanism by which pericytes stabilize blood vessels.

items.title: Where intention goes, responsibility flows: Grounding AI accountability in the machine learning paradigm
items.abstract: An opening salvo of lawsuits in US courts has begun holding AI companies accountable through independent doctrinal routes: Product liability and agency law cut as swords, while the shields of Section 230 immunity and First Amendment doctrine begin to crack. This Perspective points out that these converging paths share a unifying principle, built on the very engineering architecture of machine learning (ML) itself. Every ML system, across all variants, is constituted by a human-specified objective function before learning begins. Training data, deployment context, user interaction, and postdeployment oversight add further layers of deliberate human intention traceable to identifiable actors. AI output is therefore not the expression of a single speaker but a composite of layered human intents. It takes a village to raise an AI, and everyone in that village bears a duty of care. This transforms AI accountability from a philosophical puzzle into a tractable legal inquiry: Trace the chain of intentional design decisions across the ML pipeline, grade each actor’s responsibility by their intent’s specificity and foreseeability, and apportion liability accordingly, following the standard three doctrine-neutral questions (attribution, causation, apportionment). Sufficient for most cases, four gaps remain: who owes what share when many hands build one system, proving fault inside an opaque model, harms that surface only after deployment, and remedies that match the technology’s pace. Targeted reforms drawing on environmental, vaccine, and financial regulatory precedents can close these gaps without requiring new legal categories, AI speech rights, AI legal personhood, or defining AI consciousness.

items.title: Mark A. Ratner (1942–2026): Founded molecular electronics while spearheading the growth of science at Northwestern University
items.abstract: Recently, we lost one of the original developers of the field of molecular electronics. Mark A. Ratner wrote a famous paper in 1974 that developed the theoretical framework for making a molecule act as a rectifier. This idea, and a host of further ideas that were stimulated by this and other papers, led to a huge amount of experimental and theoretical studies that continue to this day. But Mark’s career was much more than that, with leadership at Northwestern University and beyond that continues to shape the scientific enterprise.
